Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > SCORM Content:
SCORM (Shareable Content Object Reference Model) is a standard that ensures e-learning content created using different authoring tools works with the Mindtickle platform.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > SCORM Content > Supported versions and formats:
Mindtickle supports the following e-Learning standards:

| Standard | Supported versions | File format | Recommended |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SCORM | 1.1, 1.2, 2004 (all editions) | .ZIP | SCORM 1.2 or SCORM 2004 - 4th edition |
| AICC | Supported | .ZIP | - |
| xAPI | Supported | .ZIP | - |

Note:

- For Camtasia, Mindtickle does not support SCORM 1.2. Use SCORM 2004 when exporting content from Camtasia. For tool-specific export settings, refer to the best practices articles for Articulate Storyline 360 , Articulate Storyline 2 & 3 , Articulate Rise, Adobe Captivate 9 , and Camtasia .
- xAPI packages can be uploaded and played in Mindtickle. However, advanced xAPI tracking capabilities for capturing detailed learner experience data are not currently supported.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > SCORM Content > Before you upload:
Before uploading a SCORM package, ensure the following:

- The file is in ZIP format.
- The imsmanifest.xml file is at the root level of the .ZIP archive. If the files reside in a folder, do not zip the folder; instead, select all files and subfolders within it and zip them directly.
- The SCORM package is in HTML5 output format for both web and mobile compatibility.
- If your existing content is available only in Flash format, republish it in HTML5 format using your authoring tool before uploading it to Mindtickle.

Note:

- The SCORM files are available on the mobile app but require an active internet connection. Due to the interactive nature of the SCORM content and its technical requirements for tracking user progress and performance, you cannot access the SCORM files offline.
- To improve the content upload process, admins can now use various methods to upload content in the Content Center. For more information, see Add or replace content in Content Center .

For troubleshooting common upload errors such as manifest errors, unzip errors, and validation failures, see the SCORM upload troubleshooting guide.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > SCORM Content > Upload SCORM files > Upload SCORM in Content Center:
This section explains how to upload SCORM files in Content Center.

1. On the admin site homepage , click Content Center .
2. On the Content Center page, click the New dropdown and select Add file .
3. On the Add files screen, you can either drop a file or click an option to upload. Note : The SCORM file must be in .ZIP format, and the maximum supported file size is 5 GB . Contact your Customer Success Manager (CSM) if you need to increase the file size limits. The system displays the upload progress in Notifications . The SCORM file is displayed in the Content Center.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > SCORM Content > Upload SCORM files > Upload SCORM as learning objects within modules:
Admins can add SCORM files as learning objects within courses and quick update modules.

1. Open a course or quick update module.
2. Go to the Build tab.
3. Click Add learning objects .
4. In the Add learning objects screen, click Content .
5. On the Select File window, if the SCORM file already exists in Content Center, select the required file. Use the search bar to find a specific file, or apply filters to view all SCORM files.
6. To upload a new SCORM file, click New > Add file .
7. On the Add files screen, you can either drop the file or click to browse to upload the SCORM file. The platform then validates the SCORM file. If there is an issue with the SCORM, an error message displays.
8. Click the Show error details to view the error details.
9. To reupload the SCORM file, click Add learning object and upload a new SCORM file, or reach out to your SCORM expert to resolve the error in the SCORM file. Tip: You may share the screenshot of the error with your SCORM expert for faster debugging. Once the SCORM file is uploaded successfully, it displays within the learning object.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > SCORM Content > Replace the SCORM file > Replace file in Content Center:
Note: You must have the Manage Content permission in the Content Center and on the file you want to replace.

- Selecting Replace file in Content Center so it updates everywhere the file is used, no need to update individual modules.
- Click Next to select the new file. The Replace file screen is displayed.
- Select the new file. The system processes the new file.
- Once the file is uploaded, select the configuration settings for the file.
- Click Save changes .
- After replacement, the file is saved automatically in both the learning object and the Content Center.

Important considerations:

- Changes apply to all modules containing the file.
- Learner progress in affected modules is not impacted.
- You cannot revert to the previous file version after replacement.
- The new file must be the same type as the original.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > SCORM Content > Edit SCORM configuration:
- Admins can edit SCORM configurations from Content Center or from the learning object in a Course or Quick Update where the SCORM file is used.
- When adding a SCORM file to a learning object, admins can configure how learners consume the SCORM content.
- Any configuration updates are automatically reflected everywhere the SCORM file is used across the platform. Note : If the SCORM file is added from Content Center, you can edit the configurations only if you have collaborator access to that file in Content Center.

To edit the configurations,

1. Click View configuration.2. On the View configuration pop-up, the following configurations are available:

For desktop, the following configurations are available:

- Inline: The SCORM content opens within the web page, while learners can still view topics and learning objects.
- Full Screen: The SCORM content opens in a full-screen view within the same browser tab.
- New window: The SCORM content opens in a separate browser window. Use this option for AICC packages to avoid cross-domain errors. Note: On a tablet browser, SCORM content opens inline within the Mindtickle page.

For the mobile app:

- SCORM content opens inline on the mobile screen by default.
- You can disable SCORM access on mobile by selecting the Disable on mobile option. When disabled, learners see a message prompting them to access the SCORM content on a desktop.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > SCORM Content > Test the SCORM content:
- Follows SCORM Standards : Displays a status based on whether your SCORM package meets the required standards:
  - Published using a Mindtickle-supported SCORM version and format. Mindtickle supports SCORM 1.1, SCORM 1.2, and SCORM 2004 (across all editions) in .ZIP file format. However, we recommend using SCORM 1.2 or SCORM 2004 (4th edition).
  - SCORM package size is less than 500 MB.
  - Implemented best practices for publishing SCORM content on Mindtickle using Articulate Storyline 360 , Articulate Storyline 2 & 3 , Articulate Rise , Adobe Captivate 9 , and Camtasia . A green status ( ) indicates that your SCORM meets the required standards, and an orange status ( ) indicates that it does not.
- Receiving Completion Status : Displays a status based on whether your SCORM package tracks the progress of the SCORM content and sends a completion status. A green status ( ) indicates that your SCORM works as expected and sends a completion status when the content is completed.An orange status ( ) indicates that the SCORM is not sending a completion status when the content is completed.
- Original Score from SCORM : Displays the score received from SCORM in percentage. For example, if you got 2 out of 10 questions correct in the SCORM, your score would be 20%. This score is set within the SCORM package itself. If no score is configured in SCORM, then the result would be 100% for this test if the completion status is received.
- Score in Mindtickle : Displays ON if scoring in Mindtickle is enabled, and vice versa. To learn about how scoring for a SCORM package works in Mindtickle, see the Scoring section. Note : If there is an issue with the scores or completion not being updated correctly, enable the Save and exit option and re-test the SCORM. Otherwise, refer to the SCORM Checklist for Admin for authoring the SCORM content.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > SCORM Content > How SCORM works on Mindtickle? > Scoring and completion:
The following points explain how scoring for a SCORM package works in Mindtickle:

- If the completion trigger for the SCORM package is based on the number of slides viewed, then the maximum score will be registered once the learner completes viewing the content.
- If the SCORM package score is based on quiz results, Mindtickle will update the learner's score in proportion to the score set in Mindtickle. For example, if the maximum score in your SCORM package is 100, and the maximum score in Mindtickle is set to 50. If a learner scores 50 points in the SCORM package, they will be given 25 points in Mindtickle.
- Partial scoring based on quizzes passed or failed is also replicated proportionally in Mindtickle.
- If a learner does not finish the SCORM content and exits out of Mindtickle, the Learner's completion status depends on the "resume after suspend" configuration in the SCORM package:
  - If the configuration is enabled, the learner's progress resumes from the last location within the SCORM content in Mindtickle.
  - If the configuration is not enabled, learners will have to start from the beginning.
- If the learner’s score or completion status is reflected correctly in the SCORM content but not in Mindtickle, enable Save and exit and retest the package. This setting helps the package send its latest tracking information to Mindtickle, but does not mark the module as complete.

The following points explain how a SCORM file works when you update or replace it via the Content Center.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > SCORM Content > How SCORM works on Mindtickle? > Scoring and completion:
- If learners complete the SCORM package before the SCORM file is replaced in Content Center:
  - Completion and scores are not impacted as the learner has already completed the SCORM.
  - Bookmarks from the previous SCORM are lost, and the new SCORM plays from the beginning.
  - Bookmarks for the new SCORM work as usual. That is, learners can resume the new SCORM content from where they had left off.
- If learners have partially consumed the SCORM but not completed it before the SCORM file is replaced in Content Center:
  - Scores for partial consumption (if available) are retained, and the completion status remains unchanged.
  - Bookmarks from the previous SCORM are lost, and the new SCORM plays from the beginning.
  - Bookmarks for the new SCORM work as usual. That is, learners can resume the new SCORM content from where they had left off.
  - Scores and completion status get updated as the learner consumes the updated SCORM.

  - Scores for partial consumption (if available) are retained, and the completion status remains unchanged.
  - Bookmarks from the previous SCORM are lost, and the new SCORM plays from the beginning.
  - Bookmarks for the new SCORM work as usual. That is, learners can resume the new SCORM content from where they had left off.
  - Scores and completion status get updated as the learner consumes the updated SCORM.

- The score and completion status can be tracked in Mindtickle Analytics for a given learner. Note : A SCORM package is treated as a single Learning Content item. Therefore, analytics for individual slides and/or quizzes within the SCORM package are not tracked in Mindtickle. In Mindtickle analytics, you can track the performance of learners through downloaded reports:

- Score and completion status of the SCORM package.
- Performance on questions that are part of the quiz/assessment within the SCORM package. Note : A SCORM package is treated as a single learning content item. Therefore, analytics of individual slides within the SCORM package are not tracked in Mindtickle. Refer to the Analytics reports for SCORM content article for more information on SCORM reports for analytics on questions in SCORM content quizzes.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Course and quick update:
A course is a training module used for developing in-depth training. Admins can create multiple topics and learning objects within a course. Various elements such as images, videos, text files, presentations, embedded links, and more are used to create topics within a course. Since a course facilitates microlearning, it is recommended to have a maximum of 6 topics within a course as a best practice. Adding questions within the content helps to check the learner's understanding of a course. Surveys and textual feedback implemented at the end of the Course help to reinforce learning.This article explains the steps for site owners, enablement admins, and content experts to create a course.To create a course module:

chunks.title: Create a course

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Course and quick update:
1. In the admin site sidebar, click Modules under the Training menu, and then click the Create module button. Alternatively, you can create a module in one of the following ways: A. From the Series listing page, click Create > Module button B. From within a series, click the Create module button
2. On the Add modules page that opens, hover over Course to see its details and click to get started.
3. Fill out the course details in the Create a new course pop-up: Enter the course name and a description that outlines the course information and objectives. Select the series where you want to place the course, or click Create a new series if needed. To associate tags, click Apply tags. For details, see Apply tags to modules. To learn about character limits for course attributes, see Character limits of series and module attributes. Note: If tagging isn’t enabled on your site, contact Mindtickle Support. Once all details are filled out, click Create.
4. The course overview displays where you can add topics and learning objects.Note: The default course background is Expedition.
5. Select a background for the course.
6. Click the Edit Background icon to choose a background that helps learners visualize their journey through the course. From the Select a background pane, you can:
  - Choose from available backgrounds
  - Search for a specific background
  - Upload your own by clicking Upload Background (recommended size: 1038 x 465 px in .jpeg or .png format)
7. Please note that backgrounds with a path icon are fixed, meaning topics must be placed along a set path. Backgrounds without a path icon are free, allowing flexible placement of topics. Use the filter icon to sort or filter backgrounds by type or recency, then click Apply to confirm your selection. Click Continue to proceed.
8. Choose topic view style. Select how learners will see the course topics—either as Cards or Buttons. Card view is the default for free backgrounds; Button view is the default for fixed backgrounds.

1. In the admin site sidebar, click Modules under the Training menu, and then click the Create module button. Alternatively, you can create a module in one of the following ways: A. From the Series listing page, click Create > Module button B. From within a series, click the Create module button
2. On the Add modules page that opens, hover over Course to see its details and click to get started.
3. Fill out the course details in the Create a new course pop-up: Enter the course name and a description that outlines the course information and objectives. Select the series where you want to place the course, or click Create a new series if needed. To associate tags, click Apply tags. For details, see Apply tags to modules. To learn about character limits for course attributes, see Character limits of series and module attributes. Note: If tagging isn’t enabled on your site, contact Mindtickle Support. Once all details are filled out, click Create.
4. The course overview displays where you can add topics and learning objects.Note: The default course background is Expedition.
5. Select a background for the course.
6. Click the Edit Background icon to choose a background that helps learners visualize their journey through the course. From the Select a background pane, you can:
  - Choose from available backgrounds
  - Search for a specific background
  - Upload your own by clicking Upload Background (recommended size: 1038 x 465 px in .jpeg or .png format)
7. Please note that backgrounds with a path icon are fixed, meaning topics must be placed along a set path. Backgrounds without a path icon are free, allowing flexible placement of topics. Use the filter icon to sort or filter backgrounds by type or recency, then click Apply to confirm your selection. Click Continue to proceed.
8. Choose topic view style. Select how learners will see the course topics—either as Cards or Buttons. Card view is the default for free backgrounds; Button view is the default for fixed backgrounds.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Course and quick update > Organize course structure:
This section explains how to structure your course by adding topics, organizing pages, and inserting learning objects. You'll also learn how to customize topic flow, rename or move content, and enable sequential progression for learners.

Manage pages

- Click the Page 1 dropdown and select Add page
- Use the three-dot menu next to a page to duplicate , rename , or delete it

Note: The delete option is not available if there is only one page.

Add topics

When you select a course background, one topic is added by default. To add more:

- Click the plus icon on the canvas, or
- Click the Add topic button in the side pane

Enter a relevant name for each topic.

Note: The number of topics allowed depends on the selected background layout.

Rename a topic

You can rename a topic using any of these methods:

- Click the three-dot menu next to the topic and select Rename , then click Save
- Double-click the topic in the left pane or on the canvas, enter a name, and click Save or the tick icon
- Hover over the topic card and click the rename icon , then enter a name and confirm

Organize topics

- Click the three-dot menu next to a topic or hover over the topic card to duplicate , move , rename , or delete it
- Topics can only be moved to new pages , not existing ones
- Reorder topics by dragging the six-dot handle beside the topic to a new position

Enable sequential unlocking

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Course and quick update > Add learning objects:
Within each topic, you can add one or more learning objects to enhance the course content.

- Click the Add learning objects button, or
- Hover over a topic and click the Add learning objects icon
- To insert between existing objects, hover between them and click the plus icon

Choose from the following learning object types:

- Upload content (e.g., images , videos , presentations, PDFs, embedded links)
- Build content
- Create questions and quizzes
- Gather feedback

Additional notes

- You can add in-video questions or polls to improve engagement with longer videos.
- Mindtickle supports all fonts supported by Filestack.
- For custom fonts, export content as a PDF and upload it.
- Bulk file upload is supported for creating learning objects.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Course and quick update > Preview and publish:
Preview your course to check for errors before publishing.

- Click Exit preview to return to editing.
- Contact Mindtickle Support if any issues arise.

Configure course settings before publishing. Use the To-Dos icon to track remaining tasks, which include page and topic details with clickable navigation.

After completing all tasks, go to the Publish tab to publish the module. Alternatively, check To-Dos on the Publish tab and publish from there.

Set the time it will take learners to complete this course and confirm publishing by clicking Publish now.

Upon publishing, you are directed to the Invite and track tab.

You can edit and republish the course, pushing changes selectively to learners. The module publish history is updated on the Publish tab.

To edit and republish the course module, make the required updates as discussed in previous sections, and republish it.

Note: The following course attributes are not a part of the version update and will remain the same across all versions: Name, Description, Thumbnail, Due date, and Reminders.

When republishing a course, you can choose to push the changes for the following options:

- Learners going forward (those who are invited from now on)

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Course and quick update > Edit due date > Overview:
The following three sections provide general but important details around the due date functionality:

1. “None” option to disable due date for individual learners

Using the None option in due date settings, you can disable (remove) the due date for individual learners or multiple learners in bulk. This gives you the flexibility to set a due date for some learners while leaving it unset (None) for others.

Note that the None option is available while editing an individual learner’s due date and for bulk editing of due dates (for multiple learners).

Note: The relative due date option — No. of days after the last due date set — is not available for bulk actions to prevent issues for learners with no prior due date (i.e. set to None). However, it’s available for editing an individual learner’s due date.

2. Impact of module-level due date settings

You can configure due date settings at the module level from the Settings tab > Due date and reminders > Due date for the learner. Note the following around impact of module-level due date changes:

- Turning off due dates at the module level sets the due date to None for all learners. Under the Invite and Track tab, the Due date column displays "None".
- Even if you turn off due dates at the module level, you can still assign a due date for one or more learners via the Invite and track tab.

3. Flexible due date overrides

You can edit the due date settings using one of the following three options or methods. The last option used overrides previously set due dates for learners.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Course and quick update > Edit due date > Instructions:
To edit the due date for a single learner, click theMore option against a learner to select Edit due date.

To edit the due date for multiple learners, select the checkbox next to learners and select Edit due date in the bulk action toolbar at the bottom.

The Edit due date pop-up appears.

To set a new date for learners, click the dropdown arrow and use one of the following options: Select a specific date or No. of days after the last due date set or None.

Option 1: If you select the select a specific date option, click the date dropdown arrow and select the required date from the date picker.

Click the time dropdown arrow to set the required time.

Click the timezone dropdown arrow to set the required timezone.

Option 2: If you select the No. of days after the last due date set option, enter the required number in the 'Days After Last Due Date' field.

Under What happens after the due date, select the action that should occur once the learner's due date has passed:

- Learner can still complete the course after the due date passes.
- Course freezes. Learner can’t attempt the course anymore.

Then, select the Notify selected learners about this update via email checkbox if you want to notify selected learners about the updated due date via email. Click Save once done.

Option 3: If you select the None option, the due date is disabled or removed for the learner. In other words, no deadline for this learner to complete the module. This option gives you the flexibility to set a due date for some learners while leaving it unset (None) for others. Click Save once done.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Course and quick update > Upload content:
1. In the admin site sidebar, click Modules under the Training menu, and then open the course/quick update. Alternatively, you can access the modules via the series listed under Overview and Series pages.
2. In a course or quick update, click Add learning objects .
3. From the Add learning objects drawer, select Content .
4. The Select file pop-up appears for uploading content via Content Center. Choose to upload single or multiple existing files from the Content Center or upload single or multiple new files simultaneously to create learning objects within a module (via New button). For more information, see Add or replace a file in learning object using Content Center . Note : Learn more about the file size limit in Mindtickle . To enable transcriptions and closed captions (CC) for your uploaded videos, refer to the Overview of Transcriptions and Closed Captions article.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Course and quick update > Upload content > Upload multiple content:
You can create multiple learning objects in a module by uploading multiple new files to Content Center simultaneously. This feature is available for both courses and quick updates.

For detailed instructions, see Add or replace files in course/quick update via Content Center.

Note:

- The file upload is an asynchronous process wherein, once the upload process starts, admins can continue to work on other tasks.
- The progress and status of uploads are visible in the System feedback. Any failures are also appropriately mentioned against the files in the System feedback.
- You can upload 50 files simultaneously with a maximum file size of 10GB per file.
- You cannot upload a folder for LO creation.
- Bulk upload of files is not supported in the Salesforce and Highspot external drives.
- The following file types are supported in the uploader:
  - Image: JPG, JPEG, GIF, PNG
  - Video: FLV, MP4, AVI, WMV, MOV, MKV, M4V, MPG, MPEG, VOB, WEBM
  - Audio: MP3, AAC, M4A, F4A, OGG, OGA, WAV
  - Documents: PPT, PDF, PPTX, DOCX, DOC, XLS, XLSX
  - SCORM: ZIP

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Course and quick update > Embed external content:
This section provides details on how to embed externally-hosted content into the course and quick update modules as learning objects. Use the Embed link option to add externally hosted content (like YouTube videos or Google Docs) as learning objects using a link or embed code. You’ll need to copy the shareable link or embed code from the source platform.

Click New > Embed link to add embedded content hosted on external platforms (like YouTube, Google Docs, or Slides) using an embed code or embed link. There are two key steps:

1. Get the embed code/link : Obtain the embed code or link from the source platform (like YouTube, Google Docs). Important : Mindtickle strongly recommends using the embed code if available, as it ensures more reliable embedding than a plain link.
2. Use it while adding learning objects : Perform Steps 1-3 above. In the Select file pop-up that appears, click New > Embed link . Paste the embed code or link to add the content. Click Embed once done.
  - Use the Insert iframe tag option if the source link does not contain iframe tags.
  - In the Name field, provide an appropriate name for the embed link.

Note: You can add only one embedded content item at a time; multiple embed links cannot be added at once.

Prerequisites for embedding

- Use embed code/link — not a regular URL : Only use the specific embed code or embed link provided by the platform. A regular web URL (e.g., https://docs.google.com/...) will not embed properly and may result in errors.
- Make the content publicly accessible : The content must be available to view without restrictions. For example, with Google Docs, Slides, or Sheets, you need to publish the content to the web: Go to File → Share → Publish to web → Embed. This generates a proper embed code for use in Content Center. You can also adjust sharing settings to "Anyone with the link can view" if publishing isn’t an option.

Tip: Refer to the host platform’s help documentation for steps on generating embed codes or adjusting visibility settings.

Once uploaded, you can reuse the embedded content files across the Mindtickle platform — as assets and as learning objects in courses and quick updates.

The image below shows how embedded content appears in the learning objects list.

Click Replace if you wish to replace the content and click Download if you wish to download the content to your machine.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Course and quick update > FAQs for uploading and embedding content:
1. Does the file added from Google Drive get updated on the Mindtickle platform when the source file is changed?

Yes. If the file is embedded in the Learning Object, it will be automatically updated when the source file is changed. If the file is uploaded in the learning object, it will not get updated automatically. In this case, you can re-upload the latest version of the file.

2. Do SCORM files uploaded on the Mindtickle platform appear in the Mindtickle library for later use?

Yes, SCORM files uploaded on the Mindtickle platform appear in the Mindtickle library for later use.

3. Can videos created on Vimeo be added to the Mindtickle platform?

Yes, videos created on Vimeo can be uploaded or embedded into the Mindtickle platform. It is recommended to upload videos to associate scores with them than embedding the videos.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Course and quick update > Due date and reminders > Emails for the manager:
- Choose Whom to send the email to. Select a Manager from the manager field drop-down. Note : Manager fields can be configured in the learner’s user profile. For more information, refer to Profile Management .
- Select the frequency at which the email should be sent from the Frequency drop-down and click . You can choose to send the email Daily , on every Alternate Day or Weekly . The default frequency is set to Daily . Note :
  - By default, the email will be sent at either 2 PM or 8 AM based on the manager’s timezone.
  - The frequency that you select will apply for all learners who have not completed the course and who report directly to the manager selected in the previous step.
  - If the frequency is set to Daily , the email is sent to the manager every day after the setting is configured. The email includes a list of all learners who have not completed the course within the specified due date.
  - If the frequency is set to Alternate Day , the email is sent to the manager every alternate day after the setting is configured. The email includes a list of all learners who have not completed the course within the specified due date.
  - If the frequency is set to Weekly , the email is sent to the manager on the same day of the week on which the setting was configured. For example, if the setting was configured on a Tuesday, the system runs a check on Tuesday every week. During every week, the automated email is sent to managers on Tuesday for all learners who have not completed the course within the specified due date.
  - If all learners invited to the course have completed it, the manager does not receive the escalation email.
  - If the course is multi-present, the escalation rule will apply to all learners that are invited to the course via all Series in which it is present. In this case, emails sent to the manager will receive details for learners from all Series.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Course and quick update > Gamification:
The Gamification tab provides the following settings:

- Lifeline in Questions (default): Choose to enable or disable Lifelines . Enabling it will eliminate wrong choices for the learner and reveal the correct answers depending on the number of lifelines provided. Once enabled, the lifeline option applies only to all the new learning objects added to the course. There is no change to the lifeline settings of the existing questions within the course. For example, there are five answer options in an MCQ and only two are correct answers. If you set three lifelines, it will help the learner strike out the three wrong answer choices to reveal the right ones.
- Number of Lifelines by default : Configure the number of lifelines for the learners.
- Skip learning objects (default) : Use the toggle to allow or restrict learners from skipping learning objects. When enabled, this setting applies only to newly added learning objects in the course. It does not affect the skip settings of existing learning objects. For details on the Skip setting at the learning object level, see the "Score and skip content" section in this article . Note :
  - If topics are sequentially locked, learners can still skip individual topics. Their overall progress will be marked complete once all topics are finished, but they will receive a zero score for any topic they skipped.
  - On video seeking behavior : Learners can seek (manually jump forward) in a video only if the Skip option is enabled for that learning object. If Skip is disabled, seeking forward is also restricted, and learners will be returned to their current playback position if they attempt to skip ahead. This behavior is consistent across both courses and quick updates.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Course and quick update > Gamification:
- Scoring content : Choose to enable or disable scoring on content. Note : This setting does not disable the scoring on questions and polls.
- Hall of fame : Choose to display the scores and rankings of all the participants in the course.
- Question Difficulty : Learner should answer correctly in: Configure the difficulty levels by choosing between First Attempt (Most Difficult) or Maximum Possible Attempts (Least Difficult). Note : If the difficulty is set to most difficult then the number of Wrong Attempts available to the learner is set to one. If the difficulty level is set to Least Difficult then the number of wrong attempts available to the learner is equal to the wrong answer options provided in the question. For example, A question has 5 answer options, one answer option is marked correct, the remaining 4 options are wrong. The question difficulty level is set to the Least Difficult. Then the number of Wrong Attempts available to the learner will be 4, which is equal to the number of wrong answer options. Every wrong attempt will deduct 10 points from the score.

- Badge Scheme : Based on the Max Score of the course, some of the Badges get enabled automatically. You can change the points at which these Badges are rewarded to your learners. Note : The Max Score is the sum of the scores of all the topics in a course. If scoring on content is disabled, learners cannot earn Badges.

You can also customize the badge images by following these steps.

1. Toggle on the badge to enable it if disabled.

By default, it is set to 15 days before the certificate expiry date.

- Version Learners attempt when they recertify : Allows you to select the version of the course learners attempt when they recertify. For example, if the course has changed since the learner’s previous attempt, you can choose the current or a previous version of the course on which you want the learner to recertify.

Gamification in Mindtickle helps you keep track of your progress in a module and the scores and rewards you earn for the modules assigned to you. This article is intended for learners and provides an overview of various gamification elements, such as scoring, badges, certification, and Hall of Fame.

Note: Your admin can enable and configure the elements of gamification, and can even disable gamification entirely. Therefore, the availability and scope of gamification depends on how the admin has configured it for you.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Get Started > Benefits:
Use gamification in Mindtickle for leaderboard competitions to provide an effective way to keep participants engaged and actively involved.

Team competitions

- Peers motivate each other to stay engaged.
- Group participants into meaningful teams (e.g. by sales region or onboarding cohort).

Individual competitions

- Participants enjoy competing for a top spot on the leaderboards.

Rewards

- Recognize the top performers by cohort and by week or program cadence.
- Provide recognition and/or small prizes for the winners.
- Avoid high-value prizes that can take the fun out of the competition. Prizes worth $10–50 are effective.
- Bragging rights and recognition are very motivational. For example, lunch or a meeting with a senior leader; recognition at a sales kickoff meeting.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Get Started > Scoring/module score:
You earn points in Mindtickle based on the completion of modules. The points for each module are configured by your admin. The total number of points you earn in a module is your module score.

Note: The option to re-attempt a module is available in the course, mission, and assessment module types. The admin can disable re-attempt for any of these modules.

This section explains how you earn points and how scoring works in Mindtickle.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Get Started > Scoring/module score > Course and quick update > Question Options:
While answering a question, you may see one or more of the options (as configured by the admin) that assist you in reaching the correct answer: Hint, Lifelines, and Wrong Attempts. If configured by the admin, you can also use the Skip option.

This section explains how to use the options and their impact on your score.

Image: Answering questions in a course

- Hint

Displays hints that help you find the correct answers. Click the button to display hints added by the admin. Using a hint does not invite any penalties.

- LifeLine

Note: The LifeLine option is available for courses and quick updates.

Displays the number of lifelines the admin has configured for you for the module. Click the button to eliminate incorrect answers.

You can use a maximum of two lifelines per question. Using a lifeline does not invite any penalties. When you answer questions correctly, you are rewarded with extra lifelines.

For example, there are five answer options in an MCQ and only two are correct. If you have three lifelines, you can use two lifelines to eliminate two incorrect answers to make it easier to find the correct answers.

- Attempts left

Allows you to make multiple attempts for a question. The Attempts left counter displays the number of attempts available for a question. When you select an incorrect answer, one wrong attempt is utilized automatically. Using wrong attempts invites a penalty of 10 points. If you do not answer the question correctly in the available attempts, you do not earn any points.

Note: Wrong attempts are not available for the True-False question types.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Get Started > Scoring/module score > Course and quick update > Question Options:
- Skip

The Skip button in the bottom-right corner lets you skip a question. Click the button to skip to the next question. If you skip a question, zero points are awarded and you cannot re-attempt the question.

When you finish answering a question, the score points you’ve earned for it are displayed above the question on the right. Click the score to see your score and badge details.

In the upper-right corner, your earned module score (out of the total module score), earned badges, and module progress are displayed.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Get Started > Scoring/module score > Mission:
Your submission in a mission is scored based on the Evaluation Parameters (Rating Scale and Multiple Choice) your admin has configured. The parameters evaluate you for specific skills that are defined by the admin.

Your score is calculated by averaging the Evaluation Parameter scores. If there are multiple Reviewers, the average of scores provided by all the Reviewers is considered. You receive parameter-wise scoring once all the Reviewers have reviewed your submission.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Get Started > Scoring/module score > Mission > Passing Cut-Off and Re-attempt:
If you do not meet the Passing Cut-Off score, you need to re-attempt the mission. Depending on the mission settings configured by the admin, the mission is either automatically assigned for re-attempt or you can re-attempt it yourself. When you re-attempt, you can view the scores of your previous submissions as well.

Note: In case of multiple Reviewers, if one of the Reviewers assigns the mission for a re-attempt, you will need to re-attempt it. All the Reviewers then review your re-attempted submission.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Get Started > Scoring/module score > Assessment:
In assessments, your score is calculated based on:

- The points you earn for correctly answering questions
- Whether you submit the assessment within the configured time limit
  - Time-Limit: When a time limit is configured by the admin, the timer starts as soon as you start the assessment. The timer does not pause if you navigate away from the assessment or log out of the platform. The assessment is submitted automatically when the time limit is reached.
- Whether you earn a Passing Score
  - Passing Score: You can pass an assessment only when you earn a Passing Score as configured by the admin.
- Whether you incur any wrong answer penalties
  - Wrong Answer Penalty: Your admin can set 5%, 10%, or 20% as the wrong answer penalty. For example, a question has 100 points and the penalty is set to 10%, then 10 points (10%) are deducted from your total score if your answer is incorrect.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Get Started > Scoring/module score > Quest:
In quest, your score is calculated based on:

- The response of the learner (correct or incorrect) to a question
- Bonus points earned for every saved attempt

Note: A saved attempt is an attempt that is not taken by the learner. For example, if the learner is given three attempts for a question and responds correctly in the first two, then the learner gets bonus points for the saved attempt.

Scores are awarded for every attempt to a question. You earn 100 points for a correct answer and zero points for an incorrect one. You can score a bonus of 100 points if you save an attempt.

To learn more, see How does scoring work in quests?.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Get Started > Badges > Creating meaningful badge strategies:
When deploying a new course or quick update, a well-planned badge strategy can significantly increase engagement, especially with high achievers and competitive teammates. It's a simple way to gamify your enablement content and build excitement about your program. Below are three tips to deploy a gamified badge strategy to keep learners engaged.

1. Make it universal When deciding on your badging strategy, consider a holistic approach. Create a plan that can be duplicated or even expanded from program to program. This can create a culture where learners are excited to earn a new badge(s) each time you launch a new program.
2. Don’t make it too easy Be sure each badge represents a significant and increasing level of difficulty. Don’t simply hand out badges for viewing content. Create a challenge where the learner feels a sense of pride in their accomplishment. In both Quick-Updates and Courses, you can create a multi-level badge structure, be sure the high badge is truly difficult to earn.
3. Get creative As we all know, media-rich content is a great way to engage learners, but don’t skimp on the badge design. Badges don’t have to be boring. Create an engaging theme where the badges build on each other such as an Olympics theme with bronze, silver, or gold medals, or something clever that fits with your company. For example, a gas and oil company could have regular, plus and premium badges or a telecommunications company could have fax, phone, email.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Get Started > Quest:
There are three types of badge rewards: Master Badge, Streak Badge, and Proficiency Level.

- Master Badge: A Master Badge will be awarded to you when you give consecutive correct answers. There are four levels in the Master Badge. Each level is unlocked based on a set criteria.
- Streak Badge: A Streak Badge will be awarded to you upon completing a Challenge within 24 hours from the time it was delivered, regardless of whether the response is right or wrong.
- Proficiency Level: A Proficiency Level is achieved when you score a defined percentage of the total Score of the quest. The percentage Score that earns you a Proficiency Level is defined by the admin while creating the quest. Proficiency Level is customizable and different levels can be enabled or disabled.

To learn more, see What is a Master Badge, Streak Badge, Proficiency Level, and Hall of fame in quest?.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Get Started > Certification:
Note: Certification is applicable only for the course, mission, and assessment modules.

Depending on the admin configuration, you get certified either on successfully completing a module or achieving the passing cut-off score, or both. The certificate mentions the module name and the highest badge you earned. On your profile page and the activity panel, you can see all the certificates you have earned.

You can also download the certificate, either from the email received on module completion or from the learning site (the module tile on your profile page).

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Get Started > Hall of fame leaderboard > Course and quick update > Opt in or out of Hall of Fame:
Depending on the settings configured by the admin, you may be allowed to opt in or opt out from sharing your scores and rankings with your peers in the Hall of fame leaderboard. If you opt out of sharing, then you will not be able to see the scores and rankings of Peers too.

Image: The Opt Out option in the Hall of fame leaderboard in a course

To learn more, see Opt-In/Opt-Out in Hall Of Fame.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Get Started > Series leaderboard:
The series Leaderboard enhances engagement and gamification experience for all learners at a series/scope series level.If your admin has enabled Leaderboard, then the respective Series details page also displays the Leaderboard tab.

You can use the leaderboard of a series/scoped public series the following ways:

- If you are part of a series, you can access and check the Leaderboard.
- If you have a series score more than zero, you can be part of the Leaderboard and your rank will be listed.
- If your admin invited you to the series, you can compare your rank among peers based on the given period.

Note: The feature is currently available on the web only. It will be available soon on the Mindtickle mobile app.

Refer to Series section on the learning site to learn more about the series details page for learners.Click Leaderboard on the series details page of your invited series /scoped public series, or subscribed series/ scoped public series. Filter this leaderboard based on when the learners were invited or subscribed to this series. The default time period is past 90 days. You have the following filters:

- Past 30 days.
- Past 90 days.
- Past year.
- All time.

Leaderboard determines the learner ranks by a combination of the learner’s absolute points earned for modules in the series and the timing of achieving the score, considering the day and time. For more information on how the Leaderboard calculates rank, see Mindtickle Series Leaderboard.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Get Started > Series leaderboard > Rank Determination:
The leaderboard determines the learner ranks by a combination of the learner’s absolute points earned for modules in the series and the timing of achieving the score, considering the day and time.

The leaderboard provides the following insights using its rank section:

- The respective learner viewing their leaderboard is highlighted. They can check their rank list on the left and their points on the right. The rank section also shows the total peers listed on the respective leaderboard.

- When a learner’s rank is more than the cache limit set to the leaderboard rank section, click Show more to view the subsequent ranking groups.

- In the rank section, ranks are grouped by ten learners to show the respective neighboring peers before and after the learner’s rank. For example, if the learner is ranked at 25, the rank section will show ranks from 21-30. Similarly, for rank 120, the ranking group between 111-120 is shown.

The following caveats explain how score and rank are altered based on the various actions on the series or their respective modules:

- A learner can access and view the leaderboard once they are part of the series. To participate in the leaderboard, the learner should have a score greater than zero.
- If the admin modifies the score of a module, the learner's original earned score remains unchanged.
- If the admin moves, deletes, or archives a module, the respective module scores are deducted for all learners who participated in that module.

In a mirrored module, if a learner has previously earned points but hasn't received an invitation to the module, they can only gain points on the leaderboard in the following ways:

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Course and Quick Update > Participate in discussions:
If enabled, every topic within a course has its own dedicated discussion thread. To participate, follow these steps:

1. On the topic page, the Discussions tab is open by default on the sidebar.
2. Type your question or feedback into the text box.
3. Click Post . Your post will now be visible on the Discussions tab for other learners to see, like, or reply to.
4. To respond to another learner’s query or feedback, click Reply under their post. To appreciate a learner’s post, click Like .
5. Click Full view to open the complete discussions page, where you can view questions, comments, and activities across topics and learning objects in the module.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Integrations > Single Sign-On (SSO) > How does the integration with JSON web token work?:
1. An unauthenticated user (not already logged in) navigates to your Mindtickle Learning Site URL. For example, https://<mylearningsite>.mindtickle.com/.

2. The Mindtickle SSO mechanism recognizes that SSO is enabled and that the user is not authenticated.

3. The user is redirected to the remote login URL configured for the SSO settings. For example, https://mycompany.com/mindtickle/sso?returnTo=https://<mylearningsite>.mindtickle.com/login/ssojwt.

4. A script at your end authenticates the user using your proprietary login process. The script builds a JWT request that contains the relevant user data.

5. You redirect the customer to the Mindtickle endpoint at https://<mylearningsite>.mindtickle.com/login/ssojwt?jwt=<JWT payload> with the JWT payload.

6. Mindtickle parses the user details from the JWT payload and then grants access to the user.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Integrations > Single Sign-On (SSO) > Steps to be performed in Mindtickle:
1. On the admin site homepage, hover over the Account icon on the left navigation bar, and click Settings .
2. On the Security & integrations tab, copy the API Key and Secret Key from the fields provided to create the JWT request later.
3. Scroll down to the Single Sign On section and enable the toggle switch.
4. Click the JWT SSO tab.
5. Enter the Remote Login URL as shown below.
6. https://mycompany.com/mindtickle/sso?returnTo=https://<mylearningsite>.mindtickle.com/login/ssojwt
7. Click Activate SSO .

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Integrations > Single Sign-On (SSO) > Create a JWT Request:
| Attribute | Mandatory | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| iat | Yes | “iat” refers to the Issued At time. “iat” ensures that a given token is utilized immediately after it is generated. The value in “iat” must be equal to the number of seconds since the UNIX epoch (a point in time from which system time is measured). Mindtickle allows up to a two-minute clock skew (difference in the reading of same sourced clocks). Therefore, make sure to set up a Network News Transfer Protocol (NNTP) or similar on your servers. |
| jti | Yes | “jti” refers to JSON Web Token ID. “jti” is a unique ID for the JSON web token which Mindtickle uses to prevent token replay attacks.A token replay attack occurs when a hacker eavesdrops on a secure network communication, intercepts it, and then fraudulently delays or resends the token to misdirect the receiver into doing what the hacker wants. |
| email | Yes | “email” refers to the Email Address of the user who is signing in. It is used to identify the user record in Mindtickle uniquely. |
| sub | No | “sub” refers to the Name of the User. The user may be required to update the username if “sub” is not provided during the first login. |
| exp | Yes | “exp” refers to the Expiration Time. It is the time in which the token will expire. Its value must be equal to the number of seconds since the UNIX epoch. Note:“exp” cannot be less than the issue time (“iat”). The maximum value of expiration time can be one hour from the issue time (iat < exp < iat+3600). |
| iss | Yes | “iss” contains the API Key value that you have copied in the previous step. |
| uid | No | “uid” refers to the Unique Identifier of users.If the users are uniquely identified by something other than an email address, and their email addresses are subject to change, send their unique identifier and specify the identifier as a string. |
| user_attributes | No | “user_attributes” map Profile Keys to their Values.You can request a list of valid profile keys from Mindtickle Support. Example format in which Mindtickle needs “user_attributes” is as follows:"user_attributes": [{ "type":"PROFILE", "key": "rg", "value":"Account Executive" }, { "type":"MANAGER", "key": "a_0", "value":"pamela.judd@mindtickle.com" }], |

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Integrations > Single Sign-On (SSO) > Create a JWT Request:
You can request a list of valid profile keys from Mindtickle Support. Example format in which Mindtickle needs “user_attributes” is as follows:"user_attributes": [{ "type":"PROFILE", "key": "rg", "value":"Account Executive" }, { "type":"MANAGER", "key": "a_0", "value":"pamela. judd@mindtickle. com" }], |

Refer to the sample java code below to generate the JWT request URL using returnTo, API Key, and Secret Key copied from the Mindtickle platform in the previous steps. This code uses the nimbus-jose-jwt library.

```
<dependency>  <groupId>com.nimbusds</groupId>  <artifactId>nimbus-jose-jwt</artifactId>  <version>9.8.1</version></dependency>
```

```
private static String getJwtRequestUrl() {        String JWT_RETURN_TO_URL = "https://mylearningsite.mindtickle.com/login/ssojwt";        String SECRET_KEY = "1b2050226f1268e75exxxxxxxxxxxxxxexxxxxxxxxxfb0c741be3bb5b318dc48f7497a";        String API_KEY = "4ce31feb2bxxxxxxxxxxxxxxcxxb60cba3ab";        JWTClaimsSet.Builder jwtClaims = new JWTClaimsSet.Builder();        Date date = new Date();        jwtClaims = jwtClaims.issueTime(date);        // Maximum value of expiration time can be 1 hr from the issue time        jwtClaims.expirationTime(new Date(date.getTime() + 3600000));        jwtClaims.jwtID(UUID.randomUUID().toString());        jwtClaims.issuer(API_KEY);         jwtClaims.claim("sub", "Marla Greyson");        jwtClaims.claim("email", "marla.greyson@mindtickle.com");         // Assuming "rg" as the key for the user's location, this maps to the profile fields and manager profile fields        List<Map<String, String>> userAttributes = new ArrayList<>();        Map<String, String> profileField = new HashMap<>();        profileField.put("type", "PROFILE");        profileField.put("key", "rg");        profileField.put("value", "Account Executive");        userAttributes.add(profileField);        Map<String, String> managerFields = new HashMap<>();        managerFields.put("type", "MANAGER");        managerFields.put("key", "a_0");        managerFields.put("value", "pamela.judd@mindtickle.com");        userAttributes.add(managerFields);        jwtClaims.claim("user_attributes", userAttributes);         JWSHeader.Builder header = new JWSHeader.Builder(JWSAlgorithm.HS256);        header.type(new JOSEObjectType("JWT"));         JWSObject jwsObject = new JWSObject(header.build(), new Payload(jwtClaims.build().toString()));        JWSSigner signer = null;        try {            signer = new MACSigner(SECRET_KEY.getBytes());        } catch (KeyLengthException e) {            System.err.println("Error creating signer in JWT: " + e.getMessage());            return "Error=" + e.getMessage();        }         String url = "";        try {            jwsObject.sign(signer);            url = JWT_RETURN_TO_URL + "?jwt=" + jwsObject.serialize();            System.out.println("url=" + url);        } catch (JOSEException e) {            System.err.println("Error signing JWT: " + e.getMessage());            url = "Error=" + e.getMessage();        }         return url;    }
```

This section explains how to select and add multiple users in bulk to groups.

Note: If you select any deactivated users to add to groups, then they are also restored during this operation.

1. Sign in to the admin site.
2. On the left navigation bar, click Users and select Users.
3. On the Users page, click the users' checkbox to add to groups.
4. Click Add to groups from the options at the screen's bottom.
5. Alternatively, to add an individual user to groups, click the More options icon for the user and then select Add to groups.
6. On the Add users to groups screen, select one or more groups to which you want to add the users.
7. Click the checkboxes of the groups to add the user.
8. To create a new group and add the user, click Add new groups.You can create up to five groups at once. If any of the selected users are already part of the listed groups, it is indicated in “x/y Already Added”. For example, if 2 of the 7 selected users are already part of 3 groups, then these 3 groups would show “2/7 Already Added”.
9. Click + Add another to create more than one group.
10. Once you have added the new groups, click Create (n) new groups.The new groups are displayed on the Add users to groups page.
11. Click Add to groups to add the user to the selected groups.The user is now added to the selected groups.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Course and quick update:
1. From a course or quick update, click Add learning objects button on the Build tab.
2. In the Add learning objects panel, select the question type of your choice under Create questions and quizzes section.
3. The following options are available:
  - Multiple choice questions - Has fixed options and provides immediate feedback to the learner.
  - Multiple choice images - Can be used in place of multiple choice questions if learners are expected to select images from a list of options.
  - Word guess - Similar to fill in the blank type questions.
  - Match the labels - Similar to a drag and drop type question.
  - Match image with label - Can be used when learners have to match an object name with the object image.
  - Mark the location - A hot spot question where learners must select the correct answer(s) from the options provided on the image.
  - True or false - Learner’s distinguish between true and false answer options to a question.
  - Text answer - Text answer is similar to Word guess. Here, the learner has to enter the answer manually. You can define the percentage accuracy of the answer or allow answers without accuracy enabling the learner to freely submit any answer without any accuracy check with a full score. For more information, see Question Types . Note : The Text answer learning object is enabled with an accuracy check by default. To request Text answer allowing options for answers with and without accuracy, contact your Customer Success Manager (CSM).
  - Bulk upload questions- Learners can bulk upload multiple-choice questions using an Excel sheet template. Check out the bulk upload questions article.
4. Once you add the learning object, you’re redirected to the Build tab. Refer to Question Types in Mindtickle to learn more about each question in detail.
5. All question types have three sections: Question , Answer options , and Factopedia . While the question and Factopedia sections remain the same for each question, the answer option section varies.
6. Enable or disable Factopedia by toggling the On/Off switch located on the Factopedia tab. If enabled, you can add supporting information related to the main content in the form of Text , Multimedia , or Handouts . Note: We highly recommend reading the best practices for Factopedia before using it.
7. Configure the difficulty levels by setting the number of Wrong attempts from 1 to 3 and also configure Hint .
8. Choose to enable or disable Lifeline . Enabling it will eliminate wrong choices for the learner. Note: The Lifeline functionality is available for courses and quick updates.
9. If you are using mostly multiple choice questions in course or quick update and/or text answer questions in course, you have the option to bulk upload questions .
10. Once your module is deployed, navigate to analytics to view the question response data in your course or quick update.

Note : If you do not have tags enabled for your site, contact Mindtickle Support.

Note : When you have multiple learning objects, hover between learning objects and click the plus icon that displays on hover to add a learning object between them.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Course and quick update > Score and skip content:
Score

You can add up to 20 learning objects in any combination to a quick update. Contact Mindtickle Support if you want to increase the limit and add more learning objects to a quick update. As a best practice, we recommend limiting the number of learning objects to a maximum of 25 in a quick update.

After adding the content, question, and/or feedback, you can set a score for each learning object. The score ranges between 50 to 500.

As an admin, you can assign different scores to various content parts, such as 50 points for introductions and 100 points for questions and knowledge checks. Learners earn points for correct answers, but no points are awarded for incorrect ones. You can also add badges for higher scores. This scoring system helps track learners' progress and indicates solid understanding when all questions are answered correctly.

Skip

Use the toggle to allow or restrict learners from skipping learning objects. If turned ON, learners see a Skip option for the learning object. For details on the default Skip setting at the module level, see the "Gamification" section in this article.

Note:

- If topics are sequentially locked, learners can still skip individual topics. Their overall progress will be marked complete once all topics are finished, but they will receive a zero score for any topic they skipped.
- On video seeking behavior : Learners can seek (manually jump forward) in a video only if the Skip option is enabled for that learning object. If Skip is disabled, seeking forward is also restricted, and learners will be returned to their current playback position if they attempt to skip ahead. This behavior is consistent across both courses and quick updates.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Course and quick update > Preview and publish:
After you have configured the learning objects, Preview them once before publishing to avoid any errors or inconsistencies.

Click Exit Preview to go back to the learning object. In case of any issues, click to contact the helpdesk.

Configure the quick update settings before publishing the quick update. To learn more about quick update settings, refer to the Configure quick update Settings article.

Click the To-Do(s) icon to determine if you have any tasks left to complete.

Alternatively, you can check the to-do(s) on the Publish tab. Click Publish on the navigation bar and click x to do.

Once you have completed all the tasks, toggle on to set the time for learners to complete this quick update and enter the estimated time in minutes.

Click Confirm publish. Once the quick update is successfully published, the following actions occur:

Once you have completed all the tasks, publish the quick update by clicking the Publish module button. You have the following options while publishing your quick update.

You are automatically directed to the Invite and track tab. The Publish history is updated on the Publish tab.

To edit your quick update after publishing it, make the necessary updates and follow the steps mentioned in Build content and Preview and publish, and republish it. Alternatively, select the Edit option in your Quick update thumbnail on the Content Home.

When republishing a quick update, you can choose to push the changes for the following options:

- Learners going forward (those who are invited from now on)
- Learners who haven’t started the quick update
- Learners who have not started or completed the quick update
- All learners (including those who have completed the quick update)

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Course and quick update > Edit due date > Overview:
The following three sections provide general but important details around the due date functionality:

1. “None” option to disable due date for individual learners

Using the None option in due date settings, you can disable (remove) the due date for individual learners or multiple learners in bulk. This gives you the flexibility to set a due date for some learners while leaving it unset (None) for others.

The None option is available while editing an individual learner’s due date and for bulk editing of due dates (for multiple learners). See the following image for reference.

Note: The relative due date option — No. of days after the last due date set — is not available for bulk actions to prevent issues for learners with no prior due date (i.e. set to None). However, it’s available for editing an individual learner’s due date.

2. Impact of module-level due date settings

You can configure due date settings at the module level from the Settings tab > Due date and reminders > Due date for the learner. Note the following around impact of module-level due date changes:

- Turning off due dates at the module level sets the due date to None for all learners. Under the Invite and Track tab, the Due date column displays "None".
- Even if you turn off due dates at the module level, you can still assign a due date for one or more learners via the Invite and track tab.

3. Flexible due date overrides

You can edit the due date settings using one of the following three options or methods. The last option used overrides previously set due dates for learners.

The last option used overrides previously set due dates for learners.

1. Settings tab > Due date and reminders > Due date for the learner To set due date settings at the module level for all learners. Turning off the setting will set the due date to None for all learners.

Even if you turn off due dates from module settings (1), you can still assign a due date for one or more learners via the Invite and track tab (2 & 3).

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Course and quick update > Edit due date > Instructions:
To edit the due date for a single learner, click theMore option against a learner to select Edit due date.

To edit the due date for multiple learners, select the checkbox next to learners and select Edit due date.

The Edit due date pop-up appears.

To set a new date for learners, click the dropdown arrow and use one of the following options: Select a specific date or No. of days after the last due date set or None.

Option 1: If you select the select a specific date option, click the date dropdown arrow and select the required date from the date picker.

Click the time dropdown arrow to set the required time.

Click the timezone dropdown arrow to set the required timezone. Click Save once done.

Option 2: If you select the No. of days after the last due date set option, enter the required number in the days after last due date field.

Under What happens after the due date, select the action that should occur once the learner's due date has passed:

- Learner can still complete the quick update after the due date passes.
- Quick update freezes. Learner can’t attempt the qi anymore.

Then, select the Notify selected learners about this update via email checkbox if you want to notify selected learners about the updated due date via email. Click Save once done.

Option 3: If you select the None option, the due date is disabled or removed for the learner. In other words, no deadline for this learner to complete the module. This option gives you the flexibility to set a due date for some learners while leaving it unset (None) for others. Click Save once done.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Course and quick update > Due date and reminders > Emails for the manager:
- Choose Whom to send the email to. Select a Manager from the manager field drop-down. Note : You can configure the Manager fields in the learner’s user profile. For more information, refer to Profile Management .
- Select the frequency at which the email should be sent from the Frequency drop-down. You can choose to send the email Daily , on every Alternate Day or We ekly. The default frequency is set to Daily . Note :
  - By default, the email will be sent at either 2 PM or 8 AM based on the Manager’s timezone.
  - The frequency that you select will apply for all Learners who have not completed the Quick-Update and who report directly to the Manager selected in the previous step.
  - If the frequency is set to Daily , the email is sent to the manager every day after the setting is configured. The email includes a list of all learners who have not completed the quick-update within the specified due date.
  - If the frequency is set to Alternate Day , the email is sent to the manager every alternate day after the setting is configured. The email includes a list of all learners who have not completed the quick-update within the specified due date.
  - If the frequency is set to Weekly , the email is sent to the manager on the same day of the week on which the setting was configured. For example, if the setting was configured on a Tuesday, the system runs a check on Tuesday every week. During every week, the automated email is sent to managers on Tuesday for all learners who have not completed the quick-update within the specified due date.
  - If all learners invited to the quick-update have completed it, the manager does not receive the escalation email.
  - If the Quick-Update is multi-present, the escalation rule will apply to all Learners that are invited to the Quick-Update via all Series in which it is present. In this case, emails sent to the Manager will receive details for Learners from all Series.
- Click View to view or edit the Email template to check the email template for learners with incomplete quick update. An email preview screen appears, which provides a sneak peek of how the email may appear to the recipient. Click Edit Template to edit its contents. For more information, refer to Edit Template .
- Click the Delete icon to delete the rule.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Course and quick update > Gamification:
- Lifelines in questions : Use the toggle to enable or disable lifelines for questions in this quick update. Lifelines provide learners additional chances to answer questions correctly, enhancing the gamification experience. Admins can set a site-level default to turn lifelines ON or OFF for newly created quick updates. This default can be overridden at the module level. If the toggle is turned ON, you can configure Number of lifelines by default , which lets you configure the total number of lifelines available by default. Benefits : Lifelines give admins granular control over gamification, letting you apply it where it’s most useful. They allow a tailored learner experience by enabling Lifelines in practice modules while disabling them for high-stakes assessments. This setting also ensures consistency by aligning quick update configuration with courses, providing a smoother admin experience.
- Skip learning objects (default) : Use the toggle to allow or restrict learners from skipping learning objects. When enabled, this setting applies only to newly added learning objects in the quick update. It does not affect the skip settings of existing learning objects. For details on the Skip setting at the learning object level, see the "Score and skip content" section in this article . Note :
  - If topics are sequentially locked, learners can still skip individual topics. Their overall progress will be marked complete once all topics are finished, but they will receive a zero score for any topic they skipped.
  - On video seeking behavior : Learners can seek (manually jump forward) in a video only if the Skip option is enabled for that learning object. If Skip is disabled, seeking forward is also restricted, and learners will be returned to their current playback position if they attempt to skip ahead. This behavior is consistent across both courses and quick updates.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Course and quick update > Gamification:
- Scoring on content : Choose to enable or disable scoring on content. Note : This setting does not disable scoring on Questions and Polls.
- Hall of fame: Choose to display the scores and rankings of all the participants in the Quick-Update.
- Question Difficulty: Learner should answer correctly in: Configure the difficulty levels by choosing between First Attempt (Most Difficult) or Maximum Possible Attempts (Least Difficult).Note: The Maximum Possible Attempts is equal to the number of Wrong Attempts provided to the learner in the questions. By default, it is set to the number of answer options provided in a question. For example, if you have provided five answer options for a question, the maximum possible attempts by default will be five. However, you can select any number in the range of 1-5 to change it. Every wrong attempt will deduct 10 points from the content score.

- Badge Scheme : Based on the Max Score of the Quick-Update, some of the Badges get enabled automatically. You can change the points at which these Badges are rewarded to your learners. Note : The Max Score is the sum of the scores of all the topics in a Quick-Update. If Scoring on content is disabled, learners cannot earn Badges.

You can also customize the Badge images by following these steps.

1. Click Edit against the Badge you want to customize.

2. Click the icon to upload your Badge image.

3. Upload an image from any location on your computer or drag the image to the Upload custom Badge window.

4. Click Confirm.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Integrations > Single Sign-On (SSO) > Steps to be performed in ADFS:
1. Run the ADFS software development wizard on your machine. Type ‘AD FS’ in the Search box at the bottom of the pane. Click ADFS 2.0 Management console.

2. On the left pane, open the Trust Relationships folder.

3. Right-click the Relying Party Trusts folder and click Add Relying Party Trusts.

4. The Add Relying Party Trust Wizard opens. On the Welcome page, click Start.

5. On the Select Data Source page, select Import data about the relying party from a file. Click Browse.

6. Select the metadata file saved on your local machine in Step 4. Click Open.

7. Click Next.

8. Enter an appropriate name in Display Name and a description in Notes. Click Next.

9. On the Choose Issuance Authorization Rule page, select Permit all the users to access this relying party. Click Next.

10. On the Ready to Add Trust page, select default settings and click Next.

11. On the Finish page, click the checkbox for Open the Edit Claim Rules dialog for this relying party trust when the wizard closes. Click Close.

12. On the screen that appears, click Edit Rules for MindTickle Training. Click Add Rule.

13. From the Claim rule template dropdown menu, select Send LDAP Attributes as Claims. Click Next.

14. Enter an appropriate name in the Claim rule name field. Select Active Directory from the drop-down menu for Attribute Store.

15. Select an LDAP Attribute from the drop-down and map it to the corresponding Outgoing Claim Type attribute that is sent to Mindtickle. Click Finish.Note: You can select any unique attribute such as employee email address or employee id.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Integrations > User Sync > Mindtickle SFDC User Sync Integration:
Following is a graphical representation of the Mindtickle SFDC User Sync Integration process.

The Salesforce-Mindtickle user sync occurs in batches, with a limit of 2000 users per batch.

For example, when syncing 2500 users, two batches are created:

- Batch 1 with 2000 users
- Batch 2 with 500 users

During the Salesforce-Mindtickle user sync, if a user in batch 1 has an invalid email format, the user sync fails for the entire batch of 2000 users. However, it succeeds for batch 2 with 500 users, as it contains valid data with no errors.

To sync your Salesforce users into the Mindtickle platform, complete the following steps.

Note: Please reach out to your Customer Success Manager if you would like to update or change your existing system.

2. You must have a Mindtickle admin account (at least an IT admin role).
