chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Integrations > User Sync > Setting filters on Salesforce users:
When one or several users get imported into Mindtickle, they must be confirmed before they are considered successfully imported. A Filter gets triggered automatically by Mindtickle. Mindtickle provides filters using allowlist/blocklist concept by using the following attributes:

- Domain - email domains only
- Specific emails - (allowlisting)
- Profile field or set of profile fields’ value(s) - (blocklisting)

Allowlisted users get added to Mindtickle platform only after the filter is applied.

You can use the SFDC User Sync template to map appropriate Profile Fields to the columns in Salesforce and email it to your Customer Success Manager.

Note: If the filters are set on Salesforce users, the deactivation in Mindtickle will happen only when the filter condition is met and users are no longer active in Salesforce.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Integrations > User Sync > Deactivation of Salesforce Users and Contacts from Mindtickle:
A Salesforce user gets deactivated from the Mindtickle platform if the user field isActive = False and set filter criteria on the user meet.

Similarly, a Salesforce contact gets deactivated from the Mindtickle partner site if the contact field isdeleted = True and set filter criteria on the contact meet.

Example:

Suppose a filter criterion is set that Mindtickle filters Salesforce users belonging to the sales department and there are two active users in Salesforce - User1 and User2. User1 belongs to the sales department and User2 belongs to the support department.

Since the filter is set for the sales department, only User1 gets created in Mindtickle in this case.

If User1 gets deactivated in Salesforce, Mindtickle will also deactivate User1.

Now, suppose User2 switches to the sales department. In this case, the filter criteria meet for User2 and hence, Mindtickle creates User2.

If User2 decides to go back to the support department, the filter criteria will no longer hold for User2. As a result, Mindtickle stops syncing User2 data from Salesforce but will not deactivate User2. In this case, if User2 gets deactivated from Salesforce, it will still be active in Mindtickle.

chunks.title: How do I reset my forgotten password from the learning site?

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > FAQs:
1. On the learning site homepage, click Sign In With Your Username > Forgot Password .
2. By default, the login page displays information in the platform language configured by your admin . However, you can display it in a different language by selecting it in the Language drop-down menu. Note :
  - The language drop-down menu is visible on the login page only if your learning site supports more than one (default) language.
  - The language selection depends on the languages configured by your admin.
3. In the Forgot Password pop-up that appears, enter your username (your registered email address) and click Submit .
4. Click OK in the confirmation pop-up.
5. Click the Reset Password button in the email that you received. Note : This email is displayed in the language configured by the Learner . If the Learner has not configured any language, it is displayed in the platform's default language configured by the Admin .
6. You are redirected to the Reset Password page. Enter your new password and click Reset Password . Note : This page is displayed in the language configured by the Learner . If the Learner has not configured a language, it is displayed in the Admin-configured default language.
7. When your password is reset successfully, the following confirmation message is displayed, and a confirmation email is sent to you. Note : Both the confirmation message and email are displayed in the language configured by the Learner . If the Learner has not configured any language, both are displayed in the platform default language configured by the Admin .

Now you can sign in to the learning site with your new password. If you still face any issues, please contact Mindtickle Support.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Integrations > User Sync:
The Mindtickle SCIM user provisioning through Okta can help you in the following ways:

- Manually adding, updating and removing users in Okta will be reflected on the Mindtickle platform instantly.
- State of users synced from third-party apps to Okta will also be reflected live on the Mindtickle platform.

Note: Okta will be considered as a source of truth and will override the changes in Mindtickle. Hence, if the email address for a user (who was provisioned through Okta) changes, we recommend updating the email address directly in Okta instead of creating a new user.

This article further explains how to set up and activate user sync on Mindtickle using Okta.

Note: Please reach out to your Customer Success Manager if you would like to update or change your existing system.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Integrations > User Sync > Setting up the Mindtickle app in Okta:
1. Contact your Customer Success Manager (CSM) to get your user credentials approved for Okta provisioning and to allow Okta user provisioning through Mindtickle’s Tools SVC.

Note: If Okta user provisioning is disabled in Tools SVC and Okta sends a request, the request is rejected. When you enable user provisioning in Tools SVC, it depends on Okta’s retry mechanism whether the failed request will be successful.

2. Activate your app credentials and get shortkeys for custom fields. You will also receive the shortkeys for custom profile fields that you need to use in the next step as Okta admin.

4. In the App Catalog, search the keyword “Mindtickle” and click the Add button.

5. In the General Settings tab, enter the Application label and your Mindtickle Sub Domain. Click Done.

6. In the provisioning section, click the Configure API integration button. Check the box to enable API integration and enter the username and password provided to you by Mindtickle in Step 1.

7. Click the Save button.

Note: If you are testing the Okta integration with Mindtickle over a Mindtickle sandbox instance and will move to the production instance later, please ensure you create a separate username and password for the production instance.

8. Scroll down to the Mindtickle Attribute Mappings section. Click the Go to Profile Editor button.

9. Click the + Add Attribute button on the page that opens.

10. Add shortkey as attributes to map users on Okta and click Save.

Learn how to find shortkeys for Profile Fields and Relationships in Mindtickle to map users. Manager profiles may have the same short key as non-Manager profiles.

For more details contact your Customer Success Manager (CSM).

Note:

- When creating a non-Manager profile field, the external namespace must be configured as urn:ietf:params:scim:MindtickleNameSpace .
- In case you want to add the Manager’s profile, the external namespace must be configured as urn:ietf:params:scim:ManagerNameSpace. All other steps remain the same.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > SCORM Content > Before you upload:
Before uploading a SCORM package, ensure the following:

- The file is in ZIP format.
- The imsmanifest.xml file is at the root level of the .ZIP archive. If the files reside in a folder, do not zip the folder; instead, select all files and subfolders within it and zip them directly.
- The SCORM package is in HTML5 output format for both web and mobile compatibility.
- If your existing content is available only in Flash format, republish it in HTML5 format using your authoring tool before uploading it to Mindtickle.

Note:

- The SCORM files are available on the mobile app but require an active internet connection. Due to the interactive nature of the SCORM content and its technical requirements for tracking user progress and performance, you cannot access the SCORM files offline.
- To improve the content upload process, admins can now use various methods to upload content in the Content Center. For more information, see Add or replace content in Content Center .

For troubleshooting common upload errors such as manifest errors, unzip errors, and validation failures, see the SCORM upload troubleshooting guide.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > SCORM Content > Upload SCORM files > Upload SCORM as learning objects within modules:
Admins can add SCORM files as learning objects within courses and quick update modules.

1. Open a course or quick update module.
2. Go to the Build tab.
3. Click Add learning objects .
4. In the Add learning objects screen, click Content .
5. On the Select File window, if the SCORM file already exists in Content Center, select the required file. Use the search bar to find a specific file, or apply filters to view all SCORM files.
6. To upload a new SCORM file, click New > Add file .
7. On the Add files screen, you can either drop the file or click to browse to upload the SCORM file. The platform then validates the SCORM file. If there is an issue with the SCORM, an error message displays.
8. Click the Show error details to view the error details.
9. To reupload the SCORM file, click Add learning object and upload a new SCORM file, or reach out to your SCORM expert to resolve the error in the SCORM file. Tip: You may share the screenshot of the error with your SCORM expert for faster debugging. Once the SCORM file is uploaded successfully, it displays within the learning object.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > SCORM Content > Replace the SCORM file > Replace file in Content Center:
Note: You must have the Manage Content permission in the Content Center and on the file you want to replace.

- Selecting Replace file in Content Center so it updates everywhere the file is used, no need to update individual modules.
- Click Next to select the new file. The Replace file screen is displayed.
- Select the new file. The system processes the new file.
- Once the file is uploaded, select the configuration settings for the file.
- Click Save changes .

Important considerations:

- Changes apply to all modules containing the file.
- Learner progress in affected modules is not impacted.
- You cannot revert to the previous file version after replacement.

- Follows SCORM Standards : Displays a status based on whether your SCORM package meets the required standards:
  - Published using a Mindtickle-supported SCORM version and format. Mindtickle supports SCORM 1.1, SCORM 1.2, and SCORM 2004 (across all editions) in .ZIP file format. However, we recommend using SCORM 1.2 or SCORM 2004 (4th edition).
  - SCORM package size is less than 500 MB.
  - Implemented best practices for publishing SCORM content on Mindtickle using Articulate Storyline 360 , Articulate Storyline 2 & 3 , Articulate Rise , Adobe Captivate 9 , and Camtasia . A green status ( ) indicates that your SCORM meets the required standards, and an orange status ( ) indicates that it does not.
- Receiving Completion Status : Displays a status based on whether your SCORM package tracks the progress of the SCORM content and sends a completion status. A green status ( ) indicates that your SCORM works as expected and sends a completion status when the content is completed.An orange status ( ) indicates that the SCORM is not sending a completion status when the content is completed.
- Original Score from SCORM : Displays the score received from SCORM in percentage. For example, if you got 2 out of 10 questions correct in the SCORM, your score would be 20%. This score is set within the SCORM package itself. If no score is configured in SCORM, then the result would be 100% for this test if the completion status is received.
- Score in Mindtickle : Displays ON if scoring in Mindtickle is enabled, and vice versa. To learn about how scoring for a SCORM package works in Mindtickle, see the Scoring section. Note : If there is an issue with the scores or completion not being updated correctly, enable the Save and exit option and re-test the SCORM. Otherwise, refer to the SCORM Checklist for Admin for authoring the SCORM content.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > SCORM Content > How SCORM works on Mindtickle? > Scoring and completion:
The following points explain how scoring for a SCORM package works in Mindtickle:

- If the completion trigger for the SCORM package is based on the number of slides viewed, then the maximum score will be registered once the learner completes viewing the content.
- If the SCORM package score is based on quiz results, Mindtickle will update the learner's score in proportion to the score set in Mindtickle. For example, if the maximum score in your SCORM package is 100, and the maximum score in Mindtickle is set to 50. If a learner scores 50 points in the SCORM package, they will be given 25 points in Mindtickle.
- Partial scoring based on quizzes passed or failed is also replicated proportionally in Mindtickle.
- If a learner does not finish the SCORM content and exits out of Mindtickle, the Learner's completion status depends on the "resume after suspend" configuration in the SCORM package:
  - If the configuration is enabled, the learner's progress resumes from the last location within the SCORM content in Mindtickle.
  - If the configuration is not enabled, learners will have to start from the beginning.
- If the learner’s score or completion status is reflected correctly in the SCORM content but not in Mindtickle, enable Save and exit and retest the package. This setting helps the package send its latest tracking information to Mindtickle, but does not mark the module as complete.

The following points explain how a SCORM file works when you update or replace it via the Content Center.
chunks.body:
The following points explain how scoring for a SCORM package works in Mindtickle:

- If the completion trigger for the SCORM package is based on the number of slides viewed, then the maximum score will be registered once the learner completes viewing the content.
- If the SCORM package score is based on quiz results, Mindtickle will update the learner's score in proportion to the score set in Mindtickle. For example, if the maximum score in your SCORM package is 100, and the maximum score in Mindtickle is set to 50. If a learner scores 50 points in the SCORM package, they will be given 25 points in Mindtickle.
- Partial scoring based on quizzes passed or failed is also replicated proportionally in Mindtickle.
- If a learner does not finish the SCORM content and exits out of Mindtickle, the Learner's completion status depends on the "resume after suspend" configuration in the SCORM package:
  - If the configuration is enabled, the learner's progress resumes from the last location within the SCORM content in Mindtickle.
  - If the configuration is not enabled, learners will have to start from the beginning.
- If the learner’s score or completion status is reflected correctly in the SCORM content but not in Mindtickle, enable Save and exit and retest the package. This setting helps the package send its latest tracking information to Mindtickle, but does not mark the module as complete.

  - Completion and scores are not impacted as the learner has already completed the SCORM.
  - Bookmarks from the previous SCORM are lost, and the new SCORM plays from the beginning.

  - Bookmarks from the previous SCORM are lost, and the new SCORM plays from the beginning.
  - Bookmarks for the new SCORM work as usual. That is, learners can resume the new SCORM content from where they had left off.
  - Scores and completion status get updated as the learner consumes the updated SCORM.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Course and quick update:
This article focuses on creating a rich text document in a course or quick update. The admins can create content using a combination of text, images, tables and emoticons. The enhanced editing and formatting capabilities help improve the content quality. On copying content from any source and pasting it into the rich text editor, the content retains the original formatting. While adding an image, the admin may choose to directly upload the image from the local computer or paste the image URL if sourced from the web.

The rich text editor also provides language localization support while creating content. That is, the items on the toolbar display in the default language set for the learning site. Additionally, multiple language support enables admins to create content in various languages and also use the spellcheck feature for accuracy.

For the list of languages supported in the editor, see Language support.

To learn more about creating Course and Quick update modules, refer to the following articles:

Create a Course

Create a Quick update

1. From a course or uick update, click Add learning objects on the Build tab.

2. In the Add learning objects panel, select Build content > Text document.

3. In the editor that opens, the basic editing functionalities related to font style and formatting are available on the menu bar. Rename the file by clicking Edit.

4. Click the more icon to display the additional features available in the editor. These include:

- Add a horizontal line separator
- Add a page break

This article explains how to bulk upload questions in a course or a quick update.

To learn more about how to create a course or quick update, refer to the following articles:

Create a course

Create a quick update

To bulk upload questions:

1. From a course or Quick update, click Add learning objects on the Build tab.

2. Select the question type of your choice from the Add learning objects drawer that opens on the right. Scroll down to view all the questions and quiz options.

3. Select Bulk upload questions from the list.

5. The .xls file that is downloaded to your local machine contains two sheets: Questions and Instructions.

Note: When you bulk upload Text Answer Questions, the percentage accuracy of the answer is 80% by default.

6. Click Upload questions.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > FAQs:
This article explains how you, as learners, can set your preferred language as the default language for your learning site. You are prompted to set your language while signing up for the first time. If you did not set your language when signing up, you can set it at any time by following the steps in this article.

When you change your learning site language, you change the platform's default language, not the language of uploaded content, such as modules. Essentially, you are selecting the language for the platform’s user interface (UI).

Note: If you have not configured any language, then the information is displayed in the platform default language configured by the admin.

Perform the following steps to change language settings from your profile:

1. Sign in to your learning site.
2. On the learning site home page, click the profile icon in the upper-right corner and then click My Profile and analytics.

1. On the profile page that opens, click Edit profile.

1. On the Edit Profile screen, select the language from the Language dropdown and click Done.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > User Management > Roles and Permissions:
With roles and permissions on the Mindtickle platform, you can regulate your users' access to the platform based on the type of activities they can perform. This ensures that each user can only access necessary and relevant feature capabilities and platform data. It also ensures that users do not have access to features that they don't need, minimizing the chances of errors and issues of users interfering with each other’s work.

A role assigned to a user has a defined set of permissions. Permissions determine the level of access to platform features and functionalities and what actions can be performed, such as creating or modifying content. By default, all new users are assigned the learner role and, therefore, they are learners (users) on the platform.

In addition to the default Mindtickle roles, you can create a custom role of your choice with the help of your Customer Success Manager (CSM). A custom role can have a variety of permissions across different features and functionalities on the platform. By assignsing a combination of permissions to a custom role, they can get access to specific features and functionalities on the platform.

This article provides information on the default Mindtickle roles and their permissions. For information on custom roles, see Custom roles and permissions in Mindtickle.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > User Management > Roles and Permissions > Default user roles:
There are seven default roles that you can assign to a user on the Mindtickle platform:

- Site owner
- Enablement admin
- Content expert
- Group manager
- Manager
- IT admin
- Learner

Note: Users with the following are considered as admins on the platform: site owner, enablement admin, content expert, and group manager. Additionally, if you create a custom role for a user with admin-level permissions, they are also an admin on the platform.

In addition to the default roles, you can also create custom roles.

Site owner

The site owner is the super user on the Mindtickle platform. This role has all permissions and unrestricted access and can assign roles to other users from the settings page. There can be one or more site owners for a Mindtickle learning site.

Note:

- A user can have site owner level universal and unrestricted access in two ways: through the default site owner role or through a custom role with site owner level permissions.
- Users with the site owner role cannot remove or unassign this role for themselves from the user profile . To remove your own site owner role, you need to either ask another site owner or contact Mindtickle Support. However, as a site owner, you can remove the site owner role for any user.
- In analytics, one site owner does not have access to custom reports created by other site owners.

Enablement admin

- In analytics, one site owner does not have access to custom reports created by other site owners. Enablement admin

The enablement admin orchestrates the sales readiness/enablement initiatives. There can be multiple enablement admins per site. They have full access to create and manage all types of modules including modifying the settings within each module they create. They can also apply tags to modules, files, questions, polls, and evaluation parameters (Mission and Coaching Sessions) to which they have access. They have complete control over their own initiative by defining the extent to which other users can collaborate in their series by authorizing their access from series settings. For example, enablement admins can control access of other users to Develop Content and Assign Content in their series.

The enablement admin cannot modify site-wide settings, such as security or integration options or assign roles to other users. The enablement admin also cannot see the modules or content created by another enablement admin unless invited to do so.

They are responsible for ensuring that everything goes smooth in terms of participation/performance and their readiness initiatives accomplish the set objectives.

Content expert

The content expert creates or contributes to content development and publishing. The content expert is invited by the site owner or enablement admin to contribute content to a particular series or module. They can also apply tags to modules, files, questions, polls, and evaluation parameters (Mission and Coaching Sessions) to which they have access. Content experts can invite learners to modules and series; however, they cannot invite groups to modules and series.

Group manager

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > User Management > Roles and Permissions > Default user roles:
The group manager supports enablement of a team represented by a group on the platform. This role was created specifically for channel/partner enablement use-cases in Mindtickle. It can also be used for training facilitators or regional field trainers that need the ability to manage groups of users. With this role, a key contact in the channel or partner organization will have the ability to invite select users and groups from their organization to participate in specific training modules on the platform.

Manager

The manager role allows access to managerial reports in Mindtickle. They are primarily interested in monitoring the performance of the team and reviewing their skill development through coaching and role-plays.

IT admin

The IT admin handles infrastructure integrations. They have access to technical settings of the learning site, such as integration settings and security options. Please note that they do not have access to learners' data. In case the IT team is helping you with user integration, then please assign them a custom role with “site owner” permissions. For help, contact your Customer Success Manager (CSM).

Learner

The learner role is assigned to every user on the Mindtickle platform by default. The learner can only access the learning site of the Mindtickle platform, and not the admin site. On the learning site, they can consume content based on the modules and series they have been invited to.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > User Management > Roles and Permissions > About limited/scoped access via collaborators:
This section explains how collaborator permissions are used to grant users limited/scoped access.

You can provide scoped or limited access to a user by making them a collaborator, which grants them specific collaborator-level permissions that you can modify. You can add collaborators to:

- Series
- Groups
- Assets (in Asset Hub), and
- Files/folders (in Content Center).

A collaborator can access only the specific series, groups, assets, and files/folders to which they have been explicitly added. Furthermore, they can only access the specific functionalities for which they’re assigned permissions within those areas.

Example: If you add a collaborator to a series and only grant them Manage Series, Assign Content, and Series Reports permissions, they will only be able to perform those three specific actions (managing the series, assigning content, and viewing series analytics reports).

Key rules & constraints

A. Note on modules

A collaborator’s access to modules is governed strictly through the parent series. You cannot make someone a collaborator at the individual module level. When you make someone a collaborator on a series, they automatically gain access to all modules within that series.

B. Modifying permissions for a series owner

If a collaborator is also designated as the series owner for a specific series, their collaborator permissions cannot be modified directly and will appear grayed out, with a tooltip saying "You cannot change or remove permissions for a series owner."

To update a series owner's collaborator permissions, you must temporarily transfer ownership:

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > User Management > Roles and Permissions > About limited/scoped access via collaborators:
1. Change the series owner: From series Settings → General tab, transfer ownership from the current owner (e.g., Admin A) to another admin (e.g., Admin B). This will unlock the collaborator permission settings for Admin A.
2. Update permissions: Use the Manage collaborators option in the series header to adjust the permissions for Admin A as needed.
3. Reassign ownership: Transfer the series ownership back to Admin A, if necessary.

For details on the collaborator permissions across the platform, see Collaborator management.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > User Management > Roles and Permissions > Call AI:
This section provides information about the permissions for Call AI — Mindtickle’s conversation intelligence solution.

Important: You can grant users access to Call AI based on roles as well as with the Call AI specific View call recordings permission:

- Call AI access based on roles: When you assign a Call AI role (Call AI admin, Call AI recorder, or Call AI listener) to a user, it grants access to various Call AI features. Additionally, please note that each role by default contains the View call recordings permission, with varying levels of access as appropriate for the role. See the “ Role-based access ” section for details.
- Call AI access based on a permission: The View call recordings permission is a standalone permission available for Call AI to provide users access to the call recordings. This permission is by default assigned to all three Call AI roles and all default Mindtickle roles, such as site owner, enablement admin, and content expert. Some roles have complete access to all call recordings while other roles have scoped (limited) access to certain recordings. You can also assign this permission to a custom role, with your choice of access (complete or scoped). See the “ Permission-based access ” section for details.

Note for dialer recordings: If you have integrated Call AI with a dialer software — such as Aircall, Cloudtalk, Dialpad, and Five9 — please note that Call AI provides the call recordings only for users with the Call AI recorder role.

This section provides details on:

- Permission-based access
- Role-based access
- Call AI for managers
- Coach users on the call

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > User Management > Roles and Permissions > Call AI > Role-based access:
Call AI permissions work differently compared to the rest of the platform. You can assign the following Call AI roles to a user:

- Call AI admin: Can manage the admin functionalities of Call AI from the Mindtickle admin site (listener access by default) Note: Users with the Call AI admin role cannot remove or unassign this role for themselves from the user profile . To remove your own Call AI admin role, you need to either ask another Call AI admin or contact Mindtickle Support. However, as a Call AI admin, you can remove the Call AI admin role for any user.
- Call AI recorder: Can integrate calendar, record meetings, and customize recording preferences, among other things (listener access by default)
- Call AI listener: Can only access and view the call recordings

The assigned role determines the Call AI features and functionalities that the user can access and use. Users who can access Call AI can be admins, managers of the call participants (attendees), and reps (learners) — and anyone with whom the call is shared.

Note: Each Call AI role by default contains the View call recordings permission, with varying levels of access as appropriate for the role.

This table provides information on the Call AI features and the level of access given for a particular Call AI feature/functionality to each role. For each feature, a role can have one of the following levels of access:

Full = Universal and complete access Scoped = Limited or scoped access None = No access

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > User Management > Roles and Permissions > Call AI > Call AI for managers:
In Mindtickle, a user is considered a manager if they hold the Manager role, assigned to those with teams or direct reports. This role grants access to managerial analytics and reports.

In Call AI, there is no specific manager role. Instead, you are treated as a manager when at least one of your direct reports has access to Call AI. As a result, managers gain access to Call AI’s manager-related features by virtue of having team members with Call AI access.

Managers may have either the Call AI recorder or Call AI listener role. At a minimum, they will have the View call recordings permission, which grants access similar to the Call AI listener role. Depending on their role, managers can access all Call AI features listed in the “Role-based access” section. Additionally, they get access to the following features that are specifically for managers:

Legends

Full = Universal and complete access Scoped = Limited or scoped access None = No access

| Permissions | Roles |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Call AI recorder | Call AI listener |  |
| Team recordings | Full | Full |
| Team analytics: Conversation stats | Call score | Talk track | Call activity | Voice of Market | Full | Full |

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > User Management > Roles and Permissions > Call AI > Coach users on the call:
The Coach option on the call recording page lets users coach any participant on the recorded call, even if the user is not a direct manager. This feature requires the Coach all Call AI users permission.

The Coach all Call AI users permission is assigned to the site owner, manager, and group manager roles by default — to ensure backward compatibility with earlier existing capabilities. Additionally, admins can assign this permission to any user via a custom role, and assign this role to users who are not a direct manager.

For more information on coaching on calls, see Review Coaching Session on Call AI.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > User Management > Roles and Permissions > Custom roles and permissions:
In addition to the default Mindtickle roles, you can create a custom role of your choice with the help of your Customer Success Manager (CSM). A custom role can have a variety of permissions across different features and functionalities on the platform. By assigning a combination of permissions to a custom role, they can get access to specific features and functionalities on the platform.

With a custom role, you can assign multiple permissions to a user to extend their access. For example, a user who has the manager role can also be assigned a content expert role by creating a new user who has all permissions of the manager and content expert roles. Similarly, a user that develops content may not need access to security settings. This user can exclusively be assigned the role of a content expert, restricting their access to only creating and editing content.

For more information, see Custom roles and permissions in Mindtickle.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > User Management > Roles and Permissions > Mindtickle API access:
Users can access and use the following types of Mindtickle’s APIs:

- Reporting APIs → APIs for the reporting resource, using which you can download metadata tables
- User and content APIs → APIs for the user , user group , and content resources

Prerequisite: API access must be enabled for the user looking to leverage Mindtickle's API. To enable access, contact Mindtickle Support.

Access: Access to Mindtickle’s APIs based on your role works as follows:

- Reporting APIs: All users except learners in your organization can access the reporting APIs.
- User and content APIs: Only users with the site owner role can access the user and content APIs. However, they can provide access to any other user by sharing the API and Secret keys.

Note: Only site owners can access the user and content APIs because it requires authentication through the API and Secret keys. These keys are available under Account Settings > Security and Integration, to which only site owners have access. If any other user — let’s say, a manager — wants to use the APIs, the site owner needs to share the API and Secret keys with the manager.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > User Management > Roles and Permissions > How does collaboration work when a new Series is created?:
The creator of the Series is granted full permissions by default. They can manage content and invite others to collaborate. Site Owners can access all Series regardless of collaboration settings.
chunks.body: The creator of the Series is granted full permissions by default. They can manage content and invite others to collaborate. Site Owners can access all Series regardless of collaboration settings.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > User Management > Roles and Permissions > How does scope work when a new Group is created?:
The Group creator has full permissions by default and can manage the group and invite collaborators. Site Owners have full access to all Groups by default.

No. Contact your Customer Success Manager (CSM) for more details.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > User Management > Roles and Permissions > Why do I and my colleague see different search results for the same search query?:
Search results are influenced by access restrictions. You may not see certain modules if you lack access permissions.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > User Management > Roles and Permissions > I am not able to delete some users. Why?:
Only Site Owners can delete users. However, users with the right permissions can unassign users from Series or Modules.

Yes. A Site Owner can change the roles of others and themselves, provided there is always at least one Site Owner on the platform.

Roles and permissions can be configured individually for each learning site.

Learner experience remains unaffected. The framework only impacts administrative controls.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > User Management > Roles and Permissions > How are roles assigned when Site Owner uploads a list of learners for module invitation?:
If a learner doesn't exist, they are created and assigned the Learner role. Managers are created and assigned roles accordingly, with the learner’s manager attribute set if valid.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > User Management > Roles and Permissions > How are roles assigned when a user without “Site Owner” role uploads a list of learners for module invitation?:
If the manager doesn’t already exist or doesn’t have the Manager role, the record is invalid and users aren’t created. Only valid manager-learners relationships are accepted.
chunks.body: If the manager doesn’t already exist or doesn’t have the Manager role, the record is invalid and users aren’t created. Only valid manager-learners relationships are accepted.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > User Management > Roles and Permissions > How are roles assigned when I upload a list of learners for module invitation?:
New learners are added with the Learner role. Managers are related but not given role permissions unless added separately. Invalid or duplicate records are ignored.

Managers must be active users and assigned the appropriate roles to be eligible as reviewers. Uploading them without assigning the Manager role prevents review assignment.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Analytics & Reporting > Series:
Series reports provide comprehensive analytics on all the series that your learners access in Mindtickle. These reports include performance and engagement data for modules, learners, and segments.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Analytics & Reporting > Series > Access series reports:
In the admin site sidebar, click Analytics > Training > Series to open the series reports listing page. This page displays all available series reports.

The series analytics page shows all series that you have access to on your admin homepage. By default, series are listed in descending order of their creation date. You can sort them by the duration in which they were created.

To locate a specific series, use the search bar or apply filters based on the content creator and Series type (All, Invite Only, Public).

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Analytics & Reporting > Series > Access series reports > View analytics for a specific series:
To view the analytics of a particular series, click its name. The series data is organized across five tabs.

Each tab in the provides a different view of the data:

- Overview tab : Shows a summary of learner activity and engagement across the series.
- Modules tab : Displays analytics for each module included in the series.
- Learners tab : Provides insights into individual learner progress and performance.
- Segments tab : Breaks down data by predefined learner segments.
- Heatmap tab : Visualizes engagement data across time intervals.

The Overview tab is displayed by default when you open a series. Any filters you apply within a series are retained across tabs, so you do not need to reapply them as you navigate.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Analytics & Reporting > Series > Progress visualization methods:
Learner progress in the series is represented using three different views:

1. Monthly cohort: Displays learner status and percentage completion by the month and year they were invited. Click a row to view details of learners invited during that period.

2. Manager: Shows learner status and percentage completion grouped by manager.

3. Learners: Provides individual learner metrics such as invitation date, modules completed, and score. Clicking a learner’s name redirects you to the Series > Learners tab.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Analytics & Reporting > Series > Learner vs. Module and Learner vs. Section:
Learner vs. Module displays metrics for learners across all modules they have been invited to.Learner vs. Section displays metrics across all sections of the series the learner has been invited to.

Note: In a scoped public series, invited learners can access all modules in the series. But if an admin invites them to only certain modules, only those are considered assigned. In this case, heatmap analytics will show only the modules the learner was explicitly invited to, even though they can access others in the series.

Filters

You can filter learners using the following options:

- Modules assigned during : Filter based on the assignment date of modules.
- Module type : Filter based on the type of module.
- Learner fields and More filters : Filter based on profile fields, managers, group, tag, public series data, and module relevance.

To locate a specific learner, use the Search a learner bar.

Note:

- You can select up to 60 filter values when applying filters to heatmaps.
- Detailed analytics are available for all module types except ILT. However, aggregated data for all module types, including ILT, is included in series analytics.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Mission > Before you start recording:
Complete the following checks before recording a mission.

1. Use the latest available version of a supported browser.

2. If you use Google Chrome, restart the browser before recording. Restarting is different from refreshing the page.

- Enter chrome://restart in the address bar.
- Google Chrome reopens your tabs after restarting.

3. Ensure each device has enough bandwidth for two-way roleplays:

- Recommended: 30 Mbps per device for a seamless 720p experience.
- Minimum supported: 2 Mbps per device.

For shared networks, such as training rooms or large events, confirm that the network supports this bandwidth for all learners simultaneously completing two-way roleplays.

4. Close applications that can access your microphone or webcam, such as QuickTime, Webex, Zoom, Skype, or other conferencing and recording applications.

Note: Closing an application window does not always quit the application.

5. Confirm that the microphone indicator responds when you speak.

6. Create a short test recording to check audio quality, but do not submit it.

7. If the issue continues after you complete these checks, contact Mindtickle Support.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Mindtickle APIs > Reporting APIs:
The Mindtickle Reporting API enables admins to access granular performance and engagement data for their users and content. Built on the Open Data Protocol (OData), this API allows you to seamlessly import Mindtickle data into Business Intelligence (BI) tools such as Microsoft Excel, Power BI, and Tableau.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Mobile App:
This article explains navigating a course module on the Mindtickle mobile app.

Courses are in-depth training modules and contain multiple Topics and Questions that are tied together using a visual theme.

Mindtickle courses are available on “iOS 13.x.x +” and “Android 5.0+”. Most functionalities are the same on mobile as that on the web.

After signing in to the mobile app, tap a Series under the Assigned or Public tab on the Series page to view the Modules inside the series. Read the series description. Below the description, you can see a list of all the Modules you have been invited to.

Note: The Modules that are available to you depend on your organization’s implementation of the Mindtickle platform. For information on the types of Modules, see Types of Modules in Mindtickle.

To view a Course within a Series and access its contents, on the Series tab, tap the Course tile.

The Course thumbnail on the top. Navigate to the next or previous modules by swiping the thumbnail left or right.

Below the thumbnail, you can see the course name, due date (if enabled by the Admin), description, and % completion. To view the complete description, tap it.

Tap the Map icon at the lower-right corner of the screen to unveil the theme map.

A theme map is a visual representation of the progression of Topics within a Course. Maps help you visualize the journey and track your progress in the Course module.

Note:

- The theme map only opens in full-screen mode.
- Tap the list icon to exit the full-screen mode.
- You can navigate the theme map by scrolling horizontally.

You can download and share (if enabled by the Admin) the contents of a course by tapping the Download icon from the top-right corner of the screen. To learn more, see Share Content Files.

All the learning content and Questions are laid out sequentially below the description according to their Topics.

You can bookmark a Learning Content, Download it for offline access (if enabled by the Admin), Download transcript for video, or express your reaction (,) by tapping the More icon at the lower-right corner of the screen.

If your Admin has enabled the Skip option, you’ll be able to skip content or questions. However, your score will be zero for any content or question that you skip, and you will not be able to reattempt the questions.

Every content object (learning object or question) has a score assigned to it. The score is centered at the lower part of the screen.

You can download and share (if enabled by the Admin) the contents of a course by tapping the Download icon from the top-right corner of the screen. To learn more, see Share Content Files.

All the learning content and Questions are laid out sequentially below the description according to their Topics.

Note: You may see a course overview video if your Admin has added one. To view the overview video, tap the Course thumbnail. You can download the video for offline access and share it (if enabled by your Admin). You can also see the length of the video on the course thumbnail.

Tap a Topic name to view all the learning content and questions within it. If the learning content is in the form of a document or presentation, you can scroll through it to view more.

You can bookmark a Learning Content, Download it for offline access (if enabled by the Admin), Download transcript for video, or express your reaction (,) by tapping the More icon at the lower-right corner of the screen.

If your Admin has enabled the Skip option, you’ll be able to skip content or questions. However, your score will be zero for any content or question that you skip, and you will not be able to reattempt the questions.

Every content object (learning object or question) has a score assigned to it. The score is centered at the lower part of the screen.

Using a Lifeline eliminates wrong choices. The No. of Attempts Left icon centered at the lower part of the screen shows the total number of lifelines that can be used in the course. For example, in this scenario, you can use two lifelines in the course.

Using Hint provides an indication or suggestion that leads you to the right answer. Tap the Hint icon to view the Hint.

Once you answer the question, the score is displayed on the screen.

Note: All questions have dynamic scoring and a fixed number of attempts. Once you answer a question, you cannot reattempt it.

Once you answer a question, you cannot reattempt it.

Content can also be in the form of a video. You can configure the speed and resolution of the video by tapping the Settings icon . Tap the Fullscreen icon to view the video in full screen mode.

If your admin has added in-video questions or polls, you can view the question or poll on the screen in between the video. It helps keep the interest and prevents monotonousness while watching long videos.

The following image shows an in-video question within a video learning content:

Once you answer the question, tap Resume Video to continue watching the video.

If enabled by the admin, you can choose to Skip the question and continue to watch the video. However, if the admin configured the in-video question as required, you need to answer the question to proceed in the video.

Note:

- Completion status of the video is independent of completion of the in-video question even if you skip the in-video question or answer it incorrectly.
- If you choose to attempt an in-video question later, you can attempt it until you complete the course and your lifelines exist. Once you complete the course, you cannot use the lifelines (even if present) or attempt the in-video question. You can view the selected answers and the correct answers of the in-video question in a view-only mode when watching the video again.
- The total score earned by you in a video learning content is the sum of the score earned from watching the video and the score earned from answering the in-video questions or polls.
- If you are consuming the learning content and the admin makes some changes in the video file, you need to refresh the page to view the updates.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Integrations > Data Sync and Reporting API:
This article explains how to import data in Excel using OData. For information on the data limits for various formats and querying methods, see OData Best Practices in Reporting API.

Prerequisite: Contact Mindtickle Support to enable your email address to import the Mindtickle data into your BI tools. This email address must have access to the admin site. Once enabled, the same email address can be used to import data into both Tableau and Excel.

Note: Mindtickle has discontinued support for TLS 1.0 and TLS 1.1 protocol. However, MS Excel Professional Plus 2013 still supports an older version of the TLS protocol by default, which prevents Mindtickle from importing the data. We recommend users importing data using MS Excel Professional Plus 2013 to install the Power Query Add-in to continue.

1. Open Microsoft Excel on your Windows device.

2. Click the Data tab on the Menu of your Excel sheet.

3. Click Get Data. Select From Other Sources in the drop-down. Click the From OData Feed option.

Note: If you are unable to see the options mentioned above in Excel, please contact the IT support team in your organization.

4. In the OData feed dialog box that opens, select the Basic radio button and enter https://admin.mindtickle.com/Odata.svc in the field provided for URL. Click OK.Note: If your learning site is based in the US, then please use the following URL: https://admin.prod-us.mindtickle.com/Odata.svc

Note: This is a generic URL to access OData from Mindtickle.

5. On the screen that appears, click the Basic tab, enter your Mindtickle admin Username and Password for authentication. Click Connect.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Integrations > Data Sync and Reporting API:
Prerequisite: Contact your Customer Success Manager (CSM) to enable your email address to import the Mindtickle data into your BI tools.

Note: This email address must have access to the admin site. Once enabled, the same email address can be used to import data into both Tableau and Excel.

For information on the data limits for various formats and querying methods, see Odata Best Practices in Reporting API.

Let's take a look at the procedure to configure the data import in Tableau.

1. Click File.

2. Under Connect > To a Server > More, select OData.

3. Enter the URL: https://admin.mindtickle.com/Odata.svc/<name of the table>

Note:

- This is a common URL to access OData from Mindtickle.
- The reporting API enables users to access seven types of tables. You can mention the table name in the URL as per your requirement. See this article for details on the tables that can be accessed using the Reporting API as well as the table URLs. To learn more about the attributes in these tables see the Reporting API metadata sheet.For example, if the table name is LearnerModulePerformances, the URL is: https://admin.mindtickle.com/Odata.svc/LearnerModulePerformances.

4. Enter your Mindtickle admin username and password for and click Sign In.

5. Please wait for the data to load.

6. Once the data loads, you will see the table structure as shown in the following image.

Note: This is an example of the LearnerModulePerformances table. Similarly, you can import data from other tables, such as users, series, and modules.

The article further explains how to import data from different tables.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Mindtickle APIs > Reporting APIs > Download table data:
Mindtickle’s reporting API uses OData to help you extract the platform engagement and performance data of your users in a BI tool of your choice. For each table below, we have provided a link to directly download the data.

IMPORTANT NOTES:

1. For the table update frequency marked with the asterisk (*), it may take up to 24 hours to reflect the data updates.
2. Tables marked with the double asterisk (**) are not enabled by default. Contact Mindtickle Support to enable a particular table for your Learning Site. The rest of the tables are enabled by default.
3. For the data download links provided for each table, the sample data link will download only the top 10 results. The full data link will download the entire data.
4. For fields with a timestamp (date and time) across the reporting API tables, the value is in the GMT timezone.
5. Reporting API has two different service root URLs to query and extract data. The data download links in the following table reference the default URL. Ensure that you are using the correct, applicable URL.

You can get the URL for a particular series in the following ways:

The Copy link to series button in the series header allows admins to copy the series link and share it with learners.

To copy the series link,

- Click the Copy link to series button.

A confirmation message is displayed on the screen once the URL is copied to the clipboard.Depending on your preference, you can paste it into a text editor or email and share it with other stakeholders.

For more information on how to retrieve the URL of a module, refer steps to retrieve the module URL.

Perform the following steps to update the module thumbnail:

1. On the admin site homepage, click the Training icon and select Series .

1. On the displayed Series page, click on a series. On the Modules tab, click on the module to update its thumbnail .

The Invite and enroll tab of the module is displayed.

1. Click the Settings tab.
2. Under Thumbnail, click Change to update the module’s thumbnail image. The thumbnail gallery opens. You can either upload a new custom thumbnail or select an existing thumbnail from the previously uploaded list. You can also crop the thumbnail to your liking. For detail, see this article . Once you select a thumbnail, it is saved automatically to the Content Center. Additionally, updating the module thumbnail does not require you to publish changes to learners; the updated thumbnail automatically reflects for all invited learners.

Note:

- Thumbnail images must be no larger than 10 MB, can be in any 3:2 aspect ratio (e.g., 1500 × 1000 pixels), and be in JPEG or PNG format. For details, see this article.
- You cannot reset the module thumbnail to the default thumbnail for the assessment, ILT, and quest modules. However, for courses, quick updates, missions, checklists, and competency assessments, use the Reset to default thumbnail option under module Settings → General → Thumbnail.

For updating series thumbnails, see How to update the thumbnail image of a series.

chunks.title: How can I customize a learning site URL?

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Setup > FAQs > Customize a learning site URL:
1. With the help of your webmaster or server administrator, create a CNAME DNS record of your whitelabel URL and point it to your learning site URL. For example, your Mindtickle learning site URL is company.mindtickle.com and you wish to create a whitelabel URL as enablement.company.com , then you will have to create a CNAME DNS record as shown below: NameTypeRecord valueenablement.company.comCNAMEcompany.label.mindtickle.com If you need guidance on how to create a CNAME DNS record, contact Mindtickle Support .
2. Once the CNAME DNS record is created successfully, update the value of the whitelabel domain as follows:
  1. On the admin site homepage, hover over the Account icon on the left navigation bar, and click Settings . The Settings page is displayed.
    1. On the Settings page, click the Security & integrations tab.
    2. click + Add WhiteLabel .
  2. In the displayed field, enter the text you wish to use as a whitelabel and click . Note : It is possible to have more than one whitelabel URL for the same learning site. To add more whitelabel URLs, repeat Steps 1 to 4.
3. Inform the Mindtickle Support team to create an HTTPS certificate for the newly created whitelabel URL. Note : Mindtickle will maintain and renew the HTTPS certificate annually for one custom URL and no further action is required from your organization.
4. After this, contact your InfoSec or IT Team to allowlist the new whitelabel URL in your firewall. By doing this, you can ensure there are no issues related to accessing its content. For more information on additional sites that you should allowlist to access the Mindtickle platform, refer to the Unblock Email, Video, and Media (Allowlist) article.
5. Inform the Mindtickle Support team to make the newly created whitelabel URL as the preferred URL for your learning site. This ensures that:
  1. The default learning site URL gets updated with the new (preferred) whitelabel URL.
  2. All instances of the learning site URL (on the Admin and Learner Site) are updated with the new (preferred) whitelabel URL.
  3. All email notifications (reminder/invitation/completion) that are sent to the Learners include a link with the new (preferred) whitelabel URL. Note : There can only be one preferred learning site.
6. After the Mindtickle Support team confirms that the new whitelabel URL is made the preferred URL, test if the whitelabel has been applied successfully. To test, enter the new whitelabel URL (enablement.company.com) in a new tab and see if the page that opens is the same as ‘company.mindtickle.com’.

This help article will help you implement the integration on your own. However, if you need implementation guidance, then please contact your Customer Success Manager, who will then engage our Professional Services team. Professional Services can assist you with consultation, implementation, deployment, and testing of the integration.

Note: Engaging Professional Services is a paid services engagement.

1. Login to the Salesforce platform. On the home page, click Setup on the upper right corner of your screen.

Note: If you are not using Single Sign On, you can directly jump to step 4.

2. On the left navigation panel, under the Administer section, go to Manage Apps -> Connected Apps. Click the Master Label of your connected app.

3. In the SAML Login Information section, copy IdP- Initiated Login URL. This will be used in the following steps.

4. On the left navigation panel, go to Build -> Create -> Tabs.

5. Under the Web Tabs section, click New.

6. Select default layout and click Next.

7. Fill in the mandatory fields in the Display Properties section. Click Next.Note: Tab Label can be any name such as ‘Mindtickle Courses’. Tab Name will be populated by default. Choose any Tab Style.

8. Paste the URL copied in Step 3 above in the Button or Link URL field. Click Next.

Note: If you are not using Single Sign On, you can paste your learning site URL in the Button or Link URL field.

9. On the screen that appears, leave the default settings on and click Next.Note: Select Apply a different tab visibility for each profile to assign appropriate visibility status to User Groups based on the permissions you want to grant to them.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Integrations > Single Sign-On (SSO):
Mindtickle allows integration with any identity provider (IdP) that supports SAML 2.0 protocol. Some supported IdPs are Salesforce, Okta, Google, OneLogin, Ping Identity, Symplified, ADFS, and IBM Cloud Identity Connect.

Note: This article uses Okta as an example and explains how to set up single sign-on (SSO) with SAML using Okta. Using this article as a reference point, you can set up a single sign-on with any IdP that supports SAML 2.0.

For more information on how to set up single sign-on with other protocols, see OneLogin, Okta, Impartner, Salesforce, Microsoft Entra ID (formerly called Azure Active Directory), and ADFS.

If you are using another IDP—such as OneLogin, Ping Identity, Symplified, or IBM Cloud Identity Connect—the steps mentioned in the first section to retrieve the IdP metadata file are applicable. The steps in the second section remain the same for all IDPs.

If your learning site URL is whitelisted after setting up the SSO, you should download the Mindtickle metadata again and change the SSO URL with the latest updated URL in OKTA. For information on white-labeling the learning site URL, see step 12 in Configure the application.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Integrations > Single Sign-On (SSO) > Upload the identity provider metadata in Mindtickle:
The identity provider metadata downloaded from Okta should be uploaded in Mindtickle to activate the single sign-on integration.

To upload the identity provider metadata in Mindtickle:

1. On the admin site homepage, hover over the Account icon on the left navigation bar, and click Settings . The Settings page is displayed.
2. Navigate to the Single Sign On section on the Security & Integrations tab.
3. In the SAML SSO tab, under Upload Identity Provider Meta File , click Select File .
4. Select the metadata file downloaded from Okta. For more information, see Download the identity provider metadata from Okta .
5. Click Activate SSO after the file upload. You can now assign people, groups, and map attributes to the Okta application for single sign-on with Mindtickle.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Analytics & Reporting > Modules > Module reports page > Sort options:
Modules are sorted alphabetically by name by default. You can change the sort order using the column headers:

- Module name : Names of the modules.
- Created on : Date the module was created.
- Number of learners : Total number of learners assigned to the module — including those invited by an admin or self-invited.
- Percentage completion : Formula: ( Invitations completed / Total invitations ) × 100 Where total invitations = sum of learners invited to each module.
- Scoring performance : Formula: (Sum of scores obtained by learners in assigned modules) / (Cumulative max score of all started modules) × 100
- Percentage certified : Percentage of learners certified in the module.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > FAQs:
In January 2018, Google deprecated a few permissions in the Chrome browser (v64 onwards). Due to this change, embedded applications or pages can no longer request permission to access the microphone or camera. For more details, refer to Google’s document on Deprecating Permissions in Cross-Origin Iframes.

Note: If you are using IE 11 and above, you will not face this issue.

This change in the Google Chrome settings impacts everyone who uses MindTickle’s Mission embedded in Salesforce Classic.

As per Google’s document, the embedder application (Salesforce Classic) must specify a feature policy that enables the permissions of the microphone and camera for the embedded application (MindTickle). In our investigation, we found that such a feature policy is not implemented in Salesforce Classic.

Since the MindTickle application is embedded into the Salesforce application, MindTickle is no longer able to access the microphone or camera of the user’s browser. Users who use MindTickle from a tab within Salesforce are not able to record their Missions.

To resolve the issue with the Chrome browser:

1. Open MindTickle in a new browser tab and submit your Mission from that tab.
2. If it is a Video Roleplay or Screen Capture Mission, you can record the Mission using video-recording software such as QuickTime, and upload the video in the Mission.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Integrations > Single Sign-On (SSO) > Steps to be performed in Salesforce:
1. Sign in to the Salesforce platform. Click the settings icon in the upper right corner of your screen and then click Setup . Create connected apps To create connected apps in Salesforce,
2. Follow steps 1 to 4 in the Download Metadata from Mindtickle section.
3. Search for External Client Apps in the left navigation panel.
4. Under Apps > External Client Apps > click External Client App Manager . The External Client App Manager screen is displayed.
5. Click New External Client App.
6. Fill in the mandatory fields in the Basic Information section.
7. Under the Web App (Enable SAML Settings) section, click the Enable SAML checkbox to configure the required policies. You can view the SAML Settings after enabling the checkbox.
8. Enter values for EntityID and ACS URL fields copied in Step 4 .
9. Click Create . A message notifies once the app is created, and the Manage External Client Apps screen is displayed.
10. Under the Policies tab, click the SAML Policies tab.
11. Click the SAML Login Info tab.
12. Click Download Metadata . The metadata file downloads to your local machine. This file is used to configure the Salesforce SSO in Mindtickle .
13. In the App Profiles section, click Edit .
14. Under the Select Profiles section, from the Available Profiles list, click the necessary profiles to select the profiles that need Salesforce to log in to Mindtickle.
15. Click Save . Note : Only users belonging to those profiles can log in to Salesforce. Contact your Salesforce administrator to learn more about user profiles. You can skip the steps below if UID is not enabled for your learning site. If you have UID-enabled sites , follow the additional steps below, Tip: You can identify whether a site is UID-enabled from the Add new users screen. For UID-enabled sites, the Username and Email ID fields are separate. The system uses the Email ID as the Username and the email ID receives all communication and authentication requests. The screenshot below is an example of a UID-enabled site. If your site is UID-enabled , you can use custom attributes to ensure Salesforce SSO works seamlessly. The custom attribute is unique to each user in Salesforce. It is a distinct value that integrates into Mindtickle as an identifier specific to users.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Integrations > CRMs:
You can provide your learners access to their learning site within the Salesforce platform by creating a Visualforce page.

Prerequisite:

- We recommend that you activate Salesforce Single Sign On and create Connected Apps on Salesforce before providing learners access to Mindtickle's learning site.
- If you are implementing only the web tab to access Mindtickle or starting with it in your Salesforce instance, you must add the Content Security Policy (CSP) URL to the Trusted URL Information section on the Trusted URLs screen, as Named Credentials wouldn't be available.

This article explains how you can create a Visualforce page in the Salesforce Lightning instance.

Note:

- If you are using Salesforce Classic, learn how to access Mindtickle’s learning site within the Salesforce (Classic) platform.
- If Single Sign On is not used, learners need to sign in separately to the Mindtickle tab in Salesforce.
- If you face issues while accessing the Mindtickle lightning web tab in the Safari browser, disable the Prevent Cross-Site Tracking setting in Safari Preferences.
- Mindtickle as a tab is available only in the web browser and not on the Salesforce Mobile application.
- Users can access Mindtickle from the Salesforce mobile application by clicking a menu item. For more information, see Access Mindtickle’s Learning Site using Salesforce Mobile Application .
- When you create a new Visualforce (VF) page, Salesforce adds it only to the System Admin profile by default and not to the other profiles. You must manually provide access to the VF page for the necessary profiles in the Visualforce Page Access screen. ( Setup > Profiles > [Profile Name] > Visualforce Page Access ).

However, if you need implementation guidance, please contact your Customer Success Manager, who will engage our Professional Services team. Professional Services can assist you with consultation, implementation, deployment, and testing of the integration.

Note: Engaging Professional Services is a paid services engagement.

1. Log in to the Salesforce platform.

2. Click the Settings icon in the upper-right corner of your screen and select Setup.

Note: If you are not using Salesforce Single Sign On, you can directly jump to step 7.

3. On the left navigation panel, click Platform Tools, and then under Apps, click App Manager.

4. Click the down arrow on your Connected App and click View from the drop-down menu.

5. On the screen that appears, click Manage.

6. In the SAML Login Information section, copy IdP- Initiated Login URL. This information will be used in step 10.

7. On the left navigation panel, enter Visualforce in the search and click Visualforce Pages.

The Visualforce Pages screen is displayed.

8. Click New.

9. Fill in the mandatory fields in the Page Information section. Click the checkbox for Available for Lightning Experience, Lightning Communities, and the mobile app.

Note: The label can be any name, such as ‘Mindtickle’. The Name field will be populated by default.

10. In the Visualforce Markup window, paste the URL copied in step 6 into the script (location.href) as shown and click Save.

Note: If you are not using Salesforce Single Sign On, you can paste your learning site URL in the Visualforce Markup window.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Analytics & Reporting > Home and navigation > Configurable settings:
- Financial year details : Select your organization’s financial year start date. This is used to calculate business metric cycles like monthly or quarterly metrics in reports such as the Readiness Index (RI).
- Default business metric cycle length : Choose the default cycle (e.g., monthly, quarterly) for business metrics across dashboards and reports. These are based on the financial year start date selected above.
- Default scoring metric : Choose how learner performance is displayed—either as Scoring Performance or % Score . This affects dashboards and reports like Series, Group, and Relationship-based Manager reports.
  - Scoring Performance : Calculated as (Sum of Learners’ scores in started Modules / Sum of max. scores of those Modules) × 100.
  - % Score : Calculated as (Cumulative score obtained by Learners / Cumulative score of assigned Modules) × 100.
- Note: This setting does not apply to Tag, Reviewer, Custom, or Hierarchy-based Manager reports.
- Default rows to display : Set the number of rows shown by default when loading a report. Not applicable for custom or hierarchy-based Manager reports.
- Performance checkpoints : Customize score segmentation using color-coded ranges (0–100%) in tables and charts. Drag the checkpoints to define each performance segment based on your learner evaluation criteria.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Checklist:
Many enablement programs include tasks and activities that learners should complete on the job or offline. As an admin, you can use the checklist module to create a list of tasks and activities the learners need to complete. chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Checklist > Create a checklist:
To create a checklist:

1. Sign in to the admin site.

2. On the left navigation bar, click Training and select Modules.

For more information on creating a module using a template, see Create a module using a module template.The Modules page is displayed.

3. Click Create module to create a checklist.

Alternatively, you can create a checklist from within a series by clicking the Add module button.

4. On the Add modules pop-up, hover over the checklist tile and click Create checklist.Tip: Click Browse module templates to browse pre-designed templates and create a checklist using an existing template. For more information on creating a module using a template, see Create a module using a module template.

5. On the Create new checklist pop-up, in Enter checklist name, enter an appropriate name for the checklist.

For more information about the character limit for checklist attributes, see Character limits of series and module attributes.

6. From the Select a series drop-down menu, select the series where you want to place the checklist.Note: To place the checklist in a new series, click Create a new series. Enter a name for the new series and click the Done icon. Once you click Create, the new series and the checklist are created simultaneously.

7. Click Apply tags > to associate tags with the checklist. For more information, see How to apply Tags to your Modules.Note: If tags are not enabled for your learning site, contact Mindtickle Support or your Customer Success Manager (CSM).

8. Click Description and add a brief overview of the checklist. You can choose from various format options to format the checklist description.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Checklist > Build the checklist:
- Click Add task to create a task within your checklist. You can create multiple tasks and group them together by creating sections .

- Click Add description. The Enter task description field is displayed.
- Enter the task description. The task description can include a brief overview, its objectives, or instructions for completing it. You can choose from various format options to format the task description.
- In Max Score on Task completion , set the maximum score a learner will receive on task completion. By default, the score is set to 100 points. To change it, click the default score value and select a score from the array. The score is awarded to the learner once they mark the task as complete. Note :

- You can set a different maximum score for each question.
- You can change the default maximum score.
- To disable scoring for a task, select Off from the array. For more information on how to disable scoring for all tasks by default, see Configure checklist settings .

6. Click Add files to add a file as an attachment. You can also add questions as a document, PDF, image, or PPT to provide supporting information about the task.

1. You can rename, duplicate, or delete a task from the left navigation panel. Click the More options icon against the task you wish to perform any of these actions, and select an option. To duplicate or delete tasks in bulk, select the tasks by clicking the checkbox against them. Based on the action you need to perform, click Duplicate or Delete . Note :

- Selecting a section will also select all the tasks placed within it. So, the action (copy or delete) applied to a section is applied to all its tasks. You can select multiple tasks only within the same section. To select tasks within different sections, you must select entire sections.
- To select all tasks and sections, click Select All .

You can invite learners to a checklist only after it is published. Until then, the checklist remains in the draft state. Once you have added all the tasks, configure the checklist settings. For more information about publishing a checklist and inviting learners, see Configure checklist settings.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > FAQs:
You can change the sequence of topics in a Course from the overview page.

From the left pane, hover your cursor on the six vertical dots to the left of the topic, drag and drop the topic to the new position. Alternatively, choose to long press the topic and drag it to the required position.

On the overview page, the topic number changes as per the new position.

Note: While selecting a background, if the background has a path icon in the layout, it means it is a fixed background. For a fixed background, you need to place the topics in the predefined path and cannot change the path. If there is no path icon, the layout is a free background, and you can place the topics freely across the background.

To change the position of the topic in the canvas, hover your cursor on the six vertical dots to the left of the topic, drag and drop the topic to the new position. Alternatively, choose to long press the topic and drag it to the required position.

Note: You can interchange the topic position only for a free background. For a fixed background, you need to place the topics in the predefined path.

  - New content (series, module)
  - Content progress status and reminders
  - Content modification
- Discussion-related notification (Only for learners)

- Announcement notifications

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Get Started > Learner notifications:
When a learner receives a notification, the Notification icon or bell icon in the upper right corner of the learning site is highlighted. The red bubble on the bell iconshows the number of new or unseen notifications the learner has received since the last time the learner logged into Mindtickle.

Click the Notification icon to display a list of notifications. Notifications are sorted in reverse chronological order, with the most recent displayed on top. By default, the last ten notifications will be shown in the pop-up window. By scrolling down, the learner can view additional notifications.

Clicking a notification will take the learner to the relevant page on the learning site. The See all option takes the learner to the Notifications page.
