chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Mission > Enter evaluation parameters:
Parameters for evaluating specific skills are defined here. For example, parameters for delivering a standard corporate introduction may include body language, clarity, and confidence.

The reviewers review and score the learner's submission based on the evaluation parameters. The average of the scores earned in each of the evaluation parameters should be higher than or equal to the certificate cut-off for the learners to earn a certificate for the mission (Certificate cut-off can be set in the set cut-off score step).

Each parameter can be set to a maximum of 500 points. An average of all the evaluation parameter scores is calculated for the learner’s score. If there are multiple reviewers, the average of scores provided by all the reviewers is considered.

To add a parameter:

- Click the drop-down next to the Add parameters button and select the type of parameter you want to add.

Note: Clicking Add parameter adds Rating scale parameter by default.

There are three types of parameters that you can choose from.

- Rating scale allows the reviewer to assign a rating value to the Learner based on a defined scale.
- Multiple choice allows the reviewer to pick from a set of provided options. You can create customized options for the reviewers to choose from and set the score accordingly.
- Text input allows the reviewer to enter text feedback.

Note: To publish the mission, you must have at least one scored evaluation parameter, and the score must be greater than zero (0).

This article further explains each parameter type in detail.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Mission > Guidance for reviewer:
Add a description to guide the reviewer/Copilot on how to evaluate a particular parameter.

You can also add +Examples of good rating and +Examples of bad rating. These are additional inputs that can help reviewers visualize a good/bad learner submission for the parameter.

Reviewer guidance provides a structured framework to ensure scoring consistency, reliability, and fairness.

For Human reviewers:

The guidance provides clear considerations and criteria that reviewers should consider while assessing the learner’s performance. It helps reviewers focus on relevant attributes and ensures consistent evaluation across learners.

For Copilot reviewers (AI):

The guidance serves as the framework for generating reliable and consistent scores. The AI uses the information in this section to understand how to evaluate the learner’s response and align its scoring accordingly.

Parameter configurationYou can configure the following settings under the Parameter configuration in the right pane.

- Reviewers can comment: This allows reviewers to provide additional comments in the form of positive and constructive feedback.

- Label the rating scale: This option is used for Rating scale parameters. You can enable the toggle to label the rating scale levels with the appropriate label for each level.

Eg: If the rating is Min: 0 and Max: 3. Then you can rate each level as:

0= Entry level

1= Beginner

2= Intermediate

3= Proficient

- Keyword for analysis: Define keywords for evaluation parameters. Keywords are words or phrases you want the learners to say in their mission. Reviewers will then be able to review the learners’ submissions based on the use of these keywords. Click the Add keywords button to add keywords in the categories derived from the evaluation parameters.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Mission > Guidance for reviewer:
Keywords are words or phrases you want the learners to say in their mission. Reviewers will then be able to review the learners’ submissions based on the use of these keywords. Click the Add keywords button to add keywords in the categories derived from the evaluation parameters.

Set the Minimum number of keywords expected from the Learner to use in the pitch. By default, the number is set to 80% of the total number of keywords added. For example, if you add 10 keywords and set the minimum number expected to be 8 for the first parameter, the keyword analysis conducted on the learner's submission for this parameter is marked as a good match if the recording contains 8 or more keywords. The submission will be marked as a poor match for this parameter if the recording contains less than 8 keywords.

Once you have added the keywords or terms to all your evaluation parameters, click Add.

Based on your input in these categories, the reviewer can see the suggested keywords and the number of keywords used by the learner in the submission.

- Tags on evaluation parameter: Apply relevant tags to the Evaluation parameter. Click the icon against the Tags on evaluation parameter option. You can select from the available tags, create new ones, and click Apply tags .

- Reviewers can recommend a module . Reviewers recommend modules to provide learners with knowledge and practice in the areas they need to improve. Click the Add Module button to choose a module that reviewers can assign to learners to help them improve their presentation or pitch.

Note: You can add only one module per Evaluation parameter.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Mission > Enter evaluation parameters:
Parameters for evaluating specific skills are defined here. For example, parameters for delivering a standard corporate introduction may include body language, clarity, and confidence.

The reviewers review and score the learner's submission based on the evaluation parameters. The average of the scores earned in each of the evaluation parameters should be higher than or equal to the certificate cut-off for the learners to earn a certificate for the mission (Certificate cut-off can be set in the set cut-off score step).

Each parameter can be set to a maximum of 500 points. An average of all the evaluation parameter scores is calculated for the learner’s score. If there are multiple reviewers, the average of scores provided by all the reviewers is considered.

To add a parameter:

- Click the drop-down next to the Add parameters button and select the type of parameter you want to add.

Note: Clicking Add parameter adds Rating scale parameter by default.

There are three types of parameters that you can choose from.

- Rating scale allows the reviewer to assign a rating value to the Learner based on a defined scale.
- Multiple choice allows the reviewer to pick from a set of provided options. You can create customized options for the reviewers to choose from and set the score accordingly.
- Text input allows the reviewer to enter text feedback.

Note: To publish the mission, you must have at least one scored evaluation parameter, and the score must be greater than zero (0).

This article further explains each parameter type in detail.

Add a description to guide the reviewer on how to evaluate a particular parameter.

You can also add +Examples of good rating and +Examples of bad rating. These are additional inputs that can help reviewers visualize a good/bad learner submission for the parameter.

Reviewer guidance provides a structured framework to ensure scoring consistency, reliability, and fairness.

The guidance provides clear considerations and criteria that reviewers should consider while assessing the learner’s performance. It helps reviewers focus on relevant attributes and ensures consistent evaluation across learners.

Parameter configurationYou can configure the following settings under the Parameter configuration in the right pane.

- Reviewers can comment: This allows reviewers to provide additional comments in the form of positive and constructive feedback.

- Label the rating scale: This option is used for Rating scale parameters. You can enable the toggle to label the rating scale levels with the appropriate label for each level.

Eg: If the rating is Min: 0 and Max: 3. Then you can rate each level as:

0= Entry level

1= Beginner

2= Intermediate

3= Proficient

- Keyword for analysis: Define keywords for evaluation parameters. Keywords are words or phrases you want the learners to say in their mission. Reviewers will then be able to review the learners’ submissions based on the use of these keywords. Click the Add keywords button to add keywords in the categories derived from the evaluation parameters.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Mission > Appoint reviewers > Reviewer appointment:
There are three ways in which you can appoint a reviewer to a mission.

- Manually Appoint a Reviewer for each Learner during or after an invitation
- Appoint Manager as Reviewer
- Appoint a common Reviewer for all Learners

Click +Add Another Reviewer to add multiple Reviewers. You can add up to five Reviewers to a Learner.

Note: You cannot appoint a Copilot as a reviewer for Screen Capture missions.

On the web, you can further classify these Reviewers as required or optional by:

- Setting the number of Reviewers who must review the Mission before the Mission is marked complete and the final score is generated for the Learner.
- Selecting the required Reviewers from the list.

You can edit the Mandatory/optional reviewer preference for a published mission. After making the changes to the Mandatory/optional reviewer preference, you are prompted to publish a new version of the mission to implement the changes. The version history under the Publish tab lists the changes to reviewer preference.

- For more information on how editing the Mandatory/optional reviewer preference impacts the learners and reviewers, see Editing mandatory and optional reviewer preference .
- For more information on how to calculate learner scores with optional and mandatory reviewers, see Optional Reviewers for Missions .
- Close review for reviewers that aren’t mandatory: You can set the duration for which the completed mission would be removed from the optional reviewer dashboard. The duration selection is from 1 to 99 days. By default, it is set to 90 days.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Mission > Enter evaluation parameters:
Parameters for evaluating specific skills are defined here. For example, parameters for delivering a standard corporate introduction may include body language, clarity, and confidence.

The reviewers review and score the learner's submission based on the evaluation parameters. The average of the scores earned in each of the evaluation parameters should be higher than or equal to the Certificate Cut-Off for the learners to earn a certificate for the mission (Certificate cut-off can be set in the set cut-off score step).

Each parameter can be set to a maximum of 500 points. An average of all the evaluation parameter scores is calculated for the learner’s score. If there are multiple reviewers, the average of scores provided by all the reviewers is considered.

To add a parameter:

- Click the drop-down next to the Add parameter button and select the type of parameter you want to add.

Note: Clicking Add parameter adds the Rating scale parameter type by default.

There are three types of parameters that you can choose from.

- Rating scale allows the reviewer to assign a rating value to the learner based on a defined scale.
- Multiple choice allows the reviewer to pick from a set of provided options. You can create customized options for the reviewers to choose from and set the Score accordingly.
- Text input allows the reviewer to enter text feedback.

Note: To publish the mission, you must have at least one scored evaluation parameter, and the score must be greater than zero (0).

This article further explains each parameter type in detail.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Mission > Guidance for reviewer:
Add a description to guide the reviewer/Copilot on how to evaluate a particular parameter.

You can also add +Examples of good rating and +Examples of bad rating. These are additional inputs that can help reviewers visualize a good/bad learner submission for the parameter.

Reviewer guidance provides a structured framework to ensure scoring consistency, reliability, and fairness.

For Human reviewers:

The guidance provides clear considerations and criteria that reviewers should consider while assessing the learner’s performance. It helps reviewers focus on relevant attributes and ensures consistent evaluation across learners.

For Copilot reviewers (AI):

The guidance serves as the framework for generating reliable and consistent scores. The AI uses the information in this section to understand how to evaluate the learner’s response and align its scoring accordingly.

Parameter configurationYou can configure the following settings under the Parameter configuration in the right pane.

- Reviewers can comment: This allows reviewers to provide additional comments in the form of positive and constructive feedback.

- Label the rating scale: This option is used for Rating scale parameters, you can enable the toggle to label the rating scale levels with appropriate label for each level.

Eg: If the rating is Min: 0 and Max: 3. Then you can rate each level as:

0= Entry level

1= Beginner

2= Intermediate

3= Proficient

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Mission > Guidance for reviewer:
- Keyword for analysis: Define keywords for evaluation parameters. Keywords are words or phrases you want the learners to say in their mission. Reviewers will then be able to review the Learners’ submissions based on the use of these keywords.
- Click the Add keywords button to add keywords in the categories derived from the evaluation parameters.
- Set the Minimum number of keywords expected from the learner to use in the pitch. By default, the number is set to 80% of the total number of keywords added. For example, if you add 10 keywords and set the minimum number expected to be 8 for the first parameter, the keyword analysis conducted on the learner's submission for this parameter is marked as a good match if the recording contains 8 or more keywords. The submission will be marked as a poor match for this parameter if the recording contains less than 8 keywords. Once you have added the keywords or terms to all your evaluation parameters, click Add .
- Based on your input in these categories, the reviewer can see the suggested keywords and the number of keywords used by the learner in the submission.

- Tags on Evaluation Parameter : Apply relevant tags to the evaluation parameter. Click the icon against the Tags on evaluation parameter option. You can select from the available tags or create new ones and then click Apply tags .

- Reviewers can recommend a module: Recommend modules to provide learners with knowledge and practice in the areas they need to improve. Click the Add Module button, to choose a module that reviewers can assign to learners to help them improve their presentation or pitch.

Note: You can add only one module per evaluation parameter.

- Manually Appoint a Reviewer for each Learner during or after an invitation
- Appoint Manager as Reviewers
- Appoint a common Reviewer for all Learners

Click +Add Another Reviewer to add multiple Reviewers. You can add up to five Reviewers to a Learner.

On the web, you can further classify these Reviewers as required or optional by:

- Setting the number of Reviewers who must review the Mission before the Mission is marked complete and the final score is generated for the Learner.
- Selecting the required Reviewers from the list.

You can edit the Mandatory/optional reviewer preference for a published mission. After making the changes to the Mandatory/optional reviewer preference, you are prompted to publish a new version of the mission to implement the changes. The version history under the Publish tab lists the changes to reviewer preference.

- For more information on how editing the Mandatory/optional reviewer preference impacts the learners and reviewers, see Editing mandatory and optional reviewer preference .
- For more information on how to calculate learner scores with optional and mandatory reviewers, see Optional Reviewers for Missions .

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Mission > Enter evaluation parameters:
Parameters for evaluating specific skills are defined here. For example, parameters for delivering a standard corporate introduction may include body language, clarity, and confidence.

The reviewers review and score the learner's submission based on the evaluation parameters. The average of the scores earned in each of the evaluation parameters should be higher than or equal to the Certificate Cut-Off for the learners to earn a certificate for the mission (Certificate cut-off can be set in the set cut-off score step).

Each parameter can be set to a maximum of 500 points. An average of all the evaluation parameter scores is calculated for the learner’s score. If there are multiple reviewers, the average of scores provided by all the reviewers is considered.

To add a parameter:

- Click the drop-down next to the Add parameter button and select the type of parameter you want to add.

Note: Clicking Add parameter adds the Rating scale parameter type by default.

There are three types of parameters that you can choose from.

- Rating scale allows the reviewer to assign a rating value to the learner based on a defined scale.
- Multiple choice allows the reviewer to pick from a set of provided options. You can create customized options for the reviewers to choose from and set the Score accordingly.
- Text input allows the reviewer to enter text feedback.

Note: To publish the mission, you must have at least one scored evaluation parameter, and the score must be greater than zero (0).

This article further explains each parameter type in detail.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Mission > Guidance for reviewer:
Add a description to guide the reviewer/Copilot on how to evaluate a particular parameter.

You can also add +Examples of good rating and +Examples of bad rating. These are additional inputs that can help reviewers visualize a good/bad learner submission for the parameter.

Reviewer guidance provides a structured framework to ensure scoring consistency, reliability, and fairness.

For Human reviewers:

The guidance provides clear considerations and criteria that reviewers should consider while assessing the learner’s performance. It helps reviewers focus on relevant attributes and ensures consistent evaluation across learners.

For Copilot reviewers (AI):

The guidance serves as the framework for generating reliable and consistent scores. The AI uses the information in this section to understand how to evaluate the learner’s response and align its scoring accordingly.

Parameter configurationYou can configure the following settings under the Parameter configuration in the right pane.

- Reviewers can comment: This allows reviewers to provide additional comments in the form of positive and constructive feedback.

- Label the rating scale: This option is used for Rating scale parameters, you can enable the toggle to label the rating scale levels with appropriate label for each level.

Eg: If the rating is Min: 0 and Max: 3. Then you can rate each level as:

0= Entry level

1= Beginner

2= Intermediate

3= Proficient

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Mission > Guidance for reviewer:
- Keyword for analysis: Define keywords for evaluation parameters. Keywords are words or phrases you want the learners to say in their mission. Reviewers will then be able to review the Learners’ submissions based on the use of these keywords.
- Click the Add keywords button to add keywords in the categories derived from the evaluation parameters.
- Set the Minimum number of keywords expected from the learner to use in the pitch. By default, the number is set to 80% of the total number of keywords added. For example, if you add 10 keywords and set the minimum number expected to be 8 for the first parameter, the keyword analysis conducted on the learner's submission for this parameter is marked as a good match if the recording contains 8 or more keywords. The submission will be marked as a poor match for this parameter if the recording contains less than 8 keywords. Once you have added the keywords or terms to all your evaluation parameters, click Add .
- Based on your input in these categories, the reviewer can see the suggested keywords and the number of keywords used by the learner in the submission.

- Tags on Evaluation Parameter : Apply relevant tags to the evaluation parameter. Click the icon against the Tags on evaluation parameter option. You can select from the available tags or create new ones and then click Apply tags .

- Reviewers can recommend a module: Recommend modules to provide learners with knowledge and practice in the areas they need to improve. Click the Add Module button, to choose a module that reviewers can assign to learners to help them improve their presentation or pitch.

Note: You can add only one module per evaluation parameter.

Keywords to include will state if your draft is a Good Match, Moderate Match, or Poor Match by comparing the content in your pitch with the model pitch.

It consists of Submission length, Speech pace, and Filler words.

The Submission length indicates how closely you've met or matched the target length range set by the Admin. It will state if the submission length is short, appropriate, or long based on the set target length range.

Speech pace shows how your delivery compares with the average range for speaking rate. The Speech pace insight will help you understand if the pace at which you have delivered the submission is slow, appropriate, or fast.

The Filler words insight highlights phrases or sounds that mark a pause or hesitation in your pitch or presentation. This insight identifies filler words you have used and lists the number of times each word is repeated.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Mission > Submission > Upload the presentation and then record the pitch > Text sentiment:
The text sentiment analysis analyzes the tone of your transcript based on sentiments such as Joy, Anger, Anxious, Disapproval, and Sad. The text sentiment analysis is done on the overall transcription sentiment and the keyword-level transcription.

While analyzing a transcription, the most important keywords are identified, and based on the tones identified for each keyword, they are grouped into sentiments, as mentioned earlier. For each keyword, all the occurrences in the transcript are considered. If a keyword is used multiple times in different contexts, then different tones could be identified. Such keywords would be present in the respective sentiment tabs, where you can click on the keyword pills to see the sentences where the keywords were spoken.

This approach is helpful for better understanding the context in which the learner used a particular keyword or phrase. Based on this analysis, you can improve your pitch by using the correct expected words.

The text sentiment analysis analyzes the tone of your transcript based on sentiments such as Joy, Anger, Anxious, Disapproval, and Sad. The text sentiment analysis is done on the overall transcription sentiment and the keyword-level transcription.

While analyzing a transcription, the most important keywords are identified, and based on the tones identified for each keyword, they are grouped into sentiments, as mentioned earlier. For each keyword, all the occurrences in the transcript are considered. If a keyword is used multiple times in different contexts, then different tones could be identified. Such keywords would be present in the respective sentiment tabs, where you can click on the keyword pills to see the sentences where the keywords were spoken.

This approach is helpful for better understanding the context in which the learner used a particular keyword or phrase. Based on this analysis, you can improve your pitch by using the correct expected words.

Note: The transcription language defaults to English (USA).

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Mission > Submission > Insights > Content insight:
It consists of Keywords to include and Words to avoid, which help identify the areas of improvement in your pitch.

Keywords to include will state if your draft is a Good Match, Moderate Match, or Poor Match by comparing the content in your pitch with the model pitch.

It analyzes if you have used the keywords set by the admin and displays those that you have included in your draft. It also identifies the keywords that you should consider including in your recording.

Click the right arrow icon to see a graphical representation of the insight.

Words to avoid will specify the words to avoid in your submission. If you have included any, the system highlights these words and the number of times these words have been repeated.

Click the right arrow icon to see a graphical representation of the analysis.

Quests on the Admin Site: Earlier, Quests were housed under the All Quests tab in the left navigation panel. Now, this tab is removed, and any Quests you create will reside under the Series in which you create them, just like any other Module. Your existing Quests are automatically moved to a new Series called Quests, and you can move them to another Series if necessary.

Quests on the Learning Site: Quests were earlier housed under the All Quests tab in the left navigation panel. Now, this tab is removed, and Quests will appear in the Series in which they were created. Your existing Quests are automatically moved to a new Series called Quests, and you can move them to another Series if necessary.

Overall, except for a few minor changes, the experience of creating and consuming Quests remains the same.

Because Quests are typically part of long-running enablement programs, MindTickle recommends putting the Quest Module as the last Module in a Series so that Learners can retain knowledge for a longer time.

With this change, the following is now possible for Quests:

- While publishing a Quest, on the Publish tab, you can now invite Learners who are already invited to the Series
- Quests now appear in global searches on both the Admin Site and Learning Site
- Analytics for Quests in a Series will now appear in the Series analytics
- Like for other Modules, you can do the following for a Quest:
  - Edit the Module
  - Copy it from one Series to another (either as a new draft copy or multi-present copy)
  - Move it to another Series
  - Archive it

Note:

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Quest > What’s New > Quests in Series:
- In a Series with Sequential Unlocking enabled, a Quest Module is unlocked automatically when the Learner completes the preceding Modules. And the Module after the Quest is also unlocked along with Quest. In other words, the Learner need not complete the Quest to unlock the Module after it.The goal of Quest is to help drive retention. Having a Quest in the middle of a Series can help reinforce what the Learner has learned in the preceding Modules while progressing to the next Module in the Series.For example: There is a sequentially locked Series with the following Module structure: Course > Quest > Assessment. Initially, only the first Module (Course) is unlocked. When the Learner completes the Course, both Quest and Assessment are unlocked.
- Version upgrades for changes made in a Quest are currently not available and will be provided in a future release. Currently, changes (overall and settings-related) made to the Quest cannot be tracked through versions.
- For Automation Rules, currently the Learner's status of Quest cannot be used as the condition of a rule, with the exception of Quest completion. For example, you cannot write rules with a condition, such as “If something happens in a Quest, then do this…” But a Quest can be used as an action resulting from another condition. For example, “If a Quick-Update is completed, then assign them a Quest”.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Quest > Introduction:
A Quest is a Module that contains Questions you develop on a given topic or concept. A few of the Questions are selected on a periodic basis and delivered to Learners in the form of Challenges. The Quest creation workflow contains four main tabs.

Build: The Build tab allows you to add Questions within a Quest. You can also edit and delete Questions from the Build tab before publishing the Quest.

Settings: The Settings tab allows you to configure General Settings, Question Delivery, Email and Notification settings. You can also enable Randomization and Gamification for a Quest in the Settings tab.

Publish: The Publish tab prompts you to complete all to-dos and then publish the Quest.

Invite & Track: The Invite & Track tab allows you to invite new Learners and lists the Learners already invited to the Quest. This tab also displays their progress and activity.

This article further explains how to create a new Quest Module.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Quest > Create a Quest:
1. From the admin site home page, click Training > Modules > Create modules .

Alternatively, you can create a quest from within a series by clicking Training > Series > select the required series > Create module.

Or click Training > Series > Create > Module.

2. On the Add modules pop-up, hover over the Quest tile and click Create quest.

The Create New Quest pop-up appears.

Perform the following and then click Create:

- Enter a name for the Quest Module.
- Select the Series in which you want to place it. If you don't want to place it in an existing Series, create a new Series by clicking the Create a New Series link.
- Click the Description link to add a description for the Module.Note: The Description field allows up to 1000 characters.
- Click Edit above the thumbnail to edit the Module thumbnail.

To learn about the character limit for Quest attributes, see Character limits of Series and Module attributes.

3. The Build tab in the Quest creation workflow opens.

To rename, delete, or get the URL of the Quest, click the(arrow) button next to the Quest name. You can also preview the Quest after completing all the to-dos.

When you copy the Quest URL, it is copied to the clipboard and can be pasted into a text editor, et al.

When you discard an unpublished Quest that is in draft state, it is permanently deleted and cannot be retrieved.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Quest > Add/Create Questions > Add Questions individually:
1. Click the Add a Question button on the left panel.

2. Enter an appropriate Title for the Question in the field provided. The Question Title is visible in Analytics and also to Learners when they check their performance in the MindTickle App. You can apply Tags to the Question by clicking the + icon below the Title.

Note: The Title field allows up to 50 characters.

3. Enter the text for the Question description in the text box provided. You can format the Question text using the text editor provided.

4. Click Add supporting video/image to add a video or image that you want Learners to refer to understand the Question better.

5. On the screen that appears, you can either drop files or click to browse the files you want to upload. You will be redirected based on the option you select. Follow the appropriate steps to add the supporting file.

6. Quests only allow you to add Multiple Choice Questions. In the Answer Options section, click the Add Option button. Enter the appropriate text for each answer option and select the check box for correct options. Answer Options are always randomized when displayed to Learners in a Challenge. Click the delete icon on the right of the question to delete an option.

Note: A Multiple Choice Question should have at least two options for the Learner to choose from. The Option field allows up to 200 characters.

7. Enable the Explanation toggle switch to add information to the Question which will only be visible to the Learners after they have answered the Question (correctly or incorrectly).

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Quest > Question Delivery > First Round:
In this section, you can define how you want a Challenge to be presented to the Learners the first time.

Question per Challenge - From the drop-down list, select the number of Questions that you want to ask the Learners in each Challenge. You can select up to 5 Questions. The number of Questions added in the Build tab must be equal to or more than the number you select here.

Note: See best practices you can follow to create a Quest.

Interval between Challenges - Select the number of days between two consecutive Challenges. You can select anywhere between 1 and 5 days. The date of delivery for the next Challenge is calculated only after a Learner has completed the current Challenge.

Note: Until the Learner completes the previous Challenge, further ones are not delivered.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Quest > Question Delivery > Approx number of weeks needed to finish the Quest:
Based on the values you select in the section above, and the number of Questions added in the Quest, three options are calculated automatically and displayed in the drop-down list. Select an option from the drop-down based on the pace you want to set for your Learners. According to Spaced Reinforcement fundamentals, the slower the pace of a Quest, the higher is the knowledge retention.

Note: The approximation is done considering extreme scenarios in which a Learner either answers all Questions correctly or incorrectly. However, the calculation does not take into consideration the delays that may occur if the Learner does not respond to Questions on schedule.

Depending on the option you select, the values for other parameters of the Quest are displayed. These values cannot be changed.

Reinforce incorrectly answered Questions after - The number of days after which a Question, that was previously answered incorrectly by the Learner, should be delivered again.

Reinforce correctly answered Questions after - The number of days after which a Question, that was previously answered correctly by the Learner, should be delivered again.

Maximum number of times a Question will be shown to a User - This is always set to 3 by default.

Number of consecutive correct answers to master a question - The number of times after which a Question, if answered correctly every time, can be mastered. Once mastered, the Question will not be delivered to the User again.

Learn more about the best practices to follow while creating a Quest.

Note: After publishing the Quest, you cannot edit the Question Delivery.
chunks.body:
Based on the values you select in the section above, and the number of Questions added in the Quest, three options are calculated automatically and displayed in the drop-down list. Select an option from the drop-down based on the pace you want to set for your Learners. According to Spaced Reinforcement fundamentals, the slower the pace of a Quest, the higher is the knowledge retention.

Note: The approximation is done considering extreme scenarios in which a Learner either answers all Questions correctly or incorrectly. However, the calculation does not take into consideration the delays that may occur if the Learner does not respond to Questions on schedule.

Depending on the option you select, the values for other parameters of the Quest are displayed. These values cannot be changed.

Reinforce incorrectly answered Questions after - The number of days after which a Question, that was previously answered incorrectly by the Learner, should be delivered again.

Reinforce correctly answered Questions after - The number of days after which a Question, that was previously answered correctly by the Learner, should be delivered again.

Maximum number of times a Question will be shown to a User - This is always set to 3 by default.

Number of consecutive correct answers to master a question - The number of times after which a Question, if answered correctly every time, can be mastered. Once mastered, the Question will not be delivered to the User again.

Learn more about the best practices to follow while creating a Quest.

Note: After publishing the Quest, you cannot edit the Question Delivery.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Quest > Randomization:
The Randomize Questions option chooses and delivers Questions to Learners in no particular sequence, regardless of the order in which they were created. The toggle switch is enabled by default.

If you want the Questions to be delivered in the order in which they were created in the Build tab, disable the toggle switch.

Note: The Randomization setting is applicable only to Questions. In Quests, the answer options of a Question are randomized by default.

See best practices that you can follow to configure various settings in a Quest. Learn about the Gamification step in the Settings tab of the Quest creation workflow.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Quest:
The Score of a Quest is calculated based on

- The response of the Learner (correct/incorrect) to a Question
- Bonus points earned for every saved attempt

Note: A saved attempt is an attempt that is not taken by the Learner. For example, if the Learner is given three attempts for a Question and responds correctly in the first two attempts, he saves an attempt and gets Bonus points for this saved attempt.

Scores are awarded for every attempt to a Question. If in a particular attempt, a Question is answered correctly, the Learner scores 100 points. Zero points are scored for an incorrect answer. The Learners also score a bonus of 100 points if they save an attempt.

For example, for a Quest the Question Delivery settings are as follows:

- Maximum number of times a Question is shown to a User is set to 3
- Number of consecutive correct answers to master a Question is set to 2

Learner Alex Fry answers the Question correctly in the first two attempts. She does not have to attempt it a third time. So she scores 200 points (100 for every correct answer) and a bonus of 100 points for the saved attempt. She receives a total of 300 points.

Learner Nick Max answers the Question incorrectly in the first attempt. But she answers correctly in the next two attempts. So she scores 200 points (100 for every correct answer).

Learner Peter Link answers the Question correctly only once out of the three attempts and scores 100 points.

The table below displays how Scoring is based on the various combinations or responses and the number of attempts saved.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Quest > Hall of Fame:
Hall of Fame is enabled by default and is visible to Learners on their Learning Site. It displays the scores of all the Learners invited to the Quest. Disable the toggle switch if you do not want Hall of Fame to be displayed on the Learning Site.

Note: If the Segmented Leaderboard is enabled for your Site, then the Hall of Fame will also display the Segmented Leaderboard.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Quest > Master Badges:
Master Badges are awarded when a Learner gives consecutive correct answers based on the Number of consecutive correct answers to master a Question setting in the Question Delivery step of the Settings tab.

For example, if the Number of consecutive correct answers to master a Question is set to 2, the Learner earns the next level of the Master Badge every time a Question in that Quest is answered correctly twice in a row.

There are four levels in the Master Badge. Each level is unlocked based on the following criteria.

- Level 1 when the Learner masters 10% of the questions
- Level 2 when the Learner masters 30% of the questions
- Level 3 when the Learner masters 60% of the questions
- Level 4 when the Learner masters 100% of the questions

These levels are not configurable. Enable the toggle switch to award Master Badges to your Learners. On the Learning Site, the Rules section in Quest explains details about unlocking the next level of Master Badges to Learners.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Quest > Streak Badges:
Streak Badges are awarded to a Learner upon completing a Challenge within 24 hours from the time it was delivered, regardless of whether the response is right or wrong.

Note: Challenges are not delivered on weekends. However, if a Challenge is delivered on a Friday, the Learner has to respond within 24 hours in order to earn a Streak Badge.

Each level of the Streak is unlocked based on the following criteria.

- Level 1 when the Learner completes the Challenge within 24 hours from its delivery
- Level 2 when the Learner completes 3 consecutive Challenges, within 24 hours from the time each of them was delivered
- Level 3 when the Learner completes 5 consecutive Challenges, within 24 hours from the time each of them was delivered

There is no upper limit to the levels in the Streak Badge. A Learner attains the next level after completing more Challenges, in increments of two, consecutively within 24 hours. Once a Streak is broken, the level is reset. For example, a Learner has attained a Level 3 Streak but fails to complete the next Challenge within 24 hours from its delivery, then the Streak would reset to zero.

Enable the toggle switch to award Streak Badges to your Learners. On the Learning Site, the Rules section in Quest explains details about unlocking the next level of Streak Badges to Learners.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Quest > Proficiency Level:
A Proficiency Level is achieved when a Learner scores the defined percentage of the total Score of the Quest. There are five Proficiency Levels with % values provided by default as shown below.

For example, if the total Score of the Quest is 1000 points, the Expert Proficiency Level is achieved when a Learner scores 400 points. You can disable a Proficiency Level and/or change the percentage value to suit your requirement.

Note: The names and icons of a Proficiency Level cannot be customized.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Quest > Adding Questions:
Give a relevant Title while adding a Question in the Build tab of the Quest creation workflow. We recommend giving a short summary describing the Question in the Title field as it will be visible in analytics. This Title is also seen by Learners when they receive the Question, reminders, and notifications.

We also recommend creating situation-based Questions that reflect scenarios that Learners encounter in their day-to-day work. You can use the Question description field to elaborate on the situation and also add supporting a video/image if required.

We recommend having four Answer Options to each Question. Ensure you enable the Explanation toggle switch and add information to the Question in the field provided. The Explanation will only be visible to the Learners after they have answered the Question (correctly or incorrectly).

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Quest > Question Delivery:
Ensure that the number of Questions created in the Build tab is more than the number of Questions per Challenge setting in the Question Delivery step of the Settings tab.

For example, you create only 2 Questions in the Build tab and set the Questions per Challenge to 3. You will not be able to proceed to publish the Quest. An actionable item (To-do) to be completed before you can publish the Quest will also be displayed.

To get the best out of Spaced Reinforcement, we recommend that you set

- The maximum number of Questions per Challenge to 3
- The Approx number of weeks needed to finish the Quest to the recommended value based on your settings

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Quest > Randomization:
Randomization is turned ON by default. If you want the Questions to be delivered in a specific order, ensure that you

- Create Questions in the same order that you want them to be delivered to the Learners.
- Disable the Randomize Questions toggle switch on the Settings tab.

For example, if you want easy Questions to be delivered first followed by difficult ones, add Questions in the increasing order of difficulty on the Build tab and disable Randomization on the Setting tab.

Note: The Randomization setting is applicable only to Questions. In Quests, the answer options of a Question are randomized by default.

This article explains how Scoring and delivery schedule of a Challenge adapts based on the responses of Learners.

Learn how Scoring works in a Quest.

Let's take an example of a Quest where the Question Delivery settings are as follows:

- Questions per Challenge - 2
- Interval between Challenges - 2 days
- Reinforce incorrectly answered Questions after - 7 days
- Reinforce correctly answered Questions after - 13 days
- Maximum number of times a Question is shown to a User - 3
- Number of consecutive correct answers to master a Question - 2

Note: If the Randomize Questions switch is enabled, the sequence in which Questions are delivered to each Learner will change.

The approximate timeframe for a Quest to be completed is defined based on the number of Questions added to the Quest, the Question Delivery settings, and the cadence followed by the Learner. This is displayed in the last section of the Question Delivery Settings step of the Quest creation workflow. For this example, the timeframe is 3-6 weeks.

In this example, we will see how the Question Delivery works for 2 Learners- Linn May and Jason Blake. We are assuming that the Randomization is turned off and Learners receive Questions in the same sequence.

Linn May attempts Questions without any delay, within 24 hours from the time a Challenge is delivered. The following table shows the Questions Delivery schedule, response, and Score of Linn May for a Challenge.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Quest:
Questions and Challenges are delivered to Learners only on weekdays (Monday to Friday). Based on the Question Delivery settings, if a Challenge is scheduled for the weekend, it automatically pauses and is delivered on the following Monday.

Delivery of Challenges starts on Monday at 00:00 (in the timezone of the Learner) and ends by Friday at 23:59 in Learner's timezone.

Learners will not receive invitations to a Challenge on the weekend. However, a reminder to the Challenge may be sent on the weekend based on the Email and Notifications settings applied while creating the Quest.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Quest > Preview:
After creating the Quest and completing all the to-dos, click the Preview button in the upper-right corner to see how the Quest will appear to Learners.

The preview mode helps you visualize the end-user experience so that you can improve the content if needed.

In the preview mode that opens, click the device icons to visualize how the Quest appears on various devices (computer, tablet - in portrait, tablet - in the landscape, and mobile - in portrait) before publishing it. Click Exit Preview to go back to the Quest creation workflow.

You can preview a Quest irrespective of its current state. For example, you can preview a Quest even after it is published. However, the preview mode will always show the “Did not start” state for Learners.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Quest > Publish:
To publish a Quest, make sure you have completed all the to-dos. Then perform the following:

1. In the Invite (Learners) of this Series option, choose the Learners you want to invite to the Quest. Select one of the following options from the dropdown:
  - All Learners: Invites Learners who are invited to at least one Module in the Series. Click View to view the list of invited Learners.
  - Fully invited Learners: Invites Learners who are invited to all Modules in the Series. Click View to view the list of invited Learners.
  - Select Learners: Allows you to select from the list of Learners invited to the Series.

1. Select the Also notify the Learners via email checkbox if you want the Learners to receive an email notification inviting them to the Quest. Click Confirm Publish.
2. If you want to publish without inviting any Learners, click the Don’t invite anyone button and click Confirm Publish.

Note: After publishing Quest, you cannot edit the Question Delivery. However, you can edit the following parameters from the Build tab:

- Title
- Question: You can edit the Question text but not the Answer Options. Thus, we suggest you edit the Question text only if you are correcting a typo or the phrasing of the question to ensure it still matches with the Answer Options.
- Explanation. However, you cannot edit the Explanation toggle that decides if the explanation appears once the user has answered the question or before.
- Supporting video/image.
- Add tags to the question.

Also, the above changes, once saved, will be available for all the invited users immediately, and republishing/version upgrade is not required.

A screen capture mission is a virtual scenario that allows you to practice your presentation skills, such as a product demo, with Reviewer feedback.

This article explains the steps to submit your screen capture mission submission on the web. This mission type is not supported on the mobile app.

There are three primary steps in a mission submission:

- Getting Started
- Submission
  - Content insight
  - Articulation insight
  - Text sentiment
  - Transcript
- Review/Feedback
- Re-attempt (if applicable)

You will receive an email notification when a screen capture mission is assigned to you.

Click the Get Started button in the email and sign in to your learning site with your registered email address or SSO-enabled account if you haven’t already.

Note: For a seamless recording experience, we recommend using the Google Chrome browser to access the assigned Mission.

On the page that opens, you will see the following mission attributes:

- Scenario
- Certificate cut-off
- Evaluation parameter
- Target length range and due date

This article further explains each attribute in detail.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Mission > Getting Started > Scenario:
The scenario description highlights the value and intended impact of the mission.

Attachments: The description may also contain additional attachments. These attachments may be in the form of an example video, a customer persona, or a sample presentation. Download and read the attachments before you begin the Mission.

The scenario may contain a model pitch and additional material to assist you in submitting your best pitch.

Model pitch: A model pitch is a best-practice pitch that serves as a benchmark in this scenario. It can be in the form of a video, audio, or text. The model pitch has a transcript and search bar to help find specific parts of the pitch quickly.

It may be helpful to download the model pitch so that you can use it as a reference to practice and submit your best attempt.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Mission > Getting Started > Certificate cut-off:
The Certificate cut-off is the minimum score that you are expected to achieve to earn a Certificate of completion.

If Certificate cut-off is displayed then a certificate will be awarded after you achieve the score. If the Passing cut-off is displayed then no certificate will be awarded after achieving the score.

In the following example, the Certificate cut-off is set to 80%, which means you have to score a minimum of 80% to pass this mission.

An evaluation parameter can be a statement, question, term, or phrase that defines a standard against which your knowledge, skill, or behavior is evaluated by the reviewers.

A mission can contain multiple evaluation parameters that can be grouped together under sections.

Evaluation parameters have scores assigned. It is important that you understand them and use them as guidelines when recording your submission.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Mission > Submission > Insights:
Insights have three components: Content insight , Articulation , and Text sentiment.

The Content insight analyzes your submission and verifies if you have covered the right subjects in your recording.

The Articulation insight measures how closely you have met the guidelines set for this mission.

The Text sentiment analyzes the tone of your transcript based on various sentiments.

This article further explains each component in detail.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Mission > Submission > Insights > Content Insight:
It consists of Keywords to include and Words to avoid, which help identify the areas of improvement in your pitch.

Keywords to include will state if your draft is a Good Match, Moderate Match, or Poor Match by comparing the content in your pitch with the model pitch.

It analyzes if you have used the keywords set by the admin and displays those that you have included in your draft. It also identifies the keywords that you should consider including in your recording.

Click the right arrow icon to see a graphical representation of the insight.

Words to avoid will specify the words you should prevent from using in your Mission. If you've included any, it will highlight these words and the number of times these words have been repeated.

It consists of Submission length, Speech pace, and Filler words.

The Submission length indicates how closely you have met or matched the target length range set by the admin. It will state if the submission length is short, appropriate, or long based on the set target length range.

Speech pace shows how your delivery compares with the average range for speaking rate. The Speech pace insight will help you understand if the pace at which you have delivered the submission is slow, appropriate, or fast.

The Filler words insight highlights phrases or sounds that mark a pause or hesitation in your pitch or presentation. This insight identifies filler words you have used and lists the number of times each word is repeated.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Mission > Submission > Insights > Text sentiment:
The text sentiment analysis analyzes the tone of your transcript based on sentiments such as Joy, Anger, Anxious, Disapproval, and Sad. The text sentiment analysis is done on overall transcription sentiment and keyword-level transcription.

While analyzing a transcription, the most important keywords are identified, and based on the tones identified for each keyword, they are grouped in the sentiments, as mentioned earlier. For each keyword, all the occurrences in the transcript are considered. If a keyword is used multiple times in different contexts, then different tones could be identified. Such keywords would be present in the respective sentiment tabs where you can click on the keyword pills to see the sentences where the keywords were spoken.

This approach is helpful for better understanding the context in which the learner used a particular keyword or phrase. Based on this analysis, you can improve your pitch by using the correct expected words.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > FAQs:
As an admin, you can manage all your enablement programs on the admin site by creating different modules within a Series for your learners. You can conduct any type of readiness activity through various modules in Mindtickle.

Following are the eight types of modules in Mindtickle; each has a different use case:

1. Quick update
2. Course
3. ILT (instructor-led training)
4. Checklist
5. Quest
6. Assessment
7. Mission
8. Coaching sessions

To learn about each type of module, see Types of modules.

To choose the right module for your use case, begin by asking the following question:

What is the objective of your readiness activity?

You can implement your readiness activity using one or more modules in Mindtickle. Your objective can be to:

- Impart Knowledge
- Upskill with Practice
- Evaluate and Reinforce
- Track Activities

Where:

- Grey connectors indicate Impart Knowledge flow.
- Blue connectors indicate Upskill with Practice flow.
- Orange connectors indicate Evaluate and Reinforce flow.
- Yellow connectors indicate Track Activities flow.

Note: The quick update module does not support certification. However, if you embed a mission with certification in a quick update, learners can access the mission.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > FAQs > Impart Knowledge:
If the objective of your readiness activity is to impart knowledge, decide the type of training you want to set forth for Learners:

- Bite-sized training : If you intend to impart knowledge through bite-sized training, use the Quick-Update module. A quick update is for swift consumption of content and facilitates ongoing learning and continuous communication. For example, a quick update is useful for sharing pop-quizzes on a product, leadership podcasts, sales kick-off agenda, win stories, company news, or team member spotlight.
- In-depth training: If you intend to impart knowledge through in-depth training, use the Course module. A Course gives a unique visual theme of content to the Learners and can have multiple topics and question formats. For example, a Course is useful in providing product training, tools training, or a company overview.
- Live training: If you intend to impart knowledge through live training, use the Instructor-Led Training (ILT) module. An ILT allows you to set up and track in-person and virtual training sessions. It helps you streamline all your Instructor-Led Training activities like scheduling, inviting Learners, managing enrollment. For example, an ILT is useful in conducting bootcamp, breakout sessions, open enrollment, product training, or all-hands meetings.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > FAQs > Upskill with Practice:
- If your answer is Yes , decide the seat time for your readiness activity.
  - If the seat time is less than 15 minutes, use Quick-Update .
  - If the seat time is more than 15 minutes, use Course .
- If your answer is No , do you need scenario-based role-play or activity?
  - If your answer is Yes :
    - Create an Instructor-Led Training (ILT) module if the training should be instructor-driven.
    - Otherwise, use Mission and assign it to your Learners for AI-assisted feedback on their submission. Missions allow virtual role-plays in a safe and controlled environment for various situations. It also promotes ongoing practice and skill development. For example , Missions are useful in practicing for an elevator pitch, objection handling, cold emails, product demo, using tools (for example, log an opportunity), territory and account plan, or introducing a new member to the team.
  - If your answer is No and the seat time for your readiness activity is less than 15 minutes, use Quick-Update . If the seat time is more than 15 minutes, use Course .
    - However, if you want to expedite improvement through personalized feedback, use Coaching Sessions to facilitate one-on-one Manager-driven coaching and feedback. Coaching Sessions facilitate a culture of coaching by helping you capture feedback from coaching exercises and engage coaches to assign remediation. For example , Coaching Sessions are useful in one-on-one discussions, certifications, mock call evaluation, ride-along, competency baselining, or peer-to-peer discussions.
    - If you do not want to expedite improvement through personalized feedback, use Assessment for timed reinforcement. An Assessment supports negative scoring. It evaluates the Learners’ knowledge and offers certification opportunities. For example , Assessments are useful in evaluating technical concepts, product knowledge, process, graduating boot camp, or company assessment.
- If your answer is No and you are going to test your Learners’ knowledge by setting a timer for the Questions and Answers, use Assessment . If you want to improve knowledge retention, use Quest driven by an adaptive system. Quest helps you automatically deliver short, personalized, and gamified challenges at intelligently spaced intervals. Quest offers real-time performance feedback. For example , Quest helps in continuous improvement, learning complex concepts, building proficiency, business process change, seasonal schemes, sales events, or regulatory compliance.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > FAQs > Glossary:
- Badges - Rewards earned by Learners when they achieve a certain number of points. To learn about earning badges, see the help .
- Certificate - A document confirming that the Learner has either completed the assigned Module or successfully achieved a Certificate Score. To learn when Learners achieve a certificate, see the help .
- Factopedia - Allows Admins to share additional information contextually in a Course or Quick-Update. See help .
- Hint - Using a Hint will give you an indication or suggestion that will lead you to the correct answer.
- Knowledge Content - Content created or embedded in a Module for structured training such as videos, documents, files, and demonstrations.
- Lifeline - Using a Lifeline while answering a question eliminates the wrong answer options. The lifeline count displayed for a question is the total number of lifelines that can be used for the question. Note: The Lifeline functionality is available for courses and quick updates.
- Randomization - Allows Admins to deliver questions to Learners randomly or without a specific order.
- Recertification - Allows Admins to set reminders and allow Learners to retake specific Modules after a set period.
- Seat Time - The time it takes a Learner to complete a Module.
- Self-paced Modules - Modules for which Learners have the flexibility to complete at their own time and schedule.
- Spaced Reinforcement - In a Spaced Reinforcement, short, personalized, and gamified challenges are delivered to Learners at spaced intervals helping them convert short-term memory into long-term knowledge. You can conduct this through the Quest Module.
- Timed Modules - Timed Modules are the Modules that Learners have to complete in a fixed duration of time.
- Timed Reinforcement - In a Timed Reinforcement, a fixed amount of time is allotted to Learners to attempt the reinforcement. You can conduct this through the Assessment Module.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Managers and Reviewers > Mission:
This article explains how to review your learner’s email and task evaluation mission submission.

1. Once you receive the email notification of the learner's submission, click the Review Now button.

2. You can also log in to your learning site, click Coaching on the left navigation panel, and click Mission reviews > Pending missions section.

Alternatively, you can also start reviewing the mission assigned to you by accessing the reviewer dashboard. The reviewers' dashboard lists all the Pending mission reviews.

Note: The number next to the pending mission is the sum of the Required and Recommended reviews. Optional reviews are not counted.

Using the Priority option, you can further classify the pending reviews as Required, Recommended, and Optional. For more information on the score, required, and optional reviewers, see Optional reviewers for mission.

3. Click Review on a learner submission.

4. On the page that opens, read the Scenario and the learner's mission submission. Also, go through any attached documents the learner has included.

Note: For the missions where you are an optional Reviewer and the score you give is not counted, you will see a message under the Review tab.

5. Go through the Review guidance below each evaluation parameter, located on the review pane, to view the instructions, guidelines, or review standards provided by the admin for you to follow when you evaluate a learner’s mission submission.

6. Rate the learner's submission on the evaluation parameters. If the admin has added recommended modules to an evaluation parameter, you can click the Recommend content button to assign it to the learner. Recommended content helps learners revisit gaps and work on their areas of improvement. You can also add a comment for the learner in the field provided.

Using the Priority option, you can further classify the pending reviews as Required, Recommended, and Optional. For more information on the score, required, and optional reviewers, see Optional reviewers for mission.

3. Click Review on a learner submission.

4. On the page that opens, read the Scenario and the learner's mission submission. Also, go through any attached documents the learner has included.

Note: For the missions where you are an optional Reviewer and the score you give is not counted, you will see a message under the Review tab.

5. Go through the Review guidance below each evaluation parameter, located on the review pane, to view the instructions, guidelines, or review standards provided by the admin for you to follow when you evaluate a learner’s mission submission.

6. Rate the learner's submission on the evaluation parameters. If the admin has added recommended modules to an evaluation parameter, you can click the Recommend content button to assign it to the learner. Recommended content helps learners revisit gaps and work on their areas of improvement. You can also add a comment for the learner in the field provided.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Managers and Reviewers > Mission > Transfer review:
If, for any reason, you cannot review the mission, you can transfer the review to a new reviewer.

1. Click Unable to review submission? option.

2. From the Unable to review? pop-up, select Transfer review.

3. On the drop-down list under Transfer it to, select the new reviewer.

4. Click Transfer review.

A pop-up message is displayed stating that the review is transferred. The new reviewer also receives an email about the change.

Note: You cannot transfer the review to the existing reviewer of the mission. The system displays a message as Already reviewer.

Once you transfer the review, you will then no longer be able to access the review.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Integrations > Single Sign-On (SSO) > Steps to be performed in Microsoft Entra ID:
1. Sign in to the Microsoft Entra admin center using your credentials.

2. On the left navigation panel, click Enterprise apps and select + New application on the displayed page.

3. In the Browse Microsoft Entra Gallery screen, enter Mindtickle in the search bar and select it from the displayed results.

4. On the displayed pop-up, click Create.

Note: Adding the Mindtickle application may take a few minutes.

5. On the Mindtickle | Overview page, click 2. Set up single sign on.

6. On the Single sign-on screen, click SAML.

7. Click the edit icon in the Basic SAML Configuration section.

The Basic SAML Configuration screen is displayed.

8. In the Identifier (Entity ID) field, enter the Entity Id copied in step 3 of the Download Metadata from Mindtickle section.

9. In the Reply URL (Assertion Consumer Service URL) field, enter the ACS URL Location copied in step 3 of the Download Metadata from Mindtickle section.

10. In the Sign on URL field, enter your company's sign-on URL. For example, https://<companyname>.mindtickle.com/login/auth/saml/saml.

11. Click Save and then click the close icon.

12. On the Mindtickle | SAML-based Sign-on screen and click the edit icon in the Attributes & Claims section.

13. On the Attributes & Claims screen, click User Identifier (name ID).

The Manage claim screen is displayed.

14. In the Name identifier format drop-down, select Email address.

15. In the Source attribute drop-down, select user.mail.

16. Click Save.

Note: Ensure the User unique identifier field is set to user.mail before you proceed.

14. Under the SAML Signing Certificate section, download the Federation Metadata XML. The XML file will be downloaded to your local machine. It will be used further on the Mindtickle platform.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Coaching Sessions:
Learners can schedule a coaching session with a reviewer provided it has not been scheduled by a reviewer already. This article explains how to schedule a coaching session.

1. Log in to your learning site to view the coaching sessions assigned to you.

2. Click the coaching session you wish to schedule with a reviewer.

3. Click Schedule new session.Note: If there are no reviewers appointed for the coaching session, you will not be able to schedule it.

4. On the Schedule new session pop-up screen, click the name of the reviewer you want to schedule the session with and then click Next.

Note: You can have up to five reviewers appointed to you. However, you can only schedule a session with one Reviewer at a time. You can schedule another session only after the current session has concluded.

You can also schedule and reschedule a session with the reviewer from the learner's dashboard. For more information, see Coaching rooms (learner dashboard) for coaching sessions.

5. Select the Next session date, Next session time, and time zone as appropriate.

6. Enter an Agenda (optional) for the Session in the field provided.

7. Click Schedule.

Note:

- To conduct a day-long session, click the All day checkbox.
- Timezone: You can easily browse through the comprehensive list or search for specific locations (by city, country, or timezone name), making it effortless to find and select the desired timezone.
- To get a notification 30 minutes before the session starts, click the Notify me 30 minutes before the session checkbox.

The system displays a message when the session is scheduled.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Quests:
A Challenge is a set of Questions that are delivered to you as part of a Quest that you are invited to. A Quest is a Module that contains Questions developed on a given topic or concept. A few Questions are selected periodically and delivered to you in the form of Challenges.

This article explains the steps you can follow to take a Challenge on the web interface of your MindTickle Learning Site. Learn how to take a Challenge using the mobile app.

If you are invited to a Quest, you will receive an email notification to take a Challenge. Click Get Started. Alternatively, you can log in to your Learning Site and view the Quest.

You will be directed to the Challenge on your Learning Site. An overview of the Challenge is displayed (number of Questions, Estimated Time it will take, Maximum Points you can earn, and the Achievements you can aim for). Click Start Challenge.

Note: Quests are available in all the languages supported on the MindTickle platform. See Language Support in MindTickle and Which languages does the MindTickle Mobile App support? for more information.

Read the Question, go through the supporting files (video, document, or image) if any, and choose the appropriate option(s) on the right.

As soon as you answer a Question, you will be able to see if the options you chose are correct or incorrect. The correct options are displayed in green and the incorrect ones are in red.

Tip: When attempting a quest challenge, click the series name on the top left corner of the screen to navigate to the series Modules page and view other modules.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Course and quick update > Guidelines for creating Factopedia:
Factopedia can be enabled by toggling the switch for both learning content and questions from within a course and a quick update, on the admin site.

Note: Factopedia is available to learners while going through the learning content. However, for Questions and Feedback, Factopedia is made available only after learners have submitted their responses.

There are 3 ways in which content can be shared using Factopedia:

Text: Enter the text and format it (if needed) with the toolbar provided. You can even embed a link or a URL within the text.

Multimedia: You can upload and embed images, videos, presentations, and PDFs within Factopedia. Learners can view them within the module. These cannot be downloaded.

Handouts: Upload documents, images, presentations, short videos, and PDFs that learners can download.

Learn more about Module Support on Web and Mobile devices.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Course and quick update > Best practices:
Following are some best practices on how to make the best use of Factopedia:

- Share relevant information with your learners.
- Share information that will motivate or engage your learners to learn more.
- Keep the information you share short and crisp. Note: Factopedia is to share additional information.
- Provide a suitable name for the Handouts you plan to upload in Factopedia. Note: Handouts should be easy to identify and access since they can be downloaded.
- Avoid adding long lists in the Factopedia section.
- If you edit or modify the learning content or question, don’t forget to review the Factopedia to make sure it matches the updated content.

Embedding links

Embed the right links and URLs in the Factopedia and test them, by previewing the module, before you publish it.

To embed a link:

1. In the Factopedia section, click the link icon.
2. In the Insert Link dialog box, enter the required text in the Text to display field.
3. Enter the website URL in the Web Address field and click Ok.

Saving changes

All Factopedia additions and changes for a draft/unpublished learning object are saved automatically. However, if you add new or update existing Factopedia content for a published learning object, you must save the changes manually using the Save button at the bottom of the Factopedia section. You may need to scroll down to see the Save button.

Note: Changes to Factopedia do NOT trigger a module update or impact learners’ progress on the module. The changes are directly pushed to all the learners who are invited to the module. To learn more, see this article.

The Score of a Challenge is calculated based on

- Your response (correct/incorrect) to a Question
- Bonus points earned for every saved attempt

A saved attempt is an attempt that you did not take. For example, the maximum number of times a Question can be asked is set to 3. If you respond correctly in the first two attempts, you will save the third attempt and get bonus points for this saved attempt.

Scores are awarded for every attempt to a Question. If in a particular attempt, a Question is answered correctly, you will score 100 points. Zero points are scored for an incorrect answer. You will also Score a bonus of 100 points if you save an attempt.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Quests > Streak Badge:
A Streak Badge will be awarded to you upon completing a Challenge within 24 hours from the time it was delivered, regardless of whether the response is right or wrong.

Note: Challenges are not delivered on weekends. However, if a Challenge is delivered on a Friday, you have to respond within 24 hours in order to earn a Streak Badge.

Each level of the Streak is unlocked based on the following criteria.

- Level 1 when you complete the Challenge within 24 hours from its delivery
- Level 2 when you complete 3 consecutive Challenges, within 24 hours from the time each of them was delivered
- Level 3 when you complete 5 consecutive Challenges, within 24 hours from the time each of them was delivered

There is no upper limit to the levels in the Streak Badge. You can unlock more levels when you complete two more consecutive challenges. Once a Streak is broken, the level is reset. If you fail to complete a Challenge within 24 hours from its delivery, then the Streak will reset to zero.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Integrations > User Sync > Setting rules and filters:
When Users get imported into Mindtickle, they must be authorized on the Mindtickle platform before they are considered successfully imported. Rules are triggered by Mindtickle to create, update, and remove Users. These Rules can be based on the Profile Fields or a set of Profile Fields of the Users. For example, all Users with status as ‘active’ should be added to Mindtickle and those with status as ‘inactive’ or ‘terminated’ should be removed from Mindtickle.

We also allow customers to filter the Users using allowlist/blocklist concepts for the following attributes:

- Domain - email domains only
- Specific emails
- Profile fields or set of Profile Fields

Allowlisted Users get added to Mindtickle platform only after the Rule is applied. Contact your Customer Success Manager to enable these Rules and/or filters.

You can also enable Rules in Profile Management to add Users to Group(s) in Mindtickle. These Group(s) can then be linked to Series. You can also remove Users from a Group by selecting the Remove Users from the Group when they do not match the Rule checkbox in the Advanced Options of the Rule.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Analytics & Reporting > Reference > By creating a custom group containing all learners:
1. Create a new group from the Groups page and add all learners (users) to it.
2. In the admin site sidebar, click Analytics > Users and roles > Groups to open the group reports listing page. This page displays all group reports. Note: It may take approximately 15 minutes for the group to appear in the list.
3. The Team members tab will open by default. Navigate to the Heatmap tab.
4. Ensure that Learner vs. module is selected as the default view.
5. Use the Modules assigned during filter to select the appropriate time frame for viewing completion data.
6. Set Completed % as the performance metric.
7. To export the report, click the Export icon, enter your email address, and click Submit . A detailed report will be sent to your inbox.
8. You can also bookmark the report for future reference by clicking Bookmark .
