chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Setup > Site Setup:
Module relevance allows the admin to mark a module as required or optional for a learner or group. This article provides an overview of the module relevance feature.

- Set or change module relevance
- Module relevance in analytics
- Module relevance on the learning site
- Specifications and limitations

Using the Module relevance feature, the admin can define a module's relevance for a learner or group by marking it as Required or Optional. Module relevance is useful when you want to distinguish for learners which modules are important and of priority, and which may be optional.

Note: Module relevance is available only for course, quick update, assessment, ILT, checklist, and mission modules. Module relevance is not available for quests (Spaced Reinforcement) in this release. It will never be an option for coaching sessions because this module is not intended for learners.

The module relevance can be one of the following:

- Required: The module is mandatory for the learner and must be completed.
- Optional: The module is optional for the learner and does not need to be completed.
- Unmarked: No module relevance is set. The module is neither mandatory nor optional. It is simply assigned to the learner with the expectation that they will complete the module as part of their regular training.

Note: You can go to the module’s Invite and track tab and change the module's relevance for invited learners or linked learner groups.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Setup > Site Setup > Set or change module relevance:
On the admin site, you can set the module relevance as follows:

- While inviting to a module: Set module relevance when inviting learners individually (existing or newly added), by group, or by uploading a CSV list. To learn more, see Invite learners and groups to a module .
- From module settings: Set the default module relevance for a module. Any learner or group invited to the module will have the default module relevance selected. When an automated invitation is sent via an automation rule, the default module relevance will be set.

To learn more, see Create, manage, and publish content. For example, to learn how to configure module relevance, see Settings tab > Mission.

On the admin site, you can change the module relevance as follows:

- From the module’s Invite and track tab : You can view and change the current module relevance for listed learners and linked learner groups. Change module relevance for individual learners from View by learners . For linked learner groups, change module relevance from View by groups .
- For example, if the default module relevance for a Mission is set as Required and you mark the relevance for any two learners from the Invite and track tab as Optional, then the Mission appears as Optional for those two learners.

You can also filter learners based on module relevance.

Changes to module relevance for a linked group apply only to new members who are automatically invited to the module after the change. Existing learners in the group retain their current module relevance.

For information on managing linked groups from a module, see Invite learners and groups to a module.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Setup > Site Setup > Module relevance on the learning site:
On the learning site, learners can view and filter module relevance in the Recent tab and within a series. Module relevance is indicated using the REQ (for Required) and OPT (for Optional) labels on the module thumbnails. No label is shown for Unmarked modules.

To learn more, see Learning site overview.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Setup > Site Setup > Specifications and limitations:
The following are the specifications and limitations for module relevance:

- Sequential locking: Enabling sequential locking for a series and making a module optional in the series will result in a conflict. This is because learners must complete optional modules to unlock the next module. It is recommended not to use both sequential locking and module relevance for a series.
- Due date: If a due date is set for a module, learners will see it even if the module is optional for them.
- Reminder emails and notifications: Reminder emails and notifications are sent to learners even if the module is optional for them. To disable email notifications for modules marked as optional for learners, see Email invitations, reminders, and notifications for series and modules .
- Public series: Module relevance is not visible in a public series. However, when learners are invited to or self-invite themselves to a public series, they see the relevance of published modules when they reload the series. Note: You can allow learners to view module relevance for the Public series without subscribing to it. To enable it for your learning site, contact Mindtickle Support .

Learners are invited to a public series if:

- An admin invites them.
- They subscribe to the series.
- They self-enroll in all modules in the series.

For all existing modules in the series, the module relevance is not visible before the user subscribes to the series. In this case, the admin can change/set the module relevance from the module’s Invite and track tab.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > FAQs:
This article explains how admins can download the learners’ mission video submissions.

Admins can download voice-over slideshow, video roleplay, and screen capture mission types on their local machine.

Note: For the screen capture mission, only the screen share video can be downloaded. The learner's inset video cannot be downloaded.

1. On the admin site homepage, click Training > Series.

2. On the Series page, click the series with the mission module.

3. Click the mission module to open.

2. Go to the Invite and track tab, click the learner’s name to download the mission video.

3. On the submission page, right-click on the learner’s video submission and click Save Video as…

4. On the displayed pop-up, select a location in your local drive.

5. In the Save As field, enter a name for the video, then click Save.

The system saves the mission video submission to your local drive.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Get Started with Mindtickle > Introduction > A - H:
Account settings: Feature that enables administrators to manage settings for their Admin Site, Learning Site, and Learners. See help.

Adherence: Metric that indicates whether a Reviewer has reviewed the number of Sessions in a given duration. See help.

Admin/ Enablement Admin: Role assigned to a person responsible for driving enablement initiatives and programs. See help.

Admin Homepage: Page that Users having administrative rights access when they sign into their Admin Site. See help.

Admin Site: Interface that Users designated as Administrators or Admins access to manage settings, create content, add/ delete users, create groups, and view analytics and reports in Mindtickle.

Analytics: Interface that displays engagement and performance data of users, content and enablement initiatives. See help.

Announcement: Feature that allows Admins to send broadcast information to Learners through Mindtickle. See help.

Archive: Folder on Admin Homepage containing archived Modules. See help.

Assessment: Type of a Module that helps assess & certify User's knowledge in a timed duration. See help.

Assigned Series: Series that Learners cannot access voluntarily and needs to be assigned to them.

Automation Link: Ability to link Modules and Series to Groups of Users.

Badges: Rewards earned by Users when certain number of points are achieved.

Bookmark Reports: Ability to save reports for self, Admins, and Managers. See help.

Bulk-invite: Ability to add, invite multiple Users together to a Series or Module.

Call AI: Mindtickle capability that records, transcribes conversations in online meetings and provides actionable insights.

Challenge: Set of Questions in a Quest delivered to Users at intelligently spaced intervals. See help.

Checklist: Type of Module that contains tasks that need to be completed by Learners on-the-job or offline. See help.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Get Started with Mindtickle > Introduction > I - Q:
Max Score: Maximum score that a Learner can earn for an assigned Module.

Mission: Type of Module that provides virtual environment to Users to practice work scenarios and submit the best ones for review and feedback. See help.

Module: Components within a Series that are used to achieve the purpose of a learning or enablement initiative. See help.

Module Relevance: Ability that allows Admins to define whether a Module should be marked as required or optional for a Learner. See help.

Module Score: Total number of points a Learner earns in a Module based on its completion. See help.

Module ID: An auto-generated unique identifier assigned to a module upon creation through various workflows. It can be found in the module URL on both admin and learner sites.

Notification Center: List of all notifications for Learners on invitations, updates, and reminders. See help.

Notifications: Invitations, updates, and reminders pushed to users on mobile app, slack and web. See help.

Overdue: Status of a Module after its due date has passed for the Learner.

Page: A group of Topics in a Course forms a page. The Learner must complete page(s) in order to complete the Course.

Peers: Co-workers of a Learner using the platform.

Pinned Series: Feature that allows a Series to be pinned to the top for quick access to Learners.

Poll: A type of survey that can be added to a Course of Quick-Update.

Private notes: Personal notes that a Reviewer can add while reviewing a Coaching Session.

Profile Fields: Fields that store details/ attributes regarding Users accessing the platform.

Module ID: An auto-generated unique identifier assigned to a module upon creation through various workflows. It can be found in the module URL on both admin and learner sites.

Notification Center: List of all notifications for Learners on invitations, updates, and reminders. See help.

Notifications: Invitations, updates, and reminders pushed to users on mobile app, slack and web. See help.

Overdue: Status of a Module after its due date has passed for the Learner.

Page: A group of Topics in a Course forms a page. The Learner must complete page(s) in order to complete the Course.

Peers: Co-workers of a Learner using the platform.

Pinned Series: Feature that allows a Series to be pinned to the top for quick access to Learners.

Poll: A type of survey that can be added to a Course of Quick-Update.

Private notes: Personal notes that a Reviewer can add while reviewing a Coaching Session.

Profile Fields: Fields that store details/ attributes regarding Users accessing the platform.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Quest:
Quests in Mindtickle improve knowledge retention using an intelligent and adaptive system. Short, personalized, and gamified challenges are delivered to learners automatically at spaced intervals, helping them bridge knowledge gaps.

There are four communications that can be sent to learners in the form of emails. No other emails are sent from the platform for quests.

1. Invitation to a quest: Notifies learners that they have been invited to a quest.
2. Reminder to start the quest: Sends a clubbed reminder to learners to begin all the quests assigned to them. This is similar to any other clubbed series reminder in Mindtickle.
3. Invitation to a challenge: Notifies learners that they have been invited to a challenge in the quest.
4. Reminder to start the challenge: Reminds learners to begin the challenge.

Email communication can be enabled/disabled by the Admins while creating the quest.

Mindtickle provides default email templates for all the above scenarios, which the admin can access from Account settings > Email templates. Contact Mindtickle support to customize the email templates based on your requirements.

The snapshots below represent the email communication that learners receive for each scenario:
chunks.body:
Quests in Mindtickle improve knowledge retention using an intelligent and adaptive system. Short, personalized, and gamified challenges are delivered to learners automatically at spaced intervals, helping them bridge knowledge gaps.

There are four communications that can be sent to learners in the form of emails. No other emails are sent from the platform for quests.

1. Invitation to a quest: Notifies learners that they have been invited to a quest.
2. Reminder to start the quest: Sends a clubbed reminder to learners to begin all the quests assigned to them. This is similar to any other clubbed series reminder in Mindtickle.
3. Invitation to a challenge: Notifies learners that they have been invited to a challenge in the quest.
4. Reminder to start the challenge: Reminds learners to begin the challenge.

Email communication can be enabled/disabled by the Admins while creating the quest.

Mindtickle provides default email templates for all the above scenarios, which the admin can access from Account settings > Email templates. Contact Mindtickle support to customize the email templates based on your requirements.

The snapshots below represent the email communication that learners receive for each scenario:

<aura:component implements="force:appHostable" ><aura:handler name="init" value="{!this}" action="{!c.doInit}"/></aura:component>

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Custom reports (old):
Important: On April 21 2026, we migrated custom reports to the new advanced reports. For details on the migration, see this article. For advanced reports, see the articles in this folder.

Custom reports are personalized reports that display performance and engagement data of learners for predefined metrics.

Each custom report template includes one or more default or primary columns. These columns define the structure of the report and cannot be removed. Based on the template, a report may have one or two primary columns.

Choose the appropriate template based on which attribute you want to appear as the primary column in the report table. For example, if you want to show average scores of learners for a series:

- Select the Learner report template to have Learner name as the primary column.
- Select the Series learner report template to have both Series name and Learner name as the primary columns.

Before selecting a template, hover over it and click the Preview button to see its layout.

To view more detailed data in the report, you can select additional columns from the list of available columns when customizing the report table.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Setup > Account Settings:
Email templates for notifications and reminders can be customized to suit the requirements of your organization. You can include User attributes, Series, and Module attributes in your email using shortkeys. This article lists the shortkeys that are available in email templates for Series and Module type.

- Series
- Course
- Quick update
- Assessment
- Checklist
- Instructor-led training (ILT)g ()
- Mission
- Coaching sessions
- Asset Hub

Note:

- The Quest Module type does not provide shortkeys for its email templates. Learn more about Email and Notifications in Quest .
- To configure the email template such that the manager’s email address is added to the CC field, use the shortkey $manager.a_x$ . When using this shortkey, ensure you replace x with the corresponding numerical value in the shortkey. For example, if the profile field is Manager Email and the corresponding profile shortkey is a_0 , add the shortkey as “$manager.a_0$” in the email template.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Best Practices and Use Cases > Platform Use Cases | Events > Outline for a Successful SKO:
Pre-work

- Use Mindtickle to deploy Virtual SKO pre-work over in digestible chunks.

- Launch pre-work 1-2 weeks before the virtual live event.

- Use Missions for pre-event territory planning, allowing managers to provide actionable feedback.

- Share actionable agenda and pre-event checklists.

During the SKO

- Use MindTickle to keep reps engaged with gamified post-keynote quizzes and polls.

- Easily communicate the agenda and updates during the event with Quick Updates.

- Use ILTs (Instructor Led Trainings) to track attendance.

Post-work

- Identify and bridge gaps on an automated, intelligent cadence with Quests for spaced reinforcement.

- Drive post-event engagement & behavior with Missions and scenario-based content.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Best Practices and Use Cases > Platform Use Cases | Events > Creating Content:
Strategic pre and post-meeting content is essential for a successful SKO. All content should align with the strategic initiatives of the organization and impact the metrics that frontline and senior management are focused on.

Step 1: Focus on critical topics covered at the SKO that align with the strategic initiatives of the organization.

Step 2: Identify the corresponding competencies - the knowledge, skills, processes, and tools that salespeople really need to impact the success of a strategic initiative.

Step 3: Identify the corresponding behaviors or capabilities needed to perform their role successfully. A capability answers the question, “I can do ______”, or “The salesperson must be able to do _____”.

Step 4: Identify the enablement approach you will use to help the salesperson achieve mastery. For example, the enablement content/activities to teach, show, practice, or reinforce.

Step 5: Develop targeted content for each capability. Include scenario-based content that depicts real-world scenarios whenever possible.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Best Practices and Use Cases > Platform Use Cases | Internal Engagement > Program Approach:
- Publish a 3 to 5-minute video of a senior leader talking to the sales organization.
  - Focus the presenters on strategic topics.
  - Provide guidelines and/or an outline for consistency if different presenters are used each month.
  - If presenters will vary, consider including the CEO, VP Sales, CMO, Chief Customer Officer, CFO, or CTO.
- Publish these at a regular cadence so that people expect them.
  - Monthly is recommended.
- Include either a multiple-choice poll or a text-feedback poll to solicit feedback on the session quality or input on the next presenter.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Best Practices and Use Cases > Platform Use Cases | Internal Engagement > Tips & Suggestions:
- Setting up a public series will ensure that little effort for the Mindtickle Admin - just publish a new QU and you are done.
- The executive can record the video either in Mindtickle or with external recording software such as Quicktime or Zoom.
- Send users a one-time email notification to ensure they’re made aware of the podcast. To do this, turn on email notifications for the Series invitation before inviting your users.
- Make podcasts more searchable by tagging each QU with tags that describe the presenter and topic.
- Use points and badges to help drive engagement with your podcast!

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Best Practices and Use Cases > Platform Use Cases | Internal Engagement > Messaging & Communication:
As with any program, positioning and effective communication will have a significant impact on your podcast’s engagement. Always get buy-in from senior leadership and identify an executive sponsor who can help with communications.

Pre-launch messaging should focus on awareness, engagement, and setting expectations.

- Senior Leadership
  - Describe the alignment, expected impact on field performance, and data insights.
  - Reinforce the importance of top-down commitment and communication.
- Frontline Managers
  - Describe the alignment, expected impact on field performance, and data insights.
  - Set expectations for coaching and program participation.
  - Train on the manager dashboard.
- Salespeople
  - Describe how your program will help them to succeed in the field.
    - Podcasts will drive reinforcement and alignment to help clarify company direction and positioning.
  - Describe the experience
    - The experience should be quick (ideally just 4 to 6 minutes per month) and convenient with Mindtickle’s mobile app.
  - Set expectations for program participation.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Setup > Site Setup:
The Mindtickle admin site is the interface for the administrator users (admins) in your organization. You will be given initial access to the admin site by your Mindtickle Customer Success Manager (CSM). If you are added to the Mindtickle admin site for the first time as a site owner, enablement admin, IT admin, content expert, or group manager, follow these steps to sign up:

1. Access your inbox, check for an email notification inviting you to sign up, and click Accept Invitation . For more information about the admin role and permissions assigned to it, see Roles and Permissions .
2. On the Sign Up page, enter the appropriate values in the respective fields and click Sign Up . Note :
  - Your registered email address is your username.
  - The Password field must contain at least one uppercase alphabet, one lowercase alphabet, and one number.
  - All the fields are mandatory. Once you sign up, an activation link is sent to your inbox and the following message is displayed on the screen.
3. Access your inbox, check for an activation email and click Activate Now . Note : If you do not find the activation email in your inbox, check your Spam or Junk folders.

You are directed to the Admin Site Homepage of your organization.

For more information about how to access the admin site any time after you have signed up, see Sign In to Mindtickle.

For more information about signing in to the admin site using SSO, see Access the Admin Site Using Single Sign-On (SSO).

For more information about the devices and browsers supported, see Supported Browsers and Devices.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > FAQs:
Admins can recommend one Module per Evaluation Parameter while creating Coaching Sessions and Missions. The Recommended Module has to be a published Module on the platform.

Recommended Modules enable Learners to refresh their knowledge and/or work on their areas of improvement. While Admins can suggest a Module for the Evaluation Parameter, it is the responsibility of the Reviewers to assign the Module to a Learner at the time of review if needed. The Reviewer can also add a comment explaining the purpose of assigning the Module to Learners. Learners can see the comment in their Coaching form and reviewed Mission.

The Learner receives an invitation by email for the Recommended Module only after the Reviewer has submitted the Review.

The Learners will also be able to see the Recommended Module under their Assigned Series on their Learning Site.

Note: Currently, the Admins and Reviewers can attach a recommended module that is archived. However, the Learners cannot access the content.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Mission:
The AI Assistance step in the Build tab of the Mission creation workflow allows the Admin to provide a benchmark for Learners. The instant AI-based feedback helps Learners easily identify gaps in keywords to use, words to avoid, speech pace, submission length, and filler word usage. Appointed Reviewers can also see these insights before providing their feedback.

This step is visible on the Build tab of the Screen Capture, Voice-Over Slideshow, and Video Roleplay Mission types. AI Assistance is not applicable to the Email & Task Evaluation Mission type.

Note: These settings cannot be edited once the Mission is published.

The AI Assistance tab has three sections: Content, Articulation, and Text Sentiment. This article further explains each section in detail.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Mission > Content > Keywords to include > Upload a Model Pitch to autofill keywords:
A Model Pitch ensures consistent messaging across your organization and may be created by leadership or product management. Click the Upload Model Pitch button to upload an audio or video file. To enter a Model Pitch in text format, click Enter Model Pitch as text.

Once you add the Model Pitch of your choice, the AI Assistance feature automatically transcribes it, extracts the keywords, and displays the number of keywords generated. Entities such as names of people, organizations, locations, verbs, adjectives are extracted as keywords to use. If you are uploading a Model Pitch in a video or audio format, the recording should be in American English.

Note: If recorded in any language other than English the insights generated will be incorrect and incoherent. However, if you still prefer to use another language, you can follow one of the options listed below:

- Enter keywords manually in the language of your choice.
- Upload the Model Pitch in text format (not video or audio). AI Assistance will fetch the right keywords automatically.

Your users can choose the appropriate language and accent in Mission settings before they start recording their submission. The system will auto-transcribe the recording in the set language and match the keywords set by you.

It also displays the minimum number of keywords the Learners should use (Minimum number of keywords to use) in their pitch. By default, this value is set to 80% of the total keywords generated. However, you can set a number as required.

Click Manage Keywords and Model Pitch to add or remove keywords from the list manually. You can also delete or replace the Model pitch by clicking the appropriate icons. Click Save Changes.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Mission > Articulation > Submission Length:
Submission Length indicates how closely the Learner meets the expected Target time.

Note: Target time is the set minimum time for the length of the Learner’s submission.

This section displays the submission length, the target time, and states if the length is too short, short, appropriate, long, or too long.

| Insight | Criteria |
| --- | --- |
| Too Short | The length of the submission is less than 25% of the Target time. |
| Short | The length of the submission is more than 25% but less than 80% of the Target time. |
| Appropriate | The length of the submission is more than 90% and less than 110% of the Target time. |
| Long | The length of the submission is more than 110% but less than 150% of the Target time. |
| Too Long | The length of the submission is more than 150% of the Target time. |

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Mission > Articulation > Speech Pace:
Speech Pace shows how the Learner's delivery of words compares with the Average Speaking Rate of 120-160 WPM.

The Speech Pace insight helps you understand if the pace at which the Learner delivered the submission is slow, appropriate, or fast. It displays the average number of words per minute the Learner spoke. It also displays the Average Speaking Rate for comparison.

| Insight | Criteria |
| --- | --- |
| Too Slow | If the pace of pitch is less than 100 WPM. |
| Slow | If the pace of pitch is between 100 to 120 WPM. |
| Appropriate | If the pace of pitch is between 120 to 160 WPM. |
| Fast | If the pace of pitch is between 160 to 200 WPM. |
| Too Fast | If the pace of the pitch is more than 200 WPM. |

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Mission > Articulation > Filler Words:
The Filler Words insight highlights commonly used fillers in conversation to help Learners avoid them in their submission attempts or presentation. For example, if a Learner has repeatedly used the word ‘basically’, in their submission, the Filler Words' insight will list the word ‘basically’ as a filler word along with the number of times the word has been repeated in the submission.

| Insight | Criteria |
| --- | --- |
| Too many filler words used | More than 10 filler WPM. |
| Many filler words used | Between 5-10 filler WPM. |
| Fewer filler words used | Less than 5 filler WPM. |

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Communications > Notifications and Reminders:
There are three communications sent to learners in the form of emails and notifications at different stages of a series.

1. Invitation to a series - Notifies learners that they have been invited to a series.
2. Reminder to start the series - Sends a clubbed reminder to learners about modules within the series based on the individual module reminder settings.
3. Invitation to multiple modules in a series - Invites learners to multiple modules in a series.

Admins can control the communications from the Notifications tab in series settings. Notifications are sent via the mobile app, web, and Slack (if integrated) to learners.

Note:

- Learners receive the notification digest email at a scheduled period based on the defined notification digest frequency. For more information, see Notification Digest.
- Admins can also choose not to send notifications for modules that are marked as Optional or Unmarked for a learner. If applied, this setting is applicable to modules and series across the learning site. For more information, see Disable email notifications for Optional or Unmarked modules.

Mindtickle provides default email templates for all the above scenarios that can be accessed by the admin from Account > Email Templates. All three templates can be customized to suit the requirements of your organization. Learn more about shortkeys used in the series templates.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Analytics & Reporting > Reference > On track and off track:
A Learner who adheres to the Challenge delivery schedule is counted as On Track and one who does not is counted as Off Track.

Let’s go through an example. A Challenge is delivered to three Learners - Alex, Suzy, and John - on 1st Feb. The interval between Challenges is set to 3 days, so the next Challenge is scheduled to be delivered on 4th Feb

Alex adheres to the schedule and takes the first Challenge on 1st Feb and the next one on 4th Feb. Alex is counted as “On Track” throughout the duration.

Suzy does not take the first Challenge on 1st Feb but takes it on the 3rd Feb. The day Suzy took the first Challenge falls in the 3-day period set as the interval between Challenges. As on 3rd Feb, she is counted as “On Track”. She takes the next Challenge on the 8th Feb, which is beyond the 3-day interval. To anyone viewing analytics on 8th Feb, she will be counted as “Off Track”.

John takes the first Challenge on 5th Feb. On this day, he is counted as “Off Track”. But he takes the next challenge within the 3-day interval, say on 6th Feb. So he is again counted as “On Track”, at that time.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Analytics & Reporting > Reference > Improvement:
A Learner’s current performance on a Question compared to the answer in her first attempt is termed as an Improvement.

For example, if a Learner has answered a question correctly the first time and gives an incorrect answer in the next attempt, the improvement is -100%. However, if the Learner answers the third attempt incorrectly again, then the improvement is still calculated as -100% as the first answer is the benchmark.

Similarly, if the Learner had answered the Question correctly in the third attempt, then the improvement would be 0% since she had answered correctly in the first attempt as well.

This data is then aggregated across Learners, segments, or groups of Learners and Tags.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Course and quick update:
The Content Collaboration capability in the Create Voiceover Slideshow option in Course and Quick-Update allows Admins to collaborate with multiple users and crowdsource content from multiple sources.

With this capability, the Admin can assign content creation tasks to one or more users on the platform, who may be the Subject Matter Experts (SMEs). The SME can be anyone with deep knowledge on the subject for which content needs to be created for the slideshow: product managers, customer success managers, sales reps, etc. The SMEs can create all content while the Admin facilitates and curates the content creation and publishes the final content. The collaborative nature of this capability makes it easier to manage large, complex programs where multiple Admins work on a single Module.

Using Create Voiceover Slideshow in Course and Quick-Update, you can upload a slideshow, record on each slide, and then convert and save it as a video. With Content Collaboration in Create Voiceover Slideshow, the Admin can either upload the slides and record the voiceovers themselves or assign these tasks to one or more users (assignees). The Admin can assign the task of uploading the slides and recording the voiceovers or only recording the voiceovers to any Learner in MindTickle. The Admin can select the assignees, manage their tasks, and can also configure the due date and emails so that the assignees are reminded to complete the tasks on time. chunks.body:
The Content Collaboration capability in the Create Voiceover Slideshow option in Course and Quick-Update allows Admins to collaborate with multiple users and crowdsource content from multiple sources.

With this capability, the Admin can assign content creation tasks to one or more users on the platform, who may be the Subject Matter Experts (SMEs). The SME can be anyone with deep knowledge on the subject for which content needs to be created for the slideshow: product managers, customer success managers, sales reps, etc. The SMEs can create all content while the Admin facilitates and curates the content creation and publishes the final content. The collaborative nature of this capability makes it easier to manage large, complex programs where multiple Admins work on a single Module.

Using Create Voiceover Slideshow in Course and Quick-Update, you can upload a slideshow, record on each slide, and then convert and save it as a video. With Content Collaboration in Create Voiceover Slideshow, the Admin can either upload the slides and record the voiceovers themselves or assign these tasks to one or more users (assignees). The Admin can assign the task of uploading the slides and recording the voiceovers or only recording the voiceovers to any Learner in MindTickle. The Admin can select the assignees, manage their tasks, and can also configure the due date and emails so that the assignees are reminded to complete the tasks on time. The assignees can view and complete the assigned tasks from the Tasks pane located in the navigation panel of the Learning Site.

For information about best practices for Voiceover Slideshow, see Drafting Narration for Voiceover Slideshow on Mindtickle.

Note: When you copy a Module with the Voiceover Slideshow learning content, you cannot edit the Voiceover Slideshow video in the copied version of Module. Similarly, you cannot edit the video when you restore this Module after you had archived it. For example, you have a Course Module “Product 101” with the Voiceover Slideshow learning content. In the Voiceover Slideshow, you created content through content collaboration and saved it as a video. When you copy Module “Product 101”, you cannot edit the video in the copied version. Similarly, if you archive the Module “Product 101”, then you cannot edit the video when you restore the Module.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Course and quick update > Upload Slides > Slideshow Operations:
You can perform the following operations on your uploaded slides:

- Add more slides: Click Add Slides in the upper-left corner to add more slides to your slideshow.
- Download slideshows: Click the (Download Slides) button to download any of the slideshows you or your fellow collaborator admins have uploaded through Voiceover Slideshow.The Download Slides dialog box lists the uploaded slideshows. These are the slideshows from which you have selected slides to create the slideshow in your Voiceover Slideshow learning content. Click the Download button for a slideshow to download it in its original, uploaded format (.ppt, .pptx, or .pdf).This feature is helpful when you want to edit any of your slides before converting the finalized slideshow into a video. You can download the slideshow that has the slides you want to edit, edit the information in the slides, and upload the slideshow again. Then, you can replace the existing slides with the edited slides from the latest uploaded slideshow.Note: You can download only the originally uploaded slideshows in their entirety, but not their individual slides. If the slideshow does not contain the originally uploaded slides, you cannot download the slideshow in your Voiceover Slideshow.

- Add notes: Click the (Notes) icon to access slide notes. There are two types of slide notes:
  - Personal: To jot down your observations and ideas or create to-do items for the slide. No one else can see your personal notes. These notes are auto-saved and can be edited.
  - By Assignee: Displays notes, if any, added by the assignee. For example, if the assignee declines to record on a slide and sends you a note about it, the messages appear here.Note: You cannot see the assignee’s personal notes.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Course and quick update > Record Voiceover on a Slide > Record Voiceover Yourself:
Before you begin, ensure that your browser has access to the microphone.

Click on a slide’s thumbnail and click Record to start recording the voiceover on that slide.

The Recording Settings dialog box appears the first time you are recording voiceover. Do the following and then click Done:

- Microphone Settings: Select the microphone that will be used for recording. In the Audio bar, you can view feedback of the connected mic.
- Recording Countdown: Select the countdown you want to be shown before the recording begins. The available options are 5, 10, and 20.
- Click Remember my Settings to save the settings.

Click Start Recording to start recording your voiceover. The recording starts after the countdown. You can view the microphone feedback and the length of the recording in minutes and seconds. Click the (Settings) icon to access Recording Settings.

- Pause and resume the recording: While recording, click Pause Recording anytime to pause the recording. This is useful when you want to take a quick break or take care of any interruptions. When the recording is paused, the status is shown as “PAUSED” and the following pop-up appears:Moving away from this page when the recording is paused will discard it. Stop the recording first to save it.So when the recording is paused, performing any actions in the top bar — such as clicking Exit, Preview, and To-Do — will discard the recording. If you must perform any of those actions, stop the recording first to save it.Click Resume Recording to resume the recording when you are ready. The recording resumes after the countdown.
- Stop the recording: Once you are done, click Stop Recording. The platform uploads and processes your voiceover audio and saves it as a draft.

Note:

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Course and quick update > Record Only:
For this option, you need to upload the slides yourself and then assign one or more slides to an assignee to record voiceovers. You can assign the slides to only one assignee at a time. If you want to assign the same slide to another assignee for recording voiceover, you can do it in one of the following ways:

- Assign a slide to an assignee (Assignee A). After receiving the submission from Assignee A, assign it to someone else (Assignee B) using the Assign to record option. After receiving the submission from Assignee B, you can select one of the draft recordings and approve it.
- For the slide that you want to assign to two assignees, add a copy of the slide to the slideshow so that there are two copies of the slide. Assign one copy of the slide to Assignee A and another to Assignee B. This allows both assignees to work on the slide at the same time. After receiving both the submissions, keep the slide and the submission that you like and delete the other. Then, you can approve the submission in the retained slide.

For information on how to upload slides, see Course/Quick update voiceover slideshow: upload and record yourself (admin).

Navigate to the voiceover slideshow uploaded in your Course or Quick update module.

From the slideshow, assign the slides for voiceover recording. You can assign either a single slide or multiple slides to an assignee:

- To assign a single slide, click the slide in the thumbnail pane and then click Assign to record below the slide.
- To assign multiple slides, select one or more slides in the thumbnail pane and then click Assign slides in the quick-access toolbar that appears at the bottom.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Analytics & Reporting > Modules > Overview tab:
The Overview tab provides a summary of how learners are progressing through the selected quest.

The Learner progress graph shows learner progress in four stages — Not started, On track, Off track, and Completed — over time. Click the time range tabs to view progress over 3 months, 30 days, or since the quest was published (Max).

To the right of the graph, you'll find a snapshot of key metrics.

Three additional graphs provide further visual insights:

- Learner improvement on tags: Shows how learners are performing on each tag applied to the quest. Learn how improvement is calculated.
- Learner performance: Highlights the top five performing learners and compares their scores with the average score of all learners.
- Learner improvement: Lists the top five learners who have improved the most. Learn how improvement is calculated.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Course and quick update > Operations for Record Only > Pre-Submission Operations > Download Slideshows:
Click the (Download slides) button to download any of the slideshows uploaded through Voiceover Slideshow.

The Download slides dialog box lists slideshows uploaded by you or your fellow collaborator Admins. These are the slideshows from which you have selected slides to create the slideshow in your Voiceover Slideshow learning content. Click the Download button for a slideshow to download it in its original, uploaded format (.ppt, .pptx, or .pdf).

This feature is helpful when you want to edit any of your slides before converting the finalized slideshow into video. You can download the slideshow that has the slides you want to edit, edit the information in the slides, and upload the slideshow again. Then, you can replace the existing slides with the edited slides from the latest uploaded slideshow.

Note: You can download only the originally uploaded slideshows in entirety, but not their individual slides. Also, you cannot download the slideshow in your Voiceover Slideshow learning content that is created by selecting slides from the uploaded slideshows.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Course and quick update > Operations for Record Only > Pre-Submission Operations > Slideshow Operations:
- Slide individual operations: Click a slide’s thumbnail to perform various operations on the slide depending on the slide’s status. These options are available below the slide.RECORDING PENDING slides

- Common operations for RECORD YOURSELF: When you do either Record Yourself or Upload Audio (for any of the 4 ASSIGNED cases), you see DRAFT RECORDED when your draft is saved and see the following options:
  - Record New: Record another voiceover.
  - Drafts: Select the draft that you like to use. This option will show more than one draft when, for example, you record yourself or assign another user to record.
  - Click the (More) button for the following options:
    - Record Yourself: Record the voiceover yourself. To learn more, see Course/Quick-Update Voiceover Slideshow: Upload and Record Yourself (Admin).
    - Upload Audio: Upload an audio file to use it as the voiceover. To learn more, see Course/Quick-Update Voiceover Slideshow: Upload and Record Yourself (Admin).
    - Ask to Re-Record: Ask the assignee to record the voiceover again and re-submit.
    - Replace Slide: Replace the slide with another. If the slide has a voiceover on it, it remains intact when you replace the slide.
    - Delete Slide: Delete the slide.
- Slide bulk operations: Using the checkboxes in the thumbnail pane, select one or more slides to see the quick-access toolbar that appears at the bottom. The toolbar allows you to perform various operations in bulk on multiple slides depending on the slides’ status.
  - Replace Slides: Replace the selected slides. If the slides have voiceovers, they remain intact when you replace the slides.
  - Delete Slides: Delete the slides.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Course and quick update > Operations for Upload Slides + Record > Pre-Submission Operations > Convert to Video:
Once you receive all submissions from the assignees, the Convert to video button gets enabled.

Note: To convert the slideshow to video, all the slides must be in the DRAFT RECORDED state, that is, each slide must have a voiceover draft.

Select the appropriate draft in each slide and then click Convert to video to convert the voiceover slideshow into a video.

The platform starts converting the slideshow into video and shows the video when done. You are also notified by email when the video is ready.

When the video is available, play it to ensure there are no issues. From the lower-left corner of the video, you can download the video and view it on full screen.

Click Edit in the upper-right corner to edit the slideshow and again convert it to video after making the changes.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Course and quick update > Operations for Upload Slides + Record > Post-Submission Operations > Download Slideshows:
Click the (Download slides) button to download any of the slideshows uploaded by the assignees.

The Download slides dialog box lists slideshows uploaded by your assignees. Only those slideshows are shown from which one or more slides were used by the assignee for their submitted slideshow. Click the Download button for a slideshow to download it in its original, uploaded format (.ppt, .pptx, or .pdf).

This feature is helpful when you want to edit any of the slides in the submitted slideshows before converting the finalized slideshow into video. You can download the slideshow from an assignee that has the slides you want to edit, edit the information in the slides, and upload the slideshow again. Then, you can replace the existing slides with the edited slides from the latest uploaded slideshow. The assignee’s voiceover remains intact when you replace the slide.

Note: You can download only the originally uploaded slideshows in entirety, but not their individual slides. Also, you cannot download the slideshow in your Voiceover Slideshow learning content that is created by selecting slides from the uploaded slideshows.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Course and quick update > Operations for Upload Slides + Record > Post-Submission Operations > Slideshow Operations:
- Slide individual operations: Click a slide’s thumbnail to perform various operations on the slide depending on the slide’s status. These options are available below the slide.APPROVAL PENDING slides

APPROVED slides

For an approved slide, click the (More) button for the following options:

- Slide bulk operations: Using the checkboxes in the thumbnail pane, select one or more slides to see the quick-access toolbar that appears at the bottom. The toolbar allows you to perform various operations in bulk on multiple slides depending on the slides’ status.
  - Approve Slides: Approve the selected slides. This option is available only if all the selected slides are in the APPROVAL PENDING status.
  - Replace Slides: Replace the selected slides. If the slides have voiceovers, they remain intact when you replace the slides.
  - Delete Slides: Delete the slides.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Course and quick update:
For Create Voiceover Slideshow in Course and Quick-Update, the Admin can assign the tasks (either recording the voiceovers or uploading the slides and recording the voiceovers) to one or more other users on the platform, who may be the Subject Matter Experts (SMEs).

To learn about Content Collaboration, see Content Collaboration Overview.

This article explains how to complete the following tasks assigned by the Admin:

- Record Only: Record voiceovers on the assigned slides. You will only record voiceovers on the slides provided by the Admin.
- Upload Slides + Record: Upload slides as well as record voiceovers on them.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Course and quick update > Access Your Tasks:
You can access your Voiceover Slideshow tasks in one of the following ways: through the email you receive or by directly signing in to the Learning Site.

- Email: You will receive an email with a Voiceover Slideshow task assigned to you: either Record Only or Upload Slides + Record.Click the button in the email (Go to Slideshow for the “Record Only” task and Go to Task for the “Upload Slides + Record” task) and sign in to your Learning Site with your registered email address or SSO-enabled account.

- Learning Site: Sign in to the Learning Site and click the (Tasks) button in the navigation panel to see your assigned tasks.

Note: For a seamless recording experience, we recommend using the Google Chrome browser to perform these tasks.(Email for the “Record Only” task)

(Email for the “Upload Slides + Record” task)

On the Tasks page that opens, you will see all of your assigned Voiceover Slideshow tasks. The tasks are divided into three tabs based on the status of your tasks: Submission Pending, Approval Pending, Approved.

- Start the recording: Click Start Recording to begin recording your voiceover. The recording starts after the countdown. You can view the microphone feedback and the length of the recording in minutes and seconds.
- Pause and resume the recording: While recording, click Pause Recording anytime to pause the recording. This is useful when you want to take a quick break or take care of any interruptions. When the recording is paused, the status is shown as “PAUSED” and the following pop-up appears:Moving away from this page when the recording is paused will discard it. Stop the recording first to save it.So when the recording is paused, performing any actions in the top bar — such as clicking Your Team’s Report and profile menu options — will discard the recording. If you must perform any of those actions, stop the recording first to save it.Click Resume Recording to resume the recording when you are ready. The recording resumes after the countdown.
- Stop the recording: Once you are done, click Stop Recording. The platform uploads and processes your voiceover audio and saves it as a draft.

Note:

- While the audio is getting processed, keep the browser tab open and do not sign out of your account.
- If you have transcriptions enabled for your Learning Site, you can view the auto-generated transcript in English. The transcript is available for any subsequent voiceover created on the Mindtickle platform in a Course or a Quick-Update Module. However, Admins need to enable the transcript for any existing voiceover manually. For more information, refer to the Overview of Transcription and Closed Caption (CC) in Course and Quick-Update article. Contact Mindtickle Support to learn how to enable transcriptions for your Learning Site.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Course and quick update > Task: Record Only > Slideshow Operations:
You can perform the following operations on the slideshow for the Record Only task:

- Add slides: Click Add Slides in the upper-left corner to add more slides to your slideshow.
- Add notes: Click the (Notes) icon to access slide notes.
  - Personal: Add personal/private notes for each slide that you can refer to while recording on the slide. Think of these as your sticky notes, a place to add to-do items and ideas. No one else can see your personal notes.
  - By Admin: Shows notes from the Admin, if they added any, when they assigned the slides for re-recording to you.Note: You cannot see the Admin’s personal notes.

- Slide individual operations: Click a slide’s thumbnail to perform various operations on the slide. These options are available below the slide.

RECORDING PENDING slides

DRAFT RECORDED slides

- Slide bulk operations: Using the checkboxes in the thumbnail pane, select one or more slides to see the quick-access toolbar that appears at the bottom. The toolbar allows you to perform various operations in bulk on multiple slides.
  - Submit Drafts: Submit the selected draft voiceovers for the selected slides. This option is available only when all the selected slides are in the DRAFT RECORDED status.
  - Replace Slides: Replace the selected slides.
  - Decline Slides: Decline the task of recording voiceovers for the selected slides.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Mission:
Mission submissions can be converted into a Quick-Update and published to the Series of your choice. Creating Quick-Updates from Mission submissions is helpful when you want to:

- Capture user-generated content from Subject Matter Experts, Managers, or others.
- Share top submissions with a broader audience.
- Showcase the ‘best of the best’.

The following Mission submission types can be converted into a Quick-Update.

- Video Roleplay
- Voice over slideshow
- Screen Capture

This article explains how to create a Quick-Update from a Mission submission.

1. To get started, navigate to the Mission you want to share content from.
2. On the Mission Invite & Track page that opens, select the Learner whose submission you want to convert into a Quick-Update to be shared with other Learners.
3. Click Quick-Update .
4. Name the Quick-Update .
5. Select the Series where you want to place this Quick-Update. If you do not want to place it in an existing Series, create a new Series by clicking the Create new Series link.
6. Click Create .

To learn more about creating Quick-Update Modules, refer to the Create a Quick-Update article.

1. Enter the connect domain.mindtickle.com query to connect your Mindtickle learning site to MS teams. For example, if your learning site URL is acme.mindtickle.com, then the query will be connect acme.mindtickle.com.
2. Enter the authorize query to allow Mindtickle to send notifications to your users.
3. The user-sync query ensures all your users are synced with the Mindtickle platform. Note :
  - After you perform the first sync as instructed above, Mindtickle automatically syncs users every 24 hours.
  - Mindtickle has only read access to the user profile data. This integration syncs only emails with the users’ Teams ID to send notifications. There is no other sensitive data involved.
4. Your users will now start receiving notifications in their MS Teams instance.
5. To disable MS Teams integration for your users, enter the command disconnect domain.
6. For help, enter the command help as shown below.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Integrations > Collaboration App Notifications > Types of notifications:
Once the integration is complete, users will start receiving notifications in their MS Teams workspace. Upon clicking a notification, they are redirected to the appropriate page in Mindtickle. The type of notifications and their descriptions are listed below.

| Notification | Description |
| --- | --- |
| SERIES INVITATION | Series invitation sent to a learner |
| ENTITY INVITATION | Module invitation sent to a learner |
| ENTITY REMINDER | Module reminder sent to a learner |
| ENTITY UPDATE | Notification sent to learner when a module is updated |
| FEEDBACK REVIEWER EDIT | Notification sent to a learner when reviewer edits score or feedback of a Coaching Sessions or Missions module |
| FEEDBACK REVIEWER SUBMIT | Notification sent to a reviewer to submit feedback about a Coaching Sessions or Missions module |
| INVITATION REVIEW | Coaching Sessions or Missions review invitation sent to a reviewer |
| LEARNER RESET MISSION | Notification sent to a learner when a Mission is reset |
| LEARNER REVIEW APPROVED | Notification sent to a reviewer when a learner approves a review submitted |
| LEARNER REVIEW DISAPPROVED | Notification sent to a reviewer when a learner disapproves a review submitted |
| REMINDER CLUBBED | Reminder sent to learners for the entire Series |
| COACHING SCHEDULE | Notification sent to a reviewer about scheduling a Coaching Session |
| SESSION ENROLLMENT UPDATED | Notification sent to an enrolled learner when the ILT is updated |

Users can disable the notifications if they want by using the off command. They can turn the notifications back on using the on command.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > User Management > Users and Groups > Set the password (for “Not Signed Up” users):
1. Sign in to the admin site.
2. On the left navigation bar, click Users and select Users . The Users page is displayed.
3. On the Users page, select one or more Not signed up users for whom you want to set a password.
4. From the options at the screen's bottom, click the More options icon and select Activate “Not signed up” users . This option allows you to set a password and activate the selected users. Note: Alternatively, you can activate users individually and set their passwords. To do so, click the More button for the user and select Activate .
5. Do the following in the Activate “Not signed up” users dialog box that appears:
6. Enter a password that will be set for the selected users. Ensure the password meets the requirements based on the Password strength configured in Account > Account > Settings > Security & integrations tab. Note: If there is more than one learning site in the organization, the password is set for the user for all of them. Also, if the password already exists (for example, the user has signed up from another Learning Site in the organization), it is reset, and the users are notified by email.
7. When you enter the password, the button appears, allowing you to copy the password and the learning site URL. Click the button to copy this information and paste it into a document to share later with the users.
8. Click Activate to activate the users with the set password.
9. The user is notified by email about the activation. The password is not included in the email.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > User Management > Users and Groups > Reset the password (for “Active” users):
This section explains how to reset or change the current password for “Active” users and set a new password.

1. Select one or more Active users on the Users page for whom you want to set a password.
2. From the options at the screen's bottom, click the More options icon and select Reset password for active users . This option allows you to change the user’s password and set a new one.
3. Note: Alternatively, you can reset each user’s password individually. To do so, click the More options icon for the user and select Reset password .
4. Do the following in the Reset password for active users dialog box that appears:
5. Enter a new password that will be set for the selected users. Ensure the password meets the requirements based on the Password strength configured in Account > Account > Settings > Security & integrations tab.
6. When you enter the password, the button appears, allowing you to copy the password and the Learning Site URL. Click the button to copy this information and paste it into a document to share later with the users.
7. Click Reset password to activate the users with the set password. When you reset the password, users remain logged in with the current password until they log out or the session expires. They will need to use the new password during the next login. The password is not included in the email.

There are two parts to the Competency Assessment module:

Self Assessment: In this part, Learners assess themselves on a given set of evaluation parameters.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Announcements > Features:
While creating the Module, the Admin can choose when the Learner’s evaluation will be visible to the Manager and vice versa.

The visibility options available for the Learner are:

- Manager’s evaluation will be visible only after the self-evaluation is complete. (This is applicable only for the first time an assessment is evaluated. All subsequent updates made to the evaluation will be visible to both.)
- Manager’s evaluation will always be visible.

The visibility options available for the Manager are:

- Learner’s self-evaluation will be visible after the Manager submits their Evaluation. (This is applicable only for the first time an assessment is evaluated. All subsequent updates made to the evaluation will be visible to both.)
- Learner’s self-evaluation will always be visible

Admins can also choose to display the score to both the Learner and the Manager or hide it completely by selecting one of the following options:

- Coaching Form Only: This setting only displays a filled-up form but does not show the achieved score.
- Coaching Form + Overall Score: This setting displays scores and points achieved at the parameter and section.

The Learner and Manager are allowed to review only once but can update a reviewed assessment.

This article gives an overview of the transcription and closed captioning (CC) capability in a course and quick update.

- Transcription is the process of converting the audio of a video into text.
- Closed caption (CC) is the capability to display the transcribed text of the audio of a video as it plays. CC may also include non-speech elements.

You can download the transcription and CC files. You can edit the CC file but not the transcription file. You can hide either or both from the learners.

Once you upload a video in a Course or Quick update on the Build tab, the Transcript and CC tab will be displayed next to the Factopedia tab.

The following image is an example of the Transcript and CC in a Course module.

Enable transcript by clicking the Transcript toggle button to automatically generate the transcript for learners.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Course and quick update > Closed Caption (CC) > Configure CC in a Course or Quick update:
- Click the Info icon to view the CC description.
- Select OFF if you want to turn off the default CC for learners. Note : Learners have the option to turn it on and select the language of their choice. The list of languages visible to the learners depends on the number of CC files you have uploaded for that particular content.
- Click the Horizontal More Menu icon to perform the following actions:
  - Download Closed Caption : Click this option to download the CC in VTT format.
  - Hide Closed Caption From Learners : Click this option to hide the auto generated Closed Captions from your learners. To unhide the CC, click the Horizontal More Menu icon and select the Show CC to Learners option.
  - Click the + Upload Another Language option to upload the CC of another language.
  - Drop the .srt or .vtt files in the dialog box that opens. Alternatively, you can also browse and upload the files from your computer.
  - Enter the language name for the uploaded file and click Upload .
  - The CC of the uploaded language will appear under the Closed Caption (CC) section. You can choose to upload CC in multiple languages one by one by following the above steps. There is no limit to the number of CC languages that you can upload. Select the CC language of your choice or delete it by clicking the Delete icon. Note : When you upload a CC file or enable transcription, the module update flow is not triggered. You can show/hide transcriptions anytime without impacting the learner’s progress.

- Select OFF if you want to turn off the default CC for learners. Note : Learners have the option to turn it on and select the language of their choice. The list of languages visible to the learners depends on the number of CC files you have uploaded for that particular content.
- Click the Horizontal More Menu icon to perform the following actions:
  - Download Closed Caption : Click this option to download the CC in VTT format.
  - Hide Closed Caption From Learners : Click this option to hide the auto generated Closed Captions from your learners. To unhide the CC, click the Horizontal More Menu icon and select the Show CC to Learners option.
  - Click the + Upload Another Language option to upload the CC of another language.
  - Drop the .srt or .vtt files in the dialog box that opens. Alternatively, you can also browse and upload the files from your computer.
  - Enter the language name for the uploaded file and click Upload .
  - The CC of the uploaded language will appear under the Closed Caption (CC) section. You can choose to upload CC in multiple languages one by one by following the above steps. There is no limit to the number of CC languages that you can upload. Select the CC language of your choice or delete it by clicking the Delete icon. Note : When you upload a CC file or enable transcription, the module update flow is not triggered. You can show/hide transcriptions anytime without impacting the learner’s progress.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Course and quick update > Closed Caption (CC) > Edit or Convert CC and reupload:
You can download the auto generated English Closed Caption (CC) file, and edit or convert it. Then, you can upload it in a Course or Quick update:

- Edit or modify the CC file: Edit the CC if there are typos.
- Convert the CC file: Convert the English CC into another language with the help of a translator or translation tool.

This section explains how to edit or convert a CC file and upload it.

- Click the Horizontal More Menu icon and select Download Closed Caption to download the CC in VTT format.
- Edit the download file using a text editor to correct any typos. Or convert it to another language with the help of a translator or translation tool.
- Click the + Upload Another Language option to upload the edited or converted CC file.
- Drop the .srt or .vtt files in the dialog box that opens. Alternatively, you can also browse and upload the files from your computer.
- Enter the language for the uploaded file and click Upload . For the edited file, enter a unique name so that it can be distinguished from the default English CC — for example: English New.
- The CC of the uploaded language will appear under the Closed Caption (CC) section. Select the CC language of your choice or delete it by clicking the Delete icon.
- When you have the auto generated English CC and the edited English CC, you can hide the auto generated English CC by clicking Hide Closed Caption From Learners .

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Course and quick update > Transcription and CC on the learning site:
On the learning site, learners can see the Transcript on the right panel. Transcription is grouped into 30-seconds chunks. Learners can also download the transcription or search for any keywords using the search bar. The Closed Captions will be visible in the video inset.

Learners can click the CC option to change the default language of the CC. Alternatively, they can also turn it off.

Note:

- The list of languages visible to the learner depends on the number of CC files you have uploaded for that particular content.
- Learners’ CC preference for a learning object gets saved in the browser cache. For example - If you have turned off the default CC but the learner turns it on by selecting English as the default language, the browser cache automatically saves this information. Next time the Learner accesses that learning object in the same browser, default CC will be displayed in English.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Analytics & Reporting > Reference:
The question report card in the quest (spaced reinforcement) report provides an overview of the performance and engagement of Learners for the selected question.

Note: This report takes into account all the active Learners (invited and not-started/in-progress/completed) to whom the question has been delivered in a past challenge or will be delivered in an upcoming challenge.

This article explains the question report card generated for each Question in quest reports. To view a question report card, click the question title in the table displayed in the Content Analysis tab of Quest Analytics.

The overview section displays the following metrics:

- Average Score - the average score that the Learners have achieved
- Completed Learners - The number of Learners that have completed the Question
- Mastered Learners - The number of Learners that have mastered the Question

The Question Progress chart shows the progress made by Learners on the selected Question. Click the legend to filter the chart by highlighting each category as required. Hover over the graph to see the detailed metrics of each stage.

The Attempt-wise Distribution chart shows how Learners performed in each attempt of the Question that was delivered to them. Click the legend to filter the chart by highlighting each category as required. Hover over the graph to see the detailed metrics of each stage.

The table displays a list of all Learners to whom the question was delivered, the score earned for the question, the status of mastery badge (Mastered), and their answers (correct/incorrect) for each attempt. Click Download As to choose the format in which you want to download the table.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Mobile App:
An Email & Task Evaluation mission is a virtual scenario that enables you to practice your email communication skills and improve them based on reviewer feedback.

This article explains how to submit your email and task evaluation mission submission using the Mindtickle mobile app. For information on how to submit an email and task evaluation mission on the web, refer to Email & Task Evaluation Mission.

2. Tap the Get Started button in the email. You will be directed to the mission on the mobile app. Alternatively, open the Home page on the mobile app and tap the appropriate mission assigned to you.

This article further explains different sections of the mission in detail.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Mobile App > Cut-off score:
There are two types of cut-off scores: certificate cut-off and passing cut-off.

If certificate cut-off is displayed, then a certificate will be awarded to you once you achieve this score. If passing cut-off is displayed then no certificate will be awarded.

In the below example, the passing cut-off is set to 80%, which means you have to score a minimum of 80% to pass this mission.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > General:
Automate the sequence in which the modules are made available to your users using sequential locking. This setting is on by default. Modules in a series unlocked sequentially for each learner as the learner progresses through the series completing one module at a time.

This article explains how sequential locking works per module.

| If the module is… | The next module unlocks after… |
| --- | --- |
| Assessment | The learner completes the assessment, whether they pass or fail it. |
| Checklist | The learner completes the checklist. |
| Coaching sessions | Once the reviewer is assigned and notified. The reviewer can schedule and complete the review at any time, regardless of the learner’s progress through the series. |
| Course without Certification | The learner completes the course. |
| Course with certification | The learner becomes certified in the Course. |
| ILT | The learner is marked as “attended” in a session.Note: Learners cannot access the ILT to enroll in a session until they have completed the preceding Modules. |
| Mission | The learner submits the mission.Note: Unlocking the next module is not dependent upon the review status of their mission submission. |
| Quest | The learner completes the modules preceding quest. Quests are unlocked automatically when the Learner completes the preceding Modules. And the Module after the quest is also unlocked along with quest. In other words, the learner need not complete the quest to unlock the module after it. |
| Quick-update | The learner completes the quick-update. |

In this article, we will focus on key points and best practices when structuring content in Mindtickle.

Before you structure and build your content on the Learning Site, make sure you are aware of who your audience is, their organization’s culture, and their individual skills. This will help you design purposeful training.

Let’s now take a look at the different aspects when designing training on Mindtickle.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > General > Series > Assigned, Public, or Scoped Public:
To keep Learners focused on the most relevant content, categorize it strategically within Assigned, Public, or Scoped Public Series.

- Only assign training that is relevant to a Learner's profile.
  - During the planning phase
    - define your target audience for each topic or set of objectives
    - determine if the content is required or optional
  - Create an Enablement Advisory Team or Panel internally to review the content prior to launch to ensure it is relevant to the roles. The panel should represent your audience including management (IC, Manager, Exec).
  - Use group automation to assign content to specific audiences reducing the burden on the Admins to manually assign Modules or Series.
- Limit the use of Public Series by setting its scope to make it visible only to specific Learners to display the most relevant content to them. Offering a long list of Public Series can distract Learners from completing their assigned training.

Note: Log in as a Learner and browse through the Public Series to make sure what is presented is relevant to all.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > General:
This article explains the steps to copy Modules and Series from one Learning Site (LS) on the Mindtickle platform to another.

Prerequisite: Make sure the Modules to be copied are published and updated to the latest version.

1. To request a copy of Series and Module, please send an email to Mindtickle Support with the following details:
  - Source LS URL
  - Series name
  - Module name (only if specific Module is to be copied)
  - Destination LS URL Note: Only the Modules in the Published state from the source LS can be copied. Modules in the Draft state cannot be copied.
2. Once copied, the Module will be in the Draft state in the destination LS, and you need to publish it. On request, the Mindtickle Support team will help you with the publishing in the following scenarios:
  - In case there are more than 5 Modules to be published, Mindtickle Support can help you do it using a script.
  - In case multiple Series consisting of at least 3 Modules are to be copied, Mindtickle Support can help you publish these Modules on the destination LS.Note: Only the content of the Module gets copied. The Learner data or their progress cannot be copied.
3. If the source and destination LS is the same, then an independent copy of the Module is created.
4. It may take up to 36 hours to complete this process. In case the number of Series is higher, then it may need more time. Mindtickle Support will keep you informed about the timeline.
5. If the source and destination LS are created in different regions, based on the content in the Modules, it might not be possible to copy Modules due to back-end limitations. Mindtickle Support will inform you about such scenarios.

chunks.headingPath: Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > User Management > Users and Groups
chunks.title: Important points for CSV Operations

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > User Management > Users and Groups:
- Each value in the first row of the CSV file is considered as the column name. The column names are profile fields configured in Profile management . For example, the screenshot below depicts the profile fields ( Users > Profile fields ) configured in Profile Management. The screenshot below depicts the downloaded sample CSV file that contains the same profile fields as column names.
- Each column name must match an existing profile field or relationship (Manager field). The column names that do not match are ignored and their data is not used in the process.
- The matching process is not case-sensitive.
- Username (email address) is a mandatory column. The entire CSV file is rejected in the absence of this column. In the Username column, the platform rejects individual records if information is absent or invalid.
- All columns other than Username are optional, even if the profile field for any of those columns is marked as “mandatory” in Profile fields .
- When adding multiple users via a CSV file, ensure that you use double quotes ( “” ) for values separated by commas in the different columns. Otherwise, the system displays an error. For example, in the Manager column, if you enter Aaron, Adam . The Manager name splits into Aaron and Adam during file upload, and the system displays an error. Instead, enter “ Aaron, Adam” to process the CSV file without errors.
- When adding users in bulk, you can configure their respective timezone as well. For the Timezone profile field, you must enter the timezone in the format specified for the timezone field. To check the format and view the list of supported timezones, click click here in the pop-up. This field is optional. Leaving it blank does not affect the current timezone of the learner.
