chunks.title: Important points for CSV Operations

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > User Management > Users and Groups:
- For date type profile fields, you must enter the date in the format set for the profile field. If the format of the entered value does not match the format set for the profile field, the system displays an error message and prompts you to update the data and re-upload the file.
- The file size should be less than 4 MB, which means approximately 5000 users. Note that this is an approximation. For example, a 3.2 MB file with 4000 users may fail if it has many profile fields. For any issues, contact Mindtickle Support .
- Ensure that the file is saved in the UTF-8 encoding format.
- When you are adding users via CSV, all users in the file are added to the platform unless they are already present.
- Users’ profile fields and relationships (Manager fields) are updated as per the data in the file. If any of them are blank in the CSV file, the platform does NOT delete their existing data from the platform.
- You cannot reset the data of profile fields of users in bulk. For this, you need to contact Mindtickle Support . However, to reset the relationship (Manager field) of a user, add "None" in place of the email ID for the relationship (Manager field).
- If a new username is found in relationships (Manager fields), a new user is added to the platform with that username.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > User Management > Users and Groups > The Groups page:
The Groups page displays the following group information and options:

- Header: The group header displays:
  - Group name along with the total number of group members
  - Group creator name and the date when it was created
  - Description: You can add a description for the group. The description has a limit of 250 characters. You can also edit or delete the added description.
  - The Invite group (to series and modules) and Add members options
  - The options to view and add group collaborators
- Members tab : Lists group members and their information, and allows you to perform various group operations. Using the Export report button, you can export the data of all users.
- Series links tab : Lists all series that you have access to based on your Series collaborator permissions . Using the toggle switch in Link status you can link and unlink the group from one or more series.
- Module links tab : Lists all modules that you have access to based on your Series Collaborator permissions. Using the toggle switch in Link status you can link and unlink the group from one or more modules. You can also set module relevance and a due date for group members in linked modules.
- Group analytics: The ( Group analytics ) button allows you to access the group’s analytics information.

The following sections provide detailed information about the various options and actions you can perform on the Groups page.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > User Management > Users and Groups > Invite users to a group > To series:
This section explains how to invite all members of a group to one or more series. During this process, the group is also linked to the selected series unless you choose not to.

Note: Group managers can also invite all or selected members of a group to one or more series where they have been added as collaborators. Earlier, group managers could invite users via group-to-series linking but could not directly invite a group’s members to a series.

From the header, click Invite group > To series.

In the Invite group to series dialog box that appears, do the following:

1. Select series: Select one or more series that you want to invite the group to. You can also search for a series by name.
2. Click the ( Information ) icon to view the series description.
3. Link to group: Link the group to the series. When you select a series, the toggle switch is turned on by default in the Link to group column. Once linked, current and future group members are assigned the linked series automatically. Turn the toggle switch off if you do not want to link the group to the series. You can later link and unlink the group from a series in the Series links tab .
4. Click Invite group to series to invite group members to the selected series.

This section explains everything about the Members tab of the group. The Members tab lists the users who are the members of the group, and shows the number of modules that they are invited to and the date when they were added to the group. The tab does not show deactivated users.

You can filter and sort the member information and also search for a member.

- Filters: You can filter the member list by Status (Active or Not signed up), profile fields, groups, and roles. When you apply a filter, the Reset filters option appears. Click to remove the filter.
- Search: Search for a member by name or email address.
- Sort: Sort the member list through the Members and Added on columns. Click the Up and Down sort buttons depending on the order in which you want to sort the column. The following subsections explain the following operations:

- Operations you can perform on an individual member
- Member bulk operations
- Export data of all, filtered, or selected users

- Module reports If you select this option, users continue to be a part of the module reports for modules they were invited to before the removal.
- Notifications If you select this option, users may or may not receive notifications based on whether the user is invited to the series and its modules. If users remain invited to the series and the existing modules, they continue to receive notifications for the existing modules.
  - Notifications are ON if : The Remove from group only option is selected and no new modules are published. In this case, users remain invited to the series and the existing modules. Therefore, they continue to receive notifications for those modules.
  - Notifications are ON if : The Remove from group only option is selected, and while publishing new modules, Invite all (n) learners of this series is selected. In this case, users remain invited to the series, hence they are also invited to the new modules. Therefore, they receive notifications for the new modules.
  - Notifications are OFF if : The Remove from group only is selected, publish new modules, and select Don’t invite anyone while publishing. In this case, the existing users are not invited to the new modules. Therefore, they do not receive any notifications for the new modules.

7. Select Remove from group and linked series to remove the user from the group and all the linked series.

Note: In this case, users are uninvited from the series, therefore, they are uninvited from its modules as well. They do not receive any subsequent notifications for the series or its modules.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > User Management > Users and Groups > Export user data:
This section explains how to export the data of all, filtered, or selected users in the group in a .CSV report.

- All users: To export the data of all users, click Reset filters to ensure that no filters are applied. Then, click the Export report button in the upper-right corner. In the Export data of all users pop-up, enter the email address in the field provided and then click Send .
- Filtered users: To export the data of filtered users, apply one or more filters and then click the Export report button in the upper-right corner. For example, to export a list of users belonging to a group, use the groups filter. Click Groups and select the group from the dropdown list, and click Export report. In the Export data of filtered users pop-up, enter the email address in the field provided and then click Send . The report generated is a filtered list of users belonging to the selected group.
- Selected users: To export the data of selected users, select one or more users and then click the Export selected users button in the quick-access toolbar at the bottom of the screen. In the Export selected users pop-up, enter the email address in the field provided and then click Send . Note: When you select users, the Export report button will not be available in the upper-right corner, under the Group analytics button. This is because the Export report button is used to export the data of all or filtered users.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > User Management > Users and Groups > Module links tab:
Use the Module links tab to link the group to one or more modules, configure module relevance, and set a due date for the group members in the linked modules.

Note: Module links is the same as the Automation Links feature in Automation suite. The only difference is that, in Module links, you can see linked modules in the context of the group.

In the Module links tab of a group:

- In the Modules column, you can view a list of all modules that you have access to. Click the ( Information ) icon to view the module description, if available.
- In the Due date column, you can view the due-date setting for each linked module. The due-date setting applies only to group members added to the group in the future. Existing group members keep their current due dates. For detailed information on setting due dates, see Create a course .
- In the Module relevance column, you can view the current Module relevance for the linked modules. You can also change the module relevance using the drop-down menu. When you change the module relevance, it applies only to group members added to the group in the future. The existing group members will have the module relevance that was set previously: either the relevance defined in the module’s settings or the relevance that was set while inviting the users to the module.
- In the Link status column, you can link and unlink the group from a Module using the toggle switch. Once linked, current and future group members are assigned the linked module automatically.

- Once unlinked, the toggle switch is turned off .

This section explains how you can link or unlink the group and invite users for multiple modules:

1. Select one or more modules. You can perform the following bulk operations: Note: The options that are available in the quick-access toolbar at the bottom of the screen depend on the selected modules. For example, the Link now option is available only if you selected one or more unlinked modules.

- Module relevance: When linking multiple modules, you can configure the module relevance for each selected module in the Module relevance drop-down.
- Due date: You can also configure the due date for each selected module in the Due date column.
- Unlink now: The workflow is the same as described in the Link to modules and invite group members section.
- Link now: The workflow is the same as described in the Link to modules and invite group members section. The only difference is that the default module relevance displayed in the pop-up is the site-level relevance, not the particular module's relevance.
- Invite existing users: To invite the existing group members in already linked Modules that you have selected. This option also sets Module relevance for users based on the selection in the Module relevance column. Ensure that you select the appropriate relevance first before clicking this button.
- Note: This option is available for already-linked modules for which you selected not to invite existing members when linking them.

To view a user’s profile, go to the homepage, navigate to Users, and click on a user from the list.

Alternatively, click the (More) button and select View profile.

You can also view a user’s profile wherever users are listed in the platform, such as in groups and modules.

- In modules: Within a module, navigate to the page where users are listed and click the option to view the user/learner profile.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > User Management > Users and Groups > Access a user's profile > Profile pane:
The profile pane on the left shows the user’s basic profile information, such as their name and email, KScore and total score, and various profile fields and relationships (Manager fields).

Click Edit profile to edit the user’s profile.

In the Edit profile screen that appears, edit the profile fields and then click Save.Note:

- The Language field is mandatory, and admins cannot delete it.
- Admins can view and update a user’s Language field.
- A user’s Language field cannot be empty. If it is empty, the system automatically updates it with the language of the learning site .
- For new users, the system automatically assigns the Learning site’s language to the Language field.
- If you change the learning site’s language, the system updates the Language field only for users created after the change and not for existing users.
- Based on your device settings and location data, the system automatically detects your timezone and recommends it at the very top in the list. This enables effortless setup and eliminates manual configuration errors. A wider dropdown ensures the full timezone name is visible clearly. You can easily browse through the comprehensive list or search for specific locations (by city, country, or timezone name), making it effortless to find and select the desired timezone.
- When updating date type profile fields, the system prompts you to enter the value in the format defined for the field. You can enter the date manually, or choose a date from the date picker widget that appears when you click on the field. The format defined for the profile field is visible as a placeholder.

The value is displayed in the field in the defined format. For more information, see Steps to set up date based rule for a profile field.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > User Management > Users and Groups > Access a user's profile > Invited modules pane:
The Invited modules pane on the right provides information about the modules that the user is invited to. The pane heading shows the total number of invited modules.

Note: You can only view the information on this pane. You cannot edit it.

The module information is listed in the following columns:

- Modules: Module name and the series that it is part of.
- Completion status: Current status of the Module: Did Not Start, In Progress, or Completed.
- Score: Score for the module in the achieved/total (achieved score out of the total score) format.
- Invited on: The date and time when the user was invited to the module.
- Completed on: The date and time when the user completed the module. The column shows an em dash (—) for modules that are not completed and for the ILT, coaching sessions, and competency assessment modules. The Completed on date is not shown for these three module types because they are ongoing and do not have a permanent completed state.

You can filter and sort the module information, and also search for a module.

- Filters: You can filter the modules list by Series , Module type , and Completion status (None, Did Not Start, In Progress/Not Reviewed, and Completed/Reviewed). When you apply a filter, the Reset filters option appears. Click to remove the filter.

User analytics: Click the (Go to user analytics) button to view the Learner’s overall report in analytics (opens in a new tab). This displays the overall progress of the user across the platform.

Module analytics: Click the (Module analytics) button to view the Learner’s module report in analytics (opens in a new tab). This displays the progress of the learner in a specific module. It also provides details on the learner’s performance for each content item, question, and poll.

Note:

- Report cards are not shown for ILT and coaching sessions.
- Report cards are not shown for modules that have not been started.
- In case of missions, report cards are shown for submitted and completed missions only.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Analytics & Reporting > Readiness Index (RI):
The Readiness Index (RI) is a sales readiness index available in Mindtickle Analytics. It is a unified metric that, by quantifying the capabilities of sales reps, measures their readiness to achieve business outcomes.

The Readiness Index generates the RI score for a cohort of sales reps. It performs correlations between the RI score and performance of those sales reps across teams and regions to identify how RI impacts business metrics.

RI highlights the competencies that separate your top sales reps from the ones that need improvement. It also highlights the competencies of your teams and user segments so that you can prioritize and personalize the readiness programs better.

With the Readiness Index, we are also introducing the concept of the ideal rep profile (IRP) through which you can correlate skills and behaviors with sales success. The IRP consists of the competencies that are important to your team or organization and the ideal score that should be achieved in the selected competencies (competency benchmark).

Note:

- Readiness Index (RI) data is not real-time. The data gets updated weekly — every Monday at 2 AM UTC. During the weekly data update, associated user hierarchies, competency performance data, and RI scores also get updated. For example, if there were any changes to your user hierarchies in the days between the last RI update and the upcoming update, the changes will reflect in RI after the next weekly update.
- To learn more about implementing the Readiness Index (RI) for your organization, contact your Customer Success Manager (CSM).

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Analytics & Reporting > Readiness Index (RI) > Prerequisites:
To set up and use the Readiness Index (RI), the following must be enabled and configured:

1. User hierarchyEnsure that you have enabled user-to-user hierarchy on your learning site. For help with setting up the user hierarchy, contact Mindtickle Support.

2. Tags (Competencies)In the context of RI, tags are referred to as “competencies.” The RI score is only calculated based on tags applied to specific, measurable content. Therefore, ensure that the tags you intend to use for RI are created and applied to the relevant content types listed below.

Supported content for RI tagsRI considers tags only when they are applied to:

- Evaluation parameters (used in missions and coaching sessions).
- Questions in training modules (used in courses, quick updates, assessments, and quests) of the following types:
  - Multiple choice question
  - Multiple choice images
  - Word guess
  - Match the labels
  - Match labels with images
  - Mark the location
  - True or false
  - Text answer

Note: Tags applied to modules and in-video questions are not considered for RI calculations.

To learn more about tags, see Create/manage tags and tag categories. For help with setting up tags, contact Mindtickle Support.

Permissions

Ensure that you have the necessary permissions to configure and view the Readiness Index on the admin site. For information on how to access Readiness Index on the admin and learning sites and the required permissions, see Readiness Index permissions and access.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Analytics & Reporting > Readiness Index (RI) > Ideal rep profiles:
The Readiness Index (RI) provides a unique feature of the ideal rep profile (IRP) through which you can correlate skills and behaviors with sales success. The IRP consists of the competencies that are important to your team or organization and the ideal score that should be achieved in the selected competencies (competency benchmark).

The Readiness Index (RI) provides two kinds of ideal rep profile (IRP) setups: single IRP and multiple IRPs.

- Single IRP setup: One IRP with one set of competencies. Applicable for all reps across the organization. In a single IRP setup, the RI home page takes you directly to the RI dashboards ( Track and Correlate tabs). For more information, see Create and Manage a Single Ideal Rep Profile (IRP) .
- Multiple IRP setup: Multiple IRPs with a different set of competencies for each IRP. Each IRP is created by first creating an IR group, where reps are selected through a profile field. Each IRP is applicable for the reps included in the IR group. In a multiple IRP setup, the RI home page shows the RI groups on the home page and clicking a group takes you to the RI dashboards ( Track and Correlate tabs). For more information, see Create and Manage Multiple Ideal Rep Profiles (IRPs) .

Important: Once you choose to go with a multiple IRP setup, you cannot switch back to a single IRP setup. However, you can still create only a single IRP within a multiple IRP setup by assigning a particular profile field value to all users.

For more information, see Ideal Rep Profiles in Readiness Index.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Analytics & Reporting > Readiness Index (RI) > Ideal rep profiles:
Key benefits of the Readiness Index and IRPs:

- Highlights the capabilities, strengths, and weaknesses of sales reps and helps you identify the top-performing sales reps and those who need improvement.
- Based on the top competencies of your teams and sales reps, you can better prioritize and personalize your readiness programs. Enablement Leaders can use this information to have more meaningful conversations with their Sales Leaders.
- RI is a leading indicator that provides you the confidence that your sales reps are ready to sell and capable of achieving their targets.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Analytics & Reporting > Readiness Index (RI) > How the Readiness Index is calculated:
The Readiness Index (RI) represents the capability of a sales rep on a scale of 0 to 100. It is calculated each week based on how well the sales rep is performing on key competencies. The competencies, as defined by your company, are stored as tags on the platform and tracked throughout the site.

To configure the RI for your organization, you need to choose the appropriate tags or competencies you want your sales reps to be proficient in. Ensure that these tags are applied to relevant questions (Course, Quick-Update, Assessment, and Quest Modules) and to evaluation parameters (Mission and Coaching Sessions Modules).

Then, you need to configure the weightage/contribution for each tag/competency to define the relative impact of the competency to your RI. By default, RI automatically assigns equal contribution to selected tags but you can manually assign different weightage/contribution to the tags.

Note: When you archive a module, the learners' module-level scores and points as well as the overall Knowledge Score (KScore) are retained. Therefore, archived modules do not have impact on Readiness Index, which considers the module scores for RI calculations.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Analytics & Reporting > Readiness Index (RI) > Track tab:
Once the RI is calculated, you can see RI metrics of all your sales reps in the Track tab. This tab helps you visualize your organization’s readiness level. It provides insights based on the competency benchmarks for a given period for a user’s team. You can view data and insights based on competencies, teams, and user segments in the form of actionable charts and tables. These insights help you understand which competencies some or all of your sales reps should focus on. You can identify which competencies your sales reps are good at and which not. Then you can help your sales reps achieve the ideal benchmark for the competencies where they are falling behind. This helps both managers and sales reps know what they could focus on.

You can drill down into a specific user cohort to analyze their numbers. You can further drill down to identify the specific teams and sales reps whose numbers are low or need attention.

Benefits

The Track tab offers the following benefits:

- Track RI scores by rep, team, or region and quickly address problem areas and understand how readiness scores change over time
- Identify which reps and teams within the organization need help from enablement and frontline managers
- More peak performers on the team through customized learning programs and coaching
- Optimal use of enablement efforts by focusing on reps and teams that need improvement

For more information, see Track Tab in Readiness Index.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Analytics & Reporting > Readiness Index (RI) > Correlate tab:
Through the Correlate tab in RI, you can view a correlation of your business metrics (such as quota attainment) with the Readiness Index in a quadrant chart. It helps you identify user cohorts and provides action-oriented insights. Sales teams can correlate skill, development, and knowledge with business outcomes, such as quota achievement, win rates, and sales cycle.

To view the correlation and analyze the impact of the Readiness Index (RI) on your business metrics, Mindtickle requires your business metrics data. You can either manually upload business metrics into Mindtickle or sync your Salesforce business metrics by integrating with Salesforce. You can also make use of both business metrics (manually uploaded and synced with Salesforce) simultaneously.

Benefits

The Correlate tab offers the following benefits:

- Analyze rep skills and competencies against business metrics to identify where readiness efforts need to be amplified
- Pull in business metrics from Salesforce automatically, or upload your business metrics manually
- Report the business impact of enablement and coaching
- Identify which parts of the revenue org need more help

For more information, see Correlate Tab in Readiness Index.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Analytics & Reporting > Readiness Index (RI) > Reports tab:
The Reports tab provides detailed reports related to Readiness Index (RI) in the following tabs:

- Key competencies: Provides data on the competencies you have configured for Readiness Index. For each competency, you can view its average score, any change in the score, and the competency benchmark score.
- Teams: Provides data on the managers and their teams (as configured in the user-to-user hierarchy ) in your organization. For each manager, you can view the total number of members in their team and the team’s average RI score.
- Modules: Provides data on the modules that have an impact on the competency score. For each module, you can view all competencies that the module is tagged with and the module score. Additionally, if you apply the “Competency” filter, the report displays a different set of relevant data: % contribution to competency, competency score of the module, and impact on overall competency score.
- User distribution: Provides data on the users (learners) in your organization. For each user, you can view their manager’s name and the RI score.

For more information, see Reports Tab in Readiness Index.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Analytics & Reporting > Readiness Index (RI) > Configure competencies:
To create an ideal rep profile (IRP), you need to select and configure tags/competencies that will be used for all IRP and RI calculations. You are prompted to select competencies while creating an IRP. You can also make changes to your selected competencies anytime later from Settings > Configurations.

Note:

- In the context of RI, tags are referred to as “competencies” and their respective tag categories as “competency categories.”
- In your Readiness Index Settings , if you selected a single IRP for your entire organization, the competencies that you select apply for all reps across the organization. If you selected multiple IRPs, you need to select competencies for each IRP for a particular RI group. The steps to select and configure the competencies are the same for single and multiple IRPs. For information on selecting single vs multiple IRPs, see Ideal Rep Profiles in Readiness Index .

Competencies in Readiness Index are defined through tags applied to various content in the Mindtickle platform. For example, messaging consistency, objection handling, negotiation skills, and closing skills are competencies. A competency has a knowledge piece (Do you know about negotiation?), a skill piece (Have you practiced with someone on how to negotiate?) and a behavior piece (Have you demonstrated good negotiation skills?).

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Analytics & Reporting > Readiness Index (RI) > Configure competencies:
- Select tags/competencies for your IRP that will be used for all calculations. RI automatically assigns equal % Contribution for selected tags. % Contribution indicates the importance or weightage of each tag in their contribution toward RI.
- (Optional) As mentioned in the first point, RI automatically assigns equal % Contribution for selected tags. However, you can choose to manually configure each tag’s contribution toward RI by changing their weightage. You can assign more weightage to tags that are more important for your team or organization. Tags with higher % Contribution are the tags/competencies where your sales reps are expected to perform better compared to other competencies.

To select and configure competencies for the ideal rep profile (IRP):

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Analytics & Reporting > Readiness Index (RI) > Configure competencies:
1. Once you have selected tags, they will appear in the left table under Selected competencies for ideal rep profile . For information on how the tags/competencies are used for your ideal rep profile, see Competency and RI Benchmarks in Readiness Index .
2. To remove a selected tag from your RI configuration, hover over the tag and click the X ( Delete ) icon.
3. As mentioned in Step 3, RI automatically assigns equal contribution (in %) to the selected tags. If required, you can manually configure the contribution for each tag. Click Configure Contribution to make changes to the tag contribution.
4. In the pop-up that appears, assign a weightage to any tag under the Weightage column and their contribution is updated automatically in the % Contribution column. Use the “-” and “+” buttons or manually enter the weightage. Tags with a “0” weight are not considered in the RI calculations. Assign higher weightage to tags you want to give higher importance to in RI and lower weightage to tags of lower importance. For example, if Tag A is more important than Tag B from RI perspective, then assign a weight of “2” to Tag A and “1” to Tag B. RI is a weighted average of the weightage assigned to tags that you choose for RI. When you manually assign weightage to tags, ensure that the sum of % Contribution value for tags across categories is 100%. For example, if you want 8 tags to be part of the RI calculations and 2 of them are more important than the rest, you can assign a weight of “2” to the important tags and a weight of “1” to the remaining tags. This will ensure that the overall contribution to RI for the 8 tags is 100%. Once done, click Save to save changes and update your tag contribution.
5. The Calculations section under Configurations provides information on what tags are considered for RI. RI considers only the tags applied to the following content: questions (in Course, Quick-Update, Assessment, and Quest) and evaluation parameters (in Mission and Coaching Sessions). Tags applied to Modules are not considered for RI. Currently, you cannot edit these settings. Click Save Changes to proceed with saving your RI configuration.
6. Your RI configuration consists of tags that you have selected and the % contribution defined for the selected tags. To save your RI configuration, click Save in the Save Configuration confirmation pop-up that appears.
7. Once saved, all future RI calculations will be performed using this configuration. The confirmation prompt also shows the date when RI is scheduled for calculation. RI is automatically calculated on a weekly basis every Monday at 2 AM UTC. Note: In the future whenever you edit an existing RI configuration and save it, only future RI calculations are performed using the newly-saved configuration, and the new configuration does not affect any previous RI calculations.
8. The Configuration Saved Successfully pop-up appears.
9. You can perform the following:
  - Choose to test your configuration before you click Done and finalize it. Click Test Configuration to schedule a test RI configuration, which will help you test how RI would reflect for your organization by providing you a temporary RI. The prompt mentions the time when the test RI calculations will appear on your RI dashboards (the Correlate and Track tabs). When you have already configured RI once and change the configuration the next time, the Test Configuration option will help you analyze the impact of your changes on the RI charts. This option generates a temporary RI using the following two:
    - Updated configuration that you just changed (changes to the weights applied on individual tags.)
    - Performance and tag data from the last RI run (Learners’ performance on selected tags and the application of tags on all resources in the platform.)
  - Click Done to schedule a regular RI calculation as per the weekly schedule: every Monday at 2 AM UTC. If you use this option, then the updated configuration is used for RI calculations during the next weekly run. Note: You can change the configuration of RI at any time but the data is not reflected immediately. RI is calculated weekly, so you will see the new data during the next weekly run.
10. The following pop-up appears to inform you that the process to generate the RI data has started.
11. You have now configured RI. The RI dashboards (the Correlate and Track tabs) will reflect the RI data when it’s processed and ready for viewing.
12. When you save your configuration, the Visualizations tab becomes available.
13. Click Edit and navigate to the Visualizations tab to make changes to the RI visualization settings. For more information, see the “ Configure RI Visualization Settings ” section below.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Analytics & Reporting > Readiness Index (RI) > Configure IRP benchmarks:
To create an ideal rep profile (IRP), you need to configure the benchmarks that will be used for all IRP and RI calculations. You are prompted to configure the benchmarks while creating an IRP but it’s an optional step. You can configure the benchmarks anytime later from Settings > Visualizations > Benchmark Configuration.

For configuring benchmarks, you need to select the metrics and their qualifying values. You can set one or both of the following metrics:

- Readiness Index: Set the minimum RI score as the benchmark.
- Business Metric: Select any one business metric and set a value as the benchmark.

Based on your selected benchmark metrics and their qualifying values, benchmarks are calculated by taking the average of the users who are above the qualifying value for the selected metrics.

Under Benchmark Configuration setup, select one or both of the following and configure their qualifying value (the cutoff value):

- Readiness Index: To make use of the RI score of your reps as a benchmark, select the minimum value for the RI score (out of 100) using the slider.
- Business Metric: To make use of your reps’ performance in business metrics, select any one business metric and set a value as the benchmark. Note: “Business Metric” will be available as a benchmark metric only if you have either synced the business metric data with Salesforce or uploaded manually. For more information about syncing business metrics through a CRM (such as Salesforce) or uploading manually, see the Upload or Sync Business Metric section.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Analytics & Reporting > Readiness Index (RI) > Upload or sync business metrics:
Upload or sync business metrics data with Mindtickle to measure the performance of reps through the ideal rep profile (IRP) and analyze the impact of the Readiness Index (RI) on your business metrics.

Through the Correlate tab in RI, you can view a correlation of your business metrics (such as quota attainment) with the Readiness Index in a quadrant chart. To view the correlation and analyze the impact of RI on your business metrics, Mindtickle requires your business metrics data. You can either manually upload business metrics into Mindtickle or sync your Salesforce business metrics by integrating with Salesforce. You can also make use of both business metrics (manually uploaded and synced with Salesforce) simultaneously.

Note: You can use Readiness Index (RI) without uploading business metrics. If business metrics are not uploaded and configured, the Correlate tab will show no data. And you will not be able to correlate the impact of RI and competencies on your business outcome data. However, you can continue to use the Track tab to track your competencies and analyze your sales reps’ performance against benchmarks.

Once the metrics data is uploaded, you can:

If your business metrics data resides in Salesforce CRM, you can sync the Salesforce’s sales metrics data for business outcomes, such as quota attainment and win rates, with Mindtickle. Once your Salesforce is integrated with Mindtickle and the business metrics data is synced, you can view this data in the Readiness Index.

For information on how to integrate and sync Salesforce business outcome data with Mindtickle, see Sales Outcome Data Sync with Salesforce.

For information on how the metrics are calculated, see Definitions and Calculations of Salesforce Metrics for Readiness Index.

Click Edit in the upper-right corner to enter the edit mode and make changes. Once completed making your changes, click Save Changes to save the changes. Or, click Discard to discard the changes and start over.

- Business Metric: To make use of your reps’ performance in business metrics, select any one business metric and set a value as the benchmark. Note: “Business Metric” will be available as a benchmark metric only if you have either synced the business metric data with Salesforce or uploaded manually. For more information about syncing business metrics through a CRM (such as Salesforce) or uploading manually, see the Upload or Sync Business Metric section.

Only the sales reps whose RI and business metric values are greater than the cutoff are considered for the calculation. Their scores in each competency are averaged out to create the benchmark for each competency. The ideal rep profile (IRP) and the overall RI benchmark are calculated based on this.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Analytics & Reporting > Readiness Index (RI) > Configure RI visualization settings > Miscellaneous:
You can configure the following miscellaneous settings:

Default time comparison

Configure the default time comparison for comparing between two RI values. This comparison is available for all charts and comparison parameters on the RI dashboards. You can set it to:

- Weekly: The latest RI is compared to last week’s RI.
- Monthly: The latest RI for the current month is compared to the latest RI of the last month.

Depending on the option that you select here (Weekly or Monthly), you will see weekly or monthly values in the Viewing RI as of and Show RI change from settings on the Track tab:

Control learners’ access to RI scorecard

Use the “Provide access to learners of their scorecards in profile page” option to allow or deny access to RI scorecard for your learners (reps).

- If turned ON, learners will see the Scorecard tab on their profile page on the learning site.
- If turned OFF, learners will NOT see the Scorecard tab.

Control learners’ access to distribution of peers in RI scorecard

Use the “Let learners see the distribution of other learners on their scorecard” option to allow or deny access to the distribution information of peers (other learners) in their RI scorecard.

- If turned ON, learners will be able to see and use the following option on their RI scorecard > quadrant chart (bubble chart):
  - Show cohort members in quadrant: This option allows a learner to see where they lie with respect to peers in the cohort (RI group).
- If turned OFF, learners will NOT get the above option.

Once you have set up Readiness Index and configured the necessary settings, you can view RI data and insights in the Track, Correlate, and Reports tabs.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Integrations > Web Conferencing:
Mindtickle’s integration with the Zoom video conferencing platform allows you to automate attendance tracking for your Instructor-Led Training (ILT) sessions. With this integration, when participants attend an ILT session conducted over Zoom, their attendance is marked automatically.

Note:

- Mindtickle does not support ILT integration with Zoom for Government .
- Mindtickle-Zoom paid integration works for all paid Zoom accounts, including Pro, Business, and Enterprise accounts.

The ILT-Zoom integration marks learners’ attendance automatically by matching email addresses in the Zoom attendance report with the list of email addresses of learners invited to the ILT module.

Note: If a learner’s email address is not listed in the Zoom attendance report, their attendance is marked as Did not attend. (Admins can manually change the learner’s attendance status from the admin site.) This feature is available only on request. To enable it for your organization, contact Mindtickle Support or your Customer Success Manager (CSM).

For attendance tracking, both of the following conditions must be met:

- Users are invited to the ILT module
- Users join the Zoom meeting with the email address associated with their Mindtickle user ID (email address)

Note: You can link one Zoom account to multiple Mindtickle learning sites (LS). To guarantee accurate auto-attendance tracking for learners across each site, it's important to establish separate connections between Zoom administrators and Mindtickle administrators. For instance, have Zoom admin A connect to LS1, Zoom admin B to LS2, and Zoom admin C to LS3.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Integrations > Web Conferencing > Considerations for Auto-attendance:
With Zoom’s March 2022 release, Zoom no longer shares the email addresses of guest participants in the attendance report. Therefore, the ILT-Zoom integration cannot mark the attendance of guest participants automatically. You must review your ILT sessions for guest participants and mark their attendance manually.

Zoom considers the following participants as guests:

- Any licensed or unlicensed user who is not signed in to a Zoom account
- Any unlicensed user who is not added to the meeting (on Google Calendar or Outlook) as a participant by the host
- ( For webinars ) Any user who doesn’t register as a participant through the webinar registration link

For more information on criteria that Zoom considers to mark a user as a registered participant, see Zoom’s March 2022 release note.

Tip: To automate attendance marking for unlicensed users, ensure they are added as a participant to the Zoom meeting invite (on Google Calendar or Outlook).

Note: Learners do not have to be enrolled in a session for marking attendance through ILT-Zoom integration. As long as Learners are invited to the ILT Module, their attendance can be marked automatically. However, this action is subject to the considerations mentioned above.

For more information about downloading attendance reports and marking attendance manually, see Learner’s ILT Report. In case you need more assistance, contact your Customer Success Manager (CSM).

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Integrations > Web Conferencing > Prerequisites > Accounts and roles:
The user setting up the ILT-Zoom integration must meet the following prerequisites:

- Mindtickle: A Mindtickle account with either the “Site Owner” or the “IT Admin” role. This is required to access the “Security and Integrations” settings on the platform.
- Zoom You can use Zoom to create custom roles or assign default roles with the necessary permissions.

1. Custom role You can create custom roles with the necessary permissions and assign members. All members assigned to the custom role can set up the Zoom integration for ILT sessions so that attendance and meeting management through Zoom meetings are recorded automatically. To create a custom role in Zoom and assign the necessary permissions:

1. Sign in to your organization’s Zoom account.

2. Go to Admin > User Management > Roles.

3. Click Add Role.

The Roles page is displayed.

4. On the Add Role pop-up, enter an appropriate name and description for the role and click Add.The new custom role is created.After creating the role, the following permissions must be assigned to the users added under this role.

To assign the permissions, follow the steps mentioned below.

5. On the Role Settings tab, under User and Permission Management, select View and Edit permissions for Users.

6. Click the Scope column to apply the permissions. The following options are available:

- Entire account: This option applies permissions to the entire account. Select this option only if custom scoping is unavailable.
- Custom Scope: This option applies permissions to a specific group (GTM enablement, Training facilitators). It is recommended that you use this option, as it restricts permissions to a specific user group.

7. To create a custom scope and grant permissions to a specific user group, click the Scope column and select Custom Scope from the drop-down.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Integrations > Web Conferencing > Installation and Configuration:
Perform the following steps to enable the Zoom integration for ILT and install the Mindtickle app for your Zoom account:

1. On the admin site homepage, hover over the Account Settings icon on the left navigation bar, and click Settings . The Settings page is displayed.
2. On the Security and integrations tab, scroll down to the Web Conferencing section. Under Zoom , select the checkbox to proceed with the Zoom integration. You are now directed to Zoom to sign in to your account. Sign in with your admin credentials. Note: Ensure that you have entered the correct Zoom credentials. 5. You can view the installed Mindtickle app from your Zoom account in Zoom App Marketplace > Manage > Installed Apps .

Note: Any licensed Zoom user account with the Owner, Admin, or Member role can schedule sessions, and the attendance will be marked automatically. Your license information is available on your Zoom account page under Profile.
chunks.headingPath: Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Integrations > Web Conferencing > Use Zoom integration for ILT sessions
chunks.title: ILT-Zoom integration to manage meetings and auto-attendance

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Integrations > Web Conferencing > Use Zoom integration for ILT sessions:
1. Create a new ILT session . By default, the session type is set to Classroom location . In the dialog box for creating a new session, select the session type from the Classroom / video conferencing tool details dropdown. For a video conferencing session, you can create a Webex or Zoom meeting from the session or add a meeting link manually. This article lists the procedure for creating a Zoom meeting from the ILT session. Note : While creating a meeting from the ILT session, ensure:
  - The session start and end time is set in the future.
  - The session time is more than 10 minutes.
2. Select Generate Zoom meeting link from the dropdown. The meeting link is generated, and the meeting details and host details are auto-filled in the Meeting Details section. If you create the Zoom meeting link from the session, you can add co-hosts to the meeting. Co-hosts help improve meeting productivity. The ‘co-host’ role has permissions similar to the ‘host’ role. If the host runs late or cannot attend, a co-host can start and manage the meeting. Co-hosts can also assist the host with meeting management, which is helpful for larger meetings. Click Add co-host , enter the user’s email address, and click Save . The user is added as a co-host to the meeting. Click the Edit icon to edit the details or the Remove icon to remove the user as a co-host from the meeting. Alternatively, you can add instructors or facilitators and assign them as co-hosts for the meeting. To assign an instructor or facilitator as a co-host, enter their details and select the Add as meeting co-host checkbox. The users are added to the list of co-hosts. Note :
  - You can add up to 10 co-hosts to a session with a Zoom meeting.
  - Any user who is added as a co-host, is added as an ' alternative host ' on Zoom. If this user has the appropriate permissions on Zoom, they can start and end the meeting on the host's behalf.
  - If an instructor or facilitator is added or removed as a co-host from the meeting, they receive an email notification with all session change details (if applicable). The email is sent after the session is published.
3. Alternatively, enter the Zoom meeting link manually. While entering a meeting link manually, select Enter meeting link from the dropdown.
4. Enter the meeting URL in the Enter Meeting link section. If the meeting is created from the same account through which the Mindtickle-Zoom integration is set up or from a different account, the system checks the URL for Zoom auto-attendance eligibility. If eligible, the Auto attendance toggle appears and is automatically switched ON . Note :
  - If the session type is set to Classroom location and you enter the URL of a Zoom meeting manually, the session type changes to Enter link manually . The system checks the URL for Zoom auto-attendance eligibility. If eligible, the Auto attendance toggle appears and is automatically switched ON .
  - If the toggle is switched OFF , you must mark the attendance manually or via session check-in.
  - The check-in feature is unavailable for sessions in which auto attendance is enabled. To use the check-in feature, turn the toggle switch OFF .
5. Configure the remaining settings and click Create session . A confirmation message is displayed on the screen once the session is created successfully. The session appears in the list of sessions. The Attendance Mode of the session is listed as Auto Attendance .
6. Click the session to view other details.
7. Publish the session and invite your learners. Once the session ends, participants’ attendance is marked automatically via Zoom.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Integrations > Web Conferencing > Use Zoom integration for ILT sessions > Duration-based attendance capture:
Admins can set a minimum percentage threshold to record learners’ attendance for ILT modules and individual sessions using the Duration-based attendance capture feature.

This feature automatically records learners’ attendance based on their time in ILT events and sessions.

When participants attend an ILT Webinar conducted over Zoom, their attendance is marked automatically. The Zoom integration provides the time spent by the learner in a session.

The system calculates an ILT session’s minimum attendance threshold as follows,

- Scheduled sessions: For scheduled sessions that are yet to start, the system calculates the minimum attendance threshold using the session's start and end time set during session creation. For example, in a 60-minute session with a 20% minimum attendance threshold, the system marks the learner as attended if they spend at least 12 minutes (20% of 60) in the session.
- Completed sessions: If a session ends early or extends beyond the scheduled time, the system calculates the minimum attendance threshold based on the actual session time. For example, for a 60-minute session with a 20% minimum attendance threshold, if the session ends early in 50 minutes, the system marks the learner as attended if they spend at least 10 minutes (20% of 50) in the session.

The system compares the learners’ time in session provided by Zoom with the session’s minimum attendance threshold to mark the learner's attendance for the session.

The learner’s attendance status and time spent in sessions are displayed in the Attendance status/Duration column on the Events and Sessions tab of the ILT.

For more information, see Duration-based attendance capture for learners in ILTs.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Integrations > Web Conferencing > Use Zoom integration for ILT sessions > Caveats:
- If you discard the meeting without saving the changes, Zoom meeting details are deleted from the session, and the session type is reset to Classroom location . The meeting is deleted from Zoom as well.
- If a meeting that has ended is restarted (the host restarts it or a participant joins), we get the attendance details of only the participants from the latest instance of the meeting, and the data for participants from all previous meeting instances is lost.
- If an instructor marked as a co-host is removed, the user is also removed from the Zoom meeting co-host list.
- If you copy a session in which a Zoom meeting is configured, the session type is reset to Classroom location in the copied session.
- Suppose you copy the ILT module in a different series that includes a session (or multiple sessions) in which Zoom meetings are configured. In that case, the session type for the copied sessions is reset to Classroom location .

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Integrations > Web Conferencing > Attendance calculation for ILT sessions in Zoom:
- For ILT sessions conducted in Zoom, Mindtickle fetches the attendance reports from Zoom after the scheduled session ends.
- Learners' attendance is marked from all meeting instances that start 30 minutes before and 30 minutes after the scheduled meeting time.
- If the meeting is ongoing, the system requests attendance reports every five minutes for up to 24 hours after the meeting ends.
- The table below explains the attendance capture scenarios for an ILT session scheduled on Zoom between 3 p.m. and 4 p.m.

| Scenario | Meeting start time | Meeting end time | Attendance in Mindtickle |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| The host starts the meeting early to check if the meeting link is accessible. | 2:15 pm | 2:16 pm | No |
| The learner joins the meeting early before the host joins the meeting. | 2:25 pm | 2:35 pm | No |
| The host starts the meeting early, and the session ends in 45 minutes instead of 1 hour. | 2:45 pm | 3:45 pm | Yes |
| The learner joins the meeting in the last few minutes. | 3:55 pm | 4:00 pm | Yes |
| The host starts the meeting early, and the session extends beyond the scheduled meeting time by 15 minutes. | 2:55 pm | 4:15 pm | Yes |
| The host starts the meeting early and it extends 40 minutes beyond the scheduled meeting time. | 2:55 pm | 4:40 pm | Yes |
| The learner starts the meeting late after the meeting ends. | 4:25 pm | 4:26 pm | Yes |
| The learner starts the meeting late after the meeting ends. | 4:25 pm | 4:32 pm | Yes |
| The learner starts the meeting late after the meeting ends. | 4:35 pm | 4:40 pm | No |

Mindtickle combines the attendance reports from all valid meeting instances for attendance calculation. For example, if 10 users join the meeting in the first half-hour and 5 (with 3 overlapping users) join in the second half-hour, the attendance is marked only for 12 users.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Integrations > Web Conferencing > Uninstallation > Uninstall Mindtickle from Zoom:
1. Sign in to your Zoom account and navigate to Zoom App Marketplace .
2. Enter Mindtickle in the search in the upper-right corner and click the app name in the results.
3. In the app page that appears, click Manage on the left navigation panel.
4. In the Remove the App section, click Remove .
5. In the Remove App pop-up, select the reason for removing the app and click Remove . Note: Selecting the reason for removing the app is optional. The Mindtickle app gets uninstalled from your Zoom account. Note: When you uninstall the Mindtickle app from Zoom Marketplace, Mindtickle fully complies with the Zoom Data Compliance policy regarding your Zoom data.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Integrations > Web Conferencing > Troubleshooting or FAQs:
- Common Installation Issues Please check if you have entered the correct credentials for Zoom in Step 4 of Installation and Configuration. For any issues, contact Mindtickle Support .
- Why is my meeting ID not valid for attendance tracking? All meeting IDs associated with your organization's Zoom account will be eligible for attendance tracking. Please check if the link belongs to your organization. Note: I n this case, the organization refers to the parent organization of the account used when integrating Zoom with Mindtickle.
- Why is my meeting attendance not available? Meeting attendance is uploaded on the Mindtickle platform 30 minutes after the meeting has ended. Please check if the meeting is ended by the host. It may take up to 24 hours for the attendance to reflect on the platform.
- Unsupported Scenarios The Zoom meeting/webinar link is not supported for the following scenarios:

- Unsupported meeting type: Ensure that the Zoom meeting type is supported .
- Z oom link doesn’t belong to your organization: The added Zoom meeting link does not belong to the organization for which Zoom is integrated with Mindtickle. Ensure that the Zoom meeting link belongs to the integrated organization.
- Invalid Zoom link: The Zoom meeting link is invalid. Ensure that you have entered a valid link.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Competency Assessment:
Note: We are ending support for Competency Assessment (CA) soon. Thus, we are not enabling CA for new customers.

The Competency Assessment Module (Beta) allows Learners to self-assess themselves and also lets the Managers assess the Learners on a given set of competencies. Gaps are identified by comparing these two assessments which provide Managers and Learners critical information to create a personalized development plan.

Note: Contact your Customer Success Manager to learn more about this feature for your Learning Site.

The Competency Assessment module has two parts:

1. Self Assessment : In this part, Learners assess themselves on a given set of competencies.
2. Manager Evaluation : In this part, Managers conduct their assessment using the same competencies that were assigned to the Learners. Admins assign Managers as Reviewers using a relationship field allowing Managers at different levels of the Learners’ organization to provide their assessment.

The Competency Assessment creation workflow consists of four main tabs.

Build: The Build tab allows you to add the description, create a form to configure behaviors and competencies, define proficiencies, and manage the review preferences.

Settings: The Settings tab allows you to manage General Settings and email communications for Learners and Managers.

Publish: The Publish tab prompts you to complete any remaining To-Do’s, invite Learners, and publish the Competency Assessment. It also allows you to track the version changes in the Competency Assessment.

Invite & Track: The Invite & Track tab allows you to invite new Learners to participate in the Competency Assessment and replace or remove Managers. You can use Invite & Track to manage Learners and Managers, track their activity, and follow up with them.

This article explains the steps to create a Competency Assessment. To learn more about the Competency Assessment module, refer to the Get Started with Competency Assessment article.

1. From the admin site home page, click Training > Modules > Create modules.Alternatively, you can create a Competency assessment from within a series by clicking Training > Series > select the required series > Create module.Or click Training > Series > Create > Module.

2. On the Add modules pop-up, hover over the Competency assessment tile and click Create competency assessment.

3. Enter your Competency assessment name and select the Series in which you want to place it. If you don't want to place it in an existing Series, create a new Series by clicking the Create a New Series link. Then, click Next.

5. Click Create Competency Assessment.

6. On the page that opens, there are four tabs: Build, Settings, Publish, and Invite & Track.

To rename (Rename Module), get URL of the Module (Get Module URL), or delete (Discard Module), click the down arrow to the right of the Competency Assessment's name.

Click the + button to apply Tags to the Competency Assessment Module.

1. From the admin site home page, click Training > Modules > Create modules.Alternatively, you can create a Competency assessment from within a series by clicking Training > Series > select the required series > Create module.Or click Training > Series > Create > Module.

2. On the Add modules pop-up, hover over the Competency assessment tile and click Create competency assessment.

3. Enter your Competency assessment name and select the Series in which you want to place it. If you don't want to place it in an existing Series, create a new Series by clicking the Create a New Series link. Then, click Next.

5. Click Create Competency Assessment.

6. On the page that opens, there are four tabs: Build, Settings, Publish, and Invite & Track.

To rename (Rename Module), get URL of the Module (Get Module URL), or delete (Discard Module), click the down arrow to the right of the Competency Assessment's name.

Click the + button to apply Tags to the Competency Assessment Module.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Competency Assessment > To-Do:
If there are pending To-Do’s, click the actions on the list and navigate to the appropriate step in the Competency Assessment creation workflow to complete these items.

Once you complete all the tasks, choose the Learners you want to invite to the Competency Assessment. Click the drop-down arrow next to the Invite radio button to select the available options.

- Invite All Learners of this Series - Invites Learners who are invited to at least one Module in the Series.
- Invite Fully invited Learners of this Series - Invites Learners who are invited to all Modules in the Series.
- Invite Select Learners from this Series - Allows you to select from the list of Learners invited to the Series.

Select the Also notify the Learners via email check box if you want the Learners to receive an email notification inviting them to the Competency Assessment. Click Confirm Publish.

If you want to publish the Competency Assessment without inviting any Learners, click the Don’t invite anyone radio button and click Confirm Publish.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > Admin:
Mindtickle’s Conversational Intelligence bot, Call AI, helps you review, analyze, and get insights on your calls to improve your sales conversations.

Call AI tracks your team’s activity and helps provide information on every customer touchpoint. It tracks the effectiveness of a Rep’s conversation, demonstrates what good looks like, and helps identify who your top performers are.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > Admin > Key Features > Privacy Features:
Call AI provides the following privacy features which are divided into 2 sections: Customizable and Non-customizable

Customizable features:

- You can change or customize the name of the bot for your company.
- You can customize the bot’s audio alert which plays when the participants from outside of your company join the call. Currently, it is “Your call will be recorded for quality and training purposes.”
- An email will be sent to all of the participants of the call (customers and Reps) 15 mins prior to the call, noting that the call will be recorded. You can enable or disable this email.
- You can capture the active consent of participants before recording the call using Call AI Zoom App and Call AI Google Calendar Plugin .
- You can allow/disallow Reps to enable/disable the bot from joining meetings from the Upcoming Meetings section. Based on this setting, Reps can selectively invite the bot from the list of their upcoming meetings. Reps can view at least 2 weeks of upcoming meetings on the list.
- You can define what type of calls get recorded:
  - Internal calls (where all the participants are employees of your company)
  - External calls (where the host may or may not be an employee of your company)
  - All calls
- You can trim a call recording before sharing it externally so that only the relevant part of the call plays for the external participant. You can also delete a call recording if a call recording is no longer needed or a participant requests for it.

Non-customizable features:

- What were the key topics discussed in this call.
- Which competitors were mentioned in the call and so on.
- Copilot automatically delivers a response to the query.

For more information, see Mindtickle Copilot for Call AI.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > Admin:
This article explains the initial setup requirements of Call AI and navigating the interface.

Conversation intelligence software helps sales teams close individual deals, but when salespeople struggle repeatedly, they need to identify and fix the behaviors that hold them back.

Call AI’s approach to conversation intelligence is unique because you can focus on fixing the deal before you and identify the real-world behaviors that stop your sales reps from winning deals. Call AI helps identify the skills required to be successful, measure individual and aggregate sales performance against those skills and apply individualized coaching and training to help each rep achieve top performance.

For more information about Call AI and its benefits, see Call AI Overview.

Note: Call AI is a paid feature. For more information, contact your Customer Success Manager (CSM).

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > Admin > Navigate the Interface:
Once the setup completes, sign in to your Call AI instance.

Note: Call AI widgets are available to reps on the Mindtickle learning site only if you enable them from the Dashboard Builder. For more information, see Dashboard Builder Overview.

There are 4 sections in the Call AI interface:

- Recordings : This tab displays the call recordings under the following tabs:
  - All Recordings : It displays all the recordings in the Call AI interface.
  - My Recordings: It displays all the recordings where you were a participant.
  - Shared: It displays all the recordings shared with you and by you.
  - Bookmarked: It displays all your saved recordings.

For more information, see Recordings List in Call AI.

- Team Recordings: It displays all your team member’s recordings. This tab is visible if your role is a manager.

Note:

- You can only view the call recordings of team members currently reporting to you.
- You can view all the historic call recordings of team members to review their past performance and find relevant coaching opportunities.

- Upcoming Meetings: It displays at least 2 weeks of your upcoming meetings, which Call AI will record.
- Libraries: It displays all the Libraries you can access or have created.

Creating a process to capture win stories also gives sellers the opportunity to share the good work they have been doing, and brag a bit. 2. Sales records their win stories
3. Share win stories with the sales team

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Best Practices and Use Cases > Platform Use Cases | Internal Engagement > Deploying Missions to collect win stories:
1. Standardize the format of your win stories using a PowerPoint presentation template. Download our example template here.
2. Create a Series category called Win Stories and a Series called Win Stories. You could also create a different Win Stories Series for each role, department, or region based on your organization.
3. Create a Voice Over Slideshow Mission for sellers to record their win story.
4. Under Add Scenario Details, provide clear instructions on how to perform the Mission, along with the template and recording time limits.
5. Add one or two Evaluation Parameters to validate that the story meets your criteria for a good win story. Additionally, the score associated with the parameters increases the overall K-score of the person submitting the story creating a gamified experience.
6. Configure the Mission to enable your sellers to submit multiple win stories without being assigned multiple Missions. Under Set Cut-Off Score, enable the Allow Learners to re-attempt the Mission setting and disable all others. Enabling this option will allow the sellers to perform the activity again, without the need to set up the Mission again.
7. Configure who will validate the stories.
  1. If you want one individual to validate all the recordings, select the Common Reviewer for all Learners option. This option works well when you have a smaller sales team.
  2. Alternatively, if you want the Managers to validate the stories submitted by their team members, select Appoint Manager as Reviewer. Select the appropriate relationship Profile Field to automatically send submissions to the Managers for review.
8. Add a Thumbnail to the Module and also set the Email Communications as required under the Settings tab.
9. Publish the Mission and invite Learners to the Mission to record their win stories.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Best Practices and Use Cases > Strategies:
When deploying a new Course or Quick-Update, a well-planned badge strategy can significantly increase engagement, especially with high achievers and competitive teammates. It's a simple way to gamify your enablement content and build excitement about your program. Below are three tips to deploy a gamified badge strategy to keep learners engaged.

1. Make it Universal

When deciding on your badging strategy, consider a holistic approach. Create a plan that can be duplicated or even expanded from program to program. This can create a culture where learners are excited to earn a new badge(s) each time you launch a new program.

2. Don’t Make it Too Easy

Be sure each badge represents a significant and increasing level of difficulty. Don’t simply hand out badges for viewing content. Create a challenge where the learner feels a sense of pride in their accomplishment. In both Quick-Updates and Courses, you can create a multi-level badge structure, be sure the high badge is truly difficult to earn.

3. Get Creative

As we all know, media-rich content is a great way to engage learners, but don’t skimp on the badge design. Badges don’t have to be boring. Create an engaging theme where the badges build on each other such as an Olympics theme with bronze, silver, or gold medals, or something clever that fits with your company. For example, a gas and oil company could have regular, plus and premium badges or a telecommunications company could have fax, phone, email.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Analytics & Reporting > Modules > Functionality support and limitations:
The following limitations and unsupported features will be addressed in future releases:

- Not available in series reports: Analytics for the competency assessment module are not yet available in series reports . Although the module is counted in the total number of modules, its analytics are currently excluded.
- Archived modules: Analytics for archived Competency Assessment modules are not supported.
- Tags: Tags applied to competency assessment behaviors do not contribute to the Tags dashboard or the Readiness Index (RI).
- Aggregated metrics: Metrics such as % Participation, % Completion, and % Score do not include competency assessment scores.
- Reporting API: The reporting API documentation does not yet include tables related to competency assessments. Additionally, Competency assessment data is not currently available in the LearnerModulePerformance (LMP) table.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Analytics & Reporting > Modules > Competencies tab > Trend chart:
The trend chart shows how competencies change over time and is based on data from the competencies report. By default, it displays the average assessment trend over the last six months, aggregating all competencies and behaviors.

Note: At least one month of assessment data is required for the trend chart to appear.

Use the Average assessment drop-down menu to select from the following charts:

- Average assessment: The average of the learner’s and manager’s most recent assessments across configured competencies and behaviors.
- Gap: The difference between the manager’s and learner’s most recent assessments.
- Manager’s assessment: Shows only the manager’s assessment data.
- Learner’s self assessment: Shows only the learner’s self-assessment data.

Notes:

- Only data from learner–manager pairs where both have completed at least one assessment is included.
- If assessments were completed in January and again in June, the January data will carry forward from February through May.

You can further filter the charts using:

- All competencies and All behaviors drop-downs to focus on specific areas.
- View for last drop-down to adjust the time range to 6, 12, or 24 months.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Analytics & Reporting > Modules > Competencies tab > Competencies report > Report columns:
The report includes the following columns:

- Competency: Lists competencies and associated behavior statements. Competencies group together behaviors, which are the specific items rated by both the learner and manager. For example, behaviors grouped under a "General management" competency may include:
  - Ability to analyze and evaluate information to support a decision or recommendation.
  - Ability to distinguish relevant from irrelevant information.
- Proficiencies: Both learners and managers complete their assessments using a configured proficiency scale, such as Developing, Proficient, Advanced, or Expert. Hover over each bar to see the exact score.
- Gap: The difference between the manager’s and learner’s latest assessment scores. This value helps identify alignment issues and supports the creation of personalized development plans. The gap is calculated as: Manager's score – Learner’s score Possible gap types include:
  - Positive gap: The learner rated themselves lower than the manager.
  - Negative gap: The learner rated themselves higher than the manager.
  - Neutral gap: Both ratings are equal.
- Average: The average of the learner’s and manager’s most recent scores. For example, if the manager’s rating is 3 and the learner’s is 2, the average is 2.5.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Analytics & Reporting > Modules > Learners tab > Report columns:
The tab contains the following columns:

- Learners: Lists learners along with their email addresses. The column header displays the total number of learners.
- Last assessed on: Shows the date when the learner and their manager last completed their assessments. A dash (—) appears if an assessment is incomplete. This helps track assessment progress. You can also track progress from the Invite & track tab of the module. Note: To ensure updated assessment data, admins should encourage learners and managers to complete their assessments via email communications in the module settings.
- Proficiencies: Shows ratings from both learner and manager using the configured proficiency scale (e.g., Developing, Proficient, Advanced, Expert). Hover over each bar to see exact ratings. The chart is not shown if an assessment is missing.
- Gap: The difference between the manager’s and learner’s latest assessments. This column helps identify alignment gaps and informs development plans. The gap is calculated as: manager’s score – learner’s score. Gaps may be:
  - Positive gap: The learner rated themselves lower than the manager.
  - Negative gap: The learner rated themselves higher than the manager.
  - Neutral gap: Both ratings are the same.
- Average: The average of the learner’s and manager’s latest assessments. For example, if the scores are 3 and 2, the average is 2.5.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > Admin:
This article lists the type of emails that users (reps, managers and customers or prospects) receive when performing various activities such as recording a call, deleting a call or sharing a call in Call AI.

Emails are a vibrant and powerful way to connect with users. They provide users with the essential information they need to succeed in their daily work and guide them to take the necessary actions.

Note: If you customize the sender’s email address, all emails sent from Call AI use the customized address. If you don’t customize it, emails sent from Call AI use admin@mindtickle.com by default.

For example, a Sign Up email in Call AI can impress the users and encourage them to:

- Sign in to the product
- Configure calendar and CRM integration
- Learn to use Call AI
- Read about the benefits of Call AI

Users receive the following types of emails in Call AI:

- Sign Up
- Recording Reminder for Internal Participants
- Recording Reminder for External Participants
- Recording and Insights are Ready
- Share Call or Snippet Internally
- Share Multiple Calls Internally
- Share Call or Snippet Externally
- Share Multiple Calls Externally
- Private Messages and Public Comments
- Email Digest
- Recording Enabled or Disabled
- Delete Single Recording
- Delete Multiple Recordings
- Stop Call Recording
- Custom Email Alerts

The article further explains each of these emails in detail.

This email provides an option to users to sign up to Call AI. There are 3 default roles in Call AI:

- Listener: Can only listen to the call recordings.
- Recorder: Can integrate calendar and record meetings (listener permissions by default)
- Call AI Admin: Manages admin side of Call AI (listener permissions by default)

Call AI customizes the sign up email depending on the user’s role. For more information on roles and permissions, see Call AI Permissions.
