chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Setup > Site Setup > Create a new rule:
1. On the admin site homepage, click Account and select Automation suite . The Automation suite homepage appears with two tabs: Automation rules and Automation links . The Automation rules tab lists all Automation rules created for groups, modules, profile fields, roles, and integrations. From this tab, you can create, view, edit, filter, activate, deactivate, or delete rules, as well as create rules similar to existing rules. Note : Integration-based rules are visible on this interface only if Automation Suite 2.0 is enabled on your learning site and at least one integration-based rule is created. For more information, contact Mindtickle Support or your Customer Success Manager (CSM). For more information about Automation links , see Automation links .
2. On the Automation rules tab, click Create new rules .
3. On the new rules panel that opens, enter a short description or title for the rules. Ideally, the title/description should provide a context of the rules and what it will accomplish.
4. Alternatively, you can create the rules now and add the description later. For more information, see Edit a rule. Note :

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Setup > Site Setup > Create a new rule:
1. It is not mandatory to add a rules description. However, it is recommended as a good practice as it gives a quick preview of each rule in the list.
2. The maximum character limit for a rules description is 150 characters.
3. It is possible to add/edit a rule’s description from the Automation rules tab at any point.
4. Define the qualification criteria for the learner. From the condition clause dropdown, choose whether the rules should apply if all or at least one of the conditions added to the rules are met. Select:
  - AND clause if you want the qualification criteria to be that all conditions added to the rules are met.
  - OR clause if you want the qualification criteria to be that at least one of the conditions added to the rules is met. This change applies across all condition blocks. Note :
    - By default, the AND clause is selected, which means that all conditions added to the rules must be met for them to qualify.
    - You can change the clause applied to the rules at any time in the following ways:
    - From the condition clause dropdown.
    - From the condition block tree structure.

5. Choose a condition from the Select condition dropdown. For more information, see Conditions in Automation rules.

Note:

- The SFDC - Opportunity condition is available only if Automation Suite 2.0 is enabled on your learning site. For more information, contact Mindtickle Support or your Customer Success Manager (CSM).
- You can create an automation rule based on Mindtickle conditions or Salesforce conditions. You can not combine Mindtickle and Salesforce conditions in a single rule. This step further explains the rules creation process using an example of a Mindtickle condition and a Salesforce condition .

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Setup > Site Setup > Create a new rule:
i. Select the ILT module from the module dropdown and then select At least one of the selected sessions from the module/Session dropdown.

ii. In the Select sessions pop-up, select the session from the available list. Alternatively, use the Search field to search for a particular session. You can search for a session by its name, instructor name, or date range.

You can add multiple sessions in a single rules condition.

Note: When multiple sessions are added to a rules condition, and the learner’s status on any of the sessions is as defined in the rules condition, the learner meets the rules criteria.

iii. If the condition is Status on module, set the status the learner should achieve. Choose from Enrolled, Attended, Did not attend, or Waitlisted.Note: When the rules is created based on the Enrolled status, a learner whose attendance is marked as Attended (now or in the future) also qualifies per the criteria.

iv. If the condition is Score on module, set the absolute score the learner should achieve.Note:

a. When creating session-based rules, by default, the Absolute score is selected as the conditional parameter, and the option Percentage score is disabled. You cannot set the condition based on the Percentage score.

b. If the selected condition is Status on module or Certification on module, and the status parameter is set for a particular module, you can hover over it and select Apply status to all to apply the selected status to all similar modules.

c. When adding multiple conditions and modules to a rule, ensure you select the right condition parameters for each module.

For more information on how to activate a saved rule, see Activate a rule.

Note:

- A rule starts operating only after it is activated.
- Asset recommendation through rules depends on the sync frequency set between SFDC and Mindtickle. Currently, the assets recommendation is updated every hour. For example, if the deal stage qualifies for a rule, the recommended assets start appearing in SFDC once the sync happens.
- There may be a delay between activating an automation rule and the execution of the specified action. While the Automation Suite is designed to process rules promptly, several factors, including system load, network conditions, rules complexity, dependencies on external systems, and queue size, can influence the timing of the action. We recommend considering this potential delay when setting up and relying on Automation rules for critical tasks or time-sensitive actions. If you have specific timing requirements, we encourage you to plan accordingly to ensure the desired outcomes are achieved within your expected timeframe.

- All users who qualify now and in the future

Note: If the rules is activated for Only those users who qualify in the future, the Sync icon appears against it. Clicking Sync will apply the rules to all existing learners. This applies only to user-based rules created in Mindtickle.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Setup > Site Setup > Create a new rule > Example 3: Salesforce Opportunity based rule (Recommend assets based on attributes):
In the following example, if an opportunity qualifies by meeting the set conditions, the corresponding action is taken automatically. Here, the action is to recommend assets based on the following criteria: Attributes, Hubs, Usage, and Asset type. For this example, the action is to recommend assets based on asset attributes. This rule recommends only those assets that match the attributes selected in the action.

Condition:

If SFDC - Opportunity field Stage (StageName) is ProspectingANDAccount Industry (Industry) is Technology

THEN

Action: Then Recommend assets with criteria - Attributes - Prospecting Guide and 5 more.

The backend logic around asset attribute selection in the rule action as follows:

- Within the same category , selected attributes are now evaluated with an " OR " condition. Example: Selecting Attribute1 and Attribute2 within the same category will be interpreted as "Attribute1 OR Attribute2."
- Across categories , selected attributes are evaluated with an " AND " condition. Example: Selecting Attribute1 from Category A and Attribute2 from Category B will be interpreted as "Attribute1 AND Attribute2."

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Setup > Site Setup > View a rule:
All saved rules are displayed in the list of rules on the Automation rules tab.

If more than one condition is added to the rule, by default, the first condition is visible. To view all conditions, hover over View all conditions. All conditions added to the rule are displayed in the pop-up that appears.

A rule's status automatically changes to Invalid if one or more entities (modules, groups, series, profile fields, roles, or opportunity fields) in the rule condition are archived or deleted.

If all entities in the rule condition are archived or deleted, No Conditions and the Invalid rules icon are displayed instead of the rule in the Conditions column.

You can update the rule conditions in an invalid rule and activate it later. For more information, see Edit a Rule. Once the rule conditions are updated, and the rule is no longer invalid, you can choose to Activate it based on your use case.

To view the rule details, such as its status (active or inactive), description, creator, date of creation, conditions, and actions:

1. On the Automation rules tab, click More options and click the View rule option. Alternatively, click anywhere on the rule in the list of rules. The Manage rule pop-up appears, listing the rule details. If the rule is invalid, the Manage rule page provides details about why the rule is invalid.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Setup > Site Setup > Edit a rule:
1. On the Automation rules tab, click More options and click the View rule option. Alternatively, click anywhere on the rule in the list of rules. The Manage rule page appears.
2. Based on your requirement, perform the following actions:
  1. Add or edit the rule description To add a description for an existing rule, click Add Description and enter a description in the text field that appears. To edit an existing description, click on it, and enter the new description in the text field that appears. Click Save on the Manage rule page to add or update the rule description. Note : The rule description is added or updated once you click Save on the Manage rule page.
  2. Modify conditions or actions You can modify a rule by changing the condition, changing the conditional operators, adding modules to an existing condition, adding or changing roles in an existing condition, changing modules in an existing condition , adding or changing opportunity fields in an existing condition, adding a new condition, or deleting an existing condition. Similarly, you can modify a rule, by changing the action added in the rule, adding modules to an existing action, changing modules in an existing action, adding or changing recommended assets in an action, adding or changing a role in an existing condition, adding a new action, or deleting an existing action. For more information, see Steps 4 to 9 of Create a new rule .
  3. Change the modules in a condition You can change the modules in an existing rule condition. In this way, you can update a rule without modifying or deleting the condition itself. To do so, click the module in the rule condition and select the new module from the dropdown that appears. Tip : To filter the list based on modules belonging to a particular series, and further, to a particular section in the series, select the series and section from the Series and Section dropdowns, respectively. Alternatively, enter the module name in the Search Modules field and select it from the search results. Note : Modules that are already added to a condition block in the rule, are greyed out in the dropdown and cannot be selected as a replacement. However, the same modules can be added to a different condition block in the same rule. The old module is replaced with the new one.
  4. Change the opportunity fields in a condition You can change the opportunity fields in an existing rule condition. In this way, you can update a rule without modifying or deleting the condition itself. To do so, click the field in the rule condition and select the new field from the dropdown that appears. Alternatively, enter the field name in Select field and choose it from the search results. Note : Fields that are already added to a condition block in the rule are greyed out in the dropdown and cannot be selected as a replacement. However, the same fields can be added to a different condition block in the same rule. The old module is replaced with the new one.
3. Update the condition parameters for the new module or opportunity and click Save . A confirmation message is displayed once the rule is updated and saved successfully.
4. If the updated rule is inactive, you can activate it from the Manage rule page by clicking Activate . For more information on how to activate it from the Automation rules tab, see Activate a rule . If the updated rule is active, you can choose to apply it to all learners who currently qualify by meeting all the conditions. To do so, click Apply to existing users , and click Apply . Note : This is applicable only to user-based rules.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Setup > Site Setup > Create a similar rule:
You can use an existing rule as a template to create a new rule. When you create a rule similar to an existing rule, a copy of the rule is created. You can edit or modify the conditions or actions in the copy based on your requirements and save it as a new rule. To create a similar rule:

1. On the Automation rules tab, click More options against the rule you want to copy and click the Create similar rule option. In the New rule panel that appears, the conditions and actions from the template rule are already added to the new rule. Based on your requirement, you can add more conditions and actions to it. Note : When you create a similar rule, only a copy of the rule is presented. It is important that you edit or modify the actions and/or conditions in the copied rule as two identical rules cannot be configured for a module.
2. Follow Steps 4 to 8 if you want to create and activate the rule immediately. If you want to create a rule now and activate it later, follow Steps 4 to 6 and then refer to the Activate a rule section.
chunks.body:
You can use an existing rule as a template to create a new rule. When you create a rule similar to an existing rule, a copy of the rule is created. You can edit or modify the conditions or actions in the copy based on your requirements and save it as a new rule. To create a similar rule:

1. On the Automation rules tab, click More options against the rule you want to copy and click the Create similar rule option. In the New rule panel that appears, the conditions and actions from the template rule are already added to the new rule. Based on your requirement, you can add more conditions and actions to it. Note : When you create a similar rule, only a copy of the rule is presented. It is important that you edit or modify the actions and/or conditions in the copied rule as two identical rules cannot be configured for a module.
2. Follow Steps 4 to 8 if you want to create and activate the rule immediately. If you want to create a rule now and activate it later, follow Steps 4 to 6 and then refer to the Activate a rule section.

chunks.title: Create and manage automation rules

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Setup > Site Setup > Deactivate a rule:
In order to stop a rule from operating, you can deactivate it. To deactivate a rule:

1. On the Automation rules tab, click the More options icon against the rule you want to deactivate and click the Deactivate rule option.
2. In the pop-up that appears, click Deactivate . Alternatively, select the rule from the Automation rules tab. The Manage rule panel appears. Click Deactivate .
3. In the pop-up that appears, click Deactivate .

A confirmation message appears on the screen once the rule is deactivated successfully.

Note: Deactivation will not delete the rule. To permanently delete the rule, see the Delete a rule section.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Setup > Site Setup > Delete a rule:
To delete a rule permanently:

1. On the Automation rules tab, click More options against the rule you want to delete and click the Delete rule option. Alternatively, select the rule from the Automation rules tab. Click Delete on the Manage rule panel that appears.

A confirmation message appears on the screen once the rule is deleted successfully.

  - The actions specified in the rule are not triggered moving forward.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > Admin:
This article explains the steps to make a call recording from Call AI available for content creation in Mindtickle.

1. Sign in to your Call AI interface using your Mindtickle credentials or email address registered with Call AI.

2. Go to the Recordings tab from the left navigation panel and click any of the following tabs:

- All recordings
- My recordings
- Shares
- Bookmarks

Note: Both admin and reps can make a call available for content creation. Admins can view the list of calls made available for content, but the reps cannot view the list. However, the reps can go to individual calls and see the status.

3. Hover over a recording you want to make available for content creation and click the More Options icon.

4. Click the Enable for content creation option.

Note:

- If you cannot view the Enable for content creation option, please contact your Customer Success Manager (CSM).
- The Enable for content creation option is disabled for dialer and audio recordings.

5. Enabling a recording for content creation adds the recording to the Training calls, accessible from the Call AI. The recording is also made available as a learning object in Courses and Quick updates. Click the Confirm button to proceed.

For the list of file types that can be uploaded as content, see What type of content files does Mindtickle support.

6. If you want to create a snippet of the recording and add only the snippet to the Content Center, click the Toggle Switch and move the cursor or enter the timestamps in the From and To range input boxes. This way, only the selected snippet becomes available for use as a learning object in Courses and Quick Updates. Click the Enable button to proceed.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > Admin > Share a call recording from the Recordings page:
1. Click theShare icon on a call recording and select Within your organization or Outside your organization.

2. Click the Link icon to create and copy the recording link for seamless sharing:

- If you copy the link for Within your organization sharing, users can view the recording per the recording link access setting ( Restricted or Organization ).

- If the access is set to Restricted , users with prior access permissions can view the recording using the link.
- If the access is set to Organization , any internal user can view the recording using the link.
- If you copy the link for Outside your organization sharing, anyone can view and download the recording using the link.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > Admin > Share a call recording from the Recordings page > Share a call within your organization:
This option enables you to share the call recording any user within your organization.

1. On the Share within your organization pop-up that opens:

- You can Copy link of the recording and easily share it within your organization through email, group chat, or text. Users can access the link based on the recording link access setting ( Restricted or Organization ). Click the Down arrow to modify the access to users in your organization.

- Add the user’s name or email address with whom you want to share the call. You can add multiple users. Call AI sends an email notification with the recording link when you share the call.
- When adding a user's email address, Call AI populates the list of existing users and provides prompts if the user’s email address is unavailable or the email ID is not present within the organization. For more information, see Add users to share the call recording within your organization .
- Optionally, you can add a personal message to summarize the call. The message is visible under the Private Messages section of the call.
- You can choose to share the entire call or only a snippet of the call with the user. You can share the same call or snippet multiple times. Click the Snippet option and move the cursor or enter the timestamps in the From and To range input boxes. Note:
- Call AI plays the snippet you created when you share it. However, the user can navigate to other areas of the call.
- While sharing a snippet, you must select a portion of a call. The Share button is disabled if you select the entire call duration.
- The snippet duration must be a minimum of 30 seconds.

2. Click Share to proceed.

- In Share using email , Call AI automatically populates a list of external participants who do not have access to the call. Select the participants from the list with whom you want to share the call. You can also add the external participant’s name or email address with whom you want to share the call. These participants will receive an email notification with the recording link when you share the call. For more information, see Add users to share the call recording outside your organization .

After you share the snippet, it takes 5 to 10 minutes to reflect at the recipient’s end. Note: The snippet duration must be a minimum of 30 seconds.
- To share the entire call, select the Full recording option. By default, the share snippet option is selected.
- You can choose not to include the call transcript when sharing a call externally via email. Click the Include recording transcript toggle switch to turn it off. By default, Call AI shares the transcript with the recording.
- Additionally, you can enable call download or add an expiry date to the recording link.

2. Click Share to proceed.

The number of users with whom the recording is shared is displayed in the Shared with field.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > Admin:
This article explains the steps performed by admins to share a call recording from within a course or a quick update.

1. On the course or quick update, click Add learning objects.

2. On the Add learning objects screen, select the Call AI recordings option.

Note: If you do not see the Call AI recordings option, please contact your Customer Success Manager (CSM).

3. On the Select a Call Recording pop-up, select the recording you want to include in the course or quick update and click Create.

Note:

- The list of recordings that appears depends on the number of recordings that have been made available for content creation.
- Once the recording is available for content creation, even if the recording is deleted from Call AI, it will still be available in the course or quick update module in Mindtickle.

You can filter the call recordings based on the Themes or apply additional CRM filters by clicking the More Filters button. Alternatively, you can also search for a call recording from the search bar.

The selected call recording is displayed.

3. Click Tags to assign tags. For more information, see How to Apply Tags to Your Modules.

4. Choose to enable or disable Factopedia by toggling the switch from the Factopedia tab.

If Enabled, you can add supporting information related to the main content in the form of text, multimedia, or handouts. For more information, see Best practices of Factopedia.

5. For information on enabling Transcription and CC capability for your uploaded videos, see Overview of transcriptions and closed captions.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Setup > Site Setup:
As an admin, you can access the admin site using your company’s Single Sign-On (SSO) feature. If your organization has enabled SSO for your learning site, the same credentials are used to sign in to the admin site; therefore, you no longer need a separate username and password to access it.

Note: If SSO is not enabled, your organization must set up an integration with an identity provider (IdP). For assistance, contact Mindtickle Support.

To sign in via SSO:

1. Enter the URL admin.mindtickle.com in a new tab of your web browser. You are directed to the Mindtickle admin sign-in page.
2. Enter your learning site URL and click Continue . Note : If you do not know the learning site URL, contact your Customer Success Manager (CSM) or Mindtickle Support .
3. Click the applicable SSO option to continue the sign-in process. Note : The SSO options available to you depend on the identity providers (IdPs) that your organization has integrated with Mindtickle . Once you have successfully signed in, you are directed to the admin site homepage. Note : See What to do if a user cannot log in to Mindtickle via SSO? if you face any issues while logging in via SSO. If your organization uses multiple learning sites, you can switch between the admin site interfaces of different learning sites. However, you can only switch to learning sites that you have access to and that belong to the same organization. To access a learning site belonging to another organization, you need to sign in to that learning site. For more information, see How to switch between the admin site interface of multiple learning sites?

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Course and Quick Update > Course details page:
When you click a course module — whether from a series page, modules page, homepage widgets, or series overview page widgets — you are first directed to the course details page (also known as the course overview page). The course details page provides a comprehensive summary of the course requirements and structure.

It typically includes:

- Course description: A summary of the subject matter and specific learning objectives.
- Course outline: A structured list of all levels, topics, and learning objects within the course, including their associated points, formats (e.g., PPT, PDF, video), and completion status.
- Your progress: A visual indicator showing the percentage of the course you have completed.
- Badges up for grabs: A display of any digital credentials you can earn upon completion.
- Additional details: Essential information such as the maximum score, due date, certificate of completion criteria, and estimated completion time.
- Module rating : A section where you can rate the course once you complete it.

Reviewing the outline before you begin helps you familiarize yourself with the course structure and expectations.

Note: If enabled by your admin, a course overview video appears here to provide context before you start.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Course and Quick Update > Course details page > Start or resume course:
From the course overview page, you can enter the learning environment in two ways:

- Select a specific learning object: If you wish to access a particular piece of content immediately, you can click any item directly within the course outline. This bypasses the course map and takes you directly to that learning object in the learning view. See the " Learning view " section.
- Use the primary action button: This button changes based on your current status. Clicking any of these buttons will first take you to the course map, providing a visual overview of the course structure and your progress before you begin or continue:
  - Start course: Appears if you have not yet begun the training.
  - Resume course: Appears if you have partially completed the course, allowing you to pick up exactly where you left off.
  - Reattempt course: Appears after you have finished the course, allowing you to review the course materials again.

See the "Course map" section.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Course and Quick Update > Course map:
When you click the primary action buttons (like Start course or Resume course), or when you click the Next topic button after finishing a section, the platform displays the course map. Additionally, if you are viewing a learning object and click the Back button in the top-left corner of the header, it returns you to this map.

This map is a visual representation of your journey and the entire course structure:

- Breadcrumb navigation: Use the links at the top-left to go back to the homepage or series.
- Course details button: Click this button below the breadcrumbs to return to the course overview page.
- Score and badges: View your current points and progress toward the maximum score in the top-right area.
- Top bar features: Access learning tools using the icons in the top-right corner, including handouts, discussions, and the Hall of Fame leaderboard.
- Course topics: The central area displays a visual path where topics are arranged sequentially. Your current active topic is highlighted, while future topics may display a padlock icon, indicating they are locked until you reach them.
- Course pages: If your course is divided into multiple sections (e.g., "Week 1", "Week 2"), use the toggle at the bottom of the screen to navigate between them.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Course and Quick Update > Course map > Course hierarchy and progression:
Content in the platform is organized into a clear hierarchy: levels contain topics, and each topic contains one or more learning objects (such as videos, documents, or quizzes).

Transitioning to the course map between topics is intentional for several reasons:

- Maintaining orientation: The map highlights your current position, ensuring you understand how the completed material fits into the overall curriculum.
- Providing control: It allows you to choose whether to proceed to the next sequential topic or revisit a previous section for review.
- Preventing accidental progression: The map serves as a natural pause, ensuring you are ready to move forward rather than being automatically advanced.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Course and Quick Update > Course map > How to progress to the next topic:
To move through the course efficiently, follow these steps:

1. Complete the current learning object (e.g., watch the full video or submit the quiz).
2. Click the Next button.
3. When the course map appears, select the next accessible topic in the sequence directly on the visual path.
4. The system will then open the first learning object within that new topic.

Tip: View the course map as a helpful navigation checkpoint rather than an interruption. It functions like a dynamic table of contents that helps you stay oriented throughout your learning journey.

If the topic is a quiz, you may have access to gamification helpers:

- Lifelines: Eliminates incorrect choices. You can use a maximum of two per question. How it works: Your total lifeline pool decreases when used, but increases by three for every badge you earn.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Readiness Index (RI):
There are two benchmarks in Readiness Index (RI):

- Competency benchmark
- Readiness Index (RI) benchmark

When you configure benchmarks for your competencies (competency benchmark), you get an individual benchmark score for each competency. Based on this, you get the aggregated benchmark for the overall Readiness Index (RI benchmark). These become your benchmarks for ideal rep behaviors and revenue performance.

The benchmark cutoffs are configured through the “Benchmark configuration” setting in RI.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Readiness Index (RI) > Competency benchmark:
For each competency, the competency benchmark is the average of the competency score achieved by those sales reps whose business metric and RI scores are greater than the cutoff. This number denotes the benchmark for that competency.

The benchmark cutoffs are configured through the “Benchmark configuration” setting in RI. In this setting, you need to configure the cutoff numbers for business metric and RI to define your organization’s best quadrant. Users (sales reps) whose business metric and RI scores are greater than the cutoff are considered for benchmarking calculation.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Readiness Index (RI) > RI benchmark:
RI benchmark is an aggregation of the benchmarks for individual competencies. It helps you identify what good looks like across competencies and what is the ideal RI score, which is based on the competencies and top reps that you have identified.

The overall RI benchmark for your organization is based on the benchmarks configured through the “Benchmark configuration” setting in RI. The average RI of the sales reps considered becomes the RI benchmark for the organization.

Note: If no users have qualified the RI benchmark cutoffs, the competency benchmarks are not calculated and, therefore, no insights are displayed.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Readiness Index (RI) > Configure Benchmarks:
Using the quadrant chart in the Correlate tab, you can identify your best quadrant with the best performance (sales reps with high RI and high business outcomes, such as sales). Based on the scores achieved by these sales reps, you can define the cutoff numbers for the RI benchmark. These are the sales reps whose behavior and skills you would want to replicate across the organization.

The benchmark cutoffs are defined through the “Benchmark configuration” setting in RI. In this setting, you need to configure the cutoff numbers for business metric and RI to define your organization’s best quadrant. For information on how to configure the benchmark cutoffs in the “Benchmark configuration” setting, see Configure Competencies, Benchmarks, and Visualization Settings in Readiness Index.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Readiness Index (RI) > Example scenario:
After the benchmark cutoff configuration is set, RI shows your best quadrant of high-performing sales reps in the quadrant chart. Based on these sales reps’ performance in each competency, each competency’s benchmark is calculated in the background.

Now let’s understand how competency benchmarks are calculated based on the RI benchmark cutoff configuration. For example, you have five sales reps and three competencies, and you have configured the RI benchmark cutoffs as follows:

- Business metric cutoff (on x-axis) = 70
- RI cutoff (on y-axis) = 60

| Sales reps | Competencies and scores | Business metric score (cutoff = 70) | RI score (cutoff = 60) |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  | C1 | C2 | C3 |  |  |
| S1 | 25 | 70 | 80 | 75 | 70 |
| S2 | 30 | 55 | 60 | 70 | 80 |
| S3 | 40 | 64 | 34 | 40 | 45 |
| S4 | 45 | 77 | 20 | 50 | 76 |
| S5 | 50 | 30 | 42 | 75 | 32 |
| Competency benchmark * | 27.5 | 62.5 | 70 |  |  |

* For each competency, the competency benchmark is the average of the competency score achieved by those sales reps whose business metric and RI scores were above the cutoff.

This example helps you understand the following:

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Readiness Index (RI) > Example scenario:
- Among your sales reps, you can identify which competencies they are good at and not good at. With this information, you can drive your sales reps to focus on the respective competencies they are not good at.
- S1 and S2 are your best sales reps whose behavior you would want to replicate and see in the rest of your sales reps.
- You need not focus on competency “C1” because its benchmark is so low that it would not reflect in their RI even if sales reps have this competency.
- Sales reps S3, S4, and S5 need to work on competency C3 and the sales rep S5 on competency C2 to achieve the benchmark cutoff scores. Essentially, sales reps need to work on the competencies where they are below the competency benchmark.

Once you have viewed a learning object, click Next to proceed. If the Skip option is enabled, you may skip the content, but please note:

- Zero score: You will receive 0 points for any skipped content or questions.
- No retries: You cannot re-attempt skipped questions.

Helpers and tips:

- Hints: Use the Hint button (if available) to get a suggestion that leads to the right answer.
- Mute audio: Click at the bottom-left to mute sound. This setting persists throughout the module.
- Screen experience: We recommend closing the left panel while attempting questions for a better view.

Scoring: Every content object has an assigned score displayed at the top-right. You receive full points only upon completion. Earning specific scores may award you badges. See What is a Master Badge, Streak Badge, Proficiency Level, and Hall of Fame to learn more.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Reference:
The Export button in Analytics allows you to export reports and dashboards that contained complete and detailed data about their performance and engagement. The Export functionality is available across various pages in Analytics. The CSV report is emailed to you and can be downloaded from the link in the email.

The Export functionality allows you to export a single report as well as multiple reports using Bulk Export.

Some reports provide Learner-wise data while others provide Learners’ performance data with respect to Modules, Managers, and so on.For example, in Series analytics, you can get two kinds of Learner reports for a particular Series:

- Modules tab: The exported report provides data of all Learners’ combined performance for each Module.
- Learners tab: The exported report provides data of each Learner’s performance for their Modules.

Depending on the page from which you use the Export Report functionality, you can export either all Learners’ or an individual Learner’s report.

Important: The reports that you export from Mindtickle Analytics contain information protected under privacy laws. Please do not circulate any exported report unless you have verified that the recipients are authorized to receive it.

- Learners tab: The exported report provides data of each Learner’s performance for their Modules.

Depending on the page from which you use the Export Report functionality, you can export either all Learners’ or an individual Learner’s report.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Reference > Export all learners’ report:
You can export a report of all Learners from various pages in analytics. The total number of Learners that are included in the exported report depends on various factors, such as the page on which you are, hierarchy setup, number of direct reports, number of Learners, and applied filters.

For example, in Manager analytics > Hierarchy Based Reports > Individual View tab:

- Under Only Direct Reports : The exported report provides data of only those Learners who are directly reporting to the selected manager.
- Under All Learners : The exported report provides data of all Learners who are directly or indirectly reporting to the selected manager.

The Export Report functionality is available only for certain reports across various analytics pages. Wherever this functionality is available, it is indicated by either the Export button or a button with “Export” in the name (such as the “Download/Export” button in Manager analytics). Click the button to export the Learners’ report. The report is sent to the email address that you provide in the Export Report pop-up.

SCORM reports

Module rating and feedback report

Note: The Bulk Export functionality is not available for this report. Therefore, you cannot export this report for multiple modules at once.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Reference > Export reports in bulk:
Using the Bulk Export functionality within the Export button, you can export the report of a particular page (tab) for multiple modules of the same type, as well as series and learners. Any filters that you apply on the page before exporting are considered for all selected modules/series learners.

Note: The Bulk Export functionality is released as a Beta as it is available only for some reports in Analytics, not all. However, the functionality is generally available (GA) and has no known issues.

You can export a report in bulk for up to 10 modules/series/learners. The exported report is sent via email and you can include up to 10 individuals as recipients. The exported report can be downloaded using the link in the email within 7 days.

Note: The modules and series that are available for selection is based on your access to the content for your role. For example, if an Enablement Admin has access to only 7 out of the 50 series on a Learning Site, they can export the report of the Learners tab for only 7 series. Additionally, your access to a series requires that you are a collaborator for the series and have the “view_series_analytics” permission for the series.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Reference > Export reports in bulk > Exporting a report in bulk:
This section explains how to export a report for multiple modules/series/learners.

With Bulk Export, you can export this tab’s report for multiple Quick-Updates of your choice (up to 10). Filters applied on the page before exporting are applicable for all selected modules. This report is mailed to the recipients in a consolidated .CSV format.

Note: As an example, this section describes how to export the Learners tab report in a Quick-Update with a few filters applied and for 6 Quick-Updates.

To export a report for multiple modules/series/learners:

1. In Analytics, navigate to the report page (tab) that you want to export in bulk. It can be for any of the pages listed in the Applicable reports section.
2. On the report page, apply one or more filters if you want to export the report with filters applied. Filters will be applicable for all Quick-Update modules that you will be selecting in a later step.

1. Click the Export button and then click Bulk Export in the pop-up.

1. On the Bulk Export screen that appears, perform the following and then click Export:
  - Select modules to include in the report: Click the box and select up to 10 Quick-Updates from the list. Selected modules appear below the box.Similarly, for exporting series and learner reports, you select series and learners respectively.
  - Add report recipients: Enter the email addresses of up to 10 individuals to whom you want to send the exported report. The report is mailed to the recipients in a consolidated .CSV format.

The Selected Report and Filters section displays an overview of the specific report page (tab) that you have selected to export along with the applied filters, if you have applied any.

This article explains how you can scope a public series to make it visible to specific learners. To learn more about the series, see Create a series. Setting the scope of a public series helps show learners the most relevant content.

Note: You can allow learners to view module relevance for a scoped public series without subscribing to it. To enable it for your learning site, contact Mindtickle Support.

To set the scope of a public series,

1. Sign in to the admin site.
2. On the left navigation bar, click Training and select Series .

The Series page is displayed.

3. Click on a series to modify its scope.

4. Under the Settings, click the General tab and scroll down to the Visibility section.

The following options are available to configure the scope of a Public series:

- Visible to all learners
- Visible to the following learners only (Scoped)
- Visible to all learners except (Scoped )

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Series > Visible to the following learners only (Scoped):
Learners who fulfill the set conditions can view and access the series. You can set the conditions based on the profile field or groups.

1. In Learners in groups , choose the groups to grant access to the series.
2. Click Add profile field . The Select Profile Field drop-down is displayed.
3. In Select Profile Field , choose the learner profile fields to set the condition for series access.

4. To view the number of learners who have access to the series, click Count learners with access.

The number of learners with access is displayed.

Click Refresh to view the latest number of learners.

5. After selecting the profile field, choose the values to apply the condition for in Select values.

For example, if Region is selected in the Select Profile Field drop-down, you can choose the regions applicable to this condition in the Select values drop-down. This ensures that only learners who belong to the selected regions can view the series.

6. Click Add filters to add a condition with the AND operator. This filter applies to all the conditions while filtering the learners.

For example, suppose you have added the first condition as Department = Sales 3, Sales 4, and the second condition as learners in Groups = Setting. This implies that ONLY those learners whose Department is Sales 3 and Sales 4 AND who belong to the Setting Group can view and access this series.

Note: There is no limit on the number of filters applied. However, each filter narrows down the user set. Thus, use filters appropriately to get desired results.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Series > Additional considerations:
- If your learning site is configured not to allow a sequentially locked series to be converted into a public series. You cannot convert those series into a scoped public series.
- If the learners have subscribed to a public series, and later, it is scoped:
  - they can still access the series from the Assigned section if they are out of scope
  - they can still access the series from the Subscribed section if they are part of the scope

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Readiness Index (RI):
The Scorecard tab in the Learner’s Overall Report provides a comprehensive view of the sales readiness of each of your sales reps (Learners).

Through the scorecard, admins can see a complete report card of a sales rep in the quadrant and spider charts. The quadrant chart displays progress of the rep’s performance across the latest four cadences. The spider chart displays a distribution of the rep’s competencies contributing to the organization’s RI and their comparison. This helps you identify the best and the worst performing competencies and how they have changed. In the Activity Timeline, the scorecard displays a list of modules assigned to the rep that will help improve their RI.

Note: This tab is visible only if Readiness Index (RI) is enabled for your organization. To learn more about the Readiness Index, contact your Customer Success Manager.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Readiness Index (RI) > Scorecard settings:
The scorecard page displays analytics data based on the following selections:

- View and compare growth: Select the cadence (Weekly or Monthly). With the cadence, you can choose to view comparative RI data by a weekly or monthly cycle, which can be selected in the Viewing RI as of option.
  - Monthly: The latest month’s RI is compared to last month’s RI.
  - Weekly: The latest week’s RI is compared to last week’s RI.
- Viewing RI as of: Select a date as of which you want to view the data by the cadence selected in the View and compare growth option. For example, if you select your cadence to be monthly and view data as of June 1, 2022 , then the quadrant chart displays data for the last four monthly cadences: June 1, May 1, April 1, and March 1.
- Correlate RI with: Select the business metric with which you want to correlate the RI data for the rep.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Readiness Index (RI) > Quadrant chart:
In this section, you can view the sales rep’s performance and progress, in terms of their RI score, across the four quadrants for the last four cadences. The chart displays data by correlating the rep’s RI score with the selected business metric. This helps you understand how their performance is trending and use insights and recommendations to improve their performance.

The cadences can be weekly or monthly depending on your selection in the View and compare growth dropdown menu in the upper-right corner. The data is displayed based on the date selected in the Viewing RI as of option.

Hover over the bubbles to see the rep’s RI and business metric scores.

The quadrant chart provides the following information and options:

Rep’s progress across quadrants over time

The chart displays data for the latest cadence by default. Additionally, it provides the following options:

- Show cohort members in quadrant: Use this option to view where the rep lies with respect to peers in the cohort (RI group). Note: You can disable this option in RI Settings > Visualizations > Miscellaneous .
- Show last 4 weeks/months data together: Use this option to view the rep’s data for the last four cadences at once, to understand the learner’s progress and performance over the last 4 weeks/months. It displays the option for weeks or months depending on your selection in the View and compare growth option in the upper-right corner.

Chart type

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Readiness Index (RI) > Competency distribution:
This section provides a distribution of competencies contributing to your organization’s Readiness Index (RI) and their comparison. This helps you identify the top and the bottom competencies and how they have changed.

This section provides the following information:

- Competencies above the benchmark: Lists three competencies where the sales rep has performed above the company benchmark. Provides the sales rep’s score in each competency and the positive difference compared to the benchmark.
- Competencies below the benchmark: Lists three competencies where the sales rep has performed below the company benchmark. Provides the sales rep’s score in each competency and the negative difference compared to the benchmark.

Competency Distribution chart: The chart provides company benchmark insights in green. Hover over a competency to view the benchmark score and how it compares with the achieved score for a particular period. For example, if the company benchmark for the “Negotiation” competency is 96.5 while your sales rep’s scores for the selected period are not good — this helps you understand that your sales reps need to focus on this competency to achieve the benchmark cutoff score.

Click the Chart Type drop-down to change the chart type: spider chart or bar chart. For the bar chart, you get the option to sort the chart by competency % score (highest first or lowest first).

In the spider or bar chart, hover over the chart and click a competency to view the sales rep’s performance for a particular competency with respect to the Modules that have an impact on the competency. This information is displayed under the Activity Timeline section, with the respective competency selected.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > My Analytics:
With the Share functionality in Mindtickle analytics, you can share analytics reports and dashboards with individual users (admins and managers) or user groups or both at once. It also provides an option to notify recipients by email and remind them as needed. Plus, you can copy shareable links for both admin and manager views of the shared reports and share it via chat, email, or other communication channels.

Just as you (site owners and enablement admins) can share reports with other admins and managers, other admins can share reports with you. You can even share a customized report — that is, apply filters and sorting options before sharing the report. All filters and sorting applied by you are retained for the recipients so that they see the same customized view of the report that you intended to share. It is retained for all reports except the ones listed in the July 2024 release notes.

You can view and manage shared reports from the Shared section in the analytics sidebar. It lists all reports that are shared by you and shared with you.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > My Analytics > Overview:
1. Which reports can be shared?

You can share any report in Mindtickle analytics with the Share functionality, available in the upper-right corner of the report. The following reports and dashboards can be shared:

- Reports: Series, module, group, tag, manager (hierarchy based and relationship field based), coaching (session and reviewer reports), and self-serve reports.
- Dashboards: All dashboards, such as home, adoption, and also custom dashboards created by you. However, the engagement and revenue impact dashboards are not shareable.

2. Who can share reports?

Site owners and managers can share analytics reports as they have the required permissions by default. The following permissions are available for the user who is sharing the report:

- Share Reports with Admins: Lets you share reports with other admins.
- Share Reports with Managers: Lets you share reports with other managers.

Each type of report requires specific permissions to let you share the report. For example, to share a series report, you must have the Share Reports with Admins permission. Consider the following table to know which permissions are required to share a particular type of report:

| Report type | Permissions required to share |
| --- | --- |
| Series | Share Reports with Admins(BOOKMARK_REPORT_FOR_ADMINS) |
| Module |  |
| Coaching (Session and Reviewer) |  |
| Group |  |
| Tag |  |
| Manager | Share Reports with Admins(BOOKMARK_REPORT_FOR_ADMINS)+Share Reports with Managers(BOOKMARK_REPORT_FOR_MANAGERS) |
| Self-serve |  |
| Dashboards |  |

Note: Site owners can share reports with all admins and managers by default, without requiring the above permissions.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > My Analytics > Overview:
3. With whom?

You can share analytics reports with individual users (admins and managers) as well as user groups.

You can share a specific report only with the users (admins and managers) who have necessary permissions to access the report. In other words, while sharing a report, only those users are listed with whom you can share the report. For example, to share a series report for a series called “Platform onboarding”, you can share it only with those users who have access to this series. A user can have access to the series in one of the following ways:

- Series permission: Through the Series Reports permission, which provides them access to all series.
- Collaborator access: By virtue of being added as a collaborator to a specific series.

For more information, see Roles and permissions in Mindtickle.

It is retained for all reports except the ones listed in the July 2024 release notes.
2. On the report page, click the Share button in the header. The following image considers a coaching session report as an example.

- Add a note: Add a note/description for the report that provides context to the recipients on the report you are sharing. This note/description will appear in the recipient’s Shared > Shared with me section for the shared report.
- Send email notification: Select this to notify the recipients by email that a report has been shared with them. From the email, recipients can click the View report button to open the report.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > My Analytics > View and manage shared reports > Shared by me:
The Shared by me section lists reports and dashboards that you have shared with other admins and managers. They are listed in two separate tabs: Report and Dashboard.

Let’s understand the Report tab in detail; similarly you can explore the Dashboard tab to view dashboards shared by you.

The reports shared by you are listed in four columns:

- Share name: Name and description/note for the report, added while sharing the report.
- Report type: The type of the report that you shared. For example, series report, hierarchy-based manager report, or self-serve report.
- Shared with: The total number of individual users and groups with whom you shared the report. Click the links to view the entire list of users and groups.
- Shared on: Time and date when you shared the report.

The data is sorted by the Shared on column, with the most recently shared reports appearing at the top. Use search and the Report type filter at the top to list specific reports.

Click on any of the listed reports to open and view it.

Note: For manager reports (hierarchy and relationship field based), when you click to open the report, a pop-up appears listing the users (admins and managers) with whom it was shared. From the list, click the user to view the report that shows data relevant to their role. If the user has a manager role, it will show restricted data only for their team. If the user has both admin and manager roles, it will show data for the admin role.

Click More options against a report for the following options:

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > My Analytics > View and manage shared reports > Shared by me > Manage details:
Click > Manage details to modify the shared report, such as add/remove recipients (individual users and groups), remind individual users, and edit the report name and description/note. The Manage shared report pop-up appears.

Under Select tab > Select individuals, you can select more users with whom you want to share this report. Additionally, for existing users (with whom it is already shared), you can take the following actions:

Show only individuals with whom it has been shared: Toggle this switch ON to view only those users with whom you have already shared this report.

Click the Email icon to send an email reminder to a user.

Click Remove to remove a user’s access to the report (un-share the report).

Similarly, click Select groups to select more groups with whom you want the report. For groups with whom it is already shared, you can remove their access to the report (un-share the report).

Click Next to continue. The Share details tab appears.

Here you can update the name and description (note) for the shared report, if necessary. If you added new users and groups, select the Send email notification checkbox to notify them by email.

Once done, click Update to update the shared report.

Click > Manage details to modify the shared report, such as add/remove recipients (individual users and groups), remind individual users, and edit the report name and description/note. The Manage shared report pop-up appears.

Under Select tab > Select individuals, you can select more users with whom you want to share this report. Additionally, for existing users (with whom it is already shared), you can take the following actions:

Show only individuals with whom it has been shared: Toggle this switch ON to view only those users with whom you have already shared this report.

Click the Email icon to send an email reminder to a user.

Click Remove to remove a user’s access to the report (un-share the report).

Similarly, click Select groups to select more groups with whom you want the report. For groups with whom it is already shared, you can remove their access to the report (un-share the report).

Click Next to continue. The Share details tab appears.

Here you can update the name and description (note) for the shared report, if necessary. If you added new users and groups, select the Send email notification checkbox to notify them by email.

Once done, click Update to update the shared report.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > My Analytics > View and manage shared reports > Shared with me:
The Shared with me section lists reports and dashboards that other admins have shared with. They are listed in two separate tabs: Report and Dashboard.

Let’s understand the Report tab in detail; similarly you can explore the Dashboard tab to view dashboards shared with you.

The reports shared with you are listed in four columns:

- Share name: Name and description/note for the report, which was added by other admins while sharing the report with you.
- Report type: The type of the report that you shared. For example, series report, hierarchy-based manager report, or self-serve report.
- Shared by: Name of the admin who shared the report with you.
- Shared on: Time and date when the report was shared with you.

The data is sorted by the Shared on column, with the most recently shared reports appearing at the top. Use search and the Report type filter at the top to list specific reports.

The tag appears against reports shared in the last 30 days (new reports). The new tag automatically disappears after 30 days. The tag appears against reports that you have not yet clicked to open them (unread reports). The unread tag disappears once you open the unread report.

Click on any of the listed reports to open and view it. Click More options against a report for the following options:

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Home and navigation:
The Overview dashboard, the landing page of Mindtickle Analytics, has widgets that provide insights and analytics on top platform activities. The activities are related to your users’ adoption of assigned content and their performance against it. The dashboard acts as the command center of your platform and displays data specific to your role. You can customize the widgets to further personalize this dashboard to see data more relevant to you. From most of the widgets, you can click the chart data to quickly deep-dive to the detailed reports.

The dashboard is available for Site Owners, Admins, and custom roles. On the dashboard, the number of widgets and the data in widgets that you see depends on your role and permissions. For more information, see Permissions and Access for Analytics Dashboards.

Note: Any customizations that you make to the Overview dashboard are applicable only to you and not to other users.

Other than the Overview dashboard, Analytics provides the Adoption and Performance dashboards. You can also create and view your own custom dashboards. For an overview of Analytics dashboards, see Analytics Dashboards Overview.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Home and navigation > Overview dashboard widgets:
The Overview dashboard widgets provide insights on your users’ adoption of and performance in assigned Series and Modules.

Currently widgets on the Overview dashboard are derived from the two MindTickle dashboards: Adoption and Performance. The two MindTickle dashboards have multiple widgets out of which a few important and relevant widgets are selected for Overview.

Note: The My Bookmarks widget is available only on the Overview dashboard. However, you can add it while creating a custom dashboard.

Access detailed reports from widgets:

From most of the widgets, you can quickly access relevant detailed reports. If a widget shows data for which reports are available in Analytics, you can access the corresponding reports. Click any bar in a widget to go to the relevant reports, such as Series and Module reports. For example, in the Adoption of Key Series widget, if you click the bar for a Series called “Resource Library,” you are taken to the Series report of “Resource Library.”

Download dashboards and widgets:

You can download the entire dashboard and individual widgets to your computer in a .PNG format. It instantly downloads the dashboard exactly how you see it on your screen.

To download a dashboard, click the (Download) button in the upper-right corner of the dashboard. To download a widget, hover over the widget and click the (Download) button in the upper-right corner.

The Overview dashboard has the following 12 widgets:

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Home and navigation > Overview dashboard widgets > Modules Started:
Displays the trend of how many Modules were started by your users.

The chart displays aggregated data by selected frequency: monthly, weekly, or daily view. For example, you have selected the monthly view and are viewing data for February. The chart displays data only for the modules that were started by users in February, irrespective of when the users were invited to those modules. They may have been invited in February or prior to that.

Hover over the chart to view information for each data point.

By default, the following filters and settings are applied on the widget. Edit the widget to change them:

- Applicable Filters: Public Series Data = Include Admin Assigned Only
- Default View: Data Frequency = Monthly

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Home and navigation > Overview dashboard widgets > Adoption of Key Series:

Hover over a bar to view more information on the bar data. Click any of the bars to view the detailed report. Hover over the chart legends to highlight respective data.

By default, the following filters and settings are applied on the widget. Edit the widget to change them:

- Applicable Filters:
  - Public Series Data = Include Admin Assigned Only
  - Invite Time = Last Month
- Default View: Top five Series based on the number of invitations

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Home and navigation:
The Analytics section provides a centralized location to access all key dashboards and reports related to your organization's training, performance, and engagement. To streamline navigation, dashboards and reports are grouped into seven dedicated pages. chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Home and navigation > Analytics pages and available dashboards/reports > 1. My analytics:
- Overview dashboard : Acts as a command center and the default landing page for Analytics. It displays platform activity insights and content adoption analytics using customizable widgets. Data visibility depends on your role and permissions.
- Bookmarked reports : Lists reports that you have bookmarked for personal access only. This section displays only those reports saved by you for quick access.
- Custom created reports and dashboards : Lists reports and dashboards that you have personally created. You can also quickly create new custom reports or dashboards from this section.
- Shared reports : Lists platform and custom reports that are shared by you or shared with you. The Share feature replaces the old bookmark-for-others functionality.
- Self serve reports : Provides self-service capabilities for creating and accessing customized analytics without needing support from others.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Communications > Notifications and Reminders:
This article explains how the Admins with Site Owner role can view the Email Logs.

Note: If you want the Email Logs feature to be visible to any other roles in Mindtickle, contact your Customer Success Manager or Mindtickle Support for configuration.

The logs created contain information on each email (for example, recipient name, email source, subject line, sender name, delivery status). Email Logs helps you understand how email communications are working for your Learning Site. For example, you can check statistics like how many total emails were sent in the last 60 days, how many of them got delivered, why a Learner received a particular email, did a Learner receive the invitation to a compulsory program or not, and more.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Communications > Notifications and Reminders > Export Email Logs:
You can export the email logs in .CSV format to:

- Perform detailed analysis that helps admins take corrective actions quickly.
- Store a logs backup that are about to expire.

To export email logs:

1. Click the Export logs option.Note: You can export up to 50000 logs at once. If the list of records in the email logs listing is greater than 50,000 records, the export logs button is disabled. Thus, we recommend you apply the appropriate filter to reduce the count below 50000 logs.
2. On the Export Data of Email Logs pop-up, enter the email address where you want to send the logs. By default, the email address of the logged-in user is auto-populated.Note: You can send the audit log report to only one user at a time.
3. Click Send.
4. On the confirmation message pop-up, click Done.
5. Click Download Report on the email to download the .CSV file.Note: The Download Report link is valid only 7 days from the sent date.The email contains a link to export the logs as a CSV file. The file has the following columns:
  - Receiver Name
  - Receiver Email
  - Email Type
  - Email Source
  - Series Name
  - Subject
  - Sender Email
  - Sender Name
  - Delivery Status
  - Delivered on(GMT)

Here is a snippet of the .CSV report.

chunks.title: Optional Reviewers for Missions

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Mission > Example 1:
The Admin has created a Mission with two Reviewers and set the criteria as “all”. After publishing the Mission, the Admin edits the Mission and adds one more Reviewer. In this case, the Mission is complete for the Learner only after all three Reviewers have submitted the review.

The score given to the Learner is the aggregate score of all three Reviewers.

chunks.headingPath: Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Mission > Example 1
chunks.title: Optional Reviewers for Missions

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Mission > Example 2:
The Admin creates a Mission with three Reviewers and sets the criteria as “any 2”. After publishing the Mission, the Admin edits the Mission and adds one more Reviewer (4th Reviewer). In this case, the Mission is complete for the Learner after any two Reviewers have submitted the review.

The score given to the Learner is an aggregate score of any two Reviewers who submit the feedback first. Other optional reviewers can still submit their feedback, however, it will not change the overall score for the Learner.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Mission > Example 3:
The Admin creates a Mission with three Reviewers and sets the criteria as “any 2”. The Admin also appoints one Reviewer (out of the three) as mandatory. In this case, the mission is complete for the Learner after the mandatory Reviewer, and any one Reviewer submits the review.

The score given to the Learner is an aggregate score of the mandatory Reviewer and any one Reviewer who submits the review first. Other optional reviewers can still submit their feedback, however, it will not change the overall score for the Learner.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Mission > Example 4:
The Admin creates a Mission with three Reviewers that must be appointed manually and set the criteria as “any 2”. However, after publishing the Mission, the Admin only appoints one Reviewer manually. In this case, the Mission is complete for the Learner after the one assigned Reviewer submits the review.

Later, the Admin appoints the next Reviewer, then the Mission is moved to the submitted state, and the second Reviewer can submit the feedback.

The Learner score, in this case, is calculated as follows:

- If only one Reviewer is appointed manually, then the score is based on first Reviewer feedback, and the Mission is marked complete.
- Later, if the second Reviewer is manually appointed and submits the review, the score is revised to an aggregate score of the first and second reviewer.

chunks.title: Optional Reviewers for Missions

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Mission > Example 5:
The Admin creates a mission with four Reviewers and sets the criteria as “any 3”. The Admin also appoints one Reviewer (out of the four) as mandatory. In this case:

- If the mandatory Reviewer and any two Reviewers submit the review, the Mission is complete for the Learner.
- If any of the three Reviewers (one mandatory and two optional) assign re-attempt for the Learner, the Learner must re-attempt the Mission.
- If the three Reviewers (one mandatory and two optional) submit the review and the Mission is complete for the Learner, and then the fourth Reviewer assigns a re-attempt, then it is not considered.
- If the three Reviewers (one mandatory and two optional) submit the review and the Mission is complete for the Learner, then the score from the fourth Reviewer is not considered.
- The score given to the Learner is an aggregate score of the mandatory Reviewer and any two Reviewers who submit the review first.

- If the three Reviewers (one mandatory and two optional) submit the review and the Mission is complete for the Learner, then the score from the fourth Reviewer is not considered.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Content Center:
The Content Center serves as a centralized collaborative space for content governance. Visualize it as a shared workspace, which stores all your content in one place, maintaining a single content source. It provides central management of all the content in Mindtickle. The Content center is useful for Enablement Admins, Content Experts, and Site Owners. It has a file–folder structure with a multi-level hierarchy. Users with access to the Content center can view all the files and folders present within the Content Center.

Note: If you want to add permissions to a custom role to edit, replace and delete a file in Content Center, contact your Customer Success Manager (CSM) or Mindtickle Support. The custom role must have the Manage Content permission to add or modify content on Content Center. For more information, see Roles and permissions in Mindtickle.

To access Content Center, click Content Center in the admin site sidebar.

Note:

- Content Center is initially empty. Once you add content, the files and folders appear in the Content Center. The files added in the learning object using the Content Center also start appearing within the Content Center.

- Content Center is available for the course and quick update modules, and also assets within Asset Hub .

For information on adding content to the Content Center, see Add or replace content in Content Center.

For information on adding Content Center files into learning objects, see Add or replace a file in learning object using Content Center.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Content Center > Key features:
- Central storage of content - All files added to the modules and assets can also be accessed or viewed in the Content Center.
- Centralized governance of content - Updates made in the Content Center reflect across all modules when the file is used. The Used in location column displays the number of modules when the file or folder is used.
- Content distribution - All files added to the Content Center can also be accessed from different modules and learning objects.
- Manage permissions on files - Users having specific Content Center related permissions can make changes to the files. Also, anyone with access to the Content center can view all the files present within the Content center.
- Filters based on modules, tags, and other file properties - Filter option makes it easy to locate content within the Content Center.
- Easy to find relevant content - When creating learning objects within a Course and Quick update or adding assets to Asset Hub, you can easily upload the content and assets into these learning objects using Content Center.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Content Center > Add files as learning objects:
In the Select file pop-up, you can add files as learning objects by:

- Selecting existing files (uploaded or synced) : Select files already uploaded the Content Center or synced from Adobe Experience Manager (AEM) , Google Shared Drive , or Microsoft SharePoint . Note : If you select synced files, any changes made to the source file will automatically reflect in the learning object.
- Uploading new files : Upload files directly from your computer or external storage providers (Google Drive, OneDrive, Salesforce, Box, and Dropbox) and then select them.

Note:

- You cannot select folders. To choose files from a folder, navigate to the folder and select the files inside.
- You can select up to 20 files for quick updates, but there is no file limit for courses.
- To upload a SCORM file from the Content Center, see SCORM Content on Mindtickle .

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Content Center > Add files as learning objects > Select existing files (uploaded or synced):
In the Select File pop-up, choose from files already available in the Content Center — either previously uploaded or synced from external sources like Adobe Experience Manager (AEM), Google Shared Drive, or Microsoft SharePoint.

You can browse files from the Content Center homepage or navigate to the folder where the uploaded or synced files are located.

Use search and filters (Series, Modules, File type, Created by, Tags, and Synced from) to quickly find the files you need. The Synced from filter is useful when you want to list files synced from external sources, like AEM, Google Share Drive, and SharePoint.

Click X items selected to view selected files and remove any from selection. Once done, click Select to add selected files as learning objects in the course/quick update module.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Content Center > Add files as learning objects > Upload new files:
In the Select File pop-up, you can also upload one or more new files to use as learning objects. Either upload them on the Content Center homepage or navigate to a specific folder and then click New > Add file.

You can upload files from your computer (My Device) or from external storage providers, like Google Drive, OneDrive, Salesforce, Box, and Dropbox. You can also drag and drop files to upload. Uploaded files are saved to the Content Center automatically, making them easily accessible for future reuse.

If Content Center is synced to AEM, Google Shared Drive, or Microsoft SharePoint, you can also upload new files directly in the respective synced source location. Once uploaded, these files will appear in the Content Center and can be selected as learning objects.

For details on supported file types and size limits for uploading and syncing content to Mindtickle, see this article.

The New menu also includes following options:

- Create folder : Organize your files by creating folders within the Content Center or a synced source location.
- Embed link : Add external content (e.g., web pages, videos, documents) by embedding a URL, which can also be used as a learning object.

Once you have uploaded and selected the uploaded files, click Select in the Add file pop-up to add selected files as learning objects in the course/quick update module.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Content Center > Files added as learning objects:
Once you upload or select existing (uploaded or synced) files in the Select File pop-up, they are immediately added as learning objects to the course or quick update module.

Hover over the file and use the "view options" (Fit to width/height, zoom, and fullscreen) to adjust how the file is displayed within the viewer for better readability and focus.

Once you have added the content, you can invite users and publish the course/quick update. For more information, see Create a course and Create a quick update articles.

After replacement, the file is saved automatically in both the learning object and the Content Center.

Important considerations:

- Changes apply to all modules containing the file.
- Learner progress in affected modules is not impacted.
- You cannot revert to the previous file version after replacement.
- The new file must be the same type as the original.
