Help & Support > Help Center Home > Setup > Page Builder for learning site homepages > Trending widget:
The Trending widget is a dynamic, configurable widget, available for learning site homepages and series overview pages. It allows admins to highlight and refine relevant content for learners. Specifically, the widget:

- Surfaces modules most accessed by all users in the last 30 days, sorted by views.
- Lets admins set content filters to refine what is displayed:
  - Module relevance : Required, Optional, or None (i.e. no module relevance set)
  - Completion status : Not Started, In Progress, Completed

The widget is available in the Series section in the widgets panel. You can add up to five Trending widgets on a page. Each widget can be renamed to clearly communicate its purpose. For example:

- “Completed Mandatory Training” : Set filters to Required and Completed to highlight required modules that others have finished and accessed most in the last 30 days.
- “In-Progress Optional Learning” : Set filters to Optional and In Progress to show popular optional modules learners are currently working on.
- “Discover New Content” : Set filters to None and Not Started to surface widely accessed modules that most learners haven’t yet begun.

You can use the Trending widget on learning site homepages and series overview pages. The following steps provide information on how to add a Trending widget to a learning site homepage:

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Course and quick update > Change module relevance:
Module relevance allows you to mark a module as required or optional for the learners. It is useful when you want to distinguish which modules are important and of priority and which may be optional for the learners.

You can set the module relevance while inviting learners to a module. To learn more about module relevance, refer to the Module Relevance Overview article.

To change the relevance for selected learners, click Change relevance. From the pop-up that appears, choose whether the Course should be Required, Optional, or Unmarked (Default in module settings). Click Change to proceed.

You can use the module relevance filter in Analytics to filter by Required, Optional, or Unmarked. To learn more, see articles in the Analytics and Reporting folder.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Course and quick update > Send email:
Sending bulk email helps to get your message out to the selected learners in a short amount of time.

To send an email in bulk, click Send email.

On the pop-up that appears:

- Select the email template from the Select template dropdown.
- In the From field, enter the name of the sender of the email.
- Enter the Subject of the email. An email subject is the first text learners see after your sender name when an email reaches their inbox.

Note: Entering the subject line is a mandatory step.

- Enter the main text in the body of the email. You can use different formatting options from the editor.

Once you have filled in all the information, click the Send email button at the lower-right corner of the screen to send the email or Cancel to discard the action.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Communications > Invite Learners:
A just-in-time (JIT) URL allows learners to assign a module to themselves even if the module is part of an invite-only series. After you publish the module, you can share the JIT URL with the learners. A Learner can access the JIT URL on the Mindtickle platform, and there is no need for you to assign the module.

To learn about the settings for the invite-only series, refer to the Configure series settings article.

Note: A JIT URL is different from JIT provisioning through SAML or SCIM. With JIT URLs, you can instantly invite learners to access the content on Mindtickle. With JIT provisioning, you can create, update, and deactivate users through SAML or SCIM protocols.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Communications > Invite Learners > Create the URL:
You can create a just-in-time (JIT) URL for any module using the series ID and module ID from the module’s admin site URL. Then, you can share it with your learners.

Prerequisite: You must publish the module before sharing a JIT URL with the learners. This is because the JIT URL provides instant access to the module.

Perform the following to create the JIT URL for a module:

1. Copy the admin site URL of the module to a text editor.Note: The URL syntax/format differs across module types. For example, the position of the module ID and series ID in the URL is different for courses and quick updates. See this table to know the admin site URL for each module type.Example: Let’s consider that you are creating a JIT URL for a course module. Your learning site name is enablement.mindtickle.com and the admin site URL of the course is:https://admin.mindtickle.com/new/ui/admin/course/module_ID/series_ID/track
2. Make note of the module ID and series ID in the admin site URL of the module. You will need to use them while creating the JIT URL. Use this table to figure out the module ID and series ID in the URL, which are required while creating the JIT URL.
3. Create (write) your new JIT URL in the following syntax:https://learning_site_name.mindtickle.com/login/jitredirectsso?seriesId=series_ID&moduleId=module_ID&redirecturi=%2fmodule_ID
4. In the above URL syntax, replace the following with your values:
  - learning_site_name with your learning site name
  - series_ID with the series ID (from the module’s admin site URL)
  - module_ID with the module ID (from the module’s admin site URL)
5. Now you can share the JIT URL with your learners.Example: The JIT URL for the course module will be:https://enablement.mindtickle.com/login/jitredirectsso?seriesId=1337001062105749222&moduleId=1337010507176132136&redirecturi=%2f1337010507176132136

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Communications > Invite Learners > Create the URL > Module URL syntax on the admin site:
This table lists the syntax of the admin site URL for each module type. Use the table as a reference to locate the module ID and series ID in the module’s admin site URL. The module and series IDs are required while creating the JIT URL for your learners.

Note: Ensure that you are using the correct URL depending on the module type. For example, in the admin site URL for courses and quick updates, the module_ID is listed first, followed by the series_ID. For the rest of the modules, the series_ID is listed first, followed by the module_ID.

| # | Module type | Syntax of the admin site URL |

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Communications > Invite Learners > Share the URL:
Once the just-in-time (JIT) URL is created, you can share it with your learners through various means of communication, such as email and Slack.

Single sign-on (SSO) should be enabled for the learning site. If SSO is not enabled, then learners need to sign in to Mindtickle to access the JIT URL. Learners will receive an error message if they access the JIT URL without signing in first.

Note: JIT URLs work for SAML, JWT, and Google-based SSO setups. It does not work for Open ID SSO.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Communications > Invite Learners > Caveats:
Consider the following caveats and important information:

- The Mindtickle mobile app (for iOS and Android) does not support JIT URLs.
- You cannot create a JIT URL for a series. You can only create a JIT URL for a module.
- All settings that apply to a learner when you invite them to a module from the module’s Invite and track page will apply when they access the content using the JIT URL. For example, invitation emails, reminders, module relevance.
- Do NOT create and use the JIT URL if the series is sequentially locked, as there can be a conflict when a learner tries to directly access the module through JIT while the previous modules in the series are still locked.
- Every time learners access an embedded mission in a course or quick update, they automatically receive the mission invitation email.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Series:
As an admin, you can manage all your enablement programs on the admin site by creating different modules within a series. A series in Mindtickle represents a learning initiative. It helps you organize all your relevant enablement content and activities within modules.

Your admin site can contain multiple series. A series can contain multiple modules, for example, course, quick-update, assessment, checklist. For information on when to use which type of module, see How to choose the right module.

This article explains the definitions of each series type, sample scenarios describing when to use which type of series, and how learners’ visibility, access, and invitations work for each series.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Series > When to create which type of series?:
- Create a Public series if you want the content to be visible to all learners by default. For example, If you want to create a series on company policies that you wish everyone in your organization to go through, you should create a public series. This way, the series on company policies will be available to everyone in your organization.
- Create a Scoped public series if you want the content to be publicly available but only to specific learners that fall under the series scope. For example, If you want to create a series for onboarding that you wish the new hires in your organization to go through, you should create a public series and set the scope to only include the new hires. This way, the Onboarding series will be publicly available only to the new hires.
- Create an Assigned series and invite specific learners to the series. When you assign a series to learners, the content will be visible only to learners invited to the series. For example, If you want to create a series on product releases that you wish the sales reps in your organization to go through, you should create the series and invite all the sales reps. This way, the Product release series gets assigned to the sales reps and is visible only to them.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > My Analytics:
The Bookmark functionality in Analytics provides you quick and easy access to reports you are interested in. You can bookmark any platform report for yourself. You can even bookmark a “modified” report — that is, bookmark a report after you apply filters and select tabs in the report. For Manager reports, Bookmark also saves the customized column metrics. However, any sorting applied in the report columns is not saved.

Users who have access to Analytics can bookmark any report for themselves. Use this option to bookmark reports for yourself for future reference. This article explains how to bookmark reports in Analytics and access your bookmarked reports and perform various actions on them.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > My Analytics > Bookmarked vs. shared reports:
Previously, the Bookmark functionality allowed you to bookmark reports for yourself and others (Admins and Managers). To distinguish between bookmarking and sharing and to simplify the experience, we have renamed the “bookmark reports for others” functionality to “share with others.”

- Bookmark will now allow you to bookmark reports only for yourself. The Bookmarked section in the navigation panel displays platform reports that you have bookmarked for yourself.
- The functionality to bookmark reports for others (Admins and Managers) is now renamed as Share. With Share, you can share reports with Admins and Managers. The Shared section in the navigation panel displays platform and custom reports that are shared with you and shared by you.For more information on how to share and access reports, see Share Reports and Access Shared Reports in Analytics.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > My Analytics > Bookmark a report:
To bookmark a report:

1. Open the report that you want to bookmark.Note: This article explains how to bookmark a hierarchy-based Manager report as an example.
2. Apply filters if you want to bookmark the report with certain filters applied. If you navigate to another tab within the report, this (your current view) too gets saved in the bookmarked report.
3. Click the Bookmark button in the upper-right corner.

1. Select the Bookmark this report for me check box in the pop-up.

1. Enter an appropriate name for the report (in less than 128 characters) and a note (in less than 250 characters) that will help you know the context of the report later. Then click Confirm. The report is bookmarked. The current view of the page and applied filters will be saved and available to you in the bookmarked report.
2. The Bookmark button changes to indicate that the current report is bookmarked.

Note: You cannot bookmark an already bookmarked report. However, if you make additional changes in a bookmarked report, such as apply or remove filters, it becomes a “new” report and you can bookmark it.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > My Analytics > Access bookmarked reports:
To access your bookmarked reports and perform various actions on them:

1. In the left navigation panel, click the Bookmarked section under the My Analytics category.

1. The Bookmarked page lists the reports you have bookmarked for yourself. The page provides information about bookmarked reports in the following columns:
  - Report Name: Report name and the note that was added while bookmarking the report.
  - Report Type: Type of the report that you have bookmarked, such as Modules, Series, and Groups. Use the Report Type filter to filter the reports by the report type.
  - Bookmarked On: Date and time when a report was bookmarked.

Use the search bar to search for a specific report. You can sort the listed reports by the Report Name and Bookmarked On columns in ascending and descending orders.

1. You can perform the following actions for a bookmarked report:
  - Edit the bookmark information: Click the (More) button and select Edit Details to change the name and note for the bookmarked report. For more information, see the Edit Bookmarked Reports section.
  - Delete the bookmark: Click the (More) button and select Delete to delete a bookmarked report. This will only delete the bookmark of the report and not the actual report.
  - Open the report: Click any report to open it. The report will open with all the customizations that were made before bookmarking it, such as with applied filters and tab selection.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Dashboards:
The Adoption dashboard has widgets that provide insights into how your users are starting and completing assigned content. And the time taken by users to complete the assigned content. The dashboard displays data specific to your role. You can customize the widgets to further personalize this dashboard to see data more relevant to you. From most of the widgets, you can click the chart data to quickly deep-dive to the detailed reports.

The dashboard is available for Site Owners, Admins, and custom roles. On the dashboard, the number of widgets and the data in widgets that you see depends on your role and permissions. For more information, see Permissions and Access for Analytics Dashboards.

Note: Any customizations that you make to the Adoption dashboard are applicable only to you and not to other users.

Other than the Adoption dashboard, Analytics provides the Home and Performance dashboards. You can also create and view your own custom dashboards. For an overview of Analytics dashboards, see Analytics Dashboards Overview.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Dashboards > Adoption dashboard widgets:
The Adoption dashboard widgets provide insights on your users’ adoption of assigned Series and Modules.

Access detailed reports from widgets:

From most of the widgets, you can quickly access relevant detailed reports. If a widget shows data for which reports are available in Analytics, you can access the corresponding reports. Click any bar in a widget to go to the relevant reports, such as Series and Module reports. For example, in the Adoption of Key Series widget, if you click the bar for a Series called “Resource Library,” you are taken to the Series report of “Resource Library.”

Download dashboards and widgets:

You can download the entire dashboard and individual widgets to your computer in a .PNG format. It instantly downloads the dashboard exactly how you see it on your screen.

To download a dashboard, click the (Download) button in the upper-right corner of the dashboard. To download a widget, hover over the widget and click the (Download) button in the upper-right corner.

The Adoption dashboard has the following 13 widgets, available in two sections:

- Completion: Widgets in this section provide insights into how your users are starting and completing assigned content.
- Time to Complete: Widgets in this section provide insights into how much time users are taking to complete the assigned content.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Dashboards > Adoption dashboard widgets > Invitations Sent:
Displays the trend of the total number of users invited across Modules. Invitation count includes users who self-subscribe to Modules in public Series. For Learners invited to multiple Modules, each invite is counted. The chart shows aggregated data by selected frequency: monthly, weekly or daily. Hover over the chart to view information for each data point.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Dashboards:
The Performance dashboard has widgets that provide insights into how your users are performing on assigned content. The dashboard displays data specific to your role. You can customize the widgets to further personalize this dashboard to see data more relevant to you. From most of the widgets, you can click the chart data to quickly deep-dive to the detailed reports.

The dashboard is available for Site Owners, Admins, and custom roles. On the dashboard, the number of widgets and the data in widgets that you see depends on your role and permissions. For more information, see Permissions and Access for Analytics Dashboards.

Note: Any customizations that you make to the Performance dashboard are applicable only to you and not to other users.

Along with the Performance dashboard, Analytics provides the Home and Adoption dashboards. You can also create and view your own custom dashboards. For an overview of Analytics dashboards, see Analytics Dashboards Overview.

For a video overview of the new Analytics experience, see New Analytics Experience - Overview (Video Tutorial).

From most of the widgets, you can quickly access relevant detailed reports. If a widget shows data for which reports are available in Analytics, you can access the corresponding reports. Click any bar in a widget to go to the relevant reports, such as Series and Module reports. For example, in the Performance in Key Series widget, if you click the bar for a Series called “Resource Library,” you are taken to the Series report of “Resource Library.”

Download dashboards and widgets:

You can download the entire dashboard and individual widgets to your computer in a .PNG format. It instantly downloads the dashboard exactly how you see it on your screen.

To download a dashboard, click the (Download) button in the upper-right corner of the dashboard. To download a widget, hover over the widget and click the (Download) button in the upper-right corner.

The Performance dashboard has the following 8 widgets:

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Dashboards > Performance Dashboard Widgets > Scoring Performance:
Displays the trend of your Learners’ Scoring Performance. The chart shows aggregated data by selected frequency: monthly, weekly or daily. Hover over the chart to view information for each data point.

Scoring Performance = Sum of Learners’ scores in Modules / Sum of max. score of the Modules started x 100

By default, the following filters and settings are applied on the widget. Edit the widget to change them:

- Applicable Filters: Public Series Data = Include Admin Assigned Only
- Default View: Data Frequency = Monthly

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Dashboards > Performance Dashboard Widgets > Average RI:
Displays the trend of your users’ average Readiness Index (RI). RI represents the capability of a seller on a scale of 0 to 100. It is a unified metric that, by quantifying the capabilities of sales reps, measures their readiness to achieve business outcomes.

RI highlights the competencies that separate your top sales reps from the ones that need improvement. It also highlights the competencies of your teams and user segments so that you can prioritize and personalize the readiness programs better.

Edit the widget to change the default filters and settings.

- Applicable Filters:
  - Public Series Data = Include Admin Assigned Only
  - Invite Time = Last Month
- Default View: Top five Series based on the total number of Modules started

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Dashboards:
With the custom dashboard capability, you can create personalized dashboards using widgets of your choice. These dashboards appear under the Custom Created > Custom dashboards page. On this page, use the Create new button to quickly start building a new dashboard.

In custom dashboards, you can add widgets from the default dashboards. Depending on the dashboards from which you have selected widgets, your dashboard can show insights into user adoption of assigned content, performance data, asset engagement, and revenue impact of assets. You can rearrange, edit, copy, or delete widgets and customize them to make the dashboard more relevant to your needs.

Like other dashboards, the data displayed in custom dashboards is specific to your role and permissions. Most widgets are interactive, allowing you to click on chart data to directly access related detailed reports.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Dashboards > Access and permissions:
The ability to create and view custom dashboards is available to site owners, admins, and custom roles. The widgets available for configuration and the data you see depend on your role and permissions. For more details, see Permissions and access for analytics dashboards.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Dashboards > Capabilities of custom dashboards:
Admins and eligible users can:

- Create dashboards by:
  - Selecting widgets from the widget library (based on role-based permissions)
  - Customizing filters, sorting, and default selections
  - Defining a personalized layout
- Edit existing dashboards and create copies

Note: Customizations made to your dashboards apply only to you and are not visible to other users.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Dashboards > When to create custom dashboards?:
Create custom dashboards when the default dashboards do not meet your specific requirements. Custom dashboards allow you to:

- Select only the widgets you need
- Combine widgets from Overview, Adoption, Performance, Engagement, and Revenue Impact dashboards
- Rearrange widgets to suit your workflow and data priorities

Your custom dashboard can serve as an enhanced version of the Overview dashboard, with more flexibility and tailored insights.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Dashboards > Widget information:
The dashboard widgets display data that is specific to your role and calculated based on applied metrics, filters, and settings. Each widget derives data from one or more metrics and, therefore, metrics cannot be changed. However, you can change the filters and other settings.

You can customize the widgets in a particular dashboard to further personalize the dashboard to see data more relevant to you. This section explains the information available in a widget and the actions that you can perform. Most information and actions are available when you hover over the widget.

- Widget Data: Widgets in Analytics dashboards provide information through either trend or bar chart. The data displayed in the chart is based on the filters and settings applied on the widget. The applied filters are available below the widget name. If multiple filters are applied for a widget, hover over the filter list to see all applied filters.

- Widget description or tooltip: Hover over the Help icon next to the widget name to read a brief description on what data the widget displays and how the displayed data is calculated based on metrics, filters, and settings applied .

- Data Last Updated, Download Widget, and Edit Widget: When you hover over a widget, two icons appear in the upper-right corner of the widget.
  - The ( clock ) icon displays information on when the widget’s metric data was last updated.
  - The ( Download) icon is for downloading the widget in a .PNG format to your computer.
  - The ( Edit ) icon is for editing widgets. Click the icon to open the Edit Widget panel. For more information, see Widget reports in analytics dashboards .

4. Select the Learners checkbox to select all learners or select each learner's corresponding checkbox to select them individually.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Assessment > Change module relevance:
Module relevance allows you to mark the module as Required, Optional or Unmarked for the learners. This feature is useful when you want to distinguish which modules need to be prioritized by the learner, which modules may be optional for the learner, and which modules may be left at the discretion of the learner.

Note: You can set the module relevance while inviting learners to a module. For more information, see Module Relevance Overview.

To change the relevance of the assessment for the selected learners:

1. Select the checkbox of the learners and click Change relevance .
2. In the pop-up that appears, choose whether the assessment should be Required , Optional , or Unmarked (default in assessment settings). Click Change to complete the action or click Cancel to discard the action. The Invite and track page appears and displays the updated relevance for the selected learners.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Assessment > Send reminder emails:
You can send out reminder emails to learners who have not started or have not completed the assessment. To send bulk reminder emails to all the selected learners:

1. Click Send email .
2. In the email draft pop-up, select the email template from the Select Template drop-down list. The From , Subject , Email Body , and Email Signature fields are auto-populated based on the template you select. Note :
  - You can edit or update the information in these fields, however, it is advised that you don’t edit or update the shortkeys (example $from_name$ ) in the template.
  - It is mandatory to enter a subject line.
  - To update the format of the text in the email body, choose from the available formatting options.
3. Enter the email address of participants other than the selected learners in the Cc field to send the email to them.
4. Click Send to send the email or Discard to cancel the action.

A confirmation message appears on the screen once the email is sent to the selected learners.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Assessment > Reset progress:
Resetting the progress for learners is useful if you want them to try again or to revisit the module.

Note:

- If you reset a learner's progress, they will lose any existing progress on this assessment, their score will be reset to 0 , and their completion status will be set to Did not start .
- If a learner has failed an assessment, their completion status is marked as Failed . To mark a failed learner’s progress as Complete , an admin must reset their progress and then mark it as Complete . The learner is then awarded a full score for the assessment.

To reset the progress of all the selected learners in bulk:

1. Click the checkboxes of the learners to reset progress and click Reset progress .
2. In the pop-up that appears, from the Reset learner’s progress to drop-down, select the version of the assessment on which you want them to get recertified.

- Select the version of the Assessment he/she is currently on , if you want them to get recertified on the version of the assessment they are currently on.
- Select the latest version of the Assessment if you want them to get certified on the latest version of the assessment.

6. Click Reset progress to complete the action, or click Cancel to discard the action.

The Invite and track page appears and displays the updated score and completion status for the selected learners. The score is reset to -, and the completion status is reset to Did not start.

You can choose to complete a learner’s progress on an assessment. On marking a learner’s progress as Complete, the learner will be awarded a full score and a completion certificate, and their completion status will be marked as Completed.

Note:

- On performing this action, the score achieved in the attempted part of the assessment will be retained and the learners will be given a full score for the unattempted part.

1. Click the checkbox of the learners and click Complete progress .
2. In the pop-up that appears, click Complete progress to complete the action. Or, click Cancel to discard the action.

The Invite and track page appears and displays the updated score and completion status for the selected learners. The score is reset to the maximum score, and the completion status is reset to Pass.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Assessment > Edit due date:
You can edit due dates for multiple learners in bulk or specific learner groups. You can assign a specific date by which the selected learners or groups must complete the assessment. While updating the due date, you can choose to notify learners about the revised date.

The email notification includes details about the previously set due date and the updated due date. Additionally, the admin configuring the change also receives an email notification confirming the due date has been set or revised for the selected learners or groups.

To edit the due date for multiple learners or groups:

1. Select the learners or filter the list using the Groups filter.
2. Click Edit due date .
3. In Set a due date for learners, select one of the following options:

- Choose a specific date: Select this option to send reminders to learners on a specific date.
- None: Select this option to turn off reminders for the selected learners. If selected, the Due date column in the Invite and track tab is updated as None for the learner.

4. Select What happens after due date? for individual learners.

5. To notify the learners or groups about the revised due date, select Notify selected learners about this update via email checkbox. The email notification includes details about the previously set and updated due dates.

6. Click Save.

The learners’ revised due date is displayed in the Due date column.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Communications > Notifications and Reminders:
The Mindtickle platform applies the Automation suite module & series invitation email template for bulk module and series invitations in Automation suite. The template is used for the email sent to Learners when you invite them to multiple Modules or Series: either through Automation rules, Automation links (Group to series/module linking), or the Module links tab on a group’s page.

Previously, this template was not available to admins. Moreover, this same email template was used whether a user was invited to multiple or single series/modules.

Now, we have made the following changes around the Automation suite module & series invitation template and the invitation behavior:

- This template is available in the Settings page > Email templates, and it can be customized as per your requirements.
- The template will apply only for multiple/bulk Module and Series invitations: either through Automation rules, Automation links (Group to Series/Module Linking), or the Module links tab on a Group’s page.
- The Automation rule invitation email template is triggered only if a user is invited to more than one module or series within a 5-minute window from all possible automation links and rules. It is applicable to group-to-module linking and automation rules only. It is not applicable to group-to-series linking. This is done so that a learner does not receive too many individual module and/or series invitation emails.
- Users who are invited to a series through group-to-series linking receive the series invitation email template (based on the series notification settings configuration). For more information, see Configure series Settings: Notifications.
- The template will not be used for single invitations. If a user is invited to a single module or series, then the invitation template defined in the respective module or series’ settings will be used for invitations.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Asset Hub > Admin:
This article gives an overview of Asset Hub, its features, the difference between Asset Hub and Content Center, and how you can access and navigate the Asset Hub homepage.

Note: Asset Hub is a paid feature. For more information, contact your Customer Success Manager (CSM).

An asset is a sales collateral or a document that can help a sales rep communicate effectively with prospects or customers to close deals. A hub is a logical group of assets that helps organize the entire asset repository into broad categories. These two, when combined, form Asset Hub, which manages all of your organization's sales assets. It serves as a single source of truth for your customer-facing teams to quickly access and search assets on the platform.

For example, Asset Hub allows your sales team to be well-equipped for objections and frequently asked questions so they can position your solutions strategically to win more deals. The sales team can utilize assets like case studies, sales success stories, battle cards:

- For demos, follow-up meetings, or to overcome objections
- To apply winning techniques followed by top performers to close deals
- To measure the business outcomes, products, or services up against their competitors

For information on Asset Hub roles and their permissions, see Roles and permissions in Mindtickle.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Asset Hub > Admin > Difference between Content Center and Asset Hub:
Content Center serves as a centralized collaborative space for content governance. It provides central management of all the content in Mindtickle. To learn more, see Content Center Overview.

Asset Hub manages all of your organization's sales assets. It serves as a single source of truth for your customer-facing teams to quickly access and search assets on the platform.

Following table explains the difference between Content Center and Asset Hub:

| Criteria | Content Center | Asset Hub |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Description | Centralized content governance in Mindtickle.(Central management of all content in Mindtickle) | Equip customer-facing teams with sales assets.(Content Management System or Knowledge Management System to find the right content for sales reps) |
| Useful for | Only Admin(Enablement, Product or Customer Marketing) | Admin and Sales reps(Enablement, Marketing, and Sales reps) |
| Nature of content | Learning content, referenceable content, best calls, top Missions, questions, polls | Referenceable content |
| Structure and hierarchy | File-folder structureMulti-level hierarchy | Simplified structure where the same content is available under multiple locations. |
| Key capabilities | Central storage of contentContent versioningNon-disruptive updates to content | Asset enrichment (meta-tagging)Powerful searchRecommendationsAsset analytics |
| Package | Included within the core offering | Add-on to the platform |

Note: Once content is uploaded into Content Center, it can be pulled into Asset Hub or Modules regardless of where the content is uploaded from.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Asset Hub > Admin > Actions in the hub header > Share hub access (restricted hubs):
Note: Sharing of hub access (hub access management) for users and user groups applies to restricted hubs only. Public hubs are accessible to all users, so they do not have a per-hub user or group access. The behavior described in this section is available for restricted parent (root) and child hubs.

Different access permissions in Asset Hub help to regulate access to the product based on the type of activities you perform. Permissions ensure that you are enabled to access data and product capabilities as per your job requirement, and that you will not access features that you do not need. They provide a cleaner interface to view only those elements on the screen which you are allowed to view based on your role, and minimize your chance of interfering with others' work. For more details, see roles and permissions.

Click the Share access button at the upper-right corner of the page to share the hub access with the following:

- Individual Users
- Link User Groups

Note:

- If you are sharing access to a child hub, remember that it automatically inherits the visibility type (Public or Restricted) and base access rules of its parent hub. For how access is inherited, propagated, and removed across a nested hierarchy (restricted hubs), see the Manage hub access (users and user groups) section in Create and manage nested hubs [admin].
- You can view the Share access button based on your role. To check the permissions associated with your role, see roles and permissions .

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Asset Hub > Admin > Actions in the hub header > Collaborators:
A user who works jointly on a hub is called a hub collaborator. Inviting users to collaborate helps in increasing productivity and provides easy access to information. Only Site Owners and Enablement Admins can act as collaborators for a hub. To learn more about the permissions of a hub collaborator, see the roles and permissions article.

In the hub header, you can both view and add collaborators.

While adding collaborators, you can choose to provide access to All Potential Users or Selected Users.

- All Potential Users : All those users, to whom the Site Owner has assigned appropriate role(s), can access the hub.
- Selected Users : Only those users who you select from the underlying list can access the hub. You can search for a specific collaborator using the search bar.

To add a new collaborator, click the + Collaborators button from the upper-right corner of the screen.

Note: Collaborators assigned to a parent hub will automatically inherit collaborator access to all nested child hubs within that hierarchy.

Note: If you add collaborators from any place other than this hub, they cannot access the hub by default.

- Get shareable link: Use the three-dot menu to get the shareable link for the hub so that anyone with the link can access it.
- Delete hub: Use the three-dot menu to delete the hub.

- For public hubs, anyone with a Mindtickle account can access the asset using the shareable link.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Asset Hub > Admin > Hubs and assets tab > Insights:
Asset insights help you to understand how well an asset is behaving and engaging with the sales reps:

- Asset name. The presence of after the asset name indicates a multi-present asset.
- Name of the collaborator who made the last update on the asset and the date of the update.
- Asset rating on a scale of 1 (lowest) to 5 (highest).
- Number of views of the asset.
- Number of shares of the asset.
- Number of downloads of the asset.
- Number of times the asset is bookmarked .
- The date of the last update on the asset.
- Attributes applied to the asset to filter, organize, and easily search the asset. Hover over the attribute number against an asset to view all the attributes applied to that asset.

Note: Asset Insights on views, downloads, bookmarks and ratings take a maximum of two hours to reflect from Learning Site to Admin Site.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Asset Hub > Admin > Hubs and assets tab > Filters:
- Filter by Status : You can filter assets that are recently published, assets kept as drafts , assets that are expiring soon, or the assets that have expired. By default, you can view all the assets inside a hub.
- Filter by Attributes : You can filter assets based on the attributes applied. Select the attribute(s) from the drop-down or search for a specific attribute using the search bar. Click Apply to proceed. Note : You can filter assets that do not have attributes assigned by selecting the No attributes applied checkbox.
- Filter by Asset owners : You can filter the assets by their asset owners. Select an asset owner from the drop-down or search using the search bar. Click Apply to proceed.
- Filter by Usage : You can filter assets based on the internal or external usage of the asset. By default, you can view all the assets inside a hub.
- More filters : You can apply a new set of filters on the hub page based on all possible properties of the asset. Click the Select filter dropdown to view the list of filters. Select the filter and the corresponding value in the adjacent dropdown, and click Apply . Once selected, click the Add new button to add more filters to your search. Once you are satisfied with your set of filters, click Apply .
- Asset type : Allows you to filter the assets based on media or play type like PDF, PPT, Document, link, play, audio, video, image, XLS, embedded and so on.
- Download allowed : Allows you to filter assets based on whether downloadable by the reps or not.
- Feedback status : Allows you to filter assets based on the feedback received and the status of that feedback. Select Read to view assets for which the feedback is already read, Unread to view assets for which the feedback is still pending to be read, or No Feedback to view assets for which no feedback is received.
- External sharing status: Allows you to filter assets based on whether the asset is shared externally and if the asset is part of a live Interaction with a prospect or client. Select Not shared to list assets that are not shared externally with clients or prospects. Select Expired interactions only to list assets whose expiry date is complete but still visible to the sales reps. Select Part of active interactions to list assets that are already part of client or prospect interactions.
- Description added: Allows you to filter assets with or without a description.
- Customized asset creation: Allows you to filter assets based on whether sales reps can customize the assets, using the Mix and match and Edit content features. Available options are:- Mix and match only- Edit content only- Both- No customizationNote: The customized asset creation feature is available only for assets in PDF, PPT, XLS, and Doc formats.For details on how sales reps (learners) can edit the asset content using Microsoft Office for the web (Word, PowerPoint, and Excel) or using Google Workspace apps (Docs, Slides, and Sheets), see the Edit asset content using Microsoft Office for the web: For PowerPoint, Word, and Excel files or Edit asset content using Google Docs, Slides, and Sheets help articles.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Asset Hub > Admin > Hubs and assets tab > Actions on assets:
Click the three-dot icon for an asset to perform the following actions:

Note: These options are available based on your roles and permissions.

- Publish: Available only for draft assets. Use the option to quickly publish the asset without opening it.
- Edit properties such as description, attributes, usage (internal, external), expiry date, expiry reminder, file update reminder for the asset.

Note: When you change the usage of a shared asset from external to internal, customers or prospects with whom a rep has shared the asset can still view it. Only going forward, the rep cannot share that asset.

- Replace file with a new file. To learn more about the replace flow, refer to Asset Details article.
- Rename the asset.
- Download the asset on your local machine.
- Get Shareable Link to the asset so that anyone with the link can access it.

Note:

- For invite-only hubs, only invited users can access the shareable link.
- For public hubs, anyone with the link can access the asset.

- Move the asset from one hub to another.
- Mirror the asset to make it available in multiple hubs. For the assets which are already multi-present, you will not have the Mirror option. Instead, you will have Manage Mirroring and Remove mirroring from this Hub options.
- Archive the asset to move it under the Archived tab. If the asset is present in multiple hubs, archiving removes it from all the hubs.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Asset Hub > Admin > Hubs and assets tab > Bulk actions on assets:
If you intend to avoid manual work and perform bulk actions on multiple assets, you can select the assets. Once selected, the following bulk actions appear at the lower section of the page:

- Publish
- Download
- Mirror
- Move (If one of the selected asset is multi-present, you cannot move it)
- Assign asset owner
- Archive

For detailed information on the bulk action, see Bulk actions on assets.

Note:

- When you archive assets that the reps share with their customers or prospects, you can see a message informing you that the assets are shared, and archiving them restricts recipients' access. You can view the users (reps) who have shared those assets. Additionally, mirrored assets are removed from hubs, and analytics related to respective assets get archived. You can accept the conditions and choose to archive only the unshared assets or archive all of them. If you choose to archive all of them, reps who have shared those assets receive an email notification.
- You can view and confirm the count of the selected assets when performing a bulk action.
- Bulk actions on more than 50 assets are not yet supported but will be available in future releases of the Asset Hub.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Asset Hub > Admin > Settings tab > Notifications:
Under the Notifications tab, you can edit whom to send the expiry reminders and file update reminders. Also, you can edit the collaborator information if an asset owner is changed or removed.

If assets in the hub have asset owners assigned, all expiry and file update reminders are sent to the asset owners. If no asset owners are assigned, or an asset owner is implicitly removed, in that case, all notifications related to asset owner removal, expiry and file update reminders are sent to the hub collaborators. Select the collaborators from the drop-down for each type of reminder. You can also search for a specific collaborator from the search bar. Click Apply to proceed.

Note: All email notifications for a day are clubbed together and delivered at approximately 9 AM in the local timezone of the collaborator.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Asset Hub > Admin > Settings tab > Customize end-user experience:
Under the Customize end-user experience tab, you can organize and configure the attribute categories and filters visible to the sales reps and customize the experience of each hub for the reps.

For example, let's say you have created 15 attribute categories in a hub that is specific to the competition. As an admin, you want to promote the attribute category with the competitor name since it is the primary thing a rep would look for. You can decide and re-order the category with competitor name on top of the eye for the learners such that they are able to filter by attributes or properties to get to the needed asset quickly within the specific hub.

To learn about how attributes are created and categorized, refer to the Manage Attributes in Asset Hub article.

To modify the sequence in which attribute categories and filters are visible to the sales reps, click Edit.

On the pop-up that appears, you can rearrange the attribute category order. You can also hover over to show or hide a category. Click Save to proceed.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Asset Hub > Admin:
This article explains how admins can create a single or multiple new assets via UI in Asset Hub.

An asset is a sales collateral or a document that can help a sales rep communicate effectively with prospects or customers to close deals. Creating assets brings on-the-job readiness, maintains brand consistency, decreases onboarding time, and enables sales reps in various stages of the sales funnel. For example, suppose a sales rep finishes a customer call and intends to reinforce the product value. The rep can send assets like a pitch deck or a case study about using a specific product feature to the customer.

Note: Asset Hub is a paid feature. For more information, contact your Customer Success Manager (CSM).

You can organize your content hierarchically by creating nested structures of parent and child hubs. To learn more, see Create and manage nested hubs [admin].

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Asset Hub > Admin > Overview of bulk asset creation:
Admins can create multiple assets at once directly from the UI, without needing an Excel file. You can create assets in bulk from the UI from the Assets page.

The workflow is streamlined into three steps: 1) Selecting files from Content Center, 2) filling in properties, and 3) creating and tracking assets via Notifications. While filling in properties, you can apply common properties to multiple or all assets. You can choose to create assets as drafts or publish them directly.

There are two kinds of files from which you can create assets in bulk:

- Uploaded to Content Center
- Synced from Google shared drive , Microsoft SharePoint , and Adobe Experience Manager (AEM)

Notes

- The new interface includes a page with selected assets on the left and each asset’s properties and other info on the right. On this page, any missing required (mandatory) properties must be filled in to comply with hub policies.
- If issues arise (e.g., missing required properties or unsupported file types), the platform provides helpful tooltips and messages throughout.
- This feature prevents property overrides on externally synced files (e.g., Google Drive, SharePoint). Any property changes must be made at the source.

Limitations

- You can create up to 50 assets at once. For more, use the " Multiple assets via Excel file " feature.
- Admins can only create bulk assets from existing files in Content Center, not by uploading new files or embed links.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Asset Hub > Admin > Create a single or multiple new assets:
Perform the following to create a single new asset or multiple new assets (bulk asset creation):

1. On the Assets page, click New > Select files. Use this option, when you want to create assets across multiple hubs, rather than in a specific hub.Alternatively, if you want to create new assets in a specific hub, use the Add assets > Select files option on the hub page.

2. The Select files from Content Center page appears. Select one or more files that you want to create as assets. For bulk asset creation, you can select up to 50 assets during one instance. Click Next to continue.

3. If necessary, you can upload new files directly to Content Center from this page through the New > Add file option. You can also embed links and create new folders in Content Center.

4. If creating a single asset: When creating a single asset, the following Create asset page appears. On the left, you'll see your selected file, and on the right, the asset properties that must be filled to create this file as an asset. Fill in the required properties, which are marked with a red asterisk (*). The number of required properties may vary depending on the selected hub, as they are configured at the hub level. All required fields must be completed for the asset to be created.See the "Asset properties" section for details on the properties.

5. If creating multiple assets: When creating multiple assets, the following Create assets page appears.

The page provides the following functionalities:

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Asset Hub > Admin > Create a single or multiple new assets:
Hover over the property and:

- Click the Copy to option to apply the property to selected assets. A dropdown menu lists the same number of files that are listed on the left. Select one or more files to which you want to apply the property.
- Click the Copy to all assets option to quickly apply the property to all assets, i.e. to all files listed on the left.

8. You can proceed with asset creation only after filling the missing required properties for all selected files.

9. Once done, click the Create assets button in the lower-right. The asset creation process is asynchronous. Once you click on Create assets, the action is processed in the background, letting you perform other tasks. You can track the progress and status of this action on Notifications.

10. Notifications panel displays a notification once the action of creating assets is completed.

11. Click the View action details icon against this action to view details. The assets get created in the hubs selected by you for each asset.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Asset Hub > Admin > Asset properties:
When you are creating a new asset, you need to fill in various asset properties (fields). This section provides details on all properties of an asset.

Note: You cannot publish or save an asset as a draft without filling in all the required properties marked with a red asterisk (*).

- Enter a Name for the asset. It is advisable to select a name that can immediately tell sales reps what the asset is all about and makes it easy to search.
- Add a thumbnail to the asset and start showing all the card views of the asset. A great custom thumbnail acts as a preview for the asset. It makes your asset appealing and hints to viewers about what to expect. You can select from existing thumbnails in the Gallery . Or, you can choose to Upload a thumbnail (recommended size is 540 x 360 px).
- Select Hub from the list shown in the drop-down. You can select multiple hubs to make the asset multi-present. A hub is a logical group of assets that helps organize the entire asset repository into broad categories.
- Alternatively, select an Asset Owner of the asset to divide the responsibility of asset ownership and maintenance between different users. It is an optional step. By default, Asset Hub populates the creator of the asset as the asset owner. You can choose any user as the Asset Owner who is a collaborator and has Develop Asset permissions of one of the hubs where the asset resides. This ensures that the Asset Owner always has the permissions to edit the asset. Note :

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Asset Hub > Admin > Asset properties:
- The Asset Owner field can be empty under the following scenarios:
  - You have moved the asset to a hub where the Asset Owner is not a collaborator.
  - You have changed the Asset Owner’s permission .
  - You have removed the Asset Owner as a collaborator from all the hubs where the asset resides.
  - You have removed the Asset Owner as a user from the Mindtickle platform.
- If an asset has an owner assigned, all expiry and file update reminders are sent to the Asset Owner. If the asset does not have an owner assigned, all expiry and file update reminders are sent to the hub collaborators where the asset resides.

- Optionally, you can add Attributes to the asset by clicking Apply . Adding attributes enhances the discoverability of the asset. You can search for attributes and categories using the search bar. Also, you can select an attribute from the Relevant categories for the hub or All categories displayed in the pop-up. Note :
  - If the category has more than 50 attributes, click Show more to view the complete list of attributes.
  - Attributes under Relevant categories are organized based on the selected categories under Settings > Customize admin experience . Whereas the All categories attributes are displayed based on most applied attributes by other admins and recently created attributes.

For example, if the asset is for the buyer journey stage of the sales funnel, you can add attributes like awareness, closing, or evaluation to it.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Asset Hub > Admin > Asset properties:
- Select the usage of the assets as internal or external. By default, usage is set as internal. Setting usage lets sales reps know if they can download and share the asset externally with their prospects or use it only for internal reference.
- Select Yes or No for the Allow customized asset creation option. By default, this option is set to No . If you select Yes , reps can duplicate this asset and create a new asset by adding slides from other assets, uploading new slides, or removing existing slides. Note : The customized asset creation feature is available only for PDF, PPT, XLS, and Doc formats. Additionally, asset customization is applicable only when the asset usage is external. For details on how sales reps (learners) can edit the asset content using Microsoft Office for the web (Word, PowerPoint, and Excel) or using Google Workspace apps (Docs, Slides, and Sheets), see the Edit asset content using Microsoft Office for the web: For PowerPoint, Word, and Excel files or Edit asset content using Google Docs, Slides, and Sheets help articles.
- Select an option to make the asset downloadable . If you select Yes , the asset becomes available for download by the reps. If an asset contains sensitive information that must not be customized by the reps, you can select No so that the reps cannot download the asset. However, they can use it in its original form as provided by the Asset Owner.
- Select an option to allow your learners to save the asset to Google drive.
- Additionally, you can add a description of the asset. Description conveys valuable information that helps viewers spot an asset in search results and indicate the type of content in the asset. It also guides the sales rep on which asset to use in a situation. For example, a pitch deck’s talk track helps the sales rep set the follow-up meeting, and the rep can focus on creating value, controlling the process, and winning deals.
- You can also add an expiry date , expiry reminder , or set a file update reminder by clicking the Add expiration button.
  - Setting an expiry date ensures the effectiveness of your assets. Once an asset expires, you can either choose to update the asset and extend its expiry date or archive it. Expired assets are still visible to the sales reps but flagged as Expired .
  - Expiration reminder or file update reminder helps keep your organization compliant by automatically tracking expiration date for assets such as team member certifications, contracts, licenses, marketing campaigns, and more. You can manage upcoming renewals or set reminders and follow-up alerts for files that are about to expire.
  - A file update reminder is sent regularly to a hub collaborator to ensure the asset remains up to date.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Asset Hub > Admin:
This article explains the asset details (for example, asset name, hub name, asset status), how to replace the file associated with an asset, engagement insights, asset properties, and actions that you can perform on an asset.

Note: Asset Hub is a paid feature. For more information, contact your Customer Success Manager (CSM).

Under the Assets section, click an asset to view its details.

At the top of the asset details page, you can view:

- Name of the asset. To edit the asset name, hover your cursor on the name and click the Pencil icon. Click Save to reflect the changes.
- Name of the user who last updated the asset and the time of the update.
- Status of the asset (Draft, Published, or Archived).

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Asset Hub > Admin > Properties:
- Thumbnail assigned to the asset. A great custom thumbnail acts as a preview for the asset. It makes your asset appealing and hints to viewers about what to expect. Also, the thumbnail starts showing all the card views of the asset.
  - For assets shared in DSRs, if the asset thumbnails are updated in Asset Hub, they are automatically updated in DSRs. However, if an asset's thumbnail is changed in a DSR, that thumbnail image is displayed for the asset irrespective of the changes in Asset Hub.
- Asset Owner who owns the responsibility of maintaining the asset. A user who is a collaborator and has Develop Asset permissions of one of the hubs where the asset resides, can be an Asset Owner. By default, Asset Hub populates the creator of the asset as the asset owner. Note: The Asset Owner field can be empty under the following scenarios:
  - Asset is moved to a hub where the Asset Owner is not a collaborator.
  - Asset Owner's permissions have changed.
  - Asset Owner is removed as a collaborator from all the hubs where the asset resides.
  - Asset Owner is removed as a user from the Mindtickle platform.
- Asset description , which provides a brief explanation of what the asset is all about. Description conveys valuable information that helps viewers spot an asset in search results and indicate the type of content in the asset. It also guides the sales rep on which asset to use. For example, a pitch deck's talk track helps the sales rep set the follow-up meeting, and the rep can focus on creating value, controlling the process, and winning deals.
- Attributes associated with the asset that enhance the discoverability of the asset. For example, if the asset is for the buyer journey stage of the sales funnel, it may have attributes awareness, closing, or evaluation associated with it.
- Usage (Internal or External), which lets reps know if they can download and share the asset externally with their prospects or use it only for internal reference. Note: When you change the usage of a shared asset from external to internal, customers or prospects with whom a rep has shared the asset can still view it. Only going forward, reps cannot share that asset.
- Expiry date is an indicator of the reliability of the information in the asset. It ensures the effectiveness of the assets. Once an asset expires, you can either update the asset and extend its expiry date or archive it. Expired assets are still visible to the sales reps but flagged as Expired.
- Expiry reminder reminds you to update the asset before its expiry date or archive if it is no longer needed. Expiration reminder or file update reminder helps keep your organization compliant by automatically tracking expiration date for assets such as team member certifications, contracts, licenses, marketing campaigns, and more. You can manage upcoming renewals or set reminders and follow-up alerts for files that are about to expire.
- File update reminder is sent regularly to a hub collaborator to ensure the asset remains up to date.
- An option to download the assets. If it is set to Yes , the asset is available for download by the reps. If it is set to No (in case an asset contains sensitive information that must not be customized), the reps cannot download the asset. However, they can use the asset in its original form as provided by the Asset Owner.
- An option to save the asset to Google drive. If set to Yes , the asset can be saved to Google drive by the reps.
- Customized asset creation allows reps to duplicate and create a new asset by adding slides from other assets, uploading new slides, or removing existing slides.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Asset Hub > Admin > History:
Asset Hub also saves the changes made to an asset by keeping its version history. The version history helps you track what has changed in the past or which collaborator has changed the asset.

Click the History tab on the right navigation panel to view:

- Historical versions of the asset in chronological order
- Date of the change
- Name of the person who made the change

The History section segregates the changes in the following manner to help you quickly identify major and minor updates:

- Grey dot indicates minor changes made to the metadata of the asset. For example, changes made in asset description or expiry date.
- Blue dot indicates major changes made to the file present within the asset. For example, when a collaborator replaces the file with a new file.
- Red dot indicates asset archival. For example, when a collaborator archives an asset to remove it from the sales rep's view while keeping it in the archived state for any future use.

Admins can get internal and external shareable URL links for assets from the Assets tab on the admin site.

There are two types of shareable links available for an asset:

- Internal links :
  - User : Link for sharing the asset with sales reps (i.e., learners/users) on the learning site. Example: https://deeplinks.mindtickle.com/PizZAp9vYDRb
  - Admin : Link for sharing the asset with admins on the admin site. Example: https://admin.mindtickle.com/new/ui/assets/asset/5572532161024997
- External (public) link : Link for sharing the asset with people outside your organization. After generating the public link, you can enable/disable asset downloads. You can delete the link at any time to revoke access.

For details, see Shareable internal and external links for assets (admins).

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Asset Hub > Admin:
This article explains the best practices to create attributes and their categories, steps to create a category, create or manage attributes, and perform different actions on attributes. The article also explains the difference between tags and attributes.

Note: Asset Hub is a paid feature. For more information, contact your Customer Success Manager (CSM).

Attributes are a way of describing the characteristics of an asset. They are metadata assigned to an asset that helps you filter, organize, add meaning and improve asset discoverability. A sales rep can also browse assets on the Learning Site by applying filters using attributes.

For example, suppose a sales rep intends to reinforce the product value after a customer call by sending the pitch deck and a case study about using a specific product feature. Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Asset Hub > Admin > Attributes vs Tags:
Attributes are a way of describing the characteristics of an asset. They are metadata assigned to an asset that helps you filter, organize, add meaning and improve asset discoverability. Attributes will also help in deriving meaningful analytics on assets going forward.

Tags are attributes that you can apply to all Modules, Files, Questions, Polls, and Evaluation Parameters (Mission and Coaching Sessions). Tags help you filter, organize, search and generate reports on the content (from Tag Analytics). For more information, refer to the Create and Manage Tags article.

The following table explains the difference between Attributes and Tags:

| Criteria | Attributes | Tags |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Score in Readiness Index | Attributes do not contribute towards the score in the Readiness Index. | Tags contribute towards the score in the Readiness Index. |
| Type of Content | You can apply attributes to the assets in Asset Hub. Reps can use the assets in Asset Hub to engage and build credible responses to customers or prospects. | You can apply tags to the learning & coaching content in all Modules, Files, Questions, Polls and Evaluation Parameters (Mission and Coaching Sessions) to build muscle memory and enhance the skills of Reps. |
| Search | Attributes enhance the search capability and provide dynamic sections for Reps to navigate to the right asset. | Tags enhance the search for a file or content used in a Learning Object. |

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Asset Hub > Admin > Best practices on creating attributes and categories:
Having a well-thought-out strategy in creating attributes and their categories help sales reps to quickly browse assets on the Learning Site and determine their usage.

Note: Refer to the roles and permissions article to check if you have permissions to create attributes and categories.

Following are the best practices that we recommend while creating and categorizing attributes:

- Use attributes that display product value to the customer.
- Keep the attribute or category name short.
- Pay attention to spelling.
- Define standard attributes for each category.
- Add use case specific attributes that your sales reps typically use in search.
- Categorize attributes based on different stages in the sales funnel.
- Create a taxonomy document.
- Maintain consistency in attributes and categories name.
- Clean the old irrelevant attributes.

For example, you can create a category for the buyer journey stage of the sales funnel and add attributes like awareness, closing, or evaluation to it.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Asset Hub:
This article gives an overview of Asset Hub, its features, and how you can access and navigate the Assets homepage on the learning site.

Note: Asset Hub is a paid feature. For more information, contact your Customer Success Manager (CSM).

An asset is a sales collateral or a document that helps you communicate effectively with prospects or customers to win deals. A hub is a logical group of assets that helps organize the entire asset repository into broad categories. These two, when combined, form Asset Hub, which manages all of your organization's sales assets. It serves as a single source of truth to quickly access and search assets on the platform.

For example, in Asset Hub, assets are tagged with the right keywords to help you discover them through generic searches. It also shows you the asset description and what it contains to help you quickly browse through the asset and know if it suits your needs. From the Asset Hub dashboard, you can easily spot when an existing asset gets updated and use it with your prospects.

- Monthly

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Asset Hub > Filters:
Attributes and asset properties are a way of describing the characteristics of an asset. They are metadata assigned to an asset. Attributes and asset properties help you browse and filter relevant assets according to your use case.

For example, suppose you intend to reinforce the product value after a customer call by sending the pitch deck and a case study about using a specific feature. You can quickly browse the Learning Site for these assets by applying filters using attributes like Case Study or Pitch Deck under the Collateral Type attribute category. It gives you the privilege to not only locate the right asset but also find related assets without the need to search every asset using the asset name.

From the left panel, you can view different attribute categories and asset properties. Each category relates to a different type of use case. Select the attribute(s) or properties to filter the related assets. Expand a category or property to view all the attributes inside it. You can also search for a specific attribute or property from the Search bar.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Asset Hub > Hub subscriptions:
The Subscribe button in the upper-right corner of the hub page allows you to subscribe and receive daily updates on the latest content. When new assets are added or existing assets are updated for your subscribed hubs, you will receive an email notification with details on the updates. The email is sent at 12:00 am UTC daily, but only if there have been updates to your subscribed hubs. This ensures you stay informed about the latest changes to the content you follow without receiving unnecessary notifications when no updates are available.

Two email templates are used for asset update notifications. The template selected depends on the number of subscribed hubs that contain newly added or updated assets since the previous notification:

- Up to 5 hubs with updates: A detailed email displaying individual asset information for each hub, including asset title, size, and description.
- More than 5 hubs with updates: A condensed digest email displaying each hub name along with the number of newly added or updated assets, as well as the total number of updated assets across all affected hubs.

Each hub listed in the email includes a View assets button that opens the corresponding hub, allowing you to quickly access the latest content.

If you're not signed in during your browser session, you'll be prompted to sign in first. Once signed in, you can anytime use the Change account option to connect a different Google Drive account with Mindtickle.
2. Once signed in, you can to save the asset at:

  - Select a folder within My Drive : Save the asset to a specific folder within your My Drive.
3. Once the asset is saved to your Google Drive > My Drive, a confirmation toast notification appears on the UI.
4. You can find the saved asset file on your Google Drive and make further edits (if required) and share with customers and prospects.

Continue reading for details about the following tabs available in the right panel on the asset details page:

- Details
- Your feedback

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Asset Hub > Details tab > Insights > Your Rating:
Based on your overall experience of the asset usage, discoverability, and effectiveness of the content, you can rate the asset on a scale of 1 (lowest) to 5 (highest) via the stars. You can also provide feedback when rating the asset; it is shared with the admin or asset owner.

Why are rating and feedback important?

- Rating and feedback lets you know that a peer has found the asset useful and thus helps in moving deals forward.
- Rating and feedback let the admin know how the asset has helped you and if any updates are required to improve the overall experience.
- Rating plays a crucial role in optimizing search results.
- It is social proof to validate the quality of the asset. A good rating creates a positive influence on your peers and encourages asset engagement.
- Saves time in finding reliable assets for your use case.

Note:

- You can rate the asset without providing any feedback by clicking the No, thanks button.
- You can rate and provide feedback as many times as you want.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Asset Hub > Details tab > Asset properties:
- Asset Owner (if assigned by the admin) : This section displays the name of the person who owns the responsibility of maintaining the asset. You can contact the asset owner in case you want to suggest any changes to the asset.
- Description : This section displays information about the type of content available within the asset that helps you quickly spot an asset in the search results. It also guides you on which asset to use and how to use it in a situation. For example, a pitch deck’s talk track helps you set the follow-up meeting and focus on creating value, controlling the process and winning deals.
- Attributes : This section displays the attributes associated with the asset. Attributes describe the characteristics of an asset. You can browse and filter relevant assets according to your use case using attributes. For example, suppose you want to reinforce the product value after a customer call by sending the pitch deck and a case study about using a specific feature. You can quickly browse such assets by selecting attributes like Case Study or Pitch Deck under the Collateral Type attribute category. It gives you the privilege to locate the right asset and find related assets without the need to search every asset using the asset name.
- Usage : This section displays whether to use the asset internally or externally. Internal usage indicates that you can use the asset only within your organization. External usage indicates that you can use the asset with your customers or prospects. For example, you can use a battle card when comparing your product with competitors and hence its usage is internal. You can use customer testimonials to improve trust among your prospects and hence its usage is external.
- Expiry : This section displays the asset expiry date, which ensures the effectiveness of the content. Expiry date indicates until when the content is relevant. When an asset expires, it is advisable not to refer to that asset until updated.
- Downloadable : This section displays whether you can download the asset or not. If an asset is not downloadable (in case the asset contains sensitive information which must not be customized), you can only use the asset in its original form. Contact your admin or Asset Owner for more details on using such assets.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Asset Hub > Your feedback tab:
The Your feedback tab on the asset details page allows reps to submit and share their feedback on the asset. In addition to the rating and feedback under the Insights section, you can use this tab to share your experience and overall feedback regarding the asset. The feedback is a strong mechanism to intimate the admin or asset owner about how helpful the asset is, and any improvements or updates required. Thus, establishing a feedback loop among users and admins and helping the admins to improve the content iteratively.

Type your feedback, questions, or comments on the asset in the space provided and click Submit.

If there are multiple feedback provided for the asset, you can view them in the list view. Also, you can also view if the feedback is resolved by the admin/asset owner. Next to any feedback, click theicon → Delete to delete submitted feedback.

Your submitted feedback is listed in the Your feedback tab with the “Submitted” status. Once an admin resolves the feedback, the status is updated to “Resolved”. If an admin re-opens any resolved feedback, the status is updated to “Reopened”.

Note:

- This tab also includes ratings and feedback from the Details tab → Insights section.
- Feedback is only visible to learners with access to the asset.
