Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Series:
You cannot archive and then retrieve a series. You can only delete a series permanently.

To permanently delete a published series that is no longer required:

1. On the admin site homepage, click the Training icon and select Series.

The Series page is displayed.

2. Click the series to be deleted.

3. Archive all the modules and remove all certifications within that series to enable the Delete icon.

4. Click the Delete icon in the series header section across the series name.

5. In the confirmation pop-up that appears, click Delete.

Once the series is deleted successfully, you receive a notification and redirected to the admin homepage.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Readiness Index (RI):
You can sync the Salesforce’s sales metrics for business outcomes, such as quota attainment and win rates, with Mindtickle so that the metrics can be used and viewed in Readiness Index (RI) in Mindtickle Analytics. This will give you insights into the impact of your readiness initiatives on your business outcomes.

Note: To make use of the Salesforce CRM’s business outcome metrics in Mindtickle, Readiness Index (RI) must be enabled for your Learning Site. For help, contact Mindtickle Support. For information about the Readiness Index (RI), see Readiness Index (RI) Overview.

This article provides the definitions and calculations of the Salesforce business outcome metrics that you are asked to select while integrating with Salesforce. For information on how to integrate and sync Salesforce business outcome data with Mindtickle, see Sales Outcome Data Sync with Salesforce (Beta).

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Readiness Index (RI) > List of metrics:
To make the Salesforce metrics for business outcomes easier to understand, Mindtickle has grouped the metrics into meaningful categories.

For example, the Value Per Opportunity metric under the Pipeline Sales Metrics category makes use of the “Opportunity” and “Opportunity Split” Salesforce objects with fields, such as OwnerId, Amount, Is Split, Isclosed, IsWon, and Close Date.

Note: This integration uses only standard Salesforce metrics. Custom metrics cannot be used currently.

The following are the metrics that you can sync from Salesforce into Mindtickle:

| Pipeline Sales Metrics | Primary Conversion Metrics | Sales Hiring Metrics | Sales KPI | Sales Productivity Metrics |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Average Selling Price (ASP) or Average Contract Value | % Opportunity Won | Time to Create First Opportunity | Quota Attainment | Sales Activity Per Opportunity |
| Value Per Opportunity | % Opportunity Lost | Time to First Activity | Total Revenue | Sales Velocity |
| Number of Opportunities Created | Opportunity Win Rate | Time to First Meeting |  | Sales Velocity Per Opportunity |
| Number of Opportunities Assigned | Close Rate (Closed Funnel) | Time to First Deal |  |  |
| Number of Opportunities won |  | Time to Third Deal |  |  |
| Number of Opportunities Lost |  | Time to Fifth Deal |  |  |
| Sales Cycle Length |  |  |  |  |

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Readiness Index (RI) > Metric definitions and calculations > Pipeline sales metrics > Value Per Opportunity:
Definition: The expected amount you would win from an opportunity you create.

Calculation: Close rate x Average Selling Price (ASP)

1. First, you need to calculate close rate and ASP from your Salesforce data.
  - To measure Closed Funnel close rate with Salesforce data: Count the number of opportunities won that have a close date for a given timeframe, then count the number of opportunities lost that have a close date for a given timeframe. Then, divide the opportunities won by the sum of the opportunities won + lost.
  - To measure ASP with Salesforce data: Take the sum of the amount from closed won opportunities that have a close date for a given timeframe and divide by the number of opportunities won that have a close date for a given timeframe.
2. Once you’ve calculated both close rate and ASP, multiply the two to get the value per opportunity.

Definition: Number of opportunities assigned to the sales rep.

Calculation: Sum of opportunities created by others but assigned to a sales rep + opportunities created by the rep.

1. Get the list of opportunity field history (Opportunity Owner) for a sales rep (New Value) in a given timeframe (Created Date). This will give the count of opportunities that are created by others but assigned to this rep.
2. Now, count the opportunities for the sales rep (Created by ID) in a given timeframe (Created Date). This will give the count of opportunities created by this rep.
3. Sum up the assigned and created opportunities count.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Readiness Index (RI) > Metric definitions and calculations > Sales Productivity metrics > Sales Velocity:
Definition: The expected output you would get from a sales rep or team in a given timeframe.

Calculation: (Total number of opportunities x Average Selling Price x Close rate) / Sales cycle

You need to calculate opportunities created, close rate, Average Selling Price (ASP), and sales cycle from your Salesforce data as follows:

1. To measure opportunities created, count the number of opportunities that have a Created Date in a given timeframe.
2. To measure closed funnel close rate:
  - Count the number of opportunities won that have a Close Date in the timeframe.
  - Count the number of opportunities lost that have a Close Date in the timeframe.
  - Divide the opportunities won by the sum of the opportunities won + lost.
3. To measure ASP: Sum up the amount from closed won opportunities that have a Close Date in the timeframe and divide by the number of opportunities won that have a Close Date in the timeframe.
4. To measure the sales cycle:
  - Run a report of opportunities won in a given timeframe. Count the number of opportunities that you get.
  - For each opportunity, calculate the number of days between Created Date and Close Date. Sum up the total number of days. Divide that by 30 to get the monthly value.
  - Divide the number of months by the number of opportunities you won.
5. Once you have the data for opportunities created, close rate, ASP and sales cycle, multiply the first three (opportunities created x close rate x ASP) and divide it by sales cycle.

Associated Salesforce objects and fields:

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Sales Challenges (Beta):
A live challenge can be incorporated within an ILT session. The Admin or the Instructor can configure the live challenge with questions specific to the topic of discussion to reinforce learners’ knowledge or with generic questions. Thus adding an element of fun to the session. The invited learners then join in to play the game. Once the Live Challenge ends, the Leaderboard displays data about various aspects of the game such as the total number of participants, each participant’s score, and top scorers. This data can be utilized by the Admin and/or the Instructor to gauge areas of improvement for future ILT sessions.

Thus, integrating a live challenge in an ILT session enables you to not only grab learners’ attention during the session, but also evaluate the learners’ understanding of the topic.

To conduct the live challenge as an in-session activity within an ILT session, the admin or the series collaborators can configure it in a new session or an existing session.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Sales Challenges (Beta) > Configure a live challenge within an ILT session:
1. Add a new session .
2. On the new session details page, in the In-session Activity section, click Create live challenge .
3. On the Create live challenge pop-up, click Download sample.
4. A sample file (with sample information for your reference) is downloaded to your system. It contains information for the following seven fields: Question Type, Question Text, Answer Choice 1, Answer Choice 2, Answer Choice 3, Answer Choice 4 and Question Image.
5. Update the file by entering the appropriate information in each field.Note:
  - Live Challenges only support Multiple Choice Questions (MCQs), therefore, the Question Type for each question should be set to MCQ .
  - To configure the correct answer, enter a * before the text in the corresponding Answer Choice field. For example, *Apple.
  - The supported file formats include .xlsx , .xlsb , .xlsm , .xls , .csv and .txt .
  - The file size should not exceed 4MB.
6. Live Challenges support image-based questions. To add an image to a question, copy the image URL and paste it into the corresponding Question Image field.Note:
  - Ensure that the images are publicly accessible.
  - The recommended image size is 300 x 400 pixels. Images larger than the recommended size are scaled down to maintain the aspect ratio.
7. Once you have entered all the information in the file, save it.
8. Click Upload and select the file saved on your system to upload the file. Alternatively, you can drag the file from your system and drop it onto the Create live challenge pop-up. Note : You can upload only one file at a time.
9. Once the file is uploaded successfully, two unique links, a Moderator Link and a Player Link, are automatically generated. These links are available in the Session details pop-up under the In-session activity section.The Moderator Link is used by the Instructor to conduct the live challenge, whereas the Player Link is used by the learners to play the live challenge. To copy a link, click the copy icon against it.Note:
  - The Moderator and Player Links are unique. Once a live challenge is played using these links, they cannot be used again.
  - You can replace or edit the questions that have already been added to a Live Challenge. For more information, refer Replace a live challenge .
  - You can delete the Live Challenge and remove it as part of the in-session activity from the Session. For more information, refer Delete a live challenge . To enable the Instructor in conducting the Live Challenge, share these links with them via a communication channel of your preference such as email or instant messaging communicators. You can also Email the Game Links directly from the Session Details page after you have published the Session.
10. To add Instructor details to the In-session details page, click the Instructors and facilitators tab, in the Instructors tab, enter the Instructor name, Instructor email and any additional information about the instructor in the respective fields.To notify the instructor about updates made to the session, select the Notify Instructors via email checkbox. If selected, an email is sent to the Instructors when:a. The module is publishedb. The session time or location is publishedc. An Instructor is added to or removed from the sessiond. The live challenge is added, replaced or deletedNote: If the Notify Instructors via email checkbox is selected, the Game Links (Moderator link and player link) for the live challenge are shared as a part of the email too. Publish the session .
11. To share the game links in an email from within the session, click the session on the Events and sessions tab.
12. On the in-session activity tab, click the Email links button on the Session details screen.
13. In the Email game links pop-up, enter the email address to send the game links and click Email game links.A confirmation message displays notifying that the email with the game links has been sent.The email is sent in the following format:

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Sales Challenges (Beta):
When conducting a live training Session, it is important that you:

- Find the right way to break the ice with the Learners
- Keep the Learners engaged throughout the Session
- Evaluate the Learners’ understanding of the topic
- Take necessary steps to improve future Sessions based on your evaluation

A Live Challenge helps you achieve all the above objectives. A Live Challenge is a Multiple Choice Question (MCQ) based Quiz that can be driven by the Instructor and played as a game amongst the Learners. Once the Instructor starts the game, the Learners are subjected to a series of questions, each having four answer options. The Learners select the correct answer out of the four options. For every right answer, the Learners gain points. The Leaderboard displays the live score for each Learner as the game progresses. The Leaderboard is visible to all Learners as well as the Instructor. This introduces a sense of competition amongst the Learners which drives them to perform better throughout the Session.

Note: The Live Challenges feature is available only on request. To enable it for your organization, contact your Customer Success Manager.

With this integration, you can sync and view Salesforce outcome data such as quota attainment, win rates, and more based on different metrics in Mindtickle Analytics. This integration gives you insights into the impact of your readiness initiatives on your business outcomes.

This article explains the process of setting up the integration.

Note:

- This integration can be configured for your organization only if Readiness Index is enabled and set up.
- This integration does not require the installation of the Mindtickle app from Salesforce AppExchange.

Prerequisite: Mindtickle strongly recommends using a dedicated Salesforce Integration User to perform this integration.The integration user must have access to the following objects mentioned in the table below to successfully set up the integration.

Note:

- The following permissions are required to fetch the SFDC pipeline sales data metrics, such as the number of opportunities created, assigned, won, and lost, and the sales cycle length. For more information on other data metrics, see Pipeline Sales Metrics, see Pipeline Sales Metrics .
- If you select objects not listed in the table below, you must grant View All access to those objects to fetch the data correctly.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Data Sync and Reporting API > Integration Setup Steps:
1. In the admin site sidebar, click Account > Settings > Security & integrations. On the Security and integrations page, scroll down to the Sales Outcome Data Sync section and click the Connect button.

Note:

- You can see this option only if RI is enabled on your Mindtickle Learning Site.
- If your Salesforce account is already connected via User Sync, skip steps 3 and 4.

3. On the displayed screen, enter your Salesforce admin credentials to log in.

4. On the displayed pop-up, click Allow.

4. Once your Salesforce account is connected, click the Configure to initiate sync button to select the metrics you want to sync.

5. On the Configure Sales Outcome Data Metrics page that opens, select the metrics you want to sync with Mindtickle and click Next.

6. Select the sync start date and click Next.

You can sync a maximum of the last six months’ data. All the data created or updated after midnight (based on your timezone) on the selected date is synced. We recommend selecting an older date as the historical data will help you view your reps’ incremental progress.

Note: Once the sync starts, you cannot change the sync date.

7. Click the Confirm button to confirm access to Salesforce data. The sync starts immediately.

Note: The automatic sync is initiated every 24 hours.

You can view the sync status and the last sync information under the Sales Outcome Data Sync section.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Data Sync and Reporting API > Troubleshooting:
If there are any errors during the sync, the UI will display error messages. This section explains the errors and possible solutions for scenarios you may encounter during sync.

1. Error : (n) Metrics will not be synced at this time because the Salesforce objects and fields associated with them are inaccessible. Reason : If Mindtickle fails to retrieve any object or fields from Salesforce, the related metrics will not sync. Resolution : Check your Salesforce settings to make sure Mindtickle can access those objects and fields in the next sync, or uncheck the metrics that show an error and then click Next .
2. Error : Mindtickle was not able to connect to your Salesforce. Reason : If Mindtickle cannot connect to your Salesforce account due to authentication failure such as “token expired,” then Mindtickle will stop syncing the data. Resolution : You can re-authenticate your Salesforce account to continue syncing the data.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > User Management > Users and Groups:
You can assign roles to one or more users in bulk from the Users page. You can also assign roles to users individually. This article explains how you can assign roles to users in bulk and individually.

Assign roles to users in bulk:

You can assign roles to users in bulk from the following places:

- Bulk action tray: Using the bulk action tray that appears at the bottom of the screen when you select one or more users.
- Actions via CSV: Using the Actions via CSV > Bulk assign roles option.

Assign roles to users individually:

You can assign roles to a particular user from the following places:

- From the Users page, using the More options button for a user.
- From a user’s profile page.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > User Management > Users and Groups > Assign roles in bulk > Through bulk action tray:
Perform the following steps to assign roles to one or more users in bulk at once using the bulk action tray:

1. Sign in to the admin site.
2. On the left navigation bar, click Users and select Users.
3. On the Users page, select one or more users to whom you want to assign roles. Then, in the bulk action tray at the bottom of the screen, click the More options icon and select Assign roles.The Assign roles to users pop-up is displayed. It lists all roles available on your learning site, including custom roles. For a particular role, it also displays whether it is already assigned to any of the selected users.Note: The Learner role is assigned to all users by default.
4. Select one or more roles to assign to the selected users and click Assign roles to users.
5. When the roles are assigned successfully, a notification is displayed at the top of the screen. In the Roles column, hover over the assigned roles for a user to view all roles assigned to them, including the roles you just assigned. Click the button in the bulk action tray to clear the user selection.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Sales Challenges (Beta):
1. Open any browser and enter the Moderator Link in the address bar. Press Enter . The following message is displayed on the screen until at least one Learner joins the game:
2. As and when each Learner joins the game, their name appears on the screen under the Players tab. It also displays the total number of Learners that have joined the game.
3. Click the Questions tab to view a list of questions and the time limit set for each question. Note : The default time limit for Learners to answer each question is 20 seconds.
4. Wait until all the Learners invited to the Challenge have joined, and then click Start Game . The game timer counts down from five seconds and at the end of the countdown, a question with four possible answer options appears on the screen.
5. The question timer starts counting down from 20 seconds, indicating that the Learners have only 20 seconds to choose an answer. While the Learners attempt to answer the question, the screen displays the time remaining for the Learners to answer it. It also displays a dynamic count of the number of participants who have attempted the question.
6. At the end of 15 seconds, a warning sound signal plays on the Instructor and each Learner’s system to warn them about the last 5 seconds left to answer the question. Note : If all the Learners select an answer before the 20-second time limit, the timer ends automatically once the last Learner selects an answer.
7. At the end of 20 seconds:
  - The correct answer is highlighted in green.
  - The number of Learners who answered the question is displayed.
  - The number of players who answered the question correctly is displayed.
8. Before you proceed to the next question, the Leaderboard with each participant’s current score is displayed. A Learner’s score is calculated after each question using the following formula: Score= (1 - (time taken to answer * 0.3 / total time allotted)) * maxScore Where, time taken to answer is the time taken (in seconds) by the Learner to answer the question total time allotted is the total time (20 seconds) allotted to the Learner to answer the question maxScore is the maximum score (500 points) allotted to the question Note :
  - The number of points a Learner earns depends on the following criteria:
    - Choosing the correct answer.
    - How fast the learner chooses the correct answer. For example, if the learner chooses the correct answer within the first 5 seconds, then the Learner earns more points than if they choose the correct answer within the last 5 seconds.
  - The Learner’s score remains unchanged if they select a wrong option or do not select any option.
9. To proceed with the game, click Start Next Question . As the Live Challenge progresses, the questions that have already been played are greyed out in the Questions tab.
10. Once all the questions have been played, the Live Challenge ends and the Leaderboard appears with each participant’s Final Scores . To rate your overall experience, select one of the three emoticons in the feedback section at the top of the screen. After you select a rating, you are prompted to provide additional feedback. Enter your feedback in the Any comments field and click Submit Comment . To get a detailed analysis of the different aspects of the Live Challenge, click Generate Game Report . For more information, refer Generate a Live Challenge Report .

To export a live challenge report from within a session:

1. Navigate to the ILT module with the session where the live challenge was conducted.
2. Click the Events and sessions tab. The module’s ILT sessions are displayed.
3. Click the More options icon against the session.
4. Click Email live challenge report . Note : This option is only available if a live challenge has been conducted within that session and the session has ended.
5. Enter the valid email address of the recipient in the Export live challenge report pop-up. Note : You can enter multiple email addresses separated by a comma to export the report to multiple recipients.
6. Click Export report . You will receive a notification informing you that the report will be sent shortly.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Sales Challenges (Beta):
1. Open any browser and enter the player link in the address bar. Press Enter .
2. Click Login via Mindtickle .
3. You are added to the game as a Player with your Mindtickle username. While you wait for the Moderator to start the game, a list of the learners who have joined the game and their total number is displayed. Note : If you join the game after the Moderator has started the game, the following message is displayed on the screen, and you are directed to the next new question.
4. Once the Moderator starts the game, the master game timer counts down from 5 seconds before the first question and its four answer options appear on the screen.
5. The question remains on the screen for 20 seconds. The screen also displays:
  - a timer for the current question, which counts down from 20 seconds
  - the serial number of the question
  - a dynamic count of the number of participants who have attempted the question
6. Choose an answer from the four options. Once you choose an answer, you cannot change your selection. At the end of 15 seconds, a warning sound signal plays on the instructor's and each learner’s system to warn them about the 5 seconds left to answer the question. Note : If all the Learners select an answer before the 20-second time limit, the timer ends automatically once the last Learner selects an answer.
7. At the end of 20 seconds:
  - The correct answer is highlighted in green.
  - The number of players who answered the question correctly is displayed.
  - You are notified if your selection was the correct or the wrong answer.
  - The number of points you earn is displayed. If the selection was the same as the correct answer, you earn points. Note : The number of points you earn depends on the following criteria:
    - Choosing the correct answer.
    - How fast you choose the correct answer. For example, if you choose the correct answer within the first five seconds, you earn more points than if you choose the correct answer within the last five seconds.
  - Your score remains unchanged if you select the wrong answer.
  - Your score remains unchanged if you don’t select any option before the time ends. Before the Moderator proceeds to the next question, the Leaderboard is displayed. The Leaderboard shows the top scorers as well as each participant’s score.
8. The Moderator decides the course of the game and continues accordingly by moving on to the next question. Note : The live challenge is not time-bound. The interval between questions is decided by the Moderator.
9. Once all the questions have been played, the live challenge ends, and the Leaderboard appears with each participant’s Final score . To rate your overall experience, select one of the three emoticons in the feedback section at the top of the screen. After you select a rating, you are prompted to provide additional feedback. Enter your feedback in the Any comments field and click Submit Comment .
10. To skip the above Step, click Skip Comments .

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Series:
You can mirror modules from one series to one or more series. Such modules that are present in multiple series are called multi-present modules. Mirroring a module from one series allows you to replicate it in another series quickly. You can either mirror a single module or multiple modules at once.

When you mirror a module:

- It is added to the destination series in the Published state.
- All settings and contents of the module persist in the destination series as well.
- Any changes made to an instance of a module (in any series in which it is available) are reflected in all other instances of that module in all other series. For example, any changes to the name, description, content, due date, scheduled archival settings, and learner progress (Score and Completion) are reflected in all instances of the mirrored module. However, reminders can be set independently for each instance of the mirrored module.
- When a learner completes a module in a particular series, the learner’s progress is automatically marked as Complete in all instances of the module present in other series as well. This happens only if the learner is already invited to that module or when they get invited.

Note:

- You cannot mirror coaching sessions in a public series.
- If you select a sequentially locked series as the destination series, the mirrored modules will be chronologically added after the modules that already exist in the series. Their order will be the same as that in the source series, and they will be locked by default. Each module in the destination series will be unlocked only after the previous modules are completed.

You can mirror modules in two ways:

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Series > Mirror a single module > Mirror a single module to an existing series:
To mirror a module in an existing series:

1. Navigate to the series from which you want to copy the module. Click on the More options icon and click Mirror in.
2. Click on the Search series drop-down and select the destination series to mirror the selected module.
3. For series with sections, select the sections from which you want to mirror modules.
4. To mirror the module in another series, click +Add another series and repeat Steps 3 and 4.Note: You can mirror the module to multiple destination series that are available on your admin site and you have access to.
5. Click Next.
6. You can choose which category of learners will be invited to the mirrored module in the destination series.

Click the drop-down list to select the available options.

- Invite all learners in each destination series: Invite learners who are invited to at least one module in the series.
- Invite fully invited learners in each destination series: Invite learners who are invited to all modules in the series.

Note:

- This is applicable only to published modules in the Invite-only destination series. Once mirrored, some learners in the destination series cannot access a few modules.
- By default, all learners invited to at least one module in the destination series are invited to the mirrored module.
- Learners independently subscribed to the public series are automatically invited to the newly published module. Only learners invited by the admin receive the update.

7. Select the Notify the learners via email checkbox if you want the learners to receive an email notification inviting them to the module.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Series > Manage the availability of a mirrored module > Remove an instance of a mirrored module:
1. Follow Steps 1 to 3 of the View the list of all series in which the module is present section.
2. Click the Delete icon against the series to remove the module instance from it. Once you click the Delete icon , the series is removed from the list, indicating that the module is no longer available in that series.
3. Click Confirm to complete the action. You receive a confirmation message to indicate that the action is completed successfully.

Note:

- Removing an instance of a mirrored module from a series only removes it from that series. The module will still be available in the source series and any other series in which it has been mirrored.
- Removing an instance of a mirrored module is not the same as archiving it. To archive a mirrored module, refer Archive or Retrieve a module (Beta) . Archiving a mirrored module archives it from all the series it is available in.
- When an instance of a mirrored module is removed from a series, it will no longer be visible to the learners in that series.
- When a module's instance is removed from a series, its Analytics data also becomes unavailable within that series.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > Admin > Access Call AI analytics:
In the admin site, click the Analytics > Call AI.

On the Call AI screen, you can view how your team performs in sales conversations and derive useful insights from the statistics shown under the following pages:

Adoption

Includes four adoption and usage reports that offer analytics at the organization, team (manager), and individual levels. These reports provide visibility into Call AI usage, helping admins understand adoption trends and take action to improve engagement.

1. Activation report : Tracks users with the Call AI recorder role, including total users assigned, calendar integration status, and monthly active users (active or inactive). It helps assess adoption rates and identify teams or individuals who may need additional support or training to improve activation.
2. Calls report : Provides data on total time spent on calls, recorded calls, disabled recordings, and Copilot prompts used. It offers insights into recording behavior, ensuring calls are being recorded properly and effectively.
3. Interactions report : Tracks user engagement with call recordings, including the number of unique calls reviewed, comments, private messages, and calls shared. It highlights how actively users are engaging with feedback and coaching tools, helping identify those who may need more encouragement to participate.
4. Coaching report : Focuses on manager-level coaching activities, tracking calls reviewed, coaching forms submitted, and comments or private messages on recordings. This helps managers monitor their coaching efforts and ensure they are leveraging Call AI’s features to support and develop their teams.

For information on the adoption reports for managers, see Call AI adoption reports (managers).

In the admin site, click the Analytics > Call AI.

On the Call AI screen, you can view how your team performs in sales conversations and derive useful insights from the statistics shown under the following pages:

Adoption

Includes four adoption and usage reports that offer analytics at the organization, team (manager), and individual levels. These reports provide visibility into Call AI usage, helping admins understand adoption trends and take action to improve engagement.

1. Activation report : Tracks users with the Call AI recorder role, including total users assigned, calendar integration status, and monthly active users (active or inactive). It helps assess adoption rates and identify teams or individuals who may need additional support or training to improve activation.
2. Calls report : Provides data on total time spent on calls, recorded calls, disabled recordings, and Copilot prompts used. It offers insights into recording behavior, ensuring calls are being recorded properly and effectively.
3. Interactions report : Tracks user engagement with call recordings, including the number of unique calls reviewed, comments, private messages, and calls shared. It highlights how actively users are engaging with feedback and coaching tools, helping identify those who may need more encouragement to participate.
4. Coaching report : Focuses on manager-level coaching activities, tracking calls reviewed, coaching forms submitted, and comments or private messages on recordings. This helps managers monitor their coaching efforts and ensure they are leveraging Call AI’s features to support and develop their teams.

For information on the adoption reports for managers, see Call AI adoption reports (managers).

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > Manager > Team Summary:
In the upper section of the page, you can view the Team Summary that shows your sales Reps’ average performance calculated over a set duration for the following data points. These data points give you insights into individual and team performance on qualified calls.

- Talk% : Indicates how long your team talks on calls. It is calculated as the average of the Talk% of your team’s calls for the selected time range.
- Longest monologue : Indicates how long your Reps talked uninterrupted during calls. It is calculated as an average of the longest monologues of all calls during the selected period.
- Interchanges : Indicates how often the conversation switched between your Reps and prospects or customers. Interchanges help you identify if your team is talking too much or too little in their sales meetings. It is calculated as an hourly average of interchanges during calls.
- Filler words : Indicates that the Rep is hesitant or unsure of the topic of discussion. It is calculated as the average number of filler words used by your Reps per hour in calls during the selected time range.
- Questions asked : Indicates the questions asked by your Reps. Asking the right questions shows your team's expertise in the field and that they want to solve the prospect's problem. It is calculated as an hourly average of all questions asked by your team during calls.
- Questions received : Indicates the questions asked by the prospects or customers and their interest in your product or service. It is calculated as an hourly average of all questions received by your teams during calls.
- Thinking time : Indicates the time taken by the Reps to respond during an interchange. Thinking Time helps to analyze and formulate the most appropriate response.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > Manager > Summary and Trend:
This tab allows you to view how much time your sales Rep spends talking on their calls against the winning behavior and model “Talk%” that yields the best outcomes.

For example, if the average Talk% of your team is 65% and the winning behavior is 50%. It means your team is talking more on calls than the top Reps in your organization. You can coach your Reps to listen more to the customer’s needs, build rapport with the customer and align to the winning behavior.

You can hover over the Info icon to view the Talk% description in a tooltip.

In the graph:

- The y-axis shows the average of the Talk% of your team’s calls.
- The green dotted line shows the winning behavior.
- The x-axis shows the selected time range .

Hover over a point in the graph to view the total number of team calls used for calculating the average of Talk%.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > Manager > User vs. Stage Heatmap:
This tab allows you to view each Rep’s average Talk% at different deal stages. The colors indicate deviation from the winning behavior.

For example, suppose a Rep’s average Talk% is 25% in the demo stage. It means the Rep deviates the most from the winning behavior and needs immediate coaching. The coaching can be on increasing communication and asking good questions to understand how the product can solve customers’ problems.

In the table:

- The green cells show the Reps closer to the winning behavior (75 - 100%).
- The yellow cells show the Reps that exhibit some of the traits from the winning behavior and are average performers (25 - 75%).
- The red cells show the Reps that deviate the most from the winning behavior and need immediate coaching (0-25%).
- The cells marked NA shows that no recordings are available for the Rep in that deal stage.

If you spot the Warning icon for a column in the table, it indicates that there are not enough calls to calculate the winning behavior for that stage.

Click any cell to view the Rep’s recording for that stage. To learn more, refer to the Rep Report Card article.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > Manager > Summary and Trend:
- What Your Team Spoke
  - Themes Covered: The number and the names of themes your team covered during the call. Admin can define the average number of themes to cover in a call by your team while setting up Call Score for your Call AI instance.
  - Questions Asked: The number of questions your team asked the customer or prospect on the call. The average number of questions your team should ask is 7-13 questions.
- How Your Team Spoke
  - Talk:Listen: The % of the time your team talked vs. the % of the time they listened on the call. The average talk:listen ratio is 40%:65%.
  - Speech Pace: How was the Rep’s delivery of words compared to the Average Speaking Rate of 150-190 WPM (Words Per Minute). The speech pace below 150 WPM is considered slow, and anything above 190 WPM is considered fast.
  - Filler Words: The commonly used fillers in conversation to help your team avoid them on their calls. For example, suppose a Rep has repeatedly used the word ‘basically’ in the conversation. In that case, the Filler Words parameter will list the word ‘basically’ along with the number of times the word repeats on the call. Some examples of filler words are: basically, essentially, typically, umm, hmmm, aaa, you know, and so on.
  - Call Length: How closely your team has met the average call length, which is 25 - 75 mins.

To learn more, refer to the Call Score Overview article.

In the graph:

- The y-axis shows the average Call Score% of your team.
- The green dotted line shows the winning behavior.
- The x-axis shows the selected time range .

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > Manager > User vs. Stage Heatmap:
This tab allows you to view each Rep’s average Call Score at different deal stages. The colors indicate deviation from the winning behavior.

For example, suppose a Rep’s average Call Score% is 25% in the demo stage. It means the Rep deviates the most from the winning behavior and needs immediate coaching. The coaching can be on increasing communication and asking good questions to understand how the product can solve customers’ problems.

In the table:

- The green cells show the Reps closer to the winning behavior (75 - 100%).
- The yellow cells show the Reps that exhibit some of the traits from the winning behavior and are average performers (25 - 75%).
- The red cells show the Reps that deviate the most from the winning behavior and need immediate coaching (0-25%).
- The cells marked NA shows that no recordings are available for the Rep in that deal stage.

If you spot the Warning icon for a column in the table, it means there are not enough calls to calculate the winning behavior for that stage.

Click any cell to view the Rep’s recording for that stage. To learn more, refer to the Rep Report Card article.

This article explains the Talk Track tab under the Call AI team analytics section.

Talk track analytics helps you view how often your team discusses a theme with prospects or customers. You can compare these insights with the winning behavior to understand how your team must discuss a theme during their calls.

For example, if you notice that a Rep is talking less about the pricing theme than the winning behavior, you may coach the Rep to be upfront and speak confidently about the prices. The Rep can consider sharing the price early in the sales cycle to win deals.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > Manager > Access Talk Track > Point of Comparison:
You can view the comparison of Talk Track with:

- Winning Behavior : It is the most frequent behavior exhibited by the top Reps during their sales conversations that helps in winning deals. It acts as a benchmark for each conversation stat. Winning Behavior is generated after analyzing the calls of the top Reps selected by the Admin. It is calculated every 30 days. To learn more, refer to the Calculate Winning Behavior article.
- Company Average : If winning behavior is not available (because of lack of data), you can compare your team’s performance against the company’s average. Company Average is calculated after analyzing calls of all sales Reps in your company. It is calculated every seven days.

In the center of the page, you can view a bar chart that shows the following:

- What is your team talking about?
- How is it different as compared to the top Reps?
- Which Reps tend to differ from the winning behavior?

In the bar chart:

- The blue bar indicates the themes discussed by your team and % of calls in which the team discusses a particular theme.
- The green bar indicates the winning behavior.

For example, if your team is not talking about the MEDDIC (Metrics, Economic buyer, Decision criteria, Decision process, Identify pain and Champion) theme on their calls and the winning behavior for MEDDIC is 50%. It means that the top Reps in your organization talk about MEDDIC methodology in 50% of their calls. You can coach your team to use MEDDIC for better customer qualifications.

Alternatively, you can choose to view a line graph that shows the overall trend of your team’s performance compared to the winning behavior for a particular theme.

- In the end, before making a purchase, when customers are weighing the cost and benefits of your product.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > Manager:
This article explains the Voice of Market tab under the Call AI team analytics section.

Keywords are your prospect’s intent signals. They help you know what your prospects are looking for and how you can cater to their needs. Voice of Market is a group of statistics designed to help you identify which keywords and use cases are trending and are discussed most by prospects and Reps. You can use these insights to drive product decisions and tailor your team’s sales pitch.

For example, if the external participants (prospects or customers) mention the Live Session keyword more often during calls. It indicates that they have an interest in a virtual training program.

- Prepare your team to pitch the virtual training program more efficiently and effectively.
- Get to in-market prospects before the competitors.
- Reach the prospects when it matters the most.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > Manager:
This article explains the Rep Report Card, which gives Managers a holistic view of a Rep’s performance across all analytics metrics.

A Rep Report Card is a personalized report of Reps’ performance on sales calls. It compares their performance with the top Reps in the organization or the company average. It is your go-to page for a one-on-one with a Rep. You can use the Rep Report Card to coach your Reps based on their behavioral insights and drill down the analytics data to the recording level.

For example, the Rep Report Card provides the following benefits:

- Gives timely performance updates : If you notice that a Rep is hesitant to ask questions during a call, you can immediately coach the Rep on the importance of asking questions.
- Allows you to set realistic goals : If you notice that a target of 100 calls a day is high for a Rep compared to the winning behavior, you can reduce the target and re-evaluate the Rep's performance.
- Aids informed decisions : If you notice that customers talk a lot about a competitor during calls, you can coach the Rep on objection handling and accordingly set your campaigns for better positioning in the market.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > Manager > Conversation Stats:
This tab shows the average performance of the Rep calculated over a set duration around the following data points.

- Talk% : Indicates how long your team talks on calls. It is calculated as the average of the Talk% of your team’s calls for the selected time range.
- Longest Monologue : Indicates how long your Reps talked uninterrupted during calls. It is calculated as an average of the longest monologues of all calls during the selected period.
- Interchanges : Indicates how often the conversation switched between your Reps and prospects or customers. Interchanges help you identify if your team is talking too much or too little in their sales meetings. It is calculated as an hourly average of interchanges during calls.
- Filler Words : Indicates that the Rep is hesitant or unsure of the topic of discussion. It is calculated as the average number of filler words used by your Reps per hour in calls during the selected time range.
- Questions Asked : Indicates the questions asked by your Reps. Asking the right questions shows your team's expertise in the field and that they want to solve the prospect's problem. It is calculated as an hourly average of all questions asked by your team during calls.
- Questions Received : Indicates the questions asked by the prospects or customers and their interest in your product or service. It is calculated as an hourly average of all questions received by your teams during calls.
- Thinking Time : Indicates the time taken by the Reps to respond during an interchange. Thinking Time helps to analyze and formulate the most appropriate response.

Alternatively, hover over the Info icon to view the description of each of these data points.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > Manager > Conversation Stats > Point of Comparison:
You can view the comparison of these Conversation Stats with:

- Winning Behavior : It is the most frequent behavior exhibited by the top Reps during their sales conversations that helps in winning deals. It acts as a benchmark for each conversation stat. Winning Behavior is generated after analyzing the calls of the top Reps selected by the Admin and is calculated every 30 days. To learn more, refer to the Winning Behavior article.
- Company Average : If winning behavior is not available (because of lack of data), you can compare your team’s performance with the company’s average. Company Average is calculated after analyzing calls of all Reps in your company and is calculated every seven days.

Under the Conversation Stats tab, you can choose to view the comparison of the Rep with the winning behavior around the following metrics:

- Trendline
- Breakdown by Stage

Note: Following topics show an example of Talk% data point to explain each of these metrics. Scroll down the page to compare the Rep’s performance around the rest of the data points.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > Manager > Conversation Stats > Trendline:
Choose this metric to view how much time the Rep spends talking on their calls compared to the winning behavior and model Talk% that yields the best outcome.

For example, if the average Talk% of the Rep is 65% and the winning behavior is 50%. It indicates the Rep talks a lot on calls and you can coach the Rep to listen more to understand the buyer’s needs and build rapport with the customer.

In the graph:

- The y-axis shows the average of the Talk% of the Rep’s calls.
- The green dotted line shows the winning behavior.
- The x-axis shows the selected time range .

Hover over a point in the graph to view the total number of calls used for calculating the average Talk%.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > Admin:
This article explains how to configure and activate the Winning behavior. It also explains how to recalculate the winning behavior.

Winning behavior is the most frequent behavior displayed by the top reps during their sales conversations that helps in winning deals. You can configure the winning behavior by defining the top performers in the organization. The calls of these top performers are analyzed to calculate the winning behavior.

For example, configuring winning behavior helps you to understand:

- Which activities differentiate your top sales reps from the rest of the team, aside from revenue generation?
- Key insights to better hire, ramp and coach your team.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > Admin > Why is Winning behavior required?:
Winning behavior acts as a benchmark for all other reps in your team. It uncovers actionable information, for example, the average call duration and cadence throughout the year that separates top performers from the rest of the team. It answers questions such as:

- How much time do your top reps spend on calls?
- Do the call activities of top reps differ based on seasons or peak times in the fiscal year?
- How often do the top reps discuss a particular use case with prospects or customers?
- Where do managers need to coach reps to change what they do and when they do it to be more successful?

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > Admin > Configure Winning behavior:
You can configure the winning behavior from the Analytics tab of the Call AI admin interface.

On the page that appears:

- Enter the names or email addresses of at least 3 top reps in the organization under Who are the top performing users in your organization? section.
- Select the starting month of the fiscal year in your organization under When does the fiscal year start in your organization? section. The selected month will define the quarters used in the date range filter of Call Analytics .
- Click the Save changes button in the lower-right corner to proceed.

Note:

- You can add a maximum of 10 reps to calculate the winning behavior.
- If another admin saves a list of top performers while you are configuring, you cannot save the changes. In that case, refresh the page to view the list of top reps saved by the other admin.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > Admin > Configure Winning behavior > Configure Role-Based Winning Behavior:
If you have multiple teams using the same instance of Call AI, you can set up role-based winning behavior for each team. Follow the below steps:

- Provide an excel sheet ( view sample ) to your Customer Success Manager (CSM) or Mindtickle Support mentioning the role and email address of the users whom you want to consider for calculating the winning behavior. The role can have any one of the following values:
  - Account Executive Mid Market / Corporate Account Executive
  - Account Executive Enterprise
  - Business Development Rep (BDR) / Sales Development Rep (SDR)
  - Solutions Consultant / Sales Engineer / Pre Sales Engineer / Pre Sales Consultant
  - Customer Success Manager / Account Manager / Key Account Manager
- Mindtickle Support creates a new profile field called Call AI job title for all the users and populates it with the roles mentioned in the excel sheet.
- Call AI then calculates winning behavior based on the roles of the users and reflects it as a benchmark for different statistics in Call Analytics .

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > Admin > Activate and Calculate the Winning Behavior:
There must be a minimum of 50 call recordings of top reps to activate and calculate the winning behavior. Till then, the status of winning behavior appears Not active.

Once the recording criteria fulfills, you can view the winning behavior status as Active.

The winning behavior of a particular statistic, such as Talk %, is determined by the median value of that statistic from meetings of the last 3 months by the selected top reps. These meetings are updated on the 1st of every month.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > Admin > Recalculate Winning Behavior:
Winning behavior is automatically calculated based on the top reps’ recordings of the last 3 months and recalculated every month. You can view the last updated date and next update date to decide if there is a need to recalculate the winning behavior before the set cadence.

For example, you may want to recalculate the winning behavior when:

- You need more data to compare your team’s performance.
- One of the top reps no longer works in your organization.
- You need to set new goals, sales quotas or forecasts.

Click the Recalculate now button to proceed.

The newly calculated winning behavior then reflects as a benchmark for different statistics in Call Analytics.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > Admin > Prerequisites:
Before recording a call, you may have to comply with certain rules and regulations depending on your location. For example, you may have to take the consent of at least 1 or all of the participants in the call. In addition to legal requirements, there may also be business sector-specific rules or industry standards to follow.

Similarly, there are rules, for example, General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), that mandate the deletion of participants’ personal data if the participants exercise their “Right to Erasure” under which all personally identifiable information belonging to that participant in the call recording must be deleted.

Upon contract termination, a customer’s data is retained in an inactive state for up to 180 days, after which a hard delete is performed on the data, in accordance with contractual terms. User logs are retained for up to 1 year. The logs are pseudonymized in general and is rendered anonymized upon deletion of user data.

During an active contract, the call recordings are retained for up to 2 years (customizable per customer requirements).

Note:

- Mindtickle cannot recover the deleted Call AI meetings.
- Mindtickle stores all customer data, including Call AI recordings on AWS servers located in the United States of America (USA) and Singapore. Mindtickle retains customer data throughout the duration of the contract.
- In case of the contract termination with Mindtickle, Mindtickle takes the following actions:

- Archives the call recording and restricts external access within 7 days after deletion from the Call AI Interface.
- Retains the call recording in an inactive state for up to 14 days after deletion from the Call AI Interface.
- Initiates a permanent delete after 21 days and completes within 30 days after deletion from the Call AI Interface.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > User:
Sales call recording is the best way to keep track of the conversations you have with your potential prospects or valuable customers. chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > User > How does it work?:
Navigate to the Recordings tab of the Call AI Interface. Use the search bar to locate a call recording by meeting title, account name (if CRM is integrated), participant name, theme, or a word in the meeting transcript.

Note: You can view the search tip when you hover over the search bar. You can also view your recent search results when you click on it.

Type a keyword in the search bar to look for a call recording and hit Enter.

Note: You must type a minimum of three characters for the search results to appear.

You can view a list of call recordings that match with the searched keyword on the page that appears.

The search results are based on the following parameters:

- Meeting title
- Participants
- Themes
- Transcript
- Account name (if CRM is integrated)
- Recency
- Meeting duration

For each recording, you can view the following information:

- Name of the recording
- Name of the Account
- Participants of the call
- The exact reason for the match
- Total number of mentions of the keyword
- The date of the call recording

Click the recording name to view its details.

Using the options available in the upper-right corner of the page, you can view the relevant results in:

- Meeting title
- Account
- Participant
- Themes
- Word in transcript

For example, if you want to find all the call recordings where a prospect is talking about problems with coaching, you can apply the Participant filter on the prospect's name and the Word in transcript filter on coaching.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > User > Filter recordings:
To improve the accuracy of these search results and view a specific list of recordings, you can apply the following filters:

- Date : View recordings from a specific timeline or a custom date range.
- Internal/External : Lets you filter meetings by whether they included only internal participants or external attendees.
- Account : Gain insights for a specific account.
- Call type : Categorizes the call under (Discovery, Demo, Support, or Internal Meeting). You can select a specific type from the dropdown to narrow down your recordings.
- Participants : View recordings of specific participant(s).
- Meeting duration : Filter the relevant recordings by setting the lower and upper ranges on the slider. Drag the slider from the left to increase the call duration from 0 seconds to a higher duration. Alternatively, drag the slider from the right to decrease the call duration from 2hrs+.
- Themes : View recordings from other themes that mention the searched keyword.
- Additional CRM filter : You will see an extra set of filter options based on the CRM you have integrated with Call AI. For example, use the Opportunity stage filter to analyze calls made in the Discovery phase.

To receive customized email alerts based on signals or conditions predetermined on the platform, you can set:

- Email triggers on selected filters or search results to draw immediate attention to important calls.
- Regular email updates (twice a week on Tuesday and Friday) if any new recording appears that fulfills the filter or search criteria.

Click Set alert next to the Search bar to set up alerts on specific attributes. For more information, see Recordings List in Call AI.

This article explains the details and insights available for a call recording and the actions you can perform on the recording.

The Recordings page makes it easy for Reps, Managers, and Admins to find and discover the required information while listening to a recording.

For example, you can:

- Listen to the customer's viewpoint, requirements, concerns, and questions.
- Easily remember the tasks you need to work on and create thorough follow-up emails and activities with the customers or prospects.
- Understand the gaps in your performance compared to the winning behavior.
- Skip taking notes during the call.
- Skip over the long pauses that the speaker took or the parts of the recording where no one is speaking.

- Collaborate on the queries with your peers.
- Go to a particular speaker, theme discussion, or scroll to a specific part of the transcript - budget, pricing, competitor.

Use this tab to post a public comment when recommending a certain part of the recording to other team members. For example, you can use the Public Comments section to:

- Showcase best practices to handle customer objections.
- Post shoutouts to a team member.

To post a public comment:

- Tag a person using the ‘@’ symbol and type your comment.
- Call AI displays the recording timestamp once you start typing. Click the Add Timestamp icon to add another timestamp using the ‘#’ symbol.

In case you post an incorrect comment or want to change an existing comment, you can delete the comment. Click the Vertical More Menu icon and select the Delete option.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > User > View Recording Details > Transcript:
Call transcription is the process of converting the audio track of the recording into text. Call transcripts are beneficial in various scenarios. For example:

- It helps when you want to listen to a recording in an environment not conducive to playing audio.
- It keeps you engaged as you read and listen to the recording at the same time.
- It helps people who do not have expertise in the language spoken to understand the recording better.
- It provides vocabulary and spelling references for people trying to learn the language spoken in the recording.
- It makes the recording accessible for people with limited or no hearing.

Note: The accuracy of the automated transcript greatly depends on audio clarity, accents, conciseness of the speaker and many other factors.

Above the Comments, Messages and Notes section, you can view the transcript.

Use the search bar to scan the transcript for keywords related to a specific use case. Use the following buttons to quickly look for:

- Our questions : It highlights all the questions your rep(s) asked during the call. These questions help managers understand if the rep focuses on the right questions to identify the customer's pain points.
- Their questions : It highlights all the questions the customer/prospect asked during the call. These questions help to understand customers' viewpoints, requirements, and concerns.

Click the Collapse Transcript option to close it and click the Download icon to save the transcript to your local machine.

Click the Copy icon to copy the transcript. For long transcripts, the copy option is disabled; use the Download option instead.
chunks.body:
Call transcription is the process of converting the audio track of the recording into text. Call transcripts are beneficial in various scenarios. For example:

- It helps when you want to listen to a recording in an environment not conducive to playing audio.
- It keeps you engaged as you read and listen to the recording at the same time.
- It helps people who do not have expertise in the language spoken to understand the recording better.
- It provides vocabulary and spelling references for people trying to learn the language spoken in the recording.
- It makes the recording accessible for people with limited or no hearing.

Note: The accuracy of the automated transcript greatly depends on audio clarity, accents, conciseness of the speaker and many other factors.

Above the Comments, Messages and Notes section, you can view the transcript.

Use the search bar to scan the transcript for keywords related to a specific use case. Use the following buttons to quickly look for:

- Our questions : It highlights all the questions your rep(s) asked during the call. These questions help managers understand if the rep focuses on the right questions to identify the customer's pain points.
- Their questions : It highlights all the questions the customer/prospect asked during the call. These questions help to understand customers' viewpoints, requirements, and concerns.

Click the Collapse Transcript option to close it and click the Download icon to save the transcript to your local machine.

Click the Copy icon to copy the transcript. For long transcripts, the copy option is disabled; use the Download option instead.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > User > View Recording Details > Action Items:
Action items generated by Copilot highlight tasks that the reps and customers need to finish. Copilot helps generate the list of action items in a crisp and concise format.

Note:

- Copilot is Mindtickle's suite of generative AI features across the platform. Additional features will be released with the official launch of Copilot later in August 2023.
- As a prerequisite, the customer must approve the Open AI as a sub-processor .

The list of action items helps the reps prepare well for the upcoming meetings. The action items consist of:

- Tasks to be performed after the call.
- Questions and follow-up requirements post the meeting.

To copy all the action items, click the Copy icon next to Action items.

To navigate to the part of the meeting where the action item was discussed, hover over and click the action item.

To provide feedback for an action item, hover over the action item and click the thumbs up or the thumbs down icon.

Note:

- AI-powered action items is a Beta release. Since the action items are AI-generated, they are not 100% accurate and may have slight discrepancies.
- Actions items are generated in the English language only.
- A maximum of 20 action items can be listed on the action items pane.
- A maximum of 10 action items can be listed in the recording-ready email.
- If multiple action items have the same time stamp, those action items contain the same time stamp but are listed as separate action items.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > User > View Recording Details > Key Moments:
Key moments generated by Copilot highlight the key topics discussed during the call. The Key moments provide reps and managers with the gist of the call without going through the entire recording or scanning the transcripts. This helps in saving time and quickly identifies the main topics covered during the call.

Note:

- Copilot is Mindtickle's suite of generative AI features across the platform.
- As a prerequisite, the customer must approve the Open AI as a sub-processor .

Click Key moments to view the list generated for the call.

The key moments consist of:

- Timestamp where a particular key moment started.
- Title of the key moment.
- Details of the key moment.

The list of key moments is sorted in chronological order of the timestamp.

Note: Only the top 10 key moments display in the Key moments list.

To navigate to the part of the meeting where the key moment was discussed, hover over and click the key moment.

The lightening icon on the call recording indicates the key moment timestamp in the recording.

To view the key moment details on the recording itself, hover over the lightning icon. Click the lightning icon to play the key moment.

Click the Copy icon next to Key moments to copy all the key moments.

To copy a particular key moment, hover over the key moment and click the Copy icon.

To provide feedback for a key moment, hover over the key moment and click the thumbs up or the thumbs down icon.

Note: Once the feedback is provided, it cannot be changed.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > User > View Recording Details > Summary:
Summary is generated by Copilot and displays a crisp and concise overview of the entire call. The call summary can help you understand the context of the call and generate insights for the call without listening to the entire call.Note:

- The summary is best displayed for calls recorded in English. If two languages are spoken during a call, the summary may not be generated, and you will see an error on the UI.
- A summary is generated based on the transcript, so the transcript must contain at least 150 characters.
- A call summary is generated for calls up to 5 hours.
- For calls recorded before 1st July 2024, the summary is not auto-generated. Click the Summarize call option to generate the summary for the call. This will take you to the Copilot chat window, where they can ask for the summary of the call. This summary won’t be stored in the Summary tab. For more information, see how Copilot works .
- For calls recorded after 1st July 2024, the call summary is displayed by default.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > User > View Recording Details > Share a Recording:
Share your calls within your organization or outside your organization to eliminate repeat demos and offer high-fidelity information transfer.

Click the Share button in the upper-right corner of the page.

Click the Link icon to create and copy the recording link for a seamless sharing:

- If you copy link within your organization sharing, users can view the recording per the recording link access setting ( Restricted or Organization ).

- If the access is Restricted , users with prior access permissions can view the recording using the link.
- If the access is set to Organization , any internal user can view the recording using the link.
- If you copy link outside your organization sharing, anyone can view and download the recording through the link.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > User > View Recording Details > Share a Recording > Share single call within your organization:
Select this option when you want to share the recording with your peers.

On the pop-up that appears:

- You can Copy the link for the recording and easily share it within your organization through email, group chat, or text. Users can access the link based on the recording link access setting ( Restricted or Organization ). Click the Down arrow to modify the access permission for users in your organization.

- Enter the name or email address of the person with whom you want to share the recording. You can add multiple users. Call AI sends an email notification with the recording link when you share the call. For more information, see Add users to share the call recording within your organization .
- Optionally, you can add a message for the person to summarize the call. The message is visible under the Private Messages section of the call.
- You can choose to share the entire call or only a snippet of the call. Click the Snippet option. Move the cursor or enter the timestamps in the From and To range input boxes. You can share the same call or snippet multiple times. The snippet duration must be a minimum of 30 seconds.

Note: Upon sharing the snippet, Call AI plays the snippet you created. Users get access to the complete call in case of internal sharing.

Click the Done button to proceed.

For more information, see Share a single call internally within your organization.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > User > View Recording Details > Share a Recording > Share single call outside your organization:
Select this option to share the recording with the customers, prospects, and any user outside your organization.

On the pop-up that appears:

- You can Copy link for the recording and easily share it with anyone through email, group chat, or text. By default, anyone with the link can view and download the recording. You can track the summary of the number of times a person accessed the link under the External Engagement . Click the Info icon for more information.

Note: The users with this link can view the complete recording when you share it using a link.

- Call AI automatically populates a list of external participants who do not have access to the call. Select the participants from the list with whom you want to share the call. You can also add the external participant’s name or email address with whom you want to share the call. These participants will receive an email notification with the recording link when you share the call. For more information, see Add users to share the call recording outside your organization .
- Optionally, you can add a personal message to summarize the call. The message is added to the email notification that is sent to the users when you share the call.
- To share the snippet of the call, move the cursor or enter the timestamps in the From and To range input boxes. You can play the snippet to check the trimmed part before sharing it. After you share the snippet, it takes five to ten minutes to reflect at the recipient’s end. Note: The snippet duration must be a minimum of 30 seconds.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > User > View Recording Details > Add Recording to a Library:
To easily access best practices for a particular topic, you can group similar calls in libraries. For example, if you want to group all your best demo calls for others to learn from, you can add such recordings to a library. You can also add a call to multiple libraries.

Click the Add to Library button in the upper-right corner and search for an existing library on the Call AI platform.

On the Add to Library pop-up that appears:

- Search for an existing library on the Call AI platform where you want to share the call. You can share the call with multiple libraries.
- Add a comment for the team members.
- Enable/ disable the toggle to Save a snippet of the call to the library . By default, the toggle is disabled.
- Move the cursor or enter the timestamps in the From and To range input boxes of the snippet.

Click Done.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > User > View Recording Details > Themes:
A theme can be a proof point, essential topic or use case that matters the most to your business. It helps analyze if a team uses the correct messaging and follows the right processes on their calls. Examples of a theme are pricing, competitors, next steps or partners.

Click the Themes icon on the right navigation panel to view the themes and keywords used during the call. Call AI checks for the keywords (set in a theme) in the transcript and displays all the keywords spoken and heard.

- Themes Spoken contain the keywords spoken by participants within your organization.
- Themes Heard contain the keywords spoken by participants outside your organization.

Click a Keyword to highlight it in the recording transcript.

To learn more about call statistics and insights, refer to the Call Analytics article.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > User > View Recording Details > Copilot:
Mindtickle Copilot is a generative AI productivity assistant. Ask Copilot any question related to the call recording. Copilot goes through the recording transcript for context and automatically delivers a response to the query.

Note:

- Copilot does not make use of OpenAI’s ChatGPT.
- While AI can speed up content generation, the quality and alignment with educational goals still need human oversight. AI is a tool to boost efficiency, not replace meticulous design. Admins must use their expertise to review and customize AI-generated content to ensure accuracy and alignment with learning objectives.

For more information, see Mindtickle Copilot for Call AI.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Readiness Index (RI):
The revamped and smarter quadrant chart in the Correlate tab shows the correlation of your business metric — such as quota attainment — with the Readiness Index. It’s a seller distribution correlation chart that helps you identify user cohorts across four quadrants and provides insights to help you take specific actions for those cohorts.

When you view the quadrant chart for a particular hierarchical manager, the chart helps you analyze the performance of the manager’s sales reps (learners) in each quadrant in the form of two charts:

- Segment bubble chart: Distribution of learners based on segments. Segments are user cohorts based on profile fields, as configured under Segment Selection in RI Visualization Settings.
- Learner scatter chart: Distribution of learners individually on a scatter chart.

You can more easily identify what are the behaviors of your top reps or high performers and use this data for reps who need improvement. You can also define targets for each business metric individually and allow managers to define their own targets for their business metrics.

The Correlate tab offers the following benefits:

- Analyze rep skills and competencies against business metrics to identify where readiness efforts need to be amplified
- Pull in data from Salesforce or manually uploaded business metrics in one place for correlation with Readiness Index
- Report the business impact of enablement and coaching
- Identify which parts of the revenue org need more help

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Readiness Index (RI) > Main actions:
- Correlating RI With: Correlate Readiness Index (RI) with a business metric. From the dropdown menu, you can select manually-uploaded business metrics and/or Salesforce business metrics (if Salesforce is integrated for Sales Outcome Data Sync). The dropdown menu lists up to 10 metrics, as selected by you in RI Settings > Visualizations > Business metric selection.In the dropdown list, manual metrics are ones with “(manual)” in the name and Salesforce metrics are ones with the business metric cycle in the name, such as Quarterly and Monthly.
- For (Manager): Select the manager for whose team you want to view RI.
- Viewing RI As Of: Select the week for which you want to view RI.Note: RI data is not real-time. It is calculated every Monday at 2 AM UTC. You can change the configuration of RI at any time. These changes are not permanent. They are valid only until the next scheduled run.
- Chart type: Select one of the following chart types to distribute the chart data:
  - Segment bubble chart: Displays learners grouped by your teams and distributed by the segment that you select. Segments are user cohorts based on profile fields, as configured under Segment Selection in RI Visualization Settings.
  - Learner scatter chart: Displays data for all individual learners in your team.
- Distributed by: Select the segment (user cohort) by which you want to distribute the chart data. The options in the drop-down are based on your selection in RI Settings > Visualizations > Segment Selection.
- Edit configuration: Click the (Edit) to make changes to the chart configuration. You can change the default values for the business metric and Readiness Index (RI) on the x and y-axis respectively. The default values are based on your selection in RI Settings > Visualizations > Quadrant chart configurations. You can also select a business outcome metric.Once you Apply Changes, this becomes your own personalized configuration and you can change it again as required.Note: This setting is available only if the admin sets the “Allow users to change quadrant chart origin” option to Yes in Quadrant chart configurations.
- Chart bubble: Click any bubble (user cohort) to view insights on the user cohort’s performance. For more information, see the “Segment Bubble Chart” section.
- Key insights: Listed on the right side of the chart that quickly provide an overview of each bubble's (quadrant or learner performance.
