chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Readiness Index (RI) > Main actions > Inverse metrics and metrics data updated info:
This section explains how inverse metrics are represented on the quadrant chart. It also provides information on the data last updated information, which is applicable only for manually uploaded business metrics.

Inverse (negative) metrics

Mindtickle's backend logic properly flags inverse (negative) business metrics. For example, sales cycle length is an inverse metric for which a lower value means better performance. In other words a high sales cycle length is considered negative.

When an inverse metric is selected in the Correlate tab, the quadrant chart automatically reverses the X-axis, while the Y-axis remains unchanged. For instance, a high sales cycle length — which is typically considered negative — is represented with lower values indicating better performance.

Additionally, a note appears above the chart to inform users when an inverse metric is selected from the "Correlating RI with" dropdown. It provides context on why the chart’s axis has shifted, clarifying that lower values are now categorized as high performance.

Note: The polarity (positive or negative/inverse) of Salesforce metrics will be predefined in the backend. For manually uploaded metrics, customers will need to provide additional information on whether the metric is positive or negative while sharing the metrics with Mindtickle for uploading them. We will store this information in the backend, ensuring consistent and accurate data representation in future uploads.

Data last updated info for manual metrics

Manually uploaded business metrics often result in outdated data being displayed on the dashboard, which can mislead admins and managers. To mitigate this, you can refer to the info in the top-right that provides the last updated date info for the manually uploaded metrics. This info appears whenever you select a manual metric in the “Correlating RI with” dropdown menu.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Readiness Index (RI) > Segment bubble chart:
This chart displays learners grouped by your teams and distributed by the segment that you select. Segments are user cohorts based on profile fields, as configured under Segment Selection in RI Visualization Settings.

Segments are displayed in the following four quadrants or categories. Click the Distributed by drop-down menu to view data for a particular segment.

- High Performers: High RI and high business metric data (sales) for the selected metric. These are your best user cohorts in the organization.This quadrant allows Sales and Enablement leaders to clearly identify the qualities that make their best performers tick and use this information to develop these capabilities among their lower performers. They can also use the best performers to capture win stories and drive peer-to-peer coaching initiatives.
- High Potential: High RI but are not performing in sales. These user cohorts have high potential of performing well on-field.Given that these reps went through the same readiness programs as their best-performing peers, this quadrant highlights that the capability-ready reps might have other challenges, such as their territory make-up or lead flow, resulting in their lower sales numbers.
- Needs Development: Low RI and low sales. These user cohorts need the most attention and development.They need to complete relevant enablement to fill their competency gaps to make their competency distribution look more like the Best Performers.
- Outliers: High sales numbers but lower RI. These user cohorts have the most number of learners with high business metric data for the selected metric, but low RI.If the number of learners in this category is high, you need to identify what they are doing differently and take necessary corrective actions.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Readiness Index (RI) > Segment bubble chart > Learner distribution details:
On the segment bubble chart, you can click on a bubble to drill down into a specific segment (user cohort) and analyze their numbers through learner distribution. You can further drill down to identify the specific teams whose numbers are low.

Perform the following steps to view a user cohort’s learner distribution data:

1. To get started, click on a bubble (user cohort) to view their learner distribution data and insights. As an example, we will look at a user cohort (Germany) in the Needs Development quadrant.

1. On the Learner Distribution Details pop-up that opens, you can view all learners of the user cohort distributed individually on the chart. Hover over a dot to view the learner’s quick stats and click on the dot to access their RI scorecard. Use the top drop-down menu to view data for another user cohort. Use the search bar to view data for a particular learner on the chart.

1. On the right, you can view learner details and distribution as follows:
  - Number of Learners: The tiles represent the four quadrants and display how many % of learners fall across the quadrants out of the total number of learners. Click on a tile to view related key insights.
  - Key insights: Displays top and bottom competencies for the user cohort and changes in each competency compared to the benchmark.
  - Click View underperforming learners to open the User distribution table with relevant filters automatically applied. On the other hand, if the rep falls in the High Performers quadrant, you’ll see the option to View best performing learners.
  - Click View Track dashboard to open the Track tab with relevant filters automatically applied.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Series:
A series in Mindtickle is a readiness or enablement program that organizes all related learning content in one place. It acts as the top-level container for delivering a complete learning journey.

Within a series, you can add and group different types of modules, such as courses, quick updates, assessments, instructor-led training (ILT), missions, coaching sessions, quests, and checklists.

Examples

- Sales onboarding program
- New product launch training
- Quarterly compliance certification
- Sales methodology training
- Manager coaching program

Note:

- A series contains multiple modules
- Content is structured as: Series → Modules (activities, such as courses, assessments, missions) → Learning Objects (content such as videos, questions, documents)
- Series can be organized into sections)
- Modules can be reused (mirrored) across multiple series

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Series > Key series capabilities:
Admins can configure the following settings for a series:

- Sequential unlocking – unlock modules one at a time based on completion. For more information, see How does sequential locking work per module? .
- Certifications – award certificates based on defined criteria. You can add up to 70 certifications per series. For more information, see Add series certifications .
- Notifications – send invitation and reminder emails for the series and its modules. For more information, see Email invitations, reminders, and notifications for series and modules .
- Leaderboard – rank learners based on scores within the series. For more information, see Series leaderboard .
- Series ratings – allow learners to rate the series (1–5 stars).
- Skip optional modules – allow learners to skip non-mandatory modules.
- Multilingual support – support up to 24 languages with AI or manual translations. For more information, see Create multilingual series and modules .

For more information on all series settings, see Configure series settings.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Series > Modules > Types of modules:
There are 8 types of modules in Mindtickle, each suited to different use cases:

| Module type | Purpose | Module certifications | Re-attempts |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Course | In-depth training with multiple topics, a visual theme, and knowledge check questions | Yes | Yes |
| Quick update | Bite-sized content for sharing important updates or announcements | No | No |
| Assessment | Test learner knowledge with multiple question formats | Yes | Yes |
| Mission | Virtual role-playing scenarios to practice skills (voiceover slideshow, video roleplay, screen capture, email, and task evaluation) | Yes | Yes |
| Coaching sessions | Ongoing coaching meetings between managers or coaches and learners | Yes | No |
| ILT (Instructor-led training) | Classroom or virtual webinar sessions | No | No |
| Checklist | On-the-job or offline tasks learners mark as complete | No | No |
| Quest (Spaced reinforcement) | Short, personalized, gamified challenges delivered at spaced intervals for knowledge retention | No | No |

For more information, see Types of modules in Mindtickle. To choose the right module for your use case, see How to choose the right module?.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Series:
As an admin, you can create a series using one of Mindtickle’s preconfigured templates and Ready-to-Deploy programs. When you use a template, it is copied onto your learning site, a brand new series or module is created, and you can launch it as a program for your learners.

The Mindtickle platform hosts templates and programs created by Mindtickle and industry experts in the following categories:

- Ready-to-Deploy templates (RTD) : You can use ready-to-deploy templates to launch a series with pre-built, populated content and modules. Launching these RTDs takes an average of 2 hours.
- Series templates: You can use program templates to create a series. You can customize them further and add your organization-specific content to tailor your unique enablement needs. Launching with program templates takes an average of 7 days.
- Module templates: You can use pre-designed module templates within your series to avoid building them repeatedly and from scratch.

To create a series using an RTD or a template :

1. On the admin site homepage, click Training and select Series.

2. On the Series page, click the Create button and select Template from the drop-down menu to visit the Marketplace.

Or you can also visit the Marketplace on the Add modules pop-up (Training > Modules > Create module). Scroll down to the Browse module templates and click the Next icon.

You are redirected to the Marketplace.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Readiness Index (RI):
In the Track tab, Readiness Index (RI) provides insights based on the competency benchmarks for a given period for a user’s team. You can view performance data and insights based on competencies/competency categories, teams, and user segments in the form of actionable charts and reports. You can identify which competencies your sales reps are good at and which not. Then you can help your sales reps achieve the ideal benchmark for the competencies where they are falling behind. This helps both managers and sales reps know what they could focus on.

The Track tab offers the following benefits:

- Track RI scores by rep, team, or region and quickly address problem areas and understand how readiness scores change over time
- View performance data by competencies/competency categories and their weights (contribution towards RI)
- Identify which reps and teams within the organization need help from enablement and frontline managers
- More peak performers on the team through customized learning programs and coaching
- Optimal use of enablement efforts by focusing on reps and teams that need improvement

Note: Readiness Index (RI) data is not real-time. The data gets updated weekly — every Monday at 2 AM UTC. During the weekly data update, associated user hierarchies, competency performance data, and RI scores also get updated. For example, if there were any changes to your user hierarchies in the days between the last RI update and the upcoming update, the changes will reflect in RI after the next weekly update.

This section provides an overview of the information available on the Track tab, in the form of top stats and charts.

Top stats:

For example, you can click the links in Top Insights, bars in the User Distribution chart, and the buttons that are available when you click on a competency or competency category in the Key Competency chart.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Readiness Index (RI) > 1. Measure RI by key competencies:
On the Key competencies page, you can measure and track Readiness Index (RI) by competencies that contribute to your organization’s RI. You can view the competency performance data of your sellers in one of the following types of charts:

- Spider chart
- Bar chart

For each chart type, you can also choose to view the chart data:

- Competencies
- Competency categories . In this view, you can further drill-down into any category to view data for all of its competencies.

The chart shows data by competencies by default. You can change the default settings under RI Settings > Visualizations > Competency Distribution Configurations.

The chart also displays the weights (contribution towards RI) of the competencies and their categories. This will help you understand the importance of each competency and category, and plan your enablement better.

Competencies in Readiness Index are defined through tags applied to various content in the Mindtickle platform. For example, messaging consistency, objection handling, negotiation skills, and closing skills are competencies. Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Sales Challenges (Beta):
When conducting live sessions for hybrid teams or training huge teams virtually, it becomes increasingly important to maintain a high level of interest. You need to keep your audience engaged, encourage collaboration among the team members, and ensure knowledge retention. To fulfill these conditions, it is necessary that you build a dynamic learning environment. The environment should break the monotony of long sessions, inspire teamwork, build camaraderie and introduce a sense of competition within the team.

A Team Challenge is that dynamic learning environment. It is a gamified virtual training program that can be used to spice up remote and hybrid training. Through a Team Challenge, Learners are transported into a virtual arcade in which they can engage with training content and demonstrate learning by completing fun challenges. The results of the challenge give you a better insight into individual and team progress and can help you identify knowledge gaps. Thus, a Team Challenge can be strategically used to drive:

- Reinforced learning
- Higher engagement
- Better Collaboration
- Knowledge retention
- Focused future sessions

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Sales Challenges (Beta) > Team Challenges Format:
- A Team Challenge can be organized for a single session or can be spread across multiple sessions on different days.
- All participants invited to the Team Challenge are divided amongst teams. Each participant is represented by a hot-air balloon that runs on fuel. Players need fuel to answer a question, request for the next question and reveal clues on each question.
- Throughout the game, the players are subjected to a series of questions across multiple levels. The question type can be any one of the following - Multiple-choice, Guess the Word or Finding Waldo. Two hints are available for each question.
- For every right answer the players earn points. Since it is a time-bound game, the number of points earned depends on how fast a player answers a question. Using a hint on a question decreases the number of points they can earn.
- The players lose fuel every time they attempt a question. For every wrong answer, the players lose points and fuel. For every right answer, the players lose fuel and earn points. They can earn fuel by socializing with other participants. Players cannot proceed to the next question if their fuel tank is empty.
- The number of points earned is equal to the distance that the hot-air balloon flies. The goal of the game is to answer the maximum number of questions correctly as fast as possible to gain maximum points (and win medals along the way!) so that the hot-air balloon flies the highest. Players can win Gold, Silver and Bronze medals throughout the game. The team with hot-air balloons that cover the maximum distance collectively, wins the game.

For more information on how to configure and play the game, refer Configure a Team Challenge and Play a Team Challenge.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Sales Challenges (Beta):
Currently, a Team Challenge can only be configured manually by a designated Team Challenge group at Mindtickle.

To configure a Team Challenge for the members of your organization, reach out to your Customer Success Manager (CSM). The CSM works closely with you and a dedicated team at Mindtickle to help you set up the game. Follow these steps to get started with the process:

1. Reach out to your Customer Success Manager (CSM) and discuss your requirements.
2. A dedicated team is set up and assigned to guide you through the entire process.
3. A member from the team shares the following files with you:
  1. A Game Setup Template
  2. A Team Setup Template
  3. A Question Setup Template
  4. An Invitation Email Template Fill each template with the required information and share them with the team. Note : The templates are designed in unique formats and come with specific instructions for adding the details. Reach out to the team if you have any doubts or questions about adding information to the templates.
4. The team at Mindtickle creates the Team Challenge based on your inputs in the templates. The Team Challenge can be accessed by the participants through a URL and a unique pass code.
5. The Mindtickle team shares the Team Challenge URL and the unique pass code for each player with you.
6. Add the Challenge details (Team Challenge URL, Team Name, User Name, Pass code and Game Rules) in the Invitation Email template and share it with the Learners in your organisation.

For more information on how to play the game, refer Play a Team Challenge.

  - The position of your hot-air balloon. The balloon indicates the distance it has flown and your position in the game.
3. Medals and Social Status This section displays the Medals you win throughout the game and your Social Status. The Medals that can be won are Gold, Silver and Bronze. The Social Statuses that can be achieved are Newbie, Explorer, Expert and Elite.
4. Level Completion This section displays the current level you are on and your progress of completion for that level.
5. The Gaming Console The Screen , Lift Up button, Hint buttons and the Fuel meter together constitute the Gaming Console.
  - The Screen displays the question.
  - The Lift Up button is used to bring up the next question.
  - The Hint buttons are used to reveal the clues for the question that is displayed on the screen.
  - The Fuel meter displays the amount of fuel in your fuel tank.
6. Socialize The message button directs you to the Socialize tab. You can socialize with other players during the game by sending and receiving messages. Socializing helps you earn fuel. Click this button to display the list of all the players in the game. Click on a player to start a conversation. Once you click Send , 2 liters of fuel are filled up in your fuel tank. Note : You earn fuel only for the first message you send to a player. Sending messages to the same player does not help you earn fuel. So, the next time you want to earn fuel, ensure to start a conversation with a different player.
7. Hall of Fame Click on Hall of Fame to display the game stats. The following pop-up appears: The pop-up displays the following statistics:
  1. The Top 3 Flyers , the teams they belong to and the distance they have flown until that point.
  2. The Top 2 Socializers and the teams they belong to. Amongst the top Socializers, one is the Top Message Sender and the other is the Top Message Receiver . The Top Message Sender is decided based on the number of players they sent messages to and the Top Message Receiver is decided based on the number of players they received messages from.
  3. All the gold medal winners, the teams they belong to and the distance they have flown.
  4. The remaining distance you need to fly to complete the game.
8. Team Ranking This section displays the position of each team in the game. It also displays the number of Gold, Silver or Bronze medals won by each team.
9. Feed This section shares live updates from the game. For example, Player X joined the game , Player Y completed Level 1 , Player Z from Team ABC won a Gold medal .
10. Menu You can navigate to the Tips section or log out of the game from the Menu option.
  1. Select Tips to navigate to the Playing Tips section.
  2. Select Logout to stop playing and log out of the game.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Sales Challenges (Beta) > Start the Game:
1. Click the Play icon on the screen. A video explaining the rules of the game starts playing. Once the video ends, click Lift Up . The first question appears on the screen. Questions can be any one of three types - Multiple-choice , Guess the Word , Finding Waldo .
  1. For a Multiple-choice question, the screen displays the question and four options (in a 2x2 grid). Select the correct answer. Note : A Multiple-choice question can have either one or two hints. You can choose to use one or both of the hints before selecting the answer. (The more hints you use, the more points you lose).
    - Click the Text hint button to reveal a clue about the answer.
    - Click the Eliminate button to eliminate some wrong options. Once you guess the correct answer:
    - The total number of points (total lift) you win is displayed.
    - Trivia about the question is displayed.
    - Your hot-air balloon flies higher by feet, equal to the points you win for that question. Note :
    - If the time runs out before you select an answer, you earn 0 points.
    - Every wrong answer counts as a missed attempt. After two missed attempts, the answer automatically displays and you earn 0 points.
  2. For a Guess the Word question, the screen displays the question and the number of blanks that form the answer. Guess the letters that complete the answer and enter them using the keyboard. Note : A Guess the Word question comes with two hints. You can choose to use either one or both of the hints. The more hints you use, the more points you lose.
    - Click the Get letters button to fill in some of the blanks with letters.
    - Click the Text hint button to get a clue about the answer. Once you guess the correct answer:
    - The total number of points (total lift) you win is displayed.
    - Trivia about the question is displayed.
    - Your hot-air balloon flies higher by feet equal to the points you win for that question. Note :
    - Every wrong guess counts as a missed attempt. After three missed attempts, the answer automatically displays and you earn 0 points.
    - If the time runs out before you select an answer, you earn 0 points.
  3. For a Finding Waldo question, the screen displays an image with an object hidden in it. The question describes the image and the hidden object that you need to search. Note : A Finding Waldo question comes with one hint. You can choose to use the hint before selecting the answer. If you use the hint, you lose points. Click the Eliminate button to eliminate some wrong options. Once you locate the hidden object:
    - The total number of points (total lift) you win is displayed.
    - Trivia about the question is displayed.
    - Your hot-air balloon flies higher by feet equal to the points you win for that question. By default, the scores are assigned as follows: Points for the right answer100 ftBonus points for unused hints100 ft (50 ft for each unused hint)Bonus points for no missed attempts120 ftBonus points for less time takenUp to 180 ft (1 ft per second) Note : These scores can be customized.
2. Click Lift Up to proceed to the next question. Note : Every time you click Lift Up , you lose 2 liters of fuel.
3. If at any point during the game your fuel tank gets empty, the following pop-up appears: Click on any one of the options to refuel your tank:
  1. Interact with other Pilots The list of players who have entered the challenge, appears. Select the player you want to socialize with and send them a message. You earn 2 liters of fuel for every first interaction per player.
  2. Wait for fuel tank to refill You need to wait for one minute for 2 liters of fuel.
4. At the end of every level in the game, the following pop-up appears and it displays:
  - The level you have completed.
  - The distance your hot-air balloon has flown.
  - The medals you have won.
  - Your social status. Click on Continue to Game Summary .
5. The Dashboard appears. It displays the position of your hot-air balloon and the distance it has flown until that point in the game. It also displays the other hot-air balloons and the distances that they have flown until that point in the game. Click Continue Hiflying .
6. Once the game ends, the final Dashboard appears. It displays your final score and hot-air balloon’s final position in the game.
7. Click on your Team in the Team Ranking tab to view how other players in your team have performed.

Once site-wide notifications are disabled, learners will NOT receive the following emails:

- Invitations
- Reminders
- Completion
- Reviewer

However, the following essential emails will still be sent, even if site-wide notifications are disabled:

| Email type | When it is sent |
| --- | --- |
| Email authentication | When a learner signs in to Mindtickle learning site using their email for the first time. This is the account activation email sent for authentication. |
| Password reset (user-initiated) | When a learner resets their password. |
| Password reset (admin-initiated) * | When an admin sends a password reset email to a learner. |
| Report exports | When users export reports from the Mindtickle platform. |
| Call AI emails * | Call AI emails sent when users engage with or take actions within Call AI. |

* If you do not want your learners to receive Call AI emails or admin-initiated password reset emails, please raise a separate request with Mindtickle Support to disable them.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Communications > Notifications and Reminders > Asset expiry reminder emails:
Even when site-wide email notifications are disabled, asset expiry reminder emails are still sent. These are considered mandatory actionable system emails and are triggered based on asset expiry reminders configured at the asset level, not by global notification settings.

Why these emails are sent

When creating or updating an asset, admins can configure asset expiry reminder emails via the Expiration reminder option in the asset's properties, which has three optional reminder settings:

- On the expiration date
- 7 days before expiration date
- 15 days before expiration date

These checkboxes are not selected by default while creating assets. Reminder emails are sent only when an admin selects one or more of these options while creating or updating the asset.

Once configured, the system will automatically send reminder emails to the designated recipients based on the selected schedule.

How to stop these emails

To ensure expiry reminder emails are not sent:

- For new assets: Simply leave all reminder checkboxes unchecked when setting an expiry date.
- For existing assets: If expiry reminders are already configured, you'll need to update the Expiration reminder property. You can update this property for a single asset or for multiple assets within a hub:
  - Update a single asset : Navigate to the asset → Edit properties → Expiration reminder property → U ncheck all 3 reminder options .
  - Update multiple assets at once : Navigate to a hub containing the assets → Select the relevant assets (individually or all) → Edit properties in the bulk action toolbar → Expiration reminder property → Select Remove expiration reminder in the dropdown.

This ensures no expiry reminder emails are sent for those assets, regardless of the site-wide notification setting.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Sales Challenges (Beta):
Sales Challenges help improve Learner engagement by strategically incorporating gamified and fun learning mechanisms, like Live Challenges and competitive Team Challenges, within enablement programs. Sales Challenges introduce a sense of competition that encourages Learners to learn and perform better, thus increasing the value of enablement programs. They encourage Learners to build knowledge, reinforce learning and strengthen their understanding of concepts.

Sales Challenges are of two types, Live Challenges and Team Challenges.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Sales Challenges (Beta) > Live Challenges:
A Live Challenge is a Multiple Choice Question (MCQ) based Quiz that can be incorporated within an ILT and played as a game amongst the Learners. Thus adding an element of fun to the Session. An Admin can configure the Live Challenge with questions specific to the topic of discussion to reinforce Learners’ knowledge or with generic questions.

Integrating a Live Challenge in an ILT Session enables the Instructor to not only keep the Learners engaged throughout the Session, but also evaluate the Learners’ understanding of the topic.

For more information on creating and conducting Live Challenges, refer Configure a Live Challenge within an ILT Session.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle University > On-Demand Thought Leadership:
Every deal has two sides — the buyer and the seller. On the buyer side, you create Ideal Customer Profiles (ICPs) and track the qualification process. But do you know your Ideal Rep Profile (IRP)?

In this video, you'll explore why an IRP is a key component of sales readiness – and how you can start creating yours.

You’ll learn how to:

- Identify the set of skills and competency benchmarks that make up your organization’s IRP
- Align more reps to the IRP and enable them to deliver on their numbers consistently
- Make enablement and manager-led coaching more personalised based on each rep’s IRP gaps

To learn more about ideal rep profiles, view our blog post or reach out to your Customer Success Manager.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > User > Access the recordings list > Filters:
To view a specific list of recordings, you can apply the following filters:

- Date : Filter recordings from a specific timeline or a custom date range.
- Internal/External : Lets you filter meetings by whether they included only internal participants or external attendees.
- Participants : Filter recordings of specific participant(s).
- Account : Filter recordings to gain insights for a specific account.
- Call type : Categorizes the call under (Discovery, Demo, Support, or Internal Meeting). You can select a specific type from the dropdown to narrow down your recordings.
- Meeting duration : Filter the relevant recordings by setting the lower and upper ranges on the slider. Drag the slider from the left to increase the call duration from 0 seconds to a higher duration. Alternatively, drag the slider from the right to decrease the call duration from 2hrs+.
- Themes : Filter recordings from a particular theme.
- Additional Filters :
  - Filter recordings by Call Score .
  - Filter recordings using CRM objects. For example, use the Opportunity stage filter to analyze calls made in the Discovery phase.
  - Filter recordings by recording tool. Note: Contact your Customer Success Manager (CSM) or Mindtickle Support to check Call AI’s integration with your recording tool.
  - Filter recordings by transcript language.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > User > Access the recordings list > Set Email Alerts:
To receive customized email alerts based on signals or conditions predetermined on the platform, you can set:

- Email triggers on selected filters or search results to draw immediate attention to important calls.
- Regular email updates (twice a week on Tuesday and Friday) if any new recording appears that fulfills the filter or search criteria.

Click Set alert next to the Filters to set up alerts on specific attributes.For example, you can set alerts on:

- Accounts of interest
- Salesforce stages, such as negotiation and pricing
- Specific competitor mentions
- Themes on which you want to coach

Enter the name of the alert and click Set alert to proceed.

Once the alert is set up, you can view the alert under the Preferences tab in the left navigation panel.

Note: The Set alert option remains disabled when you have not applied any filters or have only applied a date filter.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Managers and Reviewers > Mobile app:
This article explains how Manager/Reviewers can review Competency Assessment using the MindTickle mobile app.

1. Tap the Review button on the email notification. Alternatively, you can also sign in to the mobile app as a Reviewer and select the required Competency Assessment from the dashboard.

2. Click Start against the Competency Assessment you want to review.

Note: If you are re-evaluating an Assessment, you will see the View option (instead of Start) against the Competency Assessment.

3. Evaluate the learners based on the competency and evaluation parameters. Evaluation parameters marked with an asterisk are mandatory for review.

You can view the Learner’s Self Assessment and any previous Manager Assessment by clicking option.

Note: Learner’s Assessment is displayed based on the criteria set by the Admin.

4. After evaluating the Learner assessment, click Submit Assessment.

5. Click Submit on the confirmation screen.

6. The Assessment successful submission message is displayed on the screen.

If the meeting invite includes a group email, Call AI cannot identify who all are part of the group and may not send the call recording to every participant of the group. As a workaround, the meeting host must individually invite each participant of the group to the meeting or share the recording with all the participants after the call using the Share button.

The Engagement dashboard is a widget-based dashboard that provides a high-level overview of how reps engage with assets in Asset Hub. It helps figure out red flags and lets you deep dive into the specific details of the asset to take necessary actions.

The dashboard displays widgets in two sections:

- External Engagement: Widgets for engagement (viewing and downloading) on assets that a rep has shared with customers or prospects (external recipients).

For more information, see Engagement Dashboard.

It provides a high-level overview of how the assets perform in revenue generation over time. chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Dashboards > Main Features:
The following are the highlight features available for the dashboards:

- Customize widgets to personalize dashboards

You can personalize your dashboards by editing widget filters. By customizing the widgets, you will get analytics and insights relevant to you.

- Contextual widget filters

Widget filters and their values are now contextual to your selections so that it displays only relevant filter values. Contextuality amongst filters ensures you select your relevant filters with ease and helps customize the widgets faster.

When you apply filters to a widget, they are applied in a hierarchy: common filters are treated as primary filters and user and content filters are treated as secondary filters. The following image shows the order of contextuality that is maintained in filters.

Contextual filters auto-adjust to selection to ensure filter values that you see are the ones you need. The secondary filters and their values are based on your selection of primary filters and their values.

For example:

1. When you have applied the Module Type filter first (the primary filter), where you selected “Course” and “ILT” as filter values. In this case, any secondary filters show values based on the primary filter.
2. When you apply Series as the second filter, the filter values show only those Series where at least one Course Module is present.
3. Further, when you apply Modules as the third filter, the filter values show only those Modules that belong to the selected Series.

- Scoped access to admins

Only view widgets and data that you have access to. Admins can view only those widgets that serve the data they have access to. Data access is derived and scoped based on what content and groups admins have access to.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Series:
Series designed by admins play an important role in the overall development and readiness of learners. Mindtickle allows learners to provide direct quantitative feedback on these programs based on their relevance, usefulness, etc., in the form of series ratings. Learners can rate a series on a scale of 1 to 5 stars.

Note: Learners can rate a public series, scoped public, self-assigned, or assigned to them.

Series ratings, thus, bridge the gap between enablement admins and learners and help close the feedback loop. When learners provide feedback on an enablement program based on their experience in the form of ratings:

- Other learners can make quick and informed decisions on programs most instrumental in their development. They can also decide whether to invest their time in that program.
- Admins gain a better understanding of how the program is being received by the learners. They find it easy to assess the program's effectiveness and relevance. They can gauge what helped the learner and what could have been done to make the program more effective. Based on this insight, they can take the necessary action to improve or upgrade the program.

You can get granular performance and engagement data for series ratings through Mindtickle’s reporting API. The API, built over OData, allows you to import data from Mindtickle into a BI tool, such as Excel, PowerBI, and Tableau. For more information, see Download reporting API Tables.

For more information on how to configure series ratings for your enablement programs, refer to Configure series settings.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Series:
As a learner, you can rate a series (public or assigned to you) based on its overall value. Depending on your experience with its content, structure, comprehensiveness, and usefulness, you can rate a series on a 1 to 5-star scale. This allows you to provide direct feedback on the series and enables other learners to make quick and informed decisions on whether they should consume a particular series. This also enables admins to gather feedback on the programs that they create and update them if necessary.

When rating a series, consider the following parameters and ask the following questions:

- User engagement
  - Did I find the course material engaging?
  - How likely am I to retake this course?
  - Would I be willing to take up more such courses?
  - Is this training format compatible with my learning style?
  - Could I easily navigate my way through the course?
- Adoption
  - Did the series enable me to master the concept/process/product?
  - Do I feel more confident/comfortable with the concept/process/product than before taking this course?
  - Did I achieve a state in which I gained the ability to train a peer on the process/product/concept?
  - Did this course help me develop professionally?
  - Was the course material easy to understand, adaptable, and comprehensive?
- Content quality
  - Did this course meet my expectations?
  - How strongly would I recommend this content to a colleague in a similar role?
  - Was going through the content a valuable use of my time?
  - Can the content be applied to my work and daily responsibilities?
  - Will I be more effective in my work after going through this content?

You can rate the series accordingly based on whether your answers to these questions lean more towards positive or negative feedback.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Series > Rate a series:
To rate a series:

1. Open the series to provide a rating.
2. Under the series name, next to Rate series, select the number of stars that you wish to provide the series. A confirmation message displays that the series rating is complete. Your rating, the average rating, and the number of ratings for the series are adjusted and displayed.
3. To change your rating, hover over the stars next to Your rating and select the number of stars you wish to provide.The new average rating for the series is displayed. Note :

- You can rate a series at any given point in time.
- You can update your rating for a series multiple times. However, once you rate a series, you cannot unrate it or give it 0 stars. For example, if you give it 4 stars and later want to modify it, you can give it either a minimum of 1 star or a maximum of 5 stars.
- It is not possible to give decimal ratings, such as 3.5 stars. However, it is possible that the average rating for a series gets calculated as a decimal rating.
- If the Series rating feature is disabled after learners have rated it and then enabled again, the average series rating for that series continues to persist.

You can access all your top-rated series from the Top-Rated series widget on the Readiness Experience Dashboard.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > User Management > Users and Groups:
This article provides an overview of the Group to series linking feature in Automation links.

Using this feature, as an admin, you can link a group to one or more series, so that the group members are assigned to the linked series automatically. You can configure the link such as:

- Only users added to the group in the future are invited to the series. OR
- Existing group members as well as users added to the group in the future are invited to the series.

Once linked, depending on your configuration, users are assigned to the linked series automatically. You can also unlink the group from the linked series.

This article further explains how you can view linked or unlinked series, link or unlink a group with series, and view performance and engagement data of the group in the linked series.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > User Management > Users and Groups > View linked/unlinked series:
1. On the Automation links page, in the Linked series column, click or the number for a group to view and manage its linked or unlinked series. Note : ‘+’ indicates no series have been linked to the group yet, whereas, the number indicates the number of series that are linked with the group.
2. The Group panel that appears, displays a list of linked and unlinked series. If the series is already linked with the group, the toggle switch in the Link status column is enabled. It is disabled for an unlinked series. For each series, the Invited column displays how many members of the group are already invited to the series. Tip : Use the Search field to find a series. Use the Show only linked series toggle switch to show only the linked Series in the list. This option is useful when you want to manage just the linked series for a group.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > User Management > Users and Groups > Link a group to series:
To link a group to an individual series or multiple series in bulk:

1. To link the group to an individual series, turn the toggle switch ON in the Link status column. To link the group to multiple series in bulk, select the series and click the Link now button. Note : You can link upto 30 series in bulk at a time. If more than 30 series are selected, the Link now button is disabled. The following pop-up appears. Check the Invite all existing group members to the series to invite the existing group members to the series. If you invite them, members who were selectively invited to some modules are invited to the complete series. To invite only users added to the group in future, leave the checkbox unchecked.
2. Click Link now . A confirmation message is displayed on the screen indicating the linking is performed successfully. Once linked, the toggle switch is turned ON . The Linked to <x> series status at the top is updated to display the number of linked series. Note :
  - While linking, if you leave the Invite all existing group members to the series checkbox unchecked, existing members are not invited to the series. Post linking, you can click the Sync icon to invite existing group members as well to the series. This option is also available while you link multiple series in bulk and do not choose the Invite all existing group members to the series option.
  - If you select the Invite all existing group members to the series checkbox, the Invited column displays a spinning sync icon to indicate that the existing group members are being invited to the series. Based on your selection of users, they are invited to the linked series automatically.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Mobile App > Navigating nested hubs:
To provide a more organized and intuitive way to navigate content, hubs on the mobile app are organized in a parent-child hierarchy that reflects your organization's setup.

If your admin has configured an overview page for the hub:

- The hub details page displays Overview and Assets tabs.
- The configured overview page appears on the Overview tab.
- Child hubs and assets are listed on the Assets tab.

If no overview page is configured:

- Child hubs and assets are displayed directly on the hub details page.
- The Overview and Assets tabs do not appear.

- Hierarchical hub navigation: The hub detail page displays a list of nested (child) hubs, clearly distinguishing between a hub (folder/container) and an asset (individual file). Selecting a child hub navigates you deeper into that specific hub's detail page.
- Asset counts and selection: The total number of assets displayed for a hub includes the assets from all of its child hubs. If a hub only contains nested hubs and no individual assets, the "Select" option won't be available, as hubs themselves are not selectable.
- Improved search experience: Global search results display the immediate parent hub name as metadata to provide proper context. In-hub searches allow you to search specifically within the current hub and its nested child hubs.
- Home and overview page widgets: Widgets like Recently Viewed Assets and Top Rated Assets support and pull content from any level of the hub hierarchy, regardless of how deeply nested the assets are.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Mobile App > Offline hubs:
This widget displays the hubs marked and saved as offline. You can view all the offline hubs and access them anytime on your device.

You can save an entire hub and its assets offline with the offline icon at the top right of the hub. This reduces the effort of picking and choosing the assets individually from a hub. Also, the assets within a hub get updated to their latest versions automatically as and when they come back online. Thus, you can easily access, search and showcase the latest assets on your devices even without a network.

Note for nested hubs: Saving a parent hub for offline use does not automatically include its nested child hubs. You must navigate to each child hub individually to toggle offline availability.

A confirmation page appears with details about the actions available once the hub is saved as offline. You can use the Save newly added assets automatically toggle button to allow the platform to save new assets within a hub for offline viewing. Click Save.

Once saved successfully, the icon on the upper-right corner changes to a green icon, confirming the hub is saved offline.

Note: Hubs available offline are specific to your device. If you have multiple devices, you must save hubs for offline view in each device separately. You cannot select hubs from your desktop to save for offline view on your mobile.

As soon as your device loses internet connection, you can view the following message on the Asset Hub homepage:

“No internet connection available. Go to offline assets home page.”

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Mobile App > Properties:
- Asset Owner (if assigned by the admin) : This section displays the name of the person who owns the responsibility of maintaining the asset. You can contact the asset owner in case you want to suggest any changes to the asset.
- Description : This section displays information about the type of content available within the asset that helps you quickly spot an asset in the search results. It also guides you on which asset to use and how to use it in a situation. For example, a pitch deck’s talk track helps you set the follow-up meeting and focus on creating value, controlling the process and winning deals.
- Attributes : This section displays the attributes associated with the asset. Attributes describe the characteristics of an asset. You can browse and filter relevant assets according to your use case using attributes. For example, suppose you want to reinforce the product value after a customer call by sending the pitch deck and a case study about using a specific feature. You can quickly browse such assets by selecting attributes like Case Study or Pitch Deck under the Collateral Type attribute category. It gives you the privilege to locate the right asset and find related assets without the need to search every asset using the asset name.
- Usage : This section displays whether to use the asset internally or externally. Internal usage indicates that you can use the asset only within your organization. External usage indicates that you can use the asset with your customers or prospects. For example, you can use a battle card when comparing your product with competitors and hence its usage is internal. You can use customer testimonials to improve trust among your prospects and hence its usage is external.
- Expiry : This section displays the asset expiry date, which ensures the effectiveness of the content within asset. Expiry date indicates until when the content is relevant. When an asset expires, it is advisable not to refer to that asset until updated.
- Hubs : This section displays the list of hubs in which the asset is available.
- Downloadable : This section displays whether you can download the asset or not. If an asset is not downloadable (in case the asset contains sensitive information which must not be customized), you can only use the asset in its original form. Contact your admin or Asset Owner for more details on using such assets.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Communications > Notifications and Reminders > Step 1: Verify the email address:
Mindtickle uses the Amazon SES service to send email notifications and reminders to Learners and Reviewers through the Mindtickle platform. So, Amazon SES needs to verify the new email address (example: enablement@abccompany.com ) to enable Mindtickle to send emails on behalf of the new email address.

You can perform the verification in one of the following ways:

Approach 1: Verification through a link sent to the email address

1. Create a functional valid email address (example: enablement@abccompany.com) with an inbox to receive emails in its domain. Share this email address with Mindtickle.

2. Mindtickle will then send a verification email to enablement@abccompany.com with the subject - Amazon Web Services – Email Address Verification Request.

3. Click the email authorization link in the verification email. You will receive ‘success’ feedback after clicking the link.Note:

- You must have admin access to the email address to verify the link.
- The verification link is only valid for 24 hours.

4. If you do not verify the email within 24 hours, contact Mindtickle to initiate a new verification email again.

Approach 2: Verification of the domain through the creation of DNS entry

1. Mindtickle provides a DNS TXT record that needs to be created on the company domain (abccompany.com) for verification.

2. Once the text record is created on the domain, Mindtickle will verify it, post which the email address can be used as a sender email address.Example DNS record:

To improve email deliverability and support DMARC compliance, Mindtickle uses DomainKeys Identified Mail (DKIM) based domain verification through Amazon SES. If your organization has a DMARC policy configured (p=quarantine or p=reject), DKIM verification is required to prevent emails from being rejected or marked as spam.

DKIM allows recipient email servers to confirm that emails sent by Mindtickle on behalf of your domain are authentic and have not been modified during transit.

DKIM-based domain verification process

Mindtickle uses Amazon SES Easy DKIM for domain authentication. To enable this, you must add DNS records to your domain.

1. Share the Domain nameShare the domain you want to use for sending emails (example: abccompany.com) with Mindtickle.Note: The sender email address (example: enablement@abccompany.com) must belong to this domain.

2. Mindtickle provides DKIM DNS recordsMindtickle will generate and share three DKIM CNAME records specific to your domain.Example:

| Type | Name | Value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CNAME | abc123._domainkey.abccompany.com | abc123.dkim.amazonses.com |
| CNAME | def456._domainkey.abccompany.com | def456.dkim.amazonses.com |
| CNAME | ghi789._domainkey.abccompany.com | ghi789.dkim.amazonses.com |

3. Add DKIM records to your DNS

Once you receive the DKIM CNAME, create CNAME records in your domain’s DNS provider (Example: Route 53, GoDaddy, Cloudflare).

Note:

- Do not modify the record names or values.
- DNS propagation can take up to 24 to 48 hours, depending on your provider.

4. DKIM verification by Mindtickle

Once the DNS records are added:

- Mindtickle will verify the DKIM status in Amazon SES.
- After successful verification, DKIM signing is automatically enabled for all outgoing emails from your domain.

5. Update DMARC policy

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Communications > Notifications and Reminders > Step 2: Verify the domain using DKIM:
Update DMARC policy

Note: This is an optional step, but recommended.

After DKIM is enabled and verified, ensure your DMARC policy allows DKIM-authenticated emails.

Example DMARC record:

```
v=DMARC1; p=reject; rua=mailto:dmarc-reports@abccompany.com; ruf=mailto:dmarc-forensic@abccompany.com;
```

Your email/security team can change values of DMARC record as per your compliance requirement, for example, can change policy(p) to p=quarantine or p=none.

Eight out of ten teams who have effective coaching practices hit greater than 75% of sales quotas (Heinz). But, in order to see results from sales coaching efforts, you can't rely solely on your frontline managers. Your entire sales function must be behind your coaching strategy, from reps and frontline managers to enablement and sales leadership.

Informed, data-driven sales coaching is another key to creating an impactful coaching culture. Without insights into skill gaps at the rep level, your coaching efforts could be ineffective leading to stagnant sales performance.

Join Blanchard and Mindtickle for a roundtable discussion on implementing individualized and effective sales coaching backed by performance data. Learn how all of your sales roles play a part in a coaching culture to drive consistent sales success.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Managers and Reviewers > Mobile app > Insights and Transcription > Insights > Content:
The Content Insight analyzes your submission and verifies if you have covered the right subjects in your recording. It consists of Keywords to Include and Words to Avoid, which help identify the areas of improvement in your pitch.

Keywords to Include is a list of words that the Learners are expected to use in their pitch.

Words to Avoid is a list of words that the Learners are expected to not use in their pitch. This insight displays the words from the list that the Learners have used in their submission.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Managers and Reviewers > Mobile app > Insights and Transcription > Insights > Articulation:
Articulation Insights analyze the Learner’s Mission attempts and the submission against specific parameters.

The Submission Length indicates how closely the Learner meets the target length range set by the Admin.

This section displays the submission length and the target time and states if the length is too short, short, appropriate, long, or too long.

| Insight | Criteria |
| --- | --- |
| Too Short | Less than 25% of the minimum length |
| Short | Between 25% - 80% of the minimum length |
| Appropriate | Between 90% of the minimum length and 110% of the maximum length |
| Long | Between 110% to 150% of the maximum length |
| Too Long | More than 150% of the maximum length |

Speech Pace shows how the Learner’s delivery of words compares with the Average Speaking Rate of 120-160 WPM.

The Speech Pace insight helps you understand if the pace at which the Learner delivered the submission is slow, appropriate, or fast. It displays the average number of words per minute that the Learner spoke. It also displays the Average Speaking Rate for comparison.

| Insight | Criteria |
| --- | --- |
| Too Slow | If the pace of pitch is less than 100 WPM. |
| Slow | If the pace of pitch is between 100 to 120 WPM. |
| Appropriate | If the pace of pitch is between 120 to 160 WPM. |
| Fast | If the pace of pitch is between 160 to 200 WPM. |
| Too Fast | If the pace of the pitch is more than 200 WPM. |

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Communications > Invite Learners:
Inviting individual learners or groups to a series or module is an integral part of ensuring enablement programs are deployed and adopted efficiently. To deploy well-planned enablement programs for learners or groups based across different time zones, admins can schedule an invite to a series or module for a later date. When triggered, the invitation is sent to the selected learners and groups at the specified date and time.

Scheduling invites ensure well-timed communication, which, in turn, ensures increased learner engagement and better content adoption.

As an admin, you can schedule invitations for individual learners, by uploading a list of learners (CSV upload), or groups to:

- Single series
- Single module
- Multiple modules

Note:

- Only admins who have permission to invite learners/groups to series/modules can schedule invitations.
- An invitation to a series or any of its modules can be scheduled only from the series page.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Communications > Invite Learners > Schedule invitations to series > For individual learners:
1. In the admin site sidebar, click Training > Series page, and navigate to the series for which you want to schedule the invitation.
2. Click Invite learners and select Individual learners under Schedule an invitation .
3. The Schedule Invitation: Individual Learners pop-up appears. Select the learners you want to schedule the invitation for by clicking the checkbox against their names. You can also find a specific learner using the Search field or filter learners based on their Profile Fields or Groups .
4. Click Schedule Invitation for (n) learner(s) . Note : Only learners that are part of the group at the scheduled invite time are invited.
5. The Schedule Invitation pop-up appears. Use the Calendar and Time fields to select the date and time at which the invitation should be sent. Use the Time Zone field to select the time zone. You can easily browse through the comprehensive list or search for specific locations (by city, country, or timezone name), making it effortless to find and select the desired timezone. Note :
  - Select a time that is at least 15 minutes away from the time of scheduling.
  - You can schedule an invitation for a date that is upto 1 year from the date of scheduling.
  - The invitation is sent to the selected learners based on the time zone you select. Ensure that you select a time zone that is specific to the learners for whom the invitation is being scheduled.
6. Click Schedule . A confirmation message displays on the screen once the invitation is successfully scheduled.
7. For more information about viewing invitation details, see View Invitation Details . To modify the invitation, see Modify an invitation . Note : Since a learner can be invited to a series just once, only the earliest invitation (instant or scheduled) is sent to the learner. So, if a learner is already invited to a series, they will not receive the invitation that is scheduled to be sent at a later time.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Communications > Invite Learners > Schedule invitations to modules > For learner groups:
1. Navigate to the series that contains the modules.
2. Select the published modules for which you want to schedule the invitation. Note: You can schedule invitations only for published modules. If you select both draft and published modules, only the published modules are included.
3. On the quick access panel, click Schedule Invitation , and then select Learner groups .
4. In the Schedule Invitation: Learner groups screen, select the learner groups you want to invite. You can search for a group using the search field.
5. Enable Link Status for each selected group, as required, to automatically invite members added to the group in the future to the selected modules.
6. To automatically remove group members from the module when they are removed from the group, select Remove users from the linked module when they are removed from the group.
7. Click Confirm .
8. Set the Module relevance for the selected groups.
9. In the Due date column , click Edit .
10. Select one of the following:

- No. of days after invitation: The system sets the module's due date to a specific number of days after the module invitation date. Enter a value from 1 to 730.
- No due date: The system does not set a due date for group members.

11. Select whether group members can continue the module after the due date or whether the module freezes.

12. Click Confirm.

By default, the system applies due dates in the following order of priority:

1. Due date set for an individual learner from the module’s Invite and track tab
2. Due date set when linking a group to the module
3. Due date set in the module’s Settings tab

Based on its current status, a scheduled invitation is classified as either one of the following 3 types:

- Pending - the scheduled invitation is yet to be sent
- Sent - the scheduled invitation is sent
- Failed - the scheduled invitation failed and was not sent

You can view all the scheduled invitations (Pending, Sent and Failed) for a series and its modules from the Scheduled Invitations page. To navigate to the Scheduled Invitations page:

1. Navigate to the series for which you want to view or modify the scheduled invitations.

  1. all invitations scheduled for the series AND
  2. all invitations scheduled for the modules that are a part of the series

For each invitation, the following details are displayed:

Invitation To: displays all invitations scheduled for the series or its modules.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > FAQs:
Call AI ensures compliance with GDPR as follows:

- Call AI sends an email to all the participants of the call 15 minutes prior to the meeting start time, informing them that the call will be recorded. Participants have the option to withdraw consent and stop the call recording.
- MindTickle users can enable or disable the bot from joining meetings from the Upcoming Meetings tab in Call AI. For more information, refer to the How do I stop the bot from joining the call? article.
- Call AI Admins can define what type of calls get recorded in any organization .
- Call AI users can remove the bot during a meeting depending on the web conferencing tool. For example, the host or a co-host of a Zoom meeting can stop the recording whenever required and remove the bot from the meeting.

Note: In all of the above cases, if a user stops the Call AI bot from recording the call, the bot will cancel the recording for every participant.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Setup > Site Setup:
Automation rules are created by applying conditions on modules, groups, profile fields, roles, or Salesforce (SFDC) opportunities and defining actions for learners who meet the conditions.

Note: SFDC opportunity rules can be created only if Automation Suite 2.0 is enabled for your learning site. For more information, see Overview of automation suite and contact Mindtickle Support or your Customer Success Manager (CSM).

Using different combinations of Conditions and Actions, you can create rules to invite a user to a module or a series, assign roles to a user, add a user to a group, or recommend assets to reps in SFDC.

Note: Even if admins manually remove a learner from a series/module with the Invite to module rule action, the learner gets re-invited to the series/module because of the automation rule.

Mindtickle rules are triggered when the condition specified in the rule is met. Once triggered, it performs the action that is specified in the rule.

When SFDC opportunity rules are triggered, assets are recommended to reps in SFDC. Asset recommendation through rules depends on the sync frequency set between SFDC and Mindtickle. Currently, the asset recommendation is updated every hour. For example, if the opportunity qualifies for a rule, the recommended assets start appearing in SFDC once the sync happens.

This article explains each condition and action. For information on how to create rules, see Create automation rules.

Note:

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Setup > Site Setup:
- You can create Mindtickle rules for all types of modules.
- You can create Mindtickle rules for standard and custom roles.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Setup > Site Setup > Conditions > Module Score of a Learner > For ILT Modules::
- If the objective of each session in the module is the same, you can configure the rule condition based on the learner’s score on the module. For example, consider an ILT module, Business Development , which includes 5 sessions on one topic - Know Your Competition - scheduled on different days for learners in different time zones. If your use case is to automatically invite learners to the series Onboarding - Business Development based on their performance in any of the sessions, you can create a rule based on the learner’s score on the module (as all sessions within the module are based on the same topic).
- If the sessions are on different topics, you can configure the rule condition based on the learner’s score on individual sessions from the module. For example, consider an ILT module Business Development Lifecycle which includes 6 sessions on individual topics such as Research , Analysis , Investment Planning , Innovation , Strategy , and Marketing . If your use case is to automatically invite users to the series Onboarding - Business Development based on their performance on particular sessions from the list, you can create a rule based on the learner’s score on one or more sessions from the module. Note : When creating session-based rules, by default, the Absolute score is selected as the conditional parameter and the option Percentage score is disabled. You cannot set the condition based on the Percentage score .
- If the score of any of the selected sessions for a learner is as defined in the rule condition, the learner qualifies per the rule criteria.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Setup > Site Setup > Conditions > Module status of a learner > For ILT modules::
When creating ILT-based rules using the Status on module condition, you can choose to configure the condition based on:

- the status of the module OR
- the status of one or more sessions from the selected module Note: You can set up automation rules only for individual ILT sessions, not for sessions that are part of events.

If the rule condition is based on the module, you can choose to define the status value as In progress or Completed.

If the rule condition is based on one or more sessions from the module, you can choose to define the status value as Attended, Did not attend, Enrolled, or Waitlisted.

Note:

- When the rule is created based on the status Enrolled , a learner whose attendance is marked as Attended (now or in the future) also qualifies per the criteria.
- When multiple sessions are added to a rule condition and learner’s status on any of the sessions is as defined in the rule condition, the learner meets the rule criteria.

The following table shows a list of all the module types and the different status values for each of them.

| Module Type | Status Values |
| --- | --- |
| Assessment | In progressPassedFailed |
| Checklist | PendingCompleted |
| Course, Quest, Quick-Update | In progressCompleted |
| Instructor-Led Training (ILT) | For Modules:In progressCompletedFor Sessions:EnrolledAttendedDid not attendWaitlisted |
| Coaching Sessions | ScheduledClosed |
| Mission | Submission PendingReview PendingReview Completed |
| Competency Assessment | Rules cannot be created on Status of module.Note: The rules are created based on the Score provided by the learner or the reviewer. |

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Setup > Site Setup > Conditions > Module certification status of a learner:
You can create rules based on the Certification on module condition only for course, assessment, and mission modules. When you select this condition, only Course, Assessment, and Mission modules will appear in the Search Modules drop-down.

The condition Certification on module can be built on certification Received or Not received.

Note:

- If the learner re-certifies on the module, the rule will be executed again. If the learner is already added to the series, module, or group as specified in the rule action, no action will be triggered.
- No action will be triggered when the certificate expires.
- If the Certification settings for a Course module are configured after some learners have completed the Course , they still qualify to receive the certification. In such cases, these learners, too, get executed by the rule that is based on the Certification status for that module.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Setup > Site Setup > Conditions > Learner's profile field value:
- represents a text-based field, and accepts input values in the form of keywords, in the form of regular expressions: When creating a rule on text-based fields, you can choose to enter Keywords or Text conditions (Regex) for which the rule is executed. For more information, see Create rules using keywords and Create rules using text conditions .
- represents a date-based field, and accepts input values in the form of date range, cohort, keywords, or regular expressions Note :
  - Date-based rules can be created on profile fields for which the input type is set as Date input . For more information, see Create a date type profile field .
  - Date-based rules are executed when a new user is added to the platform or when an existing user’s date profile field (on which the rule is set) value is updated. Subsequently, if a user is yet to be added to a group (based on a specified date), the rules are executed every 5 minutes. You can set up rules for date-based fields based on either of the following options:
  - Date range - this option allows you to define the Start and End dates between which the rule operates.
  - Cohort - setting up a cohort automatically triggers the action for users whose date in the specified profile field is one of the following:
    - More than X days ago
    - More than Y days ago
    - Between X to Y days ago Note :
      - Less than X days ago means all the dates starting from X days less than the date of evaluation to all the dates in future. For example, if the date of evaluation is Nov 23 and X is 1, then all dates including and post Nov 22 are applicable. The rule condition is satisfied for all future dates such as Nov 22, 23, 24, 25, and so on.
      - More than X days ago means all the dates before X days from the date of evaluation. For example, if the date of evaluation is Nov 23 and X is 1, then all dates before Nov 22 are applicable. The rule condition is satisfied for all past dates such as Nov 22, 21, 20, 19, and so on.
  - Regular expressions (Regex) - Regular expressions are used to execute rules by matching one or more text matches using a specific search pattern. See screenshot below, for reference. For more information, see Best practices for creating rules using text conditions .
  - Keywords - this option allows you to filter users based on the keywords specified
- represents a dropdown-based field, and displays multiple values from which the input values can be selected. It also accepts input values in the form of regular expressions Regular expressions: When setting up rules based on text-based fields or dropdown-based fields, you can choose to change the default Advanced settings . The options are selected by default because keywords are not case sensitive and spaces are ignored. If you want to make the keywords case sensitive and recognize the spaces in keywords, clear the checkboxes.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Setup > Site Setup > Conditions > SFDC - Opportunity:
In Salesforce (SFDC), an opportunity is a standard object that represents a potential sale or a deal in progress. It contains various standard fields to store and track information related to a sales opportunity. You can also create custom fields to store required information related to the opportunity.

When configuring rules based on the Opportunity field condition, you can create rules for standard and custom fields that are set up in your SFDC account.

Note:

- You can create SFDC opportunity rules for all opportunity fields (standard and custom) configured in your Salesforce account. By default, rules can be created for the following opportunity attributes:
  - Account Industry, Account Number of Employees, Account Name, Description, Name, Owner Email, Stage, Type, Amount, Probability, Created At, Last Updated At.
- To add custom attributes and for more information on custom mapping of fields, contact Mindtickle Support or your Customer Success Manager (CSM).
- The SFDC opportunity fields are mapped and become available in Mindtickle once the integration is authorized. For more information, see User Sync/User Provisioning with Salesforce: Steps to be performed in Mindtickle .

You can configure a rule such that if the opportunity field has a specific value, then post the next Mindtickle- Salesforce sync, the rule is triggered, and depending on the action specified in the rule, the recommended assets become available to the reps in SFDC.

Note:

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Setup > Site Setup > Conditions > Advanced options in profile, role, and group-based rules > Reversal in Profile and Group-based Rules:
The reversal operation in profile and group-based rules is only possible if the rule is set on a profile, a group, or a combination of a profile and a group. Hence, the Advanced options for profile and group-based rules are only supported when:

The condition is based on any of the following attributes:

Note: It is recommended not to create a rule with more than 50 conditions.

- Profile Field
- Added to group
- A combination of Profile field and Added to group

AND

- The action is set to Add to group Note : If the action Add to group is clubbed with another action ( Invite to series or Invite to module ), the Advanced options are no longer available and applicable in the rule.

Select the checkbox,

- Remove users from the group when they do not match the rule conditions If you want to remove users from the group when the values do not match the ones mentioned in the filter conditions. By default, this checkbox is not selected.
- Remove users from the linked series when they are removed from the group If you want to unlink users from the series linked with the group when they are removed from the group. Note : The Remove users from the linked series when they are removed from the group option is enabled only when the previous check box, Remove users from the group when they do not match the rule conditions , is selected.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Setup > Site Setup > Conditions > Advanced options in profile, role, and group-based rules > Reversal in Role-based Rules:
Reversal in role-based rules ensures the role is automatically revoked from the learner if the learner no longer meets the condition defined in the rule. The reversal operation in role-based rules is possible only if the action specified in the rule is to assign a role. There are no limitations on the condition defined in the rule. Automated role reversal can be configured if the rule is set up on a profile, a group, a learner’s role, a learner’s module score, a learner’s module status, or a combination of a profile and a group.

Hence, the Advanced Options for role-based rules are only supported when:

The condition is based on any of the following attributes:

- Status on module
- Score on module
- Certification on module
- Added to group
- Profile field
- Has role

AND

- The action is set to Assign role .

Select the checkbox Unassign users from the role when they do not match the rule if you want to revoke the role from the users when the rule condition is not satisfied. By default, this checkbox is not selected.
