Help & Support > Help Center Home > Setup > Site Setup > Actions:
- For role-based rules, while admins can assign and revoke standard and custom roles, they cannot assign or revoke the learner role. This role is assigned to every user on the platform by default and cannot be changed.
- SFDC actions are available only if Automation Suite 2.0 is enabled on your learning site. For more information, see Overview of automation suite and contact Mindtickle Support or your Customer Success Manager (CSM).
- For a rule, the condition and action should be of the same category (Mindtickle or Salesforce). You cannot combine Mindtickle conditions with Salesforce actions or vice versa in a single rule. For example, in the screenshot below, the Mindtickle actions are disabled as the condition configured is an SFDC opportunity-based condition.
- For SFDC opportunity rules, you can choose if you want to recommend specific assets or assets that meet the criteria to reps. Based on your selection from the SFDC action section, the recommended assets are displayed in the reps’ Opportunity view in SFDC. For more information, see Recommended assets .
- If the rule action is Invite to Module , you can define the relevance of the selected module. Thus ensuring all users qualifying the rule criteria, are invited to the module with the relevance defined in the action. For example, in the screenshot below, the module added in the rule action is Business Communication and its relevance is set to Required . So, completion of the quick update is mandatory for all users who score more than 80% in the course Sales Communication .
  - Defining the module relevance in a rule action does not modify the module’s default relevance.
  - By default, the module relevance configured while module creation is selected and applied.
- You can add multiple actions to a rule, however, you can add each action only once. For example, in the screenshot below, Add to group is disabled in the dropdown as it is already selected as an action.

chunks.headingPath: Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > Integrations
chunks.title: Call AI Integration With Aircall

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > Integrations > How Does Call AI’s Integration With Aircall Work?:
The integration works as follows:

1. Aircall records the call and sends the audio file to Call AI.

2. Call AI processes the audio file and makes it available on your Call AI interface.

3. Call AI generates useful insights, themes, transcripts, and statistics for the call recording. You can perform different actions, such as sending a private message, taking notes, and sharing the recording with peers and customers. For more information, see Call Recording Details.

Note:

- Call AI only imports the dialer calls of users with a recorder role. For more information, see Call AI Permissions .
- Call AI displays the phone number of the prospect as the recording name.
- If the name and email address of a participant is not available in the Aircall recording, Call AI displays the dialer number as the participant’s name. You can edit the participant's name on the recording details page.
- If you delete a recorded call in Aircall, the recording remains in Call AI. To delete such a recording from the Call AI interface, refer to the Delete a Call Recording article.
- If you want to start or pause call recording for a number associated with your Aircall account, follow the steps mentioned here .

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > Integrations > Speaker Separation Type:
The speaker separation type for the Aircall dialer is Mono. Since the audio input that Call AI receives in a Mono system is merged into a single channel for both the parties (sales rep and customer or prospect), the recording quality and the participant timeline’s accuracy are less as compared to a Stereo system.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > Integrations > Steps to Integrate Call AI With Aircall:
To set up Call AI integration with Aircall dialer, follow the below steps:

1. Log in to the Admin Site Homepage.

2. From the left panel, click Account >Settings> Call AI > Integrations.

3. Click Aircall > Enable.

4. You are directed to the Aircall dashboard.

5. Click AUTHORIZE to grant permission to Mindtickle to access information about your calls.

6. Select a number from the drop-down and click the ADD NUMBER button.

Note: If you have multiple numbers associated with your Aircall account, you can connect them by following these steps.

7. Call AI is now successfully integrated with Aircall.

8. Record your call using the Aircall dialer.

9. Once your call finishes, its recording appears in the recording list on the Call AI interface within 10 to 15 minutes. To learn about the insights available for a call recording, refer to the Call Recording Details article. You can use Call AI’s powerful and guided search to quickly look for a specific recording.

Note:

- Call AI does not fetch recordings that have a duration of less than 10 seconds.
- Call AI does not import incoming calls on your Aircall number.
- Call AI ignores recordings of non-Call AI users.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > Integrations > Start or Pause Call Recording for a Number:
To start or pause call recording for a number, follow the below steps:

1. Sign in to your Aircall Dashboard.

2. Navigate to the Numbers tab from the left panel.

3. Click a number to start or pause the recording.

4. On the page that appears, click the Settings tab and scroll down to the Call recording section.

5. You can view the following two options:

- Start recording automatically
- Allow the user to start & pause recording

Note: Call AI does not import incoming calls on your Aircall number.

6. Turn on the toggle switch according to your preference for each option. If you select Allow the user to start & pause recording, each user must turn on the recording when placing a call through Aircall.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Coaching Sessions:
Here are a few recommended best practices while creating Call AI Coaching Sessions:

- Create a dedicated series for Call AI coaching sessions. For more information on reviewing coaching sessions on Call AI see, Review coaching session on Call AI .
- If Call AI is enabled for coaching sessions, provide access to managers and learners for coaching sessions only using Call AI.
- Create a maximum of 5 coaching forms for a call. This enables the manager to navigate through the forms easily.
- Ensure that the coaching forms for the Call AI and general coaching sessions differ. Maintain separate forms for the coaching sessions based on the coaching activity.
- Limit evaluation parameters to 3 to 5 per coaching form, as Call AI visualization only displays the essential parameters.
- Enable Call AI coaching sessions only on sites that use email addresses as usernames. This will ensure that the email sent out to learners is not hampered.
- When creating Call AI-based coaching sessions, the admin should avoid adding learners or reviewers. The learner and reviewer are auto-updated based on who the manager coaches in the session.
- If you create a coaching session dedicated to Call AI, here are a few email best practices you should follow:
  - Remove or archive Call AI-based test coaching sessions from the series. If they are not removed, the sales manager can see the test coaching sessions on Call AI coaching.
  - Disable the following emails:
    - Review Scheduled
    - Review Assigned
    - First Session not Scheduled/Reviewed.

Note: The above emails are disabled because coaching sessions dedicated to Call AI is not a scheduled session. The reviewer performs the coaching session as and when required.

Using the Coaching on Call AI feature, managers and users can simultaneously listen to a call and coach the learners/reps from one platform without switching between platforms.

1. Select Scorecard > Start coaching option from the call recording screen. Note : You can see the Coach option only if the admin has enabled it.

  - Coach Again if you have already coached the participant for the selected call. Click the Completed option to view the list of completed coaching sessions under the participant's name.
  - Continue if you have coached the participant but have not submitted the coaching form.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Modules:
Analytics for the ILT (Instructor-Led Training) module provides data and insights to admins on learners’ participation (attendance and enrollment) in an ILT. It provides analytics in the form of overview widgets, top stats, and detailed tables.

The ILT module report gives a consolidated view of how learners are doing across sessions for an ILT in a particular series. Moreover, if an ILT is present across multiple series, admins can apply filters to view the ILT’s data for all series where it is multi-present.

The ILT module report provides analytics for an ILT module in three tabs:

- Overview: Overview of learners’ attendance and enrollment across sessions
- Learners: Details of learners’ participation across sessions.
  - Learner’s ILT report: From the Learners tab, you can access any learner’s ILT report, which provides details on the learner’s enrolled and waitlisted sessions.
- Sessions: Details of sessions in the ILT.
  - Individual session analytics: From the Sessions tab, click any session to view its detailed analytics.

Note: ILT analytics considers all learners in an ILT: active learners as well as learners who were later removed from the module or deactivated from the platform. Removed/deactivated learners are considered even if they did not enroll into or waitlisted themselves on a session. Except for the Learner Funnel widget, which considers only active learners. On the Learners tab, removed learners are indicated with the text “(removed)” added after their name.

- Navigate back to module reports: Click the breadcrumb in the top-left to go back to the Module Reports page.
- Apply filters: On each of the three tabs, you can apply various filters. More information about the available filters is provided within each tab’s section further in the article.
- Download, share, and bookmark reports:
  - Use the Download button in the report header to download an overall visual summary (PDF) of the dashboard. This opens the PDF report settings where you can configure paper size, orientation, header/footer details, and toggle Edit mode to visually resize widget rows before downloading.
  - To download specific data from individual widgets across any tab, hover over a widget, click the three-dot menu in the top-right corner, and select Download (available in Image, CSV, or Excel formats depending on the widget type).
  - Use the ( Share ) and ( Bookmark ) buttons on any tab to share the report with others or bookmark it for yourself.
  - Click Help to open the help article for detailed documentation.

For more information, see the “Download, share, and bookmark reports” section.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Modules > Overview tab > Attendance & Enrollment by Sessions widget:
This widget provides a summary of how many learners are participating in the sessions. It shows an overview of learners’ attendance and enrollment, in percentage, across sessions.

Each session shows the attendance and enrollment % for sessions that are over, where:

- Attendance % = Attended / Enrolled x 100
- Enrollment % = No. of enrollments / No. of seats x 100

Note:

- In a case where sessions are not yet over, Enrollment % alone is shown. In this case, Attendance will be 0%.
- For sessions where enrollment seats are not fixed, the enrollment will be 100%.

The statistic below the graph shows the average attendance % across sessions (sessions that are over).

The widget shows the top five sessions based on the enrollment %. You can choose to view the top or the bottom five sessions. Click any of the legends to temporarily hide its data from the graph. Click "more" to get more information on all the sessions in this ILT. This opens the Sessions tab.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Modules > Overview tab > Attendance by User Cohorts widget:
This widget provides a comparative look at the attendance rates across various user cohorts. Cohorts can be based on groups or learner profile fields. When you select “profile fields” as the cohort, you need to select any of the available profile fields, such as Region or Designation, to view its data.

By default, the widget shows data for groups as the cohort, and for the top five cohorts with the highest attendance rates, sorted by their attendance (%). You can choose to view the top or the bottom five of the selected cohort.

The attendance % is the average of the attendance of learners in a cohort and it is calculated as follows:

Attendance % = Attended / Enrolled x 100

For example, there are three sessions in an ILT and 10 learners (from group 1 and group 2) are invited:

Group 1: 5 learners A, B, C, D, and E

- Session 1: Enrolled (A, B, C); Attended (A, B, C)
- Session 2: Enrolled (A, C, D); Attended (A, C)
- Session 3: Enrolled (A, C, E); Attended (A, E)

Group 1’s attendance % = 7/9 x 100 = 77.77%

Group 2: 5 learners V, W, X, Y, Z

- Session 1: Enrolled (X, Y, Z); Attended (X, Y, Z)
- Session 2: Enrolled (Y, Z); Attended (Y, Z)
- Session 3: Enrolled (X, Y, Z); Attended (X, Y, Z)

Group 2’s attendance % = 8/8 x 100 = 100%

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Modules > Overview tab > Filters:
- Session Date: Use this filter to view data for sessions based on the time period in which they were conducted. The available options are: Past 15 Days, Past 30 Days, Past 90 Days, Last Month, Last 3 Months, Last 6 Months, and Custom Time. Note: For the period that you select, this filter considers sessions by their start date and time, and not the session end date. So, if a session’s start date is within the selected period but the end date is after the selected period, it is still shown.

Note: When you open an ILT from the Module Reports page, the series to which it belongs is always selected by default in the Series filter.

- Learner Fields: Select one or more profile fields and their values to view data for learners who have the selected profile fields.
- More filters: The following additional filters are available:
  - Session: Select one or more sessions to view data by sessions.

By default, the report shows data for all learners (active, removed, and deactivated) with a text besides each learner when they are removed or deactivated.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Modules > Learners tab > Table data:
- Learners: Names and email addresses of learners. Click the name of a learner to view their overall ILT report . Note: ILT analytics considers all learners in an ILT: active learners as well as learners who were later removed from the module or deactivated from the platform. Removed/deactivated learners are considered even if they did not enroll into or waitlisted themselves on a session. In this table, removed learners are indicated with the text “(removed)” added after their name.
- Attendance Rate: Sessions that the learner has attended out of all the completed sessions. It is calculated as follows: Attendance % = (sessions attended / enrolled) x 100
- Attended/Enrolled: Total number of sessions that the learner attended out of the total number of sessions they are enrolled into. An orange dot in this column indicates that the learner has not marked their attendance for any of the enrolled sessions that are completed.
- Watched recording?: Number of session recordings that the learner has watched out of the total number of recordings uploaded for each session in the module. If no recording is uploaded for a session, the value will be "NA".
- Completion Status: A learner’s sessions can be “In Progress” or “Completed” depending on whether all sessions that the learner has enrolled into are over. The learner’s completion status becomes “In Progress” as soon as they enroll into a session. The status is marked “Completed” only when all sessions that they enrolled into are completed and the learner has attended them all and their attendance is marked "Yes". Additionally, in case the learner did not attend a session and the admin has uploaded the session recording, the session is marked attended only if the learner watches the session recording.
  - In Progress: When at least one out of all enrolled sessions is not yet complete. That is, when one or more sessions are either live currently (and not over) or upcoming. Additionally, the completion status will be “In Progress” if the learner either did not attend any of the enrolled sessions or attended but the attendance is not yet marked.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Modules > Learners tab > Learner’s ILT Report > Enrolled Sessions:
- Sessions: Names of enrolled sessions. Click the name of a session to view detailed analytics for this particular session. For more information, see the Individual Session Analytics section.
- Instructor: Names and emails of the session instructors.
- Session Status: Current status of the session. Whether the session is over, upcoming, live, or canceled.
- Attended?: Whether the learner attended the session and marked their attendance. If the attendance is unmarked, the column shows whether it is not marked by the admin, or the learner ( Self Check-In ), or the ILT-Zoom integration ( auto-attendance ), or the ILT-Webex integration ( auto-attendance ). For example, if a session used Self Check-In for marking attendance and the learner missed to mark their attendance, the column will show “Unmarked - via self check-in”. Note : With Zoom’s March 2022 release , the ILT-Zoom integration for Auto-Attendance feature cannot mark the attendance of guest participants automatically. When using this method to track learners’ attendance, it is advised that you review the list and mark the attendance of guest participants manually (if it is not tracked automatically). To ensure data is reported accurately, your Customer Success Manager (CSM) will help you review the attendance for all ILT sessions that are conducted post 1st March 2022. For more information about how to mark the attendance manually, see Mark Attendance .
- Watched recording?: Whether the learner has watched the session recording: not started, in progress, or completed. If no recording is uploaded for a session, the value will be "NA".
- Completion status: Whether the learner has completed the session. A session is considered completed when all enrolled sessions have been completed AND the learner attended them all (or, if not attended, watched the session recording uploaded by the admin) and their attendance is marked "Yes". If the attendance is unmarked for any session, the session is considered as "In Progress".
- Session Date: The date when the session was scheduled.
- Manage: Click the Manage link to open the ILT’s Manage Session page of the series in which this learner is invited and enrolled. In case the learner is present in two such series, it redirects you to any one of the series' Manage Session page.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Modules > Sessions tab > Individual Session Analytics:
Under the Sessions tab, click the name of a session to view an individual session’s analytics.

The session analytics page provides an overview of the session, such as the total number of learners, attendance rate, and distribution of learners with respect to attendance and enrollment. It also provides enrollment and attendance details for all learners in the session.

Below the session name, it provides basic information about the session, such as the date and time, duration, and instructor. It also provides the Enrollment Lock information — whether or not the session is locked for learner enrollment:

- For locked sessions, it displays the following message: Enrollments for this session are locked.
- For unlocked/open sessions, it displays the following message: Learners will be unable to enroll or unenroll after <date and time>

You can apply filters to view data as per your needs. You can also share and bookmark a report of this tab’s data.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Modules > Sessions tab > Individual Session Analytics > Table data:
The session table provides attendance and enrollment details for each learner, such as their attendance and enrollment status, score, and the date when they were invited to the session.

The table provides various information for each learner in the following columns:

- Learners: Names and email addresses of learners. Click the name of a learner to view their overall ILT report . Note: ILT analytics considers all learners in an ILT: active learners as well as learners who were later removed from the module or deactivated from the platform. Removed/deactivated learners are considered even if they did not enroll into or waitlisted themselves on a session. In this table, removed learners are indicated with the text “(removed)” added after their name. You can use the Removed Learners filter to filter out the removed learners from the data.
- Series Name: The series in which this session resides. If the session is multi-present , all series names are listed.
- Enrollment Status: Displays whether the learner is enrolled or waitlisted for the session.
- Attendance Status: Displays whether the learned attended the session, did not attend it, or the attendance is unmarked.
- Score: Score achieved by the learner.
- Invited On: The date when the learner was invited to the session.
- Manage: Click the Manage link to open the ILT’s Manage Session page of the series in which this learner is invited and enrolled. In case the learner is present in two such series, it redirects you to any one of the series' Manage Session page.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Modules > Download, share, and bookmark reports:
- Download reports: The analytics platform provides two ways to download your data depending on what you need:
  - Overall tab report (PDF): Click the Download button in the report header to export a visual summary of your dashboard. This opens the PDF report settings pop-up, where you can:
    - Set the Paper size (A4 by default) and Orientation (Portrait or Landscape).
    - Customize the Header (choose to display the Title, Data As Of, Dataset Name, and Dashboard Filters) and the Footer (toggle page numbers).
    - Toggle to Edit mode to manually adjust the height of widget rows before exporting.
    - Once configured, click Save at the bottom of the left panel, and then click the Download icon next to it to save the PDF.
  - Individual widget data: You can download specific data from individual widgets across all three tabs. Hover over a widget, click the three-dot menu in the top-right corner, and select Download . The available formats depend on the widget type:
    - Table data widgets: Download as an Image, CSV file, or Excel file.
    - Visual or summary widgets: Download as an Image or CSV file.
- Share reports: Use the ( Share ) button on any tab to share the report with other Admins and Managers. If you apply filters, the report is shared with filters applied. For more information, see Share Reports and Access Shared Reports in Analytics .
- Bookmark reports: Use the ( Bookmark ) button on any tab to bookmark the report for yourself. If you apply filters, the report is bookmarked with filters applied. For more information, see Bookmark Reports and Access Bookmarked Reports in Analytics .

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Setup > Site Setup > Method I:
- As an admin, you can simultaneously sign in to an admin site and its corresponding learning site (only) and vice versa.
- If you use multiple Mindtickle instances, you can access the admin site and learning site simultaneously of one instance only. When you switch to another admin site or sign in to another learning site, you get signed out of the instance you are currently logged in to. In other words, you cannot access and use multiple Mindtickle instances simultaneously. For example, if you are signed in to admin site “A”, you can sign in to learning site “A” only, and not to any other learning site. If you sign in to learning site “B”, you are signed out of admin site “A”.
- If you are signed in to learning site “A” and you navigate to admin site “A”, you are automatically signed in and can perform actions if you have admin permissions . If you do not have admin permissions, you will see an error message when you are signed in and cannot perform any actions.
- While you are signed in to admin site “A”, if you sign in to learning site “B”, when you refresh the page with admin site “A”, you are signed out of admin site “A” and are signed in to admin site “B”. You can perform actions in admin site “B” only if you have admin permissions.
- Suppose you are signed in to admin site “A” and its learning site, you switch to admin site “B” and you have admin permissions on both sites. In this case, you are automatically signed out of learning site “A” and must sign in to learning site “B” to continue.
- In case you need to sign in to multiple admin or learning sites simultaneously, we recommend using different browsers for each instance or signing in to each instance using the Incognito/Private Browsing mode in your browser.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > Integrations:
Call AI integrates seamlessly with your calendar to automatically record and transcribe meetings. This article explains how to set up the Call AI integration with Zoom, use the recording feature, and manage your recordings.
chunks.body: Call AI integrates seamlessly with your calendar to automatically record and transcribe meetings. This article explains how to set up the Call AI integration with Zoom, use the recording feature, and manage your recordings.
chunks.headingPath: Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > Integrations
chunks.title: Call AI Zoom integration

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > Integrations > Prerequisites:
Ensure you meet the following requirements:

- You must have a Zoom Pro/Business/Enterprise account.
- You must be an Account Owner or Admin (or an admin-approved user) in Zoom to set up the Call AI-Zoom integration.
- Admin permissions to auto-enable recording for a meeting.
- You must integrate your Outlook or Google calendar with Call AI. Click Preferences > Integrations > Calendar > Enable . For more information, see Integrate Outlook Calendar with Call AI or Integrate Google Calendar with Call AI .
- Calendar (Google or Outlook) event for the scheduled Zoom meeting.
- Recording consent and voice prompts are enabled for all participants in Zoom.
- Allowing only authenticated users in meetings is disabled for all participants in Zoom.
- Contact Mindtickle Support to turn on the zoom_active_consent_flag setting.
- To enable or disable Zoom cloud recording for all users in the account: a) Sign in to the Zoom web portal as an admin to edit the account settings. b) In the navigation panel, click Account Management > Account Settings . c) Click the Recording tab. d) Click the Cloud recording toggle to enable or disable the Cloud recording. e) If a verification dialog appears, click Enable or Disable to verify the change. If you cannot view the account settings or manage configurations in the Zoom application, reach out to your internal IT team to check if you have all the required permissions (licensed, pro account).

Note:

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > Integrations > How does the Call AI and Zoom integration works:
After you integrate Call AI with Zoom:

- Enable the recording for the meeting from the Upcoming Meetings page in Call AI before or during the meeting. If you enable the recording before the meeting, Call AI sends a recording reminder to all the internal and external participants of the call 12 to 15 minutes prior to the meeting start time. The bot joins as soon as the host starts the meeting.
- Zoom captures the active consent of all participants before recording the meeting:
  - Participants can see a pop-up on their screen to consent to the recording. Note: Zoom provides an option to customize the consent pop-up. For more information, see Customizing the recording consent disclaimer .
  - Participants can request the host to stop the recording at any time.
- Call AI bot records the conversation, generates meeting transcripts, and provides valuable insights .

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > Integrations > How does the Call AI and Zoom integration works > Call AI and Zoom work in sync to record the meeting as follows:
1. Sign in to your Call AI instance using your Mindtickle credentials.

2. Integrate your Outlook or Google calendar with Call AI. Click Call AI > Preferences > Integrations > Outlook calendar > Enable. For more information, see Integrate Outlook Calendar with Call AI or Integrate Google Calendar with Call AI.

Note: Currently, Call AI only supports meetings scheduled through your synced calendar. Meetings scheduled through your Zoom account are not supported.

3. Set up a Zoom meeting on your calendar.The following table explains the workflow of Call AI and Zoom recording during a meeting:

| During the meeting | The Call AI bot leaves when the host disables Zoom recording.Note: The Call AI bot does not rejoin if the host pauses or stops Zoom recording and restarts after some time. |
| --- | --- |
| The Zoom recording starts when the host enables Call AI recording from the Upcoming Meetings page. |  |
| The Zoom recording stops when the host disables Call AI recording from the Upcoming Meetings page.Note: Only users with a recorder role can enable recording for a meeting. For more information, see Call AI Permissions.Note: The Zoom cloud recording does not automatically stop if you remove the bot from the meeting. |  |
| If there are back-to-back meetings on the same Zoom link, a new Call AI bot joins every meeting, and the bot from the last meeting can be removed manually by the host. In Zoom, the same recording continues. |  |

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > Integrations > Frequently asked questions (FAQ’s):
1. When will the Call AI recordings be available if my meeting ends early?

The Call AI recordings are processed after the scheduled end time of the meeting.

2. What happens if the bot does not join the meeting?

If recording is disabled by default, the bot will not join. To enable recording, go to the Upcoming meeting page and turn it on.3: Can I remove the Call AI bot during a meeting?

Yes, the meeting host can remove the Call AI bot to stop the Call AI bot recording.4. Is the recording for webinar and Townhall supported?

No, webinar and Townhall is not supported.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > User > Install Call AI Calendar Plugin From Google Marketplace:
1. Go to Google Marketplace.

2. Search for the Call AI plugin using the top search bar.

3. From the displayed page, click Install.

4. Sign in to your Google account if not already signed in and approve the app permissions.

5. Open your Google calendar and click the Call AI icon from the right navigation panel.

6. Click AUTHORIZE ACCESS to provide access to the Call AI plugin of your Google account.

7. Sign in to your Google account.

8. Click Allow to give the following permissions to the Call AI plugin.

9. Click LOGIN to sign in to your Call AI account and authorize the add-on.

10. Enter the Call AI site URL and sign in using your Mindtickle credentials or registered email address with Call AI.

11. Give permission to the calendar plugin to create a Call AI proxy URL. Click Accept to proceed. Call AI plugin is now successfully installed in your Google account.

The Call AI dashboard shows an organized summary of all the call recordings that you can access through your Call AI interface.

The dashboard has the following widgets:

1. All recordings: Tap All recordings to access the list of all the calls within Call AI mobile.

2. Upcoming meetings: This widget lists all the calls in progress or scheduled for the day. Tap on each meeting to view the participants and change the recording status.

Note: The Upcoming meetings widget displays only if you have the recorder permission in Call AI. For more information, see Call AI Permissions.

3. My recordings: This widget lists the last seven calls in which you were a participant.

4. Shared with me: This widget lists the last seven calls your manager or other reps shared with you.

5. Bookmarked: This widget lists the last seven calls that you have bookmarked.

For more information, see Recordings List in Call AI.

Paste the action items in public messages, private messages, emails, or chats (outside the app).

For more information, see Call Recording Details.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > Mobile App > Share call recording > Share within your organization:
Tap the Share via email option under Share within your organization to share the recording with your peer via email.

On the pop-up that appears:

- Copy link: Tap this option to share the recording with your peers through group chat or text. Users can access the link based on the recording link access setting (Restricted or Organization). Click the down arrow to modify the access permission for users in your organization.

You can share the same call or snippet multiple times. The snippet duration must be a minimum of 30 seconds.Note: Upon sharing the snippet, Call AI plays the snippet you created. Users get access to the complete call in case of internal sharing.
- Tap the Share button to proceed.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > Mobile App > Picture-in-picture (PiP):
Note: The picture-in-picture feature is currently supported only for iOS. It will be supported on Android soon.

The Picture in Picture (PiP) mode lets you view the recording in a mini-player while performing other tasks.

With the help of PIP, you can multitask and listen to the call recording using other apps or locked devices.

While watching a call recording, navigate to the device home screen to trigger the PiP mode automatically. In this mode, the video appears as a pop-up (inset window) in a corner of the screen so you can use other apps.

You can take the following actions in the PiP mode:

- Resize the video window: Pinch in or out to make the video window smaller or larger.
- Show/hide controls: Tap the video window.
- Move the video window: Drag it to a different corner of the screen.
- Hide the video window: Drag it off the left or right edge of the screen.
- Close the video window: Tap the Close button.
- Return to a full video screen: Tap the Restore Full Screen button in the small video window.

For more information, see Picture-in-picture and background playback for media content (mobile app).

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > Integrations > How the integration works?:
1. Dialpad records the call and sends the audio file to Call AI.

2. Call AI processes the audio file and makes it available on your Call AI interface.

3. Call AI generates useful insights, themes, transcript and statistics for the call recording. You can perform different actions such as send a private message, take notes and share the recording with peers and customers. For more information, see Call Recording Details.

Note:

- Call AI only imports the dialer calls of users with a recorder role. For more information, see Call AI Permissions .
- Call AI displays the phone number of the prospect as the recording name.
- If the name and email address of a participant is not available in the Dialpad recording, Call AI displays the dialer number as the participant’s name. You can edit the participant's name on the recording details page.
- If you delete a recorded call in Dialpad, the recording remains in Call AI. For more information about deleting such a recording from the Call AI interface, see Delete a Call Recording .

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > Integrations > Speaker separation type:
The speaker separation type for Dialpad is Mono. Since the audio input that Call AI receives in a Mono system is merged into a single channel for both the parties (reps and customers or prospects), the recording quality and the participant timeline’s accuracy are less as compared to a Stereo system.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > Integrations > Steps to integrate Call AI with Dialpad:
To set up Call AI integration with Dialpad, follow the below steps:

Note: Only the admin of Dialpad can integrate the Dialpad account with Call AI.

1. Log in to the Admin Site Homepage.

2. From the left panel, click Account >Settings> Call AI > Integrations.

3. Click Dialpad > Enable.

4. Sign in to your Dialpad account.

5. Click Allow to give permission to Mindtickle to access information about your calls.

Call AI is now successfully integrated with Dialpad.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > Integrations > Steps to integrate Call AI with Dialpad > Recording a call with Dialpad:
1. When you make a call using Dialpad, click the Record option to record your call.

Note: The call recording is listed in Call AI only if you record the call in Dialpad.

2. Once your call finishes, the recording appears in the recording list on the Call AI interface approximately in an hour. There might be a delay in recording if there is an issue from Dialpad’s end. In that case, we recommend a wait time of up to 2 hours. You can use Call AI’s powerful and guided search to quickly look for a specific recording. For information about the insights available for a call recording, see Call Recording Details.

Note:

- Call AI does not fetch recordings that have a duration of less than 10 seconds.
- Call AI does not import incoming calls on your Dialpad number.
- Call AI does not support Dialpad call transfer and conference.
- Call AI keeps only the first recording in case a rep starts and stops recording multiple times during a call.
- Call AI does not capture shared screen in Dialpad recordings.
- Call AI ignores recordings of non-Call AI users.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > Integrations > 1-way HubSpot Integration:
The 1-way HubSpot integration allows Call AI to pull HubSpot objects into Call AI and associate it with relevant recordings. Call AI users can use HubSpot objects as filters to slice and dice the data and analyze calls that quantify the likelihood of winning a deal.

Perform the following steps to enable the 1-way HubSpot integration:

1. Log in to the Admin Site Homepage.

2. From the left panel, click Account >Settings> Call AI > Integrations.

3. Click Hubspot > Enable.

4. Sign in to HubSpot.

5. Select your HubSpot account. The 1-way HubSpot integration is now successful.

6. Select the HubSpot objects you want to sync in Call AI. These objects appear as filters under the More Filters section on the recordings list page and help you analyze calls made during different sales stages.

You can also select fields under the Promoted Filter, Account Name Field, and the Opportunity Stage Field drop-downs in the upper-right corner.

- The field selected under the Promoted Filter drop-down elevates above the other filters on the recording list page and helps you quickly filter recordings.
- The fields selected under the Account Name Field and Opportunity Stage Field drop-downs appear under the More filters on the analytics pages and help you analyze calls that quantify the likelihood of winning a deal.
chunks.body:
The 1-way HubSpot integration allows Call AI to pull HubSpot objects into Call AI and associate it with relevant recordings. Call AI users can use HubSpot objects as filters to slice and dice the data and analyze calls that quantify the likelihood of winning a deal.

Perform the following steps to enable the 1-way HubSpot integration:

1. Log in to the Admin Site Homepage.

2. From the left panel, click Account >Settings> Call AI > Integrations.

3. Click Hubspot > Enable.

4. Sign in to HubSpot.

5. Select your HubSpot account. The 1-way HubSpot integration is now successful.

6. Select the HubSpot objects you want to sync in Call AI. These objects appear as filters under the More Filters section on the recordings list page and help you analyze calls made during different sales stages.

You can also select fields under the Promoted Filter, Account Name Field, and the Opportunity Stage Field drop-downs in the upper-right corner.

- The field selected under the Promoted Filter drop-down elevates above the other filters on the recording list page and helps you quickly filter recordings.
- The fields selected under the Account Name Field and Opportunity Stage Field drop-downs appear under the More filters on the analytics pages and help you analyze calls that quantify the likelihood of winning a deal.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > Integrations > 2-way HubSpot Integration:
The 2-way HubSpot integration syncs Call intelligence data within HubSpot standard objects. It helps to view how a team performs in sales conversations and understand valuable insights into the team’s recording statistics such as Team Talk%, Team Listen%, Team Questions, Prospect Questions, Themes Spoken and Themes Heard.

In the 2-way integration, the Call AI data is available inside a HubSpot engagement object Meetings that associates with HubSpot standard objects such as Contact, Company, and Deal.

| Call AI Data | Data Flow | HubSpot Data |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Contact | -> | Contact |
| Account | -> | Company |
| Opportunity | -> | Deal |

Contact your Customer Success Manager (CSM) or Mindtickle Support to enable the 2-way HubSpot integration.

Perform the following steps to view Call AI data in your HubSpot account:

1. Sign in to HubSpot.

2. Click Contacts from the upper-left corner.

3. Select your name from the list that appears.

4. Click the Meetings object. You can view a list of recorded calls for the account and recording statistics such as Team Talk%, Team Listen%, Team Questions, Prospect Questions, Interchanges, Recording URL, Themes Spoken and Themes Heard for each call.

Note: It takes approximately 3 - 4 hours for Call AI recordings to appear within HubSpot.

For more information about recording statistics, see Conversation Stats.

This article explains how managers and reps from different teams can set their individual call recording preferences for meetings they host.

When hosting a meeting, consider whether you need to record and why. chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > User > Steps to customize recording preferences:
Perform the following steps to set recording preferences:

1. Sign in to your Call AI interface using your Mindtickle credentials.

2. Click the Preferences tab from the left navigation panel.

3. Under the Integrations tab, click Enable to sync your calendar (Google or Outlook) with Call AI and record all your meetings automatically.

Note: You can enable the calendar integration if you have a recorder role in Call AI. For more information, see Call AI Permissions.

3. You can view a list of all your Email alerts set so far on the specific search and filter attributes.

Click the More options icon for an email alert to perform the following actions:

- Rename alert : Change the alert’s name to a more relevant one.
- Delete alert : Permanently remove the alert if it is no longer required.

Click the Expand icon next to the alert name to view all the call recordings matching that search or filter criteria.

For information about setting Email alerts, see Recordings list in Call AI.

4. Select recording preferences by clicking one of the following options:

- Default preferences set by the admin : Choose this option to record only external meetings hosted by you.
- Customized preferences for the meetings hosted by you : Choose from the following 4 options:
  - Record all meetings
  - Record external meetings
  - Record internal meetings
  - Disable recording

For more information, see What type of meetings Call AI records?

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Assets > Dashboard widgets > Snapshot metrics:
The top of the dashboard displays a snapshot of key metrics for the selected time period, each shown alongside a comparison to the previous month so you can quickly assess trends:

- Published assets: Number of published assets (in filtered scope) currently on the platform (Assets page).
  - External-facing assets: Number of assets available for external sharing.
- Shares: Total number of times assets were shared during the period selected in the Duration filter.
  - vs previous month (%) : Percentage change in shares compared to the previous month.
- Users who shared assets: Number of unique users who shared assets during the selected period in the Duration filter.
  - vs previous month (%) : Percentage change in users who shared assets compared to the previous month.
- Open rate (%): Percentage of shared assets that were opened by recipients. For example, if four assets were shared and two were viewed, the open rate is 50%.
  - vs previous month (%): Percentage change in open rate compared to the previous month.
- External views: Total number of times shared assets were viewed by external recipients.
  - vs previous month (%): Percentage change in external views compared to the previous month.
- Unique external views: Number of uniquely identified external contacts who viewed shared assets. Note : Anonymous visits, where recipient consent has not been provided, are excluded from this count.
  - vs previous month (%): Percentage change in unique external views compared to the previous month.
- Total users: All Asset Hub users currently active on the platform. Note: Report filters don’t apply to this widget.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Assets > Filters > Applying a filter:
When you click into a filter category, a window opens with three distinct ways to define your data view:

- Default setting : Filters are applied by default with preselected values to display a broad dataset.
  - Duration: This and Last 4 Quarters
  - User state: Active
  - All other filters: Include all, meaning no filtering is applied and all available data is displayed
- Selection from list : You can search for and check specific items (e.g., selecting only DSR and Linkedin under Interaction source ). This is best for targeting known assets, users, attributes, groups, etc.
- Conditional filtering : This advanced option allows you to create rules using a variety of operators, including Is , Contains , Starts with , Ends with , Is empty , and their opposites (e.g., Does not contain ). - User state : This allows you to filter the data based on the status of the users, such as Active , Deactivated , or Deleted . This helps ensure your reports are only reflecting current, relevant users.

- Total assets: Total number of assets in the platform, including a count of draft assets not yet published.
- Assets without description: Number of assets that do not have a description added, which can impact searchability.

- Expired assets: Number of assets that have passed their set expiration date.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Assets > Audit tab > 1. Asset lifecycle trends:
This bar chart shows month-on-month content management activity across three actions: newly published assets, archived assets, and updated assets. This chart helps you assess the overall health of your content management practices — for example, whether you are actively archiving stale content and updating existing assets, or only creating new content without managing what already exists.

- Newly published refers to assets being published for the first time.
- Archived refers to assets that have been moved to archived state.
- Updated refers to assets whose properties have been updated or that have been republished after changes.

A healthy content library typically shows a good mix of all three activities over time.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Assets > Audit tab > 3. Audit recommendations:
This detailed table provides a per-asset audit view with an actionable recommendation for each asset. The table includes the following columns:

- Asset name: Name of the asset. Click to open the asset detail page in a new tab.
- Asset owner (username): Username of the assigned asset owner.
- Asset status: Current status of the asset, such as Published.
- Expiration date: The expiration date set for the asset, if configured.
- Asset expired: Indicates whether the asset has passed its expiration date (true or false).
- Asset description added: Indicates whether a description has been added to the asset (true or false).
- Asset owner inactive or lost access: Indicates whether the assigned asset owner is inactive or has lost access to the platform (true or false).
- Attributes added: Number of attributes currently applied to the asset.
- Days since last updated: Number of days since the asset was last modified or republished.
- Days since last engaged: Number of days since the asset last received any engagement.
- Audit recommendation: The system-generated recommendation for the asset.

The Audit recommendation column provides one of four possible recommendations for each asset, based on a combination of engagement trends, expiration settings, and file update reminders:

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Assets > Audit tab > 3. Audit recommendations:
- Keep: The asset is recent and actively receiving engagement. No action is required.
- Update: The asset has a configured expiration date or file update reminder that has passed or is approaching. The asset should be reviewed and updated accordingly.
- Review: The asset's engagement has dropped significantly compared to the previous 30 or 90 days. You should review the asset and decide whether to update it, archive it, or keep it as is.
- Archive: The asset meets the criteria for being retired from active use based on engagement and recency signals.

Note: The recommendation logic factors in a combination of parameters including recency, engagement trends, and configured reminders. The exact criteria may evolve as the feature matures based on customer feedback.

You can sort by any column and use the filters panel to narrow the table to specific subsets — for example, viewing only assets where the asset owner is inactive, or only assets where no description has been added.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Assets > Audit tab > 4. Duplicate assets:
This section identifies assets that share the same name or the same underlying file within a hub, helping you keep your content library clean and avoid confusion caused by redundant content.

Note: Hub names in both duplicate asset tables are clickable. Clicking a hub name opens that hub in a new tab, where duplicates are already highlighted in the product interface.

Duplicate assets — by name

This table lists assets that share the same name within a hub. The table includes the following columns:

- Hub name: Name of the hub containing the duplicate assets. Click to open the hub in a new tab.
- Asset name: The shared name across multiple assets in that hub.
- Assets: Number of assets in that hub sharing this name.

Duplicate assets — by file ID

This table lists assets that share the same underlying file ID within a hub, meaning the same source file has been uploaded multiple times. The table includes the following columns:

- Hub name: Name of the hub containing the duplicate assets. Click to open the hub in a new tab.
- File ID: Unique identifier of the source file.
- Content Center file name: Name of the file as it appears in the Content Center.
- Assets: Number of assets in that hub sharing this file ID.

- Selection from list : You can search for and check specific items (e.g., selecting only the "Battle Cards" attribute). This is best for auditing specific types of content or individual owners.
- Conditional filtering : This advanced option allows you to create rules using various operators, such as Is , Contains , Starts with , Ends with , Is empty , and their opposites. This is particularly useful in the audit dashboard for finding assets with specific naming patterns or missing metadata.
- Filter toggle switch : Use the toggle switch for a filter to quickly turn a specific filter off without losing your selections, allowing you to compare filtered results against the broader dataset.
- Reset filters : Click the Reset icon at the top of the panel to clear all current selections and return to the default dashboard view.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Setup > Site Setup > White-labeling Inclusions and Exclusions:
App white-labeling is different from app customization. App white-labeling is making branding-related modifications to the app so that the customer branding appears on certain screens in the app. Whereas, app customization is making changes to the app features and functionality as per the customer requirements. Mindtickle supports only app white-labeling, and does not support any app customizations around features and functionalities.

The following is provided as part of white-labeling:

- Branding on the iOS App Store and Google Play Store
- Branding in the app for onboarding, Sign Up, and Sign-In flows
- Custom SSO integration for supported SSO implementations

The following is not provided as part of white-labeling:

- Feature/functionality addition/modification requests
- Feature/functionality parity between Mindtickle web, Mindtickle mobile app, and the white-labeled app per prospect/customer requests Note : It will be performed as per the product roadmap.
- Removing Mindtickle Help site links from the app Note : When users click on a Help site link in the app, they are redirected to the Mindtickle Help site, which retains Mindtickle branding and information.
- Branding, layout, and UI changes beyond the ‘Sign In’ flow

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Setup > Site Setup > App Development & Release Timelines:
This section gives a brief overview of the processes and timelines that are followed to successfully white-label the Mindtickle mobile app.
chunks.body: This section gives a brief overview of the processes and timelines that are followed to successfully white-label the Mindtickle mobile app.
chunks.headingPath: Help & Support > Help Center Home > Setup > Site Setup > App Development & Release Timelines
chunks.title: White-label the Mindtickle mobile app

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Setup > Site Setup > App Development & Release Timelines:
1. Mindtickle educates the customer about the mobile app white-labeling process.
2. Customer chooses the distribution method for the app. Mindtickle supports the following three distribution methods for white label apps:
  - Customer manages the distribution via its MDM
  - Customer manages the distribution via iOS App Store/Google Play Store
  - Mindtickle manages the distribution on behalf of the customer via iOS App Store/Google Play Store Note : For more information about the distribution methods, contact your Customer Success Manager (CSM). Based on the distribution method the customer chooses for the app, they must provide the following details to Mindtickle:
  - App name + icon
  - Launch image
  - App screenshots
  - Onboarding screens
  - Sign In page + Landing page Note : The customer must share these details with Mindtickle irrespective of the distribution method they choose.
3. Mindtickle adds the customer’s request to the app white-labeling pipeline. Note : Depending on the size of the pipeline, the white-labeling development process starts in 8-16 weeks.
4. After Mindtickle and the customer sign off on the requirements, it takes 6-8 weeks to develop and test the app.
5. After the app is developed, Mindtickle tests the app in the Mindtickle test environment. For Mindtickle to successfully test the app, the customer must complete the following formalities for the app release:
  - Add Mindtickle test devices to Mobile Device Management (MDM)/Single Sign-On (SSO)
  - Add Mindtickle test users to MDM/SSO This is to ensure that the app does not have any SSO or app sign-in issues during the User Acceptance Testing (UAT) phase. This is applicable to the first release as well as to the regular updates.
6. The customer and Mindtickle perform the UAT of the app in the customer environment.
7. After the UAT is successfully completed and the app receives the final clearance from Mindtickle, the app is released to production.
8. Once the app is published on the app stores, iOS App Store/Google Play Store reviews the app to verify if it complies with the respective policies before releasing it to production. If the app store review is successful, the app goes live on the store within 48 hours. Note :
  - iOS App Store/Google Play Store approval window ranges from 48 hours to 2 weeks.
  - In case the review fails, it will take up to additional 7-10 days for the app to be available in the store.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Setup > Site Setup > Configure update frequency for the app:
Mindtickle uses an automated process (on the back end) to deploy updates for white-labeled mobile apps. You can set the frequency to monthly, bi-monthly, or quarterly. By default, the updates are deployed quarterly. This ensures white-labeled app customers have access to the most recent app features and fixes as quickly as possible.

Note:

- The white label release lags the standard mobile release by a month. This means, there will be a one-month delay between a Mindtickle mobile release and the corresponding white-label app update. This delay is due to the automation process and allows the system to ensure all updates are correctly integrated into the white-labeled app. For example, if you opt for a monthly update frequency for your white-labeled app, all features deployed with the Mindtickle app release for November, are deployed on your white-labeled app in December.
- Currently, the white-label automation process applies only to customers whose white-labeled mobile app releases are managed by Mindtickle via iOS App Store/Google Play Store. For such customers, to enable the white-label automation process, Mindtickle requires a certain set of actions/keys. For more information on the requirements and how to provide them, see White-label automation requirements .
- To configure or change the update frequency, contact your Customer Success Manager (CSM).
- In addition, Mindtickle fixes critical issues and makes updates in the white-labeled app as they occur. Such updates can be forced or optional for the users. For more information, contact your Customer Success Manager (CSM).
- For every white-label release, Mindtickle shares information on the updates with customers two weeks in advance. For more information, see In-app notification for new version of the Mindtickle app .

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Setup > Site Setup > Configure update frequency for the app > White-label automation requirements > Android:
Admins must follow these steps to add the white-label service account as a user on the Play Console:

1. Access the Play Store Console and tap All apps .
2. Navigate to the Users and Permissions section. If you're having trouble finding it, use the Search field within the Play Store Console to find it quickly.
3. Tap Invite new users .
4. In the Email address field, enter mindtickle-app-distribution@api-5633603804680073732-647775.iam.gserviceaccount.com .
5. Under the App permissions tab, tap Add app .
6. Choose your white-labeled app.
7. Tap Apply .
8. The Permissions for {App name} dialog box appears.
9. Select the following permissions:
  1. In the Draft apps category, choose Edit and delete draft apps .
  2. In the Releases category, enable the following:
    1. Release to production, exclude devices, and use Play App Signing.
    2. Release apps to testing tracks.
    3. Manage testing tracks and edit tester lists.
10. Tap Apply . The app permissions are updated.
11. Tap Invite user .
12. On the pop-up, click Send invite . The new user and permissions are updated successfully.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle APIs > Reporting APIs > General best practices:
The following recommendations will help you decide when to use Mindtickle’s reporting API and when to use Mindtickle’s Snowflake integration:

- Use the Snowflake integration if— you have a Snowflake data warehouse. In this case, we recommend using our Snowflake integration, which does not require use of the reporting API and provides direct and secure access to your Mindtickle data. This integration is based on Snowflake’s Secure Data Sharing feature, which lets you can directly fetch and store the data via Snowflake into your data warehouse. For more information, see Use Snowflake to directly access platform data .
- Use the reporting API if— you do not have a Snowflake data warehouse. In this case, we recommend using Mindtickle’s OData-based reporting API to import data into your BI tool, such as Microsoft Excel, Google Sheets, PowerBI, and Tableau. For more information, see Mindtickle reporting API overview .

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle APIs > Reporting APIs > Data limits:
This section provides information on the data limits when querying data for various output formats and querying methods (scripts and BI tools). For datasets larger than the standard limits, it provides recommended solutions to fetch the data.

Important: The following limits are calculated based on 20 fields/columns. If you have more than 20 fields, the limits change accordingly.

Standard limits

| Data query method | Format | Row limit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Python/script | XML | 400,000 |
| CSV | 1 million |  |
| JSON | 400,000 |  |
| JSON compact | 500,000 |  |
| BI tools* and Excel | XML | 200,000 |

* Tested with Power BI only.

Recommendations for larger dataset

- Client-side pagination: If your dataset is larger than the standard limits but less than 5 million, we recommend implementing client-side pagination to fetch up to 5 million records of data. For more information, see Client-side pagination in reporting API .
- LMPI pagination: If you are using the LearnerModulePerformanceIncremental (LMPI) table and your daily dataset is more than 1 million, we recommend implementing pagination for the table. For more information, see Pagination for the LMPI table in reporting API .
- Incremental tables: For the LearnerModulePerformances, CourseObjects, QuickUpdateObjects, and AssessmentObjects tables, if the data size is greater than 1 million, we recommend using their respective incremental tables. The incremental tables are LearnerModulePerformancesIncremental, CourseObjectsIncremental, QuickUpdateObjectsIncremental, and AssessmentObjectsIncremental.
- Download data: If you are using a BI tool and cannot use pagination or incremental tables, we recommend downloading the data in the CSV format to your local space and then connect via the BI tool.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle APIs > Reporting APIs > Query URL guidelines > Format option:
OData’s default output format is XML, but Mindtickle recommends using the CSV format for all Warehouse and non-BI tool users.

Avoid using the XML and JSON formats. If you need the response in JSON, we recommend that you use the JSON compact format instead, because JSON fetches extra metadata information.

- CSV: Smallest data size and quicker to transfer over the network. For example: https://admin.mindtickle.com/Odata.svc/LearnerModulePerformances?$format=csv
- XML: Default output format, but largest data size. For example: https://admin.mindtickle.com/Odata.svc/LearnerModulePerformances?$format=xml
- JSON: Small data size and the most standard format in development. For example: https://admin.mindtickle.com/Odata.svc/LearnerModulePerformances?$format=json
- JSON compact: Serialized JSON, with less data size than the original JSON. For example: https://admin.mindtickle.com/Odata.svc/LearnerModulePerformances?$format=json_compact

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle APIs > Reporting APIs > Query URL guidelines > Filter option:
- Use IDs instead of names in filters. Avoid using filters on the “name” fields, such as SeriesName, ModuleName, ReviewerName on live routes. You can use them on dump routes. Live routes are the tables with near real-time update frequency, while dump routes are the tables with daily update frequency. Each table’s update frequency is mentioned in this help article .
- Use the primary fields provided for each table. Primary fields for each table are the granularity fields, mentioned in the metadata sheet as well as this help article . As these fields are indexed, the query would be much faster. For example, for the SeriesModules table, the primary fields are SeriesId and ModuleId.
- You do not need to apply any filters for the following tables. Always fetch the full data for the Modules , SeriesCollection , SeriesModules , and SeriesModuleSections tables. You need not apply any filters because these tables contain a small amount of data. However, you can apply filters if you are looking for specific records, such as a particular series or module. Also, on incremental fetches, avoid any filter on any timestamp/time fields.
- Apply state-related filters to filter out learners, modules, and series by their current status on the platform. For example, you can filter out deactivated learners and archived or deleted modules. Note: It is recommended to apply state filters for all applicable tables except for LearnerModulePerformancesIncremental . For LearnerModulePerformancesIncremental, the data is fetched incrementally. Filtering out may lead to data discrepancies.
  - Use LearnerState to filter out learners by their current status on the platform. Example values: active, added, deactivated. For example: https://admin.mindtickle.com/Odata.svc/Users?$format=csv&$filter=LearnerState ne 'deactivated'
  - Use ModuleState to filter out learners by their status on the platform. Example values: archived, deleted, draft, published. For example: https://admin.mindtickle.com/Odata.svc/Modules?$format=csv&$filter=ModuleState eq 'published'
  - Use LearnerModuleState to filter out by learners and modules by status in combination. Example values: deactivated, timedout, added, submitted, active, completed, challenge_added. For example: https://admin.mindtickle.com/Odata.svc/CoachingSessions?$format=csv&$filter=LearnerModuleState ne 'deactivated'
  - Use SeriesState to filter out series by their current status on the platform. Example values: deactivated, published. For example: https://admin.mindtickle.com/Odata.svc/SeriesCollection?$format=csv&$filter=SeriesState ne 'deactivated'
- Avoid using the "or", “startswith”, and “endswith” functions in filter options because it results in an unoptimized query. For example, if you query that the Series ID is X or Module ID is Y, it searches for that Series and then Modules too, increasing the data size and the time to fetch the data. If you’re searching for a few modules or series, it’s fine to use. But if you search across parameters, it may fail in fetching the data.

- Avoid using the "or", “startswith”, and “endswith” functions in filter options because it results in an unoptimized query. For example, if you query that the Series ID is X or Module ID is Y, it searches for that Series and then Modules too, increasing the data size and the time to fetch the data. If you’re searching for a few modules or series, it’s fine to use. But if you search across parameters, it may fail in fetching the data.

Note: While using "or" is generally discouraged, it is supported in optimized queries for filtering specific IDs. You can include up to 30 "eq" conditions on indexed fields, such as UserId or ModuleId.Examples:

- Filter by multiple users: .../Users?$format=csv&$filter=UserId eq '1234567890001' or UserId eq '1234567890002' or UserId eq '1234567890003'
- Filter by multiple modules: .../Modules?$format=csv&$filter=ModuleId eq '1234567890001' or ModuleId eq '1234567890002' or ModuleId eq '1234567890003'

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle APIs > Reporting APIs > Query URL guidelines > Select option:
Similar to filters, use the Select option to limit the amount of data and get only relevant and required data. This option fetches only the selected columns and reduces the data size and the time required to fetch the data.

Example:

```text
https://admin.mindtickle.com/Odata.svc/LearnerModulePerformances?$format=csv&$select=ModuleId,UserId,Version,LearnerModuleState,EntityType,HasCompleted,
ModuleName,CompletionStatus,LearnerName,LearnerEmailId,Score,IsCertified
```

Consider the following guidelines for the Select option:

- For all tables, they can use the select option if they’re not interested in fetching data for all columns. Select helps limit the number of columns that are queried.
- The primary fields are selected by default. Primary fields for each table are the granularity fields, mentioned in the metadata sheet as well as this help article .

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle APIs > Reporting APIs > Query URL guidelines > Count option:
Use this option to reduce the number of records that are fetched in your query.

Consider the following guidelines for the Count option:

- For the LearnerModulePerformances table, avoid querying without applying any filters if the records are greater than 100,000, which is the benchmark limit. If the record count is greater than 100,000, apply filters before running the query. If you do not apply any filters, then it is likely to fail in fetching data. At the very least, we recommend applying the LearnerModuleState filter to filter out deactivated records.
- For all tables, the limit of 100,000 records can go up if you narrow down the query using the Select option.
- If you face any 504 timeout or any other issues due to data size, run the following query to check the total number of records that your query will fetch: https://admin.mindtickle.com/Odata.svc/LearnerModulePerformances?$format=json_compact&$inlinecount=allpages&$top=1

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle APIs > Reporting APIs > Query URL guidelines > Expand option:
Avoid using the Expand option to join multiple tables. This makes the querying heavy and data transfer much slower on the network because queries with Expand are unoptimized. Preferably, use the Expand option at the client side rather than the server side (Reporting API).

For example, if you want to join the LearnerModulePerformances and Users tables (https://admin.mindtickle.com/Odata.svc/LearnerModulePerformances?$expand=User&$format=csv), fetch both the tables separately as follows, and then join them using “UserId” in your script:

```text
https://admin.mindtickle.com/Odata.svc/LearnerModulePerformances?$format=csv
```

```text
https://admin.mindtickle.com/Odata.svc/Users?$format=csv
```

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle APIs > Reporting APIs > Query URL guidelines > Orderby option:
Avoid using the Orderby and similar options on the OData query to perform ordering and sorting of data.

When you need to implement client-side pagination, it’s fine to use the Orderby option. Otherwise, use this option at the client side rather than the server side (Reporting API). On the client side, you can use native script functions to sort, group, and perform other aggregate functions on the data set once the raw data is fetched through the Reporting API.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle APIs > Reporting APIs > Sample queries:
This section provides sample queries for all Reporting API tables. You can use these as reference while creating your own queries. It lists optimized and unoptimized queries for each table. Optimized queries are the queries to use, while unoptimized queries are the queries to avoid. We are listing example queries for both to help you understand which queries to use and which to avoid.

Important:

- While creating your queries, Mindtickle recommends that you use the optimized queries for reference, and not the unoptimized queries. Unoptimized queries are listed only for your reference; these are the kind of queries to avoid.
- All the table and column names are case-sensitive and must be provided as shown.

For information on the query URL’s components and its options, see Use OData for Mindtickle Reporting API and OData’s documentation on URL conventions.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Coaching Sessions:
This article explains how learners can self-review coaching sessions assigned to them.

Note: Learners can choose to schedule coaching sessions with the reviewer before starting the self-review.

1. Click the Start self review button on the invitation email.

Note: You can also start the self-review of the assigned coaching sessions from the learner’s dashboard.

2. If you have not performed any self-review of the coaching session, click Start self-review. Alternatively, you can click the + icon in the Sessions section to start a self-review.

3. The coaching session form is displayed. You can preview and download the supporting files (if any) from the Description section. The supporting files will help you understand the purpose of the session before review.

To navigate to the series Modules page, click the series name at the top-left corner of the screen. On the Modules page, you can view other available modules for completion before finishing your self-review.

4. Evaluate yourself based on the parameters provided. Parameters marked with an asterisk are mandatory, and you will have to evaluate yourself based on these before submitting the review.

You can also filter the review forms by section. From Select the Section below to review drop-down, select the required section, and click Apply. This option is visible only if the admin added sections to coaching sessions.

5. Log the duration for which you conducted the session in Session time.

Note: This option is visible only if the admin enables it while creating the coaching session.

6. At any point during the review, click Reset parameters if you wish to reset the inputs you have provided.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Readiness Index (RI) > What is an ideal rep profile?:
The Mindtickle Readiness Index (RI) helps sales leaders and enablement teams identify, create, and configure the ideal rep profile (IRP). Based on the IRP, you can create custom programs and help frontline managers with their coaching plans to address every rep’s skill gaps.

Most sales teams are composed of reps with a wide range of experience, strengths, and weaknesses. So, what makes top performers stand out among the rest? Usually, there are a number of common competencies and selling skills top performers have. Those skills are correlated with success in the field.

As the name suggests, an ideal rep profile (IRP) is a profile of a rep that’s likely to succeed at a given organization. Much like an ICP includes characteristics that make the customer “ideal,” an IRP defines the competencies and skills a rep must have to regularly close deals and meet (or even surpass) quota. In the Readiness Index, you can record your IRP right in the Mindtickle platform so you can work toward closing knowledge gaps – and getting more reps ready to sell.

An IRP provides a way to measure and improve the performance of your sales reps by primarily focusing on the strengths and weaknesses of each sales rep. It helps you fill individuals’ skill gaps and can help you develop smart, targeted training for large groups. By analyzing rep skills and competencies against business metrics, you can better prioritize your sales readiness efforts.

Creating an IRP helps ensure each seller is getting the education, content, and coaching they need to learn and are able to master the skills and competencies that are correlated with sales success. The IRP provides insights related performance improvements that are based on data.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Readiness Index (RI) > What is an ideal rep profile?:
The IRP provides insights related performance improvements that are based on data.

You can create an IRP as follows:

1. Identify sales skills and strengths: Identify the top skills and strengths across your reps, such as product knowledge, objection handling, and value articulation. These top skills are the winning behaviors.
2. Configure competencies:
  - Create tags for these skills. These tags are called competencies in the Readiness Index. For easy deployment, you can make use of our readymade series templates that come with tags (competencies) applied.
  - Assign weights to each competency in such a way that it aligns with your trainers, frontline managers, and ops.
3. Configure benchmarks: Configure the benchmarks that will be used for all IRP and RI calculations. For configuring benchmarks, you need to select the metric and its qualifying value. You can set one or both of the following metrics:
  - Readiness Index: Set the minimum RI score as the benchmark.
  - Business Metric: Select any one business metric and set the qualifying value as the benchmark.

Based on your selected benchmark metrics and their qualifying values, benchmarks are calculated by taking the average of the users who are above the minimum for the selected metrics.

For more information, see Configure Competencies, Benchmarks, and Visualization Settings in Readiness Index.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Readiness Index (RI) > Single vs Multiple IRPs:
The Readiness Index (RI) provides two kinds of ideal rep profile (IRP) setups: single IRP and multiple IRPs.

- Single IRP setup: One IRP with one set of competencies. Applicable for all reps across the organization. In a single IRP setup, the RI home page takes you directly to the RI dashboards ( Track and Correlate tabs). For more information, see Create and Manage a Single Ideal Rep Profile (IRP) .
- Multiple IRP setup: Multiple IRPs with a different set of competencies for each IRP. Each IRP is created by first creating an IR group, where reps are selected through a profile field. Each IRP is applicable for the reps selected for it through an IR group. In a multiple IRP setup, the RI home page shows the RI groups on the home page and clicking a group takes you directly to the RI dashboards ( Track and Correlate tabs). For more information, see Create and Manage Multiple Ideal Rep Profiles (IRPs) .

Important: Once you choose to go with a multiple IRP setup, you cannot switch back to a single IRP setup. However, you can still create only a single IRP within a multiple IRP setup by assigning a particular profile field value to all users.
