Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Readiness Index (RI) > Single vs Multiple IRPs > RI Groups in Multiple IRPs:
In a multiple ideal rep profiles (IRPs) setup, you first create one or more RI groups. Groups are created to bring related reps together and are selected based on profile field values. Each group represents an independent IRP.

While creating your first RI group, you need to select the profile field (such as Designation, Location, or Department) that will be used for creating all of your groups. The same profile field will be used for creating any subsequent groups, but with different profile field values/options. For example, if you’ve created your first RI group with Location as the profile field and India and Europe as the values. The next group that you create can only be based on Location, but with different values — values that you have not selected before for other groups. In this example, India and Europe are the two values already used and cannot be used for any other group unless you remove the values from the group where they are present or delete that group.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Readiness Index (RI):
In Readiness Index (RI), you can choose between creating a single ideal rep profile (IRP) or multiple IRPs. This article provides information on how to create multiple IRPs and manage them.

In a multiple IRP setup, each IRP is created through an RI group, where you can add reps related by role, department, location, and so on through profile fields. Each IRP has its own set of competencies and benchmarks so that you can better understand and track the performance of the reps. For example, if you create an IRP for Account Executives, you can select competencies and set measurement benchmarks that are more relevant for them.

To create multiple IRPs in the Readiness Index, you need to perform the following:

1. Select “multiple IRPs” as your Readiness Index setup
2. Create one or more RI groups Groups are created to bring related reps together. Each group represents an independent IRP. While creating a group, you need to select any one profile field and its values.
3. Configure the group
  - Select competencies (tags)
  - ( Optional — can be configured later) Set benchmarks for this group’s IRP

For a video overview, see Readiness Index - Multiple Rep Profiles (Video Tutorial).

For example, if you create an IRP for Account Executives, you can select competencies and set measurement benchmarks that are more relevant for them.

To create multiple IRPs in the Readiness Index, you need to perform the following:

1. Select “multiple IRPs” as your Readiness Index setup
2. Create one or more RI groups Groups are created to bring related reps together. Each group represents an independent IRP. While creating a group, you need to select any one profile field and its values.
3. Configure the group
  - Select competencies (tags)
  - ( Optional — can be configured later) Set benchmarks for this group’s IRP

For a video overview, see Readiness Index - Multiple Rep Profiles (Video Tutorial).

chunks.title: Create and manage multiple ideal rep profiles (IRPs)

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Readiness Index (RI) > Create multiple IRPs:
1. On the admin site home page, click the Analytics tab.
2. From the Analytics home page, click Readiness Index in the left panel. On the page that appears, click Let’s Get Started to create a new RI configuration.
3. On the Readiness Index Settings page, perform the following and then click Next :
  - Select the multiple IRP setup: To create multiple IRPs, select the second option to create multiple Readiness Index (RI) groups. These groups will represent multiple IRPs. Important: Once you select the “multiple IRP” as the option, you cannot switch back to “single IRP” as your IRP configuration for the organization. However, you can still create just a single IRP within a multiple IRP setup by assigning a particular profile field value to all users.
  - Define profile field: From the dropdown menu, select any one profile field based on which all of your groups will be created. Important: Any subsequent groups that you create can be based on this profile field only, but with different values. You cannot select a different profile field for a different group. On the other hand, you can change the profile field for all groups. If you change the profile field while you already have created some groups, the existing groups with the old profile field will expire and you’ll need to create new groups. For more information, see the Change Profile Field Setting section.
4. You are redirected to the home page. Click Add RI Group to create your first group based on the profile field selected in the previous step. Tip: Click the Settings icon if you want to change your profile field selection.
5. In the Add RI Group pop-up that appears, provide a name for the new group and select one or more profile field values and then click Done . For example, if you are creating an IRP of Account Executives (AEs) and the profile field is set to “Role”, the profile field value will be “Account Executive”. If the AEs in your organization have different roles, you may need to select multiple profile field values to bring all AEs in one group.
6. After the group is created, you are prompted to configure the competencies and benchmarks for the group. For instructions, see Configure Competencies, Benchmarks, and Visualization Settings in Readiness Index .
7. Click Finish to create your group and its IRP.
8. Once a group is created, you cannot immediately view and track data. Data is generated and made available during the next update of RI data. RI is automatically calculated on a weekly basis every Monday at 2 AM UTC. Note: When you edit an existing group’s configuration and save it, all future RI calculations are performed using the new configuration. The new configuration does not affect any previous RI calculations.
9. While you wait for the next scheduled update for RI, you can click Test Configuration to schedule a test RI calculation, which will reflect on your RI dashboards in 3-4 hours. Note: The “Test Configuration” option generates only temporary RI and competency numbers using the updated configuration, with the performance and tag data from the last 3-4 hours. Additionally, you can use this option only once. When you use this option, it will also update the data for the existing active IRPs (RI groups), if any.
10. Use the Add RI Group button, and repeat the steps above, to create more groups/IRPs as needed.
11. Once you have created multiple groups to track multiple IRPs, you can view quick stats for each on your Readiness Index home page.
12. Click a group to track the IRP performance for the reps included in the group through the Track and Correlate tabs.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Readiness Index (RI) > Manage IRPs:
After you have created your ideal rep profiles (IRPs) based on Readiness Index (RI) groups, you can perform the following actions on your active RI groups from the RI home page. These actions are also available on each group’s page.

Note: You must have the "Config SCI" permission to perform the actions described in this section.

- Rename the group
- Change profile field value of the group
- Delete the group

Additionally, from Readiness Index Settings, you can also change the profile field based on which your groups were created.

Important: When you change the profile field, it is an RI configuration level change and applies for your entire setup of groups. Old groups created with the previous profile field will expire. New groups that you create will be based on the updated profile field.

This section covers each action in detail.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Readiness Index (RI) > Manage IRPs > Change Profile Field Settings:
1. On the RI home page, click the settings icon in the upper-right corner.
2. On the Readiness Index Settings pop-up that appears, change the profile field using the dropdown menu and then click Next .
3. On the Important Note message, click Confirm to proceed with the profile field change. Note: When you confirm this change, your active RI groups are moved to the Expiring RI Groups section on the RI home page. The expiring groups cannot be accessed and are permanently deleted either during the next scheduled update of RI configuration, or when you run a “Test Configuration” on new groups.
4. On clicking Confirm , you are provided with two options:
  - Select Yes if you want to copy the configuration (tag contribution, visualization, and benchmarks) of any one of the RI groups to use it to create your first RI based on the new profile field. If you select this option, you need to create a new group with copied configuration as described in the following steps.
  - Select No if you do not want to retain the configuration of previous groups. If you select this option and click Confirm , your profile field is successfully updated.
5. If you select Yes , you need to select any one group to copy its configuration. Click Confirm to proceed with creating a new group based on the new profile field along with the copied configuration of the previous group.
6. On the RI group of existing configuration pop-up that appears, provide a name for the group and select the values based on the new profile field. Click Save .
7. The new group is created and you are prompted to configure the competencies and benchmarks for the group. For instructions, see Configure Competencies, Benchmarks, and Visualization Settings in Readiness Index .
8. Once the group is configured, it appears under the Active RI Groups section on the RI home page. The groups that were created with the previous profile field are moved to the Expiring RI Groups section. The expiring groups cannot be accessed and are permanently deleted either during the next scheduled update of the RI configuration or when you run a “Test Configuration” on a new group.
9. You can permanently delete the expiring RI groups. To delete a group, click the arrow next to “RI Group” and click Delete in the dropdown.
10. Use the Add RI Group button to create more groups/IRPs based on the new profile field.

To create a single IRP in the Readiness Index, you need to perform the following:

- Select “single IRP” as your Readiness Index setup
- Configure the competencies, benchmarks, and visualization settings

Perform the following steps to create one ideal rep profiles (IRP) for across the organization:

1. On the admin site home page, click the Analytics tab.
2. From the Analytics home page, click Readiness Index in the left panel. On the page that appears, click Let’s Get Started to create a new RI configuration.
3. On the Readiness Index Settings page, select the first option to create a single IRP and then click Done .
4. You are redirected to the Settings page to configure competencies, benchmarks, and visualization settings. For instructions, see Configure Competencies, Benchmarks, and Visualization Settings in Readiness Index .
5. Once the settings are configured, your IRP is configured, but you cannot immediately view and track data. Data is generated and made available during the next update of RI data. RI is automatically calculated on a weekly basis every Monday at 2 AM UTC.
6. While you wait for the next scheduled update for RI, you can click Test Configuration to schedule a test RI calculation, which will reflect on your RI dashboards in 3-4 hours. Note: The “Test Configuration” option generates only temporary RI and competency numbers using the updated configuration, with the performance and tag data from the last 3-4 hours. Additionally, you can use this option only once.
7. Once the data is ready and available, you can track the IRP performance for the reps through the Track and Correlate tabs.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Series:
You can schedule the archival of a module for a later date. If you do this, Mindtickle will keep track of all the modules and automatically remove them from the platform when not required, thus giving learners access to only those modules that are required.

Note: Scheduling auto-archival of a module is a beta feature. To enable it for your organization, contact your Customer Success Manager (CSM) or Mindtickle Support.

To schedule the auto-archival of a module on a particular date:

1. Navigate to the module you want to set the archival date, click the menu icon and select Schedule archive .
2. In the Schedule archive pop-up, click on the calendar widget.
3. From the calendar widget, select the date you want to schedule the archive. The module will be automatically archived at 5:30 AM (admin’s system timezone) on the selected date.
4. By default, the admin who created the module and the admin scheduling its archival will receive email notifications on the 1st and 15th of every month. These emails inform them about all the scheduled archives planned over the next 20 days.
5. Select the Send notification emails to series collaborators checkbox to include all series collaborators in the notification receiver’s list. Note: If a particular archive is scheduled to happen before the next email is triggered, the details are not included in that email. This is helpful when you want to update or cancel the scheduled archival.
6. Click Schedule archive . You will receive a confirmation message once the archival is scheduled successfully.

The scheduled for archival icon highlights a module that is scheduled for archival at a later date. Hover over the icon to learn more about the details of the scheduled archival.You can update or cancel a scheduled archival.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Content Center:
The Content Center serves as a centralized collaborative space for content governance. It is empty when deployed for the first time. However, the files appear in the Content Center once you add content.

If you are new to the Mindtickle platform, the Customer Success Manager (CSM) helps you copy all the data onto the Content Center as part of the initial onboarding and setup. If you are an existing user who enables the Content Center and wishes to copy content from the Mindtickle library to the Content Center, contact your CSM to help copy the content.

Note: As part of the process of copying the content, scripts are run that automatically transfer the content. After executing the scripts, any new series or modules can leverage the copied content from the Content Center. However, the existing series or modules need to be recreated and republished to leverage the centralized governance of content.

The sections below explain how admins can copy content from the following sources to the Content Center:

- External cloud storage system
- Mindtickle library
- Content Center of a Mindtickle admin site

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Content Center > Copy from Mindtickle library:
You can copy content from the Mindtickle library to Content Center. The script copies all the tags applied to the files in the Mindtickle library to Content Center.

Provide the following inputs to your Customer Success Manager (CSM):

- File Type (optional): Specify the file types the script needs to copy. If not specified, the script copies all the file types supported by Content Center.
- Ignore Duplicates :
  - If enabled : The script copies only the latest modified file among the files with the same name and file type. For example, if there are two files with the same name as Pricing, the script copies the Pricing file once.
  - If disabled : The script copies all the files and suffixes the same name files with numbers. For example, if there are two files with the same name as Budget, the script copies the file twice as Budget and Budget(1).

Note: By default, the Ignore Duplicates setting is disabled.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle APIs > Call AI API:
The Call AI API uses the OAuth 2.0 protocol to ensure secure, authorized access to your conversation intelligence data. Before making any API requests, you must generate a time-limited access token using the credentials provided by Mindtickle.

This article outlines the lifecycle of these tokens: generating an authorization code, exchanging it for an access token, and refreshing that token when it expires.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle APIs > Call AI API > Generate access token > I. Get authorization code:
First, you must obtain a temporary authorization code. Execute this query once per client.

Request URL

```
POST /get-authorisation-grant
```

Request parameters

```json

{
  "client_id": "<client_id>",
  "user_id": "<user_id>",
  "tenant_id": "<tenant_id>"
}
```

Response

```json

{
  "status": 200,
  "grant_type": "authorization_code",
  "code": "<code>"
}
```

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle APIs > Call AI API > Generate access token > II. Generate access token:
Exchange the authorization code for your Bearer token and a refresh token.

Request URL

```
POST /token
```

Request parameters

```json

{
  "client_id": "<client_id>",
  "client_secret": "<your_client_secret>",
  "grant_type": "authorization_code",
  "code": "<code>"
}
```

Response

```json

{
  "status": 200,
  "access_token": "<your_access_token>",
  "refresh_token": "<your_refresh_token>",
  "token_type": "Bearer",
  "expires_in": "<time>"
}
```

- Grant type: Must be set to authorization_code for this step.
- TTL (Time To Live):
  - access_token : Valid for 1 day .
  - refresh_token : Valid for 365 days .
- Expiration behavior: When the access_token expires (API calls return a 404 error), proceed to Step III .
chunks.body:
Exchange the authorization code for your Bearer token and a refresh token.

Request URL

```
POST /token
```

Request parameters

```json

{
  "client_id": "<client_id>",
  "client_secret": "<your_client_secret>",
  "grant_type": "authorization_code",
  "code": "<code>"
}
```

Response

```json

{
  "status": 200,
  "access_token": "<your_access_token>",
  "refresh_token": "<your_refresh_token>",
  "token_type": "Bearer",
  "expires_in": "<time>"
}
```

- Grant type: Must be set to authorization_code for this step.
- TTL (Time To Live):
  - access_token : Valid for 1 day .
  - refresh_token : Valid for 365 days .
- Expiration behavior: When the access_token expires (API calls return a 404 error), proceed to Step III .

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Assets:
This article provides an overview of Asset Hub analytics.

Asset Hub analytics gives admins and product marketing teams visibility into how sales content is performing — from how assets are shared and engaged with, to the revenue they influence, to the overall health of your content library.

Before exploring the dashboards, it is helpful to understand the two types of engagement tracked across Asset Hub analytics:

- Internal engagement: Engagement on assets within your organization, such as viewing, downloading, and sharing.
- External engagement: Engagement on assets that a rep has shared with customers or prospects, such as viewing and downloading. External engagement reflects activity by those external recipients on the shared assets.

Note: Asset Hub is a paid feature. For more information, contact your Customer Success Manager (CSM).

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Assets > Filter and download data:
Each dashboard includes filters to help you focus on the data most relevant to you. You can filter by hub, attribute category, specific attribute, asset owner, interaction source, user group, username, and user status. Applying a filter updates all widgets on the dashboard simultaneously.

You can export data from any widget directly, without any additional steps:

All widgets across Asset Hub analytics dashboards support a common set of actions.

- On chart widgets, you can toggle individual metrics on or off using the legend, hover over data points to view detailed tooltips, and click a data point to filter the entire dashboard by that selection — with all widgets updating simultaneously.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Checklist > Checklist settings > General > Configure the checklist as view-only for learners:
You can allow learners to view the checklist without marking its tasks as complete.

Note:

- View-only checklists are available only on the web and not in the Mindtickle mobile app.
- This feature must be enabled for your organization. Contact your CSM or Mindtickle Support to enable it.
- Use a view-only checklist only when checklist tasks are completed through an API. Otherwise, learners cannot complete the view-only checklist manually and cannot progress to the next module in a sequentially locked series.

1. In the General section, turn on View only Checklist for learners . By default, this setting is turned off.
2. When this setting is enabled, learners can open and view the checklist tasks, but they cannot mark them as complete. The Mark complete option is disabled for learners. To allow learners to mark checklist tasks as complete, ensure the View only Checklist for learners setting is off. Note:

- The view-only checklist is available only on the web.
- Avoid enabling View only Checklist for learners for checklist modules in a sequentially locked series. Since learners cannot mark checklist items as complete, the checklist can remain incomplete, preventing them from progressing to the next module.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Checklist > Publish:
You can invite learners to a checklist only if it is published. To publish a checklist:

1. Navigate to the Publish tab of the checklist creation canvas.
2. If there are any pending items, a message is displayed on the screen. Click the link in the message to go to the To-Do list. Alternatively, click To-Do to display the list of pending items. Click the link in the list to navigate to the task.
3. Ensure there are no pending items in the To-Do list, navigate to the Publish tab, and click Publish now . The checklist is published.

Note: It is possible to modify a published checklist and republish it. Apart from adding/removing/updating tasks and sections, you can also modify its settings under the General, Scoring, and Due date & emails tabs. You can track the Publish History of the checklist under the Publish tab. For more information on inviting learners to updated checklist versions, see Version upgrade.

4. Navigate to the Invite & Track tab to invite learners to the checklist.

5. Click Invite learners to start inviting learners to the checklist module.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Content Center > How permission in Content Center ensures content governance?:
Suppose a product (Mindtickle) has 6 streams, and Product Marketing Managers (PMMs) maintain the content for each of these streams. It becomes cumbersome to create separate file-level permissions for each PMM across hundreds of files among all 6 streams and for every newly added file.

Instead, you can create 6 separate folders for each product stream. Add or move files corresponding to different streams to their respective folders and provide PMMs with access to folders related to their stream. This ensures easy and robust content governance within your organization.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Content Center > Additional points to consider:
1. The collaborators added in the parent folder in Content Center inherit the same permissions in all its subfolders. However, if you remove a collaborator from a subfolder, that person cannot access files and folders within the subfolder and only access files and folders under the parent folder. Similarly, if you add a collaborator only to a subfolder, that person can access the files and folders within the subfolder but not other files and folders within the parent folder.

Note: A collaborator added to the root folder of Content Center can access all the files and folders within Content Center. You cannot remove such a collaborator from any folder or file.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Content Center > Additional points to consider:
- Suppose a World folder exists at the root (base) of Content Center, and A is a collaborator to the World folder. It means that A has access to all the files and folders within the World folder.
- The World folder has 2 subfolders ( India and United States ). A inherits access to both the subfolders within the World folder. However, if you add B as a collaborator only to the United States folder, then B cannot access the files and folder under the India folder and only access the files and folders within United States.
- The United States folder has 3 subfolders ( California , Texas , and Washington ) and one file ( Alaska .doc ).
  - Since A and B are collaborators to the United States folder, they inherit access to all the subfolders and files within it. However, if you remove B from the California folder and add C as a collaborator, only A and C can access the files and folders within the California folder ( Los Angeles.doc , Sacramento.pdf , and San Jose.jpg ). If you add D as a collaborator only to San Jose.jpg, then A, C (from inherited access), and D can access the San Jose.jpg file.
  - A and B can access the Texas, Washington folders and Alaska.doc file.

2. If you move a file or folder from one place to another within Content Center:

- Any collaborator added explicitly to that file or folder remains.
- The collaborator added to the root folder of Content Center remains.
- The inherited collaborators from the current parent folder get replaced with those from the new parent folder hierarchy.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > Integrations > How the Integration Works?:
The integration works as follows:

1. RingCentral records the call and sends the audio file to Call AI.

2. Call AI processes the audio file and makes it available on your Call AI interface.

3. Call AI generates useful insights, themes, transcript and statistics for the call recording. You can perform different actions such as send a private message, take notes and share the recording with peers and customers. For more information, see Call Recording Details.

Note:

- Call AI displays the phone number of the prospect as the recording name.
- If the name and email address of a participant is not available in the RingCentral recording, Call AI displays the dialer number as the participant’s name. You can edit the participant's name on the recording details page.
- If you delete a recorded call in RingCentral, the recording remains in Call AI. For more information about deleting such a recording from the Call AI interface, see Delete a Call Recording .

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > Integrations > Steps to Integrate Call AI With RingCentral:
To set up Call AI integration with RingCentral, follow the below steps:

Note: Only the admin of RingCentral can integrate the RingCentral account with Call AI.

1. Log in to the Admin Site Homepage.

2. From the left panel, click Account >Settings> Call AI > Integrations.

3. Click RingCentral > Enable.

4. Sign in to your RingCentral account.

5. Click Authorize to give permission to Mindtickle to access information about your calls.

Call AI is now successfully integrated with RingCentral.

6. Record your call using RingCentral.

7. Once your call finishes, its recording appears in the recording list on the Call AI interface approximately in an hour. There might be a delay in recording if there is an issue from RingCentral’s end. In that case, we recommend waiting for up to 2 hours. You can use Call AI’s powerful and guided search to quickly look for a specific recording or apply filters to look at RingCentral dialer calls. For information about the insights available for a call recording, see Call Recording Details.

Note:

- Call AI does not fetch recordings that have a duration of less than 10 seconds.
- Call AI does not import incoming calls on your RingCentral number.
- Call AI does not support RingCentral call transfer and conference.
- Call AI keeps only the first recording in case a rep starts and stops recording multiple times during a call.
- Call AI does not capture shared screen in RingCentral recordings.
- Call AI ignores recordings of non-Call AI users.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Asset Hub > Share assets:
You need to click Authorize to authorize your email address for the first time, which is detailed below.

Use Mindtickle admin email: Select the Continue with admin@mindtickle.com option to send the email from the Mindtickle admin email address. This option does not require email authorization.

Authorize your official email:

You need to authorize your email address for the first time. Follow the below steps:

- Click Authorize to proceed .
- Sign in to your email account. Note : If you are using Outlook, we recommend using Single Sign-On (SSO) to sign in to your account. Additionally, Asset Hub does not support Yahoo and Zoho email services.
- Read carefully and grant permission to Mindtickle to access your email account. Click Allow to proceed.

Once authorized, Asset Hub saves your email address and automatically populates it whenever you share assets via email.Note: If your organization uses a different email client such as Microsoft Office 365, see Authorize emails to share assets.

- Send to : Enter the recipient’s email address. A recipient is a person to whom you send an email. Once you enter the email address, you can choose from the following 2 options:
  - Send separate emails to each recipient (recommended): This option helps track each recipient's activity.
  - Send one email to all recipients : This option does not allow you to track each recipient’s activity separately.

Note: You can send an email to a maximum of 25 recipients at a time.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Asset Hub > Share assets:
- Subject : Enter the subject line of the email. An email subject line is the first text recipients see after the sender's name when an email reaches their inbox.
- Email message : Enter the message you want to send to the recipients. It is a freeform text field where you can insert as much text as you want and add supporting links.
- Email signature : Enter a default signature for all outgoing emails to include your name, contact information, or brand image. It helps the recipients to contact you if they want to discuss further.
- Recipient activity notifications : Turn on the setting if you want to be notified via an email whenever a recipient interacts with the shared assets. It has the following 2 options:
  - Notify when the recipient engages with the assets along with the engagement summary
  - Notify me when the recipient shares assets with their peers
  - Notify when a recipient is active
- Reminder notifications : Turn on the setting if you want to set an email reminder to check the engagement on shared assets. It has the following 3 options:
  - Remind to check engagement data
  - Remind only if there is no activity
- Allow download : Turn on the setting if you want recipients to download the shared assets to their local machine. The option to download is unavailable for embedded assets (for example, youtube video embedded link).
- Access expiration : Configure the setting if you want the recipient’s access to expire for the shared assets after the set time (for example, renewals, contracts, licenses). It ensures that the recipients always access the latest and most relevant content.
- Add internal notes (optional): Use the section as your personal notetaker to jot down the ideas or thoughts about sharing the assets. It will help you remember why you shared these assets with the customer or prospect in the later stages of the sales cycle.
- Email preview : View a glimpse of the entire email before sending it to the customers or prospects. It helps correct any apparent mistakes upfront and ensures the quality of your emails.

- Click the Share button available on the upper-right corner of the page.

- Enter the email addresses of the recipients and type the Email message . Click Share .

Once the asset is shared successfully, a confirmation message displays on the screen, and the first prospect or customer receives the following email. The email provides details about the new recipients and the original sender of the asset. Also, a separate tracking link for the same assets gets created, and their activities are tracked separately.

Additionally, the recipients of the asset can view the list of recipients with whom the asset is shared.

Also, as a sales rep, if you want to share assets with a large number of customers or prospects (for example, a research report on industry standards), you can create a link and share assets via that link. For more information, see Share assets via link.

For information on how to track the engagement of customers and prospects on the shared assets, see View engagement on shared assets.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Asset Hub:
This article explains how reps can view and track the engagement of customers and prospects on shared assets. It also explains how the engagement is tracked when the assets or links are shared with recipients (original receiver of the asset or link) and other recipients (with whom the assets are further shared by the original receiver).

Tracking asset engagement lets you understand which aspects of the product or service are valuable or intriguing to the customer or prospect. The engagement data is also critical to the Product Marketing and Enablement teams in your organization who create and manage such assets. They can understand which assets are working with customers and which are not.

A set of recipients with whom you have shared the assets forms an interaction. Each interaction has a unique link and shows the engagement data of recipients. A recipient of one interaction can view the name and email addresses of other recipients in the same interaction. Additionally, you can view the shared assets and track if they are re-shared and viewed by other prospects or peers.

For a video overview of viewing and tracking the engagement of customers and prospects on the shared assets, see Track asset engagement.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Asset Hub > Access the Interactions page:
You can view the engagement on shared assets from the Interactions page on the Assets page.

On the page that appears, you can view a list of all the interactions on the shared assets with the customers and prospects.

The following details are available for every interaction:

- Interaction name
- Indication whether you have shared the assets via email, link. Link is also used when assets were shared via room (Digital Sales Room/DSR).
- Recipient list
- Asset list
- Last time when the recipients interacted with the shared assets. If a recipient is actively viewing the shared assets, the tracking data updates once the recipient’s viewing session ends.
- Consolidated engagement data of all the recipients in an interaction on the shared assets such as the total number of views, time spent, downloads, and email opened.

Note: If you notice icon next to an asset in the interaction list, it indicates that the asset is unavailable to the recipients. The admin or asset owner might have deleted, archived or disabled the asset for external usage.

Click the More option against an interaction to perform the following actions:

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Asset Hub > Access the Interactions page:
- Preview assets : It generates a preview of the shared assets in the interaction without impacting the tracking data of the interaction and assets.
- Mark as seen : It marks the interaction as read.
- Turn on notifications : It enables the email notifications (recipient activity and reminder notifications) for the interaction henceforth. You can turn them ON from the same option whenever required.
- Edit interaction : It allows you to modify the interaction settings such as recipient activity notification, reminder notification, allow download, and access expiration. For more information on these settings, see Share Assets via Email and Share Assets via Link .
- Revoke access : It disables the recipient's access to the shared assets henceforth. You can allow access again from the same option whenever required. When you allow access again, only those recipients receive an email notification whose email addresses you have included while sharing the assets.

- Delete interaction : It deletes the interaction. Once deleted, recipients can no longer access the shared assets.

Note: These options are disabled for assets shared via room (Digital Sales Room/DSR).

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Asset Hub > Search, sort, and filter interactions:
Use the Search bar at the top to quickly find a specific interaction by its name, recipient name or email address, asset name, or email message.

Make the interaction list more readable by sorting them by:

- Recently sent (default)
- Recent activity

You can also apply the following filters to view a specific list of interactions:

- Recipient
- Date range (current week, last week, current month, current quarter, or select a custom date)
- Share type ( Shared via email , Shared via link )

Note:

- The number next to the Interactions page indicates the number of interactions you have not yet viewed. Click Mark all as seen in the upper-right corner to mark all the interactions as read.
- The number next to the interactions heading indicates the total number of interactions you have shared with the customers and prospects.

For example, in the screenshot below, the number 3 next to the Interactions page indicates that there are 3 unseen interactions. The number 5 next to the interactions heading indicates that there are a total of 5 interactions through which you have shared assets with the customers or prospects.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Asset Hub > Interaction details > Activity history:
View all the activities on an interaction. It helps you track what the customer or prospect is interested in or intrigued by and thereby decide the next steps to take the deal forward. You can also compare the previous activities of recipients and relate the value of sharing assets with the deal progression.

From the left navigation panel, you can select whether you want to view the activity history for each recipient individually or a consolidated view of all the recipients in the interaction. In both the cases, you can view the following details:

- The time when the customer or prospect received the email or link with the assets attached
- Recipient details such as email address, location, internet browser, and device using which the recipient interacted (open email or link, view or download assets)
- Details of customers or prospects with whom the asset is re-shared
- The Time spent on each asset by a recipient

Note:

- Recipient details are available only when the recipient opens the email or link, interacts with the asset, gives consent and accepts the privacy policy for tracking the engagement data.
- The number next to the Activity history tab indicates the number of new activities by recipients since you last opened the tab.

- Recipient details are shown as anonymous if the recipient does not give consent and accepts the privacy policy for tracking the engagement data.

You can also compare the previous activities of recipients and relate the value of sharing assets with the deal progression.

From the left navigation panel, you can select whether you want to view the activity history for each recipient individually or a consolidated view of all the recipients in the interaction. In both the cases, you can view the following details:

- The time when the customer or prospect received the email or link with the assets attached
- Recipient details such as email address, location, internet browser, and device using which the recipient interacted (open email or link, view or download assets)
- Details of customers or prospects with whom the asset is re-shared
- The Time spent on each asset by a recipient

Note:

- Recipient details are available only when the recipient opens the email or link, interacts with the asset, gives consent and accepts the privacy policy for tracking the engagement data.
- The number next to the Activity history tab indicates the number of new activities by recipients since you last opened the tab.

- Recipient details are shown as anonymous if the recipient does not give consent and accepts the privacy policy for tracking the engagement data.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Asset Hub > DSR interactions:
Mindtickle's deep integration between Asset Hub and Digital Sales Rooms (DSRs) allows improved tracking and reporting for DSR-specific interactions. It also enables proper and consistent attribution of prospect activity in both Asset Hub and DSRs. This section provides information on how to view prospect engagement data on assets shared to DSRs — either shared from the Assets page using the Share via room feature or uploaded to rooms from the DSR side.

From the Assets → Interactions page, click any interaction for assets shared to DSRs. Such interactions are prefixed with "DSR:" in the title for easy identification.

On the interaction page that opens, you can view engagement data for all prospects/contacts who engaged with the shared asset, along with overall engagement for all.

Click on any prospect to view details on the assets they have engaged with and the engagement activity history.

For DSR-related interactions, you cannot perform certain actions on the interaction page as these actions are not relevant. The actions are: Preview assets, copy shareable link, turn on notifications, edit interaction, revoke access, preview assets, and delete interaction.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Asset Hub > Admin > Email digest:
The Email digest setting under Account → Settings → Assets → Email digest allows admins to configure automated emails that summarize new or updated assets across hubs and new hubs.

The email digest is sent to users at a customizable email frequency and delivery time, and can be configured to exclude specific user groups. Only users with access to hubs that had updates during the selected frequency will receive the digest. Users in excluded groups won’t receive it, regardless of their hub access.

Admins can enable or disable the email digest, define the audience (by excluding groups), set the frequency and delivery time, and preview or edit the email template.

The following settings are available:

1. Send email digest to users

Use the toggle to enable or disable the asset digest email.

- When disabled , no users in the organization will receive the email.
- When enabled , only eligible users (based on hub access and group exclusions) will receive it.

2. Set frequency

Choose how often and when the email digest should be sent.

- Repeat every X weeks/months : Enter a value between 1 and 99 to set the interval.
- Cadence : Choose whether the digest should repeat weekly or monthly (e.g., every 2 weeks or every 3 months).
- Day and time : Select the specific day and time to send the email. Users will receive the email in their local time zone . Example: If the digest is scheduled for Monday at 9:00 AM, users in India will receive it at 9:00 AM IST on Monday.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Asset Hub > Admin > Email digest:
- Day and time : Select the specific day and time to send the email. Users will receive the email in their local time zone . Example: If the digest is scheduled for Monday at 9:00 AM, users in India will receive it at 9:00 AM IST on Monday.

Important: If you change the frequency (e.g., from weekly to monthly), make sure to update the email template to reflect the new frequency. For example, if the subject line or email body says “Weekly digest,” update it to say “Monthly digest” as needed.

3. Exclude groups

Control who receives the email digest by excluding specific user groups. You cannot exclude individual users directly, but excluding groups lets you prevent their members from receiving the email digest.

Select the Exclude groups checkbox and choose one or more groups to exclude. With this option, users in any excluded group won’t receive the email digest — irrespective of their membership in other (non-excluded) groups. To explain further:

- Group-based exclusion : Users who belong to the excluded groups will not receive the email digest.
- Mixed group membership : If a user belongs to both excluded and non-excluded groups, they will still not receive the digest.This is because exclusion takes priority over other group memberships.

Note:

- If no groups are excluded, the digest is sent to users who have access to at least one hub , and only if there are new or updated assets in the hubs they can access.
- If a user is removed from an excluded group, they will start receiving the digest.
- If a new user is added to an excluded group, they will stop receiving the digest.

4. Preview and edit template

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Asset Hub > Admin > Consent and privacy policy > Consent:
The General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) mandates a transparent and value-driven approach to the data exchange between organizations and customers or prospects. One of the main components of GDPR is privacy. Hence, it is essential to know exactly what data you need from your customers or prospects and only collect that.

Whenever you share an asset externally with the customers or prospects, Asset Hub tracks the engagement data, such as the time spent on the asset and the number of views. Before initiating the tracking, GDPR laws require consent from the recipients of the assets in the European Union (EU) region. It also mandates the privacy policy of your company or Mindtickle to appear when requesting the consent. The recipients have an option to accept or decline the consent.

You can configure to request consent from the recipients. According to the GDPR guidelines, it is mandatory to request consent from all the recipients in the EU region. However, you can choose to request consent from all geographies.

Note: Mindtickle platform supports 19 languages. The recipients can view the consent and interface in the preferred language.

You can also preview the consent request to see exactly what data the Asset Hub collects from the recipients.

Select consent type from the following options:

- Request consent from recipients in EU region only
- Request consent from recipients in all geographies

Note: Recipient tracking details are visible to reps only if a recipient gives consent and accepts the privacy policy for tracking the engagement data.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Asset Hub > Admin > Consent and privacy policy > Privacy policy:
Asset Hub ensures that the privacy policy is visible to the recipients before they interact with the shared assets. You can choose which privacy policy you would prefer to display:

- Mindtickle privacy policy
- Your company’s privacy policy

1. Click the Privacy Policy tab.

2. Select at least one privacy policy from the following options:

- Mindtickle privacy policy : Click View to see the content.
- Your privacy policy:
  - Enter a privacy policy name. The name you set is visible to the recipients on the consent request pop-up.
  - Paste a link for the privacy policy or enter the text manually.

Note: If you choose to only display your privacy policy, ensure that it covers the following points:

1. Type of information collected : Active time spent on the website, time spent on each document page, and geographic location.
2. Method of collecting the information : Cookies or similar technologies used to track the user (customer or prospect) activity.
3. The purpose of collecting the information : Effective conversations, understand the engagement better, and serve personalized interactions based on the activity history.

Click Save Changes to proceed.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Managers and Reviewers > Team analytics:
The Readiness Index (RI) is a unified metric that, by quantifying the capabilities of sales reps, measures their readiness to achieve business outcomes.

The Readiness Index generates the RI score for the sales reps reporting to a manager. It performs correlations between the RI score and performance of those sales reps across teams and regions to identify how RI impacts business metrics.

RI highlights the competencies that separate your top sales reps from the ones that need improvement. It also highlights the competencies of your teams and user segments so that you can prioritize and personalize the readiness programs better.

Note: Readiness Index (RI) data is not real-time. The data gets updated weekly — every Monday at 2 AM UTC. During the weekly data update, associated user hierarchies, competency performance data, and RI scores also get updated. For example, if there were any changes to your user hierarchies in the days between the last RI update and the upcoming update, the changes will reflect in RI after the next weekly update.

Note: You can view Readiness Index (RI) data only if your admin has properly configured RI from the admin site. If you are not able to view any data in Readiness Index or proper and accurate data for your team, please contact your admin to ensure that it is configured correctly for your team.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Managers and Reviewers > Team analytics > RI Dashboards > Correlate Tab:
Through the Correlate tab in RI, you can view a correlation of your business metrics (such as quota attainment) with the Readiness Index in a quadrant chart. It helps you identify user cohorts and provides action-oriented insights. Sales teams can correlate skill, development, and knowledge with business outcomes, such as quota achievement, win rates, and sales cycle.

The quadrant chart shows all individual sales reps in your team in the following four quadrants or categories:

- Best Performers: Reps with high RI and sales.
- Capability Ready: Reps with high RI but low sales performance.
- Need Improvement: Reps with low RI and sales.
- Outliers: Reps with high sales but low RI.

To view the correlation and analyze the impact of the Readiness Index (RI) on your business metrics, Mindtickle requires your business metrics data. Your admin can either manually upload business metrics into Mindtickle or sync your Salesforce business metrics by integrating with Salesforce. You can also make use of both business metrics (manually uploaded and synced with Salesforce) simultaneously.

For more information, see Correlate Tab in Readiness Index for Managers.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Managers and Reviewers > Team analytics > RI Dashboards > Reports Tab:
The Reports tab provides detailed reports related to Readiness Index (RI) in the following tabs:

- Key competencies: Provides data on the competencies you have configured for Readiness Index. For each competency, you can view its average score, any change in the score, and the competency benchmark score.
- Teams: Provides data on the managers and their teams (as configured in the user-to-user hierarchy) in your organization. For each manager, you can view the total number of members in their team and the team’s average RI score.

- User distribution: Provides data on the users (learners) in your organization. For each user, you can view their manager’s name and the RI score.

For more information, see Reports Tab in Readiness Index for Managers.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Managers and Reviewers > Team analytics > Ideal Rep Profiles and Benchmarks:
The Readiness Index (RI) provides a unique feature of the ideal rep profile (IRP) through which you can correlate skills and behaviors with sales success. The IRP consists of the competencies that are important to your team or organization and the ideal score that should be achieved in the selected competencies (competency benchmark).

RI provides two kinds of IRP setups: single IRP and multiple IRPs.

- Single IRP setup: One IRP with one set of competencies. Applicable for all reps across the organization.
- Multiple IRP setup: Multiple IRPs with a different set of competencies for each IRP. Each IRP is created by first creating an IR group, where reps are selected through a profile field. Each IRP is applicable for the reps selected in the IR group.

Important: Your IRP setup is defined by your admin and cannot be changed by you. If you are not seeing proper and accurate data for your team, please contact your admin to configure the IRP for your team.

For more information, see the Ideal Rep Profiles in Readiness Index article for admins.

There are two benchmarks in Readiness Index (RI):

- Competency benchmark
- RI benchmark

When you configure benchmarks for your competencies (competency benchmark), you get an individual benchmark score for each competency. Based on this, you get the aggregated benchmark for the overall Readiness Index (RI benchmark). These become your benchmarks for ideal rep behaviors and revenue performance.

For more information, see the Competency and RI Benchmarks in Readiness Index article for admins.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > User Management > Users and Groups:
The admins can impersonate a user from the Users page. This feature provides the admins with the site owner role, the ability to log in as any selected user to troubleshoot the user’s issues in a self-service format. Self service enables admins to view the learner's UI experience first-hand and troubleshoot their issues efficiently.

Note:

- A new permission LEARNER_IMPERSONATION is available for the site owner role by default.
- Admins can impersonate the users in the Active state only.
- When an admin impersonates a learner and views the ILT Sessions page, the calendar shows the session schedules only in the admin’s system time zone.

This article explains the steps to impersonate a user.

1. Sign in to the admin site.
2. On the left navigation bar, click Users and select Users .
3. On the Users page, click the More options icon next to the user you want to impersonate.
4. Click Impersonate user .
5. A pop-up with the following warning is displayed:
6. When impersonating a user, please note the following:

- Once you accept to sign in as the user, you will be signed out of the admin site and navigated to the learning site.
- Each impersonation session lasts only 30 minutes.
- If you have other admin tabs open, you will not be able to perform any action on them once the impersonation starts. Thus, it's recommended that you close all other admin site tabs.

7. To continue impersonating the user, click the check box to approve that you understand and accept that your progress on the learning site will be tracked and reflected as the selected user’s progress.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Managers and Reviewers > Team analytics:
In the Track tab, Readiness Index (RI) provides insights based on the competency benchmarks for a given period for a manager's team. You can view data and insights based on competencies/competency categories, teams, and user segments in the form of actionable charts and tables. These insights help you understand which competencies some or all of your sales reps should focus on. You can identify which competencies your sales reps are good at and which not. Then you can help your sales reps achieve the ideal benchmark for the competencies where they are falling behind. This helps both managers and sales reps know what they could focus on.

The Track tab offers the following benefits:

- Track RI scores by rep, team, or region and quickly address problem areas and understand how readiness scores change over time
- View performance data by competencies/competency categories and their weights (contribution towards RI)
- Identify which reps and teams within the organization need help from enablement and frontline managers
- More peak performers on the team through customized learning programs and coaching
- Optimal use of enablement efforts by focusing on reps and teams that need improvement

Note: Readiness Index (RI) data is not real-time. The data gets updated weekly — every Monday at 2 AM UTC. During the weekly data update, associated user hierarchies, competency performance data, and RI scores also get updated. For example, if there were any changes to your user hierarchies in the days between the last RI update and the upcoming update, the changes will reflect in RI after the next weekly update.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Managers and Reviewers > Team analytics > Overview:
This section provides an overview of the information available on the Track tab, in the form of top stats and charts.

Top stats:

The top section displays the following quick stats:

- Average RI: The average RI score for your organization and indicates if there is a change for the period selected in the Show RI change from setting.
- Top and bottom teams and competencies: Shows your top and bottom performing teams and competencies and indicates if there is any change in their RI score.

Charts:

1. Measure Readiness Index charts: This section provides key charts that help you measure Readiness Index (RI) by competencies, teams, and user segments.

Further down on the page, the Track tab provides the following two charts:

2. RI Trend chart: Trend of the RI score over time. For more information, see the “RI Trend Chart” section.

3. User distribution chart: Distribution of your sales reps by RI score. For more information, see the “User Distribution Chart” section.

Additionally, you can access detailed reports for the charts in the Reports tab in Readiness Index. Click the Reports tab to access the reports directly. Additionally, from the Track tab, you can access the reports in one of the following ways:

- Click the Details button in the upper-right corner of a chart.
- From Measure Readiness Index charts: Wherever chart data is clickable, you can click to open the respective report with applicable filters applied. For example, you can click the links in Top Insights, bars in the User Distribution chart, and the buttons that are available when you click on a competency or competency category in the Key Competency chart.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Managers and Reviewers > Team analytics > Tab settings:
You can change the following settings in the tab:

- Hierarchical Managers: Select a manager in the drop-down menu to view RI for their team. In the drop-down menu, you can view and select only those managers who report to you. You cannot view data for managers (and their teams) who do not report to you.
- Viewing RI as of: Select the period (week or month) for which you want to view RI data. By default, it shows either the latest week’s or month’s data depending on whether your admin has selected Weekly or Monthly as the default setting under Settings > Visualizations > More . You can view data for a previous week/month using the drop-down menu. TIP: If you do not want to change the default setting (Weekly or Monthly), you can temporarily change the period by selecting Last Week or Last Month in the Show RI change from setting. This will reflect the selected period for the Viewing RI as of setting as well.
- Show RI change from: Select the period (Last Week or Last Month) to view RI data changes for this period. If Last Month is selected, the latest month’s RI is compared to the last month’s RI. If Last Week is selected, the latest week’s RI is compared to the last week’s RI.

The following sections provide detailed information on the Track tab charts.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Managers and Reviewers > Team analytics > Measure RI by key competencies:
On the Key competencies page, you can measure and track Readiness Index (RI) by competencies that contribute to your organization’s RI. You can view the competency performance data of your sellers in one of the following types of charts:

- Spider chart
- Bar chart

For each chart type, you can also choose to view the chart data:

- Competencies
- Competency categories . In this view, you can further drill-down into any category to view data for all of its competencies.

The chart shows data by competencies by default.

The chart also displays the weights (contribution towards RI) of the competencies and their categories. This will help you understand the importance of each competency and category, and plan your enablement better.

Competencies in Readiness Index are defined through tags applied to various content in the Mindtickle platform. Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Managers and Reviewers > Team analytics > Measure RI by user segments:
Track your organization’s RI by user segments — such as job title, location, or team — to identify the high and low performing user segments across the organization.

User segment is a cohort of users and it can be based on profile fields and groups, such as department, division, hire date, and job title.

Insights on the chart: The chart indicates the company benchmark in green. Hover over a cohort to view their achieved score for a particular date in the period so you can compare the cohort’s performance with the company benchmark.

Click the Sort Chart By drop-down to sort the chart by RI score: Highest First or Lowest First. Click the Cohort drop-down to view chart data for a different cohort.

Click on any cohort in the chart to view detailed insights on the Teams report, where the table shows data with the cohort’s profile field filter applied. For example, your selected cohort is Department. When you click on the Support department’s bar in the chart, the Teams table opens with the Department profile field filter applied with Support as the value. For more information, see Reports Tab in Readiness Index for Managers.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Managers and Reviewers > Team analytics:
As a manager, you can use the Readiness Index scorecard to get a comprehensive view of the sales readiness of each of your sales reps (learners), as well as view your own RI scorecard.

Through the scorecard, managers can see a complete report card of a sales rep in the quadrant and spider charts. The quadrant chart displays progress of the rep’s performance across the latest four cadences. The spider chart displays a distribution of the rep’s competencies contributing to the organization’s RI and their comparison. This helps you identify the best and the worst performing competencies and how they have changed. In the Activity Timeline, the scorecard displays a list of modules assigned to the rep that will help improve their RI.

Note: This tab is visible only if Readiness Index (RI) is enabled for your organization. To learn more about the Readiness Index, contact your Customer Success Manager.

The scorecard page displays analytics data based on the following selections:

- View and compare growth: Select the cadence (Weekly or Monthly). With the cadence, you can choose to view comparative RI data by a weekly or monthly cycle, which can be selected in the Viewing RI as of option.
  - Monthly: The latest month’s RI is compared to last month’s RI.
  - Weekly: The latest week’s RI is compared to last week’s RI.
- Viewing RI as of: Select a date as of which you want to view the data by the cadence selected in the View and compare growth option. For example, if you select your cadence to be monthly and view data as of June 1, 2022 , then the quadrant chart displays data for the last four monthly cadences: June 1, May 1, April 1, and March 1.
- Correlate RI with: Select the business metric with which you want to correlate the RI data for the rep.

This section provides the following information:

For example, if the company benchmark for the “Negotiation” competency is 96.5 while your sales rep’s scores for the selected period are not good — this helps you understand that your sales reps need to focus on this competency to achieve the benchmark cutoff score.

In the spider or bar chart, hover over the chart and click a competency to view the sales rep’s performance for a particular competency with respect to the Modules that have an impact on the competency. This information is displayed under the Activity Timeline section, with the respective competency selected.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Course and quick update:
This article explains how admins can add in-video questions or polls in a course or quick update module.

Ensuring user engagement in long videos and content has always been challenging for enablement admins. It has elevated in the current scenario where many distractions exist in our day-to-day lives.

User engagement on questions or polls is higher compared to content. Users love a challenge when posed to them. Hence, Mindtickle enables you to ask questions and conduct surveys in between long videos in a Course or Quick update module. It helps increase user engagement on content and perform just-in-time knowledge checks.

Note:

- You can only add in-video questions and polls for videos uploaded via Mindtickle library, Content Center, third-party cloud storage systems (such as Box, Google Drive, OneDrive, Dropbox, Egnyte, Salesforce), or your personal computer. You cannot add in-video questions and polls in embedded videos (such as videos from YouTube and SlideShare).
- This article uses an example from a course module to explain the in-video questions functionality. You can follow the same steps in a quick update module to add the in-video questions or polls.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Course and quick update > Add in-video questions:
1. From the course or quick update, click the Add Learning objects button on the Build tab.
2. In the Add learning objects panel, click Content under Upload content .
3. On the Content page, upload the required video. Once you upload the video, click the Add in-video questions button to ask questions or conduct polls in between the video. Alternatively, you can also hover over the video seek bar to add in-video questions or polls.
4. You can add the following types of in-video questions and quizzes or Gather feedback :
  - Create questions and quizzes
    - Multiple choice questions
    - Multiple choice images
    - Word guess
    - Match the labels
    - Match image with label
    - Mark the location
    - True or false
    - Bulk upload questions For more information, see Question Types .
  - Gather feedback
    - Multiple choice poll
    - Feedback For more information, see Gather feedback .
5. Select the question or poll and fill in the relevant details. The following image shows an example of adding a True or false in-video question. You can set up the following additional configuration for each question type:
  - Add hint : Configure a hint to give an indication or suggestion to learners that leads them towards the correct answer.
  - Question score : Configure scores on a range of 0-500 with an incremental change of 50. For example, you can set scores to 0, 50,100,150, 200, 250, 300, 350, 400, 450, or 500.
  - Wrong attempts : Configure the difficulty level of the question by setting the number of wrong attempts in a range of 1-4.
  - Lifelines : Configure lifelines to help learners eliminate wrong choices. Learners can use a maximum of 2 lifelines per question. The total count of lifelines decreases by the number of lifelines already used by the learner and increases by 3 with every badge that a learner earns. For example, if you set 10 lifelines for a Course, the total number of lifelines that a learner can use in the Course is 10, but out of these 10, the learner can use only 2 lifelines per question. You can change the default number for lifelines (3) from Course Settings > Gamification .
  - Enable learners to answer later : Configure to enable learners to attempt in-video questions anytime before the Course completes. If you disable the setting, learners need to answer all the in-video questions as and when they occur to proceed in the video. Note :
    - The completion status of the video is independent of the completion status of the in-video question, even if the learner answers the in-video question incorrectly.
    - If a learner chooses to attempt an in-video question later, the learner can attempt it until the learner completes the Course and the lifelines exist. Once the learner completes the Course, the learner cannot use the lifelines (even if present) or attempt the in-video question. The learner can view the selected answers and the correct answers to the in-video question in a view-only mode when watching the video again.
  - Tag : Configure to associate tags with the question. Tags are attributes that you can apply to questions. Tags help to filter, organize, and search for the question. Learners can also filter search results using tags. For more information, see How to Apply Tags .
  - Time at which the question is placed on video : Configure the time where you want to place the question in the video. Use the Up and Down arrows to move the question position in the video accordingly. Click Save to proceed.
6. Hover over the video seek bar to add more in-video questions or polls. Click the Forward and Backward arrows to navigate the in-video question or poll position on the video seek bar. Note :
  - You can add up to 30 in-video questions or polls in a video with a 1 second gap. As a best practice, we recommend maintaining a gap of at least 5 minutes between every 2 questions or polls to maximize learner engagement.
  - You cannot place in-video questions or polls at the last second in the video.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Course and quick update > Calculate scores for a video with in-video questions or polls:
The total score earned by a learner for a video learning content is the sum of the score earned from watching the video and the score earned from answering the in-video questions or polls.

You can configure scores on a range of 0-500 with an incremental change of 50. For example, you can set scores to 0, 50,100,150, 200, 250, 300, 350, 400, 450, or 500.

Following are the possibilities for setting up scores for a video with in-video questions or polls:

- Total score (x) = Score earned from watching the video (x) + Sum of the score of all the in-video questions or polls (0)
- Total score (y) = Score earned from watching the video (0) + Sum of the score of all the in-video questions or polls (y)
- Total score (x+y) = Score earned from watching the video (x) + Sum of the score of all the in-video questions or polls (y)

You can hover over the Info icon next to the Total score to view the score breakdown.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Course and quick update > Replace a video with in-video questions:
Click the Replace button in the upper-right corner to change the video with another video.

When Content Center is enabled for your site, you can replace the video using the following 2 options:

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Course and quick update > Replace a video with in-video questions > Replace file in Content Center:
If you select this option:

- The new file replaces the existing file in the Content center and everywhere else it has been used (across modules and assets). It helps in managing your files better and avoids any duplication.
- There is no change in the progress of the learners who have completed the content.
- Once you replace the file, there is no need to update the module. If there are any in-video questions or polls, you can restore them after replacing the file.
- This option does not trigger any module version update, and therefore, the progress and score of the learners who have completed the learning content remain the same. However, the progress and score of the learners who have started the module but have not completed that particular learning content resets to 0 (only for that learning content).
- Once you replace the file, you cannot go back to the previous version of the file.
- The new file format must be the same as the previous file format.

For more information, see Replace a File in Content Center.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Course and quick update > Replace a video with in-video questions > Restore in-video questions:
Once you replace the video file using one of the above options, you can restore the in-video questions or polls in the new video file.

- If you replace the video using Content Center, the new video contains the in-video questions or polls in the same place as in the old video.
- If you replace the video file only in the module, click the Review and restore in-video questions button above the video seek bar to place the in-video questions or polls in the new video. Select the questions or polls to restore in the new video. Click the Restore button to proceed.

The placement of questions and polls depends on the length of the new video:

- If the length of the new video is equal to or greater than the length of the old video, the new video retains all the in-video questions or polls at the original timestamp as it was in the old video.
- If the length of the new video is less than the length of the old video, the new video retains the in-video questions or polls at the original timestamp on the new video. Any question or poll that does not fit within the length of the new video is restored towards the end of the video in a staggered manner (one second before the end of the video). However, you can manually adjust the position of these questions or polls.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Course and quick update > Update module version:
If you change the question or poll text for in-video questions or polls, there is no need to update the module version. However, if you change any other fields (such as answer text and correct answer), you must update the module version.

The impact on the learner’s progress when you update the module version for an in-video question or poll remains the same as the module version update when you edit, change, delete, or add a learning content. You can decide to whom you want to push the new module version from the following options:

- Only those who will be invited hereafter
- Only those who have NOT started the Course
- Only those who have NOT started or NOT completed the Course
- All, including those who have completed the Course

For more information, see Which changes to a published module will or will not trigger a module update?

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Communications > Notifications and Reminders:
Inviting individual learners or learner groups to a series or module is an integral part of ensuring enablement programs are deployed and adopted efficiently. As an admin, you can invite learners or groups instantaneously or you can schedule invitations for a specific date and time. When learners or groups are invited to a series or module, they receive email notifications and reminders based on how the learning site, series, module-level, or email notification digest settings are configured.

This article explains the hierarchy of notification configurability in Mindtickle, based on which, emails and notifications are triggered.

Once turned off, learners do not receive any notifications such as invitations or reminders on that specific channel. Changing these settings does not have an impact on account transactional emails for actions such as Password Reset, Email Authentication, Export Reports, and Call AI. For more information, see Disable Emails and Notifications for Learning Site.

To update the default learning site notification settings, contact Mindtickle Support.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Communications > Notifications and Reminders > Series-level notification settings > Module invitation email and mobile notifications > Disable email notifications for Optional or Unmarked modules:
You can disable email notifications for modules that are marked as Optional or Unmarked for the learner. The system identifies Required modules and sends only the relevant notifications. Thus preventing irrelevant notifications from being sent to the learner. Disabling email notifications for non-mandatory modules is governed by the setting Ignore Non-Mandatory Notifications. To enable or disable it, contact your Customer Success Manager (CSM). If enabled, the learner does not receive invitation, reminder, or completion emails for modules that are Optional or Unmarked across the learning site. They only receive emails for modules that are Required.

Note:

- This feature can be enabled only if Module Relevance is enabled.
- This feature applies only to Course, Quick update, Assessment, ILT, Checklist, and Mission modules. It does not apply to Quest and Coaching modules.
- If this feature is enabled, the following types of notifications for modules marked as Optional or Unmarked are not sent:
  - Series invitation - if none of the modules in the series have Required relevance, the notification is ignored. If at least one module in the series invitation has Required relevance, even though other modules have Optional or Unmarked relevance, the series invitation is sent.
  - Module invitation - if the module relevance for the learner is Optional or Unmarked , the email notification is ignored.
  - Module reminders - if the module relevance for the learner is Optional or Unmarked , the email notification is ignored.
  - Module completion - if the module relevance for the learner is Optional or Unmarked , the email notification is ignored.
  - All other types of notifications are sent out as is.
