chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Communications > Notifications and Reminders > Series-level notification settings > Reminder Emails and Mobile Notifications:
This setting defines whether learners in a particular series receive reminder emails for modules within that series.

By default, Mindtickle clubs reminder emails and mobile notifications for multiple modules (within a series) that are scheduled to go out on the same day into a single email to prevent learners from getting separate multiple reminders. The clubbed reminder emails are sent based on the following:

- If Reminder Emails (in Series Settings ) is Enabled
  - If the user selects the ‘ No. of days after invitation ’ option for the module-level reminder(s), a clubbed reminder email is sent on the specified day after the user receives the series invitation.
  - If the user selects the ' Select a specific date ' option for the module-level reminder(s), clubbed reminders are disabled, and individual emails are sent on the selected date.
- If Reminder Emails (in Series Settings ) is Disabled Irrespective of the module-level settings, no reminder emails are triggered.

Note:

- Clubbed reminders are delivered at approximately 8:00 AM or 2:00 PM in the local timezone of the learner. For more information, see Clubbed Reminder Settings for Reminder Emails .
- By default, clubbed reminders are turned ON for a learning site. To disable this feature for your learning site, contact your CSM. If disabled, and,
  - Reminder Emails (in Series Settings ) is Enabled Then based on the reminder settings configured in each module, individual module reminders are triggered.
  - Reminder Emails (in Series Settings ) is Disabled Irrespective of the module-level settings, no reminder emails are triggered.

Note: All series-level notification settings can be set as default series-level settings for the learning site. For more information, contact Mindtickle Support.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Communications > Notifications and Reminders > Notification digest:
Note: This is a beta feature. To enable it on your learning site, contact Mindtickle Support or your Customer Success Manager (CSM).

A notification digest provides a high-level summary of a learner’s assigned content and learning progress during a specified time interval. For example, if the specified time interval is a week, the notification digest includes information about the series and modules the learner is invited to and the modules the learner has completed during the week. It also includes information about the modules that are still pending completion by the learner. It acts as a recap and is sent as an email to the learner’s registered email address at regular intervals. Thus providing a concise and organized overview of the information. The frequency of the notification digest can vary, ranging from weekly to biweekly or monthly. Admins can also choose to allow learners to configure their preferences to determine the frequency at which they wish to receive the digest.

Notification digests provide a convenient way for learners to stay updated on multiple action items or events without being inundated with individual email notifications.

Note:

- A notification digest is not a replacement for the individual email notifications sent to a learner. If enabled, it merely provides a quick summary of the learner’s assigned content and learning progress made during a specified time interval designed to enhance learner engagement.
- A notification digest is exclusive to email notifications and does not extend to push notifications.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Communications > Notifications and Reminders > Notification digest > Notification digest settings:
- Notification Digest This is the master setting used to enable or disable the notification digest feature. If enabled, learners receive a notification digest email that provides a summary (associated with a specific time period) of the following:
  - Series invitations : The number of series the learner is invited to and the link to view the series (they have access to).
  - Module invitations : The number of modules the learner is invited to and the link to view the modules (they have access to).
  - Modules completed : The number of modules the learner has completed and the link to view the completed modules.
  - Modules pending : The number of modules the learner is yet to complete and the link to view the incomplete modules. Note :
    - The notification digest is sent to the learner depending on the digest frequency.
    - The series and module-level notification settings have no bearing on the digest email.
      - For modules marked with relevance Required , the notification is sent as per series and module settings.
      - For modules marked with relevance Optional or Unmarked , the notifications for the invitations, reminders, and completions are ignored.
- Digest Frequency This setting determines the frequency at which the digest is sent to learners. The available options are:
  - Off - if selected, the digest is not sent to any learner.
  - Weekly - if selected, the digest is sent to the learners once every week.
  - Biweekly - if selected, the digest is sent to the learners once every two weeks.
  - Monthly - if selected, the digest is sent to the learners once every month. Note : To enable this feature for your learning site, contact Mindtickle Support or your Customer Success Manager (CSM).
- User can override If enabled, learners can override the frequency configured by the admin by selecting their desired frequency. For more information, see My Profile: Settings . Note : To enable this feature for your learning site, contact Mindtickle Support or your Customer Success Manager (CSM). Learners can set their preferences by choosing from any of the following options:
  - Don’t notify at all - if selected, the learner does not receive the digest email.
  - Notify weekly - if selected, the learner receives the digest once every week.
  - Notify biweekly - if selected, the learner receives the digest once every two weeks.
  - Notify monthly - if selected, the learner receives the digest once every month. Note : By default, the frequency configured by the admin for the learning site is selected.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Communications > Notifications and Reminders > Notification digest > Additional notes:
- The digest is sent to learners on Tuesday between 11 AM to 2 PM in the learner’s timezone (as per the timezone setup in the learner’s profile field).
- If the learner has not configured the timezone in their profile, the digest is sent to their registered email address on Tuesday between 11 AM and 2 PM GMT.
- If (for any reason) the digest preparation for some learners is not completed by 2 PM, the system attempts to send the digest by no later than 5 PM.
- If the digest frequency is set to weekly , the digest is sent on Tuesday, considering the learner’s data from last week’s Monday to the current week’s Sunday.
- If the digest frequency is set to biweekly , the digest is sent on Tuesday, considering the learner’s data from Monday 2 weeks back to the current week’s Sunday.
- If the digest frequency is set to monthly , the digest is sent on the first Tuesday of the month, considering the learner’s data from the first Monday of the last month to the first Sunday of the current month.
- A record of all notification digests that are sent to learners is stored in Email Logs. For more information, see Email Logs .

To access Call AI from the Mindtickle Admin Site Homepage:

1. Enter the URL admin.mindtickle.com in a new tab of your web browser. The admin site sign in page is displayed.

2. Enter your learning site URL and click Continue.

Note: If you do not know your learning site URL, contact your Customer Success Manager (CSM).

The learning site login page is displayed.

3. Click Sign In with your username.

Alternatively, click any of the SSO sign-in options to sign in using SSO.

Note: For more information about signing in using your organization's SSO, see Access the Admin Site Using Single Sign-On (SSO).

4. Enter your username and password and click Sign In.

Note:

- Your registered email address is your username.
- If you have forgotten your password, you can reset it using the Forgot Password link. For more information, see How do I reset my forgotten password from the Learning Site? .

5. On the admin site homepage, click Account> Settings> Call AI > General.

You can view the following organization-level settings. The article further explains each of these settings in detail.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > Admin > Steps to Configure the General Settings > 3. Auto-transcribe call recordings in multiple languages:
Use this setting to configure recording transcriptions in multiple languages. Multiple languages allow your business to communicate effectively with non-English speaking customers. It helps you reach new territories, and your product lives in a global marketplace. The more languages you communicate, the more potential customers you can find.

Select the languages for transcription and click Done.

Note:

- Toggling the setting might drop the English transcription's quality.
- Setting the language preference on the Mindtickle learning site will only localize the user interface to the set language. However, to get transcripts in a particular language, you must also set your language preference in Call AI.
- If there is a language that the Mindtickle learning site supports (for example, Chinese) but Call AI does not support yet. In that case, Call AI transcriptions and insights appear in English.
- If you configure recording transcriptions in multiple languages and on a call, participants use more than one language to converse. In that case, Call AI generates transcription in the language which was conversed first.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > User:
This article explains how reps with a recorder role can integrate their Outlook calendar with Call AI.

Call AI integrates with your Outlook calendar and automatically finds your upcoming sales meetings to join and record. Once integrated, you can view up to 2 weeks of your upcoming meetings populated on the Upcoming Meetings page. You can toggle recording on or off for each meeting as needed.

For example, you have a recurring bi-weekly sync call between the product and the sales team, which you want to record by default. You can easily toggle recording ON for that meeting, and the Call AI bot automatically records all such meetings henceforth. It helps keep track of useful information that you can easily refer to later or share with your team members.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > User > Steps to integrate the Outlook calendar with Call AI > When the admin consent workflow is turned on:
1. Sign in to your Call AI instance using Mindtickle credentials.

2. Click Call AI > Preferences > Integrations > Outlook calendar > Enable.

3. Sign in to your Microsoft account.

4. You can see an approval required pop-up. Enter a justification for requesting the approval and click Request approval.

Once you request the approval, your Microsoft account admin receives an email notification. Click Back to app to return to your Call AI instance.

5. Once your Microsoft account admin approves your request, you receive an email notification. Repeat steps 2 and 3 to finish the integration.

Your Outlook calendar integration with Call AI is successful.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > SCORM Content > Limitations:
- If a learner reattempts a completed SCORM module in a sequentially locked series, the module may revert to In Progress . This can lock the next modules again until the learner completes the SCORM module.
- SCORM content on mobile depends on how the package is designed and how mobile access is configured. SCORM content requires an active internet connection and cannot be accessed offline.
- Learners should open SCORM content only from Mindtickle. Opening content from old bookmarks, copied links, browser history, or shared SCORM links can cause launch, access, or tracking issues.
- xAPI packages can be uploaded and played in Mindtickle. However, advanced xAPI tracking is not currently supported.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > SCORM Content > Create the SCORM content:
- Confirm that all required learning elements are included, such as slides, videos, questions, quizzes, interactions, and final screens.
- Verify that required media, links, buttons, and interactions work as expected.
- Check that the completion requirements are set in the authoring tool and that the package sends completion only after learners complete the required activities and final actions.
- Ensure scoring is configured for the content in the authoring tool.
- For Captivate packages, ensure the package sends SCORM data throughout the course, including after slides, interactions, and quiz actions.
- Include a Done or Submit button, or a similar final action, that learners can click after completing the required SCORM activities.
- Use HTML5 output. Do not use Flash-only content.
- If learners use the Mindtickle mobile app, ensure the content is designed for mobile playback and does not use left- or right-swipe navigation, horizontal scrolling, or drag-and-drop interactions that conflict with the mobile app's navigation.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > SCORM Content > Upload the package:
- We recommend using the latest version of the Chrome browser for a seamless experience.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > SCORM Content > Configure the learning object:
- Check whether the required desktop display mode is selected in the SCORM Configuration settings:
  - Inline (Desktop): Opens the package within the module page.
  - Full screen: Opens the package in a full-screen view.
  - New window: Opens the package in a separate browser window. Use this option for AICC packages to avoid cross-domain errors.
- Ensure that Inline (Mobile) is selected only if the package is designed for mobile playback.
- Ensure Disable on mobile is selected if the package opens in a new browser tab, requires external sign-in, uses a fixed desktop layout, or includes interactions that do not work correctly on mobile.
- Validate that scoring is enabled, so the package sends a score to the Mindtickle module when the SCORM content is completed.
- Enable the Save and exit button so learners can save progress before completing the module.

Note:

- The Save and exit button saves learner progress. Selecting this button does not mark the module as complete.
- The module is marked complete only after the learner completes all required screens, activities, interactions, quizzes, and selects Done , and the SCORM package sends completion to Mindtickle.

For troubleshooting mobile launch and playback issues, see Resolve SCORM launch, playback, and mobile issues for admins.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > SCORM Content > Test the package:
- If you upload, replace, or change the configuration of a package, refresh the browser page before running Test SCORM .
- Confirm that Test SCORM opens the package successfully.
- Complete the full package as a learner. Do not skip required screens, interactions, quizzes, or final actions.
- Check that the required media, links, buttons, and interactions work correctly after upload.
- Verify that the status of Follows SCORM standards and Receiving completion status are green.
- Confirm that the package sends completion only after the learner completes all required activities and final actions.
- If scoring is enabled, check that the original score from SCORM and Score in Mindtickle are green.
- If the package supports resume, verify that it resumes at the expected point after learners select the Save and exit button , then reopen the module.
- If Inline (Mobile) is selected, check that the package is tested in the Mindtickle mobile app on supported iOS and Android devices.
- Verify that all applicable Test SCORM results are green before publishing.

Note:

- If any Test SCORM result is orange, test the same .zip file that you uploaded to Mindtickle in SCORM Cloud . Do not re-export or modify the package before testing.
- If the issue also occurs in SCORM Cloud , work with the content owner or the SCORM vendor to resolve it and re-export the package.
- If the package works in SCORM Cloud but fails in Mindtickle, capture the Test SCORM result and continue troubleshooting in Mindtickle.

For detailed information on SCORM testing and interpreting test results, see SCORM Content in Mindtickle.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > SCORM Content > Before you begin:
- We recommend using the latest version of the Chrome browser for a seamless experience.
- Set the browser zoom to 100% before opening the content. Press Ctrl+0 on Windows or Command+0 on Mac.
- Use a screen width of 1024 pixels or wider when completing SCORM content on a desktop. A smaller screen width can affect interactive elements such as drag-and-drop activities.
- If your training is assigned for mobile completion, use the latest version of the Mindtickle mobile app .
- On a mobile device, open the Mindtickle app directly. Do not open the training from an email link or a mobile browser.
- If the Mindtickle app asks you to switch to desktop, the content is not available for mobile completion. Open it in Chrome on a computer.
- In Chrome , the SCORM content can open within the Mindtickle page, in full-screen mode, or in a separate window, depending on how the admin configured the package.
- If full-screen mode is available, use it to ensure that all interactive elements are visible and accessible.
- Keep the Mindtickle tab open until you finish the SCORM content. Do not refresh the SCORM content tab or window.
- Use a stable internet connection.
- Do not switch networks while the content is open.
- If your VPN causes loading issues, try a different network.
- Allow pop-ups, third-party cookies, and local storage for Mindtickle and the SCORM content.
- If third-party cookies are blocked in Chrome , go to Settings > Privacy and security > Third-party cookies and add exceptions for Mindtickle and the SCORM content domains.
- Allow camera or microphone access in Chrome if the content requires them.
- Use a regular Chrome window when completing SCORM content.
- Turn off ad blockers or browser extensions that might block the content.
- If you experience loading or interaction issues, retry the module in an Incognito window to check whether cached browser data, cookies, or browser extensions are causing the issue.

- Keep the Mindtickle tab open until you finish the SCORM content. Do not refresh the SCORM content tab or window.
- Use a stable internet connection.
- Do not switch networks while the content is open.
- If your VPN causes loading issues, try a different network.
- Allow pop-ups, third-party cookies, and local storage for Mindtickle and the SCORM content.
- If third-party cookies are blocked in Chrome , go to Settings > Privacy and security > Third-party cookies and add exceptions for Mindtickle and the SCORM content domains.
- Allow camera or microphone access in Chrome if the content requires them.
- Use a regular Chrome window when completing SCORM content.
- Turn off ad blockers or browser extensions that might block the content.
- If you experience loading or interaction issues, retry the module in an Incognito window to check whether cached browser data, cookies, or browser extensions are causing the issue.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > SCORM Content > Complete the content:
- Wait until the content loads fully.
- Complete the content in the required order.
- Complete all required screens, activities, interactions, quizzes, and final actions.
- Watch the required videos fully. Do not skip or fast-forward.
- Click or interact with all required buttons, links, answers, and activities.
- Do not use the browser’s back or refresh button while the content is open.
- Do not open the same module in more than one tab at a time.
- Do not minimize the Chrome window after starting the SCORM content.
- Keep the browser tab open until your progress is saved.
- If the content freezes, goes blank, or continues loading, wait 30 seconds. If the issue continues, close only the SCORM content tab or window, then reopen the module from Mindtickle. Keep the Mindtickle tab open and do not refresh the tab or window where the SCORM content is open.
- For content that takes a long time to complete, remain signed in to Mindtickle until you finish.
- If the SCORM content opens separately and the Mindtickle tab has been inactive for a long time, refresh only the Mindtickle tab before clicking the final Done or Submit button. Do not refresh the tab or window where the SCORM content is open.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > SCORM Content > Finish the module:
- Use the Save and exit button only to save your progress and return later. Save and exit does not mark the module as complete. The module completes only when you finish all required activities, select Done , and the SCORM package sends the completion status to Mindtickle.
- Some packages require you to complete the remaining content in one continuous session after using the Save and exit button . Follow the instructions provided by your admin. Closing and reopening the module again before completion can prevent the completion status from being recorded.
- Click the Exit , Finish , Submit , Done , or Exit Course button inside the SCORM content to finish or close the content, if the button is available.
- Select the Done button to complete the module in Mindtickle after you finish all required SCORM content.
- Wait until Mindtickle updates your progress, completion status, or score.
- Check the module status in Mindtickle after you finish.
- Reopen the module once if the completion status does not update after you finish the content.
- If your progress, completion status, or score still does not update, contact your admin and share:
  - A screenshot showing the module name, completion percentage, and current status, such as In Progress or Completed
  - The date and time when you completed or attempted the content
  - A screenshot of the SCORM content screen if the issue occurred inside the content.

Note: 100% progress inside the SCORM content does not always mean that the Mindtickle module is complete.For troubleshooting issues, see Troubleshoot module completion and SCORM issues.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Readiness Index (RI):
If your business metrics data resides in Salesforce CRM, you can sync the Salesforce’s sales metrics data for business outcomes (Salesforce objects and fields) — such as quota attainment and win rates — with Mindtickle. Once your Salesforce is integrated with Mindtickle and the business metrics data is synced, you can view this data in Readiness Index (RI).

This article explains the following next steps that you need to perform in Readiness Index after setting up the Salesforce Outcome Data Sync integration:

1. Select the business metrics: Select/configure the Salesforce business metrics that you want to visualize on the Correlate tab of RI. You can configure this under RI Settings > Visualizations > Business Metric Selection . For more information, see the “ Select the Business Metrics ” section.
2. View the business metrics data: View data for your selected business metrics on the Correlate tab in Readiness Index. Here, RI provides insights into the impact of your readiness initiatives on your business outcomes. For more information, see the “ View the Business Metrics Data ” section. Additionally, you can also view changes in a particular sales rep’s RI score and business metrics on their Overall Report > Scorecard tab. For more information, see Readiness Index Scorecard for Sales Reps .

Important: After you have set up the Salesforce Outcome Data Sync integration, your metrics will reflect in Readiness Index only during the next RI data refresh, which happens every Monday at 2 AM UTC.

For information on how your Salesforce metrics are calculated, see Definitions and Calculations of Salesforce Metrics for Readiness Index.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Readiness Index (RI) > 1. Select the business metrics > Business metric selection:
This setting allows you to select the Salesforce business metrics that are important to you for your Readiness Index. The first drop-down menu lists all Salesforce metrics that you selected to sync while integrating Salesforce for Sales Outcome Data Sync. The metrics that you select here will be made available in the Correlate tab so you can visualize them in the quadrant chart.

Perform the following to select one or more Salesforce business metrics:

1. Click the drop-down menu to view a list of your metrics. Select one or more metrics from the list and then click Apply.Note: The dropdown menu lists all metrics synced from Salesforce. You can sync a maximum of 22 Salesforce metrics. However, out of the 22, you can configure up to 10 metrics. Your selected 10 metrics will be made available for use on the Correlate tab > Correlating RI with dropdown menu. You can change your selection of 10 metrics anytime.

1. For any selected metric, you can also define their cycle, such as Monthly and Quarterly, using the drop-down menu for a metric. The cycle is based on your financial year’s start date defined in Analytics Settings.

1. Under Default business metric selection, select the metric that you want to set as the default metric for the quadrant chart on the Correlate tab.

Now you can view your business metrics data on the Correlate tab of Readiness Index. For more information, see the next section.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Readiness Index (RI) > 2. View the business metrics data:
The Correlate tab shows a quadrant chart showcasing the correlation of your business metric — such as quota attainment — with the Readiness Index and helps you identify user cohorts and provides insights that you can use to take specific actions for those cohorts. You can view and analyze your Salesforce business metrics data on this tab.

The Correlate tab offers the following benefits:

- Analyze rep skills and competencies against business metrics to identify where readiness efforts need to be amplified
- Pull in business metrics from Salesforce automatically
- Report the business impact of enablement and coaching
- Identify which parts of the revenue org need more help

For more information about this tab, see Correlate tab in Readiness Index.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Readiness Index (RI) > 2. View the business metrics data > Tab settings:
The following image shows the quadrant chart in the Correlate tab.

You can take the following actions around the available settings for the chart:

- Correlate Salesforce business metrics data with Readiness Index: From the Correlate drop-down menu, you can select a Salesforce business metric. The metrics in the drop-down are based on your selection in RI Settings > Visualizations > Business metric selection .
- Viewing RI for team of: Select the manager for whose team you want to view RI.
- Seller Distribution: Select one of the following options to distribute the chart data:
  - Scatter: Displays data for all individual sales reps in your team.
  - Bubble: Displays data grouped by your teams and distributed by the segment that you select. Options in the segment drop-down depend on how your admin has configured the “Segment Selection” settings on the admin site.
- Select area to zoom: Using the mouse, make a selection on the chart to zoom in the selected area. Select an area again to further keep zooming the chart. Click Reset zoom to reset the chart zoom to normal.
- Settings icon: Click to make temporary changes to the chart configuration. You can change the default values for the business metric and Readiness Index (RI) on the x and y-axis respectively. The default values are based on your admin’s configuration.
- Timeline data points: Click a data point in the timeline bar to view data for the selected data point’s time period.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Coaching Sessions > View coaching feedback > View the reviewer’s feedback on coaching sessions > Recently reviewed:
This widget displays all coaching sessions in which the reviewer submitted feedback in the last 30 days. The feedback is listed in the order it is received; the recently received feedback is displayed first, followed by the others.

The widget thumbnail displays up to 3 coaching sessions. In the last 30 days, if you have received feedback from more than 3 coaching sessions, you will see a Show all button in the top-right corner. Click the Show all button to view all the coaching sessions where you have received feedback in the last 30 days.

Click the View option to see the reviewer feedback.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Coaching Sessions > View coaching feedback > View the reviewer’s feedback on coaching sessions > Upcoming sessions:
This widget displays the upcoming coaching session for the next 30 days.

The widget thumbnail displays up to 3 coaching sessions in the order of occurrence. The upcoming session is displayed first, followed by the others.

If more than 3 upcoming coaching sessions are scheduled in the next 30 days, you will see a Show all button in the top-right corner. Click Show all to see all the upcoming coaching sessions in the next 30 days in the order of occurrence.

Click View to see the evaluation parameters for the coaching sessions.

Click the Edit schedule option to edit the scheduled session. You can only edit the sessions that you have scheduled. Learners can schedule a session with the reviewer only if the admin has enabled the option while creating the session.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Coaching Sessions > View coaching feedback > All coaching sessions > Active sessions:
This section lists all active coaching sessions assigned to you as a learner, and a reviewer has also been appointed. For each coaching session, the table displays the coaching session name, reviewer name, last session score, last session completed on date and time, and next session scheduled on date and time.

Click View to see the active coaching session.

Click the Schedule session option to schedule a session with the reviewer. Learners can schedule a session with the reviewer only if the admin has enabled the option while creating the session.

After scheduling a session with the reviewer, learners can also see the Edit schedule option. Learners can also edit the session schedule from the Upcoming session widget.

To view specific coaching sessions, apply filters by coaching session name, reviewer name, scheduled date, search (by coaching session name and reviewer), and no past sessions.

Note: No past sessions are coaching sessions assigned to you as a learner, but no action is taken on the sessions.

Click the Reset filters option to remove the applied filter.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Dashboards:
In Analytics dashboards, you can view analytics insights data in two ways:

- Widgets: Displays overview-style limited data
- Widget reports: Displays detailed analytics

In all Analytics dashboards, widgets provide overview-style insights and analytics on top platform activities. You can further access a detailed widget report by clicking the widget name.

Widgets display limited data by design, but you can click the name of the widget to view detailed analytics in the widget report. Each widget and its widget report derives data from one or more metrics. You can change various customization settings and filters, and then save the report to preserve your changes. Any customizations you make to the widget report are also reflected for the widget on the dashboard.

The following are some of the available customizations:

- Visualize the widget and widget report data in a table, area, or bar chart. You can further configure various chart settings (such as add or remove metrics, apply conditional formatting, and configure data visualization) for the selected chart type. See the “ Chart Types and Settings ” section for more.
- Configure the amount of data to view in the report and configure the data sorting settings .
- Apply various filters to view relevant data and save the report to preserve your filter settings.
- Export the widget report in a CSV format or download it to your computer in a PNG format for external use. See the “ Export and Download the Widget Report ” section for more.

You can view widgets and their reports in the following Analytics dashboards: Home dashboard, Adoption dashboard, Performance dashboard, custom dashboards (created by you), and Asset Hub Engagement dashboard.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Dashboards > Access widget reports:
Admins with access to widgets on Analytics dashboards (Home, Adoption, Performance, custom, and Asset Hub Engagement dashboards) can view and customize the widget and its corresponding widget report. This section explains how to access a widget’s report to view and customize it.

Note: The number of widgets and the data in widgets that you see depends on your role and whether you have access to the underlying Analytics data. For more information, see Permissions and Access for Analytics Dashboards.

Perform the following to access a particular widget’s report on any Analytics dashboard:

1. On the dashboard page, click the name of the widget to access the widget report. If you want to directly go into the widget/widget report editing mode, hover over the widget and click the ( Edit ) button.
2. On the widget report page that opens, you can view the report as well as customize it. For more information, see the “ Customize Widgets and Widget Reports ” section.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Dashboards > Customize widgets and widget reports:
1. On the widget report page, you can view the report as well as customize it and save your changes.
2. You can perform two kinds of customizations. Any customizations you make to the widget report are also reflected for the widget on the dashboard.
  - Edit report configuration: Click the (Edit) button to update the metrics and other configuration settings.
  - Apply filters: Certain filters are applied by default and you can change them. You can also apply additional filters using the Add filters button.
3. Click the ( Edit ) button to update the metrics and other configuration settings.
4. On the Edit configuration panel that opens, you can make changes related to the visualization (how your widget report and the widget will look) and metrics data (what data is displayed in the report and the widget). For detailed information on the customization options, see the “ Customization Options ” section.
5. Once you have made the changes, click Apply changes to apply them.
6. You are taken back to the report page, where you can review your changes made in the Edit configuration panel.
7. Additionally, you can also change existing filters, and apply new filters using the Add filters button. Similar to customization settings, any changes you make to the filters are also reflected for the widget on the dashboard.
8. Once you have made the configuration and filters related changes, you can either:
  - Save the changes: If all looks good, click Save to save the changes for the report as well as the widget.
  - Discard the changes: If you want to discard the changes made in the Edit configuration panel, use the breadcrumb at the top to navigate back to the Adoption dashboard or to the Training section.
  - Reset to default: If you want to reset all settings and filters to the default state, click Reset.
9. Changes to the widget report are also reflected for the widget on the dashboard. Note: The widgets can display only limited data. For a detailed look, click the widget to view the widget report.
10. You can now export or download your report. For more information, see the “ Export and Download the Widget Report ” section.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Dashboards > Customization options > Chart Types and Settings > Table chart:
- Add columns: Column data is derived from various metrics, which are based on generic metrics and profile fields. To start adding columns, click Add columns . On the Customize Columns panel, click the + ( plus ) button against a metric to add it as a column. After adding the columns, you can reorder by dragging them.
- Edit column metrics: Click the icon for a column to edit the column’s metric configuration and visualization. Note: You can edit only the generic metrics; profile field metrics cannot be edited. You can make the following changes to the column metrics:
  - Metric name: This is the column name. You can change it to your preference.
  - Conditional formatting: Turn the toggle switch on to configure the colors for column data and the metric range.
    - Under Apply Color On , select “Metric Value” to apply colors to the metric data and select “Column Cell” to apply colors to the column cells.
    - Under Select Range , select the data range for each color. For example, consider the Started column, which displays data on the total number of modules started by learners. And you have set “0 to 30” as the range for red and “30 onwards” as the range for green . In this case, when you view the widget report, the Started column will display data in red for learners who have started less than 30 modules, and green for learners who have started more than 30 modules.

Click Apply to apply the changes.Once you have configured the table chart, you can perform the following on the report page:

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Dashboards > Export/download widget report:
You can export and download a widget report for your own use and to share with others.

Perform the following steps to export or download a widget report:

1. Click the button in the upper-right corner.
2. In the pop-up that appears, you can select one of the following options:
  - Export all metrics: Export the report with all the metrics available for this report. This option includes data for all metrics available in the widget report. For example, if you have selected 3 metrics to display in your report but there are a total of 5 metrics available, using this option will include data for all 5 metrics. The report is sent in a CSV format to the provided email address.
  - Export selected metrics: Export the metrics that you have selected for the report. For example, if you have selected 3 metrics to display in your report, using this option will include data for only the selected metrics. The report is sent in a CSV format to the provided email address.
  - Download report: Download the report in a PNG format to your computer. Note: This option considers only the data that is in the view and visible without scrolling. The downloaded file will not contain any data that is visible only after scrolling on the report page.
3. For the exported report, open the link in the received email to download the report to your computer.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > User Management > Users and Groups:
The Automation links feature automates the task of series and module assignment for groups. It allows you to manage all your group to series and group to module linking from one place.

As an admin, you can link one or more series or modules to a group so that the group members are assigned to them automatically. Once linked, all users added to the group in the future will also be assigned the linked series or modules automatically. You can also unlink the series or modules linked with the group using Automation links.

To use Automation links, the user must meet both of the following conditions:

1. They must have at least one of these permissions to access the groups:
  - Manage groups
  - Assign content via groups The groups available to you for linking depend on which groups you are collaborating on via one of these permissions.
2. They must have at least one of these permissions to assign content to modules:
  - Manage series
  - Assign content The modules of a series available to you for linking depend on which series you are collaborating on via one of these permissions.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > User Management > Users and Groups > Access Automation links:
1. Sign in to the admin site .
2. On the left navigation bar, click Account and select Automation suite . The Automation suite page is displayed. It has two tabs: Automation rules and Automation links . By default, the Automation rules tab is displayed.
3. Click Automation links .
4. On the Automation links page, you can view a list of your groups and the number of Linked series and Linked modules . The Linked modules column sorts the list by default, but you can sort any column manually by using the Up and Down sort buttons. The columns display the total number of linked series and modules against each group. If a group is not linked to any series or module, the columns display the Add icon.
5. To manage the linked series or modules, click the number or the Add icon.
6. The group panel is displayed. If you click on a number (or the + icon) from the Linked series column, the panel lists all the series you can access. Similarly, If you click on a number (or the + Add icon) from the Linked modules column, the panel lists all the modules you can access. For information on linking a group to series or modules, see Automation links: group to series linking or Automation links: group to module linking .

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Mobile App:
This article explains how learners can self-review Coaching Sessions from the Mindtickle mobile app.

1. Tap the Start Self Review button on the invitation email.

Note: You can also start the self-review of the assigned coaching sessions from the learner’s dashboard.

2. If you have not performed any self-review of the coaching session, you can tap the Start Self Review option. Alternatively, you can tap the +New Session option to start a self-review.

3. The Coaching Session form is displayed. You can preview and download the supporting files (if any) from the Activity Details section. The supporting files will help you understand the purpose of the session before review.

Note: You cannot self-review a closed coaching session.

4. Evaluate yourself based on the parameters provided. Parameters marked with an asterisk are mandatory, and you will have to evaluate yourself based on these before submitting the review.

You can also filter the review forms based on the section. From the Select section to review drop-down, select the required section, and tap Apply. This option is visible only if sections were added to coaching sessions by the admin.

5. Log the duration you conducted the session in Enter session time.

Note: This option is visible only if enabled by the admin while creating the Coaching Session.

You can also upload a file using the Upload supporting file option.

6. At any point during the review, tap Reset Parameters if you wish to reset the inputs you have provided.

7. Tap Submit self review after filling in all the parameters.

8. The pop-up displays the summary of the self-review session. Tap Confirm.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > Integrations > Benefits of Integration:
Call AI’s integration with Salesloft helps reps and managers to leverage the following Call AI functionalities and scale the effectiveness of their sales conversations:

- Review meetings quickly (skip inactivity, speaker timeline, recording speed, search in the transcript)
- Understand latest market insights and make strategic decisions (voice of the market, refine search by word in the transcript)
- Maintain compliance (recording deletion, snippet trimming)
- Learn from winning reps (setup role-based benchmarks, best practices libraries)
- Collaborate on call recordings (add comments, view action items, share recording or snippet)

- Prepare for upcoming meetings
- Self-learn and stay up to date on field calls (extensive search, email alerts, open access of all recordings, listen to meetings on the go (mobile app))

For more information about Call AI functionalities, see Call AI Overview.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > Integrations > How the Integration Works?:
Note: Call AI supports only those Salesloft packages that have the call recording feature. Salesloft package Prospect does not have the call recording feature; hence, Call AI does not support it. For more information, see Salesloft Pricing.

1. Salesloft records the meeting and makes it available on the Salesloft platform.

2. Call AI fetches the recording from the Salesloft platform and makes it available on the Call AI interface. Call AI fetches the following metadata for every recording:

- Participants name
- Participants email address
- Audio file

Note:

- Call AI discards a recording where there is a discrepancy in matching the transcript timestamp with the recording timestamp.
- Call AI fetches only those calls for which the recording data exists in Salesloft.

3. Call AI generates valuable insights, themes, and statistics for the recording. You can perform different actions such as sending private messages, taking notes, and sharing the recording with your peers and customers. For more information, see Call Recording Details.

Note:

- If the name and email address of a participant is not available in the Salesloft recording, Call AI displays the dialer number as the participant’s name. You can edit the participant's name on the recording details page.
- If you delete a recorded call from the Salesloft platform, the recording remains in Call AI. For more information about deleting such a recording from the Call AI interface, see Delete a Call Recording .

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > Integrations > Speaker Separation Type:
The speaker separation type for Salesloft is Stereo. Hence, Call AI receives the audio from Salesloft in 2 channels: one channel includes the rep, and the other includes the customer or prospect. The Stereo telephony system ensures good quality call recordings.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > Integrations > Steps to Integrate Call AI With Salesloft:
1.Log in to the Admin Site Homepage.

2. From the left panel, click Account >Settings> Call AI > Integrations.

3. Click Salesloft > Enable.

4. Sign in to Salesloft with an admin account. We recommend that you create a shared admin account for your team. It helps when an admin leaves your organization, another admin can still access the Salesloft account and configure the integration.

Call AI’s integration with Salesloft is now successful. You can start recording your meetings through Salesloft and view their recordings on the recording list page in Call AI within 5 to 10 minutes. You can use Call AI’s powerful and guided search to quickly look for a specific recording and view useful insights generated for the recording.

Note:

- Call AI does not:
  - Fetch recordings that have a duration of less than 10 seconds.
  - Import incoming calls on your Salesloft number.
  - Support Salesloft call transfer and conference.
  - Capture shared screens in Salesloft recordings.
- Call AI ignores recordings of non-Call AI users.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Setup > Site Setup:
The Mindtickle Service Status page provides information about the operational status of the Mindtickle platform, its services, and scheduled maintenance activities.

Mindtickle services may be unavailable due to a platform-wide scheduled maintenance activity or incident-specific downtime. During a scheduled maintenance activity for the entire platform, users cannot access the Mindtickle platform including the admin site, learning site, and mobile application. All emails and notifications are also paused. Similarly, if a maintenance activity is scheduled for only a specific component (for example, Analytics or Call AI), all services related to that component are unavailable during the downtime.

Visit Mindtickle Service Status (https://status.mindtickle.com) to:

- Check the current status of all Mindtickle services and components
- Stay informed about scheduled maintenance activities (service downtime)
- Get incident-related progress reports
- Subscribe to real-time status updates

Note:

- Site admins are synced as subscribers to Mindtickle Service Status updates by default. On a weekly basis, new admins are automatically synced as subscribers and deactivated admins are unsubscribed from the list.
- Subscribers receive real-time notifications whenever an incident is created, updated, or resolved, or when the operational status of a Mindtickle service or component changes. You can choose to receive notifications via emails, text messages, in-app messages, or webhooks, or get them from the Atom Feed or RSS Feed.

chunks.body:
The Mindtickle Service Status page provides information about the operational status of the Mindtickle platform, its services, and scheduled maintenance activities.

Mindtickle services may be unavailable due to a platform-wide scheduled maintenance activity or incident-specific downtime. During a scheduled maintenance activity for the entire platform, users cannot access the Mindtickle platform including the admin site, learning site, and mobile application. All emails and notifications are also paused. Similarly, if a maintenance activity is scheduled for only a specific component (for example, Analytics or Call AI), all services related to that component are unavailable during the downtime.

Visit Mindtickle Service Status (https://status.mindtickle.com) to:

- Check the current status of all Mindtickle services and components
- Stay informed about scheduled maintenance activities (service downtime)
- Get incident-related progress reports
- Subscribe to real-time status updates

Note:

- Site admins are synced as subscribers to Mindtickle Service Status updates by default. On a weekly basis, new admins are automatically synced as subscribers and deactivated admins are unsubscribed from the list.
- Subscribers receive real-time notifications whenever an incident is created, updated, or resolved, or when the operational status of a Mindtickle service or component changes. You can choose to receive notifications via emails, text messages, in-app messages, or webhooks, or get them from the Atom Feed or RSS Feed.

In case of any other concerns, please contact Mindtickle Support.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Setup > Page Builder for learning site homepages > General widgets:
| Widget | When to use | Recommendations and best practices |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Canvas (beta) | Create a custom page section with a flexible, free-form layout when the standard widgets don't give you the design control you need. | Use Canvas for high-impact areas, such as a welcome banner or a campaign section, where you want a tailored layout.As a beta feature, verify how the section renders on both web and mobile before publishing. |
| Text | Add headings, formatted text, links, and an optional button to provide context, instructions, or announcements. | Keep text concise and action-oriented; use a heading and a short paragraph rather than long blocks.Use the button to link to the most relevant series, module, hub, asset, or URL. |
| Image | Add a linked image, with an optional description and button, to add visual interest or direct learners to content. | Use high-quality images that represent the goal of the widget.Link the image or button to relevant content so the visual doubles as navigation. |
| Video | Embed an online video or upload one directly, for example a welcome message or a how-to walkthrough. | Keep videos short and purposeful; lead with the most important message.Add a descriptive title so learners know what the video covers before playing it. |
| Spotlight | Spotlight is a dynamic widget used to prominently display and promote any initiative, announcement, series, or module to learners. It functions as a marketing or promotion banner. You can add as many Spotlight widgets as you like.Example use cases:Just before an SKO (sales kickoff), the enablement team can highlight the pre-SKO work that learners need to do.Call out a specific program for learners who have just joined the company as part of their onboarding.Highlight a new video from the CEO that everyone should view. | Keep this widget at the very top, because it is used to draw attention to essential content and resources.Provide relevant information and images in the widget banners to make them intuitive and self-explanatory.Use 2–3 banners.Update or remove the banners once the business objective is accomplished. |
| Featured resources | Share links to resources within Mindtickle and external resources.Example use cases:Link to a blog, article, or YouTube video that you want your learners to go through.Link to important internal announcements.Link to an internal Mindtickle series covering company processes and policies, dos and don'ts, the holiday calendar, and so on. | Keep this widget at the bottom of the right-side widgets.Use 5–6 links.Use public or external links to avoid accessibility and reachability issues. |
| Custom HTML and CSS | Build a fully custom widget with your own HTML and CSS when no standard widget meets your design or content needs. | Always preview the widget on the Mindtickle mobile app, as custom code may not render correctly there.If it doesn't render properly on mobile, hide it from the mobile view. |
| Overall progress | Show each learner their completed modules versus assigned modules. This is a default widget on the homepage. | Keep this widget near the top so learners see their progress as soon as they land on the homepage.Hide the learner's rank information if you don't want to emphasize competition. |
| Recent achievements | Show new badges earned by learners and increases in their knowledge score. This is a default widget on the homepage. | Keep this widget visible to reinforce positive behavior and motivate learners.Pair it with the Overall progress widget for a complete snapshot of learner achievement. |

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Setup > Page Builder for learning site homepages > Series widgets:
Series widgets surface training content, such as series and modules, to learners.
chunks.body: Series widgets surface training content, such as series and modules, to learners.
chunks.headingPath: Help & Support > Help Center Home > Setup > Page Builder for learning site homepages > Series widgets
chunks.title: Best practices: For learning site homepage widgets [admin]

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Setup > Page Builder for learning site homepages > Series widgets:
| Widget | When to use | Recommendations and best practices |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Showcased | Highlight personalized and dynamic training content (series and modules) to learners. You can select content from a list or configure filters so content is selected automatically. | Use filters to keep the widget dynamic, so it stays relevant without manual updates.Give the widget a clear title that signals what learners will find in it. |
| Featured themes | Displays themes across your site, with each theme showcasing thematically linked content. Themes are tags applied to modules, which can span multiple series, and they appear as theme tiles in the widget.Example use cases:Create themes based on skills or competencies to help learners improve in their job. For example, under a "Negotiation" theme, learners would find all the content for improving negotiation skills.Create themes based on roles to help learners quickly navigate to the content relevant to their role.Create themes for the different stages of the sales life cycle to help learners find content for the stage where they are struggling the most to close the deal. | Add this widget if the enablement team wants to group content by the broad themes they are trying to drive and help reps locate them faster.Keep this widget near the top (within the first four widgets) so reps can locate the themes.Use 10–15 tags per theme or tag category.Use 4–6 themes. |
| Upcoming ILTs | Give learners a calendar view of their live and upcoming instructor-led training (ILT) sessions so they can enroll in or join sessions without locating them in individual series and modules. | Add this widget if your program relies heavily on ILT sessions, so learners never miss a session.Keep it near the top during periods with many scheduled sessions. |
| Continue | Displays all of the learner's in-progress modules, with the most recently accessed first. Learners can click a module to quickly resume their progress.Example use cases:Help learners quickly resume the training content they have been going through.Nudge learners toward unfinished modules before they start new ones.Reduce the time it takes to locate the training modules they have been going through. | Add this widget, as it reduces the time learners take to locate the training modules they have been going through.Keep this widget near the top (within the first four widgets) so learners can quickly view unfinished training and resume their progress.Improves rep engagement as well as content completion. |
| Required | Displays modules that the admin has assigned to the learner, with module relevance set to "Required." These modules are mandatory for completion and are sorted by most recently assigned first.Example use cases:For "P1" priority trainings that are mandatory to complete.Mandatory HR trainings, such as Code of Conduct training. | Add this widget if enablement teams want to highlight mandatory training content upfront so learners don't miss it.Keep this widget in the middle. |
| Urgent | Displays modules that are due soon for the learner or have recently turned overdue. A module shows up in this widget from 15 days before the due date until 7 days past the due date, after which it is removed from the widget.Example use cases:For "P0" priority tasks that are time-bound and mandatory.Access and company compliance-related trainings. | If on-time completions are important to your program, this widget is essential.Keep this widget in the middle. |
| Trending | Displays the 20 modules most accessed by all learners across the platform in the last 30 days. The widget considers modules that learners have access to and that are assigned by the admin or self-assigned by the learner from public series.Example use cases:Peer learning: fosters a learning culture driven by peer influence.Bring parity: use it for courses where you want to bring parity within the org. For example, if 90% of users have taken a training on Salesforce Lightning and 10% have not, seeing the module trend may prompt the remaining 10% to take it. | Keep this widget near the bottom to give learners a glimpse of which training modules others are going through, to enhance peer learning. |
| Take action | Displays missions and assessments across all series that the learner has completed but failed (could not meet the passing criteria). The widget displays these modules only if reattempt is enabled by the admin, and only for assigned modules, not public modules.It lists the modules in this sort order: last completed module first. Learners can click a module in the widget to go to the module and reattempt it.Example use cases:Ensure that learners who failed missions and assessments get another opportunity to reattempt and pass them. | Keep this widget in the middle. |
| Pinned series | Show all the series that the learner has pinned, giving them quick access to the series they care about most. | Add this widget to give learners control over their own quick-access list.Pair it with Explore by series so learners can both pin and rediscover series. |
| What's new in public | Displays newly released or updated public series and modules.Example use cases:Reduces the time learners need to find content created by the enablement team and made available publicly. Instead of browsing through multiple pages, learners quickly see what's new and updated in public series and modules. | Keep this widget near the bottom of the homepage.Learners can discover new publicly available training programs to enhance their knowledge and skills.Learners can be encouraged to take trainings beyond the ones assigned by the admin. |
| What's new in assigned | Displays all the modules and series newly assigned by the admin or updated in the last 30 days, with the most recently assigned first.Example use cases:The HR team can bring learners' attention to a newly developed module to achieve a high rate of compliance.Highlight a new information security policy update that everyone should complete. | This is the ideal widget if you want to keep learners up to date with newly assigned or updated trainings.Keep this widget near the top (within the first four widgets). |
| Top-rated series | Displays the top 10 highly rated series in descending order of their average ratings. This widget considers all types of series: public, assigned, self-assigned, and scoped public. For each series, it shows the overall average rating and the total number of learners who rated the series.Example use cases:Highlight and promote your best series.Use your top-rated series to replicate their success for other series.Establish benchmarks for what makes a series and its content great. | Add this widget if the enablement team wants to promote peer learning by showcasing the training programs that are popular among learners.Keep this widget in the middle. |
| Top-rated modules (beta) | Displays the top 20 highly rated modules (course, quick update, and assessment) in descending order of their average ratings. Only modules with at least 10 ratings qualify. | Use this widget to surface proven, well-received modules and encourage further learning.As a beta feature, contact your CSM to enable module rating and feedback for your site first. |
| Explore by series | Displays the last 10 public and assigned series, sorted by most recently accessed (or alphabetically if the learner hasn't accessed any series). This is a default widget on the homepage.Example use cases:Provide learners with quick access to their 10 most recently accessed series. | Keep this widget near the bottom of the homepage so learners get quick access to their recently accessed series. |

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Setup > Page Builder for learning site homepages > Asset Hub widgets:
Asset Hub widgets surface assets and hubs to learners. They are available only if you have purchased Asset Hub.
chunks.body: Asset Hub widgets surface assets and hubs to learners. They are available only if you have purchased Asset Hub.
chunks.headingPath: Help & Support > Help Center Home > Setup > Page Builder for learning site homepages > Asset Hub widgets
chunks.title: Best practices: For learning site homepage widgets [admin]

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Setup > Page Builder for learning site homepages > Asset Hub widgets:
| Widget | When to use | Recommendations and best practices |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Multiple assets | Add multiple assets by selecting them from a list or by attributes, to surface a curated or dynamic set of assets. | Use attribute-based selection to keep the asset set dynamic and current.Group related assets in one widget so learners find them together. |
| Single asset | Highlight one important asset with its title, description, and engagement stats. | Use this widget to spotlight a must-read asset, such as a key pitch deck or policy document.Show engagement stats to signal the asset's relevance and popularity. |
| Featured or selected hubs | Show featured hubs or specific hubs you select, to tailor hub visibility on the homepage. | Feature the hubs that are most relevant to the audience for this homepage.Review the selection periodically so it reflects current priorities. |
| All hubs | Display all the hubs the learner can access, sorted alphabetically, so frequently used hubs stay handy. | Use this widget when learners rely on many hubs and need quick access to all of them.If you only want to surface a few, use Featured or selected hubs instead. |
| Top-rated assets | Display the highest-rated assets among the hubs shared with the learner. | Use this widget to guide learners toward proven, high-quality assets.Pair it with Recently added assets to balance trusted and fresh content. |
| Updated assets you may like | Display recently updated assets that the learner has bookmarked or downloaded, where there has been an update in the last 30 days. | Use this widget to bring learners back to assets they care about when those assets change.Especially useful for fast-moving content such as pricing or product sheets. |
| Recently added assets | Display assets recently added to the hubs (by the admin) that the learner can access. | Use this widget to help learners discover new content as it is published.Keep it near the bottom as a discovery aid rather than a primary action. |
| Recently viewed assets | Display the assets the learner has recently viewed, for quick return access. | Use this widget to reduce the time learners spend relocating assets they were working with.Helpful for learners who reference the same assets repeatedly during customer conversations. |
| Bookmarked assets | Show all the assets the learner has bookmarked, giving them a personal quick-access list. | Add this widget to let learners curate their own shortlist of important assets.Pair it with Recently viewed assets for complete personal asset access. |
| Plays | Show plays to your learners, surfacing guided, scenario-based content directly on the homepage. | Use this widget when plays are central to your enablement strategy.Place it where the relevant audience will see it, such as a role-specific homepage. |

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Setup > FAQs:
Our knowledge base, including help articles, release notes, video tutorials, webinar recordings, FAQs, and monthly newsletters, is available in English on the Mindtickle Help Site. To translate the content into your preferred language, we recommend using your browser’s translation feature.

Depending on your browser, access the following links to learn how to translate content on a web page:

- Google Chrome Change Chrome languages and translate webpages
- Mozilla Firefox Use Firefox in another language
- Safari Translate a web page in Safari on Mac
- Microsoft Edge Use Microsoft Translator in Microsoft Edge Browser

chunks.title: What to do if a user cannot log in to Mindtickle via SSO?

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Setup > FAQs > Troubleshooting SSO Login Issues:
- Check if SSO Login is Enabled for the Site Mindtickle currently supports SSO login through Identity Providers (IdPs) such as SAML , Salesforce (Classic) , Salesforce (Lightning) , Google , Microsoft Entra ID (formerly called Azure Active Directory) , Veeva , JSON Web Token (JWT) , ADFS , and OpenID . The SSO options available on your site depend on the IdPs your organization has integrated with Mindtickle. Check if the IdP is configured correctly on your site. For more information, see Setting Up Single Sign-On (SSO) in Mindtickle .
- Confirm if the IdP Certificate is Valid To avoid service disruption, ensure your IdP certificate is valid. Depending on your IdP, the certificate may expire up to 30 days in advance. In that case, generate a new certificate and replace the expiring certificate with the new one. For more information, see Setting Up Single Sign-On (SSO) in Mindtickle . Note : If the certificate is valid, check if it matches the one configured on the Mindtickle platform. For any further assistance, contact Mindtickle Support .
- Check if the User has Access to Mindtickle via the IdP Platform Contact Mindtickle Support to confirm. The user cannot log in to Mindtickle using SSO if they do not have access to Mindtickle via the IdP platform.
- Check if the User is Added to the Mindtickle Platform SSO login fails if:
  - A user not added to the Mindtickle platform, tries to log in via SSO (when the setting Invited Users can Sign Up is enabled and Email Domain Restrictions is disabled). For more information, see Account Settings > Security and Integrations . Note : You can add users from the Mindtickle platform or a user management system .
  - A user not added to the Mindtickle platform, tries to log in via SSO (when the setting Invited Users can Sign Up is disabled and Email Domain Restrictions is disabled).
  - A new user not added to the platform and whose email domain does not match the email domain configured on the platform, tries to log in via SSO. This is applicable when the settings Invited Users can Sign Up and Email Domain Restrictions are enabled.
  - A user added to the platform, but their email domain does not match the email domain configured on the platform, tries to log in via SSO.
  - A user added to the Mindtickle platform, but is in the Deactivated state, tries to log in via SSO. To activate deactivated users, see Restore a User .
- Check the User's Email Address On Mindtickle as well as the IdP platform. The email address used to log in through SSO should match the email address associated with the user on the Mindtickle platform. To view the email address associated with the user’s Mindtickle account, see User Profile Page Overview .
- Clear the Browser Cache and Cookies and Log In Again The browser sometimes continues to use outdated files or information. This may be one of the reasons why SSO login fails. Clearing your cache and cookies can resolve this issue. For more information, see how to clear the browser cache on Chrome , Firefox , Safari , and Microsoft Edge .
- Log In Using an Incognito Window The browser’s cache, cookies, site data, or existing information is not saved on your device when you use incognito mode. This ensures you don’t use outdated information in the SSO login flow. For more information, see how to use an incognito window in Chrome , Firefox , Safari , or Microsoft Edge .

Help & Support > Help Center Home > User Management > System and Audit Logs > Audit logs:
Audit Logs store information about admin and system-driven actions performed in Mindtickle. They also provide detailed insights, such as when the action was performed, the type of action (admin or system-driven), and its impact.

The following are a few examples of actions that are recorded in Audit Logs:

- User invited to a module by an admin or an automation rule
- User added to a group by an admin or an automation rule
- User added to the platform
- User deactivated
- User profile updated
- User archived modules

Note: Audit logs provide the audit information only for a select admin and system actions set. For more information, see Actions recorded in Audit logs.

With system logs, it becomes super easy for you to track and monitor the system and admin activity on the platform. You can quickly and easily access these logs, identify the root cause of issues, and troubleshoot them by taking the necessary remedial actions.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > User Management > System and Audit Logs > Overview:
Audit Logs store a chronological record of administrative activities or system-driven actions performed in Mindtickle. It also provides detailed information about each recorded action.

As a site owner, you can use audit logs to review:

- The list of actions performed on the Mindtickle platform
- The description of each action
- The type of the action (admin action or system-driven event)
- Details of the admin or system responsible for the action
- The entity (user, group, module, or series) on which the action was performed
- The entities (users, groups, series, or modules) impacted by the action
- The date and time on which the action was performed

This article further explains the types of actions recorded in audit logs and the benefits of using audit logs.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > User Management > System and Audit Logs > Actions recorded in audit logs:
Audit Logs track actions performed on users, groups, series, and modules. The following is a list of actions currently recorded:

| Audit Category | Actions Recorded |
| --- | --- |
| User Audit | User added to the platformUser name/email/profile updatedUser activated/deactivated/restoredRole assigned to the userUser username replacedUser timezone updatedUser relationship updatedUser role updatedUser impersonated |
| Group Audit | User added to/removed from a groupGroup created/updated/deletedGroup collaborators updated |
| Module Invitation Audit | User invited to moduleUser removed from module |
| Archived Module Audit | User archived module |
| Series Invitation Audit | User invited to seriesUser removed from seriesUser subscribed to seriesUser unsubscribed from series |
| Profile Management Audit | Profile field created/updated/deletedRelationship field created/updated/deleted |

Note:

- The records are available from the day and time the Audit Logs feature is deployed in Mindtickle (Aug 16, 2022). Past data is unavailable and cannot be retrieved.
- The system stores audit logs recorded during the last 365 days (from the present day). For more information on how to take a backup of logs that are about to expire, see Export Audit Logs .
- Audit Logs will be released as a complete feature in phases. Currently, the feature records audit information for only the events listed above. Audit information about other events related to series, modules, ILT sessions, account settings, and email templates will be available in the subsequent releases.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > User Management > System and Audit Logs > Benefits of audit logs:
- Track System and Admin Activity Audit logs help you track and monitor the activity on the platform, quickly diagnose an issue, identify its cause, and take the necessary remedial actions to troubleshoot it.
- Maintain Protocol and Transparency within Your Organization If multiple admins manage your site, you can use data from the audit logs to track down who was responsible for a particular action. Creating awareness about this ensures admins follow company protocol. So you can maintain transparency and accountability within your organization.
- Reduce Support Involvement and Dependency Using audit logs, you become self-sufficient. You can easily access and review the records without involving or depending on the support team at Mindtickle. This ensures you save time, make informed decisions faster, and thereby improve the efficiency and performance of your organization.

For more information about accessing the feature and viewing audit logs on the Mindtickle platform, filtering the event records, and exporting them, see View, Filter, and Export Audit Logs.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > User Management > System and Audit Logs:
Audit logs record administrative activities and system actions performed on the platform. These records are beneficial when you need to investigate user management, content assignment, or profile management issues, evaluate system performance, track an event trail, or detect admin malpractices on the platform.

As a site owner, you may be interested in reviewing a specific action associated with a particular user, group, module, or series.

For example, if a user is added to the platform, you may want to find out which admin added the user and the date and time on which the user was added to the platform.

Or, if multiple site owners manage your site, you may want to track down which admin assigned a role incorrectly to a user. Or, if a user was assigned a module, you may want to know whether the user was invited to the module by an admin or a system action. Or, you may want to examine the actions performed on the platform within a specific date range.

You can access this information and share it with other stakeholders using Audit Logs.

This article explains how you can access audit logs, view event details, apply filters, search for an event, and export the logs for further analysis.
