Help & Support > Help Center Home > Asset Hub > Admin > Create a new hub overview page:
You can create a new hub overview page from the following places:

- In the admin site sidebar, click Assets > Hub overview pages to open the page that lists all hub overview pages. Click Create overview page in the page header to create a new one.
- In the admin site sidebar, click Assets > Hubs to open the page that lists all hubs. Click to open the hub to which you want to add an overview page. Next, click Add overview page in the header and select Create new in the dropdown menu. You can also select an existing overview page from the list to add it to this hub.

The Create new page option allows you to create a new overview page from scratch. You can customize the page using the system-available asset hub templates and widgets. Select a template from the pre-built templates available in the left panel to get started. Currently, the Mindtickle platform provides 5 pre-built templates that can be used as asset hub overview pages.

After selecting the template, click the Use this template button. A message appears confirming the successful creation of the page.

Once you select the template, the page builder displays. You can modify the page name mentioned in the existing overview page section. Add widgets available in the left navigation panel or modify the widgets already available within the template. The page displays Draft status until it is published. For more information on customizing the overview page and adding widgets, see Customize Hub Overview Page and Page Builder Overview.

Once the widgets selection and other changes are complete, the draft is saved automatically. You can publish the overview page.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Asset Hub > Admin > Multiple assets:
You can select the Multiple assets widget under the Asset Hub section on the left panel to customize the asset hub overview page or play. You can drag and drop the widget from the left panel to the right pane, and the New multiple assets widget page is displayed. The page consists of 2 tabs:

- Assets - This allows you to select specific or dynamic assets.
- Configuration - This allows you to configure the display settings of the assets within the hub page or play.

Content tab

- Asset selection : Select assets using either from the list or through filters. Additionally, following two checkbox settings appear once you select assets:
  - Open in a new tab : Lets you define whether the asset opens in a new tab for the learners/reps.
  - Keep widget visible even if some selected hubs or attributes are deleted : This setting is available only for assets selected through filters and allows admins to define the widget’s behavior if the configured filter criteria become invalid (e.g., due to the deletion of attributes or hubs). Select this setting to keep the widget visible to learners based on the remaining criteria, or unselect it to hide the widget entirely. When editing an existing widget, admins are informed if any missing filter values impact the original filter criteria.
- Widget description
  - Use this field to add both the title and description for the widget.
  - Use various text formatting options in the description toolbar to customize the description text, including heading styles, text and background colors, text alignment, linking, and listing options. Tip : Use the improved link option in the toolbar to link the text to a series, module, hub, asset, or to any website/webpage.

Settings tab

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Asset Hub > Admin > Multiple assets > Content tab > Add from list:
The Add from list option allows you to select assets within the hub or play based on their significance and display them in the widget under the page. The grouping of assets within a widget allows you to display the critical assets you want your reps to focus on.

From the New multiple assets widget page, click the Add from list button to view the assets you have access to. You can further filter and sort the assets by using any of the available options.

- Use the Hubs dropdown to search a specific hub or multiple hubs and select a single hub or multiple hubs to view the assets available under those hubs. Once selected, you can click the Apply button. The total number of chosen hubs display next to the Apply button. You can clear the selection by clicking the Clear All button.
- Use the Attributes dropdown to filter the assets based on attributes. The attributes lists under the specific attributes category. Click Apply to filter the assets.
- Use the Asset type dropdown to filter the assets by their type, such as PDF, video, PPT, and image.
- Search the assets based on their usage . The usage can be Internal , External , or All .

Note:

- You can view only those assets you can access and make them available in a widget. Once the page is published, the reps can view those assets from the widget they can access.
- If there are more than 50 assets in a hub, based on the attributes selected, only the top 50 assets in a hub are displayed to the reps.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Asset Hub > Admin > Featured or selected hubs:
The Featured or selected hubs widget allows admins to control which hubs are displayed on a page. You can either show all hubs marked as featured or choose specific hubs to highlight based on the page’s purpose. Admins can "feature" a hub using the "Feature this hub" option in the hub header or via asset settings → Featured hubs.

This widget can be added to learning site homepages, as well as series and hub overview pages.

When you add or edit the widget, you'll see two configuration tabs: Content and Settings.

Content tab

In the Content tab, you can choose how the hubs will be displayed:

- Featured hubs : Displays all hubs that are marked as featured across the site. No additional configuration is needed.
- Selected hubs : Allows you to manually select and display specific hubs. When this option is selected, you can:
  - Select specific hubs : Choose up to 25 hubs to display. A search field helps you find hubs by name. Note : Learners will only see the hubs they have access to.
  - Add a description (optional): Provide context or guidance by adding a short description that appears below the widget title.

Settings tab

In the Settings tab, you can customize the widget title:

- Rename the widget to match its use case or audience (e.g., Sales Enablement Hubs , Onboarding Resources ).
- By default, the title will reflect the selected hub configuration, either Featured hubs or Selected hubs .

Learner experience

Learners can hover over a hub to view its description and the number of assets it contains. Clicking a hub opens it, allowing them to explore the assets inside.Note: Learners will only see hubs they have access to.

Content tab

- Button position: This option is available if you added the button in the Content tab. This setting lets you define the button’s position in the widget: left, right, or center.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Setup > Overview pages:
With the overview pages feature, admins can create and configure an overview page that becomes the landing page for the series to which it is linked. An overview page is an immersive experience made up of widgets, through which admins can highlight important content and action items in a series to learners. The page helps you set context and enable findability for the series and its content.

This feature consists of the following functionalities:

- Page Builder: Use it to create and configure overview pages with the help of templates and widgets.
- Series overview pages: This is the central place where admins can find all the series overview pages they created. You can view and manage the pages, such as edit, publish, deactivate, and delete pages.

Note: This feature is also available for hubs in Asset Hub. For more information, see Hub overview page.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Setup > Overview pages > Permissions and access:
To create and manage pages, you must have the Manage Pages (MANAGE_PAGES) permission. By default, two admin-level users — site owners and enablement admins — have this permission with universal access. You can also assign this permission to a custom role with the help of your CSM.

The permission allows you to create, edit, and view pages, as well as manage pages: activate, deactivate, publish, and delete pages.

For more information, see Roles and permissions in Mindtickle.

You need to perform the following three steps to create an overview page and link it to a series:

1. From Training > Series overview pages in the admin site sidebar, click the Create new page button to get started with creating a new page .
2. Create and configure the page with the Page Builder and publish it.

Once the page is linked with a series, it is immediately available to learners when they access the series on the learning site.

You can also use the Series overview pages page to manage your overview pages, such as edit, publish, deactivate, and delete pages.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Setup > Overview pages > Manage overview pages > Page actions:
You can take the following actions on a page depending on its status (draft, active, or inactive):

- On draft pages: Edit, duplicate, publish & activate, and delete it.
- On active pages: Edit, duplicate, and deactivate it.
- On inactive pages: Edit, duplicate, and activate, and delete it.

Note:

- Only active pages can be linked to and used as an overview page for a series.
- Only draft and inactive pages can be deleted. To delete an active page, you must first deactivate it.

To take an action on a page, click the More Options icon for a page.

Information on all available actions:

- Edit: To make any changes to the page. It opens the page in the Page Builder for editing.
- Duplicate: Duplicates the page and all of its content.
- Publish and Activate: To publish and activate the page so that you can use it for a series. This option is available only for draft pages.
- Activate: To activate the page so that you can use it for a series. This option is available only for inactive pages.
- Deactivate: To deactivate an active page. Use this option when you want to remove the page from any series where it is linked, but not delete the page permanently.
- Delete: To delete the page and its content (widgets and any other data) permanently. Once deleted, the page cannot be restored .

- On draft pages: Edit, duplicate, publish & activate, and delete it.
- On active pages: Edit, duplicate, and deactivate it.
- On inactive pages: Edit, duplicate, and activate, and delete it.

Note:

- Only active pages can be linked to and used as an overview page for a series.
- Only draft and inactive pages can be deleted. To delete an active page, you must first deactivate it.

To take an action on a page, click the More Options icon for a page.

Information on all available actions:

- Edit: To make any changes to the page. It opens the page in the Page Builder for editing.
- Duplicate: Duplicates the page and all of its content.
- Publish and Activate: To publish and activate the page so that you can use it for a series. This option is available only for draft pages.
- Activate: To activate the page so that you can use it for a series. This option is available only for inactive pages.
- Deactivate: To deactivate an active page. Use this option when you want to remove the page from any series where it is linked, but not delete the page permanently.
- Delete: To delete the page and its content (widgets and any other data) permanently. Once deleted, the page cannot be restored .

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Setup > Overview pages > Page Builder widgets > General widgets > Custom HTML and CSS widget:
Add your own HTML and CSS code to create a custom widget. You can add as many Custom HTML and CSS widgets on a page as you like.

HTML and CSS tabs

- Add your code: Add your CSS code separately from the HTML for better organization and easier editing. Alternatively, you can add both the HTML and CSS code in the HTML tab. Note: You can add up to 100 KB of code in total, including both HTML and CSS.
- Beautify: Click Beautify to format the code.
- The enlarged coding experience is available whether you are adding a new widget or editing an existing one.

Settings tab

- Title: (Optional) Add a title for the widget.
- Widget height: Select Auto , Fixed , or Custom height for the widget. The Custom option lets you define a minimum and maximum height. For the maximum height, enter "auto" to auto-adjust the image height.
- Widget layout: Set the width for the height defined in the previous setting. The default setting is Landscape (5:4 aspect ratio). Other options are: Ultrawide (4:1), Widescreen (16:9), Square (1:1), and Portrait (4:5). Note that the widget layout option is not available if your height setting is set to Fixed .

Note: The Custom HTML and CSS widget may not always function correctly on the Mindtickle mobile app due to limitations. We recommend testing it on the mobile app after adding it to ensure it works as intended. If issues arise, consider removing it from the series or hub overview page.

Here's what the configured widget looks like. The widget adds a scroll if the content exceeds the maximum defined height.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Setup > Overview pages > Page Builder widgets > General widgets > Image widget:
The Image widget lets you add content in the form of an image, which can be linked. It also provides an option to add a button with a link to the widget, so you can add two links to this widget: one to the image and another to the button. You can use the Image widget for learning site homepages, series overview pages, and hub overview pages. You can add as many Image widgets on a page as you like.

Content tab

- Add image: Choose from the gallery of previously uploaded images or upload a new image. Ideally, the thumbnail should represent the goal and content of the widget.
- Description (optional): Add description text that provides context or information on the image, the image link, or both.
- Link to (optional): Add a link to the image. Learners can then click the image to open the link. Link to a URL or Mindtickle content (series, module, hub, or asset). Use the search option to look for the Mindtickle content that you want to link to.
- Add button: Select the checkbox to add a linked button to the widget.
  - Button text: Call-to-action (CTA) name for the button.
  - Link to: Link to a URL or Mindtickle content (series, module, hub, or asset). Use the search option to look for the Mindtickle content that you want to link to. Note: Asset Hub customers can also link to assets based on conditions or filters.

Settings tab

- Customize widget size and appearance: These options give you greater flexibility in defining the widget size and appearance. You can configure the widget height, widget layout (aspect ratio), image fit, description placement, and button placement.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Setup > Overview pages > Page Builder widgets > General widgets > Text widget:
Create a text widget with options for a heading, links, and formatted text. Additionally, you can add a button to the widget and link it to Mindtickle content (series, module, hub, or asset) or any URL. You can add as many Text widgets on a page as you like.

Content tab

- Text content: Write the content of the widget in the text box. You can also copy and paste text here. Use the text formatting toolbar to format the text to your liking. For instance, use the Link option in the toolbar to link to Mindtickle content (series, module, hub, or asset) or any URL.
- Add button (optional): Select the checkbox to add a linked button to the widget.
  - Button text: Call-to-action (CTA) name for the button.
  - Link to: Link to a URL or Mindtickle content (series, module, hub, or asset). Use the search option to look for the Mindtickle content that you want to link to. Note: Asset Hub customers can also link to assets based on conditions or filters. Learners are shown the list of all assets with the selected conditions applied. For details, see Customize hub overview pages and play pages .

Settings tab

- Max height: Use this setting to define the maximum height for the widget. Text is truncated if it exceeds the height specified here, and learners click View more to see the full text.
- Button position: This option is available if you added a button in the Content tab. It lets you define the button's position in the widget: left, right, or center.

Note: The max height setting is currently unsupported on the Mindtickle mobile app. As a result, this widget may display correctly on the web but not render properly on the mobile app.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Setup > Overview pages > Page Builder widgets > General widgets > Video widget:
Embed any online video or upload one directly. You can add as many Video widgets on a page as you like.

Configure the widget as follows:

Content tab

- Add video: Click this button to upload the video that you want to use in this widget. Once the video is uploaded, you can replace it with another one if needed. Additionally, you can upload a custom thumbnail for the video. If the default thumbnail is not visually appealing, you can upload a new thumbnail or choose from already uploaded thumbnails. You can add custom thumbnails only for manually uploaded videos, not for embedded videos. Note: Custom thumbnails for videos are currently not supported on the mobile app.
- Description (optional): Add a description for the video. You can also use various text formatting options, such as heading styles, text color, and font size. For example, you can add both a heading and a description for the video using this single field. Later, in the Settings tab, you can define the description placement (either above or below the video).

Settings tab

- Widget height: Select Auto , Fixed , or Custom height for the widget. The Custom option lets you define a minimum and maximum height. For the maximum height, enter "auto" to auto-adjust the image height.
- Widget layout: Set the width for the height defined in the previous setting. The default setting is Landscape (5:4 aspect ratio). Other options are: Ultrawide (4:1), Widescreen (16:9), Square (1:1), and Portrait (4:5). Note that the widget layout option is not available if your height setting is set to Fixed .
- Description placement: Select whether to place the description text above or below the video in the widget.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Setup > Overview pages > Page Builder widgets > Series widgets > Trending widget:
The Trending widget is a configurable widget available for learning site homepages and series overview pages. It surfaces the modules most accessed by all users in the last 30 days, sorted by views. You can further refine what is displayed by applying filters based on:

- Module relevance: Required, Optional, or None (no module relevance set)
- Completion status: Not started, in progress, or completed

You can add up to five Trending widgets on a page, each with its own title and filter settings. The widget dynamically adjusts its layout based on placement and can be edited anytime to update its configuration. Rename the widget to clearly signal its purpose (for example, "Completed mandatory training," "In-progress optional learning," or "Discover new content").

For details on how to configure this widget, see Add dynamic widgets to learning site homepages.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Setup > Overview pages > Page Builder widgets > Series widgets > Take action widget:
Displays missions and assessments across all series that the learner has completed but failed (could not meet the passing criteria). The widget displays these modules only if reattempt is enabled by the admin, and only for assigned modules, not public modules.

The widget is displayed to a learner only if they have failed a mission or assessment and need to reattempt it. It lists the modules in this sort order: last completed module first.

Learners can click a module in the widget to go to the module and reattempt it. You can add only one Take action widget on a page. The widget requires no configuration.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Setup > Overview pages > Page Builder widgets > Series widgets > Showcased widget:
Showcased is a dynamic widget that is used to showcase (highlight) personalized and dynamic training content (series and modules) to learners. It enhances the overall learning experience while simplifying content management for admins.

You can add content (series or modules) to the widget either by selecting the series or modules from a list, or by configuring filters based on which series or modules are selected automatically.

Note: Whether you add only series, only modules, or a mix of both, learners see up to 20 series and modules in the widget, and only those to which they have access.

You can add as many individual Showcased widgets to the overview page as you like.

Configure the widget: This widget is also available for learning site homepages, and you configure it the same way for overview pages. For detailed instructions, see Add dynamic widgets to learning site homepages.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Setup > Overview pages > Page Builder widgets > Hub widgets > Single asset widget:
Highlight one important asset over others as a single entity. You can configure the widget to show the asset description, engagement stats, asset owner name, and last-modified information.

Content tab

- Select asset: Use the button to select the single asset that you want to display in the widget. Once you have selected the asset, you can define whether the asset opens in a new tab for the reps. Note: You can view and add only those assets you have access to. Once the page is published, reps can view the asset if they have access to it.
- Description: Add both a title and description, or only the description, for the widget. Use the text formatting toolbar to format the text to your liking.

Settings tab

- Thumbnail placement: Select whether the asset thumbnail appears to the left, to the right, or above the asset metadata information.
- Asset information: Choose the asset metadata information that you want to display in the widget. You can show or hide the asset description, engagement stats, last-modified date, and asset owner information.
- Information alignment: Adjust the alignment of both the asset thumbnail and its metadata information. For the selected asset, the widget displays the thumbnail alongside its metadata, and you can align both elements to the left, right, or center as you prefer.

Tip: In addition to aligning the thumbnail and metadata, you can align the widget description text (under the Content tab) using the text formatting toolbar. This ensures all content within the widget is aligned to your preference.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Setup > Overview pages > Create an overview page:
1. In the admin site sidebar, click Training > Series overview pages to view all series overview pages.Similarly, click Assets > Hub overview pages to view all hub overview pages.
2. The Series overview pages listing page opens. If no pages are created, click Create overview page to start creating one.
3. The Page Builder opens with the template picker page. From the two sections, select a template depending on whether you are creating the page for a series or hub (Asset Hub). You can select one of the pre-built templates or a blank one to start from scratch. When you click a pre-built template, the Page Builder displays a preview of the preconfigured widgets and content of the template page. Click Use this template to use the template as a basis that you can further customize on the next page.Note: When you create a page using a pre-built series or hub template, the page can only be used for that use case.
4. On the next page, your page is created in a draft state. Hover over the page name for the option to edit the name given to this overview page. Be sure to provide a meaningful name so it is easier for you and other page creators (site owners and enablement admins) to know what it is for.This is the page where you set up your page by adding and configuring widgets. All changes you make are automatically saved to the draft.See this section for a list of all available widgets and their use and configuration. The amount of page configuration that you need to do depends on the template you selected. For a pre-built template, you can make changes to the already added widgets as well as add new ones. For a blank template, you need to add widgets fresh.
5. To add a widget, drag it from the widget library (left) and drop it on the canvas. Before dropping it on the canvas, move it around to trigger a dotted blue bar on which you can drop it.Widgets are displayed vertically in rows, and one row can have a maximum of 4 widgets side by side. You can add widgets above or below a widget, and on either side of a widget (to form a row of widgets next to each other).For example, the following screenshot shows adding a Text widget to the left of a Video widget.
6. To continue the example in the previous step, once you add two widgets side by side, it would look as follows:
7. Once you have added and configured a widget, you can take various actions on the widget and the widget row. Widget actions let you make changes to the widget. Row actions let you make changes to the row (which can have 4 widgets) to help you structure the order of widgets on the page. Hover over a widget to view the options as well as the widget's name (type).
8. The following widget actions are available:
  - Edit: Edit and reconfigure the widget.
  - Hide: Hide the widget from the overview page for all learners. This option is useful when you want to retain the widget for future use and not delete it.
  - Move (horizontally): Use the left and right arrows to move the widget. This option is available only when a row has more than one widget.
  - Delete: Delete the widget (content and configuration) permanently from the page. If you delete a widget from an active and published page, changes reflect to learners when you publish the page again. Important: Proceed with caution; this action cannot be undone.
9. The following row actions are available:
  - Drag (vertically): Drag the row vertically across the canvas. This option is fast but the same as the Move option listed below. Use it to organize the order of rows on the page.
  - Move (vertically): Use the up and down arrows to move the row vertically.
  - Delete: Delete the row and both of its widgets (including their content and configuration) permanently from the page. If you delete a row from an active and published page, changes reflect to learners when you publish the page again. Important: Proceed with caution; this action cannot be undone.
10. Once you have added and configured the widgets, you can create sections (group multiple widget rows) and enable the page outline for the sections. For more information, see the Page sections and outline section.
11. Once you have made all changes, click Publish in the upper-right corner to activate and publish the page.
12. To make this page available to learners, you must link it with a series. Only then will learners see it as the Overview tab when they access the series. For information on how to link the overview page with a series, see Page Builder and overview pages.
13. You can manage this and your other overview pages from (More options) > Manage pages in the upper-right corner. For more information, see View and manage overview pages.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Setup > Overview pages > Create an overview page > Page sections and outline:
This section provides information on how to create sections for an overview page and enable the page outline.

- Sections: Group multiple widget rows into a section to integrate the rows. Sections are useful for keeping multiple related widgets together and occupy less screen space compared to independent widget rows.
- Page outline (optional): After adding and naming sections, you can enable the page outline, which creates links to all sections on the page. The page outline is like a table of contents; learners can click the section links in the outline to quickly navigate to the sections. You can display the outline on the left or right of the page. Additionally, and only for Sales Plays pages, you can display the outline at the top.

There are no limits to the number of sections you can add on a page and the number of widget rows you can add to a section.

This feature is available for all types of overview pages: series, hubs, and Sales Plays. It is particularly useful for Sales Plays.

Note: You can also add sections and create a page outline for learning site homepages. For more information, see Create and manage custom homepages for the learning site.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Setup > Overview pages > Create an overview page > Page sections and outline:
1. Open an overview page for editing in the Page Builder.
2. First, convert any widget row into a section. To do this, hover over a widget row and click the icon.
3. Once a widget row is converted to a section, it is highlighted in yellow. In the upper-right corner, provide a meaningful name for the section that is easy for learners to understand. Hover over the section to view section-related options (actions) on the right; hover over the widget row to view its options on the left.
4. To add multiple widget rows into a section, drag and drop any widget row into the section you created. The UI displays a blue highlight where you can drop the widget row. You can add it above or below an existing row in the section.
5. Once you have added multiple widget rows into a section, you can take various actions using the options for the section, the added rows, and the individual widgets in each row. The options appear when you hover over them. Options for a section appear on the right and on the left for a widget row. Widget actions appear above it.
6. The following options are available for the entire section, the widget rows, and the widgets in each row:
  - Section options:
    - Drag (vertically): Drag the section vertically across the canvas. This option is fast but the same as the Move option listed below. Use it to organize the order of rows on the page.
    - Remove separator line: Remove the gray separator line that appears between two widget rows. Use this option to integrate the rows seamlessly.
    - Move (vertically): Use the up and down arrows to move the section vertically.
    - Delete: Delete the entire section (including the widget rows and the widgets in each row) permanently from the page. If you delete a section from an active and published page, changes reflect to learners when you publish the page again. Important: Proceed with caution; this action cannot be undone.
    - Tooltip: Provides a quick overview of the sections feature.
  - Widget row options:
    - Drag (vertically): Drag the row vertically across the canvas. This option is fast but the same as the Move option listed below. Use it to organize the order of rows on the page.
    - Move (vertically): Use the up and down arrows to move the row vertically.
    - Delete: Delete the row and both of its widgets (including their content and configuration) permanently from the page. If you delete a row from an active and published page, changes reflect to learners when you publish the page again. Important: Proceed with caution; this action cannot be undone.
  - Widget options:
    - Edit: Edit and reconfigure the widget.
    - Hide: Hide the widget from the overview page for all learners. This option is useful when you want to retain the widget for future use and not delete it.
    - Move (horizontally): Use the left and right arrows to move the widget. This option is available only when a row has more than one widget.
    - Delete: Delete the widget (content and configuration) permanently from the page. If you delete a widget from an active and published page, changes reflect to learners when you publish the page again. Important: Proceed with caution; this action cannot be undone.
7. If you have created multiple sections, you can enable the page outline, which creates links to all sections on the page. The page outline is like a table of contents; learners can click the section links in the outline to quickly navigate to the sections.Tip: Ensure that you have named the sections appropriately so learners can easily understand the section context from the names.
8. From the page settings, enable the toggle switch for the Show page outline option to enable the outline. Under Outline alignment, select whether you want the outline to appear on the left or right side of the page.Note: For Sales Plays pages, you can display the outline at the top as well. This option is not available for series and hub overview pages.Click Update to save the setting changes. The Page Builder displays a preview of how the page outline will appear to learners.
9. Once you have made all changes, click Publish in the upper-right corner to publish the updated page for your learners.
10. The following screenshot displays how the page outline appears to learners on a series overview page. Learners can click the sections in the outline to quickly navigate to them.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Setup > Overview pages > Page-level settings:
Page-level settings give you more control over the look and feel of your series and hub overview pages, letting you customize the vertical alignment of widgets within a row, the space between widgets, and the widget card style at the page level. These settings are available for both single-column and two-column layout pages.

The following settings are available:

- Vertical alignment: Adjust the vertical position of widgets within a row:
  - Top (default)
  - Middle
  - Bottom
  - Justify (only applicable to Text and Image widgets with buttons)
- Spacing: Control the space between widgets:
  - Narrow (default)
  - Wide
- Widget card styles: Customize the shape and shadow of widgets:
  - Square flat
  - Rounded raised (default)

Note: Page-level settings are not applicable to the Mindtickle mobile app, where widgets are stacked vertically.

Page-level settings are also available for homepages. For more information, see Create and manage custom homepages for the learning site.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Setup > Site Setup:
Mindtickle allows you to create custom-branded certificates that you can award learners upon successful completion of series-level certifications. As an admin, you can:

- Personalize the certificate design and align it with your brand by using appropriate background images, certification titles, font, and text colors.
- Create a certificate, save it as a template, and reuse it for multiple series certifications.
- Enable your learners to feel a sense of pride and achievement when they earn and share these certificates and build brand awareness.

This article further explains the permissions required to create and manage certificate templates. It also gives step-by-step guidance for creating a certificate.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Setup > Site Setup > Permissions:
Your role and assigned permissions determine your ability to create and manage certificate templates. You can create and manage the templates if:

- Your role is that of a site owner .
- Your role is other than that of a site owner, but your role has the MANAGE_CERTIFICATES permission.

Note:

- This permission is available to the site owner role by default.
- To create a custom role for a user and grant them the required permissions, contact Mindtickle Support .

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Setup > Site Setup > Create a certificate template:
To create a new certificate template:

1. On the admin site home page, click Training and select certificate templates on the sidebar. The certificate templates page appears with all the available certificate templates. You can create, edit, duplicate, publish, activate, deactivate, and delete certificates from this page. Note : The page is blank if no templates are created.
2. Click Create certificate template . The certificate Gallery appears and displays a list of three pre-built certificates you can choose from and customize. Click any one of the pre-built certificates from the list to preview it. Click Use this certificate -> to use the template. Alternatively, you can click New blank certificate in the left panel or create your own from scratch in the right panel to create a new certificate template from scratch. Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Series:
Once you add certifications to a series, you can edit, activate, deactivate, and delete them. Your role and assigned permissions determine your ability to manage the certifications. You can manage the certifications if:

- Your role is that of a site owner .
- Your role is other than that of a site owner, but your role has the MANAGE_SERIES permission for that series. This permission is available to the site owner role by default.

Note: To create a custom role for a user and grant them the required permissions, contact Mindtickle Support.

To manage certifications added to a series, you first need to navigate to the Certifications tab of the series. To do that:

1. On the admin site homepage, click Training on the left navigation panel and select Series . The Series page is displayed.
2. Select the series to add a certificate.
3. Navigate to the series Settings tab and click the Certifications tab.
4. Alternatively, click the Certifications link in the series header. Note: The active certifications link is available in the site header only if one or more certifications are active on the series. The Certifications tab displays the list of certifications available in the series. From this interface, you can add new certifications and edit, activate, deactivate, and delete existing certifications.

This article further explains how you can perform each of these actions.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Series > Edit a series certification:
You can edit an existing certification by changing its name and description, updating its criteria or validity, enabling or disabling recertification, redefining recertification criteria, and applying a different certificate template. You can edit both active and inactive certifications.

To edit a certification:

1. Click the More options icon and select Edit . Alternatively, click anywhere on the certification row.The Certification details page is displayed.
2. Edit the details based on your requirements and click Save . For more information on updating each element, see Add series certifications .

Note:

- If the certification criteria are changed, nothing changes for the learners who have already earned the certificate. They will continue to have the certificate. The updated criteria will only apply to learners who have not earned the certificate and the learners eligible for recertification.
- When learners recertify for a series, their progress resets for all modules within that series. The series invitation date remains unchanged, but the system updates the series completion date and time when learners successfully complete all modules.

Once the certification is successfully updated, a confirmation message is displayed on the screen. The updated certification is available to all learners invited to the series in the future.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Series > Activate a series certification:
Learners can only access a certification created on a series after it is activated. You can activate certifications that are Inactive.

To activate a certification:

1. Click More options icon and select Activate .

2. Click Yes, activate in the pop-up.

Once the certification is activated successfully, a confirmation message is displayed. The certification’s status changes to Active. It becomes available for all learners invited to the series. All learners who meet the certification criteria are automatically awarded the certificate.

Note: If a learner has met the certification criteria before the certification is activated, the learner is not eligible for the certification.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Series > Activate a series certification > How does the system award certificates to learners for a series?:
Learners are awarded certificates for a series when the following conditions are met.

- Module completion: Learners must complete all modules in the series that are part of the certificate criteria.
- Module invitation: The learner must be invited to all modules in the series that are part of the certificate criteria.
- Certificate activation date: The learner must complete at least one module after the certificate's activation date. Their latest or recent invitation to the module should also be before the certification activation date.

The scenarios below explain how the system awards a series certificate to a learner.

- Learner receives the series certificate
- Learner does not receive the series certificate

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Series > Activate a series certification > How does the system award certificates to learners for a series? > Learner receives the series certificate:
The following example scenario explains why learners receive a certificate for a series.

For example, consider a Series A with a certificate activated on October 10, 2025. A learner was invited to the series on October 15, 2025. The learner completed the modules in the series on October 20, 2025. The learner receives the Series A certificate because:

- The learner has completed all modules in the series.
- The learner was invited to all modules in the series before completing all modules.
- The learner completed at least one module after the certificate activation date, and their series invitation date is after the certificate activation date.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Series > Activate a series certification > How does the system award certificates to learners for a series? > Learner does not receive the series certificate:
The following example scenarios explain why learners do not receive certificates for a series.

Scenario 1 - The Learner completes all modules in the series before the certificate activation date

Consider a Series A with a certificate activated on October 1, 2025. A learner was invited to the series on September 1, 2025. The learner completed all modules in the series on September 28, 2025.

Result: The learner does not receive the Series A certificate because they had completed the Series A modules on September 28, before the series certification activation date of October 1.

Scenario 2 - The Learner completes all modules in a series before the certificate activation date

A learner completes all modules in Series B on September 28, 2025. The Series B modules are also mirrored in another Series A. The learner was invited to Series A on October 31, 2025, while its certificate was activated on October 1, 2025.Result: The learner does not receive the Series A certificate because:

- The learner had already completed the Series A modules on September 28, 2025 , since they were mirrored in Series B.
- The learner was invited to Series A only on October 31, 2025, after completing its modules .
- The Series A certificate was activated on October 1, 2025 , after the learner had completed all modules.

Scenario 3 - The learner completes all mirrored modules in series, but the series invitation date is after the module completion date

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Series > Deactivate a series certification:
You can temporarily stop issuing a certification to learners by deactivating it. You can deactivate only those certifications that are Active.

To deactivate a certification:

1. Click More options icon and select Deactivate .

2. Click Yes, deactivate in the pop-up.

Once the certification is successfully deactivated, a confirmation message is displayed on the screen. The certification’s status changes to Inactive, it becomes unavailable, and no new certificates are awarded to learners. Learners who already have the certificate are not affected and continue to view the certificate.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Series:
Earning a series-level certification proves your achievement of a common objective standard your organization defines.

To get certified on a series:

- You must have access to the series.
- Your admin should add certification to the series.
- The certification must be active.
- You must fulfill the specified certification criteria completely.
- You must be eligible for the certification. If you have already met the certification criteria in the past (before activating the certification), you will not be automatically awarded the certificate.
- For public and scoped-public series, you earn a certificate when you meet all certification criteria, even if you do not subscribe to the series.
- For an invite-only series, you must have access and meet all certification criteria to receive the certificate. Note:
  - You must enable the Access-Based Certifications feature to enable series certification without a subscription for public, scoped public, and invite-only series.
  - Contact Mindtickle Support to enable this feature for your learning site.
- For mirrored modules,
  - If a mirrored module belongs to a public series and an invite-only series that you can access. Completing the module in either the public or invite-only series earns you certification for both series.
  - If a mirrored module belongs to a public series and an invite-only series to which you do not have access. Completing the module in the public series earns you a certificate only for the public series, not for the invite-only series.

To discover and earn a series certificate:

1. Sign in to the learning site.

2. Click Training in the left navigation bar, and then click Series.

1. You receive the certificate in an email. Click Download certificate . The certificate opens as an image in a new tab on the browser. Right-click on the image and select Save Image as . Note : If you use the Safari browser, you can even select Save Image to Downloads to save the image in your Downloads folder. Enter a title for the certificate, select your preferred location to save it, and click Save . It is saved as a .png file. You can share it socially and use it to display your competency and qualifications on a specific subject matter.
2. The certification tile on the Certifications tab is updated with the details. The certification's status changes from Available to Completed, and the certificate awarded date and validity are displayed. Click View certificate . The certification details screen displays the certificate with the award date and validity details. Click Download certificate . The certificate opens as an image in a new tab on the browser. Right-click on the image and select Save Image as . Note : If you use the Safari browser, you can even select Save Image to Downloads to save the image to the Downloads folder. Enter a title for the certificate, select your preferred location where you want to save it, and click Save . The certificate is saved as a .PNG file. You can share it socially and use it to display your competency and qualifications on a specific subject. Click Share on LinkedIn to add the certification to your LinkedIn profile. For more information, see Share Series Certificates on LinkedIn .

  - If your admin deactivates the certification after you are certified, your certification is retained and not impacted.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Series > Share series certificates on LinkedIn:
1. Navigate to the Certifications tab on the All Series page and click View certificate on the certification you want to add to LinkedIn.
2. On the displayed certification details screen, click Share on LinkedIn . Note : The Share on LinkedIn option is available only for valid certificates. It is not available for expired certificates. Contact your admin if this option is unavailable for valid certificates. If you are not already logged in to LinkedIn, you are redirected to LinkedIn’s login page. Click Sign in and enter your credentials to sign in. Once the sign-in is successful, the Add license or certification pop-up is displayed. Note : If you have never added a certification, you would first want to add a Licenses & certifications section. For more information, see Manage licenses & certifications on LinkedIn . Each field on the pop-up is auto-filled with the appropriate value from the certificate. The Credential URL is auto-generated and is unique to the certification. Note :
  - Contact your admin if the Issuing organization field is not auto-filled. This is a mandatory field.
  - The certificate expiry date set for the series in Mindtickle is valid for certifications. The Expiration date set in LinkedIn's Add license or certification screen is not considered.
3. Click Save . Once the certification is added to your profile, a confirmation message is displayed. Click Next to share the certification as a post on your profile. In the post, you can include your learning and takeaways from the course, a new skill you picked up and mastered, or a simple reason why you are proud of this accomplishment. It is recommended that you add relevant tags in the post to increase its reach across your network. This enables you to highlight your accomplishments, skills, and credentials. If you don’t wish to share the certification in a post, click Skip . The certification and its unique Credential ID are added to your LinkedIn profile's Licences & certifications section . To view a certificate, click Show credential . The certificate is displayed.
4. Click to update the certification details or delete it from your profile.

- When unlocked, you can change height and width independently of each other.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Web Conferencing:
Mindtickle’s integration with the Webex video conferencing platform allows you to manage (create/update/delete) meetings and automate attendance tracking forthe your Instructor-Led Training (ILT) sessions. With this integration, when participants attend an ILT Webinar conducted over Webex, their attendance is marked automatically.

This integration is powered through Webex App Hub. To access the Mindtickle app on App Hub, click here.

The ILT-Webex integration marks learners’ attendance automatically by matching email addresses in the Webex attendance report with the list of email addresses of learners invited to the ILT module.

Note:

- If a learner’s email address is not listed in the Webex attendance report, their attendance is marked as Did not attend . (Admins can manually change the learner’s attendance status from the admin site.) This feature is available only on request. To enable it for your organization, contact Mindtickle Support or your Customer Success Manager (CSM).
- If the host sets up breakout rooms during a meeting, the attendance report includes data for participants in both, the breakout rooms and the main session.

For attendance tracking, both of the following conditions must be met:

- Users are invited to the ILT module
- Users join the Webex meeting with the email address associated with their Mindtickle user ID (email address)

This article explains how you can set up the ILT-Webex integration if admin-level authentication is enabled on your learning site. For more information on how to use the ILT-webex integration with user-level authorization, see ILT-Webex (User-level Auth) Integration to Manage Meetings and Auto-Attendance.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Web Conferencing > Prerequisites > Accounts and roles:
The user setting up the ILT-Webex integration must meet the following prerequisites:

- Webex : A licensed Webex user account with the ‘full org admin’ and ‘host’ role permissions. The host is the person who schedules, starts, and ends the session or records a session. A host can also assign roles to other participants in the session. The host can be reassigned once in a session.
- Mindtickle : A Mindtickle account with either the ‘site owner’ or the ‘IT admin’ role. This is required to access Security & Integrations settings on the platform.

The two accounts on Webex and Mindtickle must belong to the same user setting up the integration.

Note:

- The Webex admin setting up the Mindtickle-Webex integration must have ‘host’ role permissions.
- You can integrate one Webex account with only one Mindtickle learning site.
- The Mindtickle-Webex integration can be set up only with a licensed Webex user account. It is not available for free Webex account users.
- For more information on how to use the ILT-webex integration with user-level authorization, see ILT-Webex (User-level Auth) Integration to Manage Meetings and Auto-Attendance .
- You can configure the ILT-Webex setup using either the admin-level authorization or user-level authorization. By default, admin-level authorization is configured.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Web Conferencing > Installation and Configuration:
Perform the following steps to enable the Webex integration for ILT and install the Mindtickle app for your Webex account:

1. On the Mindtickle admin site homepage , click Account and select Settings .
2. On the Settings page, click the Security & integrations tab.
3. Under the Security & integrations tab, scroll down to the Web Conferencing section. Under Webex , select the checkbox to proceed with the Webex integration.
4. You are now directed to Webex to sign in to your account. Sign in with your admin credentials. Note :
  - Ensure that you have entered the correct credentials for Webex. For any issues, contact Mindtickle Support .
  - If the integration is not continuously used for 3 months, the client needs to re-authorize it. Reauthorization might not be required indefinitely when the integration is constantly used. Also, these tokens can be invalidated before their expiry from Webex’s side in case of a change in the user's scope, password update, etc. The Mindtickle authorization page appears. Click Accept .
  - For the integration to work successfully, the following scopes are requested by Webex: ScopeUsagemeeting:admin_participants_readRead the meeting's participants to mark auto-attendance in Mindtickle ILTmeeting:admin_schedule_readValidate the Webex meeting URL for auto-attendance eligibility in ILTmeeting:admin_schedule_writeCreate, update, and delete Webex meeting in ILTspark-admin:people_readValidate the user to assign co-host for a meetingspark-admin:roles_readValidate the user role to assign co-host for a meeting You are redirected to the Security & integrations tab on the Mindtickle platform. The Webex integration checkbox is checked, indicating the integration is successfully enabled.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Web Conferencing > Use Webex integration in ILT sessions:
- Create a new ILT session . By default, the session type is set to Classroom location. In the dialog box for creating a new session, select the session type from the Classroom/video conferencing tool details dropdown. For a video conferencing session, you can create a Webex meeting from the session or add a meeting link manually. This article lists the procedure for creating a Webex meeting from the ILT session for reference purposes. Note :
  - While creating a meeting from the ILT session, ensure:
    - The session start and end time is set in the future.
    - The session time is more than 10 minutes.
- Select Generate a Webex meeting link from the dropdown.
- If your account is authenticated, the meeting link is generated, and the meeting details and host details are auto-filled in the session details section.
- If the meeting link is associated with the Webex account integrated with your Mindtickle learning site, the Auto attendance toggle is set to ON , indicating that the attendance for this meeting will be automatically recorded. If your account is not authenticated, the system prompts you to enter the email address of the host for the meeting.
- Enter the host details and click Confirm host . The meeting link is generated, and the meeting and host details are auto-filled in the session details section. Note : If you enter the email address of a user who is not authenticated, the system prompts you to enter the details of an authenticated user.
- To enter a meeting link manually, select Enter meeting link from the Classroom/video conferencing details dropdown and enter the meeting URL in the Enter Meeting URL section.
  - If the meeting is created from the same account through which the Mindtickle-Webex integration is set up, the system checks the URL for Webex auto-attendance eligibility. If eligible, the Auto attendance toggle appears and is automatically switched ON.
  - If the meeting is created from an account different from the one used to set up the Mindtickle-Webex integration, the system prompts you to enter a meeting password.
  - If the session type is set to Classroom location and you enter the URL of a Webex meeting manually, the session type changes to Enter link manually. The system checks the URL for Webex auto-attendance eligibility. If eligible, the Auto attendance toggle appears and is automatically switched ON.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Web Conferencing > Use Webex integration in ILT sessions > Duration-based attendance capture:
Admins can set a minimum percentage threshold to record learners’ attendance for ILT modules and individual sessions using the Duration-based attendance capture feature.

This feature automatically records learners’ attendance based on their time in ILT events and sessions.

When participants attend an ILT Webinar conducted over Webex, their attendance is marked automatically. The Webex integration provides the time spent by the learner in a session.

The system calculates an ILT session’s minimum attendance threshold as follows,

- Scheduled sessions: For scheduled sessions that are yet to start, the system calculates the minimum attendance threshold using the session's start and end time set during session creation. For example, in a 60-minute session with a 20% minimum attendance threshold, the system marks the learner as attended if they spend at least 12 minutes (20% of 60) in the session.
- Completed sessions: If a session ends early or extends beyond the scheduled time, the system calculates the minimum attendance threshold based on the actual session time. For example, for a 60-minute session with a 20% minimum attendance threshold, if the session ends early in 50 minutes, the system marks the learner as attended if they spend at least 10 minutes (20% of 50) in the session.

The system compares the learners’ time in session provided by Webex with the session’s minimum attendance threshold to mark the learner's attendance for the session.

The learner’s attendance status and time spent in sessions are displayed in the Attendance status/Duration column on the Events and Sessions tab of the ILT.

For more information, see Duration-based attendance capture for learners in ILTs.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Web Conferencing > Use Webex integration in ILT sessions > Caveats:
- If you discard the meeting without saving the changes, the Webex meeting details are deleted from the session, and the session type is reset to Classroom location . The meeting is also deleted from Webex.
- If a meeting that has ended is restarted (the host restarts it or a participant joins), we get the attendance details of only the participants from the latest instance of the meeting, and the data for participants from all previous meeting instances is lost.
- If an instructor marked as a co-host is removed, the user is also removed from the Webex meeting co-host list.
- If you copy a session in which a Webex meeting is configured, the session type is reset to Classroom location in the copied session.
- Suppose you copy the ILT module in a different series that includes a session (or multiple sessions) in which Webex meetings are configured. In that case, the session type for the copied sessions is reset to Classroom location .

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Web Conferencing > Attendance calculation for ILT sessions in Webex:
- For ILT sessions conducted in Webex, Mindtickle fetches the attendance reports from Webex after the scheduled session ends.
- Learners' attendance is marked from all meeting instances that start 30 minutes before and 30 minutes after the scheduled meeting time.
- If the meeting is ongoing, the system requests attendance reports every five minutes for up to 24 hours after the meeting ends.
- The table below explains the attendance capture scenarios for an ILT session scheduled on Webex between 3 p.m. and 4 p.m.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Web Conferencing > FAQs:
Q: If I have already created a Webex meeting, can I add it to the ILT session in Mindtickle? Will attendance still be marked?

A: Yes, you can add the Webex meeting URL. As long as you have authenticated your account, the session is eligible for auto-attendance.

Q: What if an ILT participant attends the session just for a couple of minutes? Are they marked as attended?

A: Yes, the participant is marked as attended. The integration does not have a way to capture the time spent in the ILT.

Q: Do learners need to enroll for auto-attendance to work?

A: Learners do not have to enroll to a session but must be invited to the ILT module to be automatically marked as attended.

A: Yes, the participant is marked as attended. The integration does not have a way to capture the time spent in the ILT.

Q: Do learners need to enroll for auto-attendance to work?

A: Learners do not have to enroll to a session but must be invited to the ILT module to be automatically marked as attended.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Asset Hub > Admin:
This article explains the importance of plays as an asset and how it helps admins to provide a guided experience to the learners or sales reps. Plays are designated pages created by admins for different business scenarios. It helps admins to identify and share messages on how best to utilize the underlying assets and content available within these plays.

Note: Asset Hub is a paid feature, and the play is enabled by default for all customers who have purchased Asset Hub. For more information, contact your Customer Success Manager (CSM).

Plays as an asset allow admins to perform the following:

- Communicate the best practices to handle a given scenario associated with a deal motion or any other complex scenario
- Guide learners to navigate a situation in a certain way with the help of the available content
- Communicate the context behind the messaging of specific assets
- Guide learners and reps to identify the right assets, and decide the preferential order of assets based on the relative applicability in a given scenario
- Communicate the need and context of a hub and asset that evolves over time

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Asset Hub > Admin > Create play as an asset:
On the Assets page, click New > Build a play.

Alternatively, you can click Add assets > Build a play inside a hub to start creating a play.

The page to create a new play from scratch displays. You can customize the page using the default play templates. Select a template from the 3 pre-built templates available in the left panel to get started.

After selecting the template, click the Use this template button. Alternatively, you can click New blank page or create a new play.

The page to select and customize the widgets displays. Add widgets available in the left navigation panel or modify the widgets already available within the template. Click Continue to manage the play. For more information on customizing the page and adding widgets, see Page Builder Overview.

The Enter asset details page allows you to enter the play details. You can perform the following:

- Enter a Name for the play. It is recommended to select a name that can immediately tell sales reps what the play is all about and makes it easy to search.
- Select Hub from the list shown in the drop-down. You can select multiple hubs to make the play multi-present. A hub is a logical group of assets that helps organize the entire asset repository into broad categories.
- Select an Asset Owner of the play to divide the responsibility of play ownership and maintenance between different users. This is an optional step. By default, Asset Hub populates the play's creator as the asset owner. You can choose any user as the asset owner who is a collaborator and has Develop Asset permissions of one of the hubs where the play resides. This ensures that the asset owner always has permission to edit the play.

By default, Asset Hub populates the play's creator as the asset owner. You can choose any user as the asset owner who is a collaborator and has Develop Asset permissions of one of the hubs where the play resides. This ensures that the asset owner always has permission to edit the play.

Note: Attribute suggestions displayed are based on most applied attributes by other admins and recently created attributes.

For example, if the play is for the buyer journey stage of the sales funnel, you can add attributes like awareness, closing, or evaluation to it.

- Under Usage , the play usage is by default set to Internal and cannot be changed. Plays can only be used internally and cannot be shared externally.
- Additionally, you can add a description of the play. Description conveys valuable information that helps viewers spot a play in search results and indicate the type of content in the play. It also guides the sales rep on which play to use in a situation. For example, a pitch deck’s talk track helps the sales rep focus on certain important aspects, thus allowing the rep to create value, control the process, and win deals.
- You can also add an expiry date, an expiry reminder, or a file update reminder.
- Setting an expiry date ensures the effectiveness of your plays. Once a play expires, you can either choose to update the play and extend its expiry date or archive it. Expired plays are still visible to the sales reps but are flagged as Expired.
- Expiration reminder or file update reminder helps to ensure that you keep your plays up to date. You can review the feedback received from your learners and keep the play up to date.
- A file update reminder is sent regularly to a hub collaborator to ensure the play remains up to date.

All expiry and file update reminders are sent to the asset owner. If there is no asset owner assigned, all the expiry and file update reminders are sent to the hub collaborators where the play resides.

For information on hub collaborators and notifications, refer to the Hub Settings article.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Modules:
This article provides information on the analytics reports for learning contents added through a SCORM package in course and quick update modules. These reports provide insights on learners’ performance around the questions (with scoring) that are part of the quizzes in the SCORM content. This is in addition to the already available SCORM analytics on overall completion status, % completion, and the overall score for a learner.

SCORM analytics data is currently not available through the platform UI. Therefore, you can only view the data by exporting the reports in a CSV format. The following analytics reports are available for SCORM content:

- SCORM detailed report: Contains question attempt data for each learner and for each question in the SCORM.
- SCORM question overview report: Question-level overview that shows questions on which learners are doing good and questions where they are struggling.
- SCORM learner overview report: Learner-level overview that shows which learners are doing good and which are struggling, with respect to the questions.

You can export the three reports for a single module or use the Bulk Export option to export them for multiple modules at once.

Note:

- The reports provide analytics only on those questions in SCORM quizzes that have scoring enabled. These reports are available for all standards supported on Mindtickle: SCORM 1.1, SCORM 1.2, SCORM 2004 (across all editions), and AICC and xAPI packages.
- The reports provide analytics data only on the questions (with scoring) that are part of the quizzes in the SCORM content, and not on any other interactions. The reports are not intended to match xAPI standards and provide analytics on all interactions.

In addition to the reports that you can export from the platform, you can also use our reporting API to fetch the same data.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Modules > Export SCORM reports:
1. In the admin site sidebar, click Analytics > Training > Modules to open the module reports listing page.
2. On the Modules page, click the name of a course or quick update module to view their analytics. To quickly find the module you're looking for, use search or the Module type filter.
3. Let's consider the course module as an example.
4. On the course module report page, navigate to the Content > Learning content tab. This tab lists all learning objects within the module, including SCORM learning objects. Then, click the Export button to start exporting reports for SCORM content.
5. The Export Report pop-up that appears.
6. Perform the following to export the report of SCORM content in this module:
  1. Select the type of report: You can export one of the following three types of SCORM reports:
    - SCORM detailed report: Contains question attempt data for each learner and for each question in the SCORM.
    - SCORM question overview report: Question-level overview that shows questions on which learners are doing good and questions where they are struggling.
    - SCORM learner overview report: Learner-level overview that shows which learners are doing good and which are struggling, with respect to the questions.
  2. Select SCORM objects: Select the SCORM-based learning objects that you want to include in the report.
  3. Enter recipient’s email: Enter the email address of the user to whom you want to send the report. The recipient will receive a link in the email using which they can download the report in a CSV format. The link expires in 7 days.
7. Click Export This Report to export the report by email. The recipient shortly receives the email with a link to download the report. They can view the downloaded report file (.CSV) using Google Sheets or Microsoft Excel. Note: Reports exported from Analytics are for the latest version of the SCORM learning object. If the SCORM file linked in the SCORM learning object is replaced, then the Select SCORM objects option (while exporting reports) displays only the most recent SCORM learning object. To fetch data for previous versions of the same learning object, either use the Bulk Export option or use the reporting API .

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Modules > Export SCORM reports in bulk:
1. On the Export Report pop-up, you can export a report for multiple modules at once using the Bulk Export option.
2. First, select one of the three SCORM content reports that you want to export for multiple modules:
  - SCORM detailed report: Contains question attempt data for each learner and for each question in the SCORM.
  - SCORM question overview report: Question-level overview that shows questions on which learners are doing good and questions where they are struggling.

3. Click Bulk export to start exporting the report in bulk.
4. The Bulk export pop-up appears.
5. The current module is selected by default. Click the “select modules” box for a list of modules from which you can select up to 10 modules. The dropdown menu lists the same type of module for which you are exporting the report. For example, if you are on a course, the dropdown menu lists only course modules. Select the modules for which you want to export the report and click Apply . Note:
  - When you select multiple modules, it’s not necessary all modules have SCORM learning objects. Therefore, exported reports will contain data only for those modules that have SCORM learning objects.

The recipients will receive a link in the email using which they can download the report. The link expires in 7 days.

It will be a consolidated report for selected modules and for all SCORM learning objects within each module. The recipients can view the downloaded report file (.CSV) using Google Sheets or Microsoft Excel.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Modules > Important caveats:
1. Learners’ attempt data on questions within the SCORM are based on the run-time interactions captured by the SCORM engine as learners interact with the questions. If the author of the SCORM file has not enabled run-time interactions, the SCORM engine will not be able to capture any run-time interactions and, therefore, analytics on questions will not be available.
2. If you are using SCORM 1.1 or SCORM 1.2, then the exported reports may not capture the titles of questions. Instead, it will include the question IDs. Similarly, learners’ responses and correct responses recorded in SCORM 1.1 or SCORM 1.2 may not be in a usable format. For more information, see this SCORM article . Therefore, we recommend using SCORM 2004, which does not have the above two issues.
3. Question titles in the SCORM Detailed Report are used for generating the SCORM Learner Overview and Question Overview reports. Therefore, all the questions must have unique titles. In case the author of the SCORM file has used the same title for different questions, the SCORM reports will consider only one of the questions among the questions with duplicate titles. It considers the question that the learner attempted first.
4. The result of a question is reported as received from the SCORM engine and depends on how the SCORM is authored. For multiple choice questions with multiple answers, partially correct answers may get reported as incorrect .
5. Data for the following columns in SCORM will be reported as received from the SCORM engine. If not received, it will be blank in the reports: Completion % (in SCORM) , Completion Status (in SCORM) , Learner Score (in SCORM) , Max Score (in SCORM) , and Latency (in seconds) .
6. Data for all three SCORM reports are refreshed every 2 hours. Therefore, if your exported reports do not have any data, please export them again after 2 hours.
7. If the admin has changed the title of the SCORM learning object in a course or quick update, then it would take up to 2 hours to reflect in the reports. Until then, the learning object title would be blank in the reports.
8. Reports exported from Analytics are for the latest version of the SCORM learning object. If the SCORM file linked in the SCORM learning object is replaced, then the Select SCORM objects option (while exporting reports) displays only the most recent SCORM learning object. To fetch data for previous versions of the same learning object, either use the Bulk Export option or use the reporting API .

Similarly, learners’ responses and correct responses recorded in SCORM 1.1 or SCORM 1.2 may not be in a usable format. For more information, see this SCORM article . 3. Question titles in the SCORM Detailed Report are used for generating the SCORM Learner Overview and Question Overview reports. Therefore, all the questions must have unique titles. In case the author of the SCORM file has used the same title for different questions, the SCORM reports will consider only one of the questions among the questions with duplicate titles. It considers the question that the learner attempted first.
4. The result of a question is reported as received from the SCORM engine and depends on how the SCORM is authored. For multiple choice questions with multiple answers, partially correct answers may get reported as incorrect .
5. Data for the following columns in SCORM will be reported as received from the SCORM engine. If not received, it will be blank in the reports: Completion % (in SCORM) , Completion Status (in SCORM) , Learner Score (in SCORM) , Max Score (in SCORM) , and Latency (in seconds) .
6. Data for all three SCORM reports are refreshed every 2 hours. Therefore, if your exported reports do not have any data, please export them again after 2 hours.
7. If the admin has changed the title of the SCORM learning object in a course or quick update, then it would take up to 2 hours to reflect in the reports. Until then, the learning object title would be blank in the reports.
8. Reports exported from Analytics are for the latest version of the SCORM learning object. If the SCORM file linked in the SCORM learning object is replaced, then the Select SCORM objects option (while exporting reports) displays only the most recent SCORM learning object. To fetch data for previous versions of the same learning object, either use the Bulk Export option or use the reporting API .

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Modules > Reporting API:
In addition to the reports from the platform, you can also fetch the SCORM analytics data using Mindtickle’s reporting API. You can fetch the data using the following tables in the reporting API:

- ScormDetailed: Contains question attempt data for each learner and for each question in the SCORM.
- ScormQuestionOverview: Question-level overview that shows questions on which learners are doing good and questions where they are struggling.
- ScormLearnerOverview: Learner-level overview that shows which learners are doing good and which are struggling, with respect to the questions.

The tables provide the same data that you get by exporting the reports from Analytics on the platform. Additionally, using the tables, you can also fetch data for previous versions of any SCORM learning object.

For more information, see Download reporting API tables.
