chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > Digital Sales Rooms > Key Benefits:
- Build impressive experiences Instead of receiving multiple emails with several attachments over weeks and months or waiting for a time that is convenient for everyone to coordinate a meeting, your contacts can receive a link to a single room complete with content, collaboration tools, and clear next steps. Reps can add information that is unique to the deal and the buyer, and create a customized experience in each room.

- Design a centralized communication and collaboration space Display all deal-related information in a single shared space to simplify and enhance the buyer-seller collaboration. DSRs also allow you to support a sales cycle or customer relationship over time by adding content, additional case studies, and references as they get closer to a buying decision.

- Create a persistent shared space by sharing your DSR Once you have built an engaging DSR with consolidated data, share your room with prospects and customers. As you share your rooms, you will start to get alerts when your room is viewed and shared or when someone asks a question. This will help you identify which prospects and customers are engaged and where to spend your time on follow-up and which stakeholders have been invited to the table.

- Use insights to fastrack deal closures Impress buyers and customers with collaborative, engaging rooms, and ultimately help you sell by getting detailed insights into what matters to your buyers to move deals along faster. Track buyer engagement and gain actionable insights to create effective selling processes.

Room templates allow you to quickly and easily build a room without having to filter, select, and organize content each time. If you're sharing similar content when building out that initial room for your prospect or customer, create templates to apply after selecting a deal, add a few final touches if needed, and then send!

Different access permissions in Digital Sales Rooms (DSRs) help regulate your access to the product based on the activities you perform. Permissions ensure you can access data and product capabilities per your job requirement. They also ensure that users do not have access to features they do not need, minimizing the chances of errors and issues of users interfering with each other’s work.

This article further explains the main permissions for DSRs. It provides information in the following two tables:

- Permission access : Information on the level of access granted to each role for a particular permission.
- Permission actions : Information on the actions allowed for each permission. This table essentially defines the permissions by listing the actions associated with each permission.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Digital Sales Rooms > Permission access:
This table provides information on the level of access granted to each user role for a particular permission. For a permission, a role can have one of the following levels of access:

Universal and complete access

Limited or scoped access

No access

| Permissions | Roles |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Site Owner | Enablement Admin | Content Expert | Group Manager | Manager | IT Admin | Learner |  |
| Manage DSR |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Access DSR |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

Note:

- Once DSR is enabled for your organization, two new roles DSR Admin and DSR User are created on your site. By default, the DSR Admin role has the Manage DSR permission and the DSR User role has the Access DSR permission. If the roles are not created automatically, contact your Customer Success Manager (CSM) or Mindtickle Support .
- The Manage DSR (MANAGE_DIGITAL_SALES_ROOMS) permission is available to the site owner roles by default.
- DSR permissions are not scoped.
- The Access DSR permission is not available to any role by default.

To create a custom role for a user and grant them the required permissions, contact Mindtickle Support.

When sharing rooms with prospects, sending a link that displays your domain adds credibility and further emphasizes your brand.

With a vanity URL, you can replace the default start of URLs for shared rooms with a custom domain of your choice. For example, yourlearningsitename.share.mindtickle.com is replaced with share.yourlearningsitename.com.

By default, Mindtickle creates a vanity URL for your organization in the format yourlearningsitename.share.mindtickle.com. For example, if your learning site name is aviatoone, the vanity URL generated for your learning site is https://aviatoone.share.mindtickle.com. If you want the vanity URL for your default share room link, then it can be replaced with a new custom URL. For example, share.salesaviatoone.com or share.customlearningsitename.com.

Note: You can request for your vanity URL to be whitelabled. To whitelabel your vanity URL, contact your Customer Success Manager (CSM) or Mindtickle Support.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Digital Sales Rooms > Prerequisite:
Before you contact the support team or your CSM, ensure you have added the CNAME record where you must map the whitelabel domain to “<subdomain>.share.mindtickle.com” in your DNS authority. With the help of your webmaster or server administrator, create a CNAME DNS record of your whitelabel URL and point it to your learning site URL. For example, if you want to use share.salesaviatooneunviersity.com as the vanity URL for your DSR, you must create the cname record for your domain as mentioned below.

Note: It is not mandatory to use ‘share' in the white-labeled vanity URL. The URL mentioned in the table below is only an example.

| share.salesaviatooneuniversity.com / defaultlearningsitename.share.mindtickle.com | CNAME | Old: share.salesaviatooneuniversity.com / defaultlearningsitename.share.mindtickle.comNew:go.salesaviatoone.com |

Once you have performed the steps mentioned above, contact Mindtickle Support, to activate the vanity URL.

Integrating Digital Sales Rooms with Salesforce is a great way to access all opportunities, contacts, and accounts and start building rooms. It improves reporting and sales processes by bringing more data and notifications into existing platforms within your organization.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Digital Sales Rooms > Key benefits:
The following are the benefits of the DSR-Salesforce integration:

- Enhance rep productivity: Reps can quickly identify and link new rooms to existing opportunities, saving time and effort. The linked rooms are automatically updated with Salesforce opportunity information.
- Track user engagement for opportunities: Identify and track the engagement of multiple contacts for opportunities. If a new user from a buying organization accesses a room, the user’s contact is automatically created and enriched in Salesforce. The room activity details are automatically written to the linked Salesforce opportunity, account, and contact.
- View actionable insights: Analytics provide valuable information on your rooms' performance and the efficacy of content shared in rooms. View content shared for opportunities, generate reports, and gain insights into the impact and ROI of assets shared in DSRs.
- Increase DSR adoption: Mindtickle notifies reps to create rooms for synced Salesforce opportunities. The notifications can be configured based on the opportunity type, stage, and amount. This increases DSR usage and helps implement best practices for room creation.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Digital Sales Rooms > Sync data from Salesforce to DSR:
If your organization uses Salesforce integration, you can quickly integrate it with DSR from Settings > Integrations. This allows you to pull in opportunities, contacts, and accounts to spot which opportunities do not have a room created or edit an existing one as the sale progresses. This sync is also a requirement to sync activities back into Salesforce.

To integrate Salesforce with DSR:

1. On the admin site homepage, click Rooms and select Settings.

2. On the Settings page, click the Integrations tab.

3. Under CRM, click Connect next to Salesforce to begin the authentication process.

Note: You can perform this action only if you have the Manage DSR (MANAGE_DIGITAL_SALES_ROOMS) permission.

4. On the displayed screen, enter your Salesforce admin credentials to log in.

5. On the displayed pop-up, click Allow.

6. After logging into Salesforce, on the left navigation panel, click Apps > Connected Apps > Connected Apps OAuth Usage.

The Connected Apps OAuth Usage screen is displayed.

7. Under the Connected App column, click the Install button on Enable Us by Mindtickle.

8. On the displayed pop-up screen, click Install.

The Enable Us by Mindtickle app is now installed on the Salesforce instance

9. Once the integration is successfully set up, a confirmation message displays on the screen. It also lists the most recent sync(s) along with the details such as the number of users, accounts, contacts, and opportunities that were synced from your Salesforce account.

The data is auto-synced periodically. To perform a manual sync, click Sync.

Note:

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Digital Sales Rooms > Push data from DSR to Salesforce:
In addition to pulling data from Salesforce, you can decide whether to push data into Salesforce and create activities and contacts for key events.

Activities can be created when:

- a room is created, edited, and visited
- a new comment is posted under Conversations
- a mutual action plan task is marked as Completed

Contacts can be created when a room is visited by a contact not already in your CRM (will be associated with an Opportunity and Account, if available).

Note:

- DSR creates contacts in Salesforce if the following conditions are met:
  - The room contact’s email domain is not listed in the DSR Settings > Company Profile tab. This condition also impacts the writing of the room activity to Salesforce.
  - A Salesforce contact with the visitor’s email address does not exist.
  - The Require email to view switch is ON o n the room's Access options screen.
  - The room owner's email in Mindtickle and Salesforce is the same.
- The Room visitor link in Salesforce updates when a user creates, deletes, or modifies a room in DSR. This occurs instantly or after a few minutes.

To enable Salesforce activity creation, when setting up a new sync, you are presented with the following options:

Tip: Enable Create new Contacts for unmatching emails to ensure a contact is created in Salesforce automatically every time a new visitor visits a room. Furthermore, to enhance the contact information of customers visiting your DSR, enable Allow automatic enrichment of contact data from the Company Profile page. Users receive enriched contact data that may include the customer’s first and last name, phone number, organization, job title, LinkedIn profile link, and profile image. For more information, see Set Up Digital Sales Rooms: Company Profile.

Tip: Currently, when someone visits a DSR, an activity is created in Salesforce. The information written into the activity includes the shareable room link, administrative/stats link, number of DSR visits, visit duration (seconds), and percentage of items viewed. This data is added in a text box format and can be difficult to report on. For example, it becomes hard to perform calculations, averages, sums, and counts from this format. Also, accessing information from the Description field before performing calculations can be challenging. To solve this problem, you can create custom fields at the opportunity level in Salesforce. You can create a custom field for the DSR link, and have your Salesforce developer set up a trigger or rule to map the incoming activity data from the DSR to this new custom field. This automates the data entry process, ensuring accuracy and efficiency. With this data in the custom fields, it becomes much easier to build reports and dashboards using Salesforce.

You can create a custom field for the DSR link, and have your Salesforce developer set up a trigger or rule to map the incoming activity data from the DSR to this new custom field. This automates the data entry process, ensuring accuracy and efficiency. With this data in the custom fields, it becomes much easier to build reports and dashboards using Salesforce.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Digital Sales Rooms > Key benefits:
The following are the benefits of the DSR-HubSpot integration:

- Enhance rep productivity: Reps can quickly identify and link new rooms to existing deals, saving time and effort. The linked rooms are automatically updated with HubSpot deal information.
- Track user engagement for deals: Identify and track the engagement of multiple contacts for deals. If a new user from a buying organization accesses a room, the user’s contact is automatically created and enriched in HubSpot. The room activity details are automatically written to the linked HubSpot deal, company, and contact.
- View actionable insights: Analytics provide valuable information on your rooms' performance and the efficacy of content shared in rooms. View content shared for deals, generate reports and gain insights into the impact and ROI of assets shared in DSRs.
- Increase DSR adoption: Mindtickle notifies reps to create rooms for synced HubSpot deals. The notifications can be configured based on the deal type, stage, and amount. This increases DSR usage and helps implement best practices for room creation.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Digital Sales Rooms > Sync data from HubSpot to DSR:
1. On the admin site homepage, click Rooms and select Settings .
2. On the Settings page, click the Integrations tab.
3. Under CRM , click Connect next to HubSpot to begin the authentication process. Note : You can perform this action only if your role has the Manage DSR ( MANAGE_DIGITAL_SALES_ROOMS ) permission.
4. A confirmation message is displayed on the screen once the integration is successfully set up. The initial sync is performed after HubSpot is successfully integrated with DSR. Reps do not have to wait for the initial sync to complete and start creating rooms because:
  - Companies, contacts, and users are excluded from the first sync.
  - Only deals created during the last 6 months are synced. Of these deals, closed lost and closed won deals are excluded from the sync. Moreover, any changes in HubSpot get synced into DSRs in real-time, enabling reps to search for deals immediately. This ensures that the most relevant deals get synced first. Moreover, since HubSpot APIs power the search, reps can search for deals, companies, and contacts yet to be synced into DSRs.
5. The screen displays the initial and last synced date, time, number of users, companies, contacts, and deals that were synced from your HubSpot account. The data is auto-synced from HubSpot to DSR in real-time, eliminating the need for periodic sync jobs. If necessary, click Sync to initiate a manual sync. Note :

- The CRM contacts must have an email address to sync.
- Deals do not require a primary contact.

To see all the synced data within the platform,

In addition to pulling in data from HubSpot, you can decide if you want to push data into HubSpot and create activities and contacts for key events.

Activities can be created when:

These options are configurable by company to ensure they match up with your CRM needs. Switch the respective toggle to ON or OFF based on your requirements.

The Configure HubSpot data sync pop-up appears.

Make the necessary updates and click the Close icon.

- The Notifications are configured on the DSR's Settings page. From this tab, you can set up notifications for new deals created in HubSpot.

- In HubSpot, activities are created in the following format. The corresponding data for each activity is displayed depending on your configuration settings.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Digital Sales Rooms:
The cloud storage integrations in Digital Sales Rooms (DSR) enable users to pull sales content from other sources. You can determine which content storage options (including local devices, Call Recordings, or Asset Hub) users can connect with Mindtickle. When your users create or update a room, they can pull in content from locations that have been approved.

As a DSR admin, you can configure org-level cloud storage accounts and allow users to connect to their personal accounts to access content. Based on the settings you configure, reps can pick content from the allowed sources and add it to the rooms or templates they create.

Note: DSRs support the following file formats when uploading content:

| Video | .mp4 |
| --- | --- |
| Audio | .wav |
| Document | .pdf, .ppt, .pptx, .doc, .docx, .xls, .xlsx |
| Image | .jpeg, .png, .gifNote: The recommended file size is 1432 x 806 px. |

This article explains how to:

- Configure cloud storage integrations
- Integrate org-level Google Drive accounts

Note: Call AI is available as a cloud storage option only if your organization has purchased Call AI.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Digital Sales Rooms > Integrate org-level Google Drive accounts:
Integrating org-level Google Drive accounts within Digital Sales Rooms provides seamless access to org-specific files and documents, enabling effective collaboration and sharing within the sales process. Here are some key advantages of using org-level Google Drive accounts:

- Enhanced collaboration With org-level accounts, teams can easily collaborate on shared files, simultaneously editing and commenting on documents. This promotes efficient teamwork and improves productivity.
- Centralized storage and access An organizational Google Drive account provides centralized storage. This means files are stored in a common location accessible to authorized individuals, making it easy to find and access documents. This eliminates the need for multiple file versions stored on different devices, reducing confusion and saving time.
- Sharing and permissions management Org-level accounts enable administrators to set permissions at the organizational, team, or individual level, ensuring data security and confidentiality. It also simplifies the process of sharing files with external collaborators.
- Advanced administrative controls Administrators can manage user accounts, set up security policies, monitor usage, and enforce data retention policies. This level of control helps organizations maintain data security and compliance.

A successful integration of an org-level Google Drive account within DSR is completed in two stages:

- Connect an org-level Google Drive account
- Configure access permissions

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Digital Sales Rooms > Integrate org-level Google Drive accounts > Configure access permissions:
Define permissions and access levels for users within Digital Sales Rooms to determine who can view, access, or upload files from the connected org-level Google Drive account. The selected users or teams can access the connected account while uploading content in rooms or room templates.

To configure access permissions, follow the steps mentioned below:

1. Navigate to Integrations > Cloud Storage > Google Drive > Org-level account.
2. Click Select who can access .
3. On the Select who can access? screen, choose whom you want to provide access to. Select:
  - All users - to grant access to all DSR admins and users.
  - Specify teams/users - to grant access to specific teams or users.
4. If you select Specify teams/users , the Teams/Users field is displayed. Enter the email address of all users or teams you want to provide access to or select from the available list. Note : You can only add users (or teams of users) with the DSR User or DSR admin role.
5. Click Save .
6. To revoke the selected users’ or teams’ access, click Remove . The number of teams or users granted access is updated and displayed under the connected org-level account.
7. To update the access list by adding teams/users or revoking their access, click the number or Configure . The Select who can access? panel is displayed from where you can update the permissions.
8. To connect multiple org-level accounts, repeat the steps mentioned above.

Tip: When connecting multiple accounts, use appropriate names for each account so the users can understand which account to use while uploading content in DSRs. You can update the account names later, but it is recommended to set the appropriate names right from the beginning.

Room templates allow sales reps to quickly and easily build a room without having to filter, select, and organize content each time. Sales reps sharing similar content can quickly build a room for their prospect or customer by applying an existing room template to a deal and adding a few final touches.

As an admin, you can create multiple templates for specific audiences, industries, use cases, and any combination you may need. You can either start from scratch or turn an existing room into a template.

You can create a room template:

- From scratch
- From an existing template (Clone a Template)
- From an existing room

This article further explains each of these processes in detail.

  - When uploading content from cloud storage options such as Google Drive, you can choose to upload content from the org-level account or your personal account. If your DSR admin has configured an org-level account, you can access the content stored on it without connecting to your personal Google Drive account. If multiple org-level Google Drive accounts are connected, and you are granted access to them, the accounts are visible as a list. You can choose to connect your personal account on top of the org-level account to upload content in the DSR. If you have selected content from an account and then try to switch the account, the following warning is displayed: Clicking Change Account changes the account, and all your selected content is deselected.

Cover images can provide a visual preview of the content, helping to tell a story and set the context before the user engages with the full content piece. They make the content visually appealing and help users quickly identify and differentiate between various pieces. This significantly enhances the room template’s overall experience and effectiveness. See Edit cover images for more information on adding or editing cover thumbnail images for content in room templates. Note : If you edit a cover image in the room template and save it, then any room created using that template will have the updated cover image.
8. To hide or unhide the content name, description, or adjust its downloadable settings, click . The Edit Details panel appears. Click to unhide the content details. Similarly, click to hide the content details. Switch the Allow viewers to download toggle ON or OFF based on whether you want the viewers to download the content.
9. Click Done .
10. Once you are done updating the room, click Create Template .

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Digital Sales Rooms > Create a room template from an existing template:
If a template is well structured, you can save it as a template for further reuse. To create a room template from an existing template:

1. On the admin site homepage, click Rooms and select Templates . On the Templates page, the Rooms tab displays the already created Organization templates (available to the entire organization) or Private templates (available only to you).
2. Click Organization to view the organization templates.
3. Click the M ore options icon on the template you want to create a template from and click Clone .
4. In the Clone Room Template pop-up, enter the template name and description and click Clone Template . The cloned template shows up as a new template on the Templates page. Note : The default room settings of the base template are copied over to the cloned template. To customize it, click the More options icon and select Edit .
5. Customize the template to make the required changes. You may update the default room settings, background, add new content or reorder existing content, add or remove sales actions, add section headers, create a new welcome message, and so on.
6. Click Save Changes .

The template is saved and added to the Templates page.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Digital Sales Rooms > Create a room template from an existing room:
If a room is well structured and has received a lot of engagement or feedback, you can save it as a template for further reuse. To create a room template from an existing room:

1. On the Digital Sales Rooms tab, click the More options icon against the room and select Save As Template from the dropdown. Tip : If you do not see the room in the list, use the filters or the Search field to search for the room.
2. In the Save as Template pop-up, enter the name and description for the template and click Save as Template . Once the template is created successfully, a confirmation pop-up displays on the bottom left portion of the screen. Click Preview template to view it. Alternatively, you can view it later from the Templates > Room Templates tab. A preview of the room is displayed. Click Create Room to use it to build a room.
3. If you want to edit the room design before using it to build a room, click the More options icon and select Edit from the dropdown. On the Edit Sales Room Template page, make the required changes. You may update the default room settings, background, add new content or reorder existing content add or remove sales actions, add section headers, create a new welcome message, and so on. Tip :
  - When creating a template from an existing room, edit the room title as it includes the company or contact name. Make it more generic and include the {{company}} placeholder.
  - Make sure to remove any content, welcome message, or sales action specific to the prospect or customer. Click Preview to view the changes, or click Save Changes to save the updated template design.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Digital Sales Rooms > Benefits of MAPs:
- Foster collaboration between all stakeholders Gain full transparency and accountability of next steps (and stakeholders) needed from both sides to close a deal or onboard a new customer with one mutual plan.
- Ensure targeted interactions Streamline communication by making it more targeted, efficient, and productive. Tag specific individuals in MAP discussions to ensure messages reach the intended recipients instantly. Tagged individuals receive email notifications, prompting them to engage with the conversation or task. This ensures users do not miss important updates.
- Close more deals Build project plans, assign tasks and due dates, and monitor progress to keep them moving forward and on track.
- Deliver a repeatable process Use MAP templates to guide sellers and customer success managers consistently through a process without missing important steps.
- Improve Sales and Delivery Forecasting Review MAP task statuses to monitor opportunity progress and better predict the likelihood of deal closures.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Digital Sales Rooms > Use Cases for MAPs:
Mutual Action Plans can be leveraged by sales teams in two ways:

- Externally-facing Mutual Action Plan By default, action plans are visible in a room to create a collaborative timeline with prospects to meet deadlines and engage all stakeholders. Example
- Internal-only Close Plan Decide to keep an action plan hidden in the room so it's only visible to sellers and sales leaders. These checklists can be created by sales leadership illustrating all the steps necessary to close the deal and serve as a guide to the seller but do not involve the prospect. Example
- MAPs for new customer onboarding (Customer Success) When a room is used for a new customer, customer success teams can create an onboarding checklist to set expectations and a clear timeline of everything that needs to happen for a timely and successful launch. Assign tasks to the different people/departments that are needed to implement successfully so everyone can be aware of and accountable for their role. Example
- MAPs for new employee onboarding (Training/Management) Rooms can be used for many purposes, including internal onboarding for new hires. You can direct new employees to an onboarding room with all the necessary training and leverage the action plan as a checklist for their onboarding - from specifying which modules to complete and when they should be completed. This provides a great onboarding experience with clear expectations and an easy way to ask questions while ensuring they are moving along the designated timeline. Example

For more information, see Create a Mutual Action Plan Template.

Welcome messages provide a personal touch welcoming a prospect to a room ahead of your first meeting, thanking them for their time on a demo, or showing your excitement for next steps as they review content. They can be updated with a new message over time, as you add more content along the sales cycle or welcome them as a new customer.

This article further explains how you can create a welcome message for a room. It also provides a few welcome message examples you could get inspired by.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Digital Sales Rooms > Create a welcome message:
1. While creating or editing a room, click + Create Welcome Message .
2. On the Add welcome message page, select from any of the following options:

- Record Audio or Video
- Directly record voice or video messages into the platform. For video, once you have recorded it, you can also select a frame from the video as the cover image or upload a custom cover image.
- If you are unable to record a video, see Why can’t I record a video in DSR?
- Text or URLs
- Add a text welcome message, including links, to further provide context around the room.
- Upload
- Upload an audio, video, image, or gif file from your device or any cloud storage options available for your account. This is a great option for videos if you want to use a virtual background. You can also record something more generic to use with room templates or before you have had a chance to meet.

The welcome message is the first thing your customers, prospects, or anyone with whom the room is shared, would view when they visit the room.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Digital Sales Rooms > Welcome message examples:
- Sales - Before a Meeting

"Hello! It's (seller name) from (seller organization). I'm looking forward to meeting with you shortly to discuss how (seller organization) can help you (value proposition). I've put some initial content together here in this room to provide some more context before the call. Take a look around and talk to you soon".

"Hello it's (seller name) from (seller organization). It was great meeting with you earlier to hear more about (customer name) and what your goals are this year and where (seller organization) might be able to help. I've added our demo recording to this room along with some relevant case studies for your use cases to socialize within your team. Let me know if you have any questions and I'm looking forward to our next meeting"

"Hello it's (seller name) from (seller organization). I'm excited about the opportunity to partner with (customer name) to help you achieve (value proposition). I've added the proposal we discussed to the room for you to review. Please let us know if you have any questions. Once it's ready to sign, we can send over a link for signature. Thanks again!"

"Hello it's (CSM name). Welcome to (CSM company)! We're excited you're here and are looking forward to kicking things off for your onboarding and implementation. This room will contain our overview materials, project timeline, and training videos - as well as any recordings or additional materials we generate along the way. Let me know if you have any questions!"

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Digital Sales Rooms > Set a default banner image for the account:
As an admin, you can set a default banner image for all newly created rooms by following the steps mentioned below:

1. Navigate to Settings > Room Options > Room Design .
2. Hover over BANNER IMAGE and click Edit .
3. On the Customize Room page, in the Banner Image section, click Select Image and upload a new banner image. If a banner image already exists, click the Delete icon and select a new image to replace it.
4. On the Select banner image panel, upload a new image or select an image from the pre-loaded gallery.
5. Crop the banner image as needed for display and click Add Banner
6. Click Done .

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Digital Sales Rooms:
A Mutual Action Plan (or MAP) is a document that contains a list of agreed-upon list of tasks needed to get through a deal. It can contain task descriptions, due dates, and ownership assignments for accountability (and alerts) ensuring all stakeholders are aligned on tasks to be performed and deadlines.

You can add multiple MAPs to a room while creating it or editing it. You can:

- Create an MAP from scratch
- Create an MAP using a template

This article further explains each process in detail. It also explains how you can manage mutual action plans within your room.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Digital Sales Rooms > Create a Mutual Action Plan from scratch:
1. Navigate to the room and click + Add to room .
2. Click Add Mutual Action Plan .
3. In the Select template panel, click Create from scratch to create a new MAP template. For more information, see Create a Mutual Action Plan Template .
4. In the Create mutual action plan panel, enter a name for the plan and click Continue .
5. Add a task. Enter the task name and description.
6. Click the Set owner icon to assign the task owner. Owners are users who take ownership of the task and receive email notifications for assignments and updates.
7. Search for the necessary users and select their checkboxes to assign them as task owners.
8. Click Done after selecting the users.
9. Click the Set due date icon and select a date to set the due date for the task. Setting a due date organizes tasks in order by due date. Note : Task owner notifications are triggered only if the room is published.
10. Click on the task to open it.
11. Tag specific individuals on a task to notify them. Type your message in the text box and insert @ before the name of the person you want to mention. Alternatively, select from the list of collaborators and room contacts displayed when you click the @ symbol. This clarifies who the message is intended for and ensures they don’t miss critical updates. Note : The text box is prepopulated with the room owner's name for visitors and the primary contact's name for administrators. The list includes everyone invited to the room, including room collaborators and contacts. To tag someone not invited to the room, type @ followed by their email address. If the system does not find the email address, you can invite that person to the room from this flow. When you tag someone, they receive instant email notifications, prompting them to engage with the conversation or task. Additionally, if you are tagged, you receive an email notification whenever someone replies to the thread. If you reply to a thread and mention someone, they receive a single email notification, not duplicates.
12. If needed, click Mark as Milestone to mark the task as a milestone. This visually signifies a more meaningful step in the MAP (it has no functional difference from a regular task).
13. Click Save .
14. Similarly, add more tasks to the MAP. Once you are done adding all tasks, click X to return to the room. The MAP is added to the room. By default, the MAP is visible. To hide it, click .
15. To add another new MAP to the room, repeat the steps mentioned above.
16. Publish the room to save the MAPs.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Digital Sales Rooms > Create a Mutual Action Plan using a template:
If your organization has MAP templates set up, when you add a mutual action plan, you will see available templates to select from, customize, and save. Templates consist of a name (which is pre-populated as the MAP name), description (for internal guidance only), and tasks.

To create a mutual action plan using a template:

1. Navigate to the room and click + Add to room .
2. Click Add Mutual Action Plan .
3. In the Select template panel, select the template from the list. The plan is created with a pre-populated plan name, plan description, tasks, and milestones.
4. You can customize the plan by updating the plan name and description, adding task owners, dues dates, adding new tasks, and updating or deleting existing tasks.
5. Once you are done updating the plan, click X to return to the room. The MAP is added to the room. By default, the MAP is visible. To hide it, click .
6. To add another MAP to the room, repeat the steps mentioned above.
7. Publish the room to save the MAP.

This article further explains how you can manage mutual action plans.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Digital Sales Rooms > Manage Mutual Action Plans within your room:
Once you have added a MAP to a room, there are several things to expect around updating the plan, email notifications, and discussion options.

At a glance, you can see the progress of your MAPs on the Rooms page:

- On track - - list of tasks and how many have been completed so far
- Fire icon - - indicates tasks due soon
- Info icon - - tasks overdue

If multiple MAPs are added to a room, the MAPs are displayed on the DSR room listing page.

Hover over the pill to view the plans added to the room.

Clicking the pill opens the Mutual Action Plans panel. From this panel, you can add more mutual action plans to the room, view and edit the tasks in existing MAPs, and copy the link to the DSR.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Digital Sales Rooms > Manage Mutual Action Plans within your room > Managing MAPs in rooms:
Mutual action plans are meant to be utilized throughout a longer, multi-step process, which means constantly updating the owners, due dates, and task lists.

You can easily manage your action plan in a room, while editing a room, on the room overview page, or even from the rooms list to quickly update multiple projects you are managing at once by clicking on the MAP icons under each room name.

- You can add new room contacts to the room while assigning tasks.
- By clicking on a specific task, visitors and users can have a discussion to ask clarifying questions, provide more details, or attach files as part of the task before marking it complete.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Digital Sales Rooms > Additional considerations for MAPs:
- After a visitor clicks View Tasks and the MAP tasks are displayed in the right panel, tracking for any content visible in the browser window is disabled.
- If you do not publish your room after adding a MAP, the MAP does not appear in your room. The MAP only shows up to contacts after you publish your room with the MAP visibility turned on.
- After publishing your room with MAP visibility enabled, any changes to the MAP take effect immediately without needing to republish.
- If someone is editing a MAP task while another person saves a change, a pop-up appears with the two versions. You can pick which version to move forward with.
- Email notifications are sent out when tasks are assigned, statuses are updated, and deadlines approach. For more information on when email notifications are sent and to whom they are sent, see Mutual Action Plans - Email Notifications .

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Digital Sales Rooms > Tips for sharing rooms:
- Introduce rooms early on in the cycle

So your prospects see the value in keeping everything in one spot versus multiple email chains and attachments.

- Provide clear calls to action

Give your buyers a reason to click by making sure they know what's in the room, whether it's information to provide context ahead of a demo or the case study they asked for.

- Create email templates

Have templates ready in your engagement solution or email client for different situations to save yourself time - and use personalization tokens when possible.

- Use the Chrome extension

If you're a Gmail or Chrome user, use the email extension to easily insert links into your existing messages.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Digital Sales Rooms > Sample email templates > Sales email: sending a room link before a meeting:
- Goal : Provide valuable content for prospects to educate themselves on your solution and come prepared for a more impactful first demo.
- Timing : Send at least 4-5 hours prior to your scheduled meeting to give them time to review it and yourself time to prepare based on what they engaged with.
- Tip : Don't [over] explain the digital sales room - it's there for their benefit!

Sample email

Hi {First Name},

We are eager to connect with you soon to learn more about the {Buyer Problem/ Challenges Solved} challenges you are currently facing. We are also excited to share how {Seller Company Name} has been helping organizations like yours {Value Proposition}.

To provide some context heading into our meeting, I created a personalized sales room {hyperlink "personalized sales room" text with room link} with some informational materials for you to review. It's about a 4-minute commitment.

If there is anything top of mind that you would like to discuss and have us prepare, please let me know. Looking forward to meeting you and talking to you at {enter date/time of meeting}.

Thanks,

{Seller Signature}

Thank you,

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Digital Sales Rooms > Room overview page > View visitor activity by session:
In DSRs, you can view detailed information about a visitor's activity by session. This provides valuable insights into visitor behavior and engagement in rooms.

Note: When a visitor visits a DSR, it is called a session.

To view the detailed visitor activity for a DSR,

1. Click Rooms in the left navigation bar and then click on Rooms . The Rooms page is displayed.
2. Click on a room. The room overview page opens.
3. Scroll down to the Room Contacts section, then click a contact name.

The following details are displayed:

- Date and time: the date and time of the visit.
- Location: the visitor's location. For example, Los Angeles.
- Device: the device type of the visitor. For example, Mac.
- Visits: number of times the visitor visited the DSR.
- Items viewed: number of items viewed by the visitor.
- Total Time Spent: total time spent in the DSR by the visitor.

Note: The Show stats for filter allows you to view the displayed visitor activity information for all visits or by a specific date and time. The number of content pieces viewed is displayed next to each visit date. This filter is displayed only if a contact visits the room more than once.

4. You can click on a date and time to view detailed visitor activity information.

If content is viewed more than once, you can hover over a date in the Viewed column; the different sessions are displayed.

5. Click View on a session to view the visitor activity details for that particular session.

Click View on a session to view the visitor activity details for that particular session.

The room owner receives an email notification whenever a visitor enters the room. For more information, see Configure notifications sent to room owners.

The email includes a link to the DSR, an overview of the visit, and the time spent on each item in the DSR for each visit. It includes:

- Number of visits: The number of visits to the room by the visitor.
- Items viewed: The number of assets viewed from the total assets shared in the room.
- Time spent: The total time spent by the visitor in the room for the session.

You can also view the time spent by the visitor on each content item. The email sent to notify the room owner is displayed below:

You can click the room name to visit it. Click on View details to view the visitor's detailed analytics for a specific visit.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Digital Sales Rooms > Room overview page > Configure notifications sent to room owners:
You can configure the notifications sent to room owners when a visitor visits a room in the DSR.

To configure notifications for a new visitor,

1. Click Rooms in the left navigation bar and then click on Rooms . The Rooms page is displayed.
2. Click edit room on a DSR.

The Edit Sales Room page opens.

3. Click the Room settings menu.

4. Select the Notifications option.

The Notifications screen is displayed.

- Email when viewed: An email is sent to the room owner when the room is viewed
- Post to Slack when viewed: A Slack notification is sent when the room is viewed

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Digital Sales Rooms > Asset management based on status:
The assets shared from Asset Hub to DSRs are synchronized automatically based on their status and displayed in DSRs.

If an asset's status changes to archived, deleted, or marked as internal in Asset Hub, it is automatically removed from any rooms and room templates where it’s shared.

Note: The asset synchronization is not applicable to internal rooms.

If an asset was viewed in DSR before being archived, deleted, or marked as internal, its view metrics are still displayed on the room overview page.

1. On the Rooms page, click on a room.
2. Click on a room. The DSR opens.
3. Scroll down to the Room Contacts section and click on a contact name. Any Asset Hub content previously viewed and now archived, deleted, or marked as internal is struck out and highlighted by a message. These assets are not displayed in the DSR.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Digital Sales Rooms > How is time tracked?:
The time spent by a visitor is tracked in the following ways:

- For audio and video content, the playback time is tracked.
- For documents, images, text, and embedded content, the time during which they are visible in your active browser tab is tracked.
  - Time does not get tracked when you are on another browser tab.
  - Time is not tracked if the content is not visible in the viewable area of your active browser tab.
  - For rooms in the Tiles layout, time does not get tracked until you click on the piece of content to view.
- For URL links opened in a pop-up window, the time for which the pop-up window is open is tracked.
- For URL links opened in a new browser tab, the tracking is based on whether the link is clicked or not.

In addition to tracking time on content engagement, you can also access the following engagement metrics that are specific to rooms:

- If visitors enter the room, but don't engage with the content
- Sales Actions clicked on
- Room shared with additional email addresses
- Content not viewed

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Digital Sales Rooms:
A Mutual Action Plan (MAP) is a document that contains a list of tasks needed to get through a deal. It can contain task descriptions, due dates, and ownership assignments for accountability ensuring all stakeholders are aligned on tasks to be performed and deadlines.

As an admin, you can create multiple templates for specific audiences, industries, use cases, and any combination you may need. A template consists of a name, description, and tasks. You can create a mutual action plan template:

- From scratch
- From an existing template (Clone a template)

This article further explains each of these processes in detail.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Digital Sales Rooms > Create a Mutual Action Plan template from scratch:
1. On the admin site homepage, Click Rooms and select Templates.
2. Click the Mutual Action Plans tab.
3. Click Create template to create a new template.
4. On the Create template page, enter the template name and description and click Continue .
5. Create a task. Enter the task name and description. Ideally, the name and description should provide a brief overview of the plan and the tasks added to the plan. To mark the task as a milestone, click Mark as Milestone . A milestone visually signifies a more meaningful step in the plan (it has no functional difference from a task).
6. Click Save .
7. Similarly, add other tasks to the plan and click Create Template . Once the template is created successfully, it is added to the list of Mutual Action Plan Templates. Hover over it and click Preview to preview the template design or click the More Options icon to Edit , Clone , or Delete the template. Reps can use this template when adding a mutual action plan to a room. Note :
  - Only admins can create, edit , clone , and delete MAP templates.
  - Both, admins and reps, can view and use MAP templates.
  - MAPs and MAP templates cannot be added or saved to room templates.
  - MAP templates can be added to a room only while creating/editing a room.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Digital Sales Rooms > Edit a Mutual Action Plan template:
Admins can edit the name, description, and tasks added to a MAP template. To edit any of these attributes:

1. On the Templates page, click the Mutual Action Plans tab.
2. Hover on a Mutual Action Plan template and click Edit .
3. Based on your requirements, you can edit the plan by performing the following actions:
  1. Reorder the tasks in the plan.
  2. Unmark a task as a milestone.
  3. Add a new task to the plan.
  4. Delete an existing task.
4. Click Save Changes .

The template is saved with the updated changes.

Note: The changes don’t impact the rooms in which the template is used.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Digital Sales Rooms:
You can collaborate in rooms by starting conversations, sharing content, posting messages, and tagging specific individuals for targeted and efficient interactions. The Conversations feature in DSRs allows you to do all this. It is a great way to keep all stakeholders on the same page over time by storing all of the shared content and any prior conversations and questions that have already been asked and answered.

Using this feature, you can:

- Collect signed agreements, internal process documents, security requirements, or anything prospects typically share with your sellers during sales.
- Receive new customers' logos, user lists, or brand materials as part of their onboarding process.
- Have employees add demo calls or assignments as part of employee onboarding or training rooms.

This article further explains how you can:

- Start a conversation in a room
- Manage file attachments
- Email notifications for conversations
- Hide/Disable conversations in a room

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Digital Sales Rooms > Start a conversation in a room:
1. In the room, click Start a conversation .
2. Type your message in the text box. Tag specific individuals to notify them by inserting @ before their name. Alternatively, select from the list of collaborators and room contacts displayed when you click the @ symbol. Tagging the user clarifies who the message is intended for and ensures they don’t miss critical updates. Note : In the first post of the conversation, the text box is prepopulated with the room owner's name for visitors and the primary contact's name for users. The list that pops up when you type @, includes everyone invited to the room, including room collaborators and contacts. To tag someone not invited to the room, type @ followed by their email address. If the system does not find the email address, you can invite that person to the room using this flow. When you tag someone, they receive instant email notifications, prompting them to engage with the conversation or task. Additionally, if you are tagged, you receive an email notification whenever someone replies to the thread. If you reply to a thread and mention someone, they receive a single email notification, not duplicates. For more details, see DSR email notifications . Tip : Hover over a user’s tag in an existing post to get more details about them, such as their contact number, email address, and job title.
3. To upload an attachment to a post, click the Attach file icon. Select a file downloaded on your system and add a note to provide better context. Note : Adding a note is optional. However, it is recommended as a good practice. You can attach a file even while responding to a comment in a conversation. For more information on how users are notified about attachments, see Email notifications for conversations .
4. Click Post . An email notification is sent to the user to whom the comment is addressed, to tagged users, and to all other users who have commented on the conversation. For more information, see DSR email notifications .

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Digital Sales Rooms > Manage file attachments:
You and your room visitors can download the files directly from the room. To download files attached to a room:

1. Hover over the attachment. The Download icon appears.
2. Click the Download icon. The file is downloaded to your system.
3. As a room owner, you can also manage all attachments from the Room Statistics page. Click the Show icon in the Attachments section. The Files panel opens and displays a list of files attached to the room. It also displays the date on which the most recent file was uploaded.
4. Click the View discussion icon against the file to view the discussion to which the file is attached. You can also click the Download icon to download the file.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Digital Sales Rooms > Email notifications for conversations:
Email notifications are triggered when a new post is made under Conversations, a file is attached to a post, a user is tagged in a post, or a response is received on the post. See below for more information on emails received for each action.

- Initial conversation thread started - Both the seller and room visitor can start the initial thread. When the seller posts a message, the primary contact and all tagged users receive an email notification. When a visitor posts a message, room owners receive alerts. The emails include a link to reply that navigates them to the room.
- Replies in a conversation thread - When replying to a conversation thread, the initial visitor who started the conversation thread, anyone else who has commented in that conversation thread, and anyone tagged on the thread receive an email notification that a new reply has been posted. These messages also include a Reply button. Note : Email notifications are not sent to the author of the message.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > SCORM Content:
SCORM (Sharable Content Object Reference Model) is a standard that ensures any e-Learning content created using various authoring tools is compatible with the Mindtickle platform. SCORM as a learning object is used in courses and quick updates.

This article explains how to navigate SCORM in Mindtickle.

1. Sign in to your learning site and select the required course within the series.

2. Click Start course to start the course and access its content.

3. Within the topics, navigate to the SCORM learning object.

4. Depending on the SCORM configurations set by the admin, the SCORM file opens either in-line within the learning object or in full-screen mode.

For information on setting the SCORM configurations, see SCORM Content on Mindtickle.

- If the SCORM file opens in-line, it displays as follows.
- If the SCORM file opens in full-screen mode, an Opening in full screen message displays. Click Yes to continue viewing the SCORM content.

Note:

- Full-screen mode ensures minimal distractions so you can focus better on the content. If you are facing issues with the content, click the Facing issues with this content link in the footer to navigate to the SCORM Checklist for learner article.
- If you’re unable to access the SCORM content and see the error message MissingKey – Missing Key-Pair-Id query parameter or cookie value , it means that cookies are disabled in your web browser for the Mindtickle site. Mindtickle requires cookies to authenticate your session and load SCORM content. To access the SCORM content,
  - Enable cookies in your web browser for the Mindtickle website.
  - Refresh the page or try accessing the SCORM content again.

If you’re still unable to access the SCORM content after enabling cookies, contact the Mindtickle Support team for further assistance

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Digital Sales Rooms > Key benefits:
The following are the benefits of the DSR-Pipedrive integration:

- Enhance rep productivity: Reps can quickly identify and link new rooms to existing deals, saving time and effort. The linked rooms are automatically updated with Pipedrive deal information.
- Track user engagement for deals: Identify and track the engagement of multiple contacts for deals. If a new user from the buying organization accesses a room, the user’s contact is automatically created and enriched in Pipedrive. The room activity details are automatically written to the linked Pipedrive deal, organization, and contact.
- View actionable insights: Analytics provide valuable information on your rooms' performance and the efficacy of content shared in rooms. View content shared for deals, generate reports and gain insights into the impact and ROI of assets shared in DSRs.
- Increase DSR adoption: Mindtickle notifies reps to create rooms for synced Pipedrive deals. The notifications can be configured based on the deal type, stage, and amount. This increases DSR usage and helps implement best practices for room creation.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Digital Sales Rooms > Sync Data from Pipedrive to DSR:
If your organization uses Pipedrive integration, you can quickly integrate it with DSR from Settings > Integrations. The integration allows you to pull in deals, contacts, and organizations to spot which deals do not have a room created or edit an existing one as the sale progresses. This sync is also a requirement to sync activities back into Pipedrive.

To integrate Pipedrive with DSR:

1. On the admin site homepage, click Rooms and select Settings .
2. On the Settings page, click the Integrations tab
3. Click Connect next to Pipedrive to begin the authentication process. Note : You can perform this action only if your role has the Manage DSR ( MANAGE_DIGITAL_SALES_ROOMS ) permission. For more information, see Digital Sales Rooms Permissions .
4. A confirmation message displays on the screen once the integration is set up successfully. It also lists the most recent syncs and the details, such as the number of users, organizations, contacts, and deals synced from your Pipedrive account. The data is auto-synced periodically. To perform a manual sync, click Sync . Note :
  - The initial data sync takes several hours, depending on how many records exist in the CRM. However, it is processed without any work on your part. Future syncs only validate for changes to any records and take a few minutes.
  - The CRM contacts must have an email address to sync.
  - Deals do not require a primary contact.
5. To see all the synced data within the platform, click Rooms on the left navigation bar and select Deals & Contacts . The Deals & Contacts page displays the following tabs:

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Digital Sales Rooms > Push Data from DSR to Pipedrive:
In addition to pulling data from Pipedrive, you can decide whether to push data into Pipedrive and create activities and contacts within the platform for key events.

Activities can be created when:

- a room is created, edited, and visited
- a new comment is posted under Conversations
- a mutual action plan task is marked as Completed

Contacts are created when a room is visited by a contact not already in your CRM. The new contact is associated with a Deal and Organization, if available.

To enable Pipedrive activity creation, when setting up a new sync, you are presented with the following options:

Tip: Enable Create new Contacts for unmatching emails to ensure that contacts are created in Pipedrive automatically every time a new visitor visits a room. Furthermore, to enhance the contact information of customers visiting your DSR, enable Allow automatic enrichment of contact data from the Company Profile page. Users receive enriched contact data that may include the customer’s first and last name, phone number, organization, job title, LinkedIn profile link, and profile image. For more information, see Set Up Digital Sales Rooms: Company Profile.

These options are configurable by organization to ensure they match your CRM needs. Switch the respective toggle to ON or OFF based on your requirements.

To update these settings:

1. Click Configure . The Configure Pipedrive data sync pop-up appears.

Make the necessary updates and click the Close icon.

Once these settings are configured:

- The Notifications tab is configured on the DSR Settings page. You can set up notifications for new deals created in Pipedrive from this tab.
- Activities are created in the following format in Pipedrive. Depending on your configuration settings, the corresponding data for the activity is displayed.

Note:

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Mobile App:
SCORM (Sharable Content Object Reference Model) is a standard that ensures any e-Learning content created using various authoring tools is compatible with the Mindtickle platform.

This article explains how to navigate SCORM in the Mindtickle Mobile App.

1. Once you log in to the Mindtickle mobile app as a learner, navigate to the required series.

2. In the series, navigate to the module and tap the SCORM learning object to consume the SCORM content.

3. The SCORM content is displayed.

Note: SCORM content is available on a mobile app with an active internet connection.

Tap anywhere to interact utilizes the entire screen of the mobile app for the SCORM interaction.

Any swipe gesture such as drag and drop is applicable to the SCORM content. The traditional swipe to move to the next content is disabled until you Close the SCORM content.

4. If SCORM is disabled for the mobile app, a message displays to access the SCORM content on the web browser.

5. The score and competition status is displayed at the bottom of the screen.

6. Once you have completed the SCORM, click Save and exit to save the score and completion status manually. If the score and completion status are reflected correctly within SCORM but not on Mindtickle, the Save and exit option allows learners to get their scores and completion updated on Mindtickle.

Note: The Save and exit option displays only if the admin has enabled it for the SCORM. If the Save and exit option does not display, click the Close icon to exit the SCORM.

- Receive opportunity data from Salesforce: Enable this toggle to get all the SFDC opportunity information in Mindtickle.
- Send coaching data to Salesforce opportunity: Select the required field option from the drop-down list under Select Opportunity Field. After completing a Coaching Session, the field under the Opportunity on SFDC is set to true.Note: You must select the Checkbox Data type custom field option from the drop-down list. For more information on how to create a Data type field in SFDC, see Create Custom Fields. By default, this field should be unchecked.
- Click Save.

7. The Coaching and SFDC syncing process begins.

Note: It may take up to 24 hours for the sync to complete.

After the sync is successfully completed, you can see a green check mark, as shown in the image below.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Collaboration App Notifications > Set up Mindtickle in your Webex Teams workspace:
1. Open Webex Teams workspace and click the + icon next to the search bar. From the options that appear, select Send a direct message .
2. On the screen that appears, type in Mindtickle@webex.bot and click the Invite button. The Mindtickle bot appears in the left panel.
3. Click the Mindtickle bot and enter the connect command: connect domain.mindtickle.com in your workspace to ensure your learning site is connected to the app. For example, if your learning site is acme.mindtickle.com, then the command will be connect acme.mindtickle.com.
4. A Connect button appears.
5. Click Connect . You are redirected to the Mindtickle admin site on a different tab. Log in with your admin credentials.
6. On a successful connection, the following message displays.
7. To disable the integration for your learners, enter the following command: disconnect domain.mindtickle.com. For example, if your learning site is acme.mindtickle.com , then the command will be disconnect acme.mindtickle.com.
8. After the connection is made, the learners start receiving Mindtickle notifications. To learn more about the types of notifications, see the Types for notifications section.

Once the integration is complete, learners and managers will start receiving notifications in their Webex workspace.

Note: To ensure Mindtickle notification deep links work as expected on Webex iOS mobile app, make sure the following setting is enabled.

1. Open the Webex Mobile App .
2. Open Settings > General and enable Open web links in default browser .

The type of notifications and their descriptions are as listed below.

| Notification | Description |
| --- | --- |
| SERIES INVITATION | Series invitations sent to learners |
| ENTITY INVITATION | Module invitations sent to learners |
| ENTITY REMINDER | Module reminders sent to learners |
| ENTITY UPDATE | Module updates sent to learners |
| FEEDBACK REVIEWER EDIT | Notifications sent to learners when the reviewer edits the score or feedback of a Coaching Sessions or Missions module |
| FEEDBACK REVIEWER SUBMIT | Notifications sent to a reviewer to submit feedback about a Coaching Sessions or Missions module |
| INVITATION REVIEW | Coaching Sessions or Missions review invitation sent to reviewer |
| LEARNER RESET MISSION | Notifications sent to learners when a Mission is reset |
| LEARNER REVIEW APPROVED | Notifications sent to the reviewers when a learner approves a submitted review |
| LEARNER REVIEW DISAPPROVED | Notifications sent to the reviewer when a learner disapproves a submitted review |
| REMINDER CLUBBED | Reminders sent to learners for the entire Series |
| COACHING SCHEDULE | Notifications sent to reviewers about scheduling a Coaching Session |
| SESSION ENROLLMENT UPDATED | Notifications sent to the enrolled learners when the ILT is updated |

Note:

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Data Sharing:
This article explains how to directly access your Mindtickle platform data for reporting purposes by integrating your Snowflake account with Mindtickle’s Snowflake account. In addition to accessing Mindtickle analytics data through the OData-based reporting APIs, customers can take advantage of Snowflake Data Sharing, a more scalable and flexible solution that has been widely adopted. This integration enables seamless and near real-time access to your analytics data, empowering more advanced and customizable reporting and analytics capabilities.

Secure access to your Mindtickle data is provided through Snowflake’s Secure Data Sharing feature. It delivers direct access to ready-to-query data from Mindtickle to your Snowflake account across clouds and regions. Accessing your Mindtickle data through Snowflake Secure Data Sharing is similar to accessing it using the reporting APIs. Mindtickle’s metadata tables are shared as “views” in Snowflake. The “views” provide granular information related to modules, content, users, and your users’ performance on the assigned modules.

All reporting API tables are available in Snowflake Secure Data Sharing as “views” except for the Asset Hub tables. For information on the available tables/views, see Mindtickle metadata tables for Snowflake Data Sharing.

Here is how Secure Data Sharing differs from the Mindtickle's reporting APIs:

- Access to ready-to-query data. Eliminates the need to copy or transfer data. With direct access to the database, you can analyze the data even before copying it.
- No data limits (unlike the reporting API, which has certain OData-related limitations). Scalable to 10M records and beyond.
- No need to apply pagination.
- Mindtickle’s OData-based reporting API has “incremental” tables, but Snowflake Data Sharing does not require such tables (views). All data can be fetched from the primary table, which includes all the historical data for both active and inactive users.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Data Sharing > Prerequisites:
The following are the prerequisites to use Snowflake Data Sharing:

1. Snowflake account: You must have a Snowflake account to make use of Secure Data Sharing to access your Mindtickle data. If you do not have a Snowflake account, you can use our reporting API to access data.
2. Snowflake permissions: To access a share from Mindtickle and create a database from it, the user must have the ACCOUNTADMIN role in your Snowflake account. If you want a user with other roles to perform this task, they must be assigned the following permission:

- IMPORT SHARE: Enables viewing the inbound shares shared by Mindtickle with your (customer’s) Snowflake account. Also enables creating databases from inbound shares; requires the global CREATE DATABASE privilege.

For more information, see Snowflake’s documentation.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Data Sharing > Integrate your Snowflake account with Mindtickle:
Before you can access your Mindtickle data in Snowflake through Secure Data Sharing, you need to integrate your Snowflake account with Mindtickle. To initiate the integration, you need to provide a few details on your Snowflake account to Mindtickle.

Perform the following to integrate your Snowflake account with Mindtickle:

1. In the admin site sidebar, click Account > Settings > Security & integrations. On the Security and integrations page, scroll down to the Data Sharing section.

1. Under this section, enter the following details on your Snowflake account and then click Submit to initiate the process of connecting your Snowflake with Mindtickle. You can find your Snowflake account information using the Snowflake web interface. Click the user profile menu in the top-right corner to view the details under Account Information.
  - Organization Name: The organization name given in your Snowflake account.
  - Account Name: The name of your account in Snowflake.
  - Account Identifier (Locator): Your Snowflake account identifier.
  - Cloud: The cloud storage of your Snowflake account. The available options are: AWS (Amazon Web Services), Azure (Microsoft Azure), and GCP (Google Cloud Platform).
  - Region: The region of the selected cloud storage of your Snowflake.
2. Once you have submitted your Snowflake details, we will start the process of integrating your Snowflake data with Mindtickle. It takes a few days to enable the functionality and complete the data integration with your Snowflake. Your Mindtickle CSM will inform you once the data integration is successful and the Mindtickle data share is available to use in your Snowflake. Additionally, when the integration is successful, the Data Sharing section displays a green checkmark next to the “Snowflake” heading.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Data Sharing > Verify Snowflake account details:
After integrating Snowflake with Mindtickle, it’s important to verify that the account details you entered in Mindtickle match exactly with those shown in your Snowflake account. Even minor mismatches, especially in the Account Identifier or Region, can cause connection issues and prevent data from syncing correctly. The steps below explain how to find and review these details.

Perform the following to verify your Snowflake account details:

1. Sign in to your Snowflake account.
2. Open your account settings: Click the user profile icon, select Account / Organization , and then click View account details .
3. The Account details pop-up opens, displaying your account’s identification information along with the associated cloud provider and regional deployment details.
4. In the Account tab, review the following values and confirm they match exactly with what you entered in Mindtickle during integration:
  - Organization name: The organization name shown in your Snowflake account.
  - Account name: The name of your specific account in Snowflake.

After integrating Snowflake with Mindtickle, it’s important to verify that the account details you entered in Mindtickle match exactly with those shown in your Snowflake account. Even minor mismatches, especially in the Account Identifier or Region, can cause connection issues and prevent data from syncing correctly. The steps below explain how to find and review these details.

Perform the following to verify your Snowflake account details:

1. Sign in to your Snowflake account.
2. Open your account settings: Click the user profile icon, select Account / Organization , and then click View account details .
3. The Account details pop-up opens, displaying your account’s identification information along with the associated cloud provider and regional deployment details.
4. In the Account tab, review the following values and confirm they match exactly with what you entered in Mindtickle during integration:
  - Organization name: The organization name shown in your Snowflake account.
  - Account name: The name of your specific account in Snowflake.
  - Account identifier (locator): Your Snowflake account identifier.
  - Cloud: The cloud storage of your Snowflake account. The available options are: AWS (Amazon Web Services), Azure (Microsoft Azure), and GCP (Google Cloud Platform).
  - Region: The region of the selected cloud storage of your Snowflake.
5. Ensure that the above details exactly match the values entered in Mindtickle. Any discrepancies (such as extra spaces, case differences, or incorrect regions) can prevent the integration from functioning properly. Review each field carefully and update any mismatched information to ensure a successful connection.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Data Sharing > Access your platform data in Snowflake:
Perform the following to access your Mindtickle data in Snowflake through Secure Data Sharing:

1. Sign in to your Snowflake account.
2. On the home page, go to Shares > Inbound. The Secure Shares page lists inbound shares that includes shared with your account by Mindtickle.

1. For the share that is shared by Mindtickle, you need to first create a database out of it to run queries. You can view the Comment column to identify the share from Mindtickle. Select the share in the list and click Create Database From Secure Share.

1. Perform the following on the Create Database from Secure Share pop-up and then click Create Database:
  - Database name: Provide an appropriate, identifiable name for the database.
  - Grant access to: Select the roles to whom you want to grant access to this database. Only the users with selected roles will be able to run queries on the database.
  - Comment: (Optional) Add any comments that will help identify this database.

1. The Database Overview pop-up provides an overview of the actions performed in the previous step. Click OK.

1. The newly-created database is listed under the Secure Shares page.

1. Now, navigate to Worksheets. This is where you will run queries on the database. The left navigation panel lists the database and the “views” within the database. These views have the same columns and data as the tables in Mindtickle’s reporting API.

1. Before running a query on a view, ensure to check that the appropriate role, warehouse, database, and scheme are selected.

1. To run a query against a view, hover over the name, click the three-dot button and then select Place Name in SQL.

1. Modify the query as required and then click Run to run the query.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Data Sharing > Access data from multiple learning sites:
On the Mindtickle platform, a customer organization can have multiple learning sites for various purposes. For example, Acme Inc. as an organization has two learning sites on Mindtickle: acme.mindtickle.com and acmepartners.mindtickle.com. This section explains how to access and analyze data of two learning sites through Snowflake Data Sharing.

In Data Sharing with Snowflake, you can create a separate database for each learning site. If you have two learning sites, you need to create two databases; a single database cannot accommodate multiple learning sites. Then, make use of SQL queries to retrieve data from both databases simultaneously.

Example scenario

Let’s take the example of Acme Inc. as the customer organization, who wants to retrieve the user group data of their learning site using the UserGroups table. They have two Mindtickle learning sites:

- acme.mindtickle.com
- acmepartners.mindtickle.com

Mindtickle has created data shares in Snowflake for both learning sites and Acme has created two databases (“acme” and “acmepartners”) from the shares. Acme can now run SQL queries to retrieve data from the two databases as explained below.

- To retrieve the UserGroups data from the acme.mindtickle.com learning site:SELECT *, “acme” AS CompanyName FROM acme.usergroups;The query returns the following data:

| UserId | GroupId | AddedOn | GroupName | CompanyName |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 1 | 02/03/2023 | Sample Group | acme |
| 2 | 1 | 02/03/2023 | Sample Group | acme |

- Likewise, to retrieve the UserGroups data from the acmepartners.mindtickle.com learning site:SELECT *, “acmepartners” AS CompanyName FROM acmepartners.usergroups;The query returns the following data:
