chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Data Sharing > FAQs:
The following are the frequently asked questions (FAQs):

- Who can use Snowflake Secure Data Sharing?
  - Any Mindtickle customer with a Snowflake account can use it to access their Mindtickle data for reporting purposes.
- What are the prerequisites for using Snowflake Secure Data Sharing?
  - Must have a Snowflake account and appropriate permissions. See the prerequisites.
- What are the tables (views) available in Snowflake Secure Data Sharing?
  - All reporting API tables are available in Snowflake Secure Data Sharing as “views” except for the Asset Hub tables. For information on the available tables/views, see Mindtickle metadata tables for Snowflake Data Sharing.
- Is the view data realtime/live? What is the refresh rate for the view data?
  - No, the data is not realtime/live. There are three data refresh rates for various views as follows:
    - Views with a 2-hour refresh rate: Users, UserGroup, SeriesModules, Modules, SeriesModuleSections, SeriesCollection, LearnerModulePerformances, LearnerModulePerformancesIncremental, ModuleTags, LearningObjectTag, RIUser, CompetencyUser, and CohortCadencesDate.
    - Views with a 6-hour refresh rate: SeriesCertification and SeriesUserCertification.
    - Views with a 24-hour refresh rate: CourseObject, CourseObjectIncremental, QuickUpdateObject, QuickUpdateObjectIncremental, AssessmentObject, AssessmentObjectIncremental, MissionParameter, CoachingSessionParameter, Checklist, ILT, ILTSession, QuestObject, MissionAIInsight, CompetencyAssessmentParameter, SeriesRating, SeriesUserRating, MissionAIInsight, Mission, CoachingSession, and CompetencyAssessment.
- Can customers keep using the reporting API while also using Snowflake Secure Data Sharing?
  - Yes, you can keep using both ways to access your Mindtickle data. We recommend using Snowflake Secure Data Sharing because it provides an enhanced approach to access data.

Note: Currently, Mindtickle creates a dedicated data share for each customer based on their region and cloud service. Mindtickle plans to support Snowflake Private Listings in a future release, which will eliminate the need to create separate shares for different regions and cloud providers.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Data Sharing:
This article provides information on Mindtickle’s metadata tables that you can query in Snowflake through Secure Data Sharing. Mindtickle’s metadata tables are shared as “views” in Snowflake. The tables (views) provide engagement and performance data of your users on content on the Mindtickle platform.

You can directly access your Mindtickle platform data for reporting purposes by integrating your Snowflake account with Mindtickle’s. Secure access to your Mindtickle data is provided through Snowflake’s Secure Data Sharing feature. It delivers direct access to ready-to-query data from Mindtickle to your Snowflake account across clouds and regions, with on-demand fulfillment.

For information on using Snowflake’s Secure Data Sharing to query and access your Mindtickle data, see Use Snowflake to directly access platform data. This article also includes a quick overview of the data update frequency (data refresh rate) in the FAQs section.

| Performance and Completion DataThese tables provide performance and completion data for learners across content in Mindtickle. |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MODULE LEVEL: Generic | LearnerModulePerformances | This table contains each Learner's performance & engagement details, for all Modules that they have been invited to. These details include variables like SeriesId, ModuleId, UserId, invitation date, start & end date, and metrics such as Completion Percentage and Score.Note: The “CompletionStatus” field for Missions will not include Review Pending statuses, such as 1/2 review pending and 2/2 review pending.Granularity: UserId x ModuleId x SeriesIdUpdate Frequency: 2 hoursYou can calculate series completion rate as follows:Series completion rate = (Modules completed by a learner in the series) / (Modules assigned to the learner in the series) x 100Where:Modules completed by a learner in the series can be identified by filtering for HasCompleted = True.Modules assigned to the learner in the series can be obtained by including both HasCompleted = True and HasCompleted = False. |
| MODULE LEVEL: Specific Modules | CoachingSessions | This table contains Session level information. For each Coaching Session, you can find a ModuleId, the Session number, name and email address of the Reviewer, and the time at which Session was reviewed and scheduled.Granularity: UserId x ModuleId x SessionNoUpdate Frequency: 24 hours |
| Mission | This table contains information for each reattempt that a Learner takes for a Mission. You can find details such as the ModuleId, the reattempt number, the name and email address of the Reviewer, the time when the Mission was reviewed and submitted.Granularity: UserId x ModuleId x ReattemptNo x ReviewerIdUpdate Frequency: 24 hours |  |
| CompetencyAssessment | This table contains module-level information such as Learner and Manager/Reviewer names, records of completed assessments.Granularity: UserId x ModuleId x SessionNoUpdate Frequency: 24 hours |  |
| CONTENT ITEM LEVEL | CoachingSessionsParameters | This table contains information for Evaluation Parameters within each Session for a Learner. You can find a ModuleId, the Session number, its version; the name, Score, and feedback of the Evaluation Parameter, name of the Section it belongs to.Granularity: UserId x ModuleId x Parameter x SessionNoUpdate Frequency: 24 hours |
| MissionParameters | This table contains information for Evaluation Parameters within a Mission for each Learner. You can find the ModuleId, the reattempt number, the name and email address of the Reviewer; name, Score of the Evaluation Parameter.Granularity: UserId x ModuleId x ReattemptNo x ParamIdUpdate Frequency: 24 hours |  |
| MissionAIInsights | This table contains Mission AI insights data for each Learner. You can find metrics, such as the ModuleId, number of reattempts, score on various insights (content, articulation, and text sentiment), and keywords to use and avoid.Granularity: UserId x ModuleId x ReattemptNoUpdate Frequency: 24 hours |  |
| CompetencyAssessmentParameters | This table contains parameter-level data of the assessments completed by the Learner and the Manager/Reviewer such as score, feedback, and rating.Granularity: UserId x ModuleId x Parameter x SessionNoUpdate Frequency: 24 hours |  |
| CourseObjects | This table contains Learners' details for all Learning Content, Questions, and Feedback in a Course that they have attempted. You can find metrics such as Completion State, start time, end time, correct and incorrect responses to Questions, number of Lifelines used by a Learner.Granularity: UserId x ModuleId x LearningObjectIdUpdate Frequency: 24 hours |  |
| QuickUpdateObjects | This table contains Learners' details for all Learning Content, Questions, and Feedback in a Quick-Update that they have attempted. You can find metrics such as Completion State, start time, end time, correct and incorrect responses to Questions, number of Lifelines used by a Learner.Granularity: UserId x ModuleId x LearningObjectIdUpdate Frequency: 24 hours |  |
| AssessmentObjects | This table contains Learner's details for all Questions in the Assessment they have attempted. You can find metrics such as Completion State, start time, end time, correct and incorrect responses to Questions, number of Lifelines used by a Learner.Granularity: UserId x ModuleId x LearningObjectIdUpdate Frequency: 24 hours |  |
| ChecklistObjects | This table contains Learner's details for all Tasks in the Checklist that they have completed. You can find metrics such as Completion Status, Score, number of reattempts for each Task.Granularity: UserId x ModuleId x TaskIdUpdate Frequency: 24 hours |  |
| ILTObjects | This table contains the Learner's details for each ILT session. For each session the Learner has enrolled in, you can find various metrics, such as Score, Attendance Status, Session Location, Start Time, End Time, and Instructor Names.Granularity: UserId x ModuleId x SessionIdUpdate Frequency: 24 hours |  |
| ILTSessions | This table contains metrics for ILT sessions. For each session, you can find various metrics, such as Session Type, Start Time, End Time, Maximum Enrollments, and Instructor Names. Also provides metrics that show if Self Check-In, auto-attendance (for ILT-Zoom webinars), automatic enrollment, and waiting list were enabled. The metrics also show the number of Learners who were enrolled, attended, and waitlisted for a session as well as the number of Learners invited to the ILT.Granularity: ModuleId x SessionIdUpdate Frequency: 24 hours |  |
| QuestObjects | This table contains granular level data of Learners for all Questions in a Quest. You can find metrics such as the number of attempts, start time, percentage improvement, responses given by the Learner for each attempt, total Score, Mastery status.Granularity: UserId x ModuleId x LearningObjectIdUpdate Frequency: 24 hours |  |
| MetadataThese tables provide metadata details for objects in Mindtickle, such as users, series, series ratings, modules and content items. |  |  |
| USER DETAILS | Users | This table provides attributes for each user like UserId, the date & time on which the user was added to the platform, the email address, name, location, department, and job title of the user.Granularity: UserIdUpdate Frequency: 2 hoursNote: The UserID (a unique identifier) in the tables is stored in a decimal format, whereas the platform displays user IDs in a hexadecimal (alphanumeric) format. If you’d like to view the UserID in the same format as on the platform UI, you can convert it from decimal to hexadecimal when querying or creating views. For this conversion, you can use the HEX_ENCODE function in Snowflake, as outlined in the Snowflake documentation. |
| UserGroups | This table contains the mapping of Users within a Group. For each Group (GroupId and Group Name) you can find a list of UserIds and the date on which the Users were added to the Group.Granularity: UserId x GroupIdUpdate Frequency: 2 hours |  |
| SERIES/MODULE DETAILS | SeriesCollection | This table contains Series attributes such as SeriesId, Series name, name of the User who created the Series, date & time at which the Series was created, the current state of the Series, visibility of the Series to Users, and the number of published Modules in the Series.Granularity: SeriesIdUpdate Frequency: 2 hours |

| MODULE LEVEL: Generic | LearnerModulePerformances | This table contains each Learner's performance & engagement details, for all Modules that they have been invited to. These details include variables like SeriesId, ModuleId, UserId, invitation date, start & end date, and metrics such as Completion Percentage and Score.Note: The “CompletionStatus” field for Missions will not include Review Pending statuses, such as 1/2 review pending and 2/2 review pending.Granularity: UserId x ModuleId x SeriesIdUpdate Frequency: 2 hoursYou can calculate series completion rate as follows:Series completion rate = (Modules completed by a learner in the series) / (Modules assigned to the learner in the series) x 100Where:Modules completed by a learner in the series can be identified by filtering for HasCompleted = True.Modules assigned to the learner in the series can be obtained by including both HasCompleted = True and HasCompleted = False. |
| MODULE LEVEL: Specific Modules | CoachingSessions | This table contains Session level information. For each Coaching Session, you can find a ModuleId, the Session number, name and email address of the Reviewer, and the time at which Session was reviewed and scheduled.Granularity: UserId x ModuleId x SessionNoUpdate Frequency: 24 hours |
| Mission | This table contains information for each reattempt that a Learner takes for a Mission. You can find details such as the ModuleId, the reattempt number, the name and email address of the Reviewer, the time when the Mission was reviewed and submitted.Granularity: UserId x ModuleId x ReattemptNo x ReviewerIdUpdate Frequency: 24 hours |  |
| CompetencyAssessment | This table contains module-level information such as Learner and Manager/Reviewer names, records of completed assessments.Granularity: UserId x ModuleId x SessionNoUpdate Frequency: 24 hours |  |
| CONTENT ITEM LEVEL | CoachingSessionsParameters | This table contains information for Evaluation Parameters within each Session for a Learner. You can find a ModuleId, the Session number, its version; the name, Score, and feedback of the Evaluation Parameter, name of the Section it belongs to.Granularity: UserId x ModuleId x Parameter x SessionNoUpdate Frequency: 24 hours |
| MissionParameters | This table contains information for Evaluation Parameters within a Mission for each Learner. You can find the ModuleId, the reattempt number, the name and email address of the Reviewer; name, Score of the Evaluation Parameter.Granularity: UserId x ModuleId x ReattemptNo x ParamIdUpdate Frequency: 24 hours |  |
| MissionAIInsights | This table contains Mission AI insights data for each Learner. You can find metrics, such as the ModuleId, number of reattempts, score on various insights (content, articulation, and text sentiment), and keywords to use and avoid.Granularity: UserId x ModuleId x ReattemptNoUpdate Frequency: 24 hours |  |
| CompetencyAssessmentParameters | This table contains parameter-level data of the assessments completed by the Learner and the Manager/Reviewer such as score, feedback, and rating.Granularity: UserId x ModuleId x Parameter x SessionNoUpdate Frequency: 24 hours |  |
| CourseObjects | This table contains Learners' details for all Learning Content, Questions, and Feedback in a Course that they have attempted. You can find metrics such as Completion State, start time, end time, correct and incorrect responses to Questions, number of Lifelines used by a Learner.Granularity: UserId x ModuleId x LearningObjectIdUpdate Frequency: 24 hours |  |
| QuickUpdateObjects | This table contains Learners' details for all Learning Content, Questions, and Feedback in a Quick-Update that they have attempted. You can find metrics such as Completion State, start time, end time, correct and incorrect responses to Questions, number of Lifelines used by a Learner.Granularity: UserId x ModuleId x LearningObjectIdUpdate Frequency: 24 hours |  |
| AssessmentObjects | This table contains Learner's details for all Questions in the Assessment they have attempted. You can find metrics such as Completion State, start time, end time, correct and incorrect responses to Questions, number of Lifelines used by a Learner.Granularity: UserId x ModuleId x LearningObjectIdUpdate Frequency: 24 hours |  |
| ChecklistObjects | This table contains Learner's details for all Tasks in the Checklist that they have completed. You can find metrics such as Completion Status, Score, number of reattempts for each Task.Granularity: UserId x ModuleId x TaskIdUpdate Frequency: 24 hours |  |
| ILTObjects | This table contains the Learner's details for each ILT session. For each session the Learner has enrolled in, you can find various metrics, such as Score, Attendance Status, Session Location, Start Time, End Time, and Instructor Names.Granularity: UserId x ModuleId x SessionIdUpdate Frequency: 24 hours |  |
| ILTSessions | This table contains metrics for ILT sessions. For each session, you can find various metrics, such as Session Type, Start Time, End Time, Maximum Enrollments, and Instructor Names. Also provides metrics that show if Self Check-In, auto-attendance (for ILT-Zoom webinars), automatic enrollment, and waiting list were enabled. The metrics also show the number of Learners who were enrolled, attended, and waitlisted for a session as well as the number of Learners invited to the ILT.Granularity: ModuleId x SessionIdUpdate Frequency: 24 hours |  |
| QuestObjects | This table contains granular level data of Learners for all Questions in a Quest. You can find metrics such as the number of attempts, start time, percentage improvement, responses given by the Learner for each attempt, total Score, Mastery status.Granularity: UserId x ModuleId x LearningObjectIdUpdate Frequency: 24 hours |  |
| MetadataThese tables provide metadata details for objects in Mindtickle, such as users, series, series ratings, modules and content items. |  |  |
| USER DETAILS | Users | This table provides attributes for each user like UserId, the date & time on which the user was added to the platform, the email address, name, location, department, and job title of the user.Granularity: UserIdUpdate Frequency: 2 hoursNote: The UserID (a unique identifier) in the tables is stored in a decimal format, whereas the platform displays user IDs in a hexadecimal (alphanumeric) format. If you’d like to view the UserID in the same format as on the platform UI, you can convert it from decimal to hexadecimal when querying or creating views. For this conversion, you can use the HEX_ENCODE function in Snowflake, as outlined in the Snowflake documentation. |
| UserGroups | This table contains the mapping of Users within a Group. For each Group (GroupId and Group Name) you can find a list of UserIds and the date on which the Users were added to the Group.Granularity: UserId x GroupIdUpdate Frequency: 2 hours |  |
| SERIES/MODULE DETAILS | SeriesCollection | This table contains Series attributes such as SeriesId, Series name, name of the User who created the Series, date & time at which the Series was created, the current state of the Series, visibility of the Series to Users, and the number of published Modules in the Series.Granularity: SeriesIdUpdate Frequency: 2 hours |
| SeriesModules | This table contains the mapping of Modules within a Series. You can find the SeriesId, ModuleId of Modules within the Series, and the current state of each Module.Granularity: SeriesId x ModuleIdUpdate Frequency: 2 hours |  |
| SeriesModuleSections | This table contains the mapping of Modules to Sections within the Series. You can find the SeriesId, SectionId, Section name, and the date on which the Section was created.Note: This table is visible only if you have enabled Sections for your Learning Site and at least one Series contains a Section in it.Granularity: SeriesId x ModuleId x SectionIdUpdate Frequency: 2 hours |  |
| Modules | This table contains Module attributes such as ModuleID, Module version, Certificate Score, passing Score, Module name and type, name of the User who has created the Module, date and time when it was created and last modified.Granularity: ModuleIdUpdate Frequency: 2 hours |  |
| SERIES RATING DETAILS | SeriesRating | This table contains information about Learners’ ratings for a particular Series. For each Series, it provides information on the total number of Learners who rated the Series and the average of their ratings.Granularity: SeriesIdUpdate Frequency: 24 hours |
| SeriesUserRating | This table contains information about a particular Learner’s rating for a Series. For each Series, it provides information on the Learner who rated the Series and their latest rating.Granularity: SeriesId x UserIdUpdate Frequency: 24 hours |  |
| SERIES CERTIFICATION DETAILS | SeriesCertification | This table contains information about all certifications for all the series in your learning site. A series can have a maximum of 4 certificates. For each series, it provides certification information, such as the certification name, ID, description, state (active, inactive, or deleted), and the date when it was created.Granularity: SeriesId x CertificationIdUpdate Frequency: 6 hours |
| SeriesUserCertification | This table contains information about users who have been awarded certification across all series. For each user and series, it provides certification information, such as the certification name, ID, description, state of the user’s certificate (awarded, revoked, or expired), date when the certificate was awarded, and date when the certificate will expire.Granularity: SeriesId x UserId x CertificationIdUpdate Frequency: 6 hours |  |
| TAG DETAILS | ModuleTags | This table contains the mapping of Modules to Tags. For each Series, you can find details such as the TagId, Tag Name, and Tag Category.Granularity: ModuleId x TagIdUpdate Frequency: 2 hours |
| LearningObjectTags | This table contains the mapping of Tags to content items within Courses, QuickUpdates, and Assessments. For each Learning Object, you can find a TagId, Tag name, Module Type, and Tag Category.Granularity: ModuleId x LearningObjectId x TagIdUpdate Frequency: 2 hours |  |
| Readiness Index DataThese tables provide user, competency, and cadence related metadata for Readiness Index (RI) in Mindtickle Analytics. |  |  |
| READINESS INDEX DETAILS | RIUser | This table contains information on a user, such as the user's RI score in their cohort (RI groups) for a given cadence (period). Columns include ID of user and cohort (RI group), ID of the cadence, cohort (RI group) name, and Readiness Index (RI) score of the user.Granularity: User x RI for given cadence(s)Update Frequency: 2 hours |
| CompetencyUser | This table contains information related to a user's competency score for a given cadence (period). Columns include ID of the user and cohort (RI group), ID of the cadence and the competency (tag), cohort (RI group) name, and user's score on the competency, competency benchmark score, and difference of user's score on competency and the competency benchmark score.Granularity: User x Competency for given cadenceUpdate Frequency: 2 hours |  |
| CohortCadencesDate | This table contains information on all cadences (periods) across cohorts (RI groups). Columns include ID of the cohort (RI group) and cadence, cadence name, and creation date of the cadence.Granularity: Cohort x CadenceIdUpdate Frequency: 2 hours |  |

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Mission:
Admins can change the Mandatory/optional reviewer preferences for a published mission.

After making the changes to the reviewer's preference, admins are prompted to publish a new version of the mission to implement the changes. The changes leading to the new version are listed as Unpublished changes in the Publish tab. Admins must click the Publish changes option to confirm and publish a new version.

Let us understand how this will impact the learners and reviewers of the mission. As an example, let’s say the initial mission created is version 0, and the new version published after making reviewer changes is version 1.

1. Scenario 1: If the learners have completed the mission and the review for the mission is also completed. The learner Status under the Invite and track page displays Review completed.

In this scenario, there is no change in the final score and the mission completion status.

1. Scenario 2: If the learners have submitted the mission, however, one or more review is still pending for the final score. The learner Status under the Invite and track page displays review pending.In this scenario, there are two possibilities:

- As learners have already submitted the mission (on version 0), there is no change to the reviewer appointment, and pending reviews are done as per the reviewer selection of version 0.
- The admin can manually Reset Progress for the learner. In this case, the learner must submit a new mission, and the review is done per the latest mission (version 1).

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Mission:
1. Scenario 3: If the learners have started but have not submitted the mission. The learner Status under the Invite and track page displays Submission pending.In this scenario, there are two possibilities.
  - The learners can submit the mission on the version they started the mission (on version 0) and the review is done as per the reviewer setting of version 0.
  - The admin can manually upgrade the learners from the Invite and track page. If the learners are upgraded (say from version 0 to version 1), the reviewer appointment setting will change to the upgraded version (to version 1).
2. Scenario 4: If the Learners have not started the mission. The learner Status under the Invite and track page displays Did not start. In this scenario, the learners are automatically upgraded to the mission's latest version (version 1).
3. Scenario 5: If the admin adds a reviewer.In this scenario, a new version of the mission is not published. However, this change impact all the version of the mission; hence, the evaluation algorithm would dynamically re-compute the Required/Optional/Recommended reviewer preference based on the latest Mandatory/Optional reviewer preferences settings.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Coaching reports:
This article provides detailed information on the new and improved reports for the coaching sessions module in Mindtickle Analytics. The reports provide analytics on reviewers, learners, and evaluation parameters. Coaching insights in these reports will help you identify skill/competency gaps at a more granular level to create more effective, customized enablement programs.

The old coaching sessions reports are available under module reports (Analytics > Training > Modules) and will continue to be functional for now. The new coaching session reports are available as a new section in the sidebar under Analytics > Coaching > Sessions.

Note:

- This feature is available only for site owners , and not for any other user roles.
- Reporting API (OData) support and analytics on archived coaching sessions are currently not available.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Coaching reports > Access coaching sessions reports > Table data:
The table provides the following information:

- Coaching name: Name of the coaching session module.
- Created on: Date and time when the report was created.
- Self-review: Whether self-review is enabled or not for the module.
- Learners: Total number of learners assigned to the module, both admin-invited and self-invited.
- Reviewers: Total number of reviewers assigned to the module.
- Completed sessions: Total number of sessions completed within the period selected in the Time period filter.
- Adherence: The session adherence (in %) is a metric that indicates whether the reviewer has reviewed the expected number of sessions in the set duration. It is calculated as follows: (Number of session completed by reviewers) / (Expected sessions to be completed) x 100 Expected sessions are calculated based on the review cadence of each coaching sessions module.
- Last session on: Date and time when the last session was completed by reviewer/learner.

Click any coaching session report to open detailed analytics for the module. When you open a report, it displays analytics in the following tabs:

- Reviewers: Analytics for the reviewers assigned to the module.
- Learners: Analytics for the learners assigned to the module.
- Sections and parameters: Analytics for the scoring-enabled evaluation parameters and parameter sections of the module.

The article further provides detailed information on each tab.

- File name: Change the default name of the report file.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Get Started:
The Scorecard tab on the sales rep (learner) profile page provides analytics related to the rep’s Readiness Index (RI), which is a sales readiness index available in Mindtickle Analytics. It is a unified metric that, by quantifying the capabilities of sales reps, measures their readiness to achieve business outcomes.

Through the scorecard, you can view a report on your performance across key competencies and gaps in your ideal rep profile (IRP). You can improve skills or identify performance gaps through scorecard insights. For example, using the insights, you can proactively take up modules (to which you are invited) to improve knowledge and skills and, thereby, your RI score.

The scorecard visualizes your strengths and weaknesses in terms of competencies in comparison to the RI benchmark. It also shows the module activities that impact competencies. This helps you identify competencies and modules where you are performing well and lagging behind.

Feature highlights:

- Reps can access their scorecard for insights on their skills and performance and drive their own learning initiatives
- Reps can look at data over the last 4 cadences and see their performance trends
- Reps can identify where they lie with respect to peers in their cohort (RI group)
- Get personalized insights on modules to be focused on and competency gaps
- Managers can also access their own scorecards via My profile and analytics instead of Team analytics .
- Through RI settings, the admin can disable access to the scorecard for reps.

For an overview of Readiness Index, see Readiness Index overview.

Note: This tab is visible only if Readiness Index (RI) is enabled for your organization. To learn more about the Readiness Index, contact your Customer Success Manager.

The scorecard page displays analytics data based on the following selections:

- View and compare growth: Select the cadence (Weekly or Monthly). With the cadence, you can choose to view comparative RI data by a weekly or monthly cycle, which can be selected in the Viewing RI as of option.
  - Monthly: The latest month’s RI is compared to last month’s RI.
  - Weekly: The latest week’s RI is compared to last week’s RI.
- Viewing RI as of: Select a date as of which you want to view the data by the cadence selected in the View and compare growth option. For example, if you select your cadence to be monthly and view data as of June 1, 2022 , then the quadrant chart displays data for the last four monthly cadences: June 1, May 1, April 1, and March 1.
- Correlate RI with: Select the business metric with which you want to correlate the RI data for the rep.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Get Started > Quadrant chart:
In this section, you can view your performance and progress, in terms of their RI score, across the four quadrants. The chart displays data by correlating your RI score with the selected business metric. This helps you understand how your performance is trending and use insights and recommendations to improve performance.

The cadences can be weekly or monthly depending on your selection in the View and compare growth dropdown menu in the upper-right corner. The data is displayed based on the date selected in the Viewing RI as of option.

Hover over the bubbles to see your RI and business metric scores.

The quadrant chart provides the following information and options:

Rep’s progress across quadrants over time

The chart displays data for the latest cadence by default. Additionally, it provides the following options:

- Show cohort members in quadrant: Use this option to view where you lie with respect to peers in your cohort (RI group). Note: This option is available only if your admin has enabled it.
- Show last 4 weeks/months data together: Use this option to view the rep’s data for the last four cadences at once, to understand the learner’s progress and performance over the last 4 weeks/months. It displays the option for weeks or months depending on your selection in the View and compare growth option in the upper-right corner.

Chart type

By default, the quadrant chart is displayed as a bubble chart. Click the Bubble dropdown menu for the option to view the chart as a Distribution Map, which allows you to view the entire cohort’s data plotted in terms of percentage across the four quadrants. You can view in which quadrant they lie and the percentage of cohort members (peers) who make up the particular quadrant.

Rep’s progress across quadrants over time

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Set Up and Content Management > Prerequisites:
To deploy the Seismic - Mindtickle integration, your organization needs to hold a production instance of both Mindtickle and Seismic.

1. Before you begin, please ensure you have decided on the following items.
2. Name of the folder to be created in Seismic.
3. Type of account to be created for authentication (Premium user account or full admin account).
4. If you are an existing customer, confirm if sync is required for historical data on Mindtickle. You can choose to include only specific modules from the historical data. Contact your Customer Success Manager (CSM) and provide a list of modules to be included.

You can either select a specific set of Series you want to sync to Seismic or allow auto-syncing of all Series on an ongoing basis. Contact your Customer Success Manager (CSM) to learn more about selective syncing of Series.

Once you finalize these points, the Seismic administrator needs to perform the following steps to initiate the deployment.

1. Create a profile and then create a folder in Seismic for all content being synced from Mindtickle.
2. Set up the content properties you want to include along with the Mindtickle content URL. For example, Mindtickle Content.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Set Up and Content Management > Derive values from Seismic instance:
Tenant Name: This is the subdomain name from the URL of your Seismic instance. Copy-paste this value into the Tenant Name field on the Mindtickle platform.Note: This value is case-sensitive.

Team Site Name:

- Click the hamburger menu on the upper-left corner of your Seismic instance and click Settings > TeamSite Settings .
- Copy the team site name visible in the drop-down and paste it into the Team Site Name field on the Mindtickle platform. Note: This value is case-sensitive.

Root Folder Name: Add the name of the same folder you created in Seismic Library for Mindtickle content sync.

Tag Property: This tag is applied on all the Mindtickle modules as Custom Properties inside Seismic.

- Click the hamburger menu on the upper-left corner of your Seismic instance and click Settings > TeamSite Settings .
- Click Content Properties under Settings . Click + to add the tag. Give an appropriate name and click Save . Add the same tag to the Tag Property field on the Mindtickle platform.

3. The Seismic login page opens in a new tab. Enter the username and password and click Login.Note: Ensure that the user whose credentials you enter has privileges to view all content in Seismic and is a Premium user of the Seismic community.

4. Seismic integration is now complete. You can click Edit to change the values or Disable to disable the integration.

Notify your Customer Success Manager (CSM) about the completion of these actions.

Our team will take the following actions to complete the deployment.

- Run a bulk migration for historical data (for existing customers) and confirm that the sync is successful.
- Configure the webhooks for an ongoing real-time sync.
- Inform you about the completion of these actions and details of the configuration deployed.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Set Up and Content Management > Validate sync:
Refer to this video to understand how to validate the sync. Alternatively, refer to the following steps to validate it.

1. Log in to the Seismic platform using your credentials.
2. Click Library on the left panel of the screen.
3. Select the appropriate folder that you created earlier in Seismic.
4. URL Content items with names corresponding to the names of Series in Mindtickle will be visible. Click the Series to view the synced modules.

Note: After the synchronization of content items is complete, the Seismic administrator can:

- In a separate browser tab for Mindtickle

On the pop-up, select Dialogue and click Ok. The content opens in an iframe inside Seismic.

1. Go to the Mindtickle app listing on Salesforce AppExchange . Note : This integration is compatible with the latest version of the Mindtickle app installed from Salesforce AppExchange .
2. Click the Get It Now button on the listing.
3. Click on login with Trailblazer .
4. Login to your account via SFDC.
5. Select the SFDC environment (production or sandbox) and the account to install the package.
6. Review the details and confirm the installation.
7. The Salesforce administrator can decide whether to install the application for all users or only for the administrator . If your organization uses custom profiles or non-admin roles, then select Install for All Users and install the package. Note :
  - For custom profiles with non-admin roles, ensure the user's profiles have access to all the object and apex classes. For more information, see Grant users access to classes and objects .
  - For non-admin and community (partner/customer) users, ensure the user's profiles have access to all the apex classes. For more information, see SFDC Class Access (Community/Non-Admin Users) .

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Asset Hub > Admin > Create Named Credentials:
Named credentials provide a way to define the scope of access to the external service, including specifying which Salesforce users or profiles can access it. They are a secure way to store authentication information for an external service or API. To create named credentials:

1. Click the gear icon on the upper-right corner and select Setup in Salesforce.
2. On the left panel, go to Security and click Named Credentials .
3. Click New Legacy .
4. The Label and Name must be Mindtickle_Asset (case sensitive).
5. URL should be ‘ https://<learning site>.mindtickle.com ’.
6. Select the certificate generated in the previous section.
7. Set the Identity Type as Per User .
8. Set the Authentication Protocol as JWT .
9. Set the Issuer as Mindtickle (case sensitive).
10. Set Per User Subject as $User.Username . Note : You can configure any user attribute other than the username. For example, you can configure Per User Subject as $User.Email or $User.User . If your Mindtickle email address or username differs from your Salesforce email address, you must specify a custom user attribute to ensure successful authentication.
11. Audiences must contain the company ID (cname) of your Mindtickle instance.

The company ID is displayed in the Security & Integrations tab on the Account settings page of your learning site.

12. Set the Token Validity for 365 Days.

13. Select the Mindtickle certificate as the JWT Signing Certificate. This must be the same certificate as the one selected in step 6.

Note: Do not change any other default attributes.

14. Click Save.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Asset Hub > Admin > SFDC Class Access (Community User/Non-Admin User):
For community (partner/customer) users and non-admin users, ensure that access to all the apex classes that start with MindTickleDev is granted. For example,

- MindTickleDev.MDTAssetHubIntegrationController
- MindTickleDev.MdtBookmarked_Assets
- MindTickleDev.mdtHubList

This is applicable for internal sales customers and partner portal profiles.

Follow the steps mentioned below to provide users access to the apex classes:

1. In the Quick Search field, enter the keyword Profile .
2. Select the Profile of the user who is facing the issue. In this example, the selected profile is a Standard Sales User .
3. Under the Standard Sales User profile select Apex Class Access .
4. Click Edit .
5. Add all Apex classes that start with MindTickleDev from the Available Apex classes to Enabled Apex classes. For example: MindTickleDev.MDTAssetHubIntegrationController MindTickleDev.MdtBookmarked_Assets MindTickleDev.mdtHubList Note : Ensure you add all Apex classes that start with MindTickleDev from the Available Apex classes. Failing to do so will restrict access to the users and non-admin users.
6. Click Save to save the changes. Tip : Configure this setting for all the user profiles that need access to the Mindtickle assets.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Asset Hub > Asset Hub capabilities in Salesforce > Share assets:
This button allows you to select assets to share. You can also open an individual asset and share only that asset with the customers or prospects. On the Share assets page, you can filter the assets by hubs, attributes, shared by you and bookmarked (under the More filters drop-down), or search for a specific asset using the Search bar.

You can also sort the assets by:

- Recently modified
- Average rating
- Number of views
- Number of shares
- Alphabetically

After selecting the assets you can share them either by Share via room, Share via email or Share via link option.

Contact suggestions

While sharing assets, the Send to option automatically displays suggested contacts that you can quickly add as recipients.

Important: This feature is available only for the Mindtickle app for Salesforce version "Summer Release 2024 - 2.1618". It is not supported on the older versions of the app. Ensure that the app is updated to this latest version.

The Send to dropdown menu suggests contacts that you can quickly add as recipients. These are contacts associated with the opportunity, as well as contacts from the account linked to the opportunity. It displays the name, email, and title (if available) of the contacts. Contact suggestions reduce the need for manual copying and pasting of email addresses, thereby enhancing the user experience. Reps can also manually enter the email address of recipients.

Note:

- Initially, contact suggestions will be displayed only for the opportunities updated in the past 6 months. After the initial configuration, it will display contact suggestions for all opportunities.
- You can add a maximum of 25 contacts/recipients per instance of asset sharing.

Additional points to consider:

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Asset Hub > Recommended assets:
This widget displays the assets in context to the Opportunity object as and when the reps access an opportunity. Thus helping the reps to close or move a deal with the help of the recommended assets.

Important: The section will now appear only if admins have defined display rules and at least one asset matches those rules. If no assets qualify based on the configured rules, the Recommended assets section will not be shown to sales reps.

The recommended assets are determined based on their relevance to the opportunity, such as rating, usage, and downloads by default. It can be influenced by rule-based recommendations also if the Rule as a Service (RaaS) is enabled. Admins can configure rules that empower reps to easily find assets and share appropriate content in the context of the deal. For instance, based on the opportunity data from Salesforce (SFDC), admins can set rules such as if the deal stage is X and the industry is Y, recommend assets A, B, and C.

Asset recommendation adds tremendous value to the deal journey of reps by ensuring that they don’t spend too much effort in getting to the relevant assets.

Note:

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Asset Hub > Recommended assets:
- The rule-based assets are recommended and listed in the widget if a rule is set on the opportunity. Further, the listing depends on the asset's relevance.
- Asset recommendation through rules depends on the sync frequency set between SFDC and Mindtickle. Currently, the assets recommendation is updated every hour. For example, if the deal stage qualifies for a rule, the recommended assets appear once the sync happens.
- By default, if the rule is not applied on the opportunity, Asset Hub displays assets from hubs shared with the rep. The listing depends on the asset relevance.
- Asset recommendation through rules is not supported for closed and deleted opportunities.
- You must upgrade the new version of the Mindtickle app from the Salesforce app exchange.
- Opportunity sync with Mindtickle must be enabled if not already done.
- The Rule as a Service (RaaS) feature must be enabled.

Click View all to list all your recommended assets within Salesforce. You can also sort the assets by:

- Recommended
- Recently modified
- Average rating
- Number of views
- Number of shares
- Alphabetically

After selecting the assets, you can share them either by Share via room, Share via email, or Share via link option available at the bottom tray.

Note: To access Share via room, DSR should be enabled for the organization, and users should have Access DSR permission assigned to them.

You can also select the options at the bottom to share the assets.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > FAQs > Who is an instructor?:
An instructor is someone who conducts the ILT session. For example, a user who delivers the content or conducts the session on the topic of the session.

chunks.title: Who are instructors and facilitators in ILT sessions?

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > FAQs > Who is a facilitator?:
A facilitator is someone who manages the session. For example, someone who tracks the attendance or someone who allows learners to join a video conferencing session.

Note:

- Admins can also perform the above mentioned tasks. However, you can use this option in specific use cases where sessions are managed by separate users.
- Instructors and facilitators do not have a dedicated user role on the Mindtickle platform.
- Instructors and facilitators may or may not be users added to the platform (Mindtickle).
- In some cases, users added to the Mindtickle platform are instructors. While adding these users as an instructor to the ILT session, they are added as a non-platform user. The non-platform role of an instructor signifies that there is no dedicated workflow or user role available for them in the Mindtickle platform.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > FAQs > What are the settings associated with instructors and facilitators?:
- Since both roles are non-platform users, they do not have dedicated workflows unlike admins, learners, or managers.
- In case these roles are applicable for a session, then the admin needs to enter their details such as, name, email address, and description (only email in case of facilitators).
- Both roles can be assigned as co-hosts for the session. Co-hosts have certain privileges for managing video conference meetings and it varies for zoom and webex. For more information, see ILT-Zoom Integration to Manage Meetings and Auto-Attendance or ILT-Webex Integration to Manage Meetings and Auto-Attendance .
- Both roles can be selected to receive the session QR code via mail in the session check-in option. They can further share this code with the learners.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > FAQs > Why the facilitator of the session is not visible to the learners on the learning site?:
Since facilitators do not play an active role in learning and content delivery, their details are not displayed as part of the session details on the learning site. Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Mobile App:
This article explains how to enroll in, self check-in to, and unenroll from an ILT session using the mobile app.

Note:

- You must enroll in a session prior to the session start date and time. You cannot enroll for a session if the session date and time has passed. To enroll or unenroll post the session start date and time, contact your admin.
- If enrollment lock is enabled on a session, you must enroll prior to the enrollment lock date and time. You cannot enroll or unenroll from the session after the enrollment lock date and time. To enroll or unenroll post the enrollment lock date, contact your admin.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Mobile App > Enroll in a session:
1. In the email invitation for the ILT Session, tap the Enroll button. Alternatively, log in to your learning site and tap the ILT module assigned to you. The ILT Overview section provides a quick overview of the sessions you are invited to. At any point of time, it provides information about the number of any one of the following type of enrolled sessions:
  - Your live sessions If you are enrolled for a session that is currently ongoing and live, this section displays this information.
  - Your upcoming sessions It displays the total number of sessions (from that ILT module) for which you are enrolled. This information is displayed only if there are no live sessions ongoing at the moment.
  - Your past sessions It displays the total number of past sessions (from that ILT module) you were enrolled for and each session’s attendance status. This information is displayed only if there are no live sessions ongoing at the moment.
  - If you have not enrolled for any session, it displays - 0 enrolled Sessions . This page is further divided into the following sections:
  - Live Sessions This section displays the live ongoing session you have enrolled for. It also displays session details, such as session name, session type (classroom or video conferencing), location, date, and time.
  - Upcoming Sessions This section displays all the upcoming sessions you have enrolled for. For each session, it also displays session details, such as session name, session type (classroom or video conferencing), location, date, and time.
  - Past Sessions This section displays all the past sessions you have enrolled for. For each session, it also displays session details, such as session name, session type (classroom or video conferencing), location, date, time, attendance status, and score. Use the Search sessions field to find a specific session.
2. Tap against a particular session to learn more about it. The session details page appears.
  - If your admin has enabled an enrollment limit, the total number of seats and the available seats are displayed next to the Enroll button.
  - If your admin has enabled enrollment lock, the enrollment lock details are displayed next to the Enroll button.
  - If your admin has set up a video conference meeting for the session, the Location section displays meeting details such as the meeting URL, meeting number, and meeting password.
  - If your admin has set up a classroom session, the Location section displays the physical location of the meeting.
  - The Enroll button is disabled if the enrollment lock date and time has passed. Contact your admin to enroll for this session.
3. Tap Enroll to register for the session. The status changes to Enrolled . Note :
  - You can enroll for multiple sessions at a time.
  - When you enroll for a session, you receive a session enrollment email, and the following actions occur automatically:
    - The event is added to your synced calendar. For more details about the ILT-calendar auto-sync feature, see ILT-Calendar auto-sync notes .
    - If the session details, such as type, time, or location are changed, a new event with the updated details is created on the calendar, and the old event is deleted.
    - If the session is canceled, the event is deleted from your calendar.
    - To receive automatic updates on the calendar, you must set calendar permissions accordingly.
      - For Google calendar, in Settings > Events from Gmail , ensure the Show events from Gmail toggle is ON .
      - For Outlook calendar, in Settings > Events from email , ensure the calendar event options are configured as follows. Note : Although the settings in Outlook help, they are not a definite measure of enabling/disabling events sync from mail. In most cases, the events are synced if the correct .ics file is sent, irrespective of these settings.
4. If the seats are full and a waiting list is available, tap the Join waiting list button to add yourself to the waiting list. Note :
  - In case other enrolled learners unenroll from the session, the next person on the waiting list is enrolled in the session. Enrolled learners receive an email notification confirming their enrollment.
  - If enrollment lock is enabled, the enrollment lock details are displayed next to the Join waiting list button.
  - The Join waiting list button is disabled if the enrollment lock date and time has passed. Contact your admin to join the waiting list for this session. The status changes to Leave Waiting List . Tap it to leave the waiting list. This article further explains how you can self check-in to a session and unenroll from a session .

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Mobile App > Self Check-in to mark your attendance:
The self check-in option enables you to mark your attendance for a session. It is available only if your admin has enabled it for the session. The check-in window is open based on the check-in validity period set by the admin. You can self check-in by entering the check-in code or by scanning the QR code provided by your admin, instructor, or facilitator.

You can self check-in for the following types of sessions:

- Live or ongoing session
- Upcoming session (if the check-in period is valid)
- Past session (if the check-in period is valid)

To self check-in:

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Mobile App > Self Check-in to mark your attendance:
1. Navigate to the session for which you want to self check-in and mark your attendance.
2. You can self check-in by entering the check-in code or by scanning the QR code provided by your admin, instructor, or facilitator. Contact your admin if the check-in details are not already shared with you. To check in using the check-in code, tap Self Check-In . Alternatively, tap the Self Check In button at the bottom of the screen. Note :
  - The Self Check-In option in the session card and the Self Check In button at the bottom of the screen are available only during the check-in validity period.
  - If the check-in period is not valid, the system displays a pop-up that includes the check-in validity period information.
  - When you tap on the button in offline mode, an error message is displayed on the screen.
3. Tap Enter check-in code . Note : To check in using the QR code, see Step 7 .
4. Enter the check-in code in the pop-up. Note : A check-in code is an alphanumeric code, for example 1EmPs2, shared with you by the admin.
5. Tap Check-In . A confirmation message is displayed in the pop-up once the check-in is successful, notifying that your attendance is marked.
6. Tap Done . The sessions page appears. The attendance status for the session is marked as Attended and the completion score is awarded to you (if your admin has set a completion score for the session).
7. To check in using the QR code, tap the Self Check In button at the bottom of the screen.
8. Tap Scan check-in QR code .
9. Allow camera access for the Mindtickle mobile app. Note : The screen and options may differ depending on the device and OS you use. Based on your preferences, tap While using this app or Only this time . Note : Selecting Don’t allow restricts camera access for the app and displays the following prompt. Tap Turn on to provide camera access.
10. The QR code scanner opens. Use it to scan the QR code shared by the admin for the session. A confirmation message is displayed on the screen once the check-in is successful, notifying that your attendance is recorded. On the sessions page, the attendance status for the session is marked as Attended and the completion score is awarded to you (if your admin has set a completion score for the session).

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Mobile App > Watch session recording:
If your admin has uploaded the session recording for a session that you have enrolled for, you can access it from the session details page and watch it later. This enables you to go through the session content even if you have not attended it. You can also download the recordings and use them for future reference.

When the admin uploads a recording to the session, you receive an email notifying that a new recording has been uploaded to the session. You can:

- Access the recording from the email
- Access the recording from the mobile app

To access the recording from the email:

1. Tap View session in the email.
2. You are directed to the session details page in the mobile browser. Tap Watch recording against the session.
3. The video opens in a media player. Tap the Play button to start watching the recording. For more details on how to get a better viewer experience, see Watch the session recording . Note : The Download recording option is available only on Android devices. You cannot download the recording on an iOS device. To watch the recording and download it from the web browser, see Watch the session recording .

To access the recording from the mobile app:

1. Tap Watch recording .
2. In the pop-up, click Copy Link to copy the link to the recording.
3. Paste the link in your browser tab to start watching it. For more details on how your session completion is marked when you watch a session recording, see Watch the session recording .

Following are the different scenarios and the actions that must be performed in each scenario.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Setup > FAQs > User scenarios and system functionality > Scenario 1:
Old email address has all Kscore/progress, and the new email address has 0 Kscore or is in a “did not sign-up” state. In that case, follow the below steps:

1. Replace/swap the new email address with a dummy email address. For example, replace johnnew@test.com with johnnew+1@test.com .
2. Replace johnold@test.com with johnnew@test.com .
3. Go to the Users tab and deactivate johnnew+1@test.com .

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Setup > FAQs > User scenarios and system functionality > Scenario 3:
Old email address (johnold@test.com) has some Kscore, and the new email address (johnnew@test.com) also has some Kscore on different modules. In that case, we need to perform the following steps:

First, Export the user report for both email addresses and analyze the below points:

To learn more, see Learner analytics.

1. Check if there are any modules the learner has completed from the old email address but not from the new email address.
2. Check if there are any modules the learner has completed from the new email address but not from the old email address. If the count of modules in point 1 is higher than point 2, manually invite the learner’s old email address to the modules they completed from the new email address and mark them as complete. Once this is done, follow the steps mentioned in Scenario 1 . If the count of modules in point 2 is higher than point 1, manually invite the learner’s new email address to the modules they completed from the old email address and mark them as complete. Once this is done, follow the steps mentioned in Scenario 2 .

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Setup > FAQs > User scenarios and system functionality > Scenario 4:
Old email address is present on the platform, and the new email address is not present on the platform. In that case, simply replace the old email address with the new email address.

Important notes:

- As per the product behavior, the system keeps the module assignment for one user account only when we replace the user email address. It does not merge the module assignment. For example: In the above scenarios, when you follow the steps in scenario 1 , the current user will have all modules assigned to johnold@test.com , and the modules assigned to johnnew@test.com (Which were not assigned to johnold@test.com ) will no longer be seen as invited to the current user.
- The Complete Progress option is available only for the Course , Quick-Update , and Assessment modules.
- The Complete Progress option can only mark learners as 100% complete. The progress for learners who are under in-progress status cannot be transferred.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Digital Sales Rooms:
As an admin, you can define default room settings for room templates. These settings include:

- Access Options
- Notifications
- Layout
- Room Thumbnail

The default settings are applied to all rooms created using the template. When reps create rooms using these templates, it eliminates the need for them to define room settings for each room separately, thus saving their time. It also ensures the room creation process is more efficient.

Note:

- If required, reps can edit the default room access settings before publishing the room.
- For settings that require specific inputs, such as expiration date or passcode, the reps must define the values while publishing the room.

This article further explains how you can configure default room settings.

chunks.title: Configure default room settings

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Digital Sales Rooms:
1. On the Create Sales Room Template ( Rooms > Templates > Create Template ) page, click Room Settings .
2. Based on your preferences, select Access Options , Notifications , Layout , or Room Thumbnail from the drop-down list.
3. Update the settings in the Room Settings panel. Learn how to configure the settings under each category in the respective section below. Tip : Click All room settings to go back to the main menu and navigate between different settings.
  1. Access options
    1. Who can enter? By default, anyone with the room link can access the room. We recommend anyone with the link (and requiring an email to enter) to allow your contacts to easily bring in new stakeholders or socialize your solution. If you want to set more restrictions, select Allowed viewers only . If a primary contact is configured for the room, they are added to the Access List by default. To add more contacts or domains, click Edit . Note : If a primary contact is not configured for the room, the Access List is empty. In this case, click Add to add individual contacts or domains to the Access List . Enter the domains or contacts you want to provide access to. You can:
      - Use the search field to add existing contacts.
      - Enter a domain name to display users from that domain. For example, Acme.com.
      - Enter @<domain name> to allow the entire domain to access the room. For example, @Acme.com.
      - Copy and paste email addresses to grant room access in bulk. You can add up to 50 email addresses. Note: When bulk adding users, if the user does not exist in the system, the system automatically creates a new contact and adds them to the room’s Access list.
      - Enter an email address and click Add as new contact if the user does not already exist as a contact. Note : You can change the room’s primary contact. Click Make Primary to set the contact as the room's primary contact. If a user does not already exist as a contact, enter their email address and click Add as new contact? This allows only specified emails and domains to access the room. If someone not on the Access list tries to enter the room, the room owner and collaborators are emailed a notification about the unauthorized access attempt. Note : The allowed email addresses or domains that can enter the room must be specified by the rep at the room level before publishing the room.
    2. Email options Define if you want the visitors to enter their email address to enter the room. We recommend having Require email to view set to ON for all rooms. This helps you track specific visitors by their email address and analyze what content each individual is viewing. Based on these insights, you can determine your further plan of action. For engagements earlier in the sales cycle, you may want to keep it OFF to reduce any friction between your prospect and the room. Note :
      - You can block specific email domains from entering the DSR. For more information on adding domains to the block list, see Set Up Digital Sales Rooms: Block email domains. The system notifies you if certain email domains are already blocked. To view the list of blocked domains, hover over the View icon. The tooltip displays the entire list of blocked domains. When a user from a blocked domain attempts to access the DSR, they receive an error message. The room owner and collaborators receive an email ( similar to the one below ) detailing the unauthorized access attempt. Clicking Provide access in the email provides access to the user trying to access the room. The user receives an email notifying that access is granted. Note : Clicking Provide access provides access only to the individual user trying to access the room. This action does not provide access to the blocked domain. These insights allow you to monitor who is trying to access your DSRs and take necessary action, such as granting access if the attempt was legitimate or investigating further in case of suspicious activity. In this section, you can also decide if you want to automatically remind visitors that a room was shared with them or to have them verify their email before entering. For more options, see Send Automated Email Reminders to Visit a Room . Switch the Verify email with PIN toggle to ON if you want viewers must verify their identity using the 6-digit PIN sent to their email address.
    3. Advanced options Depending on the security needed for the content being shared, you can add options such as an expiration date or a passcode. Note : The rep must configure the passcode and expiration date at the room level when creating the room.
  2. Notifications Decide if the rep should receive email alerts when the room they create is visited. By default, the Email when viewed toggle is set to OFF . Switch it ON to enable email alerts.
  3. Layout Select how the room content is presented to room visitors. Selecting the right room layout helps guide the visitors through the experience the reps built and make sure they understand what to do once they enter the room. You can choose from 3 available layout options:
    1. Story - 3 columns This layout is best for displaying content to visitors in a particular order to tell a curated story with your content. It has a list of sections on the left that allows them to easily navigate around, like in a table of contents.
    2. Story - 2 columns This layout creates a similar experience to the Story - 3 columns layout, but with the section headers at the top of the room instead of on the left. This makes the content appear larger. This can also be used if you only have a few pieces of content to share and do not need sections.
    3. Tiles - 3 columns This layout is useful when you have many content items to share. It has three columns. On the left, it displays the section headers, which allow visitors to navigate the room easily. In the center, it displays a content preview, where you can preview the content file, whether documents or videos. An additional section on the right displays the welcome message, room owner name, collaborator details, and sales action buttons.
    4. Tiles - 2 columns This layout creates a similar experience to the Tiles - 3 columns layout, but with the section headers at the top of the room instead of on the left. It also has a section on the right that displays the welcome message, room owner name, collaborator details, and sales action buttons . When sharing a few pieces of content, whether at the beginning of a new deal or following up after the first product demo, choosing one of the Story layouts is a great way to introduce visitors to your content and guide them through it. As the relationship builds, the room will typically evolve to host more content, in which case, the best practice may be to move to a Tiles layout. Things to consider when choosing the room layout:
      1. Number of content pieces being shared
        1. 1-7 pieces of content - Story 2 or 3 columns
        2. 7+ pieces of content - Tiles
      2. If content needs to be presented in a particular order
        1. Yes, content should be scrolled through in order - Story 2 or 3 columns
        2. No, visitors can click around a section in any order - Tiles
      3. Number of stakeholders in the room (if different departments/teams have distinct content needs)
        1. Need different sections for each team - Tiles (to see more content at once) or Story - 3 column (to see a table of contents on the left side)
        2. Only a few visitors with same goals - Any layout based on other needs
      4. How far along you are in a deal or customer relationship
        1. Just getting started - Story 2 or 3 columns to focus visitors on a few pieces
        2. Longer relationship - Tiles to collect all of the resources shared over time for reference
  4. Room Thumbnail Select a room thumbnail. You can upload a new thumbnail or select one from the available options under All , This room , or Gallery . The recommended thumbnail size is 1200 x 630 px.
4. Once you have updated all settings, click Done .

No, enhanced domains do not have an impact on any of the Mindtickle - Salesforce integrations.

However, if enhanced domains are not deployed in your Salesforce org before Salesforce deploys the feature, here are some issues that can arise.

- Users can experience errors when attempting to access Salesforce, including but not limited to Experience Cloud sites, Salesforce Sites, and Visualforce pages.
- Some embedded content stored in Salesforce no longer appears.
- Third-party applications can lose access to your data.
- Single sign-on integrations with sandboxes can fail.
- Single sign-on integrations with orgs using the *.cloudforce.com and *.database.com domain suffixes can fail.

For more information about enhanced domains, enhanced domain formats, timeline of enforcement of enhanced domains, the potential impact, and how to avoid the issues, see Enhanced Domains.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Self-serve reports:
This section explains how to create a new self-serve report based on a pre-built template. It provides information in the following subsections, which are in the order of the tasks you need to perform to create and save a self-serve report:

1. Select a pre-built template : Select from 14 pre-built report templates to get started.
2. Configure the report : Select the format/layout for your report: table or bar chart. For the selected format, configure data metrics, row grouping, and sort settings. Note that the two asset reports have only the table format.
  - Configure a table report
  - Configure a bar report
3. Apply filters : Apply filters to expand or narrow the scope of metrics data that you want to include in the report.
4. Preview and save the report : Finalize and preview customization changes, and then save the report. A new self-serve report gets created only after you manually save it . Your changes are not auto-saved. Similarly, when you edit a report, you must manually save it to retain your changes.

Important: Self-serve reports provide data only for the series/modules that were assigned to learners during the past one year from the date of report creation. In other words, only for the series/modules to which learners were invited within the past year. If you want to view data for series/modules that were assigned to learners more than one year ago, please use the OData-based reporting API as a workaround.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Self-serve reports > 1. Select a pre-built template:
Perform the following to select from 14 pre-built report templates to get started fast. The template will be used as a base for the report; you can then further build (configure) the report:

1. On the Analytics home page, click Custom created > Self serve reports > Create new report to get started. Alternatively, use this shortcut: click the button (highlighted in yellow) next to Custom created and select Report in the dropdown.

1. On the report type selection pop-up, click Use self serve report.

1. On the template selection page, view all available templates and select a template that you want to use as a base. When you click on a template in the left panel, on the right you can see a preview of what the report will look like. Click See available metrics to view a list of metrics (generic and profile field based) that are available for use in the report. Click Use template to use the selected template.Note: All following steps provide information on creating and customizing a self-serve report using the Learner by module report template as an example. The information is applicable for all other templates.

1. A new report gets created and the report configuration page appears. On top of the selected template, you can further configure the report and save it:
  1. Add or remove metrics and configure other settings
  2. Apply filters to expand or narrow the scope of metrics data that you want to include in the report.
  3. Preview the report, and
  4. Save the report.

Next steps:

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Self-serve reports > 2. Configure the report > a. Configure a table report:
Perform the following in the Configure panel on the right to configure a table report:

1. Under Chart type, select table as the format/layout for the report. In a table report, you can select more metrics to cover a large amount of data.Important: This is the primary setting for the report. Depending on the selected format (chart type), you will get a different set of metrics and other configuration options.

1. Under Chart settings > Columns, add or remove metrics for the report. Metrics are displayed as columns on the report.Add metrics:

- The Columns section lists metrics that are pre-added by the template. Click Add columns to add more metrics.
- The Customize columns panel opens. It lists metrics in two sections: generic and profile field metrics. Scroll down each section to view all available metrics.Important: If you add a row grouping (series and module) in Step 3, each grouping provides additional metrics for selection under generic metrics. If you add both groupings (series and module), it provides additional metrics for both. Furthermore, when a grouping is added and you have selected one or more of its metrics, then removing the grouping will also remove the metrics derived from the grouping. See Step 3 for details.
- Click thebutton against a metric to add it. Important: If you add more than 10 metrics (including two metrics under Group by if you add both groupings), Mindtickle does not display the report on the UI (the report page) to avoid user experience and performance issues. However, you will still be able to export the report data (in a .csv file) and share it with others. We recommend adding a maximum of 8 metrics for an optimal experience.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Self-serve reports > 2. Configure the report > b. Configure a bar report:
1. Before creating a bar report, please note the following important points:
  - A bar report displays data in horizontal bars across the x-axis and y-axis. For the x-axis, you can select a maximum of 3 metrics. The y-axis is fixed and cannot be changed. Depending on the template, the y-axis has learner, series, module, or group metric selected by default.
  - A bar report provides only a limited number of metrics compared to the table report. Therefore, when you switch to the bar report, many table metrics will not be available for selection.
  - Unlike the table report, the bar report cannot have a mix of percentage (%) metrics and non-percentage (non-%) types of metrics. For example, Score % and Completed % are percentage metrics, while Module invites started and Module invites completed are non-percentage metrics. Therefore, for the x-axis metrics, you cannot use a mix of percentage and non-percentage metrics. You can only use either type of metrics at once. If your current table report has a mix of the two metric types, you are prompted to select only one type of metrics when creating a bar report.
2. When you switch from a Table to a Bar report, one of the following happens:
  - If the current table report has a metric/column that is not supported in the bar report, all metrics will be cleared. Now you need to add metrics as described in Step 4.
  - If the current table report has a mix of percentage and non-percentage metrics, you are prompted to select only one type of metrics.Note: You can always change this later. For example, if you first selected percentage metrics, you can remove them and select non-percentage metrics instead.
3. Under Chart settings > X-axis, add or remove metrics for the report and set the bar colors. Selected metrics will be displayed as horizontal bars on the report.

- Changes to available metrics: As mentioned in the previous step (Step 4), if you add a row grouping (series and module) in Step 5, it will increase or reduce the number of available metrics that you can add. Adding a series grouping provides additional metrics, while adding a module grouping reduces the number of available metrics. Furthermore, when a grouping is added and you have selected one or more of its metrics, then removing the grouping will also remove the metrics belonging to that grouping.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Self-serve reports > 3. Apply filters:
1. Default filters: All templates come with the following two filters applied by default. You can change their values to your liking.
  - Modules assigned during: Past 30 days (default value) Important: For the Custom Time option, you can set the maximum date range to one year in the past from today. This is because self-serve reports provide data only for the series/modules that were assigned to learners during the past one year from the date of report creation. In other words, only for the series/modules to which learners were invited within the past year.
  - Assigned by: Include admin assigned only (default value)
2. Add filters: Click the button to view all available filters, add one or more filters, and then select the filter values to apply the filters. See details here . Important: You must select a filter’s values/options to apply the filter. If no values are selected, the filter will not be retained when you save the report.
3. Reset filters: Click the button to reset filters to default. This will keep only the default filters with their default values. See details here .
4. View and remove applied filters: Click the button to view all of the applied filters. You can also remove any of your applied filters. See details here .

Once you save the report after applying filters, the applied filters are displayed at the top of the report under the Selected filters section.
