Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Mobile App:
An assessment is a great way to test or certify your skill or knowledge on a particular subject. Mindtickle’s Assessment module offers a clean interface that helps you focus on the question and possible answers.

This article explains navigating an assessment on the Mindtickle mobile app.

To navigate an assessment on the mobile app:
chunks.body:
An assessment is a great way to test or certify your skill or knowledge on a particular subject. Mindtickle’s Assessment module offers a clean interface that helps you focus on the question and possible answers.

This article explains navigating an assessment on the Mindtickle mobile app.

To navigate an assessment on the mobile app:
chunks.headingPath: Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Mobile App
chunks.title: Navigate an Assessment (Mobile)

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Mobile App:
1. Sign in to the Mindtickle mobile app .
2. Navigate to the assessment. You can access it from the Home tab under one of the sections, for example, What’s new , Required . Or, you can access it from the Series tab from the series it is present in. Note : Depending on the module relevance set on the assessment for you by your admin, the assessment appears under the appropriate section. For example, if the module is assigned to you and the module relevance is set to Required , it appears under the What’s new in assigned and Required sections on the Home tab. If you don’t see the module under any section, use the Search field to find the assessment.
3. Tap the assessment. The Assessment details page appears and displays the following details:
  - Thumbnail
  - Name
  - Description
  - Time limit (if it is a timed assessment)
  - Maximum score
  - Passing score
  - Instructions If the questions are categorized under topics, it also displays the following details:
  - Topics
  - Number of questions under each topic
  - The total score on the topic
4. Tap Start assessment . Tip :
  - Tap Instructions to read the instructions before you start the assessment.
  - For effective sync with other devices, ensure you have a good internet connection.
5. The first question appears on the screen. It displays the question number, question score, topic (if the questions are categorized under topics), question text, and answer options. If it is a timed assessment, the countdown timer is also displayed. The timer starts when you begin the assessment and cannot be paused or stopped. Note : The question and its answer options are displayed based on the question type. For more information, see Question types in an assessment .
6. Choose the answer by selecting the correct option/s.
7. If you are unsure about the answer, tap Mark for review to mark it for review and revisit it later. To unmark the question, tap Marked for review . Note : All questions marked for review are highlighted by the Marked for review icon.
8. Swipe left or right on the screen to navigate to the next or previous question.
9. Tap Review & Submit to view a summary of your assessment. If questions are categorized under topics, it displays the following tabs:
  - All - displays all topics and the number of questions under each topic.
  - Marked - displays the list of topics which has questions marked for review. Tap on a topic to expand or collapse the list of questions marked for review in that topic.
  - Unanswered - displays the list of topics which has questions that are unanswered. On each tab, tap on a topic to expand or collapse the list of questions in that topic. Tap on a question to navigate to the question and its answer options. If questions are NOT categorized under topics, it displays the following tabs:
  - All - displays all questions and their score.
  - Marked - displays the list of questions marked for review.
  - Unanswered - displays the list of questions that are unanswered. On each tab, tap on a question to navigate to the question and its answer options. Note : The Marked tab appears only if there is at least one question in the assessment marked for review. Similarly, the Unanswered tab appears only if there is at least one unanswered question in the assessment.
10. To exit from the assessment, tap on the top right corner of the screen. Note :
  - If you exit from a timed assessment (or the internet connection drops off, or you navigate away from the assessment, or log out from the platform), the timer continues to run. The assessment is auto-submitted once the time is up.
  - If you exit from a non-timed assessment (or the internet connection drops off or you navigate away from the assessment or log out from the platform), your progress on the assessment is retained.
  - If you are attempting a non-timed assessment (the time limit is disabled) and you navigate away from the assessment or sign out from the app, the status of the module is set to In Progress . The status continues to remain In Progress until you submit the assessment. The assessment is submitted only when you submit it by clicking Submit .
11. To submit the assessment, tap Submit assessment .
12. The next screen displays the number of questions you are yet to attempt and the number of questions marked for review. Tap Cancel to go back to the assessment and review the questions. Else, tap Submit . The assessment results are displayed on the screen.
13. If reattempt is enabled on the assessment, the result displays the number of reattempts you are left with. Click Reattempt to take the assessment again.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Modules:
This article provides detailed information on the revamped reports for the assessment module in Analytics > Module Reports.

Assessment reports provide analytics on the module content (assessment questions), adoption, and performance with respect to invited learners. Its widget-based architecture provides a better user experience and allows you to drill into multiple levels of data. It provides analytics in the form of widgets, top stats, and detailed table reports.

Note:

- Assessment reports provide the analytics data only for the latest version of the assessment module. You cannot view analytics for any previous version of the module.
- Analytics on topics is currently not available on the platform UI; assessment reports will display analytics only on the questions. (Topics are used to logically group/organize the assessment questions.) However, you can get analytics on topics through Mindtickle’s reporting API, where we have added new topics related to fields to the assessment tables. For more information, see the reporting API metadata sheet and the Download reporting API tables article.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Modules > Access assessment reports:
In the admin site sidebar, click Analytics > Training > Modules to open the module reports listing page. The Modules page lists reports for all module types. Click the Module type filter and select Assessment to view only assessment reports in the list.

In this table, you can view high-level data on all assessment reports in the following columns:

- Module name: Name of the assessment module.
- Created on: Date when the module was created.
- Learners: Total number of learners assigned to the module, both admin-invited and self-invited.
- % Completion: Module completion in terms of percentage (%), for the period selected in the Time period filter. It is calculated as follows: (invitations completed by learners / total invitations in a module) x 100 Where, total invitations = sum of the total number of learners invited to each module
- Scoring performance: Overall scoring performance of learners for modules assigned to them in the series. It is calculated as follows: (sum of scores obtained by learners in the modules assigned to them in the series / cumulative max score of all modules started by learners in the series) x 100
- % Module certifications: Percentage of learners certified in the module.

You can use the filters, search bar, and column sorting to view data only for a specific set of assessment reports. For example, click More Filters > Module Status to view the archived assessment modules.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Modules > Access assessment reports > Individual assessment report:
On the Modules page, click an assessment module to view its analytics on the assessment module report. To quickly find the assessment module you're looking for, use search or the Module type filter.

The assessment report displays analytics in the following tabs:

- Overview : Overview analytics for the module in the form of 6 widgets that address top questions on analytics for the module, such as the adoption of the module, scoring performance, and learners who passed/failed. The widgets provide analytics on the module content (assessment questions), adoption, and performance with respect to invited learners. For applicable widgets, you can remind learners (through an email notification) to complete the module.
- Learners : Detailed analytics on the learners assigned to the module, presented in a table report. It provides data on learners with respect to completion status, scoring performance, certification status, and so on. You can edit (customize) the report further and add more columns.
- Content : Detailed analytics on the module content (assessment questions), presented in a table report. It provides data on assessment questions with respect to learner responses, scoring performance, performance distribution, and so on. You can edit (customize) the report further and add more columns.

The article further provides detailed information on each tab.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Modules > Overview tab > 2. Average scoring performance widget:
This widget displays a breakdown of the scoring performance of all learners invited to the module. The scoring segmentation is based on your configuration in Analytics Settings > Performance Checkpoints.

In the widget name, it displays the average scoring performance (in %) across learners invited to the module. It is calculated as follows:(Score obtained) / (Total score of the module) x 100

Widget report

Click on any of the circle bars to view a detailed report of the widget in the Average scoring performance pop-up. It displays the report data in three Score tabs, which are based on the scoring segmentation configured in Analytics Settings > Performance Checkpoints.

Each tab represents a scoring segment. The report buckets learners across three tabs based on their scoring performance.

For example:

- Score < 30% ➔ Learners whose scoring performance is less than 30%. These are low-performing learners.
- Score (30 - 80)% ➔ Learners whose scoring performance is in the range of 30% to 80%. These are learners who are doing well.
- Score > 80% ➔ Learners whose scoring performance is greater than 80%. These are high-performing learners.

Under each tab, you can view a list of learners and their scoring performance. By default, the table data is sorted by the “Scoring performance” column in ascending order (lowest to highest). You can change the sort order by any of the two columns, in ascending/descending order.

- Export the report: Use the ( Export ) button to export the report in a CSV format to an email address.

- Failed: Learners who did not achieve the passing score.

Select learners whom you would like to reattempt the module and click the Remind button to send them a reminder email to complete the module.
- Export the report: Use the ( Export ) button to export the report in a CSV format to an email address.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Modules > Overview tab > 4. Overdue status widget:
This widget displays a breakdown of the assessment module overdue status for invited learners. The assessment becomes overdue for a learner if they fail to complete it by the due date set by the admin.

Note: This widget displays data only if the due date to complete the module is configured in the assessment module Settings > Due date and emails > Due date for the learner.

The widget displays the number of learners for whom:

- The assessment is overdue, and
- Learners for whom the assessment will be due in :
  - the next 7 days ,
  - in the next 7 to 15 days , and
  - in the next 16 to 30 days .

Note: As the “due in” information is based on the due date set in the assessment, you may see data in all three “due in” statuses for some or all of your assessments.

Widget report

Click on any of the circle bars to view a detailed report of the widget in the Learners due in pop-up. It displays the report data in the following tabs:

The widget displays the following information:

- Overdue: Learners whose assessment is overdue. These are learners who did not complete the assessment by the due date .
- Due in < 7 days: Learners whose assessment is due for completion in less than 7 days. In other words, the due date to complete the module is within the next 7 days.
- Due in (7-15) days: Learners whose assessment is due for completion in the next 7 to 15 days.
- Due in (16-30) days: Learners whose assessment is due for completion in the next 16 to 30 days.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Modules > Learners tab:
This tab provides detailed analytics (in the form of a table report) on the progress and performance of learners assigned to the assessment module. It provides learner data with respect to completion status, scoring performance, certification status, and so on.

DATA UPDATE FREQUENCY: For any activity or changes in the assessment module, the analytics data will reflect under the Learners tab within 60 minutes.

Here are the actions you can take on the report page:

- Report filters: Use the filters at the top to view (filter out) all report data on the page by applied filters. For details on filters, see the “ Report filters ” section.
- Export the report: Use the ( Export ) button to export the entire report in a CSV format to an email address.
- Edit the report: Use the ( Edit ) button to customize the report further and save it. You can add more columns and configure other settings.
- Bookmark and share the report: Use the ( Bookmark ) and ( Share ) buttons in the upper-right corner to bookmark (for yourself) and share (with other admins) this tab’s report.

Summary metrics

Provides a quick summary of important stats/insights:

- Total learners: Total number of learners assigned to the module.
- Scoring performance: The average scoring performance (in %) across learners invited to the module. It is calculated as follows: (Score obtained) / (Total score of the module) x 100

You can hide the summary metrics section from the report configuration (edit the report).

Table data

The table provides detailed analytics for each learner in the following columns by default. You can customize the report to add more columns and configure other settings. Furthermore, the report displays data for the selected filters, which you can change.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Modules > Learners tab > Customize Learners report:
This section explains how to customize (edit) the Learners tab report. It allows you to add more columns (data metrics) to the report, define the default sorting for the table, and show/hide the summary metrics section.

To get started, click the (Edit) button in the upper-right corner of the report. The Edit configuration panel opens, where you can make changes to the report and click Apply changes to save it.

You can make the following configuration changes to the report:

1. Add more columns to the report
2. Default sort settings: configure the default data sorting (sequencing) for the table data
3. Show/hide the summary metrics section.
4. Click Apply changes to save the report.

1. Add columns

Under Chart settings > Columns, click the Add columns button. In the Customize columns panel, click thebutton for a metric to add it as a column to the report.

Click the button against a metric to remove it from the report.

Click the button to drag and rearrange the order of added metrics. This defines the order of columns in the report.

2. Default sort settings

You can configure the default data sort order (sequencing) for the table data.

Under Sort table by, select the column by which you want to sort the table data. Then, under Sort order, select the default sort order (ascending or descending) for the selected column.

3. Summary section

You can choose to show or hide the summary metrics section that appears above the table. By default, it is set to show, with two metrics selected. You can select up to 3 metrics.

This section explains how to customize (edit) the Content tab report. It allows you to add more columns (data metrics) to the report, define the default sorting for the table, and show/hide the summary metrics section.

To get started, click the (Edit) button in the upper-right corner of the report. The Edit configuration panel opens, where you can make changes to the report and click Apply changes to save it.

You can make the following configuration changes to the report:

1. Add more columns to the report
2. Default sort settings: configure the default data sorting (sequencing) for the table data
3. Click Apply changes to save the report.

1. Add columns

Under Chart settings > Columns, click the Add columns button. In the Customize columns panel, click thebutton for a metric to add it as a column to the report.

Click the button against a metric to remove it from the report.

Click the button to drag and rearrange the order of added metrics. This defines the order of columns in the report.

2. Default sort settings

You can configure the default data sort order (sequencing) for the table data.

Under Sort table by, select the column by which you want to sort the table data. Then, under Sort order, select the default sort order (ascending or descending) for the selected column.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Modules > Report filters:
- [ Default filter ] Modules assigned during: Use this filter to view data for learners based on the time period during which they were invited to the module. The available options are: Past 15 days, Past 30 days, Past 90 days, Past 1 year, Last month, Last 3 months, Last 6 months, All time, and Custom time.   - Groups: Select one or more groups to view data for learners in the selected groups.
  - Profile fields: Select one or more profile fields and their values to view data for learners who have the selected profile fields.
  - Manager fields: Select one or more relationship manager profile fields and their values to view data for learners who have the selected manager fields.
  - Hierarchical managers: Select one or more hierarchical managers and their values to view data for learners who have the selected hierarchical managers.
  - Module relevance: Select one or more module relevance types (Required, Optional, and Unmarked) to view data for learners who were assigned the selected relevance when they were invited to the module.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Assets:
The Revenue impact dashboard in Asset Hub analytics provides a holistic view of how assets are influencing deals and revenue. It brings together external engagement data and revenue impact in a single view — recognizing that external engagement is a leading indicator of revenue influence. Admins and product marketing teams can use this dashboard to understand which assets are driving deal activity, how assets are performing across different prospect titles, and how individual deals are progressing with respect to content usage and engagement.

For an overview of all available dashboards, see Asset Hub analytics overview.

This is the default (out-of-the-box) dashboard. Alternatively, use the asset revenue impact template in advanced reports, where you can add, remove, and customize widgets and filters.

Note:

- Asset Hub is a paid feature. For more information, contact your Customer Success Manager (CSM).
- Revenue impact is attributed only to assets shared via email (including integrations like Outlook, Outreach, and Gmail) and Digital Sales Rooms (DSR) , as these are directly connected to your CRM (e.g., Salesforce), enabling association with specific opportunities and deal stages.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Assets > Dashboard widgets > Snapshot metrics:
The top of the dashboard displays a row of key metrics for the selected time period:

- External assets: Total number of assets currently in the platform that are configured for external sharing.
- Unique assets shared in deals: Number of unique assets that have been shared in deals.
- Unique assets engaged in deals: Number of unique assets that have received external engagement in deals.
- Deals with assets engaged: Number of deals in which shared assets have received external engagement.
- Total revenue influenced: Total revenue influenced across all deals where assets have been shared and externally engaged with.
- Closed won revenue: Total revenue from closed won deals where assets were shared and externally engaged with.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Assets > Dashboard widgets > 1. Revenue influenced trends (Last 4 quarters):
This chart tracks revenue influenced by assets over the last four quarters. It shows a monthly trend of:

- Revenue influenced : The total value of all deals touched by assets.
- Ongoing revenue : The value of active deals where assets are currently being used.
- Closed won revenue : The value of deals successfully closed with asset involvement.

- Asset name: Name of the asset. Click to open the asset detail page in a new tab.
- External views: Total number of times the asset was viewed by external recipients.
- External downloads: Number of times the asset was downloaded by external recipients.
- External time spent (mins): Total time spent by external recipients on the asset, in minutes.
- Ongoing deals: Number of ongoing deals the asset is associated with.
- Won deals: Number of closed won deals the asset is associated with.
- Revenue influenced: Total revenue influenced by the asset across all associated deals.
- Ongoing revenue: Revenue value of ongoing deals the asset is associated with.
- Closed won revenue: Revenue value of closed won deals the asset is associated with.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Assets > Dashboard widgets > 4. Asset engagement by prospect title:
This section shows which prospect titles are engaging with assets across deals. It helps you understand which types of decision-makers and stakeholders are interacting with your content.

Top prospect titles by asset engagement

This scatter chart identifies which buyer personas are most engaged. It plots prospect titles based on the number of unique assets viewed (x-axis) versus external views (y-axis), helping you see if you are reaching key decision-makers like "Economic Buyers" or "CMOs." The size of each bubble reflects the relative volume of engagement.

Asset usage and engagement by prospect titles

This table provides a detailed breakdown of engagement by prospect title. The table includes the following columns:

- Prospect title: Job title of the external contact who engaged with assets (e.g., Head of Dept, Lead).
- Shares: Number of times assets were shared with contacts of this title.
- Unique assets shared: Number of distinct assets shared with contacts of this title.
- Open rate (%): Percentage of shared assets opened by contacts of this title.
- External views: Total number of asset views by contacts of this title.
- External downloads: Total number of asset downloads by contacts of this title.
- External time spent (mins): Total time spent by contacts of this title on shared assets, in minutes.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Assets > Dashboard widgets > 5. Asset usage in deals:
This section provides visibility into which deals are involving the most asset activity, and allows you to drill down into individual deals for a complete picture.

Top deals with assets shared

This scatter chart plots individual sales opportunities. It identifies each deal name based on total shares (x-axis) versus unique assets shared (y-axis), allowing you to identify highly active or complex deals that require more content support. The size of each bubble reflects the relative scale of asset activity in that deal.

Deals with assets used

This table lists all deals in which assets have been used, with the following columns:

- Deal name: Name of the deal. Click to open the deal-level dashboard.
- Current stage: Current pipeline stage of the deal.
- Unique assets shared: Number of distinct assets shared in the deal.
- Unique assets engaged: Number of distinct assets that received external engagement in the deal.
- Deal value (org currency): Value of the deal in your organization’s currency.

Deal-level drill-down

Clicking a deal name in the Deals with assets used table opens a dedicated dashboard for that deal, with the deal filter pre-applied.

This gives you a complete picture of asset activity within that specific deal, including:

- Total shares, unique assets shared, and engagement summary for the deal.
- Which assets were shared most repeatedly across different prospects or at different times within the deal.
- Which assets received the most external views in the deal.
- A detailed table of all assets shared in the deal, including their open rates and engagement metrics.
- Which prospect titles were present in the deal and what engagement each title generated.
- A breakdown by individual prospect email, showing which assets each contact engaged with and how much time they spent on them.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Assets > Dashboard widgets > 6. Asset usage by deal stage (available on request):
Note: The following widgets are hidden by default and must be enabled for your organization. They provide visibility into content effectiveness across deal stages (e.g., Prospecting, Negotiation) and require specific configuration using data from your Salesforce instance. To enable stage-level visibility, contact your Customer Success Manager (CSM).

When enabled, two additional widgets appear on the dashboard providing visibility into asset activity by deal stage:

- Asset usage by deal stage — shares: Shows how many assets were shared in each deal stage.
- Asset usage by deal stage — engagement: Shows how many assets received external engagement in each deal stage.

These widgets allow you to:

- Identify which assets are most frequently shared and engaged within a particular stage.
- Click a specific stage (like "Prospecting") to open a dashboard dedicated to that phase of the sales cycle.
- Determine what content "works" best to move deals from one stage to the next based on external view and open rate trends.

Stage-level drill-down

Clicking either of the stage-level widgets opens a dedicated dashboard for that specific stage, showing:

- Total shares and assets shared in that stage.
- Top assets shared most frequently in that stage.
- Top assets receiving the most external engagement in that stage.
- A detailed table of the most frequently engaged assets in that stage, which can be exported for use in automation rules or other workflows.
- Top deals in which assets are being shared in that stage.
- Which prospect titles are engaging most frequently in that stage.
- A breakdown by individual prospect, showing which assets each contact engaged with, their title, and their engagement metrics.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Assets > Filters > Applying a filter:
When you click into a filter category, a window opens with three distinct ways to define your data view:

- Default setting : Filters are applied by default with preselected values to display a broad dataset.
  - Duration (for trend charts): This and Last 4 Quarters
  - User status: Active and Added
  - All other filters: Include all, meaning no filtering is applied and all available data is displayed
- Selection from list : You can search for and check specific items (e.g., selecting only a few specific Opportunity names ). This is best for targeting known deals, accounts, or assets.
- Conditional filtering : This advanced option allows you to create rules using various operators, such as Is , Contains , Starts with , Ends with , Is empty , and their opposites (e.g., Does not contain ). This is useful for filtering deals or assets based on specific naming conventions.
- Filter toggle switch : Use the toggle switch for a filter to quickly turn a specific filter off without losing your selections, allowing you to compare filtered results against the broader dataset.
- Reset filters : Click the Reset icon at the top of the panel to clear all current selections and return to the default dashboard view.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Assets > Filters > Available filters:
- Opportunity name : This filter allows you to focus on one or more specific sales deals. It is ideal for reviewing the content history of a high-value opportunity.
- Account industry : Use this to analyze which assets are driving revenue in specific market sectors, such as "Healthcare," "Manufacturing," or "Technology."
- Current stage : This helps you see which assets are being used—and which are most effective—at specific points in your sales funnel (e.g., Proposal/Price Quote vs. Negotiation ).
- Asset name : Use this to filter the entire dashboard by a specific file. This helps you see exactly how much revenue a single asset has influenced across all deals.
- Asset owner : This allows you to focus on assets managed by a specific team member, helping you track the financial impact of content created by individual authors.
- Attribute categories : Filter the dashboard by broad asset groupings, such as "Asset Type" or "Product Line."
- Attributes : Provide a more granular filter within your categories, such as looking specifically at "Case Studies" or "Technical Specs."

- Current stage : This helps you see which assets are being used—and which are most effective—at specific points in your sales funnel (e.g., Proposal/Price Quote vs. Negotiation ).
- Asset name : Use this to filter the entire dashboard by a specific file. This helps you see exactly how much revenue a single asset has influenced across all deals.
- Asset owner : This allows you to focus on assets managed by a specific team member, helping you track the financial impact of content created by individual authors.
- Attribute categories : Filter the dashboard by broad asset groupings, such as "Asset Type" or "Product Line."
- Attributes : Provide a more granular filter within your categories, such as looking specifically at "Case Studies" or "Technical Specs."
- User status : This allows you to filter the data based on the status of your team members, such as Active or Added . This ensures your reports are reflecting current, relevant users.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Series > Ready-to-Deploy template structure:
The ready-to-deploy template structure is meticulously crafted to use immediately. This template setup makes it simple to get started, helping you improve engagement.

Note: We have illustrated the structure using the Anti-Bribery template. The structure follows the same information and user experience for all the listed ready-to-deploy templates.

The template details page provides the following insights to help you make an informed decision:

- Explore the template details from the template header. To learn more, see Browse marketplace .
- Take a visual tour and preview the template to grasp its layout and how the modules engage with the audience.

- Understand the listed template categories, included modules, the estimated learning time, and the set-up guide.
- What's in this series? section lists the modules within the template. To learn more, see Browse marketplace. Click Expand/Collapse to expand/collapse this section.
- Explore the Why use this template? section to discover how it provides clear definitions, exceptions, roles, guidelines, policies, and real-life examples, enabling effective anti-bribery practices. Click Show more / Show less for more details.
- Refer to the Other FAQs section to know the target audience, any prerequisites, and customization options for the Anti-bribery series template. Click Expand all to expand the answers.
- Lastly, the template creator details are listed. Click on the Website and Contact Us for more information on the template author. Here, the Anti-bribery template is created by Mindtickle CaaS.

After you’ve gone through the ready-to-deploy template details, deploy it directly. Refer to Step 7 of Create a series using a series template to deploy the Anti-bribery template.

Note: This template is available in English, Chinese, Japanese, and Korean.

Empower your sales teams with the highly effective MEDDPICC Foundations template in Sales Qualification Methodology through our Ready-to-deploy series. Utilize this series to drive 500+ successful enablement outcomes by eliminating guesswork and implementing a structured approach to deal sales qualification. Admins can track your reps’ knowledge and skill development levels faster compared to ideal rep profiles.

MEDDPIC Foundations stands for:

| M | E | D | D | P | I | C | C |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Metrics | Economic Buyer | Decision Criteria | Decision Process | Paper Process | Identify Plan | Champion | Competition |

3. Interactive self-assessment tool for deal qualification.
4. Manager-led coaching forms based on self-assessment results.
5. Series feedback module for continuous improvement.
6. Pre-tagged content for Ideal Rep Profile (IRP) analytics.

The MEDDPICC Foundations series template is ideal for sales teams seeking to enhance their sales qualification conversations and provides foundational knowledge with practical applications. Streamline your sales process, industry, and product knowledge, drive consistency, and achieve greater success with this powerful series.

The following shows the preview of the Paper Process quick update of the newly created series:

Once you publish, the series is ready to be implemented. Invite learners and groups to the series to help them get started with the series and enable their progress.

The Mastering Negotiations series gives your teams a proven negotiation strategy that helps them plan and execute every move and countermove in a negotiation. chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Best Practices and Use Cases > Security and Privacy > View room visitor logs:
Mindtickle gives a comprehensive overview of room visits. It provides detailed logs of all visitors, including their activity and engagement with assets. The logs include the following details:

- Visitor : Details of the visitor such as name, business email ID, approximate location, and device type (Windows/Mac) are visible depending on the default sharing/access configurations of a room.
- Last Activity : Last time they visited the room.
- Visits : Total number of visits to the room. On hovering over this number, the exact information on when these visits occurred can be viewed.
- Items Viewed : Number and percentage of items that have been at least partially viewed.
- Total Time Spent : Total time spent in the room.

These logs act as an audit trail that helps keep track of all the visitors who have accessed the shared room.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Best Practices and Use Cases > Security and Privacy > Consent capturing:
DSRs can track the engagement data, such as who visited the room, the time spent in the shared room, the number of content/assets viewed, and the number of views. This kind of tracking requires consent from the asset recipients under various data privacy laws.

To help customers comply with international privacy laws, Mindtickle enables customer admins to configure consent options. The privacy policy to be displayed on the consent capturing message is the customer’s or Mindtickle’s privacy policy, as configured by the admin for all the DSRs. The recipients have a choice to accept or decline the consent.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > CRMs > Create a new user profile:
To create a profile for an integration user in Salesforce (SFDC):

1. Log in to your Salesforce org with an administrator account.
2. On the homepage, click the Setup icon and click Setup . The Setup homepage opens in a new tab of your browser.
3. In Quick Find , enter the keyword Profile and select Profiles under the Users section.
4. On the Profiles page, click New Profile .
5. On the Clone Profile page:
  1. From the Existing Profile dropdown, select Minimum Access - Salesforce and
  2. In the Profile Name field, enter an appropriate username for the user profile. Make sure to choose a username that represents the integration purpose, such as "MT Integration User" or as required.
6. Click Save . The user profile is created. Tip : To browse, search, and modify settings and permissions in a profile through a streamlined user interface, ensure the Enhanced Profile User Interface setting is enabled. To enable it, go to User Management Settings and switch the Enhanced Profile User Interface toggle On .

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > CRMs > Define system permissions:
Define the system permissions to provide admin access to the integration user profile. System permissions, such as 'Modify All Data' are needed to perform actions that apply across apps.

To define the system permissions:

1. On the user profile’s homepage, in the System section, click System Permissions .
2. A list of all permissions is displayed. To modify the access, click Edit . Note : Depending on the user profile template used to create the user profile, some permissions may be granted to the user by default.
3. Check the checkboxes for the following permissions from the list to ensure the integration user profile has all the required permissions. Permission NameDescriptionApprove Uninstalled Connected AppsThis permission allows the user to approve access to connected apps that aren’t installed in the organization.API enabledThis permission allows the user to access any Salesforce.com API.Apex rest servicesThis permission allows the user to access the Apex REST services.Edit TasksThis permission allows the user to create, edit, and delete tasks.View all usersThis permission allows the user to view all users, regardless of sharing settings.View roles and role hierarchyThis permission allows the user to view roles and the role hierarchy.View Concealed Field DataThis permission enables the user to view field data, including sensitive or personally identifiable information, that is concealed from other users.

See the example in the screenshot below.

5. Click Save.

6. In the Permission Changes Confirmation pop-up that appears, click Save.

The permissions for the user profile are updated.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > CRMs > Define object settings:
Object settings are permissions to access objects and fields and settings that specify which record types, page layouts, and tabs are visible.

To define the object settings:

1. On the user profile’s homepage, in the Apps section, click Object Settings .
2. To provide access to a field of an object, click the object. For example, to update the access for the object Opportunity, click Opportunities .
3. Click Edit .
4. In the Object Permissions section, check the View All checkbox. Providing View All access automatically grants Read access. In the Field Permissions section, check the Edit Access checkbox for the required fields (see the tables in the individual sections for each integration below). Providing Edit access automatically grants Read access. Similarly, provide access for each field of the objects for the required integrations mentioned below.

9. Under the Connected App column, click the Install button on Mindtickle Salesforce OAuth.
10. On the displayed pop-up screen, click Install.

The Mindtickle Salesforce OAuth app is now installed on the Salesforce instance.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > CRMs > Create Named Credentials:
1. Click the gear icon on the upper-right corner and select Setup in Salesforce .
2. On the left panel, go to Security and click Named Credentials .
3. Click New Legacy .
4. Enter an appropriate Label and Name . Note : The label and name for each learning site must be unique.
5. Enter the value https://<learning site>.mindtickle.com in the URL field.
6. Select the Salesforce certificate generated in the previous section.
7. Set the Identity Type as Per User .
8. Set the Authentication Protocol as JWT .
9. Set the Issuer as Mindtickle (case sensitive).
10. Set Per User Subject as $User.Username .
11. Audiences must contain the company ID (cname) of your Mindtickle instance.

You can find the company ID in your learning site's Settings page > Security & integrations tab.

12. Set the Token Validity for 365 Days.

13. Select the Mindtickle certificate. This must be the same certificate as the one selected in Step 6.

Note: Do not change any other default attributes.

14. Click Save.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > CRMs > Configure learning site mapping with the user > Configure learning site mapping with multiple users in bulk:
1. Create a new MS Excel file with two columns: User ID ( MindTickleDev__User__c ) and LS CName ( MindTickleDev__Cname__c ).
2. Each row in the CSV file should represent a user, and the columns should correspond to the relevant user fields in Salesforce, such as User ID and learning site CName.
3. To get the user ID, navigate to the user’s profile and copy the 15-digit alphanumeric code from the URL.
4. The LS cname is based on the learning site you want to map the user with. For example, in this case, it could be Mindtickle1 , Mindtickle2 , or Mindtickle3 .
5. Save the sheet as a .csv file.
6. In Salesforce, go to App Launcher and search for LsUserSettings .
7. Click LsUserSettings .
8. Click Import to upload a list of new records. This creates a one-to-one mapping with the user and the respective learning site.
9. On the Import your Data into Salesforce setup page, Click LsUserSettings .
10. Click Add new records .
11. Drag and drop the .csv file created above or click CSV to launch the file uploader and upload the .csv file.
12. Click Next .
13. The Edit Field Mapping: LSUserSettings page appears. From here, you can map the data to the respective fields. Based on the file that is uploaded, the data may be auto-mapped to existing Salesforce fields. To edit the mapping, click Map on the respective field.
14. In the pop-up that appears, based on the type of data being mapped, select the field. The first row contains the user ID, hence, select User and click Map .
15. Similarly, to map data in the second row (Cname), repeat this step and select Cname in the pop-up.
16. Once all the fields are mapped, click Next . Note : Unmapped data is not imported into Salesforce.
17. Click Start Import .
18. Click OK on the pop-up that appears. The Bulk Data Load Jobs page appears and displays the status of the job. If you have followed all steps mentioned in this article and still receive an error, contact Mindtickle Support or your Customer Success Manager (CSM).

This section explains how to create a flow in SFDC that automatically maps new or updated users to the respective learning site based on defined attributes.

For explanatory purposes, let’s assume the problem statement is:

If a new user is created whose Department is set to Sales or if an existing user’s department is updated to Sales, then map the user with learning site 2 (Mindtickle2). In this case,

- Object = User
- Condition is Department = Sales
- Action is Map user with Department = Sales to Learning Site 2 ( Mindtickle2 )

The following steps explain how to create an automated flow for the problem statement mentioned above.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > CRMs > Configure learning site mapping with the user > Create a flow to configure learning site mapping for new or updated users on an ongoing basis:
1. Log in to your Salesforce org with an administrator account.
2. On the homepage, click the Setup icon and click Setup . The Setup homepage opens in a new tab of your browser.
3. In Quick Find , enter the keyword Flows . In the Process Automation section, select Flows .
4. Click New Flow .
5. On the New Flow pop-up that appears, select Record-Triggered Flow and click Create .
6. On the Configure Start pop-up, enter User in the Object field and select User from the list.
7. Select the Configure Trigger as A record is created or updated .
8. In the Set Entry Conditions section, from the Condition Requirements dropdown, select All Conditions Are Met (AND) .
9. To configure the first condition, set Field = Department , Operator = Is Null , and Value = False . Tip : Click each field to display the list of values and select. Note : Based on your requirement, the object fields and the respective conditions may change.
10. Click Add Condition .
11. To configure the second condition, set Field = Department , Operator = Equals , and Value = Sales .
12. To ensure the flow is triggered when the specified conditions are met, select Only when a record is updated to meet the condition requirements from the When to Run the Flow for Updated Records .
13. In the Optimize the flow for: section, select Actions and Related Records .
14. Click Done . The Flow Builder page appears and displays the flow layout.
15. Click Add Scheduled Paths (Optional) .
16. On the Configure Scheduled Paths pop-up, enter the following details: Path Label = Async Flow for Learning Site User Mapping API Name = Learning_Site_User_Mapping Time Source = When User is Created or Updated Offset Number = 0 Offset Options = Hours After Click Done .
17. The Flow Builder page appears and displays the updated flow. Hover on the arm of the flow you created in the above step and click to create a record.
18. The Add Element pop-up appears. Scroll down to the Data section and click Create Records .
19. On the New Create Records pop-up, enter the following details. Label = Learning Site User Mapping API Name = Learning_Site_Users_Mapping Description = This flow is created to automatically assign a new or existing user to Mindtickle2 if the user’s Department is Sales. How Many Records to Create = One How to Set the Record Fields = Use separate resources, and literal values Object = LsUserSetting Field 1 = MindTickleDev_Cname_c Values for Field 1 = Mindtickle2 Field 2 = MindTickleDev_User_c Values for Field 2 = Id ({!$Record.Id})
20. Click Done .
21. The Flow Builder page appears and displays the updated flow. Click Save .
22. On the Save the flow pop-up that appears, enter the Flow Label , Flow API Name , and Flow Description . Click Save .
23. Click Save .
24. Click Activate to activate the flow. A confirmation message is displayed on the screen once the flow is successfully activated. The flow runs every time the specified conditions are met. Note : This flow is triggered only for the new users created or updated after it is activated. For existing users, perform the one-time data load. For more information, see Configure learning site mapping for multiple users in bulk .

9. To configure the first condition, set Field = Department , Operator = Is Null , and Value = False . Tip : Click each field to display the list of values and select. Note : Based on your requirement, the object fields and the respective conditions may change.
10. Click Add Condition .
11. To configure the second condition, set Field = Department , Operator = Equals , and Value = Sales .
12. To ensure the flow is triggered when the specified conditions are met, select Only when a record is updated to meet the condition requirements from the When to Run the Flow for Updated Records .
13. In the Optimize the flow for: section, select Actions and Related Records .
14. Click Done . The Flow Builder page appears and displays the flow layout.
15. Click Add Scheduled Paths (Optional) .
16. On the Configure Scheduled Paths pop-up, enter the following details: Path Label = Async Flow for Learning Site User Mapping API Name = Learning_Site_User_Mapping Time Source = When User is Created or Updated Offset Number = 0 Offset Options = Hours After Click Done .
17. The Flow Builder page appears and displays the updated flow. Hover on the arm of the flow you created in the above step and click to create a record.
18. The Add Element pop-up appears. Scroll down to the Data section and click Create Records .
19. On the New Create Records pop-up, enter the following details. Label = Learning Site User Mapping API Name = Learning_Site_Users_Mapping Description = This flow is created to automatically assign a new or existing user to Mindtickle2 if the user’s Department is Sales. How Many Records to Create = One How to Set the Record Fields = Use separate resources, and literal values Object = LsUserSetting Field 1 = MindTickleDev_Cname_c Values for Field 1 = Mindtickle2 Field 2 = MindTickleDev_User_c Values for Field 2 = Id ({!$Record.Id})
20. Click Done .
21. The Flow Builder page appears and displays the updated flow. Click Save .
22. On the Save the flow pop-up that appears, enter the Flow Label , Flow API Name , and Flow Description . Click Save .
23. Click Save .
24. Click Activate to activate the flow. A confirmation message is displayed on the screen once the flow is successfully activated. The flow runs every time the specified conditions are met. Note : This flow is triggered only for the new users created or updated after it is activated. For existing users, perform the one-time data load. For more information, see Configure learning site mapping for multiple users in bulk .

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > CRMs > Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs):
1. I want to connect 3 learning sites to my single SFDC instance what should I do? Follow the steps listed in this article again. While configuring the mapping in the LsUserSettings object, add the name of the fresh Named credentials created for learning site 3 in the Cname field and the user’s name (for whom learning site 3 is being configured) in the User field.
2. I have configured a few users for learning site 2 but now they want to switch back to the Default learning site (or Let’s say learning site 1)? Remove their mapping in the LsUserSettings object in either of the fields ( Cname / User ) for that user. If more than 100 users are configured, then use the Data loader to do a bulk upload. If you see that the user keeps on changing their learning site frequently (for any reason), then ask them to write a Flow in SFDC based on their condition and update ( Cname/User ) in LsUserSettings object.
3. Which learning site is the default learning site? The first learning site configured (With Named credentials : Mindtickle_Asset ) is considered the default learning site and is applicable to all the users.
4. Is there any Limit on the number of learning sites we can configure with a single SFDC instance? As per the design, the setup is capable of handling one learning site per user. For example, if there are 20 individual users and all of them have their own 20 learning sites, by design it is possible that each user can view their individual learning site. However, SFDC limitations may need to be checked here as it varies for every customer.
5. What if I get an error on the Asset page? Make sure the user who is getting the error has access to Apex classes and LsUserSettings object View all access .
6. What if I have 500 users? Do I need to configure the mapping manually? No, you just need to create a CSV file with 2 columns Cname and User. Upload this file using the salesforce data loader / Import wizard . This is a one-time setup you need to configure. For more information, see Configure learning site mapping with multiple users in bulk . For the ongoing user, you can write a flow on the User object to create a new record on the LsUserSettings object based on your condition (wherever a new user is created / Department is updated), trigger this flow. This is applicable for learning site 2 or learning site 3, not for users who are currently using the default learning site.
7. What will be the learning site for a user not mapped/blank Cname/User in the LsUserSettings? In the case of a blank Cname / UserId , it does not give any error. However, it uses the default learning site for that user.
8. What is the API name of LsUserSettings? MindTickleDev__LsUserSetting__c
9. When do we have to make use of the LsUserSettings object in SFDC? If the customer is using 2 learning sites , then we can make use of this object to configure the setup. Else no action is needed.
10. What happens if I have configured a user on LsUsersetting but is not present on learning site 2? It will show an Error page. Since the user is not present on the learning site 2.
11. How long does it take for the changes to reflect after all the configurations are done? Ideally, the changes start reflecting in 5-10 minutes. However, in some instances, a delay of 30-40 minutes has been observed.
12. What if I the Mindtickle asset section is displayed but I don’t see the asset under it? Please check if the GQLEndpoint is configured properly in SFDC custom metadata. Confirm that the learning site has the asset and it is shared with the user who is logged in.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Asset Hub > Admin:
This article explains how admins can create multiple assets using a Microsoft Excel file. The process of creating multiple assets not only helps admins save time but also manage assets more efficiently.

Additionally, the article provides information on generating the Excel file after selecting files from the Content Center and uploading the Excel file with asset details.

There are two kinds of files from which assets are created:

- Uploaded to Content Center
- Synced from Adobe Experience Manager (AEM) , Google shared drive , and Microsoft SharePoint

For information on the supported file types, see this article.

Note:

- You cannot upload files from the local system directly to Asset Hub. Instead, the files must be either uploaded or synced as mentioned above.
- At least one hub must be available to create assets via Excel file.
- Asset Hub is a paid feature. For more information, contact your Customer Success Manager (CSM).

Creating assets in bulk brings on-the-job readiness, maintains brand consistency, decreases onboarding time, and enables sales reps in various stages of the sales funnel.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Asset Hub > Admin > Prerequisites:
- Content Center : All the files on which you want to create assets must be in the Content Center.
- Hubs : All the hubs under which assets are created must be in Asset Hub.
- Collaborators : All the users marked as asset owners must be present as hub collaborators of respective hubs.
- Attributes : All the attributes to be applied to the assets must be present in the system so they can be applied to assets while creating assets.

Note: Collaborators and attributes can also be added at a later point in time using the bulk actions on assets.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Asset Hub > Admin > Create multiple assets via Excel file:
In the admin site sidebar, click Assets > Assets to open the page that lists all assets. In the header, click New > Multiple assets via Excel file.Alternatively, go to a hub, click Add assets, and select Multiple assets via Excel file.

On the pop-up that appears, click Generate Excel file if you are creating multiple assets for the first time.

The following pop-up displays to select the folders and files to create assets from the Content Center.

Apply filters based on Series, Modules, File type, and More filters to search for the content you want to upload. You can also search for specific files using the search field.

Note:

- You cannot select the SCORM files when creating assets.
- If you do not have Microsoft Excel to edit the Excel template, you can use Google Drive to edit it and then export it as an XLSX file to upload to Mindtickle.

The progress of the Excel file generation is displayed in the Notifications. Click the View action details icon to view the progress and status.

The selected files, folders list, and the Download generated Excel file link are displayed. Additionally, the validity of the link displays. By default, the link is valid for one week.

Click the Download generated Excel file link to download the Excel file.

The Excel file has the following details or tabs:

1. Create assets : This sheet contains details about the files selected from the Content Center.
2. Hubs and Collaborators : This sheet contains details of current hubs and their collaborators.
3. Attributes : This sheet contains details of all attribute categories and attributes currently available in Mindtickle.
4. Instructions : This sheet contains instructions you must follow before filling in the details.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Asset Hub > Admin > Create multiple assets from synced files:
While creating assets in bulk, you can use files synced from Adobe Experience Manager (AEM), Google shared drive, and Microsoft SharePoint. When you select the synced files and download the generated Excel file, the sync properties will be auto-filled in the Excel file.

The steps to create multiple assets from synced files remain the same as described in the “Create multiple assets via Excel file” section. The only change is that, while selecting the files, you can apply the Synced from filter to only list files that are synced from Adobe Experience Manager, SharePoint, and Google Drive. Please see the following screenshot for reference.

Once the Excel file is generated, you can view the following details and instructions for synced files.

The “Externally synced” column

In the generated Excel file, the Create Assets sheet contains the “Externally synced” column, with “Yes” or “No” as values against each file. This column helps you identify externally synced files.

Instructions for synced files

The Instructions sheet in the generated Excel file contains instructions on how to fill in the properties for the synced files.

The synced properties of an asset are already filled and marked in yellow for easy identification in the Create assets sheet.

You cannot edit any properties of the synced files, except their attributes in the “Attributes” column. However, if “Attributes” is a synced property, then only non-synced attributes can be added to the file. The non-synced attributes can be viewed in column D in the Attributes sheet; this column will be available only when at least one synced file was selected.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Asset Hub > Admin:
Mindtickle's integration with Salesforce allows admins to track the revenue impact of assets in deals. Admins can view a summary of the revenue impact of an asset in all deals where the asset is shared. Additionally, admins can monitor the revenue impact of assets to determine asset popularity, understand deal performance, and evaluate the impact of content strategies on revenue generation. This information enables admins to make informed decisions, optimize asset usage, and refine content strategies to achieve desired outcomes in the deal journey.

This article provides information on the settings that the admins must configure to track the revenue impact of asset.

Note: Asset Hub is a paid feature. For more information, contact your Customer Success Manager (CSM).

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Asset Hub > Admin > Setup Mindtickle Salesforce connection:
1. In the admin site sidebar, click Account > Settings > Security & integrations . On the Security and integrations page, scroll down to the User Sync section and then select the Salesforce tab.
2. Select the User and Contact checkboxes and click Save and then click Connect .
3. On the displayed screen, enter your Salesforce admin credentials to log in.
4. On the displayed pop-up, click Allow.
5. After logging into Salesforce, in the left navigation panel, click Apps > Connected Apps > Connected Apps OAuth Usage . The Connected Apps OAuth Usage screen is displayed.
6. Under the Connected App column, click the Install button on Mindtickle Salesforce OAuth.
7. On the displayed pop-up screen, click Install.

The Mindtickle Salesforce OAuth app is now installed on the Salesforce instance.

Once you have performed the steps mentioned above, contact your Customer Success Manager (CSM) or Mindtickle Support to complete the integration configuration.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Mobile App > Picture-in-picture (PiP):
Important: Currently, the picture-in-picture feature is supported only for iOS; it will be released for Android in a future release. The background playback feature is available for both iOS and Android devices.

Now you can multitask and watch a video on the Mindtickle app while using other apps on your device.

While watching a video on the Mindtickle app, navigate to the device home screen to automatically trigger the PiP mode. In this mode, the video appears as a pop-up (inset window) in a corner of the screen so you can use other apps.

Note: To use Picture-in-Picture mode, make sure the Start PiP Automatically setting is enabled in your iOS device under Settings > General > Picture in Picture.

The following iPhone image shows a video from the Mindtickle app playing in PiP while using the Safari browser:

You can take the following actions on the PiP video:

- Resize the video window: Pinch in or out to make the video window smaller or larger.
- Show/hide controls: Tap the video window.
- Move the video window: Drag it to a different corner of the screen.
- Hide the video window: Drag it off the left or right edge of the screen.
- Close the video window: Tap the Close button.
- Return to a full video screen: Tap the Restore Full Screen button in the small video window.

chunks.title: Notification digest - FAQs

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Communications > Notifications and Reminders:
1. How do I enable this feature on my learning site? Evaluate the following four questions and share the answers with your Customer Success Manager (CSM) or Mindtickle Support . Based on your responses, the respective settings are enabled for your learning site.
  1. Do you want the notifications for modules marked as Optional or Unmarked to be disabled and NOT go out to the learners?
    - If the above setting is enabled, the following notifications for modules marked as Optional or Unmarked for learners are not sent out.
      - Series invitation If none of the modules in the series are marked as Required , the notification is not sent. If at least one module in the series invitation is marked as Required , the series invitation is sent even though other modules are marked as Optional or Unmarked .
      - Module Invitation If the module relevance is marked as Optional or Unmarked , the email notification is not sent.
      - Module reminders If the module relevance is marked as Optional or Unmarked, the email notification is not sent.
      - Module completion If the module relevance is marked as Optional or Unmarked the email notification is not sent.
    - All other types of notifications are sent as is.
  2. Do you want learners to receive a digest email containing a summary of the series and modules they are invited to, modules they have completed in a specific time period, and the modules that are pending for them?
  3. If the answer to the above is Yes , what should be the digest frequency - weekly, every 2 weeks, or monthly?
  4. Do you want learners to be able to change the digest frequency on their own from the learning site, i.e., choose the frequency with which they wish to receive the digest?
2. What notifications are halted when the Ignore non-mandatory notifications setting is enabled for my site?
  1. The following learner-specific notifications (in which the module relevance is marked as Optional or Unmarked ) are ignored and not sent out if this setting is enabled:
    - Series invitation If none of the modules in the series are marked as Required , the notification is not sent. If at least one module in the series invitation is marked as Required , even though other modules are marked as Optional or Unmarked , the series invitation is not sent.
    - Series reminders If there are no Required modules in the series, the series reminder email is not sent. If at least one module in the series is marked Required, even though other modules are marked Optional or Unmarked, the system sends a reminder email listing only the Required module. Note: The Ignore non-mandatory email notifications setting ensures the system sends emails only when a Required module exists, but it does not change the email content. For example, in a series with 10 modules (8 Optional and 2 Required), the system sends one reminder email listing only the 2 Required modules.
    - Module invitation If the module relevance for the user is Optional or Unmarked , the email notification is ignored.
    - Module reminders If the module relevance for the user is Optional or Unmarked , the email notification is ignored.
    - Module completion If the module relevance for the user is Optional or Unmarked , the email notification is ignored.
  2. All other types of notifications are sent as is.
3. Do manager or reviewer-related notifications get affected by the Ignore non-mandatory notifications setting? Only the learner-specific notifications where learner is marked as Optional and Unmarked are affected. Manager escalation, review notifications, and reminders remain unaffected and are sent as configured on the platform. With the exception of learner-specific series invitations, module invitations, reminders, and completion notifications, all other types of notifications are sent out as they are.
4. Are other learner-specific notifications apart from invitations, reminders, and completions affected for Optional and Unmarked modules? With the exception of invitations, reminders, and completions for modules where the learner is marked as Optional or Unmarked , all other types of notifications remain unaffected. Notifications like series certifications, ILT enrollments, mission review acknowledgments, and others continue to function according to the module configurations and are not influenced by the Ignore non-mandatory notifications setting.
5. If an email notification is ignored due to it being marked as Optional or Unmarked for the learner, does it mean that the notification will still be sent through other channels such as Slack, Teams, or Webex? No, invitation, reminder & completion notifications for all channels, including Slack, MS Teams, and Webex, are ignored if the user is marked Optional or Unmarked on the module.
6. Can I just have the email digest sent to learners without ignoring invitations, reminders, and completions for Optional and Unmarked modules? Yes, Ignore non-mandatory notifications and email digest are separate independent settings and can be enabled independently, i.e., you can have email digest enabled for your learning site without notifications being ignored and vice-versa.
7. Can I prevent my users from being able to change the digest frequency on their own? The ability for learners to independently override the digest frequency is a separate setting from the Email digest feature. You have the option to enable the digest with a specified frequency for all learners without granting them the ability to override the frequency themselves.
8. Can I customize the attributes of the notification digest email, such as the subject line or email body text? No. We currently do not offer customization capabilities for any attributes of the notification digest.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Series > Overview:
The series leaderboard is a Mindtickle gamification feature to rank learners at a series level. Learners can use the leaderboard to check their scores and rank among participating peers in the series. It gives learners a more fun and engaging experience as they progress through the series. It also brings global visibility and fosters healthy competition among learners at a series level.

Learners understand where they rank among participating peers, this enables active participation and thus, continuous improvement. Using this feature, admins can enhance learner engagement and the gamification experience for learners.

Note:

- Currently, the feature is not GDPR compliant and learners cannot opt in or opt out. To ensure that admins are aware of this, Mindtickle issues a privacy notice in the product for each series while enabling the feature. The series leaderboard displays the names, photos, ranks, and scores of all series participants. This is personally identifiable information and employee performance data. Before enabling it, evaluate the privacy requirements applicable to your organization. For more information on the timelines for a complete feature release, contact your Customer Success Manager (CSM).
- Once enabled for your learning site, the leaderboard is available for each series. It is disabled by default.
- The feature is still evolving, so we have retained its beta tag.
- The feature is currently available on the web only.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Series > Enable series leaderboard:
As an admin, you can enable the series leaderboard individually for each series. It can be enabled for public, public scoped, and private series. Once enabled, all invited learners can view their scores and rank among participating peers in the series.

To enable the leaderboard for a series:

1. Navigate to the Settings tab of the series you want to enable the leaderboard. On the left navigation panel, click Leaderboard . By default, the leaderboard is disabled.
2. Switch the toggle to enable the leaderboard for the series. The privacy notice pops up. The series leaderboard displays the names, photos, ranks, and scores of all series participants. This is personally identifiable information and employee performance data. To avoid privacy or security issues, Mindtickle issues a privacy notice for each series. Before enabling it, evaluate the privacy requirements applicable to your organization. If the requirements are aligned, click Enable .
3. Click Save changes . The series leaderboard is enabled. The preview shows a sample representation of how the leaderboard appears to the learners of the series.

For more information on configuring the rest of the series settings, see Configure Series Settings.

The leaderboard has two sections:

1. The top 3 ranked learners : View the top 3 ranked learners based on the selected filter. Learners can filter the leaderboard based on when they subscribed or were invited to the series. The default time period is 90 days. The other available filters are past 30 days , past 1 year , or all time .
2. The ranking section : Learners can scroll down to the rank section to check ranks on the leaderboard among their participating peers.

For information on more available gamification options in Mindtickle, see Gamification Overview.

As an admin, you can enable the series leaderboard individually for each series. It can be enabled for public, public scoped, and private series. Once enabled, all invited learners can view their scores and rank among participating peers in the series.

To enable the leaderboard for a series:

1. Navigate to the Settings tab of the series you want to enable the leaderboard. On the left navigation panel, click Leaderboard . By default, the leaderboard is disabled.
2. Switch the toggle to enable the leaderboard for the series. The privacy notice pops up. The series leaderboard displays the names, photos, ranks, and scores of all series participants. This is personally identifiable information and employee performance data. To avoid privacy or security issues, Mindtickle issues a privacy notice for each series. Before enabling it, evaluate the privacy requirements applicable to your organization. If the requirements are aligned, click Enable .
3. Click Save changes . The series leaderboard is enabled. The preview shows a sample representation of how the leaderboard appears to the learners of the series.

For more information on configuring the rest of the series settings, see Configure Series Settings.

The leaderboard has two sections:

1. The top 3 ranked learners : View the top 3 ranked learners based on the selected filter. Learners can filter the leaderboard based on when they subscribed or were invited to the series. The default time period is 90 days. The other available filters are past 30 days , past 1 year , or all time .
2. The ranking section : Learners can scroll down to the rank section to check ranks on the leaderboard among their participating peers.

For information on more available gamification options in Mindtickle, see Gamification Overview.

Below is the questionnaire for Google Meet. For details on integrating Google Meet with Call AI, see Call AI Integration with Google Meet.

Q1 How can I manage the recording status before the Google Meet meeting starts?

There are 3 ways by which you can manage the call recording status before the Google Meet meeting starts.

a) From the Daily email digest - If you have integrated the calendar, you can disable the recording by navigating to the Upcoming calls page.

b) From the Upcoming calls page - If any participant has integrated their calendar with Call AI, they can enable or disable the recording using the toggle button.

c) From the Pre-meeting reminder email - All participants can disable the recording for the meeting.

Q2 How to start or stop recording during an ongoing Google Meet meeting?

There are 2 ways by which you can start or stop the call recording during an ongoing Google Meet meeting.

a) Any participant who has integrated the calendar in Call AI can start the recording by clicking the Record button on the Upcoming calls page in Call AI.

b) To stop the recording, click the Stop recording button on the Upcoming calls page in Call AI.

Q3 Can I remove the Call AI bot during the Google Meet meeting?

Yes, the meeting host or the co-host can remove the Call AI bot during an ongoing meeting. You can remove the Call AI bot from the People panel from the waiting lobby or after the bot joins the call.

a) From the waiting lobby.

a) The meeting host can start the recording by clicking the Record button. Also, the meeting host must ensure that Webex Assistant is enabled during the entire duration of the meeting.

Q3 Can I remove the Call AI bot during the Webex meeting?

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Automated Sync:
Google Shared Drive is a cloud-based file storage and synchronization service developed by Google. It allows users to store content securely on Google's servers, making it accessible virtually anywhere.

Integrating Google Shared Drive on the Mindtickle platform enables admins to sync designated content from Google Shared Drive to Mindtickle automatically.

The Google Shared Drive content sync is one-way from Google Shared Drive to Mindtickle.

This article explains how admins can integrate Google Shared Drive with Mindtickle.

Google Shared Drive is a cloud-based file storage and synchronization service developed by Google. It allows users to store content securely on Google's servers, making it accessible virtually anywhere.

Integrating Google Shared Drive on the Mindtickle platform enables admins to sync designated content from Google Shared Drive to Mindtickle automatically.

The Google Shared Drive content sync is one-way from Google Shared Drive to Mindtickle.

This article explains how admins can integrate Google Shared Drive with Mindtickle.
chunks.headingPath: Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Automated Sync
chunks.title: Content Center–Google Shared Drive sync: Integrate Google Shared Drive with Mindtickle

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Automated Sync > Benefits of integration:
Integrating Google Shared Drive to sync the content from Google Shared Drive to Mindtickle automatically improves the productivity and efficiency of enablement admins. They would no longer need to update the content on the Mindtickle platform manually.

Features of the automated sync from Google Shared Drive:

- Admins can designate specific folders to sync from Google Shared Drive to Mindtickle’s Content Center.
- In Google Shared Drive, updating the content in the designated folders automatically updates the content in the Content Center.
- Moving the files or folders in Google Shared Drive automatically replicates the files and folders synced to the Content Center.
- Deleting files and folders in Google Shared Drive also deletes the corresponding files in Mindtickle only if they are not used in modules or assets. If they are used in modules or assets, the files and folders are converted to regular files and folders. That is, they are no longer synced with Google Shared Drive.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Automated Sync > Steps to integrate Google Shared Drive with Mindtickle > Add account details:
1. In the admin site sidebar, click Account > Settings > Security & Integrations.On the Security & Integrations page, scroll down to the Content Sync section and click the Google Shared Drive tab.

2. Under Google Shared Drives, click Add account to get started.

3. On the Add account pop-up, enter a unique connection name, which will be used to create a folder in Content Center for syncing with your Google Shared Drive. Then, click Connect with Google to sign in and authenticate using a valid Google account. During this process, Mindtickle requires the following permissions on your Google Drive: See and download all your Google Drive files and View the activity record of files in your Google Drive. These are required to set up the sync between your selected Google Shared Drive folder and Mindtickle's Content Center.

4. Once done, the Google account is configured successfully. To change the synced Google account, click Use a different account. Click Save and proceed.
