chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Automated Sync > Steps to integrate Google Shared Drive with Mindtickle > Map folders:
1. Admins must map folders from the Google Shared Drive to sync content with Mindtickle. Mindtickle automatically pulls content, including all sub-folders, from the configured folders. To do this, click Add folder, select the desired folders from Google Shared Drives, and click Select.

2. Once the folder is connected, you hover over it to view it on Google Drive. Use the Delete option to delete the connected folder. Repeat this process by clicking Add folder again to link additional folders as needed.

Note:

- You can add a maximum of 50 folder paths.
- The folder path can have at most 9 levels of nested folders. Mindtickle does not sync content beyond 9 nested folders.
- You cannot configure the same folder path multiple times.
- You cannot configure a child folder for an already configured parent folder.

3. Once done, click Save and proceed.

1. Click the Sync frequency drop-down arrow to set how often content syncs from Google Shared Drive to Mindtickle's Content Center.

2. If a sync fails, users with the TECHNICAL_SETTINGS permission will receive notifications. To enable this, select the desired users in the Notify users in case of sync failures dropdown menu and click Apply.

After configuring these settings, click Add to complete the integration.

The integration gets listed in the Configured accounts section.

For the activities admins can perform on the configured account, see Automated content sync: Manage integration and sync settings.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Automated Sync > Limitations:
- If a synced folder (along with the folder content) is deleted on Google Drive, one of the following happens to the folder and its files on Content Center:
  - If any files are currently in use (added to module learning objects or assets) on Mindtickle, then Content Center retains these files along with the folder. However, they will no longer be synced.
  - If any files are NOT in use on Mindtickle, we delete the files along with the folder from Content Center.
- Sync selection
  - Sync is possible only for folders within the Google Shared Drives .
  - Sync does not apply to the complete Google Shared Drive.
  - Sync does not apply to a single file or selection of files. You can only select folders for sync.
  - Sync can be configured with folders in Shared Drive only. Content sync from My Drive or Shared with me is not supported.
- Folder hierarchy
  - The selected folder for sync can have a maximum of 9 levels of nested folders under it.
- File and folder names
  - The use of the special characters ‘ / ’ and ‘ \ ’ is not supported in the file and folder names. The use of all other special characters is supported.
  - The file name cannot exceed the maximum limit of 250 characters.
- File size limitations
  - For details, see Supported file types and size limits for uploading and syncing content to Mindtickle .

  - For details, see Supported file types and size limits for uploading and syncing content to Mindtickle .

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Automated Sync > Frequently asked questions (FAQs):
What can I do if I have more than 9 nested folders within the folder path configured to sync?

Instead of configuring the parent folder with more than 9 nested folders, configure its child folders so that none have more than 9 folders. Alternatively, configure the parent folders in Google Shared Drive so the configured folder does not have more than 9 nested folders.

Note: At a later point (after successfully activating the Google Shared Drive connection), in the configured folders, if the admin breaches the limit of 9 nested folders and creates more nested folders, the content is not synced from the folder beyond 9-levels of the hierarchy.

What if I need more than 50 folder paths in the mapping?

Add another account with the remaining folders. Multiple Google Shared Drive accounts can be created and connected.

What if the sync fails for a file not supported on Content Center?

To avoid sync failures, move the unsupported files outside the folder paths configured to sync into Mindtickle.

What are the different types of sync failures?

The table below highlights the various types of sync failures and their solutions.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Automated Sync:
Google Shared Drive is a cloud-based file storage and synchronization service developed by Google. It allows users to store content securely on Google's servers, making it accessible virtually anywhere.

Integrating Google Shared Drive with Mindtickle platform enables admins to automatically sync content from Google Drive to Asset Hub.

The Google Shared Drive content sync is one-way from Google Shared Drive to Asset Hub.

Additionally, the synced content gets automatically updated across all instances where it has been utilized, such as in modules, assets, and DSR. This sync ensures the information is up-to-date across the board.

This article explains the UI and functional changes the admins experience on the Asset Hub side when Google Shared Drive integrates with Mindtickle. It also describes how Asset Hub adds, modifies, or replaces externally synced assets.

Note: Asset Hub is a paid feature. For more information, contact your Customer Success Manager (CSM).

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Asset Hub > My assets page:
My assets is a dedicated space to store, organize, and manage your customized assets. This dedicated space allows you to create hubs and organize the customized assets in those hubs. This feature empowers you to personalize and manage your sales materials, making it easy to create, share, and track assets while staying in sync with the organization's broader asset management system used by admins.

The key benefits of this personalized space are:

- Asset creation : Create your own sales materials and use them as an asset. The source of the sales material can be in PDF, PPT, XLS, and Doc format. Additionally, you can now directly upload supported file types (such as videos, images, or documents) as assets into your personal hubs without using the slide customization flow.
- Hub creation : Create folders (hubs) to group related assets together.
- Sharing : Share these customized assets with prospects and customers.
- Tracking : Track how these assets perform when shared externally.
- Ownership and management : Full control over the assets you create; you can edit, move, or delete them.

To access the My assets page, click the Assets icon → My assets option in the sidebar.

If you are accessing the My assets for the first time, it prompts you to create assets.

Click the Create asset button to start creating customized assets. Clicking the button opens a new tab where you can start adding slides from existing assets (only customizable ones) or uploading slides (if enabled for the learning site) from the local computer or the cloud storage.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Asset Hub > Manage hubs > Access assets in hubs:
You can view the customized assets within your hub. You can search and sort the relevant assets within a hub. When sorting by Recently Modified, assets are listed based on the most recent edits made after their initial creation.

Note: If the source assets used to create your customized assets are updated, archived, expired, or marked as non-customizable, or if your access to them is restricted, a note appears at the top of the hub telling you how many assets need your attention. Click View X assets to list them.

Each affected asset also shows a label next to its name:

- Old version : One or more pages/slides in this customized asset come from a source asset whose content has changed. Your asset is still shareable. Open the asset details page to see which pages/slides are affected, then click Accept changes or update them yourself.
- Unshareable : At least one page/slide in this customized asset comes from a source asset that is no longer available — it has been deleted, archived, or expired, is marked as non-customizable, or your access to it is restricted. The Share button is unavailable until you resolve those pages/slides. Anything you shared earlier stays accessible to those recipients.

For details, see Source asset states on customized assets.

Hover over the asset for options to preview, share (via room, email, or link), edit (Mix and match OR Edit a copy to mix and match) and more options (rename, move, download, or delete the asset). Click anywhere on the asset row to open the asset details page.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Asset Hub > A) Create assets via file upload:
Under Add → Asset, the Upload new file option allows you create an asset based on a file uploaded from your computer or supported cloud storage providers, such as Dropbox and Google Drive.

Note:

- The option to upload file is available only if the feature is enabled for your Mindtickle instance. Contact your CSM to enable it.
- Files uploaded from cloud storage providers are not synced after the upload.
- Various file formats (like documents, images, audio, and video) are supported; however, embedded link type of assets are not supported.
- Uploading from mobile phones or tablets is currently not supported. You can view the My assets page on tablets (in landscape mode); however, it is currently not accessible on mobile phones.

Perform the following to create a custom asset by uploading a file:

1. On the My assets page, click Add → Asset → Upload new file .
2. Select an existing personal hub or create a new one to save the asset to. Click Continue to upload .
3. Choose a file from your local device or supported cloud storage (Google Drive, Dropbox, Box, OneDrive). You can upload only one file at a time. Files from cloud storage do not sync automatically after upload. Hover over "See supported file types" link to view all supported file types.
4. The system processes the uploaded file and creates the asset in the selected hub.
5. After processing, the newly-created asset appears on the page. You can edit the asset, manage it (move, download, or delete), and share it with prospects and customers and track engagement.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Asset Hub > B) Create assets via mix and match > I. Add slides from assets:
1. Click Add slides from assets button to add slides from existing assets (only customizable ones).
2. The Add slides page appears and lists all customizable assets (PDF, PPT, XLS, and Doc formats) available to you. You can filter assets (by hubs, attributes, and more), search for a specific asset, and sort the list as needed. If you have any customized assets available under the My assets tab, you can select them too.
3. Select the assets you want to add. The number of pages/slides displayed on an asset indicates that the entire asset is selected. To view only the selected assets, turn on the Show selected only toggle. Alternatively, click the arrow next to an asset to view its individual pages/slides. You can choose all or specific pages/slides. Hover over a page/slide and click the preview icon to preview it. Then, click Add <x> slides to proceed.
4. The asset draft appears with your selected pages/slides. You can perform the following:
  - Click Add slides from assets to include additional pages/slides from other assets.
  - Click Upload slides button to upload a file and add pages/slides from it (specific or all pages). Note : The Upload slides option is available only if the feature is enabled for your Mindtickle instance. Contact your CSM to enable it.
  - Switch between Grid view and Panel view to manage your slides.
  - Select some or all pages/slides to include in the final asset.
  - Drag and drop pages/slides to rearrange their order.
  - Hover over a page/slide and click delete to remove it.
  - Use the undo and redo buttons to reverse or reinstate your changes.
5. Before saving the curated asset, the system checks that all pages/slides are in a valid state. Any page/slide whose source asset has a problem is labeled:
  - Updated : The source asset’s content has changed. You can still save the asset. Compare the page/slide with the updated source asset and decide whether to replace it.
  - Deleted , Archived , Expired , Non-customizable , or No access : The source asset is no longer available. You must delete these pages/slides before you can save the asset.
6. A banner at the top tells you how many changes there are and which pages/slides are affected. Turn on View changed pages only to show just those pages/slides, or click Accept changes to update them all at once. For details, see Source asset states on customized assets .
7. To save your changes and create the asset, click Save asset . A pop-up appears asking you to select any of your personal hubs or create a new one and save the asset there. Note : If all selected slides are from PowerPoint sources, you will also have the option to choose the output format (PPT or PDF). If the selection includes mixed file types, the asset will be saved as a PDF by default.
8. The asset appears once it's created successfully.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Asset Hub > B) Create assets via mix and match > Personalize slides using variables (customize slides):
1. In the mix and match flow, click the Customize slides button.
2. The Customize your slides panel opens and lists the variable fields for the asset. Each field shows the label your admin defined, an info icon with a description (where provided), and the number of slides the variable appears on.
3. If the template uses Salesforce Opportunity data, the panel displays a Select deal field at the top. Search for and select the relevant deal (Salesforce Opportunity). Mindtickle then automatically fills the mapped fields using data from that deal. For example, selecting a deal can populate the AE name, company name, and AE title. Note : You can edit any auto-filled value, and you can fill in any field that was not mapped to a Salesforce field manually.
4. For image variables (such as a company logo), add the image manually. Logos are not pulled from Salesforce. Click Upload new to add a logo, or Replace to change it. The selected image is fit within the placeholder's dimensions.
5. Close the Customize your slides panel. The personalized values are not reflected in the preview immediately; they are applied when you save the asset.
6. Click Save asset , choose the output format (PPT or PDF, depending on the selected slides), and select a personal hub to save it to.
7. Mindtickle processes and generates the asset with your personalized values applied. Keep the tab open while the asset is being saved.

Once generated, the personalized asset is ready to share directly with your prospect via a room, email, or link.

Using the Page Builder, you can create custom homepages for the learning site to provide unique, personalized pages to your learners. chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Setup > Page Builder for learning site homepages > Access and manage homepages:
- Unique, personalized pages for different sets of learners: You can configure the content for each page to provide a customized homepage experience for learners in the groups selected for the page. It helps you ensure that learners see content that is more specific and relevant to them, rather than get overwhelmed by or spend time in figuring out what content to consume next, what is complete and incomplete, and so on.
- Page visibility: The default homepage is global and it will always be visible to all existing and future learners on the platform. This page cannot be unpublished or deleted. On the other hand, when you create a custom homepage, you can configure its visibility/audience to:
  - Selected learner groups: Only the learners belonging to the selected groups will be able to view the page.
  - All learners: All existing and future learners on the platform will be able to view the page — similar to the visibility set for the default homepage.
  - No learners: No learners will be able to view the page.
- Same editing experience: Custom pages are edited/configured in the same way as the default homepage. We made no changes to this experience you are already familiar with!
- Nested pages: Nest homepages within each other to create a more seamless experience in discovering training contents/assets. Using the permanent link of a page, you can link it in other pages by adding the link in various widgets, such as Spotlight, Text, Image, and Custom HTML/CSS.
- Page order: Rearrange pages to define the order in which the pages will appear to learners. Setting appropriate page order helps learners easily switch between pages.
chunks.body:

It helps you ensure that learners see content that is more specific and relevant to them, rather than get overwhelmed by or spend time in figuring out what content to consume next, what is complete and incomplete, and so on.

Once you have created a page, you can make further changes anytime by editing the page. On the Homepages listing page, do one of the following to edit a page:

- Click> Edit.
- Click the page to open it for editing.

Page Builder opens the page in editing mode so you can make changes to the widgets, layout, and more. Once done with your changes, you can either publish or discard your changes. Learners will see your changes only after you publish the page again.

Manage unpublished changes

When you have made any changes to an active and published page but missed to publish your changes, the page header displays a red dot over the page status (the “Active” label). On the Page Builder homepage, click the page in the left panel to see the red dot in the page header.

Click Edit page to enter page editing mode. You can either publish or discard your changes. Learners will see your changes only after you publish the page again.

Publish draft pages

After creating and configuring a page, you need to publish and activate it so that it becomes visible to learners. Any new or duplicated page remains in the draft state until you publish it. You must publish and activate the draft page to make it active. Only active pages will be visible to the learners.

You can publish and activate it in one of the following ways:

- Click> Publish and activate.
- Click the page to open it for editing. Click Publish in the edit mode.

For the custom homepages you have created for the learning site, you need to set each page’s visibility to a set of learners based on groups or to all learners. This lets you restrict or broaden learners’ access to the custom pages, show or hide pages from learners as necessary.

Note: The default homepage is global and it will always be visible to all existing and future learners on the platform. You cannot deactivate (unpublish) or delete it.

A newly published custom page is not visible to any learners by default because the default visibility is set to no learners. For information on how to set the page visibility for a new page, see Steps 7-11 in the “Create a custom homepage” section. This section provides information on how to manage already set visibility settings.

To manage the visibility of a page for learners, select the page in the left panel and then click Manage visibility in the page header.

You can configure page visibility/audience as one of the following:

- Selected learner groups: Only the learners belonging to the selected groups will be able to view the page.
- All learners: All existing and future learners on the platform will be able to view the page — similar to the visibility set for the default homepage.
- No learners: No learners will be able to view the page.

Additionally, for the Selected learner groups option, you can add or remove groups associated with the page. For information on how to add groups, see Steps 7-11 in the “Create a custom homepage” section.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Setup > Page Builder for learning site homepages > Manage custom homepages > Use as a nested/linked page:
You can copy the unique and permanent link of any custom homepage (and the default homepage) and add it in other custom pages through widgets. Using the link URL, you can link to a custom page in multiple other custom pages. Simply put, the link functionality lets you cross-link custom pages with each other. You can nest homepages within each other to create a more seamless experience in discovering training contents/assets. If there are multiple levels of nesting, learners can click the browser back and forward buttons to navigate back and forth between linked pages and other linked content, such as series and modules or external content.

On the Page Builder homepage, select the page in the left panel. Then, from the page header, click the link button to copy the link to this page to your clipboard.

Anyone with access to your site can view the page using this link. You can link this page in other custom homepages by adding the link in a widget, such as Spotlight, Text, Image, and Custom HTML/CSS widgets.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Setup > Page Builder for learning site homepages > Sections and page outline:
You can create sections for any homepage and, optionally, enable the page outline that appears like a table of contents (ToC).

Important: You can enable the page outline only if the homepage was created with a single column (1 column) layout. Page outline is not supported for two column layouts.

- Sections: Helps you group multiple widget rows into a section to integrate the rows. Sections are useful for keeping multiple related widgets together and occupy less screen real estate compared to independent widget rows.
- Page outline (optional): After adding and naming sections, you can also enable the page outline, which creates links to all sections on the page. The page outlines are like a table of contents (ToC); learners can click the section links in the outline to quickly navigate to the sections. You can display the outline on the left or right of the page.

There are no limits to the number of sections you can add on a page and the number of widget rows you can add to a section.

Creating sections and page outline for a learning site homepage works the same way as for overview pages. For instructions, see Create and edit overview pages.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Setup > Page Builder for learning site homepages > Page-level settings:
Page-level settings offer you more control over the look and feel of your learning site homepages, letting you customize the vertical alignment of widgets within a row, space between widgets, and the widget card style at the page level. These settings are available for both single-column and two-column layout pages.

The following settings are available:

- Vertical alignment: Adjust the vertical position of widgets within a row:
  - Top (default)

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Web Conferencing:
Mindtickle’s integration with the Webex video conferencing platform allows you to manage (create/update/delete) meetings and automate attendance tracking for your Instructor-Led Training (ILT) sessions. With this integration, when participants attend an ILT Webinar conducted over Webex, their attendance is marked automatically.

This integration is powered through Webex App Hub. To access the Mindtickle app on App Hub, click here.

The ILT-Webex integration marks learners’ attendance automatically by matching email addresses in the Webex attendance report with the list of email addresses of learners invited to the ILT module.

Note:

- If a learner’s email address is not listed in the Webex attendance report, their attendance is marked as Did not attend . (Admins can manually change the learner’s attendance status from the admin site.) This feature is available only on request. To enable it for your organization, contact Mindtickle Support or your Customer Success Manager (CSM).
- If the host sets up breakout rooms during a meeting, the attendance report includes data for participants in both, the breakout rooms and the main session.

For attendance tracking, the following conditions must be met:

- Users are invited to the ILT module
- Users join the Webex meeting with the email address associated with their Mindtickle user ID (email address)

This article explains how you can set up the ILT-Webex integration if user-level authentication is enabled on your learning site. User-level authentication within the ILT-Webex integration mandates admins to authenticate their Webex account in Mindtickle before creating Webex meetings in ILT sessions. This is a one-time configuration that needs to be done by every host*. Non-authenticated users would be unable to perform any operations as a host of the meeting. Meeting validations and auto-attendance are not be tracked for the meetings whose host is an unauthenticated user.

- You can configure the ILT-Webex setup using either the admin-level authorization or user-level authorization. By default, admin-level authorization is configured.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Web Conferencing > Use Webex integration in ILT sessions:
1. Create a new ILT session . By default, the session type is set to Classroom location . In the dialog box for creating a new session, select the session type from the Classroom / video conferencing tool details dropdown. For a video conferencing session, you can create a Webex meeting from the session or add a meeting link manually. This article lists the procedure for creating a Webex meeting from the ILT session for reference purposes. Note :
  - While creating a meeting from the ILT session, ensure:
    - The session start and end time is set in the future.
    - The session time is more than 10 minutes.
2. Select Generate Webex meeting link from the dropdown. If your account is authenticated, the meeting link is generated, and the meeting details and host details are auto-filled in the Meeting Details section. If the meeting link is associated with the Webex account integrated with your Mindtickle learning site, the Auto attendance toggle is set to ON , indicating that the attendance for this meeting is automatically recorded. If your account is not authenticated, the system prompts you to authenticate your Webex account. Click Authenticate to validate your account. You are directed to the Webex sign-in page. The Mindtickle authorization page appears. Click Accept . Upon successful validation, you are redirected to the ILT session and the meeting is created successfully. Alternatively, click Enter host email ID . Enter the host’s email address, and click Create meeting . The meeting link is generated, and the meeting details and host details are auto-filled in the Meeting Details section. Note :
  - If you enter the email address of a user who is not authenticated, the system prompts you to enter the details of a user with host permissions.
  - Suppose an admin who has a valid Webex license and is authenticated, attempts to create the meeting. The meeting is created successfully without the need to perform any additional steps.
  - Suppose an admin who has a valid Webex license but is not authenticated, attempts to create the meeting. The system prompts the user for authentication before proceeding further. In this case, the admin may click Authenticate to validate their account on Webex and proceed further. They are directed to the Webex sign-in page. Ensure that you have entered the correct credentials for Webex. For any issues, contact Mindtickle Support . If the integration is not continuously used for 3 months, you must re-authorize it. Reauthorization might not be required indefinitely when the integration is constantly used. Also, these tokens can be invalidated before their expiry from Webex’s side in case of a change in the user's scope, password update, etc. The Mindtickle authorization page appears. Click Accept . For the integration to work successfully, the following scopes are requested by Webex: ScopeUsagemeeting:participants_readRead the meeting's participants to mark auto-attendance in Mindtickle ILTmeeting:schedules_readValidate the Webex meeting URL for auto-attendance eligibility in ILTmeeting:schedules_writeCreate, update, and delete Webex meeting in ILTspark:people_readValidate the user account in Mindtickle Or, click Enter host email ID and enter the email address of an admin whose Webex account is authenticated.
  - If an admin without a Webex license attempts to create a meeting via a user who has a Webex account but is not authenticated, the system prompts the admin for authentication. Once authenticated, the admin is redirected to the ILT page and the meeting is created successfully.
3. While entering a meeting link manually, select Enter meeting link from the dropdown and enter the meeting URL in the Enter Meeting URL section.
  - If the meeting is created using an account that has ‘host’ privileges, the system checks the URL for Webex auto-attendance eligibility. If eligible, the Auto attendance toggle appears and is automatically switched ON.
  - If the meeting is created from an account that doesn’t have ‘host’ privileges, the system prompts you to authenticate the Webex account or enter the email address of a user with ‘host’ privileges.
  - If the session type is set to Classroom location and you enter the URL of a Webex meeting manually, the session type changes to Enter link manually . The system checks the URL for Webex auto attendance eligibility. If eligible, the Auto attendance toggle appears and is automatically switched ON .
4. You can add co-hosts to the meeting. Co-hosts help improve meeting productivity. The ‘co-host’ role has permissions similar to the ‘host’ role. If the host is running late or cannot attend, a co-host can start and manage the meeting. Co-hosts can also assist the host with meeting management, which is helpful for larger meetings. Click Add co-host , enter the user’s email address, and click Save . Note : If details of users added as co-hosts are invalid, a failure message is displayed on the screen indicating that the users are not added as co-hosts to the meeting. The user is added as a co-host to the meeting. Click to edit the details or to remove the user as a co-host from the meeting. Alternatively, you can add instructors or facilitators and assign them as co-hosts for the meeting. To assign an instructor or facilitator as a co-host, enter their details on the Instructors and facilitators tab, and select the Add as meeting co-host checkbox. The users are added to the list of co-hosts. Note :
  - There is no limit to the number of co-hosts you can add to a meeting.
  - If an instructor or facilitator is added or removed as a co-host from the meeting, they receive an email notification with all session change details (if applicable). The email is sent after the session is published.
  - All the meeting links that belong to the authenticated hosts’ Webex account on Mindtickle are eligible for auto-attendance.
  - If the Auto attendance toggle is switched off, you must mark the attendance manually or via session check-in.
  - The check-in feature is unavailable for sessions in which auto attendance is enabled. To use the check-in feature, turn the toggle switch off.
  - You cannot generate Webex webinar links from the ILT session. However, you can add a webinar link that belongs to the authenticated hosts’ Webex account manually. Attendance is recorded automatically for webinar links added manually.
5. Configure the remaining settings and click Create session . A confirmation message is displayed on the screen once the session is created successfully. The session appears in the list of sessions. The Attendance mode of the session is listed as Auto attendance . Click the session to view other details.
6. Publish the session and invite your learners. Once the session ends, participants’ attendance is marked automatically via Webex.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Web Conferencing > Use Webex integration in ILT sessions > Duration-based attendance capture:
Admins can set a minimum percentage threshold to record learners’ attendance for ILT modules and individual sessions using the Duration-based attendance capture feature.

This feature automatically records learners’ attendance based on their time in ILT events and sessions.

When participants attend an ILT Webinar conducted over Webex, their attendance is marked automatically. The Webex integration provides the time spent by the learner in a session.

The Webex integration provides the time spent by the learner in a session.

The system calculates an ILT session’s minimum attendance threshold as follows,

- Scheduled sessions: For scheduled sessions that are yet to start, the system calculates the minimum attendance threshold using the session's start and end time set during session creation. For example, in a 60-minute session with a 20% minimum attendance threshold, the system marks the learner as attended if they spend at least 12 minutes (20% of 60) in the session.
- Completed sessions: If a session ends early or extends beyond the scheduled time, the system calculates the minimum attendance threshold based on the actual session time. For example, for a 60-minute session with a 20% minimum attendance threshold, if the session ends early in 50 minutes, the system marks the learner as attended if they spend at least 10 minutes (20% of 50) in the session.

The system compares the learners’ time in session provided by Webex with the session’s minimum attendance threshold to mark the learner's attendance for the session.

The learner’s attendance status and time spent in sessions are displayed in the Attendance status/Duration column on the Events and Sessions tab of the ILT.

For example, in a 60-minute session with a 20% minimum attendance threshold, the system marks the learner as attended if they spend at least 12 minutes (20% of 60) in the session.
- Completed sessions: If a session ends early or extends beyond the scheduled time, the system calculates the minimum attendance threshold based on the actual session time. For example, for a 60-minute session with a 20% minimum attendance threshold, if the session ends early in 50 minutes, the system marks the learner as attended if they spend at least 10 minutes (20% of 50) in the session.

The system compares the learners’ time in session provided by Webex with the session’s minimum attendance threshold to mark the learner's attendance for the session.

The learner’s attendance status and time spent in sessions are displayed in the Attendance status/Duration column on the Events and Sessions tab of the ILT.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Web Conferencing > FAQs:
Q: If I have already created a Webex meeting, can I add it to the ILT session in Mindtickle? Will attendance still be marked?

A: Yes, you can add the Webex meeting URL. As long as you have authenticated your account, the session is eligible for auto-attendance.

Q: What do I do if I am not hosting the meeting, but I am setting it up for the host?

A: Create the ILT session. When creating the Webex meeting from the session, click Enter host email id on the first pop-up that appears.

Enter the host’s email address in the next pop-up and click Create Meeting.

Or, click Authenticate your Webex account to authenticate a new account and enter the host’s email ID on the pop-up.

If your account is authenticated, the meeting is generated with you as the host. You may then add the actual host as the co-host.

Q: What if an ILT participant attends the session just for a couple minutes? Are they marked as attended?

A: Yes, the participant is marked as attended. The integration does not have a way to capture the time spent in the ILT.

Q: Do learners need to enroll for auto-attendance to work?

A: Learners do not have to enroll to a session but must be invited to the ILT module to be automatically marked as attended.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Mobile App > Share assets:
To share assets on your mobile, sign in to the Mindtickle mobile app and tap the Assets option on the bottom navigation bar.

The Asset Hub homepage displays. The homepage is a widget-based content dashboard that holds all the assets and hubs on the platform.

Tap the hub to view the assets and share. Alternatively, you can tap Share in the upper-right corner of the Asset Hub homepage.

The Share assets page displays. Select the assets from the Assets and My assets tabs. You can share a maximum of 20 assets at a time.

Note:

- You can only share assets marked External by the admin or asset owner and have not expired .
- The My assets tab lists the customized assets. If there are no customized assets available, this tab is empty. For more information on customizing assets and My assets tab, see My assets tab (mobile) .

To check if an asset suits your requirements, tap the asset to view its details, such as description, external engagement, expiration date, and last updated date.

Additionally, to ensure you share the right assets, you can tap the Arrow for each asset in the list to quickly view its details, such as asset preview, description, engagement insights, expiry, and last updated date.

You can apply different filters to view a specific list of search results. Tap the Filter icon in the lower-right corner of the screen.

On the Sort and filter page, sort the assets by:

- Recently modified
- Average rating
- Number of views
- Number of shares
- Alphabetically

Use the Filters section to filter the assets by hubs, attributes, shared by you, and bookmarked (under the More filters dropdown). Once done, tap the Apply button to proceed.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Copilot > For admins > About Copilot:
Mindtickle Copilot is a suite of generative AI capabilities purpose-built for sales, enablement, and revenue operations teams. Embedded in the sales workflow, it supports onboarding, training, deal coaching, and buyer engagement — providing guidance that accelerates pipeline growth, shortens ramp time, enhances coaching, and boosts quota attainment. By combining Mindtickle’s data with enterprise-grade AI, it helps teams stay focused on revenue-driving work: selling more and delighting customers.

Copilot powers a wide range of AI-driven features across the Mindtickle platform, including mission creation and review, content and video generation, coaching feedback, call analysis, and chat-based guidance. These features support roles such as admins, sales reps, and managers, and are available via the admin site, learning site, mobile app, Salesforce, and APIs.

Mindtickle Copilot is built on secure, enterprise-grade large language models, including GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 (via Microsoft Azure OpenAI Service) and Claude Haiku and Sonnet (via Amazon Bedrock). It does not use OpenAI’s public ChatGPT. All Copilot features are developed with robust security and privacy and operate within Mindtickle’s SOC 2 Type II and GDPR-compliant infrastructure.

On Copilot accuracy

chunks.body:
Mindtickle Copilot is a suite of generative AI capabilities purpose-built for sales, enablement, and revenue operations teams. Embedded in the sales workflow, it supports onboarding, training, deal coaching, and buyer engagement — providing guidance that accelerates pipeline growth, shortens ramp time, enhances coaching, and boosts quota attainment. By combining Mindtickle’s data with enterprise-grade AI, it helps teams stay focused on revenue-driving work: selling more and delighting customers.

Copilot powers a wide range of AI-driven features across the Mindtickle platform, including mission creation and review, content and video generation, coaching feedback, call analysis, and chat-based guidance. These features support roles such as admins, sales reps, and managers, and are available via the admin site, learning site, mobile app, Salesforce, and APIs.

Mindtickle Copilot is built on secure, enterprise-grade large language models, including GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 (via Microsoft Azure OpenAI Service) and Claude Haiku and Sonnet (via Amazon Bedrock). Note: Available only for AI video roleplay missions. Help article BETA Copilot as mission reviewer Configure Copilot as an automated reviewer for the learner’s mission submissions, making large-scale practice easy while enabling managers to focus their attention where feedback is most impactful.

Upon mission submission, Copilot evaluates the scenario and criteria, delivering personalized feedback that combines qualitative insights with quantitative scores. This helps sales reps continuously improve their skills and performance — accelerating development while minimizing the manual review burden on managers.

You can configure Copilot as reviewer under the Build tab → Reviewers → Appoint reviewers setting.

Note: Available only for voiceover slideshow, video roleplay, and email and task evaluation missions. Not supported for screen capture missions.

Help article

Copilot-generated reviewer guidance

Under the Build tab → Evaluation parameters, each parameter includes a Guidance for reviewer textbox with a Generate Guidance option. You can further tailor it using the Improve guidance option with suggested prompts or your own input.

This guidance helps the human/Copilot reviewer in ensuring consistent scoring with minimal variation and also helps in clearly differentiate across good, average, and poor submissions.

Note: Available only for voiceover slideshow, video roleplay, and email and task evaluation missions. Not supported for screen capture missions.

Not supported for screen capture missions. Help article AI assistance: Copilot insights to improve learner drafts

Under the Build tab → AI assistance, you can configure three parameters that generate AI-based insights for learners, helping them refine their mission drafts before submitting their best version for review. These insights help learners easily identify gaps in keywords to use, words to avoid, speech pace, submission length, and filler word usage. Appointed reviewers can also view these insights before providing their feedback.

AI assistance includes three key parameters: Content (model pitch, keywords to include or avoid, and minimum keyword usage), Articulation (target pitch length and speech pace), and Text Sentiment (English-only sentiment analysis of the transcript for tones like anger, anxiety, or joy).

Note:

- These settings cannot be changed once the mission is published.
- Available only for voiceover slideshow , video roleplay , and screen capture missions. Not supported for email and task evaluation missions.

Help article

CLOSED BETA Insights: Optimize learner roleplay performance with AI insights and custom feedback

Under the Build tab → Insights, you can customize the AI-generated insights and feedback provided to learners on their drafts and submissions, specifically for AI roleplay missions. You can enable or disable the display of insights to learners, and configure up to three custom feedback areas with explanations for the AI. The insights offer qualitative feedback on clarity, tone, and structure, while submitted drafts receive a quantitative review score. Additionally, you can manage roleplay metrics and set recommended limits for each parameter.

Note: Available only for AI video roleplay missions.

Seller Copilot adoption and engagement reports

The Copilot section under Analytics shows how your team is adopting and engaging with Seller Copilot, across two tabs: Adoption and Engagement. Adoption covers active users, usage trends, usage breakdown, and user activity. Engagement covers session and usage measures along with engagement signals such as suggestion clicks, response copies, and source-link clicks. Access is controlled by the View Copilot Analytics permission.

Help article

Copilot prompt analytics in Call AI adoption reports

In the Call AI adoption reports → Calls report, the Copilot prompts column shows the total number of prompts entered by a team or individual user. These prompts are the queries users enter while interacting with Copilot on the call recording page.

Managers can view this data on the learning site under Team analytics → Call AI analytics.

Help article

AI-powered coaching insights in reviewer reports

The Coaching insights tab in the coaching reviewer reports gives senior leaders and enablement admins an AI-driven assessment of coaching quality across the organization. It synthesizes text, scores, and metadata from individual coaching sessions into executive-level intelligence, so leaders can spot systemic risks and target developmental support without reviewing every session manually.

The tab includes a Team overview widget summarizing coaching behaviors across the organization, a Reviewer summary for each manager describing their coaching focus, strengths, patterns, and improvement areas, and a Learners and sessions table for drilling into specific coaching sessions in view-only mode.

Note: This feature is not enabled by default. It also requires user hierarchy to be configured. To enable it, contact Mindtickle Support.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Copilot > For admins > Available Copilot features > B. Learning site > Copilot assistant:
Chat with Seller Copilot on the learning site

Seller Copilot helps sales reps boost productivity by providing AI-powered, real-time answers on products, processes, customers, and more. It respects your existing access and permissions, ensuring you only see content relevant to you, as configured by your admin.

Access Copilot: You can open Seller Copilot via the button on the learning site or through global search. This opens a chat interface where you can type your own question or pick from suggested prompts.

Ask questions: Copilot pulls answers from modules (assigned or public), assets, and Call AI calls available to you. Use it for quick support, from prepping for a call to handling objections and follow-ups.

You can also point Copilot at specific Mindtickle resources or your own files. Type @ in the chat input, or use the + button, to link a module, asset, or call recording, or to upload a file (beta) and ask questions about it.

Help article

Search-integrated Copilot Assistant for Sellers

Copilot Assistant for Sellers is an AI-powered search tool built into the learning site’s global search. It combines semantic search with just-in-time (JIT) enablement to deliver relevant, context-aware information on products, personas, value propositions, competitive insights, and more.

Simply type a question or request into the search bar, and Copilot provides a concise summary, source links, and related content. Answers are drawn from modules and assets you have access to.

You can seamlessly continue the in-search answer into a full conversation. Selecting a suggested follow-up question or clicking Continue with Copilot opens Seller Copilot and transitions the interaction into a full chat thread, with context carried forward.

Copilot features on the call recording page

Draft emails with Copilot while sharing assets via email

Mindtickle Copilot helps sales reps quickly draft personalized, high-impact emails when sharing assets via email with customers or prospects in the following ways:

- Directly from the Mindtickle platform
- Through Mindtickle Gmail extension
- Through Mindtickle Outlook add-in

In each case, Copilot leverages generative AI to craft relevant, impactful email drafts tailored to the recipient and the shared asset. This allows reps to communicate more efficiently and effectively, saving time while ensuring consistency, professionalism, and personalization in every message.

Help article

Explore similar assets with Copilot on the asset page

The Similar Assets feature uses Copilot to recommend up to 10 relevant assets related to the one you’re viewing, helping reps quickly find impactful, up-to-date content.

When you open an asset from a hub or search, click the icon (visible only if similar assets exist) to see related assets. Suggestions are based on content, asset properties (name, views, shares, ratings, downloads, recency), and your access permissions. The list updates daily as assets change or new ones are added. Click any asset to preview it and open it in a new tab.

Chat with Seller Copilot (mobile)

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Copilot > For admins > Available Copilot features > D. Mindtickle APIs > Copilot assistant:
Seller Copilot APIs

Mindtickle Seller Copilot APIs let you embed our AI-powered assistant directly into your own applications, chatbots, or AI workflows. Built on RESTful architecture and the OpenAPI Specification (OAS), these APIs are accessible via standard HTTP requests and work in any environment that supports HTTP.

Use the Authentication API to generate access tokens and the Chat API to send prompts and receive streaming responses with context retention and content links. All interactions respect Mindtickle’s existing permissions and access controls.

You can query modules, assets, and Call AI calls — getting instant answers for pre-call prep, post-call follow-ups, product questions, and more. Built-in rate limits and error handling ensure the APIs are production-ready and scalable across your sales enablement stack.

Beyond its traditional role of delivering notifications and reminders, the app now supports interactive AI conversations with Seller Copilot.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Copilot > For learners:
Mindtickle Copilot is a generative AI productivity assistant. Copilot combines the power of enablement and revenue operations data with enterprise-ready generative AI so revenue teams can focus on their most important jobs — selling more and delighting customers.

Copilot provides various AI-powered features across the platform, including the ability to interact with Copilot in a chat interface for certain features. For example, chat with Copilot for answers and insights or automatically deliver results and insights via Copilot.

For more information on Copilot, see Copilot Overview.

Note:

- Copilot does not utilize OpenAI’s ChatGPT.
- While AI can speed up content generation, the quality and alignment with educational goals still need human oversight. AI is a tool to boost efficiency, not replace meticulous design. Admins must use their expertise to review and customize AI-generated content to ensure accuracy and alignment with learning objectives.

For questions around Copilot, see Mindtickle Copilot FAQs.

In Call AI, instead of going through the entire call recordings to find insights, just ask Copilot questions about the call recording. For example, Summarize this call for me in less than 200 words, What were the key topics discussed in this call, Which competitors were mentioned in the call, and so on. Copilot automatically delivers a response to the query.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Copilot > For learners > How Copilot works:
1. Navigate to the Recordings tab of Call AI Interface. Click a call listed under any of the following tabs or find a specific call using the search bar:

- My Recordings
- All Recordings
- Shared with me
- Bookmarked

2. On the call details page, click the Copilot widget.

3. The Copilot interface opens with a welcome message along with predefined examples.

4. If your question is similar to the predefined examples, directly select the example and click the Send icon.

5. If your question is not listed in the predefined prompts, enter your question in the Type here box and click the Send icon.

6. Copilot goes through the recording transcript for context to fetch the information for the query.

7. Based on the transcript, Copilot responds to the query.

Note: If the question is outside the transcript context, Copilot cannot provide a suitable response.

- When you ask follow-up questions in Copilot, Copilot keeps a record of the last 5 questions in context to respond to the follow-up questions.
- If you accidentally close the Copilot interface, Copilot still retains the context of the conversation. For example, if you navigate to another section on the same page, like Themes , Stats , Coach , Action items , or Key moments , and return to the Copilot interface. In that case, you can continue the conversation from where it was left.
- If you refresh the page, the content of the conversation is not stored. You need to start a new conversation.
- For information on Copilot capabilities, click Summary , Action items , and Key moments .

Note:

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Copilot > For admins:
Creating missions with role-play scenarios for sales representatives can be quite time-consuming and manual. This typically consists of the enablement admin outlining detailed situations for reps to practice their skills. However, Mindtickle Copilot presents a solution that expedites this process. This innovative approach substantially reduces the sales enablement team's manual workload and time investment. It allows them to kickstart the training process promptly. After Copilot generates the initial content, the admin can take over to review, make changes, incorporate additional reviewers, and finalize other relevant details before the mission is published.

Copilot is a tool to boost efficiency, not replace meticulous design. Admins must use their expertise to review and customize the Copilot-generated content to ensure accuracy and alignment with learning objectives.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Copilot > For admins > To create a mission:
1. From the admin site home page, click Training > Modules > Create modules.

Alternatively, you can create a mission from within a series by clicking Training > Series > select the required series > Create module.

Or click Training > Series > Create > Module.

2. On the Add modules pop-up, hover over the Mission tile and click Create mission.Note: If you have enabled Mindtickle Copilot for your site, you can see the Create with AI Assistance tag in the Mission tile.

3. On the Create new mission pop-up, click the Use Mindtickle Copilot option.

4. On the Mindtickle Copilot pop-up, click Start building with Copilot option.Note: As you have clicked Add Modules from within a series (see step 1), the series name is automatically added. Alternatively, if you click the Create new option, you have to select the series from the drop-down list.

5. The Copilot pop-up will prompt you for details to create a mission. You can choose the existing example scenario or provide a custom scenario to create a mission.

Example: We have selected the example Video roleplay for objection handling option and then pressed enter. The Copilot has generated a mission summary with Name, Type, Description, Evaluation parameters, Cut-off score, and Passing Certificate.

Here are a few example scenarios that you can provide to create a mission:

Example 1: Craft a convincing 30-second pitch for our latest product to a potential client you've unexpectedly met in an elevator.

Example 2: Role-play a scenario where a potential customer is resistant due to perceived high cost, and you have to negotiate to alleviate their concerns while driving towards a profitable deal.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Copilot > For reviewers:
Constructive feedback plays a pivotal role in honing skills for revenue-facing teams. Sales reps can leverage Mindtickle’s missions capability to practice their skills and get valuable feedback to refine their techniques, leading to improved sales performance. Our existing approach involves reviews as the primary means of providing feedback to reps. Helping reps practice and giving feedback at scale is becoming increasingly important; however, this is hindered by the significant time investment needed by managers or other reviewers.

Introducing Mindtickle’s Copilot as an automated reviewer for role-play submissions enabling easy practice at scale while ensuring managers can focus their attention on providing feedback, especially where it’s needed.

The Copilot evaluates the submission, scenario, and evaluation criteria upon submitting a mission. The Copilot-generated feedback encompasses both qualitative insights and quantitative scores, thereby furnishing sales reps with a comprehensive understanding of their performance.

By implementing Mindtickle Copilot, we aim to enhance the feedback experience, expedite skill development, and enable our customers to harness the full potential of our mission capabilities, all while minimizing the constraints posed by time-intensive manual reviews.

This article discusses adding Mindtickle Copilot as an additional reviewer for your missions.

Note:

- Mindtickle Copilot is a beta feature and is available only on request. To enable it for your site, contact Mindtickle Suppor t or your Customer Success Manager (CSM).
- The Mindtickle Copilot for reviewing missions feature is supported on the web and mobile.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Copilot > For reviewers > Copilot generated evaluation parameters guidance for reviewer:
Click the Generate guidance option to automatically generate tuned parameter guidance by analyzing the mission scenario, parameter name, parameter type, and details (such as the question type, like Rating scale and Multiple choice).

The Generate guidance improves the accuracy and fairness of learner evaluations by:

- Ensuring consistent scoring with minimal variation.
- Differentiating clearly between good, average, and poor submissions.

For Multiple-choice questions, the guidance is tuned to describe the criterion for selecting one of the choices or provide relevant context for choice selection. The Generate guidance option is available for Video roleplay, Email and task evaluation, and Voice-over slideshow mission formats, and can also be used with the Copilot reviewer.

You can click Improve guidance to generate custom guidance based on your requirements. The Improve guidance would use the previously available guidance as additional context input, along with the parameter name, parameter configurations (such as the question type, like Rating scale and Multiple choice), to tune the guidance definition further. When you select the Improve guidance option, a pop-up appears with suggested prompts. You can choose one of the available suggestions or enter your own prompt based on your specific requirement.

Use the Undo option to revert to the previous generated guidance.

While the guidance is being generated, you can click on Stop generating to stop the guidance generation.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Copilot > For reviewers > To appoint reviewers for a mission > Reviewer appointment:
You can appoint a reviewer to a mission in four ways.

1. Appoint reviewer manually for each learner
2. Appoint manager as reviewers
3. Appoint a common reviewer for all learners
4. Appoint AI as reviewer for all learners (Copilot)

Note: You can see the Copilot option only if you have enabled Mindtickle Copilot for your site. For more information, contact Mindtickle Support or your Customer Success Manager (CSM).

Click +Add Another Reviewer to add multiple reviewers. You can add up to five Reviewers to a learner.Note: If Copilot is appointed as a reviewer for the mission, you can set the Copilot scoring moderation to Relaxed, Moderate, or Critical by clicking on the option.

Here are the explanations for each moderation method:

- Moderate: This default behavior tends to provide a balanced review for user submission.
- Relaxed: The Copilot reviewer grades the learner's submission leniently.
- Critical: The Copilot reviewer grades learner submissions in a stringent manner.

Note: The scoring mode is available only for the one-way mission.

If admins have appointed Copilot as a reviewer for Email and Task Evaluation missions:

- If the description is less than 200 characters, a warning notification is displayed. Admins must provide a detailed description for all mission types so the Copilot can perform a comprehensive review.
- Learners can only submit up to 3 attachments with their submissions.
- Learners must upload files with the following extension: ' .flv ,' ' .mp4 ', ' .avi ,' ' .wmv, ' ' .mov, ' ' .mkv ,' ' .m4v ', '. mpg ,' '. mpeg ,' '. vob ,' '. webm ,' '. pdf ,' '. doc ,' ' .ppt ,' '. docx ,' ' .pptx ,' ' .xls ,' ' .xlsx ,' ' .mp3 ', ' .wav '.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Best Practices and Use Cases > Best Practices for DSR > DSR features:
Here's how you can use Mindtickle's DSR to create a customized buying experience:

- Mutual action plans: DSR collaborates with prospects and customers to set specific milestones and track progress throughout their journey. This collaborative approach allows you to align with the customer’s goals and can proactively address any roadblocks.
- Frictionless content sharing: DSR eliminates the friction and knowledge silos associated with one-on-one content sharing. You can share materials with multiple stakeholders simultaneously, ensuring everyone can access the latest information.
- Access for all collaborators: Provide access to all involved collaborators, including managers, engineers, subject matter experts (SMEs), and more. This inclusivity allows you to tap into the expertise of your entire team to address customer needs comprehensively.
- Static, shareable URLs: Maintain a static, shareable URL for all buyer stakeholders, whether old contacts or new prospects. This static URL ensures that everyone stays up to date and has a consistent source of information.
- Granular engagement insights: DSR provides sales reps with detailed engagement insights asset-by-asset. Reps can see how prospects and customers interact with the content, helping them further tailor their approach.
- DSR-CRM integrations: This allows sellers to add their Salesforce (or other CRM) opportunity and associated contacts to a DSR with a single click. DSRs also automatically write room activity to the Salesforce opportunity, account, and contact.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Copilot > For learners:
Mindtickle Copilot helps sales reps quickly draft personalized, high-impact emails when sharing assets via email with customers or prospects in the following ways:

- D irectly from the Mindtickle platform (covered in this article)
- Through Mindtickle Gmail extension ( help article )
- Through Mindtickle Outlook add-in ( help article )

In each case, Copilot leverages generative AI to craft relevant, impactful email drafts tailored to the recipient and the shared asset. This allows reps to communicate more efficiently and effectively, saving time while ensuring consistency, professionalism, and personalization in every message.

For more information, see Mindtickle Copilot overview and Mindtickle Copilot frequently asked questions (FAQs).

Mindtickle Copilot is built on secure, enterprise-grade large language models, including GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 (via Microsoft Azure OpenAI Service) and Claude Haiku and Sonnet (via Amazon Bedrock). It does not use OpenAI’s public ChatGPT. All Copilot features are developed with robust security and privacy and operate within Mindtickle’s SOC 2 Type II and GDPR-compliant infrastructure.

On Copilot accuracy

Mindtickle Copilot leverages generative AI to provide helpful responses and insights. However, it may sometimes produce information that is inaccurate or incomplete. While Copilot enhances productivity and efficiency, it is not a replacement for human judgment. Always review and verify its output to ensure it is accurate, complete, and relevant.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Copilot > For learners > Benefits:
Mindtickle Copilot represents a significant advancement in customer-facing communication. This innovative AI-based technology is poised to revolutionize how sales reps engage with customers and prospects through emails. By leveraging Mindtickle Copilot, reps can enhance their ability to craft compelling emails for various scenarios. Some of the key benefits of leveraging Mindtickle Copilot in drafting emails while sharing assets:

- Tailored and impactful emails: Reps can provide specific prompts to generate email drafts tailored to the needs of individual customers and prospects. Mindtickle Copilot's adaptability enables reps to address various scenarios, ensuring that each email is relevant, informative, and engaging. Contextually relevant emails contribute to enhanced customer satisfaction and loyalty.
- Effortless customization: Reps can iteratively refine and edit AI-generated email drafts to infuse their unique voice, style, and context into each communication. This customization maintains a personal touch while benefiting from AI-generated insights.
- Faster response and outreach: Reps can quickly draft high-quality emails, enabling prompt responses and proactive outreach. Once the prompts are submitted, Mindtickle Copilot generates an initial email draft based on the provided information. Reps can review this draft, considering its tone, content, and relevance to the communication goal.
- Consistency in brand messaging: Reps can adhere to brand guidelines and messaging standards, creating a unified and professional customer experience.
- Driving deal success: Reps can confidently communicate the value of offerings, address objections, and guide prospects through decision-making.

If you want to leverage Copilot, follow the steps provided in this article. If you prefer to write and compose your email without using the AI-based Copilot, follow the steps in Share Assets via Email.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Copilot > For learners > Share assets:
- Sent from : Enter your official email address to send and receive emails directly to your inbox. Note : Asset Hub supports multiple email clients, such as Gmail, Outlook, and Yahoo. For more information on authorizing your email address, see Share Assets via Email .
- Send to : Enter the recipient’s email address using the following 2 options:
  - Send separate emails to each recipient (recommended): This option helps track each recipient's activity.
  - Send one email to all recipients : This option does not allow you to track each recipient’s activity separately. Note : You can email a maximum of 20 recipients at a time.
- Subject : Enter the subject line of the email.
- Email message : Enter the message you want to send to the recipients. You can choose from the following 2 options:
- Write with Mindtickle Copilot : This option helps you to compose your email using Copilot. To use the AI-based Copilot, see the Draft email with Mindtickle Copilot section below.
- Enter email message : This option allows you to write your email in a freeform text field where you can insert as much text as you want and add supporting links.
- Email signature: Enter a default signature for all outgoing emails, including your name, contact information, or brand image.
- Recipient activity notifications: Turn on the setting if you want to be notified via email whenever a recipient interacts with the shared assets. It has the following 3 options:
  - Notify me when the recipient engages with the assets along with the engagement summary
  - Notify me when the recipient shares assets with their peers
  - Notify when a recipient is active
- Reminder notifications: Turn on the setting if you want to set an email reminder to check the engagement on shared assets. It has the following 2 options:
- Remind to check engagement data
- Remind only if there is no activity
- Allow download: Turn on the setting if you want recipients to download the shared assets to their local machine. The option to download is unavailable for embedded assets (for example, a youtube video embedded link).
- Access expiration: Configure the setting if you want the recipient’s access to expire for the shared assets after the set time (for example, renewals, contracts, and licenses). It ensures that the recipients always access the latest and most relevant content.
- Add internal notes (optional): Use the section as your notetaker to jot down the ideas or thoughts about sharing the assets. It helps you remember why you shared these assets with the customer or prospect in the later stages of the sales cycle.
- Email preview: View a glimpse of the entire email before sending it to the customers or prospects. It helps correct any apparent mistakes upfront and ensures the quality of your emails.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Copilot > For learners > Draft emails using Copilot:
1. On the Share assets via email pop-up window, click the icon available under the Email message section and next to Write with Mindtickle Copilot . The section expands, allowing you to write your prompt and provide instructions to the AI-based Copilot. You can click the icon to minimize the section. Note : The Copilot recognizes and addresses you in the highlighted section. It prompts you to get started with the drafting of the email for a specific scenario.
2. You can use one of the sample prompts available to provide instructions to the Copilot. The corresponding instructions are displayed in the text input (typing) field. Let’s say you want to draft an email to share two assets with your customer or prospect who has raised objections about your offerings regarding capabilities, pricing, or time to delivery. In that case, you can select the Objection handling sample prompt. Note : The sample prompts are static. You can select only one sample prompt at a time.
3. You can also write your prompt to provide instructions to the Copilot. Once entered, click the icon to submit the prompt. Note : When you submit your prompt, the platform ensures to pass the following instructions of its own:
  - Name of the assets, if any assets are attached to the email
  - Email subject, if any
  - Instruct the AI tool to only respond with email drafts as responses and not respond to general queries (as the flow intends to help you draft emails for a specific scenario).
4. Copilot displays a suggestive draft for the email. The Copilot uses the prompt to generate an initial email draft, which you can further review, customize, and send to the potential customer. If you are satisfied with the draft text, click the Use draft and edit button to proceed. Otherwise, you can refine the email draft by providing secondary prompts, as shown below. Let’s say you want to shorten the draft. In that case, you can click the Shorten prompt. Note : The secondary prompts are static and can be used to customize your email draft further.
5. Select a secondary prompt or enter your text based on your requirement to customize the draft according to your specific need. The Copilot generates a draft based on your prompt. Once submitted, Copilot uses the prompt to generate the second email draft, which you can further review and customize. You can continue to submit your prompt iteratively unless you are satisfied with the draft. Click the Use draft and edit button to proceed. Note : You can keep regenerating the responses until you reach a version of the email draft that you think is best for the provided scenario.
6. The section below displays the selected draft content. You can further edit and customize the content based on your requirements. Additionally, you can edit the receiver details and your signature. Once satisfied with your email content, click Send to share the assets via email.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Best Practices and Use Cases > Best Practices for Asset Hub > User Groups:
A group is a set of users filtered and categorized based on their profile fields, such as location, department, or hiring date..Groups are used to assign to hubs so that learners can access the hub and its content. If you have multiple learner audiences in your organization. In that case, you will likely have hubs that contain assets that pertain to particular groups of learners.

1. Define a clear and logical group structure: Plan and design the group structure based on your organization's sales process, product lines, target audience, or other relevant criteria.
  1. These can also be done through profile fields like region, job title, business units, geos, etc.
2. Keep it simple and intuitive: Avoid overly complex group structures. Ensure that sales reps can easily navigate and locate the desired content.
3. Consider permissions and access: Assign appropriate permissions to groups based on the intended audience. Ensure that sensitive or restricted content is accessible only to authorized users.
  1. Group structure:
    1. Region: Americas, Europe, Asia-Pacific
    2. Product Lines: Software, Hardware, Services
  2. Group Names:
    1. Americas -> Software -> Prospecting
    2. Europe -> Hardware -> Proposal
    3. Asia-Pacific -> Services -> Closing
    4. Americas -> Client servicing
    5. Europe -> Account manager

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Best Practices and Use Cases > Best Practices for Asset Hub > Naming Convention for Collateral:
Naming conventions help guide content curators, give clear direction to sellers, and help with search results.

1. Consistency is key : Establish a consistent naming convention across all collaterals to ensure easy identification and searchability.
2. Include relevant information : Use descriptive and meaningful names that convey the collateral's purpose, type, and target audience. Include key details such as product name, version, language, or format (e.g., brochure, presentation, case study).
3. Use a standardized format : Define a specific format or structure for the names, such as starting with the product name, followed by the type, and ending with the version number.
  1. Descriptive Names :
    1. Brochure_v2_ProductName
    2. CaseStudy_CustomerName
    3. Presentation_ProductX_Overview
  2. Standardized Format :
    1. [CollateralType][VersionNumber][ProductName]
    2. AviatoSoftware_Brochure
    3. [Product / Solution Name] [Content Type]
    4. Webinar: [Webinar Name] Recording OR [Webinar Name] Slides
4. Avoid using
  1. Dates (exceptions for market reports & newsletters)
  2. Over capitalization
  3. Extra punctuation (brackets, parentheses, hyphens, commas)
  4. Lengthy titles (shorten titles if needed, long titles do not appear well in search results)

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Best Practices and Use Cases > Best Practices for Asset Hub > Descriptions:
1. Descriptions should be kept to 1-2 sentences and written in a manner that is appropriate for sellers to read (especially if it is for client-facing assets).
2. Include keywords that are not included in the asset title, as they will influence the user's search returns.
3. For some content types, descriptions should include date or year (ex: letters, emails, newsletters, webinars, market reports) so the user knows the recency of the asset.
4. While designing the description, the field supports rich text, which means you can also format sentences/words with bold, italic, and text size. The description can also host links if required.
5. Provide Context and Positioning:
  1. Describe how the collateral fits into the sales process or buyer's journey.
  2. Explain how sales reps can effectively use it to address customer pain points or objections.
6. Include Call-to-Action (CTA):
  1. Encourage sales reps to take action by mentioning what they can do with the collateral.
  2. For example, "Use this presentation to showcase our latest features and benefits to prospects."
7. Update Descriptions Regularly:
  1. Assign an owner or content administrator responsible for reviewing and updating collateral descriptions whenever there are version changes.
  2. Ensure the descriptions reflect any updates or changes to the content or messaging.
8. Maintain Consistency:
  1. Establish a consistent format and tone for collateral descriptions.
  2. Align descriptions with the overall branding and messaging guidelines of your organization.

These guidelines are intended to help you create compelling and informative descriptions for collaterals. Adapt them based on your specific content and target audience to ensure the descriptions accurately represent the value and relevance of the assets in Asset Hub.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Best Practices and Use Cases > Best Practices for Asset Hub > Expiration Dates for assets:
1. Set realistic expiration dates : Determine a reasonable timeframe for the relevance of each collateral based on its content type, industry trends, product lifecycle, or any other relevant factors.
2. Regularly review and update expiration dates : Assign an owner or team responsible for periodically reviewing and updating the expiration dates to ensure the content remains up-to-date and relevant.
3. Configure the platform to send notifications to content owners or administrators before the expiry dates, prompting them to review and update the content or determine its retirement.
4. Realistic Expiration Dates:
  1. Brochures: 12 months from creation date
  2. Presentations: 6 months from creation date
  3. Case studies: 18 months from creation date,
5. Review and Update:
  1. Assign a quarterly review to the marketing team to update expiration dates based on content relevance and feedback from sales reps.
6. Notifications or Reminders:
  1. Configure the platform to send a reminder to content owners days before the expiration date, prompting them to review and update the collateral or retire it.
    1. There are three configurations for the expiry date
      1. On the day of expiry
      2. Seven days before expiry
      3. 15 days before expiry

1. Content-Type:
  1. Categorize the collaterals based on their type, such as brochures, case studies, presentations, videos, whitepapers, etc. This allows users to filter and search for specific types of content.
2. Product/Service:
  1. Assign each collateral's relevant product or service category to ensure it is associated with the correct offering. This helps users find content specific to the products or services they are focused on.
3. Industry/Vertical:
  1. Tag the collaterals with the relevant industry or vertical to enable filtering by industry. This helps users find content tailored to specific industries or vertical markets.
4. Target Audience:
  1. Specify the intended audience for each collateral, such as prospects, existing customers, decision-makers, technical users, etc. This allows users to search for content relevant to their specific audience.
5. Sales Stage:
  1. Identify the stage of the sales process or buyer's journey for which the collateral is most suitable, such as prospecting, qualifying, presenting, closing, etc. This helps users find content aligned with their current sales stage.
6. Language:
  1. If your organization operates in multiple languages, include a language attribute to allow users to filter content by language preference.
7. Version Number:
  1. Assign a version number to collaterals that undergo updates or revisions, allowing users to differentiate between different versions of the same collateral.
