chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Best Practices and Use Cases > Best Practices for Asset Hub > Ownership:
1. Sales Enablement Manager/Team :
  1. Overall ownership of the sales content management process and strategy.
  2. Defining the organization's sales content management goals and objectives.
  3. Managing the implementation and administration of Asset Hub.
  4. Collaborating with marketing, sales, and other teams to ensure alignment and effective use of the platform.
  5. Monitoring and measuring the performance and usage of the Asset Hub.
  6. Providing training and support to sales reps on navigating and utilizing the platform effectively.
  7. Overseeing content creation, organization, and updates in the Asset Hub.
  8. Establishing and enforcing best practices for content naming, categorization, and expiration dates.
  9. Conduct regular audits to ensure content relevance and accuracy.

  1. Collaborating with the sales enablement team to develop and maintain a centralized content repository within Asset Hub.
  2. Creating and updating marketing collaterals, such as brochures, presentations, case studies, and industry reports.
  3. Applying branding guidelines and ensuring consistency across all marketing materials.
  4. Uploading and organizing marketing content in the appropriate groups and categories within the Asset Hub.
  5. Collaborating with the sales team to gather feedback and insights on the effectiveness of the collaterals.

  1. Providing guidance to sales reps on using the Asset Hub effectively.
  2. Ensuring that the sales team is trained on accessing and utilizing the relevant content in the platform.
  3. Monitoring the usage and adoption of the Asset Hub within their respective teams.
  4. Providing feedback to the sales enablement team and marketing team regarding the usability and effectiveness of the content.
  5. Encouraging and reinforcing the use of the Asset Hub as a central resource for sales content.
4. Sales Representatives :
  1. Actively using Asset Hub to access the latest sales collateral and content.
  2. Providing feedback on the content's relevance, usefulness, and effectiveness.
  3. Suggesting updates or additions to the content library based on customer needs and market trends.
  4. Adhering to the established best practices for content management, including naming conventions and expiration dates.
  5. Collaborating with the sales enablement and marketing teams to ensure the content meets their specific needs.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Best Practices and Use Cases > Best Practices for Asset Hub > Engagement with Sales Team:
In addition to the quantitative, data-driven content analysis we gain from Mindtickle through reporting dashboards, engaging with your sales teams for qualitative real-time feedback on content pieces available in Mindtickle is equally important. Mindtickle users can engage with content pieces and may ask for clarification and corrections or even guide content creation with ideas generated from customer inquiries. When a user comments on their owned content items, it is advised that they respond to questions/comments within 72 hours to ensure relevancy, timeliness, and a good user experience. This feedback can help drive content updates or new content pieces to be created.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Best Practices and Use Cases > Best Practices for Call AI > Challenges addressed by Call AI:
Traditionally, organizations relied on the top 20% of their sales reps to close most deals while hoping for the best from the remaining reps. However, this approach creates a lose-lose situation: most reps struggle to achieve success, and sales managers find it challenging to help them meet quotas.

Recently, sales professionals have recognized that the 80-20% rule is no longer scalable. Instead, the focus has shifted toward elevating the entire team’s performance rather than relying solely on a small percentage of top performers1. Organizations can bridge these gaps and drive collective success by leveraging conversation intelligence.

chunks.headingPath: Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Digital Sales Rooms > Integrate Digital Sales Rooms with Slack
chunks.title: Integrate Digital Sales Rooms with Slack

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Digital Sales Rooms > Integrate Digital Sales Rooms with Slack:
- Navigate to Organization Settings > Integrations > Alerts .
- Click Connect next to Slack to begin the authentication process. Note :
  - You can perform this action only if your role has the Manage DSR ( MANAGE_DIGITAL_SALES_ROOMS ) permission.
  - You must be the owner of the Slack workspace to make the connection.
  - If you are not logged into Slack, the system prompts you to log in and allow permissions. Select the Slack workspace you want to connect to and click Allow to authorize the access permissions. The Slack workspace is connected, and you are redirected to the Alerts tab on the Organization Settings page. If the connection is successful, the Connect button is replaced by the Configure button.
- Click Configure to set up the Slack alerts. In the Configure Slack Integration pop-up:
  - Use the Send notifications to dropdown to choose where you want to send the notifications (or as a direct message). Choose Individuals (Direct message) if you want the notifications to be sent to individuals as direct messages on Slack. Choose the channel from the dropdown list if you want the notifications to be sent in a specific Slack channel. Note : If you choose Individuals (Direct Message) , the room owner and collaborators receive the notifications. If you choose to send notifications to Individuals (Direct Message) , ensure your DSR account email matches your Slack account email and that you are the room’s owner or collaborator. Collaborators only get Slack notifications if they are also marked to receive emails.
  - Use the When dropdown to choose when you want the notifications to be sent to the selected individuals or channels. By default, all options are selected.
- Click Add More to set up additional notification configurations. For example, set up some alerts to go to a shared channel and then other alerts to individuals.
- Click Save Changes . Based on your selection, the notifications are sent to the individual or channel after the event. Note : The ‘visit DSR’ notifications are sent to the individual or channel ~ 3 minutes after the event. All other notifications are sent immediately. Reps receive Slack alerts when prospective buyers:
  - Visit a DSR Clicking View Stats redirects you to the Room Statistics page.
  - Share a DSR Clicking View Room Details redirects you to the room.
  - Initiate a chat in the DSR Clicking Reply redirects you to the message posted on the room’s Conversations tab, from where you can instantly reply to the message.
  - Reply to a chat in the DSR Clicking Reply redirects you to the response posted on the message in the room’s Conversations tab. Note : The DSR visitor must view a document, image, text, or link, or play the audio/video content in the DSR for at least a few seconds for the notification to be pushed. DSR waits 3 minutes before sending a notification after a room visit. This delay enables some activity in the room before a notification is sent, providing more useful analytics when the notification is viewed.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Digital Sales Rooms > Disconnect DSR - Slack Integration:
If you no longer wish to receive notifications, you can disconnect the Slack integration. You can disable notifications at the org level or at the room level.

To disable Slack notifications at the org level, navigate to the Alerts tab on the Integrations page under Organization Settings and click Disconnect next to Slack.

To disable notifications at the room level, navigate to Room Settings. Under Notifications, switch the Post to Slack when viewed toggle off and click Done.

This disables notifications for the room owner as well as collaborators.

To disable notifications only for the collaborators, ensure their role is set to Show Profile in Room. This disables all notifications (Slack and email) for collaborators, but has notifications enabled for room owner.

Note: For collaborators to receive Slack notifications, they must be marked as receiving emails

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Best Practices and Use Cases > Best Practices for Governance > What is governance?:
Governance or a governance model is a structured framework that outlines the policies, roles, responsibilities, guidelines, and decision-making processes necessary manage and oversee enablement within an organization. It provides a clear roadmap for how enablement programs are planned, developed, implemented, monitored, and evaluated. In other words, It is the blueprint that ensures your Mindtickle instance aligns with your strategic goals, remains secure, and operates efficiently.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Best Practices and Use Cases > Best Practices for Governance > Why is governance important?:
A well-implemented governance model improves the experience of everyone involved in the enablement experience. It ensures that your enablement programs are efficient, effective, and aligned with the organization's strategic objectives.

Enablement team

- Clarity in roles, responsibilities, and the process for how to develop and deploy relevant training for their audience.
- Governance streamlines administrative tasks, automates routine processes, and optimizes content management, saving time and resources.

Learners

- Consistent quality across programs in content, communications, and accessibility.
- A well-governed platform leads to a better user experience. Users can easily find content, have clear roles, and experience seamless onboarding.

Decision-makers

- Transparency and accountability in the management of the enablement initiatives.
- Confidence that their teams are getting the relevant training when they need it
- As your organization grows, governance models help adapt the Mindtickle platform to accommodate increased usage.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Best Practices and Use Cases > Best Practices for Governance > Define and implement a governance model > Leadership, oversight, and strategic alignment:
Establish an enablement governance committee or stakeholder team responsible for setting the strategic direction, approving resources/budgets, and ensuring alignment with your organization’s goals. Depending on the size of your organization, the team could be comprised of executive leadership from the areas you support and partner with, such as the CRO, Head of Revenue Operations, the CMO, and/or the CHRO. In larger organizations, the governance committee could include the heads of the departments you support directly, such as the head of sales, solution consulting, success, and services.

It’s essential to agree on the roles and responsibilities of the governance committee. Set up a regular cadence to meet with the team, agree on priorities, report on progress, and discuss obstacles you need help to overcome.

Work with your governance committee to align your enablement programs with your organization's strategic objectives, business goals, and team member development needs. This step can be integrated into the design process at the needs analysis stage.

See the Mindtickle Best Practice: Creating a Center of Excellence for Platform Governance (Templates) document below for Governance Alignment Templates with examples.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Best Practices and Use Cases > Best Practices for Governance > Define and implement a governance model > Program Development:
Create standards and guidelines for your enablement programs' design, development, deployment, and evaluation.

Define the process for designing, developing, and updating training programs, including links to tools, templates, methodologies, and best practices you want your teams to use.

Establish quality standards and mechanisms to monitor and evaluate training program effectiveness. Conduct regular assessments, gather feedback, and make improvements as needed.

Your standards and guidelines should include:

- How to define the learning objectives for the target audience
- The naming conventions to use to make the training easy to find
- Branding, look, and feel (standard templates for different types of content)
- Your tagging structure for tagging learning objects correctly
- An internal review process
- The content assignment process
- The maintenance process for reviewing content periodically for relevancy

See the Mindtickle Best Practice: Mindtickle Best Practice: Content Management and Assignment Guidelines - EXAMPLE document below for a customizable Template with examples.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Best Practices and Use Cases > Best Practices for Governance > Define and implement a governance model > Continuous Improvement:
Establish mechanisms for gathering feedback from learners, trainers, and other stakeholders to make necessary improvements, such as The Kirkpatrick Model. Foster a culture of continuous improvement by regularly reviewing and updating enablement programs to meet evolving business needs and industry trends.

You can use the following approaches in Mindtickle to collect feedback throughout and at the end of a program:

1. Use thumbs up/thumbs down on learning objects.
2. Include a short survey at the end of each section in a Series or at the end of the series, depending on the length.
3. Email an overall enablement survey periodically to see how perception is changing as our recommendations are implemented.

We recommend targeting 80% as a starting point and then moving the target up to 90% (4 or 5 on a 5-point scale) as recommendations are implemented.

A survey may be added as a learning object at the end of a course or quick update. You can embed a survey from an external tool, use a Google survey, or use Mindtickle’s poll and text feedback questions.

See the Mindtickle Best Practice: Define and Implement a Governance Model (Templates) document below for a Continuous Improvement template and examples.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Best Practices and Use Cases > Best Practices for Tags > Why use tags?:
Tags serve multiple purposes:

- Improve content discoverability : Tags help users easily locate relevant content through search and thematic categorization. This is especially valuable when your instance contains substantial content.
- Bring meaning to content : Tags provide context to your content, making it easier to understand the subject, intended audience, or purpose of a particular module, file, question, or poll.
- Enhance analytics : Tags allow you to filter and report on analytics data. You can track the performance of specific tag categories or assess how particular content types impact readiness.

- Enhance analytics : Tags allow you to filter and report on analytics data. You can track the performance of specific tag categories or assess how particular content types impact readiness.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Best Practices and Use Cases > Best Practices for Tags > Tagging best practices:
Let's explore best practices for tagging:

- Consistent tagging conventions : Establish clear and consistent tagging conventions across your organization. Ensure that everyone understands the purpose of tags and how they should be used.
- Use descriptive tags : Create tags that accurately describe the content. This makes it easier for users to understand the content's relevance and purpose.
- Avoid over-tagging : While tags are valuable, it's important not to over-tag content. Use only the tags that are most relevant tags to the content, avoiding redundancy.
- Limit the number of tags : Aim to keep the number of tags per content item manageable. Too many tags can overwhelm users and dilute the meaning of each tag.
- Regularly review and update tags : Periodically review your tags and their categories to ensure they remain relevant. Remove or update tags as needed to keep your tagging system effective.
- Educate users : Provide training and guidelines to users on how to use tags effectively. Encourage them to tag content appropriately to benefit the entire organization.
- Consider Readiness Index (RI) : Keep the RI in mind when tagging. Tags can impact readiness calculations, so make sure your tags align with your readiness assessment goals.
- Monitor analytics : Regularly use the analytics features in Mindtickle to track the performance of tagged content. This will help you identify trends and areas for improvement.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Best Practices and Use Cases > Best Practices for Driving Adoption > Introduction:
Driving adoption on Mindtickle involves a combination of strategies to attract, engage, and retain users. Here are some effective methods to achieve this:

1. Content Quality and Relevance

Ensure your training content is high-quality, up-to-date, and relevant to your target audience. Content that meets users' needs will keep them coming back for more. For best practices for creating engaging content, please see this related article. If you need help in developing your content, Mindtickle offers content as a Service & Success Accelerators. Please reach out to your Customer Success Manager for additional information.

2. User Onboarding

Create a smooth onboarding process that helps new users get started quickly. Mindtickle provides tutorials, guides, and introductory courses to help them understand how to use your platform effectively. In addition to these offerings, several Success Accelerator programs are available for administrators & end users.

3. Personalization

Implement personalization features that recommend courses or content based on a user's interests, previous interactions, or skill level. Personalization increases engagement by tailoring the experience to individual preferences. You can achieve personalization by leveraging a number of features like role-based Readiness Dashboards, Dynamic widgets and Series Overview pages.

4. Gamification

Gamify the learning experience by adding badges, points, leaderboards, and quests challenges. Gamification can make learning more fun and encourage users to return to earn rewards and compete with others.

5. Feedback and Communication

Allow users to provide feedback on modules and the platform itself. Encourage discussions, comments, and questions to foster a sense of community. Respond to user feedback promptly and make improvements accordingly. You can leverage the survey questions module & series level ratings to accomplish this.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Copilot > For admins:
With Mindtickle Copilot, our generative AI productivity assistant, you can build your assessments quickly with AI-generated questions based on topics of your choice. Copilot automates and streamlines various aspects of assessment creation, such as transcribing the base content, generating a wide variety of questions, and configuring selective assessment attributes, such as name, description, time limit, passing score, and certification. Thus significantly reducing the time and effort required to create assessments, allowing admins to focus on other important tasks. It also ensures that questions are accurately phrased, grammatically correct, and aligned with learning objectives. Using AI assistance to create assessments offers efficiency and scalability. However, human expertise is essential, and admins should carefully review and validate them to ensure accuracy, relevance, and alignment with learning objectives.

For more information, see Mindtickle Copilot overview and Mindtickle Copilot frequently asked questions (FAQs).

Note:

- Copilot is built on large language models — such as GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 (hosted on Microsoft’s Azure Open AI Service ) and Claude Haiku and Sonnet (hosted on AWS Bedrock ) — providing excellent security and privacy. It does not utilize OpenAI’s ChatGPT.
- Mindtickle Copilot is powered by generative AI and, while the content (responses, insights, and more) generated by Copilot is typically accurate, it can make mistakes and may not always provide accurate or complete information. Copilot helps boost efficiency and productivity but it is not a replacement or substitute for your teams. We recommend always reviewing and updating (where necessary) Copilot-generated content and responses so that it is accurate, complete, and relevant to your needs.
- Copilot can create Multiple Choice Questions (MCQs), Match the text label, and Text answer-based questions only. It cannot create image-based questions.
- For more information on how to create the assessment yourself from scratch, see Create an assessment.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Copilot > For admins > Copilot’s processing limit for assessment creation:
Copilot’s ability to create assessments from existing content depends on the content’s language complexity (short or long, technical terms) and the formatting (font size, line spacing, margins, inclusion of images, etc.).

Based on the complexity of the content, Copilot can process up to 192 to 384 (128,000 tokens) PDF pages. This is an approximate value.

The content processing logic for assessment creation depends on the following,

- Tokens to Words: Copilot converts approximately 0.75 words for 1 token (or 100 tokens ≈ 75 words). This conversion rate varies; in some cases, 1 word is about 1.3 tokens, or even 2-3 tokens for complex and other languages. Therefore, based on the existing conversion limits, assuming 0.75 words per token, 128,000 tokens×0.75 words/token = 96,000 words.
- Words per Page: This varies based on the page’s spacing and format.
  - A double-spaced page (manuscript) has 250 words (approximately).
  - A single-spaced page with standard formatting (e.g., 12pt font, 1-inch margins) has 500 words (approximately).
  - PDFs, academic papers, or technical documents with dense text, smaller fonts, or multiple columns have higher word counts.

The word-to-page conversion calculation for both double and single-spaced pages is as follows:

- Double-spaced pages (approx. 250 words/page): 96,000 words/250 words/page = 384 pages.
- Single-spaced pages (approx. 500 words/page): 96,000 words/500 words/page = 192 pages.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Copilot > For admins > Create an assessment using Copilot:
To create an assessment using Copilot:

1. On the admin site home page, click Training and click Modules.
2. On the Modules page, click Create module. Alternatively, on the series page, click Create and select Module.

3. On the Add module pop-up, hover over the Assessment tile and click Create assessment. 4. On the Create new assessment pop-up, click Use Mindtickle Copilot.

The Mindtickle Copilot chat window appears. It contains interactive elements you can use to engage with the AI-powered Copilot. In the chat window, specify your requirements to create the assessment in stages. For example, specify the destination series and assessment topic in the first stage. Note: If you exit the Copilot chat window anytime, you will lose all chat history from that instance.

5. Use the Select a Series dropdown to select the series you want to place the assessment in.

Note: If you start this process from a series, the series name is auto-populated. At this step, you can still choose to change the series in which you want the assessment to be created. Click the dropdown and select the new series.

6. [Optional] Select the base module. You can select multiple base modules for the assessment creation. Select the modules from the list and click Apply.

Note: To enable multi-selection of modules, contact your Customer Success Manager (CSM). Copilot evaluates the module/s content, comprehends its learning objectives, and understands what knowledge or skills learners are expected to acquire. This helps Copilot generate relevant and coherent questions that align with the content of the selected module/s. Note:

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Copilot > For admins > Create an assessment using Copilot:
- Copilot is capable of generating assessments independently. It can create assessments without the need to select a specific base module. In other words, Copilot can create assessments based on any topic and content not hosted within any Mindtickle module.
- Copilot is capable of comprehending content types limited to PDFs, PPTs, and videos.
  - Ensure the content within the base module is added in the supported type format. Content not available in the supported file formats is not transcripted and cannot be used by Copilot for assessment creation.
  - Ensure content transcription for PDF/PPT files is available and extractable. This is enabled by default for files uploaded after March 2021.
  - Ensure video transcription is enabled on your learning site. For more information, contact Mindtickle Support or your Customer Success Manager (CSM).
- Only course and quick-update module types can be selected as the base module.
- Only a published module can be selected as the base module.
- If the selected series does not have the supported base modules, the dropdown displays None as the only option.
- If Copilot cannot gather enough information from the module/s to generate the questions, the module remains disabled and cannot be selected for assessment creation.
  - Copilot’s question generation depends on whether the content is retrieved from the learning objects or files in modules.
  - For question generation, Copilot retrieves the text available in modules and transcribes the videos and PDFs in modules.
  - Copilot transcribing fails if a module contains PDFs with text that is not extractable.
  - Copilot cannot create questions if a module has insufficient text.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Best Practices and Use Cases > Best Practices for Enablement > 3. Gamification elements in Mindtickle:
- Progress and achievement : Reward small achievements throughout the learning journey. Use gamification elements in Courses and Quick Updates, such as learning objects that include quiz questions with assigned scoring and badges to acknowledge completion. Define mastery using Assessments and certifications throughout milestones in their learning path.
- Leveling up : Set incremental goals for learners. They must accomplish specific tasks before advancing to the next level or accessing additional content. Use the “sequentially locked” series setting to define learning paths that keep learners focussed and on track.
- Quests : Create and use Quests as spaced reinforcement to reinforce adult learners and ensure ROI of time spent creating and engaging in content.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Copilot > For admins > Artificial intelligence > What is artificial intelligence and machine learning?:
Artificial intelligence (AI) refers to computer programs that can learn and perform tasks typically requiring human intelligence. Including things like understanding language, recognizing patterns, analyzing data and making recommendations.

Machine learning (ML) is a subset of AI that automatically enables a machine or system to learn and improve from experience. Machine learning uses algorithms to analyze large amounts of data, learn from the insights, and then make informed decisions without human direction. ML aims to teach a machine how to perform a specific task and provide accurate results by identifying patterns.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Copilot > For admins > Artificial intelligence > What is generative AI?:
Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) is a specialized branch of AI that goes beyond recognizing patterns and making decisions. Unlike traditional AI systems that may just analyze and interpret information, generative AI takes an extra step: it creates something new.

Imagine having a conversation with a machine that not only understands what you're saying but can also respond with original thoughts, write a poem, or even create a piece of art. Generative AI can do just that, generating content like text, images, or videos based on the data it has learned from.

This technology offers a multitude of applications, from improving customer interactions by providing more personalized responses to aiding businesses in analyzing large quantities of data more creatively. It's a more advanced form of AI, unlocking possibilities that extend far beyond what traditional AI systems have offered.

This is how generative AI models work: you enter a prompt to which the models respond with text, images, videos, code, and more. After an initial response, you can also customize the results with feedback about the style, tone and other elements you want the generated content to reflect.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Copilot > For admins > Artificial intelligence > What are large language models (LLMs)?:
A large language model (LLM) is a type of machine learning program that can perform a variety of natural language processing (NLP) tasks, such as generating and classifying text, answering questions in a conversational manner, and translating text from one language to another. LLMs are a type of generative AI that has been specifically architected to help generate text-based content in the form of natural-sounding language.

Mindtickle leverages LLM capabilities to offer a highly personalized and efficient sales enablement experience, empowering sales teams to perform at their best. Currently we leverage LLMs for content generation, sales coaching, knowledge retrieval, and performance analytics. For more information, see Leveraging LLM capabilities for Mindtickle Copilot.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Copilot > For admins > Artificial intelligence > How can AI help my go-to-market teams?:
AI technologies can help with account planning and research, increased personalization of content, automating repetitive tasks at scale, and more effective onboarding, training, and coaching.

AI can evaluate rep pitches at scale and provide unbiased and timely feedback on which sales reps are ready to pitch to prospects and which reps require more coaching and training. It can be used to personalize training programs based on the strengths and weaknesses of individual sellers. AI can automate the analysis of large amounts of sales data and provide insights into which strategies, processes and programs are most effective at driving sales revenue.

Example use cases where AI can help you focus on key tasks by doing some work for you:

- Enablement: Focus on high impact enablement planning, while AI helps with:
  - Specific guidance on program needs of your sales reps
  - Engaging content creation
- Sales reps: Focus on strategically executing opportunities, with AI assistance on:
  - Meeting prep
  - Deal navigation
  - Buyer engagement
- Sales Management: Focus on leading a team of quota achievers, while AI works on:
  - Team insights
  - Coaching recommendations

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Copilot > For admins > Mindtickle Copilot > What is Mindtickle Copilot? What AI technologies does it use?:
Mindtickle Copilot is a suite of generative AI capabilities purpose-built for sales, enablement, and revenue operations teams. Embedded in the sales workflow, it supports onboarding, training, deal coaching, and buyer engagement — providing guidance that accelerates pipeline growth, shortens ramp time, enhances coaching, and boosts quota attainment. By combining Mindtickle’s data with enterprise-grade AI, it helps teams stay focused on revenue-driving work: selling more and and delighting customers.

Copilot powers a wide range of AI-driven features across the Mindtickle platform, including mission creation and review, content and video generation, coaching feedback, call analysis, and chat-based guidance. These features support roles such as admins, sales reps, and managers, and are available via the admin site, learning site, mobile app, Salesforce, and APIs.

For all the Mindtickle Copilot AI features, we use the following large language models (LLMs) to provide you excellent security and privacy:

- Models such as Claude Haiku and Sonnet (hosted on Amazon Bedrock )
- Models such as GPT-3.5-turbo and GPT-4-turbo (hosted on Microsoft Azure OpenAI Service ) Note: Mindtickle Copilot does not utilize OpenAI’s ChatGPT.

This ensures our customers get the best performance and accuracy when using Mindtickle Copilot. By incorporating both Amazon Bedrock and Azure OpenAI models, we aim to provide a more robust and versatile AI infrastructure that ensures Mindtickle customers benefit from the best performance, accuracy, and adaptability, regardless of the scenario.

For a detailed list of all the processors and their locations, see the sub-processor repository. If you have any concerns or need further information, contact your CSM.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Copilot > For admins > Mindtickle Copilot > Is Copilot and your use of generative AI secure?:
We take a security-first approach to incorporating AI into our offerings under Mindtickle Copilot. Unlike publicly available forms of generative AI like ChatGPT, Mindtickle’s Copilot was created for organizations with the highest levels of security, privacy, and compliance in mind.

Your data is safe

- Copilot is built on the large language models offered by Microsoft Azure OpenAI Service and Amazon Bedrock (AWS).
- Mindtickle’s implementation of Azure OpenAI and Amazon Bedrock models will not learn from or share customer data across instances.
- Additional information will not be fetched to enrich users’ personal information or to identify additional information about an individual.
- Customers’ confidential or personal information is never permanently stored with Azure OpenAI, Amazon Bedrock, or any other machine learning systems.
- Mindtickle has opted out of sharing customer information for training or improving the models, even in the pseudonymized or anonymized form.

Copilot is compliant with global privacy laws

- Mindtickle’s implementation of Azure OpenAI and Amazon Bedrock models is compliant with global privacy laws — personal information is used only where we have the legal basis for processing that information.

Mindtickle Copilot is powered by generative AI and, while the content (responses, insights, and more) generated by Copilot is typically accurate, it can make mistakes and may not always provide accurate or complete information.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Copilot > For admins > Mindtickle Copilot > What is the difference between Copilot and ChatGPT?:
ChatGPT is a product from OpenAI that is built for consumers. Data entered into ChatGPT can and may be used to train future LLM models from OpenAI. Consequently it is not safe to enter confidential business data into ChatGPT.

Mindtickle’s Copilot is built on large language models offered by Azure OpenAI and Amazon Bedrock, that provide the greatest security and privacy. Copilot does not use data entered into it for improving the models nor does it share data across customer instances.

Note: Copilot does NOT utilize OpenAI’s ChatGPT.

The Azure OpenAI and Amazon Bedrock gives customers advanced language models with the security and enterprise promise of Microsoft and AWS. Azure OpenAI and Amazon Bedrock co-develop the APIs with their respective AI model providers, ensuring compatibility and a smooth transition from one to the other.

With Azure OpenAI and Amazon Bedrock, customers get the security layer of Microsoft and AWS with the capability of various AI models.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Copilot > For admins > Mindtickle Copilot > Do you store or share customer data for training and improving Copilot?:
No, neither Mindtickle nor Azure OpenAI and Amazon Bedrock language models behind Copilot will store, use, or share personal identifiable information (PII), customer data for training or improving Copilot or the underlying language models. Your data will never be used to contribute to Azure OpenAI and Amazon Bedrock's knowledge base.

Azure OpenAI and Amazon Bedrock have temporary access to only relevant extracted data required for processing the request. Depending on the Copilot features leveraged by you, Mindtickle may require sharing metadata/content of learning objects, sales assets, or snippets of call transcripts. In most cases, this data may have personal information that is unstructured and fragmented, and it may or may not identify an individual.

Additionally, we do not share any customer user IP addresses with Azure OpenAI and Amazon Bedrock. Azure OpenAI and Amazon Bedrock requests are made directly from Mindtickle servers and do not contain customer or user IP addresses.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Copilot > For admins > Mindtickle Copilot > How do I share feedback on content generated by Copilot?:
Your feedback and suggestions are valuable in helping us continuously enhance Copilot. We will ensure to address errors or any problematic content that may arise from using our AI technology, by way of your feedback and through rigorous testing by our teams. We strive to curate the language models behind Copilot and ensure they are accurate and align with Mindtickle’s principles of responsible and ethical AI.

With this aim, we have implemented a feedback mechanism directly within Copilot. Hover over any response from Copilot to view the two options for feedback:

- Thumbs up: Positive feedback; the Copilot response was helpful.
- Thumbs down: Constructive feedback; the Copilot response was not helpful.

Furthermore, for the thumbs down option, you can write additional comments and select the following applicable options to help us categorize your feedback and address it swiftly:

Response is not accurateResponse is not completeResponse is harmful/unsafe

Like always, you can also provide your feedback to your CSM or Mindtickle Support.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Copilot > For admins > Subprocessor controls > Have you signed data processing and transfer agreements (DPA and SCC) with AWS and Microsoft?:
Yes. We have signed a Data Processing Addendum (DPA) containing Standard Contractual Clauses (SCC) with AWS and Microsoft.

- A Data Processing Agreement (DPA) is a contract between a data controller and a data processor that describes the roles and responsibilities of the parties when personal data is processed. A DPA must satisfy a number of requirements in order to be compliant with data privacy laws, including the EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR).
- The Standard Contractual Clauses (SCC) are a data transfer mechanism issued by the European Commission that are used for the transfer of personal data from the EEA and Switzerland. The SCC are required by the GDPR for transfers of personal data to certain countries, including the United States.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Best Practices and Use Cases > Best Practices for Content Center > Create an Appropriate Folder Structure:
An organized folder structure is the backbone of efficient content management, making locating and accessing resources easy.

In this section, we'll explore how to create a logical and user-friendly folder structure to keep your content well-organized and readily accessible.

- Establish a well-organized folder structure within your Content Center. Dividing your Content Center into main categories, such as "Training Materials," "Documentation," "Sales Resources," and "Marketing Collateral."
- Categorize content into relevant folders to facilitate easy access and retrieval. Within each main category, use subfolders for further organization. For example, under "Training Materials," you can have subfolders like "Onboarding," "Advanced Training," and "Compliance."
- Ensure clear and intuitive naming conventions for folders and content items. Ensure folders and files have clear, consistent naming conventions. For instance, use YYYY-MM-DD for dated content, and include keywords describing the content's purpose.

Regular content review ensures that outdated or irrelevant materials do not clutter your repository, maintaining content freshness.

Discover how to establish review schedules, assign ownership, and set criteria for archiving content, ensuring your repository remains up-to-date.

- Review content every six months or as needed based on content type and relevance.
- Assign content owners who are responsible for initiating the review process.
- Implement a systematic archiving process for expired or obsolete content to declutter the repository.

Efficient content categorization and tagging are essential to help users quickly locate relevant resources within your Content Center. Without proper categorization, content can become disorganized and challenging to navigate.

In this area, you'll learn how to structure your content library effectively through categorization and tagging. By assigning appropriate categories and tags to content items, you make it easier for users to find what they need, improving their overall experience.

- Consistent tagging : Use standardized tags that describe content attributes consistently.
- User feedback : Encourage users to suggest tags or categories to continuously improve content organization. See the MindTickle Best Practice: Tagging Best Practices document for examples and details on using Tags

Analytics and reporting provide valuable insights into how users interact with your content, helping you make data-driven decisions, optimize content, and measure the impact of your resources.

This section explores analytics and reporting for your Content Center. You'll gain insights into user behavior, content performance, and engagement metrics.

- Key metrics : Define key performance indicators (KPIs) relevant to your content goals, such as views, downloads, or completion rates.
- Regular reports : Schedule automated reports to inform stakeholders about content usage and effectiveness.
- A/B testing : Experiment with different content formats or structures and use A/B testing to measure their impact.
- Feedback loop : Use analytics to identify areas for content improvement, based on user behavior.
- Gather feedback : Survey learners, content creators and other stakeholders to make necessary improvements on how content is organized.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Best Practices and Use Cases > Best Practices for Enablement > Define Your Content Strategy:
Before you start adding content to your sales management platform, it's essential to have a clear content strategy in place. Consider the following:

- Target audience : Understand who will use the platform and tailor your content to their needs.
- Content types : Identify the types of content that will be most useful to your sales team, such as product information, sales collateral, training materials, or competitive intelligence. A mix of content is recommended for the best learner experience.
- Content sources : Determine where your content will come from, such as marketing, product development, or external sources.
- Content management : Define how content will be organized, updated, and accessed within the platform.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Best Practices and Use Cases > Best Practices for Enablement > Perform Content Audits:
Conduct periodic content audits to assess the relevance and effectiveness of the content within your sales management platform. During audits:

- Identify outdated content : Remove or update content that is no longer accurate or useful. It may vary by industry, but typically content that has not been accessed in 2 years will not be relevant.
- Analyze usage metrics : Examine which content is frequently accessed and rarely used. This helps you focus on what matters most to your sales team.
- User feedback : Collect feedback from your sales team to understand their content needs and preferences. Reach out to your Customer Success Manager (CSM) for more details on running a content audit

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Best Practices and Use Cases > Best Practices for Enablement > Key settings to keep content fresh and easy to Find in Mindtickle:
In a Mindtickle-powered sales management platform, there are key settings to pay attention to in order to maintain content freshness and accessibility. These settings include:

- Series name: Ensure that each series is appropriately named, making it easy for users to identify its purpose.
- Series description: Providing descriptive information about each series helps users understand its content and relevance.
- Series page (if applicable): If a series has a dedicated page, ensure it is updated and offers valuable information.
- Series certificate (if applicable): Update certificates to reflect the latest achievements or qualifications.
- Targeted audience: Confirm that the specified audience for each series is accurate and up-to-date.
- Public or assigned?: Clearly define whether a series is public or assigned and review access permissions accordingly.
- Module relevance: Required or Optional?: Indicate whether modules are mandatory or optional for users.
- Estimated time to complete (for Courses and Quick Updates): Keep estimated completion times accurate. This allows the learner to allocate the proper time for training and plan accordingly for longer training.
- Should this module be archived? If so, use Archival settings: Archive outdated content to prevent users from accessing irrelevant information.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Mobile App:
Whenever a new version of the app is available, you are notified through an in-app notification banner at the top of the Home tab. You can click the Update now button in the banner to directly go to the App Store or Play Store (depending on your device) and update the Mindtickle app. The banner ensures all users consistently update their app to the latest available version to enjoy all new features and improvements.

The banner is displayed only if you have not updated the app to the latest available version. The banner is automatically removed when you click Update now and update the app. It will show up again if the app update is not successful. You can also close the banner. If you do, it will not appear again until the next version of the app or 15 days after the last release, whichever is earlier.

This banner is also displayed under the Profile tab > Settings page. You cannot dismiss or close the banner. It gets removed only when you update the app, and shows up again if the app update is not successful.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Get Started with Mindtickle > Seller Intel (Beta) > About Seller Intel:
Sales leaders always face a challenge to meet sales targets. They have limited visibility into revenue attainment, and insights are only available after the quarter closes, lacking detailed analysis and leading indicators. This lack of granularity makes it challenging to distinguish high achievers from outliers who benefit from exceptional events, hindering consistent revenue attainment.

Moreover, while sales leaders have access to various performance tracking tools, there is a gap in comprehensive analytics to identify gaps in the go-to-market process and enhance overall sales productivity. Current solutions in the market often involve manual data collation and analysis, creating inefficiencies.

Mindtickle Seller Intel solves these challenges, offering a unique blend of real-time seller feedback and deal insights. This intelligent platform empowers Chief Revenue Officers (CROs) and sales leaders with actionable recommendations for success, bridging the gap between data and informed decision-making. It operates in three essential steps:

- Predicts revenue attainment potential for reps based on their historical and current performance.
- Provides in-depth insights into team and individual gaps in activities, behaviors, and skills compared to top performers.
- Recommends next-best actions for reps, sales leaders, and enablement teams to drive revenue attainment.

With Mindtickle Seller Intel, sales teams can excel and consistently surpass their goals, ensuring that your organization maximizes revenue achievement.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Get Started with Mindtickle > Seller Intel (Beta) > Seller Intel features:
1. Identify strengths and weaknesses: Seller Intel analyzes your team's performance to highlight strengths and areas of improvement. You can view the performance trends of individual sales reps or teams and understand how their strengths or weaknesses impact their sales results.
2. Predict quota attainment: Using a CRM data model, Seller Intel predicts the potential quota attainment of each sales representative and team. This insight can help you understand which team members are likely to meet their quotas and which ones might need extra support.
3. Analyze sales funnel: Seller Intel gives a detailed view of your sales funnel, including conversion rates at each stage. This analysis can help you identify where your funnel is leaking and take steps to improve conversion rates.
4. Uncover winning traits: Seller Intel analyzes successful deals to identify the traits that have the most significant impact on winning. These insights can help you understand what your top performers are doing right and share these best practices with the rest of your team.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Get Started with Mindtickle > Seller Intel (Beta) > Enable Seller Intel:
Seller Intel is currently in the beta phase and available only on request. To enable it for your learning site:

1. Contact your Customer Success Manager (CSM) or Mindtickle Support.
2. CSMs and the Seller Intel product teams conduct an initial call with you to understand your sales process and how data structure in Salesforce (SFDC):
  1. Understand sales stages.
  2. Map the key SFDC fields (if customers have used any custom fields). For more information, see Create an Integration User in Salesforce (SFDC).
  3. Understand the quota plan for the previous and current year for all reps.
3. Then, Mindtickle will provide you with a customized dashboard for Seller Intel.

Note: After completing all the necessary setup steps, it takes around two weeks to activate the product.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Get Started with Mindtickle > Seller Intel (Beta) > Home tab:
Here are all the details users with the HOS role can view on the Home tab, along with a brief explanation of the sections marked in the image above.

1. You can use the toggle on the upper-right corner to switch between light mode and dark- mode .
2. The name and designation of the logged-in user is displayed in the upper-left corner. You can use the down arrow option to view and search the dashboard for your reportee.
3. Rev Q score: This section shows your team's projected quota attainment for the fiscal year. It's calculated by analyzing various performance metrics from the past period (one or four quarters) across the sales funnel stages. Quota attainment is calculated by dividing revenue earned for completed quarters in the year by the targets for those quarters. For Q1, Seller Intel displays the quota attainment for the past year.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Get Started with Mindtickle > Seller Intel (Beta) > Seller performance insights > Managers:
All the managers reporting to the HOS are displayed on the graph under the Managers tab. The vertical axis represents the future quota potential, and the horizontal axis reflects year-to-date quota attainment.

Note: The cutoff value dividing the four quadrants is customized per your company's standards.

The graph future is divided into four quadrants:

1. High performers : These are all the managers reporting to the HOS who have a track record of consistently meeting or exceeding their sales targets in the past and are well-positioned to continue achieving high levels of quota fulfillment in the future.
2. High potential : These managers have underperformed recently, but there is a high chance of them improving their quota attainment in the future if they persist with and improve upon the main areas where they are lagging.
3. Needs development : These managers have a recent history of lower performance; there is a significant likelihood of them enhancing their quota achievement in the future if they are given continued support and work on improving the areas where they are currently falling short.
4. Outliers : These managers have performed admirably in meeting their quotas, but it is unlikely to keep on attaining higher quotas going forward. To ensure a sustained high level of quota attainment, they should focus on addressing their key areas of improvement.

Note:

- The bubbles on the graphs represent the team's size. Smaller bubbles represent smaller teams, and larger bubbles indicate larger teams.
- You can click the download icon on the top-right corner to download the graph and analysis for your presentation or share it with the team.
- The values displayed for the managers on the graph are the average value of all the reps reporting to the manager.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Get Started with Mindtickle > Seller Intel (Beta) > Analyze > Sales funnel:
The Sales funnel is divided into 5 stages:

| Stage | Explanation |
| --- | --- |
| Prospect | Prospect is the first stage in the sales process. It includes all the opportunities during the initial outreach, and the first call with the customer is set. |
| Qualify | Qualify is the second stage in the sales process. This is a discovery phase where the leads that match your target customers are qualified. |
| Prove | Prove is the third stage in the sales process. During this stage, the value proposition of the offering is established through demos and walkthroughs with key customer stakeholders. |
| Negotiate | Negotiate is the fourth stage in the sales process. During this stage, the pricing negotiation, due diligence, and contract finalization are carried out. |
| Closed | Closed is the fifth and final stage in the sales process. During this stage, an opportunity is completed and marked as closed won. |

When you click on any stage of the funnel, Seller Intel displays the following insights for each stage:

Identify top and bottom teams/reps for a stage

- First, Seller Intel identifies the key performance metric at each stage that significantly influences meeting your goals (as determined by your model).
- Next, Seller Intel identifies the top-performing reps or teams, those in the upper 25% bracket (above the 75th percentile) for that specific metric.
- Similarly, Seller Intel identifies the underperforming reps or teams in the lower 25% bracket (below the 25th percentile) for the same metric.

Identify the strengths of top teams/reps

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Get Started with Mindtickle > Seller Intel (Beta) > Analyze > Deal trends:
The Deal trends tab provides information on won deals, optimized deal types for reps, and new pipeline insights for the past four quarters.

The Won deal traits section lists all the key trends seen in the deals won by the reps vs the deals that were lost. You can click on any of these traits to view the winning behavior insights.

Click the View all option to see the list of the deals that belong to this cohort and resulted in a win.

To download the list of won deals in .csv format, click the icon.

The Pipeline insights help to identify two types of cohort of deals :

- those with a higher win rate compared to the organization's average
- those with a lower win rate compared to the organization's average

You can use this information to gain insights into a cohort of deals that are more likely to be successful and those that require attention.

Note: Cohorts are a group of deals with a shared characteristic.

You can click on any of these insights, to view the root cause analysis (RCA) page that highlights important details. You can see the win rate of the selected deal cohort compared to the average win rate of all deals across the organization. Additionally, you can see the deals that were won and belonged to the cohort for a positive insight and the deals that were lost and belonged to the cohort for a negative insight.

Click the View all option to see the list of the deals that belong to this cohort and resulted in a win/loss.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Get Started with Mindtickle > Seller Intel (Beta) > Quadrant progression:
The rep's performance for the last four quarters is displayed on the graph. The vertical axis represents the future quota potential, and the horizontal axis reflects year-to-date quota attainment.

Note: The cutoff value dividing the four quadrants is customized per your company's standards.

The graph is divided into four quadrants:

1. High performers: If the rep has a track record of consistently meeting or exceeding their sales targets in the past and is well-positioned to continue achieving high levels of quota fulfillment in the future.
2. High potential: If the rep has underperformed recently, but there is a high chance of them improving their quota attainment in the future if they persist with and improve upon the main areas where they are lagging behind.
3. Needs development: If the rep has recently performed well and the likelihood of closing deals given the current trajectory is also low. They need to work on their key weaknesses to improve their performance.
4. Outliers: If the rep has performed admirably in meeting their quotas, but they are unlikely to keep on attaining higher quotas going forward. To ensure a sustained high level of quota attainment, the reps should focus on addressing their key areas of improvement.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Get Started with Mindtickle > Seller Intel (Beta) > Movement insights:
Seller Intel analyzes and compares the RevQ score and Quota attainment score from the previous quarter to the current quarter. With this, Seller Intel determines any shifts or changes in performance. We then investigate the factors driving these changes by closely examining the performance metrics that have seen significant shifts over the past quarter. Furthermore, we delve into the underlying root causes that have led to alterations in these metrics. Using this method, we bring to light the following noteworthy performance movements:

- The teams/reps that consistently fall within the Needs development category.
- The teams/reps transitioning to the High performer category (indicating a positive change in projected revenue attainment between the previous and current periods).
- The teams/reps moving to the Needs developments category (reflecting a decrease in projected revenue attainment from the previous quarter to the current quarter).
- The teams/reps progressing from the Needs development category to High potential.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Get Started with Mindtickle > Seller Intel (Beta) > Organization, team, and rep level insights:
We conduct a comprehensive performance analysis by comparing your team, individual reps, or the entire organization with a benchmark. The benchmark calculation is outlined below. This analysis helps us identify significant areas of improvement and highlight areas where you outperform the benchmark.

Revenue impact: We measure the difference in revenue achievement due to variations in performance metrics between your target reps/team and the top-performing reps/teams.

Areas for enhancement: We arrange the performance metrics in ascending order based on the variance between the benchmark and the performance of your selected group of reps, whether it's an individual, a team, or the entire organization. We only present performance metrics where your group is significantly below the benchmark, showcasing their areas of enhancement.

Strengths: We arrange the performance metrics in descending order based on the variance between the performance of your selected group of reps and the benchmark. We only present performance metrics where your group meets or exceeds the benchmark, showcasing your strengths.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Get Started with Mindtickle > Seller Intel (Beta) > Root cause analysis:
We have a comprehensive mapping that associates all root cause metrics with their corresponding stages. When we identify a performance metric, we then examine the list of root cause metrics aligned with the same stage as the performance metric. The objective is to pinpoint the most significant root cause metrics contributing to underperformance or outperformance. This determination is done using the following impact score calculation:

1. Identify all the root cause metrics associated with the performance metric.
2. Calculate impact score = ( Correlation * ( Root Cause Metric Value - Benchmark Value ))

Where:

- Correlation refers to the correlation between the root cause metric and the performance metric
- Root Cause Metric Value is the value of the root cause metric for the specific rep or team.
- Benchmark Value is the benchmark or 75th percentile value of the root cause metric.

1. If the performance indicator indicates a strong performance, we highlight the two factors (RCA) that contribute the most positively to this performance.
2. If the performance indicator reveals an area of weakness, we highlight the two factors (RCA) that have the most negative impact on their performance metric.

For example, rep A’s main area of improvement is Qualify to Prove stage conversion. This metric belongs to the Qualify stage. We then go through all the RCA metrics related to the Qualify stage.

| RCA metric | Correlation with given perf metric | Value | Benchmark (P75 value of RCA) | Impact Score |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CHAMP Score | 0.4 | 40 | 80 | -16 (40-80)*(0.4) |
| Qualifying Competency | 0.5 | 50 | 60 | -5 (50-60)*(0.5) |

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Get Started with Mindtickle > Seller Intel (Beta) > Winning behavior insights:
We calculate various metrics for reps per-opportunity basis, excluding performance metrics. This approach allows us to assess behaviors or characteristics that greatly enhance the likelihood of successfully closing a deal. These forecasts are generated using a decision tree model that examines opportunity-level metrics and identifies specific thresholds for each metric that significantly affect the win rate.

For instance, the model analyzes the number of visitors to DSR data and determines that a win rate of 60% occurs when the number of visitors exceeds 4, compared to just 30% when the number of visitors is less than 4. This information is presented as insights into winning behavior.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Get Started with Mindtickle > Seller Intel (Beta) > Calculate Revenue impact:
Revenue impact provides the yearly financial impact resulting from the current performance of your sales reps, groups of reps, or teams. To determine these impacts, we calculate revenue changes for various insights, shedding light on the revenue loss that may occur due to disparities and any additional revenue generated by high-performing reps compared to their peers.

Performance Insights is the difference in quota attainment if the rep performs at the same level as top reps on a specific performance metric.

Formula: (Current YTD Quota Attainment)*(Quota plan for the year)*(Diff/(1+Diff)

Where:

Diff = (Performance metric of rep/team) - (75th Percentile value of Performance metric)

If the performance metric is a ratio, else

Diff = (Performance metric of rep) - (75th Percentile value of the performance metric)/ (75th Percentile value of performance metric)

Revenue Impact : (Current quota attainment - Previous quota attainment)*(Quota plan)

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Get Started with Mindtickle > Seller Intel (Beta):
1. For which industries or types of businesses is Seller Intel designed?Seller Intel is suitable for companies involved in B2B sales, with a particular emphasis on technology.

2. Who is the target audience for Seller Intel?Seller Intel is tailored to cater to all sales team members, encompassing sales leaders, sales reps, and individuals in enablement and revenue operations (Revops) roles.

3. How is the data in Seller Intel collected?Seller Intel uses data from your Salesforce (CRM) and Mindtickle's platform. The data in CRM is used to predict quota attainment potential and analyze the sales funnel. Data from Mindtickle's platform is used to uncover winning traits and identify areas of improvement.

4. How is the Revenue score calculated?The Revenue score is calculated based on data from the CRM.

5. How does Seller Intel predict future performance?Seller Intel uses historical data and current metrics to predict future performance. It looks at the sales pipeline, how deals have transitioned from one stage to another, and other factors to predict the quota a sales representative can achieve.

6. Do customers require any other Mindtickle products to enable Seller Intel?Yes, you must use two or more Mindtickle products from Readiness Index, Call AI, Asset Hub, or Digital Sales Room. If you are using only one Mindtickle product, it must be Call AI.

7. The sales stages in our organization are different from those used in SFDC. Will Seller Intel support the sales stages of our organization?Seller Intel leverages a set of common stages for all users and maps them to your company stages. For example:

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Best Practices and Use Cases > Use Cases for Mobile App > Retail:
Use case 1: Mobile certification convenience

Imagine a world where dealers in the retail industry can keep up with their certifications while on the go. With the Mindtickle mobile app, this is a reality. Dealers are incentivized to stay updated on their certifications, and there's no need for bulky laptops or desktop computers. It's the perfect solution for dealers in the retail world.

Use case 2: Engaging dealers and consumers

Picture a scenario where dealerships have fully embraced tablet and mobile app usage. Account Holders and Dealer Sales Representatives (DSRs) use the app to engage with end consumers, even sharing assets via text. Push-to-text functionality enhances communication, making it an invaluable tool for the retail industry.

Use case 3: Efficient compliance training

In a busy retail environment, all employees need to stay compliant with regulations. However, finding the time for in-person training can be a challenge. The Mindtickle mobile app comes to the rescue, reducing downtime and training costs. It's a cost-effective solution for ensuring compliance among retail staff.

Use case 4: Boosting sales and marketing

Suppose you could influence your sales reps to promote a specific product over another or meet quotas and spiffs more effectively. The Mindtickle mobile app can make that happen. Store managers can also use the app to organize store layouts, saving time and costs by eliminating the need for HQ visits.

Use case 5: Streamlining new employee onboarding

Imagine a world where new hires receive comprehensive training without the need for costly on-site visits. The Mindtickle mobile app provides training on machine operation, brand knowledge, competitor differentiation, store design, and upselling techniques. It's a cost and time-saving solution for retail businesses.

Use case 11: Maintaining engagement for remote or dispersed teams

During modern times, the Mindtickle mobile app helps maintain engagement with remote audiences. Companies run competitions and activities, offer yoga sessions, and distribute prizes, ensuring users stay connected.

The app supports various content formats, including podcasts. Bring Your Own Device (BYOD) policies are easily implemented. Sales reps and Account Executives (AEs) can engage in ride-alongs, enhancing real-world experience.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Asset Hub:
This article explains how sales reps can share assets via Outlook with their customers or prospects by installing the Mindtickle add-in for Outlook. Asset Hub integrates with Outlook through the Mindtickle add-in, enhancing accessibility and user experience.

This integration allows reps to access the asset picker of their respective Mindtickle learning site and pick and share assets directly via email or link without the need to exit the Outlook platform. When selecting assets to share, reps can choose from both admin-enabled shared assets and their own customized assets. The integration also ensures tracking of those shared assets under the Interactions tab in Mindtickle. This kind of tracking allows reps to understand the prospects' engagement on the shared assets, gauge prospects' interest, and plan their next steps to take the best step forward.

Further, the article explains the multi-platform approach for tracking customer engagement/activity.

Note: Asset Hub is a paid feature. For more information, contact your Customer Success Manager (CSM).

Benefits

Using the Mindtickle for Outlook add-in provides threefold benefits to the reps:

- Improved accessibility : Assets can be accessed directly on Outlook, eliminating platform switching.
- Customizable notifications and access control: Reps can set activity and reminder notifications and control access to the content being viewed by the customer on content shared through Outlook.
- Trackable customer activity : When you share assets from the Mindtickle platform, reps can track customer activity on those assets, thus providing valuable insights into where the customer interests lie.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Asset Hub > Prerequisites:
To use the Mindtickle add-in for Outlook, ensure that the following prerequisites are met:

- The Mindtickle add-in is supported only on the new Outlook app UI (for Windows and Mac). It is not supported if you use Outlook on the classic/legacy UI.
- System and client requirements:
  - Windows
    - OS: Windows 10 or later
    - License: Microsoft 365 subscription OR Retail perpetual Outlook 2016 or later
    - Outlook version: 2206 (build 15330.20196) or later
  - Mac
    - OS: macOS 12 or later
    - Outlook version: 16.65.827.0 or later
  - Outlook on the web
    - Modern UI
- The add-in is not supported for the following:
  - On-premises Outlook Exchange
  - Mindtickle mobile app (iOS and Android)

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Asset Hub > 1. Add assets to Outlook email:
1. In Outlook, access the Mindtickle for Outlook add-in. The following options appear:
  - Add assets to email
  - Share assets via link
2. The add-in appears in the right panel. Click Add assets to email .
3. Authenticate your account by entering your learning site name and proceeding to the Mindtickle login screen.
4. The Add assets to email page displays. When selecting assets, you can choose from both admin-enabled shared assets ( Assets tab) and your own customized assets ( My assets tab). You can narrow the asset list by selecting Hubs or Attributes from the respective drop-down or search for an asset directly by typing the asset name in the Search bar. Once you filter the assets, you can sort the assets using the Sort by dropdown based on recently modified, average rating, number of views, number of shares, and alphabetically. Click the Add <x> assets button to proceed. Before sharing, turn on the Show selected assets toggle switch in the upper-right corner to view all the selected assets.
5. The selected assets are displayed on the settings page.
  - Write with Copilot: Use Mindtickle Copilot to draft the email message with the help of AI. For details, see the “ Write email with Copilot ” section.
  - Recipient activity notifications : Turn on the setting if you want to be notified via email whenever a recipient interacts with the shared assets. It has the following 3 options:
  - Notify when the recipient engages with the assets along with the engagement summary
  - Notify me when the recipient shares assets with their peers
  - Notify when a recipient is active
  - Reminder notifications : Turn on the setting if you want to set an email reminder to check the engagement on shared assets. It has the following 2 options:
  - Remind me to check engagement data
  - Remind me only if there is no activity
  - Allow download: Turn on the setting if you want recipients to download the shared assets to their local machine from the asset link. The option to download is unavailable for embedded assets (for example, a YouTube video embedded link).
  - Access expiration: Configure the setting if you want the recipient’s access to expire for the shared assets after the set time (for example, renewals, contracts, and licenses). It ensures that the recipients always access the latest and most relevant content.
  - Add internal notes: Use the section as your personal notetaker to jot down the ideas or thoughts about sharing the assets. It will help you remember why you shared these assets with the customer or prospect in the later stages of the sales cycle.
6. Under the Reorder and rename assets section:
  - You can rearrange selected asset order to keep the most relevant asset at the top.
  - You can Edit the name to be more customer-centric or Delete an asset by hovering on its thumbnail.
  - You can still go back (using the Back arrow in the upper-left corner) to the asset selection window and select more assets. The email details filled in so far remain intact.
7. Click Add to email to proceed. The selected assets are attached to the compose box of Outlook, and you can click the Send button to send out the email.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Asset Hub > Write email with Copilot:
While sharing assets using either of the two options (Add assets to email and Share assets via link), you can use Mindtickle Copilot to draft the email message. With the Write with Mindtickle Copilot option on the settings page, you can make use of AI to help you write the draft email message while sharing assets. Use prompts with Copilot to generate an email message. Once generated, the draft message appears in the email message field. The draft can be further edited either in the configuration settings or in the Compose Email window.

Mindtickle Copilot is our generative AI based revenue productivity assistant. Copilot is already available for drafting emails while sharing assets on the Mindtickle platform or using our extension for Gmail. This release brings the same capability to our Outlook add-in for Asset Hub.

For enabling this AI-powered functionality, you must have opted for (enabled) Copilot, Mindtickle’s AI-based capability on the platform. For more information on Copilot, see this FAQ article. To enable Copilot, please contact your CSM or Mindtickle Support.

For detailed information on how to use Copilot to draft emails, see the “Draft Emails using Mindtickle Copilot” section in this article.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Asset Hub > Multi-platform approach for tracking customer engagement:
The multi-platform approach is designed to increase the accuracy of tracking emails sent via the platform. Using this approach, the reps get customer activity/engagement on assets sent via unsupported platforms. This involves adding a system-generated email ID to the BCC field of the emails sent by the reps. Thus allowing Mindtickle to confirm whether an email and its associated assets have been sent successfully.

When reps add assets to their emails via the Outlook add-in, the system email ID is automatically added to the BCC field of the email. Once the email is sent, Mindtickle receives a confirmation via this BCC email and publishes the related interaction.

After selecting the relevant assets and configuring the notification and access settings, a consent form displays. This form has details of the benefits of adding the system email.

Reps can consent to the BCC approach by clicking Yes, I agree. A system email ID is added to the BCC field of the current and all future emails. If they choose not to consent, the system email ID will not be added to any email.

To respect privacy and comply with security standards, Mindtickle seeks consent at two levels before implementing the BCC approach:

- Admin level : Admins can enable the multi-channel feature for their organization.
- Rep level : The consent form is displayed to reps when they add assets to their email for the first time. They can choose to agree (opt-in) or disagree (opt-out) to have the system email ID added to the BCC field of their emails.

Reps can change this setting anytime by clicking the Tracking settings option.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Digital Sales Rooms:
Note: This article explains role-based access control permissions for DSRs. These permissions are not to be confused with Digital Sales Room Permissions.

To effectively manage and regulate your sales reps' access to digital sales rooms, you must define and implement permissions that align with their roles and responsibilities. This ensures they have appropriate access to perform their job responsibilities, minimizes the risk of unauthorized access, and prevents the misuse of resources. You can choose to allow reps to:

- View and edit all rooms, including the ones where they are not the owner or a collaborator
- View all rooms, including the ones where they are not the owner or a collaborator, but edit only rooms where they are the owner or a collaborator
- View and edit only rooms where they are the owner or a collaborator

To define role-based permissions:

1. Navigate to Organization Settings > Permissions .
2. Choose a permission set from the available options. Note : By default, reps can view and edit all rooms, including the ones where they are not the owner or a collaborator.
3. Click Save Changes .

Each permission set impacts reps’ access to DSRs and DSR insights, the content within them, and the actions they can perform in rooms. This article further explains each permission set and its impact in detail.

Tip: Regularly assess and update these permissions to ensure the ongoing security of the content in your digital sales rooms.
