chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > User Sync > Steps to be performed in Personio > Steps to create Client ID and Client Secret in Personio:
1. Go to Settings > Integrations > API credentials .
2. Click Generate new credentia l . The Add new credential drawer appears.
3. In the Name field, enter a meaningful name (for example, 'Custom Reports') for the credentials. Select Employees and the attributes that Mindtickle should be able to fetch. Use the checkbox to define the desired access levels. Select Read to allow third-party systems to pull employee data from Personio. Note : Access to Personal Data , Attendance , Absence , and Write permissions is not required.
4. Click Generate new credential .
5. Share the generated Client ID, Client Secret, and API URL with your CSM.
6. Personio’s field names must be mapped with Mindtickle’s user profile fields. Share the required mapping and filters for users in the Deployment Workbook created for the project ( sample ) with your CSM. This sheet specifies which Personio profile attributes should correspond to which Mindtickle profile fields.

Once you have performed the above mentioned steps, inform your CSM, who will engage our Professional Services team to take the next steps and complete the integration configuration process.

Note:

- Users are fetched from Personio into Mindtickle every 12 hours (this is configurable). To update the cadence, contact your CSM.
- The platform’s timezone is UTC. For example, if you add a user to Personio on 16.10.2024 at 11 PM PST, the user is added to the Mindtickle platform on October 17 because of the timezone difference.
- The integration performs add, update, or deactivate operations based on the user's status.

The global search on the learning site is a hybrid implementation that makes use of the traditional keyword-based search in combination with the modern, AI-powered semantic search. You can use the global search to search for everything on the learning site in one place — except for Call AI calls and Digital Sales Rooms (DSRs) content, both of which can be searched on their respective pages.

The global search is also available on the Mindtickle mobile app and works in the same way. For details, see this article. See this article for Mindtickle API for the global search.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Get Started > Overview:
The traditional keyword-based search looks for information only by the keyword (search query) in the name, description, and tags/attributes of the content. The global search is hybrid, and delivers more relevant and contextual results based on keyword and semantic search powered by AI. Semantic search tries to understand the context and intent behind user queries through advanced machine learning models to transform unstructured data into a semantic representation, enabling more accurate and contextually relevant search results. For example, if you search for “country”, you will get results that have “country” in the content as well as results that are related to the term “country”, such as the United States, India, and Japan.

Highlight features

- Precision: The AI-powered semantic search digs deep to understand the meaning behind user queries, delivering more accurate and satisfying results.
- Engagement: With filters and sort options, the search experience becomes interactive and engaging.
- Decision power: Equips users with precise, decision-shaping information, guaranteeing better outcomes.
- Productivity boost: More relevant and fast search results; saves time and accelerates user productivity.
- Multilingual search: Search for translated content in multilingual series and modules using your preferred language. For more information, see Search for translated content in your preferred language .
- Clean results: When there are duplicate files (whether they are duplicate instances of the file or are used within one or more assets), the system uses duplicate file grouping to automatically consolidate them into a single search result, reducing clutter and helping you find the right content faster.

- The global search bar is available in the top navigation bar on the homepage as well as the other pages, such as Training , Coaching , Assets , and Digital Sales Rooms .
- Call AI calls and Digital Sales Rooms (DSRs) content are currently not available in the global search results; they will be included in a future release. In the meantime, you can search for calls from the Call AI page and DSR content from the Digital Sales Rooms page. Both have their separate search functionality.
- All newly-added content will appear in the global search in near realtime. In most cases, within a minute. However, there could be delays in case of bulk operations on the platform, such as bulk module operations and bulk asset creation .
- Site owners can remove any entity from appearing in the global search by writing to Mindtickle Support . We will remove it from being searched for your users. Example use case: You do not want people to search and access their peers’ info.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Get Started > Prerequisites and caveats > Supported entities:
The global search supports various entities (types of content) on the Mindtickle platform. It displays all results from across various entities: assets, modules, module tags, files, series, hubs, and peers. Think of entities as categories or types of content on the platform. We have also provided entity related filters so you can view results by one or more entities.

You can search on the following entities. The global search looks for your searched term into the mentioned properties for each entity:

- Assets: Asset name, description, attributes, asset file content, and the hub names where the asset resides
- Modules: Module name and description
- Tags: Tags applied to modules only. Tags applied to files, questions, polls, and evaluation parameters (for missions and coaching sessions) are currently not supported.
- Files: File name and file content
- Series: Series name and description
- Asset hubs: Hub name, description, and overview page content
- Peers (colleagues): Name, username, and email address

Note: By default, the search is enabled for all entities. However, you can choose to enable it only for specific entities. Please contact Mindtickle Support for further help.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Get Started > Prerequisites and caveats > Evaluating and optimizing search quality:
The quality of the search results using the global search feature is evaluated through a combination of precision and recall measures. A generic algorithm is used to assign a certain amount of weight to keyword-based results and a certain amount of weight to semantic results. The cumulative score is then calculated, and the results are displayed in the order of highest relevance.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Get Started > Get started with search:
You can run a search across the learning site using the global search bar, available in the top navigation bar on the homepage as well as other pages, such as Training, Coaching, Assets, and Digital Sales Rooms.

1. Click the search bar to get started. In the search pop-up, you can either run a search or ask Seller Copilot.It also displays a dropdown menu with a list of your seven recent/previous searches, if any. Use the Clear all option to remove recent searches.
2. Simply start typing what you are looking for. You must enter at least 3 characters to search. What you enter in the search bar is referred to as a search query, search keyword, or search.
3. The dropdown menu automatically lists top results as you start typing.

You can take the following actions:A. Click any of the suggested results to open it directly in a new tab.B. Click View all results or press to view all results on the search results page, where you can apply filters and sort the results.C. Ask Seller Copilot directly using your entered search query, instead of running a search.D. View duplicate files and assets: In the search bar's suggested results dropdown, the double arrow (View locations) icon next to any result indicates duplicate file grouping. Click the icon to open a menu on the right that displays all associated locations. You can then click a location to navigate directly to the specific file or asset (opens in a new tab).

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Get Started > Get started with search > Search for translated content in your preferred language:
You can search for translated content (series name, module names, learning objects, and content files) in multilingual series using your preferred language in the global search.

Note: The other language search works only for training content (Modules, learning objects, and files) available within a multilingual series.

When you open translated content available in a multilingual series using a specific language, the system records it as your preferred language for that content. You can now use that language to search for the training content in the learning site.

For example, if a series has English as its language and you change it to French and open the series, the system records French as the preferred language for that series. You can now search for its name, modules, learning objects, and content files in French.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Get Started > Results page:
In the search bar, when you click View all results or press after typing your query, you are taken to the search results page. It lists all available results for your searched query. As you scroll down, more results appear automatically. You can click on any result to open the content, which opens in a new tab/window by default.

Above the search results, you will see a response from the search-integrated Copilot Assistant for Sellers. Click "Show more" to view the complete response and also for the option to continue the conversation with Seller Copilot.

To ensure a clean and highly scannable experience, the results page automatically applies duplicate file grouping. When there are duplicate files (whether they are duplicate instances of the file or are used within one or more assets), the system consolidates them into a single search result with an expandable list of the associated locations.

The results page lets you further narrow down your search results using a variety of filters and sort options. You can also provide your feedback on the results.

Additionally, you can take certain quick actions from the results and view useful information.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Get Started > Results page > Actions on the results:
You can take various actions right from the displayed results, such as preview assets, bookmark and share assets, and pin series.

The following actions are available:

A. For assets

Preview asset: Click theicon to quickly preview the asset contents.

Assets engagement stats: Each asset displays key engagement stats. Hover over theicon to view details on the internal and external views. It also displays asset shares and overall rating.

Bookmark assets: Click theicon to quickly bookmark the asset. Additionally, if the asset is marked for external sharing, then the (Share) icon is available. Click the icon to directly share the asset via email or link.Note: You can only share assets marked as External and have not expired with your customers and prospects.

B. For series

Click the icon to quickly pin a series. You can view your pinned series under the Training > Series page.

C. For grouped duplicate files

View duplicate files and assets: When there are duplicate files (whether they are duplicate instances of the file or are used within one or more assets), the system automatically consolidates these entries into a single search result. On these specific results, a locations summary appears at the bottom (for example, "Used in 15 locations"). Click the dropdown arrow next to this summary to expand a scrollable list of all the standalone duplicate file instances and associated assets. You can then click any specific entry within this list to navigate directly to that exact file or asset.

D. Additional information

In addition to the above actions, the results page provides certain helpful information about each result through icons.

When searching for enablement content, you may occasionally encounter the exact same file appearing multiple times. To streamline your content discovery, global search automatically applies duplicate file grouping.

This consolidated experience is visible in both the quick search dropdown and on the main search results page, as shown in the examples below:

- Context preservation: The original locations of the file are preserved at the bottom of the search result. A summary tag displays the total number of associations (for example, "Used in 15 locations").
- Direct navigation in quick search: In the search bar's suggested results dropdown, the double arrow ( View locations ) icon next to any result indicates duplicate file grouping . This list displays the specific names, types (such as File or Asset), and visual icons for every associated standalone file and asset. You can click any specific item in this list to navigate directly to that exact file or asset [opens in a new tab].

Note: This functionality applies exclusively to pure duplicates (files sharing the exact same underlying entity identifier).

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Get Started > Filter and sort results > Apply filters:
By default, the search results page displays all results from across various entities: assets, modules, files, series, hubs, and peers. Think of entities as categories or types of content on the platform. We have also provided entity related filters so you can view results by one or more entities.

Important: The Filters panel displays only the filters applicable to your search query. For example, if you search for something for which there are no assets, then assets related filters will not appear in the panel.

The following image provides an overview of the available filters:

Think of the entity filters as primary filters. While the rest of the filters are for each of the entities:

| Entity filters | Relevant additional filters |
| --- | --- |
| Assets | The Asset Attribute and Hub filters |
| Modules | The Module type and Module tags filters |
| Files | The File type and File modules filters |
| Peers | The Profile fields filter |
| Note: No additional filters are available for the Series and Hubs entities. |  |

In the Filters panel, entities are listed first. Select one or more entities to view the results specific to them. For example, click Assets to view only the assets (from Asset Hub) in the results.

Additionally, the filters in the panel are adaptive. When you select an entity, the left panel displays only those filters that are relevant to the selected entity. For example, when you select Modules and Files entities, the side panel displays only module and file related additional filters, and hides the rest of the filters.

To use the Mindtickle add-in for Outlook, ensure that the following prerequisites are met:

- The Mindtickle add-in is supported only on the new Outlook app UI (for Windows and Mac). It is not supported if you use Outlook on the classic/legacy UI.
- System and client requirements:
  - Windows
    - OS: Windows 10 or later
    - License: Microsoft 365 subscription OR Retail perpetual Outlook 2016 or later
    - Outlook version: 2206 (build 15330.20196) or later
  - Mac
    - OS: macOS 12 or later
    - Outlook version: 16.65.827.0 or later
  - Outlook on the web
    - Modern UI
- The add-in is not supported for the following:
  - On-premises Outlook Exchange
  - Mindtickle mobile app (iOS and Android)

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Asset Hub > Admin > Installing the Mindtickle add-in:
1. Log into the Microsoft 365 admin center and go to Settings > Integrated apps > Add-ins page.
2. Select Deploy Add-in at the page's top, then select Next .
3. The Deploy a new add-in page displays. Select Choose from the store option.
4. Search the Mindtickle for Outlook add-in and click Add to proceed.
5. On the Configure add-in page, select any of the below options to deploy the add-in:

6. Once selected, click Deploy . The add-in gets deployed across your organization, and the Mindtickle add-in icon appears to the users.

When planning your room template strategy, consider the following best practices:

- How many templates to create:
  - Tailor templates based on teams, messaging differences, and specific needs such as product, team type, persona, industry, region, etc.
  - Define use cases for DSRs in your organization. Aim to get users through 90% of the room creation process up to a completed digital sales room for each use case, allowing for minor edits before they share it.
- Naming and describing templates:
  - Give each template a clear name and description to help users choose the most suitable one.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Copilot > For admins > About Copilot:
Mindtickle Copilot is a generative AI based revenue productivity assistant. Copilot combines the power of enablement and revenue operations data with enterprise-ready generative AI so revenue teams can focus on their most important jobs — selling more and delighting customers.

Copilot provides various AI-powered features across the platform, including the ability to interact with Copilot in a chat interface for certain features. Copilot is built on large language models — such as GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 (hosted on Microsoft’s Azure OpenAI Service) and Claude Haiku and Sonnet (hosted on Amazon Bedrock) — providing excellent security and privacy. It does not utilize OpenAI’s ChatGPT.

For information on Copilot, see Copilot overview and the frequently asked questions (FAQs).

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Copilot > For admins > Responsible AI principles:
At Mindtickle, we believe in an ethical and trusted approach to AI that puts people, transparency, and safety first. We have implemented AI through Copilot features across the platform with the following principles in mind:

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Copilot > For admins > Responsible AI principles > AI should be used for good:
AI technology should be developed and deployed with the primary aim of improving the lives of the users it interacts with. This involves using AI to solve problems, enhance productivity, and create new opportunities for growth and learning.

- Positive example: Implementing an AI-driven system that helps sales reps close deals faster by providing pre-call prep and post-call summaries that help them execute action items effectively.
- Negative example: Using an AI system to analyze and rank sales reps based on their performance metrics, and then using these rankings to limit access to advanced coaching resources or opportunities. This could lead to a self-perpetuating cycle where lower-ranked reps have fewer opportunities to improve and decisions are made on their employment solely based on AI.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Copilot > For admins > Responsible AI principles > AI should prevent bias and discrimination:
The principle of Diversity, Non-discrimination, and Fairness asserts that AI systems should be designed and operated in a way that ensures fairness and equity. AI systems should not perpetuate bias or discrimination and should actively work to mitigate such issues when they arise.

- Positive example: Implementing an AI system that is trained on a diverse dataset, representing a wide range of sales scenarios, customer interactions, and sales rep performances. This helps to ensure that the system's recommendations and insights are fair and unbiased, benefiting all sales reps equally.
- Negative example: Deploying an AI system that has been trained predominantly on data from reps in a specific geography. This could lead to a system that is biased towards strategies and styles that work in that geography, potentially putting other reps at a disadvantage who have different but equally effective approaches.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Copilot > For admins > Responsible AI principles > AI should be safe and reliable:
The principle of Reliability and Safety requires that AI systems should be designed to be safe, robust, and perform consistently under different conditions. AI systems should be resilient to manipulation and malicious attacks. Furthermore, it should not pose any risk to the safety of individuals, society, or the environment.

- Positive example: Implementing a robust AI system that includes built-in redundancies and error-checking mechanisms. For instance, if the system is providing coaching feedback, it cross-verifies its suggestions with multiple data points to ensure accuracy and reliability.
- Negative example: Deploying an AI system that doesn't have safeguards against erroneous inputs or outputs. For instance, an AI system that generates sales strategies without validating the data could lead to flawed strategies, potentially causing financial loss or damage to customer relationships.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Copilot > For admins > Responsible AI principles > People should be in control of AI:
The principle of Human Agency And Oversight emphasizes that AI should be developed and used in a way that respects and prioritizes people's rights and freedoms. Human oversight and control over AI systems should be maintained, allowing people to understand, influence, and contest decisions made by AI.

- Positive example: Providing a feature for sales reps to review and override AI suggestions as well as give feedback on the suggestions. For example, if AI suggests a piece of content based on a call and a rep believes a different piece of collateral would be more effective in their sales situation, they can select the more relevant content.
- Negative example: Implementing an AI system that automatically sends collateral to clients without allowing sales reps to review or modify the selection.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Copilot > For admins > Responsible AI principles > AI should be transparent and accountable:
The principle of Transparency, Accountability, and Remedian calls for clarity and openness in the design and operation of AI systems. Developers and users of AI should be held accountable for its actions, and AI systems should be designed in a way that their workings can be understood by the relevant stakeholders. This requires observability, explainability, and auditability in the decision-making of the AI system, and a way to get an inadvertent error rectified.

- Positive example: Implementing an AI system that not only provides sales reps with coaching feedback but also explains the reasoning behind the feedback. For instance, if a rep is advised to improve their product knowledge, the system could point to specific instances in their sales calls where this was an issue.
- Negative example: Deploying an AI system that automatically flags and penalizes sales reps for certain behaviors during sales calls, without providing any explanation or context. This lack of transparency could lead to confusion, mistrust, and potentially unfair penalties, undermining the accountability of the AI system.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Best Practices and Use Cases > Best Practices for Enablement > Tailor surveys to gather relevant insights:
The key to effective surveying lies in crafting questions that elicit meaningful responses. Customize surveys to capture data aligned with specific learning objectives, program outcomes, and user experiences. Also, ensure that you have a standard set of questions in each survey to allow comparison across learning modules and programs.

Use a blend of quantitative and qualitative questions to obtain diverse perspectives. For instance, inquire about the relevance of content, the clarity of learning materials, or the applicability of training to their roles. Additionally, avoid leading, biased, or misleading questions that could influence or confuse your learners.

Example:

- On a scale of 1 to 5, how relevant do you find the content to your day-to-day responsibilities?
- What improvements would you suggest for enhancing your learning experience on Mindtickle?

Use a blend of quantitative and qualitative questions to obtain diverse perspectives. For instance, inquire about the relevance of content, the clarity of learning materials, or the applicability of training to their roles. Additionally, avoid leading, biased, or misleading questions that could influence or confuse your learners.

- On a scale of 1 to 5, how relevant do you find the content to your day-to-day responsibilities?
- What improvements would you suggest for enhancing your learning experience on Mindtickle?

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Best Practices and Use Cases > Best Practices for Enablement > Common pitfalls and challenges to avoid:
- Survey Fatigue : Bombarding learners with frequent or lengthy surveys.
  - Avoidance strategy : Keep surveys concise, targeted, and timed appropriately. Utilize periodic but strategic surveying.
- Lack of Clear Objectives : Conducting surveys without clear objectives can result in vague or unactionable feedback.
  - Avoidance strategy : Define specific goals for each survey. Are you seeking feedback on a specific module, overall platform experience, or learning initiative? Having clear objectives helps in framing survey questions to gather relevant insights.
- No variety in Survey Formats : Repeating the same survey format with each survey may lead to survey fatigue and monotonous responses.
  - Avoidance strategy : Vary the survey formats – from multiple-choice to open-ended questions, ratings, and scaled responses. This approach engages different learner preferences and elicits more diverse feedback.
- Ignoring Feedback or Not Closing the Loop : Not closing the feedback loop by acting on the feedback may lead to learner disengagement.
  - Avoidance strategy : Create a systematic approach to analyze and act on feedback. Communicate the changes or improvements based on what you learn from the surveys, fostering a sense of involvement and demonstrating the value of learners' input.
- Overlooking Actionable Insights : Collecting feedback without analyzing or acting upon the insights renders the process ineffective.
  - Avoidance strategy : Implement a robust feedback analysis system. Review data provided to identify trends or areas requiring improvement.
- Inadequate Communication and Transparency : Failing to communicate the purpose of surveys or the subsequent actions taken based on feedback can result in reduced participant engagement.
  - Avoidance strategy : Communicate the rationale behind surveys and their importance in enhancing the learning experience. Follow up with transparent communication regarding the changes implemented based on the collected feedback.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Best Practices and Use Cases > Best Practices for Enablement > Understanding module relevance:
Mindtickle’s Module Relevance feature allows administrators to categorize modules as "Required," "Optional," or leave them "Unmarked." This feature helps you distinguish which modules are important and of priority and which may be optional for the learner. Module relevance can also help you to increase learner engagement, motivation, and retention by aligning the modules with the learner’s goals, needs, and interests.

This designation indicates the importance and priority level of modules for learners.

- Required modules: Designates a module as mandatory for learners, necessitating its completion. This classification implies its critical relevance to their training.
  - Example use case: Compliance training modules, core skill development, or essential onboarding materials.
- Optional Modules: Marks a module as supplementary or non-essential for learners. While beneficial, completion of optional modules is not obligatory.
  - Example use case: Additional learning resources, supplementary materials, or advanced training for interested learners.
- Unmarked Modules: Represents modules with no specified relevance. They are assigned to learners, typically as part of their regular training, without mandatory or optional implications.
  - Example use case: Standard training materials that form part of the regular learning curriculum.

Module relevance can help you to increase learner focus by:

- Providing clarity and direction to the learners about which modules are essential and which are not.
- Creating a sense of urgency and accountability for the learners to complete the required modules.
- Offering flexibility and choice to the learners to complete the optional modules according to their preferences and needs.
- Aligning the modules with the learner’s goals, needs, and interests can enhance their engagement, motivation, and retention.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Best Practices and Use Cases > Best Practices for Enablement > Best practices for maximizing module relevance:
Module Relevance can be a powerful tool to enhance the effectiveness and efficiency of your training program. However, it also requires careful planning to ensure that it aligns with your learning objectives and outcomes. The following best practices will help you maximize Module Relevance:

- Strategic Prioritization: Assign the 'Required' status to modules critical for foundational knowledge or compliance requirements. Use the 'Optional' status for supplementary or advanced learning content.
- Clarity in Expectations: Communicate the importance and rationale behind the relevance designation to learners. This ensures your learners understand what they should focus on.
- Adaptation to Learning Styles: Cater to varied learning preferences by marking modules as optional, allowing learners to explore topics aligned with personal or role-specific interests.
- Continuous improvement: Review and revise the module relevance based on the learner’s feedback, performance, and progress, as well as the module’s effectiveness and impact.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Best Practices and Use Cases > Best Practices for Enablement > Leveraging Module Relevance:
When looking at ways to get the most out of your programs with module relevance, it is always good to consider how you want to use this and the impact you are seeking to drive. Here are some ways to better leverage Module Relevance:

- Using group and module linking, you can invite learners to a module and specify the module relevance you want to assign to that particular user.

Example: A course is mandatory for one group but optional for another (Invite Learners and Groups to a Module and Automation Links: Group to Module Linking)

- Use Module relevance to create an ongoing, unique learning path for your learners.

Example: Once learners have completed their mandatory modules, provide them with optional modules to build on or support the knowledge they just gained.

- Enable learners to filter modules based on relevance, promoting focused engagement.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Best Practices and Use Cases > Best Practices for Enablement > Pre-implementation considerations:
Before you implement Module Relevance, there are some important factors and steps that you need to consider and prepare; here are some of the factors that may affect the module relevance:

- Relevance Definition: Clearly define the criteria for marking a module as 'Required' or 'Optional,' ensuring alignment with learning objectives and learner needs.
- Balance in Module Assignment: Strive for a balance between 'Required' and 'Optional' modules to maintain learner interest and engagement. Understand that having everything as optional or required will make it difficult for learners to prioritize.
- Public Series: Module Relevance is not visible in a public series. However, when a learner subscribes to a public series, the learner would be able to see the relevance of any new Modules that are published going forward.
- Due date: If a due date is set for a Module, learners will see the due date even if the Module is optional for them.
- Learner Communication: by default, Reminder emails and notifications are sent to the Learners even if the Module is optional. However, please note that you have the option to disable this. See Disable email notifications for Optional or Unmarked modules for more information.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Best Practices and Use Cases > Best Practices for Enablement > Communicating module relevance with learners:
Communication is key to ensuring that your Learners understand and appreciate the value and purpose of Module Relevance. It is also essential to provide clear and consistent guidance and feedback to your Learners throughout their learning journey. Here are some tips and strategies for communicating Module Relevance with your Learners:

- Transparent communication: Inform learners of the purpose and use of 'Required' and 'Optional' designations to manage expectations and aid their learning journey.
- Emphasize priority: Highlight the significance of "Required" modules for learner success. This should also be supported by leadership.
- Guidance for module selection: Offer guidance on the implications of 'Required' versus 'Optional' modules, helping learners make informed choices about their learning path.
- Provide context: Explain how completing "Optional" modules can enhance their learning journey and provide learners with a more engaging experience.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Best Practices and Use Cases > Best Practices for Enablement > Common pitfalls to avoid:
As with all features in the platform, ensuring that these are used correctly will help you ensure its success. Here are some pitfalls to avoid.

- Overuse of required: Avoid marking an excessive number of modules as 'Required' unless necessary. Doing this might overwhelm learners and dilute the importance of essential content.
- Misalignment with learner needs: Ensure the designated relevance aligns with learners' expectations and learning goals to prevent disengagement or confusion. So, making a required compliance module Optional can confuse learners.
- Sequential locking: Enabling Sequential Locking for a Series and making a Module Optional in the Series will result in a conflict. This is because Learners must complete Optional Modules to unlock the next Module. We recommend not using Sequential Locking and Module Relevance for the same Series.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Best Practices and Use Cases > Best Practices for Enablement > Leverage a mix of all the Mindtickle modules:
Utilize the diverse range of MindTickle modules for varied learning experiences. Incorporate interactive elements, quizzes, videos, and role-plays to cater to different learning preferences and enhance engagement.

Mindtickle offers a variety of modules that fall under the Teach, Show, Practice, Reinforce (TSPR) model, and you can use it to create different types of learning content and activities. These modules include:

- Teach: This module allows you to create interactive and multimedia content that covers the essential knowledge and skills for your learners. You can use videos, images, audio, text, quizzes, and more to deliver engaging and effective learning content.
- Show: This module allows you to create objective and measurable assessments that evaluate the knowledge and performance of your learners. You can use multiple-choice questions, fill-in-the-blanks, drag-and-drop, and more to measure your learner’s learning outcomes and competencies.
- Practice: This module allows you to create realistic and challenging scenarios that test and reinforce the skills and behaviors of your learners. You can use role-plays, simulations, video pitches, and more to provide feedback and coaching to your learners.
- Reinforce: This module allows you to create spaced and adaptive reinforcement activities that help your learners retain and apply the knowledge and skills they have learned. You can use flashcards, trivia, puzzles, and more to boost the memory and confidence of your learners.

Using a mix of all these modules, you can create a comprehensive and holistic learning experience that covers all the aspects of learning: acquisition, application, evaluation, and retention. You can also use different modules for different purposes, such as onboarding, upskilling, certification, etc.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Best Practices and Use Cases > Best Practices for Enablement > Incorporate more microlearning:
Break down learning content into bite-sized, easily digestible nuggets. Microlearning boosts retention and allows learners to absorb information in shorter, focused bursts, improving their overall learning experience.

Microlearning is a learning strategy that involves delivering short and focused learning content and activities aligned with the learners' specific needs and goals. Microlearning can help you:

- Increase learner engagement: Microlearning can capture and sustain your learners' attention by providing them with bite-sized and relevant content they can consume at their own pace and convenience.
- Improve learner retention: Microlearning can enhance the memory and recall of your learners by providing them with frequent and spaced repetition and reinforcement of the key concepts and skills.
- Boost learner performance: Microlearning can improve the transfer and application of the knowledge and skills of your learners by providing them with immediate and actionable feedback and guidance.

To incorporate more microlearning in your training programs, you can use the following tips:

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Best Practices and Use Cases > Best Practices for Enablement > Use notifications to help learners focus:
Send targeted and personalized notifications to guide learners toward their learning goals. Notifications can be gentle reminders, updates, or nudges to keep learners engaged and focused on their learning journey.

Notifications inform and remind your learners about the learning content and activities that are available and due for them. Notifications can help you:

- Increase learner awareness: Notifications can make your learners aware of the new and updated content and activities that are relevant and important to them.
- Motivate learner participation: Notifications can encourage your learners to participate and complete the content and activities assigned and recommended for them.
- Improve learner performance: Notifications can give your learners feedback and recognition for their progress and achievements.

To use notifications to help your learners focus, you can use the following tips:

- Use different notification channels: Keep your learners informed using notifications through either email or the in-app notification center.You can use the Notification settings to choose the channels that suit your learners’ preferences and devices.
- Use different notification types: You can use different notifications to send different messages to your learners, such as reminders, alerts, updates, and more. You can use the Notification settings to choose the types that match your learners’ needs and goals.
- Use different notification triggers: You can use different triggers to send notifications to your learners, such as time, event, action, and more. You can use the Notification settings to choose the triggers that align with your learners’ behavior and performance.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Best Practices and Use Cases > Best Practices for Enablement > Drive engagement with series overview pages:

Series overview pages are the pages your learners see when they click on a series from their homepages or dashboards. Series overview pages can help you:

- Provide an overview and introduction of the series: Series overview pages can give your learners an overview and introduction, such as the title, description, objectives, duration, and more. You can use the Series settings to create and edit the series overview page for each series.
- Provide a preview and summary of the modules: Series overview pages can provide your learners with a preview and summary of the modules that are included in the series, such as the title, description, type, status, and more. You can use the Module settings to create and edit the module preview and summary for each module.
- Provide a progress and completion tracker: Series overview pages can provide your learners with a progress and completion tracker that shows them how much they have completed and how much they have left to complete in the series. You can use the Series and Module settings to set the completion criteria and tracking for each series and module.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Best Practices and Use Cases > Best Practices for Enablement > Use module relevance to drive learner focus:
Employ Module Relevance settings to distinguish between required and optional modules. This feature directs learners' attention to crucial content, guiding their focus and ensuring the completion of priority modules.

Module relevance is a feature that allows you to set the relevance level of each module for each role or group of your learners. Module relevance can help you:

- Prioritize and recommend the most relevant modules: Module relevance can help you prioritize and recommend the most relevant modules for your learners based on their roles, goals, and competencies. You can use the Module Relevance settings to set the relevance level of each module for each role, such as mandatory, recommended, or optional. You can also use the Module Relevance settings to set the order of the modules for each role, such as sequential, parallel, or random.
- Filter and sort the modules by relevance: Module relevance can help learners filter and sort the modules by relevance on their home pages and dashboards. You can use the Homepage and Dashboard settings to enable the relevance filter and sort options for your learners. You can also use the relevance icons and labels to indicate the relevance level of each module to your learners.
- Track and report the module relevance: Module relevance can help you track and report the module relevance for your learners and their progress and performance on the relevant modules. You can access and export the module relevance data for your learners and their groups using the Reports and Analytics settings. You can also use the module relevance metrics and charts to visualize and analyze the module relevance data.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Best Practices and Use Cases > Best Practices for Enablement > Create an engaging experience with gamification:
Gamification is a learning strategy that involves applying game elements and mechanics to your training programs to make them more fun and motivating for your learners. Gamification can help you:

- Increase learner engagement: Gamification can increase learner engagement by giving them a sense of challenge, curiosity, and achievement. You can use the contests, leaderboards, badges, certificates, and points features to create and run competitive and collaborative games for your learners and to reward and recognize their progress and performance.
- Improve learner retention: Gamification can improve learner retention by providing them with a sense of feedback, reinforcement, and mastery. You can use the quizzes, simulations, video pitches, and flash card features to create and deliver interactive and adaptive learning activities for your learners and to provide them with immediate and constructive feedback and guidance.
- Boost learner performance: Gamification can boost learner performance by providing them with a sense of alignment, relevance, and application. You can use the role-plays, scenarios, case studies, and call-scoring features to create and deliver realistic and relevant learning activities for your learners and to help them apply and transfer the knowledge and skills they have learned to their real-world situations.

You should align your gamification elements and mechanics with your learning objectives and outcomes and ensure they support and enhance your learning content and activities, not distract or detract from them.

You should also give your learners options and choices to customize their gamification experience according to their preferences.

You can also use the gamification settings to set the rules, criteria, and rewards for your gamification features, such as the contest duration, leaderboard type, badge criteria, certificate expiration, and point allocation.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Best Practices and Use Cases > Best Practices for Enablement > Increase knowledge retention with spaced reinforcement (Quests):
Spaced reinforcement is a learning strategy that involves delivering learning content and activities to your learners in a spaced and repeated manner over time to help them retain and recall the knowledge and skills they have learned. Spaced reinforcement can help you:

- Enhance learner memory and recall: Spaced reinforcement can enhance learner memory and recall by providing them with frequent and spaced repetition and review of the key concepts and skills. You can use the Quests feature to create and deliver spaced and adaptive reinforcement activities for your learners, such as flashcards, trivia, puzzles, and more.
- Reduce learner forgetting and decay: Spaced reinforcement can reduce learner forgetting and decay by providing timely and relevant reinforcement activities aligned with their forgetting curves. You can use the Quests feature to schedule and automate the delivery of reinforcement activities for your learners based on their completion and performance data and to adjust the difficulty and frequency of the reinforcement activities based on their mastery levels.
- Increase learner confidence and application: Spaced reinforcement can increase learner confidence and application by providing feedback and recognition for reinforcement activities. You can use the Quests feature to provide your learners with immediate and constructive feedback and guidance for their reinforcement activities and to reward and recognize their progress and achievements with points, badges, and certificates.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Best Practices and Use Cases > Best Practices for Enablement > Increase Engagement with Series Certification:
Encourage learner engagement and recognition by implementing a series certifications. These certifications serve as milestones and incentives, boosting motivation and commitment to completing the learning series.

Series certification is a feature that allows you to award certificates to your learners upon completing a series or a set of series. Series certification can help you:

- Recognize and reward your learners: Series certification can help you recognize and reward your learners for their achievements and accomplishments in completing the series or the set of series. You can use the Series Certification settings to create and edit the certificates for your series or the set of series. You can also use the certificate settings to customize the certificate title, description, logo, signature, and more.
- Motivate and challenge your learners: Series certification can help you motivate and challenge your learners to complete the series or the set of series and earn the certificates. You can use the Series Certification settings to set the completion criteria and expiration date for your certificates. You can also use the certificate preview and badge to display the certificate to your learners before and after they earn it.
- Share and promote your learners: Series certification can help you share and promote your learners and their certificates with their peers, managers, and external parties. You can use the Series Certification settings to enable the sharing and verification options for your certificates. You can also use the certificate URL and QR code to allow your learners to share and verify their certificates online.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Best Practices and Use Cases > Best Practices for Enablement > Streamline operations with automation:
Automation is another way to customize the learning experience on MindTickle. Automation allows you to assign different learning modules to learners based on their roles, knowledge levels, or other criteria. This way, you can create personalized and relevant learning paths for each learner and ensure they receive the most appropriate and effective training for their needs.

For example, you can use automation to assign different modules to sales reps and managers, depending on their responsibilities and goals. You can also use automation to assign different modules to beginners and experts, depending on their skill level and learning gaps. Or, depending on their performance and progress, you can use automation to assign different modules to those who need a refresher or a challenge.

Automation can also help you trigger notifications and reminders based on learner behavior or performance. This way, you can motivate and guide learners throughout their learning journey and provide timely and relevant feedback. You can also use automation to send personalized messages to learners, such as congratulating them on completing a module, encouraging them to continue learning, or suggesting they revisit a topic.

You can leverage automation by using:

- Rules: Rules allow you to define conditions and actions for automation. For example, you can create a rule that assigns a module to a learner if they belong to a certain role, score below a certain threshold on a quiz, or complete a specific activity. You can also create a rule that sends a notification to a learner if they complete a module if they achieve a specific badge, or if they are inactive for a certain period.
- Groups: Groups allow you to create dynamic groups of learners based on their attributes, such as role, location, department, or custom fields. For example, you can create a group of sales reps in North America, managers in the finance department, or learners who have completed a particular module. You can then use these groups to assign modules, send notifications, or generate reports.

Automation can help you save time, reduce errors, and increase efficiency in delivering customized learning experiences on MindTickle. Using automation, you can avoid manual and repetitive tasks, such as creating and assigning modules, sending notifications, or tracking learner progress. You can also ensure consistency and accuracy in your training delivery, as automation can eliminate human errors and biases. Moreover, you can optimize your training outcomes, as automation can enable you to adapt and adjust your training content and strategy based on learner data and feedback.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Best Practices and Use Cases > Best Practices for Enablement > Common Pitfalls to Avoid:
- Overloading your learners with too much content and activities : While providing your learners with comprehensive and relevant content and activities is important, it is also important to avoid overwhelming them with too much information and tasks. Too much content and activities can lead to cognitive overload, boredom, frustration, and dropout. To avoid this pitfall, you should:
  - Use the 80/20 rule : You should focus on 20% of the content and activities that deliver 80% of the value and impact for your learners. You should prioritize the content and activities that are essential and critical for your learners’ roles, goals, and competencies and eliminate or reduce the content and activities that are redundant, irrelevant, or outdated.
  - Use the micro-learning and sequencing techniques : You should break down your content and activities into smaller and manageable chunks that cover one topic or skill at a time. You should also sequence your content and activities in a logical and progressive order that helps your learners build on their prior knowledge and skills.
  - Use feedback and analytics : Use feedback and analytics to monitor and measure the engagement and performance of your learners on your content and activities. Use this data to identify and address the gaps and challenges that your learners face and to adjust and improve your content and activities accordingly.
- I gnoring the diversity and preferences of your learners : While providing your learners with consistent and standardized content and activities is essential, it is also important to acknowledge and accommodate the diversity and preferences of your learners. Your learners may have different backgrounds, experiences, learning styles, and motivations, and you should respect and cater to their needs and wants. To avoid this pitfall, you should:
  - Use personalization and customization : Use the personalization and customization features of Mindtickle to tailor and optimize the learning experience for each learner. Features such as role-based homepages, module relevance, series certification, and notifications can provide learners with a personalized and curated experience aligned with their roles, goals, and competencies.
  - Use the gamification and social learning features : You should use the gamification and social learning features of Mindtickle to enhance and enrich the learning experience for your learners.
- Neglecting the quality and consistency of your content and activities : While providing your learners with diverse and engaging content and activities is essential, it is also important to ensure the quality and consistency of your content and activities. Your content and activities should be accurate, relevant, up-to-date, and aligned with your learning objectives and outcomes.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Automated Sync > Introduction:
SharePoint is a web-based collaborative platform that allows organizations to create, manage, and share content. Integrating SharePoint with Mindtickle enables admins to automatically sync designated content from SharePoint into Content Center.

The SharePoint sync is one-way, from SharePoint to Mindtickle. You can configure it at different levels depending on the scope of content you want to sync:

- Tenant-level sync: Sync files and folders across all SharePoint sites (including team sites) in your organization’s tenant, giving Mindtickle access to all content.
- Site-level sync: Sync files and folders from a specific SharePoint site, such as a department or project site, restricting sync to that site.
- Team site-level sync: Sync files and folders from a specific SharePoint team site, typically used by a workgroup for collaboration.

Note: Subsites are not supported; folders within subsites will not be synced.

This article explains how admins can integrate SharePoint with Mindtickle end-to-end — covering authentication, account setup, folder mapping, optional metadata sync, and notifications. It also includes guidance for migrating existing syncs from legacy authentication.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Automated Sync > About Entra ID authentication for SharePoint syncs:
Mindtickle now supports Microsoft-recommended Entra ID (certificate-based app-only) authentication, replacing the legacy Azure ACS app-only (client secret) authentication.

Microsoft is retiring the legacy Azure Access Control Service (ACS) authentication: it has already been retired for new tenants and will be fully retired for all tenants on April 2, 2026.

To comply with Microsoft’s security standards, all new SharePoint syncs must use Entra ID certificate-based authentication. Existing syncs using ACS must be migrated before the retirement date to ensure uninterrupted content sync.

This authentication method provides a secure, app-only identity for Mindtickle to access SharePoint and ensures that all future integrations align with Microsoft’s recommended practices.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Automated Sync > How the integration works:
The Mindtickle–SharePoint integration provides a secure, automated, and reliable way to sync content from SharePoint into Mindtickle while maintaining structure and optional metadata. Key aspects of the integration include:

- Configuration: Admins select the SharePoint folders to sync in Mindtickle. Optionally, asset metadata from Mindtickle can be mapped to SharePoint properties for richer content organization and searchability.
- Scheduled and on-demand sync: Content is automatically pulled from SharePoint at the frequency configured by the admin. Additionally, admins can trigger a manual sync at any time to immediately propagate updates.
- Automatic updates: Any changes made in SharePoint, such as new files, edits, or deletions, are automatically reflected in Mindtickle’s Content Center, as well as in any linked modules, assets, or digital sales rooms (DSRs).
- Preservation of folder structure: The original folder hierarchy from SharePoint is maintained in Mindtickle, ensuring that content organization remains consistent.
- Error notifications: Admins and users can receive alerts if a sync fails, enabling faster issue resolution.
- One-way sync: This is a one-way integration and SharePoint remains the source of truth. Changes should be made in SharePoint only; editing content within Mindtickle can cause conflicts.

This integration ensures that content updates are seamless, structured, and always aligned with SharePoint, while giving admins control over sync frequency, folder selection, and optional metadata mapping.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Automated Sync > Prerequisites:
Before setting up the SharePoint integration in Mindtickle, ensure the following prerequisites are met:

- Admin permissions in Mindtickle: You must have admin access to the Mindtickle admin site, along with the Technical Settings (TECHNICAL_ADMINISTRATION) permission to configure SharePoint sync settings under Account → Security & integrations.
- SharePoint permissions: Ensure you have access to the sites you plan to sync. For tenant-level syncs, you should have access to all sites in the tenant. For site-level or team site syncs, you must have access to the specific site.
- Admin access to Microsoft Entra ID: You must have permissions to create and manage app registrations in your organization’s Entra ID (formerly Azure AD) tenant.
- Microsoft Graph Explorer or equivalent tool: Required only if you plan to use site-level or team site-level syncs with Sites.Selected, to grant site-specific permissions.
- Asset Hub license: To sync metadata along with content, your organization must have an active Asset Hub license on the learning site. Without it, only the content itself will be synced.

These prerequisites ensure a smooth integration and prepare you for the steps to configure SharePoint sync in Mindtickle.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Automated Sync > Section 1A: Configure SharePoint account details (new syncs) > Step 1: Register new app [Entra ID]:
To enable Mindtickle to connect securely with your SharePoint tenant, you must create an app registration in Entra ID. This app serves as the identity for Mindtickle when requesting access to your SharePoint data.

Perform the following steps to register an Entra ID app:

1. Sign in to the Microsoft Entra admin center with admin credentials.
2. In the left navigation panel, navigate to Entra ID → App registrations and then click New registration .
3. The Register an application page appears . Perform the following:
  - Enter a name that clearly identifies the app (e.g., Mindtickle-SharePoint Sync) to easily recognize it later as the Entra ID application used for this integration.
  - For Supported account types, select Accounts in this organizational directory only (Single tenant).
  - Leave Redirect URI blank (not required for app-only authentication).
  - Click Register.
4. The application page opens once it’s created successfully.
5. In the Overview tab of the app, copy the Application (client) ID .

Note: You’ll need the Application (client) ID from your Entra app for the Client ID field when entering Mindtickle account details in order to generate a certificate. See Step 2 for details.

To enable Mindtickle to connect securely with your SharePoint tenant, you must create an app registration in Entra ID. This app serves as the identity for Mindtickle when requesting access to your SharePoint data.

Perform the following steps to register an Entra ID app:

1. Sign in to the Microsoft Entra admin center with admin credentials.
2. In the left navigation panel, navigate to Entra ID → App registrations and then click New registration .
3. The Register an application page appears . Perform the following:
  - Enter a name that clearly identifies the app (e.g., Mindtickle-SharePoint Sync) to easily recognize it later as the Entra ID application used for this integration.
  - For Supported account types, select Accounts in this organizational directory only (Single tenant).
  - Leave Redirect URI blank (not required for app-only authentication).
  - Click Register.
4. The application page opens once it’s created successfully.
5. In the Overview tab of the app, copy the Application (client) ID .

Note: You’ll need the Application (client) ID from your Entra app for the Client ID field when entering Mindtickle account details in order to generate a certificate. See Step 2 for details.

The format of the URL will vary depending on whether you're syncing at the tenant, site, or team site level: ● Tenant-level sync : Use this if you want to sync files and folders across all SharePoint sites (including team sites) within the tenant. Format : https://<companyname>.sharepoint.com Example: https://contoso.sharepoint.com ● Site-level sync ( /sites ) : Use this to sync files and folders from a specific SharePoint site , such as a department site, project site, or communication site. Certificate expiry date: By default, this is set to a date two years from the current date. You can adjust it if needed.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Automated Sync > Section 1A: Configure SharePoint account details (new syncs) > Step 4: Configure application permissions [Entra ID]:
1. In the Entra admin center, go to the Entra app you registered ( Step 1 ) for the Mindtickle–SharePoint content sync.
2. In the left menu, go to API permissions → click + Add a permission .
3. In the Request API permissions panel, select SharePoint under the Microsoft APIs section .
4. In the SharePoint API, select Application permissions to view available permissions .
5. Under Select permissions → Sites , select one of the following : Note : The permission you configure depends on the type of SharePoint sync (tenant-level or site-level) you are setting up. This is determined by the SharePoint site URL entered in Mindtickle ( Step 2 → Account details).
  - Sites.Read.All – Use for tenant-level syncs Allows the Mindtickle Entra app to read files and folders across all SharePoint sites in the tenant. This permission gives the app access to documents and list items across all site collections, so you don’t need to grant access to each site individually.
  - Sites.Selected – Use for site-level or team site syncs Restricts the app to read files only within specific SharePoint sites .
6. Click Add permissions to add the selected permission.
7. Finally, on the to API permissions page, click Grant admin consent to grant consent for the permission for all accounts in the tenant (organization) .
8. Grant consent successful message appears and is also indicated in the Status column against the permission .
9. If you selected Sites.Selected in the previous step, you must explicitly grant the Mindtickle Entra app access to each SharePoint site it needs to sync via Microsoft Graph APIs. This step is required because Sites.Selected does not provide access to any site by default; access must be assigned individually.
10. See the next step ( Step 5 ) for details.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Automated Sync > Section 1A: Configure SharePoint account details (new syncs) > Step 5: Assign site-specific permissions [Graph API]:
1. Open Microsoft Graph Explorer or use another tool that can call Microsoft Graph APIs. Ensure you are signed in as a tenant admin.
2. Get the siteId for the SharePoint site by sending a GET request : Request URL : GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/sites/{hostname}:/sites/{siteName} Replace {hostname} with your SharePoint tenant domain (for example: contoso.sharepoint.com) Replace {siteName} with the display name of the site. Copy the site ID : Copy the id value from the response; this is the siteId that will be used while running the POST request in Step 9.
3. Microsoft requires the Sites.FullControl.All Graph application permission for the POST /sites/{siteId}/permissions request (in Step 9) to succeed. If this permission is not granted with admin consent before running the request, Graph Explorer will return a 403 Forbidden error indicating insufficient privileges or missing required permissions. For more details, see Microsoft Graph API documentation.
4. To grant the required permission, select the POST request for: the https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/sites/{siteId}/permissions Replace {siteId} with the ID retrieved earlier, but do not run the request yet.
5. With the POST request selected, go to the Modify permissions tab and click Open the permissions panel.
6. In the permissions panel, expand the Sites section and click Consent next to Sites.FullControl.All to grant access to the Mindtickle Entra application.
7. An admin consent dialog will appear. Review the details and click Accept to authorize access for the Mindtickle Entra application.
8. After consent is successfully granted, the button will change to Unconsent, indicating the permission is now active for the Mindtickle Entra application.
9. Now, assign the Mindtickle Entra app the required read permissions for the specific SharePoint site by sending the following POST request: Request URL : POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/sites/{siteId}/permissions Request body : { "roles": ["read"], "grantedToIdentities": [ { "application": { "id": "{Application Id}", "displayName": "{site name}" } } ] }
  - Request URL : Replace {siteId} with the ID retrieved in Step 2.
  - Request body : Replace {Application Id} with the Application (client) ID of your Mindtickle Entra app. Optionally, also replace {site name} with the name of your SharePoint site.
10. Repeat the POST request for each SharePoint site you want to sync with Mindtickle.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Automated Sync > Section 1B: Migrate existing SharePoint syncs to Entra ID:
If you have SharePoint syncs configured with the legacy Azure ACS app-only (client secret) authentication, they must be migrated to the new Entra ID certificate-based app-only authentication before April 2, 2026, when Microsoft retires ACS and these connections will stop working.

In the SharePoint sync settings in Mindtickle, you’ll see a Switch to new authentication option for each existing ACS-based connection. Selecting this option starts the migration flow, allowing you to reconfigure authentication using Entra ID.

Note: Each SharePoint account configured in Mindtickle (under Security & Integrations → Content Sync → SharePoint) requires its own certificate to authenticate with SharePoint via Entra ID. You need to generate and upload a certificate for each account being migrated. Since certificates are managed at the account (connection) level, multiple certificates can be uploaded to the same Entra ID application.

This section provides step-by-step guidance for updating your existing syncs so they continue functioning seamlessly. The migration process covers updating account details, generating and uploading certificates, and configuring permissions in Entra ID, while retaining your existing folder mappings and sync settings in Mindtickle.

Note: Once a sync has been migrated to Entra ID authentication, it cannot be reverted to ACS-based authentication.

Perform the following steps to migrate an ACS-based SharePoint sync to Entra ID authentication:

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Automated Sync > Section 2: Map folders and asset metadata:
After setting up your SharePoint account (new sync or migrated), you can choose which SharePoint folders to sync into Mindtickle. You can also optionally map asset metadata so that Mindtickle assets match SharePoint properties, helping keep your content organized and easier to find.

In this section, you’ll learn how to:

- Map folders : Select the SharePoint folders you want to sync.
- Map asset metadata : Optionally, configure metadata fields so that the metadata of your Mindtickle assets aligns with SharePoint data.

Perform the following steps to map folders and metadata:

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Automated Sync > Section 2: Map folders and asset metadata > Map folders:
1. In Mindtickle, navigate to Account → Security & integrations → Content Sync → SharePoint.

2. Click and select Edit for a configured account to open sync settings.

3. Open the Map folders and asset metadata section and click Add folder.

4. Enter the folder name and the nested folder in the SharePoint folder path.

- For tenant-level sync , enter the complete path. For example, https://mindtickle.sharepoint.com.
- For site-level sync , specify only the folder path. For example, if the folder path is “https://mindtickle.sharepoint.com/sites/TestSite/Shared Documents/Onboarding”, then enter “ /Shared Documents/Onboarding ”.
- Similarly for team site level sync , specify the only the folder path. For example, if the folder path is “https://mindtickle.sharepoint.com/teams/my-team-site/Shared Documents/Meeting Notes”, then enter “ /Shared Documents/Meeting Notes ”.

For information on entering the folder path, see How do I copy the SharePoint folder path.

The system does validation checks to ensure the folder path is valid in your SharePoint instance.

An error message displays if the validation fails. The error message mentions that the folder path is not in the corresponding SharePoint instance.

Note: When the first sync runs, the Content Center creates the SharePoint folder with the account name configured per the Account details section.

5. Click Add folder to add multiple folder paths.

Note:

- You can add a maximum of 50 folder paths.
- The folder path can have at most 9 levels of nested folders. Mindtickle does not sync content beyond 9 nested folders.
- You cannot configure the same folder path multiple times.
- You cannot configure a child folder for an already configured parent folder.
- Currently, SharePoint does not support syncing files and folders from OneNote.
- You must not add the same SharePoint folders to different accounts in Mindtickle.

- You cannot configure a child folder for an already configured parent folder.
- Currently, SharePoint does not support syncing files and folders from OneNote.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Automated Sync > Handling sync errors:
While configuring or running SharePoint sync in Mindtickle, you may encounter the following errors. This section explains the cause of each error and how to resolve it.

| Error message | Reason | Solution |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Certificate is missing, invalid, or expired. Please upload a valid one on the Azure portal. | The user has not uploaded a certificate to the Entra ID (formerly Azure AD) portal, or the existing certificate has expired. | Upload a valid certificate to the Entra ID (Azure AD) admin center portal. |
| Insufficient sync permissions for this SharePoint site. Change permissions or choose another site. | The SharePoint site does not have the required permissions. | Assign the necessary permissions through the Entra ID admin center. For site-specific syncs, use Site.Selected with Graph API permissions (via GET/POST calls). For syncing across the entire tenant, use Site.Read.All permission. |

Note: Always verify that the certificate and permissions align with your intended sync scope (site-specific vs tenant-wide) to avoid sync failures.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Automated Sync > Limitations:
A. SharePoint limitations

The following limitations specific to Microsoft SharePoint:

- Currently, SharePoint does not support syncing files and folders from OneNote.
- Mindtickle only supports SharePoint versions after 2016. This is due to incompatible APIs and changes in architecture in versions before 2016. Also, the SharePoint versions before 2016 lacked features such as hybrid deployments, communication sites, and PowerApps integration. These limitations cause errors and limit Mindtickle’s capability to sync seamlessly with SharePoint.
- The SharePoint versions before 2016 pose potential security risks. However, the latest SharePoint versions address any security vulnerabilities that may arise.
- SharePoint versions before 2016 did not support shortcut links within document libraries. However, later SharePoint versions support shortcuts (links to other libraries or files within the same site). The SharePoint sync with Mindtickle deals with syncing files and folders within documents. However, errors due to shortcut links lead to sync failure.
- Metadata associated with files, such as custom column names or values, may contain characters incompatible with Mindtickle. For example, column names with a space in their names do not sync with the Mindtickle platform.
- Incorrect user-level permissions, apart from those mentioned in Set up SharePoint authentication , lead to sync failure and prevent the account setup.
- Mindtickle recommends that clients provide details of their data set. The data set details ensure optimal migration planning.
- Synchronizing large files, such as videos or large data sets, can be slow and impact sync performance. Files also take a longer time to sync during limited bandwidth in networks. Syncing many files might require admins to trigger sync multiple times to fetch all the files.

B. General limitations

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Automated Sync > Limitations:
General limitations

Apart from the SharePoint limitations mentioned above, the following are the limitations related to content sync.

- Sync selection
  - Sync is possible only for folders within the SharePoint.
  - Sync does not apply to a single file or selection of files. You can only select folders for sync.
- Folder hierarchy
  - The selected folder for sync can have a maximum of 9 levels of nested folders under it.
- File and folder names
  - The special characters ‘/’ and ‘\’ are not supported in the file and folder names. The use of all other special characters is supported.
  - Though SharePoint supports files and folders with a max length of 400 characters, in Mindtickle, the file name cannot exceed the maximum limit of 250 characters.
- File size limitations
  - For details on supported file types and size limits for uploading and syncing content to Mindtickle, see this article .
- File types supported
  - For details on supported file types and size limits for uploading and syncing content to Mindtickle, see this article .
- File types not supported
  - For details on supported file types and size limits for uploading and syncing content to Mindtickle, see this article .

Syncing unsupported files in folders would result in partial sync failure. In that case, the sync would fail for the unsupported files. However, the valid files successfully sync. The sync failure error is available in the View Sync Log section.

Note: Mindtickle recommends removing unsupported files from the SharePoint folder before you start the Resync process.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Automated Sync > FAQs (frequently asked questions):
How do I find the SharePoint instance URL?

The SharePoint instance URL is available from the browser bar. The image below highlights the SharePoint instance URL.

How do I copy the SharePoint folder path?

There are two methods to copy the Sharepoint folder path.

a) Select the required folder and copy the folder URL.

b) Select the required folder and click the information icon. In the information panel, scroll to the bottom of the Activities section and click Path.

The folder path is automatically truncated in the Mindtickle while mapping the folder path.

What are the different types of validation failures while mapping a folder?

a) The folder path is invalid and unsupported for sync.

To resolve the error, check the folder path in SharePoint and copy the correct folder path.

b) The folder path is not available in SharePoint.

To resolve this error, check if the folder exists in the SharePoint repository. If the folder is not available in SharePoint, copy another folder path.

c) Configure an already existing folder path again.

To resolve this error, add a different folder path.

What can I do if I have more than 9 nested folders within the folder path configured to sync?

Instead of configuring the parent folder with more than 9 nested folders, configure its child folders so that none have more than 9 folders.

Alternatively, configure the parent folders in SharePoint so the configured folder does not have more than 9 nested folders.

Note: At a later point (after successfully activating the SharePoint connection), in the configured folders, if the admin breaches the limit of 9 nested folders and creates more nested folders, the content is not synced from the folder beyond 9-levels of the hierarchy.
