chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Best Practices and Use Cases > Best Practices for Mobile App > Content Best Practices:
- Powerpoints, PDFs, and Google slides
  - Readability - Use high-contrast colors and minimal text that is well-spaced and sized to read on mobile devices. Charts must be simple, easy to read, and include labels and keys.
  - Simplicity - avoid too much scrolling for the learner by breaking down content into multiple learning objects. Clickable content should have sufficient spacing.
- S CORM
  - Left/right swipe - swiping gestures to move to the next or previous slides in SCORM should be avoided as it will conflict with native gestures in Mindtickle.
  - Horizontal scrolling - may conflict with Mindtickle swipe gestures and should be avoided. Vertical scrolling is fully supported.
  - Drag and drop - avoid using touch and drag (or drag and drop) operations
  - Embedded files - Do not embed external files like PDFs, docs, spreadsheets, PPTs, etc, to be downloaded on the user’s device in SCORM. Most devices open the embedded file in full-screen web view; in such cases, the user cannot navigate back to the original SCORM content. We recommend using links to the file or adding files as separate learning objects in the Course or Quick Update.
  - Confirm if the SCORM content should play on the Mindtickle mobile app by selecting either In-line or Disable on mobile.
  - For all SCORM Content best practices, see SCORM Content .
- Videos
  - Use in-video questions to keep learners engaged and check for understanding.
- Videos and Audio
  - Picture -in-picture is available for iOS Mindtickle mobile app users.
  - Background playback is available for iOS and Android users.
  - Share with learners how to use picture-in-picture and background playback. For more information, see Picture-in-picture and background playback for media content (mobile app)Questions .
  - Mark the location - ensure there is sufficient space between the location markers.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Web Conferencing:
Mindtickle’s integration with the MS Teams video conferencing platform allows you to manage (create/update/delete) meetings and automate attendance tracking for your Instructor-Led Training (ILT) sessions. With this integration, when participants attend an ILT webinar conducted over MS Teams, their attendance is marked automatically.

The ILT-MS Teams integration automatically marks learners' attendance by matching email addresses in the MS Teams attendance report with the list of learners invited to the ILT module.

Note: If a learner’s email address is not listed in the MS Teams attendance report, their attendance is marked as Did not attend. (Admins can manually change the learner’s attendance status from the admin site.) This feature is available only on request. To enable it for your organization, contact Mindtickle Support or your Customer Success Manager (CSM).

For attendance tracking, you must fulfill the following conditions:

- Invite users to the ILT module
- Users must join the MS Teams meeting with the email address associated with their Mindtickle user ID

This article explains how you can set up the ILT-MS Teams integration.

Note:

- The ILT-MS Teams integration mandates admins to authenticate their MS Teams account in Mindtickle before creating MS Teams meetings in ILT sessions. This is a one-time configuration that needs to be done by every host*.
- Non-authenticated users cannot perform any host operations.

chunks.body:
Mindtickle’s integration with the MS Teams video conferencing platform allows you to manage (create/update/delete) meetings and automate attendance tracking for your Instructor-Led Training (ILT) sessions. With this integration, when participants attend an ILT webinar conducted over MS Teams, their attendance is marked automatically.

The ILT-MS Teams integration automatically marks learners' attendance by matching email addresses in the MS Teams attendance report with the list of learners invited to the ILT module.

Note: If a learner’s email address is not listed in the MS Teams attendance report, their attendance is marked as Did not attend. (Admins can manually change the learner’s attendance status from the admin site.) This feature is available only on request. To enable it for your organization, contact Mindtickle Support or your Customer Success Manager (CSM).

For attendance tracking, you must fulfill the following conditions:

- Invite users to the ILT module
- Users must join the MS Teams meeting with the email address associated with their Mindtickle user ID

This article explains how you can set up the ILT-MS Teams integration.

Note:

- The ILT-MS Teams integration mandates admins to authenticate their MS Teams account in Mindtickle before creating MS Teams meetings in ILT sessions. This is a one-time configuration that needs to be done by every host*.
- Non-authenticated users cannot perform any host operations.
- Meeting validations and auto-attendance are not tracked for those meetings in which the host is an unauthenticated user.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Web Conferencing > Use MS Teams integration in ILT sessions:
1. Create a new ILT session . Next, add an MS Teams meeting to the session. You can generate an MS Teams meeting from the session or manually enter the link of an existing MS Teams meeting.
2. To generate a meeting link from the session, in the Classroom/video conferencing details section, click the Classroom location dropdown and select Generate MS Teams meeting link . Note : While creating a meeting from the ILT session, ensure:
  - The session start and end time is set in the future.
  - The session time is more than 10 minutes. If your account is authenticated, the meeting link is generated, and the meeting details and host details are auto-filled in the Meeting Details section. If the meeting link is associated with the MS Teams account integrated with your Mindtickle account, the Auto attendance toggle is set to ON , indicating that the attendance for this meeting is automatically recorded. If your account is not authenticated, the system prompts you to authenticate your MS Teams account. Click Authenticate to validate your account. Enter your MS Teams registered email address on the Microsoft sign-in page and click Next . Enter the password and click Sign In . The following pop-up is displayed if a global administrator performs the authentication. Check the Consent on behalf of your organization checkbox and click Accept . The following pop-up is displayed if a non-admin user performs the authentication (and admin approval is needed). Enter the justification for requesting the consent. The request is sent via email to admins who are designated as reviewers. A reviewer takes action on the request, and the user is notified of the action. The following pop-up is displayed if a non-admin user performs the authentication (and admin approval is not needed). Click Accept to complete the authentication flow. Upon successful validation, you are redirected to the ILT session, and the meeting is created successfully. For more information, see Configure user consent, permissions, and API call details for ILT-MS Teams integration . Note :
    - The user authentication process is a one-time configuration required only the first time the user tries to generate an MS Teams meeting. Once completed successfully, you do not have repeat it.
    - Ensure that you have entered the correct credentials for MS Teams. For any issues, contact Mindtickle Support .
    - If the integration is not continuously used for 3 months, you must re-authorize it. Reauthorization might not be required if the integration is constantly used. Also, these tokens can be invalidated from MS Teams’ side before expiry in case of a change in the user's scope, password update, user deactivation from MS Teams, etc.
    - If the host token is expired, only the same host can perform reauthorization. Until then, the host’s meetings cannot be managed by anyone in Mindtickle. If you are an enablement admin (without host privileges), you can generate a meeting on behalf of an authenticated user. Click Enter host email ID . Enter the host’s (authenticated user’s) email address, and click Create meeting . The meeting link is generated, and the meeting and host details are auto-filled in the Meeting Details section. Note :
    - Suppose an authenticated admin with a valid MS Teams license attempts to create the meeting. The meeting is created successfully without the need to perform any additional steps.
    - Suppose an admin with a valid MS Teams license but not authenticated attempts to create the meeting. The system prompts the user for authentication before proceeding further.
    - If an admin without an MS Teams license attempts to create a meeting via a user with an MS Teams account that is not authenticated, the system prompts the admin for authentication. Once authenticated, the admin is redirected to the ILT page, and the meeting is created successfully.
    - If you enter the email address of a user who is not authenticated, the system prompts you to enter the details of a user with host permissions. For the integration to work successfully, the following scopes are requested by MS Teams: ScopeUsageoffline_accessMaintain access to data you have given it access toOnlineMeetingArtifact.Read.AllRead user’s online meeting artifactsOnlineMeetings.ReadWriteRead and create user’s online meetingsUser.ReadSign in and read user profile For more information on the API calls used in the integration, see Configure user consent, permissions, and API call details for ILT-MS Teams integration .
3. To add an existing meeting manually, enter the meeting link in the Enter location or meeting link field. Note :
  - If the meeting is created using an account with ‘host’ privileges, the system checks the URL for MS Teams auto-attendance eligibility. If eligible, the Auto attendance toggle appears and is automatically switched on.
  - If the meeting is created from an account that doesn’t have ‘host’ privileges, the system prompts you to authenticate the MS Teams account or enter a user's email address with ‘host’ privileges.
  - If the session type is set to Classroom location and you manually enter the URL of an MS Teams meeting, the session type changes to Enter meeting link . The system checks the URL for MS Teams auto-attendance eligibility. If eligible, the Auto attendance toggle appears and is automatically switched on.
4. You can add co-hosts to the meeting. Co-hosts help improve meeting productivity. The ‘co-host’ role has permissions similar to the ‘host’ role. If the host is running late or cannot attend, a co-host can start and manage the meeting. Co-hosts can also assist the host with meeting management, which is helpful for larger meetings. Click Add co-host , enter the user’s email address, and click Save . Note : If the details of users added as co-hosts are invalid, a failure message is displayed on the screen indicating that the users were not added as co-hosts to the meeting. The user is added as a co-host to the meeting. Click to edit the details or to remove the user as a co-host from the meeting. Alternatively, you can add instructors or facilitators and assign them as co-hosts for the meeting. To assign an instructor or facilitator as a co-host, enter their details on the Instructors and Facilitators tab and select the Add as meeting co-host checkbox. The users are added to the list of co-hosts. N ote :
  - There is no limit to the number of co-hosts you can add to a meeting.
  - If an instructor or facilitator is added or removed as a co-host from the meeting, they receive an email notification with all session change details (if applicable). The email is sent after the session is published.
  - All the meeting links that belong to the authenticated hosts’ MS Teams account on Mindtickle are eligible for auto attendance.
  - If the Auto attendance toggle is switched off, you must mark the attendance manually or via session check-in.
  - The check-in feature is unavailable for sessions where auto attendance is enabled. To use the check-in feature, disable auto attendance.
5. Configure the remaining settings and click Create session . A confirmation message is displayed on the screen once the session is created successfully. The session appears in the list of sessions. The attendance mode of the session is listed as Auto attendance . Click the session to view or edit details.
6. Publish the session and invite learners. Once the session ends, participants’ attendance is marked automatically via MS Teams. Note :
  - Learners must be enrolled in a session or invited to the ILT module to capture attendance via auto-attendance.
  - Attendance is captured for a meeting link added manually by the enablement team (if it is for the same account linked to the Mindtickle platform).
  - Auto-attendance does not apply to meetings where the host is not authenticated or is a non-Mindtickle user.
  - To ensure the MS Teams meeting is compatible with ILT, you must create an additional user account (of the host) in Mindtickle.
  - Auto-attendance applies only to users invited to the ILT module or enrolled in the session.
  - Auto-attendance applies only to MS Teams meetings held at the specified time in Mindtickle.
    - Admins must ensure that the session start and end times are not updated on MS Teams once the session is created in Mindtickle. If the times are updated, they should sync with the Mindtickle session.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Web Conferencing > Use MS Teams integration in ILT sessions > Duration-based attendance capture:
Admins can set a minimum percentage threshold to record learners’ attendance for ILT modules and individual sessions using the Duration-based attendance capture feature.

This feature automatically records learners’ attendance based on their time in ILT events and sessions.

When participants attend an ILT Webinar conducted over MS Teams, their attendance is marked automatically. The MS Teams integration provides the time spent by the learner in a session.

The Webex integration provides the time spent by the learner in a session.

The system calculates an ILT session’s minimum attendance threshold as follows,

- Scheduled sessions: For scheduled sessions that are yet to start, the system calculates the minimum attendance threshold using the session's start and end time set during session creation. For example, in a 60-minute session with a 20% minimum attendance threshold, the system marks the learner as attended if they spend at least 12 minutes (20% of 60) in the session.
- Completed sessions: If a session ends early or extends beyond the scheduled time, the system calculates the minimum attendance threshold based on the actual session time. For example, for a 60-minute session with a 20% minimum attendance threshold, if the session ends early in 50 minutes, the system marks the learner as attended if they spend at least 10 minutes (20% of 50) in the session.

The system compares the learners’ time in session provided by MS Teams with the session’s minimum attendance threshold to mark the learner's attendance for the session.

The learner’s attendance status and time spent in sessions are displayed in the Attendance status/Duration column on the Events and Sessions tab of the ILT.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Web Conferencing > Use MS Teams integration in ILT sessions > Caveats:
- If you discard the meeting without saving the changes, MS Teams meeting details are deleted from the session, and the session type is reset to the Classroom location . The meeting is deleted from MS Teams as well.
- If a meeting that has ended is restarted (the host restarts it or a participant joins), we get the attendance details of only the participants from the latest instance of the meeting, and the data for participants from all previous meeting instances is lost.
- If an instructor marked as a co-host is removed, the user is removed from the MS Teams meeting co-host list.
- If you copy a session in which an MS Teams meeting is configured, the session type is reset to the Classroom location in the copied session.
- Suppose you copy the ILT module in a different series that includes a session (or multiple sessions) in which MS Teams meetings are configured. In that case, the session type for the copied sessions is reset to the Classroom location .

| Scenario | Meeting start time | Meeting end time | Attendance in Mindtickle |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| The host starts the meeting early to check if the meeting link is accessible. | 2:15 pm | 2:16 pm | No |
| The learner joins the meeting early before the host joins the meeting. | 2:25 pm | 2:35 pm | No |
| The host starts the meeting early, and the session ends in 45 minutes instead of 1 hour. | 2:45 pm | 3:45 pm | Yes |
| The learner joins the meeting in the last few minutes. | 3:55 pm | 4:00 pm | Yes |
| The host starts the meeting early, and the session extends beyond the scheduled meeting time by 15 minutes. | 2:55 pm | 4:15 pm | Yes |
| The host starts the meeting early and it extends 40 minutes beyond the scheduled meeting time. | 2:55 pm | 4:40 pm | Yes |
| The learner starts the meeting late after the meeting ends. | 4:25 pm | 4:26 pm | Yes |
| The learner starts the meeting late after the meeting ends. | 4:25 pm | 4:32 pm | Yes |
| The learner starts the meeting late after the meeting ends. | 4:35 pm | 4:40 pm | No |

Mindtickle combines the attendance reports from all valid meeting instances for attendance calculation. For example, if 10 users join the meeting in the first half-hour and 5 (with 3 overlapping users) join in the second half-hour, the attendance is marked only for 12 users.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Web Conferencing > Disable the integration:
You can disable the MS Teams integration by performing the following steps:

1. On the Mindtickle admin site homepage , click Account and select Settings .
2. On the Settings page, click the Security & integrations tab.
3. Under the Security & integrations tab, scroll down to the Web Conferencing section. Under MS Teams , click the checkbox to disable the integration.
4. Click Yes in the confirmation prompt. The MS Teams integration is disabled successfully.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Web Conferencing > FAQs:
Q: If I have already created an MS Teams meeting, can I add it to the ILT session in Mindtickle? Will attendance still be marked?A: Yes, you can add the MS Teams meeting URL. Once you have authenticated your account, the session is eligible for auto-attendance.

Q: What do I do if I am not hosting the meeting but I am setting it up for the host?A: Create the ILT session. When creating the MS Teams meeting from the session, click Enter host email id on the first pop-up that appears.Enter the host’s email address in the next pop-up and click Create meeting.Or, click Authenticate your MS Teams account to authenticate a new account.And enter the host’s email ID on the pop-up.If your account is authenticated, the meeting is generated with you as the host. You may then add the actual host as the co-host.

Q: What if an ILT participant attends the session only for a few minutes? Are they marked as attended?A: Learner attendance depends on the session’s attendance threshold and the learner’s time spent in the session. For more information on configuring the minimum attendance threshold, see Duration-based attendance capture for learners in ILTs.

For example, if a one-hour session has a 30-minute (50%) minimum attendance threshold, the system marks the participants who attend for 30 minutes or more as attended.

If a session has no minimum attendance threshold, the system marks the attendance of the participant even if they join the session for only a minute. The system does not mark attendance for participants who attend the session for less than 30 minutes, for example, 10 minutes.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Best Practices and Use Cases > Best Practices for Asset Hub > Overview:
Let’s understand why a communication strategy is critical to successfully launching Asset Hub. Strong communication efforts with your team and your entire organization make facilitating change easier, resulting in higher engagement and adoption.

Like other product or feature launches, launching Asset Hub launch is requires careful attention to align your development and planning efforts with your communication strategy.

A collaborative communication strategy for your entire organization would make it more accessible to achieve the objectives, such as

1. Outreach
2. Engagement
3. Adoption
4. Involvement
5. Positive results

Relaying the pertinent information and providing training, if necessary, will enable everyone in the organization to use Asset Hub effectively.

Note: This document lists ways to orchestrate communication for the launch of Asset Hub effectively. You can choose from the multiple options listed here depending on the bandwidth, resources, and on-ground feasibility of the implementation.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Best Practices and Use Cases > Best Practices for Asset Hub > Challenges:
One of the biggest challenges faced by organizations is surfacing the right content or assets across different teams and user personas.

Why?

Organizations face challenges with the collateral and assets in more ways than one, for example:

1. Surfacing the right content at the right time
2. Ability to view consumption and progress of assets with dashboards
3. Update documents with the most recent trends and content
4. Providing advanced searching capabilities for quick accessibility

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Best Practices and Use Cases > Best Practices for Enablement > Deep Dive into best practices::
- Courses in Mindtickle should be designed to balance the depth of content with learner engagement. The ideal length for a course varies based on factors like the complexity of the topic, the audience, and the intended learning outcomes. However, as a general guideline:
  - Microlearning Modules: Create courses with shorter modules that focus on specific learning objectives. Each module should be concise, typically 5-15 minutes in length. Shorter modules are easier to digest and retain, leading to higher engagement.
  - Chunking Content: Divide longer courses into smaller, logically organized sections. This allows learners to consume content in manageable portions, increasing retention and engagement.
  - Learning Paths: Arrange courses in learning paths, guiding learners through modules. A learning path could span several weeks or months, but individual modules should remain relatively short.
  - Assessments: Include quizzes or knowledge checks at the end of each module to reinforce learning and ensure comprehension.
- Quick updates in Mindtickle are designed for timely, focused communication. The primary goal is to provide learners with concise, actionable information.
  - Short and Snappy: Quick updates should be brief and to the point. A typical quick update should not exceed 2-3 minutes in length.
  - Frequency: Quick updates are often delivered regularly. Consistency is key for learner engagement. You can send quick updates daily, weekly, or as needed, but ensure they remain concise.
  - Actionable Content: Each quick update should have a clear, actionable message. Learners should understand what action to take after watching the update, whether it's a product update, policy change, or a sales tip.
  - Feedback Mechanism: Enable feedback options for learners to respond to quick updates with questions or comments. This encourages engagement and clarifies any uncertainties.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Best Practices and Use Cases > Best Practices for Enablement > General Best Practices for Engagement and Adoption:
- Personalization: Tailor content to the specific needs and preferences of your learners. Mindtickle allows you to segment your audience and provide customized content based on roles, departments, or individual interests.
- Interactivity: Use interactive elements such as quizzes, surveys, and discussions to engage learners. This makes the learning experience more dynamic and engaging.
- Progress Tracking: Enable progress tracking to allow learners to monitor their advancement through modules and courses. Knowing their progress can motivate learners to complete modules.
- Feedback Mechanisms: Encourage learners to provide feedback on the content. Act on this feedback to continuously improve the quality and relevance of your modules and quick updates.
- Gamification: Consider gamification elements such as badges, points, and leaderboards to make the learning experience more enjoyable and competitive. For more information, see Creating Meaningful Badge Strategies.
- Mobile Accessibility: Ensure your modules and quick updates are accessible and optimized for mobile devices. This flexibility allows learners to engage with content on the go.

By following these best practices, you can create modules in Mindtickle that are engaging, effective, and conducive to high adoption rates among your learners. Remember to regularly analyze engagement metrics and gather learner feedback to fine-tune your content and delivery methods for maximum impact.

About the Content Center–SharePoint syncWith Mindtickle Content Center’s automated content sync for SharePoint, you can automatically sync SharePoint files and folders in the Content Center. For every configured SharePoint account, Content Center automatically creates a root folder, where all the synced folders from the SharePoint account are made available. Content updates to the SharePoint source file are seamlessly reflected in the Content Center. Additionally, the synced content gets automatically updated across all instances where it has been utilized, such as in modules, assets, and digital sales rooms (DSRs).

2. Integrate SharePoint with Mindtickle — Help article
3. Map Mindtickle assets metadata with SharePoint — Help article
4. Manage the integration and sync settings — Help article
5. View and manage SharePoint content in Content Center — Help article

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Automated Sync > Introduction:
A prerequisite for setting up SharePoint content sync with Mindtickle is that the SharePoint admin must authenticate SharePoint. The authentication process includes generating the Client ID and Client Secret. This process needs to be performed by the Sharepoint admin. While setting up the SharePoint connection on the Mindtickle platform, admins must enter the Client ID and Client Secret key.

The SharePoint content sync is a one-way content sync from SharePoint to Mindtickle. You can sync either at the tenant-level or at the site-level depending on whether you want to provide access to all sites or an individual site:

- Tenant-level sync: When you want to sync and provide access to the folders and files of all SharePoint sites within the tenant.
- Site-level sync: When you want to sync and provide access to the folders and files of an individual SharePoint site within the tenant.
  - SharePoint team sites are also supported.

Important: The content sync with SharePoint is currently not supported at the subsite level; folders within a subsite are not synced.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Automated Sync > Introduction > Important note on authentication:
Mindtickle currently supports SharePoint content sync authentication using the app-only method via Azure ACS. ACS will be deprecated by Microsoft on April 2, 2026, but Mindtickle will continue supporting this authentication method until migration to the new method is complete.

In the coming months, we will transition to the new, recommended authentication method via Azure AD registered apps (Microsoft Entra ID). Customers will receive advance notifications and step-by-step guidance for migrating to the new authentication method.

Key points about the upcoming authentication migration:

- Current support : Customers can continue using the legacy (app-only via ACS) authentication method without disruption.
- Simple credential update during migration : The migration process will involve a straightforward update of credentials via Mindtickle’s admin panel.
- Minimal permissions : The new method will require only the minimum necessary permissions for accessing SharePoint APIs.
- Zero downtime : Updating credentials will not disrupt or cause downtime for your existing integration.
- Dual Support : Both legacy (ACS) and new (Azure AD via Entra ID) authentication methods will be supported simultaneously during the transition period. Note : Simultaneous use of both methods for the same site will not be supported.
  - Sites authenticated using the legacy method will continue to sync without interruption.
  - For re-authentication or new integration setups, only the new method (Azure AD via Entra ID) will be supported.
  - Once authenticated with the new method, your existing syncs will continue to work seamlessly.

We are committed to clear, proactive communication throughout the transition to ensure a smooth migration experience.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Automated Sync > Introduction:
The metadata sheet contains the properties of Mindtickle assets and attributes created for that learning site till that point in time. Admins can then map the corresponding SharePoint properties. After filling out the metadata sheet, admins must upload that file to Mindtickle.

When the automated sync job runs, based on the metadata mapping, it fetches the metadata properties from SharePoint and populates them in the Mindtickle assets. The mapped properties are in read-only format in the Mindtickle assets. To edit any mapped asset property within Mindtickle, keep the asset property value blank in the metadata mapping sheet and re-upload the .csv file.

Automated metadata sync helps to improve the admin's efficiency as they do not have to manually update the asset properties in Mindtickle.

Note: Adding the metadata details is a one-time setup to map the asset data. However, editing the synced account details updates the metadata details.

To add the metadata details:

1. In the admin site sidebar, click Account > Settings > Security & Integrations.On the Security & Integrations page, scroll down to the Content Sync section and click the SharePoint tab.

2. Under SharePoint, click Add account to get started.

3. On the Add account modal, enter the Account details and navigate to Map folders and asset metadata.

4. After entering the folder details, click the Map asset metadata toggle to enable the mapping of Mindtickle’s assets metadata to SharePoint.

5. Click Download metadata.

The .csv file containing the metadata template, the asset properties and the asset attributes of your learning site gets downloaded to your local computer.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Automated Sync > Introduction:
csv file containing the metadata template, the asset properties and the asset attributes of your learning site gets downloaded to your local computer.

Open the downloaded file in Microsoft Excel or a similar tool to map the SharePoint properties.

The template lists all the asset properties and attributes in Mindtickle for the particular learning site.

Note: Do not update the data in the columns:

- Type
- Property/Attribute ID (Mindtickle)
- Property/Attribute Value (Mindtickle)
- Property/Attribute Description (Mindtickle)
- Attribute Category (Mindtickle)

6. Enter the mapping details in the below columns:

- Property/Attribute ID (SharePoint)
- Property/Attribute Value (SharePoint)

Note:

- The property identifier names are case-sensitive. Do not add spaces in the property identifier name.
- Filling the data for all the properties and attributes is not mandatory.
- SharePoint does not map empty property fields to Mindtickle.
- Admins can edit the blank property manually in Mindtickle.
- When the metadata sheet is uploaded, these mapped properties and attribute values automatically populate in the synced asset. On the asset, the mapped properties are in read-only format.
- Do not add new rows or delete any existing rows in the .csv file.
- SharePoint does not map multiple fields to a single asset property.

For the complete SharePoint column types (properties and attributes) list, click Add column > Select all column types > Next.

The Create Column page displays all the properties and attributes in SharePoint.

Currently, Mindtickle supports limited SharePoint ColumnType.

- For Property mapping, 4 ColumnTypes are supported.
  - Single line of text
  - Choice (menu to choose from)
  - Date and Time
  - Yes/No (check box)

- For Attribute mapping, the ColumnType supported is Managed Metdata .

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Automated Sync > Frequently asked questions (FAQs):
What happens if you do not map the asset properties?

The asset properties do not get synced from SharePoint. The admins can edit the corresponding asset properties in Mindtickle.

Can I create (add and delete) rows in the downloaded metadata file?

Mindtickle recommends not adding and deleting rows from the downloaded metadata .csv file. Only add the mapping for the required properties. Refrain from creating new rows in the downloaded metadata file. If you do not want to sync specific properties from SharePoint, leave the properties empty.

What happens if the mapping is incorrect?

When the mapping is incorrect, the data from SharePoint to Mindtickle does not sync. The property identifier names are case-sensitive. Do not add spaces in the property identifier name. In the case of incorrect mappings, the sync does not fail, but the incorrect and unsupported mappings are ignored.

Can I update the mapping later?

Yes. You can upload the .csv file again to update the mapping. Once you update the mapping, it affects all the existing assets as per the changes made in the mapping. The mapped properties are then displayed on the asset in Mindtickle. You can edit the unmapped properties of the asset in Mindtickle.

If you update the .csv sheet:

- For properties previously unmapped but now mapped - In Mindtickle, you cannot edit the property values. The values of the properties are displayed in read-only format.
- For properties previously mapped but now unmapped - These properties are no longer updated via sync in SharePoint. You can edit the property values in Mindtickle.

If you disable the asset metadata sync, asset properties no longer sync. However, the values for asset properties remain intact. You can edit the asset properties in Mindtickle.

You can edit the asset properties in Mindtickle.

Can Customized Asset Creation properties can be synced?

Yes. The metadata mapping sheet includes 4 rows to define customization options:

- allowMixAndMatch = TRUE → Users can mix and match slides from this asset when creating customized assets.
- allowMixAndMatch = FALSE → Users cannot mix and match slides from this asset.
- allowEditingContent = TRUE → Users can edit the asset content when creating customized assets, through Microsoft Office for the web (PowerPoint, Word, and Excel) or Google Workspace (Slides, Docs, and Sheets).
- allowEditingContent = FALSE → Users cannot edit the asset content.

Once this property is synced:

- It becomes read-only inside Mindtickle (as with other synced asset properties).
- Any changes to the properties must be made in the source (SharePoint or AEM).
- Synced values automatically populate for assets during creation or update; otherwise, the default is No .

To access the Asset Hub, sign in to the Admin Site homepage and click the Assets tab on the top header.

On the homepage, you can view assets with the following cloud icons:

- Indicates that the sync was successful from SharePoint.
- Indicates that the sync is in progress from SharePoint.
- Indicates that the sync has failed.
- Indicates that the sync has temporarily paused. You can pause the sync using the Account Settings page.

Navigate to the hub and click Add asset. On the New asset pop-up, click Select file to upload an asset. You can either upload an existing file from the Content Center or upload a new file using one of the following options:

- Embed links from YouTube, Slideshare, and so on

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Web Conferencing > Configure user content settings:
To configure user consent settings through the Microsoft Entra admin center:

1. Sign in to the Microsoft Entra admin center as a Global Administrator .
2. Browse Identity > Applications > Enterprise applications > Consent and permissions > User consent settings .
3. Under User consent for applications , select which consent setting you want to configure for all users. If you select Do not allow user content , admin consent is required to complete the authentication flow. Users can request admin approval hen they try to authenticate the integration but cannot provide consent. The request is sent via email to admins who have been designated as reviewers. A reviewer takes action on the request, and the user is notified of the action. In this case, ensure that you first configure the admin consent workflow . The admin consent workflow gives admins a secure way to grant access to applications that require admin approval. If you select Allow user consent for apps , all users can allow consent for any application to access the organization’s data. We recommend selecting Allow user content for apps from verified publishers for selected permissions . This reduces the risk of malicious applications attempting to trick users into granting them access to your organization's data. The permission set needed to authenticate is configured by default as part of this setting.
4. Click Save to save your settings. Based on the user consent settings configured, the authentication flow ( see Installation and Configuration ) is processed and completed. Note : To revoke the permissions, see Review permissions granted to enterprise applications .

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Asset Hub > Admin:
With the Manage required properties setting under the hub settings, admins can configure certain asset properties as mandatory (required) for assets and plays in a specific hub. The required properties are configured at the hub level, which ensures that all assets in the hub are compliant in terms of the mandatory properties. Once you have configured one or more properties as required for a hub, reps would need to fill in these properties while creating assets in this hub or editing their properties. All required properties are indicated with an asterisk (*).

Through required properties, you can define and maintain hub-level policies for all assets and plays across the platform. This lets you enforce compliance and consistency among all assets. Furthermore, it ensures that hub collaborators working on assets in a certain hub or across the platform are compliant in terms of the mandatory properties of each hub.

Note: While the article provides information on the mandatory properties for assets, the information is also applicable for plays.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Asset Hub > Admin > Mandatory properties:
- Asset owner: The asset owner is responsible for maintaining the asset. By default, Asset Hub populates the creator of the asset as the asset owner. You can choose any user as the asset owner who is a collaborator and has the “ Develop and Publish Assets ” permission for one of the hubs where the asset resides. This ensures that the asset owner always has the permissions to edit the asset.
- Attribute categories: Attribute categories are used to group or categorize related attributes together.
- Description: Provides a brief explanation of what the asset is all about. Description conveys valuable information that helps viewers spot an asset in search results and indicate the type of content in the asset. It also guides the sales rep on which asset to use.
- Expiration date: Setting an expiration date ensures the effectiveness of the assets. It is useful for assets that are valid for a specific period. Assets with an expiry date convey that the information in the asset is reliable and up-to-date.. Once an asset expires, you can either update the asset and extend its expiry date or archive it. Expired assets are still visible to the sales reps but flagged as Expired.
- Expiration reminder: Expiry reminder reminds you to update the asset before its expiry date or archive if it is no longer needed. Expiration reminder or file update reminder helps keep your organization compliant by automatically tracking expiration date for assets, such as team member certifications, contracts, licenses, and marketing campaigns. Note: This property is available for use only when the “Expiration date” is marked as a required (mandatory) property.
- File update reminder: These reminders will notify the asset owners to update the asset at periodic cycles. If no asset owner is assigned, the hub collaborators will receive notifications.

1. Select one or more properties that you want to configure as required (mandatory) and then click Save changes. Note: You can change the mandatory properties for a hub at any time. The latest changes will apply to all existing and new assets in the hub.
2. While you select properties to configure them as mandatory, a message may appear indicating that the required properties (configured by you) are missing their values or details in the existing assets for this hub. That is, one or more mandatory properties are empty in these assets. You can click View assets to view the list of all such assets. It opens the hub homepage > Assets tab, with the Required properties missing filter set to Yes and applied automatically.For more information, see the “View assets with mandatory properties missing” section.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Asset Hub > Admin > View assets with missing properties:
This section explains how to view the assets where the required properties (configured by you) are missing their values or details. That is, one or more mandatory properties are empty in these assets. You can view a list of such assets from a particular hub (the hub homepage) and across hubs (Assets tab main homepage). You can also view the details when you open any asset.

Perform the following to view the assets for which the values for the mandatory properties are missing or empty:

1. On a hub’s homepage, click the Assets tab. Under More filters, select the Required properties missing filter and set it to Yes to view the list of assets for which at least one required (mandatory) property is missing values or details. This filter makes it easier for the admin to quickly identify and correct these assets.

1. Assets for which the values of the required properties are missing are indicated with th e icon. Hover over the icon to view the list of mandatory properties that are missing their details in a pop-up. For mirrored assets, the pop-up lists the properties missing in the current hub and the other hubs where it is mirrored. Make sure to scroll inside the pop-up to view all the details.

1. In addition to the hub homepage tab, you can also view assets with missing required properties on the Assets page.

1. Similarly, when you click any asset and open it, the asset page also highlights the required properties that are not filled in.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Asset Hub > Admin > View assets with missing properties > Filters for mandatory properties:
On the hub homepage > Assets tab, you can use the following three filters under More filters that are specifically for the mandatory properties: Required properties missing, Expiration, and File update reminder.

The following filters are available for mandatory properties:

- Required properties missing: Lists all assets where at least one of configured mandatory properties are missing. This is a general filter and applicable for all mandatory properties. You can also use the Expiration and File update reminder filters that provide details specific to their respective mandatory properties.
- Expiration: This filter allows you to sort assets based on their current expiration settings. You can display assets that have no expiration date, only an expiration date, or both an expiration date and reminders. Select one or more of the following filter values: No expiration, Only expiration date, and Expiration date and reminder.
- File update reminder: This filter lets you sort assets based on their file update reminder settings. Select one or more of the following filter values: No reminder, Every week, Every 2 weeks, Every month, Every 3 months, Every 6 months, and Every year.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Asset Hub > Admin > Update missing properties:
You can update the missing values for the mandatory properties for a hub at any time. When creating a new asset or editing an existing asset, details for the mandatory properties must be provided before the asset can be published or saved respectively.

To update the missing properties for any asset, open the asset and click Properties > Edit.

The Properties pop-up appears, where you can edit the asset properties. Mandatory or required properties are indicated with an asterisk (*). You can save your changes only after entering the values or details for all the mandatory (required) properties marked with an asterisk (*). Similarly, while creating a new asset for a hub where mandatory properties are configured, you cannot publish the asset until you enter the values for all the mandatory properties.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Asset Hub > Admin > Update missing properties > Update properties in bulk:
Admins can update one or more mandatory properties for multiple assets at once using bulk actions. Updating properties in bulk is particularly useful when a large number of assets are missing a specific property that is common across assets. Or when a new property is set as mandatory for a hub that already contains assets.

Perform the following to update the mandatory properties in bulk:

1. Ensure that you have applied the Required properties missing filter (set to Yes ) so that the Assets tabs lists only those assets where the mandatory properties are empty. You can also use the Expiration and File update reminder filters to update these specific properties.
2. Select one or more assets for which you want to update the mandatory properties.
3. Click Edit properties bottom tray. The property editing pop-up appears where you can provide the missing value for each missing property so that the same value is added to all selected assets for that specific property. Note: You can update all properties in bulk, except the description because the description is usually unique for each asset.
4. You can view the status of this action in Notifications , available in the header. Once it is completed, you can view details about each action (property update) for each asset.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Asset Hub > Admin:
Widgets are no longer tied to a single page type. Using the Page Builder, you can add widgets from different families across your learning site, so you can build a consistent experience whether a learner lands on a homepage, a series overview page, a hub overview page, or a play. In particular:

- You can use series widgets on hub overview pages and plays, in addition to series overview pages.
- You can use asset widgets on series overview pages, in addition to hub overview pages and plays.
- You can use both series widgets and asset widgets on learning site homepages, alongside the general and Call AI widgets.

Not every widget is available on every page, and a few behave differently depending on the page. The availability matrix below shows exactly which widgets you can add to each page type, followed by a short description of each widget.

Note: Hub overview pages and plays support the same set of widgets, so they are shown together in a single column. A play is a type of asset (similar to a sales play), and its overview page is built the same way as a hub overview page.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Reference > System logs for download and export of reports:
Analytics users can download and export the reports available under Analytics on the admin site and under Team analytics on the learning site. We have enhanced the functionality of audit logs of reports across analytics: for admins on the admin site and for managers on the learning site.

When an admin or a manager downloads or exports a report, this activity is logged and can be accessed from the UI under Systems logs.

On a report page, the user can use the Download/Export button to download or export the report in multiple formats:

- Download As: Click to download a partial report in a format of your choice: PDF, XLSX, XLS, or CSV. Note: This will download only summarized data as displayed on the UI. For complete data, use “Export”.
- Export: The detailed report with complete data in a CSV format is sent to the email address provided by you.

Under System logs on the admin site, admins can view the audit logs and email logs for data on which users downloaded and exported the reports and when:

- Audit logs: Contain logs for analytics report downloads
- Email logs: Contain logs for analytics report exports

See the following sections for details.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Reference > System logs for download and export of reports > Audit logs for report downloads:
Perform the following to view the audit logs for all the reports downloaded by the users in your organization, such as admins and managers:

1. In the admin site sidebar, click Account > System logs.

1. The System logs homepage appears. You can view both Audit logs and Email logs here.
2. Under the Audit logs tab, apply the Filter by event type > User downloaded analytics report filter. With this filter, the page displays only the logs related to downloading of analytics reports.
3. Click on any event (log) in the Event details column to view details about it.

1. The Event details pop-up provides all the helpful details.

1. Click Export logs to export the filtered log data. You can export up to 50,000 logs at once. The audit log data is exported in a CSV file to the email address provided by you. The CSV file is made available via a link sent in the email and it expires in 7 days.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Reference > System logs for download and export of reports > Email logs for report exports:
Perform the following to view the email logs for all the reports exported by the users in your organization, such as admins and managers:

1. Under Account > System logs, click Email logs to view report export related logs. You can identify logs related to exported reports from the Subject column. The email subject will be something like: Members detailed report for <report page>.

1. Click on the log entry to view a preview of the email that was sent to a recipient by the user. You can click Download Report in the email preview to download the report that the user sent to the recipient. However, please note that the report can be downloaded within 7 days from the date when it was sent. You would not be able to download the report from here after 7 days.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle University > What's New in Mindtickle > How to get started:
All admins have access to Mindtickle University and can access it through the URL university.mindtickle.com.

If you find that you do not have access or your want to add another admin from your organization, reach out to us at enablement@mindtickle.com.

Note: You cannot be signed in to 2 Mindtickle instances in the same browser. To use Mindtickle University, use a different browser or use the private browsing mode in your current browser, through a new Incognito window (Chrome) / Private window (Safari) / InPrivate window (Edge).

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle University > What's New in Mindtickle > How to sign up and sign in:
Method A: Using a different browser: Perform the following to sign up using a different browser:

1. Open a different browser. For example, if you usually use Chrome, open up Edge or Safari to access Mindtickle University. See this article for information on supported browsers.
2. Go to: https://university.mindtickle.com .
3. Select Create account or password .
4. Sign up with your company username (email ID) and activate your account.
5. Once you have signed in, start exploring!

Method B: Using the private browsing mode: Perform the following to sign up using the private browsing mode in your current browser:

1. Top open the private browsing mode, right-click on your browser icon and select the option to open an Incognito window (Chrome), Private window (Safari), or InPrivate window (Edge) to access Mindtickle University. Tip: You can use a keyboard shortcut to quickly open the private browsing mode. See your browser's documentation for information on the shortcuts.
2. Go to: https://university.mindtickle.com .
3. Select Create account or password .
4. Sign up with your company username (email ID) and activate your account.
5. Once you have signed in, start exploring!

For more instructions on how to sign up and sign in, read the How to sign in to Mindtickle as a learner or reviewer article.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Communications > Notifications and Reminders:
This article explains how to select an email template while configuring the email notification settings in series and modules. The selected email templates are used for sending different types of emails to learners, such as invitation and reminder emails.

Important:

- The new experience of selecting templates is available only for series and the course, quick update, assessment, and ILT modules. The rest of the modules (checklist, quest, mission, coaching session, and competency assessment) will continue to have the old experience.
- The template selection functionality works in the same way across other modules and series. This article provides instructions for a course module as an example. You can use these steps to select templates in other modules as well as series.

The following list provides information on where the email notification setting is located in series and modules. Under this setting, you can select the template for each kind of email setting.

- Series: Settings > Notifications
- Modules
  - Course: Settings > Due date and reminders
  - Quick update: Settings > Due date and reminders
  - Assessment: Settings > Due date and emails
  - ILT: Settings > Emails and notifications

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Communications > Notifications and Reminders > Configure email templates:
Perform the following to configure (select) the email templates that will be used while sending emails to learners. As mentioned above, these instructions use course as an example:

1. Navigate to the course module in a series and click the Settings tab > Due date and reminders.

1. Under Emails for the learner, you can configure four types of emails for learners. T hese are based on the learner’s progress status on the module:
  - Invited: Sends the invitation email when learners are invited to the module.
  - Did not start: Sends the reminder email when learners have not yet started the module. Additionally, you can use the Repeat after X days/weeks option to send repeating reminder emails by configuring the recurrence cadence. See this section for details.You can also use the Add reminder option to configure additional reminder emails.
  - In progress: Sends the reminder email when learners have not yet started the module.Additionally, you can use the Repeat after X days/weeks option to send repeating reminder emails by configuring the recurrence cadence. See this section for details.You can also use the Add reminder option to configure additional reminder emails.
  - Completed: Sends the completion email when learners complete the module.
2. In the Email template column, click the pencil button for an email type to get started with selecting a template.
3. The Select email template pop-up page appears, where you can view a list of available templates, preview them, and then select one.The following screenshot provides an overview of the available functionalities. Core functionalities are explained in blue while additional functionalities are in green.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Communications > Notifications and Reminders > Configure email templates:
1. In the scrollable template list, you can view all of your templates. Click a template to view its preview on the right. Click Use this email to select the template. Here are all the actions you can take on the Select email template page:
  - Find a template: The default/system is selected by default. However, you can select any template. Use the filter, sort, and search options to find a template of your choice:
    - Use the All categories filter to view templates for a specific category.
    - Use the Most used sort to sort the list by usage (highest to lowest) or alphabetically (A to Z or Z to A). The number against each template indicates the number of times the template is selected (in module settings) across all modules in your Mindtickle instance. Templates selected for use in more modules will have a higher usage count.
    - Use the search option to quickly find a template.
  - Disable notifications: If you want to disable email notifications, you can use the None option in the template list and then click Save. Search for "None" to quickly find this option.
  - Template details: In the header above the preview, you can view the following details:
    - Template name. Hover over theinformation icon to view the template description in a tooltip.
    - Edit template: If you would like to make further changes or customizations, click this button to open the template in Account settings > Email templates for editing [opens in a new tab].
    - Created by: Information on the user who created the template. For default/system templates, it will be Mindtickle. For copied templates, it will be the name of the admin who created it by making a copy of a default template.
    - Last updated by: Information on the user who last updated the template. For default templates, it will be the name of the admin who edited the default template; N/A if the template is unchanged. For copied templates, it will be the name of the admin who last edited the template, along with the date.
  - Manage email templates: Click this option at the bottom to view all of your templates in Account settings > Email templates [opens in a new tab].
  - Use this email: Once you have finalized the template, click this button to set it as the template for sending emails to learners.
2. Once you have selected the template, it shows up in the Email template column. In this example, when learners are invited to this course module, the “Course Invitation” template will be used for sending invitation emails. You can anytime click thepencil button to change the template again.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Communications > Notifications and Reminders > Configure repeating reminders:
With the Repeat after X days/weeks option, you can send repeating reminder emails to learners by configuring the recurrence cadence. By setting a recurrence, you can ensure that important communications are not missed, while also saving time by automating the email sending process. This new feature is part of our ongoing effort to make communication management more efficient and effective.

IMPORTANT: Please note the following important caveats regarding this option:

- This option is available only for the course, quick update, assessment, and ILT modules.
- It is available only for the following types of reminder emails, which are based on the learner’s progress status on the module:
  - Emails to learners for the Did not start and In progress status for course/quick update/assessment
  - Emails to learners for the Not enrolled in any session or event status for ILT
- For the above reminder emails, It’s available only for the following reminder options in the dropdown menu. It’s not applicable and available for the Specific date option.
  - No. of days after invitation
  - No. of days after start
  - No. of days before due date

Perform the following to configure the recurrence settings:

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Communications > Notifications and Reminders > Configure repeating reminders:
1. Click the pencil button next to the Repeat after X days/weeks option for a reminder email: The Recurrence settings pop-up appears.
2. In the Recurrence settings pop-up, first configure the Repeat every setting to define the email cadence (days or weeks):
  - Repeat every X days: In the first text box, enter the number of days (whole numbers between 1 and 100) at which the reminders should repeat. In this example screenshot, the reminder email will be sent every 3 days.
  - Repeat every X weeks: In the first text box, enter the number of weeks (whole numbers between 1 and 100) at which the reminders should repeat. Select the days of the week when the reminder should repeat. In this example screenshot, the reminder email will be sent every 3 weeks on Monday, Wednesday, and Friday.
3. Next, configure the Ends setting to define when the recurring reminders stop. This can be based on one of the following:
  - Learner’s status on the module (Started or Completed for course/quick update/assessment and When learners enroll in a session for ILT)
  - After a specific number of reminders (whole numbers between 1 and 100). Note: The repeat reminder emails will end automatically when the learner’s status for this module changes — irrespective of the number of reminders configured.
4. At the bottom, you can view a summary of your configured recurrence settings.
5. Click Done if all looks good.
6. After configuring the recurrence settings, ensure to save your changes for the Repeat after X days/weeks option: select the checkbox and then click Save.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Get Started:
This article provides information on how to sign up and sign in to your Mindtickle learning site. Any Mindtickle user who has access to the learning site, such as learners, managers, and admins, can access the learning site.

- Sign up: Applicable for new users
- Sign in: Applicable for signed up (registered) users

While signing up or signing in, you can also take the following actions on the sign-in (login) page:

1. Language selection: Use the language dropdown menu to change the language of the learning site user interface (UI) to your preferred language. You can also change the language from your profile after you have signed up/in.
2. Organization social media: Use the social media icons to access your organization’s social media accounts and follow them.
3. Contact support: Use this option to report any issues and errors to Mindtickle Support .

chunks.title: Sign up and sign in to your Mindtickle learning site

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Get Started > Sign up:
1. Enter your Mindtickle learning site URL (for example, acmeuni.mindtickle.com) in a new tab or window of your web browser. The learning site sign-in (login) page appears.Tip: If you do not know your learning site URL, contact your Mindtickle admin.
2. Before continuing with the signing up, note that you can change the user interface (UI) language to your preferred language using the dropdown menu in the upper-right corner. You can also change the language from your profile after you have signed up.
3. You can sign up either with your username (your work email address) or with a single sign-on (SSO) option, such as Google, Okta, and Salesforce.Note: SSO options are available only if SSO is configured by your admin. The number of SSO options also depends on your admin’s configuration.
4. Under Sign in, click Sign up. All sign-in options will change to sign-up options.
5. Let’s consider how to sign up with your username. Click Sign up with your username.
6. Enter your work email address and a password of your choice. If your admin has shared a password with you, ensure to enter the same password. Click Sign up.
7. The following pop-up message appears confirming that an account activation email is sent to your email address. It contains a link to activate your account.
8. You will receive an email message with the “Activate your Mindtickle account” as the subject. Click the Activate now button or the link to activate your account.
9. The email link opens in your web browser and takes you to the learning site homepage, where you need to fill up certain profile fields to set up your Mindtickle user profile. The profile fields are set up by your admin. All fields marked with an asterisk are mandatory. Click Save changes once done.
10. Now you have successfully created your Mindtickle account and can start exploring content on the learning site.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Sales engagement:
Outreach is a sales engagement platform that helps sales representatives manage their sales processes, particularly in the prospecting and pipeline management stages. Mindtickle's Asset Hub is a powerful tool that allows users to share assets, such as documents, images, and attachments.

The integration of Mindtickle with Outreach is designed to enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of your sales activities. By integrating the two platforms, sales reps can easily enrich their outbound emails with relevant assets from Mindtickle's Asset Hub during the prospecting stage.

This allows sales reps to provide valuable and engaging content to potential customers without the need to switch between multiple platforms. The integration also enables detailed tracking of customer engagement on the shared assets, providing valuable insights that can inform future sales strategies and decisions.

This article is intended for admins and provides information on:

1. Key features of the integration
2. How to set up the integration
3. Caveats and important callouts

Click here to view the article for sales reps (learners), which provides information on how to share assets via Outreach and track engagement.

The Mindtickle-Outreach integration includes the following features:

1. Asset sharing: Admins and reps can add assets directly to emails, templates, snippets, or sequences from Mindtickle's Asset Hub. This allows them to send enriched emails, enhancing the prospecting process.
2. Asset engagement tracking: After an email is sent, you can track recipient (prospect) engagement on the sent assets. The system tracks customer activities, such as opening the email, clicking on the asset links, viewing the assets, and the time spent on each asset. You can track their engagement with the shared assets on both Outreach and Mindtickle:
  - On Outreach: Overview-level engagement data on Outreach. Prospect activity (engagement) is written back to Outreach and you can view it in the Activity tab of the prospect. It provides data on the time spent on the assets, asset downloads (if downloading was enabled), and asset names.
  - On Mindtickle: Deeper engagement data on Mindtickle (on the interaction page). It provides more detailed asset interaction and engagement data, such as total number of views, time spent, downloads, and time when the recipient last interacted with the shared assets. It also provides various activity information on the interaction, such as the time when the email was opened, asset was viewed, asset was downloaded, and if assets were shared with other recipients.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Sales engagement > Set up the integration:
Only admin users (either a site owner or an IT admin) can set up the Mindtickle-Outreach integration. Perform the following to set up the integration:

1. On the admin site homepage, click Account on the left navigation bar.
2. Select Settings from the drop-down menu.
3. On the Settings page, click the Security & integrations tab.
4. Scroll down to the Sales engagement section.
5. Click Enable in the Outreach tab to enable the integration.
6. You are taken to the Mindtickle application page on the Outreach Marketplace (app store), where you need to install the Mindtickle app. Click Install app to install it.Alternatively, you can directly go to the Outreach Marketplace to find and install the Mindtickle app for Outreach.
7. In the pop-up that appears, click Allow to give access to required permissions.
8. On the next page in the pop-up, select whether you would like to install the app for all users or only selected users and profiles, and then click Install.
9. Once the app is installed successfully, you are redirected back to the Security and integrations page on your Mindtickle admin site. The green checkmark indicates that Mindtickle is successfully integrated with Outreach.
10. To remove the integration, you can uninstall the Mindtickle app from Outreach > Administration > Integrations > Apps.

Now your sales reps (learners) can start sharing Mindtickle assets through Outreach emails, templates, snippets, and sequences. For details, see Mindtickle–Outreach integration: Share assets and track engagement.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Sales engagement > Caveats:
Consider the following caveats and important information on Mindtickle’s integration with Outreach:

- This integration is supported only for Outreach on the web, available at https://web.outreach.io . It is not supported for the Outreach mobile app.
- The integration does not support engagement data tracking if you share assets using the Outreach Everywhere extension for Google Chrome browser. You can add assets to your email using the extension; however, engagement tracking will not be available.
- The integration supports white-labeled Mindtickle instances. However, the Mindtickle icon remains visible in the Outreach UI, appearing as the Mindtickle app in the email composer toolbar and in the Activity tab for engagement tracking.
- The activity (asset engagement) writeback to Outreach is enabled by default and you cannot disable it.
- If assets are added to an email through a template — and not through the Mindtickle app in the toolbar — then the recipient's information will not be captured. This means that the tracking data will not include specific information about who viewed the assets.
- When assets are shared with the prospects via Outreach, they are asked to provide consent for Mindtickle to track their asset engagement. If a prospect does not provide consent, then Mindtickle cannot trace the interaction back to the prospect. Therefore, Mindtickle can neither receive nor share the activity (engagement) data on the assets for this prospect.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > AI Interactive roleplay (Beta) > For admins:
In one-way roleplay, admins meticulously construct a scenario (description) for learners by presenting a situation from the buyer's perspective, enabling learners to make relevant pitch.

On the other hand, interactive missions take a different approach. Admins do not need to describe the buyer's perspective extensively; instead, admins can focus on the business situation to guide learners through the conversation. The copilot independently sets the context and introduces the conversation based on the information provided by admins.

Admins must adopt a different approach while defining the learner and copilot roles in the scenario. Providing the copilot with a business scenario and relevant context helps the AI understand the circumstances and behavior of the buyer, allowing it to engage with the learner more effectively.

The scenario for interactive roleplay considers the learner as a seller or revenue team member pitching a product, service, feature, or update to the Copilot, who is a buyer or customer.

Note: Interactive missions is only applicable to Video roleplay missions.

- Learners should initiate the conversation and set the agenda before Copilot. This ensures a two-way dialogue and empowers learners to take control of the conversation.
- Create achievable scenarios relevant to the learner's domain within a specified timeframe and help learner enhance their skills through practice. This makes the roleplay more meaningful and impactful for skill development.

- Personality traits influence copilot behavior and set the stage for the introduction phase of the conversation.
- Personality parameters can include aspects such as motivation, goals that inspire a user, and the user's experience and value sets.
- Other considerations may involve extremeness, such as what triggers conversation shifts and swings and how decision-making occurs.
- Emotional tone and qualities are essential, reflecting the state of mind that the copilot would adopt when initiating the simulation. For example, the copilot could be professional, polite, or rude.
- Depending on the maturity of the seller, the personality is tuned from relaxed to supportive or rude.
- Establish behavioral expectations for the copilot, such as maintaining professionalism, managing temper in stressful scenarios, or demonstrating enthusiasm and interest in the user's proposals.
- Personality traits can also be referenced in a business situation, depending on how a person would react while dealing with challenges and problems. Eg: If the desired business outcome is not achieved promptly, the individual's attitude may tend to become more desperate.

Daniel is highly data-driven and skilled at identifying potential flaws. He is upfront in rejecting and challenging bold claims.Example 2: Kristy is generally high-strung and a perfectionist. She can be rude and abrupt when pushed out of her comfort zone. She dislikes cold calls but may be persuaded once or twice.

The following best practices ensure that Copilot's instructions are clear, effective, and conducive to a learning environment that mimics real-world business scenarios:

- Admins can choose the depth of details for Copilot based on their needs. When specifying the Copilot instruction, admins should avoid tight guidelines that hard code AI behavior. Instead, admins should provide guidelines for Copilot to operate without solidifying behavior, which maintains the Copilot's engagement and makes it realistic to how an actual buyer would behave.
- Admins must avoid providing contradictory information to Copilot, which can confuse it and lead to unrealistic conversational outcomes. Precise guidance to Copilots ensures appropriate conversational behavior in various business situations.
- Admins should be precise when setting the scenario for Copilot, as this helps it understand its stakes and dynamics. They should outline the business situation and define the context in which Copilot will act.
- Admins should also specify the goals of the interaction, stating what Copilot aims to achieve in the conversation. This could be to gather more information, push for a closing, or explore potential objections, guiding Copilot's strategy.
- Admins can outline how Copilot should react to different user strategies, encourage clear, specific answers, manage the conclusion of the interaction, and set expectations for the emotional tone Copilot should adopt based on the scenario needs.
- Admins can provide guidelines on concluding negotiations or discussions, and articulating reasons for ending without an agreement can also be helpful.
- Admins can adjust Copilot's demeanor based on the business situation and the seller's approach to the conversation, ensuring an interaction that mimics real-life dynamics.

Example 1: Role-play scenario for cold call

Help & Support > Help Center Home > AI Interactive roleplay (Beta) > For admins > Instructions for creating the custom Copilot profile > Persona guidelines for custom profile (Copilot):
- Objective: You aim to finalize and close the agreement with the vendor. This solution should integrate diverse business units, ensure data governance, and offer customization flexibility for your business needs.
- Objection management: You must raise solid objections in the closing stage of the deal and validate if the responses effectively address your queries. If not, follow up with further questions for clarification.
- Negotiation: Negotiate strongly with the seller to identify reasons for the proposed contract value and duration. You can also convince the seller of the growing business value post-engagement, especially with future rollouts.
- Questioning approach: Limit yourself to one key question or topic area per interaction phase, allowing for a focused and in-depth discussion.
- Critical analysis: Apply a critical lens to the responses received, avoiding settling for superficial assurances and generic sales pitches.
- Consideration for next steps and decisions: Focus on concrete details, clarifications, and finalizing terms as the deal closes. Establish immediate next steps post-agreement, including points of contact and initial setup meetings.
- Decision-making: If you decide not to proceed with the deal, address your concerns to the sellers. If the seller cannot respond effectively to your objections, voice your concern before ending the call.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Copilot > For admins:
Mindtickle Copilot enables you to get quickly create a series. Anybody, regardless of expertise level, can create a new series. It generates a foundational structure for a series, including sections and modules, based on the detailed prompt the series creator provides. Copilot uses new ways to engage audiences on certain topics using different Mindtickle modules. Admins can modify the generated outlines based on their requirements or stakeholder feedback. This feature significantly reduces the time and effort spent by admins on series planning and creation.Note:

- Copilot does not add any content to the modules. It only provides a skeletal structure consisting of different module types. You need to add the content to the modules manually later.
- Copilot is based on the generative language models, such as GPT-3.5 and GPT-4, from Microsoft’s Azure Open AI Service that provide the greatest security and privacy. Copilot does not make use of OpenAI’s ChatGPT.
- Copilot is powered by generative AI and while the content (responses, insights, and more) generated by Copilot is typically accurate, it can make mistakes and may not always provide accurate or complete information. It is currently in beta as we refine the offering across our platform. It helps boost efficiency and productivity but is not a replacement or substitute for your teams. We recommend always reviewing and updating (where necessary) Copilot-generated content and responses so that it is accurate, complete, and relevant to your needs.
