chunks.body:
Mindtickle Copilot enables you to get quickly create a series. Anybody, regardless of expertise level, can create a new series. It generates a foundational structure for a series, including sections and modules, based on the detailed prompt the series creator provides. Copilot uses new ways to engage audiences on certain topics using different Mindtickle modules. Admins can modify the generated outlines based on their requirements or stakeholder feedback. This feature significantly reduces the time and effort spent by admins on series planning and creation.Note:

- Copilot does not add any content to the modules. It only provides a skeletal structure consisting of different module types. You need to add the content to the modules manually later.
- Copilot is based on the generative language models, such as GPT-3.5 and GPT-4, from Microsoft’s Azure Open AI Service that provide the greatest security and privacy. Copilot does not make use of OpenAI’s ChatGPT.
- Copilot is powered by generative AI and while the content (responses, insights, and more) generated by Copilot is typically accurate, it can make mistakes and may not always provide accurate or complete information. It is currently in beta as we refine the offering across our platform. It helps boost efficiency and productivity but is not a replacement or substitute for your teams. We recommend always reviewing and updating (where necessary) Copilot-generated content and responses so that it is accurate, complete, and relevant to your needs.
- For more information, see Mindtickle Copilot frequently asked questions (FAQs).

- Discard and exit This deletes the entire chat history and outline. To do this, click Discard and exit.

To save the outline as a draft, click Back on the left panel. You are navigated to the series homepage. Note: At this stage, if you decide to build the series on your own by adding a section or module, the system will delete the existing draft outline created by Copilot. Similarly, during an active Copilot session for one admin, if another admin adds a module or section to the draft, the system automatically deletes the existing draft outline Copilot creates. In each case, the system prompts the admins to inform them before proceeding. If the admin clicks Review outline, they are redirected to the Copilot outline preview. Outline generation usually takes a few seconds. While the system generates the outline, you can view its progress in Notifications. If the series generation is 100% successful (all modules and sections are created), a prompt to refresh the series page to view the updates is displayed on the screen. Otherwise, click Refresh series to view the updated series. You can now add content to the modules, configure series settings, and invite learners to the series.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > AI Interactive roleplay (Beta) > For admins > Learner brief:
- Cold calling: This conversation simulates an initial outreach call made by a sales or business development representative to a prospect who may not know your company. The avatar focuses on determining whether your solution is relevant to their needs. It tests the seller’s ability to build trust quickly, show why the solution is relevant, and arrange a follow-up meeting.
- Discovery: This conversation simulates an important call after the initial outreach. The avatar expects the learner to ask smart questions and build trust to understand the prospect’s specific challenges, goals, and evaluation of solutions.
- Mutual discovery: This conversation simulates a two-part discovery call. First, the avatar expects the learner to ask the right questions to learn important information. Then, the avatar assesses how well the learner understands the needs shared before moving to the next steps.
- Product pitch: This conversation simulates a product pitch to a persona focused on long-term business value. The avatar tests the learner's ability to tailor their value proposition to their business priorities and steer the conversation toward building a strategic partnership.
- Differentiation: This conversation simulates a competitive evaluation in which the avatar is aware of alternative solutions. Based on the buyer's perspective, the avatar expects the learner to clearly explain their unique value and demonstrate how their solution stands out from the competition.
- Negotiation: This conversation simulates a commercial negotiation, with the avatar discussing deal terms. The avatar uses realistic negotiation tactics to encourage learners to explain and prove their value, helping them secure favorable terms.
- Renewal management: This conversation simulates a discussion with an existing customer who is reviewing the partnership's value. The avatar refers to past interactions and changing needs, encouraging the learner to explain the value provided and agree on terms for renewal.
- Inbound calling: This conversation simulates customer support use cases in which a customer calls a learner to report a concern about a product or service they are using. The avatar responds based on how well the learner shows empathy, handles the issue, and navigates challenging conversational behaviors.
- Others: Selecting this option starts a flexible process to create a custom roleplay. The copilot identifies the structure of your roleplay conversation, then collaborates with you to gather the precise information needed to set it up.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > AI Interactive roleplay (Beta) > For admins > Learner brief > Brief for the learner:
Add a description of the mission to help the learner understand the objective and the approach they should take while submitting their roleplay. For more information on adding guidelines for learners, see Guidelines for learner.

The admins can type in a detailed description if they have it handy. Alternatively, they can click Generate brief and use the Mindtickle Copilot assistant to generate a detailed description for the learner. The Copilot asks a series of questions to gather all the necessary information for the roleplay scenario.

These questions cover details such as the buyer persona, the prospect’s company and industry, and key decision-makers involved in the scenario.

Based on your answers, the Copilot automatically generates a comprehensive learner brief. This brief includes background information, the scenario's goals, and all key details the learner needs to understand and practice the roleplay effectively.

You can then review the generated learner brief to ensure it correctly reflects your intended scenario. This ensures the learner understands the expectations and objectives from the associated roleplay training before attempting it.

Once you answer the Copilot questions and the brief is generated, click Confirm to copy the content under the Brief for the learners option. After you have clicked Confirm, you can make any necessary edits.

Note:

- If Copilot is not generating the desired results, you can use the Start over option to restart the instruction generation.
- Use the Hide option to close the Copilot window.

Click Generate instructions to use the Copilot to create the scenario. Copilot asks guided, context-based questions to create tailored avatar instructions for a realistic roleplay scenario.

The guided inquiry questions are contextually relevant to the roleplay conversation type and cover details necessary to meet the use-case needs, such as the avatar’s behavior, objective, context, and conversation guidelines for interacting with the learner in the roleplay.

Users are always assisted with dynamic, contextual suggestions that provide appropriate, relevant responses when they are unsure.

Based on your responses, the Copilot automatically generates a detailed avatar instruction for the roleplay scenario.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > AI Interactive roleplay (Beta) > For admins > Evaluation parameters:
Evaluation Parameters are the criteria used to assess learner performance in a mission. Each parameter represents a specific skill or behavior you want to measure, such as communication, accuracy, or objection handling. They help reviewers evaluate responses consistently and ensure that scoring aligns with your training objectives, that feedback remains structured, and that results remain comparable across missions and learners.

To simplify setup, Mindtickle Copilot can automatically generate Evaluation Parameters based on your mission context, learner brief, and Avatar instructions. This auto-creation saves time, improves consistency, and creates relevant criteria instantly with aligned structure, wording, and objectives. As a result, you can launch missions faster while maintaining reliable, standardized evaluations and easily scale them across missions.

On the Evaluation parameter screen, click Generate with AI option to auto-generate the evaluation parameters. The Mindtickle Copilot analyzes the Learner brief and Avatar instructions and generates up to 6 evaluation parameters.

To simplify setup, Mindtickle Copilot can automatically generate Evaluation Parameters based on your mission context, learner brief, and Avatar instructions. This auto-creation saves time, improves consistency, and creates relevant criteria instantly with aligned structure, wording, and objectives. As a result, you can launch missions faster while maintaining reliable, standardized evaluations and easily scale them across missions.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > AI Interactive roleplay (Beta) > For learners > Getting Started:
You will receive an email notification when an interactive video roleplay mission is assigned to you. Click the Get Started button in the email and sign in to your learning site with your registered email address or SSO-enabled account if you haven’t already.

On the page that opens, you will see the following mission attributes:

1. Instructions for roleplay
2. Certificate Cut-Off
3. Evaluation Parameter
4. Prospect in the scenario
5. Target Length Range, Due Date, and Time limit
6. Record your submission below

This article further explains each section in detail.

1. Instructions for roleplay

The instructions describe and highlight the value and intent of the mission. This section describes the scenario and the approach the learner must take to interact with the copilot to complete the submission.

Attachments: This section may contain additional attachments, such as an example video or a sample presentation. Download and read the attachments before you begin the mission.

2. Certificate cut-off

The Certificate cut-off is the minimum score that you are expected to achieve to earn a certificate of completion.

If the Certificate cut-off is displayed, then a certificate will be awarded after you achieve the score. If the Passing cut-off is displayed, no certificate will be awarded after achieving the score.

3. Evaluation parameters

The evaluation parameter can be a statement, question, term, or phrase that defines a standard against which your knowledge, skill, or behavior is evaluated by the reviewers.

A mission can contain multiple Evaluation parameters, which can be grouped together under sections.

Evaluation parameters are assigned scores. It is important that you review them before using them as guidelines when recording your submission.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > AI Interactive roleplay (Beta) > For learners > Insights and suggestions:
This section is mainly divided into the following three sections:

- Summary : Displays the summary of the call.
- Insights : Displays the following attributes:
- Sentiment: Analyze the tone of your transcript and help you understand if the sentiment of the roleplay was Positive/Negative/Neutral.
- Relevance: Analyzes the relevance of the draft against the parameters set by the admin.
- Talk%: Displays your talking percentage during the call. Ideally should be below 44%.
- Pace: Shows how your delivery compares with the average range for speaking rate. The pace insight will help you understand if the pace at which you have delivered the submission is slow, appropriate, or fast.
- Filler words: Highlight phrases or sounds that mark a pause or hesitation in your pitch or presentation. This insight identifies filler words you have used and lists the number of times each word is repeated.
- Longest monologue: Analyzes the longest longest duration for which the learner spoke continuously.
- Suggestions and improvements : After analyzing your roleplay submission, a few improvement suggestions are displayed.

During your interaction with the Copilot, you will be prompted with appropriate warnings based on the following criterion. The warnings aim to ensure a smooth conversation. If you don't adhere to the warnings, the conversation will be concluded.

- Frequent pauses.
- Long monologue
- Interrupting the Copilot frequently

A warning is also displayed pre-timeout to ensure users are able to conclude the roleplays within the prescribed time window.

Copilot will also iterate the reason for the conclusion if the roleplay is concluded for any of the above reasons.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Copilot > For learners > Overview:
Here is an overview of how the Copilot Assistant for Sellers works:

- To ask a question, enter a query or request in the search bar. It does not need to be phrased as a question, but providing specific input generally results in more accurate responses.
- The Copilot Assistant displays a summarized, helpful answer at the top of the search results, along with links to the sources used and related content.
- Responses are generated from training modules and assets you have access to, including assigned and public series, assets across hubs, video transcripts, and text-based files such as PDFs, PowerPoint, and Word documents. SCORM content (closed format) and images cannot be searched.
- You can seamlessly continue the in-search answer into a full conversation. Selecting a suggested follow-up question or clicking Continue with Copilot opens Seller Copilot and transitions the interaction into a full chat thread, with context carried forward.

Image A: Copilot Assistant for Sellers response within global search

Image B: Continue with Copilot to open a full Seller Copilot chat

About Mindtickle Copilot

Mindtickle Copilot is a generative AI based revenue productivity assistant. Copilot combines the power of enablement and revenue operations data with enterprise-ready generative AI so revenue teams can focus on their most important jobs — selling more and delighting customers. Copilot provides various AI-powered features across the Mindtickle platform, including the ability to interact with Copilot in a chat interface for certain features.

Copilot is built on generative language models offered by Microsoft Azure OpenAI and AWS Bedrock, which provide the greatest security and privacy. Copilot does not utilize OpenAI’s ChatGPT.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Copilot > For learners > How to use it:
Perform the following to use the Copilot Assistant for Sellers on the learning site:

- On the learning site homepage, type a question, keyword, or phrase in the search bar.For the most accurate and relevant results, try to frame your query as a specific question or instruction. For example, asking “What is Seller Intel?” may be too broad; the Copilot Assistant may not know whether you want a summary, strengths, weaknesses, or other details. More specific questions generally produce better answers.
- In the search box pop-up, after entering your query, press Enter or click View all results for.
- The search results page appears, with the Copilot Assistant’s response displayed at the top. The Copilot Assistant generates answers from training modules and assets you have access to, including assigned and public series, hub assets, video transcripts, and text-based files such as PDFs, PowerPoint, and Word documents. It cannot search SCORM content (closed format) or images.Note:
  - Copilot Assistant can make mistakes. Please ensure to review the information in the response for accuracy as necessary before making use of the information.
  - Only documents under 500,000 characters are searchable. This limit applies to documents added to modules and assets, including PDFs, PowerPoint files, and transcripts. As a reference point, a document of roughly 800 pages (about 600–700 words per page) would fall within this limit.
  - Content based-responses only: Copilot Assistant generates responses and identifies relevant modules or assets using only the information explicitly stated in the content (raw text). It does not use module or asset names, links, descriptions, or tags (metadata). As a result, it does not support questions about specific modules when only a module name or link is provided.Examples of unsupported questions: “Summarize the “Platform training” course module”“Summarize this course module: https://acmeuni.mindtickle.com/new/ui/learner/course/7571288691371765086/overview?series=1553462122991359568”

Close the Copilot Assistant response: Click the (Close) button to close/hide the in-search Copilot Assistant response, allowing you to focus on the standard search results.
2. The results that appear below the Copilot Assistant section are the standard search results, which are also powered by AI. For more information, see Global search on the learning site.

The Mindtickle integration with Microsoft Office for the web allows sales reps to customize and edit the content of assets directly in Microsoft web applications: PowerPoint for Web, Word for Web, and Excel for Web. This means reps can make changes to the content of slides or pages, add a customer logo, change the title, or make minor adjustments as needed. Reps can use this functionality while accessing editable assets on the learning site. This feature provides flexibility for sales reps to edit and personalize marketing-approved assets, enhancing their ability to tailor content to specific client needs or sales scenarios.

The aim of this integration is to address the need for sales reps to have the ability to make certain customizations to the marketing-approved assets, improving the efficiency and effectiveness of their sales presentations and pitches. This feature is designed to be intuitive and easy to use, making the process of editing and customizing assets straightforward.

Note:

- This feature is in beta and not enabled by default. To enable it for your Mindtickle instance, please reach out to your CSM or Mindtickle Support .
- You must have a valid Microsoft Office 365 business license to use this feature.
- With this feature, you can only edit assets containing PowerPoint, Word, and Excel files. It is not supported for other file types.
- All changes to the asset file are saved directly with Mindtickle.

For information on editing assets using Google Workspace apps (Docs, Slides, and Sheets), see this article.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Asset Hub > Which assets can be edited?:
With this integration, you can only edit assets containing PowerPoint, Word, and Excel files. It is not supported for other file types. Additionally, the ability to allow asset editing is controlled by your admin, who can configure which assets can be edited by sales reps (learners). Reps can edit only those assets for which the admin has enabled the following properties for a particular asset:

1. Usage > External: Customized asset creation (the second setting) is applicable only if the asset is marked for external usage.

2. Allow customized asset creation > Edit content: Sales reps can edit the slides or pages of the asset using Microsoft Office for the web: PowerPoint, Word, or Excel.

This setting is designed to provide admins with control over the level of customization that sales reps can apply to assets, ensuring that the integrity of marketing-approved assets is maintained while still offering flexibility for sales reps to tailor content to their specific needs.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Asset Hub > How to edit assets:
When a sales rep chooses to edit an asset in Microsoft Office for the web, a copy of the original asset is created. This copy becomes a customized asset that the sales rep can edit while the original marketing-approved asset remains unchanged. The sales rep can choose the name of the new asset and the personal hub where it will be saved. After editing the asset, any changes made will be automatically saved in Mindtickle.

Note: The following steps consider an asset with a PowerPoint (PPT) file as an example. Similarly, you can also edit Word and Excel files.

Perform the following to edit or customize an asset with a PowerPoint/Word/Excel file using Mindtickle’s integration with Microsoft Office for the web:

1. From the Assets homepage on the learning site, go to the Assets or My assets tab and click an asset within a hub.
2. If your admin has allowed customized asset creation, then you can edit the asset using Microsoft Office for the web. If it’s allowed, thebutton appears in the header. Additionally, you can confirm this by checking if Edit content is listed under the Customized asset creation property.
3. Click thebutton and select Edit in PowerPoint for the web.

1. A copy of the original asset will be created. You are first asked to specify the hub in which to save the copied version of the asset. You can create a new hub or save it to any of the listed hubs. You can also change the name of the asset.Note: Assets and hubs created by you will be saved under the My assets tab on the Assets homepage.Click Save and continue.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Asset Hub > How to edit assets:
1. A copy of the asset gets created and it becomes a customized asset that you can edit, while the original, marketing-approved asset remains unchanged. The copied version opens in Microsoft PowerPoint for the web [in a new tab], where you can make all kinds of changes, such as modify the contents of slides, reorder/hide/add/delete slides, and so on. See the next step for important callouts.
2. Note the following callouts on the ability to edit content in Microsoft PowerPoint/Word/Excel for the web:
  - You must have a valid Microsoft Office 365 business license to use this feature.
  - Ensure that pop-ups are not blocked in your browser. See the browser documentation for information on how to allow pop-ups.
  - The maximum file size supported by Microsoft Office for the web is 100 MB.
  - All changes to the asset file are automatically saved to Mindtickle directly.
  - Your customized asset is never updated automatically. However, Mindtickle tracks the original asset your copy was created from, and flags your copy if that asset is updated or becomes unavailable. For details, see Source asset states on customized assets.
3. When you navigate back to the previous tab where the original asset is open, it displays the following toast notification. Click Go to asset to open the copied version of the asset, which you are editing in Microsoft PowerPoint for the web.
4. The asset page displays the “Editing in progress” message while you are editing the asset in PowerPoint.
5. Once you have made all changes in PowerPoint, simply close the PowerPoint tab in your browser so that Mindtickle will automatically process and reflect the changes in your customized (copied) asset. The asset page displays the “Processing changes” message once you close the PowerPoint tab.See the next step for an alternative approach.
6. In case your changes are not processed automatically or for any issues while closing the tab with PowerPoint, you can click Sync now on the asset page to process and save the changes.
7. Once the changes are processed and reflect on the asset page, you can click theEdit button to make further edits using Microsoft PowerPoint. Since this is your own customized copy of the original asset, you now have two options:
  - Edit in PowerPoint for the web: Lets you make direct edits to this asset.
  - Edit a copy in PowerPoint for the web: Lets you create a copy of this asset before making the edits.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Asset Hub > How to edit assets:
7. Once the changes are processed and reflect on the asset page, you can click theEdit button to make further edits using Microsoft PowerPoint. Since this is your own customized copy of the original asset, you now have two options:
  - Edit in PowerPoint for the web: Lets you make direct edits to this asset. - Edit a copy in PowerPoint for the web: Lets you create a copy of this asset before making the edits.

This process allows sales reps to easily customize assets in a controlled manner while ensuring that the original, marketing-approved assets remain intact.

Note: Mindtickle never changes your customized asset on its own — your copy stays as you left it. However, Mindtickle does track which asset your copy was created from:

- If the original asset is updated, the affected slides in your copy are labeled Old version , and a banner on the asset page tells you what changed. Click Accept changes to update your copy, or compare the slides with the updated asset and edit them yourself.
- If the original asset is archived, expired, or deleted, is marked as non-customizable, or your access to it is restricted, your copy is labeled Unshareable and you cannot create new shares of it. Anything you shared earlier stays accessible to those recipients.

For details, see Source asset states on customized assets.

Note: Customized assets created using Edit in PowerPoint for the web before the July 2026 release are not tracked.

Once the customized asset is created, you can share and track it as usual. Here's how:

- Share the asset: The rep can share the customized asset with other team members or clients as needed. This allows for greater collaboration and ensures that the most relevant and customized content is being circulated. For details, see Share assets (reps) .

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Asset Hub:
This article provides information on AI-powered similar asset suggestions from Mindtickle Copilot. The Similar assets feature leverages Copilot to suggest/recommend assets similar to the one currently being viewed. It enables reps to quickly find relevant assets, saves time on searches, and ensures access to the most up-to-date and impactful content.

When you open an asset from a hub or through search, click theicon on the asset page to view a list of similar or related assets. The Similar assets panel lists up to 10 similar assets primarily based on the content and asset properties, such as the asset name and engagement (views, shares, ratings, downloads, and recency). It lists only those assets to which you have access. The list gets updated daily as assets are updated or new ones are published.

Note:

- This feature makes use of AI through Mindtickle Copilot. To use this feature, you must first opt for Mindtickle’s AI capability on the platform. To enable the AI capability (if you haven’t already) and this feature, please contact your CSM or Mindtickle Support .
  - If you are enabling our AI capability on your Mindtickle instance for the first time, then you will start seeing similar assets from the next day onwards.
- The feature is available only on the web and not on the Mindtickle mobile app.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Asset Hub > View similar assets:
Perform the following to view similar assets for an asset:

1. Open any asset from a hub or through search.
2. On the asset page, click theicon on the asset to view a list of similar or related assets. Note: The icon appears only if there are similar assets.
3. The Similar assets panel lists up to 10 similar assets primarily based on the content and asset properties, such as the asset name and engagement (views, shares, ratings, downloads, and recency). It lists only those assets to which you have access. Assets with the highest similarity score are displayed at the top of the list. The list gets updated daily as assets are updated or new ones are published.Note: Assets without content transcription — such as image-based assets, embedded URL assets, audio assets, and plays — are not presented in the similar assets list.
4. Click an asset in the list to view it on the right. Click the Go to asset button to open it [in a new tab]. You can then take further actions on the asset, such as share it with prospects and download or bookmark it.

This article provides an overview of how Mindtickle users can access Notion content from Mindtickle and further share it with their prospects using the existing capabilities of both platforms.

Note:

- Add shareable links of Notion pages

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > External Content Access > Export Notion pages as PDFs:
You can export Notion pages as PDFs and upload them in Mindtickle.

1. Click the ••• More options icon at the upper right corner of any Notion page and select Export from the dropdown menu.
2. On the pop-up window, choose PDF from the Export format dropdown. Specify if you would like to export everything or exclude files and images in the Include content dropdown. Select the Page format and adjust the scale if necessary.
3. Click Export and choose a location to save the file on your device. You can add the exported PDF (wherever applicable) to Mindtickle. For example:
  - Upload content in a course or quick-update
  - Add content in Content Center
  - Add content to Factopedia
  - Create overview pages
  - Add and configure widgets for learning site homepages
  - Create a new asset

Advantage of exporting Notion pages as PDFs in Mindtickle:

- Through this mode, scoring and completion of the content can be tracked granularly (as is for any PDF) in Mindtickle.

Disadvantage of exporting Notion pages as PDFs in Mindtickle:

- Since the PDFs are static files, any updates made on the source Notion page will not be automatically updated in the exported PDF in Mindtickle. Users must manually update the export and replace the file in Mindtickle to ensure the latest information is available. For more information, see Add or replace a file in learning object using Content Center .

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > External Content Access > Add shareable links to Notion pages > Share with members of your organization:
To create a shareable link for members of your organization:

- Click Share on the upper right corner of any Notion page.
- On the Share tab, select Anyone with link at your org or Everyone at your org from the dropdown.
- Click Copy link . The link is copied to the clipboard. You can add the shareable link (wherever applicable) in Mindtickle. For example:
  - Add shareable link on Overview pages
  - Add shareable links to series overview page
  - Add links to series descriptions
  - Create a rich text document and add the link to it
  - Create a one-pager PDF/PPT and add the link to it Clicking the link opens the Notion content in a new tab. Note : Users who receive this link must have a Notion account.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > External Content Access > Add shareable links to Notion pages > Share with the web:
To create a public shareable link:

- Click Share on the upper right corner of any Notion page.
- On the Publish tab, click Publish . The content is published on the web and is accessible to everyone (even users who do not have a Notion account). Copy the link and add to Mindtickle via a text document, PDF, or PPT. For example:
  - Add shareable link on Overview pages
  - Add shareable links to series overview page
  - Add links to series descriptions
  - Add links to spotlight banners or assets Clicking the link opens the Notion content in a new tab.

Advantage of adding shareable links to Notion pages in Mindtickle:

- Since the Notion content is available over a URL, the updates made on the source Notion page are automatically available in Mindtickle. So learners always have access to the most recently updated Notion pages.

Disadvantage of adding shareable links to Notion pages in Mindtickle:

- The learner’s score and completion status are marked as 100% and Complete once the learner clicks the link to the Notion page. Hence, through this mode, analytics or progress on the Notion links cannot be tracked granularly in Mindtickle.

Tip:

- For a better user experience, it is suggested to have the metadata such as title, description, and some visual information in the document along with the link in Mindtickle.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > User Management > FAQs:
For your Mindtickle instance, you can choose to enable unique identifier (UID) based method for authentication and signing in to the platform. With UID is enabled, you can configure a unique username for each of your users, in addition to their email address. Username is used for authentication and signing in to the Mindtickle platform, while the email address is used for communication, such as sending invitation and reminder emails from the platform.

The username can be anything of your choice. For example, it can be "alexfry", "alex.fry", "alex1234", or "3214768". You can also configure their email address for authentication by setting it as the username.

To enable UID for your Mindtickle instance, please contact Mindtickle Support.

Identify if your Mindtickle instance uses UID

You can identify whether your Mindtickle instance is UID-enabled through the Add users to the platform workflow. See the following screenshots to identify whether UID enabled for your Mindtickle instance:

- UID enabled : If UID is enabled, then Username and Email ID are available as two separate fields while adding new users. The username is used for authentication while the email address is used for communication from the platform. In case you want to set up the email address for authentication, you must configure it as the username too.
- UID not enabled : If UID is NOT enabled, then only the Username field is available while adding new users. There is no separate field for email address. The email address is configured as the username and is used for communication as well as authentication.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle APIs > User Management APIs:
The User APIs allow you to manage the entire user lifecycle and organizational structure at scale. You can use these endpoints to programmatically provision (create, update, deactivate) users individually or in bulk, manage group memberships, and track the status of these asynchronous operations.

Key capabilities include:

- User management: Create, update, search, and deactivate individual or bulk users.
- Group association: Add or remove users from specific groups to automate hierarchy management.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle APIs > User Management APIs > Search users:
To search for users on Mindtickle.

Request URL

```http
POST /services/data/v4.0/mtobjects/Users
```

- An empty JSON request will return all the users in the learning site.
- A maximum of 50 records are returned per request. Use nextRecordsUrl from the response to fetch subsequent sets of 50 records.

Request parameters

JSON REQUEST PARAMETERS

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle APIs > User Management APIs > Remove users from a group:
To remove one or more users from a Mindtickle group.

Request URL

```http
POST /services/data/v4.0/mtobjects/Group/{groupId}/users/delete
```

Request parameters

PATH PARAMETERS

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| groupIdREQUIRED | string | Mindtickle ID of the group from which you want to remove users. |

JSON REQUEST PARAMETERS

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| userids | Array[string] | Mindtickle IDs of users that you want to remove from a group.Multiple IDs should be comma-separated as shown in the request example below this table. |
| usernames | Array[string] | Mindtickle usernames/email IDs of the users that you want to remove from a group.Provide the usernames of the users if UID is enabled for your Mindtickle instance.Provide their email addresses if UID is not enabled. |

Request example

```json
{
  "userids": [
    "452146abcd",
    "891011efgh",
    "12131415yjkl"
  ]
}
```

— OR —

```json
{
  "usernames": [
    "alex.fry@mindtickle.com",
    "anna.cruz@mindtickle.com",
    "james.smith@mindtickle.com"
  ]
}
```

Response messages

The following table lists possible response messages along with their HTTP status code:

| HTTP Code | Response message |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | Users removed from group successfully. |
| 400 | Invalid request. |
| 401 | Invalid token. |
| 404 | Invalid groupid/userid/username. |
| 429 | Too many calls. Retry after 5 min. |
| 500 | Internal server error. |

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle APIs > User Management APIs:
The User Group APIs allow you to programmatically manage your organization's hierarchy and streamline bulk training administration. You can use these endpoints to create, update, search, and delete user groups, as well as efficiently assign or revoke access to series and modules for entire cohorts at once.

Key capabilities include:

- Group management: Create, update, retrieve, delete, and search for user groups.
- Bulk content assignment: Enroll or remove entire groups from series and modules, ensuring efficient training distribution.
- Process tracking: Monitor the status of asynchronous group operations.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle APIs > User Management APIs > Search groups:
To search for groups on Mindtickle. You can search for groups by either their name or ID.

Request URL

```http
POST /services/data/v2.0/mtobjects/Groups
```

Request parameters

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |

Request example

```json
{
  "names": "APAC Sales, EMEA Sales",
  "ids": [
    "1521745579029284469",
    "1521752425688619769"
  ]
}
```

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| requestId | string | null |
| responseCode | string | Special response codes from the server. |
| responseType | string | Type of response from the server. |

| totalSize | string | Total number of groups returned in the response. |
| groupsnameid | Groupstringstring | Information on the groups you have searched.Name of the group.Mindtickle ID of the group. |

Response example

```json
{
  "requestId": null,
  "responseCode": 0,
  "responseType": "GROUP_SEARCH_RESPONSE",
  "taskCompleted": true,
  "totalSize": 2,
  "groups": [
    {
      "name": "APAC Sales",
      "id": "1521752425688619769"
    },
    {
      "name": "EMEA SALES",
      "id": "1521745579029284469"
    }
  ]
}
```

To check the status of one or more processes by specifying the process ID. This API request is used for the user group API.

Request URL

```http
POST services/data/v2.0/status
```

Request parameters

PATH PARAMETERS

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| processIdsREQUIRED | Array[string] | ID of the process. Multiple IDs should be comma-separated as shown in the request example below this table. |

```json
  "processIds": [
    "1519737873610326017",
    "3415677887651032261",

  ]
}
```

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| requestId | string | null |
| responseCode | string | Special response codes from the server. |

```json
  "status": {
    "1519737873610326017": "SUCCESS",
    "3415677887651032261": "SUCCESS",

  }
}
```

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle APIs > Training APIs:
The Training Content APIs allow you to programmatically retrieve your organization's training content (series and modules). Use these endpoints to list all available series and modules, or access structured data for specific learning objects complete with granular metadata like media URLs, transcriptions, and correct answer flags.

Key capabilities include:

- Series & module listing: Retrieve a complete list of all series and the modules contained within them.
- Content details: Access structured data for specific content assets — including files, assessments, and quizzes — complete with granular metadata like media URLs, transcriptions, and correct answer flags.

For more information, see Get started with Mindtickle APIs.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle APIs > Training APIs > Get module learning object details:
Retrieve structured learning object (LO) details for a specific module in Mindtickle. The API returns a list of learning contents such as content files, assessments, and quizzes, supporting multiple content types with transcription, media, and correct answer flags.

Request URL

```http
GET /api/v2/entity/{moduleid}/learning_objects HTTP/1.1
```

Request parameters

PATH PARAMETERS

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| moduleIdREQUIRED | string | Mindtickle ID of the module. |

This endpoint does not have any JSON request parameters.

Response structure

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| requestId | A unique identifier for the request. |
| learning_contents | A list of content objects, each with an id, type, and relevant attributes. |
| total | The total number of content items returned. |

Response example

```json
{
  "requestId": "SS-alexfry-RXFM9WMX15.mufWO1740120408302",
  "learning_contents": [
    {
      "id": "1372841425782881792",
      "type": "Content",
      "media": {
        "url": "https://cf-picasso-us1.mindtickle.com/...",
        "id": "1315942122305946352",
        "type": "IMAGE",
        "title": "Sales rep.png"
      }
    },
    {
      "id": "1372841439402146358",
      "type": "Multiple choice question",
      "question": "Building a good app is complex as...",
      "options": [
        { "option": "Developers spend time dealing with conflict resolution", "isCorrect": true, "order": 0 },
        { "option": "Mobile developers spend a lot of time in no-value coding", "isCorrect": true, "order": 1 },
        { "option": "Object databases are more tedious", "isCorrect": false, "order": 2 },
        { "option": "All of the above", "isCorrect": false, "order": 3 }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "total": 2
}
```

Supported content types:

- Content (with or without transcription)
- Multiple choice question
- Match the labels
- Multiple choice images
- Word guess
- Mark the location
- Text answer
- True or false
- Multiple choice poll

Error codes:

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle APIs > User Management APIs:
The table in this article provides information on the time zones supported on the Mindtickle platform and their ID values that you can use in the user APIs. To configure the time zone for a user, provide the appropriate time zone ID from the following table in the request parameter.

For example, while creating a user, you can provide the time zone in the request as follows:

```json

{
  "name": "Alex Fry",
  "username": "alex.fry@mindtickle.com",
  "id": "123456abcd",
  "timezone": "America/Costa_Rica",
  "profile": {
    "dp": "abc"
  }
}
```

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Digital Sales Rooms:
Digital Sales Rooms (DSRs) come with strategic advantages. They present opportunities for driving growth and fostering deeper client relationships.

This article explores the diverse use cases for which customers have successfully implemented DSRs, showcasing how these environments can transform sales strategies and outcomes.

It also lists potential use cases that organizations may consider when contemplating the integration of DSRs.

For more information on creating DSRs, see Create a Digital Sales Room.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Digital Sales Rooms > Use cases for Sales teams:
1. Engage/Sell to a single deal or opportunity : The primary use case Digital Sales Rooms excel at engaging and selling to a single deal or opportunity, their most essential and widely-used function . By providing a centralized platform for all sales materials, tracking buyer engagement, and enabling personalized communication, DSRs enhance the sales process's efficiency and effectiveness, significantly boosting the likelihood of closing deals.
  - Create a DSR tailored for a single prospect or opportunity to create a personalized and immersive experience.
  - Include customized product demos, relevant case studies, and specific pricing options.
  - Showcase portfolios, testimonials, and service offerings.
  - Focus on a single prospect to address specific pain points and questions to enhance the likelihood of conversion.
  - When selling physical services, enable prospective clients to explore the DSRs remotely or during in-person consultations and gain insights into the quality and value of the services.
2. Align prospects on the next steps with Mutual Action Plans (MAPs).
  - MAPs within DSRs keep the sales team and the prospect aligned on the sales process.
  - Outline clear, agreed-upon next steps, deadlines, and responsibilities for each party.
  - Bring transparency and avoid misunderstandings by ensuring everyone is on the same page.
3. Provide self-guided selling paths .
  - This flexibility caters to prospects who prefer to conduct their research independently before engaging in direct conversations. It enables prospects to explore the DSR at their own pace and reduces constant interaction with a sales rep.
  - Include interactive product tours, video testimonials, and educational resources that present the product’s value proposition.
4. Share individual content links during sales sequences.
  - Share specific content links with prospects during various stages of the sales process.
  - Include links to product brochures, case studies, or demo videos relevant to the current stage.
  - Ensure prospects receive the correct information at the right time to support their decision-making process.
5. Share proposals.
  - The sales team can upload and update the proposals as needed.
  - Prospects can review detailed information about the offerings, terms, and conditions.
  - Streamline the proposal review and negotiation process by enabling prospects to ask questions and request modifications within the same platform.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Digital Sales Rooms > Use cases for Customer Success Teams:
1. Customized customer portals.
  - Create customized portals for individual clients to provide a personalized space that caters to each customer's unique needs and preferences.
  - The portal allows the customer to access all relevant information and resources.
  - Include account details, support tickets, project updates, and customized reports on the portal.
2. Customer portals for self-service onboarding.
  - Provide self-service onboarding portals to enable new customers to get started with minimal assistance.
  - Include step-by-step guides, video tutorials, and interactive checklists that help customers set up and use the product or service independently.
  - Reduce the burden on customer success groups and enhance the onboarding experience by allowing customers to learn at their own pace.
3. Help centers .
  - Provide a centralized location for accessing help and support resources.
  - Include FAQs, knowledge bases, and troubleshooting guides.
  - Enable customers to find solutions quickly and independently by offering comprehensive help and support materials.
4. Training and onboarding .
  - Provide structured learning paths for customers within dedicated training and onboarding sections.
  - Include webinars, interactive training modules, and certification programs.
  - Improve adoption rates and ensure better outcomes by offering thorough and easily accessible training.
5. Implementation projects .
  - For customers undergoing complex implementations, DSRs can serve as project management hubs.
  - Create spaces to allow collaboration between the customer success team and the client’s project team, facilitate communication, track milestones, and share important documents.
  - Ensure implementation projects stay on track and meet their goals.
6. Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs)
  - Use DSRs to conduct QBRs with clients.
  - Include detailed performance reports, discussions on key metrics, and strategic planning for the next quarter.
7. Sign renewals and upsells or cross-sells.
  - Streamline the process of managing renewals and identifying opportunities for upsells or cross-sells.
  - Track usage patterns and customer satisfaction levels to propose relevant upgrades or additional services.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Digital Sales Rooms > Use cases for Marketing:
1. Gated website content.
  - Require visitors to provide their contact information before accessing content on your website, such as whitepapers or exclusive reports.
  - Capture leads and gather insights into potential customers’ interests and needs.
  - Place gated content in DSRs to create an engaging experience that provides desired content and additional resources.
2. Landing page website content.
  - Use DSRs for landing pages to capture leads or drive specific actions, such as signing up for a webinar or downloading a resource.
  - To make the landing page more engaging and effective in converting visitors into leads, include dynamic elements such as product demos, customer testimonials, and chat features.
3. Single links in email campaigns .
  - Include single links in email campaigns that lead to a DSR to boost engagement.
  - Personalize the DSR to tailor it to the email campaign’s theme.
  - Provide targeted content, such as product information, special offers, and interactive elements, to increase the recipient's likelihood of taking the desired action.
4. Generic rooms by persona to use in campaigns.
  - Create generic DSRs tailored to different customer personas.
  - Deliver highly relevant content to various segments of the audience.
  - Customize rooms with content that addresses a particular persona's needs, challenges, and interests.
  - Create DSRs for industry-specific case studies, product features that solve common points, and testimonials from similar clients.
  - Use these rooms across multiple marketing campaigns to ensure each segment receives personalized and engaging content.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Digital Sales Rooms > Use cases for Enablement Training:
1. Training rooms for new talk tracks.
  - Enable sales teams to master and internalize key messaging and strategies for engaging with prospects.
  - Provide a virtual space where sales professionals can access training materials, such as scripts, presentations, and role-playing exercises to practice and refine their communication skills.
  - Offer structured and interactive training environments to ensure consistency in messaging.
2. SKO kits .
  - Support sales teams with comprehensive resources during kickoff events or training sessions.
  - Include product guides, competitive analyses, sales playbooks, and training videos.
  - SKOs in DSRs enable organizations to centralize access to these resources and make it easy for sales reps to reference and utilize them before, during, and after SKO events.
3. Supplement DSR for a live training course .
  - Provide supplementary resources for live training courses conducted by enablement teams.
  - Include training materials, interactive quizzes, and discussion forums to reinforce concepts covered during the live sessions.
  - Allow participants to revisit and deepen their understanding of the content at their own pace.
4. Internal onboarding of new employees.
  - Onboard new employees, including sales professionals.
  - Provide centralized access to onboarding materials, such as company policies, product information, training modules, and interactive elements like virtual tours, welcome messages from leadership, and peer introductions.
  - Help new hires acclimate to the company culture and connect with their colleagues.

  - Empower customers and partners to successfully implement and integrate the product into their systems.
  - Accelerate time-to-value, enhance customer satisfaction, and reduce support overhead.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Asset Hub:
Mindtickle's LinkedIn integration is designed to enhance the effectiveness of social selling on LinkedIn, one of the world's largest professional networking platforms. It aims to empower sellers to build networks, share content, and track engagement seamlessly.

The integration with LinkedIn is through our Mindtickle for Chrome extension for the Chrome browser. Using the extension, users can add Mindtickle assets directly to their LinkedIn posts and direct messages (DMs), thereby streamlining the content sharing process. Moreover, users can track user engagement on the shared assets, offering valuable insights into how the content is being received by their network.

Note:

- Asset Hub is a paid feature. For more information, contact your Customer Success Manager (CSM).
- As the Mindtickle-LinkedIn integration works through the Chrome extension, this feature is supported only on the Google Chrome web browser. Additionally, it does not work on mobile devices as they do not support extensions.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Asset Hub > Install the Mindtickle for Chrome extension > Sharing assets in a post vs message:
The feature works the same way whether you are sharing assets in a LinkedIn post or message. However, there are a few differences due to the nature of posts and messages. Posts are public, while direct messages are sent to one or more recipients.

Differences between sharing assets in a LinkedIn post vs message:

- Sharing settings: While sharing assets through a post, the viewers will not be able to see other viewers while viewing the asset. While sharing assets through a message, reps can choose whether to allow viewers to see one another.
- Engagement tracking: For LinkedIn posts, the engagement data will not contain viewer personal identifiable information. For direct messages, the recipient list shall have the list of the viewers but the data will be aggregated data for all viewers.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Asset Hub > Share assets with a LinkedIn post or message > Select assets:
1. While drafting a post or direct message on LinkedIn, keep the mouse cursor in the post/message body text, and then click the Mindtickle for Chrome extension icon in the Chrome browser extension list.

2. In the Add assets to post/message pop-up that appears, you can select assets under the Assets and My assets tabs that you want to include in the post or message. Please note the following:

- Assets tab: You can only share assets marked as External by the admin or asset owner and have not expired.
- My assets tab: Lists the assets that you have customized and created on the learning site under Assets > My assets . You can create your own sales materials and use them as an asset, provided they are saved as PDF. The source of the sales material can be in PDF, PPT, XLS, and Doc format.

3. Perform the following to select assets:

Select one or more assets under the Assets and My assets tabs.

Under each tab, use filters, search, and sort options to narrow down the asset list and find the exact assets you want to add.

Click Add assets to move to the next page where you need to configure the sharing and tracking settings for the selected assets.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Asset Hub > Share assets with a LinkedIn post or message > Configure sharing settings:
After selecting the assets, configure various sharing and tracking related settings on the next page. Configure settings, such as recipient activity notifications, reminder notifications, allow download, and access expiration. You can also rename and reorder the selected assets.

You can configure the sharing, tracking, and other settings for the selected assets:

Interaction name

Provide a name for this instance of asset sharing so that you can easily track it under Assets > Interactions tab on the learning site.

Recipient activity notifications

Turn on the setting if you want to be notified via email whenever a recipient interacts with the shared assets. It has the following options:

- Notify me when the recipient engages with the assets along with the engagement summary
- Notify me when the recipient shares assets with their peers
- Notify me when a recipient is active

Reminder notifications

Turn on the setting if you want to set an email reminder to check the engagement on shared assets. It has the following options:

- Select the date when you would like to be notified. By default you are reminded in a week. Other options are: 3 days, 2 weeks, and custom date.
- Remind me to check engagement data
- Remind me only if there is no activity

Allow download

Turn on the setting if you want recipients to download the shared assets to their local machine. The option to download is not provided for embedded assets, such as a YouTube video embedded link.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Asset Hub:
Mindtickle’s Share via room feature allows you to share assets directly from the Assets section of the platform into Digital Sales Rooms (DSRs) — making it efficient and user-friendly to distribute and manage content. The feature not only simplifies content sharing across Mindtickle products but also saves valuable time and resources. It is particularly helpful when you want to share new content, such as an industry report or a new promotional material, across several DSRs.

The Share via room feature is built into the existingShare functionality for assets in the Assets section of the learning site. While sharing (adding) assets to rooms, the feature also provides options to specify the section headers under which the assets should be placed in the rooms. Furthermore, you can also select who you want to notify about this update.

This article explains how DSR admins and users can share/add assets to one or more digital sales rooms (DSRs).

Note:

- You can only share assets that are marked External by the admin or asset owner and have not expired.
- This feature is not available for the Mindtickle mobile app or from a mobile web browser. It is available only on the web, that is, when accessing Mindtickle from a web browser.
- You can share up to 20 assets at once.
- Asset Hub and Digital Sales Rooms are standalone, paid products from Mindtickle. You must have a license for both to make use of this feature. Please contact your CSM for more information.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Asset Hub > Share assets to rooms > Select rooms:
Once you have selected the assets you want to share, the next step is to select one or more digital sales rooms (DSRs) where you want to share them.

1. On the Select rooms to share assets page, you can share assets in the existing rooms or share them in a new room. You can also add more assets in case you missed to select them in the previous step.

1. Let’s first look at how to find the existing rooms to which you want to share the assets. You can either select them directly from the list or use the filters, search, and column sort options to narrow down the listed rooms and find the exact rooms.

The following filters are available:

- All rooms: View all rooms or only rooms created by you ( My rooms ). By default, all rooms are listed. Note: For DSR admins, all rooms are listed by default. For DSR users, My Rooms is selected by default. Depending on the DSR user’s permissions, they may not see this filter at all.
- Status: View rooms by their status, published or draft. By default, both published and draft rooms are listed.
- Teams: View rooms by one or more teams assigned to them. By default, rooms for all teams are listed.
- Owner: View rooms by a specific room owner. By default, rooms belonging to all owners are listed.
- Template: View rooms that are created with a particular room template. By default, rooms created on all templates are listed.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Asset Hub > Share assets to rooms > Select room section headers:
In this step, you have the option to select the section header for each selected asset. It lets you define where the assets should be placed in a room. Sections are strategic parts of a room under which users can structure sales content. You may have organization-level section headers available and users can create them at the room level as well.

Your assets are added to the section headers selected by you. Assets are added to the top of the room if no section header is specified.

The Select section headers page lists the assets you have selected for sharing.

Perform the following on this page:

- Name in room: Provide a name of your choice for each asset. This can be different from the original name of the asset, which is populated by default.
- Section header: For each asset, select the section header under which it will be added. Note: Assets are added to the top of the room if no section header is specified.

The following two options are available for the section header:

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Asset Hub > Share assets to rooms > Select room section headers:
- Common headers: Section headers that exist across all the selected rooms. For example, if you have selected five rooms and each contains a section header called “Business profile”, this section will appear under common headers.
- Organization headers: Section headers that are set by your admin at the organization level and available for use in all rooms. These headers may or may not exist in the selected rooms, but you can always select them. For example, if the selected rooms do not have any common headers, you can always select organization headers. Note: Let’s say you select an organization header for a room. However, the header currently does not exist in that room. In this case, Mindtickle automatically creates the organization header at the top of the room and adds the asset under the newly-created header. Additionally, if the selected section header exists in the room, the asset is added to the top of that section (just under the section label), and the section itself does not move.

Once done, click Continue to move to the next step.
chunks.body:
- Common headers: Section headers that exist across all the selected rooms. For example, if you have selected five rooms and each contains a section header called “Business profile”, this section will appear under common headers.
- Organization headers: Section headers that are set by your admin at the organization level and available for use in all rooms. These headers may or may not exist in the selected rooms, but you can always select them. For example, if the selected rooms do not have any common headers, you can always select organization headers. Note: Let’s say you select an organization header for a room. Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Coaching reports:
The coaching sessions reviewer reports (or, coaching reviewer reports in short) in Mindtickle analytics provide reviewer analytics and AI-powered insights on coaching sessions, enabling efficient tracking and top-down visibility of coaching initiatives. The reports are available for admins and managers.

With the coaching reviewer reports, admins can monitor whether managers are effectively conducting coaching sessions with their teams, identify competency gaps, and use AI-driven synthesis to assess the quality of feedback. Likewise, managers can monitor their teams. The reports help in maintaining an efficient coaching culture within your organization by providing a detailed view of coaching review progress, adherence, individual performance, and behavioral patterns

Highlight features

- Enable admins to identify teams efficiently conducting coaching sessions and pinpoint teams falling behind in their coaching initiatives.
- Provide AI-powered reviewer summaries to help senior leaders understand dominant coaching identities and behavioral patterns.
- Detailed insights for admins into individual manager and reviewer coaching sessions.
- Empower senior managers to understand how their teams conduct coaching sessions, allowing them to drill down into teams and review coaching progress.
- Provide clear visibility into whether teams are adhering to set coaching schedules and conducting sessions in a timely manner.
- Equip managers with easy access to their past coaching sessions for efficient review and assessment.
- Quantitative insights for coaching activities conducted by teams within the organization, with the ability to drill down to identify teams lagging in coaching activities.

Note: The old reviewer reports are also available under Analytics > Users and roles > Reviewers > Coaching Sessions and will continue to be functional for now. The new coaching session reports are available as a new section in the sidebar under Analytics > Coaching > Reviewers.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Coaching reports > Overview:
Coaching plays a crucial role in improving team performance, enhancing skills, and increasing productivity. However, without a clear overview of the coaching process, it becomes challenging to evaluate its effectiveness and identify areas of improvement. This is where the coaching reviewer reports come into play, which are designed to foster a robust coaching culture in your organization. The reports provide admins and managers with comprehensive insights into the performance and progress of coaching sessions across teams, including AI-generated synthesis of manager behaviors.

The reports offer a structured and admin-driven approach to coaching. Admins have the autonomy to create coaching forms and assign managers to the forms. The assigned managers are then responsible for reviewing their respective teams. This streamlined process ensures uniformity and consistency in the coaching process throughout the organization.

The coaching reviewer reports offer crucial insights into who is conducting coaching, who is not, and the overall progress of the sessions. Such detailed reporting aids in maintaining accountability and ensuring the regular execution of coaching sessions. The hierarchical view lets you monitor the performance of teams and individual reviewers. The reports provide a top-down visibility of coaching sessions and behavioral patterns, eliminating the need for admins to sift through individual manager reports.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Coaching reports > Coaching insights tab:
The Coaching insights tab provides senior leadership and enablement admins with an AI-powered synthesis of manager coaching behaviors. By automatically analyzing historical data from 1:1 coaching sessions, this dashboard provides immediate executive-level intelligence. This allows leaders to easily assess coaching quality, identify systemic alignment, spot variances, mitigate repetitive or low-effort feedback, and proactively coach their frontline managers without needing to read through individual coaching sessions.

Note: This feature is currently not supported on the Mindtickle mobile app.

Prerequisites

To access and use the coaching insights dashboard, ensure the following requirements are met:

- Mindtickle’s AI capabilities are enabled on the platform, as they are required for AI-powered coaching insights. To enable them, contact your CSM or Mindtickle Support .
- User hierarchy is properly configured within the platform to establish reporting relationships.

How insights are generated

The platform uses AI to process and evaluate the text, scores, and metadata from coaching sessions to identify behavioral patterns over time.

- Analytical breakdown: The AI applies a 60/40 analytical lens, weighting 60% on coaching quality and 40% on coaching process and hygiene.
- Minimum data threshold: To prevent inaccurate insights or hallucinations, a manager must have a minimum of 3 completed coaching sessions. This can be one session filled three times, or three separate sessions filled once. If this threshold is not met, the system will explicitly flag the profile as having insufficient data.
- Maximum data limits: To reflect the most current coaching behavior, the AI considers a maximum of 20 learners and the 10 most recent coaching sessions per reviewer.
- Update frequency: The dashboard insights are refreshed bi-weekly to ensure leaders are always reviewing the latest behavioral trends. It does not support real-time data or historical date filtering. I

Coaching insight widgets

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Coaching reports > Coaching insights tab > Learners and sessions:
The Learners and sessions widget is a collapsible pivot table that details the selected manager's specific coaching engagements with up to 20 learners. The table includes columns for the learner name, module name, module URL, completed sessions, and the last session score.

Clicking the arrow next to a learner's name expands the row to reveal the specific coaching modules. From here, clicking the hyperlinked module URL opens the actual coaching session in a new browser tab. Leaders are granted view-only access to these sessions, allowing them to see specific evaluation parameters and ratings without the ability to edit the feedback or close the session.

Viewing individual coaching sessions

Leaders can drill down directly into the source material to observe exactly what feedback was given.

- Direct access: Within the Learners and sessions table, clicking on a hyperlinked module name or URL opens the actual coaching session in a new browser tab.
- View-only permissions: To maintain data integrity and respect the reviewer's process, leaders and admins are granted view-only access to these sessions. You can scroll through all evaluation parameters and ratings across multiple sessions, but all editing capabilities and administrative buttons (such as "Close coaching session") are hidden.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Coaching reports > Team reports tab > Page functionalities:
The following image provides an overview of the options or functionalities available on the Team reports page:

FILTERSUse the filters at the top to view the report data accordingly:

- Time period: View data for a specific period during which your team members were assigned as reviewers on coaching sessions. By default, it displays data for the last one year.
- Reviewer profile fields: View data by one or more profile fields that are common across reviewers.
- Coaching: View data for the coaching sessions modules to which your team members are assigned as reviewers.
- More filters
  - Reviewer groups: View data for one or more reviewer groups.
  - Reviewers: View data for one or more reviewers.

Use the search box to search for a specific reviewer.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Copilot > For admins > How Mindtickle leverages LLM:
Large language models (LLMs) are advanced AI systems trained on vast amounts of text data to understand and generate human-like language. LLMs have transformed numerous industries by providing sophisticated language processing capabilities. At Mindtickle, LLMs play a pivotal role in enhancing the platform's functionality and customer experience in several ways. The following LLM capabilities enable Mindtickle to offer a highly personalized and efficient sales enablement experience, empowering sales teams to perform at their best.

- Content generation : LLMs can generate personalized training content, sales pitches, and follow-up emails tailored to individual needs, helping sales representatives deliver compelling messages.
- Sales coaching : LLMs provide real-time feedback and insights by analyzing sales calls and helping sales teams refine their communication skills and strategies.
- Knowledge retrieval : LLMs can quickly answer queries and provide relevant information from extensive knowledge bases, ensuring that sales representatives have access to the information they need when they need it.
- Performance analysis : LLMs identify patterns and trends in sales data, offering actionable insights and recommendations for improving sales strategies and performance.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Copilot > For admins > Data safety with LLMs:
Data security and privacy are paramount at Mindtickle. When processing data with LLMs, we adhere to stringent security protocols to ensure that all information remains confidential and secure. By implementing the following measures, we ensure that our customer's data remains safe and secure while leveraging LLMs' capabilities:

- Data encryption : All data processed by LLMs is encrypted both in transit and at rest, protecting it from unauthorized access.
- Access control : We implement strict access controls to ensure that only authorized personnel can access sensitive data.
- Compliance : We comply with all relevant data protection regulations, including GDPR and CCPA, to ensure that our data handling practices meet the highest standards of privacy and security.
- Regular audits : We conduct regular security audits and assessments to identify and address potential vulnerabilities in our systems.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Asset Hub:
Outreach is a sales engagement platform that helps sales representatives manage their sales processes, particularly in the prospecting and pipeline management stages. Mindtickle's Asset Hub is a powerful tool that allows users to share assets, such as documents, images, and attachments.

The integration of Mindtickle with Outreach is designed to enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of your sales activities. By integrating the two platforms, sales reps can easily enrich their outbound emails with relevant assets from Mindtickle's Asset Hub during the prospecting stage.

The integration allows sales reps to provide valuable and engaging content to potential customers without the need to switch between multiple platforms. The integration also enables detailed tracking of customer engagement on the shared assets, providing valuable insights that can inform future sales strategies and decisions.

This article is intended for sales reps (learners) and provides information on:

1. Key features of the integration
2. How to share assets via Outreach
3. How to track engagement on shared assets
4. Caveats and important callouts

Click here to view the article for admins, which provides information on how to integrate Outreach with Mindtickle.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Asset Hub > Key features:
The Mindtickle-Outreach integration includes the following features:

1. Asset sharing: Admins and reps can add assets directly to emails, templates, snippets, or sequences from Mindtickle's Asset Hub. This allows them to send enriched emails, enhancing the prospecting process.
2. Asset engagement tracking: After an email is sent, you can track recipient (prospect) engagement on the sent assets. The system tracks customer activities, such as opening the email, clicking on the asset links, viewing the assets, and the time spent on each asset. Prospect activity (engagement) is written back to Outreach and you can view it in the Activity tab of the prospect. It provides data on the time spent on the assets, asset downloads (if downloading was enabled), and asset names. This engagement data is available only on Outreach and not on the Mindtickle platform.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Asset Hub > Share assets > Overview:
Once your admin has integrated Outreach with Mindtickle, you can add Mindtickle assets to Outreach emails, templates, snippets, and sequences. You can add assets to them using the Mindtickle app button in the toolbar.

For example, you or your admin can create a template/snippet/sequence with most frequently used assets. You can then make use of the template/snippet/sequence (with pre-populated assets) while sending emails to prospects, saving time in having to manually select and add assets for each email.

You can add Mindtickle assets to the following on Outreach:

- Email templates: You can create email templates with Mindtickle assets added to it. Users can use these templates while composing an email to automatically add assets through the templates.
- Snippets: Create snippets with assets added to it. Think of snippets as short email templates and adding of assets works similar to the email templates.
- Sequences: You can add assets for the email type of steps within a sequence. You can add assets to two step types: Automatic email and Manual email . Configuring the email steps in a sequence is similar to configuring an email template.
- Emails: The email functionality on Outreach lets you add Mindtickle assets and share them with prospects as part of the email. Later, you can track recipient engagement on the shared assets. You can add assets to an email in two ways:
  - Manually: Use the Mindtickle app button in the toolbar to select and add assets manually.
  - Through a template/snippet/sequence: Use a template/snippet/sequence with pre-populated assets to automatically add assets. This saves time in having to manually select and add assets. You can add more assets using the Mindtickle app button in the toolbar, if required.
