3. Here, you can add assets to the email in two ways:
  - Manually: Use the Mindtickle app button in the toolbar to select and add assets manually.
  - Through a template/snippet/sequence: Use a template/snippet/sequence with pre-populated assets to automatically add assets. This saves time in having to manually select and add assets. You can add more assets using the Mindtickle app button in the toolbar, if required.
4. Let's consider how to manually add assets. After writing the email message, place the cursor in the email body where you want assets to appear and click the Mindtickle app button.
5. If you are not already signed in to your Mindtickle instance, you are asked to sign in.
6. In the Add assets pop-up that appears, select one or more assets listed under the Assets and My assets tabs. Use the filters, search, and sort options at the top to find specific assets. Click the button against an asset to preview it and view other details.Once done, click Add assets to move to the next step.
7. On the next page, you can configure the various sharing related and other settings, which are explained in the next step.
8. You can configure the following sharing related and other settings for the selected assets:
  - Recipient activity notifications: Turn on the setting if you want to be notified via email whenever a recipient interacts with the shared assets. It has the following options:
    - Notify me when the recipient engages with the assets along with the engagement summary
    - Notify me when the recipient shares assets with their peers
    - Notify me when a recipient is active
  - Reminder notifications: Turn on the setting if you want to set an email reminder to check the engagement on shared assets. It has the following options:
    - Remind me to check engagement data
    - Remind me only if there is no activity
  - Allow download: Turn on the setting if you want to allow recipients to download the shared assets. The option to download is unavailable for embedded assets (for example, a youtube video embedded link).
  - Access expiration: Configure the setting if you want the recipient's access to expire for the shared assets after the set time (for example, renewals, contracts, and licenses). It ensures that the recipients always access the latest and most relevant content.
  - Add internal notes: Use the section as your personal notetaker to jot down the ideas or thoughts about sharing the assets. It will help you remember why you shared these assets with the customer or prospect in the later stages of the sales cycle.
  - Additionally, under the Reorder and rename assets section on the right side, you can:
    - Rearrange the selected assets in your preferred order.
    - Hover over an asset for options to rename or delete the asset.

10. The selected assets get added to the email body (where your cursor was placed), not as attachments. You can view a preview of the email message along with the assets on the right.Click Send a test email to send a test email to yourself, to check how the email would look to the recipients.At last, click Send if all looks good. Or, click Save as draft to save this email for later.
11. The following image shows an example of the email that recipients receive.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Asset Hub > Track recipient engagement > Overview:
Once the recipients (prospects) interact with the assets sent via Outreach, you can track their engagement with the shared assets on Outreach. Prospect activity (engagement) is written back to Outreach and you can view it in the Activity tab of the prospect. It provides data on the time spent on the assets, asset downloads, and asset names.

Note:

- All Outreach users can view the asset engagement data. Additionally, the page provides activity data for all recipients if the email was sent to multiple prospects.
- This engagement data is available only on Outreach. It is no longer shown on the Mindtickle platform.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Asset Hub > Caveats:
Consider the following caveats and important information on Mindtickle's integration with Outreach:

- This integration is supported only for Outreach on the web, available at https://web.outreach.io . It is not supported for the Outreach mobile app.
- The integration does not support engagement data tracking if you share assets using the Outreach Everywhere extension for Google Chrome browser. You can add assets to your email using the extension; however, engagement tracking will not be available.
- The activity (asset engagement) writeback to Outreach is enabled by default and you cannot disable it.
- If assets are added to an email through a template — and not through the Mindtickle app in the toolbar — then the recipient's information will not be captured. This means that the tracking data will not include specific information about who viewed the assets.
- When assets are shared with the prospects via Outreach, they are asked to provide consent for Mindtickle to track their asset engagement. If a prospect does not provide consent, then Mindtickle cannot trace the interaction back to the prospect. Therefore, Mindtickle can neither receive nor share the activity (engagement) data on the assets for this prospect.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > External Content Access:
This article provides an overview of how Mindtickle users can access Confluence content in Mindtickle and further share it with their prospects using the existing capabilities of both platforms.

Note:

- The Mindtickle-Confluence out-of-the-box integration is currently unavailable.
- Due to Confluence's content policy, Confluence pages cannot be embedded or placed within the iframes of external systems.

The ways to access Confluence content in Mindtickle are:

- Export Confluence pages as PDFs
- Add shareable links to Confluence pages

- Export Confluence pages as PDFs
- Add shareable links to Confluence pages

chunks.title: Access Confluence content in Mindtickle

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > External Content Access > Export Confluence pages as PDFs:
You can export Confluence pages as PDFs and upload them in Mindtickle.

1. Click the ••• more options icon at the upper right corner of any Confluence page, select Export from the dropdown menu, and click Export to PDF .

The Export PDFs page appears with the time elapsed, time remaining, and the completion percentage for the PDF file.

2. Click Download PDF to save the file on your local drive.

You can add the exported PDF (wherever applicable) to Mindtickle. For example:

- Upload content in a course or quick-update
- Add content in Content Center
- Add content to Factopedia
- Create overview pages
- Add and configure widgets for learning site homepages
- Create a new asset

Advantages of exporting Confluence pages as PDFs in Mindtickle

Through this mode, scoring and completion of the content can be tracked as they appear in the PDF in Mindtickle.

Disadvantages of exporting Confluence pages as PDFs in Mindtickle

Since the PDFs are static files, any updates made on the source Confluence page is not automatically updated in the exported PDF in Mindtickle. Users must manually update the export and replace the file in Mindtickle to ensure the latest information is available. For more information, see Add or replace a file in learning object using Content Center.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > External Content Access > Add shareable links to Confluence pages > Share with members of your organization:
To share a Confluence page with the members of your organization:

1. Click the copy link icon directly on a confluence page

or

Click Share on the upper right corner of any Confluence page and select Copy link.

The link is copied to the clipboard. You can add the shareable link (wherever applicable) in Mindtickle. For example:

- Add shareable link on Overview pages
- Add shareable links to series overview page
- Add links to series descriptions
- Create a rich text document and add the link to it
- Create a one-pager PDF/PPT and add the link to it
- Clicking the link opens the Confluence content in a new tab.

Note: Users who receive this link must have a Confluence account.

Advantages of adding shareable links to Confluence pages in Mindtickle

Since the Confluence content is available over a URL, the updates made on the source Confluence page are automatically available in Mindtickle. So learners always have access to the most recently updated Confluence pages.

Disadvantages of adding shareable links to Confluence pages in Mindtickle

The learner’s score and completion status are marked as 100% and Complete once the learner clicks the link to the Confluence page. Hence, through this mode, analytics or progress on the Confluence links cannot be tracked granularly in Mindtickle.

Tip: For a better user experience, it is suggested that metadata such as title, description, and some visual information be included in the document along with the link in Mindtickle.

This article explains how reps can share assets from a Salesforce opportunity to a linked Digital Sales Room (DSR) using the Share via room feature.

The Share via room feature is built into the existingShare functionality for assets, available in multiple places in the Assets section of the learning site. While sharing (adding) assets to rooms, the feature also provides options to specify the section headers under which the assets should be placed. Furthermore, you can also select who you want to notify about this update.

Note:

- You can only share assets marked External by the admin or asset owner that have not expired.
- This feature is not available for the Mindtickle mobile app or from a mobile web browser. It is available only on the web when accessing Mindtickle from a web browser.
- Asset Hub and Digital Sales Rooms are standalone, paid products from Mindtickle. To use this feature, you must have a license for both. Please contact your CSM for more information.
- You must have an active DSR to Salesforce connection. Users cannot share via room if the DSR to Salesforce connection is unavailable.
- This connection is different from the Asset Hub - Salesforce connection.

To add assets to an existing digital sales room (DSR) from a Salesforce opportunity, you need to perform the following sub-tasks:

1. Select assets to share
2. Select room section headers
3. Select to notify room contacts

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Asset Hub > Select room section headers:
In this step, you can select the section header where the selected assets are added to the room linked to the opportunity. Sections are strategic parts of a room where users can structure sales content.

You may have organization-level section headers available; users can create them at the room level. Your assets are added to the section headers you select or the top of the room if no section header is specified. For more information on section headers, see Set Up Digital Sales Rooms.

The Select section headers page lists the assets you have selected for sharing.

Perform the following on this page:

- Name in room: Provide a name of your choice for each asset. This can be different from the original name of the asset, which is populated by default.
- Section header: For each asset, select the section header from the room to add the asset.

Note: Assets are added to the top of the room if no section header is specified.

The following options are available for the section header:

- Common headers: The existing section headers in the room are displayed.
- Organization headers: These are section headers set by admins at the organization level and are available for use in all rooms. These headers may or may not exist in the selected rooms, but you can always select them. For example, if the selected rooms does not have any common headers, you can always select organization headers.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Asset Hub > Select to notify room contacts:
As a last step, choose whether you want to notify the room contacts (recipients) about the assets you are adding/sharing to the selected room. If you choose to notify, you can further select groups of recipients whom you want to notify. An email is sent to selected room recipients.

The following options are available:

- No, don’t notify: Select if you do not want to notify the room contacts about this change.
- Yes, notify: Select if you want to notify the room contacts. The following additional options are available:
  - Email message (Optional): You can add a message to the email sent to the contacts.
  - Select recipients: Select which room contacts (recipients) should receive the email.
    - All: All room contacts
      - Visited: Contacts who have already visited the room
      - Didn’t visit: Contacts who have not yet visited the room
      - Collaborators: DSR admins and users who are collaborators in the room
    - Send a copy to me: Select if you want to receive a copy of the email
  - Preview email: Select to preview the email sent to the room recipients.

4. Once done, click Share to add assets to the selected rooms.

A message confirms that assets are added to the room.

Additionally, if you had selected to notify the room contacts, all contacts (recipients) are notified through email. Everyone with room access can now view the newly shared assets when visiting the room.

Note: If you share assets in a room where they already exist, they are not shared again to avoid duplication. A message is displayed that the assets are not added to the room since it already has them.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Asset Hub > Share assets via new room:
The Share via new room option allows users to share assets for a Salesforce opportunity that does not have a room in DSR.

When reps try to share assets for an opportunity without a room, a new room is created and linked to that opportunity. The selected assets are shared in the new room. For more information on creating a new room, see Create, Save, Publish, and Share a Digital Sales Room.

To share assets via a new room,

1. Click the Share assets button in the lower-right corner of the Opportunity page in Salesforce.
2. Select the assets you want to share on the pop-up that is displayed.
3. Once assets are selected, click Share assets and select Share via new room .

The Create Sales Room page opens in a new tab. The opportunity details for the new room are automatically updated from Salesforce in the Select Opportunity tab.

A message is displayed that assets were added successfully; you can view them on the Review page.

4. Click Next Step.

The Review page is displayed with the assets added.

5. Click Publish to publish the room with the assets. The selected assets are now shared in the new room.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Mobile App > Overview > Semantic global search:
The global search on the Mindtickle app is a hybrid implementation that makes use of the traditional keyword-based search in combination with the modern, AI-powered semantic search. It delivers more accurate and relevant results, improving the overall search quality and the user experience for our learners.

The traditional keyword-based search looks for information only by the keyword (search term) in the name, description, and tags/attributes of the content. Mindtickle's global search is hybrid, delivering results based on keyword and semantic search powered by AI. Semantic search tries to understand the context and intent behind user queries through advanced machine learning models to transform unstructured data into a semantic representation, enabling more accurate and contextually relevant search results. For example, if you search for “country”, you will get results that have “country” in the content as well as results that are related to the term “country”, such as the United States, India, and Brazil.

Learners can search across different entities: series, modules, assets, hubs, files, and peers. You can apply various filters and sort options to further narrow down the results to what you are looking for.

Highlight features

- Precision: The AI-powered semantic search digs deep to understand the meaning behind user queries, delivering more accurate and satisfying results.
- Engagement: With the improved interface and filters, the search experience becomes interactive and engaging.
- Decision power: Equips users with precise, decision-shaping information, guaranteeing better outcomes.
- Productivity boost: More relevant and fast search results; saves time and accelerates user productivity.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Mobile App > Overview > Search-integrated Copilot Assistant for Sellers:
Mindtickle’s Copilot Assistant for Sellers is an AI-powered search capability, available right within the global search functionality on the Mindtickle app. The Copilot Assistant provides an advanced, AI-powered search functionality blended with just-in-time (JIT) enablement, making it a versatile tool for sellers. It helps sellers with the most relevant and accurate information about their products and personas, competitive differentiators, and value proposition, among other things.

Here is how it works:

- The way to ask questions to the Copilot Assistant is straightforward. You can simply type in a question or request in the search bar. The question does not necessarily need to be framed as a question; it can be framed as a request. However, it's recommended to specify your request or question for more accurate responses. You can ask any questions related to the content available on your learning site.
- The Copilot Assistant quickly provides a summarized and helpful answer, along with links to the sources of the answer and related content.
- The Copilot Assistant generates answers from training modules and assets that the user has access to. These include assigned series and modules, public series and modules, assets across hubs, video transcriptions, text, PDF, PowerPoint, and Word files. However, it cannot search in SCORM content because it is a closed format, and it also cannot search images.

What would usually take sellers significant time and effort in trying to find the right information by navigating across modules and assets is now easily available in seconds.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Mobile App > Prerequisites and caveats:
Prerequisites

- To enable the AI-powered global search and the Copilot Assistant for Sellers, you must first opt for Mindtickle’s AI capability on the platform. This is because the global search makes use of AI to provide most relevant and accurate results. To enable the AI capability (if you haven’t already) and the global search, please contact your CSM or Mindtickle Support . It gets enabled within 72 business hours.
- If Mindtickle Copilot is not enabled for your Mindtickle instance, then the traditional keyword based search will be available instead of the AI-powered semantic search.

Caveats and notes

Please consider the following caveats and other important information:

- Call AI calls are currently not available in the global search results; they will be included in a future release. In the meantime, you can search for calls from the Call AI tab. Both have their separate search functionality.
- All newly-added content will appear in the global search in near realtime. In most cases, within a minute. However, there could be delays in case of bulk operations on the platform, such as bulk module operations and bulk asset creation .
- Site owners can remove any entity from appearing in the global search by writing to Mindtickle Support . We will remove it from being searched for your users. Example use case: You do not want people to search and access their peers’ info.
- The global search works only when you are online; not supported in offline mode.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Mobile App > Prerequisites and caveats > Supported entities:
The global search supports various entities (types of content) on the Mindtickle platform. It displays all results from across various entities: series, modules, hubs, assets, files, module tags, and peers. Think of entities as categories or types of content on the platform. We have also provided entity related filters so you can view results by one or more entities.

You can search on the following entities. The global search looks for your searched term into the mentioned properties for each entity:

- Assets: Asset name, description, attributes, asset file content, and the hub names where the asset resides
- Modules: Module name and description
- Tags: Tags applied to modules only. Tags applied to files, questions, polls, and evaluation parameters (for missions and coaching sessions) are currently not supported.
- Files: File name and file content (including Content Center files)
- Series: Series name and description
- Asset hubs: Hub name, description, and overview page content
- Peers (colleagues): Name, username, and email address

Note: By default, the search is enabled for all entities. However, you can choose to enable it only for specific entities. Please contact Mindtickle Support for further help.

You can run a search across the learning site using the search icon, available in the top navigation bar on the homepage as well as other pages, such as Series, Assets, and Coaching.

1. Tap the search icon in the top-right corner to get started. It displays a dropdown menu with a list of your seven recent/previous searches, if any. Use the Clear all option to remove recent searches.
2. Simply start typing what you are looking for. You must enter at least 3 characters to search. What you enter in the search bar is referred to as a search query, search keyword, or search.
3. The dropdown menu automatically lists top results as you start typing.

You can take the following actions: Tap on any of the suggested results to open it. Tap View all results or press to view all results on the search results page, where you can apply filters and sort the results.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Mobile App > A. Copilot Assistant:
Perform the following to use the Copilot Assistant for Sellers through the ssearch functionality:

1. Type a question, keyword, or phrase in the search bar and then press Enter.It is recommended to frame your queries as specific questions or instructions for most accurate and relevant results.For example, if you ask "What is Seller Intel?", the Copilot Assistant may not know whether you want a summary, strengths, weaknesses, or other details about Seller Intel. Therefore, enter specific questions as much as possible.
2. The search results page appears, where the response from the Copilot Assistant is available at the top, in a light-orange background.The Copilot Assistant generates answers from training modules and assets that the user has access to. These include assigned series and modules, public series and modules, assets across hubs, video transcriptions, text, PDF, PowerPoint, and Word files. However, it cannot search in SCORM content because it is a closed format, and it also cannot search images.Note: The Copilot Assistant can make mistakes. Please ensure to review the information in the response for accuracy as necessary before making use of the information.
3. You can take the various actions in the response from the Copilot Assistant. Continue reading for details.
4. Tap the icon to collapse or expand the entire Copilot Assistant section on the results page. Tap Show more/less to collapse or expand the response (answer) provided by the Copilot Assistant.

1. When you tap Show more, it displays the complete response along with all sources and related content from which the Copilot Assistant derived the information. Tap on any of the links to go to the content, such as a module or an asset.In the response, you can select and copy specific parts or the entire response.

- Mirrored module: Mirrored (multi-present) modules in the results are indicated with the icon.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Announcements > FAQs > What happens during the migration process?:
- The automation suite service will be unavailable for 3 hours during migration. All other operations on the platform are operational; only the automation suite service will be unavailable.
- All automation rules are rewritten from the old automation suite to the new automation platform during the migration.
- If any changes are made during this migration process, the system ensures that they are evaluated and related automation rules are executed.

- The migration agent ensures that the user is assigned to the series ‘Sales-US-Strategy’ only after completing the migration process.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Get Started > About semantic search:
The traditional keyword-based search looks for information only by the keyword (search query) in the name, description, and tags/attributes of the content. Mindtickle's new global semantic search is hybrid, and delivers more relevant and contextual results by combining both keyword-based search and semantic search powered by generative AI. Semantic search tries to understand the context and intent behind user queries through advanced machine learning models to transform unstructured data into a semantic representation, enabling more accurate and contextually relevant search results. For example, if you search for "country", you will get results that have "country" in the content as well as results that are related to the term "country", such as the United States, India, and Brazil.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Get Started > About semantic search > How the search works:
Mindtickle's global semantic search is available for both the learning site and the Mindtickle app. For the keywords (words or phrases used to search) that you enter while searching, the search looks for results in the content metadata/properties, such as content name, description, and attributes. It looks into the metadata of various entities, such as assets, modules, module tags, files, and series. Think of entities as categories or types of content on the platform. Use entity related filters to view results for one or more entities.

Note: To provide a cleaner search experience on the web platform, global search automatically uses duplicate file grouping to consolidate identical standalone files and files used within assets into a single search result. For more information, see Global search on the learning site.

For your searched keywords, the global semantic search looks into the metadata/properties of the following entities:

- Assets: Asset name, description, attributes, asset file content, and the hub names where the asset resides
- Modules: Module name and description
- Tags: Tags applied to modules only. Tags applied to files, questions, polls, and evaluation parameters (for missions and coaching sessions) are currently not supported.
- Files: File name and file content
- Series: Series name and description
- Asset hubs: Hub name, description, and overview page content
- Peers (colleagues): Name, username, and email address

Note: The global semantic search is enabled for all entities by default. However, you can choose to enable it only for specific entities. Please contact Mindtickle Support to disable searching on certain entities.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Get Started > About semantic search > Types of search:
There are two types of search or ways of searching:

- Normal search is when you simply enter your query in the search bar, without closing your query in double quotation marks (" "). Example of a normal search query: sales enablement . It fetches results containing "sales", "enablement", and both.
- Exact search is when you enter your search query in double quotation marks (" "), which ensures that the global semantic search looks only for the exact search query (word or phrase). Example of an exact search query: "sales enablement" . It fetches results containing "sales enablement" only.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Get Started > Content matching for search queries:
When you enter your query in the search bar, the global semantic search looks for results by matching your search query against various content metadata/properties in the platform.

The global semantic search does the following with respect to your search query (word or phrase) to deliver accurate and relevant results:

- Match variants of your query: Tries to match variants of your query: match the exact query, match all words of the query, partially match all words, and match one or more stemmed words of the query.
- Match query against: Tries to match the query against content metadata, such as series name/description, asset name/description/content.

Consider the following example based on the table below:

If you are searching for "sales enablement", the global semantic search looks for "sales enablement", "sales", "enablement" in series name/description, module name/description/tags, asset name/description/content/attributes, and so on. The most relevant results appear first, be it assets, modules, files, series, etc.

Important: The following table information is for a normal search. However, you can refer to it also for exact searches: look for the "exact match" criteria in this table to know how it works for exact searches.

For your searched query, the global semantic search looks for matching content in the following metadata/properties of various entities (modules, assets, etc.) and exactly in the order listed for each entity:

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > CRMs > Create Named Credentials:
Named credentials provide a way to define the scope of access to the external service, including specifying which Salesforce users or profiles can access it. They are a secure way to store authentication information for an external service or API. To create named credentials:

1. Click thegear icon on the upper-right corner and select Setup in Salesforce.

2. On the left panel, go to Security and click Named Credentials.

3. Click New Legacy.

4. The Label and Name should be Mindtickle_Asset (case sensitive).

5. URL should be ‘https://<learning site>.mindtickle.com’.

6. Select the certificate generated in the previous section.

7. Set the Identity Type as Per User.

8. Set the AuthenticationProtocol as JWT.

9. Set the Issuer as Mindtickle (case sensitive).

10. Set Per User Subject as $User.Username.

Note: You can configure any user attribute other than the username. For example, you can configure Per User Subject as $User.Email, or $User.User. If your Mindtickle email address or username differs from your Salesforce email address, you should specify a custom user attribute to ensure successful authentication.

12. Audiences should contain the company ID (cname) of your Mindtickle instance.

13. Set the Token Validity for 365 Days.

14. Select the Mindtickle certificate as the JWT Signing Certificate. This should be the same certificate as the one selected in step 6.

Note: Do not change any other default attributes.

15. Click Save.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > CRMs > Frequently asked questions (FAQs):
1. What should I do if I cannot access the Readiness Dashboard page and receive an error?

Check that the user has access to all the apex classes listed below:

- MindTickleDev.MDTAssetHubIntegrationController
- MindTickleDev.MdtBookmarked_Asset
- MindTickleDev.MdtCommonController
- MindTickleDev.MdtExternallyShareableController
- MindTickleDev.mdtHubList
- MindTickleDev.MdtPlayController
- MindTickleDev.MdtRecommendedAssets

The SFDC user on the Mindtickle instance has the same username as SFDC.

2. What is the recommended web browser?

For the best experience use the Google Chrome web browser.

3. Can we show different readiness dashboards to different users based on their access to them?

If you have the latest version of Salesforce installed, you can configure Multiple LS settings using the LSusersetting object in Salesforce. For more details, contact Mindtickle Support.

4. Is there any other way to configure this component besides adding it as a Tab?

Yes, as this is a lightning component, you can add it anywhere.

5. Can we add this to the Account/Contact/Opportunity detail page?

Yes. Drag and drop the mtReadinessdashboard component on the Account/Contact/Opportunity detail page.

4. Is there any other way to configure this component besides adding it as a Tab?

Yes, as this is a lightning component, you can add it anywhere.

5. Can we add this to the Account/Contact/Opportunity detail page?

Yes. Drag and drop the mtReadinessdashboard component on the Account/Contact/Opportunity detail page.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > CRMs:
This article explains the steps to connect the learning site to a Salesforce sandbox instance after a refresh.

Note: You can also use the same steps to connect the learning site to a new Salesforce sandbox instance created from production (with Mindtickle configuration).

A Salesforce sandbox refresh is a process that copies data and metadata from production (with Mindtickle configuration) to a different sandbox, making the sandbox similar to production.

The steps to configure the connection are:

1. Modify named credentials
2. Download the certificate from Salesforce
3. Perform an OAuth on the Mindtickle learning site
4. Upload the certificate to the Mindtickle learning site

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > CRMs > Prerequisites:
The prerequisites for this connection are:

- Create two users with the following permissions:
  - Create a user and assign a System Administration profile in Salesforce. OR You can create a custom user role from the System Administration profile and assign it ModifyAllData or ModifyMetadata permissions.
  - Mindtickle strongly recommends using a dedicated Salesforce integration user.For more information on creating an integration user and granting the required permissions, see Create an Integration User in SFDC.
  - Create a user and assign an IT admin role to Mindtickle. For more information on assigning an IT admin role for a user, see Roles and permissions in Mindtickle.
- Install the Mindtickle packages in production. Contact Mindtickle Support for the installation.
- Connect the Salesforce production environment to the Mindtickle production environment.

7. Under the Connected App column, click the Install button on Mindtickle Salesforce OAuth.
8. On the displayed pop-up screen, click Install.

The Mindtickle Salesforce OAuth app is now installed on the Salesforce instance.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Digital Sales Rooms:
DSR admins and reps can configure access permissions for content shared in DSRs. The restricted content is visible only to reps with permissions and is highlighted by a lock icon in the DSR.

For example, if you want to share a sensitive deal contract document with your prospect’s CFO and avoid showing it to other reps visiting the room, you can configure permission for the document and share it in a DSR. The content is visible only to the CFO and other reps with permission.

To configure permissions for a content in a DSR:

1. Log on to your learning site and click the Digital Sales Room icon. The R ooms page is displayed.
2. Click the Edit room icon on a DSR. The Edit Sales Room page is displayed.
3. Click the edit icon on a content item to configure access permissions.

The Edit content screen is displayed.

In the Who can view? section, the following options are available:

- All room visitors: This is the default option; it makes the content visible to all visitors.
- Visitors with access only: This option displays the content only to reps with permissions.

4. Click Done after selecting the content permission.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Digital Sales Rooms > Share restricted content:
To share restricted content in a DSR,

1. On the Who can view? section, select the Visitors with access only option.
2. Click Add to select the rep to provide access to the content.

Note: It is mandatory to add at least one contact to share the content.

The Access list screen is displayed.

You can search for an existing contact by name or email address to provide access to the content.

You can also enter a new contact’s name or email address and click Add as new contact to create a new contact and provide access to the content.

3. Click Done, and share the room. The specified members are provided access to the content.

Hover over the lock icon of restricted content in a DSR to view the list of members with access. You can view the names of the last 5 members granted access.

Note: When sharing content, if a section header contains only the restricted content, that section is not displayed to buyers without permission. For information on creating section headers, see Set Up Digital Sales Rooms.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Instructor-Led Training (ILT):
The Instructor-led trainings (ILTs) page allows administrators and site owners to view ILT sessions across various modules in a calendar format on a single page. They can view the total number of sessions on the learning site and individual sessions scheduled by date.

Note:

- The sessions displayed on the Instructor-led trainings (ILTs) page are based on the settings configured on the Settings page. For more information, see Configure the Instructor-led trainings (ILT) page settings .
- To modify a session, you must be the module creator or collaborator for the series with the session. For more information on collaborators, see Collaborator Management .

You can perform the following on the Instructor-led trainings (ILTs) page

- View sessions
- Create an event
- Create a session
- Edit a session
- Manage a session
- Copy session link
- Export session schedules
- Download QR code for sessions

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Instructor-Led Training (ILT) > View sessions:
To view the scheduled ILT sessions from across modules on the Instructor-led trainings (ILTs) page,

1. Sign in to the admin site .
2. On the left navigation bar, click Settings and select the ILTs .

The Instructor-led trainings (ILTs) page is displayed.

You can view the following details on the Instructor-led trainings (ILTs) page:

- Date: The scheduled date of the session or event.
- Time (GMT+5:30): The scheduled time of the session or event. The system displays the session schedule based on the admin’s system time zone.
- Session: The name of the session or the name of the session and the event when the session is part of an event.
- Module: The name of the module.
- Series: The name of the series.
- Instructor: The instructor for the session.
- Enrolled: The number of enrollments for the session.

Users can search for a session by name. The ILT sessions can be filtered by Series, Module, Instructor, Event, and Created by.

You can select multiple filters. If no sessions are available for the applied filters, a message displays that no upcoming sessions are scheduled.

You can click Reset to clear all applied filters.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Instructor-Led Training (ILT) > Create an event:
This section explains how to create a new event on the Instructor-led trainings (ILTs) page.To create a new event,

1. On the Instructor-led trainings (ILTs) page, click Scroll to date and select a date to view the training sessions created for that date.

Note: You can also scroll down the page to see upcoming sessions and scroll up to see sessions from the past.

2. Click the Create button and select the Event option to create a new event.

The Create Event screen is displayed.

3. In Where should the event be created? select the series to create the event.

4. Click Go to module after selecting the series.

Note: You should create at least one session on the module page to publish an event.

For more information on how to create a new event, see Create ILT Events or Sessions.

Once the event is created, it is displayed on the module page.

Once the changes are published, the session details are added to the series, module, and Instructor-led trainings (ILTs) page.

To return to the Instructor-led trainings (ILTs) page, click on All sessions.

You can also click Add session on a date on the Instructor-led trainings (ILTs) page to create a new session.

This section explains how to create an ILT session on the Instructor-led trainings (ILTs) page.To create a session,

1. On the Instructor-led trainings (ILTs) page, click Scroll to date and select a date to view the training sessions created for a specific date.

2. Click the Create button and select the Session option to create a new session.

You can also click Add session on a date to create a new session.

The Create session screen is displayed.

3. In Where should the session be created? select the series or a module to create the session. This is mandatory.

4. In Select the module that it should be created in? select a module to create the session. This field is displayed only if a series is selected in Where should the session be created?. This is mandatory.

5. In Select this option if the session is part of an event you can select the event to schedule the session.

Note: The events in Draft status are not displayed for selection in this menu.

6. Select the Start date and Start time for the session.

7. Select the End date and End time for the session.

8. Click Go to module.

For more information on creating a new ILT session, see Create ILT Events or Sessions.

The session is created and displayed in the series. Once published, the module is added to the series, module, and Instructor-led training (ILTs) page.

The Deals report provides information on deals and the rooms associated with them. It includes information on the deal stage, value, opportunity closing date, and room activity. This report helps you understand how teams use DSRs for deals.

A message is displayed that the report will be emailed once the data is ready.

The report includes the options selected in the Teams, Deal Owner, Deal Stage, Deal Type, and Minimum Deal Amount filters.

Tip: You can configure the word ‘Deal’ to say ‘Opportunity’ for this report. Contact Mindtickle Support for this customization.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Digital Sales Rooms > Signing a Docusign envelope:
To sign a Docusign envelope, you should be added as a signer by the Docusign envelope owner. The Docusign envelope owner can add or remove signers in Docusign. Only assigned signers can sign the Docusign envelope and download the completed envelope.

Note:

- Docusign sends an email notification to the signers when they are added for signing.
- The Mindtickle-Docusign integration for DSRs does not impact the emails Docusign sends to signers and envelope owners. You will continue to receive emails from Docusign.

To sign the envelope as an assigned signer,

1. Click on a room with the Docusign envelope.

2. Click View Room to view the DSR.

The DSR opens.

3. Click the Sign button on the Docusign envelope.

The document opens in Docusign.

4. Click Continue.

5. Review and sign the document wherever necessary.

6. On the displayed pop-up, click Finish.

Once all the designated signers sign the envelope, the Docusign envelope status is updated to Completed, and the Download button is displayed.

Docsign sends an email notification to the envelope owner and the signers once the document signing is completed.

Note:

- Only assigned signers can download the completed Docusign envelopes.
- A Docusign envelope can be accessed and signed through email, even if the envelope is attached to the room.

7. In the DSR, click the Download button on the Docusign envelope to save a copy of the completed envelope.

The completed document is now saved to your computer.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Instructor-Led Training (ILT):
The Duration-based attendance capture feature lets admins automatically record learners’ attendance based on time spent in ILTs. Admins can configure a minimum percentage threshold to record learners’ attendance for ILT modules or individual sessions.

The Duration-based attendance capture feature can be set at the:

- Learning site level
- ILT module level
- Individual session level

Note:

- You must be an admin to view the learner's attendance for ILT sessions. To assign roles and permissions to a user, see Assign roles and permissions in Mindtickle .
- The Duration-based attendance capture feature applies only to ILTs conducted in Zoom, Teams, and Webex with auto attendance enabled. It does not apply to classroom training.
- This feature is enabled by default for the learning site.

Attendance calculation

The web conferencing integration tool (Zoom, Teams, and Webex) provides the learner's time in a session.

The system calculates an ILT session’s minimum attendance threshold as follows,

- Scheduled sessions: For scheduled sessions that are yet to start, the system calculates the minimum attendance threshold using the session's start and end time set during session creation. For example, in a 60-minute session with a 20% minimum attendance threshold, the system marks the learner as attended if they spend at least 12 minutes (20% of 60) in the session.
- Completed sessions: If a session ends early or extends beyond the scheduled time, the system calculates the minimum attendance threshold based on the actual session time. For example, for a 60-minute session with a 20% minimum attendance threshold, if the session ends early in 50 minutes, the system marks the learner as attended if they spend at least 10 minutes (20% of 50) in the session.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Instructor-Led Training (ILT) > Configure duration-based attendance capture for the learning site:
To configure the duration-based capture for the learning site:

1. Sign in to the admin site .
2. On the left navigation bar, click Account and select Settings . By default, the Training tab is displayed on the Settings page.
3. Click the Instructor-led trainings (ILTs) tab. The Instructor-led trainings (ILTs) page is displayed. The following options are available:

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Instructor-Led Training (ILT) > Configure duration-based attendance capture for the learning site > Configure the minimum attendance percentage for ILT modules:
You can customize the attendance percentage at the ILT module level to suit specific training needs. For example, you might set a lower attendance percentage for optional ILT modules and a higher percentage for mandatory compliance training modules.

The changes to an ILT module's minimum attendance percentage apply only to new sessions, not existing sessions or sessions from the past.

The learners’ attendance status is always calculated based on the minimum attendance percentage set at the ILT session level, irrespective of the default minimum percentage set for the learning site.

The minimum attendance percentage applies to the actual session time. The system marks the attendance by comparing the learners’ time in session with the actual session time.

Note: To configure the minimum attendance percentage at the ILT module level, admins need to enable the Allow editing at the module and session level switch in the Instructor-led trainings (ILTs) tab of the Settings page.

To configure the minimum attendance for an ILT module,

1. Sign in to the admin site .
2. On the left navigation bar, click Training and select Series.
3. Click the series with the ILT module. For example, Acme Product Training .
4. Click the ILT module. For example, Acme Sales Kick-Off 2025 .
5. Click Settings to view the ILT module settings.
6. Select the Scoring and completion tab.
7. Click the Default minimum time to record learners' attendance switch to enable the duration-based attendance for the ILT module.
8. In Set a minimum time to record learners’ attendance , enter the minimum attendance percentage for the ILT module. By default, the value is set to 60%. You can modify this setting.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Instructor-Led Training (ILT) > View learners' attendance in ILTs:
The Attendance status/Duration column displays the learner’s attendance status for ILT modules and individual sessions. You can also view the time spent by the learner in the ILT sessions.

The learners’ attendance status (Attended or Did not attend) is calculated based on the minimum attendance percentage configured for the session.

- The learners are marked as Not Attended , and their attendance duration is not displayed,
  - If a session extends 30 minutes past its scheduled time, the minimum attendance percentage setting is ON .
- The learners are marked as Attended , and their attendance duration is not displayed,
  - If a session extends 30 minutes past its scheduled time, the minimum attendance percentage setting is OFF.

Note:

- You must be an admin to view the learner's attendance for ILT sessions.
- Attendance and completion status are calculated separately. A learner who watches a session recording could be marked as Did not attend but still achieve a Completed status.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > FAQs:
The additional users are automatically added to Mindtickle during user sync because:

- When creating new users in a platform (for example, Salesforce), if you link a manager without a Mindtickle account to a new user, the system creates a new account for the manager in Mindtickle.

During user sync, both the manager and the new user accounts are added to the Mindtickle platform.

Note: This applies to both manual and bulk uploads of users in Mindtickle.

For example, when bulk uploading 200 users to Mindtickle using a CSV, if you link 100 users to 100 managers without a Mindtickle account, Mindtickle automatically creates 100 user accounts for the managers.

During user sync, the 100 managers and the 200 new user accounts are added to Mindtickle.

- When adding users from other platforms (for example, Salesforce) to Mindtickle, if a deactivated manager is linked to a user. The new user is added during user sync, and the linked manager’s account is also reactivated on the Mindtickle platform.

Tip: Before deactivating a manager’s account, unlink it from any linked users to prevent reactivations in the future.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Digital Sales Rooms > Map room links to Salesforce custom fields:
Admins can map the room visitor and room analytics links to the custom fields created in Salesforce.

To map the custom fields to room links:

1. Sign in to the admin site .
2. Click Rooms and select Settings .

1. On the Settings page, select the Integrations tab. The CRM tab is displayed by default.
2. Click Configure to configure Salesforce settings.

The Configure Salesforce data sync screen is displayed.

5. Click the Map custom fields tab. The following options are displayed:

- Room visitor link: This is the link used to share the room. This displays the link to the DSR in the Salesforce opportunity.
- Room analytics link: This is the link to view the Room overview page. You can view the room's deal, contact, and visitor information on this page.

6. To map the Room visitor link, select the custom field created in Salesforce for the room from the Salesforce field menu.

Note:

- You first need to create the custom Salesforce opportunity fields for the custom fields to appear on the Salesforce field menu.
- When creating the custom fields in Salesforce, it is recommended that they be labeled as Room visitor link and Room analytics link .
- The custom fields should have the field type URL , or have the type Text with at least a 255-character limit.

7. To map the Room analytics link, select the appropriate custom field created in Salesforce from the Salesforce field menu.

A message is displayed once the fields are mapped successfully.

You can hover over the screen tip to view the screenshots of the Room visitor link and the Room analytics link.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > User Sync:
This article explains how to integrate Mindtickle with OneLogin for automated user provisioning using SCIM (System for Cross-domain Identity Management).

OneLogin is an identity provider that performs authentication, authorization, and user provisioning. It supports SAML 2.0 for SSO and SCIM for automated user provisioning.

The benefits of Mindtickle SCIM user provisioning through Onelogin are:

- When users are added, updated, or deleted in Onelogin, they are updated automatically in the Mindtickle platform.
- The state of users synced from third-party apps to Onelogin will also be reflected live on the Mindtickle platform.

Note: Onelogin will be considered a source of truth and will override the changes in Mindtickle. Hence, if a user's email address (provisioned through Onelogin) changes, we recommend updating it directly in Onelogin instead of creating a new user.

This article further explains how to set up and activate user sync on Mindtickle using Onelogin.

1. Sign in to OneLogin using your credentials.

2. To open the admin page, click Administration.

3. To view the Applications page, click the Applications menu and select the Applications option.

The Applications page is displayed.

4. To add a new application, click Add App.

5. Enter SCIM Provisioner with SAML (SCIM v2 Enterprise) in the search.

The search results are displayed.

6. Click on SCIM Provisioner with SAML (SCIM v2 Enterprise) to add the application.

7. Enter a display name for the application. For example, Mindtickle.

8. Select icons for the Mindtickle application in Rectangular Icon or Square Icon. This helps identify the application quickly.

Note:

- For the application icon, you can select a transparent .PNG or .SVG file.
- For the Rectangular Icon , upload a file with 2.64:1 aspect ratio .
- For the Square Icon , upload a file of size, 512x512px .

9. Click Save.

The Mindtickle application is added, and the Info tab is displayed.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > User Sync > Setting up the Mindtickle app in OneLogin > Configure the SCIM application:
To configure the SCIM application,

1. On the Configuration tab, scroll down to the API Connection section.

2. In the SCIM Base URL, enter https://scim.mindtickle.com/{domain}/scim/v2.

3. Replace domain with the customer domain name in mindtickle. For example, https://scim.mindtickle.com/acme/scim/v2. This is required for handling multi-region routing.

The default template details are displayed in the SCIM JSON Template section.

4. Remove the details from the SCIM JSON Template.

5. In the SCIM JSON Template section, enter the following:

```
{ "schemas": [    "urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:User", "urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:extension:enterprise:2.0:User", "urn:ietf:params:scim:MindtickleNameSpace", "urn:ietf:params:scim:ManagerNameSpace" ], "active": "{$user.status}", "name": {   "familyName": "{$user.lastname}",   "givenName": "{$user.firstname}",   "formatted": "{$user.display_name}" }, "emails": [{   "type": "other",   "primary": true,   "value": "{$user.email}" }], "displayName": "{$user.firstname} {$user.lastname}", "externalId": "{$parameters.externalId}", "urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:extension:enterprise:2.0:User": {}, "urn:ietf:params:scim:MindtickleNameSpace": {   "dg": "{$user.title}",   "rg": "{$user.location}",   "rgn": "{$user.region}",   "dp": "{$user.department}",   "a_13": "{$parameters.date}" }, "urn:ietf:params:scim:ManagerNameSpace": {   "a_0": "{$parameters.manager_id}",   "a_3" : "{$parameters.manager_email}" }}
```

Note: For unique identification (UID) enabled learning sites, update the "userName": "{$user.username}" in the template above. It is not required for non-UID learning sites.

6. In the following section of the template, update the user profile fields and their short keys from Mindtickle in the following format, “Profile field’s shortcut from Mindticke”: "{OneLogin profile field}."

Note: The mapped profile fields should be added to the Parameters tab to prevent errors during data sync. For more information, see Configure application parameters.

For example,

```
 "urn:ietf:params:scim:MindtickleNameSpace": {   "dg": "{$user.title}",
```

In the above example, "dg": "{$user.title}",

- dg : the shortcut key of the Job title profile field in Mindtickle.
- $user.title: the user’s job title field in OneLogin.

For more information on where to find custom field short keys in Mindtickle, see how to get short keys for custom fields.

7. In the following section of the template, update the relationship type fields and their corresponding short keys from Mindtickle.

For example,

```

8. In the Custom Headers section, enter:

```

```

Note: Contact the Mindtickle support team to get your user credentials approved for Onelogin provisioning and to allow Onelogin user provisioning.

```

If successfully enabled, the API Status changes to Enabled.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > User Sync > Setting up the Mindtickle app in OneLogin > Enable user provisioning:
To enable provisioning for the application,

1. Go to the Provisioning tab.

2. In the Workflow section, select the Enable provisioning checkbox to enable user provisioning for the SCIM app.

3. Under Require admin approval before this action is performed, select the operations allowed for the SCIM app:

- Create user
- Delete user
- Update user

Note:

If any of the above checkboxes are enabled, admins must approve the action each time it occurs. For example, if the Create user checkbox is selected, admin approval is required each time a user is created in Mindtickle.

It is recommended that the above options are not enabled for automatic user provisioning.

4. Click Save.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > User Sync > Setting up the Mindtickle app in OneLogin > Configure application parameters:
When creating a new application in OneLogin, adding user profile fields in the Parameters tab is mandatory. These fields are necessary to establish integration and ensure users are added successfully.

To add the user profile fields,

1. Go to the Parameters tab.

2. Click the plus icon to add a new parameter.

Note:

For UID sites, the SCIM username and Manager fields should be mapped as follows:

- SCIM Username: Username
- Manager ID: Manager Username

For non-UID sites, the SCIM username and Manager fields should be mapped as follows:

- SCIM Username: Email
- Manager ID: Manager Email

3. In Field Name, enter the short key used for the custom user profile field in OneLogin.

4. Select the Include in User Provisioning checkbox to include the custom user profile field in user provisioning.

5. Click Save.

7. Click Save.

The created custom profile fields are added to the Parameters tab.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > User Sync > Setting up the Mindtickle app in OneLogin > Automate user role assignment > Mapping the roles:
Once created, the roles must be configured with the automation condition and action. You can create a new role mapping to automate user role assignment based on specific conditions

1. On the Roles page, click on a role to create a mapping.

2. On the displayed screen, click the Users tab.

3. Click the New Mapping button to create automation rules for the role.

The Mappings screen is displayed.

4. In Mappings, enter a name for the automation rule.

5. In the Conditions section, select the rule conditions for the automation.

For example, if you set the rule condition as Department equals Sales, then all users from the Sales department are considered for the automation rule.

Click the plus icon to add another condition if necessary.

6. In the Actions section, select the action to be performed if the system realizes the configured conditions.

For example, If you select the Action as Set role for a Mindtickle user.

Users from the sales department are automatically assigned the Mindtickle user role. Click the plus icon to add another action for the set condition.

7. Click Save after making the configurations.

- If a user’s provisioning has failed, the reason for the failure is displayed in the Notes column.

In Mindtickle’s Content Center, admins can automatically sync content (files and folders) from supported external storage providers. These providers serve as the source locations for the content that appears in the Content Center.

- Adobe Experience Manager (AEM)
- Google shared drive
- Microsoft SharePoint
- Egnyte

For each configured account — whether it's from AEM, Google Shared Drives, SharePoint, or Egnyte — the Content Center automatically creates a root folder where all synced folders from that source are made available. Any updates made to the original files or folders in these external systems are seamlessly reflected in the Content Center during the next sync cycle.

The sources listed above are pull-based: Mindtickle connects to each source on a schedule and pulls in the latest content. In addition, Content Center supports two push-based sources, where an external system sends content to Content Center through the Content Center APIs rather than Mindtickle pulling it:

- AEM (DAM) : Content pushed from the Adobe Experience Manager (AEM) digital asset management (DAM) module through the Content Center APIs. This is distinct from the native, pull-based AEM source listed above.
- API : Content pushed from any other external content management system (CMS) or digital asset management (DAM) platform through the Content Center APIs.

Because the external system initiates and manages all syncs for push-based sources, these sources are not configured on the admin site and have no scheduled sync. As a result, manual resync is not available for them. For more information on setting up push-based integrations, see Content Center APIs for synced content. Push-based sources are available only if enabled for your account.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Content Center > Sync status:
Perform the following to view the sync status for files and folders synced to Content Center:

1. In the admin site left navigation bar, click Content Center to access Content Center.

1. The Content Center homepage appears. It lists all folders and files to which you have access, sorted by the Last modified column (latest first).It lists the current sync status under the name of each file/folder.

1. You can choose to view files and folders synced from one or more external storage providers (source locations of your content synced to Content Center). Use the More filters > Synced from filter to view files and folders synced from: Adobe Experience Manager (AEM), Google Drive, Microsoft SharePoint, and Egnyte. If push-based sources are enabled for your account, the filter also includes AEM (DAM) and API.

1. The status can be one of the following. See details in the “Sync status types” section.
  - Success: All files were successfully synced.
  - Completed: Files skipped: At least one file was skipped (not synced).
  - Completed: Files failed: At least one file failed to sync.
  - Failed: All files failed to sync.
  - In progress: Sync in progress currently.
  - Paused: Sync paused.
2. Hover over the sync status icon for quick information on the current status. It provides the sync status at the mentioned date and time, source location, name of the admin who synced the folder, and the date and time for the next scheduled sync. For push-based sources (AEM (DAM) and API), the next scheduled sync is not shown, because these sources do not run on a Mindtickle-managed schedule.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Content Center > Sync status > Sync status types:
The following table explains different types of sync statuses in detail:

| Sync icon | Status type | Details |
| --- | --- | --- |
|  | Success | Indicates that all files in the sync (run) were successfully synced. |
|  | Completed: Files skipped | Indicates that at least one file was skipped (not synced) due to issues in the source files, while remaining files synced successfully. This status also appears when all files in the sync were skipped.Files are skipped when they do not meet the prerequisites for source files.How to fix: Admins can review the sync logs and take corrective actions on the source files. |
|  | Completed: Files failed | Indicates that at least one file failed to sync due to technical or authentication issues on the Mindtickle platform, while remaining files either synced successfully or were skipped or both.How to fix: You can contact Mindtickle Support to help fix them. |
|  | Failed | Indicates that all files failed to sync, due to technical or authentication issues. |
|  | In progress | Indicates that the sync is currently in progress. You cannot view the sync logs or perform any other actions until the sync is complete. |
|  | Paused | Indicates that the sync is currently paused. |

Note: The Completed: Files skipped and Completed: Files failed statuses provide more granular and contextual details in the sync logs. This makes it easier to determine whether the sync issues originate from the source files or the Mindtickle platform.

For details on supported file types and size limits for uploading and syncing content to Mindtickle, see this article.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Content Center > Sync logs:
Sync logs offer detailed sync and status details for all files and folders. Files are marked with either of the following statuses: Success, Skipped, or Failed. Additionally, for skipped and failed files, the logs offer detailed error messages to help you identify and resolve the issues effectively.

Perform the following to view detailed sync logs for files and folders synced to Content Center:

1. For all status types except “in progress”, you can view detailed sync logs on all files in a folder. Click View sync details to view the sync logs for a folder. Alternatively, click More options > View sync details.

1. The Last sync details for <folder name> page appears. It provides the last available sync status and details for all files within a folder. For example, let’s consider the sync logs for theCompleted: Files failed status type as it encompasses all sync outcomes. This status indicates that at least one file failed to sync due to technical or authentication issues on the Mindtickle platform, while remaining files either synced successfully or were skipped or both. The next steps cover the information and actions available on this page.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Content Center > Sync logs:
1. In the header, you can see the latest sync status and an overview of sync details. It includes the following sync details: Displays the sync status icon. Lists total number of files synced successfully / skipped / failed. Mentions sync completion date and time. Source: The source location of the files and folders. It can be Google Shared Drives, Microsoft SharePoint, Adobe Experience Manager (AEM), or Egnyte. If push-based sources are enabled for your account, the source can also be AEM (DAM) or API. Synced by: Name of the admin who initiated the sync. Next sync: Date and time when the next automated (scheduled) sync will happen. This is not shown for push-based sources (AEM (DAM) and API), which do not run on a Mindtickle-managed schedule.
2. Let’s now understand the table data and available options. The table provides information in three columns: File name, Sync status, and Details. Search and filters: Use the search bar to look for a specific file. Use the Status filter to filter the data by the sync status: Success, Skipped, or Failed. The filter is useful when you want to view skipped or failed files only. Sync status column: It lists the sync status of each file. It can be , , or . Details column: For files with or status, this column displays an error message explaining why the file was not synced (skipped) or failed to sync. The message helps you determine whether the sync issue originates from the source file or the Mindtickle platform. Admins can themselves resolve issues in the source files and re-initiate a sync. For platform issues, you can contact Mindtickle Support. For push-based sources (AEM (DAM) and API), a failed file caused by an internal processing issue displays the following message, and manual resync is not available because these sources do not support automatic retry: An internal error occurred. Automatic retry is not available for this sync type. For these sources, the external system controls the sync. To re-sync a failed file, push the content again from the external system. For persistent issues, contact Mindtickle Support.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Content Center > Prerequisites for source files:
The following table outlines the prerequisite criteria for files and folders in your source location (e.g., Google Shared Drives). To ensure successful sync with Content Center, your source files and folders must meet these criteria. For each prerequisite, the table also describes the consequences of non-compliance—i.e., the sync behavior for files or folders that do not meet the specified requirements.

In summary, any files that do not meet the listed prerequisites are skipped (not synced) during the sync. For skipped files, sync logs display their status as , along with an appropriate error message to help you take corrective actions on the source files.

| # | Prerequisites | Impact of not meeting prerequisites |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Supported file typesEnsure that the source location contains only files in supported formats.For details on supported file types and size limits for uploading and syncing content to Mindtickle, see this article. | Files with unsupported file types are skipped (not synced) and the following message appears in the sync log:We can't copy this file type yet. Please move this file outside the configured <source location> folders. |
| 2 | File size limitsEnsure that source files do not exceed the supported maximum size limits. For details on supported file types and size limits for uploading and syncing content to Mindtickle, see this article. | Files that exceed the maximum limit are skipped and the following message appears in the sync log:File size exceeds the maximum limit. |
| 3 | Corrupted filesEnsure that all files in the source location are not damaged (corrupted). | Damaged files are skipped and the following message appears in the sync log:The <file type> file is corrupted. Please re-upload it on <source location> to sync. |
| 4 | Password-protected PDFsEnsure that PDFs in the source location are not password protected. | Password-protected PDF files are skipped and the following message appears in the sync log:Password-protected PDFs cannot be synced. Please remove the password to sync. |
| 5 | File/folder not foundEnsure that files/folders you want to sync are present in the source location. | Files/folders that are missing in the source location are skipped and the following message appears in the sync log:The specified <file/folder> does not exist in the source location. |
| 6 | Nested folder structure limitEnsure that the folder structure or hierarchy does not exceed 10 levels of nested folders. In other words, a root folder in your source location must not contain more than 9 levels of subfolders within each other.For example: Level 1: Root folder Level 2: Subfolder inside the root folder Level 3: A subfolder inside the subfolder (nested one more level) And so on... | Files/folders that exceed the maximum limit for nested folders are skipped and the following message appears in the sync log:Limit for folder hierarchy has been reached. |
| 7 | Character limit for file/folder nameEnsure that the name of a file or folder does not exceed 250 characters. | Files/folders that exceed the maximum character limit for their names are skipped and the following message appears in the sync log:<File/folder> name exceeds the maximum character limit of 250. Please try a shorter name. |
| 8 | Unsupported characters in file/folder nameEnsure that the name of a file or folder does not contain unsupported special characters, such as the forward slash (/) and the backward slash (\). | Files/folders that contain any unsupported characters in their names are skipped and the following message appears in the sync log:<File/folder> name contains unsupported characters: '/ \'. Please remove them. |

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Content Center > Actions on synced folders:
Click the horizontal more menu (⋯) next to a folder to access the following actions:

1. Get info

- Number of files and subfolders
- Folder hierarchy (parent folder)
- Creation date and creator
- Last modified date and modifier
- Folder collaborators

2. Add collaborators

Add existing or new users as collaborators. Collaborators gain access to all files and subfolders within the folder.

3. Manage collaborators

- Modify permissions for existing collaborators
- Grant access to all current and future users with Manage Content permission

4. Resync

Admins can manually trigger a sync for the folder.

Note: Resync is disabled if the sync is paused or in progress for the synced account. It is also disabled for push-based sources (AEM (DAM) and API), which are managed by the external system and do not support manual resync. The sync status may take time to reflect based on data volume.

5. View sync details

View all files synced within the folder, including nested subfolders. Admins can also initiate a resync from this view.

Note: This option is disabled for in-progress syncs.

See this article for supported file types and size limits.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Content Center > B. Actions not allowed:
The following actions are not allowed for synced folders and files in the Content Center:

- Uploading new files or creating new folders within synced folders
- Renaming, moving, or deleting externally synced content
- Performing bulk actions on externally synced folders or files Note: Replacing a synced file automatically updates it in all modules and assets listed under the Locations used panel.
- No version update occurs, so learner progress and scores for completed objects remain unchanged
- Learners who started but didn’t complete the updated object will have their progress and scores reset to zero (only for that object)

Note: The effect of this automated sync on modules and assets is the same as manually replacing a file in Content Center.

- When a synced file is replaced, it updates in all modules and assets where it is used (listed under the Locations used panel).
- This sync update does not trigger a module version change; therefore, the progress and scores of learners who have completed the learning object remain unchanged. However, the progress and scores of learners who have started the module but have not yet completed that specific learning object will be reset to zero (only for that learning object).
- If Microsoft Viewer is enabled and the uploaded file contains hidden slides, you may notice a discrepancy between the number of pages displayed inside the player and those shown in the sidebar. This occurs because Microsoft Viewer hides slides marked as hidden in the original document.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Content Center > Email notifications for synced files deleted at source:
Mindtickle sends an email notification to admins when Content Center synced files, which are used in modules and assets, are deleted from their source locations, such as Google shared drive, Microsoft SharePoint, and Adobe Experience Manager (AEM).

The email includes direct links to affected files, enabling quick resolution of broken references and helping maintain content integrity by prompting timely remediation of deleted source files.

Note: If a synced file is deleted at the source but is actively used in modules or assets, it is retained in Content Center and an email notification is sent to admins. Files not used anywhere are automatically removed from Content Center when deleted at the source.

Content Center does the following:

- Detects deletion of synced files, which are used in modules and assets, in their source location: Google shared drive, SharePoint, and AEM
- Sends email notifications to admins, which includes names and direct links to the referencing Content Center files

This ensures timely awareness and remediation when actively referenced files are removed at the source level — helping maintain content integrity, reduce broken links, and support better compliance.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Content Center > FAQs > What happens if a file or folder is moved within other synced paths?:
If a file or folder is moved within other configured synced paths in AEM, Google Shared Drives, or SharePoint, the move is reflected in the Content Center after the next scheduled sync.

To apply the move immediately, you can:

You will receive an email notification when an interactive video roleplay mission is assigned. Tap the Get Started button in the email and sign in to your Mindtickle mobile app with your registered email address or SSO-enabled account if you haven’t already.

On the page that opens, you will see the following tabs and mission attributes:

1. Overview

2. Due date

3. Scenario

4. Attachment

5. Passing Cut-off

6. Target Length

7. Prospect in the roleplay

8. Evaluation parameters

9. Start roleplay

This article further explains each section in detail.

1. Overview

This is the first tab on the mission details page and has the following sections:

2. Due date

If a due date has been set for the submission, you are expected to submit your mission on or before the due date.

3. Scenario

The instructions describe and highlight the mission's value and intent. This section describes the scenario and the approach the learner must take to interact with the copilot to complete the submission.

4. Attachments

This section may contain additional attachments, such as an example video or a sample presentation. Download and read the attachments before you begin the mission.

5. Passing cut-off

The Passing cut-off is the minimum score that you are expected to achieve to earn a certificate of completion.

6. Time limit

This is the maximum time limit the admin sets for recording your video submission. Record your video according to this Time limit.

7. Prospect in the scenario

This section displays the name, picture, and position of the Copilot prospective buyer set by the admin. You can use this information while creating your video roleplay.
