Help & Support > Help Center Home > AI Interactive roleplay (Beta) > For learners > Insights and suggestions & Transcripts:
This section is mainly divided into the following three sections:

- Summary: Displays the summary of the call.
- Insights: Displays the following attributes:
  - Sentiment: Analyze the tone of your transcript and help you understand if the sentiment of the roleplay was Positive/Negative/Neutral.
  - Relevance: Analyzes the relevance of the draft against the parameters set by the admin.
  - Talk%: Displays your talking percentage during the call. Ideally should be below 44%.
  - Pace: Shows how your delivery compares with the average range for speaking rate. The pace insight will help you understand if the pace at which you have delivered the submission is slow, appropriate, or fast.
  - Filler words: Highlight phrases or sounds that mark a pause or hesitation in your pitch or presentation. This insight identifies filler words you have used and lists the number of times each word is repeated.
  - Longest monologue: Analyzes the longest duration for which the learner spoke continuously.
- Suggestions and improvements: After analyzing your roleplay submission, a few improvement suggestions are displayed.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > AI Interactive roleplay (Beta) > For learners > Warning and termination during roleplay interaction:
During your interaction with the Copilot, you will be prompted with appropriate warnings based on the following criterion. The warnings aim to ensure a smooth conversation. If you don't adhere to the warnings, the conversation will be concluded.

- Frequent pauses.
- Long monologue
- Interrupting the Copilot frequently

A warning is also displayed pre-timeout to ensure users are able to conclude the roleplays within the prescribed time window. Copilot will also iterate the reason for the conclusion if the roleplay is concluded for any of the above reasons.

Learners can view their attendance status for individual sessions and sessions that are part of an event.

To view the learner’s duration-based attendance in sessions,

1. Sign in to the learning site.
2. Click Training on the left navigation bar and then click Series .

3. Click on the series with the ILT modules.

4. Click the ILT module to view the scheduled sessions and events.

The scheduled ILT sessions and events in the module are displayed.

Learners can view the attendance status in individual sessions and event-based sessions. The learner’s attendance status and the time spent in the session are displayed below the session name.

The following attendance statuses are available for learners:

- Attended: The learner’s time in the session is above the minimum attendance threshold, highlighted in green.
- Did not attend: The learner’s time in the session is below the minimum attendance threshold, highlighted in red.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Series:
The multilingual series in Mindtickle helps admins create and manage learning content in multiple languages. Admins can add translations manually, use AI to generate translations, or enable Auto translation to automatically translate supported text-based content when additional languages are added.

The Multilingual icon highlights multilingual series and modules on the learning site.

Learners can easily switch between multiple languages during training programs, ensuring a seamless, personalized learning experience.

The multilingual series streamlines the creation of learning programs across geographies, eliminating the need to duplicate content for each language.

For example, admins can enable multilingual support for an English series to make it available in other geographies, like Europe or the Middle East, without recreating it.

Note: Contact Mindtickle support to enable the Auto translation feature in your learning site.

Series

- Create multilingual series: Create a series with a default language and additional languages.
- Add languages to a series: Add multiple languages to a new or existing series.
- Manage overview pages: Add, update, or remove series overview pages across languages.
- Manage series translations: Add translations manually , use AI , or enable Auto translation for supported text-based series content.
- Review translations: View missing translations and AI-generated translations available for review.
- Set up notifications: Send series invitations and notifications in different languages.

Modules

- Create multilingual modules: Create modules with a default language and additional languages.
- Add languages to modules: Add multiple languages to existing modules.
- Manage module translations: Add translations manually , use AI , or enable Auto translation for supported text-based module content.
- Review translations: View missing translations and AI-generated translations available for review.
- Set up reminders: Send due-date and reminder emails in multiple languages.

Learning objects

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Series:
- Manage text translations: Translate text-based LOs such as MCQs and text questions.
- Review automatic translations: Review, edit, and approve auto-translated text LO content.
- Manage translations for uploaded content: Upload translated files for uploaded content LOs.
- Manage video translations: Upload translated videos, generate AI video translations, edit AI-generated translations, and regenerate videos.
- Manage closed caption translations: Add or generate closed captions for videos and translated videos.
- Manage in-video question translations: Add or generate translations for questions embedded in videos.

Note:

- To enable the multilingual series feature for your Mindtickle instance, contact Mindtickle support or your Customer Success Manager (CSM).
- This feature is available only for courses, quick updates, and assessment modules.
- Admins should configure the list of supported languages for the Mindtickle instance in the Settings > Language page. The languages selected here are displayed for selection when creating a multilingual series.
- Admins cannot change the default language set during series creation.
- If translations are unavailable for a language, learners view the content in the default series language.
- Reviewing automatically generated translations is optional. Admins can publish content even if translations are missing or pending review.
- Auto translation is not applicable to videos. Admins must manually add video translations or trigger AI translation from the video learning object.
- When Auto translation is in progress, language settings and translation actions are restricted until the translation is complete.
- The system provides unified analytics across all languages in the series to support learner engagement and progress. This helps protect the learner's progress, as changing the module language resets all learning objects that the learner has not fully completed, such as a partially watched video.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Series > Create a multilingual series:
To create a multilingual series,

1. Sign in to the Mindtickle admin site.
2. Click Training and click Series . The Series page is displayed.
3. Click the Create button and select Series to create a new series.
4. In the New series pop-up screen, enter a name for the series.
5. Click Multilingual support to add different languages for the series. The Multilingual support settings are displayed.
6. Click the Default Language drop-down and select the default language for the series.
7. Click the Select languages for translation (Maximum 24) field to select the languages for the series. You can choose a maximum of 24 languages. The languages displayed for selection in the drop-down are from the Languages page. For more information, see Settings > Language . Note: You cannot change the default language after creating the series. The selected languages are also available for the modules and LOs in the series.
8. Click Create after selecting the necessary languages to create the multilingual series. After adding languages to the series, you must add translations to the languages for the content. For more information, see the Series section.

Admins can set up overview pages in multiple languages for a multilingual series.

1. Go to the series Settings tab and select the Multilingual support tab.

3. Click Add overview page, and the system navigates you to the Overview pages section.
4. Click Add on a language to add a series overview page for a language. The menu displays the available series overview pages. The options displayed here are from the Series overview pages screen ( Training > Series overview pages ).
5. Search for existing overview pages in the search field
6. Click on an option to select. Or Click + Create new to create a new series overview page. If you add new overview pages here, the system updates them in the Series overview pages screen. The Add overview page pop-up is displayed.
7. Click Add overview page to continue. The system updates the selected overview page for the language in the Overview pages section. Similarly, add overview pages are all languages in the series. Note: If the series overview page for a language is unavailable, learners will see it in the default language.

Modify a series overview page

1. To modify an overview page, click the Edit icon in the Overview pages section. The overview page opens. For detailed information on modifying overview pages, see Create and edit overview pages . After modifying the overview page, click Use as overview to select the overview page.

If admins want to add more languages to a series, they can add them in the Multilingual support tab.

To add additional languages to a series after its creation,

1. Go to the series Settings tab and select the Multilingual support tab. The multilingual support settings are displayed.
2. Click the Multilingual support switch to activate or deactivate additional languages for the series.
3. Click + Add languages to add more languages to the series. The Add languages pop-up screen is displayed.
4. Click the languages to add to the series in the Select languages for translation (maximum 24) field. You can select a maximum of 24 languages.
5. Click Yes, add . Note:

- You must add translations for every language. If a language does not have translations, the system displays the series in the default language. For information about adding translations, see Manage translations .
- The series languages are also available for the modules and learning objects.

The system adds the new language to the Multilingual support tab.

6. Click Save.

After adding languages to the series, you must add translations for the content in those languages. For more information, see the Series section.If Auto translation (Settings > Multilingual support > Auto translation) is enabled in the series, Mindtickle automatically starts translating supported series content after the language is added. This includes the series name, series description, section names, module names, and module descriptions.While translation is in progress, language settings and translation actions are restricted until the translation is complete.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Series > Manage translations > Series > Add translations manually:
After adding additional languages for a series, admins must add translations. The system displays the series in the default language if no translations are available.

To add translations for series languages,

1. Click the series Settings tab and then click the Multilingual support tab. The multilingual support settings are displayed.
2. Click the Translation tab. The system highlights the missing translations. Note: The attention icon highlights all languages with missing translations.
3. Click the drop-down to select a language to add translation. For example, French.
4. Enter the series name in the selected language in the Series name field.
5. Click Save .
6. In the Series description field, enter the description for the series in the selected language.
7. Click Save . The system displays a green checkmark when you complete a language’s translations.
8. Ensure to add translations for all languages by following the steps above.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Series > Manage translations > Learning objects > Add translations manually for text LOs:
To add translations for learning objects,

1. Go to the module's Build tab.
2. Click on the learning object to select it.
3. Click the Translations tab. The attention icon highlights the missing translations for the learning object.
4. In the Translations tab, click the drop-down and select the language to add the translations.
5. Manually enter the translations for the Question and the Answer options . Note: You cannot change the correct answer options for the questions when adding translations. To change the correct answers, go to the Multiple-choice question (default language) tab.
6. Ensure to add translations for all languages in the Translations tab. If there are no translations for a language, the system displays the content in the default language.

Translations save logic

There are two field types in all modules: static and non-static.

- Static fields
  - Display a Save button when updated.
  - Changes are visible to learners immediately after saving.
  - Republishing is not required.

The example below illustrates the static fields (Question and Answer options) in an MCQ within a course module.

- Non-static fields
  - Changes are auto-saved.
  - Learners see these changes only after the module is republished.

The example below illustrates the non-static field (Answer) in a text answer question within an assessment module.

Note:

- If you update a non-static field and then update a static field, the system does not display the Save button. The changes are auto-saved, but learners see them only when the module is republished.
- The save logic applies to both the Translations and the default language tab.
- In unpublished modules, all changes are automatically saved in all module types.
- In published modules, adding a new learning object is automatically saved in all modules.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Series > Manage translations > Manage closed caption translations > Add CC manually for existing videos:
To add closed captions for a video,

1. Follow steps 1 to 3 in the Add translations for learning objects section.
2. In the Select file screen, click the checkbox of the video file to add to the LO.
3. Click Select . The system adds the video to the LO. The video's default language is displayed as a tab.
4. Click the Transcript and CC tab to view the video transcript and available closed captions (CC). You can also add closed captions in other languages for the video. The system automatically generates the CC in English for the video.
5. Click + Upload another language to add a CC in another language.
6. In the Upload CC of another language pop-up, you can drag and drop the CC file or click to browse and select it.
7. In the displayed pop-up, enter the language of the CC file, then click Upload . The system adds the other language CC file to the video. You can click the Delete icon to remove the CC file. Note: Learners can view closed captions in other languages only when watching the video in its default language under the Video (English) tab. The other language closed captions are not available for translated videos in the Translations tab.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Series > Manage translations > Manage video translations > Edit AI-generated video translations:
Admins can edit AI-generated video translations even after the video is created. If there are inaccuracies or incorrect translations, admins can update the translations and regenerate them. This helps ensure accuracy, correct terminology, and alignment with brand and compliance requirements.

1. Go to the module's Build tab .
2. Click the learning object with the video.
3. Click the Translations tab.
4. Click Edit on the translated video.
5. Click a timestamp and edit the translated text.
6. Click Translate . The system regenerates the translated video with the updated changes.

Additional actions

- To delete the video translation, click the Delete icon.
- To rename the video translation, click the Rename icon.
- To download the video translation, click the Download icon.
- To replace the translated video, click Replace . The following pop-up is displayed. For detailed information on replacing files, see Add or replace files in course/quick update via Content Center .

Limitations

Video translations may fail or produce poor results because of:

Audio issues

- Loud background music can interfere with speech
- Multiple people talking at once can confuse the system
- Poor audio quality, such as noise, echo, or muffled audio, can reduce accuracy
- Distorted or clipped audio may cause important words to be missed
- Background noise, such as traffic, wind, or crowds, can affect clarity
- Videos with no audio track cannot be processed

Speech issues

- Very fast speech may lead to missed words
- Mumbling or unclear speech causes errors
- Strong or uncommon accents can reduce accuracy
- Whispering or very quiet speech may not be captured properly

Content limitations

- Music or singing may not translate accurately
- Loud sound effects can overpower speech
- Non-speech sounds, such as laughing or shouting, are not handled well
- Heavily modified voices using effects or auto-tune may reduce accuracy

Translation challenges

- Technical terms may be translated incorrectly
- Names and brand terms may change unexpectedly
- Idioms may lose meaning when translated literally
- Dates, numbers, and units may appear in different formats

Timing issues

- Some languages naturally take more or less time to speak
- Fast scene changes can affect synchronization and flow

Video generation failures

In some cases, the translation process may fail completely, and the video will not be generated. Users are directed to this help article when these failures occur.

Common causes include:

- Videos with no audio track
- Unsupported languages
- Corrupted or unsupported video files
- Large video files exceeding 1 GB
- Very long videos:
  - More than 45 minutes for editable translations with review
  - More than 2.5 hours for automatic translations without review

Admins must open each translated version of the video, select the newly added in-video question, and either manually add the translation or generate it using AI.

To translate a new in-video question added after translation

1. Go to the module’s Build tab.
2. Click the video learning object.
3. In the Video tab, hover over the timestamp where you want to add the in-video question.
4. Click Add in-video questions .
5. Select the question type. For example, Multiple choice question .
6. Enter the question and answer options.
7. Select the correct answer and configure the question settings, such as score, attempts, and timestamp.
8. Click Save .
9. Click the Translations tab.
10. Select a translated language from the language drop-down. For example, Chinese Simplified .

12. Select the newly added in-video question.
13. In the question editor, click Translate . The system displays a notification that the translation is in progress.
14. After the translation is complete, review the translated question and answer options.
15. Click Save . The system saves the in-video question in the selected language video. Note: New in-video questions added after a video has already been translated must be manually translated for each translated language.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Series > Manage translations > Review translations:
The Review translations button on the series and module headers lets admins view missing and AI-generated translations for review.

The Review translations screen displays the following,

- Language drop-down: Select a language to view its missing translations and translations available for review.
- Missing translations: View content without translations for the selected language.
- AI-generated translations available for review: Review AI-generated translations before learners view the content.
- Links to the affected series, module, or learning object: Open the related item directly to add, update, or review the translation. Missing translations appear first. Translations available for review appear after the missing translations.

The Review translations screen allows admins to

- Add missing translations
- Review AI translations

Note: Reviewing translations is optional. Admins can publish content even if translations are missing or available for review. If a translation is missing, learners see the content in the default language.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Instructor-Led Training (ILT):
Admins can configure a minimum threshold for learner enrollment in ILTs. If the number of learner enrollments for a session is below the specified threshold, the session creator receives an email. Admins can promote session enrollment and decide whether to combine, postpone, or cancel sessions based on the number of enrolled learners.

The minimum enrollment threshold can be configured at:

- Learning site level
- ILT module level
- Individual session level

Note:

- The minimum enrollment email sent to admins is not configurable or available in the email template library.
- This feature is enabled by default for the learning site.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Instructor-Led Training (ILT) > Configure the minimum enrollment threshold for the learning site:
To configure the duration-based capture for the learning site:

1. Sign in to the admin site .
2. On the left navigation bar, click Account and select Settings .

By default, the Training tab is displayed on the Settings page.

3. Click the Instructor-led trainings (ILTs) tab.

The Instructor-led trainings (ILTs) page is displayed.

The following options are available:

- Send an email to the admin when session enrollment is below a specified threshold : This switch enables the minimum enrollment threshold for the learning site. It is enabled by default.
- Do you want to keep the settings enabled for both module and session levels? : This switch allows admins to configure the minimum enrollment threshold at the ILT module and individual session levels.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Instructor-Led Training (ILT) > Configure the minimum enrollment threshold for the learning site > Configure the minimum enrollment threshold for ILT modules:
To configure the minimum attendance for an ILT module,

1. Sign in to the admin site .
2. On the left navigation bar, click Training and select Series .
3. Click the series with the ILT module. For example, Acme Product Training.
4. Click the ILT module. For example, Acme Product Training.

5. Click Settings to view the ILT module settings.

6. Click the Scoring and completion tab.

7. Click the Set threshold and remind admin on low session enrollment switch to enable the minimum enrollment threshold feature for the ILT module.

8. In Minimum number of enrollments, enter the minimum number of learners required for the session. For example, 8.

Note: Admins can change the minimum enrolment threshold at any time. The setting applies only to new sessions created and not to sessions already created on the platform.

9. In Reminder, select when to send reminders to the admin. The following options are available:

- No. of days before session: Select this option to send reminders to admins a certain number of days before the session. For example, 5 days before the session.
- Specific date: Select this option to send reminders to admins on a specific date before the session. Choose a specific date from the calendar. For example, Jan 21, 2025.

10. Select the Repeat every # days checkbox to send the recurring minimum enrollment email to admins every # days before the scheduled session date.

11. Click the edit icon on Repeat every # days to modify the recurrence settings for the minimum enrollment email.

Click the edit icon on Repeat every # days to modify the recurrence settings for the minimum enrollment email.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Digital Sales Rooms:
The page-level analytics feature provides detailed insights into how Asset Hub content is viewed within a DSR. Admins and sales reps can understand how much time users spend on each page of a shared document. This helps to understand the shared content's effectiveness and user engagement.

To view page-level analytics of Asset Hub content shared in DSRs:

1. Sign in to the learning site.

2. Click Rooms and then select Rooms in the left navigation bar. The Rooms page is displayed.

3. Click on a room.

The room overview page opens.

4. Scroll down to the Room Contacts section and click on a contact name.

The content viewed by the contact and the time spent on each page are also displayed. You can also click the link displayed at the bottom of the content to view the shared content.

Page-level analytics are supported for the following document types: DOC, DOCX, PDF, PPT, and PPTX.

Note: The analytics are not displayed for different versions of a document. If a document is updated, the analytics will aggregate the time spent across all versions.

For example, if a document is updated from version 1 to version 2, the analytics will show the combined time spent on both versions without distinguishing them.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Digital Sales Rooms:
Sales reps can configure whether the content shared in DSRs can be downloaded, even if they did not upload it. This ensures that only the intended content is downloadable in a DSR, helping to provide accurate analytics on content engagement within DSRs.

Note:

- When you add Asset Hub content to new rooms and room templates, it is not downloadable by default.
- For Asset Hub content, a tooltip displays the message, "The option to download will be unavailable for embed type assets."
- For existing room templates, all content is now configured as non-downloadable.
- Content types such as URLs, embeds, and text are not downloadable.

To make content downloadable in a DSR:

1. Sign in to the learning site.

2. Click Rooms in the left navigation bar and then click Rooms. The Rooms page is displayed.

3. Hover over a room and click the Edit icon.

The Edit Sales Room page opens.

4. Hover over the piece of content you wish to edit.

5. Click the Edit icon.

The Edit content pop-up screen is displayed.

6. Click the Allow viewers to download switch to make the content downloadable.7. Click Done.8. Click Save after making changes to the room.

The Download option is displayed when users click on content in a DSR. Users can now download content from DSRs.

Note:

When you clone a room template, create a room from a template, or save a room as a template, the downloadable setting of each content item is retained.

For example, if you have a room template with two content items, the first document is downloadable, but the second is not. When you create a room from that room template, the first document is configured as downloadable, and the second is not.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Asset Hub > Admin:
This article outlines how admins can effectively track and manage feedback on their assets. You can access and oversee all feedback through the following channels:

- Weekly asset feedback email : Every Monday, admins receive an email summarizing feedback from reps across their assets in the previous week. This proactive, consolidated update helps you stay informed and manage feedback efficiently. You can quickly review the feedback in the email or click through to the asset for more details.
- Asset details page : Access feedback directly from the asset's page on the platform, either by navigating there directly or using the assets linked in the weekly email.

The article provides details on the key steps of the feedback process:

1. Reps provide feedback
2. Admins receive the asset feedback email (weekly)
3. Admins take action on the feedback

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Asset Hub > Admin > 1. Reps provide feedback:
The Your feedback tab on the asset details page allows reps to submit and share their feedback on the asset. In addition to the rating and feedback under the Insights section, you can use this tab to share your experience and overall feedback regarding the asset. The feedback is a strong mechanism to intimate the admin or asset owner about how helpful the asset is, and any improvements or updates required. Thus, establishing a feedback loop among users and admins and helping the admins to improve the content iteratively.

Type your feedback, questions, or comments on the asset in the space provided and click Submit.

If there are multiple feedback provided for the asset, you can view them in the list view. Also, you can also view if the feedback is resolved by the admin/asset owner. Next to any feedback, click theicon → Delete to delete submitted feedback.

Your submitted feedback is listed in the Your feedback tab with the “Submitted” status. Once an admin resolves the feedback, the status is updated to “Resolved”. If an admin re-opens any resolved feedback, the status is updated to “Reopened”.

Note:

- This tab also includes ratings and feedback from the Details tab → Insights section.
- Feedback is only visible to learners with access to the asset.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Asset Hub > Admin > 2. Asset feedback email:
Once reps provide feedback on one or more assets, admins receive a weekly email every Monday morning (in their local timezone). The asset feedback email lists all assets that received feedback in the previous week along with the feedback comments.

The email lists three summary stats at the top:

- Assets: Total number of assets with feedback listed in the email.
- Feedback: Total number of feedback received.
- Actionable: Total number of feedback marked as 'Actionable" by Mindtickle Copilot. Copilot identifies feedback that requires follow-up or further action. Such feedback is marked with the tag.

Click any asset to open the asset details page in a new tab and access the feedback.

Click Resolve to directly open the feedback panel on the asset details page and mark the feedback resolved.

Note: While you can read the asset feedback email on both web and mobile (via Mindtickle mobile app), actions like navigating to the asset from the email is supported only on the web.

Key highlights

Key highlights of the asset feedback email:

Single email: A single, consolidated email includes all feedback for the assets owned by the admin.

Frequency: Weekly emails are sent every Monday morning, based on the admin's time zone. Additionally, please note the following:

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Asset Hub > Admin > 2. Asset feedback email:
- Only new feedback from the previous week is included. No email is sent if there is no feedback. Additionally, the email excludes any feedback manually resolved by the admin in the prior week.
- The email includes up to five feedback items per asset. If there are more than five feedback, you can click a button to view all feedback on the asset details page.
- If the feedback is resolved by the admin, it means some action is taken and such feedback will not show up in the email.

Actionable feedback via Copilot

For AI-enabled learning sites, Mindtickle Copilot will mark feedback as "Actionable," helping admins quickly filter and prioritize feedback for appropriate follow-up on the asset. Such feedback is marked with the tag, in the Feedback panel of the asset details page as well as in the asset feedback weekly email.

Note: If Mindtickle Copilot is not enabled for your organization, feedback will not be marked as actionable and the “Actionable” tag will not appear. The actionable feedback count will also be excluded from the email summary section.

- For organizations that had AI enabled before this release, previous feedback will be categorized as actionable or non-actionable.
- For organizations enabling AI after this release, only new feedback will be tagged as actionable.

Fallback notification for unassigned asset owners

If an asset doesn't have an assigned owner, you can configure one or more hub collaborators to receive the weekly email notification. Set this up under hub Settings > Notifications using the Asset Feedback Notifications option.

Before viewing and acting on asset feedback, locate the asset with new feedback in one of these ways:

In the Feedback panel, you can:

Note: Admins cannot comment on or respond to feedback from reps. Replying to feedback is not currently supported.

Filters

In the Feedback panel, you can use the following two types of filters:

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Single Sign-On (SSO) > Create the application in OneLogin:
Perform the following steps in OneLogin:

1. Sign in to the OneLogin platform, click the Applications menu, and select the Applications option.

1. Click Add App to create the application.

1. On the Find Applications page, enter SAML Custom Connector (Advanced) in the search.

Note: If you already created your application, select it from the list and move to the Configure the Application section.

1. Click SAML Custom Connector (Advanced) from the search results.

1. In Display name, enter the application name. For example, Mindtickle.
2. You can modify the custom images for the application in Rectangular Icon and Square Icon. This helps admins quickly identify the Mindtickle application on the Applications page. You can download the logo icons to download here.
3. In Description, enter the application details. For example, Access your enablement in Mindtickle.
4. Click Save.

The application is created, and the Info tab is displayed.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Single Sign-On (SSO) > Steps to be performed in Mindtickle:
Perform the following steps in Mindtickle:

1. Login to the admin site.
2. Click Account and select Settings.The Settings page is displayed.

1. Click the Security and Integrations tab, scroll down to the Single Sign-On section.
2. Click the toggle switch to enable SSO.
3. In the SAML SSO tab, click Download Metadata.

An .XML file is saved to your computer. You can use the data from this file to enter appropriate settings in your IdP (Identity Provider).

6. Open the XML file in a text editor and copy the values for Audience (Entity ID), ACS (Consumer) URL Validator, and ACS (Consumer) URL. These details are used on the OneLogin platform. The following image shows sample values for Audience (Entity ID), ACS (Consumer) URL Validator, and ACS (Consumer) URL in the XML file.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Single Sign-On (SSO) > Steps to be performed in OneLogin > Configure the application:
1. On the OneLogin home page, click the Applications menu.
2. Select the Applications option.
3. On the Applications page, click SAML Custom Connector (Advanced).

1. Go to the Configuration tab.

Note: The Audience (Entity ID), ACS (Consumer) URL Validator, and ACS (Consumer) URL details are mandatory fields. Their details are available in the XML metadata file downloaded from Mindtickle. For more information, see Step 6 of the Steps to be performed in Mindtickle section.

1. In Audience (Entity ID), enter the entityID. For example, 1836829602567025795_mindtickle.com.
2. In the ACS (Consumer) URL Validator, enter the endpoint validator URL for authentication. For example, https://acme.mindtickle.com/login/ssosaml.
3. In ACS (Consumer) URL, enter the endpoint URL for authentication. For example, https://acme.mindtickle.com/login/ssosaml.

1. In the SAML initiator dropdown, select the OneLogin.

1. Click Save.
2. From the header, click More Actions.
3. Select SAML Metadata to download the metadata XML file.

The SAML metadata XML file is saved on your local drive.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Single Sign-On (SSO) > Steps to be performed in OneLogin > Map attributes:
To map the application attributes,

1. Go to the Parameters tab.
2. Click the add sign to create a new attribute.

The New Filed pop-up is displayed.

1. In Field name, enter id.
2. In Flags, select the Include in SAML assertion checkbox.
3. Click Save.

The Edit Field id pop-up screen is displayed.

1. In the Value drop-down, select UUID.
2. Click Save.

The custom attribute is created and displayed on the Parameters tab.

Similarly, follow steps 1 to 7 to create and map the following custom attributes.

| SAML Customer Connector Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| email | Email |
| firstname | First Name |
| lastname | Last Name |

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Single Sign-On (SSO) > Steps to be performed in Mindtickle:
Perform the following steps in Mindtickle:

1. Sign in to the admin site.
2. Click Account in the left navigation pane, then click Settings.

1. On the Security & integrations tab, scroll down to the Single Sign-On section and click the toggle switch to enable SSO.
2. Under SAML SSO, click Select File and upload the metadata file that you saved to your computer in Step 3 of the previous section.
3. The Redirect URL, Post URL, and Certificate fields are populated automatically.
4. Click Advanced Settings, and select the appropriate values for each option as required.
5. Click Activate SSO.

Your learners can now sign in to the Mindtickle learning site with Okta.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > Admin:
This article provides information about the four adoption and usage reports in Call AI analytics for admins:

1. Activation
2. Calls
3. Interactions
4. Coaching

These reports provide comprehensive visibility into the usage and adoption of Call AI within your organization. The reports are designed to help admins and managers understand how Call AI is being utilized and to take necessary actions to improve adoption and usage.

Call AI adoption report email

For information on the Call AI adoption reports for managers, see Call AI adoption reports (managers).

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > Admin > Overview:
The Call AI adoption reports provide comprehensive visibility into the usage and adoption of Call AI within your organization. Here’s a brief summary of the data in each of the four reports:

1. Activation report: Tracks users with the Call AI recorder role, including:

- Total users assigned the role
- Calendar integration status (Yes/No)
- Monthly active users and their status (Active/Inactive)

Benefit: Gauges Call AI adoption and identifies teams or users needing support or training to improve activation.

2. Calls report: Provides data on:

- Total time spent on calls
- Recorded calls, disabled recordings, and Copilot prompts used

Benefit: Insights into recording behaviors, helping ensure calls are being recorded correctly.

3. Interactions report: Tracks user engagement with call recordings:

- Number of calls reviewed/accessed (unique views)
- Comments, private messages, and calls shared

Benefit: Highlights active engagement with Call AI’s feedback and coaching tools, identifying users who may need more encouragement.

4. Coaching report: Provides data on coaching activities for managers:

- Calls reviewed/accessed (unique views)
- Coaching forms submitted
- Comments and private messages on recordings

Benefit: Helps managers track coaching efforts, ensuring effective team support and maximizing Call AI’s potential.

Note:

- All four reports provide data only on active users; deactivated users are not considered.
- For the Activation report, only users with the recorder role are considered. For the Calls , Interactions , and Coaching reports, all engaged users are considered.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > Admin > Report navigation and options:
1. Switch between reports

Use the View dropdown menu to switch between the four types of Call AI adoption reports.

2. View data at different levels

The adoption reports provide analytics data at the organization, team (manager), and individual levels.

Use the “Show data for” dropdown menu to view data for the entire organization or for a specific manager (and their team).Note: The “Show data for” dropdown menu lists only those managers who have at least one user in their team and hierarchy with the Call AI recorder role. Switch between the Teams and Individuals tabs to view team-level or individual-level data.

3. Overview of report options/functionalities

This section provides an overview of various options or functionalities common to all four reports. You can apply various filters, sort data by columns, drill down to view more data, and download the full report to your computer.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > Admin > Call AI adoption report email:
The Call AI adoption report (monthly) email provides a snapshot of key Call AI adoption metrics, with a call-to-action (CTA) button linked to the Call AI adoption reports for deeper insights. The detailed adoption data are accessible only on the Call AI adoption reports in Mindtickle Analytics, encouraging platform engagement.

The adoption report email is sent to Call AI admins on the 1st of every month at 2:00 PM UTC. The subject line of the email will be “Call AI Adoption Report - <Month and Year>”, such as “Call AI Adoption Report - February 2025.”

The email provides the following Call AI adoption metrics for each month:

- Total users : Total number of users onboarded to Call AI in this month. Also indicates increase or decrease (in percentage) compared to the previous month.
- Monthly active users : Total number of monthly active users (engaging with Call AI). Also indicates increase or decrease (in percentage) compared to the previous month.
- New calls : Total number of new calls recorded with Call AI in this month.

Click the View your team's Call AI adoption button to view detailed analytics in the Call AI adoption reports.

The Zoom recordings stored on your device are .mp4 files and can be directly uploaded as learning objects or assets into Mindtickle.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > External Content Access > Embed Zoom recordings from the cloud:
You can embed Zoom cloud recordings into Mindtickle using an iframe.

To embed a zoom recording from the cloud:

- Sign in to your Zoom account and click the Recordings tab.
- Click Share on the cloud recording you want to add to Mindtickle. For more information, see Managing and sharing cloud recordings.
- On the displayed pop-up, click Share Settings to validate or adjust the share settings as required. For more information, see Settings for sharing cloud recordings.
- Click Copy to copy the URL and navigate to Mindtickle to embed the cloud recording.The link is copied to the clipboard. You can add the shareable link (wherever applicable) in Mindtickle. For example:

- Add a shareable link on the Overview page
- Add shareable links to the series overview page
- Add links to series descriptions
- Create a rich text document and add the link to it

Note: Once the learner clicks the link to the Zoom recording, Mindtickle marks the learner’s score and completion status as 100% and Complete. Hence, Mindtickle does not granularly track the analytics or progress on the Zoom links.

1. On the Embed link pop-up, click Embed.

For a better user experience, include metadata such as title, description, and visual information with the recording and the link in Mindtickle.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > FAQs:
If learners are unable to access Seismic content in Mindtickle, try the following:

- Verify access permissions

Learners should have the necessary permissions to access the Seismic content in Mindtickle.

- Embed the SSO sign-in page for authentication

If the refused to connect error is displayed when learners try to connect to Seismic from Mindtickle, it indicates that the Seismic SSO provider does not allow sign-in within an iFrame. To enable the connection, embed the SSO sign-in page using Trusted Origins for authentication.

For example, if Okta is used for SSO authentication, embed the Okta sign-in page within an iFrame using Trusted Origins.

On the iFrame embed tab in Okta, add the trusted origin URL,

```
https://<learningsitename>.okta.com
```

For more information, see Embed the Okta sign-in page or resource in an iFrame.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Best Practices and Use Cases > Best Practices for DSR > Build rooms quickly and easily > Connect your CRM:
Integrating CRMs with DSRs lets sales reps easily create rooms for CRM deals/opportunities. The following are the benefits of connecting your CRM with DSRs,

- Reps are notified when to create a room for the CRM deal/opportunity
- Reps can select a deal/opportunity from the CRM, and all of its details will be pre-populated, as well as its associated company/account and contacts
- DSR room engagement activity is automatically written to the linked CRM deal/opportunity.
- When there are new visitors to a DSR, contacts are automatically created for them in the CRM.
- Room insights provide sales reps with detailed information on the impact of DSRs.

To connect your CRMs with DSR,

1. Navigate to DSR Settings > Integrations tab.
2. Click Connect on your CRM to connect to DSR.

For more information on DSR-CRM integrations, take a look at the help article for your CRM:

- Integrate Digital Sales Rooms with Salesforce
- Integrate Digital Sales Rooms with HubSpot
- Integrate Digital Sales Rooms with Pipedrive
- Integrate Digital Sales Rooms with Microsoft Dynamics 365

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Best Practices and Use Cases > Best Practices for DSR > Gain additional value from rooms > Connect your Slack:
If your organization uses Slack, connect it to DSRs. For DSR engagement, such as room visits, you can configure notifications to be sent to a Slack channel, room owner, or both.

Posting DSR activity to a public Slack channel encourages more sales reps to use DSRs. Watching team members visit DSRs and seeing helpful analytics motivates sales reps to increase DSR adoption.

For more information on connecting Slack with DSR, see Integrate Digital Sales Rooms with Slack.

To connect Slack with DSR,

1. Navigate to DSR Settings > Integrations > Alerts tab.
2. Click Configure on Slack.

The Configure Slack Integration screen is displayed.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Best Practices and Use Cases > Best Practices for DSR > Gain additional value from rooms > Consistently position DSR as the one place for everything you need:
Communicate to sales reps to share DSRs with prospects early in the sales cycle. Emphasize that all deal-related information should be added to the DSR. Remind sales reps to include the DSR link in every communication.

When questions are asked outside the DSR, add them to the DSR along with the answers. Consistency in communication helps all stakeholders stay aligned. DSR makes it easy for them and has all the information they need in one place.

After reps close a deal using DSR, they can easily transfer DSR ownership to the CSM. This allows for a seamless transition in the customer life cycle, provides CSMs with the full context of the deal, and helps move forward with the onboarding.

DSR provides context and helps customer success representatives understand past sales discussions and processes. It also includes call recordings for reference, which helps foster the successful implementation of the sales deal.

1. You should have the following apps installed on your phone.

- Mindtickle mobile
- Salesforce mobile

2. You should have a Salesforce admin account. Mindtickle strongly recommends using a dedicated Salesforce integration user to perform this integration.

The integration user should have access to the API enabled permission and have access to the following apex classes:

- MindTickleDev.MDTAssetHubIntegrationControllerMockTest
- MindTickleDev.MDTAssetHubIntegrationController
- MindTickleDev.MDTAssetHubIntegrationControllerTest

For more information on the permissions and apex classes, see Create an Integration User in Salesforce (SFDC).

3. You should have a Mindtickle admin account (at least an IT admin role).

4. If Asset Hub is already set up, skip the Setup Mindtickle Salesforce connection section.

The Mindtickle Salesforce OAuth app is now installed on the Salesforce instance.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > CRMs > Install the app:
1. Go to the Salesforce AppExchange page and enter Mindtickle in the search.Note: This integration is compatible with the latest version of the Mindtickle app installed from Salesforce AppExchange.

2. Click Mindtickle from the search results.

3. Click Get It Now to install the application.

4. On the LET’S GET STARTED screen, click Log In.

5. Login to your Salesforce account.

6. Select the SFDC environment (production or sandbox) and the account to install the package.

7. Review the details and confirm the installation.

8. The Salesforce administrator can decide whether to install the application for all users or only for the administrator. If your organization uses custom profiles or non-admin roles, select Install for All Users and install the package.

Note:

- For custom profiles with non-admin roles, ensure the user's profiles have access to all the object and apex classes. For more information, see Grant users access to classes and objects .
- For non-admin and community (partner/customer) users, ensure the user's profiles have access only to the apex classes. For more information, see SFDC Class Access (Community/Non-Admin Users) .

9. Select the Grant third-party access box checkbox and click Continue.

Note: An email is sent when the installation is completed successfully.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > CRMs > Download the Salesforce certificate:
1. Click thegear icon in the top-right corner and select Setup in Salesforce.

2. Enter Certificate in the search.

3. From the search results, Under Security, click Certificate and Key Management.

4. Click Create Self-Signed Certificate. Alternatively, you can use an existing self-signed certificate.

5. On the Certificate and Key Management page, under Certificates, enter the following:

- In Label Name , enter Mindtickle .
- In Unique Name , enter Mindtickle .
- In Key Size , set the value as 2048 .

Note:

- If a previously generated certificate is used, rename the label and unique name to Mindtickle. Ensure the certificate is not expired or near the expiry date
- Do not change any other default attributes.

6. Click Save.

7. Click Download Certificate.

The certificate is downloaded to your local drive.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > CRMs > Create Named Credentials:
Named credentials provide a way to define the scope of access to the external service, including specifying which Salesforce users or profiles can access it. They are a secure way to store authentication information for an external service or API. To create named credentials:

1. Click thegear icon in the upper-right corner and select Setup in Salesforce.

2. Enter Named Credentials in the search,

3. From the search results, under Security, click Named Credentials.

4. On the Named Credentials page, click the New drop-down and select New Legacy.

5. In Label, enter Mindtickle_Asset.

6. In Name, enter Mindtickle_Asset.

7. Enter the URL in the following format: https://<learning site>.mindtickle.com. For example, https://acme.integration.mindtickle.com

8. Select the certificate downloaded in step 6 of Download the Salesforce certificate section.

9. Set the Identity Type as Per User.

10. Set the Authentication Protocol as JWT.

11. Set the Issuer as Mindtickle.

12. Set Per User Subject as $User.Username.

Note:

- You can configure any user attribute other than the username. For example, you can configure Per User Subject as $User.Email .
- During sign-in, ensure your Mindtickle username matches your Salesforce username. If the usernames do not match, automatic login does not work.

13. Audiences should contain the Company ID (cname) of your Mindtickle instance.

Tip: The Company ID is displayed in the Security & Integrations tab on the Account settings page of your learning site.

14. Set Token Valid for 365 Days.

15. Select the Mindtickle certificate as the JWT Signing Certificate. For more information, see step 6 of the Download the Salesforce certificate section.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > CRMs > Create a tab for the Mindtickle mobile app:
1. On the Salesforce homepage, click thegear icon in the top-right corner and select Setup.

2. Enter Tabs in the search.

3. In the search results, under User Interface, click Tabs.

The Setup Tabs page is displayed.

4. In the Lightning Component Tabs section, click New.

The New Lightning Component Tab page is displayed.

5. In the Lightning Component drop-down, select MindTickleDev:mtMobile.

6. In Tab Label, enter the application label. The label entered here is how the application’s tab is displayed on Salesforce. For example, Mobile App.

7. In Tab Name, enter the application name. For example, Mobile_App.

8. In Tab Style, select the icon for the tab. For example, Apple.

9. In the Description, enter the objective of the application. For example, Auto-login on Mobile.

10. Click Next.

11. On the displayed screen, click Save.

Once saved, the Mobile App is added to the Tabs page under the Lightning Component Tabs section.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Digital Sales Rooms > Prerequisites:
The following are the prerequisites to create rooms automatically for Salesforce opportunities,

- The Mindtickle-Salesforce and DSR-Salesforce integrations must be available.
- You must be a DSR Admin to configure templates, set up automatic room creation rules, and view available templates.
- At least one organization room template should be set up in advance. When building a room auto-creation rule, this template must be selected to define how the rooms are created.

Note:

- If multiple rules apply to a Salesforce opportunity, one is randomly selected.
- Without DSR-Salesforce integration, the Create draft room option is hidden from the Select Action drop-down of the Create new rule screen.
- When the system automatically creates a room for an opportunity, an email notification is sent only to the room owner, not the collaborators. If a company is not associated with an opportunity, the system labels the room as Room created for {{company}}.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Digital Sales Rooms > Create a rule for automatic room creation:
To create an automation rule for automatic room creation,

1. Sign in to the admin site.

2. Click Account and select Automation suite

The Automation suite page displays the Automation rules tab open by default.

3. Click Create new rule.

4. Under Description, enter a description for the new rule.

5. From the Select condition drop-down, click SFDC opportunity.

6. From the Select field drop-down, click the field to set the rule criteria.

The following options are available:

- Account Industry: This option sets industry type as the rule criteria, for example, Manufacturing. The rooms are automatically created for all manufacturing industry opportunities.
- Account Number of Employees: This option sets the number of employees in the account as the rule criterion, for example, 10. Rooms are automatically created for all accounts with 10 or more employees.
- Currency Iso Code: This option sets the opportunity’s currency as the rule criterion, for example, U.S. dollars. Rooms are automatically created for all opportunities with U.S. dollars as the deal currency.
- Deal Value: This option sets the deal’s value as the rule criterion, for example, $100,000. Rooms are automatically created for all opportunities valued at $100,000 or more.
- Owner Email: This option sets the email address as the rule criterion, for example, Jane.doe@acme.com. The rooms are automatically created for all opportunities with Jane.doe@acme.com as the owner's email.
- Stage: This option sets the deal stage as the rule criteria, for example, Prospecting. Rooms are automatically created for all opportunities in the Prospecting stage.
- Type: This option sets the deal type as the rule criterion, for example, New Business. Rooms are automatically created for all New Business opportunities.

7. After selecting the rule condition and criteria, choose the rule value.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Digital Sales Rooms > Sales representative workflow:
This section explains the notifications sent to reps when a room is automatically drafted for a Salesforce opportunity.

To create a new Salesforce opportunity,

1. Sign in to Salesforce.

2. Click New.

3. On the New Opportunity screen, enter the OpportunityName, OpportunityCurrency, Amount, CloseDate, and Stage.

4. Click Save.

The opportunity is created in Salesforce.

During the DSR-Salesforce data sync process, the automation rule checks if the rule conditions are met for the opportunity. If they are, a draft room is automatically created for it using the configured room template.

When a room is created for the opportunity, the rep receives an email notification.

To review the automatically created room,

5. Click the Review and publish room button in the email.

The Edit Sales Room screen is displayed.

6. [Optional] To view the linked Salesforce opportunity and room contacts, click the Select deal tab. Then, click Next Step to continue.

7. On the Edit Sales Room screen, make the necessary changes to the room and click Publish.

The room is published and displayed on the Rooms page.

If the Salesforce token has expired in DSR, follow the steps below to refresh the token and re-enable the DSR-Salesforce integration with Mindtickle.

Note: This does not apply to the Call AI-Salesforce and Mindtickle-Salesforce integrations.

For more information on resetting the Salesforce user token for the mindtickle platform and Call AI, see:

- What should I do if my Salesforce User Sync token has expired in the Mindtickle platform?
- What should I do if my Salesforce user sync token has expired in Call AI?

To update the Salesforce token in DSR,

1. On the admin site homepage, click Rooms and select Settings.

The Settings page is displayed.

2. Click the Integrations tab.

3. Under the CRM tab, click Connect on Salesforce.

4. On the displayed screen, enter your Salesforce admin credentials to log in.

5. On the displayed pop-up, click Allow.

6. After logging into Salesforce, on the left navigation panel, click Apps > Connected Apps > Connected Apps OAuth Usage.

The Connected Apps OAuth Usage screen is displayed.

7. Under the Connected App column, click the Install button on Enable Us by Mindtickle.

8. On the displayed pop-up screen, click Install.

The Enable Us by Mindtickle app is now installed on the Salesforce instance.

The following message is displayed for Salesforce on the CRM tab when the integration is successful.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Asset Hub > Admin:
Admins can get internal and external shareable URL links for assets from the Assets tab on the admin site.

There are two types of shareable links available for an asset:

- Internal links :
  - User : Link for sharing the asset with sales reps (i.e., learners/users) on the learning site. Example: https://deeplinks.mindtickle.com/PizZAp9vYDRb
  - Admin : Link for sharing the asset with admins on the admin site. Example: https://admin.mindtickle.com/new/ui/assets/asset/5572532161024997
- External (public) link : Link for sharing the asset with people outside your organization. After generating the public link, you can enable/disable asset downloads. You can delete the link at any time to revoke access.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Asset Hub > Admin > Internal links:
Shareable internal links of the asset are intended for sharing with people within your organization. You can share these unique links with sales reps (users) and other admins.

Perform the following to access and copy internal links of the asset:

1. Click for an asset → Get shareable link . The below pop-up appears where you can access both internal and external shareable links.
2. Under Internal links , the following internal links are available for an asset: User : Link for sharing the asset with sales reps (i.e., learners/users) on the learning site. Example: https://deeplinks.mindtickle.com/PizZAp9vYDRb Admin: Link for sharing the asset with admins on the admin site. Example: https://admin.mindtickle.com/new/ui/assets/asset/5572532161024997
3. Click to copy the internal links of the asset for sharing with users (sales reps) and admins.
4. The recipients (users and other admins) are required to sign in to the Mindtickle platform to access the asset that you shared via internal links.

Note:

- For invite-only hubs, the internal link is accessible to invited users only.
- For public hubs, anyone with a Mindtickle account can access the asset using the internal link for users.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Asset Hub > Admin > External (public) link > Overview:
Admins can generate shareable public links for assets to share them externally, which users can access without requiring to sign in. This feature enhances the admin's ability to efficiently share assets and monitor user engagement, ensuring a seamless content-sharing experience. It’s ideal for sharing assets via newsletters, websites, or other platforms where public access to the linked assets is essential.

Admins can generate shareable public links via > Get Shareable link option for an asset.

Key benefits

1. Ease of sharing : Admins can quickly generate public links to share assets across platforms like newsletters and websites.
2. User accessibility : Users can access the assets without signing in, removing barriers and boosting engagement.
3. Engagement data : Admins can track user interactions through detailed metrics on the asset detail page.
4. Link settings :
  - Once generated, the link never expires, but you can delete the generated link to restrict access to the asset.
  - Allow download : Admins can allow downloading of the shared asset. To prevent downloads, simply turn off the Allow asset download toggle, which is enabled by default.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Asset Hub > Admin > External (public) link > Get the public link:
Perform the following to generate and access the shareable public link of the asset:

1. Click for an asset → Get shareable link . The below pop-up appears where you can access both internal and external shareable links. Note : Shareable public links cannot be generated for expired assets.
2. Under External link (public), perform the following: Generate link : Generate the public link for the asset you want to share. This link will allow external users to access the asset. Copy link and more : After generating the public link, you can:
  - Allow asset download : Enable or disable asset downloads. Turn the toggle on to allow external users to download the asset shared via the public link.
  - Copy link : Click to copy the shareable external/public link.
  - Delete link : Once generated, the link does not expire, but you can delete it at any time to revoke access.
3. Since the link is publicly accessible, external recipients (people outside your organization) do NOT need to sign in to the Mindtickle platform to access the asset shared via internal links.

Note: If the admin deletes the public link, users will see a "Content unavailable" message.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Asset Hub > Admin > External (public) link > Track engagement:
1. Open the asset to view engagement data generated from the shared public link.
2. On the asset details page, you can view the engagement on the asset’s public link under Details tab → Insights → External (public) link engagement . It provides a summary of engagement with all external recipients who accessed the public link: Views : Number of times the asset has been viewed. Downloads : Number of times the asset has been downloaded (if enabled). Average time spent : The average time spent on the asset by external recipients, calculated by dividing the total time by the number of views.
3. Click View detailed engagement to open the engagement data in a side panel. Note : The detailed engagement panel displays different data points for each asset type, such as documents, videos, images, and audio. This step focuses on engagement data for a document asset, specifically a PDF. The detailed engagement panel displays the following data: Asset version : Use the dropdown menu to engagement data for all versions of the asset, starting from the version when the asset was shared via the public link. It shows data for the latest version by default. Engagement summary : Shows the same engagement metrics as in Step 2. Additionally, it also lists maximum time spent data for a particular page. Views graph : Displays page-level engagement for document assets. For video assets, it shows views at different timestamps, and for other file types, it shows relevant engagement. Time spent details : For document assets, it lists all pages/slides with the average time spent by external recipients on each, highlighting the page with the longest time spent using the “Max. time spent” tag. For other file types, it shows relevant data points specific to those assets.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Collaboration App Notifications > Limitations:
WhatsApp limits or bans a phone number,

- If users block or report WhatsApp notifications, the quality rating of the phone number is lowered. If the rating stays low, WhatsApp:
  - Limits the number's daily message limit and message delivery
  - Downgrades the number’s maximum number of recipients. For example, from 10,000 users per day to 1,000.
  - Marks the number’s status as Flagged in Meta
- If users report or block a notification,
  - The message template is paused. To enable it again, revise it and re-submit it for approval by the Meta team.
- WhatsApp bans a phone number if message notifications are spammed to users and they report it. For example, sending messages without user opt-in results in the number ban.

For modules: The "last modified date" is updated when you perform any of the following actions AND publish the module:

- Update the module name or description
- Add certificates or learning objects to the module

For series: The "last modified date" field is updated when you modify the series metadata:

- Change the series name or description

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Modules > Access the data > Through self-serve reports:
The series last updated on and module last updated on fields/metrics are available in the following self-serve reports:

- Series reports
  - Series report → “Series last updated on” field
- Module reports
  - Module report → “Module last updated on” field
  - Module by series report → “Series last updated on” and “Module last updated on” fields
- Learner reports
  - Learner by series report → “Series last updated on” field
  - Learner by module report → “Module last updated on” field
  - Learner by module by series report → “Series last updated on” and “Module last updated on” fields

Perform the following to add the series last updated on and module last updated on fields to a self-serve report:

1. Create a self-serve report using any template that contains series and/or module data. See this article for detailed instructions. The series last updated on and module last updated on fields/metrics are available various types of self-serve reports listed above.
2. Let’s walk through an example of how to view this data in the Module by series report self-serve report, which includes both “Series last updated on” and “Module last updated on” fields or metrics. Similarly, you can view this data in other templates mentioned in the introduction of this section.
3. In the right-side Configure panel of the report editing mode, click Add columns and select the Series last updated on and Module last updated on fields/metrics to add as columns. Then, click Preview to preview the report. The added fields appear as columns in the table report.
4. Click Save to save the report. You can then export the report data in a .csv format, share it with other admins and managers, and also delete the report permanently when required. See this article for details.

DSR admins can bulk change room owners for multiple rooms and reassign owners for rooms owned by deactivated reps.

Note:

- Reps can only edit their rooms.

The user who changes the owner and the new room owner receive an email about the room assignments.

This feature simplifies room owner updates, saving time and effort. It also prevents room abandonment when reps leave the firm and enables admins to reassign room owners when a deal’s territory or value changes.

Example Scenarios

- Suppose US Central deals change to a new territory, US North. Admins can bulk assign the US Central deal rooms to the US North territory owner.
- If a customer’s annual recurring revenue (ARR) changes, bulk room ownership changes are necessary to transfer ownership to the appropriate team or owner. For example, if the threshold for commercial customers is $10,000 in ARR and changes to $15,000, rooms with customers who meet the new threshold can be reassigned to the appropriate team or owner.
- If the customer segment criteria change from commercial to enterprise, bulk room ownership change is necessary. This ensures that the right team is managing the appropriate set of customers based on thresholds.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > External Content Access:
This article explains how admins can embed Klue content (Battlecards, Dashboards, Feeds, and Digests) and dashboards in Mindtickle and DSR using shareable URLs.

This enables learners to access Klue content and view competitive intelligence from within Mindtickle.

The Klue battlecard can be embedded as learning objects using an iFrame within Mindtickle courses and quick update modules. The Klue dashboard can be embedded as tabs on the learning site homepage.

The Klue content can also be embedded in DSR rooms and templates as URLs.

Note:

- The embedded Klue content can be accessed only via the web, not on mobile or iPad.
- When embedding content, using only one Klue dashboard/battlecard is recommended.
- To embed content in Mindtickle courses or learner homepages, the below code line should be added to the iframe tag, <iframe src="v2.app.klue.com/dashboard?group=-1&sort=cards" style="width: 100%; height: 500px; border: none;"> </iframe>.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > External Content Access > Embed Klue content in Mindtickle > Embed a battlecard in Mindtickle:
Admins can embed Klue battlecards as learning objects in Mindtickle courses to summarize competitor information to learners.

To embed a Klue battlecard as a learning object:

1. Sign in to Klue.

2. On the homepage, click on a battlecard to embed.

The battlecard is displayed.

3. Copy the battlecard’s URL from the web browser, for example, v2.app.klue.com/dashboard?group=-1&sort=cards.

After copying the battlecard’s URL, perform the following,

4. Sign in to the Mindtickle admin site.

5. Go to the module where you want to embed the battlecard.

6. Click the Build tab and click Add learning objects.

7. On the Add learning objects pop-up, click Content in the Upload content section.

8. On the displayed pop-up, click New and click Embed link.

The Embed link pop-up is displayed,

9. Under Link, paste the copied battlecard URL (Step 3).

10. Click the Insert iframe tag checkbox to add an iFrame to the content.

11. Name: You can customize the battlecard’s name if necessary.

Preview: You can see how the battlecard is displayed in the module.

12. Click Embed.

The battlecard is added to the module.

13. Click the Publish tab.

14. From the Push these changes for drop-down, select the learner type to publish the changes.

15. Click the Notify learners via email checkbox to email learners about the changes.

16. Click Publish changes to publish the module.

Once the module is published, the battlecard is displayed to the learners in the module.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > External Content Access > Embed Klue content in Mindtickle > Embed the dashboard in Mindtickle:
Admins can embed Klue dashboards as a new tab on the learning site homepage to provide insights to learners from within Mindtickle.

To embed the Klue dashboard as a new tab:

1. Sign in to Klue.

2. Copy the URL of the dashboard from the web browser.

3. Sign in to the Mindtickle admin site.

4. Click the Account and select Homepages.

The Homepages screen is displayed.

5. Click Create new page.

6. On the Add homepage screen, click One column (Full width) on the Choose page layout pop-up.

The New Page Draft is displayed.

7. From the Widgets section, drag and drop the Custom HTML and CSS widget to the new page.

8. On the New custom HTML and CSS widget screen, paste the following code line in the HTML tab:

<iframe src="<Klue Dashboard URL>" style="width: 100%; height: 500px; border: none;"></iframe>.

For example, <iframe src="v2.app.klue.com/dashboard" style="width: 100%; height: 500px; border: none;"></iframe>

9. Click Add widget.

Tip: If the dashboard is incorrectly displayed in the widget, hover over the custom HTML and CSS widget, click the Edit icon, and modify the widget width and height in pixels.

10. Click the Copy link icon to copy the link to the page and share it with users.

11. Click Publish after making all changes.

When learners sign in to the learning site, the dashboard is displayed as a tab on the homepage.

The Klue content is added to the DSR.

Users can now view the Klue content in the DSR.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > ILT > View sessions from across modules:
To view ILT sessions from across modules,

1. Sign in to the learning site.

2. On the learning site homepage, click Training in the left navigation bar, and then click ILT Sessions.

Note: The Upcoming ILTs widget on the learning site's homepage allows learners to view and enroll in the promoted ILT sessions within the organization.

The ILT Sessions page is displayed.

Learners can view the following details on the ILT Sessions page:

- Date and time: The date and time of the scheduled session or event.
- Session: The name of the session and the event if the session is part of an event.
- Series: The series name and module name are listed below the series name.
- Enrollment status: The learner’s enrollment status for the session.

Learners can view the following tabs in the ILT Sessions page.

- My sessions: View all ILT sessions you can access in this tab.
- Hierarchy based team: View ILT sessions of direct reportees based on organizational hierarchy. This tab is displayed only for managers with reportees.
- Relationship based team: View ILT sessions of team members linked to you by a relationship field. This tab is displayed only for managers with reportees or teams linked to them by a relationship field. For more information on how Managers can manage their direct reportees and team members' enrollment in ILT sessions, see Manage enrollment of team members in ILTs.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Content Center > Bulk actions:
Bulk actions in Content Center help you save a lot of time and reduce the chance of human error when performing operations on a large number of files and folders.

1. Select items

You can select multiple items (files and folders) to perform bulk actions in the following ways:

- Individually : Use the checkbox next to each item to select them one by one. Note : Items that cannot be moved/deleted are disabled from selection. Hover over the checkbox to view the reason in a tooltip.
- All at once : Use the Select All checkbox in the header row to select all items. You can apply filters before using Select All to select only items that meet the filter criteria. Note :
  - When you select all items using Select All , all items on the page are selected—including those that may not be eligible for the bulk action. After the bulk action completes, you can check Notifications to see which items were not moved or deleted. Items that cannot be moved/deleted are covered in the Limitations of the Select All option section.
  - Scope : The Select All option includes all items on the page, not just those visible without scrolling.
  - Immediate item count : The Select All option counts only direct items on the page (Content Center homepage or folder page), excluding nested items in subfolders.

Note: You can select up to 2,000 items (files and folders) in a single bulk action.

2. Perform bulk actions

Once you have selected the items (files and folders), you perform the following bulk actions:

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Content Center > Limitations of the Select All option:
The Select All option in Content Center allows users to perform bulk move or delete actions efficiently. However, certain types of content may be excluded based on system rules and permissions. This section outlines the limitations that apply when using Select All to manage multiple items.

For Select All → Move

- Excessive nesting : Folders cannot be moved if the combined nesting level (source folder + destination folder) exceeds 10 levels.
- Self-nesting : Folders cannot be moved into their own subfolders.
- Scoped access : Items with scoped access cannot be moved. Additionally, public files cannot be moved to scoped folders without proper access.
- Insufficient permissions : Items without the appropriate permissions cannot be moved.
- Externally synced items : Items synced with external storage providers (SharePoint, Google shared drive, and AEM) cannot be moved.

For Select All → Delete

- Files in use : Files that are currently open or in use in other locations (in assets and modules) cannot be deleted. To view where the file is in use, click the number in the Locations used column.
- Non-empty folders : Folders that contain items cannot be deleted.
- Insufficient permissions : Items without the appropriate permissions cannot be deleted.
- Externally synced items : Items synced with external storage providers (SharePoint, Google shared drive, and AEM) cannot be deleted.
