Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > Integrations > How does the Call AI and Google Meet integration work:
1. Users with a valid Call AI recorder license can integrate their calendar with Call AI to record meetings. For more information, see Integrate Outlook Calendar with Call AI or Integrate Google Calendar With Call AI .
2. Meetings on the integrated user's calendar are automatically recorded based on preferences set by the admin or user. For more information, see Customize recording preferences .
3. Users can also enable or disable recording from the Upcoming calls page for specific meetings. For more information, see Upcoming meetings details .
4. When a meeting starts, a bot joins and announces that the meeting is being recorded.
5. After recording, the meeting is processed, and insights are generated and displayed on the Call AI platform. For more information, see Call Recording Details .

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > Integrations > Frequently asked questions (FAQ’s):
1. Why does Unverified appear next to the bot’s name?The Call AI bot joins the meeting as an unsigned user. Thus, Google Meet labels it as Unverified. This does not affect recording functionality.

2. What happens if the bot does not join the meeting?If recording is disabled by default, the bot will not join. To enable recording, go to the Upcoming meeting page and turn it on.

3. Can I remove the bot during a meeting?Yes, the meeting host can remove the bot to stop recording.

4. If a meeting on my calendar is scheduled by an external participant, will it be recorded?Yes, Call AI will join meetings where the host is an external participant. Depending on the recording preferences set by your admins, these meetings will either be recorded automatically, or you can manage the recordings through the Upcoming meeting page.

5. How to remove Pexip Interoperability

To remove Pexip interoperability on Google Meet, you have to delete Interoperability tokens and then disable the Gateway Interoperability settings:

To delete Interoperability tokens

1. On the Google Workspace administrator console, go to Apps > Google Workspace > Settings for Google Meet > Interoperability tokens.

2. Click the arrow icon next to the Interoperability tokens.

3. Remove any tokens that you have created for Pexip by clicking the Delete icon next to the token. 4. Click Delete on the displayed pop-up.

To disable the Gateway Interoperability settings

1. Click on Apps> Google Workspace > Settings for Google Meet > Meet video settings.

2. Click the Edit icon next to the Gateway Interoperability setting.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Digital Sales Rooms:
Reps and admins can use the Mindtickle mobile app on a tablet to manage (create and edit) DSRs. The DSRs can be managed only in the landscape view on tablets and not using mobile phones. Room visitors can view DSRs on any device, web, mobile, or tablet.

Prerequisite: The Mindtickle app should be installed on the tablet.

Managing DSRs on tablets enables reps to efficiently manage rooms without computer access, simplifying room management and helping close deals faster.

Note:

- DSRs can be managed only by reps and admins on tablets, not by room visitors.
- The DSRs can be managed only in the landscape view due to space constraints.
- To access DSRs on a tablet, an active internet connection is required as offline mode is not supported.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Announcements > I. Colors, typography, and iconography:
Image: The new admin site

A. Color palette and contrast

We've introduced a vibrant Persian blue as the main interface color, giving the admin site a modern and distinctive look. This rich, bold color improves the overall visual appeal while maintaining a clean and professional aesthetic that aligns with the Mindtickle brand.

Furthermore, we've enhanced contrast ratios across the site to improve text visibility, especially for users with visual impairments. These updates bring the UI in line with WCAG accessibility standards, providing a more inclusive and user-friendly environment.

B. Typography and iconography

As part of our ongoing commitment to accessibility, we’ve further enhanced our typography. In March 2024, we updated our platform to the Inter font family for a cleaner, more legible experience. With this release, we've made additional improvements to the typography, including adjustments to font sizes and line heights to ensure optimal readability.

We’ve also refined iconography across the admin site to align with the updated visual language. Icons are now more consistent, modern, and easier to recognize, contributing to a cleaner and more intuitive interface.

C. Overall user experience

In addition to the color and font improvements, the overall interface has been polished for smoother interactions. Subtle design tweaks, like more consistent spacing and streamlined icons, create a visually cohesive environment that feels intuitive and easy to navigate. These changes not only improve the visual appeal but also contribute to a faster, more responsive experience for all users.

- Account settings

Hover over any primary menu item in the sidebar to preview and navigate to its subpages with a single click. You can also right-click to open pages in new tabs, making it easier to work across multiple areas simultaneously.

A2. Collapsible sidebar

Click thebutton at the bottom of the sidebar to collapse or expand it as needed. Even when collapsed, the sidebar remains fully functional — use the hover menu to access all menus and their pages seamlessly. The sidebar’s state (expanded or collapsed) is saved across logins, so your sidebar preference is retained even if you sign out and sign back in.

A3. Auto-collapse behavior

The sidebar is designed to automatically adapt based on the type of page you're on: expanded on listing pages for easier access, and collapsed on detail pages to maximize workspace.

Let’s understand this in detail:

- Expanded on listing pages : The sidebar remains expanded by default on pages that list multiple items of a specific type: modules, series, assets, or hubs. Examples of listing pages: The Modules page lists all modules across series and the Series page lists all training series. You can manually collapse the sidebar on listing pages if needed. Tip : All pages under each main menu in the sidebar are listing pages and will keep the sidebar expanded by default.
- Collapsed on detail pages : The sidebar automatically collapses on pages where you view or edit a single item: a specific module, series, hub, or homepage. This gives you more space to work with content in detail. On these pages, the sidebar cannot be expanded manually . Examples of detail pages : The page that you land on after opening a specific series from Training → Series , opening a hub from Assets → Hubs , or editing a homepage under Account → Homepages .

A. Assets page

The new Assets page under the Assets menu lists all of your assets in the following tabs:

- Active tab (new): Lists all active assets across different hubs. You can apply filters, search for an asset, and sort the assets by name, modified date, or overall engagement. - Archived tab (previously a separate page): Lists archived assets. You can either restore an archived asset and edit it or delete it. You can also delete archived assets in bulk.

Page deprecation:

The previous Assets tab → Home page, which displayed Recently Published, Expiring Soon, Expired, and Draft assets, has been deprecated. We have incorporated the previous Home page’s functionality into this new Assets page.

Previously, the admin site lacked a dedicated page listing all assets across different hubs. Additionally, the Archived assets page, which existed as a separate page, only listed archived assets.

B. Homepages landing page

Under Account, we have added the new Homepage page that lists all learning site homepages. This page lists homepages, along with their status, who created it, page visibility, date when it was last updated, shareable link to the page, and an option to preview the page. You can filter the list of pages by status (Draft, Active, and Inactive) or by visibility (No learners, Visible to groups, and No learners). You can also search for a specific page. Use the More actions button against each page to edit, duplicate, deactivate, or delete the page. Drag and drop to reorder the pages to your liking.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Announcements > VII. Other key changes:
A. Training page updates

- The previous Training tab landing view is now the Overview page under the Training menu.
- Marketplace is now directly accessible from the Training menu for easy discovery of series and module templates.
  - Previously accessible only via the Marketplace banner or the Create new → Template option.
  - You can still access Marketplace from the Create button on the Training → Series page.

B. Unified page layout & design improvements

- All pages now follow a standardized layout for a cleaner and more consistent user experience across the admin site.
- All listing pages (such as modules, series, and hubs) now include:
  - Header : Breadcrumb → Page title → Page description (left); action buttons (right).
  - Content area : Search and filters, tabular list of items, and item-level and bulk actions.

C. Consistent button placement

- Create new buttons have been moved from the left sidebar (in the old experience) to the top-right of each relevant page.
  - Example pages with “Create” action buttons: Training, Assets, Users and Groups, and Homepages.
  - This ensures that all action buttons (CTAs) now appear consistently in the header on the right.

For example:

- Create a new module or series from the Series page via the top-right Create button.
- Create a new module from the Modules page via the top-right Create module button.

D. Feature renaming

- Profile management page is renamed to Profile fields , with UI/UX improvements.
- System Feedback is renamed to Notifications and now uses a bell icon instead of the old feedback icon. It remains accessible in the top-right corner of the header.

E. New Settings tab on group page

- Visibility: This column displays the series by its visibility, whether Public , Invite-only , or Public (Scoped) .
- Created by: This column displays the series creator's name.
- Created on: This column displays the series creation date.

- Overall engagement: This column displays the asset’s number of views, shares, and downloads. Click the column header to view the most engaged or least engaged assets on top.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Asset Hub > Admin > Archived tab:
Archiving an asset removes it from the sales rep’s view while keeping it in the archived state for any future use. It also reduces storage costs while maintaining search capabilities. The Archived tab lists all of the assets that were archived in the past.

Note: If the asset is present in multiple hubs, archiving removes it from all the hubs. Additionally, asset insights on views, downloads, shares, and ratings take a maximum of two hours to reflect from the learning site to the admin site.

The Archived tab displays the following columns:

- Name: This column displays the asset’s name. Click the column header to sort the names in ascending or descending order.
- Asset owner: This column displays the asset’s owner name.
- Archived on: This column displays the asset’s archive date. Click the column header to view the most recent or oldest archived assets on top.
- Feedback: This column displays the feedback received for the archived asset. Click the column header to sort the feedback by rating and comments in ascending or descending order.
- Overall engagement: This column displays the asset’s number of views, shares, and downloads. Click the column header to view the most engaged or least engaged assets on top.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle APIs > Copilot APIs:
The Mindtickle Seller Copilot API allow you to embed our AI-powered assistant directly into your custom applications, chatbots, and workflows. The Seller Copilot Chat API handles prompts and returns streaming responses with context retention and citations. The API enables you to query assigned and public modules, assets, and Call AI recordings to retrieve real-time answers for tasks such as pre-call preparation, post-call follow-ups, and product inquiries.

Key benefits

- Seamless integration: Embed AI-powered conversations directly into your existing tools and interfaces.
- Real-time streaming: Receive token-by-token responses for a smooth, interactive user experience.
- Context awareness: Maintain conversational history to support multi-turn interactions and follow-up questions.
- Security compliance: All interactions follow Mindtickle’s existing permissions and access controls, authenticated via JWTs.

Seller Copilot is also available on the learning site, Slack, Salesforce, and the Mindtickle mobile app.

Availability & access control

- Seller Copilot API is not enabled by default and require the Seller Copilot feature to be active on your Mindtickle instance. To enable both the feature and the API, please contact your CSM or Mindtickle Support .
- Only users authorized by an admin can use the API. Admins can control access from the admin site under Account → Settings → Seller Copilot using the Audience setting (e.g., all users, specific groups, or fully restricted).

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle APIs > Copilot APIs > Chat API:
This endpoint allows you to engage in AI-powered conversations with Seller Copilot using a single, unified chat endpoint. You can initiate chat sessions, send user queries, continue conversations while maintaining context, and stream assistant responses in real-time. This API enables seamless, interactive, and personalized user experiences with AI.

You can perform the following operations:

- Initiate a new chat session : Start a conversation by sending the first set of messages between the user and assistant.
- Send a user query : Submit a new prompt from the user for a response from the Seller Copilot assistant.
- Continue a chat with context : Include previous message history to maintain continuity in the conversation.
- Stream assistant responses in real time : Receive the Seller Copilot assistant’s reply incrementally via server-sent events (SSE) for a smooth and responsive user experience.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle APIs > Copilot APIs > Chat API > Request:
Request URL

```
POST /copilot/chat
```

Request headers

```
Content-Type: application/json
```

Request parameters

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| usernameREQUIRED | string | The username of the Mindtickle user initiating the chat. |
| inputREQUIRED | array | A list of message exchanges in the conversation, including both user and assistant messages. Each message must have the following attributes: |
| input.roleREQUIRED | string | The role of the persona in the conversation (user or assistant). |
| input.contentREQUIRED | string | The content of the message. For user messages, this will be the user's input, and for assistant messages, it will be the assistant's response. |

Request example

```json

{
  "username": "dummy-user",
  "input": [
    {"role": "user", "content": "knock knock."},
    {"role": "assistant", "content": "Who's there?"},
    {"role": "user", "content": "ABC"}
  ]
}
```

Rate limiting:

- 600 requests per minute (RPM)
- Payload size : Approximately 200KB/request (~200,000 characters).
- Parallelism : Multiple requests can be made concurrently, as long as the RPM limit is not exceeded.

Performance:

- Initial chunk timeout : 60 seconds
- Average latency between initial and final chunks : 10 seconds (may vary depending on volume and agents).
- SLA : 99.9% uptime.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle APIs > Training APIs:
The Module Completion APIs allow you to programmatically mark modules as complete for individual learners or entire cohorts. These endpoints support backdated timestamps, enabling you to record past progress or migrate user history when aligned with backdated invitations.

Key capabilities include:

- Single & bulk completion: Mark a specific module as complete for an individual user or apply updates to a large group of learners in a single request.
- Backdated progress: Record completions with past timestamps to accurately reflect training history. This feature works in tandem with backdated invitations (available via the User APIs) to ensure data consistency during migration.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle APIs > Training APIs > Backdated invitations:
When migrating users or recording past progress, invite dates must align with completion dates. Completion APIs accept backdated completions as long as the learner’s invitation date is also backdated appropriately. To support this, the User APIs allow you to set a past invite date using an epoch timestamp. For details on how to create backdated invitations, see the "Backdated series invitation" and "Backdated module invitation" sections in User APIs.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle APIs > Content Center APIs:
The Content Center APIs for synced content enable you to build custom integrations between Mindtickle Content Center and your external Content Management Systems (CMS) or Digital Asset Management (DAM) platforms. Use these endpoints to securely upload files, initiate content management jobs to synchronize assets, monitor execution history, and permanently delete synced root folders.

Key capabilities include:

- Integration setup: Establish a persistent connection between your external source and a root folder in the Mindtickle Content Center.
- Secure file upload: Generate secure, temporary URLs to safely transfer files before processing.
- Job execution & monitoring: Trigger content management jobs to create or update assets and track their status asynchronously using unique execution IDs.
- Lifecycle management: Audit sync history or permanently delete synced root folders when integrations are no longer needed.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle APIs > Content Center APIs > Available API endpoints:
The Content Center APIs includes the following key endpoints, typically used in this sequence:

1. Create an Integration Establish a persistent connection between your external CMS/DAM and Mindtickle’s Content Center. This one-time setup generates an integration_id and root_folder_id , which are required for all subsequent API calls related to this integration.
2. Get Upload URL Obtain a secure, temporary URL for uploading files to the server. This step ensures that your content can be safely transferred to Content Center before initiating any content management operations.
3. Initiate a Content Management Job Start a job that processes and synchronizes uploaded content between your external system and Content Center. This includes creating or updating content assets according to the integration’s configuration.
4. Check Content Management Job Status Monitor the progress and final outcome of a content management job using its execution_id . This endpoint helps track job completion, detect failures, and confirm successful synchronization.
5. Get All Executions for an Integration ID Retrieve a paginated list of all content management job executions associated with a specific integration ID. Useful for auditing, reporting, or reviewing the history of sync operations.
6. Delete Synced Root Folder Permanently remove a synced root folder and all its associated content from Content Center. This administrative operation is irreversible and should be used with caution to prevent unintended data loss.

- AEM_DAM : Use this value when the pushing system is the Adobe Experience Manager (AEM) digital asset management (DAM) module.
- API : Use this value for any other external CMS, DAM, or content system that pushes content through these APIs.

Both values use the same endpoints and follow the same flow; the difference is only in how the source is labeled for attribution and filtering in the Content Center.

```json

{
  "root_folder_id": "123456",
  "integration_id": "AEM Content-789012"
}
```

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle APIs > Content Center APIs > API endpoints > 4. Check Content Management Job Status > Request URL:
```
GET /services/data/v1.0/content/management/{execution_id}
```

Example request

```
GET /services/data/v1.0/content/management/exec-987654
```

Example response

```json

{
  "status": "SUCCESSFUL",
  "entities": [
    {
      "external_id": "brochure-2025-Q1",
      "file_id": "file-123456",
      "status": "SUCCESSFUL"
    }
  ]
}
```

Possible sync statuses

- SUCCESSFUL : All operations completed successfully
- FAILED : The job failed
- IN_PROGRESS : The job is still running
- PARTIALLY_FAILED : Some operations succeeded, some failed

Handling failed or skipped files

Content synced through these APIs is push-based: your external system pushes content to Content Center rather than Mindtickle pulling it from the source. As a result, Mindtickle does not automatically retry a file that fails to sync or is skipped, and the Resync action is not available for this content in the Content Center.

In the Last sync details view, such files display the message: An internal error occurred. Automatic retry is not available for this sync type. To re-sync a failed or skipped file, resolve the underlying issue and submit the file again through a new content management job.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle APIs > Content Center APIs > API endpoints > 6. Delete Synced Root Folder > Query parameters:
| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| rootFolderIdREQUIRED | string | The unique identifier of the root folder in Content Center that you want to permanently delete. When this folder is deleted, all its subfolders and files are also removed. |

Request example

```bash

curl --location --request DELETE \
'https://api.mindtickle.com/services/data/v1.0/content/integration/<integrationId>?rootFolderId=<rootFolderId>' \
--header 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' \
--header 'X-Consumer-Custom-Id: <companyId>' \
--header 'Content-Type: application/json'
```

Response

Success (200 OK)

Usage notes

- This operation deletes the specified root folder and all its subfolders and files.
- Only users with admin privileges can perform this operation.
- The action is irreversible; ensure you have backups if necessary.
- In case a file is being used while running this API, then the file will go into offline mode. The file and folders in its hierarchy will not get deleted. You need to manually delete the file along with relevant folders and subfolders from the Content Center.

| metadata.source_path | string | Yes | Web accessible URL of the original file. |
| metadata.additional_properties | object | No | Any additional properties to store with the file. |

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle APIs > Content Center APIs > Usage examples > Complete workflow example:
1. Create an integration:

Request

```json

"// POST /services/data/v1.0/content/integration"
{
  "source_name": "AEM_DAM",
  "root_folder_name": "Marketing Content"
}
```

Example Curl:

```bash

curl --location 'https://proxy.kong.staging.mindtickle.com/services/data/v1.0/content/integration' \
--header 'Authorization: Bearer <JWT>' \
--header 'Content-Type: application/json' \

    "root_folder_name": "Marketing Content"
}'
```

1. Get upload URL:

```
GET /services/data/v1.0/content/upload-url?file_name=annual-report-2025.pdf
```

Example Curl:

```bash

curl --location 'https://proxy.kong.staging.mindtickle.com/services/data/v1.0/content/upload-url?file_name=abc.pdf' \
--header 'Authorization: Bearer <JWT>'
```

1. Upload a file to Presigned URL (received in previous step)

This should be a PUT request on the presigned URL.

```bash

curl --location --request PUT '<PRESIGNED_URL>' \
--header 'Content-Type: application/pdf' \
--data-binary '@/Users/ig/MT/content/test-data/sample.pdf'

      }
    }
  ]
}
```

1. Check sync status:

```
GET /services/data/v1.0/content/management/exec-456789
```

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle APIs > Content Center APIs > Best practices:
1. Error Handling
  - Always check the HTTP status code and error responses.
  - Implement exponential backoff for retries on 429 and 5xx errors.
  - Log detailed error information for troubleshooting.
2. Performance Optimization
  - Batch related operations in a single sync job when possible.
  - Perform status checks efficiently by not polling too frequently.
3. Security
  - Use HTTPS for all API calls.
4. Integration Management
  - Create logical separation between different source systems.
  - Use consistent naming conventions for integrations.

1. File upload failures
  - Ensure file names are under 250 characters and include valid extensions.
  - Check that the file size is not too large.

2. Sync failures

  - Confirm that the integration_id and root_folder_id are valid.
3. Status checking issues
  - Ensure you're using the correct execution_id.
  - Remember that large sync jobs may take time to complete.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > User Management > Users and Groups:
Collaborator management in Mindtickle allows admins to easily assign and manage individual users and groups as collaborators to Series, Asset Hub, and Content Center.

Admins can add only individual users as collaborators to manage groups.

Note: Collaborators are users who work alongside the creator of a series, Asset Hub, Content Center, or groups to manage content, assets, files, and users. Based on their roles and permissions, collaborators can manage content, assign learners, manage permissions, modify assets, content folders, and group members.

Admins can configure collaborator permissions for individual users and groups to view, create, and manage content within series, modify assets in Asset Hub and Content Center, and add or remove members from groups. For more information on collaborator permissions, see collaborator permissions.

For information on the roles and permissions available in Mindtickle, see Roles and permissions in Mindtickle.

This article lists the collaborator's permissions and explains the steps to add or remove individual users and groups as collaborators to Series, Asset Hub, and Content Center. It also includes steps to add individual users as collaborators to manage groups.

Although this article explains how to add series collaborators, you can follow the same steps to add, remove, and manage collaborators in Asset Hub and Content Center.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > User Management > Users and Groups > Caveats > Series:
- Only site owners, enablement admins, content experts, group managers, and managers can be series collaborators.
- By default, site owners are series collaborators.
- Only users with limited collaborator permissions can be series collaborators.
- Before adding a series collaborator, verify if they are already a collaborator with limited permissions.
- Only site owners and enablement admins can add series collaborators.
- Site owners can add new and existing users as series collaborators. When adding new users, site owners must ensure that they have the series collaborator permissions.
- Enablement admins can add only existing users (with limited collaborator permissions) as series collaborators.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > User Management > Users and Groups > Manage existing collaborators and their permissions > Series:
Series collaborators work alongside series creators to manage content and learners.

To manage existing series collaborators and their permissions,

1. On the admin site homepage, click Training and select Series .
2. Click on a series to open.
3. In the series header, click Manage collaborators to view and modify the collaborators.
4. On the Manage collaborators pop-up, use the search bar to quickly search for a particular user or group.
5. Click the Users or Groups button to filter the collaborator list by users or groups. You can also click the All button to view both groups and users.
6. Hover over the Role column of a user to view their assigned roles.
7. If a user or group has limited permissions, you can assign other permissions by clicking the Permissions dropdown.
8. To update the collaborator permissions of a user or group, click the Permissions drop-down. For information on series collaborator permissions, see Series . Note :

- You cannot change the permissions of site owners and other series, hub, and content folder creators.
- Site owner users are series collaborators by default and have all permissions.
- To add additional permissions, a user should have the necessary collaborator permissions .

9. Select the necessary permissions, and click Apply.

10. Click Save changes. This updates the user’s collaborator permissions.

To add a new user or group as a series collaborator, follow the steps mentioned under the Add collaborators section.

To remove a series collaborator, see Remove collaborators.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > User Management > Users and Groups > Manage existing collaborators and their permissions > Content Center:
Content Center collaborators help manage content folders, manage access, and add, remove, or modify content in folders.

Site owners can view and edit all content in the Content Center. They can also add collaborators at the file and folder levels. Collaborators receive the Manage Content permission on the respective file or folder to manage content center folders.

For more information on Content Center permissions, see Content Center permissions.

To manage existing collaborators and their permissions in Content Center,

1. On the admin site homepage, click Content on the left navigation panel.
2. Click the More options icon and select Manage collaborators to view and modify the folder collaborators. Alternatively, you can click the More options icon from inside a Content Center folder.
3. Follow Steps 2 to 8 from the Series section to manage the Content Center collaborators.

For information on Content Center collaborator permissions, see Content Center.

To add a new user or group as a folder collaborator in Content Center, follow the steps mentioned under the Add collaborators section.

To remove a Content Center collaborator, see Remove collaborators.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > User Management > Users and Groups > Manage existing collaborators and their permissions > Groups:
Group collaborators help add or remove users to manage groups and their members.

To verify existing group collaborators and update their permissions,

1. On the admin site homepage, click Users and select Groups .
2. On the Groups page, click on a group.
3. In the group header, click the number of collaborators.
4. On the Add collaborators pop-up, hover over a user’s permissions to view if they have the necessary permissions. Use the Search collaborators field to quickly search for a particular user.
5. If a user has only limited permissions, you can assign other permissions through the user’s Permissions dropdown.
6. To update the user's collaborator permissions, click the drop-down menu, select the applicable options, and click Apply (n) . For information on Group collaborator permissions, see Groups . Note: You can modify a user’s permissions only if they do not have the Site owner role. By default, users with this role are series collaborators and have all necessary permissions.
7. Click Save . This updates the user’s permissions. Tip: Choose whether to provide series access only to selected or all potential users. If you select All potential users , all existing and future users with the appropriate roles receive access to the series.
8. To add a new user as a group collaborator or remove a group collaborator, follow the steps mentioned in the Add collaborators to manage groups section.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > User Management > Users and Groups > Add collaborators to manage series, Asset Hub, and Content Center > Add collaborators manually > Add individual users as collaborators:
You can add individual users as collaborators to a series to help create and manage the series content and modules.

To add an individual user as a collaborator,

1. On the series header, click Manage collaborators.

Note:

- The Manage collaborators button is visible based on your Role on the admin site.
- By default, the system adds all site owners as collaborators.
- Only site owners and enablement admins can add collaborators.

The Manage collaborators screen is displayed.

2. Click the Manually assign collaborators option to add users as collaborators.

3. In the + Add users or groups as collaborators field, search for users to add as collaborators.

4. Select the checkbox of the necessary users and click Add collaborator.

5. Click the Permissions drop-down and select permissions for the selected user.

6. Click Save changes.

This adds the user as a collaborator.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > User Management > Users and Groups > Add collaborators to manage series, Asset Hub, and Content Center > Add collaborators manually > Add managers as series collaborators:
You can add managers (users with the Manager role) as collaborators to a series, enabling them to assign training series and modules to their team members through the Command Center on the learning site and Mindtickle mobile app. When a manager is added as a series collaborator, the Assign Content via Learning Site permission is automatically enabled, giving them the ability to assign training content directly from the Command Center.

Managers can assign content only from the specific series where they have been added as collaborators by an admin. Once added, they can assign the full series or select individual modules from that series to their team members.

Note: Adding managers as series collaborators does not grant access to the admin site. Their permissions are limited to assigning training content to their team members through the Command Center.

To add an managers as series collaborators:

1. On the series header, click Manage collaborators .

1. The Manage collaborators screen appears. You can add managers as series collaborators using either the Manually assign collaborators or the Automatically assign collaborators option. This procedure explains how to manually assign collaborators. The automatic option will add managers as collaborators without requiring further input.

1. Click the Manually assign collaborators option to add manager users as collaborators.
2. In the + Add users or groups as collaborators field, select one or more users with the Manager role to add as series collaborators. Alternatively, you can use the Add as a user and collaborator directly option to create new users with the Manager role and add them as series collaborators at the same time.
3. Select the checkbox next to the manager users you want to add, then click Add collaborator .

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > User Management > Users and Groups > Add collaborators to manage series, Asset Hub, and Content Center > Add collaborators manually > Add groups as collaborators:
Admins can add groups as collaborators, saving time and allowing them to add multiple users as collaborators simultaneously.

When you add a group as a collaborator, group members with the necessary roles will automatically become collaborators.

For example, if you assign the group "Acme Sales" as a collaborator to the "Acme Sales Onboarding" series:

- John, with the learner role, does not become a collaborator for the group because he does not have the necessary role.
- Mike, with the enablement admin role, becomes a collaborator for the group because he has the necessary role.

Note:

- Only site owners, enablement admins, content experts, and group managers can be collaborators.
- You can add groups as collaborators only when manually assigning collaborators.
- If a group member is already an individual collaborator, the system combines their existing permissions with the group's permissions.

Admins can modify the group’s permissions on the Manage collaborators screen if necessary. For more information on modifying collaborator permissions, see Edit collaborator permissions.

Caveats

The examples provided below use the series as a reference. They are also applicable to Asset Hub and Content Center folders.

- When a user is both an individual collaborator and a group collaborator

If a user who is already an individual series collaborator is also added as a group collaborator, the system combines both their individual and group permissions.

For example, if an admin adds John from the ‘Acme Sales’ group as a collaborator with view-only permissions to the series ‘Acme Training’.

Then, the admin also adds the ‘Acme Sales’ group as a collaborator to the same series ‘Acme Training’ and provides edit permissions for the group.

You can automatically add series collaborators based on the admin site users' roles and permissions. The system automatically selects all users with collaborator permissions and adds them to the series, Asset Hub, and Content Center folder.

Note:

- When you add collaborators automatically, all previously added groups and individual collaborators will lose access to the series, Asset Hub, and Content Center folder.
- If you switch to manual collaborator assignment from automatic, only the users populated automatically by the system during automatic assignment are displayed for manual selection.

To add collaborators automatically,

1. On the series header, click Manage collaborators . The Manage collaborators screen is displayed.
2. Click Automatically assign collaborators The Automatically assign collaborators pop-up is displayed.
3. Click Confirm . All users with collaborator roles ( Site Owner, Enablement admin, Content expert, and Group manager ) on the admin site are automatically added and displayed in the collaborators list. The Users added as collaborators (n) section displays the number of users selected. Note: When an admin switches from automatic to manual collaborator assignment, the system displays the following pop-up. 4. To proceed, click Confirm . The system automatically copies the first 1000 users in alphabetical order. If there are more than 1000 users, the admin needs to manually review and add the remaining users. Follow the same steps mentioned above to automatically add collaborators in Asset Hub and Content Center.

Only a site owner and an enablement admin can remove series collaborators. However, admins cannot remove a site owner’s access.

To remove collaborators from a series Asset Hub or Content Center,

5. Click Save changes . This removes the user as a collaborator. Follow the same steps mentioned above to remove collaborators from Asset Hub and Content Center.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Mobile App > Overview:
Mindtickle’s Seller Copilot enhances the productivity of sales reps and managers by leveraging AI to provide real-time access to key information, streamline workflows, and ensure readiness for customer interactions. With multi-chat functionality, users can manage multiple conversations by topic without losing context, similar to modern AI chat tools. Copilot follows the Mindtickle platform's existing permissions and access policies, ensuring secure, compliant interactions. It also ensures only sales reps configured by the admin can access Copilot.

- Access Copilot : Access Seller Copilot on the Mindtickle mobile app by tapping the icon in the top-right corner to open the chat interface. You can type your question or choose from suggested questions, and easily close or return to the window as needed. Copilot supports multiple conversation threads, so you can organize discussions by topic and switch between chats while keeping context intact.
- Ask questions : You can ask questions related to modules (assigned and public), assets, and Call AI calls available to you. Copilot provides instant answers and support across your queries and tasks — from pre-call preparation to post-call follow-ups and answers on products, processes, or customers.

Seller Copilot retains all your chat history even if you log out. Chat history is deleted only when you manually delete it — a permanent action that cannot be undone.

Seller Copilot is also available on the learning site, Slack, Salesforce, and through Mindtickle APIs.

For information about Mindtickle Copilot, see Mindtickle Copilot overview.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Mobile App > How it works:
Mindtickle’s Seller Copilot is designed for intuitive, conversational interaction. Here’s how it works:

1. Starting a conversation: Use the options in the “Access Copilot” section to begin a chat. You can either type your own query or select from suggested questions/prompts. For best results, frame queries as specific questions or requests.
2. Multi-chat support: You can create and manage multiple conversation threads. Each chat thread is saved separately, allowing you to switch between topics, deals, or customers without losing context. Chats are automatically named based on your first query, and you can rename or delete threads as needed.
3. Instant, context-aware answers: Copilot provides quick, summarized answers, drawing from modules (assigned and public), assets, and Call AI calls available to you. Responses include relevant links and related content when applicable.
4. Saved chat history: All messages are saved automatically within each chat thread, so you can revisit past conversations anytime. On the web, you can access all saved chats through thenavigation panel.
5. Suggested follow-ups: After each response, Copilot suggests follow-up questions to help you dive deeper into the topic or continue the conversation seamlessly.
6. Chat actions: While interacting with Copilot, you can:
  - View related sources : Click links to see the content Copilot referenced.
  - Copy response : Copy the answer for use elsewhere.
  - Provide feedback : Use thumbs up or thumbs down to rate Copilot’s response and provide detailed feedback if needed.

The following subsections — Access Copilot and Chat with Copilot — outline how to access Seller Copilot on the mobile app and use it effectively.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Mobile App > How it works > Chat with Copilot:
1. Start a conversation with Seller Copilot by using one of the options listed in the “Access Copilot” section.
2. In the Seller Copilot chat window, either choose from the suggested questions or type your own in the input box , and then press Enter . You can ask questions related to modules (assigned and public), assets, and Call AI calls available to you on the mobile app. It is recommended to frame your queries as specific questions or instructions for most accurate and relevant results. For example, you can ask: “ Help me prepare for my next call with Acme ” or “ Can our product integrate with Acme? ”. Tip : Press Shift + Enter to start a new line in the chat input box, as pressing Enter sends your message to Copilot .
3. See the “Supported content and files” and “Limitations” sections for details on the types of questions Seller Copilot supports and its current limitations. See the “Sample questions” section for example questions and the responses.
4. While Seller Copilot is responding, click the Stop button to immediately halt the response generation. The Stop button appears once the response starts streaming .
5. Seller Copilot generates answers from content across modules, assets, and Call AI calls to which you have access. Copilot then streams a clear and actionable response in real-time, ensuring you receive timely, relevant information. Actions you can take on Copilot's response: Related sources : These are the sources and related content from which Copilot generated its response. Note that related sources are only listed if they are applicable and available for the specific query. You can click on any of the links to view the full source content [opens in a new tab]. Copy response : Click Copy to copy Copilot’s response/answer for use elsewhere. Tip : Using the Copy option includes markdown and CSS syntax in the copied text. Alternatively, select the text directly in the chat window and right-click to copy it with cleaner formatting. Provide feedback : You can provide your feedback on Copilot’s response. Click Thumbs up if Copilot’s response was helpful. Click Thumbs down if the response wasn’t helpful, where you can provide detailed feedback.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Mobile App > How it works > Chat with Copilot:
1. Please note the following:
  - Mindtickle Copilot can make mistakes. Please ensure to review the information in the response for accuracy as necessary before making use of the information.
  - The content within a document is searchable only if it contains fewer than 500,000 characters. This limit applies to documents added to modules and assets, including PDFs, PowerPoint presentations, and transcripts. For reference, documents with approximately 800 pages of text (assuming 600–700 words per page with standard margins and line spacing) would be searchable.
2. Follow-up questions : After each response, Copilot suggests follow-up questions related to your query and the response. You can choose any of these suggestions or ask your own. You can engage in a back-and-forth interaction with Copilot, asking follow-up questions to dive deeper into the insights provided .
3. Close the chat window : Click Close in the top-right corner to close the chat window. When you reopen Copilot, the chat window will reappear with your past chat history .
4. Rename or delete chat thread : Click for options to Rename and Delete the current chat thread. Caution: Deleting a chat thread will permanently remove the entire conversation history. Proceed with care; this action cannot be undone .
5. Start new chat: To begin a new conversation, click the + New chat button at the top of the current thread. Alternatively, use the + Start a new chat option in the navigation panel .
6. Navigation panel actions : Click the navigation panel icon to access the navigation panel, , where you can view and manage your past chat threads and access additional options :
  - Start new chat: Click + Start a new chat to begin a new conversation with Copilot.
  - Access past chats: Browse all past conversation threads directly in the panel.
  - Search chats: Use the search bar to find chats by name.Note: Search is currently limited to chat titles only. Searching within chat content will be available in a future release.
  - Rename or delete chats: Use the Rename and Delete options to rename or delete any chat. Rename chats to keep them organized and easy to find. Delete chats to remove old or irrelevant conversations (confirmation required).

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Mobile App > Supported content and files:
I. Content types

Seller Copilot can search and retrieve information from various content types available on the mobile app. It can search content from modules (assigned and public), assets, and Call AI calls, but will only provide answers based on the items you have access to.

Supported questions

Seller Copilot provides instant answers and support across your queries and tasks — from pre-call preparation to post-call follow-ups and answers on products, processes, or customers. Copilot supports both general and specific questions about accessible content. When referring to specific calls or assets, provide the name or link as described below:

- Calls: Copilot can identify a call by its name or direct link. It can also recognize recent calls (e.g., "last call" or "last 2 calls"), but cannot identify older calls based on specific dates. Note : Questions about Call AI listing pages or analytics (Recordings, Upcoming Meetings, My Analytics) are not supported.
- Assets: Copilot can identify an asset by its name only.

Note: Copilot cannot currently identify modules by name or link.

See the “Limitations” section for Seller Copilot’s current limitations and the “Sample questions” section for example questions and responses.

II. File types

Seller Copilot can search and retrieve information from the following supported file types:

- Video: MP4, MOV, AVI, MKV, WMV, WEBM, M4V, MPEG, MPG, FLV, VOB
- Audio: MP3, M4A, AAC, WAV, OGG, OGA, F4A
- Documents: PDF, Word documents (DOC/DOCX), PowerPoint files (PPT/PPTX), Excel files (XLS/XLSX)

Note: Copilot cannot search within SCORM content or images.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Mobile App > Limitations:
While Seller Copilot offers a wide range of features to support sales teams, some functionalities are not yet supported but are planned for future releases:

- Content-based responses only : Seller Copilot generates responses and identifies relevant modules or assets using only the information explicitly stated in the content (raw text). It does not use module or asset names, links, descriptions, or tags (metadata). As a result, it does not support questions about specific modules when only a module name or link is provided. Examples of unsupported questions: “ Summarize the “Platform training” course module ” “ Summarize this course module: https://acmeuni.mindtickle.com/new/ui/learner/course/7571288691371765086/overview?series=1553462122991359568 ”
- General questions on module assignment and progress: Copilot currently does not support general questions related to training modules, including:
  - Module assignment or invitation (e.g., assigned modules)
  - Module status or progress (e.g., not started, in progress, or completed)
  - Module relevance (e.g., required, optional, or none)

Examples of unsupported questions on training modules: “List all modules assigned to me in the last 15 days”“What modules do I have to complete?”“What’s my training completion percentage?”“List the modules assigned to me last month”“Tell me if I have any required modules that are not completed”“Give me a list of optional modules in the last 6 months”See the “Supported content and files” section for details on the types of questions Seller Copilot supports.

Admins can integrate Mindtickle with external content repositories such as SharePoint, Google Shared Drive, or Adobe Experience Manager (AEM) to automate content sync. Once an account is configured, you can manage the following actions:

- Edit the account
- Pause syncs
- Resume paused syncs
- Resync the account
- View the sync logs
- Delete the account

For configuration instructions, see the relevant integration article for your content source.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Automated Sync > Edit the account:
To edit a configured account:

1. Click the horizontal menu icon and select Edit .
2. In the Edit account modal, click Edit for the section you want to update.

1. Edit account details

You can update the Account name and Connection details. These updates also change the folder name in Content Center.

2. Edit mapped folders and asset metadata

Admins cannot modify existing folder paths directly, as this affects the files synced from that path. Instead:

- To remove a folder path: Click the Delete icon , then confirm by clicking Yes, delete .
- To add a new folder path: Use the option to configure a new path.

You can disable asset metadata sync by toggling off the Map asset metadata option. To update asset metadata mapping:

- Click the Delete icon to remove the current mapping.
- Edit the metadata template.
- Upload the updated file.

Note:

- If you disable metadata sync, properties stop syncing but remain editable in Mindtickle.
- When you update the CSV metadata file:
  - Previously unmapped properties now mapped will appear as read-only in Mindtickle.
  - Previously mapped properties now unmapped can be edited in Mindtickle and will no longer sync.

3. Edit sync and notifications

To configure sync frequency and notifications:

- Select the desired option from the Sync frequency dropdown.
- Use the Users to notify dropdown to add users for sync failure alerts.

For details on each of the three settings, see their respective articles.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Automated Sync > View sync logs:
Sync logs show completed jobs, file sync status, and failure reasons for corrective action.

Click the horizontal menu icon and select View sync log.

Sync logs offer detailed sync and status details for all files and folders. Files are marked with either of the following statuses: Success, Skipped, or Failed. Additionally, for skipped and failed files, the logs offer detailed error messages to help you identify and resolve the issues effectively.

Sync logs provides details on:

- Number of sync jobs
- Sync type (manual or automated)
- Start and completion times
- Sync status (Success or Failed)
- Number of failed file syncs

You can access the same sync logs here as you would in the Content Center. For details on sync logs, see View and manage synced content, sync status, and logs in Content Center.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Copilot > For admins:
The Seller Copilot configuration settings allow admins to customize both the experience and access to Seller Copilot for sales reps (learners) on both the learning site and the Mindtickle mobile app. The settings ensure that sellers receive more relevant, tailored, and effective answers each time they interact with Seller Copilot.

Admins can define various aspects of how Copilot behaves, how it presents itself to your reps, and how it can be customized to align with your company’s goals and language. These settings provide flexibility in controlling the accessibility, tone, and experience of Copilot.

Admins can configure the following settings:

- Description : Introduce Copilot with a tailored description and provide quick details on what it can do.
- Audience : Choose who can access Copilot (everyone, a specific group, or no one). Important : We highly recommend reviewing our Phased rollout strategy before enabling Copilot for all users to ensure a smooth deployment.
- Custom instructions : Set the tone, language, and company-specific terminologies for Copilot's responses. Also see the best practices article.

With these customizations, admins can integrate Seller Copilot into organizational workflows, tailoring it to meet users' specific needs. This improves the user experience and maximizes the effectiveness of Seller Copilot.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Copilot > For admins > Configure settings > Description:
The Description setting allows you to introduce Copilot to your sellers and provide them with key information about its features and capabilities. This description should help your sellers understand what Copilot can do for them and how it can assist with their learning and sales tasks.

- Character limit : 1,000 characters
- Insert variables : You can use the following variable: username, user email, and company name.
- Reset to default : Click to restore the description to its original setting.

Example I:

```
Hi {{user_name}}!
I am your AI assistant. Here to make your work easier by answering any questions on {{company_name}} University modules, assets, and calls available to you.
```

Example II:

```
Hello {{user_name}}!
Welcome to Seller Copilot! I’m your personalized AI assistant to help you prepare for calls, get answers to your questions, and streamline your workflows. Copilot provides tailored insights to help you improve your customer interactions and accelerate deal closures.
```

The Custom instructions setting allows you to define how Seller Copilot should respond when engaging with your sellers. You can adjust the tone, conciseness, and specify company terminologies for more relevant and accurate answers.

- Character limit : 10,000 characters
- Insert variables : You can use the following variable: username, user email, and company name.
- Reset to default : Click to restore custom instructions to its original setting (empty).

This setting ensures Seller Copilot aligns with your organization's needs and preferences. Key aspects of custom instructions include:

- Define the persona : Admins can specify the persona Seller Copilot should adopt, ensuring a consistent and relatable interaction style that matches company culture and communication style.
- Set Dos and Don'ts : Admins can define guidelines for tone, language, and interaction protocols to guide Seller Copilot's behavior.
- Provide additional context : Admins can add company-specific information, industry terms, or other relevant details to improve response accuracy and context.
- Enhance response relevance : Custom instructions ensure responses are tailored to your organization’s workflows and requirements.
- Dynamic adaptation : Instructions can be updated as needed, allowing Seller Copilot to adapt to evolving organizational needs and policies.

For best practices, see Best practices for Seller Copilot custom instructions.

Example I:

```
When responding, please keep the tone friendly and professional. Use concise language and always include company-specific terms like [company-specific term 1] and [company-specific term 2] to ensure the response is relevant to our processes.
```

See the following for an example of detailed custom instructions:

```
# ROLE & OBJECTIVE
You are an expert sales assistant for Mindtickle. Your primary goal is to help sales representatives with immediate sales tasks, customer engagements, and communications. 

# TONE & STYLE
- Professional and Approachable: Speak as a knowledgeable colleague. Be friendly but maintain a crisp, corporate standard.
- Concise: Provide short, direct responses. Do not use unnecessary filler words or generic introductions.
- Action-Oriented: Summarize answers in a few sentences and always conclude with key action points or next steps. Offer clear recommendations when presenting multiple options.

# COMPANY TERMINOLOGY
Strictly adhere to the following terminology rules:
- Company Name: Always spell "Mindtickle" as one word with a lowercase "t".
- Acronyms: Use "DSR" (Digital Sales Rooms), "ILT" (Instructor-led training), and "CRM" (Customer Relationship Management). Do not expand them.
- Roles: Use "sales rep" (Never "sales representative").
- Activities: Use "sales engagements" (Never "sales tasks").
- Metrics: Use "KPIs" (Never "performance measures").

# GUARDRAILS & RESTRICTIONS
- Prioritize sales enablement and customer communication queries over general trivia or non-sales inquiries.
- Never engage with queries containing explicit, inappropriate, or harmful language. Instead, politely reply: "Please keep queries professional and relevant to your sales engagements."
```

Use the Audience setting to control who can access Seller Copilot during the pilot phase. Keep your target audience stable during this phase to ensure user feedback is consistent and easy to evaluate.

Set the Audience configuration to your designated rollout group. Decide your rollout path upfront so the eventual transition to the entire organization is straightforward.Choose a group (e.g., group for a specific sales team or group based on role) that you want to grant access to Seller Copilot. Best practice: Use the pilot as an "instruction-tuning window"

Configuring Custom instructions early is one of the fastest ways to maximize pilot value. Start with a lightweight set focused on:

- Tone: Professional, crisp.
- Structure: Direct answer → key points → next steps.
- Terminology: Official product/feature names and "use X, not Y" mappings.

This builds immediate trust with sellers. Capture terminology gaps and style preferences from these pilot users, update your Custom Instructions once or twice based on their feedback, and then use that improved version when you switch your Audience settings to Everyone for the global rollout.

Before expanding access globally, conduct lightweight evaluations to ensure organizational readiness:

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Managers and Reviewers > Team analytics:
The Command Center is a dedicated dashboard designed to help managers track their team’s training completion, coaching progress, call performance, Readiness Index, and view reports shared with them. The Command Center dashboard, available on the learning site homepage, consolidates all critical metrics into a single, easy-to-navigate interface — empowering managers to take timely and informed actions to elevate team performance.

Managers can also access the Command Center from the Mindtickle mobile app. For details, see this article.

Key features

- Assign training as a manager: From the Training summary widget, assign full series or specific modules to one or more team members on both the web and mobile app. Managers can assign content only for series where they have been added as collaborators by an admin.
- Priority training tracking : Monitor critical training programs defined by the admin, ensuring team activities align with organizational goals.
- Coaching progress monitoring : Track insights into coaching sessions, role plays, and actions taken, with the ability to send reminders and kudos.
- Call performance insights : Review detailed call performance data, with calls scoring less than 50% highlighted. Leave comments and take actions to improve call quality.
- Readiness Index insights : Get weekly calculations of team readiness, offering insights into competencies and skills, and compare current readiness scores with previous weeks.
- Shared reports : Access reports shared by the admin directly from the Command Center, with newly shared reports marked with a "new" tag for easy identification.
- Email digest : Receive a bi-weekly summary email from the Command Center, offering a snapshot of team performance over the past two weeks, including key metrics and highlights. For detail, see the “ Email digest ” section.

Benefits

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Managers and Reviewers > Team analytics > 1. Readiness Index:
The Readiness Index widget provides managers with a powerful view of sales or role readiness across their reporting structure. By aggregating scores, surfacing coaching opportunities, and identifying competency gaps, the widget helps managers make data-driven decisions to elevate performance.

Unlike other widgets that rely on real-time or daily data, the Readiness Index (RI) is calculated weekly. This provides a stable and strategic benchmark of how well team members are prepared across key competencies.

If there are more than 5 scores and competencies, the widget displays the top 5 and bottom 5. If there are 5 or fewer, the widget displays all of them.

Note:

- This widget is available only if Readiness Index is enabled and configured on your Mindtickle instance.
- While the Average RI and Competencies widgets aggregate data across your entire reporting hierarchy (including both direct and indirect reportees), the RI Scores widget evaluates performance based solely on your direct reportees.
- If there are more than 5 scores and competencies , the widget displays the top 5 and bottom 5. If there are 5 or fewer, the widget displays all of them.

The Readiness Index section provides:

1. RI scores
  - Displays the top and bottom performers on the team based on individual Readiness Index scores.
  - The widget evaluates individuals based solely on the manager’s direct reportees, highlighting the highest and lowest performing members among the immediate team.
  - Managers can click on individual names to open the learner scorecard and explore detailed insights.
2. Competencies
  - Highlights the top 5 and bottom 5 competencies across the team.
  - The widget evaluates competencies across the manager’s entire reporting hierarchy, including both direct and indirect reportees.
  - Helps managers identify skill gaps and prioritize enablement efforts accordingly.

Clicking View RI dashboard takes managers to the Readiness Index dashboard. From there, they can:

- Explore detailed learner scorecards

Data refresh and cadence

The Readiness Index is calculated and updated weekly, every Monday. If a recalculation is triggered manually (e.g., via a test configuration), the widget reflects the latest calculation date and compares against the prior cadence period selected (7, 15, 30, or 90 days).

Time filters and historical comparisons

Although the Readiness Index is calculated weekly, managers can use the time filters (Last 7, 15, 30, or 90 days) to compare how readiness has evolved over time. These comparisons help identify trends, such as improvements after training initiatives or declines following organizational changes.

The widget compares the current average score against the score from the equivalent past cadence (e.g., comparing this Monday’s score to last Monday’s). This enables a consistent week-over-week analysis.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Managers and Reviewers > Team analytics > 2. Training > 2.1 Assign training as a manager:
Managers can assign training content directly to their team members from the Command Center on both the web and the Mindtickle mobile app. Using the Assign Content option in the Training Summary widget, managers can assign full training series or individual modules, such as courses, quick updates, missions, assessments, and instructor-led trainings (ILTs).

Managers can assign content only from series where they have been added as collaborators by an admin. A new permission, Assign Content to Reportees, is included by default in the Manager role and works specifically with the series collaborator feature; the permission is listed as Assign Content via Learning Site when adding series collaborators. This means that once a manager is added as a collaborator to a series, they can assign content from that series. For details, see the Collaborator management article.

When content is assigned, team members receive notifications and can view their assignments in the Training section. Full series appear under Training → Series → Assigned, while individual modules appear under Training → Modules → Assigned. Completion progress is updated in real time and reflected back in the Command Center, allowing managers to track progress, completion percentages, and actionable insights for timely follow-ups.

This feature enables managers to provide timely, personalized learning to their teams, while admins maintain governance and oversight through collaborator-based access and the Assign Content to Reportees permission.

Steps to assign training content

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Managers and Reviewers > Team analytics > 2. Training > 2.1 Assign training as a manager:
1. Open the Command Center on the web or mobile app.
2. Navigate to the Training Summary widget on your dashboard. Click the Assign Content option.
3. The Assign training to panel opens, where you can select the team members to assign content to choose either a full series or specific modules .
4. In the Select team members dropdown menu, select one or more of your team members to assign the training content to. Alternatively, select the " Showing X team members " checkbox to select all of your team members at once.
5. In the Training tab, choose either a full series or specific modules (such as courses, quick updates, missions, assessments, ILTs) to assign.
6. Click the Email template tab to view a sample preview of the email that will be sent to learners. Note that this tab shows a generic preview; the actual email will include personalized data relevant to each learner. Note : If the manager assigns a series or module that the team member is already assigned, the Command Center email will still be sent, but the team member’s existing progress will remain unchanged. Your admins can customize the email templates from the admin site. For details, see this article .
7. Review the selection, then click Assign training to X team members and confirm by clicking Assign training to send notifications to the team members.
8. Track completion progress, percentages, and actionable insights directly in the Command Center.

This highlights time-sensitive or high-impact series (trainings) selected by the admin. Managers can monitor completion of up to five priority trainings as configured by the admin.

Note: Series marked as priority are visible only to managers via the dashboard. Learners do not see any “priority” tag on the series on their end. Admins or managers may need to communicate priority series separately to learners.

How admins can mark trainings as priority

Admins can designate up to five active series (trainings) as priority to highlight them for managers in the Command Center. These trainings typically reflect high-impact initiatives, such as product launches, process changes, or urgent upskilling needs.

To mark trainings as priority:

1. In the admin site sidebar, navigate to Account > Settings > Training > Priority training.
2. On the Priority training page, use the Select series dropdown menu to select up to 5 series (trainings) you want to mark as priority for learners.
3. Click Save changes once done.

The marked trainings will now appear under the Priority training widget in the manager’s Command Center. If needed, admins can update or remove priority trainings at any time by returning to the same Priority training tab.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Managers and Reviewers > Team analytics > 2. Training > 2.3 Required training:
This includes all series (trainings) marked as required by the admin, such as onboarding, compliance, or certifications series. These series are non-optional and must be completed by assigned team members. The widget shows how much of the team has completed required content and flags any drop in completion trends.

Required vs. Priority training

Required training refers to mandatory series (trainings) that learners must complete, marked by admins for compliance, onboarding, or certification. Completion is expected from all assigned learners and is often enforced with due dates.

Priority training, in contrast, is strategically important but not necessarily mandatory. It highlights series (trainings) that enablement or admin teams want to bring to the manager’s attention due to its urgency, business relevance, or high impact—without forcing formal completion.

These series are non-optional and must be completed by assigned team members. The widget shows how much of the team has completed required content and flags any drop in completion trends.

Required vs. Priority training

Required training refers to mandatory series (trainings) that learners must complete, marked by admins for compliance, onboarding, or certification. Completion is expected from all assigned learners and is often enforced with due dates.

Priority training, in contrast, is strategically important but not necessarily mandatory. It highlights series (trainings) that enablement or admin teams want to bring to the manager’s attention due to its urgency, business relevance, or high impact—without forcing formal completion.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Managers and Reviewers > Team analytics > 2. Training > 2.4 Overdue training:
Tracks required series (trainings) that are past their due dates. These represent the most urgent follow-up areas. The system automatically detects due dates and flags overdue modules so managers can quickly identify at-risk learners and take corrective action.

Training targets and status indicators

Mindtickle Team can define completion targets for series (trainings). Contact your CSM or Mindtickle Support to customize the thresholds from the backend to align with your organizational expectations. The default threshold is 80%, meaning a team is considered “on target” when at least 80% of members complete the assigned training.

Each widget uses clear status labels:

- Below target : Completion is below the defined threshold
- Above target : Target met, but full completion not yet reached
- Completed : All assigned learners have completed the training

Manager actions

Managers can take the following actions from within each training widget:

- Send kudos : Recognize individuals or teams meeting or exceeding targets
- Send reminders : Notify team members who are behind on training, encouraging them to complete it

Note: Managers cannot customize the reminder emails sent to learners from the command center.

The system supports bulk reminder functionality and provides a preview of the reminder email before sending. Separate templates are used for kudos and reminders, ensuring communication tone is appropriate.

Detailed training insights & actions

The Training section widgets support deeper dives into individual learner progress and more contextual actions while sending kudos or reminders:

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Managers and Reviewers > Team analytics > 3. Coaching:
The Coaching section gives managers visibility into their coaching responsibilities — specifically mission reviews and coaching sessions assigned to them. It helps managers stay accountable for delivering timely and consistent feedback, while also ensuring their teams receive the support needed to develop and improve.

Note: The Coaching section only displays data for a manager's direct reportees. Mission reviews or coaching sessions completed for learners who do not report to the manager will not appear here.

This widget is essential for answering key questions:

- Am I up to date with the coaching I’m expected to complete for my direct reportees?
- Are there assigned sessions or missions from my reportees I haven’t reviewed yet?
- How does my recent coaching activity for my team compare to expectations?

The coaching widget displays the number of completed mission reviews and coaching sessions for the manager's direct reportees, over the selected time filter (Last 7, 15, 30, or 90 days). These are compared against system-defined targets to show how the manager is progressing.

Targets and status indicators

Coaching targets represent the expected number of completed coaching actions—such as mission reviews or coaching sessions—within a given time frame (e.g., weekly or monthly). These targets help managers track whether they're consistently delivering feedback and support to their team.

Note: These targets are not editable from the UI. To adjust them to better align with your goals, cadence, and coaching philosophy, please contact your CSM or Mindtickle Support.

The Command Center uses the following status indicators to show progress against the defined coaching target:

- Below target : Fewer coaching actions completed than expected
- On target : Coaching delivery is meeting expectations
- Above target : More coaching actions completed than required

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Managers and Reviewers > Team analytics > 4. Calls:
The calls widget highlights team calls with scores below 50%, helping managers focus on critical reviews. Managers can:

- Play and review low-scoring calls
- Leave comments — counted as coaching moments

The Calls section offers visibility into two important areas related to call-based performance of the team:

1. Calls to review : Highlights team calls with scores below 50%, helping managers focus on critical calls requiring their review. Managers can play and review low-scoring calls. They can also leave comments, which are counted as coaching moments.
2. Upcoming meetings to review : A list of scheduled calls and meetings involving direct reports. These are the calls with potential opportunities to coach your team members. Managers can either discuss these calls in 1:1s with their team or join these calls to coach and assist team members.

Together, these give managers insight into how reps are performing in live interactions, and what’s coming up that may require attention or preparation.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Managers and Reviewers > Team analytics > 4. Calls > 4.1 Calls to review:
The Calls to review widget focuses on real customer or internal calls involving the manager’s direct reports. These calls are automatically scored by Mindtickle’s Call AI, and the widget filters out only those calls with a score below 50%, highlighting areas where the manager might need to step in.

Note: Only calls with scores below 50% are shown; this threshold cannot be adjusted.

Manager actions

- Play and listen to low-scoring calls directly from the widget
- Leave comments at specific timestamps, which are counted as coaching moments
- Provide structured feedback using coaching forms

Note: Any comment left by a manager — whether formal or informal — is counted as a coaching moment and contributes to the overall coaching metrics in the Summary > Coaching moments widget. However, informal comments may not affect the coaching progress bar in the Coaching widget.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Managers and Reviewers > Team analytics > 4. Calls > 4.2 Upcoming meetings to review:
The Upcoming meetings to review widget lists all upcoming calls or meetings involving the manager’s direct reports scheduled within the next 30 days. This gives managers a forward-looking view of team engagements and helps them:

- Prepare for important or high-stakes calls
- Shadow upcoming meetings as part of onboarding or coaching
- Identify reps with low engagement or call volume

Note: This 30-day window is fixed and does not change based on the time filter applied at the top of the dashboard.

Use cases for managers

- Coaching prep : Know when team members have high-stakes meetings and plan pre-call or post-call coaching.
- Performance tracking : Spot reps with too few upcoming engagements, which may indicate pipeline or scheduling gaps.
- Call review planning : If a manager notices a low-performing rep has an important call coming up, they can proactively listen in or plan to review the recording later.
