Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Coaching reports:
The coaching sessions learner reports (or coaching learner reports) provide detailed analytics on learners’ self-reviews for assigned coaching sessions, offering clear visibility into adherence, progress, and completion across teams.

Designed for senior leaders, managers, and admins, these reports support effective coaching practices by highlighting learner engagement, tracking self-review consistency, and identifying gaps in learner follow-through.

They enable admins and managers to monitor how consistently learners are completing their self-reviews as part of the coaching process. Overall, the reports reinforce a culture of accountability by delivering actionable insights into learner-driven coaching activity.

Key features

- Completion tracking : View how many self-reviews have been assigned and completed, and identify learners falling behind.
- Adherence monitoring : Track if self-reviews are completed regularly and on schedule.
- Role-based visibility : Managers, sales leaders, and admins can view data appropriate to their scope, from individuals to teams to the entire organization.
- Clear, accessible reports : Flat, easy-to-read reports make it simple to interpret key metrics and revisit specific past sessions with the help of filters.

Note: This article focuses on coaching learner reports available on the admin site, but the information also applies to manager-level coaching learner reports on the learning site, as both reports offer similar data and functionality.

Permissions and access

Access to learner self-review reports varies by role:

- Admins can view data for all learners across the organization.
- Sales leaders can view data for learners within their assigned teams.
- Managers can view data only for their own team’s learners — and only if they are invited as a reviewer.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Coaching reports > Individual learners tab > Page functionalities:
The following options are available on the Individual learners page:

SWITCH VIEWIn the upper right corner, toggle between All learners or Only direct reports.

FILTERSUse the filters at the top of the page to narrow down report data:

- Time period: View data for a selected time range. By default, it shows data from the past year based on when coaching sessions were assigned.
- Learner profile fields: Filter by one or more shared learner profile attributes.
- Coaching: Filter by the coaching session modules assigned to learners.
- More filters
  - Learner groups: Filter by one or more learner groups.
  - Learners: Filter by individual learners.
  - Session type: Filter by session type (single or multiple).

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Coaching reports > Individual learners tab > Table data:
The Individual learners table includes the following columns:

TABLE DATA

- Learners: Displays the names of all learners assigned to coaching sessions. Includes both admin-assigned and self-assigned modules.
- Coaching assigned: The total number of coaching sessions with self-review enabled for the learner.
- Review completed: The number of completed self-reviews out of the total assigned coaching sessions.
- Session adherence: The session adherence (in %) shows how closely a learner is following their expected self-review schedule over time. It helps measure whether learners are completing reviews at the intended cadence, rather than rushing or skipping them. It is calculated as follows: (Number of self-reviews completed) / (Number of self-reviews expected to be completed) x 100 The expected number of reviews is determined on a prorated basis, depending on the cadence set for each assigned coaching session. A legend at the top of the table helps interpret adherence levels.
- Last self-review: The date and time when the learner last completed a self-review.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle APIs > Introduction:
Mindtickle offers a comprehensive set of public REST APIs that allow you to interact programmatically with the platform to automate tasks, integrate with external systems, and manage data efficiently. Built on the OpenAPI Specification (OAS), formerly known as Swagger, these APIs provide a standardized, language-agnostic interface that enables developers to integrate with minimal setup.

This article covers the foundational concepts common across Mindtickle’s public REST APIs, including authentication methods, base URLs, rate limiting, and standard status codes. These standards apply to all Mindtickle APIs — such as the Training Content, User Management, and Asset Hub APIs — with the exception of the reporting APIs.

For any questions or assistance, please contact Mindtickle Support.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle APIs > Introduction > Rate limits > Handling rate limits:
When a limit is reached, the API responds with:

- Status code: 429 Too Many Requests
- Header: Retry-After (indicating how many seconds to wait before retrying)

Best practice: We strongly recommend implementing an exponential backoff strategy. If a request fails with a 429 error, pause your script for the duration specified in the header (or a default wait time) before retrying.

Mindtickle APIs use standard HTTP status codes to indicate request outcomes. Where applicable, response bodies also include specific error descriptions to provide further context on failures.

| Code | Status | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 200 | OK | The request was successful. |
| 400 | Bad Request | The request was invalid or missing required parameters. |
| 401 | Unauthorized | Authentication failed. The token is missing, invalid, or expired. |
| 403 | Forbidden | You do not have permission to access the requested resource. |
| 404 | Not Found | The requested resource or endpoint does not exist. |
| 429 | Too Many Requests | Rate limit exceeded. Retry after a delay. |
| 500 | Internal Server Error | An unexpected error occurred on the server side. |

Benefits

Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Release Notes > New features > 4 new APIs for Asset Hub:
This release introduces 4 new Asset Hub Content APIs that enable secure, programmatic access to Asset Hub content, including hubs, assets, asset details, and associated media or transcripts.

These APIs are designed to make it easier for enterprise customers and partners to consume and integrate Mindtickle content into their own systems and workflows.

These read-only APIs are especially useful for integration developers who need to pull content into CRMs, LMSs, or knowledge platforms, as well as for admins looking to enable content discovery and distribution outside of the Mindtickle UI.

Key features

- Secure : All media and transcript URLs are time-bound and signed.
- Paginated : Supports skip and limit for scalable data retrieval.
- Filterable : Filter by IDs or sharing type (where applicable).
- Sortable : Sort responses by metadata like title, created date, etc.
- Error handling : Standardized error codes: 400, 403, 404, 429, 500 .

Note: These APIs are read-only. Uploading, editing, or deleting content via API is not supported in this release.

The following 4 public APIs are now available:

1. List all active hubs

- Method: POST /api/assethub/v1/hubs
- Description: Fetches a paginated list of all active hubs.
- Features: Optional filtering by hub IDs, pagination, and sorting.

2. List all published assets in a hub

- Method: POST /api/assethub/v1/hub/{hub_id}/assets
- Description: Fetches all published assets within a specific hub.
- Features: Filter by asset ID and sharing type, supports pagination and sorting.

3. Get details of an asset

- Method: POST /api/assethub/v1/asset/{asset_id}
- Description: Retrieves detailed metadata and attributes for a specific asset.

4. Get media and transcript for an asset

Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Release Notes > New features > New API to get learning object details by module:
This release brings a new API to help developers and integration partners retrieve detailed learning object (LO) data for a specific module.

Endpoint: GET /api/v2/entity/<module_id>/learning_objects

This API is designed for developers, integration partners, and AI/data teams who need programmatic access to module-level learning content. Whether you're powering content analytics, integrating Mindtickle modules into another platform, or training AI systems, this new endpoint gives you clean, structured, and secure access to module contents—without manual work or data exports. It enables seamless integration, improves developer experience, and supports AI-driven analysis at scale — positioning Mindtickle as an API-first, extensible platform.

Key features

- Fetch learning objects by module ID
- Returns structured content:
  - Content with media and transcription

Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Release Notes > Enhancements > Asset Hub enhancements:
This release brings three key enhancements to improve the user experience and functionality of Mindtickle’s Asset Hub. These updates help streamline workflows, improve asset relevance, and simplify content management for both users and admins.

1. Filter assets by status on Assets page: New Status filter on the Assets page allows admins to quickly find and manage assets based on status: All (default), Draft, Expired, Expiring Soon, and Published.
2. Ability to share customized assets via Outlook add-in: Reps can share their own customized assets when using Mindtickle’s add-in for Microsoft Outlook.
3. Enhancement for recommended assets in Salesforce: The Recommended assets section in Salesforce will now appear only when admins have set display rules and at least one asset matches those rules, ensuring reps see only relevant, curated content.

Continue reading for details on each enhancement.

1. Filter assets by status on Assets page

To support better content governance, we have introduced the Status filter for admins on the Assets section > Assets page. This makes it easier for admins to locate, track, and manage content based on its lifecycle stage.

Admins can now filter active assets by the following statuses:

- All (default)
- Draft
- Expired
- Expiring Soon
- Published

For more information, see Assets page (admins).

2. Share customized assets via Outlook add-in

Reps can now share their own customized assets when using Mindtickle’s add-in for Microsoft Outlook. While adding assets to an email, they can choose from both admin-enabled assets and rep-created customized assets.

Assets enabled for external sharing by admins appear under the Assets tab, while customized assets created by the rep appear under the My assets tab in the asset selection workflow.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Release Notes > Enhancements > Content Center sync: Email notifications for synced files deleted at source:
This enhancement introduces email notifications for admins when Content Center synced files, which are used in modules and assets, are deleted from their source locations, like Google shared drive, Microsoft SharePoint, and Adobe Experience Manager (AEM). The email includes direct links to affected files, enabling quick resolution of broken references and helping maintain content integrity by prompting timely remediation of deleted source files.

Note: If a synced file is deleted at the source but is actively used in modules or assets, it is retained in Content Center and an email notification is sent to admins.

Files not used anywhere are automatically removed from Content Center when deleted at the source.

Previously, there was no automated alert when a synced source file was removed. This created visibility gaps that allowed:

- Broken references to persist in Content Center modules
- Obsolete or deprecated documents to remain in use
- Potential security and compliance risks due to outdated content

With this release, Content Center:

- Detects deletion of synced files, which are used in modules and assets, in their source location: Google shared drive, SharePoint, and AEM
- Sends email notifications to admins, which includes names and direct links to the referencing Content Center files

This ensures timely awareness and remediation when actively referenced files are removed at the source level — helping maintain content integrity, reduce broken links, and support better compliance.

For more information, see View and manage synced content, sync status, and logs in Content Center.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle APIs > Asset Hub APIs:
The Asset Hub content APIs enable you to programmatically discover and retrieve content from your organization's Asset Hubs. Use these endpoints to list active hubs and published assets, or access granular details for specific items, including metadata, media files, and transcripts.

Key capabilities include:

- Hub & asset discovery: Retrieve paginated lists of all active hubs and the published assets contained within them.
- Asset details: Access comprehensive metadata and attributes for specific assets to ensure accurate display in third-party applications.
- Media & transcript retrieval: Securely fetch signed URLs for raw content files, along with associated thumbnails and text transcripts.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Digital Sales Rooms:
The Visits report provides insights into room visitor behavior and content engagement within rooms. It contains the number of visitors, total visits, content views, and the time spent on each content item. The Visits report provides insights into how visitors interact with rooms and engage with the shared content.

Note: The email link to download the .CSV file is active for 7 days from the report generation date.

To export the room visits report,

1. Sign in to the learning site.
2. Click Rooms in the left navigation bar and then click on Rooms . The Rooms page is displayed.
3. Click on a room to open. The room opens.
4. Click the More icon and click Export Visits to export the room visits report. A message displays that the system emails the report when the data is ready. Note: The report's file name includes the date and time of report generation.

The Visits report contains the following information:

- Contact Email: The email address of the visitor.
- Contact Name: The name of the visitor.
- Contact Phone: The visitor's phone number.
- Contact Job Title: The job title of the visitor.
- Company: The visitor’s company name.
- City: The city of the visitor.
- Country: The country of the visitor.
- Device: The room visitor’s device information, whether mobile or web.
- Room Owner: The name of the room owner.
- Content Name: The name of the content file in the room.
- Content Visited At (UTC): The time when the content was viewed in the room.
- Time Spent (Seconds): The time spent on the content in the room.
- Downloaded At (UTC): The content download time from the room.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Mobile App:
The Command Center is a dedicated dashboard designed to help managers track their team’s training completion, coaching progress, call performance, and Readiness Index. Available on the Mindtickle mobile app homepage, Command Center consolidates all critical metrics into a single, easy-to-navigate interface — empowering managers to take timely and informed actions on the go to elevate team performance.

Managers can also access the Command Center on the web (desktop). For details, see this article.

Key features

- Assign training as a manager: From the Training summary widget, assign full series or specific modules to one or more team members on both the web and mobile app. Managers can assign content only for series where they have been added as collaborators by an admin.
- Priority training tracking: Monitor important training programs defined by admins to ensure alignment with business goals.
- Coaching progress monitoring: View coaching activities, role plays, and actions taken. Send reminders or kudos to multiple learners.
- Call performance insights: Access key call performance data, with calls scoring below 50% highlighted.
- Readiness Index insights: See weekly team readiness scores, compare them over time, and understand skill gaps .
- Email digest : Receive a bi-weekly summary email from the Command Center, offering a snapshot of team performance over the past two weeks, including key metrics and highlights. For detail, see this article.

Benefits

- On-the-go visibility: Get a quick overview of team performance anytime, anywhere.
- Focused management: Access essential insights across training, coaching, calls, and readiness in a single mobile view.
- Efficient follow-up: Take action quickly by sending bulk reminders or kudos with just a few taps.
- Better decisions: Leverage data from performance metrics to guide team development.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Mobile App > Dashboard overview:
The Command Center dashboard is designed to provide managers with a single, consolidated view of all key enablement metrics relevant to their direct reports. Instead of navigating across multiple pages or generating complex reports, managers can now access real-time data and take action directly from one place.

This dashboard is composed of several interactive widgets, also referred to as KPI cards, that each represent a core area of enablement responsibility. These cards include high-level metrics and visual cues (like status indicators and progress bars) to help managers quickly interpret their team’s status in each area.

Each KPI card is also tappable, allowing managers to drill down into detailed insights, view lists of affected team members, and take relevant actions such as sending reminders or reviewing pending coaching items.

Main components

Here’s a breakdown of each section in the Command Center dashboard. Use the Jump to button to quickly navigate between sections.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Mobile App > Dashboard overview:
- Summary widgets Located at the top of each section (Training, Coaching, Calls, and Readiness Index), the Summary widget gives managers a high-level snapshot of how their team is performing. It helps managers identify areas that need attention at a glance. From the Training summary widget, managers can also assign full series or specific modules to one or more team members on both the web and mobile app. For details, see the "Assign training as a manager" section.
- Training Widgets in this section show how the manager’s team is performing in three training categories:
  - Priority : Time-sensitive or high-impact series highlighted by the admin.
  - Required : Series marked as mandatory by the admin.
  - Overdue : Required series that have passed their due dates.
- Coaching Shows managers their assigned mission reviews and coaching sessions , helping them stay accountable for delivering timely, consistent feedback and supporting team development.
- Calls
  - Team recordings : Flags team calls with scores below 50% for follow-up. Managers can review, comment, and provide coaching—each comment counts as a coaching moment.
  - Upcoming meetings : Lists scheduled calls for direct reports, helping managers plan for coaching opportunities or provide real-time support.
- Readiness Index Provides a comprehensive view of sales or role readiness. Depending on the widget, insights are surfaced for either a manager's direct reportees or their entire reporting hierarchy (including both direct and indirect reports). This data helps managers identify individual coaching needs and broader competency gaps to drive performance.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Mobile App > 2. Training > 2.1 Assign training as a manager:
Managers can assign training content directly to their team members from the Command Center on both the web and the Mindtickle mobile app. Using the Assign Content option in the Training Summary widget, managers can assign full training series or individual modules, such as courses, quick updates, missions, assessments, and instructor-led trainings (ILTs).

Managers can assign content only from series where they have been added as collaborators by an admin. A new permission, Assign Content to Reportees, is included by default in the Manager role and works specifically with the series collaborator feature; the permission is listed as Assign Content via Learning Site when adding series collaborators. This means that once a manager is added as a collaborator to a series, they can assign content from that series. For details, see the Collaborator management article.

When content is assigned, team members receive notifications and can view their assignments in the Training section. Full series appear under Training → Series → Assigned, while individual modules appear under Training → Modules → Assigned. Completion progress is updated in real time and reflected back in the Command Center, allowing managers to track progress, completion percentages, and actionable insights for timely follow-ups.

This feature enables managers to provide timely, personalized learning to their teams, while admins maintain governance and oversight through collaborator-based access and the Assign Content to Reportees permission.

Steps to assign training content

1. Open the Command Center on the web or mobile app.
2. Navigate to the Training Summary widget on your dashboard. Click the Assign Content option.
3. The Assign training to panel opens, where you can select the team members to assign content to choose either a full series or specific modules .

5. In the Training tab, choose either a full series or specific modules (such as courses, quick updates, missions, assessments, ILTs) to assign.
6. Click the Email template tab to view a sample preview of the email that will be sent to learners. Note that this tab shows a generic preview; the actual email will include personalized data relevant to each learner. Note : If the manager assigns a series or module that the team member is already assigned, the Command Center email will still be sent, but the team member’s existing progress will remain unchanged. Your admins can customize the email templates from the admin site. For details, see this article .
7. Review the selection, then click Assign training to X team members and confirm by clicking Assign training to send notifications to the team members.
8. Track completion progress, percentages, and actionable insights directly in the Command Center.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Mobile App > 2. Training > 2.3 Required training:
This includes all series (trainings) marked as required by the admin, such as onboarding, compliance, or certifications series. These series are non-optional and must be completed by assigned team members. The widget shows how much of the team has completed required content and flags any drop in completion trends.

Required vs. Priority training

Required training refers to mandatory series (trainings) that learners must complete, marked by admins for compliance, onboarding, or certification. Completion is expected from all assigned learners and is often enforced with due dates.

Priority training, in contrast, is strategically important but not necessarily mandatory. It highlights series (trainings) that enablement or admin teams want to bring to the manager’s attention due to its urgency, business relevance, or high impact—without forcing formal completion.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Mobile App > 2. Training > 2.4 Overdue training:
Tracks required series (trainings) that are past their due dates. These represent the most urgent follow-up areas. The system automatically detects due dates and flags overdue modules so managers can quickly identify at-risk learners and take corrective action.

Training targets and status indicators

Mindtickle Team can define completion targets for series (trainings). Contact your CSM or Mindtickle Support to customize the thresholds from the backend to align with your organizational expectations. The default threshold is 80%, meaning a team is considered “on target” when at least 80% of members complete the assigned training.

Each KPI card uses clear status labels:

- Below target : Completion is below the defined threshold
- Above target : Target met, but full completion not yet reached
- Completed : All assigned learners have completed the training

Manager actions

Managers can take the following actions from within each training widget:

- Send kudos : Recognize individuals or teams meeting or exceeding targets
- Send reminders : Nudge team members who are behind on training

Bulk actions are supported, and managers can preview emails before sending. Separate templates are used for kudos and reminders to keep communication tone appropriate.

Setting training targets

Your admins with the help of the Mindtickle Team can define completion targets for each training type. By default, the system uses an 80% threshold, meaning a team is considered “on target” when at least 80% of members have completed the assigned training. This helps managers assess overall progress—even if a few individuals are behind.

Note: These targets are not editable from the UI. To adjust them to better align with organizational expectations, please contact your CSM or Mindtickle Support.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Mobile App > 3. Coaching:
The Coaching section gives managers visibility into their coaching responsibilities — specifically mission reviews and coaching sessions assigned to them. It helps managers stay accountable for delivering timely and consistent feedback, while also ensuring their teams receive the support needed to develop and improve.

This widget is essential for answering key questions:

- Am I up to date with the coaching I’m expected to complete?
- Are there assigned sessions or missions I haven’t reviewed yet?
- How does my recent coaching activity compare to expectations?

The coaching widget displays the number of completed mission reviews and coaching sessions over the selected time filter (Last 7, 15, 30, or 90 days). These are compared against system-defined targets to show how the manager is progressing.

Targets and status indicators

Coaching targets represent the expected number of completed coaching actions (mission reviews or coaching sessions) within a given time frame. These targets help managers track whether they're consistently delivering feedback and support to their team.

Note: These targets are not editable from the UI. To adjust them to better align with your goals, cadence, and coaching philosophy, please contact your CSM or Mindtickle Support.

The Command Center uses the following status indicators to show progress against the defined coaching target:

- Below target : Fewer coaching actions completed than expected
- On target : Coaching delivery is meeting expectations
- Above target : More coaching actions completed than required

These indicators give managers a quick sense of how well they’re meeting their enablement responsibilities and where additional focus may be needed.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Mobile App > 4. Calls:
The calls widget highlights team calls with scores below 50%, helping managers focus on critical reviews. Managers can:

- Play and review low-scoring calls
- Leave comments — counted as coaching moments

The Calls section offers visibility into two important areas related to call-based performance of the team:

1. Team recordings : Highlights team calls with scores below 50%, helping managers focus on critical calls requiring their review. Managers can play and review low-scoring calls. They can also leave comments, which are counted as coaching moments.
2. Upcoming meetings : A list of scheduled calls and meetings involving direct reports. These are the calls with potential opportunities to coach your team members. Managers can either discuss these calls in 1:1s with their team or join these calls to coach and assist team members.

Together, these give managers insight into how reps are performing in live interactions, and what’s coming up that may require attention or preparation.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Mobile App > 4. Calls > 4.1 Team recordings:
The Team recordings widget focuses on real customer or internal calls involving the manager’s direct reports. These calls are automatically scored by Mindtickle’s Call AI, and the widget filters out only those calls with a score below 50%, highlighting areas where the manager might need to step in.

Note: Only calls with scores below 50% are shown; this threshold cannot be adjusted.

Manager actions

- Play and listen to low-scoring calls directly from the widget
- Leave comments at specific timestamps, which are counted as coaching moments
- Provide structured feedback using coaching forms

Note: Any comment left by a manager — whether formal or informal — is counted as a coaching moment and contributes to the overall coaching metrics in the Coaching moments summary widget. However, informal comments may not affect the coaching progress bar in the Coaching widget.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Mobile App > 4. Calls > 4.2 Upcoming meetings:
The Upcoming meetings widget lists all upcoming calls or meetings involving the manager’s direct reports scheduled within the next 30 days. This gives managers a forward-looking view of team engagements and helps them:

- Prepare for important or high-stakes calls
- Shadow upcoming meetings as part of onboarding or coaching
- Identify reps with low engagement or call volume

Note: This 30-day window is fixed and does not change based on the time filter applied at the top of the dashboard.

- Coaching prep : Know when team members have high-stakes meetings and plan pre-call or post-call coaching.
- Performance tracking : Spot reps with too few upcoming engagements, which may indicate pipeline or scheduling gaps.
- Call review planning : If a manager notices a low-performing rep has an important call coming up, they can proactively listen in or plan to review the recording later.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Mobile App > 5. Readiness Index:
The Readiness index widget gives managers a powerful view into their team’s overall sales or role readiness. This widget aggregates team-level scores, surfaces coaching opportunities, and identifies competency gaps — helping managers make data-driven decisions to elevate performance.

Unlike other widgets that rely on real-time or daily data, the Readiness Index (RI) is calculated weekly, providing a stable and strategic benchmark of how well team members are prepared across key competencies.

Note:

- This widget is available only if Readiness Index is enabled and configured on your Mindtickle instance.
- While the Average RI and Competencies widgets aggregate data across your entire reporting hierarchy (including both direct and indirect reportees), the RI Scores widget evaluates performance based solely on your direct reportees.
- If there are more than 5 scores and competencies, the widget displays the top 5 and bottom 5. If there are 5 or fewer, the widget displays all of them.

The Readiness Index section provides:

1. RI scores
  - Displays the top and bottom performers on the team based on individual Readiness Index scores.
  - The widget evaluates individuals based solely on the manager’s direct reportees, highlighting the highest and lowest performing members among the immediate team.
  - Managers can tap on individual names to open the learner scorecard and explore detailed insights.
2. Competencies
  - Highlights the top 5 and bottom 5 competencies across the team.
  - The widget evaluates competencies across the manager’s entire reporting hierarchy, including both direct and indirect reportees.
  - Helps managers identify skill gaps and prioritize enablement efforts accordingly.

Data refresh and cadence

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Mobile App > 5. Readiness Index:
The Readiness Index is calculated and updated weekly, every Monday. If a recalculation is triggered manually (e.g., via a test configuration), the widget reflects the latest calculation date and compares against the prior cadence period selected (7, 15, 30, or 90 days).

Time filters and historical comparisons

Although the Readiness Index is calculated weekly, managers can use the time filters (Last 7, 15, 30, or 90 days) to compare how readiness has evolved over time. These comparisons help identify trends, such as improvements after training initiatives or declines following organizational changes.

The widget compares the current average score against the score from the equivalent past cadence (e.g., comparing this Monday’s score to last Monday’s). This enables a consistent week-over-week analysis.

- No hierarchy support : Managers can view data only for their direct reports. Indirect reports (i.e., those who report to your direct reports) are not included.
- Features not supported on mobile : The following features are currently unavailable on mobile but are supported in Command Center on the web:
  - The “ Reports shared with me ” widget
  - Feature page links in widgets: “See all team recordings” in the Calls widget (opens the Call AI Recordings tab) and “View RI dashboard” in the Readiness Index widget (opens the Readiness Index dashboard)
  - Quick action icons to send reminders or kudos to individual learners (you can still send them to multiple or all learners via checkboxes)

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Digital Sales Rooms > Prerequisites:
The prerequisites to view the reportees’ rooms in DSR are,

- Admins must create a new relationship field on the learning site or select an existing one, such as Manager, for mapping.
- After creating or selecting a relationship field, contact Mindtickle Support to map the field.

Note: If the relationship field changes, notify the support team so they can map the new field. This ensures that the system displays the reportees’ rooms correctly in DSR.

- To enable this feature for DSR managers and admins, assign the Manager role to them .
- Ensure DSR users (reportees) select their manager on the User profile page to ensure managers have access to the reportees' rooms.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Digital Sales Rooms > Manage reportees' rooms:
Managers can view and edit the rooms of their reportees in the Digital Sales Rooms page. They can also view the rooms of their direct reports and the users who report to their direct reports.

To manage the reportees' rooms,

1. Sign in to the admin site .
2. Click Rooms in the left navigation bar and then click Rooms .

The Rooms page is displayed. The Rooms drop-down displays the Rooms rolling up to me option by default.

The rooms created by you and your reportees are displayed. You can also view the rooms of users who report to your reportees.

Note:

- Managers with edit permissions can view and edit the reportees' rooms in the Rooms > Rooms > Deals & Contacts tab. For more information on DSR permissions, see Permissions .
- They can also share files directly from Asset Hub to the reportees room.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Release Notes > New features > Edit asset content using Google Docs, Slides, and Sheets (beta):
This release introduces a new Asset Hub–Google Workspace integration that allows sales reps to customize and edit marketing-approved assets directly in Google Docs, Google Slides, and Google Sheets without leaving Mindtickle.

Through the integration, the Edit content feature gives sales reps the flexibility to personalize marketing-approved assets for specific client needs or sales scenarios, helping them deliver more relevant, impactful presentations and documents. A copy of the asset is created in the rep’s hub, ensuring the source file remains unchanged. Edits happen natively in Google Workspace, helping preserve formatting and streamlining the customization process for organizations that primarily work in Google Workspace. Already available for Microsoft Office for the web (PowerPoint, Word, and Excel), this capability is now extended to Google Workspace. If your organization uses both Microsoft and Google, reps can choose their preferred editing option.

Key features

- Admins have complete control and decide which assets are editable.
- Edit PDF, Doc, XLS, and PPT files directly in Mindtickle using Google Workspace (Docs, Sheets, and Slides).
- Personalize for clients by adding logos, modifying text, adjusting formatting, or reordering slides/pages.
- Changes made in Google Workspace are saved back to Mindtickle in real time.
- A copy of the original asset is created for editing, leaving the original intact.
- Track and share customized assets from the rep’s personal hub.

Benefits

- Improved efficiency : Edit assets in Google Workspace without downloading or re-uploading files.
- Flexibility : Reps can use the platform (Google or Microsoft) that their team prefers.
- Relevance : Tailor content to client-specific needs and boost sales conversations.
- Integrity maintained : Original marketing-approved assets remain unchanged.

Notes

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Release Notes > New features > Edit asset content using Google Docs, Slides, and Sheets (beta):
- This feature is in beta and not enabled by default. Please contact your CSM or Mindtickle Support to enable it for your Mindtickle instance.
- A valid Google Workspace account is required to edit assets.
- Supported file types : You can edit assets that are in PDF, Microsoft Office file formats (.doc, .docx, .xls, .xlsx, .ppt, .pptx), or Google Workspace formats (Docs, Sheets, Slides). Other file types are not supported.
- File size limits apply as per Google Workspace restrictions. You cannot edit assets in non-Google formats that are larger than 100MB (e.g., PPTX files).
- All changes to the customized asset file are saved directly in your connected Google Drive and synced with Mindtickle.
- Reps can edit only those assets for which admins have enabled the following properties:
  - Usage = External (asset approved for external sharing)
  - Allow customized asset creation → Edit content = enabled

For more information, see Edit asset content using Google Docs, Slides, and Sheets (beta).

Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Release Notes > Enhancements > Configure "Allow customized asset creation" property: For SharePoint/AEM content sync and bulk asset creation:
Until now, the Allow customized asset creation property could not be set for external syncs or bulk asset creation. With this release, admins gain two new ways to configure this property:

1. Asset metadata sync from Microsoft SharePoint and Adobe Experience Manager (AEM)
2. Creating bulk assets from synced files via Excel upload

This enhancement allows admins to manage asset customization governance directly from external systems (SharePoint, AEM) or while creating assets in bulk from synced files via Excel.

1. Asset metadata sync from SharePoint & AEM

- The metadata mapping sheet now includes 4 new rows to define customization options:
  - allowMixAndMatch = TRUE → Users can mix and match slides from this asset when creating customized assets.
  - allowMixAndMatch = FALSE → Users cannot mix and match slides from this asset.
  - allowEditingContent = TRUE → Users can edit the asset content when creating customized assets, through Microsoft Office for the web (PowerPoint, Word, and Excel) or Google Workspace (Slides, Docs, and Sheets).
  - allowEditingContent = FALSE → Users cannot edit the asset content.

- Once this property is synced:
  - It becomes read-only inside Mindtickle (as with other synced asset properties).
  - Any changes to the properties must be made in the source (SharePoint or AEM).
  - Synced values automatically populate for assets during creation or update; otherwise, the default is No .

2. Creating bulk assets from synced files via Excel upload

When creating multiple assets by selecting files synced from SharePoint, AEM, or Google Drive, admins can now configure customization options directly in the Excel sheet using the following values:

Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Release Notes > Enhancements > Seller Copilot is now available in Salesforce:
We’re excited to bring Seller Copilot, Mindtickle’s chat-based AI assistant, directly into Salesforce.

Already available on the web, Mindtickle mobile app, and through APIs, Seller Copilot can now be launched inside Salesforce page layouts, including standard objects like Opportunities, Accounts, Leads, and Contacts, as well as custom objects. This means sales reps can access real-time insights, instant answers, and call prep tools without leaving their CRM, reducing context switching and driving productivity.

What is Seller Copilot?

Seller Copilot is a chat-based AI assistant that streamlines sales workflows and helps sales reps and managers prepare for and follow up on customer interactions.

In Salesforce, Copilot appears as an embedded Lightning Web Component. Just type your question or pick from suggested prompts — Copilot instantly responds with tailored, context-aware answers powered by Mindtickle.

Each session is personalized, automatically authenticated, and linked to the logged-in Salesforce user.

Key features

- Embedded in Salesforce : Drag and drop the Seller Copilot component into any standard or custom object page layout (for example, Opportunities, Accounts, Leads, or Contacts) using Lightning App Builder.
- Call preparation : Get summaries, insights, and recommended next steps before customer conversations.
- Post-call follow-up : See automatic summaries, key moments, and action items from recorded calls.
- Instant answers : Ask about training content, product details, or processes; Copilot replies in real time.
- Seamless authentication : Uses the existing AppExchange package setup; no extra logins required.
- Always up to date : Any enhancements made to Copilot on the Mindtickle platform automatically apply inside Salesforce.
- Configurable placement : Salesforce Admins can place Copilot wherever it fits best on page layouts.

Benefits

Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Release Notes > Enhancements > Command Center for managers is now GA:
Following a beta release on the web in June and on the Mindtickle app in July, the Command Center for managers is now generally available (GA) for all users across web and mobile platforms.

Designed for sales and frontline managers, the Command Center centralizes key performance insights in one place, helping managers work more efficiently and coach more effectively.

With this GA release, we've also introduced layout improvements and training widget enhancements that significantly improve usability and actionability.

What is the Command Center?

Located on the learning site homepage, the Command Center offers managers a consolidated view of their team’s:

- Training completion
- Coaching progress
- Call performance
- Readiness Index scores
- Shared reports

It empowers managers to streamline daily activities and make more informed, data-driven coaching decisions.

New in this release

1. Unified and consistent layout (web & mobile)

To ensure a consistent experience across platforms, the Command Center layout has been restructured:

- The Summary section has been removed. Each insight (e.g., Readiness Index, Training, Coaching, Calls, Reports) now appears in its own dedicated row, making each section easier to focus on and navigate.
- The Reports shared with me section now appears at the bottom of the page for a cleaner layout.

2. Enhanced training insights & actions

The Training section now supports deeper dives into individual learner progress and more contextual actions:

Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Release Notes > Enhancements > Module-level Lifeline settings for quick updates:
Quick updates now give admins more flexibility in how gamification is applied. With this release, you can manage the Lifelines feature at the module level instead of relying on a single site-wide setting. This ensures more control, better alignment with learning goals, and a consistent configuration experience with courses.

Admins can now configure the Lifelines in questions setting at the individual quick update module level:

- A new toggle has been added under the Gamification tab in quick update settings, where you can further configure the total number of Lifelines by default.
- Admins can enable or disable Lifelines per module, offering greater flexibility.
- A new site-level default controls whether Lifelines are ON or OFF when a quick update is created, which can be overridden at the module level.
- The edit experience is consistent with courses, making configuration more intuitive.

Benefits

- Granular control : Apply gamification where it’s most useful.
- Tailored learner experience : Use Lifelines in practice modules but disable them for high-stakes assessments.
- Consistency : Aligns quick update settings with courses for a smoother admin experience.

Impacted personas

- Admins : Gain fine-grained control over gamification.
- Learners : See Lifelines only when relevant to the module.

Previously, Lifelines for quick updates were managed by a single site-wide setting, which applied the same configuration across all modules.

For more information, see Configure quick update settings.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Release Notes > Enhancements > Enhanced Trending widget with configurable filters:
The Trending widget available for learning site homepages and series overview pages has been enhanced into a dynamic, configurable widget. Admins can now decide what content to surface by applying filters for module relevance (e.g., mandatory, optional) and learner completion status (e.g., completed, in progress, not started). The widget is available in the Series section in the widgets panel.

Previously, the Trending widget was static. It displayed only the most-viewed modules in the past 30 days, with no admin control over what surfaced. Since only one widget could be added, admins could not highlight different categories of popular content (e.g., mandatory vs. optional training).

Key improvements

- Multiple widgets : Add up to five Trending widgets per homepage or series overview page (previously limited to one).
- Custom titles : Rename each widget to match its purpose (e.g., Trending Mandatory Training, Popular Optional Courses).
- Content filters : Control what each widget displays by setting filters by:
  - Module relevance: Required, Optional, and None (No module relevance)
  - Completion status: Not Started, In Progress, and Completed
- Inline editing : Modify a widget’s title and filters anytime via the edit icon on the widget.
- Clearer limits : The info icon has been updated to explain the 5-widget maximum.

Benefits

- Greater admin control : Curate the homepage with targeted, relevant content.
- Enhanced relevance : Learners see content tailored to their needs, not just forced compliance modules.
- More flexibility : Use multiple widgets to highlight different content categories side by side.
- Improved engagement : Learners discover and interact with more relevant training materials.

For more information, see Add dynamic widgets to learning site homepages and Create and edit overview pages.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Series > Assigned series:
Learners can skip individual or multiple Optional modules in a sequence in the Assigned series.

To skip an optional module in an Assigned series,

1. Sign in to the Mindtickle learning site.
2. Under Training , click Series in the left navigation bar. The Series page opens, and the system displays the All series tab by default.
3. Click the Assigned series tab and select a series. For example, Acme Training. The series opens and displays the available modules. You can view the relevance of the modules in the series, whether Required or Optional .
4. Click on an Optional module. For example, Sales Introduction. The Skip optional module? pop-up is displayed. The Note displays the number of optional modules that the learner is about to skip.
5. Click Skip . The system navigates you to the next Required or Unmarked module in the series.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Asset Hub:
Mindtickle’s Asset Hub integration with Google Workspace allows sales reps to customize and edit the content of assets directly in Google Docs, Google Slides, and Google Sheets. This means reps can make changes to the content of asset pages, like add a customer logo, change the title, or make any other content adjustments as needed. Reps can use this functionality while accessing editable assets on the learning site, without needing to download files or switch between applications.

Through the integration, the Edit content feature gives sales reps the flexibility to personalize marketing-approved assets for specific client needs or sales scenarios, helping them deliver more relevant, impactful presentations and documents. A copy of the asset is created in the rep’s hub, ensuring the source file remains unchanged. Edits happen natively in Google Workspace, helping preserve formatting and streamlining the customization process for organizations that primarily work in Google Workspace.

- Feature availability: This feature is in beta and is not enabled by default. To enable it for your Mindtickle instance, contact your CSM or Mindtickle Support .
- Account requirement: You must have a valid Google Workspace account to use this feature.
- Supported file types: You can edit assets that are in Microsoft Office file formats ( .doc , .docx , .xls , .xlsx , .ppt , .pptx ) or Google Workspace formats (Docs, Sheets, Slides). Other file types are not supported.
- File storage: All changes to the customized asset file are saved directly in your connected Google Drive and synced with Mindtickle.

For information on editing assets using Microsoft Office for the web (PowerPoint, Word, and Excel), see this article.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Asset Hub > Google Drive permissions:
To enable the editing of assets using Google Workspace, admins must contact Mindtickle Support to configure the level of access Mindtickle is granted to a user's Google Drive. This feature requires a backend configuration (Allow Asset Curation using Google Workspace) that is not directly accessible in the site settings.

When requesting Mindtickle Support to enable this feature, you must specify which permission model you want to apply to your learning site. The selected model determines the consent screen sales reps see when they first authenticate their Google account to edit an asset.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Asset Hub > Google Drive permissions:
- Full permissions (recommended)
  - Scope: Mindtickle can access all files and folders in the user's Google Drive, including those in shared drives.
  - File formatting: This option ensures the best results for layout and design. Because Mindtickle can access the original file, it uses Google APIs to create an exact copy, retaining all fonts, positioning, and animations.
  - User experience: Users will see the full permission consent dialog when they initiate the edit of an asset.
- Scoped access (limited)
  - Scope: Mindtickle is restricted to accessing only the files it creates or files the user explicitly opens with the Mindtickle app. It cannot view or access other files in the user's Google Drive. The "scoped access" option is intended for organizations with strict security policies that prevent granting third-party applications full access to users' Google Drives.
  - File formatting: Formatting may be lost or altered, particularly for complex PowerPoint presentations. Since Mindtickle cannot access the original source file to perform a direct copy, it must convert the Mindtickle-hosted file into a new Google format. This can result in layout shifts or loss of complex styling and formatting elements.
  - User experience: Users will see the limited (scoped) permission consent dialog when they initiate the edit of an asset. This is often preferred by organizations with strict security policies.

Once enabled, the ability to edit content is supported for PPT, DOC, and XLS file types. These assets can be files uploaded directly to Mindtickle or synced from a Google Drive.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Asset Hub > Which assets can be edited?:
Sales reps can edit certain types of assets, depending on file format and Admin-enabled asset properties. Below is a breakdown of supported formats and permission requirements.

- Supported file types: You can edit assets that are in Microsoft Office file formats (.doc, .docx, .xls, .xlsx, .ppt, .pptx) or Google Workspace formats (Docs, Sheets, Slides). Other file types are not supported.Both Microsoft Office and Google Workspace formats are supported. Files such as .xlsx can be edited in Google Sheets, and Google Sheets files can be exported as .xlsx for use in Excel. However, not all advanced features may be preserved across formats.
- Admin-enabled asset properties: The ability to allow asset editing is controlled by your admin, who can configure which assets can be edited by sales reps (learners) via asset’s properties. The Edit content feature is available to reps only for assets with the following properties enabled by admins:
  - Usage → External: This means that the asset is enabled for external sharing
  - Allow customized asset creation → Edit content: This means that the asset is also enabled for editing content in Google Workspace and/or Microsoft Office for the web.

These controls ensure that admins maintain oversight of marketing-approved assets while enabling reps to adapt materials for specific opportunities.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Asset Hub > How to edit assets:
1. From the Assets homepage on the learning site, go to the Assets or My assets tab and click an asset within a hub.
2. If your admin has allowed customized asset creation AND the asset file’s format is supported for editing , then you can edit the asset using Google Workspace (Docs, Sheets, Slides). If it’s allowed, the button appears in the header. Additionally, you can confirm this by checking if Edit content is listed under the Customized asset creation property.
3. Click the button and select Edit in Google Slides . For other supported file formats, you will see Edit in Google Docs or Edit in Google Sheets , as applicable.
4. If this is your first time editing an asset using Google Workspace, you will be prompted to sign in to your Google account and grant permissions to the Mindtickle app. This enables Mindtickle to save a copy of the asset file (which you are editing) in your personal Google Drive (My Drive).Edited assets are stored in a new folder created at the root of your My Drive. Any changes made in Google Workspace will automatically sync back to Mindtickle.If already signed in, continue to Step 8.
5. During the integration with your Google Drive account, Mindtickle first asks which Google account you want to connect with Mindtickle. Select any existing account you are already signed into or click Use another account to sign in and use another Google account.
6. Next, it requests access to view your Google email address. Click Continue .
7. Next, it requires the following permissions. Click Allow to continue. A. See and download all your Google Drive files B. See, edit, create, and delete only the specific Google Drive files you use with this app
8. You are redirected back to the asset page. In the Save asset pop-up, you are asked to specify the hub in which to save the copied version of the asset. You can create a new hub or save it to any of the listed hubs. You can also change the name of the asset. Note: Assets and hubs created by you will be saved under the My assets tab on the Assets homepage. Click Save and continue .

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Asset Hub > How to edit assets:
1. A copy of the asset gets created and it becomes a customized asset that you can edit, while the original, marketing-approved asset remains unchanged. The copied version opens in Google Slides [in a new tab], where you can make all kinds of changes, such as modify the contents of slides, reorder/hide/add/delete slides, and so on. See the next step for important callouts.
2. Note the following callouts on the ability to edit content in Google Workspace apps (Docs, Sheets, Slides):
  - You must have a valid Google Workspace license to use this feature.
  - Ensure that pop-ups are not blocked in your browser. See the browser documentation for information on how to allow pop-ups.
  - The maximum file size supported by Google Workspace is 100 MB.
  - All changes to the asset file are automatically saved to Mindtickle directly.
  - Your customized asset is never updated automatically. However, Mindtickle tracks the original asset your copy was created from, and flags your copy if that asset is updated or becomes unavailable. For details, see Source asset states on customized assets.
3. When you navigate back to the previous tab where the original asset is open, it displays the following toast notification. Click Go to asset to open the copied version of the asset, which you are editing in Microsoft PowerPoint for the web.
4. The asset page displays the “Editing in progress” message while you are editing the asset in Google Slides.
5. Once you have made all changes in Google Slides, simply close the Google Slides tab in your browser so that Mindtickle will automatically process and reflect the changes in your customized (copied) asset. The asset page displays the “Processing changes” message once you close the Google Slides tab.See the next step for an alternative approach.
6. In case your changes are not processed automatically or for any issues while closing the tab with Google Slides, you can click Sync now on the asset page to process and save the changes.
7. Once the changes are processed and reflect on the asset page, you can click the Edit button to make further edits using Google Slides. Since this is your own customized copy of the original asset, you now have two options:
  - Edit in Google Slides: Lets you make direct edits to this asset.
  - Edit a copy in Google Slides: Lets you create a copy of this asset before making the edits.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Asset Hub > Share and track customized assets:
Once the customized asset is created, you can share and track it as usual. Here's how:

- Share the asset: The rep can share the customized asset with other team members or clients as needed. This allows for greater collaboration and ensures that the most relevant and customized content is being circulated. For details, see Share assets (reps) .

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Copilot > For learners > Overview:
Mindtickle’s Seller Copilot enhances the productivity of sales reps and managers by leveraging AI to provide real-time access to key information, streamline workflows, and ensure readiness for customer interactions. With multi-chat functionality, users can manage multiple conversations by topic without losing context, similar to modern AI chat tools. Copilot follows the Mindtickle platform's existing permissions and access policies, ensuring secure, compliant interactions. It also ensures only sales reps configured by the admin can access Copilot.

Already available on the web, Mindtickle mobile app, and through APIs, Seller Copilot can now be launched directly inside Salesforce. Copilot appears as an embedded Lightning Web Component within Salesforce page layouts — including standard objects like Opportunities, Accounts, Leads, and Contacts, as well as custom objects. This means sales reps can access real-time insights, instant answers, and call prep tools without leaving their CRM, reducing context switching and driving productivity.

Seller Copilot is also available on the Mindtickle learning site, the Mindtickle mobile app, Slack, and through Mindtickle APIs.

For information about Mindtickle Copilot, see Mindtickle Copilot overview. For reporting on how your team uses Seller Copilot, see Seller Copilot analytics (admin).

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Copilot > For learners > How it works:
Mindtickle’s Seller Copilot is designed for intuitive, conversational interaction. Here’s how it works:

1. Starting a conversation : Use the options in the “Access Copilot” section to begin a chat. You can either type your own query or select from suggested questions/prompts. For best results, frame queries as specific questions or requests.
2. Multi-chat support : You can create and manage multiple conversation threads. Each chat thread is saved separately, allowing you to switch between topics, deals, or customers without losing context. Chats are automatically named based on your first query, and you can rename or delete threads as needed.
3. Instant, context-aware answers : Copilot provides quick, summarized answers, drawing from modules (assigned and public), assets, and Call AI calls available to you on the learning site. Responses include relevant links and related content when applicable.
4. Bring your own context : Use the + button in the chat input to link a specific module, asset, or call recording ( Link resources ), or to add your own documents ( Upload files ). See “ Bring your own context .”
5. Saved chat history : All messages are saved automatically within each chat thread, so you can revisit past conversations anytime. On the web, you can access all saved chats through the navigation panel.
6. Suggested follow-ups : After each response, Copilot suggests follow-up questions to help you dive deeper into the topic or continue the conversation seamlessly.
7. Chat actions : While interacting with Copilot, you can:
  - View related sources : Click links to see the content Copilot referenced.
  - Copy response : Copy the answer for use elsewhere.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Copilot > For learners > Chat with Copilot:
Seller Copilot interacts in a conversational way. The dialogue format enables Seller Copilot to answer followup questions, admit its mistakes, question false assumptions, and decline inappropriate requests.

Seller Copilot helps sales reps efficiently prepare for calls, complete post-call tasks, and get quick answers to their questions, all within a user-friendly interface. This leads to more effective and informed interactions with customers.

Seller Copilot is designed to be intuitive and easy to use. Here’s how you can chat with Seller Copilot:

1. You can access Seller Copilot in Salesforce via the embedded component added by your admin in page layouts. Copilot appears as a chat window.
2. In the Seller Copilot chat window, either choose from the suggested questions or type your own in the input box , and then press Enter . You can ask questions related to modules (assigned and public), assets, and Call AI calls available to you on the Mindtickle learning site. It is recommended to frame your queries as specific questions or instructions for most accurate and relevant results. For example, you can ask: “ Help me prepare for my next call with Acme ” or “ Can our product integrate with Acme? ”. Tip : Press Shift + Enter to start a new line in the chat input box, as pressing Enter sends your message to Copilot.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Copilot > For learners > Bring your own context > Link resources:
Use Link resources to point Seller Copilot at a specific module, asset, or call recording. Copilot then answers using that resource as the source. To start, type @ directly in the chat input, or click the + button and select Link resources.

Then choose a resource type (Suggested, Asset, Module, or Call AI) and type at least three characters after the @ to search and narrow the results. The resource you select appears as a chip in your question, and you can link more than one resource in a single question. Linked resources appear under Related sources in the response; click a source to open it in a new tab.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Copilot > For learners > Bring your own context > Upload files (beta):
Note: The Upload files feature is in beta and not enabled by default for your Mindtickle instance. To enable it, contact Mindtickle Support.

Use Upload files to bring in a document Copilot has not seen before, such as a customer RFP, a deal deck, or a pricing sheet, and ask questions about it. To add files, drag and drop them into the Add files window, or click the + button, select Upload files, and choose your files.

You can add files from your device or from cloud storage (for example, Google Drive, Box, Dropbox, OneDrive, and Salesforce). Supported file types are PDF, DOC/DOCX, PPT/PPTX, and XLS/XLSX, with up to 5 files per message and a maximum of 5 MB per file. Uploaded files stay available as context for follow-up questions in the same conversation, and you can click an attached file to open it in the in-app viewer.

Seller Copilot in Salesforce functions the same as on the Mindtickle learning site. For details on chatting with Copilot, linking resources, uploading files, supported content and files, limitations, and sample questions, see Chat with Seller Copilot on the learning site.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > Admin:
The Call Intel page provides admins with a centralized workspace to create and manage contextual call-level insights for all recorded conversations in Call AI. It enables admins to move beyond generic analysis and gain a deeper, more structured understanding of what happens in their calls.

Debriefs allow you to define the themes, topics, or business-specific signals that matter most. After configuration, Call AI uses these definitions to analyze each call and highlight insights that align with your priorities.

Scorecards work in conjunction with debriefs by helping you define what a good call looks like. They provide a consistent framework for evaluating conversations, enabling admins or managers to offer clear, repeatable feedback. This ensures that all calls are assessed using the same criteria, supporting coaching, quality assurance, and performance improvement.

Together, Debriefs and Scorecards help teams:

- Identify the most important insights from their calls.
- Standardize how conversations are evaluated.
- Strengthen feedback loops and coaching.
- Maintain higher call quality and consistency.
- Understand trends and performance over time.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > Admin > Create and configure debriefs:
1. Log in to Admin Site Homepage ,
2. Click the Account > Settings > Call AI > Call intel setup.
3. On the Call intel setup page, you can:
  - Select one of the three default templates:.

4. On the New debrief pop-up that appears, fill in the following details:

| Use case | Bad guidance | Good guidance |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Objection handling | Track when the rep handled objections. | Identify moments where the rep acknowledged and responded to a customer objection. Ignore general questions or feature clarifications. If no objection was raised, state: ‘No objection was discussed. |
| Next steps | Identify whether the next steps were discussed. | Highlight when the rep summarized the next steps and assigned ownership. Ignore vague mentions like ‘we’ll reconnect soon.’ If no next steps were mentioned, state: ‘No next steps confirmed. |
| Value proposition | Highlight where the rep discussed value. | Identify where the rep tied product capabilities to customer pain points, ROI, or quantified impact. Exclude generic product descriptions. If no value was discussed, state: ‘Value articulation was not observed. |
| Pricing discussion | Track pricing mentions | Identify instances where the representative discussed pricing details, discounts, or contract terms. Ignore casual mentions or jokes about price. If pricing was not discussed, state: ‘Pricing was not mentioned.’ |
| Success Criteria | Look for important criteria | Highlight when the rep discussed success criteria or desired outcomes with the customer. Exclude unrelated statements. If none were discussed, state: ‘Success criteria were not mentioned. |

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > Admin > View Debrief for a Call:
- The Debrief section offers AI-generated insights for your recorded calls.
- Once a call is recorded, the AI analyzes the transcript to identify the type of conversation, such as prospecting, negotiation, customer support, etc.
- It then applies the relevant active templates configured for that call type to generate structured insights.
- These insights are available under the Debriefs tab, where users can view and compare different perspectives by switching between multiple debrief templates using a drop-down menu.

This helps users quickly understand key takeaways and improve call effectiveness.

Note: You can view debriefs only for calls that are recorded after the feature is implemented on your site.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > Admin > Scorecards > Create and configure scorecards:
1. Log in to Admin Site Homepage ,
2. Click the Account > Settings > Call AI > Call intel setup.
3. On the Call intel setup page, click Scorecards :

- Select one of the three default templates:
  1. Discovery Scorecard : This template evaluates the effectiveness of participants in conducting sales discovery calls. It examines key behaviors, including establishing the purpose of the call, building rapport, identifying customer pains and current processes, exploring the impact of those challenges, and determining key stakeholders or constraints. It also checks whether the rep confirmed alignment and clarified next steps. Overall, this scorecard provides an objective way to measure discovery quality, ensuring teams conduct consistent, buyer-focused conversations.
  2. Deal Negotiation Scorecard: This evaluates the effectiveness of participants in negotiating. It assesses key behaviors, such as establishing context, uncovering buyer needs and constraints, reinforcing value, addressing objections, applying value-based give-and-get tactics, and maintaining control and professionalism. It also checks whether the rep advanced the deal and confirmed the next steps. This scorecard helps ensure negotiations are conducted with confidence, alignment, and a focus on protecting value.
  3. Default AI Scorecard : It is a system-managed, general-purpose scorecard designed to evaluate the effectiveness, clarity, and structure of any business conversation across sales, success, support, or internal calls. It provides a balanced and objective assessment based on core conversational behaviors that apply consistently across all call types.

4. On the New scorecard pop-up that appears, fill in the following details:

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > Admin > Scorecards > Create and configure scorecards:
- Title : Add a unique name for the scorecard.
- Description : Add a description to convey information on what the scorecard template is all about.
- Call types : From the drop-down list, select the type of call you want to apply the scorecard template. For more information about the call types, see Step 4 in the Create and configure debriefs section. Note: You can apply 1 scorecard template per call type.
- Evaluation parameters : These are the key topics or criteria used to assess and score a call. Each parameter represents a specific behavior, action, or outcome that the AI evaluates during the conversation, for example, uncovering customer pain points, reinforcing value, handling objections, or confirming next steps. These parameters form the foundation of the scorecard, helping ensure that calls are evaluated consistently and objectively. By defining clear, focused parameters, admins can guide the AI to measure the elements of a call that matter most for each call type. Click Add parameter. Note : You can add up to 10 evaluation parameters per scorecard.
  - Name : A unique name for the Evaluation parameter.
  - Description : Add a description for the parameter.
  - Guidance for Copilot : This field explains what the AI should look for when scoring a parameter and how it should assign a score ranging from 0 to 10. The guidance should clearly define what constitutes strong performance, what constitutes weak performance, and what aspects should be emphasized or disregarded. This helps the AI understand exactly how to interpret the rep’s behavior for that parameter, similar to the way the default templates describe the expected actions for Discovery or Negotiation. Note : Clear guidance ensures the AI scores each parameter accurately and consistently.
  - Guidance for Copilot : Click the Generate guidance option to automatically generate guidance by analyzing the tracker name and description. The Generate guidance helps improve the analysis of what the AI should look for when scoring a parameter and how it should assign a score ranging from 0 to 10. Clear guidance ensures the AI scores each parameter accurately and consistently. You can click Improve guidance to generate custom guidance based on your requirements. The Improve guidance would use the previously available guidance as additional context, along with the tracker name and description. Use the Undo option to revert to the previous generated guidance.
  - Use the following options to:
    - Copy : Create a duplicate item, including all its settings and content, to save time when adding similar entries.
    - Move Up / Down Arrow : Change the position of this item within the list by moving it up or down.
    - Delete : Remove this tracker from the system.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > CRMs > Setup the Mindtickle-Salesforce connection:
1. On the admin site homepage, hover over the Account icon on the left navigation bar, and click Settings . The Settings page is displayed.
2. Click the Security & integrations tab, scroll down to the User Sync section, and select the User / Contact check box under the Salesforce section.
3. Click Save and then click Connect .
4. On the displayed screen, enter your Salesforce admin credentials to log in.
5. On the displayed pop-up, click Allow . The Connected Apps OAuth Usage screen is displayed.
6. After logging into Salesforce, in the left navigation panel, click Apps > Connected Apps > Connected Apps OAuth Usage .
7. Under the Connected App column, click the Install button on Mindtickle Salesforce OAuth.
8. On the displayed pop-up screen, click Install.

The Mindtickle Salesforce OAuth app is now installed on the Salesforce instance.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > CRMs > Install the app:
1. Go to the Mindtickle app listing on Salesforce AppExchange .
2. Click the Get It Now button on the listing.

- Click on login with Trailblazer .
- Login to your account via SFDC.

3. Select the SFDC environment (production or sandbox) and the account to install the package.

4. Review the details and confirm the installation.

5. The Salesforce administrator can decide whether to install the application for all users or only for the administrator. If your organization uses custom profiles or non-admin roles, select Install for All Users and install the package.

Note: For non-admin and community (partner/customer) users, ensure the user's profiles have access to all the

apex classes. See SFDC Class Access (Community/Non-Admin Users) for more information.

6. Check the Grant third-party access box and click Continue.

Note: The installation takes some time to complete. You receive an email on successful installation.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > CRMs > Generate and download the Salesforce certificate:
1. Click the gear icon in the top-right corner and select Setup in Salesforce.
2. On the left panel, go to Security and click Certificate and Key Management .
3. Click the Create Self-Signed Certificate button. Alternatively, you can use an existing self-signed certificate.
4. Add the following Label Name and select the Key Size as 2048

- The label Name should be ‘Mindtickle’ (case sensitive)
- The Unique name should also be ‘Mindtickle’ (case sensitive)
- If the previously generated certificate is used, rename the label and unique name to ‘Mindtickle’ - ensure the certificate is not expired or near the expiry date

Note: Do not change any other default attributes.

5. Click Save.

6. Click the Download Certificate button.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > CRMs > Create Named Credentials:
Named credentials provide a way to define the scope of access to the external service, including specifying which Salesforce users or profiles can access it. They are a secure way to store authentication information for an external service or API. To create named credentials:

1. Click thegear icon in the upper-right corner and select Setup in Salesforce.

2. On the left panel, go to Security and click Named Credentials.

3. Click New Legacy.

4. The Label and Name should be Mindtickle_Asset (case sensitive).

5. URL should be ‘https://<learning site>.mindtickle.com’.

6. Select the certificate generated in the previous section.

7. Set the Identity Type as Per User.

8. Set the AuthenticationProtocol as JWT.

9. Set the Issuer as Mindtickle (case sensitive).

10. Set Per User Subject as $User.Username.

Note: You can configure any user attribute other than the username. For example, you can configure Per User Subject as $User.Email, or $User.User. If your Mindtickle email address or username differs from your Salesforce email address, you should specify a custom user attribute to ensure successful authentication.

12. Audiences should contain the company ID (cname) of your Mindtickle instance.

13. Set the Token Validity for 365 Days.

14. Select the Mindtickle certificate as the JWT Signing Certificate. This should be the same certificate as the one selected in step 6.

Note: Do not change any other default attributes.

15. Click Save.

For community (partner/customer) users and non-admin users, grant access to the following apex classes.
