Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > AI video > Introduction:
Mindtickle’s AI video feature enables admins to transform long, complex documents (PDF, DOC, or PPT) into concise and engaging narrated videos using AI. The feature automatically summarizes core ideas, highlights key points, and produces content with digital avatars, realistic lip-syncing, and visually appealing backgrounds and animations. This enables you to turn information-heavy content into dynamic, professional videos without requiring scripting, filming, or editing expertise.

The AI video feature helps you save time while boosting learner engagement. It turns complex material into focused, visually appealing, and interactive learning materials. You can also create language variants and customize narration, visuals, and scene elements for diverse audiences.

This feature is available in both course and quick update modules and allows you to convert documents into videos that can be added as learning objects.

Note: The AI video feature is currently in BETA. Please contact Mindtickle Support to enable it for your Mindtickle instance.

Key capabilities

1. AI-generated draft video: Convert your document into a first draft video with narration, avatars, visuals, and animations automatically created from your content.
2. Further customization and localization: Refine and enhance the draft using the AI Video Editor , including editing narration, adjusting visuals, creating language variants, and previewing the video before generating the final output.
3. Edit the generated video: When you click Edit on a video added to a course or quick update learning object, it opens in a new tab in the AI Video Editor . After making changes and generating the updated video, the system automatically replaces the existing video in the learning object and updates the corresponding version stored in the Content Center.

Benefits

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > AI video > Creating the video:
Follow these steps in a course or quick update to create a custom narrated video using AI from a PDF, DOC, or PPT file. Once generated, the video will also be saved to the Content Center (in the folder you selected) for future use in other modules and assets.

1. In a course or quick update module, under the Build tab, click Add learning objects to get started.
2. In the Add learning objects panel, click the AI video option.
3. The Select file to convert pop-up opens and lists files and folders in the Content Center. Select a PDF, DOC, or PPT type of file that you want to convert to video — either the Content Center homepage or by navigating through folders. Once selected, click Select & continue . Note : Currently only PDF, DOC, and PPT files are supported. Use the File type filter set to PDF, DOC, and PPT to show only relevant files.
4. In the Select folder for converted video pop-up, specify a folder in the Content Center where the AI-generated video will be saved. Use the New folder option to create a new folder anywhere in the Content Center. For example, you can create a folder called “AI videos” to store all AI-generated videos in a single folder in the Content Center. Once done, click Select & continue .

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > AI video > Creating the video:
1. In the Select video template pop-up, choose any template and then click Select & convert . Each template includes default settings such as an avatar, fonts, backgrounds, narration, and more — all of which you can customize later to suit your needs. Mindtickle will use both your selected PDF/DOC/PPT file and the chosen template to create the video.
2. You are redirected to the module’s Build tab, where a new learning object is automatically added. Mindtickle then begins generating a draft video using AI, based on the content transcript from your selected PDF/DOC/PPT file.
  - The Open Preview button appears once the draft video is ready. Click it to view and edit the AI-generated video in the AI Video Editor (opens in a new tab).
  - Alternatively, delete the learning object to discard the draft video.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > AI video > Creating the video:
1. The AI Video Editor opens in a new tab, where you can make various customizations to the video before generating the final output. In the AI Video Editor, you can edit and further customize the video , create language variants to auto-translate the video in other languages, preview the video , and finally generate the video . For details, see AI video - Customize videos with AI Video Editor . Note : The editor tab expires after 8 hours for security, but you can reopen the draft anytime via the Open preview button in the module LO with your last changes auto-saved.
2. Before generating the video, select the language variant in which you want the final video to be created and saved on Mindtickle. You can create up to two language variants of an AI video, including the default.
3. Once the video is finalized, click Generate to start generating the video. The following message appears: Generation request submitted .
4. You can close the editor and return to the module tab. Mindtickle starts processing the final video, which typically takes 10-15 minutes to complete. You can track the progress in real time within the learning object created for the AI video. Video generation continues even if you close the module tab. Note that no notifications are sent when the video is ready; you need to check the learning object for it.
5. Once the finalized video is generated, it will appear within the learning object. Using the option on the video, you can download it to your computer, replace it with another video, and edit the video further via the AI Video Editor.
6. The AI-generated video is also automatically saved to the Content Center , in the folder you selected in Step 4 . You can reuse the video in other places, such as in assets and modules.
7. Click the video to open it in the Content Center on its file page. Here, you can play the video and take actions, such as apply tags, see locations where the video is used (in modules and assets), manage collaborators, download or replace the video file, view file details, move the file, or delete it.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > AI video > Editing the video:
Once a video has been added to a course or quick update learning object, you can revise it at any time. The video opens directly in the AI Video Editor, and when you generate the updated version, it automatically replaces the video in both the learning object and the version stored in the Content Center.

1. In a course or quick update module, open the learning object where the AI video has been added. Click Edit on the video .
2. This opens the AI Video Editor in a new browser tab. Make the necessary updates in the editor, such as adjusting narration, visuals, or other elements. You can also create localized versions or refine the overall structure.
3. Once you begin editing the video, it remains in a draft state. The learning object page then displays two options: Discard edits and Open preview . The Discard edits option removes your changes and restores the previously published video. The Open preview option reopens the draft in the AI Video Editor, which is useful if you’ve closed the editor tab.
4. Once done with all changes, click Generate in the editor to generate the updated video. The system processes your changes and replaces the previous version in both the learning object and the Content Center.
5. Return to the learning object to verify that the updated video appears correctly.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > AI video > Document guidelines:
To get the best results from the AI video feature, select documents that are well-suited for video conversion — focused, practical, and structured to help the AI summarize and visualize content effectively.

Also see the “Limitations” section.

Ideal document characteristics

- Focused and practical: Helps learners take action (e.g., applying techniques, understanding features).
- Concept-driven with key points: Clear topics with identifiable takeaways for the AI to highlight.
- Logical flow: Content that explains a process or tells a story with a clear beginning, middle, and end.
- Visualizable topics: Even abstract concepts that can be represented visually (e.g., product launches, sales funnels).
- Self-contained messages: Viewers should understand the video without needing the original document.
- Concise language: Clear, straightforward writing helps the AI summarize efficiently.

Suitable document types

- Sales playbooks or methodologies: For example, objection handling, discovery call frameworks, closing techniques.
- Customer success stories or case studies: For example, testimonial highlights, short problem-solution-impact narratives.
- Market research or persona briefs: For example, ICP summaries, buyer persona overviews.
- Product updates or release notes: For example, feature launches, version updates, bug fixes.
- Competitive battle cards or analysis: For example, competitor comparisons, SWOTs, talking points.
- Compliance updates (key highlights only): Videos supplement full legal/policy documents.
- Training module overviews: For example, course previews, module objectives, “what to expect” videos.

Unsuitable document types

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > AI video > Limitations:
These are the key limitations of the AI video feature, including the AI Video Editor:

- Image-only PDFs are not supported : The AI cannot extract usable information from documents that consist entirely of images. This includes PDF files created by converting image files. In such cases, the AI cannot transcribe or summarize text, so the video cannot be generated successfully.
- Speaker notes in PPTs not supported : Speaker notes within PPT files are currently not supported and are not used when generating videos. If needed, you can manually copy the speaker notes and add them to the relevant video scenes during the editing process.
- Maximum of two language variants : You can create up to two language variants of a video, including the default language.
- Limited customization of stock avatars : Stock avatars have predefined appearances, and full generative customization options (like outfits or expressions) are not available.
- Rendering times may vary : Complex videos with multiple scenes, avatars, or animations may take longer to generate.
- Video LO duplication behavior: Duplicated AI video learning objects (LOs) share the same underlying video file. Any edits made to the video in one LO will automatically appear in all duplicated LOs. To create an independent version, generate a new video from the source document instead of duplicating the LO.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > AI video > Introduction:
Mindtickle’s AI video feature enables admins to transform long, complex documents (PDF, DOC, or PPT) into concise and engaging narrated videos using AI. After your draft video is ready, you can open it in the AI Video Editor to refine and enhance every aspect before generating the final output. The editor lets you edit narration, visuals, animations, and transitions, preview your changes in real time, and create language variants to reach viewers in multiple languages.

Example use cases:

- Corporate training : Keep learners engaged with custom avatars, voiceovers, and background music.
- Marketing videos : Capture attention by adding animations and sound effects.
- Product demonstrations : Clearly explain features using detailed text editing and avatars.

Note: The AI video feature is currently in BETA. Please contact Mindtickle Support to enable it for your Mindtickle instance.

This help article focuses on customizing AI videos with the AI Video Editor: How to refine and enhance the drafted video, including customizing narration, visuals, animations, transitions, and creating language variants to reach a wider audience.

For step-by-step guidance on creating an AI-generated video from a PDF/DOC/PPT and editing the generated video, see AI video - Generate videos from documents using AI.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > AI video > Key features and actions:
To understand each area of the AI Video Editor, start with the “Editor functionality overview” section, which includes an annotated screenshot and explanations of the canvas, script panel, toolbar, timeline, right-panel controls, language variants, preview, and generation options.

Using the editor, you can:

- Design and customize scenes using the scene canvas: add and arrange avatars, shapes, media, and text, and adjust layout, size, and formatting.
- Control visual settings with canvas controls, including aspect ratios, grids, draft naming, and applying default or custom brand styles.
- Write, refine, and manage scripts for each scene, assign voices or avatars, add pauses or pronunciation adjustments, and use the AI Assistant for script improvements.
- Add new elements using the toolbar, such as avatars, shapes, text, images, videos, and other media.
- Edit music, backgrounds, transitions, and element-specific settings through the right-hand panel.
- Manage scenes using the timeline to navigate, reorder, duplicate, insert, delete, and preview individual scenes, as well as adjust transitions.
- Create language variants to automatically translate narration and on-screen text, customize formatting per language, and sync changes from the default version.
- Preview your video to review narration, visuals, animations, transitions, and scene timing.
- Generate the final video , which becomes available in the learning object (LO) and is saved to the Content Center for reuse.
- Edit the video at any time by reopening it in the AI Video Editor to update scripts, visuals, languages, or scenes as needed.

Continue reading for details on each feature.

- Design and customize scenes using the scene canvas: add and arrange avatars, shapes, media, and text, and adjust layout, size, and formatting.

- Write, refine, and manage scripts for each scene, assign voices or avatars, add pauses or pronunciation adjustments, and use the AI Assistant for script improvements.
- Add new elements using the toolbar, such as avatars, shapes, text, images, videos, and other media.
- Edit music, backgrounds, transitions, and element-specific settings through the right-hand panel.
- Manage scenes using the timeline to navigate, reorder, duplicate, insert, delete, and preview individual scenes, as well as adjust transitions.
- Create language variants to automatically translate narration and on-screen text, customize formatting per language, and sync changes from the default version.
- Preview your video to review narration, visuals, animations, transitions, and scene timing.
- Generate the final video , which becomes available in the learning object (LO) and is saved to the Content Center for reuse.
- Edit the video at any time by reopening it in the AI Video Editor to update scripts, visuals, languages, or scenes as needed.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > AI video > Editor functionality overview:
All the controls shown in the screenshot are editing options for the scene at the center of the screen. Each scene can be customized with narration, avatars, visuals, and design elements. The numbered annotations correspond to:

Scene canvas (center panel)

The scene canvas is the main workspace for designing each scene. You can:

- Add, select, and arrange elements such as avatars, shapes, media, and text.
- Edit all text elements directly on the canvas.
- Move, resize, rotate, and layer elements to build your layout.
- Preview the scene as it plays from the timeline.

Canvas controls + brand styles (top-left corner)

Click the (hamburger) button for options to:

- Resize the canvas by choosing a preset aspect ratio or entering a custom size.
- Rename your draft.
- Apply styles using default or custom brand styles, and further customize colors and fonts.
- Show grid to help align elements on the canvas.
- Access the Help center or send feedback.
- Undo/Redo recent actions using the buttons next to the menu.

Script panel (left panel)

This panel is where you write and control the script for each scene. In the Script panel, you can:

- Write and edit the script text for the selected scene.
- Assign voices or avatars for narration to lines of dialogue.
- Add pauses, control pronunciation, and insert animation markers.
- Upload and use custom audio instead of generated narration.
- Use the AI Assistant to write and refine your script, such as correcting grammar, adjusting length, and generating new ideas.
- Resize the panel to give yourself more space while editing.

Script changes apply to the currently selected scene and update the narration and preview accordingly.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > AI video > Editor functionality overview:
Toolbar for new elements (top center)

Provides access to the various elements you can add to the scenes:

- Avatar : Select or change presenter (actor) avatars, position them on the canvas, adjust size or placement, and remove/add multiple avatars.
- Shape : Add and style arrows, boxes, or callouts to highlight key content.
- Text : Add written elements using title, subtitle, or body text. Customize style, position, layering, and animations to match your scene and narration.
- Media : Add stock or uploaded images and videos; also supports screen recordings.

Music, background, transitions + Element editing (right panel)

The right panel serves a dual role depending on context: it shows global scene settings (music, background, transitions) when nothing is selected, and detailed editing options when you select an element on the canvas.

I. Music, background, transitions

When no element is selected on the scene, the right panel shows global scene settings. In this mode you can:

- Music : Add background music for the audio, either from the library or by uploading your own audio. Adjust the music volume and apply it to a single scene or all scenes.
- Background : Apply a color or image/video as scene background. For image/video, you can either choose from the stock images in the library or upload your own. You can also use the AI Assistant to generate an image.
- Scene transition : Choose and apply scene transitions (fade, slide, wipe, etc.) adjust the duration.

These options let you define the overall audiovisual styling and the flow between scenes.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > AI video > Editor functionality overview:
II. Element editing

When an element on the canvas (avatar, shape, text, or media) is selected, the right panel switches to element editing mode. In this mode you can:

Adjust element-specific properties such as position, size, rotation, visibility, formatting, and animations (entry/exit effects and timing).

- Avatar : Assign or change avatars, adjust view and placement.
- Shapes : Add, resize, position, and layer shapes.
- Text : Edit content, style, color, alignment, and position.
- Media (images/videos) : Insert, resize, reposition, crop, and set playback behavior (for videos: loop, freeze last frame, adjust speed).

Timeline controls (bottom panel)

Shows all scenes in the video as thumbnails in sequence.

- Navigate between scenes by clicking thumbnails. Reorder scenes with drag-and-drop.
- Use hover menu actions to duplicate, insert, or delete scenes.
- Add, edit, or remove transitions between scenes.
- Preview scenes and play them back individually.

Language variants | Preview | Generate (top-right corner)

I. Language variants

Create translated versions of your video to reach audiences in different languages. The default language serves as the source, and additional languages are called language variants. The AI video Editor auto-generates translated scripts, matching voices, and updates on-screen text.Note: You can create up to two language versions of an AI video, including the default.

- Create variants: Auto-translate script, voice, and on-screen text.
- Edit scripts and text: Refine translations for accuracy and tone.
- Customize scenes: Adjust voices, avatars, backgrounds, media, shapes, and text formatting per variant.
- Sync from default: Push default-script changes to all variants.
- Adjust text formatting: Resize or reformat text independently in each variant.
- Preview variants: Play back translated versions before generating the video.

II. Preview & generate video

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > AI video > 1. Scene canvas:
The scene canvas is the main working area where you design and arrange the visual content for each scene of your video. It provides a real-time, editable view of how your scene will appear in the final output.

On the canvas, you can:

- Add and position elements such as avatars, shapes, media (images, videos, icons), and text to build the structure of your scene.
- Select and edit elements you’ve added; clicking any element activates its editing options in the right-hand panel.
- Move, resize, rotate, and layer elements to control layout, visual hierarchy, and composition.
- Edit text directly on the canvas , including text boxes, styled text components, subtitles, and callouts.
- Preview the scene in context as you play the video from the timeline, allowing you to see layout, timing, and interactions as they will appear in the final video.

When you select any element on the canvas, all available customization options for that element appear in the right-hand editing panel, enabling precise control over its appearance and behavior.

- Add and position elements such as avatars, shapes, media (images, videos, icons), and text to build the structure of your scene.
- Select and edit elements you’ve added; clicking any element activates its editing options in the right-hand panel.
- Move, resize, rotate, and layer elements to control layout, visual hierarchy, and composition.
- Edit text directly on the canvas , including text boxes, styled text components, subtitles, and callouts.
- Preview the scene in context as you play the video from the timeline, allowing you to see layout, timing, and interactions as they will appear in the final video.

When you select any element on the canvas, all available customization options for that element appear in the right-hand editing panel, enabling precise control over its appearance and behavior.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > AI video > 2. Canvas controls + brand styles:
The top-left corner of the editor contains key controls for managing your canvas, video settings, styling, and general editor actions. These options help you adjust the visual format of your video, maintain brand consistency, and access support or feedback tools.

Click the (hamburger) button for options to:

- Resize (aspect ratio) : Lets you change the aspect ratio of your video, with presets such as 16:9 for desktop and YouTube, 9:16 for Instagram stories, 1:1 for square posts, or a custom size you define. For the custom size, only values between 1 and 50 are allowed. The height:width ratio cannot be smaller than 1:5 or larger than 2:1. Note : Changing the size does not automatically reorganize existing content. You may need to manually adjust elements to fit the new layout.
- Rename draft : Rename the video. Alternatively, directly click the video name to rename.
- Apply styles : Choose between the default and your custom brand styles (colors and fonts) for the video. You can also further customize the selected style. See details in the “ Apply styles ” section.
- Show grid : Toggle gridlines on the scene canvas to help align and position elements accurately.
- Help center : Access documentation on the AI Video Editor.
- Feedback : Share feedback on the AI Video Editor. For details, see the “ Feedback ” section.

Undo/Redo: Use the (Undo) and (Redo) buttons to revert or repeat recent actions. These buttons are available next to the hamburger menu.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > AI video > 2. Canvas controls + brand styles > Apply styles (default and custom):
The Apply styles option lets you define the overall visual style of your video, controlling colors, fonts, and branding for a consistent look across all scenes. You can choose between the default styles and your custom brand styles, further customize the selected style, and switch styles at any time during editing.

- Default styles: The default style uses the editor’s built-in colors and fonts, providing a clean, neutral baseline. It’s ideal for quick videos or projects that don’t require specific branding.
- Custom styles (via brand kits): Custom styles are based on your brand kits, which define your brand identity, including colors, fonts, and logos. Setting up a brand kit requires providing details such as color hex codes, font files, and the company logo file. For assistance with setting up a brand kit, please contact Mindtickle Support.

Here’s how you can apply styles (colors and fonts) to your entire video. All changes are previewed live on the scenes displayed to the right:

Select a style: In the first dropdown menu, choose between Default styles or your custom brand styles. Customize colors: For the selected style, available color options are listed. You can modify each color or choose a custom color of your choice. Randomize colors: You can also use the Randomize colors option to apply colors automatically. Customize fonts: For the selected style, available font options are listed. You can change each font using the dropdown menu for each option.

Once satisfied, click Apply styles. All video scenes will update to reflect the selected colors and fonts.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > AI video > 3. Script panel:
The Script panel is where you write, edit, and manage the narration that your AI avatar will speak in a scene. Everything you enter here is converted into spoken audio by your chosen avatar. It also includes tools for controlling voice, pronunciation, pacing, and tone. This makes the Script panel the starting point for building your video scenes.

Note: Certain characters are blocked in the Script panel to ensure smooth audio generation and video creation. For details, see this article.

A) Script text editing

- Script text editor : The main area for editing your scene’s script. You can customize the AI-generated draft and add your own text to fit your needs.
  - Use paragraphs (press Enter ) to separate ideas and to target paragraph-level actions like previewing or assigning different voices.
  - Each scene in the video has its own separate script, so text changes apply only to that specific scene. This also makes it easy to organize narration across different video sections.
  - Select words or phrases for options to listen to it (play audio) and edit it with AI.
- Upload your own audio (optional) : You can upload an audio file in place of text. The system will detect the language automatically. You may choose Narration only for pure voiceover scenes or assign the audio to the scene’s avatar for lip-sync.
- AI assistant for the script : Use the AI Assistant to refine your text. Common actions include correcting grammar, shortening, changing its tone (e.g., formal, conversational), or brainstorming ideas. You can access it in the following ways: Select text → Edit with AI , or type a forward slash (/) → AI assistant , or the AI assistant button in the script toolbar.

B) Avatar, narration, and voice controls

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > AI video > 3. Script panel:
- Avatar narration: Assigns the script to the chosen avatar so that the text is spoken in sync with the video. Each scene can have its own narration. You can choose whether narration is active (with avatar or narration only) or leave the scene silent . From the avatar chip above the script editor, you can:
  - Pick an avatar to appear and narrate the text.
  - Switch to Narration only mode for voiceover without an on-screen avatar.
  - Remove the avatar from the scene entirely.
  - Add a new avatar. Alternatively, you can add new avatars via the Avatar option in the toolbar at the top-center of the editor.
  - You can also mix delivery methods within the same scene. For example, assign one paragraph to an avatar and the next to narration-only.
- Voice and language selection: Control how the narration sounds. The editor automatically detects language as you type and also selects the appropriate voice in case you have created language variants for the video. From the voice option, you can:
  - Select a voice by accent, age, tone, or scenario. Configure the voice speed and stability.
  - Each voice lists voice personality attributes, along with the default and other supported languages and accents. Example: Alice (voice name) | American English (language and accent) | Young Adult (age) | Calm, Friendly, Soft, Conversational, Explainer, Narration (personality attributes)
  - Preview the voice and then apply it to either the current block, the scene, or all scenes in the video.
- Pauses : Inserts natural breaks in narration. Use the script toolbar or type a forward slash (/) → Pause to insert a break/pause between words or sentences. Choose a preset duration (from 0.5 to 5 seconds), then adjust it using the pencil icon.
- Multilingual support: Ensures scripts can be spoken in multiple languages. Applicable if you have added any language variants.Typing directly in another supported language will automatically adjust voice delivery. Alternatively, users can manually pick a language/voice pair from the dropdown.

- Multilingual support: Ensures scripts can be spoken in multiple languages. Applicable if you have added any language variants. Typing directly in another supported language will automatically adjust voice delivery. Alternatively, users can manually pick a language/voice pair from the dropdown.

C) Animation markers

Add animation markers in the script to synchronize the script with animations added to elements (e.g. text, media, shapes) in the scene. These act like pins that you place in your script to specify starting and ending points for animations. They link narration timing with visual effects.

- Placing markers: Use the script toolbar or type a forward slash (/) to add markers. The marker appears both in your script and in the Animate tab for elements (e.g. text, media, shapes).
- Using markers with elements: After placing markers, select an element on the canvas and open the Animate tab . Choose an animation type (Fade, Slide, Grow) and behavior:
  - Enter: Element enters at the marker and stays until the end of the scene.
  - Exit: Element enters at the beginning and exits at the marker.
  - Enter & exit: Choose separate markers for entry and exit timings.
- Managing markers: Markers remain visible in the script box, making it easy to adjust the timing of visual effects in sync with narration. You can move their position by dragging and dropping the animation marker icon.

D) Preview the audio

Audio preview button: Preview how the script sounds with the selected voice before generating the full video, or as an alternative to previewing the scene from the timeline.

  - Exit: Element enters at the beginning and exits at the marker.
  - Enter & exit: Choose separate markers for entry and exit timings.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > AI video > 4. Toolbar for new elements > I. Avatar:
The Avatar option in the toolbar lets you control which on-screen avatar (actor) appears in your video, how they are styled, and how they deliver narration. It centralizes all avatar-related customization so you can decide how your script is presented visually.

There are three ways to add or manage avatars in a scene: Use the Avatar option in the toolbar at the top to add new avatars. Use the Avatar option in the script to add or remove avatars. Click on the added avatar in a scene to apply the avatar to all scenes, replace the avatar, and customize various avatar settings.

When you click Apply to all scenes, you’re prompted to either Add to all scenes (new avatar is added alongside existing ones) or Replace on all scenes (new avatar replaces the existing one throughout the video). Click Delete on your keyboard to delete the avatar.

Avatar features:

- Avatar library : Browse and select from a range of prebuilt avatars. Options vary by gender, age, ethnicity, and style (e.g., formal, casual, expressive). You can preview how each avatar looks delivering narration before applying it to the scene. Selected avatars apply only to the current scene.
- Custom avatars: Upload or manage personalized avatars. These may be photo-based (created from a picture) or video-based (created from video recordings). Uploaded avatars appear in the library alongside stock avatars and can be used the same way.
- Avatar positioning : Control how the avatar appears in your scene. Depending on the avatar type, you can choose full-body, waist-up, or cropped modes. Drag, resize, and position the avatar directly on the canvas. Avatars can be layered with other elements like backgrounds, shapes, or text.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > AI video > 4. Toolbar for new elements > II. Shape:
The Shape option in the toolbar lets you add and style geometric or illustrative elements — such as arrows, circles, rectangles, or callouts — to enhance the visual storytelling in your scenes. These can help emphasize information, guide viewers’ attention, or reinforce branding.

You can insert shapes directly from the toolbar, customize their appearance, and add animations to bring them to life on screen. Shapes can overlay backgrounds, appear alongside avatars, or act as visual indicators during narration.

- Insert shapes : Choose from a variety of options such as arrows, circles, rectangles, and callouts. Click the Shape option for available shapes.
- Style and formatting : Customize each shape’s fill color, border, opacity, and line thickness. For example, you might create a transparent circle with a bright outline to highlight part of the screen.
- Positioning & sizing : Drag, resize, and place shapes anywhere on the canvas. Shapes can be layered with text, backgrounds, or avatars to frame or highlight important details.
- Animation options :
  - Use animation markers in your script to define when shape animations begin or end.
  - Select a shape, click Animate in the sidebar, and choose from animation types such as Fade , Slide , or Grow .
  - Set the animation behavior to Enter , Exit , or Enter & Exit and sync timing with your script.
- Screen-recording overlays : Shapes can also be used in screen capture scenes to highlight or obscure specific areas, such as placing an arrow to point at a button or a rectangle to hide sensitive information.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > AI video > 4. Toolbar for new elements > III. Text:
The Text option in the toolbar lets you add written elements to your video, making it easy to highlight key points, display titles, captions, or on-screen prompts. Text can be purely decorative, functional (like callouts or lower thirds), or informational (like subtitles).

Allows you to add written elements to your video. You can insert:

- Title : For main headings or scene intros.
- Subtitle : For secondary headings or supplementary text.
- Body text : For captions, callouts, or detailed explanations.

Each text type can be styled with font, size, color, and formatting options, positioned on the canvas, layered with other elements, and animated to match narration or scene transitions.

- Add text boxes : Click the Text option to insert text directly onto the canvas. You can add multiple text boxes per scene to create titles, subheadings, or labels.
- Text styling : Customize fonts, size, weight, alignment, and letter spacing. Choose from the available font library. Colors can be set using the color picker or hex codes to ensure consistency with your brand palette.
- Formatting options : Apply formatting such as bold, italics, underline, and bullet lists. Text boxes support multi-line editing, making it easy to create structured content like quotes or step-by-step instructions.
- Backgrounds and shapes for text : Add colored backgrounds, highlights, or shape containers (e.g., rectangles, callouts) behind text to improve readability and emphasize key points.
- Positioning and layering : Drag and resize text boxes anywhere on the canvas. Text can be layered in front of or behind other elements like images, avatars, or shapes to create the desired visual hierarchy.
- Text animations : Bring text to life with entry and exit effects. Options typically include fade, slide, and grow. You can define whether text enters, exits, or does both. Animations can be timed using script markers, so text appears in sync with narration or scene transitions.
- Captions and accessibility : For improved accessibility, you can add text to serve as captions or subtitles. This ensures your video remains effective even when played without sound.
- Consistency across scenes : Apply the same text style across multiple scenes for a unified look, or customize text per scene to highlight transitions or new topics.

Stock assets can be previewed before adding to ensure they fit the tone and purpose of your video.
- Upload your own media : Import images, videos, and icons directly from your computer. This is useful for branded graphics, screenshots, or custom visuals that align with your project.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > AI video > 5. Music, background, transitions + Element editing:
The right panel serves a dual role depending on context: it shows global scene settings (music, background, transitions) when nothing is selected, and detailed editing options when you select an element on the canvas.

Click anywhere outside the scene canvas to open the right-hand panel for music, background, and transition settings. Click any element on the scene canvas to open the right-hand panel for element editing/customization options.

When no element is selected on the scene, the right panel shows global scene settings. In this mode you can:

- Music : Add background music for the audio, either from the library or by uploading your own audio. Adjust the music volume and apply it to a single scene or all scenes.
- Background : Apply a color or image/video as scene background. For image/video, you can either choose from the stock images in the library or upload your own. You can also use the AI Assistant to generate an image.
- Scene transition : Choose and apply scene transitions (fade, slide, wipe, etc.) adjust the duration.

These options let you define the overall audiovisual styling and the flow between scenes. Continue reading for details on each.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > AI video > 5. Music, background, transitions + Element editing > I. Music:
The Music option lets you add background audio that sets the mood and supports the overall tone of your video. Music can run across the entire video to create a consistent soundscape.

You can select from the built-in stock music library or upload your own tracks. Music elements are applied quickly and can be adjusted to complement narration, avatars, and other media.

- Stock music : Browse and preview royalty-free tracks covering different moods and genres, such as upbeat, cinematic, corporate, or calm.
- Upload your own music : Import audio files directly from your computer. Supported formats include .mp3 and .wav, allowing use of branded jingles, licensed tracks, or custom compositions.
- Music adjustments : For any stock or uploaded music, you can control its application and audio level.
  - Play everywhere : Use the toggle to apply the selected music across all scenes for a unified audio experience.
  - Volume : Adjust the music level to ensure it complements narration and other audio elements without overpowering them.
- Preview : Listen to music alongside narration, avatars, and animations before generating your video to ensure balance and timing are correct.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > AI video > 5. Music, background, transitions + Element editing > II. Background:
The Background option controls the visual setting of your video. It allows you to set a consistent style across scenes or customize each one independently.

You can use an image or any color as the background. For image, you can either select from the available stock images, upload your own, or use AI to generate an image. For image backgrounds, you can apply film filters and blur effects.

- Image library : Browse from a wide selection of stock background images, videos, and colors. Backgrounds can be applied per scene, and you can preview them before saving.
- Image uploads : Upload your own images (e.g., brand graphics, photos) to use as custom backgrounds. Uploaded images can be resized and positioned within the canvas.
- Color picker : For simple and clean designs, you can choose a single solid color or gradient as the background. The color picker supports custom hex codes to match your brand guidelines.
- Scene-by-scene customization : Different backgrounds can be applied to different scenes. This helps create visual variety or emphasize scene transitions. It’s also possible to keep the same background across all scenes for a unified, branded look.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > AI video > 5. Music, background, transitions + Element editing > III. Transition:
The Transition option lets you add visual effects between scenes, enhancing the flow and engagement of your video. You can add, edit, and remove transitions by clicking either the Transition option or the Transition icon between scenes in the timeline. Using the Apply to all scenes toggle, you can either apply the same transition globally or customize different transitions for individual scenes.

Select a transition: Choose the type of transition for the scene, such as Fade, Slide, or Zoom.For the selected transition, you can adjust:

- Apply to all scenes : Use the button to apply this transition across all scenes for a consistent visual flow.
- Duration (sec) : Set the length of the transition to control how quickly or gradually one scene moves into the next.

Preview: View the transition in action before finalizing your video to ensure it achieves the desired effect.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > AI video > 6. Timeline controls:
The Timeline panel appears below the scene and provides a structured view of your video’s scenes. It helps you navigate, reorder, and manage scenes, and it also gives quick access to transition controls between scenes.

Note: Scene-level changes made in the Timeline (adding, reordering, deleting, or setting per-scene transitions) apply to the video as a whole and affect all language variants.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > AI video > 6. Timeline controls:
- Scene overview and organization : Each scene appears as a thumbnail, giving you a clear overview of the video’s flow. From here, you can:
- Navigate : Click a scene thumbnail to jump directly to that scene for editing.
- Reorder : Drag and drop thumbnails to adjust the sequence and narrative flow.
- Rename : Edit thumbnail names to make them easier to identify while editing. These names are for reference only and do not appear in the generated video.
- Hover menu actions : When you hover over a scene thumbnail and click the three-dot menu, you can duplicate, delete, or add a new scene . Available actions:
  - Duplicate scene : Create a copy of the scene to reuse or modify.
  - Insert new scene : Add a new blank scene immediately after the selected one. You can also add new scenes at the end, after the last scene.
  - Delete scene : Remove the selected scene from the project.
- Add or edit transitions : Between two scene thumbnails, click the Add transition icon to set transition or click the Edit transition icon to change the transition for that cut . For the selected transition you can:
  - Apply between all scenes : Toggle to apply the chosen transition across the entire video; when OFF you can set different transitions per cut.
  - Duration (sec) : Set how long the transition lasts to control the pacing between scenes.
- Preview scenes : Click a scene thumbnail → Preview button to play just that scene. Tip : You can preview the entire video using th e Preview button in the top-right of the editor.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > AI video > 7. Create language variants (translations):
The Language variants feature in the AI Video Editor allows you to create versions of your video in different languages (automatic translations), enabling you to reach a broader audience and cater to diverse linguistic preferences.

The main language of the video is the default language variant, which serves as the source for all translations. Additional languages you create are called language variants. You can generate videos using multiple language variants at the same time.

The AI Video Editor automatically generates a translated script, assigns a matching voice, and updates on-screen text where applicable. This saves time and ensures consistency across versions.

Note: You can create up to two language versions of an AI video, including the default.

Auto-translate the video: The Language variant feature instantly and automatically translates your video into various languages. To translate your video: Click on the language selector in the top-right corner of the editor. Select the desired language variant from the dropdown menu and click Translate.

The AI Video Editor automatically generates a translated script, assigns a matching voice, and updates on-screen text where applicable. This saves time and ensures consistency across versions.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > AI video > 7. Create language variants (translations):
- Script and text editing : Within a language variant, you can directly refine the translated script and on-screen text. This allows you to improve the accuracy of automated translations, adapt tone and phrasing for cultural context, and correct specialized terminology. Note : All edits made in a language variant are unique to that variant and will not affect the default variant or variants for other languages.
- Scene customization in variants: In addition to the script and text changes, a language variant can be customized just like the default version. You can adjust voices, switch avatars, update backgrounds, replace or edit media, and modify shapes or text formatting. These edits ensure the localized video is not only linguistically accurate but also visually and stylistically aligned with your target audience. Note : All edits made in a language variant are unique to that variant and will not affect the default variant or variants for other languages.
- Syncing updates from the default variant: You can replicate script and on-screen text changes made in the default language across all other variants to keep translations consistent. Any changes in the default variant are indicated with a red dot on the language icon.
  - Switch to the default language variant. Make the necessary edits in the script or text elements.
  - Click Language variant → Update variants to push changes to all other language variants. Note : Edits from the default variant are applied to all other language variants, but edits made within individual variants remain unchanged .
- Customize text formatting in a language variant : When working with translated variants, you may find that the automatically applied formatting doesn’t fit well (for example, translated text may appear too long for the scene). You can adjust the appearance of text elements in each variant without affecting the default language or other variants.
  - Switch to the desired language variant.
  - Select the text box you want to edit.
  - Check Detach text format to unlock formatting options for that variant.
  - Adjust the font size, spacing, or other formatting as needed to make the text fit and look consistent. Note: Formatting changes are unique to the selected variant and will not be applied to the default variant or other translations.
- Change the default language: You can change the default language of the video by removing all existing scripts from your draft and creating a new script in your preferred language. The default language variant will then reflect the new language.
- Preview : Before finalizing the video, you can preview the translated version to ensure accuracy and make any adjustments as needed.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > AI video > 9. Generate video:
The Generate button starts the process of rendering your video into a final version with all avatars, voiceovers, animations, transitions, and other customizations applied. Then, you can close the AI Video Editor tab and access the generated video in the course or quick update module’s learning object (LO) for the video. Generation typically takes 10-15 minutes.

Once generated:

- The video becomes available in the module LO.
- It is saved to your selected Content Center folder for reuse in other modules or assets.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > AI video > Feedback:
The Feedback option, available in the (hamburger) menu in the top-left corner, lets you share your experience directly with the product team. You can use it to report issues, suggest new functionality, or provide general comments about the AI Video Editor.

Available options:

- Report a bug : Share details about errors, glitches, or unexpected behavior you encounter while using the editor.
- Feature request : Suggest improvements or new capabilities that would enhance your video creation experience.
- General feedback : Provide broader input on usability, design, or your overall experience with the editor.

When reporting a bug, please include details like your browser and OS, video editor URL, steps to reproduce, expected vs. actual behavior, and any supporting screenshots or recordings. This helps the team continuously improve the editor and ensure it meets your needs.

For each feedback type, you can enhance your submission with:

Screenshot: Use the in-built screenshot tool to capture your screen, highlight specific areas, and add comments before attaching it.

Screen recording: Record your screen directly from the editor to show the issue or workflow in action.

Attach a file: Upload files from your computer (e.g., images, documents) to support your feedback.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Announcements:
Salesforce is implementing a new connected app usage policy, effective September 2, 2025, to enhance security. This update will restrict the use of connected apps that are not installed.

If you have authorised a Mindtickle connected app in Salesforce without installing it, Salesforce does not guarantee long-term support. To avoid disruptions, Salesforce recommends that admins install and approve the required Mindtickle connected apps.

The steps to install the Mindtickle connected apps are below.

1. Sign in to Salesforce as an admin.
2. On the Salesforce homepage, in the left navigation panel, click Apps > Connected Apps > Connected Apps OAuth usage .

The Connected Apps OAuth Usage screen is displayed.

3. Under the Connected App column, click the Install button on the necessary Mindtickle application:

- Mindtickle Salesforce OAuth
- CallAI
- Enable Us by Mindtickle

4. On the displayed pop-up screen, click Install.

For information on the Salesforce connected app policy change updates, see Prepare for Connected App Usage Restrictions Change.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Announcements > Frequently asked questions (FAQ):
1. Why is this change required now? Due to recent privacy incidents, Salesforce has enforced new policies on app usage with immediate effect. For more information, see the Manage Access to a Connected App article.
2. How can I see which user authorised the apps? A. On the Salesforce homepage, in the left navigation panel, click Apps > Connected Apps > Connected Apps OAuth usage . B. Review the Actions column. If an app is not installed, the Install button is displayed. The User Count column displays the number of users active on the app. C. Click the number to view detailed user information for an app. The number of users using the app, the first connection date, the last used date, and their usage count are displayed.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Release Notes > Enhancements > Featured hubs widget: New option to select specific hubs for display:
The Featured hubs widget has been enhanced to give admins greater flexibility and control over what hubs are displayed. In addition to showcasing all featured hubs (previous behavior), admins can now choose to display specific hubs, control their order, and tailor the widget’s appearance based on the context of each page where it's added. To reflect these new capabilities, the widget has been renamed from Featured hubs to Featured or selected hubs.

This widget can be added to learning site homepages, series overview pages, and hub and sales play overview pages.

Previously, the widget displayed all featured hubs from the site, with no ability to filter, reorder, or customize. This limited its usefulness in highlighting strategic or contextually relevant hubs.

Key improvements

Admins can now choose between two configuration options:

- Featured hubs (retains previous behavior)
- Selected hubs (new)

If selected hubs is chosen, admins can configure the following:

- Select specific hubs : Choose up to 25 hubs to display. Learners will only see hubs they have access to.
- Custom display order : Use drag-and-drop to arrange hubs in the desired sequence.
- Add description : Include an optional description below the widget title to provide context.

Widget title: For either option, admins can configure the widget title/name in the Settings tab to reflect its purpose (e.g., “Sales Enablement Hubs” or “Regional Onboarding”). By default, the title will match the selected option (featured or selected hubs).

You can update the widget settings, including the hub selection (Featured or Selected), at any time.

Note:

- Existing pages using the Featured hubs widget will continue to function as before. Admins can edit these widgets to enable the new capabilities.
- Mobile support for these enhancements will go live with the September mobile release.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Release Notes > Enhancements > Content Center–SharePoint Sync: Introducing Entra ID Authentication, replacing ACS:
Mindtickle Content Center integrates with Microsoft SharePoint to automatically sync files and folders. Updates made in SharePoint are reflected in the Content Center and everywhere the content is used — including modules, assets, and digital sales rooms (DSRs).

What’s changing?

- The legacy Azure ACS (client secret-based) authentication is being retired by Microsoft and replaced with Entra ID (certificate-based app-only) authentication for all new and migrated SharePoint syncs.
- New SharePoint syncs now use Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure AD) authentication by default. As part of setting up the account, admins configure a new Entra ID app, generate a certificate in Mindtickle and upload it to the Entra app, assign the required API permissions, and, if needed, grant site-specific access for site-level or team site syncs.
- Existing syncs using ACS will continue to work until April 2, 2026 , but must be migrated to Entra ID before that date. In the SharePoint sync settings, admins can use the “Switch to new authentication” option to migrate. The migration requires performing the same steps as a new sync (creating an Entra app, configuring the certificate and permissions). Folder mappings, metadata sync, and sync frequency/notifications are preserved. Note : Once migrated, a sync cannot be reverted to the old ACS authentication .

Benefits

- Aligns with Microsoft’s latest security best practices.
- Ensures long-term support and uninterrupted sync of SharePoint content.
- Provides a certificate-based, more secure authentication mechanism that is compatible with tenant-level, site-level, and team site-level syncs.

Action required

- No immediate action is required for existing syncs; they will continue working until April 2, 2026.
- Admins should plan to migrate existing ACS-based syncs to Entra ID well before the retirement deadline to ensure uninterrupted content sync.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Release Notes > Enhancements > Introducing multi-chat functionality in Seller Copilot:
We’re enhancing Seller Copilot with a multi-chat experience on the web and in Salesforce, making it easier than ever to manage multiple conversations while keeping context intact.

Previously, Copilot supported only a single chat thread, which made it harder to separate topics or start new conversations. With this release, users can now create and manage multiple chat threads, allowing sales reps and managers to organize their workflows just like they would in other modern AI chat tools — whether they are working on the learning site or directly inside Salesforce.

What’s new

Seller Copilot now includes full multi-chat functionality:

- Create : Start new chats anytime using the New chat button in the Copilot interface.
- Automatic naming : Each new chat is auto-titled based on your first query, making it easier to identify later.
- Access past chats : Access any past conversation from a new left-hand navigation panel.
- Search : Use the search bar to find chats by name. Note : Search is currently limited to chat titles only. Searching within chat content will be available in a future release.
- Rename or delete chats : Rename chats to keep them organized and easy to find. Delete chats to remove old or irrelevant conversations (confirmation required).

Your chat history stays saved and instantly accessible, letting you switch between topics without losing progress.

Benefits

This release brings significant improvements to how you work with Copilot:

- Smarter context management : Keep separate threads for different topics, deals, or customers.
- Greater productivity : Save time by quickly finding and revisiting past chats instead of starting over.
- Modern experience : Manage conversations the way you’re used to in other AI chat tools.
- Cross-platform consistency: Work seamlessly on the learning site or directly within Salesforce.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > AI Interactive roleplay (Beta) > For admins > Create a mission:
To create a roleplay mission:

1. On the admin site homepage, click the Training > Series .
2. From the Series page, click Create > Module to create a mission.
3. On the Add modules pop-up, hover over the Mission tile and click Create mission . Note : You cannot create interactive missions using Mindtickle Copilot . Alternatively, use the Mindtickle copilot within the module workflow to set up AI roleplays.
4. Enter your mission name and select the series in which you want to place it. If you don't want to place it in an existing series, create a new series by clicking the Create a New Series link. Then, click Next .
5. Choose Video roleplay under the Select mission type option. Then, click Next . Note : AI Roleplay - AI Scenario Creator is only applicable to Video roleplay missions.
6. Select roleplay style : You have two options:
  1. Practice solo : When you create a mission using the One-way method, you do not get Copilot assistance. For more information on how to create the mission, see Build tab > Video Roleplay Mission .
  2. Practice with avatar: Select this option to create a mission where learners practice conversation skills with an AI avatar.
7. Click Create mission .

The avatar responds based on how well the learner shows empathy, handles the issue, and navigates challenging conversational behaviors.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > AI Interactive roleplay (Beta) > For admins > Learner brief > Brief for the learner:
Add a description of the mission to help the learner understand the objective and the approach they should take while submitting their roleplay. For more information on adding guidelines for learners, see Guidelines for learner.

The admins can type in a detailed description if they have it handy. Alternatively, they can click Generate brief and use the Mindtickle Copilot assistant to generate a detailed description for the learner. The Copilot asks a series of questions to gather all the necessary information for the roleplay scenario.

These questions cover details such as the buyer's persona, the prospect company and industry, and key decision-makers involved in the scenario.

Based on your answers, the Copilot automatically generates a comprehensive learner brief. This brief includes background information, the scenario's goals, and all key details the learner needs to understand and practice the roleplay effectively.

You can then review the generated learner brief to ensure it correctly reflects your intended scenario. This ensures the learner understands the expectations and objectives from the associated roleplay training before attempting it.

Once you answer the Copilot questions and the brief is generated, click Confirm to copy the content under the Brief for the learners option. After you have clicked Confirm, you can make the necessary edits.

Note:

- If Copilot is not generating the desired results, you can use the Start over option to restart the instruction generation.
- Use the Hide option to close the Copilot window.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > AI Interactive roleplay (Beta) > For admins > Avatar instructions > Generate Instructions:
Click Generate instructions to use the Copilot to create the scenario. Copilot asks guided, context-based questions to create tailored avatar instructions for a realistic roleplay scenario.

The guided inquiry questions are contextually relevant to the roleplay conversation type and cover details necessary to meet the use-case needs, such as the avatar’s behavior, objective, context, and conversation guidelines for interacting with the learner in the roleplay.

Users are always assisted with dynamic and contextual suggestions, which provide appropriate and relevant responses to help users find a suitable response if they are unsure.

As you answer each guided question, you can enter a detailed response of up to 4,000 characters (about 500–600 words). A character counter shows how much space you have left as you type, so you can provide rich context in a single response without having to shorten it.

Based on your responses, the Copilot automatically generates a detailed avatar instruction for the roleplay scenario.

Click the Duplicate option on an existing profile to create a custom profile for the mission.After you have selected a copilot profile, add Instructions for the copilot.

Select who will start the conversation

Select who begins the roleplay.

- If you select Avatar, the conversation starts with a greeting message and ends with a closing message, both of which you type for the avatar.
- If you select Learner, the avatar will wait for the learner to start the conversation.

Instructions for Avatar

Define the roleplay scenario from the avatar's point of view and how the avatar should behave during the roleplay. Specify the objectives, conversation guidelines, and the situational context in which they operate. Include what the avatar already knows before the conversation and what they want to achieve.

These details enable the avatar to respond dynamically and naturally to the learner’s input, making the conversation realistic.

Define the following:

- Context : Describe the conversation's background, including avatar and learner roles, organization industry, and interaction reason. This sets the tone and direction of the dialogue. For instance, specify if the avatar is a potential customer, a manager giving feedback, or a collaborating partner.
- Avatar’s objectives : State what the avatar aims to accomplish in the conversation.
- Constraints or challenges : Describe the realistic limitations or pressures the avatar faces to help learners demonstrate real-world problem-solving skills.
- Success criteria : Explain what needs to happen for the avatar to agree to a next step, such as scheduling a follow-up meeting, requesting a demo, or reviewing a proposal.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Release Notes > New features > Mission API to migrate learner data for email and task evaluations:
The new Mission Learner Data Migration API enables seamless migration of learner mission data, specifically for email and task evaluation missions. It transfers completion status, reviewer scores, timestamps, and submission details from an old user ID to a new one across all module IDs, ensuring continuity when learner identities change due to organizational restructuring, mergers, or user ID updates. The migration runs asynchronously and returns a workflowID to track job status.

The API migration job transfers:

- Completion status of email and task evaluation missions
- Reviewer details and scores
- Submission and completion timestamps
- Submission-related details associated with the missions

Note: If the old user has not started or submitted a mission, the status is retained as “Not Started” in the new user’s record. Modules already completed by the new user are excluded from migration to prevent overwriting existing progress. The “Attempted” status is only carried over when the old user has made some progress and the new user has not yet started.

API details

- Endpoint: POST /api/migrate/user_data (POST)
- Authentication: Bearer token via Authorization header
- Concurrency: Processes up to 5 migration jobs concurrently
- Timeouts: 60 seconds for HTTP operations; 10 seconds for database operations
- Retry policy: Up to 5 retries with exponential backoff (1s to 1000s)
- Processing: Returns immediately with workflowID ; migration executes in background.
- Rate limits: 5 requests per second, 220 requests per minute, and 3000 requests per hour

Caveats and limitations

- The API response confirms job acceptance but does not indicate completion; migration occurs asynchronously.
- Migration applies to complete mission data for the specified modules, not partial data fields.
- Both old and new user IDs must be active and exist in the system for the migration to succeed.
- Invitation timestamps for modules already present under the new user ID will not be updated during migration; this will be addressed in a future release.
- Migration jobs are processed with a concurrency limit of 5 workers to ensure system stability.

Error handling

The API detects and reports errors such as workflow service unavailability, job enqueue failures, worker processing errors, and database issues. It provides descriptive error messages and employs a retry mechanism with exponential backoff to improve success rates.

For more information, see Learner mission data migration API.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Release Notes > New features > Global Search API to search learning site content from external tools:
The new Global Search API enables third-party applications to perform global searches across Mindtickle learning site content, including modules, files, series, and assets. Currently, Mindtickle’s global search is accessible only via the learning site on the web app (browser) and mobile apps (iOS and Android). This API opens up access to these search capabilities for external tools by accepting natural language queries with filters and pagination, returning ranked results based on relevance.

This API empowers customers to embed Mindtickle global search inside CRMs, collaboration platforms, AI assistants, and other systems, extending search beyond the Mindtickle learning site.

Key features

- Enables global search across multiple content types on the learning site, such as modules, files, series, assets.
- Supports filtering by module types and tags for precise queries.
- Returns ranked results based on semantic relevance scores.
- Supports pagination with cursor-based navigation, limited to 50 results per page.
- Provides total counts per entity type in the response.

API details

- Endpoint : POST /v1/global-search
- Authentication : Bearer token via Authorization header
- Request payload :
  - username (string, required) — the user performing the search
  - search_text (string, required) — natural language search query
  - entities (array, required) — specifies entity types (modules, files, etc.) and filters
  - pagination (object, optional) — page size (max 50) and cursor for paging
- Response : Returns search results with metadata, counts by entity type, and pagination info. Maximum of 50 results per page (page size ≤ 50).
- Rate limits : 600 requests per minute, 3000 requests per hour per account

Error handling

Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Release Notes > Enhancements > Direct content upload to My Assets for reps:
Reps can now directly upload personalized content, such as presentations, PDFs, and videos, into the Assets > My assets page on the learning site. This enhancement removes the dependency on the Mix & Match flow and enables reps to more efficiently manage, share, and track engagement on self-created collateral. It streamlines content workflow, allowing reps to quickly bring in their own content and leverage platform-native sharing and analytics capabilities.

Until now, uploading content to My assets required going through the Mix & Match flow, which was better suited for building new presentations than for quickly uploading existing materials. This enhancement introduces a direct upload path, making it easier for sellers to bring in their own content and track engagement without extra steps.

Note: This feature is not enabled by default. To enable it for your Mindtickle instance, please contact your CSM or Mindtickle Support.

New upload option

If the feature is enabled for your Mindtickle instance, the new Upload new file option appears in the Create asset button. This option is available on the Assets page and within a hub. Sellers can upload one file at a time, either from their computer or supported cloud storage.

When uploading from the Assets page, sellers are prompted to choose a personal hub, while uploads initiated within a hub automatically select that hub as the destination.

Sellers can view engagement metrics like views and time spent on any shared asset, while admins access usage reports and can impersonate reps to see assets from their perspective.

Note:

- Various file formats including documents, images, audio, and video are supported; however, embedded link type of assets are not supported.
- Uploading from mobile devices or tablets is currently not supported; however, you can view the My assets page on tablets (in landscape).

Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Release Notes > Enhancements > Restricting duplicate assets within the same hub:
This enhancement prevents duplicate published assets within the same hub. Previously, the system allowed multiple assets in a hub to share the same name or link to the same Content Center file, which led to redundant, confusing, and messy asset lists.

With this release, Mindtickle proactively blocks duplicate creation, helps admins identify and clean up existing duplicates, and enforces duplicate checks across all key asset workflows.

Why this change

In large or shared hubs, multiple collaborators often created assets with identical names or linked to the same Content Center file. Automated syncs could also lead to unintentional duplicates, since file names in cloud storage systems like Google Drive are not unique.

This caused significant clutter and confusion for admins and made it difficult to identify the right assets, and reps faced multiple versions of the same content.

Benefits

This enhancement addresses duplicate asset issues with the following key improvements:

- Prevents duplicates by blocking asset creation with a duplicate name or file.
- Simplifies cleanup by highlighting existing duplicates for quick bulk removal.
- Protects bulk actions by excluding or resolving duplicates before publishing, mirroring, or moving.
- Keeps hubs clean by avoiding future duplicates and removing existing ones.
- Reduces admin errors with built-in validation for consistent content handling.
- Improves rep experience by reducing clutter and making content easier to find and use.

What’s new

A. Duplicate definition

Within the same hub, two published assets are considered duplicates if they:

- Use the same Content Center file - this is considered duplication by file .
- Have the same name (case-insensitive) – this is considered duplication by name .

Note: Duplicate validation applies only to published assets. Draft assets can have duplicate names or files, but validation will be enforced upon publishing.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Release Notes > Enhancements > Restricting duplicate assets within the same hub:
Draft assets can have duplicate names or files, but validation will be enforced upon publishing.

B. Duplicate validation coverage

The system now performs duplicate checks across the following flows:

- Single or bulk asset creation from the UI
- Bulk asset creation via Excel upload
- Single or bulk mirror operations
- Single or bulk move operations
- Single or bulk publish actions
- Restoring archived assets
- Renaming a published asset
- Replacing a file using Replace file in asset only (not replacing the file in Content Center)

Note: For draft assets, these checks are applied only while publishing. Other draft actions (rename, move, mirror, or replace file) do not trigger duplicate validation.

C. Validation behavior and feedback

- When a duplicate is detected, the system displays clear error messages such as:
  - “Asset with the same name already exists in this hub.”
  - “Asset with the same file is already published in one or more hubs.”
- Admins can click the message link to open a filtered view showing the conflicting assets (either by name or file). This lets them quickly review existing assets and decide whether to rename, delete, or archive.
- For bulk actions (create, move, mirror, publish):
  - Duplicate-related failures appear in the Notifications panel with precise failure reasons.
  - When uploading via Excel, the generated failure sheet lists each failed asset with the duplicate reason.

D. Duplicate discovery and cleanup

Automatic hub-level flag

When an admin opens a hub, a banner automatically indicates if published duplicates exist in that hub — showing the count by both name and file.

- Admins can view duplicates by name or by file .
- Duplicate assets are grouped together for clarity.
- Each group shows asset metadata such as creator, owner, and engagement metrics to help decide which version to retain.
- Admins can take bulk actions (archive or delete) on selected duplicates directly from this view.

Note: To preserve logical groupings, sorting, searching, and filtering are disabled within the duplicate views. Regular filters and sorting options remain available once you return to the standard (ungrouped) asset list.

Edge case handling

- Scope limited to same hub : Duplicate validation applies only within the same hub . Assets across different hubs can share the same name or file ID.
- Mirrored or multi-present assets : When replacing a file in a mirrored asset, the system validates across all hubs where that asset exists to ensure the new file does not already exist in any of those hubs.
- Draft asset movement : If a draft asset is moved or mirrored, validation occurs only against published assets in the destination hub.
- Existing duplicates : The system does not auto-archive existing duplicates. Admins can clean them up using the new duplicate filters.
- Metadata updates : Property updates (like description, tags, or owner) on existing duplicate assets are allowed and do not trigger validation.

Example scenarios

Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Release Notes > Enhancements > Thumbnail management migrated to Content Center:
Important: While this feature is included in the release notes, its rollout for all customers is scheduled for the week of October 20.

This release introduces a significant improvement in how thumbnails are managed across the Mindtickle platform. Thumbnails used across series, modules, hubs, and assets are now managed exclusively through the Content Center. The new uploader lets you upload or select images directly from the Content Center and manage them with ease. All existing thumbnails have been migrated.

This change streamlines workflows, improves governance, and lays the foundation for further content unification across Mindtickle. Previously, thumbnail files were stored exclusively in the MT Library and uploaded using a legacy picker. This created operational inefficiencies and lacked centralized governance.

Migration details

- All newly uploaded thumbnails will be stored in the Content Center by default. Support for the legacy MT Library for thumbnails is now deprecated.
- All existing thumbnails in the MT Library are now automatically migrated to the Content Center under the new Content Center → System Files → Thumbnails folder. Admins do not need to take any manual action for this migration.

Benefits

- Centralized governance : All thumbnails are now stored in one place, improving control and consistency.
- Improved visibility : See exactly where each thumbnail is used across the platform.
- Streamlined workflows : Users no longer need to switch between MT Library and Content Center.
- Easier cleanup : Identify and bulk-delete unused thumbnails with built-in safety checks.
- Future-ready architecture : Lays the groundwork for platform-wide content unification.

What's new

A. Thumbnail management via Content Center
