chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Release Notes > Enhancements > Thumbnail management migrated to Content Center:
Thumbnail management via Content Center

- Thumbnails are now stored in the system-generated Content Center → System Files → Thumbnails folder , which is accessible to all users.
- No manual creation needed; this folder is auto-generated and managed by the platform.
- All newly uploaded thumbnails will be stored here by default.

B. Enhanced thumbnail picker

- The old MT Library picker is replaced with a Content Center file picker .
- Default view: Gallery (with option to switch to list view).
- Thumbnails can be selected from existing files or uploaded afresh via the new uploader.

C. Thumbnail metadata & usage insights

- Using the Locations used column, you can see where the thumbnail file is being used across the platform (series, modules, hubs, and assets).
- This allows admins to trace usage and make informed decisions before deletion or replacement.

D. Improved cleanup & bulk actions

- You can rename, download, and delete thumbnail files and view the file details using Get Info.
- Unused thumbnails ( Locations used = 0 ) can be identified and bulk deleted from the Content Center. Note : System prevents deletion of thumbnail files currently in use, files with insufficient permissions, files synced from external folders, and files that are open or locked.

Caveats and limitations

- Selecting the same image from non-thumbnail folders creates a new copy in the Thumbnails folder. This will be fixed in a future release.
- Currently, basic cropping is supported for thumbnail images. More advanced resizing will be available in a future release.
- If a thumbnail originates from a synced folder and that source file changes (e.g., resolution update), the change does not propagate automatically.

For more information, see Upload and manage thumbnails for series, modules, hubs, and assets.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Instructor-Led Training (ILT):
Managers can enroll their team members in training sessions from the ILT Sessions page. Managers can view the ILT sessions that their direct and indirect reportees can access based on the organizational hierarchy.

Note: This feature is not enabled by default. To enable it for your Mindtickle instance, please contact Mindtickle Support.

They can also view the ILT sessions of reportees associated with them through the relationship fields.

This feature allows managers to easily view and enroll team members in training sessions, align training schedules with business needs, and improve the efficiency and impact of training programs.

Note:

- Managers can view the sessions their team members are invited to, as well as the sessions in public series.
- To enable this feature, admins must create a custom profile field, for example, Manager (if it does not exist), and contact Mindtickle Support to map the organizational hierarchy.
- The system utilizes the custom field to identify a manager’s reportees and displays the ILT sessions they can access under the Hierarchy based team tab.
- For managers to view their reportees' ILT sessions in the Relationship-based team tab, learners must link them in their user profile .
- The system utilizes the manager-reportee relationship to display the reportees’ ILT sessions to managers in the Relationship based Team tab.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Instructor-Led Training (ILT) > Caveats:
Managers cannot enroll their reportees in ILT sessions if:

- Sequential locking prevents learners from viewing or self-enrolling in ILT modules until they complete the previous modules.
- Managers can enroll reportees in a session or event only if the learner has access to the ILT module. If a module is locked due to sequential unlocking, the learner will not appear in the enrollment list until they complete the previous modules.
- If the module is a mirrored module and the learner has access to it through another series, the manager can enroll the learner in the session.
- The Restrict learners from enrolling option is enabled for the ILT session in the Enrollments tab of the ILT module’s Settings page.
- If the session is Live , managers cannot enroll their reportees in it.

The ILT Sessions page has the following tabs,

- Hierarchy based team tab
- Relationship based team tab

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Instructor-Led Training (ILT) > Hierarchy based team tab:
This tab enables managers to view the ILT sessions that their direct and indirect reportees can access based on organizational hierarchy.

The system displays the ILT sessions of the manager’s direct reports by default in this tab. Managers can also view the ILT sessions of their indirect reports by using filters in this tab.

Note:

- The system utilizes the Manager field in the learner’s user profile to identify their manager and displays the ILT sessions that the manager’s reportees can access in this tab.
- When a learner links a new manager in their user profile , the system takes two hours to update that manager’s name in the Team of filter in the Hirearchy based team tab.

For example, John is a reporting manager with two direct reports (managers), Sarah and Mark. Jane is another learner who reports to Sarah, and Maria reports to Mark.

- In the Hierarchy based team tab, John can view the ILT sessions of all his reportees (Sarah, Mark, Jane, and Maria), even if he doesn’t have access to the sessions.
- By default, he sees the sessions of his direct reportees, Sarah and Mark. Using the Team of and Learners filters, he can also view the sessions accessible to Jane and Maria, his indirect reportees.

Managers can perform the following actions in the is tab.

- View sessions for a specific date
- View session details
- Copy the session link
- Manage direct reports' enrollment in sessions
- Manage indirect reports' enrollment in sessions
- View learners' attendance in sessions

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Instructor-Led Training (ILT) > Hierarchy based team tab > View sessions for a specific date:
To view the sessions for a specific date.

1. Sign in to the learning site
2. Click Training in the left navigation bar, then click ILT Sessions . The ILT Sessions page is displayed. The system displays the ILT sessions. You can scroll up to view the past sessions and scroll down to view the upcoming sessions. Note:

- If you create ILT sessions in a new series or module, the system takes 5 minutes to update the sessions in the ILT Sessions page.
- If you create ILT sessions in an existing series or module, the sessions are updated instantly in the ILT Sessions page calendar.

3. Click the Hierarchy based team tab.

4. In the Hierarchy based team tab, click Go to date.

The ILT calendar is displayed. The calendar displays the date based on the manager’s system time zone.5. Click on a date to view the scheduled ILT sessions.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Instructor-Led Training (ILT) > Hierarchy based team tab > Manage direct reports' enrollment in sessions:
Managers can manage the enrollment of their direct reports in ILT sessions in the Heirarchy based team tab.

Note: The system displays the ILT sessions of the direct reports by default.

To manage the enrollment of direct reports in sessions,

1. In the ILT Sessions page, click the Hierarchy based team tab. The ILT sessions are displayed. Note: In the Hierarchy based team tab, the system automatically selects the manager’s name in the Team of filter
2. Click the More icon of a session.
3. Click Manage enrollment . The Manage enrollment pop-up screen is displayed.
4. Search for a learner in the search bar.
5. You can apply the following filters to filter the displayed list of learners.

- Enrollment: This option filters learners by their enrollment status. The following options are available.
  - All: This option displays all reportees.
  - Enrolled : This option displays the reportees who are enrolled in the session.
  - Waitlisted : This option displays the reportees who are waitlisted for the session.
- Unenrolled : This option displays the reportees who have unenrolled from the session.
- Groups: This option filters the learners by their user group name.

To remove all filters, click Reset.

6. Click Enroll on a learner to enroll them in the ILT session.

The system updates the Enrolled/waitlisted on and the Status column of the learner upon successful enrollment.

7. To remove a learner from a session, click Unenroll.

When enrolling learners, if there are no available seats in a session, the system displays a message indicating that no seats are available.

Managers can manage the enrollment of their indirect reports in ILT sessions in the Heirarchy based team tab.

To manage enrollment of indirect reports in sessions,

1. In the Hierarchy based team tab, click the Team of filter and select a manager's name. The Team of filter lists all managers reporting to the manager based on organizational hierarchy. The Learners filter displays the manager’s reportees.
2. Click the Learners filter and select the checkboxes of the necessary learners to view the ILT sessions to which they have access, and click Apply . You can use the search bar to search for a specific learner. The system displays the ILT sessions to which the selected learners have access. You can scroll up to view the past sessions and scroll down to view the upcoming sessions.
3. Click the More icon of a session to manage reportee enrollment , view session details , copy the session link , or view learners’ attendance in sessions .

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Digital Sales Rooms:
DSR allows admins from a primary organization to create multiple DSR environments for their partners. Admins can configure the partner’s company profile, set room options, and create default templates with consistent branding in the partner DSR environment.

This enables admins to efficiently manage partner environments and track overall sales progress across partner companies.

Note:

- A primary organization is the main company that oversees multiple partner organizations.
- A partner is a company that operates under the primary organization and collaborates with it. For example, a dealership.

Admins from a partner company can also customize their DSR to fit their business requirements. They can select banners, cover images, and thumbnails, manage notifications and permissions, and configure integrations to run sales activities independently.

For example,

Acme, an automotive manufacturer, can create a separate DSR environment for each dealership to manage sales. Each dealer’s environment is unique, allowing sales reps to manage leads, track deals, and access training materials.Dealers cannot see other dealerships’ data, ensuring privacy and security, while Acme can monitor overall performance and usage across all dealer DSRs.

Note:

- To enable the multi-organization support feature in DSR, admins must create a custom profile field , such as Dealership ID , in their learning site (if it doesn’t exist) and share it with Mindtickle Support for mapping. The Dealership ID is only an example; you can create a custom profile field and label it as necessary.
- The system creates a DSR environment for each partner’s Dealership ID .
- The system assigns the DSR users and admins with a Dealership ID in their profile to the corresponding partner’s DSR environment.
- If a DSR user’s Dealership ID field is empty, the system adds the user to the primary organization.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Digital Sales Rooms > Benefits:
The following are the benefits of creating multiple DSR environments for partners.

- Enhanced Data Security: Ensure sensitive data is accessible only to authorized users.
- Centralized Management: Simplify partner management by centralizing management of multiple partners while maintaining data separation and integrity.
- Scalability: provides a flexible and scalable platform for managing multiple organizations.
- Enhanced Collaboration: Improves collaboration between the main organization and its partners while maintaining data integrity and accuracy.
- Customizable environment: Enables the customization of the partner environment to suit the specific business needs of partner companies.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Digital Sales Rooms > Configure a partner’s DSR > Set up room templates > Create new templates:
Admins from primary organizations can create new, consistently branded room templates as default templates for their partner companies.

Note: Partners can also create templates for their DSR environments; however, they cannot modify or delete the default templates created by the primary organization.

To create new templates,

1. Click Rooms on the left navigation pane and then click Templates . The Templates screen is displayed.
2. Click the Partners tab to view all partner templates. The system displays the available partner templates.
3. To create a new template, click Create template . The Create Sales Room Template screen is displayed.
4. In the Template name field, enter a name for the new partner template.
5. In the Template description field, describe the template, state its objective, and specify its intended users (e.g., Enablement Team, Sales Operations). This helps ensure consistent and correct use in the partner DSR.
6. In Visibility , click the Partner radio button.
7. Click Next Step .
8. On the Create Sales Room Template page, add content to start building the template. Configure the room settings , add a banner image , section headers , sales actions , and create a welcome message . For detailed information on creating a new room template, see Create a room template .
9. After setting up the new room template, click Create Template . The system adds the new template to the Partners tab in the Templates screen.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Digital Sales Rooms > Configure a partner’s DSR > Set up room templates > Clone an existing template:
Admins can create room templates by cloning existing templates. This allows admins to save time and quickly build new templates by reusing a template’s structure and format.

To clone an existing template,

1. On the Partners tab of the Templates screen, click the More options icon on the template you want to create a template from and click Clone . In the Clone Room Template pop-up, enter the following.
2. In the Template name , enter a name for the new template.
3. In the Template description , enter a description for the template.
4. In Visibility , click the Partner radio button.
5. Click Clone Template . The system adds the cloned template to the Templates screen. Note: The default room settings of the base template are copied over to the cloned template. You can customize the cloned template by clicking the More options icon and selecting the Edit option. For detailed information on setting up templates, see Create a room template .

4. In Visibility , click the Partner radio button.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Digital Sales Rooms > Add a recording to an existing room:
To add a Call AI recording to existing rooms,

1. Sign in to the learning site.

2. Click the Call AI in the left navigation pane and then click Recordings.

The Recordings page is displayed.

3. To add a recording to a room, click the Share icon on the recording and select Share via room.

Or

On the Recordings page, click on a meeting recording to open, then click the Share button and select Share via room.

4. In the Select a room to share your recording screen, you can use the search bar to find a specific room.

5. To filter the displayed rooms, use the following options.

- All Rooms: This option displays all the rooms to which you have access.
- Rooms rolling up to me: This option displays the rooms of your team members.
- My rooms: This option displays the rooms you own.
- Status: This option displays the room by its status. The following options are available,
  - Published: This option displays only the published rooms.
  - Draft: This option displays the draft rooms.
- Teams: This option filters the rooms by team name.
- Owner: This option filters the rooms by the room owner's name.
- Template: This option filters the rooms by room template.

6. To sort the displayed rooms, use the following options,

- Updated at: This option sorts the rooms by their last update date.
- Room name: This option sorts the rooms by the room name.
- Room owner: option sorts the rooms by the room owner's name.

7. Click Select on a room to add the recording.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Set Up and Content Management:
Mindtickle supports integration with Glean. Glean is an enterprise search application that allows users to search for Mindtickle training content across various sources, including Confluence, Google Drive, Dropbox, Mindtickle, and Salesforce.

Users can search for the following Mindtickle training content in Glean.

- Series: Title and description.
- Modules: Title, description, and module tags.
- Assets: Title, description, and asset attributes.
- Hubs: Title and description.

Note: When searching for Mindtickle training content, Glean searches only the Title, Description, and Tags of files in series, modules, assets, and hubs. It doesn’t search for terms inside content files (such as PDFs). For example, if a term exists only within a content file like a PDF, Glean doesn’t show it in the search results.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Set Up and Content Management > Set up the integration:
Contact your Customer Success Manager (CSM) or Mindtickle Support for details on the steps and configuration required to set up the Mindtickle-Glean integration.

1. Create the Mindtickle data source in your Glean instance with the following parameters.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| name | Mindtickle |
| displayName | Mindtickle |
| datasourceCategory | KNOWLEDGE_HUB |
| urlRegex | ^<LS URL>.For example, ^https://acme.mindtickle.* |
| isUserReferencedByEmail | TRUE |

2. After setting up the data source, share the following details with the Mindtickle Support team to enable the integration.

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Display Name | Name used to identify the data source in Mindtickle.For example: Mindtickle. |
| Host | Glean server instance URL.For example: https://xxxx.glean.com/ |
| Base API Path | Base API endpoint for indexing and data access.For example: https://xxxx.glean.com/api/index/v1/ |
| Bearer Token | Authentication token used to authorize API requests. |

Note: Contact Mindtickle Support if you have any questions or face any issues during the setup.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Asset Hub > Admin:
This article provides information on how Mindtickle restricts duplicate assets within the same hub and how admins can manage and clean up duplicates.

Asset Hub now prevents duplicate published assets within the same hub. This ensures hubs remain clean and organized, reduces confusion for admins, and makes it easier for sellers to find the right content. The system automatically blocks new duplicates, highlights existing duplicates for cleanup, and enforces duplicate checks across all key asset workflows.

The duplicate asset restriction ensures that each hub contains a unique set of published assets. Admins have visibility into existing duplicates, can clean them up in bulk, and benefit from automatic validation that keeps hubs consistent and organized.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Asset Hub > Admin > Duplicate validation coverage:
Duplicate checks are enforced across these workflows:

- Single or bulk asset creation from the UI
- Bulk asset creation using Excel upload
- Single or bulk mirror operations
- Single or bulk move operations
- Single or bulk publish actions
- Restoring archived assets
- Renaming a published asset
- Replacing a file in an asset only (not replacing the file in Content Center)

Note: For draft assets, validation runs only during publishing. Other actions like renaming, moving, or mirroring drafts do not trigger duplicate checks.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Asset Hub > Admin > Validation behavior and feedback:
- If a duplicate is detected, the system displays a clear error message:
  - “Asset with the same name already exists in this hub.”
  - “Asset with the same file is already published in one or more hubs.”
- Admins can click the message link to open a filtered view showing conflicting assets, grouped by name or file.
- For bulk actions, the Notifications panel lists all failed items with specific reasons, such as “Duplicate by name” or “Duplicate by file ID.”
- For Excel uploads, the failure sheet lists each failed asset and its duplicate reason.

Admins can view duplicates in two ways:

- By name: Groups assets with the same name
- By file: Groups assets linked to the same Content Center file

Each group displays metadata such as creator, owner, and engagement metrics to help decide which version to retain. Selected assets can be archived or deleted in bulk.

Note: Sorting, filtering, and searching are disabled within duplicate views to preserve logical grouping. Returning to the standard hub view restores these options.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Asset Hub > Admin > Edge case handling:
- Scope limitation: Duplicate validation applies only within the same hub; assets across different hubs can share the same name or Content Center file.
- Mirrored or multi-present assets: Replacing a file in a mirrored asset checks all hubs where it exists. The replacement is blocked if the file already exists in any of those hubs.
- Draft asset movement: Moving or mirroring a draft asset validates only against published assets in the destination hub.
- Existing duplicates: The system does not automatically remove duplicates; admins must clean them up using the duplicate view.
- Metadata updates: Editing title, owner, tags, or description for existing duplicates is allowed and does not trigger validation.

- Bulk mirror or move: Assets that would cause duplicates fail and are listed in the feedback panel; others complete successfully.
- Bulk publish from drafts: Duplicate drafts fail validation; valid drafts are published normally.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Content Center > Cropping thumbnails:
After selecting or uploading a thumbnail, you can adjust the crop directly within the platform — no external editing tools required. Refer to the annotated image below for guidance on how to adjust the crop.

Key features

- Integrated cropping & resizing : Users can now position and crop images directly within the tool. Whether you want to use a specific area or the entire image, you have full control over the composition.
- Fixed aspect ratio (3:2) : To ensure visual consistency across the platform, the cropping tool locks the crop frame to the required 3:2 aspect ratio (for example: 1500 x 1000 pixels). You can resize this selection box, but the shape will remain fixed.
- Canvas & background handling : The interface provides a fixed canvas for your image. Note : If you extend the crop selection beyond your image boundaries into the empty background, the system will automatically fill that area with white space in the final thumbnail.
- Platform-wide support : These enhancements apply everywhere thumbnails are used, including series, modules, hubs, and assets.

Note:Please ensure your file is a .png, .jpg, or .jpeg and does not exceed 10 MB. For details, see What image formats does Mindtickle support?.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle APIs > Training APIs:
The Mission Learner Data Migration API enables administrators to transfer mission progress from one user ID to another. Designed specifically for email and task evaluation missions, this API is essential for preserving learning history during organizational transitions, mergers, or internal ID updates.

Key capabilities include:

- Data migration: Transfers mission completion status, reviewer scores, timestamps, and submission metadata across all module IDs.
- Conflict resolution: Intelligent logic ensures that modules already completed by the new user are excluded from migration to prevent overwriting existing progress.
- Status preservation: Carries over "Attempted" status if the new user has not yet started the mission; otherwise, not started missions remain "Not Started."
- Asynchronous processing: Operations run in the background and return a workflowId for tracking the status.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle APIs > Training APIs > Backdated invitations:
When migrating users or recording past progress, invite dates must align with completion dates. The migration workflow automatically supports backdated invitations using an epoch timestamp, ensuring migrated completions are accepted and rewards are calculated correctly.

- For new users who are not already invited to the module, the system automatically creates a backdated invitation that matches the old user’s original invite timestamp. This ensures that historical completion data is processed correctly.
- If the new user is already invited to the module, the existing invitation timestamp is not modified during migration. Updating existing invitation dates is planned for a future release.

For additional context on backdated invitations in general, see the "Backdated series invitation" and "Backdated module invitation" sections in User APIs.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle APIs > Search APIs:
The Global Search API enables customers to programmatically search content available on the Mindtickle learning site — the same global search capability that’s accessible via the Mindtickle web and mobile apps.

This API allows developers to integrate search capabilities into third-party tools like CRMs, enablement hubs, AI assistants, or internal portals by querying Mindtickle content using natural language search. The results are returned in a structured format ranked by semantic relevance.

What can you search?

The API enables searches across a variety of entities (types of content) available on the Mindtickle learning site. Think of entities as categories or types of content on the platform. We have also provided entity-related filters so you can view results by one or more entities.

- Assets : Asset name, description, attributes, asset file content, and the hub names where the asset resides
- Modules : Module name and description
- Tags : Tags applied to modules only. Tags applied to files, questions, polls, and evaluation parameters (for missions and coaching sessions) are currently not supported.
- Files : File name and file content
- Series : Series name and description
- Asset Hub : Hub name, description, and overview page content
- Peers (colleagues) : Name, username, and email address

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Digital Sales Rooms:
The Geo-target Consent Request allows room visitors to give consent for GDPR and privacy compliance. This enables the system to track and manage the engagement data of room visitors in DSRs securely and transparently.

When you visit a DSR for the first time, the We value your privacy pop-up screen is displayed.

You can click the Privacy Policy link in the pop-up screen to view the terms and conditions of the privacy policy.

1. Click Continue to open the DSR. The DSR opens.
2. If you click Start a conversation to send messages in the room, the Please enter your email to continue pop-up screen is displayed.
3. In Email , enter your email address to send messages to room visitors.
4. Click Continue to open the DSR. Otherwise, click Cancel .

The sections below explain the geo-target experience for new visitors in.

- Rooms with an email requirement
- Rooms with email and passcode requirements
- Rooms with email, pin, and passcode requirements

Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Release Notes > New features > Create multiple DSR environments for partners:
With this release, DSR admins can create and configure multiple DSR environments for partners, complete with preset profiles, room options, and default templates, with consistent branding. This feature enables admins to easily manage partner DSRs and track partner usage of DSRs for deals.

Note:

- To enable the multi-organization support feature in DSR, admins must create a custom profile field, such as Dealership ID , in their learning site (if it doesn’t exist) and share it with Mindtickle Support for mapping. The Dealership ID is only an example; you can create a custom profile field and label it as necessary.
- The system creates a DSR environment for each partner’s Dealership ID .
- The system assigns the DSR users and admins with a Dealership ID in their profile to the corresponding partner’s DSR environment.
- If a DSR user’s Dealership ID field is empty, the system adds the user to the primary organization.

The partner companies can also customize their DSR to suit their specific business requirements.

For more information, see Create multiple DSR environments for partners.

Scorecards enable admins to define clear scoring parameters, ensuring that every conversation is assessed based on its call type. With structured scoring and deeper insights, managers can quickly identify strong calls, pinpoint areas for improvement, and deliver targeted coaching to enhance overall representative performance.

Key benefits:

- Contextual scoring tailored to each call type and purpose.
- Consistent evaluation across teams for fair and clear assessments.
- Actionable insights that support stronger coaching and performance development.
- Customizable scoring criteria aligned with your business needs.

For more information, see Scorecards.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Release Notes > Enhancements > Managers can now assign training content directly from the Command Center:

Managers can assign either full training series or individual modules using the Assign content option in the Training summary widget. Managers can only assign content from series where admins have added them as collaborators.

This enhancement removes dependency on admins, accelerates learning interventions, and allows managers to act immediately on real-time coaching insights. With controlled self-serve assignment capabilities, teams benefit from faster, more personalized, and more relevant development experiences.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Release Notes > Enhancements > Managers can now assign training content directly from the Command Center:
- Assign training directly from the Command Center Managers can now assign full series or individual modules (such as courses, quick updates, missions, assessments, and ILTs) directly to their team members. Assignments can be made from the Command Center on both the web and the Mindtickle mobile app, via the Training widget → Assign training option.
- Admin-controlled access & governance Admins control which training series managers can assign by adding them as collaborators through the series collaborator feature. A new permission, Assign Content to Reportees , has been added to the Manager role by default. This permission works specifically with the series collaborator feature: once a manager is added as a collaborator to a series, they can assign content from that series, ensuring strong governance and controlled access.
- Enhanced rep experience Reps receive notifications when new training is assigned and can view all manager-assigned content within the Training section. Full series assignments appear under Training → Series → Assigned , while individual module assignments appear under Training → Modules → Assigned . Completion progress is automatically updated in real time and reflected back in the Command Center for managers.
- Integrated tracking in the Command Center Managers can track all assigned content within the Command Center, including completion progress, percentages, and actionable insights, enabling timely follow-ups and more effective coaching.

Value and impact

For managers

- Assign training instantly based on coaching insights to close skill gaps faster.
- Reduce dependency on admins for routine assignments, saving time.
- Track assignments and progress in the Command Center.

For admins

- Maintain governance through collaborator-based access and the Assign Content to Reportees permission.
- Cut operational overhead and manual assignment work.
- See which content managers assign and how teams engage.

For reps (sellers)

Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Release Notes > Enhancements > Copilot Assistant in global search now connected to Seller Copilot:
This release introduces major improvements to the Copilot Assistant for Sellers, the AI-powered response embedded directly in global search results. Previously, the in-search Copilot provided inline answers as a standalone response, with no continuity into the main Seller Copilot interface.

With this update, the Copilot Assistant is fully connected to the broader Seller Copilot experience. Users can seamlessly transition from an in-search answer into a full chat, carry context forward, and explore follow-up questions naturally.

Image A: Copilot Assistant for Sellers response within global search

Image B: Continue with Copilot to open a full Seller Copilot chat

Key changes

- Continue into a full chat thread : The in-search Copilot response provides a complete, inline answer tied to the current search. You can engage further by selecting a suggested follow-up question beneath the answer or by using Continue with Copilot . Both actions navigate to Seller Copilot and transition the interaction into a full chat thread, which is saved in recent chats.
- Close the in-search Copilot response : You can now close/hide the in-search Copilot Assistant response using the ( Close ) button, allowing you to focus solely on the standard search results.

These enhancements turn the in-search Copilot answer from a one-off response into the starting point of a continuous, contextual conversation.

Benefits

- Creates a seamless, connected experience : Users can seamlessly move from an inline answer in global search into a full Copilot chat without copying information or switching tools.
- Boosts seller productivity : Every search can evolve into a contextual, continuous conversation, enabling faster insights and more efficient decision-making.

Note:

Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Release Notes > Enhancements > Earn certificates for public and scoped public series without subscribing:
With this release, learners who meet all certification criteria for public and scoped public series can earn certificates for the series without needing to subscribe to them.

For a private or invite-only series, learners must have access to the series and meet all certification criteria to receive the certificate.

For mirrored modules:

- If a mirrored module belongs to a public series and an invite-only series that you can access. Completing the module in the public series earns you certification for both the public and invite-only series.
- If a mirrored module belongs to a public series and an invite-only series to which you do not have access. Completing the module in the public series earns you a certificate only for the public series, not for the invite-only series.

Note:

- You must enable the Access-Based Certifications feature to enable series certification without a subscription for public, scoped public, and invite-only series.
- Contact Mindtickle Support to enable this feature for your learning site.

For more information, see Earn and manage series certifications.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Advanced reports > Data refresh frequency:
The data in all advanced reports is updated every 6 hours.

This refresh cycle represents the time required to process and display the latest platform activities, including content creation, learner consumption, and engagement metrics.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Advanced reports > Create an advanced report:
1. Sign in to the admin site.
2. Navigate to Analytics → My analytics → Custom created . Then, click Create new → Advanced report to get started.
3. On the report templates page, choose a template that suits your reporting needs (e.g., learner-centric, module-centric, or series-focused). Click Use template . For a complete list of available templates, see the “ Report templates ” section.
4. The report template opens in edit mode by default, allowing you to configure existing widgets, add new widgets, adjust existing filters, add new filters, and then publish the report. All changes are autosaved.
5. Use the report features to select a report mode and customize widgets and filters. You can also resize widgets and add or manage filters to control the report’s data. For an overview of the report features and functionalities, see the “ Report features overview ” section.
6. Add new widgets or edit existing ones using the + Widget button. For detailed steps on selecting fields, configuring options, choosing widget types, and using advanced configuration, see the Widgets and filters in advanced reports article.
7. Drag widget edges or corners to adjust size and reposition them on the report canvas for optimal layout.
8. Use the filter panel to add new filters, edit existing ones, configure filter settings, define default filter states, or reset filters to default. Background filters can be set to apply to the entire report.
9. Once configured, publish the report for others to access. The report will be visible to all admins and managers.
10. You can also download the report or any of the widgets.
11. The entire report can be downloaded as PDF. Individual widgets can be downloaded as CSV or image files for offline analysis or sharing. You can also email and share the report with other admins and managers, make a copy (duplicate) of the report, and delete the report.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Advanced reports > Report features overview:
This section provides an overview of the core features available when editing or customizing advanced reports. It covers the key actions you can perform, including selecting a report mode, adding and modifying widgets, adjusting layout and sizing, and creating or managing filters to control the data shown in the report.

Note: Each advanced report acts as a single shared (“source”) version of the report. All admins can access it, but only one can edit it at a time.

Add widget or text: Click the (+ Widget) button to add a new widget to the report. Click the Text (“T”) button to add a text widget. Edit widget and widget actions: Edit or customize any of the added widgets. You can also view widget details and take actions, such as rename, download (image or CSV file), duplicate, and delete the widget. Resize widgets: Drag the widget’s edges or corners to adjust its size. Add and manage filters: Add new filters, edit existing filters, configure filter settings, set the current filter state as your default, or reset filters back to that default. Show/hide filter panel: Click the filter-panel icon to toggle the panel on or off.

It covers selecting data, reviewing suggested visualizations, customizing design and calculations, configuring date or time fields, and finalizing the widget in your report layout. It also includes best practices to help you avoid common issues.

chunks.title: Widgets and filters in advanced reports [admin]

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Advanced reports > Widgets:
1. Navigate to Analytics → My analytics → Custom created → Advanced reports .
2. Open the advanced report to which you want to add widgets and click ( Edit ) to edit the report. Alternatively, under Advanced reports , click → Edit report .
3. Click the ( + Widget ) button to open the widget creation wizard.
4. In the New Widget screen, choose data using suggested fields or the Select Data button : The first screen displays suggested fields based on commonly used or relevant data. You can click a suggested field to add it immediately, or click Select Data to open the full data selection view. You may choose one or multiple fields, and you can expand fields to view available aggregations or numeric behaviors.
5. Use the Select Data option to browse all available fields : This view lists all tables and their fields, allows searching for specific fields, and also shows suggested fields at the top. For details on all available tables and their fields along with descriptions, see the Mindtickle Analytics Data Model sheet .
6. Review and configure field options : When you click a field, it is added with an automatically chosen default field option (aggregation or behavior). Each field shows an icon indicating its data type (e.g., numeric, date, text), helping you identify the right kind of field. Hovering over a field reveals a More menu (or “quick functions”), giving you aggregation and filter options (called “field options”). For numeric fields, the default aggregation might be Sum , but other options include All Items , Count All , Count Unique , Min , Max , Average , etc. For text (string) fields, the default might be All Items , but “More” allows you to choose Count Unique or Filter . If you choose Filter , you can then specify whether you want to include/exclude values, or based on conditions like “is”, “is not”, “contains”, or even define a custom filter.
7. Add additional fields using Add More Data : After selecting the first field, you can continue to pick more using Add More Data (or equivalent action). Each selected field appears as a “pill” at the top of the wizard, showing the field name and its chosen “field option” (aggregation or filter). You can click these pills to edit the field option (change aggregation or filter) or remove the field entirely.
8. Apply field-level filters (if needed) : Apply conditions to fields to include or exclude data points. Filters applied here affect only the widget, not the entire report. You can combine multiple filters for the same field or across multiple fields to focus on relevant data. For numeric fields, you can filter by ranges or specific values. For text fields, you can filter by:
  - Include or exclude specific values.
  - Conditional logic, such as is / is not / contains / does not contain
  - Custom filters combining multiple conditions
9. See available widget types : Once you add at least one field, a panel on the left displays all visualization types compatible with your current field selection. Common types include indicator (used for single-value KPIs), pivot table , bar chart , column chart , line chart , area chart , pie chart , funnel chart , scatter plot , and table .
10. Open Advanced Configuration for deeper customization : The Advanced Configuration panel provides granular control over your widget, allowing you to adjust data, layout, and visual properties beyond the default setup.
  - Field roles and placement: Drag fields into specific roles such as values, categories, series, or rows/columns (for tables and pivot-style widgets).
  - Aggregation and calculations: Adjust aggregation methods (Sum, Average, Min, Max, Count, Count Unique, All Items) or apply custom expressions to individual fields.
  - Filters and conditions: Apply field-level filters, including include/exclude lists, conditional filters (is, is not, contains, custom), or dynamic calculations.
  - Visualization type and orientation: Switch chart types, change orientation (horizontal/vertical), or adjust chart stacking/grouping options.
  - Formatting and styling: Customize labels, number formats, decimal precision, colors, legends, tooltips, gridlines, and axis formatting.
  - Sorting and grouping: Define sorting rules for fields, group data by categories, and configure subtotals/totals for pivot or table views.
  - Advanced table/pivot options: Configure row and column layout, enable row/column totals, control hierarchical grouping, and set aggregation behavior for multiple measures.
  - Preview and adjust: See live updates in the widget preview as you make changes to ensure the configuration displays correctly before adding it to the report.
11. Review the live preview: As you add or change fields, the wizard updates a preview of the widget. The preview reflects both the data and the visualization type, giving you immediate feedback.
12. Give your widget a title: Enter a clear, descriptive name for the widget during or after configuration so it's easily identifiable in the report.
13. Configure date/time granularity (if applicable): If you select a date/time field, you can choose how to break it down by year, quarter, month, week, day, or even hour depending on the data type. This affects how the timeline is shown in your widget.
14. Finalize and create the widget : Once all fields, options, and settings are in place, click Create confirm your configuration to add the widget to the report.
15. Place and size the widget in the report layout: Drag the newly created widget to the position you want in your report. Resize it by dragging its edges (or corners) so it fits well and remains readable.
16. Verify the widget’s behavior with filters: Test the widget by applying report-level filters or switching between different views to make sure the widget data responds as you expect. If it uses date/time fields or custom formulas, verify that the aggregation or calculation works correctly.

  - Click the Add Filter button in the filters panel. Select the field you want to filter by from any of the listed tables.
  - Choose the filter type based on the field’s data type:
    - List / categorical filters : Select one or multiple values to include or exclude.
    - Numeric filters : Define operators such as Equals, Greater Than, Less Than, or ranges.
    - Text filters : Set conditions such as Is, Is Not, Contains, Does Not Contain, or custom logic.
    - Date filters : Choose a time period or granularity (day, month, year).
  - Confirm the filter to add it to the panel.
2. Edit existing filters
  - Click an existing filter in the panel to modify its field, conditions, or selected values.
  - Reorder filters by dragging them up or down.
  - Advanced filter options allow combining multiple criteria for the same field using AND/OR logic.
3. Apply widget-specific filters (optional)
  - Some filters can be applied only to specific widgets rather than the whole report.
  - This lets you control widget data independently without affecting other visualizations.
4. Save current filters as default
  - After configuring your filters, click Set as My Default Filters to save the current state.
  - This default configuration includes filter types, selected values, and order.
  - When the report is reopened, the default filters are automatically applied.
5. Reset filters to default
  - Click Reset Filters to restore all filters to the saved default configuration.
  - This resets selections, order, and conditions to the baseline state without deleting any filters.
6. Enable or disable filters
  - Toggle individual filters on or off to temporarily remove their effect without deleting them.
  - Disabled filters can be re-enabled later without losing configuration.
7. Lock filters
  - Locking a filter prevents other users from changing its configuration.
  - Locked filters show a lock icon, indicating their settings are fixed.
8. Create or Set a Background Filter
  - Background filters restrict the data permanently for the report (or the part of the report they’re applied to) and they apply before regular filters. A filter marked as a background filter shows a special icon in edit mode.
  - From a filter’s menu, if no values are currently selected, choose “Create background filter” . Or, if the filter already has selections, pick “Set as background filter” to turn it into a background filter.
  - To change a background filter later, use “Edit background filter” , make your changes, and confirm. To remove it, choose “Remove background filter” from the same menu.
9. Define filter relationships (AND/OR logic)
  - Combine multiple filters using AND/OR logic to define how they interact. This determines how multiple filters are applied together, affecting the data returned in widgets.
  - Specify whether all filters must apply simultaneously or if only one needs to match. Save filter relationships as part of the default configuration.
  - AND relationship: All filters must match for a data point to be included. Example: Filter on Region = US AND Product = Widget A returns only US data for Widget A.
  - OR relationship: A data point can match any one of the filters to be included. Example: Filter on Region = US OR Region = Canada returns data for either region.
  - Dependent filters (cascading filters): Some filters can depend on others, e.g., a City filter shows only cities in the selected Region. This is configured through filter relationships.
  - Saving relationships: When you set up AND/OR logic or dependent filters, you can save this as part of the report’s default filter configuration, so users see the correct logic applied every time.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Advanced reports > Understanding filter levels > Filter interaction and override logic:
- Identical granularity (override) If a secondary dashboard-level filter is set to a specific value but a primary widget-level filter specifies a different value, the primary widget-level filter overrides the dashboard setting. For example, if the dashboard is filtered for one country and the widget is filtered for another, the widget will only display data for its specified country. Example: If you set a secondary dashboard-level filter to Country = United States , but a specific widget contains a primary widget-level filter set to Country = United Kingdom , the widget completely ignores the dashboard setting and only displays data for the United Kingdom.
- Different granularity (combination) If a secondary dashboard-level filter targets a broad category and a primary widget-level filter targets a narrower subset, advanced reports apply both filters simultaneously. For example, if the dashboard filters for a specific year and the widget filters for a specific quarter, the widget will display data filtered for that specific quarter within that year. Example: If you set a secondary dashboard-level filter to Year = 2026 and a primary widget-level filter is configured for Quarter = Q1 , the two filters combine. The widget displays data filtered specifically for Q1 2026.
- Contradictory filters (no results) If a secondary dashboard-level filter and a primary widget-level filter apply conflicting criteria at the same level of granularity, the criteria cancel each other out, and the widget will display no results. Example: If you set a secondary dashboard-level filter to Year = 2025 but the primary widget-level filter is hardcoded to Year = 2026 , the widget attempts to find data that simultaneously belongs to both 2025 and 2026. Because this is impossible, the widget displays no results.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Advanced reports > Caveats and limitations:
- Apply button in filters always enabled The "Apply" button in report filters remains clickable even when no changes have been made to the filter selection. This can lead users to click "Apply" unnecessarily, which may cause confusion about whether their filter changes have actually been registered. While this does not result in errors, it is helpful to know that clicking "Apply" repeatedly is not always required.
- Duplicate tooltips when viewing in Safari When viewing reports with long descriptions in the Advanced SSR listing page using Safari, two tooltips may appear at the same time. This can clutter the interface and make it difficult to read the full description. Using a different browser, such as Chrome or Firefox, can help avoid this issue.
- Unnecessary search bar in Status filter The status filter in Advanced SSR displays a search bar even when there are only two filter options available. This may be confusing, as the search bar serves no purpose in this context. Users can simply ignore the search bar when only two options are present.
- Simultaneous edit flow UI issues If two users attempt to edit the same report at the same time, the edit icon becomes greyed out for one user, and the notification message may appear in the wrong position, overlapping other elements instead of being centered. This can cause confusion about editing permissions and may lead to missed notifications. It is advisable to coordinate with team members to avoid editing the same report at the same time.
- Rename popup unresponsive If the "Rename" popup is opened and no text changes are made, the action buttons can become unresponsive. Clicking outside the text area does not allow users to resume editing, so it may be necessary to close and reopen the popup or ensure a text change is made before saving.
- Pagination lacks loader When navigating between pages in learner reports, there is no loading indicator, which can make the interface appear unresponsive during slow loads. Users may click multiple times, causing repeated requests or confusion. Waiting a few seconds after clicking can help ensure the page loads properly.
- Draft report name/description sync issue Custom names and descriptions added to draft reports may not update correctly in the listing page or report view, with only the last change being displayed. Refreshing the page after making changes can help ensure the latest information is shown.
- Dashboard autoscroll fails during widget drag-and-drop Dragging a widget to the bottom of a dashboard does not trigger auto-scrolling, making it difficult to place widgets in lower sections. Manually scrolling the page before dragging the widget can help with placement.
- Pivot table scroll limitation When the mouse pointer is over an expandable pivot table, users may be unable to scroll to the top of the report using the mouse wheel. Moving the mouse pointer outside the pivot table or using the scrollbar can help with navigation.
- Incomplete profile fields in data source Not all profile fields are available for selection when searching and scrolling through the data source in the Profile field framework. If a required field is missing, users may need to contact support for assistance.
- Widgets missing when cloning from template Occasionally, when cloning a report from a template, none of the widgets are copied over, and the report opens empty except for the "+ add widgets" option. In such cases, retrying the cloning process or manually adding widgets may be necessary.
- Archived modules and invitation status When a module is archived, the learner module invitation status for all invited learners changes to “REMOVED.” As a result, reports filtered with “INVITED” in the Learner module invitation status filter will exclude archived module data. To view archived module data, include “REMOVED” in the filter.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Advanced reports:
This article provides detailed guidance on managing advanced reports within Mindtickle Analytics. It covers how to download full reports or individual widgets, share reports with other admins or managers, create duplicates for experimentation or alternate views, and delete reports that are no longer needed.

Using these capabilities, admins can efficiently distribute insights, maintain report versions, and manage report lifecycle without affecting other users' access or data.

This article covers:

- Downloading reports and widgets : Export reports in PDF format and widgets as images or CSV files.
- Emailing reports : Email reports to other admins and managers.
- Sharing reports : Share reports with other admins and managers via the platform's in-built sharing functionality.
- Duplicating reports : Create copies of existing reports for experimentation, customization, or version control.
- Deleting reports : Delete reports permanently.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Advanced reports > Email report > Email and schedule the report:
1. On the advanced reports home page, click the report that you want to email.
2. On the report page, click the Email report button in the header.
3. In the dropdown pop-up that appears, select one of the following options:
  - Email to admins : Use this option to email the report to other admins. The emailed report will appear exactly as configured by the report creator (either you or another admin), including all applied filters.
  - Email to managers : Use this option to email a personalized version of the report to managers. Each manager will only see data related to their direct reportees — meaning both individual contributors and team leads who report to the manager. All applied filters are preserved in the emailed report.
4. Let's now understand how to email the report to admins. Click Email to admins in the previous step. Note : The following instructions are also applicable for emailing the report to managers — except that you need to select managers instead of admins.
5. Under Email report to admins > Select admins , select one or more admins as recipients with whom you want to share the report via email. Note : You can select up to 1000 recipients at a time. This limitation does not include recipients added as CC in the next step. To search for a particular admin, use the search bar. When you select an admin after running a search, your selection is retained when you clear the search results. Use the Profile field filter to view only a specific set of admins in the list. Use the button in the column header to sort the list in the ascending/descending order. Select admins individually or use the check box in the column header to select all admins at once. Click Next to continue.
6. Under Add CC , for each selected admin, you can add other admins as CC (carbon copy) recipients. Admins added as CC will also receive the same report by email. Click the + Add CC , select admin users in the dropdown menu, and then click Next .
7. Under Share details , first select whether you want to email the report immediately ( send now ) or schedule it for sending later ( schedule email ). Continue to the next steps for information on both options.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Advanced reports > Create:
You can create a copy of an advanced report — that is, duplicate the report — when you want to keep the original report intact, so you can make further changes to the copied version of the report. This is helpful, for example, when you want to share the same report but with less (or more) data with a different set of stakeholders.

1. On the advanced reports home page, click the report that you want to duplicate.
2. On the report page, click the button in the header.
3. The copied version of the report opens in edit mode, with the prefix "Copy of" added to the report name.

You can make all kinds of changes, similar to creating a new report.Once done with your changes, click Save to save the report. Or, click Discard to discard the copied report and not create the report.

Important: The copied version of the report remains in the draft mode until you save it. Therefore, you must save the report to successfully create a copy.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Advanced reports > Delete report:
You can permanently delete advanced reports created by you and other admins if you no longer need them.

1. Open the report that you want to delete. You can open a report for deleting in two ways from the advanced reports homepage:

  - From the list of reports, click the report that you want to delete. On the report page, click the button in the header to delete the report.
2. In the confirmation pop-up that appears, click Delete to permanently delete the advanced report.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > AI video > Overview:
In the AI Video Editor, some characters are blocked in the Script panel to ensure smooth audio generation and video creation. Using unsupported characters can cause errors or affect Text-to-Speech (TTS) quality. Blocking certain characters helps improve:

- TTS compatibility: Prevents characters that can break or confuse TTS engines.

- User experience: Reduces script validation failures and ensures smoother video creation.

- Arrows : →, ←, ↑, ↓, etc.

If your script contains any unsupported characters, the following error message appears on the UI: Symbols are not supported in the script.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Release Notes > Enhancements > Native thumbnail crop and resize for thumbnails for series, modules, hubs, and assets:
This release introduces a new thumbnail editing experience across series, modules, hubs, and assets, giving users greater flexibility when uploading and adjusting images. You can now upload high-resolution images and adjust the crop directly within the platform, eliminating the need for external editing tools to achieve the perfect fit.

Key features:

- Integrated cropping & resizing : Users can now position and crop images directly within the tool. Whether you want to use a specific area or the entire image, you have full control over the composition.
- Fixed aspect ratio (3:2) : To ensure visual consistency across the platform, the cropping tool locks the crop frame to the required 3:2 aspect ratio . You can resize this selection box, but the shape will remain fixed.
- Canvas & background handling : The interface provides a fixed canvas for your image. Note : If you extend the crop selection beyond your image boundaries into the empty background, the system will automatically fill that area with white space in the final thumbnail.
- Platform-wide support : These enhancements apply everywhere thumbnails are used, including series, modules, hubs, and assets.

Note:

- File requirements : Please ensure your file is a .png, .jpg, or .jpeg and does not exceed 10 MB. For details, see What image formats does Mindtickle support? .
- Storage location : Newly uploaded images during thumbnail selection are automatically stored in Content Center → System files → Thumbnails . Please note that this default storage location cannot be changed.

Value & impact:

To invite one or more users to a Mindtickle series. Invites users on the current date.

Request URL

```

Request parameters

JSON REQUEST PARAMETERS

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Note: You must provide one of the following: userids, usernames, or userInvitations. userInvitations will take preference over the other two fields. |  |  |
| userids | Array[string] | Mindtickle IDs of the users that you want to invite to the series.Multiple IDs should be comma-separated as shown in the request example below this table. |
| usernames | Array[string] | Mindtickle usernames/email IDs of the users that you want to invite to the series.Provide the usernames of the users if UID is enabled for your Mindtickle instance.Provide their email addresses if UID is not enabled. |

If this field is omitted or left blank, the current date and time will be used by default. |

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle APIs > Training APIs > Invite users to a module > Backdated module invitations:
You can invite users to a module with a backdated timestamp using the invited_on field. This allows the system to recognize completion dates earlier than the current invite date, ensuring accurate migration of historical completions and correct alignment of completion dates for rewards and reporting.

- The backdated invite date must be earlier than the completion date.
- Completion APIs will respect backdated module invitations and accept earlier completion timestamps.
- Module invitations must be backdated independently of series invitations if historical module completions need to be migrated.
- Use epoch timestamp format for the invited_on field.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle APIs > Training APIs > Assign reviewers to users:
To assign and replace reviewers in bulk for users in the mission and coaching sessions modules. Allows you to seamlessly set reviewers from an external system for your users in missions and coaching sessions. You can assign a user’s peers as reviewers.

For example, the appointment method in a Coaching Sessions module settings is set to “Appoint Manager as Reviewer”. In this case, if you define a non-manager as the reviewer in the API, the reviewer specified in the API overrides the reviewer configured through module settings.

- This API supports only Mission and Coaching Sessions modules. Also, it does not support removal of reviewers.
- For a particular module, a maximum of 100 users and 5 reviewers per user are supported in a single request.
- For Missions, you cannot add or replace a reviewer if the review is already completed by the reviewer assigned on the platform.
- For closed Coaching Sessions , you cannot replace reviewers.
- For Coaching Sessions, the API does not support learner self review .
- The reviewer can be added to the set index but cannot be replaced where the review is already completed.
- You cannot assign a reviewer to a user who is not invited to the module.
- Module invitation is not handled through this API. No error message is displayed if the learner is not invited to the module.

Possible errors returned for this API and their reasons:

- Invalid body: request body invalid
- Empty body: Request body cannot be empty
- User/reviewer is not found/Inactive: userId: <list> not found

Request URL

Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Release Notes > New features > Introducing Seller Copilot in Slack (beta):
Mindtickle’s Seller Copilot is now available directly within Slack. It allows users to prepare for calls with interaction histories, automate post-call summaries and action items, and get context-aware answers to product and process questions directly within Slack, eliminating the need to switch platforms. This feature extends the capabilities of the existing Mindtickle app for Slack. Beyond its traditional role of delivering notifications and reminders, the app now supports interactive AI conversations with Seller Copilot.

Note: This feature is currently in beta.

Key features

- Interactive AI chat: You can now engage directly with Seller Copilot in the Messages tab of the Mindtickle app. Simply tag @mindtickle followed by your question to get instant answers.
- Context-aware threading: The Copilot supports deep-dive research by treating every Slack thread as a unique session. It retains the context of previous questions within a thread, allowing for natural follow-up queries.
- Feedback mechanism: Built-in Thumbs up and Thumbs down buttons allow users to rate responses and provide detailed feedback to improve accuracy over time.

Integration & setup

Admins can now configure the integration directly within Slack using simple chat commands to connect their instance and synchronize users. Additionally, feature visibility is fully governed by the "Audience" settings in your Mindtickle platform, allowing you to grant Copilot access to everyone, specific groups, or restrict it entirely.

Limitations

- No follow-up suggestions: Due to Slack’s character limits, clickable "suggested follow-up" chips are not available.
- Public mention restrictions: To prevent data leaks, the @mindtickle mention is currently disabled in public channels and DMs. It functions exclusively in the Messages tab.

Coming soon (pending app upgrade)

Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Release Notes > New features > Asset Hub APIs to create hubs, assets, attribute categories, and attributes:
This release introduces the Asset Hub management APIs, a new set of 4 REST API endpoints designed to help admins and developers automate content operations at scale. These APIs enable you to programmatically create and organize your content ecosystem — including hubs, assets, attributes, and attribute categories — without relying on the manual user interface.

New APIs

- Create a hub: Programmatically provision new private or public hubs with defined access settings and descriptions. Ideal for automating large-scale onboarding across different business units.
- Create assets (async): A robust asynchronous endpoint to bulk create assets using files from the Content Center. It supports comprehensive metadata tagging (permissions, expiry, usage) and governance checks, returning an execution ID to track progress via the status endpoint.
- Create attribute categories: Define high-level taxonomy structures (e.g., Region, Product Line) to organize your content library.
- Create attributes: Bulk populate categories with specific attributes (e.g., Americas, APAC), ensuring consistent tagging standards across your organization.

Benefits

- Scalability: Automate the setup of hundreds of hubs or assets in a single workflow.
- Governance: Enforce consistent metadata and taxonomy standards programmatically.
- Efficiency: Reduce manual administrative effort during initial setup or migration.

For more information, see Asset Hub management APIs.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Release Notes > New features > New MissionSubmissions table in the reporting API:
This release brings the MissionSubmissions table to Mindtickle’s OData-based reporting API. This new reporting resource is designed to provide granular visibility into learner submissions for email and task evaluation missions, offering detailed tracking of learner attempts, reviewer feedback, and media assets.

Key data points

This table captures a comprehensive set of fields to analyze learner performance. Key fields include:

- Completion Status: Indicates the precise state of the learner's submission. Values include SUBMITTED , COMPLETED , MACHINE_REDO (system-triggered reattempt), REVIEWER_REDO (manual reviewer request), and RESET .
- SignedMedia: A JSON-serialized string providing time-limited, pre-signed URLs. These allow you to download the submitted media file and its corresponding transcription. Note that this field must be parsed as JSON before use.
- AttemptNo: An integer (e.g., 1 , 2 ) that distinguishes between multiple submissions or retakes.
- UserId: The learner’s user ID, represented as a hexadecimal string.
- Timestamps: Includes SubmissionDate and ReviewDate to track when work was submitted and evaluated ( ISO 8601 format).

Data frequency & granularity

- Update Frequency: Data in this table is refreshed every 6 hours.
- Granularity: Records are unique at the level of: SeriesId x ModuleId x UserId x AttemptNo x ReviewerId .

Caveats & constraints

Please note the following logic and limitations when building reports with this table:

- Mission types: This table currently only supports email and task evaluation mission types.
- Learner scope: Learners who have not made any submissions will not appear in this table.
- User status: Data is provided for all users, including those who are currently active or deactivated.
- Draft handling: For learners with multiple submissions, data for each draft is recorded separately.
- Timezone: All timestamp fields are recorded in GMT .

Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Release Notes > Enhancements > Multi-currency support for Salesforce deals in DSR:
With this release, DSR supports multiple currencies for Salesforce deals. DSR displays deal values in the opportunity currency from Salesforce and uses the corporate currency when filtering deals or generating reports. This ensures consistent currency display and accurate calculations across DSR.

Note:

- To enable this feature for your Mindtickle instance, contact Mindtickle support .
- This feature is available only for Salesforce deals in DSR.
- The opportunity currency is the currency set for a deal in Salesforce.
- The corporate currency is the default currency set for the organization in Salesforce.

For more information, see Multi-currency support for Salesforce deals in DSR.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Digital Sales Rooms:
DSR supports multiple currencies for deals synced from Salesforce. DSR displays the deal amount in the opportunity currency and uses the corporate currency when filtering deals or generating content usage reports.

This ensures the correct currency is displayed for deals and the deal amount calculations remain accurate when filtering deals and generating reports.

For example,

- Opportunity currency: If a deal uses Fiji dollars as the opportunity currency in Salesforce, DSR displays the deal amount in Fiji dollars.
- Corporate currency: If the American dollar (USD) is set as the organization's corporate currency in Salesforce, when you filter deals using the Min. deal amount filter on the Rooms page, DSR converts all deal amounts to USD and displays only the matching deals.

Note:

- The opportunity currency is the currency set for a deal in Salesforce.
- The corporate currency is the default currency set for the organization in Salesforce.
- This feature is available only for Salesforce deals in DSR.
- If the corporate currency in Salesforce changes, contact Mindtickle support to update it in DSR. This ensures the system displays the correct currency for deals.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle APIs > Asset Hub APIs:
The Asset Hub management APIs allow you to automate the full lifecycle of content organization within Asset Hub. These endpoints support the programmatic creation of hubs, management of collaborators and user access, the bulk processing of assets, and the maintenance of your taxonomy through attribute categories and attributes.

Key capabilities include:

- Hub management: Programmatically create new private or public hubs to scale your content organization.
- Access control: Manage access by bulk-updating hub collaborator permissions and controlling individual user access to restricted hubs.
- Asset operations: Asynchronously create assets, permanently delete them, use the mirror/move functionality to map assets globally across hubs, or programmatically archive assets in bulk.
- Taxonomy governance: Define your organization structure by creating attribute categories and attributes, with the ability to delete them when necessary.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle APIs > Asset Hub APIs > Available endpoints:
Select an API below to view its specification.

| API Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Hubs & Access |  |
| 1. Create a hub | Programmatically creates a new hub. Ideal for onboarding multiple business units or geographies. |
| 2. Manage hub collaborators | Bulk adds or removes hub-level permissions for multiple collaborators in a single request. |
| 3. Manage user access for restricted hubs | Shares or revokes access to a restricted hub for individual users. Equivalent to the "Share access" UI feature. |
| Assets |  |
| 4. Create assets (async) | Asynchronously creates new assets from Content Center files. Returns an execution ID to track progress. |
| 5. Archive assets | Programmatically archives Asset Hub assets in bulk using a single request. |
| 6. Mirror or move assets | Asynchronously mirrors assets (adds to new hubs) or moves them (exclusively replaces existing hub mappings) using the global Asset ID. |
| 7. Delete assets | Permanently deletes multiple assets by ID in a single request. |
| Attributes & Taxonomy |  |
| 8. Create attribute categories | Creates attribute categories to organize assets (e.g., Region, Product Line). |
| 9. Create attributes | Creates attributes under an existing attribute category (e.g., adding "Americas" under "Region"). |
| 10. Delete attributes | Deletes one or more asset attributes by ID. Supports an optional force-delete for attributes currently linked to assets. |

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle APIs > Asset Hub APIs > 1. Create a hub > Request parameters:
Request parameters

| Parameter | Type | Description | Values/Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| hub_nameREQUIRED | string | Name of the hub | Max 50 characters. Cannot contain /, \, or .. |
| access_typeREQUIRED | string | Hub access setting | Values: "HUB_ACCESS_PUBLIC" or "HUB_ACCESS_RESTRICTED".• HUB_ACCESS_PUBLIC: Public hub; everyone has access.• HUB_ACCESS_RESTRICTED: Restricted hub; only selected users have access. |
| description | string | Description of the hub | Max 1000 characters (excluding HTML tags). |
| user_idREQUIRED | string | ID of the user performing the operation | Must have HUB_MANAGEMENT permission. |

Request example

```json

{
  "hub_name": "Team Hub",
  "access_type": "HUB_ACCESS_RESTRICTED",
  "description": "This is a private hub for my team",
  "user_id": "1b6bde72724a4000"
}
```

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle APIs > Asset Hub APIs > 2. Manage hub collaborators > Notes:
- Limits: Max 50 collaborator entries per request.
- Partial success: This API supports partial success. Entries that pass validation are processed, while invalid entries are returned in the failure_details array. If all entries fail static validation, the API returns HTTP 200 with status: FAILED .
- Validation:
  - Each collaborator entry must specify either collaborator_user_id or collaborator_username . When both are provided, collaborator_user_id takes precedence and both values must resolve to the same user ; otherwise, a matching error is returned.
  - The permissions array cannot be empty.
- Common error reasons:
  - User not found by User ID or User not found by Username / Email .
  - Permission is at override level and cannot be removed .
  - Permission does not exist for user (when attempting to REMOVE a missing permission).
  - User already has this permission (when attempting to ADD an existing permission).

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle APIs > Asset Hub APIs > 3. Manage user access for restricted hubs:
Allows external systems to programmatically share or revoke access to a restricted hub for individual users. This functionality is equivalent to the "Share access" feature for individual users in the Asset Hub UI.

- This API is applicable for restricted hubs ( access_type = HUB_ACCESS_RESTRICTED ) and not public hubs.
- The API currently supports managing (sharing or revoking) access for only individual users, and not user groups (available only in the UI).
