Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle APIs > Asset Hub APIs > 4. Create assets (async) > Notes:
- Limits: Max 50 assets per request. Asset name limit: 250 chars. Description limit: 1000 chars.
- Validation:
  - The file_id must correspond to a valid, published file in the Content Center.
  - Asset name cannot contain / or \ .
- Synced files: The system internally checks if the file_id is a synced file. If metadata is available via sync, the system uses the latest synced metadata (ignoring explicitly passed values for those properties). For non-synced properties, the explicitly passed metadata is used.
- Properties object:
  - Defaults:
    - allow_download defaults to true .
    - Other boolean flags default to false .
  - Dependent properties: If a parent property is missing (e.g., expiry_date ), dependent properties (e.g., expiry_reminder ) are ignored.
  - Governance rules:
    - Embedded assets cannot have Allow download = Yes.
    - Only PPT/PDF/DOCX/XLSX assets can have Allow customization = Yes.
    - PDF assets cannot have Edit content = Yes.
  - Attributes: Must pass an array of unique attribute IDs (e.g., ["attr_123", "attr_456"] ), not the display names. To find these IDs, refer to the response of the Create attributes API.
  - Feature flags: Properties controlled by disabled feature flags are gracefully ignored.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle APIs > Asset Hub APIs > 4. Create assets (async) > Track request status:
Fetch the progress or completion status of an async asset creation request using the execution_id returned by the Create assets API.

Endpoint:

```
GET /api/assethub/v2/assets/async/{execution_id}
```

Query parameters

| Parameter | Type | Description | Values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| user_idREQUIRED | string | User ID for authorization | Must be a valid User ID. |
| limit | integer | Max number of tasks to return | Max 100. Default 0. |
| skip | integer | Number of tasks to skip | Default 0. |

Response example

```json

{
  "execution_id": "w123436",
  "status": "success",
  "total_tasks": 25,
  "completed_tasks": 24,
  "failed_tasks": 1,
  "tasks": [
    {
      "task_id": "t_101",
      "status": "success",
      "asset_id": "a98765"
    },
    {
      "task_id": "t_102",
      "status": "failed",
      "asset_id": "",
      "error": "Asset already exists with same name in one or more hubs."
    }
  ],
  "request_id": "req_556677"
}
```

Response values

- Execution status: in_progress , success , failed , not_dispatched
- Task status: success , failed , in_progress , not_dispatched

Note: limit cannot be greater than 100.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle APIs > Asset Hub APIs > 6. Move or mirror assets:
Allows external systems to asynchronously move or mirror assets across hubs.

Move

This operation replaces the asset’s entire existing hub list with the new target hubs specified in the request. The asset is removed from all current hubs and added only to the new ones.

Examples:

- Example 1: Asset is currently in New York hub. Move it to San Francisco hub → After the operation, the asset is only in San Francisco hub. Removed from New York hub.
- Example 2: Asset is currently in London , Berlin , and Paris hub. Move it to Tokyo and Sydney hub → After the operation, the asset is only in Tokyo and Sydney hub. Removed from London , Berlin , and Paris hub.

Mirror

This operation keeps the asset in its existing hubs and adds the new target hubs specified in the request.

Example:

- Asset is currently in London , Berlin , and Paris hub. Mirror it to Tokyo and Sydney hub → After the operation, the asset remains in London , Berlin , and Paris hub, and is also in Tokyo and Sydney hub.

    }
  ]
}

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Copilot > For learners:
Mindtickle Seller Copilot in Slack is an AI-powered knowledge companion designed to integrate seamlessly into your flow of work. It allows users to prepare for calls with interaction histories, automate post-call summaries and action items, and get context-aware answers to product and process questions directly within Slack, eliminating the need to switch platforms.

This feature extends the capabilities of the existing Mindtickle app for Slack. Beyond its traditional role of delivering notifications and reminders, the app now supports interactive AI conversations.

You can ask questions related to modules (assigned and public), assets, and Call AI calls available to you on the learning site. This ensures that every response is securely grounded in your organization's approved enablement content and real-world customer interactions.

Seller Copilot is also available on the Mindtickle learning site, Mindtickle mobile app, Salesforce, and through Mindtickle APIs.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Copilot > For learners > Access and prerequisites:
Before using Mindtickle Slack app to chat with Seller Copilot, ensure the following requirements are met:

- Seller Copilot enabled: Ensure that Seller Copilot is enabled on your Mindtickle instance. To enable it, please contact Mindtickle Support .
- Mindtickle Slack app: Ensure the Mindtickle app is installed in your Slack workspace. If not, please reach out to your admin.
- User permissions: Seller Copilot availability is strictly based on the Audience settings configured by your admin:
  - Authorized access: You can chat with Copilot in Slack if your admin has enabled Copilot for everyone or for a specific group (e.g., your sales team) that you belong to.
  - Restricted access: If Copilot is set to None or you are not part of the authorized group, interacting with the @mindtickle bot will result in an error message.

This configuration must be performed by a Mindtickle admin directly within the Slack workspace. You can view a full list of available commands at any time by typing @mindtickle help. Additionally, see this article for detailed setup and integration information.

Disconnecting an instance

If you need to unlink a specific site from your Slack workspace, use the disconnect command.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Copilot > For learners > Enable private slash commands:
The /mindtickle slash command allows users to have private, ephemeral 1:1 conversations with Copilot directly within channels and group DMs. Depending on when your app was installed, you may need to re-authenticate the app to enable this.

Check your installation date:

- Installed on/after Jan 23, 2026: Private slash commands are enabled by default . No additional action is required.
- Installed before Jan 23, 2026: A one-time re-authentication is required to enable the new functionality. Follow the steps below.

Re-authenticate Mindtickle app

To enable the new slash command permissions for your workspace, your Slack workspace admin must complete the following one-time setup:

1. Initiate re-authentication: Click the link below to start the permission update process: Authorize Mindtickle App Updates
2. Select your Slack workspace: On the page titled "Allow the 'Mindtickle' app to access Slack," select the specific Slack workspace where you want to enable the slash command.
3. Confirm Access: Click Allow to complete the authentication. The setup is now complete, and the /mindtickle command is active.

See the "this section" for details on how to use it.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Copilot > For learners > Ways to chat with Seller Copilot:
Once the app is set up, there are two primary ways to interact with Seller Copilot, depending on your needs for privacy and conversation history:

- Method 1: The Messages tab (@mindtickle) Best for in-depth research and call preparation. These conversations happen in the dedicated Mindtickle app tab, are persistent (saved history), and allow for threaded follow-up questions. See this section for details.
- Method 2: Slash command (/mindtickle) Best for quick, private answers while collaborating in a public/private channel or group DM. These responses are ephemeral (visible only to you) and do not save a chat history in the channel, keeping your team space clutter-free. See this section for details.

Tip: You can also check the Home tab in the app for visual guides and quick tips on using these features.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Copilot > For learners > Method 1: Chat via Messages Tab (@mindtickle) > Initiate a chat:
1. Open the app: Navigate to the Mindtickle app under "Apps" in your Slack sidebar, or use the Slack search bar to find and open it.
2. Send a query: In the Messages tab, @ mention/tag the bot explicitly to start a chat: @mindtickle [Your Question] .
3. Processing: A temporary "Getting a response for you" message appears as a reply in the thread, confirming your query is being processed so you can multitask while waiting.
4. View response: Seller Copilot replaces the temporary message with the final answer in the same thread. You will receive a Slack notification for all Copilot responses. Each thread functions as an independent chat session and Copilot retains context for that specific conversation.

- Follow-up queries: To ask a follow-up question, you must reply in the thread and explicitly tag @mindtickle again. Important: If you type without the tag, the bot will not process your question and will instead respond with a prompt asking you to use the correct format.

- New topics: To start a fresh topic without previous context, post a new message directly in the Messages tab (outside any threads).

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Copilot > For learners > Method 2: Chat via Slash Command (/mindtickle) > Step I: Add Mindtickle to a channel or group DM:
Before you can use the slash command, the Mindtickle app/bot must be a member of the specific conversation. The method for adding the bot depends on whether you are in a channel or a group DM.

Note: To ensure a seamless experience, Seller Copilot provides proactive setup guidance if the /mindtickle command is used in a channel or group DM where the app hasn't been added yet. Instead of no response, you will receive a ephemeral guidance message with clear, instant steps to add the app and continue using Copilot.

For channels (public & private)

You can add the bot to a channel at any time using either of these methods:

- Option A: Type @mindtickle in the message box and hit Send . Slack will prompt you that the bot is not in the channel. Click Add them to join it.
- Option B: Click the channel name at the top → Integrations tab → Add an app → Search for "Mindtickle" and click Add .

For group DMs

Important limitation: You must add the Mindtickle app while creating the group DM. Slack does not allow adding apps to an existing group DM.

- Option A: Type @mindtickle in the message box and hit Send . Slack will prompt you that the bot is not in the channel. Click Add them to join it.
- Option B: Click the channel name at the top → Integrations tab → Add an app → Search for "Mindtickle" and click Add .

For group DMs

Important limitation: You must add the Mindtickle app while creating the group DM. Slack does not allow adding apps to an existing group DM.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Copilot > For learners > Method 2: Chat via Slash Command (/mindtickle) > Step II: Use the slash command:
Once the Mindtickle app is added, you can start a private chat at any time using the /mindtickle slash command.

Pro tip: Don't worry if you forget to add the app first. If you run the /mindtickle command in a channel or group DM where the app isn't a member, you'll receive an ephemeral ("Only visible to you") message with instant instructions on how to add it so you can get right back to your workflow.

1. Navigate to a channel/group DM: Navigate to any public/private channel or group DM where the Mindtickle app is added.
2. Send a query: Use the the /mindtickle slash command to start a chat: /mindtickle [Your Question] . Example: /mindtickle What is the pricing structure for the Enterprise plan?
3. Processing: A temporary "Getting a response for you" message appears, confirming your query is being processed so you can multitask while waiting.
4. View response: Seller Copilot responds to your question. You will receive a Slack notification for all Copilot responses. Note : This ephemeral, temporary response is only visible to you . See the message lifespan note below for details.

Note on message lifespan

Ephemeral responses are temporary and exist only in your current view. They are not saved to the channel or group DM history and will disappear permanently if you:

- Reload Slack ( Cmd+R or Ctrl+R ).
- Close and reopen the Slack application.
- Log out of your workspace.

If you receive an answer you need to reference later or share with the team, please copy and save it immediately.

Seller Copilot helps sales reps perform critical tasks efficiently by:

- Preparing for calls: Summarizes past customer interactions, highlights relevant context, and recommends next steps to help you get ready for upcoming conversations.
- Handling post-call actions:
  - Summarizing the call: Provides concise summaries of key discussion points to ensure nothing important is missed.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Copilot > For learners > Limitations:
Please note the following limitations for Copilot in Slack:

- No follow-up suggestions: Unlike Seller Copilot in other platforms (web, mobile, and Salesforce), Seller Copilot in Slack does not support clickable follow-up suggestions due to Slack character limits.
- Public mention restrictions: To prevent the accidental broadcasting of sensitive information, the @mindtickle command is disabled in channels and direct messages. Attempting to use it in these spaces will not trigger a response (please use the /mindtickle slash command for these scenarios instead).

See this article for other common limitations of Seller Copilot.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Copilot > For learners > Customize the bot name:
To align with your organization's internal branding or enablement initiatives, you can customize the name of the Mindtickle bot within Slack (e.g., renaming it to "Sales Coach" or "Enablement Bot").

Note: This step is optional. While you can change the bot's display name, Slack does not currently allow you to customize the bot's profile picture; it will retain the standard Mindtickle "M" logo.

1. Log in to Slack using your admin credentials.
2. Access the app configuration page: The quickest way is to click this direct link to open the Mindtickle App Configuration tab . Alternatively, navigate manually within Slack:
  - Navigate to the Apps section on the left sidebar and click the Mindtickle app.
  - Click the bot name located below the main search bar.
  - In the menu that appears, click Configuration . This will open the Mindtickle Slack app page in a new browser tab.
3. On the configuration page, scroll to the Bot User section and click Edit .
4. Enter your preferred name in the text field and click Save changes .

Important updates to commands

- Once the name is changed, you must address the bot mentions using the new name . Example: If you renamed the bot to "Nirvana", the connection command becomes @nirvana connect [domain.mindtickle.com] . Where domain is your learning site name.
- Please allow approximately one hour after saving for the new bot name and commands to become fully active in your workspace.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Collaboration App Notifications > Types of notifications:
The following table lists the specific events that trigger a Slack notification for learners and managers.

| Notification type | Description |
| --- | --- |
| SERIES INVITATION | You have been invited to a new series. |
| ENTITY INVITATION | You have been invited to a new module. |
| ENTITY REMINDER | A reminder to complete a pending module. |
| REMINDER CLUBBED | A consolidated reminder for multiple pending items in a series. |
| ENTITY UPDATE | A module you are assigned to has been updated. |
| SESSION ENROLLMENT UPDATED | Details for an instructor-led training (ILT) session you are enrolled in have changed. |
| Coaching & reviewer notifications |  |
| INVITATION REVIEW | (Reviewers) You have been invited to review a coaching session or mission. |
| FEEDBACK REVIEWER SUBMIT | (Reviewers) Reminder to submit feedback for a pending review. |
| FEEDBACK REVIEWER EDIT | (Learners) Your reviewer has edited their score or feedback on your submission. |
| LEARNER REVIEW APPROVED | (Reviewers) The learner has approved the review you submitted. |
| LEARNER REVIEW DISAPPROVED | (Reviewers) The learner has disapproved the review you submitted. |
| LEARNER RESET MISSION | (Learners) Your mission attempt has been reset. |
| COACHING SCHEDULE | (Reviewers) Notification regarding the scheduling of a coaching session. |

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Series:
Bulk actions for modules enable admins to update settings for multiple modules at once from the Modules and Series page.

Admins can set module relevance, manage email reminders, add or update tags, set due dates, and configure settings for Published and Draft modules in bulk. This reduces repetitive manual work and improves consistency across training programs.

Note:

- The system highlights the settings you cannot configure in the Edit settings screen.
- When updating modules, if the changes are not static, you must publish the modules to apply the changes. For more information, see the Publish changes section.
- When adding module tags or reminders, you can either append new tags and reminders to the existing ones or replace them entirely.
- The system applies the tags to multiple modules at the module level.
- You can select a maximum of 50 modules to configure settings at once.

The steps to bulk update settings across multiple modules are.

- Select modules
- Choose settings
- Confirm settings

Note: When updating certain settings, the system prompts you to publish the module to apply the changes. For more information, see the Publish changes section.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Series > Choose settings > Set module relevance:
This option allows admins to set or update module relevance for multiple modules in bulk. For detailed information on module relevance, see Module relevance overview.To set module relevance for modules in bulk,

1. Go to a series or the Modules page.
2. Select the modules' checkboxes to update their settings.
3. Click the Edit settings option.
4. Click Set module relevance in the Edit settings screen. You can click the <#> modules selected link to view the selected modules. In the Make changes screen, the system displays the number of modules compatible with the setting. Hover over the number to view the supported module types.
5. Click the necessary option to set the module relevance. For example, Required. The system sets the selected option as the module's default relevance. You can change it for individual learners in the module's Invite and track tab.
6. Click Continue . In the Confirm changes screen, the Current value and Will be changed to columns display the current and updated settings in the modules. The system also displays the modules where the module relevance setting is not applicable. To not make a change to a module, click the Remove icon. If you remove a module by mistake, click Undo to reverse the action.
7. After validating the changes, click Confirm changes . The system displays a notification that updates are in progress, along with the time saved. Note: If the module relevance update fails for some modules, the system notifies you. You can retry the update for the failed modules. You can click Back to series page to navigate to the Series page.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Series > Choose settings > Manage reminders:
This option allows admins to configure email reminders for multiple modules in bulk. For detailed information on setting up email templates and repeating reminders in series and modules, see Configure email templates and repeating reminders in series and modules.

To manage reminder emails for multiple modules,

1. Go to a series or the Modules page.
2. Select the modules' checkboxes to update their settings.
3. Click the Edit settings option.
4. Click Manage reminders in the Edit settings screen. You can click the <#> modules selected link to view the selected modules. The system displays the selected module types as tabs for configuring the reminder email.
5. Click the tab of a module’s type to configure email reminders. The Make changes screen displays the number of modules selected The available reminder email options are displayed.
6. To configure an email reminder, click the checkbox of an email type.
7. Select an option from the Apply reminders drop-down. The following options are available.

- Add to existing reminders: This option adds additional reminders to existing email reminders in the selected modules.
- Replace existing reminders: This option replaces all previously configured email reminders in the selected modules.

8. Click the Edit icon in the Email template column to select a reminder email template.

The Select email template screen is displayed.

9. Click on a template to select it.

10. Click Use this email to select the template for the reminder email.

The system updates the module's email template.

11. Similarly, configure emails for the other selected modules. The system displays the total number of selected settings across all modules at the bottom of the screen.

This option allows admins to set new or extend due dates for multiple modules in bulk.

To update due dates for multiple modules,

1. Go to a series or the Modules page.
2. Select the modules' checkboxes to update their settings.
3. Click the Edit settings option.
4. Click Set due date in the Edit settings screen. You can click the <#> modules selected link to view the selected modules. The Make changes screen displays the number of modules selected.
5. To set a new due date or extend the existing due date for the modules,
6. Click the Set a new due date option to set a new due date for the modules. You can choose to perform the following actions: Specify the No. of days after invitation or Select a specific date from the dropdown. Note: The number of days after invitation can be set between 1 to 730 days. Or
7. Click the Extend due date by option to extend the modules’ due date. Note: The number of days after the last due date can be set between 1 to 730 days. For example, if the due date for a module is 10 January and it is extended by 10 days, the new due date will be 20 January.
8. In What happens after the due date? , choose what happens to the modules after the due date:

- Learners can still complete the quick update after the due date passes.
- Module freezes. Learner can’t attempt the module anymore.

9. Click Continue.

In the Confirm changes screen, the Current value and Will be changed to columns display the current and updated settings in the modules. The system highlights the modules where the due dates are not applicable.

2. Click the Default minimum time to record learners attendance checkbox, then turn ON the toggle to enable the duration-based attendance for the ILT module.

- No. of days before session: Select this option to send reminders to admins a certain number of days before the session. For example, 5 days before the session.
- Specific date: Select this option to send reminders to admins on a specific date before the session. Choose a specific date from the calendar. For example, Jan 21, 2025.

7. Select the Repeat every # days checkbox to send the recurring minimum enrollment email to admins every # days before the scheduled session date.

It shows how the learners and their peers performed in the module.For information on enabling the Hall of Fame setting in quests, see Gamification settings in a quest.

Emails and notifications

This tab allows admins to configure learner enrollment and reminder emails in quests.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Copilot > For learners:
Embeddable Seller Copilot enables you to integrate the full Seller Copilot experience directly into your internal web applications, such as SharePoint sites, partner portals, LMS, or intranets.

Seller Copilot creates the most value when it is available at the point of work. When assistance is separated from the daily workflow, teams often lose context, speed, and consistency. This release solves that challenge by providing a secure, repeatable integration model that delivers reliable answers and guidance exactly when and where decisions are made.

By embedding Seller Copilot into your own platforms, you achieve:

- Faster execution and decision-making: Answers are available immediately within the flow of work, reducing time lost to context switching or searching across disconnected tools.
- Reduced dependency on SMEs: Frontline users can resolve common questions and "how-to" requests instantly, freeing up experts and support teams to focus on high-leverage work.
- Operational scalability: A reusable embed pattern allows you to deploy a consistent coaching and enablement experience across multiple internal surfaces without building custom solutions for each one.
- Unified conversation history: Chat sessions are fully synchronized across platforms. Conversations started on the Mindtickle web or mobile app are automatically available in the embedded view, and any new chats initiated within the embed are instantly accessible on the main platform.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Copilot > For learners > Prerequisites:
Before implementing the integration, ensure the following requirements are met:

Who does what?

- Mindtickle Support will (a) provide your unique shared secret and (b) whitelist your domain.
- Your team will (a) generate the secure signature in your backend and (b) embed the Copilot in your application.

Requirements:

- Iframe support: The target platform (e.g., SharePoint or a custom app) must support embedding external content via iframes.
- Domain whitelisting: Your application's domain must be whitelisted by Mindtickle to allow the Seller Copilot component to load. Contact Mindtickle Support to configure this.
- Shared secret: You must obtain a secure COPILOT_EMBED_SECRET from Mindtickle Support . This key is used to generate the secure signature for authentication.
- User provisioning: The users accessing the embedded copilot must already exist as learners in the Mindtickle platform.
- Browser and environment requirement: Ensure that your hosting environment allows iframe embedding and third-party cookies. Strict browser privacy settings or security policies may block Copilot from loading.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Copilot > For learners > Integration overview:
The integration follows a secure handshake process to authenticate the user and load the copilot interface.

1. Generate signature: Your backend server generates an HMAC-SHA256 signature using the user's details and the shared secret.
2. Authenticate: Your application makes a POST request to the Mindtickle authentication endpoint with the signed parameters. This request is used to securely start the Copilot embed session inside the iframe.
3. Redirect & load: Upon successful validation, the endpoint redirects automatically, and the Copilot interface loads directly within the iframe.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Copilot > For learners > Step 1: Generate the secure signature:
To ensure security, every request to load Seller Copilot must be signed using an HMAC-SHA256 algorithm.

1. Construct the Data String

Concatenate the required fields into a single string. The order is strict:

```
movingFact = name + username + timestamp + sharedSecret
```

2. Generate the Hash

Calculate the signature using the SHA-256 algorithm with your shared secret as the key, and output the result as a hexadecimal string.

Node.js Example (JavaScript)

```javascript
const crypto = require('crypto');

function generateSignature(name, username, timestamp, sharedSecret) {
  const movingFact = `${name}${username}${timestamp}${sharedSecret}`;
  const hmac = crypto.createHmac('sha256', sharedSecret);
  hmac.update(movingFact);
  return hmac.digest('hex');
}
```

Parameters

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| name | The user's display name (can be dynamic). |
| username | The unique identifier (usually email). Must match the user in Mindtickle. |
| timestamp | The current time in epoch milliseconds. |
| sharedSecret | The COPILOT_EMBED_SECRET provided by Mindtickle Support. |
chunks.body:
To ensure security, every request to load Seller Copilot must be signed using an HMAC-SHA256 algorithm.

1. Construct the Data String

Concatenate the required fields into a single string. The order is strict:

```
movingFact = name + username + timestamp + sharedSecret
```

2. Generate the Hash

Calculate the signature using the SHA-256 algorithm with your shared secret as the key, and output the result as a hexadecimal string.

Node.js Example (JavaScript)

```javascript
const crypto = require('crypto');

function generateSignature(name, username, timestamp, sharedSecret) {
  const movingFact = `${name}${username}${timestamp}${sharedSecret}`;
  const hmac = crypto.createHmac('sha256', sharedSecret);
  hmac.update(movingFact);
  return hmac.digest('hex');
}
```

Parameters

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| name | The user's display name (can be dynamic). |
| username | The unique identifier (usually email). Must match the user in Mindtickle. |
| timestamp | The current time in epoch milliseconds. |
| sharedSecret | The COPILOT_EMBED_SECRET provided by Mindtickle Support. |

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Copilot > For learners > Step 2: Implement the authentication API:
Once the signature is generated, your application must send these details to the Mindtickle authentication endpoint.

1. Authenticate partner user

This endpoint validates the partner's signature and returns the session details required to load the embedded copilot.

Request URL

```
POST https://<your_subdomain>.mindtickle.com/api/user/login/partner/copilot
```

Request parameters

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| nameREQUIRED | string | The display name to show in the chat interface. This does not need to match the user's official Mindtickle name record. |
| usernameREQUIRED | string | The user's email address or unique identifier. This must match the user's record in Mindtickle exactly. |
| timestampREQUIRED | number | Current epoch time in milliseconds. |
| signatureREQUIRED | string | The HMAC-SHA256 hex digest signature. |
| redirecturi | string | OPTIONAL Custom redirect URI. Defaults to /new/ui/learner/singleton/copilot. |

Request example

Note: You will pass these fields as part of the iframe embed flow (see the Frontend embedding section).

```json
{
  "name": "Jane Doe",
  "username": "jane.doe@example.com",
  "timestamp": 1705132800000,
  "signature": "5d41402abc4b2a76b9719d911017c592..."
}
```

2. Backend output (Data for frontend)

After generating the signature, your backend service should construct and return the following object to your frontend application. Your frontend will use this data to submit the form request to the iframe.

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| url | The full authentication endpoint URL, including your specific tenant domain. |
| body | Object containing the verified parameters (signature, timestamp, etc.) to be submitted. |

Example output

```json
{
  "url": "https://acme.mindtickle.com/api/user/login/partner/copilot",
  "body": {
    "name": "Jane Doe",
    "username": "jane.doe@example.com",
    "timestamp": 1705132800000,
    "signature": "5d41402abc4b2a76b9719d911017c592..."
  }
}
```

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Copilot > For learners > Step 3: Frontend embedding:
Once your backend receives the response, your frontend should create a hidden form and submit it to the iframe target.

1. Create an <iframe> with a unique name attribute (e.g., copilot-frame ).
  - Note: For platforms like SharePoint, you may need to wrap the iframe in an app package rather than embedding the HTML directly.
  - Sizing: It is recommended to set the iframe height and width to 100% of the container or a fixed convenient size (e.g., 600px) to ensure the interface is usable.
2. Construct a <form> with method="POST" , action=response.url , and target="copilot-frame" .
3. Add hidden input fields for every key-value pair in response.body .
4. Submit the form to load the authenticated session into the iframe.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Copilot > For learners > API error reference:
If the authentication fails, the API returns a JSON response with an error message and status code.

| HTTP status | Error message | Cause | Resolution |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | Missing required fields | One or more parameters are missing from the request body. | Ensure all 4 required fields are included in the payload. |
| 400 | Invalid username | The username format is invalid or malformed. | Verify the username is a valid email format without special characters. |
| 401 | Copilot embed not configured | The COPILOT_EMBED_SECRET is not set on Mindtickle's server. | Contact Mindtickle support to check the server-side configuration. |
| 401 | Invalid signature | The signature in the request does not match the expected value. | Verify: (1) Correct shared secret, (2) Exact concatenation order, (3) Correct hashing algorithm. |
| 401 | Request expired | The timestamp is older than 5 minutes or in the future. | Generate a fresh Date.now() timestamp immediately before the request. Sync server clock. |
| 404 | User not found | The username does not exist as a learner in Mindtickle. | Ensure the user is provisioned in Mindtickle. Check for case sensitivity or trailing spaces. |
| 500 | Internal server error | Unexpected server-side error. | Retry the request. If persistent, contact support with request details. |

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Copilot > For learners > Troubleshooting guide:
If the embedded component fails to load, use the following guide to resolve common errors.

- Invalid signature (401): Verify that the shared secret is correct and that the concatenation order for the signature is exactly name + username + timestamp + sharedSecret . Ensure there is no extra whitespace.
- Request expired (401): The timestamp is older than 5 minutes. Generate a fresh Date.now() timestamp immediately before the request and ensure your server clock is synchronized (NTP).
- User not found (404): The username provided does not exist in Mindtickle. Ensure the user is provisioned and the email format matches exactly.
- Iframe shows a blank page: This often indicates a Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) or X-Frame-Options issue.
  - Checklist: Confirm your admin has completed domain whitelisting and shared secret setup with Mindtickle Support.
  - Support tip: If you need to contact Mindtickle Support , provide your domain and the request timestamp to speed up resolution.
- Redirect not working: Ensure third-party cookies are enabled or configured with SameSite=None; Secure to allow the session to be established within the iframe.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Managers and Reviewers > Mission > Pending missions:
This tab displays all the missions assigned to you as a reviewer that have not been reviewed. You can further filter these missions by:

- Mission : Use this filter to sort missions by their mission name.
- Learner : Use this filter to sort missions using the learner's name.
- Priority : Use this filter to sort missions where the admin has assigned you as a Required , Recommended, or Optional reviewer
  - Required : Review is mandatory to calculate the learner's final score.
  - Recommended : Your review counts towards the learner's final score, but it isn't mandatory.
  - Optional : You can submit your review, but it won't count towards the learner's final score.
- Sort submissions by: Use this option to choose how submissions are ordered in the list to help you review them easily.
  - Oldest submitted first : Shows older submitted missions at the top.
  - Recently submitted firs t: Shows the most recently submitted missions at the top.
  - Mission name (A–Z) : Shows submissions by mission name in alphabetical order
  - Mission name (Z–A) : Shows submissions by mission name in reverse alphabetical order.

Note: If missions assigned to you are not reviewed and have passed their due date, they appear next to the Priority option, as "x" missions are overdue.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Content Center > Version types:
Every file in Content Center automatically maintains a complete version history. The system differentiates between updates by categorizing them into minor and major versions, depending on the type of change applied.

| Version type | Triggeredby | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Minor version | Metadata updates | Created when adjustments are made to specific file metadata rather than the physical file itself. A minor version is triggered only when the file name is updated or when tags are added or removed. The version number remains the same (e.g., V1), but the version history records these specific updates. For example, the version history log details exactly when tags are modified or when a file name is updated:Tags modified (Feb 20, 2026, 3:29 PM by Alex Fry)Tags added: Communication SkillsTags modified (Feb 20, 2026, 3:29 PM by Alex Fry)Tags removed: QuestioningInfo modified (Feb 20, 2026, 12:51 PM by Alex Fry)File name: Define excellence with Mindtickle.pdf → Define Excellence with Mindtickle |
| Major version | File replacements | Created when a) the current file is replaced with a newly uploaded file, b) when an external system syncs a new file update, or c) when a previous version is restored. This action bumps the version number up (e.g., from V1 to V2).Important: Please note the following impacts when replacing files:The new file will automatically reflect across all locations where it is currently used. To see exactly where the file is used across assets, hubs, modules, and series, check the "Used in location" tab in the file details sidebar.The original file will not be available once replaced.Learners who have already completed this content in their modules will keep their scores. |

Note:

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Content Center > View version history:
You can easily identify and access version information directly from the Content Center interface by following these steps:

1. Locate the file: On the Content Center homepage or within any folder, locate your file. You can see the total number of versions at a glance in the dedicated Version column.
2. Open the file details page: Click on the specific file to open its details page.
3. Access version history: From the file details page, you can open the version history view in one of two ways: Header link: Click the current version number listed directly below the file name in the header. More options menu: Click the the More options menu located in the header and select Manage versions .
4. Review the version history: Once the version history view is open, the Version history sidebar appears on the right side of the screen. This displays a chronological audit log of all changes, the user who made the edits, and the exact timestamp of the update. For details on minor and major versions, see the “ Version types ” section.
5. You can use the browser back button or the breadcrumb navigation at the top of the page to exit this view.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Content Center > Preview and restore versions:
1. From the Version history sidebar, you can click on any previous version to preview what the file looked like before deciding to restore it.
2. Once you have previewed a previous version, you can click the Restore button to revert the file to that specific state.
3. The following pop-up appears: Important: Please note the following impacts when restoring files:
  - The selected version will be restored as a completely new version (for example, restoring version 1 will create the next sequential version number).
  - The file will be automatically updated across all locations where it is currently used. To see exactly where the file is used across assets, hubs, modules, and series, check the "Used in location" tab in the file details sidebar.
  - Learners who have already completed this content in their modules will keep their scores.
4. Click Restore to restore the file to a previous version.
5. Restoring a file does not delete the history. Instead, the restored file becomes the new active version and receives a major version bump. Note : The Restore action only restores the physical file itself; it does not revert metadata like the file title or tags. For example, if you are currently on version 6 and choose to restore version 3, the newly restored file will be labeled as version 7, and it will retain the title and tags from version 6.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle APIs > xAPI APIs:
This article documents Mindtickle's read-only xAPI statements endpoint for retrieving learner progress and activity records. Applicable to all Mindtickle module types, it allows external systems, such as a Learning Record Store (LRS) or an enterprise data warehouse, to programmatically query and extract this data.

Conforming to the standard Experience API (xAPI) specification, this endpoint provides structured data regarding module-level engagement. External systems can retrieve learner progress by tracking standard verbs representing their status, specifically not_started, in_progress, and completed. Every statement returned by this API strictly adheres to the core xAPI data model, defining a comprehensive learning event through the following components:

- Actor: The individual Mindtickle learner performing the action, uniquely identified by their email address (mbox).
- Verb: The action taken or the specific progress state achieved by the learner.
- Object: The target learning activity, such as a specific Mindtickle module or Instructor-Led Training (ILT) session.
- Timestamp: The precise date and time the learning event occurred.

Mindtickle APIs use OAuth 2.0 authentication. To authorize your request, you must include a Bearer token in your HTTP header. This token is generated by exchanging your API Key and Secret Key (found in your admin settings) via the authentication endpoint.

For detailed information, see the "Authentication" section in this article.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle APIs > xAPI APIs > Endpoint details > Request parameters:
Query parameters

| Parameter | Type | Description | Values/Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| agentREQUIRED | string | The Mindtickle learner (xAPI Agent) for whom you want to retrieve records | Note: You must URL-encode the JSON object. For example, {"mbox":"mailto:alex@mt.com"} becomes %7B%22mbox%22%3A%22mailto%3Aalex%40mt.com%22%7D.Incorrect encoding will result in 4xx errors. The mbox value must be a full mailto IRI. |
| verb | string | Filters by module status | Supported values:• not_started: Learner has not begun the module.• in_progress: Learner has started but not completed the module.• completed: Learner has completed the module. |
| limit | integer | Maximum number of statements to return in the current page | Controls how many statements are returned at once. Use this to break large data sets into smaller chunks, then use the more URL in the response to fetch the next page. |

Request example

```http
GET https://api.prod-us.mindtickle.com/services/data/v4.0/xapi/statements?agent=%7B%22mbox%22%3A%22mailto%3Aalex.fry%40mindtickle.com%22%7D&limit=2&verb=not_started
```

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle APIs > xAPI APIs > Endpoint details > Response:
The API returns a JSON object with statement results and a continuation cursor (if more data is available).

Response parameters

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| statements | array | A list of xAPI statement objects representing individual learner activities. |
| statements[].id | string | The unique identifier for this specific learning record. |
| statements[].actor | object | The Mindtickle learner performing the action. This object includes their name (name) and email address/username (mbox). |
| statements[].verb | object | The specific status update or action recorded for the learner. The display field will show the current progress state: not_started, in_progress, or completed. |
| statements[].object | object | The specific Mindtickle activity being tracked. This includes the unique module ID (id), the module name (definition.name), and the module type (e.g., ILT, course, quick update, and so on). |
| statements[].timestamp | string | The exact date and time the learner reached this progress state (ISO 8601 format). |
| statements[].stored | string | The date and time this record was officially saved in Mindtickle’s database (ISO 8601 format). |
| more | string | A continuation URL with more_id. Provided when there are more results than the current page limit. To fetch the next set of records, make a GET request to this exact URL without modification. |

Response example

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle APIs > xAPI APIs > Notes:
- Agent parameter encoding: URL-encoded form is required in the final request. For example, by email (mbox): agent={"mbox":"mailto:alex.fry@mindtickle.com"} becomes %7B%22mbox%22%3A%22mailto%3Aalex.fry%40mindtickle.com%22%7D . Always URL-encode the agent JSON. Incorrect encoding is a common source of 4xx errors. The mbox value must be a full mailto IRI (e.g., mailto:user@domain.com ).
- Pagination: When the response includes more , perform another GET using that exact URL (including the encoded more_id ). Continue until more is absent or empty. Always follow the exact more URL until it is absent; do not re-apply original query parameters when using continuation.
- Best practices:
  - Use limit to manage payload size and iterate via more for full result sets.
  - Cache or store the last processed statement ID if building incremental syncs.
  - Validate timestamps in ISO 8601; use stored for ordering when reconstructing event timelines.
- Troubleshooting: If no results are returned, confirm the agent is correctly URL-encoded and exists in the tenant. Try removing filters ( verb ) to broaden the search.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Setup > Page Builder for learning site homepages:
The Canvas widget is a powerful, no-code design tool within the Page Builder that empowers administrators to create visually rich, brand-consistent content. Available for learning site homepages, series pages, and hub overview pages, it eliminates the need for custom HTML or engineering support.

By using an intuitive drag-and-drop interface, you can build modular, responsive layouts that maintain your brand's visual identity while seamlessly coexisting alongside standard out-of-the-box widgets.

Designed specifically for enablement teams, this feature transforms how you deliver and structure content. It allows you to visually construct pages using distinct, purpose-driven elements — such as text, images, and buttons — without relying on external development resources. You have full control over the visual hierarchy, allowing you to intentionally design what your audience sees first, what supports that message, and what actions they should take next.

Because the Canvas widget is modular, it enables faster content updates and ensures a consistent aesthetic across your entire enablement journey. Whether you are highlighting key announcements, surfacing specific assets, or structuring a complex learning environment, the widget provides true design flexibility directly within the platform.

Note: The Canvas widget is currently in beta and not enabled by default. To enable it for your Mindtickle instance, please contact Mindtickle Support.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Setup > Page Builder for learning site homepages > Add the Canvas widget to a page:
You can seamlessly integrate the Canvas widget alongside your existing standard widgets on the homepage or series/hub overview page. Perform the following to add the Canvas widget:

1. Open the Page Builder for your desired learning site homepage , series overview page , or hub overview page .
2. In the Widgets side panel → General category, drag and drop the Canvas widget onto your page layout.
3. Double-click the widget or click the Edit icon to open the full-screen Canvas editor and begin designing. Your progress will save automatically.
4. Click Preview in the top-right corner to preview how the Canvas widget will appear on the page. Click Exit to leave the widget editor and return to the homepage or series/hub overview page, where you can publish the page to make your changes visible to all learners.
5. The following image shows an example of a configured Canvas widget.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Setup > Page Builder for learning site homepages > UI overview:
Use the descriptions below to familiarize yourself with the key areas of the Canvas widget interface. This provides a quick understanding of the user interface (UI) and the actions available to you.

Top navigation bar: Switch between web and mobile views, adjust the zoom level, check the auto-save status, preview your design, and exit the editor.

Left panel → Section: Establish the structural foundation of your design. Drag and drop a section onto the canvas to define column structures (ranging from one to five columns) and organize your content.

Left panel → Text, image, and button: Access your core design elements. Drag and drop text, image, and button elements directly into your sections to build out the user experience.

Central canvas: Drag and drop elements here to build your page, and use inline controls directly on the canvas to reposition, duplicate, or delete specific elements.

Right panel: Configure detailed styling and layout properties. This context-aware panel updates automatically to show specific settings — such as padding, colors, typography, and links — for the currently selected canvas, section, or element.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Setup > Page Builder for learning site homepages > UI overview > On-canvas actions:
- Section actions: Hover over a section, then hover over the More options (three-dot) icon on its left edge to access an inline menu with these actions:
  - Edit: Opens the section's layout and styling configurations in the right panel.
  - Move up / Move down: Vertically reorder the entire section within your page layout.
  - Delete: Remove the section and all of the columns and elements housed within it.
  - Add below: Quickly insert a new, blank section directly beneath the current one.
  - Add columns: Hover a section, then click the plus button on its right edge to add columns.
  - Adjust section height: Click the border of a section and drag it vertically using the button to manually increase or decrease the section's overall height.
- Column actions: Hover over a column, then hover over the More options (three-dot) icon on its top edge to access an inline menu with these actions:
  - Edit: Opens the column’s layout and styling configurations in the right panel.
  - Move left / Move right: Horizontally reorder the column's placement within its parent section.
  - Delete: Remove the column and all of the elements housed within it.
  - Adjust column width: Hover over the vertical separator line between two columns and drag it horizontally using the button to change the width of the adjacent columns.
- Element actions: Hover over on any individual element ( Text , Image , or Button ) to access an inline menu with these actions:
  - Edit: Opens the element's specific configuration settings in the right panel (or activates the text editor for text blocks). Note : Deleting an element removes it and all associated content. Learners will only see this change after you publish the page (homepage, series, or hub overview) you are currently editing.
  - Clone: Instantly duplicate the element, placing the copy immediately below the original within the same column/section.
  - Delete: Promptly remove the specific element from the canvas.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Setup > Page Builder for learning site homepages > Structure and layout hierarchy:
The Canvas widget uses a flexible, tiered architecture to organize content. This hierarchy ensures that designs remain visually cohesive, properly aligned, and fully responsive across different devices. Every piece of content exists within a defined section, preventing layout issues and making responsive design straightforward.

| Configuration level | Description | Customization options |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Canvas level | Foundational, global settings that define the overall look and feel of your entire widget. | Background colors, gradients, and images. Font and typography defaults (web-safe fonts like Inter, Open Sans, Lato, Open Sans, Helvetica, Montserrat, and Arial). Default padding and spacing. |
| Section level | Structural building blocks that organize your layout into columns. | Column layouts (from 1 to 5 columns). Precise column width adjustments (e.g., 50-50, 70-30). Section-specific backgrounds, shadows, padding, borders, and corner radius. |
| Element level | The individual content components that you drag and drop into your section columns. | Fine-tuned styling for specific text blocks, images, and buttons, overriding canvas-level defaults when necessary. |

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Setup > Page Builder for learning site homepages > Structure and layout hierarchy > Canvas-level configurations:
These foundational settings define the overall look and feel of the entire canvas widget. Establishing these global/default parameters ensures a consistent design language that cascades down to all subsequent content.

Note: The configurations applied at the canvas level establish the global defaults for your entire design. With the exception of the structural Canvas spacing and the overall page Background, you maintain complete flexibility to override the rest of the global default settings. You can easily apply custom settings directly to individual Section, Text, Image, and Button elements as you build your canvas.

You can access these in the canvas settings panel by clicking the Settings icon in the top navigation bar.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Setup > Page Builder for learning site homepages > Structure and layout hierarchy > Canvas-level configurations:
- Canvas : Manage the overall visual density of the widget. Note : Unlike other defaults, this is a strict global setting and cannot be overridden at the element level.
  - Padding (in px) : Set the default inner spacing by adjusting the left, top, right, and bottom values.
  - Space between sections (in px) : Define the exact vertical gap between different structural blocks.
- Section : Establish the default structural behaviors for all sections added to your layout.
  - Padding (in px) : Configure the default inner spacing (left, top, right, bottom) for your sections.
  - Space between columns (in px) : Set the default horizontal gap between columns within a section.
  - Corner radius (in px) : Define the default rounding for section corners (top left, top right, bottom left, bottom right).
  - Shadow : Apply a default visual drop shadow (none, light, medium, or dark).
- Background : Set a primary visual backdrop for the entire widget. Note : Unlike other defaults, this is a strict global setting and cannot be overridden at the element level.
  - Background : Choose a solid color, apply a gradient, or upload a custom image.
- Styles : Define the global color scheme for your text elements.
  - Font color : Specify the default color for all standard text.
  - Link color : Set the default color for all hyperlinks.
- Typography : Standardize your text appearance across the widget.
  - Default font size (in px) : Establish the base text size.
  - Default font : Select the primary font family (such as Inter).
- Button : Establish a universal style for all call-to-action button elements.
  - Button color : Set the default resting color of the button.
  - Button hover color : Choose the color displayed when a user hovers over the button.
  - Text color : Specify the font color inside the button.
  - Font size (in px) : Define the text size for the button label.
  - Corner radius (in px) : Adjust the top left, top right, bottom left, and bottom right corners to create square, rounded, or pill-shaped buttons.
  - Padding (in px) : Set the inner spacing (left, top, right, bottom) around the button text.
  - Weight : Select the font thickness: regular or bold.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Setup > Page Builder for learning site homepages > Structure and layout hierarchy > Section-level configurations:
Sections and section columns act as the foundational building blocks of your canvas layout. A section defines the broader structural row, while section columns exist within that section to house your specific design elements (like text, images, and buttons).

Because they serve similar but distinct structural purposes, both sections and section columns offer similar configuration settings, such as backgrounds, borders, and shadows. However, they are customized separately. This separation gives you the ultimate flexibility to style an overarching parent section entirely differently from the individual columns inside it.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Setup > Page Builder for learning site homepages > Structure and layout hierarchy > Section-level configurations > Section configurations:
- Layout : Control the spacing and shape of the parent section.
  - Padding (in px) : Adjust the inner spacing of the section by setting the left, top, right, and bottom values.
  - Corner radius (in px) : Adjust the rounding of the section's outer edges by setting values for the top left, top right, bottom left, and bottom right corners.
- Styles : Customize the visual appearance of the section to make it stand out or visually separate it from other blocks.
  - Background : Select the primary fill for the section.
    - Color : Choose a standard solid fill color.
    - Gradient : Create a multi-color transition. You can choose a LINEAR or RADIAL gradient style. For linear gradients, you can set the exact angle (°). Use the Stop field to control the exact percentage where a color transitions. The advanced color picker allows you to use an eyedropper tool, manually enter exact color values across multiple models ( HEX , RGB , HSL , HSV , CMYK , and A for alpha/opacity), and utilize a Color Guide to automatically generate mathematically harmonious colors ( Analogous , Monochromatic , Triad , Tetrad ).
    - Image : Upload or select an image to use as the background. Set the Image fit to either Cover (scales the image to fill the entire space, potentially cropping it) or Contain (scales the image so the entire image is visible within the space).
  - Border size (in px) : Define the thickness of the section's outer border.
  - Border : Select the exact color for the section's border using the color picker.
  - Shadow : Apply a visual drop shadow to the section (choose from none, light, medium, or dark).

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Setup > Page Builder for learning site homepages > Structure and layout hierarchy > Section-level configurations > Column configurations:
When you select an individual column within a section, the right panel updates to show column-specific settings. This allows you to highlight or frame individual blocks of content inside the parent row.

- Styles : Customize the visual appearance of the individual column.
  - Background : Select the primary fill specifically for the column. You have the exact same robust options here as you do for the section background, including Color , Gradient (with advanced color models and guides), and Image .
  - Border size (in px) : Define the thickness of the column's outer border.
  - Corner radius (in px) : Round the outer edges of the individual column by setting values for the top left, top right, bottom left, and bottom right corners.
  - Border : Select the exact color for the column's border using the color picker.
- Layout : Control the depth and visual hierarchy of the column.
  - Shadow : Apply a visual drop shadow specifically to this column (choose from none, light, medium, or dark) to make it visually pop out from the parent section.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Setup > Page Builder for learning site homepages > Add and customize elements:
Elements are the core visual and interactive components — specifically text, images, and buttons — that you drop into your section columns to build the actual user experience. While your canvas and section settings provide the structural foundation of the page, elements are the specific pieces of content your audience will read, see, and interact with.

Once an element is placed on the canvas, selecting it opens a dedicated set of configuration options in the right panel. This allows you to fine-tune its specific content, add interactive links, control its precise alignment, and apply custom styling that overrides your global canvas defaults.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Setup > Page Builder for learning site homepages > Add and customize elements > Text elements:
Use text elements to add messaging, instructions, or context to the canvas widget. When you select a text element on your canvas, you can access the following configuration options in the right panel:

- Text editor : Format your content using the built-in rich text editor controls.
  - Standard formatting : Apply bold, italic, and underline styles to your text.
  - Colors : Customize the specific text color or apply a background highlight color.
  - Styles and sizes : Choose a specific text block format (such as Paragraph) from the dropdown and set an exact font size (e.g., 16px).
  - Links and emojis : Embed hyperlinks or add emojis directly into your messaging.
  - Lists : Organize information cleanly using bulleted or numbered lists.
  - Clear formatting : Quickly remove all applied styles to reset the text to its default state.
- Layout : Control the precise positioning and depth of the text block within its column.
  - Alignment : Align the text block to the Top , Middle , Bottom , Left , Center , or Right of its container.
  - Arrangement : Manage overlapping text elements on your canvas by selecting Move to the top , Move forward , Move behind , or Move backward . This setting is available when there are at least two text elements.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Setup > Page Builder for learning site homepages > Add and customize elements > Image elements:
Upload and manage visuals to make your canvas more engaging. When you select an image element on your canvas, you can access the following configuration options in the right panel:

- Content : Choose the specific visual asset you want to display.
  - Add image : Click to upload a new image file or select an existing one.
- Add link : Make the image interactive by turning it into a clickable resource.
  - External URL or Mindtickle content : Enter any external webpage URL, or search directly for internal Mindtickle content (a specific series, module, hub, or asset) to link it to the image.
- Style : Customize the framing and visual effects applied to the image.
  - Border size (in px) : Define the thickness of the image's outer border.
  - Border : Select the exact color for the border using the color picker.
  - Corner radius (in px) : Adjust the rounding of the image's corners by setting values for the top left, top right, bottom left, and bottom right.
  - Shadow : Apply a visual drop shadow to the image (choose from none, light, medium, or dark).
- Arrangement : Control the precise positioning and depth of the image within its column.
  - Alignment : Align the image to the Top , Left , Middle , Center , Bottom , or Right of its container.
  - Arrangement : Manage overlapping elements on your canvas by selecting Move to the top , Move forward , Move behind , or Move backward .

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Setup > Page Builder for learning site homepages > Add and customize elements > Button elements:
- Add link : Configure the destination and the visible label of the button.
  - Display text : Customize the exact text that appears on the button (e.g., "Click here").
  - External URL or Mindtickle content : Enter any external webpage URL, or search directly for internal Mindtickle content (a specific series, module, hub, or asset) to link it to the button.
- Styles : Customize the visual appearance and shape of the button.
  - Button color : Select the default resting color of the button using the color picker.
  - Button hover color : Choose the color displayed when a user hovers over the button.
  - Text color : Specify the font color inside the button.
  - Corner radius (in px) : Adjust the rounding of the button's corners by setting values for the top left, top right, bottom left, and bottom right (allowing you to create square, slightly rounded, or fully pill-shaped buttons).
  - Padding (in px) : Set the inner spacing around the button text by adjusting the left, top, right, and bottom values.
- Text : Define the typography of the button label.
  - Font size (in px) : Define the precise text size for the button label.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Setup > Page Builder for learning site homepages > Mobile view customization:
The Canvas widget is inherently responsive, automatically translating your web layout into a stacked, mobile-friendly format. However, to ensure your content looks perfect on any device, you have access to a dedicated mobile view workspace. This allows you to hyper-optimize the mobile experience without disrupting your desktop design.

- Design workflow : Always build, structure, and finalize your web view (desktop view) first. Once your core design is complete, click the Mobile view icon in the top navigation bar to switch workspaces and begin your mobile-specific tweaks.
- Layout and spacing adjustments : In the mobile view, you can independently modify settings like padding, alignment, font sizes, and element arrangement. This ensures you can tighten up spacing, adjust column flows, or make key messaging more prominent for mobile users without altering the web/desktop version.
- Content tailoring : You can customize the actual content specifically for mobile screens. For instance, you can truncate lengthy text blocks so they are easier to read on the go, or replace a high-resolution, full-width desktop image with a separate, vertically oriented image that fits smaller screens better.
- Element restrictions : To maintain the underlying structural consistency between your views, you cannot add new elements or delete existing ones while in the mobile view (all elements in the left panel will be disabled). All structural additions and deletions must be handled exclusively in the primary web/desktop view.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Setup > Page Builder for learning site homepages > Best practices:
To ensure your pages are visually engaging, consistent, and easy to maintain, keep these best practices in mind as you build the Canvas widget:

- Establish global defaults first: Before adding any individual text blocks or buttons, configure your Canvas level configurations (like default typography, link colors, and button styles). Setting this global baseline first saves you from having to manually style every single element and ensures strict brand consistency across the page.
- Design for web, optimize for mobile: Always build your complete structural layout and finalize your content in the web view first. Because you cannot add or delete elements in the mobile workspace, treat the mobile view strictly as a final polish step to tweak padding, alignment, and font sizes for smaller screens.
- Leverage internal content links: When configuring buttons and images, use the internal search feature to link directly to specific Mindtickle series, modules, or hubs. This creates a seamless learning journey and keeps users engaged within the platform rather than bouncing them out to external URLs.
- Use spacing intentionally: Avoid cluttered layouts by utilizing the Padding and Space between sections configurations. Giving your sections and columns ample visual "breathing room" (white space) makes the content much easier for learners to scan and digest.
- Ensure high text contrast: If you use gradients or uploaded images for section backgrounds, make sure your text elements remain highly legible. You may need to override the global font color on specific text blocks (e.g., using white text over a dark image) to maintain accessibility.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Copilot > For admins > Best practices for custom instructions:
- Keep it focused on communication style: Custom instructions work best when they define how Copilot should communicate, such as tone, brevity, structure, and terminology. Avoid turning it into a long policy document.
- Start with a simple baseline and iterate: Begin with a core set of rules (tone + conciseness + terminology + structure). Once your sellers start using Copilot, refine the instructions based on what they actually need most (e.g., tighter talk tracks, more email-ready outputs, clearer terminology).
- Be explicit about terminology (highest impact): Include your official names and common aliases so responses match the language your teams use every day:
  - Product and feature names (and legacy names to avoid)
  - Editions/packages naming
  - Internal program names (plays, initiatives, frameworks)
  - Acronyms to use consistently
- Use a consistent response structure: A predictable structure makes answers easier to scan and reuse. A common default is:
  - Direct answer (1–2 lines)
  - Key points (3–5 bullets)
  - Next steps (2–3 bullets)
- Prefer a few strong rules over many weak ones: 3–8 clear instructions usually work better than 25+ vague suggestions. Keep wording direct and unambiguous (e.g., "Use bullets," "Avoid fluff," "Use exact product names").
- Add clear do’s and don’ts: Do’s and don’ts help keep responses consistent across different users and question types:
  - Do: keep answers concise, structured, and seller-ready
  - Do: use official terminology and spellings
  - Don’t: use generic filler or overly long paragraphs by default
- Keep it maintainable: Use one core template. Update terminology periodically as names evolve.
- Test before rolling out broadly: Try your custom instructions with a small set of common seller questions (call prep, objections, follow-ups). If the outputs feel too long, too generic, or use the wrong terminology, refine the instructions and retest.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Copilot > For admins > Key components of custom instructions:
The most successful enterprise organizations structure their custom instructions using a declarative framework. You don't need to implement all of these on day one, but a robust configuration typically includes:

1. Role & objective: Give the AI a clear persona (e.g., "You are an expert sales enablement assistant").
2. Tone & style: Define the voice (e.g., "professional yet approachable") and specify what to avoid (e.g., "marketing fluff" or "hype").
3. Default structure: Provide a visual layout for easily scannable answers (e.g., requiring a 1–2 line direct answer, followed by bullets).
4. Company terminology: List exact brand names, mandatory acronyms, and direct "use X, not Y" mappings.
5. Do's and don'ts: Guidelines for consistent behavior (e.g., "keep it practical," "avoid absolute claims," "don't use unapproved language").
6. Optional: Industry guardrails: Recommended for regulated verticals (e.g., Pharma, Medical devices) to reinforce approved language and avoid risky phrasing.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Copilot > For admins > Custom instruction examples > Core example (recommended baseline):
You can use this baseline as a starting point and fill in your company details:

```
# Role & tone
- Act as an expert sales assistant for [Company name]. 
- Respond in a friendly, professional tone suitable for corporate communications. Keep it approachable, as if speaking to a colleague.
- Avoid hype, marketing fluff, and overly salesy language. Use measured language ("recommended," "typically") instead of absolutes ("guaranteed," "always").

# Conciseness & structure
- Provide short, direct responses without unnecessary elaboration. Expand only when the user explicitly asks for deep detail.
- Default to this structure whenever possible:
  1. Direct answer / summary (1-2 lines)
  2. Key points (3-5 bullets)
  3. Next steps / talk track (2-3 bullets)

# Company & product terminology
Strictly adhere to our official naming conventions:
- Company name: Spell exactly as "[Company name]"
- Products: [Product A], [Product B], [Platform name]
- Editions/packages: [Starter / Pro / Enterprise]
- Feature mappings: Always say "[Preferred feature name]" (Never use the legacy term "[Old/internal name]")
- Acronyms: Use [List of acronyms] as-is. Do not expand them unless explicitly asked.

# Guardrails
- Do keep responses structured, specific, and seller-ready.
- Don't use generic filler language or long unstructured paragraphs by default.
```

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > FAQs > Will IP restrictions affect the Mindtickle integration:
Yes, IP restrictions affect the Mindtickle integration. If your company allows access only from approved IP addresses, it blocks requests from other IPs. Since Mindtickle sends API requests from its own IP addresses, your system blocks those requests unless you approve them, which can disrupt the integration.

To avoid disruptions, contact Mindtickle Support to obtain the outbound IP address ranges and whitelist them in your system. This ensures that your system approves Mindtickle’s API requests and the integration functions without interruptions.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Release Notes > Enhancements > Upgraded Asset Hub analytics: Redesigned dashboards and enhanced insights:
This release introduces upgraded Asset Hub analytics, featuring redesigned dashboards, unified reports, and expanded data visualizations. These improvements make it easier to track asset engagement, understand revenue impact, and maintain content hygiene, all in one place.

Access the updated analytics under Analytics → Assets on the admin site. The new design consolidates the previous five dashboards and reports into three unified tabs, making it easier to find and analyze your data.

A. Unified navigation and reporting

- Merged dashboards and reports: High-level charts and granular reports are now combined.
  - Engagement dashboard tab: Engagement dashboard and report are consolidated.
  - Revenue impact dashboard tab: Revenue impact dashboard and report are combined.
- Consistent layout: All dashboards share a standard structure for filtering, sorting, and exporting, reducing the need to switch between tools.

B. Enhanced visualizations and interactive tables

- Expanded charts: Trend lines, donut charts, and scatter plots provide deeper insight into asset shares and buyer engagement.
- Detailed tables: Row-level tables for assets, users, and deals allow in-depth analysis without exporting separate reports.
- Interactive widgets: Clicking a chart element dynamically updates all related tables and charts to explore specific data points.

C. Dashboard highlights

- Engagement dashboard: Tracks monthly internal and external asset usage and shows which marketing assets are used as templates and which slides are most personalized.
- Revenue impact dashboard: Displays engagement by prospect title, reveals which content resonates with roles such as economic buyers, provides deal-level insights, and shows revenue from assets shared through email and Digital Sales Rooms (DSR) linked to your CRM.
- Audit report: Provides maintenance recommendations, identifies duplicate assets, and shows asset distribution by type, owner, and usage to highlight content gaps.

D. Filters and data download

Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Release Notes > Enhancements > Setup guidance for the /mindtickle command in Copilot for Slack:
Seller Copilot now guides users when the /mindtickle command is used in a channel or group DM where the Mindtickle app hasn’t been added yet. Instead of no response, users will see a private guidance message with clear steps to add the app and continue using Copilot.

This update improves the Seller Copilot experience in Slack by reducing setup confusion and helping users quickly understand why Copilot is not responding and what to do next.

How it works

When the /mindtickle command is used in a channel or group DM where the Mindtickle app hasn’t been added, users receive an ephemeral message (visible only to them) with guidance tailored to the conversation type:

- Channel: The message includes simple steps to add the Mindtickle app to the channel and retry the command.
- Group DM: The message offers two options: Create a new group DM with the Mindtickle app added from the start, or convert the existing group DM to a private channel and invite the app there.

Note: This enhancement applies only to the /mindtickle slash command. It does not affect @mindtickle mention flows.

For more information, see Chat with Seller Copilot in Slack.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Assets > Actions on all widgets > Download widget data:
Use the three-dot menu in the upper-right corner of a widget to download its data. Download options vary by widget type.

Chart widgets can be downloaded as:

- PNG image (for sharing or presentations)
- CSV file (for data analysis)

Table widgets can be downloaded as:

- PNG image (for sharing or presentations)
- CSV, Excel, or PDF file (for data export and analysis)

Note: When downloading a table as a PNG image, only the rows and columns currently visible on your screen are captured in the file.

When downloading a table as an Excel file, you can choose between the following formats:

- Repeat rows (recommended): Each row repeats all values, making the data easier to filter, sort, and analyze in a spreadsheet — particularly if you plan to use the data in a pivot table or similar analysis.
- Merge rows: Identical consecutive values are combined into a single cell for a more compact layout. Note that this format may be harder to manipulate in spreadsheets.
