Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Series > Modules tab > Change learner relevance:
This option allows admins to change module relevance for learners across multiple modules.

To change learner relevance,

1. Sign in to the admin site.
2. Click Training in the left navigation panel, then click Series . The Series page is displayed.
3. Select a series. The series is displayed.
4. Click the Modules tab.
5. Select the required modules.
6. Click Edit settings .
7. In the Edit settings screen, click Change learner relevance . The Make changes screen is displayed. Hover over the selected module count to view the supported module types.
8. Select one of the following options:

- All learners in selected modules
- Selected learners in selected modules

9. If you choose the Selected learners in selected modules option, click Select learners.

10. In the displayed pop-up, select the required learners, then click Select.

11. Select a module relevance option for learners: Required, Optional, or Unmarked.

12. Click Continue.The Confirm changes screen is displayed.

13. Review the Current value and New value columns.

The system also displays the modules where the setting is not applicable.

(Optional) Click the Remove icon to exclude a module.

(Optional) Click Undo to restore a module.

14. Click Confirm changes.

A notification displays that updates are in progress and shows the time saved.

Note: If the update fails for any modules, you can retry those modules.

Click Back to series page to navigate to the Series page.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Series > Modules tab > Update progress:
This option allows admins to reset or complete learners' progress across multiple modules.

To update learner progress in multiple modules,

1. Open a series.
2. Click the Modules tab.
3. Select the required modules.
4. Click Edit settings .
5. In the Edit settings screen, click Update progress . The Make changes screen is displayed.
6. Select one of the following options:

- All learners in selected modules
- Selected learners in selected modules

7. If you choose the Selected learners in selected modules option, click Select learners.

8. In the displayed pop-up, select the required learners, then click Select.

9. Select how to update progress:

- Complete progress: Marks the learners as completed for the selected modules. The learners retain their current scores for the modules they have completed and receive the full score for the remaining modules.
- Reset progress: Resets the learner's progress for the selected modules.

10. Click Continue.

The Confirm changes screen is displayed.

11. Review the Current value and New value columns.(Optional) Click the Remove icon to exclude a module.

(Optional) Click Undo to restore a module.

12. Click Confirm changes.A notification displays that updates are in progress.

Note: If the update fails for any modules, you can retry those modules.Click Back to series page to navigate to the Series page.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Series > Modules tab > Edit due date:
This option allows admins to edit learners' due dates across multiple modules.

To edit the learners’ due dates,

1. Open a series.
2. Click the Modules tab.
3. Select the required modules.
4. Click Edit settings .
5. In the Edit settings screen, click Edit due date . The Make changes screen is displayed.
6. Select one of the following options:

- All learners in selected modules
- Selected learners in selected modules

7. If you choose the Selected learners in selected modules option, click Select learners.

8. In the displayed pop-up, select the required learners, then click Select.

9. Select how to update the due date:

A. Set a new due date for learners.

- No. of days after invitation: Set the due date based on a fixed number of days from the invitation date. The number of days after invitation can be set between 1 to 730 days.
- Select a specific date : Choose a specific date as the new due date.

Or

B. Extend due date for learners by.

- Extend the due date by 1–730 days from the existing due date. For example, if the due date is 10 January and it is extended by 10 days, the new due date becomes 20 January.

10. In What happens after the due date?, choose what happens to the modules after the due date:

- Learners can still complete the quick update after the due date passes.
- Module freezes. Learner can’t attempt the module anymore.

11. Click Continue.

The Confirm changes screen is displayed.

12. Review the Current value and New value columns.(Optional) Click the Remove icon to exclude a module.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > AI Interactive roleplay (Beta) > For admins:
Admins can export AI interactive video roleplay missions from a Public series as SCORM packages and embed them in any third-party LMS as courses or quick-update modules. Learners can access mindtickle SCORM role-play content as learning objects (LOs) within modules, creating a seamless, engaging learning experience.

Note: The SCORM package supports only AI interactive roleplay missions in the Public series, with Copilot as the only reviewer.

To export the interactive video roleplay mission as SCORM,

1. Sign in to the admin site.
2. Click Training on the left navigation pane, and then click Series . The Series page opens.
3. Click the public series with the AI interactive video roleplay mission. The series opens.
4. On the Modules tab, click the module with the published video roleplay mission.
5. Click the More options icon, then select Export as SCORM . The system saves the SCORM package as a .ZIP file to your local drive. For detailed information on the AI interactive roleplay mission, see Create an interactive video roleplay mission .

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > AI Interactive roleplay (Beta) > For admins > Embed the SCORM package in training modules:
Admins can embed the SCORM package as a learning object in the course or quick-update modules for learners.

To embed the SCORM in a course or quick-update module,

1. Open a series.
2. Click a course or quick-update module.
3. In the Build tab, click Add learning objects . The Add learning objects pop-up is displayed.
4. Click SCORM to upload the SCORM package from your local drive. The Add SCORM pop-up is displayed.
5. In the Upload file section, select the .ZIP file from your local drive.
6. In the Configure file section, choose how learners view the SCORM file. The following options are available,

- Desktop: This displays the settings for web browsers on desktop devices.
  - Inline (Desktop): Displays within the course page
  - Full screen: Opens in full-screen mode for better focus
- Mobile app: This displays the settings for mobile apps.
  - Inline (Mobile): Displays within the app screen
  - Disable on mobile: Prevents access on mobile devices
- Enable save and exit: Allows learners to save progress and exit anytime

7. Click Save changes.

The system adds the SCORM as an LO.After adding the SCORM, you can rename it using the Edit icon.

You can download the SCROM file to your local drive by clicking the Download icon.

After adding a SCORM file, admins can,

- View configuration
- Replace the SCORM file
- Test the SCORM

Help & Support > Help Center Home > AI Interactive roleplay (Beta) > For admins > Learner tracking:
When learners access the SCORM roleplay, the system updates learner details in the Invite and track tab of the original mission module used to create the SCORM package.

- Learner: The learner’s name and email address.
- Relevance: The module relevance for the learner, whether Required, Optional, or Unmarked.
- Status: The learner’s status for the mission, whether submission pending or completed.
- Reviewers: The mission reviewer. SCORM packages support only Copilot as the reviewer for the AI roleplay mission.
- Submissions: The number of learner submissions.
- Score: The learner’s score.
- Invited on: The invitation date of the learner.

For detailed information on the AI interactive roleplay mission, see Create an interactive video roleplay mission.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > AI Interactive roleplay (Beta) > For admins > Learner experience:
Learners can access the SCORM content as an LO within the course or quick-update modules.To access the SCORM content,

1. Sign in to the learning site.
2. Click Training in the left navigation pane, then click Series . The Series page opens.
3. Click the Assigned tab.
4. Click on a series. For example, Acme Training. The series opens.
5. Click the module with the SCORM content. For example, Acme training. The module overview page displays the course’s description, outline, maximum score, and completion time.
6. Click Start course to begin the module. The module opens.
7. Click the LO with the SCORM video roleplay mission.
8. Click Start roleplay to record your submission. The system generates the insights and transcript for the mission.
9. Click Submit this draft to submit the mission recording.
10. In the Submit Draft? pop-up, click Yes, submit to confirm submission.
11. Click Done . The system updates the learner's score for the LO and completion status in the course overview page. Note: If a learner does not meet the passing criteria, the system shows the Re-attempt module option if the admin enables it.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > FAQs > Common reasons a certificate is not awarded > The learner has not met the certification criteria:
Completing all modules in a series does not always guarantee a certificate. Certifications can be completion-based, score-based, or both. Not all modules in a series may be part of the certification criteria, and criteria may include rule-based logic (for example, Module A AND (Module B OR Module C)).

To verify:

1. Go to the admin site > Training > Series .
2. Select the series and click Settings > Certifications .
3. Click the More options icon on a certificate and select Edit to review the criteria.
4. Compare against the learner's progress in the Learners tab.
5. Criteria by module type: Module typeCertification criteriaSeriesThe learner must complete all modules added to the certification criteria and meet any defined cut-off scores.CourseThe course must be 100% completed. If a score-based cut-off is configured, the learner must also meet the cut-off score.AssessmentThe learner must complete the assessment and achieve a score higher than the passing score.MissionIf a certificate cut-off is configured, the average evaluation score must meet or exceed the cut-off.

For more information, see Add series certifications.

If the certification depends on a reviewer-graded module (such as an assessment or mission), the certificate is awarded only after the review is complete.

3. Alternatively, navigate to the specific assessment or mission module to view pending reviews. If the review is pending, follow up with the assigned reviewer.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > FAQs > Common reasons a certificate is not awarded > The learner completed modules before the certification was activated:
If a learner completed all required modules before the certification was activated, the system does not automatically award the certificate. The learner must complete at least one module in the certification criteria after the activation date.

To resolve:

- Ask the learner to reattempt any one module in the certification criteria, or
- Manually award the certificate to the learner. See How can I manually award or revoke series certifications?

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > FAQs > Common reasons a certificate is not awarded > A required module was moved, archived, or removed:
If a module in the certification criteria is moved to another series, archived, or removed from the learner's access, the certification may become inactive, or the system may not recognize the learner's completion.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > FAQs > Common reasons a certificate is not awarded > A required module was updated, and the learner's progress was reset:
When you update a module and publish the changes for all learners, including those who have already completed it, the learner's completion progress for the changed content is reset:

- Learning content that has changed becomes incomplete - the learner must redo it.
- Content that was not changed remains complete.

This means the learner may have previously met the certification criteria, but the update caused the system to stop recognizing their completion.

To resolve:

- Ask the learner to reattempt the changed content, or
- Manually award the certificate if appropriate. See How can I manually award or revoke series certifications?

For more information on what triggers a progress reset, see:

- How do I update the content in a course or quick update?
- Which changes to a published module trigger a module update or impact learner progress?

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > FAQs > Common reasons a certificate is not awarded > Sequential locking is preventing the learner from completing a required module:
If sequential locking is enabled in a series, modules unlock one at a time. In courses with certification, the next module unlocks only after the learner is certified, not just after completing the course.

If the learner did not meet the course certification criteria (for example, did not achieve the required score), the next module remains locked.

To resolve:

- Ensure the learner can reattempt the course (check if re-attempts are enabled in the course settings).
- If re-attempts are not available, enable them or manually award the course certificate so the next module unlocks.

For more information, see How does sequential locking work per module?

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > FAQs > Common reasons a certificate is not awarded > The certification has expired:
Certifications have a validity period (for example, 3 months, 12 months, or always valid). If the learner's certification has expired, the status shows Expired on the Certifications tab.

If the certificate shows as expired immediately after completion, the validity period may be misconfigured. Review the certification settings and reissue if needed.

Additional scenarios:

- If the learner already has an active certification, the system does not issue a duplicate.
- If the learner is outside the recertification window, they cannot earn a new certificate until the window opens.
- During the recertification window, you cannot manually award the certification. The learner must complete the criteria again within the recertification period.
- After the recertification window has passed, you can manually award the certificate. See How can I manually award or revoke series certifications?

For more information, see Manage series certifications.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > FAQs > Manually awarding a certificate:
If the learner has met all criteria and the system has not issued the certificate, you can manually award it:

1. Navigate to the Learners tab in the series.
2. Click the More options icon, and select Award certificate(s) .
3. Select the certifications to award and click Award certificate .
4. Once awarded, the Certificates awarded column is updated. Note: You must have the Site Owner role or MANAGE_SERIES permission to manually award certifications.
5. For more information, see How can I manually award or revoke series certifications?

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > FAQs > Troubleshooting certification issues > You have not met all certification criteria:
Completing all modules in a series or course does not always guarantee a certificate. Certifications can be completion-based, score-based, or both. Ensure you have met all the criteria defined for the certification.

To view the criteria:

1. Go to the learning site > Series .
2. Click on the series.
3. Click the Certifications tab.
4. Click View details on the certification. The certification details screen displays the criteria you must complete, the certificate sample, and the validity period. Note:

- Not all modules in a series may be part of the certification criteria.
- You may not need to complete every module in the series to qualify.

Criteria by module type:

| Module Type | Certification Criteria |
| --- | --- |
| Series | Complete all modules included in the certification criteria and meet any defined cut-off scores. |
| Course | Complete 100% of the course and meet any configured cut-off score. |
| Assessment | Complete the assessment and achieve a score higher than the passing score. |
| Mission | If a cut-off is configured, your average evaluation score must meet or exceed the cut-off. |

For more details, see Earn and manage series certifications.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > FAQs > Troubleshooting certification issues > Sequential locking is preventing you from completing a required module:
If your series has sequential locking enabled, modules are unlocked one at a time as you complete them. You cannot skip ahead to a later module.

If a course module in the series has its own certification requirement, the next module unlocks only after you become certified in that course - not just after you complete it. If you did not meet the course certification criteria (for example, you did not achieve the required score), the next module remains locked, and you cannot complete all the modules required for the series certification.

For example, if Module 2 is a course with its own certification, you must earn that course certificate before Module 3 unlocks. Simply completing Module 2 is not enough; you must also meet the score or other criteria required for that course's certification.

To resolve this, reattempt the course to meet its certification criteria. If reattempts are not available, contact your admin.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > FAQs > Troubleshooting certification issues > The certification has expired:
Certifications have a validity period configured by your admin (for example, 3 months, 12 months, or always valid).

To check:

Go to the learning site > Series > Certifications tab.

If expired, the status shows Expired.

If the certificate is displayed as expired immediately after completion, it may be misconfigured. Contact your admin to review and reissue it.

Additional scenarios:

- If you already have an active certification, the system does not issue a duplicate.
- If you are outside the recertification window, you cannot earn a new certificate until the window opens.
- If recertification is enabled:
  - Your admin may configure recertification so that you must re-earn the certificate periodically.
  - When the recertification window opens, you receive an email notification.
  - You must complete the criteria again within the recertification period to earn a new certificate.
  - If the recertification window has passed and you did not complete it in time, contact your admin to manually award the certificate.

For more information, see Earn and manage series certifications.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > FAQs:
Mindtickle delivers content securely through AWS CloudFront, which requires your browser to hold short-lived authentication cookies before it can load any protected content. If those cookies are missing, blocked, or expired, you'll see the MissingKey-Pair-Id query parameter or cookie value error. This is usually caused by your browser's security settings blocking the necessary credentials.

This error can appear across the platform — including SCORM modules, videos, documents, digital sales rooms, images, and assets — whenever your browser can't supply the required authentication cookies.

The fix is almost always the same: make sure cookies are enabled + pop-ups are allowed in your browser.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > FAQs > How to fix it:
1. Enable third-party cookies: The site needs to set "signed cookies" to authenticate you, so make sure your browser isn't blocking them:
  - Chrome : Settings → Privacy and Security → Third-party cookies → Allow third-party cookies
  - Safari : Safari → Preferences → Privacy → uncheck "Prevent cross-site tracking"
  - Firefox : Settings → Privacy & Security → Enhanced Tracking Protection → select Standard
  - Edge : Settings → Privacy, search, and services → Cookies → turn off Block third-party cookies
  - Opera : Settings → Advanced → Privacy & security → Site settings → Cookies and site data → Allow all cookies
2. Allow pop-ups: Some content (such as SCORM courses) uses pop-ups to establish authentication sessions. Make sure pop-ups are allowed for the Mindtickle site in your browser settings.
3. Clear your cache and cookies: Old or corrupted cookies can cause authentication failures. Clear them and try again; if the issue persists, close and reopen your browser before retrying.
4. Refresh the page: If your cookies expired mid-session, refreshing re-triggers authentication and issues fresh cookies.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > FAQs > What is the Mindtickle learning site URL?:
Your Mindtickle learning site URL is the unique web address assigned to your organization's Mindtickle instance. It is the primary link that all learners and managers use to access your company's Mindtickle platform.

By default, it follows the format:

https://[your-company-name].mindtickle.com

Example: If your company is Acme Corp, your learning site URL might be:

https://acme.mindtickle.com

If your organization has configured a custom (white-label) domain, it may instead look like:

https://learning.acmecorp.com

Note: Mindtickle does not have a single public login page for all users. Each company has its own instance of the learning site. Your login credentials (username/email and password, or SSO) are tied to that specific learning site URL. If you enter the wrong learning site URL, you won't be able to sign in even with the correct credentials.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > FAQs > Where can I find my Mindtickle learning site URL?:
You can find your learning site URL in the following ways:

1. Welcome or invitation email: When your organization sets up Mindtickle, an invite or welcome email is sent to you (typically with the subject line: Your Mindtickle Account is active now). This email contains a direct link to the learning site. If you received an invite email for a specific module, simply click the Accept Invite or Get Started button in the email to be taken directly to your learning site.
2. Check your company's internal wiki or intranet: Many organizations list their Mindtickle URL in their onboarding documentation or internal tools page.
3. Look for an SSO/SAML login option: If your organization uses Single Sign-On (e.g., Google, Okta, Azure AD), you may be redirected automatically from your company portal — no manual URL entry is needed.
4. Ask your team or manager: If you did not receive an invitation or cannot locate it, ask your manager, or reach out to your HR, IT, or L&D team. They manage your Mindtickle instance and can give you the exact URL.
5. Mobile app assistance: If you are signing in via the Mindtickle mobile app and do not remember your learning site URL, use the “Don’t know your learning site URL?” option on the app’s sign-in page. Enter your Mindtickle email address, and you will be directed to the correct sign-in screen if your email is linked to a single learning site.

After you submit a mission, the Review pending status means one or more required reviewers have not completed their review or submitted a score. The mission is complete only after all required reviews are finished.

On the learning site, the mission’s status appears as Submitted for review. For more information about learner and reviewer statuses, see Learner and reviewer status in module reports.

The status remains as Review pending because,

- A required reviewer has not submitted their review.
- Multiple reviewers are assigned, and not all required reviews are complete.

What you can do

- Wait for the reviewer or reviewers to complete their review.
- If the delay is longer than expected, contact your reviewer, manager, or Mindtickle admin.

Note: If a certificate depends on this mission, it is awarded only after all reviews are complete and any score requirements are met. For more information, see Why am I not certified after completing all required modules?

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > FAQs > How completion is tracked:
To ensure your progress is accurately tracked, follow these guidelines:

- Do not skip required content: Complete content in sequence when required without skipping or seeking ahead, as this can affect your progress, completion status, and score.
- Interact fully: Open and complete all required content, activities, questions, and interactions to ensure your progress is tracked.
- Always click to exit: Most modules require you to complete the required activity and then click the appropriate navigation or exit button, such as Next , Exit , or X ( Close ). Simply viewing the content or reaching the end of a video does not automatically register completion.
- Check for variations: Behavior can vary depending on your admin’s configuration. When in doubt, complete the required activity and click the appropriate navigation or exit button before leaving the module.

Note:

- For SCORM modules, completion depends on the requirements set inside the SCORM package. For instructions on saving progress, completing SCORM content, or troubleshooting SCORM issues, see Troubleshoot module completion and SCORM issues .
- Progress percentage and completion status are not always the same. A module can show progress, but it is marked Completed only after all required completion criteria are met and the completion data is recorded in Mindtickle.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > FAQs > Completion requirements by module type:
Mindtickle offers various module types, each with specific requirements to change your status from In progress to Completed.

| Module type | Completion criteria |
| --- | --- |
| Course | Complete all required learning objects and quizzes or questions within the course. |
| Quick update | Complete all learning objects in the bite-sized training, along with quizzes or questions. |
| Assessment | Answer all questions and submit. If a time limit is set, complete and submit before it expires. |
| Checklist | Check off all required task-based items. |
| Instructor-led training (ILT) | Attend scheduled sessions and be marked "attended" by the instructor. |
| Coaching sessions | Submit your recording or deliverable for the coaching activity. Depending on the setup, the session can be marked complete after the assigned reviewer submits their evaluation and feedback. |
| Mission | Complete the assigned practice, role-play, or submission activity. Depending on the mission setup, completion can require AI feedback, reviewer feedback, or both. |
| Quest | Complete all assigned reinforcement challenges and questions in a gamified experience. |
| Competency assessment | Complete your self-evaluation using the proficiency scale and submit the form. |

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > FAQs > Completion requirements by content type:
Modules are made up of individual learning objects (content). Each content type requires specific actions to register as complete and avoid progress-tracking errors.

| Content type | Completion criteria | Interaction guidelines |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Reading / Document | View the entire document and click the completion button. | Scroll through multi-page documents to ensure all pages render fully before marking the item complete. |
| Video / Audio | Watch or listen to the required percentage and click the completion button. | Let the media play until the progress bar reaches 100%. Do not refresh the page while playback is in progress to avoid losing progress. |
| Interactive elements | Answer and submit all embedded prompts, and complete any required links or interactions. | Complete any in-video questions, polls, or embedded links as they appear. |
| SCORM package | Complete the requirements defined in the SCORM content, such as viewing required slides, completing activities, or passing an embedded quiz. | For steps to complete SCORM content and troubleshoot completion, progress, access, playback, recording, interaction, or mobile issues, see Troubleshoot module completion and SCORM issues. |
| Test / Quiz | Submit all answers and meet the minimum passing threshold, if required. | Read instructions carefully, as some quizzes do not allow retakes. Radio buttons indicate single-choice; checkboxes allow multiple answers. |
| Poll / Survey | Complete all mandatory questions and submit your responses. | Ensure all required fields are completed, and then click Submit when the button is enabled. |
| Competency assessment | Complete your self-evaluation using the proficiency scale and submit. | Review any attached supporting files first. Depending on your visibility settings, you might not see your manager’s evaluation until you submit your self-assessment. |

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > FAQs > Troubleshoot common completion issues > The module is not showing as completed:
Probable causes:

- Required completion action missed: You might not have completed the required action, such as selecting Next , Exit , X ( Close ), or Submit .
- Incomplete criteria: You might have missed a core requirement, such as submitting an assessment, completing a required learning object, or having an instructor mark you as "attended" for an ILT. You might also be waiting on a manual manager review for an assignment.
- Sequential locking active: If modules are locked in sequence, an incomplete status on a previous module blocks subsequent modules from registering completion.
- Module version update: An admin might have published a new module version and enforced it for all users. If this occurs, your previous completion status is reset, and you must complete the updated content again.
- Browser and network interruptions: Disabled browser cookies, closing the browser before progress syncs, or a network drop can disrupt tracking.

Steps to resolve:

- Re-enter the module and verify that you completed all required activities. Use the required button, such as Next , Exit , X ( Close ), or Submit , before leaving the module.
- Verify that you met the requirements for the module type. For example, submit an assessment, complete required learning objects, attend an ILT session, or submit a required recording.
- Ensure that your browser allows cookies for the Mindtickle platform.
- For SCORM-specific troubleshooting, see Troubleshoot module completion and SCORM issues .

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > FAQs > Troubleshoot playback, recording, and interaction issues:
If you experience playback, recording, or interaction issues, try the following general checks:

- Video playback errors: Check your internet connection, clear your browser cache, and try a supported browser, such as Chrome or Firefox. If you use a VPN, try disconnecting or switching to a different network.
- Video buffering or freezing: Lower the video quality in the video player. Close unnecessary browser tabs and applications.
- Microphone and recording failures: Allow microphone and camera access. Close other applications, such as Zoom or Teams, that might be using your microphone or camera.
- Audio playback issues: Ensure that your browser tab is not muted, check your system volume, or try a different output device.

For SCORM content that does not open, freezes, has non-working interactions, has recording issues, or does not work on mobile, see Troubleshoot module completion and SCORM issues.

If you have completed all required steps and the issue persists, follow this escalation path:

- Refresh the session: Refresh the module page, or sign out of Mindtickle and sign back in. Then check whether your scores and completion statuses have updated.
- Clear browser data: Clear your browser’s cache and cookies, then restart the browser.
- Switch browser or internet connection: Try a different supported browser or Wi-Fi connection to rule out local issues.
- For SCORM issues: Follow the steps in Troubleshoot module completion and SCORM issues .

If completion still fails to register, contact your training admin. Contact Mindtickle Support only after the relevant admin or IT checks are complete, or when an article specifically asks you to contact Support.

Include the following details:

- Module name
- Series name, if available
- Learning site URL
- Screenshot or screen recording
- Browser and device details
- Error message, if any
- Whether the issue occurs in another browser or network
- Steps already tried

Alternatively, report an issue from the learning site using the Report an issue or Get support button. This option automatically captures a screenshot of your current page and sends it to Mindtickle Support to help diagnose the issue more quickly.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Automated Sync > Transition sync to a new admin > A. Re-authenticate the integration:
A currently active admin must update the connection details for the existing account using their credentials.

1. From the admin site sidebar, navigate to your content sync integration settings under Account → Settings → Security & integrations . Scroll down to the Content Sync section on the page and click the Google shared drives tab.
2. Click the horizontal More options icon next to the configured account, and select Edit .
3. In the Edit account pop-up, click Edit to edit the account details.
4. The Account details section displays the message: " You have been logged out. Please login to continue. " Click Connect with Google to authenticate with the new active admin's Google credentials and sync their Google shared drive. See this article for details on connecting Google shared drive, mapping folders, and the sync settings.
5. Please note that updating the connection name will also update the folder name in Content Center.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Release Notes > New features > Module completion API for email and task evaluation missions:
The new module completion API for email and task evaluation missions allows you to programmatically mark modules as complete for individual learners. This API automates the entire lifecycle of an email and task evaluation mission to ensure consistent progress reporting. The API is designed to synchronize data from external partner portals or third-party certification sites, ensuring the platform remains the central system of record for all readiness data.

Here are the key capabilities:

- Lifecycle automation : The API automatically initiates learner sessions, creates submission drafts, and attaches static media placeholders to fulfill all technical requirements for completion.
- Silent completion : Manual reviewer workflows are bypassed. The system automatically starts and submits evaluations using the provided score, ensuring no "pending review" tasks or notifications are generated.
- Instant progression : Completion triggers downstream logic immediately, including series unlocking, certification eligibility, and real-time analytics updates.

Technical specifications

Endpoint:

POST /api/v1/cag/<companyId>/series/<seriesId>/entity/<entityId>/learner/<learnerId>/email/_complete

Supports binary scoring of 0 (fail) or 100 (pass). The system defaults to 100 if the score is omitted. A static default media artifact is attached to every completion to maintain data integrity.

Audit and visibility

- Origin tagging : API-driven completions are labeled with a completion_origin tag of external_completion_api in all admin reports and analytics.
- Learner experience : Learners will see their mission marked as "Completed" with a note stating: "Externally reported completion" in the submission view.
- Request tracking : Every response includes a requestId for simplified troubleshooting and internal logging.

Scope and limitations

- Mission type : Exclusively available for email and task evaluation missions .
- Reviewer assignments : An active reviewer must be assigned to the learner for the mission prior to triggering the API.
- Status : Supports final completion status only; in-progress states or granular rubric scoring are not supported.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Release Notes > New features > Introducing nested hubs:
The nested hubs feature introduces a hierarchical structure that mirrors real-world business divisions (e.g., Global -> EMEA -> Germany). Nested hubs make content navigation intuitive, streamline discoverability, and reduce administrative overhead and governance complexity.

Core architecture and governance

The architecture is built on a strict parent-child relationship to ensure secure and scalable content governance.

- Up to 10 levels of hierarchy: Admins can build an organizational tree of hubs up to 10 levels deep within a parent (root) hub.
- Automatic inheritance: Child hubs automatically inherit all permissions, access controls, and settings (such as hub type, collaborators, and access settings) from their parent hub. A child hub cannot grant more access than its parent hub.
- Access constraints: To maintain security, a child hub must use the same visibility type (public or restricted) as its parent hub. Moving a hub instantly changes its access based on the new parent hub.

Enhanced navigation and user experience

The platform-wide hierarchical experience improves discoverability for all users.

- Hierarchical browsing and context: Hubs are displayed in a collapsible tree view, replacing flat lists. Navigating deep into the content shows a clear breadcrumb trail (e.g., "Global -> EMEA -> Germany") in the hub header that gracefully collapses beyond five levels.
- Universal hierarchical filters: Hub filters now use a nested tree with expand/collapse arrows across the entire platform, including asset listing pages, sharing modals, Digital Sales Rooms ( DSR ), and Page Builder widgets. Selecting a parent hub automatically cascade-selects all child hubs.
- Enhanced search and asset details: Global search results display the full hub path on the asset card. Searching within a specific hub automatically includes results from all nested child hubs.

Platform-wide impact and integrations

Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Release Notes > New features > Bring Mindtickle into your AI clients with the Mindtickle MCP server - beta:
The Mindtickle MCP server is now available in beta, giving your teams a secure, governed way to access Mindtickle from any MCP-compatible AI client. Built on the open Model Context Protocol (MCP), the integration exposes Mindtickle search and Seller Copilot chat as tools that AI clients can call directly during user conversations; no custom API integration required.

Note: This integration is currently available in beta. For details, please contact your CSM.

Why this matters

Sales teams increasingly work inside AI clients: IDEs like Cursor, enterprise tools like Claude for Teams, and in-house copilots. Until now, surfacing Mindtickle inside these tools required a custom integration for every client.

The Mindtickle MCP server replaces that complexity with a single, standards-based entry point that any MCP-compatible client can connect to — bringing Mindtickle content and Seller Copilot answers into the tools reps already use.

Key highlights

This release delivers the Mindtickle MCP server and the authentication backbone needed to connect AI clients to it.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Release Notes > New features > Bring Mindtickle into your AI clients with the Mindtickle MCP server - beta:
- Two Mindtickle capabilities exposed as MCP tools:
  - Global search ( mindtickle_search ): Search across Mindtickle learning content — including assets, modules, files, series, asset hubs, tags, and peers — using the same hybrid keyword and AI-powered semantic search that powers global search on the learning site.
  - Seller Copilot chat ( mindtickle_copilot_chat ): Chat with Mindtickle's Seller Copilot from inside any MCP-compatible client. Returns instant, context-aware answers drawn from modules, assets, and Call AI recordings available to the user.
- Two ways to connect, for two different audiences:
  - Programmatic integration for developers and integrators building custom AI clients, agents, or scripts. Uses the OAuth 2.0 client credentials grant to obtain a short-lived JWT, configured directly in the client (for example, in Cursor's mcp.json ).
  - Custom connector setup for organization admins of managed MCP client applications such as Claude for Teams and Claude Enterprise. Admins publish the Mindtickle MCP server as a custom connector once, and individual users authorize their own access through an OAuth consent flow.
- Governed, scope-based access: Every request is authenticated with a Bearer JWT and validated against scopes ( read:search , read:copilot_chat ) on every call. Only tools the user has been granted access to are callable.
- Two scope-control modes for connector setup: Admins can let users choose their own scopes (user-controlled, default) or enforce a fixed set of scopes for the entire organization (admin-controlled) using Mindtickle-issued credentials.
- Existing Mindtickle access controls preserved: Tool calls run in the context of the authorized user. Results respect the same permissions and content access policies that apply to that user inside Mindtickle.

Benefits

Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Release Notes > Enhancements > Asset dashboards now available as advanced report templates:
This release brings updates to the Asset Hub template section in advanced reports. The two legacy templates - Asset engagement and Asset revenue impact - have been retired and replaced with three new templates that map directly to the enriched out-of-the-box (OOTB) dashboards released in March. Admins now have access to richer, more comprehensive starting points that can be fully customized within the standard advanced reports experience.

When creating a new advanced report, the Asset Hub template section now includes three templates.

1. Engagement dashboard (replaces Asset engagement ): Provides a comprehensive snapshot of asset performance, utilization, and adoption across the organization. Covers asset utilization rate, engagement trends, user engagement and adoption by group, utilization trends for internal and external assets, top assets and attributes, and sharing and viewing trends.
2. Revenue impact dashboard (replaces Asset revenue impact ): Tracks how assets influence deals and revenue across the pipeline, from deal stage to individual contacts. Covers deals and revenue influenced by assets, revenue influence trends, asset utilization, and engagement by deal stage, engagement by contact title, and asset utilization in individual deals.
3. Audit dashboard ( new ): A net-new template that expands the available templates from two to three, covering a previously untemplated use case. Provides visibility into asset health, coverage, and actionable management recommendations. Covers asset distribution by type, usage, status, attributes, and owners; assets missing metadata; recommendations to keep, review, or archive based on utilization trends; expired and archived assets; and duplicate assets identified by name or file ID.

You can customize the report as needed. Components can be added, removed, reordered, or modified using the standard advanced reports editing experience. Access to data within each template remains governed by existing Asset Hub permissions and access controls.
chunks.body:

Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Release Notes > Enhancements > Expanded .zip file support in Content Center and Asset Hub:
Mindtickle now supports general-purpose .zip file uploads in Content Center and Asset Hub. Admins can upload, store, and share compressed file bundles directly from the platform. The behavior of the existing SCORM .zip file remains unchanged.

The platform automatically detects whether an uploaded .zip file is a SCORM package or a non-SCORM archive and applies the appropriate behavior. Both SCORM and non-SCORM .zip files support a maximum file size of 5 GB.

Supported behavior by file type

- SCORM .zip files
  - Continue to work as before
  - Supported for upload, playback, and download, where applicable
  - Rendered through the SCORM player in training modules
- Non-SCORM .zip files
  - Stored as downloadable assets
  - No preview or inline rendering available
  - Search and filter support available in Content Center
  - Can be shared through Asset Hub

File behavior by location

| Upload location | File type | Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Training module | SCORM .zip | Opens in SCORM player |
| Training module | Non-SCORM .zip | Not supported |
| Content Center | SCORM .zip | Upload, playback, and download are supported |
| Content Center | Non-SCORM .zip | Upload and download are supported |
| Asset Hub | SCORM .zip | No change to existing behavior |
| Asset Hub | Non-SCORM .zip | Download and sharing are supported |

Limitations

- No preview or inline rendering is available for .zip files
- .zip archive contents cannot be browsed or unpacked within the platform
- Non-SCORM .zip files are not supported in training modules
- .zip file contents are not indexed for Copilot search

Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Release Notes > Enhancements > Duplicate file grouping in global search:
This release brings a major enhancement to your content discovery experience: duplicate file grouping.

Previously, searching for enablement content could result in the exact same file appearing multiple times in your search results. This repetition cluttered the top results, pushed down other relevant materials, and required you to manually verify which link to click.

With duplicate file grouping, we have streamlined this experience to help you find the right content faster, with less effort, and with a higher degree of trust in your search results.

How it works

When duplicate files exist (either as duplicate instances or used within assets), the system automatically consolidates them into a single search result.

- Unified search results: A single, clean result is displayed for each unique file, prioritizing the standalone or most direct version.
- Context preservation: The original locations are preserved in a summary tag at the bottom of the result (for example, "Used in 15 locations").
- Direct navigation in quick search: In the search bar’s suggested results dropdown, the double arrow icon next to any result indicates duplicate files. Click the icon to open a menu on the right that displays all associated locations for direct navigation.
- Direct navigation on the results page: Click the dropdown arrow next to the locations summary to view a scrollable list of all associated files and assets. Click any entry to navigate directly to it.

Key benefits

- Faster content discovery: Access assets mid-workflow without spending time filtering through redundant entries.
- Improved search relevance: Consolidating duplicates naturally pushes other highly relevant, unique content higher up on the first page.
- Cleaner interface: Enjoy a highly scannable results page focused entirely on enablement content.

Scope and availability

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > AI podcast > Introduction:
Mindtickle's AI podcast feature enables admins to transform long, complex documents (PDF, DOC, or PPT) into concise and engaging audio podcasts using AI.

The feature automatically summarizes core ideas, highlights key points, and produces audio content by allowing you to choose between two distinct formats: a multi-speaker conversation or a single-speaker monologue. Admins can further customize the output with specific duration controls, podcast language settings, and realistic digital voice selection for both hosts and guests.

The AI podcast feature helps you save time while boosting learner engagement by turning complex material into focused, accessible, and on-the-go learning materials without requiring scripting or recording expertise. You can also use an optional text prompt to target specific document topics for the AI to emphasize. After a podcast is generated, you can also edit its script and voices and regenerate the audio, without starting over from the source document.

This feature is available in course and quick update modules, allowing you to convert documents into audio files that can be added as learning objects.

- The AI podcast feature is currently in BETA. Please contact Mindtickle Support to enable it for your Mindtickle instance.
- After a podcast is generated, you can edit its script and voices and regenerate the audio. However, the source file, podcast format, language, duration, and focus instructions cannot be changed after generation; to change any of these, generate a new podcast. For more information, see the " Editing the podcast " section.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > AI podcast > Creating the podcast:
1. In a course or quick update module, under the Build tab, click Add learning objects to get started. The following image shows multiple ways to access the Add learning objects option in courses.
2. In the Add learning objects panel, click the AI podcast option.
3. The Select file to convert pop-up opens and lists files and folders in the Content Center. Select a text-based PDF, DOC, or PPT file that you want to convert to a podcast. Once selected, click Select & continue . Use the File type filter set to PDF, DOC, or PPT to show only relevant files.
4. In the Select folder for converted podcast pop-up, specify a folder in the Content Center where the AI-generated podcast will be saved. Use the New folder option to create a new folder anywhere in the Content Center. Once done, click Select & continue .
5. The Generate podcast pop-up appears. Configure the following audio settings for the podcast:
  - Podcast format : Choose between Conversation (multi-speaker style audio) or a Monologue (single-speaker style audio).
  - Duration : Select the desired length of the podcast: Short , Medium , or Long .
  - Podcast language : Select the language for the generated audio content. You can choose from 28 supported languages, encompassing a wide variety of regional accents and voice personas. For a complete list of available options, see the " Supported languages and voices " section below.
  - Host voice and guest voice : Choose the digital personas that will narrate the podcast. Within this setting, you can perform the following actions to customize your speakers:
    - Preview current voices : Click the Play icon next to the assigned host or guest voice to hear a brief audio sample.
    - Change a voice : Click the Change voice icon to open the voice selection menu. In the Choose a voice pop-up, filter the system library using the Language , Gender , and Accent drop-down menus to narrow down your options. Click the Play icon next to any listed voice to preview its tone, style, and delivery. Select your preferred voice and click Choose voice to apply the new persona to your podcast. For more details on how these voice characteristics interact with your chosen podcast language, see the " Understanding language and voice settings " section below.
  - Focus (optional) : Enter specific instructions in the text field if you want the AI podcast to focus on certain parts or topics from the original file. For example, you might enter:
    - "Focus on the new objection handling techniques for the Q3 product launch."
    - "Emphasize the three main benefits of the updated compliance policy."
    - "Highlight the buyer persona pain points and skip the technical specifications."
6. Once you have configured your settings, click Generate podcast . Important : The podcast format, language, duration, and focus instructions cannot be changed after generation. Review these settings carefully before proceeding. (After generation, you can still edit the script text and change the host or guest voices. For more information, see the " Editing the podcast " section.)
7. The generation process runs asynchronously in the background. You do not need to remain on the screen and can continue working elsewhere in the platform while the podcast is processed.
8. Once the finalized podcast audio file is generated, it will appear within the learning object. You can also download the podcast audio file to your computer and replace it with another file.
9. The AI-generated podcast audio file is also automatically saved to the Content Center , in the folder you selected in Step 4 . You can reuse the podcast audio file in other places, such as in assets and modules.
10. Click the audio file to open it in the Content Center on its file page. Here, you can play the audio and take actions, such as apply tags, see locations where the file is used (in modules and assets), manage collaborators, manage versions, download or replace the file, view file details, move the file, or delete it.
chunks.body:
1. In a course or quick update module, under the Build tab, click Add learning objects to get started. The following image shows multiple ways to access the Add learning objects option in courses.
2. In the Add learning objects panel, click the AI podcast option.
3. The Select file to convert pop-up opens and lists files and folders in the Content Center. Select a text-based PDF, DOC, or PPT file that you want to convert to a podcast. Once selected, click Select & continue . Use the File type filter set to PDF, DOC, or PPT to show only relevant files.
4. In the Select folder for converted podcast pop-up, specify a folder in the Content Center where the AI-generated podcast will be saved. Use the New folder option to create a new folder anywhere in the Content Center. Once done, click Select & continue .
5. The Generate podcast pop-up appears. Configure the following audio settings for the podcast:
  - Podcast format : Choose between Conversation (multi-speaker style audio) or a Monologue (single-speaker style audio).
  - Duration : Select the desired length of the podcast: Short , Medium , or Long .
  - Podcast language : Select the language for the generated audio content. You can choose from 28 supported languages, encompassing a wide variety of regional accents and voice personas. For a complete list of available options, see the " Supported languages and voices " section below.
  - Host voice and guest voice : Choose the digital personas that will narrate the podcast. Within this setting, you can perform the following actions to customize your speakers:
    - Preview current voices : Click the Play icon next to the assigned host or guest voice to hear a brief audio sample.
    - Change a voice : Click the Change voice icon to open the voice selection menu. In the Choose a voice pop-up, filter the system library using the Language , Gender , and Accent drop-down menus to narrow down your options. Click the Play icon next to any listed voice to preview its tone, style, and delivery. Select your preferred voice and click Choose voice to apply the new persona to your podcast. For more details on how these voice characteristics interact with your chosen podcast language, see the " Understanding language and voice settings " section below.
  - Focus (optional) : Enter specific instructions in the text field if you want the AI podcast to focus on certain parts or topics from the original file. For example, you might enter:
    - "Focus on the new objection handling techniques for the Q3 product launch."
    - "Emphasize the three main benefits of the updated compliance policy."
    - "Highlight the buyer persona pain points and skip the technical specifications."
6. Once you have configured your settings, click Generate podcast . Important : The podcast format, language, duration, and focus instructions cannot be changed after generation. Review these settings carefully before proceeding. (After generation, you can still edit the script text and change the host or guest voices. For more information, see the " Editing the podcast " section.)
7. The generation process runs asynchronously in the background. You do not need to remain on the screen and can continue working elsewhere in the platform while the podcast is processed.
8. Once the finalized podcast audio file is generated, it will appear within the learning object. You can also download the podcast audio file to your computer and replace it with another file.
9. The AI-generated podcast audio file is also automatically saved to the Content Center , in the folder you selected in Step 4 . You can reuse the podcast audio file in other places, such as in assets and modules.
10. Click the audio file to open it in the Content Center on its file page. Here, you can play the audio and take actions, such as apply tags, see locations where the file is used (in modules and assets), manage collaborators, manage versions, download or replace the file, view file details, move the file, or delete it.

Note:

- The Edit podcast option is available only after a podcast has been generated successfully. You cannot edit a podcast that failed to generate.

Edit the script

- Host : The primary speaker.
- Guest : The secondary speaker (present only in Conversation format podcasts).

Each segment is an editable text field. To edit the script:

1. Click any text segment to enter edit mode. A "Click to edit" tooltip confirms the field is editable.
2. Type your changes directly in the field.

The following character limits apply when editing:

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > AI podcast > Language and voice settings:
When configuring an AI podcast, you must select both a podcast language and specific host or guest voices. These two settings function independently to control different aspects of the final audio:

- Podcast language (what is said) : This setting determines the language of the actual content. The underlying script is generated in this language, and the conversation between the host and guest occurs in this language. For example, if you select English, the podcast dialogue will be spoken entirely in English.
- Host and guest voices (how it sounds) : These settings control how the podcast is spoken, rather than the language itself. Voices define characteristics such as accent, tone, speaking style, and gender. While voices are labeled with specific regional accents (such as American, Japanese, or Italian), they can read and pronounce content in different languages.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > AI podcast > Language and voice settings > How the settings work together:
Because the podcast language dictates what is being said and the voice dictates how it sounds, you can mix and match these settings to achieve specific auditory profiles.

Example scenario: If you want to create an English podcast tailored for an Indian audience, you can set the podcast language to English and select a Hindi voice for the host. The resulting audio will be spoken entirely in English, but the host will have an Indian (Hindi) accent.

Examples of mixing languages and voices include:

- English podcast + Indian voice : English content spoken with an Indian accent.
- Hindi podcast + American voice : Hindi content spoken with an American accent.
- Spanish podcast + British voice : Spanish content spoken with a British accent.

Regardless of the combination chosen, the final output is an audio file delivered in your selected language with your chosen voice styles applied.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > AI podcast > Limitations:
These are the key limitations of the AI podcast feature:

- Settings fixed after generation : After a podcast is generated, you can edit the script and change voices, but you cannot change the source file, podcast format, language, duration, or focus instructions. To change any of these, generate a new podcast.
- Predefined voice personas : You must select from the available library of system voices. The ability to create or upload custom voice personas is not currently supported.
- Language restrictions : A small number of languages may not be supported, mirroring the existing constraints of the standard AI translation feature.
- Text file requirement : Only text-based files (PDF, DOC, PPT) are supported. You cannot upload video or image-heavy files to create a podcast.
- Podcast LO duplication behavior : Duplicated AI podcast learning objects (LOs) share the same underlying podcast audio file. Any edits made to the podcast in one LO will automatically appear in all duplicated LOs. To create an independent version, generate a new podcast from the source document instead of duplicating the LO.

Unlock a module

If an admin has configured prerequisites for a module, the module remains locked until you complete the required prerequisite modules. The system highlights the locked modules in the series.

To access a locked module:

1. Hover over a locked module. The system displays the number of prerequisite modules you must complete to unlock it.
2. Click View (n) modules . The required modules are displayed with your completion progress.
3. Click Go to module next to the required module, then complete the module.
4. Complete all required prerequisite modules. After you complete all required prerequisite modules, the locked module becomes available automatically. Note: If the next module displayed after you complete a module is locked, click View (n) modules to view the prerequisite modules you must complete to unlock it.

Open a module

To open a module:

1. Click the Modules tab.
2. Click a module. The module details page opens, and learners can start or continue the module.

Note:

- When a learner opens and completes a mirrored module, the system displays the next module from the series they were invited to.

  - Scoped public series

- If the module is available in any of these series, the learner can open and complete it from that series. After completion, the system shows the next module from the original invited series.

3. Click Start course to begin a course, or click Continue if the module is already in progress.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Asset Hub > Admin:
Large organizations and enterprise customers often find flat organizational structures difficult to scale. To bring hierarchy, clarity, and control to the platform, nested hubs enable admins to organize content in a nested structure that mirrors real-world business divisions; for example, Global → EMEA → Germany → Product Line.

By matching the organizational capabilities of Content Center, nested hubs make navigation more intuitive for sellers, streamline content discoverability, and drastically reduce administrative overhead and governance complexity.

chunks.title: Create and manage nested hubs [admin]

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Asset Hub > Admin > Overview > Core principles and capabilities:
The architecture of nested hubs relies on a strict parent-child relationship to ensure secure and scalable content governance.

- Parent-child hub hierarchical depth: Admins can build an organizational tree of hubs within a parent (root) hub that can be up to 10 levels deep. The top-level hub is referred to as the parent or root hub, and any hubs created within it are child hubs. You can create multiple parent hubs and multiple child hubs within each parent hub.
- Moving hubs across the hierarchy : You can move child hubs between public and restricted hubs, move parent hubs under another parent hub to make them child hubs, or move child hubs to the Hubs page to make them parent hubs. When a hub is moved, it inherits the access settings and supported hierarchy rules of its new parent hub. For example, moving a hub under a public parent makes it accessible to all users, while moving it under a restricted parent grants access only to the parent hub’s users and user groups.
- Inherited child hub settings: By default, a child hub automatically inherits all permissions, access controls, and settings from its parent hub. This includes:
  - Hub type (public or restricted)
  - Collaborators
  - Access settings (public or restricted via invited users and linked groups, depending on hub type)
  - Required properties
  - Notifications for admins (asset expiration and file update reminders, asset feedback notifications, and asset owner removal notifications)
  - Admin and learner experience settings

A child hub cannot grant more access than its parent hub. Inherited settings appear as read-only in the child hub settings panel and display an “Inherited from parent hub” tooltip with a clickable link to the parent hub for easier auditing.

Inherited settings appear as read-only in the child hub settings panel and display an “Inherited from parent hub” tooltip with a clickable link to the parent hub for easier auditing.

- Independent child hub settings: The following settings are not inherited from the parent hub and can be configured separately for each child hub:
  - Hub name, description, and thumbnail
  - Hub overview page
  - Featured hub setting
- Child hub naming rules: Duplicate child hub names are allowed if they belong to different parent (root) hubs. However, child hubs under the same parent hub must have unique names.
- Hub type constraints: To maintain security and access consistency across the hierarchy, a child hub must use the same visibility type as its parent hub. The platform does not allow:
  - A public child hub under a restricted parent hub
  - A restricted child hub under a public parent hub
- Access changes when moving a hub: When a hub is moved, its access changes based on the new parent hub. If the new parent hub is public, the hub becomes accessible to all users. If the new parent hub is restricted, the hub inherits access from the parent’s users and user groups.
- Hub access management (restricted hubs): For restricted hubs, admins can manage which users and user groups can access each hub at any level in the hierarchy, and see how each user or group got access. Note : This per-hub access management applies to restricted hubs only. Public hubs are open to all users, so they have no per-hub user or group access list. For details, see the " Manage hub access (users and user groups) " section.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Asset Hub > Admin > Overview > Platform navigation and filtering:
- Hierarchical browsing: Hubs are displayed in a collapsible tree view rather than a flat list. When navigating the seller dashboard, the hub header displays a clear breadcrumb trail (e.g., "Global → EMEA → Germany") to establish immediate context. To maintain a clean interface, the navigational breadcrumb trail displays a maximum of five items when you are deeply nested within a hub. If a seller only has access to a child hub, parent hubs will appear in the breadcrumb trail to provide navigation context, but they will remain non-selectable unless explicit access is granted.
- Hub detail pages: Items are grouped with child hubs shown first and assets shown second. Sorting applies separately within each group, ensuring child hubs always appear above assets.
- Universal hub filters: Everywhere a hub filter appears, users now interact with a nested tree featuring expand and collapse arrows instead of a flat list. Selecting a parent hub automatically cascade-selects all of its associated child hubs (while selecting a child hub scopes only to that hub and its children). This consistent, hierarchical filtering experience is implemented across the following areas:
  - Asset listing pages (for both admins and reps/learners)
  - Content picker and "View all assets" pages
  - Asset sharing modals
  - The hub Users tab (when managing access for restricted hubs)
  - Page Builder widgets in series/hub overview pages and learning site homepages
  - Analytics and reporting dashboards
  - Digital Sales Rooms (DSR)
  - Browser extensions (including the general Chrome extension, Gmail, and LinkedIn), Outlook add-in, and Outreach integration
- Cascade-selection filters: Everywhere a hub filter appears — including the asset listing page, the content picker, and the "View all assets" page — users interact with a nested tree featuring expand and collapse arrows. Selecting a parent hub in these filters automatically cascade-selects all of its associated child hubs.
- Page Builder widgets: All hub-related filters and options in Page Builder widgets (for series/hub overview pages and learning site homepages) display hubs in a nested tree structure during widget configuration.

To maintain a clean interface, the navigational breadcrumb trail displays a maximum of five items when you are deeply nested within a hub. If a seller only has access to a child hub, parent hubs will appear in the breadcrumb trail to provide navigation context, but they will remain non-selectable unless explicit access is granted.
- Hub detail pages: Items are grouped with child hubs shown first and assets shown second. Sorting applies separately within each group, ensuring child hubs always appear above assets.
- Universal hub filters: Everywhere a hub filter appears, users now interact with a nested tree featuring expand and collapse arrows instead of a flat list. Selecting a parent hub automatically cascade-selects all of its associated child hubs (while selecting a child hub scopes only to that hub and its children). This consistent, hierarchical filtering experience is implemented across the following areas:
  - Asset listing pages (for both admins and reps/learners)
  - Content picker and "View all assets" pages
  - Asset sharing modals
  - The hub Users tab (when managing access for restricted hubs)
  - Page Builder widgets in series/hub overview pages and learning site homepages
  - Analytics and reporting dashboards
  - Digital Sales Rooms (DSR)
  - Browser extensions (including the general Chrome extension, Gmail, and LinkedIn), Outlook add-in, and Outreach integration
- Cascade-selection filters: Everywhere a hub filter appears — including the asset listing page, the content picker, and the "View all assets" page — users interact with a nested tree featuring expand and collapse arrows. Selecting a parent hub in these filters automatically cascade-selects all of its associated child hubs.
- Page Builder widgets: All hub-related filters and options in Page Builder widgets (for series/hub overview pages and learning site homepages) display hubs in a nested tree structure during widget configuration.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Asset Hub > Admin > Create nested hubs > Create a parent (root) hub:
When initiating the hub creation flow, establishing a top-level parent hub (also known as a root hub) is the first step in building a new hierarchy.

1. Under Assets → Hubs homepage on the admin site, click New → Hub .
2. In the New hub pop-up, enter the hub name, select the hub type (restricted or public), and the hub description (optional). The "Creating in" field indicates that the new parent (root) hub will be created under the Hubs page, which is the homepage of hubs and lists all parent (root) hubs.
3. Any child hubs you create within this parent (root) hub will automatically inherit all permissions, access controls, and settings of the parent hub. This includes: hub type (public or restricted), collaborators, users and user groups, required properties, notifications, and admin and learner experience settings.
4. Now you can add assets in this hub and manage the hub, such as feature the hub, and add hub overview page, create child hubs to organize assets, and move or delete the hub. As it’s a parent hub, you can also manage permissions, access controls, and settings mentioned in the previous steps that will also apply to its child hubs.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Asset Hub > Admin > Create nested hubs > Create a child hub:
Please consider the following before creating a child hub:

- Hierarchy limits: You can create up to 10 levels of child hubs within a parent hub hierarchy.
- Inherited child hub settings: By default, a child hub automatically inherits all permissions, access controls, and settings from its parent hub. This includes:
  - Hub type (public or restricted)
  - Collaborators
  - Access settings (public or restricted via invited users and linked groups, depending on hub type)
  - Required properties
  - Notifications for admins (asset expiration and file update reminders, asset feedback notifications, and asset owner removal notifications)
  - Admin and learner experience settings
- A child hub cannot grant more access than its parent hub. Inherited settings appear as read-only in the child hub settings panel and display an “Inherited from parent hub” tooltip with a clickable link to the parent hub for easier auditing.
- Independent child hub settings: The following settings are not inherited from the parent hub and can be configured separately for each child hub:
  - Hub name, description, and thumbnail
  - Hub overview page
  - Featured hub setting
- Hub type constraints: To maintain security and access consistency across the hierarchy, a child hub must use the same visibility type as its parent hub. The platform does not allow:
  - A public child hub under a restricted parent hub
  - A restricted child hub under a public parent hub
- Inherited access for restricted hubs: For restricted hubs, a new child hub inherits the users and user groups of its parent hub at creation — which already includes everyone inherited from hubs higher up in the hierarchy. Admins can then manage access at the child level. For details, see the " Manage hub access (users and user groups) " section.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Asset Hub > Admin > Manage nested hubs > Add and manage assets:
Any hub, regardless of its level in the hierarchy, can house assets directly. Bulk asset moves fully support nested hub destinations, and permissions will automatically inherit from the destination hub's parent chain.

1. Navigate to a parent or any child hub to which you want to add assets.
2. Click New → Assets → Select files . Alternatively, use the Multiple assets via Excel file option to add multiple assets via an Excel file.
3. On the select files from Content Center screen, you can either select files available in Content Center (whether uploaded or synced) or click New for options to upload new files. Apply one or more filters to narrow down the files you are looking for. For example, use the Hubs filter to select Content Center files that are already used in the selected parent or child hubs. In this filter you can inverse the selection by turning on the “Hide files used in selected hubs” toggle.
4. After selecting the files, click Next to continue.
5. In the Create assets screen, configure all required asset properties for the selected files. You can configure properties for any one asset and hover over each property to copy it to all assets. For example, click the + (plus) button for the Hubs property to select other parent or child hubs where you want to add these files as assets, in addition to your current hub. The assets will be mirrored to the selected hubs.
6. The Select hubs pop-up lets you navigate across all hubs, including parent and child hubs.
7. Once done, click Create assets . You can track the asset creation process status in the Notifications panel.
8. Refresh the hub to view the newly-created assets.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Asset Hub > Admin > Manage nested hubs > Mirror or move assets:
While mirroring or moving assets, the Select hubs hub selector pop-up displays the same hierarchical tree structure to let you select parent and child hubs.

Note: You can move child hubs between public and restricted hubs, move parent hubs under another parent hub to make them child hubs, or move child hubs to the Hubs page to make them parent hubs. When a hub is moved, it inherits the access settings and supported hierarchy rules of its new parent hub. For example, moving a hub under a public parent makes it accessible to all users, while moving it under a restricted parent grants access only to the parent hub’s users and user groups. For how a move affects the user and group access list of a restricted hub, see the "How moving a hub affects access" section.

You can mirror or move assets individually using theMore options icon available to the extreme right for the asset row in the hub. Or you can select multiple assets in the hub and use the toolbar at the bottom to mirror or move assets in bulk.

In the next screen, you can navigate the parent-child hierarchy of nested hubs and select the destination hub to which you want to mirror or move the assets.

For mirroring, you can select multiple destination hubs one at a time. The next and final screen displays all selected destination hubs. On the final screen, click + Add another to select more hubs and click the Delete icon to delete any of the selected destination hubs.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Asset Hub > Admin > Manage hub access (users and user groups) > How hub access works:
A user or user group has access to a restricted hub through one of the following sources, which is shown for each row on the hub’s Users tab:

- Granted directly: The user or group was added directly to this hub.
- Inherited from a parent hub: The user or group was added to a hub above this one in the tree, so access flows down to this hub.
- Granted via a child hub: The user or group was added directly to a hub below this one in the tree. That access propagates up so admins of the parent hubs can see who has access within the hierarchy. The originating child hub is recorded as the source.

The following rules govern how access is granted and propagated:
