chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Asset Hub > Admin > Manage hub access (users and user groups) > How hub access works:
- Adds cascade in both directions. Adding a user or group to a hub grants access downward to all of its child hubs (inherited) and propagates upward to all of its parent hubs (granted via the originating child hub).
- No duplicate access. If a user or group already has access through any source (direct, inherited from a parent, or granted via a child hub), they cannot be added again at a hub where access already exists. In bulk flows, they are skipped and shown with a clear status, such as “Already has access via [hub name]”.
- Adding at a parent overrides a direct grant at a child. If a user or group was added directly at a child hub and is later added at a parent hub, the child-level direct grant is replaced. The parent-level grant then governs access across all hubs under that parent.
- New child hubs inherit access. When a child hub is created under a restricted parent, it inherits the parent hub’s users and user groups at creation — which already includes everyone inherited from hubs higher up in the hierarchy.
- Users and groups combine as a union. If a user has access both individually and through a user group, the two sources combine. Removing one source does not remove access granted by the other.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Asset Hub > Admin > Manage hub access (users and user groups) > View hub access:
On a restricted hub’s Users tab, you can review access in two ways:

- View by users: Lists individual users with access to the hub.
- View by groups: Lists user groups with access to the hub.

Each row shows the user or group name, the date access was added, and how access was obtained for this hub (granted directly, inherited from a parent hub, or granted via a child hub) along with the source detail—for example, the name of the parent or child hub the access came from. Users who receive access through a user group are labeled so you can distinguish group-based access from individual access.

Both View by users and View by groups include a nested-hub filter, so you can narrow the list to a specific hub and its descendants within the hierarchy.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Asset Hub > Admin > Manage hub access (users and user groups) > Add users and user groups:
1. In the restricted hub header, click Share access → Individual users or User groups , as appropriate. Next, select the users or user groups you want to grant access to.
2. Selected users or groups are added based on the hub level:
  - At a parent (root) hub: Access is granted to the hub and inherited downward by all of its child hubs.
  - At a child hub: Access is granted directly to that child hub and propagated upward to all of its parent hubs (recorded as granted via the originating child hub).
3. If any selected user or group already has access through another source, they are skipped and shown with a status such as “Already has access via [hub name]”. No duplicate entry is created.
4. When you add access to a hub that has multiple descendant hubs, a confirmation modal summarizes the impact before you proceed. No confirmation modal is shown when access is being shared with only one hub.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Asset Hub > Admin > Manage hub access (users and user groups) > Remove users and user groups:
- Access can only be removed from the hub where it was granted directly. If you attempt to remove a user or group from a hub where their access is inherited from a parent or root hub, the action cannot be completed and the following error message is displayed: "This user group does not have direct access to this hub. Remove access from the hub where it was granted." To revoke inherited access, navigate to the hub where the access was originally granted and remove it there.
- Removing revokes the related access. When you remove a user or group from the hub where access was granted directly, they also lose the inherited access on that hub’s descendants and the propagated access on its ancestors (because the source is gone).
- Other direct sources are preserved. If the user or group still has access through another direct grant elsewhere in the tree (for example, they were added directly to two different child hubs), the access from the remaining source stays in place.
- User group membership stays in sync. When a user is added to or removed from a user group, their hub access updates automatically across all hubs the group can access; no admin action is needed.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Asset Hub > Admin > Manage hub access (users and user groups) > How moving a hub affects access:
Moving a restricted hub changes how access is calculated for the moved hub and its descendants. A confirmation modal summarizes the impact before any move that changes access.

- Move under a new parent hub: The moved hub and all its descendants inherit access from the new parent. Access that was granted directly within the moved subtree — and access that propagated up from within the subtree—is preserved. Access that the moved hub inherited from its old parent is removed and replaced by access inherited from the new parent. Any users or groups that had propagated up to the old parent only from the moved hub are removed from the old parent.
- Move to become a parent (root) hub: Inherited access is cleared, because there is no parent to inherit from. Access that was granted directly within the moved subtree, and access that propagated up from within the subtree, is preserved.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Asset Hub > Admin > Rep experience:
When a rep (learner) visits the Assets section on the learning site, hubs can contain other hubs, creating a hierarchy of content that mirrors how a sales organization might structure its materials (e.g., Global → EMEA → Germany).

Note: Only admins can create nested hubs. Reps (learners) cannot create nested hubs under Assets → My assets on the learning site.

Browsing into a hub

On any hub detail page, content is presented as a unified list of child hubs and assets. Child hubs appear as rows with a thumbnail, hub name, and a count label (e.g., "4 assets, 2 hubs"). Clicking a child hub navigates you into that hub, reloading the same hub detail page with the child hub's content — keeping the experience consistent at every level of depth.

You can navigate to a hub from the following places:

- From the Assets section → Assets page
- From assets related widgets on homepages or hub overview pages

When you navigate to a hub, the hub details page view varies depending on whether the admin has added a hub overview page.

A. With hub overview page: Displays the Overview (for the hub overview page) and Hubs and assets tabs.

B. WITHOUT hub overview page: Displays hubs and assets directly.

Always know where you are

As you navigate deeper, a breadcrumb bar in the hub header tracks their position: Assets → Global → EMEA → Germany. Each ancestor in the breadcrumb is a clickable link, letting reps jump back up to any level instantly.

Directly below the hub title, a "Parent hub: [Name]" metadata line provides a one-click shortcut to the immediate parent. Breadcrumbs collapse gracefully at depths beyond five levels.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle APIs > Training APIs:
The module completion API allows you to programmatically mark modules as complete for individual learners across multiple mission types. This endpoint is designed to synchronize data from external partner portals or third-party certification sites, ensuring the platform remains the central system of record for all readiness data.

A single dispatcher endpoint resolves the mission type automatically and drives the appropriate completion flow, so you do not need to know the mission type in advance.

Key capabilities include:

- Silent completion: Bypasses manual reviewer workflows by automatically starting and submitting reviewer evaluations for all active reviewers associated with the learner. This process results in a silent completion, meaning no "pending review" tasks are generated and no automated email notifications are triggered for either the learner or the reviewer.
- Automated draft and media management: To maintain valid data and prevent workflow failures, the system initializes a draft and attaches a static media placeholder. This ensures the mission has the required artifact for status changes while removing the need for external media uploads.
- Programmatic logic triggers: Instantly triggers downstream series unlocking and certification eligibility once the completion is recorded.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle APIs > Training APIs > Supported mission types:
The API completes the following mission types. The dispatcher resolves the mission type from the entity ID and delegates to the matching completion flow.

| Mission type | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Email and task evaluation | Learners submit a write-up (such as an email) and/or upload documents, media, and zipped files as a task. The review is done by the reviewers you appoint. |
| Screen capture | Learners record their narration or video over a screen-share demo. The review is done by the reviewers you appoint. |
| Voice over slideshow | Learners record their narration over a slideshow. The review is done by the reviewers you appoint. |
| Video roleplay | Learners record their video directly through Mindtickle or upload a pre-recorded video. The review is done by the reviewers you appoint. |
| AI Roleplay | Learners complete an AI Roleplay scenario. The review is done by the reviewers you appoint. |

Purpose: Marks a mission as complete for a specific learner. The API resolves the mission type from the entity ID, then drives the full lifecycle for that type: it starts the learner session, initializes a draft, attaches media, submits the learner activity, and submits the reviewer evaluation for all active reviewers associated with the learner.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Mindtickle MCP server:
The Mindtickle MCP server lets you connect AI clients to your Mindtickle instance over the Model Context Protocol (MCP) and access Mindtickle capabilities from external agentic platforms. You exchange Mindtickle-issued client credentials for a short-lived JWT and use that token to call the Mindtickle MCP server from your AI client.

The server currently exposes two Mindtickle capabilities as tools:

- Global search: Search across Mindtickle learning content — including assets, modules, files, series, asset hubs, tags, and peers — using a hybrid keyword and AI-powered semantic search. Returns the most relevant and contextual results based on the user's query. For more details, see this article .
- Seller Copilot chat: Chat with Mindtickle's Seller Copilot to get instant, context-aware answers drawn from modules, assets, and Call AI recordings available to the user. Useful for pre-call preparation, post-call follow-ups, and questions about products, processes, and customers. For more details, see this article .

This article describes the programmatic integration path, in which you obtain client credentials, generate access tokens, and configure your AI client directly (for example, by editing Cursor's mcp.json file). If you instead want to set up Mindtickle as a custom connector inside a managed MCP client application such as Claude for Teams or Claude Enterprise, see the Set up Mindtickle as a custom connector in MCP client apps.

Note:

- This integration is currently in BETA . For details, please contact your CSM.
- This integration is not self-service. Credentials are issued only by the Mindtickle team, and there is no public API to register MCP clients. Contact your Customer Success Manager (CSM) or account team to set up this integration.

Key capabilities

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Mindtickle MCP server > How the integration works:
The end-to-end flow involves four stages:

1. Get credentials: The Mindtickle team provides you with a client_id and a client_secret .
2. Generate an access token: Your client sends a POST request to the Mindtickle token endpoint and receives a short-lived access token.
3. Connect: Your client uses the Mindtickle MCP server URL with the Bearer token in the Authorization header.
4. Use tools: Your client discovers and invokes MCP tools. The server validates the token and scopes on every request.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Mindtickle MCP server > Generate an access token > Request:
Request URL

```
POST https://{mindtickle-instance-url}/api/auth/token
```

Request headers

```
Content-Type: application/json
```

Request parameters

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| grant_typeREQUIRED | string | The OAuth grant type. Set this to client_credentials. |
| client_idREQUIRED | string | The client ID issued by Mindtickle. |
| client_secretREQUIRED | string | The client secret issued by Mindtickle. |
| usernameREQUIRED | string | The email address of the Mindtickle user on whose behalf the token is issued. |
| scopeREQUIRED | string | The scopes required for the request, separated by spaces. For example, read:search read:copilot_chat. |

Request example

```json

{
  "grant_type": "client_credentials",
  "client_id": "YOUR_CLIENT_ID",
  "client_secret": "YOUR_CLIENT_SECRET",
  "username": "user@example.com",
  "scope": "read:search read:copilot_chat"
}
```

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Mindtickle MCP server > Discover and use MCP tools:
Once your client is connected, it can discover the tools available on the Mindtickle MCP server using the tools/list method. The tools returned depend on the scopes included in your access token.

Available tools

| Scope | Tool | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| read:copilot_chat | mindtickle_copilot_chat | Lets the AI client interact with Mindtickle Copilot through chat. |
| read:search | mindtickle_search | Lets the AI client search for content, including series, modules, files, and users. |
| * | All tools | Grants access to all tools when the token includes the wildcard scope. |

Notes:

- The server validates the token on every request.
- Tool access is restricted based on the scopes in the token.
- Tools are dynamically filtered based on the permissions granted.

End-user interaction guidance

End users typically ask task-based questions rather than platform-specific ones. For example:

- "Find learning content to understand product XYZ."
- "Learn more about product XYZ."
- "Find the battle card for competitor ABC."
- "Identify training for objection handling for product XYZ."

Integrator responsibilities

- Configure your agent or copilot to map user intent to the appropriate tool.
- Do not depend on users explicitly referencing Mindtickle in their queries.
- Use explicit tool references only for manual or developer testing. Do not require explicit tool names in production user experiences.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Mindtickle MCP server > Best practices:
Follow these practices to ensure a secure and reliable Mindtickle MCP server integration:

- Secrets management: Store the client_secret in a secure vault or secret manager. Never expose it in code, logs, or shared documents.
- Access token handling: Avoid logging or exposing access tokens in logs or responses. Use secure storage mechanisms such as environment variables or secret managers.
- Token lifecycle: Cache tokens and refresh them before they expire. Always rely on the expires_in value returned by the token endpoint rather than hardcoding a duration.
- Least-privilege scopes: Request only the scopes required for your use case to ensure controlled and secure access to MCP tools.
- Authorization header: Include the Authorization: Bearer <access_token> header on every request to the Mindtickle MCP server .
- Conversation history: Send the complete conversation history with each Copilot request to maintain context, accuracy, and continuity across interactions.
- End-user experience: Automatically route user intent (for example, training or content queries) to the appropriate MCP tools. Do not require users to reference Mindtickle explicitly.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Mindtickle MCP server > FAQs:
How do I get the MCP credentials?

Contact your Customer Success Manager or account team to obtain the required credentials. There is no self-service option.

What happens when the access token expires?

Call the token endpoint again to generate a new access token before making further requests.

Can I use MCP tools without specifying scopes?

No. Scopes determine which tools are accessible, so you must include at least one valid scope when requesting a token.

Why does my request return a 401 error?

A 401 error occurs when the client credentials are invalid or when the access token has expired.

Why does my request return a 403 error?

A 403 error occurs when the specified user does not have the required access within the organization.

Do I need to include conversation history in Copilot requests?

Yes. Include the full conversation history in each request to ensure consistent and accurate responses.

No. Scopes determine which tools are accessible, so you must include at least one valid scope when requesting a token.

Why does my request return a 401 error?

A 401 error occurs when the client credentials are invalid or when the access token has expired.

Why does my request return a 403 error?

A 403 error occurs when the specified user does not have the required access within the organization.

Do I need to include conversation history in Copilot requests?

Yes. Include the full conversation history in each request to ensure consistent and accurate responses.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Mindtickle MCP server:
The Mindtickle MCP server can be added as a custom connector in any MCP-compatible client application, allowing your team to use Mindtickle capabilities directly inside the client's interface. Once an admin publishes the connector for the organization, individual users authorize their own access through an OAuth consent flow and start using Mindtickle tools in their conversations.

Through this connector, your team gains access to two Mindtickle capabilities:

- Global search: Search across Mindtickle learning content — including assets, modules, files, series, asset hubs, tags, and peers — using a hybrid keyword and AI-powered semantic search. Returns the most relevant and contextual results based on the user's query. For more details, see this article .
- Seller Copilot chat: Chat with Mindtickle's Seller Copilot to get instant, context-aware answers drawn from modules, assets, and Call AI recordings available to the user. Useful for pre-call preparation, post-call follow-ups, and questions about products, processes, and customers. For more details, see this article .

The exact setup experience depends on the client application you are using. This guide uses Claude for Teams and Claude Enterprise as the worked example because they support MCP custom connectors natively. The menu paths and screen names referenced here are specific to Claude. The underlying concepts — the connector URL, the OAuth consent flow, and the scopes — are identical across any MCP-compatible client. For clients other than Claude, consult that client's own documentation for the equivalent steps.

Note: This integration is currently in BETA. For details, please contact your CSM.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Mindtickle MCP server:
Note: This integration is currently in BETA. For details, please contact your CSM.

This article covers two workflows in sequence: how an organization admin adds the Mindtickle MCP server as a custom connector for the team, and how an end user connects their own account to that connector. If you are a developer integrating Mindtickle into an AI client directly through code or configuration files, see Integrate with the Mindtickle MCP server.

Key capabilities

- One-time setup per organization: Admins publish the Mindtickle MCP server as a custom connector once, and the connector becomes available to authorized team members.
- Per-user authorization: Each user authorizes their own access independently through an OAuth consent screen. Connecting does not affect other users.
- Two scope-control modes: Admins can let users choose their own scopes (user-controlled) or enforce a fixed set of scopes for the entire organization (admin-controlled).
- Native tool use in conversations: Once connected, the client automatically uses Mindtickle tools based on the user's prompts. No additional setup is required for end users.

How it works

1. Admin adds the connector: An organization admin registers the Mindtickle MCP server URL as a custom connector in the client application.
2. User connects their account: Each team member opens the connector in their own client account and clicks Connect.
3. User authorizes access: The user is redirected to a Mindtickle OAuth consent screen, reviews the requested permissions, and grants access.
4. User starts using tools: The client uses Mindtickle search and Copilot chat in the user's conversations, based on the user's prompts.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Mindtickle MCP server > Part 1: Admin — Add the Mindtickle MCP server as a custom connector > Advanced settings: scope control:
The Mindtickle MCP server supports two ways to control which tools the connector exposes. In both modes, end users see an OAuth consent screen before the connector can access Mindtickle. The difference is who decides which tools (scopes) are available to grant.

|  | User-controlled (default) | Admin-controlled (Client ID and Secret) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| What it means | Users have access to all tools supported by the Mindtickle MCP server and can choose which ones to grant. | The admin configures which tools are available to users across the entire organization. |
| Client ID and Secret required? | Not required. Leave the Advanced settings blank. | Required. Enter the credentials issued by your Mindtickle CSM or account team. |
| Scopes available to end users | All scopes supported by the Mindtickle MCP server (currently: read Copilot conversations, search content). | Limited to the scopes defined by the admin in the client configuration. |
| OAuth consent screen | Shown to every user. The user can toggle which scopes to grant. | Shown to every user. The user can toggle only within the scopes the admin has permitted. |
| Best for | Organizations that want a simple setup and trust users to manage their own access. | Organizations that want to enforce a consistent, restricted scope policy across all users. |

The Mindtickle MCP server URL always follows this fixed pattern:

```
https://{instanceurl}/mcp
```

For example:

```
https://revup.mindtickle.com/mcp
```

Replace {instanceurl} with your organization's Mindtickle instance domain. The /mcp path is fixed and must not be changed.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Mindtickle MCP server > Part 2: User — Connect your account to the Mindtickle connector > Step 6 — Choose how the client requests permission for each tool call:
After connecting, the tool permissions panel for the Mindtickle connector shows two tools: mindtickle_search and mindtickle_copilot_chat. For each tool, you can choose between two permission modes that control how the client asks for permission each time it wants to use the tool.

| Mode | Behavior | Best for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Needs approval (default) | The client pauses each time it wants to use the tool and asks you to allow the call. You approve each invocation individually within the conversation. | Most users, especially when getting started with the connector. You stay aware of every Mindtickle tool call, which helps build trust and predictability. |
| Always allow | The client uses the tool automatically whenever its reasoning calls for it, without prompting you each time. | Frequent, repeated use of Mindtickle inside conversations — for example, when you expect the client to pull Mindtickle context turn after turn — and you have already developed confidence in how the connector behaves. |

If you are unsure which to choose, leave both tools set to Needs approval. You can switch to Always allow later from the connector's settings once you are comfortable with how the tools are used.

Note: The Mindtickle tools currently granted through this connector are read-only — they only search and read Mindtickle content on your behalf. If Mindtickle introduces tools that modify content in the future, reconsider Always allow for those tools, because the client would be able to perform changes without prompting you.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Mindtickle MCP server > Part 2: User — Connect your account to the Mindtickle connector > Disconnect the connector:
To revoke the client's access to the Mindtickle MCP server from your account:

1. Go to Settings → Connectors .
2. Find the connected Mindtickle connector. It displays a Connected badge.
3. Click Disconnect .
4. Confirm in the dialog. The client will no longer have access to that connector's tools from your account.

Disconnecting removes your personal OAuth grant for the connector. Your organization's connector configuration remains in place. If your organization uses admin-controlled scopes and needs to fully revoke the underlying client_id and client_secret, the admin should contact their Mindtickle CSM or account team.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Mindtickle MCP server > Troubleshoot common issues:
| Problem | Resolution |
| --- | --- |
| Connection test fails (admin) | Verify that the server URL is correct and reachable over HTTPS. Confirm that the URL ends with /mcp and that your Mindtickle instance is running. |
| Connector not visible to users | Check the Workspace availability setting on the connector. Ensure that the user is a member of the workspace or group the connector is assigned to. |
| The client does not use the connector tools | Confirm that the connector status shows Connected in the user's settings. Check that the connector is not turned off in the conversation's tools panel. |
| "Unauthorized" error when using the connector | The user's OAuth token may have expired. Ask the user to disconnect and reconnect to re-authorize. |
| Connectors option not visible in settings | Custom connectors are available only on certain client plans (for example, Claude Teams and Enterprise). Verify your organization's subscription level with the client application's vendor. |

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Mindtickle MCP server > Security considerations:
Keep the following practices in mind when deploying the Mindtickle MCP server as a custom connector:

- Use HTTPS exclusively: Never configure the connector URL over unencrypted HTTP.
- Apply least privilege: Grant only the scopes that the client actually needs. Use admin-controlled scopes when you need to enforce a fixed policy across the organization.
- Rotate credentials regularly: If you use admin-controlled scopes, rotate the client_id and client_secret on a schedule by requesting new credentials from your Mindtickle CSM.
- Audit access: Periodically review which users have connected to the connector in the client application's connector settings.
- Monitor activity: Use your Mindtickle audit logs and the client application's logs to review tool calls and access patterns.

Privacy note

Mindtickle hosts and processes MCP traffic entirely within Mindtickle-controlled infrastructure. Once data is returned to the MCP client application, it is subject to that application's data handling practices. Depending on the client vendor and configuration, returned data may be stored, logged, or included in conversation context. Review the data exposed through the connector before enabling it for your organization.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Mindtickle MCP server > FAQs:
Does Mindtickle use any third-party services for MCP hosting, routing, or processing?

No. Mindtickle hosts the MCP server entirely on Mindtickle-controlled infrastructure. All MCP-related data routing and processing are handled within Mindtickle's own systems. No third-party services are used to host the MCP server or to route or process data transmitted through the MCP connection.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Release Notes > What’s new > Introducing nested hubs:
Nested hubs are now available in the Mindtickle mobile app, providing a more organized and intuitive way to navigate content. With a hierarchical hub structure that reflects your organization's setup, learners can more easily discover, access, and navigate relevant content across teams, regions, and business units.

Highlight features

- Hierarchical hub navigation: Hubs can now be organized in a parent-child hierarchy, helping reps and learners navigate content in a more structured and intuitive way.
- Improved content discovery: Browse hubs using an expandable hierarchy instead of a flat list, making it easier to locate relevant content across teams, regions, and business units.
- Improved search experience: Search results display the full hub path, providing additional context and helping learners identify the most relevant content. Searches performed within a hub also include content from its nested child hubs.
- Home and overview page widgets: Widgets such as "Recently viewed assets" and "Featured hubs" now surface content from any level of the hub hierarchy, regardless of how deeply nested it is.
- Consistent with web: Mobile now reflects the same nested hub structure already available on the Asset Hub web experience, ensuring a seamless experience across devices.

For more information, see Assets homepage on the mobile app.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Release Notes > What’s new > Improved sign-in, sign-up, and password reset experience:
The sign-in (login), sign-up (registration), and password reset (forgot password) screens in the Mindtickle mobile app have been redesigned to provide a more streamlined and consistent authentication experience.

Key changes

- Streamlined sign-in (login) flow: The sign-in (login) screen has been redesigned with an improved layout and navigation, enabling users to access their accounts more efficiently.
- Enhanced sign-up (registration) experience: The registration workflow has been simplified with a cleaner, guided experience that reduces the number of steps required to create an account.
- Simplified password reset (forgot password) process: Password recovery has been updated with clearer instructions and an improved user flow to help users reset their credentials more easily.
- Strengthened account security: Authentication workflows have been enhanced with additional security improvements to provide stronger protection for user accounts and data.

These enhancements deliver a more intuitive authentication experience while improving usability, reducing friction during account access and registration, and strengthening overall account security.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Release Notes > What’s new > Content Center files in global search:
Content Center files are now included in global search, making it easier to discover and access relevant training content from a single search experience. Search results are automatically filtered based on your access permissions, ensuring that only content available to you is displayed.

Key changes

- Content Center files in global search: Search across Content Center files alongside other training content and assets directly from global search.
- Permission-aware results: Only Content Center files that you have access to are displayed in search results. Restricted content remains hidden.
- Direct access to files: Open Content Center files directly from search results in the file details page.

For more information, see Global search and Copilot Assistant for Sellers on the mobile app.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Web Conferencing:
The ILT-Zoom integration automatically marks learners’ attendance by matching email addresses in the Zoom attendance report with the list of learners invited to the ILT module.

This integration enables you to:

- Create, update, or delete Zoom meetings from ILT sessions.
- Automate attendance tracking for Instructor-Led Training (ILT) sessions conducted on Zoom.

This integration is powered through the Zoom App Marketplace. To access the Mindtickle app on the Zoom App Marketplace, click here.

Note:

- You can configure the ILT-Zoom setup using either admin-level or user-level authorization. By default, admin-level authorization is configured. To enable Zoom ILT integration with user-level authentication for your organization, contact Mindtickle Support or your Customer Success Manager (CSM).
- If a learner’s email address is not listed in the Zoom attendance report, their attendance is marked as Did not attend . (Admins can manually change the learner’s attendance status from the admin site.) This feature is available only on request.
- If the host sets up breakout rooms during a meeting, the attendance report includes data for participants in both the breakout rooms and the main session.

For attendance tracking, the following conditions must be met:

- Users must be invited to the ILT module
- Users must join the Zoom meeting with the email address associated with their Mindtickle user ID (email address)

This article explains how to set up the ILT-Zoom integration when user-level authentication is enabled on your learning site.

In user-level authentication, each host must authenticate their Zoom account in Mindtickle before creating Zoom meetings in ILT sessions. This is a one-time configuration for every host.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Web Conferencing > Prerequisites > Accounts and roles:
The user setting up the ILT-Zoom integration must meet the following prerequisites:

- Zoom : A licensed Zoom user account with ‘host’ role permissions. The host is the person who schedules, starts, ends, or records the session. A host can also assign roles to other participants in the session.
- Mindtickle : A Mindtickle account with either the Site Owner or IT Admin role . This is required to access the Security & integrations tab on the platform.

Note:

- The Mindtickle-Zoom integration can be set up only with a licensed Zoom host user account. It is not available for free Zoom account users.
- You can configure the ILT-Zoom setup using either admin-level authorization or user-level authorization. By default, admin-level authorization is configured.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Web Conferencing > Prerequisites > Zoom scopes requested:
For the ILT-Zoom integration to work successfully, Mindtickle requests the following Zoom scopes during authorization:

| Scope | Usage |
| --- | --- |
| user:read:user | Validates the authenticated Zoom user account in Mindtickle. |
| meeting:write:meeting | Creates Zoom meetings from ILT sessions. |
| meeting:update:meeting | Updates Zoom meetings from ILT sessions. |
| meeting:delete:meeting | Deletes Zoom meetings from ILT sessions. |
| meeting:read:meeting | Validates Zoom meeting details for auto-attendance eligibility. |
| meeting:read:list_meetings | Lists meetings associated with the authenticated Zoom host, if required for validation. |
| meeting:read:list_past_participants | Reads past meeting participants to mark auto-attendance in Mindtickle ILT. |
| webinar:read:webinar | Validates manually added Zoom webinar links for auto-attendance eligibility. |
| webinar:read:list_past_participants | Reads past webinar participants to mark auto-attendance for manually added Zoom webinar links. |

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Web Conferencing > Use Zoom integration in ILT sessions:
Follow these steps to configure Zoom to automatically track attendance in ILT sessions.

- Create a new ILT session . By default, the session type is set to Classroom location.
- In the dialog box for creating a new session, select the session type from the Classroom / video conferencing tool details dropdown. For a video conferencing session, you can create a Zoom meeting from the session or add a meeting link manually. This article explains how to create a Zoom meeting from the ILT session. Note :
  - While creating a meeting from the ILT session, ensure:
    - The session start and end times are set in the future.
    - The session duration is longer than 10 minutes.
- Select Generate Zoom meeting link from the dropdown.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Web Conferencing > Use Zoom integration in ILT sessions > Create a Zoom meeting link > If your Zoom account is not authenticated:
If your Zoom account is not authenticated, the system prompts you to authenticate it.You can proceed in one of the following ways:

- Option 1: Authenticate your Zoom account
- Option 2: Enter an authenticated host email ID

Option 1: Authenticate your Zoom account

1. Click Authenticate .
2. You are directed to the Zoom sign-in page.
3. Enter your Zoom credentials.
4. On the Mindtickle authorization page, click Allow .
5. After successful validation, you are redirected to the ILT session page. The Zoom meeting is created successfully.

Option 2: Enter an authenticated host email ID

Use this option when you are creating the ILT session on behalf of another Zoom host whose account is already authenticated in Mindtickle.

1. Click Enter host email ID .
2. Enter the host’s email address.
3. Click Create meeting . The meeting link is generated, and the meeting details and host details are auto-filled in the Meeting Details section. Note:

- The Zoom host must have a licensed Zoom account, a Mindtickle user account, and an authenticated Zoom account in Mindtickle.
- If the host is not authenticated in Mindtickle, the system prompts you to enter the details of another user with host permissions.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Web Conferencing > Use Zoom integration in ILT sessions > Create a Zoom meeting link > Zoom authorization expiry and reauthorization:
Zoom authorization can expire if the integration is not used continuously for 3 months. Zoom can also invalidate authorization tokens before expiry in cases such as a password update or a change in the user’s Zoom scope.

If Zoom authentication fails, reauthorize the Zoom account or contact Mindtickle Support.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Web Conferencing > Use Zoom integration in ILT sessions > Enter a Zoom meeting link manually:
When entering a meeting link manually, select Enter meeting link from the dropdown and enter the meeting URL in the Enter Meeting URL section.

If the meeting is created using an account that has host privileges, the system checks the URL for Zoom auto-attendance eligibility. If eligible, the Auto attendance toggle appears and is automatically switched ON.

If the meeting is created from an account that does not have host privileges, the system prompts you to authenticate the Zoom account or enter the email address of a user with host privileges.

When the session type is Classroom location, and you enter the URL of a Zoom meeting manually, the session type changes to Enter link manually.

The system checks the URL for Zoom auto-attendance eligibility. If eligible, the Auto attendance toggle appears and is automatically switched ON.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Web Conferencing > Use Zoom integration in ILT sessions > Add co-hosts to the meeting:
You can add co-hosts to the meeting. Co-hosts help improve meeting productivity.

The co-host role has permissions similar to the host role. If the host is running late or cannot attend, a co-host can start and manage the meeting. Co-hosts can also assist the host with meeting management, which is helpful for larger meetings.

1. Click Add co-host .
2. Enter the user’s email address.
3. Click Save . Note: If the details of users added as co-hosts are invalid, a failure message appears on the screen indicating that the users are not added as co-hosts to the meeting. The user is added as a co-host to the meeting. You can click the Edit icon to edit the details or click the Remove icon to remove the user as a co-host from the meeting.

Alternatively, you can add instructors or facilitators and assign them as co-hosts for the meeting.

To assign an instructor or facilitator as a co-host:

1. Enter their details on the Instructors and facilitators tab.
2. Select the Add as meeting co-host checkbox. The users are added to the list of co-hosts.

Note:

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Web Conferencing > Use Zoom integration in ILT sessions > Add co-hosts to the meeting:
- There is no limit to the number of co-hosts you can add to a meeting.
- If an instructor or facilitator is added or removed as a co-host from the meeting, they receive an email notification with all session change details, if applicable. The email is sent after the session is published.
- All meeting links belonging to the authenticated hosts’ Zoom account on Mindtickle are eligible for auto-attendance.
- If the Auto attendance toggle is off, you must manually mark attendance or use the session check-in option.
- The check-in feature is unavailable for sessions in which auto-attendance is enabled. To use the check-in feature, turn the toggle switch off.
- You cannot generate Zoom webinar links from the ILT session. You can manually add a Zoom webinar link, but auto-attendance is available only if the webinar link belongs to an authenticated Zoom host and is eligible for attendance tracking.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Web Conferencing > Use Zoom integration in ILT sessions > Create and publish the session:
1. Configure the remaining settings.
2. Click Create session . A confirmation message appears after the session is created successfully. The session appears in the list of sessions. The session's attendance mode is set to Auto Attendance . Click the session to view other details. Publish the session and invite your learners. After the session ends, participants’ attendance is marked automatically through Zoom.

Note:

- Learners do not have to enroll in a specific session, but they must be invited to the ILT module for auto-attendance to work.
- Attendance must be marked manually for meeting links added by the enablement team, even if the link belongs to the same Zoom account connected to Mindtickle.
- Auto-attendance does not apply to meetings where the host is not authenticated or is not a Mindtickle user.
- To use a Zoom host for ILT auto-attendance, the host must have a Mindtickle user account and must authenticate their Zoom account in Mindtickle.
- Auto-attendance applies only to Zoom meetings held at the specified time in Mindtickle.
- Admins must ensure that the session start and end times are not updated on Zoom after the session is created in Mindtickle. If the times are updated in Zoom, they should also be synced with the Mindtickle session.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Web Conferencing > Use Zoom integration in ILT sessions > Duration-based attendance capture:
Admins can set a minimum percentage threshold to record learners’ attendance for ILT modules and individual sessions using the Duration-based attendance capture feature.

This feature automatically records learners’ attendance based on their time in ILT events and sessions.

When participants attend an ILT session via Zoom, their attendance is automatically recorded if the meeting or webinar is eligible for auto-attendance. The Zoom integration provides the time spent by the learner in a session.

The system calculates an ILT session’s minimum attendance threshold as follows:

- Scheduled sessions: For sessions yet to start, the system calculates the minimum attendance threshold based on the session start and end times set during session creation. For example, in a 60-minute session with a 20% minimum attendance threshold, the system marks the learner as attended if they spend at least 12 minutes in the session.
- Completed sessions: If a session ends early or extends beyond the scheduled time, the system calculates the minimum attendance threshold based on the actual session time. For example, for a 60-minute session with a 20% minimum attendance threshold, if the session ends early in 50 minutes, the system marks the learner as attended if they spend at least 10 minutes in the session.

The system compares the learner’s time in the Zoom session with the session’s minimum attendance threshold to mark the learner’s attendance.

The learner’s attendance status and time spent in the session are displayed in the Attendance status/Duration column on the Events and Sessions tab of the ILT.

For more information, see Duration-based attendance capture for learners in ILTs.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Web Conferencing > Use Zoom integration in ILT sessions > Caveats:
- If you discard the meeting without saving the changes, Zoom meeting details are deleted from the session, and the session type is reset to Classroom location . The meeting is also deleted from Zoom.
- If a meeting that has ended is restarted (either by the host or by a participant joining), Mindtickle receives attendance details only from the latest meeting instance, and data for participants from all previous instances is lost.
- If an instructor marked as a co-host is removed, the user is also removed from the Zoom meeting co-host list.
- If you copy a session that has a Zoom meeting configured, the copied session's session type is reset to Classroom location .
- If you copy the ILT module into a different series that includes one or more sessions with Zoom meetings configured, the session type for the copied sessions is reset to Classroom location .

- Create a meeting

- Update a meeting
  - Admin edits the session name.
  - Admin edits the start or end date/time.

  - Admin edits the session and removes the meeting from the session creation page.

- Remove co-hosts from an already-created meeting
  - Admin edits the session and removes co-host(s) from both the meeting details section and the instructor/facilitator section.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Web Conferencing > Attendance calculation for ILT sessions in Zoom:
For ILT sessions conducted on Zoom, Mindtickle fetches the attendance reports from Zoom after the scheduled session ends.

Learners’ attendance is marked for all valid Zoom meetings that start 30 minutes before and 30 minutes after the scheduled meeting time.

If the meeting is ongoing, the system requests attendance reports every five minutes for up to 24 hours after the meeting ends.

The table below explains the attendance capture scenarios for an ILT session scheduled on Zoom between 3 p.m. and 4 p.m.

| Scenario | Meeting start time | Meeting end time | Attendance in Mindtickle |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| The host starts the meeting early to check if the meeting link is accessible. | 2:15 p.m. | 2:16 p.m. | No |
| The learner joins the meeting early before the host joins the meeting. | 2:25 p.m. | 2:35 p.m. | No |
| The host starts the meeting early, and the session ends in 45 minutes instead of 1 hour. | 2:45 p.m. | 3:45 p.m. | Yes |
| The learner joins the meeting in the last few minutes. | 3:55 p.m. | 4:00 p.m. | Yes |
| The host starts the meeting early, and the session extends beyond the scheduled meeting time by 15 minutes. | 2:55 p.m. | 4:15 p.m. | Yes |
| The host starts the meeting early and it extends 40 minutes beyond the scheduled meeting time. | 2:55 p.m. | 4:40 p.m. | Yes |
| The learner starts the meeting late after the meeting ends. | 4:25 p.m. | 4:26 p.m. | Yes |
| The learner starts the meeting late after the meeting ends. | 4:25 p.m. | 4:32 p.m. | Yes |
| The learner starts the meeting late after the meeting ends. | 4:35 p.m. | 4:40 p.m. | No |

Mindtickle combines the attendance reports from all valid meeting instances for attendance calculation. For example, if 10 users join the meeting in the first half-hour and 5 (with 3 overlapping users) join in the second half-hour, the attendance is marked only for 12 users.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Integrations > Web Conferencing > FAQs:
- If I have already created a Zoom meeting, can I add it to the ILT session in Mindtickle? Will attendance still be marked? Yes, you can add the Zoom meeting URL. As long as the Zoom host has authenticated their account in Mindtickle and the meeting is eligible for auto-attendance, attendance is marked automatically.
- What do I do if I am not hosting the meeting, but I am setting it up for the host? Create the ILT session. When creating the Zoom meeting from the session, click Enter host email ID on the first pop-up that appears. Enter the host’s email address in the next pop-up and click Create meeting . Or, click Authenticate your Zoom account to authenticate a new account and enter the host’s email ID in the pop-up. If your account is authenticated, the meeting is generated with you as the host. You may then add the actual host as the co-host.
- What if an ILT participant attends the session just for a few minutes? Are they marked as attended? If duration-based attendance capture is not enabled, the participant is marked as attended if they join a valid Zoom session. If duration-based attendance capture is enabled, the participant must meet the configured minimum attendance threshold to be marked as attended.
- Do learners need to enroll for auto-attendance to work? Learners do not have to enroll in a session, but they must be invited to the ILT module to be automatically marked as attended.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Release Notes > New features > Archive assets API:
This release brings the Archive assets API for Asset Hub. This new endpoint empowers developers and system administrators to programmatically archive assets in bulk, streamlining the content lifecycle management process and making it easier to keep your repositories clean and up-to-date at scale.

Key capabilities

- Bulk processing: Transition up to 50 assets to an archived state simultaneously in a single API request.
- Granular partial success tracking: The API automatically segregates successfully archived items from failed entries. You will receive unique status updates and specific error explanations for every individual asset ID included in your payload, rather than failing the entire request due to one invalid item.
- Idempotent execution: Resending identical payloads does not create unintended side effects. Assets that are already archived are safely handled and documented as a success or a no-op without triggering unnecessary errors.

Technical details

- Endpoint: POST /api/assethub/v2/assets/archive
- Required Parameters:
  - asset_ids: An array of unique asset IDs to archive.
  - user_id: The identifier of the user performing the action.
- Permissions: The specified user_id must explicitly possess asset management clearance.
- Limits: Maximum of 50 assets per request. Clients are encouraged to clear duplicate entries from the payload array before sending to reduce validation overhead.

Audit and reporting

All completion processes triggered through this API are transparently logged across system environments. Successfully archived items will track the associated request_id and the performing user_id to ensure full administrative compliance and auditability.

For more information, see Asset Hub management APIs.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Release Notes > New features > New advanced report template for missions:
Admins can now create a custom report for mission performance using the new Mission learners report template in advanced reports. The template provides a ready-made starting point to track how learners are performing in a mission, reporting on their performance, engagement, and completion metrics. Admins can then customize, save, schedule, and share like any other advanced report.

The Mission learners report covers all mission types (such as one-way and two-way role plays) and surfaces learner-level detail that previously required custom data pulls: attempts, percentage score, completion status, mission due date, reviewer, positive and constructive feedback, and mission section, parameter name, outcome, and score. Data is shown at the mission, learner, reviewer, and parameter level, so a learner reviewed on multiple parameters — or by multiple reviewers, including the AI reviewer (Mindtickle Copilot) — appears across multiple rows.

Once created, the report can be customized (add or remove fields and configure pivot, export, and display settings), filtered (by mission, series, reviewer, completion status, group, and date range), saved and published, shared with individuals or groups (with managers automatically scoped to their reportees), and scheduled for recurring email delivery.

For more information, see Advanced reports overview [admin].

Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Release Notes > New features > Introducing AI podcasts: Turn documents into audio podcasts (beta):
Admins can now transform long, complex documents into concise, engaging audio podcasts using AI, with the new AI podcast feature. It automatically summarizes core ideas and key points from a PDF, DOC, or PPT file and produces a narrated audio file that can be added as a learning object in course and quick update modules — no scripting or recording expertise required. Generated podcasts are also saved to the Content Center for reuse across other modules and assets.

Creating a podcast

When adding a learning object in a course or quick update, admins select AI podcast, choose a source file, and configure the audio output before generating:

- Format: Choose a Conversation (multi-speaker dialogue) or a Monologue (single-speaker bulletin).
- Duration: Select Short, Medium, or Long.
- Language and voices: Choose from 28 supported languages with a range of regional accents and gender options, and select distinct host and guest voices. Language (what is said) and voice (how it sounds) are independent, so you can pair any language with any accent — for example, English content spoken with an Indian accent.
- Focus (optional): Add a text prompt to have the AI emphasize specific topics or sections of the document.

Generation runs in the background, so admins can continue working elsewhere while the podcast is produced.

Editing a podcast

Admins can also edit a podcast after it is generated, so the output can be refined without starting over from the source document.

Note:

- The AI podcast feature is in beta. Contact Mindtickle Support to enable it for your instance.
- Source files must be text-based (PDF, DOC, or PPT); image-only or video files are not supported.

For more information, see AI podcast - Generate podcasts from documents using AI - beta [admins].

Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Release Notes > Enhancements > Upgraded report downloads in analytics:
Report downloads in the new analytics experience now match the on-screen view. Previously, an export could include more fields than were shown on screen — such as profile fields and other extra columns — so users had to reconcile the downloaded file against what they saw in the report. Now the download contains exactly the data shown on screen, with no additional fields, so what you see is what you download.

This applies across analytics reports and wherever a download option is available (both report-level and widget-level downloads), giving admins cleaner, more predictable exports for day-to-day tracking.

For more information, see Manage advanced reports [admin].

Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Release Notes > Enhancements > Analytics reports now support your local time zone:
Date and time values in analytics reports now display in your local time zone, based on your device's time zone setting. Previously, all timestamps rendered in UTC regardless of where you were located, which caused global users to misread session times, enrollment dates, and activity timestamps. Now the same report shows each date and time in the viewer's own local time — so a report viewed in PST and IST displays the same underlying value in each viewer's respective time zone.

The conversion applies automatically to all date and time fields across analytics reports — such as invited on, started on, start time, end time, and created or updated dates — and to both interactive report views and scheduled email exports. No configuration or dashboard changes are required.

Exception: ILT session times remain in the time zone in which the session was scheduled, rather than converting to the viewer's local time zone. This is intentional, as the session time is tied to the time zone selected when the session was created.

For more information, see Local time zone support in analytics reports [admin].

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Release Notes > Enhancements > XLSX support for exporting advanced reports via email:
You can now export advanced reports in XLSX format when emailing or scheduling them, in addition to CSV. Previously, the new analytics experience supported export in CSV only, which does not preserve formatting. XLSX produces presentation-quality output that preserves report-friendly formatting — visible column headers, correct number and date typing (so values are not exported as plain text), and consistent column ordering and structure. This export option is currently available for advanced reports only.

When you email or schedule an advanced report, the flow remains the same — select the recipients (admins, managers, or learners), add CC, and choose the email template — with one addition: you now choose the export format. CSV remains the default; select XLSX to export in Excel format instead.

Widget support for email exports has also expanded. Previously, only expandable pivot and advanced table widgets could be exported; this release adds the standard pivot widget, bringing the total to three supported widget types. Only titled table widgets can be emailed, so ensure your table widgets are titled before exporting.

Exports continue to respect the report's filters, data permissions, and access controls. XLSX is intended for presentation-quality spreadsheet output and does not include advanced Excel features such as formulas, macros, or custom styling; CSV remains available for raw-data workflows.

For more information, see Manage advanced reports [admin].

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Release Notes > Enhancements > Added “Updated on” and “Next refresh” timestamps in analytics reports:
Analytics reports now display Updated on and Next refresh timestamps, so admins and managers can see how current the data is and when it will refresh next. Previously, these indicators appeared only in legacy analytics reports; reports in the new analytics experience — including advanced reports, custom reports, and out-of-the-box (OOTB) reports — did not show them. With this release, the timestamps appear consistently across these report types.

Updated on indicates the point up to which the data shown is guaranteed to be current: all activity before this time is reflected in the report. Some more recent activity may also appear, but everything up to the Updated on time is always included. Data is not real-time, so there is always some delay. Next refresh indicates when the report's data will update next. Both timestamps are shown in your local time zone, based on your device's time zone setting.

Most reports follow the standard refresh schedule, with the following exceptions:

- Call AI reports update every 24 hours, at 12:00 AM in your local device time zone.
- Readiness index updates weekly, every Monday at 2:00 AM UTC.

For more information, see Data update frequency for analytics reports and dashboards [admin].

Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Release Notes > Enhancements > Manage restricted hub access across your nested hub hierarchy:
You can now control exactly who can access each restricted hub in a nested hierarchy. From a hub's Users tab, admins can add or remove users and user groups at any level — parent (root) or child — with full visibility into how each user or group obtained access.

Note: This feature applies to restricted (private) hubs only. Public hubs are accessible to all users and have no per-hub access.

See how access was granted

Each hub's Users tab shows, for every user and user group, how they got access to that hub:

- Granted directly to this hub
- Inherited from a parent hub above it
- Granted via a child hub below it

Review access in two views, View by users and View by groups, and use the new nested-hub filter to focus on a specific hub and its sub-hubs.

Add users and user groups at any level

- Add at a parent (root) hub to grant access to the hub and all of its child hubs.
- Add at a child hub to grant access there; it's also surfaced to the parent hubs above it in the hierarchy for visibility.
- Anyone who already has access is automatically skipped with a clear Already has access status — no duplicates.
- When a change affects multiple child hubs, a confirmation summarizes the impact before you proceed.
- New child hubs automatically inherit the users and user groups of their parent hub at creation — which already includes everyone inherited from hubs higher up in the hierarchy.

Remove access safely

For more information, see Create and manage nested hubs [admin].

Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Release Notes > Enhancements > Set up deck templates with variables in Content Center for personalized customized assets (beta):
Reps can now create personalized, prospect-ready assets in minutes using admin-approved templates that contain variables (placeholders) for details such as company name, contact name, job title, and logo. Admins map text variables to Salesforce Opportunity fields, so a rep simply selects a deal to auto-fill those details, removing manual data entry and keeping personalized content consistent and on-brand. This release introduces template and variable support for PPT/PPTX assets.

Note: This is a beta feature. To enable it for your Mindtickle instance, please contact Mindtickle Support.

For reps

When creating a customized asset (via Mix and match) from a template, reps click Customize slides, select a deal to auto-fill the mapped fields from Salesforce, add the logo manually, and save the personalized asset as PPT or PDF. Auto-filled values remain editable, and any unmapped variables are filled in manually.

For admins

Admins author variables in the PPT using the double curly brace format (for example, {{company_name}}), then in the Content Center select Set as template from the file's More menu and define each variable's label, description, and optional Salesforce Opportunity field mapping. Once an asset is created from the template with Allow customized asset creation enabled, it is ready for reps. Because templates are internal assets, this release also removes the earlier restriction that limited customized asset creation to external assets.

Notes:

- Templates and variables are currently supported for PPT/PPTX files only.
- Salesforce Opportunity mapping applies to text variables only; logos are added manually.

For more information, see Set up PowerPoint templates with variables for customized assets (admins, reps) and My assets page: Create and manage customized assets (reps).

Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Release Notes > Enhancements > Call AI June enhancements:
Call AI includes the following enhancements in this release:

- Call recording details page now includes adjustable panel sizes. You can allocate more space to either the recording or insights, depending on your focus. Your preference is saved within a single session. The layout also automatically optimizes screen space as you scroll and consume video insights (Key moments, Themes, Comments, etc.).

Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Release Notes > Enhancements > Embed link in Content Center now supports plain links:
The Embed link option in Content Center now lets admins add a plain external link, not just an iframe-able embed code. You can set the link to open in a new browser tab, which unblocks content from sites that prevent iframe embedding — such as LinkedIn, external LMS platforms, and secure dashboards. Previously, these links rendered inline as an iframe and showed a "Refused to connect" error, leaving learners with no way to reach the content.

When adding content via New > Embed link, the Link settings section offers two mutually exclusive options: Insert iframe tag (embed inline) and Open in a new tab. For a plain link that is not embeddable, select Open in a new tab, since such links cannot render inline. Learners then see a placeholder screen and click to open the destination URL in a new tab. For module learning objects, View and Completion events fire as soon as the learner clicks to open the link.

All existing links keep their current iframe behavior, so nothing changes for content already embedded.

For more information, see Add or replace content in Content Center (admin).

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Content Center:
This article explains how admins set up PPT/PPTX templates with variables in Content Center and enable them for customized asset creation, and how reps then use those templates to quickly personalize assets for their prospects.

Templates let your marketing and enablement teams create approved, reusable decks (such as a first-call deck or an industry-specific pitch) that contain variables (placeholders) for prospect-specific details, such as company name, contact name, job title, or logo. Admins can map text variables to CRM Opportunity fields. When a rep creates a customized asset from the template and selects a deal (e.g., Salesforce Opportunity), the mapped fields are filled in automatically from that Opportunity, with no manual data entry. Variables that are not mapped are filled in manually by the rep.

Note:

- This is a beta feature. To enable it for your Mindtickle instance, please contact Mindtickle Support .
- Templates and variables are currently supported for PPT/PPTX files only.
- You need the Manage Content permission to set a file as a template and define its variables.
- Customize slides is intended for light personalization, such as updating a logo, company name, or job title. It does not support heavier edits, such as moving images or rewriting slide content. For heavier edits (beyond variable personalization), we recommend using Microsoft Office for the web or Google Workspace .
- Asset Hub is a paid feature. For more information, contact your Customer Success Manager (CSM).

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Content Center > How templates and variables work:
Setting up and using a template involves three roles and stages:

1. Author the placeholders : A marketer or content author adds variables (placeholders) to a PPT file using the double curly brace format, then uploads the file to Content Center.
2. Set up the template : An admin sets the file as a template, defines each variable (label, optional description, and an optional Salesforce Opportunity field mapping) using the Variables option on the file details page, creates an asset from it, and enables customized asset creation.
3. Personalize and share : A rep creates a customized asset from the template and selects a deal (Salesforce Opportunity) to auto-fill the mapped fields. The rep fills any unmapped variables and the logo manually, and then shares the personalized asset with the prospect.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Content Center > Author placeholders in the PPT file:
Before a file can become a template, variables must be added to its slides. This is typically done by a marketer or content author in Microsoft PowerPoint or Google Slides, and must be completed before the file is uploaded to Content Center.

A variable is a placeholder written in double curly braces, for example {{company_name}}, {{contact_name}}, or {{title}}. When a rep later personalizes the asset, Mindtickle replaces each placeholder with the value provided for that variable.

Keep the following in mind while authoring placeholders:

- Supported variable types : You can add both text variables and image variables.
- Text variables : Type the placeholder directly into the slide text using double curly braces (for example, {{company_name}} ).
- Image variables (such as a logo): Insert a placeholder image into the slide, then add the placeholder to the image's alt text. This tells Mindtickle that the image is a variable that the rep can replace.
- Placement : You can add variables on a single slide, several slides, or all slides. The same variable can be reused on multiple slides; every occurrence is replaced with the same value.
- Authoring tool : Author the placeholders in Microsoft PowerPoint or Google Slides.

Once the placeholders are in place, upload the file to Content Center so that it is available for the admin to set up. For more information, see Add or replace content in Content Center.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Content Center > For admins > Set the file as a template and define variables > Define each variable:
For each detected variable, you can define the following using the Variables option on the file details page:

- Field label (mandatory): A clear, rep-friendly name for the variable (for example, "Company name" or "Job title") so that reps understand what to enter.
- Description (optional): Additional guidance for the rep, such as "Enter your job title here." This will appear as a field tooltip for the rep.
- Salesforce Opportunity field (optional): Map the variable to a single field from your Salesforce Opportunity so that the value is filled in automatically when a rep selects a deal (such as account name, opportunity stage, or contact title).

Note:

- Each variable can be mapped to only one Salesforce Opportunity field. This is a one-to-one field-to-variable mapping, because different data is stored in different fields.
- Salesforce Opportunity field mapping is currently supported for text variables only. Image variables (such as a logo) cannot be mapped to a Salesforce field at this time; reps select the image manually.
- If you leave a variable's Salesforce Opportunity field unmapped, reps enter that value manually when they personalize the asset. For example, if the slide contains a {{ae_name}} variable that you do not map, the rep enters the AE's name.

After you define the labels, descriptions, and Salesforce mappings, the template setup in Content Center is complete.
chunks.body:
For each detected variable, you can define the following using the Variables option on the file details page:

- Field label (mandatory): A clear, rep-friendly name for the variable (for example, "Company name" or "Job title") so that reps understand what to enter.
- Description (optional): Additional guidance for the rep, such as "Enter your job title here." This will appear as a field tooltip for the rep.
- Salesforce Opportunity field (optional): Map the variable to a single field from your Salesforce Opportunity so that the value is filled in automatically when a rep selects a deal (such as account name, opportunity stage, or contact title).

Note:

- Each variable can be mapped to only one Salesforce Opportunity field. This is a one-to-one field-to-variable mapping, because different data is stored in different fields.
- Salesforce Opportunity field mapping is currently supported for text variables only. Image variables (such as a logo) cannot be mapped to a Salesforce field at this time; reps select the image manually.
- If you leave a variable's Salesforce Opportunity field unmapped, reps enter that value manually when they personalize the asset. For example, if the slide contains a {{ae_name}} variable that you do not map, the rep enters the AE's name.

After you define the labels, descriptions, and Salesforce mappings, the template setup in Content Center is complete.

If you no longer want a file to be treated as a template, you can remove its template designation.

2. Select Remove as template .
3. In the Unmark as template? confirmation pop-up, click Unmark .

The file is no longer a template, and its variables are no longer available for customized asset creation.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Content Center > For admins > Create an asset and enable customized asset creation:
To make the template usable by reps, create an asset from it in the Asset Hub and enable customized asset creation.

Note: A template is an internal asset. Reps create external, prospect-facing assets from it, but the template itself remains internal. Previously, customized asset creation was limited to external assets (Usage = External). With this release, that restriction is removed: you can enable customized asset creation on internal assets as well. This applies to both template and non-template assets.

1. Add the template file as an asset in the Asset Hub.
2. Mark the asset's Usage as Internal .
3. Enable the following properties on the asset:
  - [Main property] Allow customized asset creation = enabled
  - [Sub-property] Mix and match = enabled
4. Optionally, enable the Edit content sub-property if you want reps to make heavier edits (beyond variable personalization) using Microsoft Office for the web or Google Workspace .
5. For detailed information on creating assets, see this article .

Once these properties are enabled, the template is available for reps to use. Enabling customized asset creation on an internal asset has no negative impact on the rest of the platform.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > Content Center > For reps > Personalize and share an asset from a template:
1. Start a mix and match flow for an asset that contains variables. As long as at least one selected slide contains a variable, a Customize slides button appears.
2. Click Customize slides to open the Customize your slides panel. The panel lists the variable fields, each showing the label you defined, an info icon with your description (where provided), and the number of slides the variable appears on.
3. If the template uses Salesforce Opportunity data, the panel displays a Select deal field. The rep selects the relevant deal (Salesforce Opportunity), and Mindtickle auto-fills the mapped fields using data from that deal. The rep can edit any auto-filled value, and fills any unmapped field manually (for example, entering the AE's name for a {{ae_name}} variable).
4. For image variables (such as a company logo), the rep adds the image manually using Upload new (or Replace ), since logos are not pulled from Salesforce. The selected image is fit within the placeholder's dimensions.
5. The rep saves the asset (as PPT or PDF, depending on the selected slides) to a personal hub. Mindtickle processes and generates the personalized asset with the variable values applied, ready to share with the prospect via a room, email, or link.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Reference:
Analytics reports now show dates and times in your local time zone, instead of UTC. This article explains what changed, which values are affected, and the cases where local time does not apply.
chunks.body: Analytics reports now show dates and times in your local time zone, instead of UTC. This article explains what changed, which values are affected, and the cases where local time does not apply.
chunks.headingPath: Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Reference
chunks.title: Local time zone support in analytics reports [admin]

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Reference > What changed:
Earlier, analytics reports showed all dates and times in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC), because the underlying data is stored in UTC. This often led global users to misread session times, enrollment dates, and other timestamps.

Now, reports automatically show each date and time in your local time zone. Two people in different regions see the same value in their own local time. For example, a session that starts at 4:30 PM IST appears in the equivalent local time for a viewer in the United States.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Reference > Time zone used:
Reports use your device's local time zone — the time zone set on the computer you are viewing the report on. This is not a separate Mindtickle profile setting, and there is no option to manually choose a different time zone.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Reference > What is covered:
Local time applies automatically to date and time fields across analytics reports (such as invited on, started on, start time, end time, and created or updated dates). It applies both when you view a report and in scheduled or email exports. No setup is needed, and you do not need to change any dashboards, widgets, queries, or filters.

The Updated on and Next refresh timestamps are also shown in your local time zone. For how often report data refreshes, see Data update frequency for analytics reports and dashboards.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Reference > Exception: ILT session times:
Instructor-led training (ILT) session times do not convert to your local time zone. They stay in the time zone selected when the session was scheduled, which is shown next to the session time. This is intentional, so admins always see a session in the time zone it was set up for. The same applies to any other value that has a time zone explicitly assigned to it.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Advanced reports > When to use this template:
Use this template when the module is your unit of analysis and you want a row per learner per module: who was invited, who has started or completed, and how they scored. It's the right choice for tracking progress on specific modules across a group of learners.

Choose a different template when your question is different:

- For a learner's overall progress across everything assigned to them, use learner summary .
- For learners tracked through a series of modules, use learner series summary or series summary .
- For module-level totals rather than a row per learner, use modules summary .
