Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Advanced reports > Download and:
Once the report is published, the report header gives you six actions: Edit, Download, Email, Share, Duplicate, and Delete.

- Download: Save the whole report as a PDF, with options for paper size, orientation, and the header and footer details to include. To download a single widget's data as CSV or Excel, use that widget's Options menu instead.
- Email: Send the report to admins (the full report) or to managers (a personalized report covering only their reportees). You can send it now or schedule it, choose the widgets to include, and pick CSV or Excel.
- Share: Share the published report with admins, managers, or scope admins, individually or by group. Recipients can apply their own filters.
- Duplicate and Delete: Copy the report, or remove it.

For the full steps on downloading, emailing, scheduling, and sharing, see Manage advanced reports.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Advanced reports > FAQs:
Why don't I see any data in the report?Data appears only for modules and learners that have been invited. If nothing shows, check that the modules and learners in scope have invitations and that your filters aren't excluding them.

A learner I expected isn't in the report. Why?The report includes a learner only if they were invited to a module in scope and they pass the current filters. If someone's missing, check that they were invited, that their module is in scope, and that no filter is excluding them. What you can see can also depend on your own access to the data.

Why is the completion percentage lower than expected?The percentage is based on invited learners in the current filter scope. Widen or reset the filters to confirm the population you're measuring.

Why is a module "in progress" but its completion percentage is 0?Starting a module marks it as in progress right away. The completion percentage is tracked separately and only rises as the learner gets through the content, such as watching a video, viewing pages in a document, answering questions, or attending a session. So a module can sit at 0% for a short time after it's opened, before any trackable content is finished. This is expected.

Why doesn't a completed module show a certificate?A certificate is awarded only when the module offers one and the learner meets its requirements, usually completing the module and reaching the score required for certificate. So a module can be complete but show no certificate if it doesn't offer one, or if the learner finished it without reaching the required score. The certificate fields are listed under Available fields.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > SCORM Content > Before you start:
Perform the following checks before troubleshooting SCORM export or external LMS issues.

1. Ensure SCORM export is enabled for Mission or AI roleplay modules in the learning site. If the SCORM export option is not visible to admins, contact your Customer Success Manager to enable it.
2. Ensure the module is published before exporting it. Exported content uses the published version.
3. Confirm that the content works in the Mindtickle platform before troubleshooting it in the external LMS.
4. Do not modify the original exported .zip file. Unzipping, editing, renaming, or rezipping internal files can break the manifest or launch path.
5. Test the original exported .zip file in SCORM Cloud . If it fails there, record the result before contacting Mindtickle Support .

Note: The external LMS owner manages the external LMS player, iframe rules, attempt settings, cookie settings, and report refresh behavior.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > SCORM Content > Before you start:
Perform the following checks before diagnosing a SCORM issue.

1. Run Test SCORM after every upload, replacement, or configuration change.
2. Use the exact same .zip file that was uploaded to Mindtickle for testing.
3. Complete the full SCORM content without skipping required screens, interactions, quizzes, or final actions.
4. Test the same .zip file in SCORM Cloud to confirm the package behavior.
5. Compare the Test SCORM and SCORM Cloud results to identify the issue.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > SCORM Content > Interpreting Test SCORM results:
An orange Test SCORM result indicates an issue that must be resolved before learners access the content. The issue can be in the SCORM package or in the Mindtickle platform configuration.

| Test SCORM result | Recommended steps | Who to contact |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Receiving completion status | Complete all required screens, interactions, and final actions.Click Save and exit to save progress, then click Done to submit the module.If the result remains orange, the package is not sending a completion status to Mindtickle.Ask the content owner or SCORM vendor to review the package completion logic. | Content owner or SCORM vendor |
| Original score from SCORM | The package is not sending an original score.Ask the content owner or SCORM vendor to check scoring settings in the authoring tool and re-export the package. | Content owner or SCORM vendor |
| Score in Mindtickle | Scoring is not enabled for this SCORM learning object.Open View configuration, enable scoring, and click Save changes.Run Test SCORM again. | Admin |
| Follows SCORM standards | The package format, version, manifest, or file size does not meet SCORM requirements.Check the .zip file’s format to confirm that imsmanifest.xml is at the root, and verify the SCORM version and file size.Ask the content owner or SCORM vendor to re-export the package. | Content owner or SCORM vendor |

Perform the following checks before troubleshooting SCORM completion, score, or reporting issues.

1. Run Test SCORM and check whether the Receiving completion status is green. If the result is orange, test the same .zip file in SCORM Cloud . If the issue also occurs in SCORM Cloud , contact the content owner or SCORM vendor.
2. Ensure that the learner completed all required elements: all slides, videos, questions, interactions, quizzes, and final confirmation screens without skipping any content.
3. For scoring issues, ensure that the SCORM package sends a score and that scoring is enabled in the View configuration screen.
4. Before escalating, check the report filters, date range, learner status, archived content, and report refresh timing for differences.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > SCORM Content > SCORM score and points issues:
How SCORM scoring works

- The SCORM package sends an original score to the Mindtickle platform.
- Mindtickle uses the scoring settings in View configuration for the SCORM learning object to map that score.
- Module points are awarded based on the module scoring rules.
- If the package does not send a score, scoring is not enabled, or module scoring rules do not use the SCORM score, the learner’s score or points do not update.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > SCORM Content > Frequently asked questions:
1. Why does a module stay incomplete when the learner fails a quiz? Some SCORM 1.2 packages link completion to passing. If the learner fails a quiz, the package might not send a completion status. Ask the content owner or SCORM vendor to re-export using SCORM 2004 to separate completion from passing.
2. Does the Save and exit button mark the SCORM module complete? No. The Save and exit button saves the learner’s progress only. The module is marked complete only when the learner completes the required activities, clicks Done , and the SCORM package sends a completion status to Mindtickle.

Perform the following checks before troubleshooting SCORM setup, replacement, configuration, or testing issues.

1. Ensure you have edit access to the series or module that contains the SCORM learning object.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > SCORM Content > SCORM on mobile:
- Packages must support inline mobile playback.
- Packages that open in a new browser tab are not supported in the Mindtickle mobile app.
- Packages that require a camera, microphone, Flash, external login, or a fixed desktop layout do not work reliably on mobile.
- Test the package on iOS and Android before assigning it to mobile learners.
- Ask the content owner or SCORM vendor to provide a mobile-compatible package if it does not work with inline playback.

| Works on mobile | Does not work on mobile |
| --- | --- |
| Packages configured for inline display in the mobile appHTML5 packages without browser-only features, such as camera, microphone, or screen sharingPackages without external login requirements | Packages that open in a new browser tabPackages that require a microphone or camera accessFlash-based packagesPackages with fixed layouts |

Note:

- Confirm that the SCORM package sends a completion status when run on mobile. Completion tracking must work correctly for the module to register as complete on a mobile device.
- To configure a package for inline mobile playback:
  - Go to the SCORM learning object and click View configuration .
  - Under the Mobile app , change the setting to Inline (Mobile) .
  - Click Save changes .
  - Confirm with the content owner or SCORM vendor that the package supports inline playback before making this change.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Content Development > SCORM Content > Before you start:
Perform the following checks before troubleshooting SCORM upload or publishing issues.

1. Use Chrome on a desktop and upload the SCORM package from a local folder. Chrome is the recommended browser for SCORM.
2. Do not upload from OneDrive , Dropbox , or Google Drive .
3. Ensure the file is an actual .zip file exported from the authoring tool. Do not rename .rar , .7z , or .tar files to .zip .
4. Open the .zip file and confirm that the imsmanifest.xml file is at the root of the package, not in a subfolder. Example:
5. The maximum allowed file size is 5 GB .
6. If the upload fails, test the same .zip file in SCORM Cloud . If it also fails there, the content owner or SCORM vendor must fix the package.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > SCORM Content > Before you start:
Perform the following checks before troubleshooting module completion, SCORM launch, playback, recording, or interaction issues.

1. Open the module directly from Mindtickle. Do not use an old bookmark, copied link, browser history, or shared URL.
2. Use the latest version of Chrome on a desktop for SCORM completion, score, progress, launch, or playback issues.
3. Allow cookies and pop-ups for the Mindtickle site and the SCORM content.
4. Use a stable internet connection. Avoid switching networks while the module is open.
5. If your organization allows it, try without a VPN or proxy.
6. Allow microphone and camera access if the module requires recording.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Advanced reports > When to use this template:
Use this template to understand content performance and buyer engagement: which assets and attributes get shared and viewed, how engagement trends over time, which teams and people are most active, and how content is reused to build customized copies.

Choose a different Asset Hub template for a different question:

The report opens with a row of summary widgets, each with a comparison to the previous month where that data is available:

- Published assets: The number of published assets in scope, with external assets shown below.

- Users who shared assets: The number of unique users who shared an asset.
- Open rate: The percentage of shared assets that recipients opened.
- External views: How many times external recipients viewed shared assets.
- External downloads: How many times external recipients downloaded shared assets.
- Unique external views: The number of uniquely identified external contacts who viewed shared assets. Note: Anonymous visits, where recipient consent has not been provided, are excluded from this count.
- Total users: All Asset Hub users currently active on the platform. Note: Report filters don’t apply to this widget.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Advanced reports > FAQs:
Why don't I see any data in the report?You see asset analytics only for the hubs where you have the Hub Analytics permission, and only for assets and users that match your filters. If nothing shows, check that you have access to the hubs in scope and that your filters aren't excluding the data. Asset Hub is a paid feature; if you're not sure whether it's enabled, contact your Customer Success Manager.

Why don't my numbers match another report, or what I saw before?Totals depend on the filters and time period applied, so two reports with different scopes show different numbers. Check that the filters match before comparing. For what each metric counts, see the Data & metrics reference guide for advanced reports.

How current is the data?The Updated on and Next refresh timestamps at the top of the report show when the data last refreshed and when it will refresh next. For the refresh schedule, see Data update frequency for analytics reports and dashboards.

Why is one of the channel charts blank?The charts in Sharing and external view trends only show data for channels your organization actually uses. A channel you haven't set up, such as Outlook or Outreach, stays empty.

Why does the Interaction source filter show different channels than the Sharing and external view trends charts?The trend charts always show the same fixed set of channels, with an empty chart for any your organization hasn't used. The Interaction source filter, though, only lists channels with recorded activity, so its list can look shorter, longer, or worded slightly differently than the chart names.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Release Notes > What’s new > Support for plain external links:
When opening website links — whether accessed as standalone assets or as learning objects (LOs) inside training modules (like courses and quick updates) — the app now supports two distinct experiences depending on how the link file was set up by your admin:

- New plain external links: Supports any external website links. This is particularly useful for external links that block iframe embedding (such as LinkedIn, secure dashboards, or LMS platforms).
- Standard embedded links (Existing): These continue to work exactly as they always have, loading and rendering content instantly right inside the app screen.

Key changes

- Flexible browser options: Plain external links open within the app's in-built browser, with a quick action button to open the link in your phone's default browser.
- Instant progress tracking: Because plain links open in a browser rather than inline, view and completion progress triggers the moment you open the link.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Release Notes > What’s new > Expanded .zip file support:
Mindtickle now supports general-purpose .zip file uploads within both the Content Center and Asset Hub. Admins can seamlessly upload, store, and share compressed file bundles directly through the platform, broadening the types of media and file packages accessible on mobile devices.

Highlight features

- General-purpose archives: Beyond traditional training formats, you can now upload, manage, and distribute general-purpose, non-SCORM compressed file bundles directly within the system.
- Intelligent package detection: The platform automatically scans uploaded files to determine if they are a SCORM package or a standard non-SCORM archive, applying appropriate backend handling instantly.
- Massive size threshold: Enjoy robust file sharing options with generous support for file package uploads up to a maximum size of 5 GB for both SCORM and non-SCORM formats.
- Asset Hub distribution: Non-SCORM archives are stored safely as downloadable assets, supporting full searchability, filtering, and cross-team sharing capabilities throughout Asset Hub.
- Unchanged SCORM workflows: Traditional SCORM .zip structures function exactly as they did before, playing back seamlessly through the integrated SCORM player within training modules.

- General-purpose archives: Beyond traditional training formats, you can now upload, manage, and distribute general-purpose, non-SCORM compressed file bundles directly within the system.
- Intelligent package detection: The platform automatically scans uploaded files to determine if they are a SCORM package or a standard non-SCORM archive, applying appropriate backend handling instantly.
- Massive size threshold: Enjoy robust file sharing options with generous support for file package uploads up to a maximum size of 5 GB for both SCORM and non-SCORM formats.
- Asset Hub distribution: Non-SCORM archives are stored safely as downloadable assets, supporting full searchability, filtering, and cross-team sharing capabilities throughout Asset Hub.
- Unchanged SCORM workflows: Traditional SCORM .zip structures function exactly as they did before, playing back seamlessly through the integrated SCORM player within training modules.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Advanced reports > FAQs:
What does "revenue influenced" mean?It's the total value of the deals that an asset was shared into and externally engaged with. For the exact definition and the related revenue metrics, see the Data & metrics reference guide for advanced reports.

Why is revenue influenced blank or lower than expected for some assets?Revenue is attributed only to assets shared by email (including Outlook, Outreach, and Gmail) and Digital Sales Rooms, because those channels connect to your CRM and can be tied to specific deals. Assets engaged through other channels, or not linked to a deal in your CRM, won't show revenue influence.

Why don't I see any deal or revenue data in the report?Deal and revenue data come from your connected CRM, and you see asset analytics only for the hubs where you have the Hub Analytics permission, and only for data that matches your filters. If nothing shows, check that deals are linked in your CRM, that you have access to the hubs in scope, and that your filters aren't excluding the data. Asset Hub is a paid feature; if you're not sure whether it's enabled, contact your Customer Success Manager.

Why don't my numbers match another report, or what I saw before?Totals depend on the filters and time period applied, so two reports with different scopes show different numbers. Check that the filters match before comparing. For what each metric counts, see the Data & metrics reference guide for advanced reports.

How current is the data?The Updated on and Next refresh timestamps at the top of the report show when the data last refreshed and when it will refresh next. For the refresh schedule, see Data update frequency for analytics reports and dashboards.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Advanced reports > Audit > Audit recommendations:
A per-asset table with an actionable recommendation for each asset. Alongside the recommendation, it shows the asset name, asset owner (username), asset status, expiration date, whether the asset is expired, whether a description was added, whether the owner is inactive or has lost access, the number of attributes added, days since last updated, and days since last engaged. Asset names link to the asset.

The Audit recommendation column gives one of four values:

- Keep: The asset is recent and actively engaged with. No action needed.
- Update: An expiration date or file update reminder has passed or is approaching. Review and update the asset.
- Review: Engagement has dropped compared to the previous 30 or 90 days. Decide whether to update, archive, or keep it.
- Archive: The asset meets the criteria for being retired from active use.

Note: The recommendation weighs a combination of signals, including recency, engagement trends, and configured reminders. The exact criteria may change as the feature matures.

The Coverage tab shows how your published assets are distributed, so you can spot gaps and imbalances across the library.

- Asset distribution by usage: The split between internal and external assets.
- Asset distribution by type: The split by file type, such as PDF, PPT, video, image, and DOC.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Advanced reports > Default filters:
The report applies a set of filters that scope the data you see. When you change a filter, the widgets on both the Audit and Coverage tabs update to match. chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Advanced reports > FAQs:
What do the audit recommendations (Keep, Update, Review, Archive) mean?Keep means the asset is recent and engaged with. Update means an expiration date or file update reminder has passed or is approaching. Review means engagement has dropped and you should decide what to do. Archive means the asset meets the criteria for retirement. The recommendation weighs recency, engagement trends, and configured reminders, and the exact criteria may change over time. For more, see the Data & metrics reference guide for advanced reports.

Why is an asset flagged as having no owner?An asset loses its owner when the assigned user is deleted or deactivated. Reassign these assets to an active team member so they stay maintained.

Why do the Coverage charts show fewer assets than Total assets?The Coverage charts count published assets, so drafts and archived assets aren't included in those distributions.

Why don't I see any data in the report?You see asset analytics only for the hubs where you have the Hub Analytics permission, and only for data that matches your filters. If nothing shows, check that you have access to the hubs in scope and that your filters aren't excluding the data. Asset Hub is a paid feature; if you're not sure whether it's enabled, contact your Customer Success Manager.

Why don't my numbers match another report, or what I saw before?Totals depend on the filters applied, so two reports with different scopes show different numbers. Check that the filters match before comparing. For what each metric counts, see the Data & metrics reference guide for advanced reports.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Advanced reports > FAQs:
Why do I only see recent invitations?The Module invited during filter covers a recent window by default (today and the previous days shown in the filter). Change that filter to widen the range and include older invitations.

What does Completion % mean?It's the percentage of a learner's invited modules that they've completed. A learner invited to five modules who has completed one shows 20%.

Why don't my numbers match another report, or what I saw before?Totals depend on the filters and time period applied, so two reports with different scopes show different numbers. Check that the filters match before comparing. For what each metric counts, see the Data & metrics reference guide for advanced reports.

How current is the data?The Updated on and Next refresh timestamps at the top of the report show when the data last refreshed and when it will refresh next. For the refresh schedule, see Data update frequency for analytics reports and dashboards.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Advanced reports > What this report shows > Table widget:
The Learner by module by series summary table lists one row per learner, module, and series. For each row, it shows:

- Module invitation date: When the learner was invited to the module.
- Module completion status: Where the learner is on that module, for example not started, in progress, or pass.
- Module completion percentage: How much of the module the learner has completed, as a percentage.

The table widget scrolls rather than splitting into pages, and you can widen columns to read long values. Large reports load in batches (for example, the first 100 rows of several hundred), so scroll to load more.

Tip: In a widget, you can click a value to filter the rest of the report by it. Use the filter panel to clear it again.

- Module status: Includes published modules by default.

- Learner module invitation status: Includes invited learners by default.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Advanced reports > Download and:
Once the report is published, the report header gives you six actions: Edit, Download, Email, Share, Duplicate, and Delete.

- Download: save the whole report as a PDF, with options for paper size, orientation, and the header and footer details to include. To download a single widget's data as CSV or Excel, use that widget's Options menu instead.
- Email: send the report to admins (the full report) or to managers (a personalized report covering only their reportees). You can send it now or schedule it, choose the widgets to include, and pick CSV or Excel.
- Share: share the published report with admins, managers, or scope admins, individually or by group. Recipients can apply their own filters.
- Duplicate and Delete: copy the report, or remove it.

For the full steps on downloading, emailing, scheduling, and sharing, see Manage advanced reports.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Advanced reports > FAQs:
Why is Average module rating 0 or blank?The average counts only modules with more than 10 ratings submitted. If your modules haven't received enough ratings yet, the widget shows 0. The number of module ratings submitted is shown below the widget.

What's the difference between module invitations sent, started, and completed?Sent is the number of module invitations issued. Started is how many of those a learner has begun. Completed is how many a learner has finished. The percentages next to started and completed show each as a share of all invitations sent.

Why don't my numbers match another report, or what I saw before?Totals depend on the filters and time period applied, so two reports with different scopes show different numbers. Check that the filters match before comparing. For what each metric counts, see the Data & metrics reference guide for advanced reports.

How current is the data?The Updated on and Next refresh timestamps at the top of the report show when the data last refreshed and when it will refresh next. For the refresh schedule, see Data update frequency for analytics reports and dashboards.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Advanced reports > FAQs:
What's the difference between % learner started and % learner completed?% learner started is the share of a module's invited learners who have begun it. % learner completed is the share who have finished it. Both are calculated against the learners invited to that module.

Why does a module appear under more than one series?A module can be part of more than one series. When it is, it appears once under each series it belongs to, so you can see how it performs in each context.

Why do I only see recent invitations?The Module invited during date filter covers the last 90 days by default (today and the previous 89 days). Change that filter to widen the range and include older invitations.

Why don't my numbers match another report, or what I saw before?Totals depend on the filters and time period applied, so two reports with different scopes show different numbers. Check that the filters match before comparing. For what each metric counts, see the Data & metrics reference guide for advanced reports.

How current is the data?The Updated on and Next refresh timestamps at the top of the report show when the data last refreshed and when it will refresh next. For the refresh schedule, see Data update frequency for analytics reports and dashboards.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Advanced reports > What this report shows > Table widget:
The Series summary table lists one row per series. For each series, it shows:

- Module invitations: The number of module invitations in the series.
- Module invitations started and Module invitations completed: How many of those invitations learners have started and completed.
- Completion %: The completion percentage for the series.
- Score %: The average score for the series, as a percentage.
- Total group ID: The number of groups the series is assigned to.

The table widget scrolls rather than splitting into pages, and you can widen columns to read long values. Large reports load in batches (for example, the first 100 rows of several hundred), so scroll to load more.

Tip: In a widget, you can click a value to filter the rest of the report by it. Use the filter panel to clear it again.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Advanced reports > Default filters:
The report applies a set of filters that scope the data you see. When you change a filter, the widgets update to match. To change, add, or reset filters, see Widgets and filters in advanced reports. The filter panel includes a Restore my default filters option to return to the original setup.

The default filters are:

- Days in module invitation date: Includes modules invited today and in the last 89 days by default (about the last 90 days). Widen this to see older invitations.
- Series name: Includes all by default. Focus on specific series.
- Learner status: Includes active and added learners by default.
- Learner module invitation status: Includes invited learners by default.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Advanced reports > Default filters:
The report applies a set of filters that scope the data you see. When you change a filter, the widgets update to match. To change, add, or reset filters, see Widgets and filters in advanced reports. The filter panel includes a Restore my default filters option to return to the original setup.

The default filters are:

- Days in module invitation date: Includes modules invited today and in the last 29 days by default. Widen this to see older invitations.
- Learner display name: Includes all by default. Focus on specific learners.
- Series name: Includes all by default. Focus on specific series.
- Module name: Includes all by default. Focus on specific modules.
- Module status: Includes published modules by default.
- Module type: Includes all by default. Filter by the type of module.
- Learner status: Includes active and added learners by default.
- Learner module invitation status: Includes invited learners by default.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Advanced reports > Download and:
Once the report is published, the report header gives you six actions: Edit, Download, Email, Share, Duplicate, and Delete.

- Download: save the whole report as a PDF, with options for paper size, orientation, and the header and footer details to include. To download a single widget's data as CSV or Excel, use that widget's Options menu instead.
- Email: send the report to admins (the full report) or to managers (a personalized report covering only their reportees). You can send it now or schedule it, choose the widgets to include, and pick CSV or Excel.
- Share: share the published report with admins, managers, or scope admins, individually or by group. Recipients can apply their own filters.
- Duplicate and Delete: copy the report, or remove it.

For the full steps on downloading, emailing, scheduling, and sharing, see Manage advanced reports.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Analytics & Reporting > Advanced reports > FAQs:
What's the difference between invitations sent, started, and completed?Sent is the number of module invitations issued. Started is how many of those a learner has begun. Completed is how many a learner has finished. The percentages next to started and completed show each as a share of all invitations sent.

Why do I only see recent invitations?The Days in module invitation date filter covers the last 29 days by default. Change that filter to widen the range and include older invitations.

Why don't my numbers match another report, or what I saw before?Totals depend on the filters and time period applied, so two reports with different scopes show different numbers. Check that the filters match before comparing. For what each metric counts, see the Data & metrics reference guide for advanced reports.

How current is the data?The Updated on and Next refresh timestamps at the top of the report show when the data last refreshed and when it will refresh next. For the refresh schedule, see Data update frequency for analytics reports and dashboards.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Announcements > Overview:
Until now, attributes, tags, and asset properties lived separately across Mindtickle. This update brings them into one connected system. Three things are changing: attributes merge into tags, asset properties move to files in Content Center, and you can create assets directly from Content Center. For admins, this means content governance becomes easier and more centralized. You maintain one labeling system instead of two, manage a file's information in one place, and spend less time switching between Asset Hub and Content Center.

Most of this happens automatically. Everything you've built is preserved, your sellers and learners won't notice a difference, and you don't need to do anything to migrate. This article walks through what's changing so you know what to expect and where to find things afterward.

At a glance:

- Attributes are becoming tags
- Managing tags moves to a single Tags page under Account
- Asset properties move to the file
- You can create assets directly from Content Center

Your existing tags, attributes, and property values are all preserved.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Announcements > Benefits:
This release is about making content easier to organize, govern, and find, with the biggest gains for admins who manage content day to day.

- One labeling system and centralized content governance. Attributes and tags did the same job in different parts of the product, so you maintained two separate lists and kept them in sync. Now a single tag system works across Content Center, Training, and Asset Hub, managed from one screen under Account → Tags .
- A file's information lives in one place. Asset properties like usage, download, and customization settings move to the file in Content Center, alongside its tags and other details. You manage everything about a file from one panel instead of splitting it across Asset Hub and Content Center.
- Fewer context switches when creating assets. Because a file already carries its properties and tags, you can create assets directly from Content Center without switching to Asset Hub to fill in details. One place to create and manage, with fewer hops.
- Better content discovery. One set of tags across training and assets means consistent labeling in both the admin experience and the learner experience, so it's faster to filter and find what you need.

Here's a summary of what's in this release. Each item is explained in detail below.

| Change | What it means for you | Suggested action |

| Attributes become tags | The separate "attributes" concept in Asset Hub is being unified with tags. Everything you labeled with attributes is now labeled with tags, and you work from one shared tag vocabulary across Content Center, Training, and Asset Hub. | None |
| Tag management moves to Account → Tags | The page for managing tags now lives under Account → Tags, instead of separately under Training and Asset Hub. | Note the new location |
| Asset properties move to files | Properties that were set on the asset in Asset Hub, such as usage, download and customization settings, description, thumbnail, owner, expiration, and reminders, now live on the file and appear in Content Center. | None |
| New permission for creating tags | A new, narrower permission — Create Tags (CREATE_TAGS) — lets users create tags and tag categories without being able to edit or delete existing ones. | Review custom roles (if any) that manage attributes |
| Create assets from Content Center | You can now create assets directly from Content Center, without switching to Asset Hub to fill in properties. | Optional shortcut |
| Assets no longer saved as drafts | Assets are no longer saved as drafts. Your existing draft assets stay accessible through a filter in each hub. | None |

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Announcements > 1. Attributes are now tags:
Until now, Mindtickle had two separate labeling systems that did very similar jobs: tags, used in Content Center and Training, and attributes, used in Asset Hub. Keeping both meant doing the same work twice. You'd create a label in one system, recreate it in the other, and then keep them in sync over time.

With this release, attributes and tags become a single system called tags. Wherever you used to see "attributes," you'll now see "tags." A tag you create or apply in any product is available everywhere, so there's one vocabulary to maintain instead of two.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Announcements > 1. Attributes are now tags > What happens to existing attributes:
- Everything is preserved. Every attribute category becomes a tag category, and every attribute value becomes a tag. Nothing is deleted.
- Values stay on your content. All attribute values currently applied to your assets carry over as tags, so your content stays labeled exactly as it was.

Note: Tags have always lived at the file level. Because attributes are becoming tags, a file that was used to create several assets now inherits the combined set of labels from all of them. You won't lose any labeling. If two assets from the same file had different attributes, the file ends up with both as tags.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Announcements > 1. Attributes are now tags > How duplicates are handled:
When attributes become tags, the migration handles overlaps in three ways, shown below.

- Exact duplicates are merged. If a tag category and an attribute category have the same name, such as "Region" in both, they combine into a single tag category. Name matching ignores capitalization, so "Region" and "region" are treated as the same. Matching tags within a merged category combine into one, and your content associations are remapped automatically.
- Near-duplicates are kept separate. Tag names must be unique across categories. If migrating an asset attribute would create a duplicate, the attribute's category name is added as a suffix instead of merging. For example, if "APAC" is an attribute under a "Region" category, and "APAC" is also under a "Regions" category in tags, the two categories will not merge because the names differ. A new "Region" category is created in tags, and the attribute becomes the tag "APAC (Region)." The same happens when the same attribute name exists in two different attribute categories: for example, "APAC" under both "Region" and "Sales Territory" becomes "APAC" in one and "APAC (Sales Territory)" in the other, so both are preserved as separate tags.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Announcements > 2. Tag permission changes > New permission: Create Tags:
We're introducing a new, create-only permission called Create Tags (CREATE_TAGS). Users with this permission can create new tags and tag categories and apply them, but not edit or delete existing ones. This is useful for people who need to add tags without changing or removing tags others rely on. It doesn't reduce anyone's existing access; full edit and delete capability continues to live with the Create and Manage Tags (CREATE_EDIT_TAGS) permission.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Announcements > 3. Asset properties move to files:
Previously, some properties were set on the asset in Asset Hub, things like usage, download permission, and customization settings, while other information lived on the file in Content Center. That meant managing one file's information in two places.

With this release, all of that information moves to the file level, and Content Center becomes its single home. A file's information used to be split across two tabs, Info and Tags. These are now combined into a single Info tab, in this order: general info, then tags, then properties, with the fields that moved over from the asset and any custom properties you've defined included alongside them. When you open an asset in Asset Hub, you'll see the underlying file's information instead of separate asset properties. When you edit a file's information, a "Hide non-editable info" toggle lets you focus on just the fields you can change.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Announcements > 4. Create assets from Content Center:
Today, creating an asset takes two steps. You upload a file and fill in its details in Content Center, then switch to Asset Hub to complete the required properties before the asset can be used. Now that file information lives in one place, there's a faster path.

You can create assets directly from Content Center. Open a file and click the Create asset with this file button to get started. Then, choose the hub you want to add it to, and create the asset, editing the file's information inline as you go without leaving Content Center. Asset creation from Asset Hub still works as before. This is an extra entry point, not a replacement.

Assets are no longer saved as drafts. Any draft assets you already have stay accessible through a filter in each hub.

Why this matters: This is the payoff of the changes above. With tags and properties together on the file, you manage everything in Content Center and send content to hubs from there. One place to create and manage, with fewer hops.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Announcements > Recommended actions:
Migration is automatic and nothing here is required, but a quick review before your account is updated helps avoid surprises.

- Review your tags and attributes for duplicates. Where a tag and an attribute share a name, they merge during migration, and this can't be undone. Cleaning up duplicates beforehand gives you control over what merges and what stays separate. See How duplicates are handled for details.
- Review custom roles that manage attributes. These roles move to create-only tag access. If any need to edit or delete tags, grant them Create and Manage Tags (CREATE_EDIT_TAGS) . See Tag permission changes for details.
- Note the new Tags location. Tag management moves to Account → Tags .

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Announcements > Attribute APIs:
If your team built integrations on the attribute APIs, those keep working for 180 days after your account is migrated, with deprecation notices. The affected endpoints are the ones that create attribute categories, create attributes, and delete attributes. Move your integrations to the equivalent tag endpoints before that window closes.

The impacted attribute-related endpoints in the Asset Hub APIs:

- Get details of an asset [ POST /api/assethub/v1/asset/{asset_id} ]
- Create attribute categories [ POST /api/assethub/v2/attribute_categories ]
- Create attributes [ POST /api/assethub/v2/attribute_categories/attributes ]
- Delete attributes [ DELETE /api/assethub/v2/attribute_categories/attributes ]

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Announcements > FAQs:
Where did the old Attributes and Tags pages go?

If you're looking for the Attributes page (previously under Assets) or the Tags page (previously under Training), everything will be in one place under Account → Tags. All your existing attribute values are there as tags.

Are my old attribute values still on my content?

Yes. Every attribute value currently applied to your assets carries over as a tag. Nothing is lost.

Do I need to do anything to migrate?

No. Migration is automatic and happens in the background. We'll let you know before your account is updated.

Will this affect my sales reps and learners?

Only the label. "Attributes" now reads "tags" in the places they'd see it, like filters, search, and asset preview. How they search, filter, and discover content doesn't change.

Will my reports and dashboards still work?

Yes. Existing analytics that referenced attributes keep working, with the labels updated to "tags."

Will my API integrations break?

Not right away. The existing attribute API endpoints keep working for 180 days after your account is migrated, with deprecation notices. Update your integrations before the window closes.

Can we opt out of this change?

No. This is a foundational, platform-wide update, so there isn't an opt-out.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Copilot > For admins > Controls > Filters:
Use the Filters panel on the right to narrow the data. The available filters are User group, User role, User status, Date range, and Channel. The Channel filter covers the three channels these reports track: Salesforce, Slack, and web and mobile (combined). Your filter selections carry over when you switch between the Adoption and Engagement tabs.

- Edit a filter : Select the edit (pencil) icon on a filter to open it. You can choose Include all (no filter applied), select specific values from the list, or use the Is not condition to exclude values. Use Select All or Clear All to manage your selections, then select Apply .
- Search within a filter : In a filter with a long list of values, start typing to search and narrow the list.
- Turn a filter on or off : Use the toggle on a filter to enable or disable it without losing your selection.
- Restore default filters : Select the restore icon to return to your default filters.
- Manage default filters : Select the more options (three-dot) icon for Default Filters and Set as My Default Filters , so the filters you use most are applied automatically.
- Collapse the panel : Collapse the Filters panel to give the reports more room, and expand it again when you need it.

Note: Some filters, such as User status and Date range, may be locked depending on report configuration.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Release Notes > New features > DSR reporting API tables for rooms, deals, and room contact visits:
Mindtickle’s OData-based reporting APIs now include Digital Sales Room data, through three new tables you can pull into your own reporting and BI tools:

- DsrRooms: One row per room, covering room details, owner and creator, the linked deal, and access settings.
- DsrDeals: One row per CRM deal linked to a room, covering deal amount, currency, stage, and account details.
- DsrRoomContactVisits: One row per visit, covering who visited, and the device and location they visited from.

Each table returns row-level data, so you can build your own counts, filters, and joins in tools like Tableau, Power BI, or Excel. Join the tables on the room ID and deal ID to answer questions such as how many rooms each user created, how many had at least one visitor, and how many of those were tied to a CRM deal.

For more information, see the Download reporting API tables and the metadata sheet.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Release Notes > Enhancements > Export default report data via email:
You can now export report data directly from a default report (out-of-the-box report) page and have it emailed to you, without going to advanced reports. This adds an Email button to any default report page that includes a table, so you can send the table's data to an admin or manager as a CSV or Excel (.xlsx) file.

This is available on default report pages that include a table. It is not available on advanced reports, or on default report pages without a table (such as Mission Overview).

Here's how it works:

- On a default report page that includes a table, select the Email button in the page actions at the top.
- Choose the recipients (admins or managers), and add anyone to CC.
- Select the table to export, and enter the email subject and body.
- Choose the format, CSV or Excel (.xlsx), and the email template.
- The system exports all rows and columns currently shown in the table.
- Recipients receive an email with a link to download the file.

What the export includes:

- Learner profile fields : Each learner row is appended with all configured learner profile fields for that learner, such as name, email, manager, and custom fields. On Coaching and Missions pages, profile fields are added to the Learners tab data only, not the Reviewers tab. If a table has no learner rows, no profile fields are added.
- Applied filters : Any filters applied to the report at the time of export are preserved in the exported file.
- Data scoping : The export includes only the rows you have permission to see.
- Empty tables : If the table has no data, the export is a header-only file.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Release Notes > Enhancements > Independent control of shared-report access and analytics data scoping:
Shared-report visibility and analytics data scoping are now controlled by two separate permissions. Previously the two were linked, so granting a user access to shared reports also affected how their analytics data was scoped, and vice versa. You can now control each independently.

Two new permissions:

- View shared report (VIEW_SHARED_REPORT): Controls whether a user sees the "Shared with Me" tab and can open and share reports shared with them, on both the learning site and the admin site.
- Unscoped analytics access (UNSCOPED_ANALYTICS_DATA_ACCESS): Controls whether a user bypasses analytics data scoping. This is only meaningful for users who already have a scoping context, such as enablement admins, managers, and scoped admins. For users with no scoping role, it has no effect, because no scoping applies to them.

Because these are independent, you can, for example, give a scoped admin access to shared reports while keeping their analytics data scoped, or grant unscoped data access without changing their report visibility.

Existing access is preserved. Users who already qualify for shared-report access under current rules keep it. Removing the new shared-report permission does not remove access from those users.

Change to data visibility for some role combinations: A legacy filter that limited data for admin + manager and admin + scoped admin role combinations on the learning site has been removed. Users with these role combinations may now see a broader set of analytics data than before. Review these users if you want their data scoping to stay as it was.

This affects enablement admins, managers, and scoped admins. Users with no scoping role are minimally affected.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Release Notes > Enhancements > Introducing AI-powered coaching insights in reviewer reports:
The new Coaching insights tab in the coaching reviewer reports provides senior leadership and enablement admins with an automated, AI-driven assessment of coaching quality across the organization. Evaluating the effectiveness of manager feedback at scale has traditionally been a time-consuming manual process, often making it difficult for leaders to identify systemic risks or provide targeted developmental support. Coaching insights addresses this gap by using AI to synthesize text, scores, and metadata from individual coaching sessions into actionable, executive-level intelligence.

Key highlights

- Executive-level team synthesis: The Team overview widget provides a high-level summary of the coaching behaviors across your entire organization. It highlights collective strengths and improvement opportunities while identifying exactly which managers are generating specific behavioral signals.
- Manager coaching summaries: The AI creates a Reviewer summary for each manager, defining their dominant coaching identity. This helps leaders quickly understand a manager's habits, such as their primary focus, key strengths, established behavioral patterns, and specific improvement opportunities.
- Direct session visibility: The Learners and sessions collapsible table allows leaders to drill down directly into specific coaching engagements. Clicking a hyperlinked module URL opens the actual coaching session in a new browser tab with view-only permissions, hiding editing capabilities to preserve data integrity.

How it works

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Release Notes > Enhancements > Introducing AI-powered coaching insights in reviewer reports:
- AI-powered analysis: The system evaluates coaching sessions using a 60/40 analytical lens, weighting 60% on coaching quality and 40% on coaching process and hygiene.
- Data accuracy guardrails: To prevent inaccurate insights, a manager must have a minimum of 3 completed coaching sessions (either one session filled three times or three separate sessions filled once). If this threshold is not met, the profile explicitly flags the data as insufficient.
- Maximum data limits: To ensure reflections remain relevant to current behaviors, the AI analyzes a maximum of 20 learners and the 10 most recent coaching sessions per reviewer.
- Bi-weekly refresh cadence: Dashboard insights refresh automatically on a bi-weekly schedule. Real-time data updates and historical date filtering are not supported.

Prerequisites for access

To access the Coaching insights tab, the following requirements must be met:

- This feature is not enabled for your Mindtickle instance. To enable it, please contact Mindtickle Support .
- Mindtickle’s AI capabilities must be enabled on your platform. To enable these features, contact Mindtickle Support .
- User hierarchy must be properly configured within the platform to accurately establish top-down reporting relationships.

For more information, see Coaching sessions reviewer reports.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Release Notes > Enhancements > Module completion API extended to all mission types:
The module completion API now supports five mission types, extending beyond the email and task evaluation missions covered in the May 2026 release. A single endpoint now completes email, screen-capture, voice-over-PPT, AI roleplay, and one-way video-pitch missions. This lets you programmatically mark these missions as complete for individual learners with a final score. The API synchronizes completion data from external partner portals, third-party certification sites, and legacy systems, ensuring the platform remains the central system of record for all readiness data.

Here are the key capabilities:

- Multiple mission modalities : Complete email, screen-capture, voice-over-PPT, AI roleplay, and one-way video-pitch missions through one endpoint. You do not need to know the mission type in advance; the system resolves it automatically.
- Final score override : Submit a single final score without a detailed rubric breakdown or a submission artifact.
- Silent completion : Manual reviewer workflows are bypassed. The system automatically starts and submits the evaluation using the provided score, so no "pending review" tasks or notifications are generated for the learner or the reviewer.
- Instant progression : Completion triggers downstream logic immediately, including series unlocking, certification eligibility, and real-time analytics updates.

Technical specifications

Endpoint:POST /api/v1/cag/<companyId>/series/<seriesId>/entity/<entityId>/learner/<learnerId>/_complete

Supports binary scoring of 0 (fail) or 100 (pass). The system defaults to 100 if the score is omitted. A static default media placeholder is attached to every completion to satisfy existing pipeline requirements. Every response includes a requestId for troubleshooting and internal logging.

Audit and visibility

Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Release Notes > Enhancements > Module completion API extended to all mission types:
- Origin tagging : API-driven completions are labeled with a completion_origin tag of external_completion_api in all admin reports and analytics, distinguishing them from organic submissions.

- Request tracking : Every response includes a requestId for simplified troubleshooting and internal logging.

Scope and limitations

- Supported mission types : Email, screen-capture, voice-over-PPT, AI roleplay, and one-way video-pitch missions only. Other mission types are not supported.
- Reviewer assignments : An active reviewer must be assigned to the learner for the mission before triggering the API.
- Scoring : Supports binary 0/100 scoring only. Granular rubric or parameter-level scoring is not supported.
- Final completion only : Supports final completion status. In-progress states from external systems are not tracked.
- No media uploads : External videos, PDFs, or audio files cannot be uploaded as part of the completion.

For more information, see Module completion API for missions.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Release Notes > Enhancements > Source asset changes in customized assets (beta):
Customized assets on the My assets page (under Assets section on the learning site) are now linked to the assets they were created from, whether created through Mix and match, Edit in PowerPoint for the web, or Edit in Google Slides. Mindtickle records which asset each page came from and flags the customized asset when that asset changes.

Page labels

- Updated: The source content has changed.
- Deleted, Archived, Expired, Non-customizable, No access: The source is no longer available, including pages dropped from a newer version of the source asset.

Asset labels on the My assets page

- Old version: All pages still usable; sharing unaffected.
- Unshareable: At least one page not usable; new shares blocked, though existing shares stay accessible.

Bringing an asset up to date

Opening a flagged asset displays a banner naming the number of changes and the affected pages.

- Accept changes: Replaces updated pages with the latest version from the source, removes unusable pages, and saves. Available on the asset details page and in the mix and match editor. Applies all pending changes at once
- Edit → Mix and match: Remove or replace pages individually, for reps who want to keep some pages as they are
- Delete asset: Replaces Accept changes on the asset details page when every page is unusable. The banner then reads "All pages in this asset are unusable."

Accepting changes can reduce an asset's page count, and a PPT asset may be saved as a PDF — the same rule that already applies when a customized asset is first created.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > What's New > Release Notes > Enhancements > Link Mindtickle resources and upload files (beta) in your Seller Copilot conversations:
Seller Copilot can now work directly with the specific content you care about. Two new options in the Copilot composer let you ground a conversation in exact Mindtickle resources or your own documents, so answers come from the material you point to instead of a broad search.

Link resources

Point Copilot at a specific module, asset, or call recording, and it answers using that resource as the source. There are two ways to start:

- Type @ directly in the chat input, or
- Select the + button, then choose Link resources .

Either way, the resource picker opens. From there:

- Choose a resource type: Suggested , Asset , Module , or Call AI .
- Type at least three characters after the @ to search and narrow results.
- Select a resource. It appears as a chip in your question, and Copilot answers using that resource as the source.
- You can link more than one resource in a single question.

Linked resources appear under Related sources in the response. Click any source to open it in a new tab.

Upload files (beta)

Note: The Upload files feature is in beta and not enabled by default for your Mindtickle instance. To enable it, contact Mindtickle Support.

Bring in a document Copilot has not seen before — a customer RFP, a deal deck, a pricing sheet — and ask questions about it. There are two ways to add files:

- Drag and drop files into the "Add files" window, or
- Select the + button, choose Upload files , then pick your files.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > Admin > What a scorecard does:
A scorecard defines how AI evaluates a specific type of call. It consists of evaluation parameters that represent the behaviors and outcomes you want the AI to assess during a conversation.

For every recorded call, AI:

- Score each evaluation parameter on a scale of 0 to 10 based on the guidance you provide.
- Generates a short coaching note with evidence from the call transcript to explain the score.
- Combines the individual parameter scores into an overall score, displayed as a percentage from 0 to 100%.

The scorecard is designed to support coaching conversations by providing context behind every score. Instead of only showing a score, such as Confirming Next Steps: 40%, it also explains why the score was given.

For example, the rep mentioned 'we'll schedule a demo' but did not confirm a date or assign ownership.

The AI also provides a suggestion on how the conversation could be improved.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > Admin > Best practices:
1. Cover the call types your team actually has, including Default

Configure scorecards for the call types your team handles most often. For example, if your team primarily conducts discovery and demo calls, create scorecards for those call types first.

Always configure a scorecard for the Default call type. Mixed-purpose calls, unusual conversations, and calls that the Call AI cannot confidently classify are automatically routed to Default. If no scorecard is assigned to the Default call type, those calls are not scored.

The built-in Default AI Scorecard is designed for these scenarios. Enable it for the Default call type from the beginning to ensure all eligible calls receive a score.

2. Write guidance as a scoring rubric, not a topic

Most scoring issues occur because the guidance is too vague.

AI uses your guidance as the scoring rubric for each evaluation parameter. It looks for evidence in the transcript and assigns a score based on the criteria you define. If the guidance is unclear or open to interpretation, the AI applies a stricter interpretation, which can result in lower or inconsistent scores.

- Less effective guidance : Evaluate whether the rep asked good discovery questions.
- Effective guidance : Score how well the conversation uncovered the customer's needs.
  - 0 to 2 : No discovery questions asked, or questions ignored the customer's responses.
  - 3 to 5 : General questions were asked, but core needs were not uncovered or validated with the customer.
  - 6 to 8 : Multiple needs uncovered and connected to business impact, with their importance validated with the customer.
  - 9 to 10 : The customer's needs, current state, and business impact were explicitly explored and confirmed, with priorities agreed upon.

3. Specify how to score when a behavior does not occur

If the AI finds no evidence for an evaluation parameter in the transcript, it assigns a score of 0. Some evaluation parameters apply only to specific situations. For example, objection handling is relevant only when the customer raises an objection. If the behavior never occurs and the guidance does not explain how to handle that scenario, the call may receive an unnecessarily low score.

To avoid this:

- Choose evaluation parameters that are expected to occur in every call of that type, such as setting the agenda, uncovering customer needs, or confirming next steps.
- If a parameter applies only in certain situations, clearly specify how it should be scored when that situation does not occur.

For example: If the customer raised no objections during the call, score 10.

This helps ensure that calls are scored fairly and consistently.

It does not have access to any information outside that conversation, such as:

- CRM data
- Previous calls

As a result, guidance such as "Check whether the rep followed up on last meeting's action items" or "Score against the account plan" cannot be evaluated.

When writing your scoring guidance, ensure that every evaluation criterion is based on information that can be directly observed in the call transcript. This helps the AI score calls accurately and consistently.

5. Keep the number of evaluation parameters focused

A scorecard can include up to 10 evaluation parameters, and each parameter contributes equally to the overall score.

This means that:

- In a 10-parameter scorecard, each parameter accounts for only 10% of the total score.
- A less important behavior has the same impact on the overall score as a critical one.

For most teams, five to seven well-defined evaluation parameters produce more meaningful scores and more focused coaching than a scorecard with 10 broad parameters.

Include only the behaviors that matter most. If evaluating a behavior would not change how a manager coaches a representative, it is better to leave it out.

6. Score observable behaviors, not personal traits

AI evaluates observable actions and outcomes in the conversation. It does not assess personality, enthusiasm, tone of voice, or speaking style.

Guidance based on subjective qualities, such as confidence or energy, can lead to inconsistent scoring. Instead, describe behaviors that can be identified in the transcript.

For example:

- Instead of : Sounded confident on pricing.
- Write : Stated pricing clearly and responded to pushback without deflecting or deferring.

Instead, describe behaviors that can be identified in the transcript. For example: - Instead of : Sounded confident on pricing. - Write : Stated pricing clearly and responded to pushback without deflecting or deferring.

The score also reflects the overall quality of the conversation, not the performance of an individual participant. If multiple members of your team participate in a call, the score applies to the conversation as a whole rather than to a single representative.

7. Test the scorecard using previously reviewed calls

Before enabling a scorecard, test it against 3 to 5 recorded calls that you have already reviewed.

Include a mix of calls, such as one strong call, one average call, and one weak call

When reviewing the results, verify that:

- The AI ranks the calls in the same order that you would.
- The coaching notes for each evaluation parameter reference the correct evidence from the transcript.

If the results are not what you expect, the guidance is usually too broad or unclear. Refine the scoring criteria to better describe the behaviors you want to evaluate, then test the scorecard again.

8. Treat guidance updates as a new baseline

Changes to a scorecard affect only future calls. Previously scored calls are not rescored.

Because AI closely follows the guidance you provide, even small changes to the scoring rubric can affect overall scores and team averages.

When reviewing score analytics, make sure anyone interpreting the results is aware of when the scoring rubric was updated.

For example, if the team's average score increases after a rubric change, the improvement may reflect the updated scoring criteria rather than an actual improvement in performance.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > Admin > Best practices:
9. Align scorecards and debriefs using the same methodology

Scorecards and debriefs serve different purposes but work best when they follow the same evaluation framework.

- Scorecards answer the question, "How well did the call go?"
- Debriefs answer the question, "What happened during the call?"

Both are configured on the same page and applied using the same call-type routing.

For example, if your organization uses MEDDIC:

- A MEDDIC debrief template captures the key evidence from the conversation.
- A MEDDIC-aligned scorecard evaluates how well those behaviors were demonstrated.

Using the same methodology for both provides managers with a consistent and complete coaching view for every call.

For more information, see Best practices to configure Call AI debriefs.

10. Understand the scoring limitations

Keep the following limitations in mind when configuring and using scorecards:

- Very short calls, typically with less than one minute of conversation, and calls with empty transcripts are skipped and do not receive a score.
- Calls longer than 2 hours are not scored.
- Scoring accuracy is highest for English language calls. Calls that switch between languages during the conversation may produce less accurate results.
- If a scorecard is not configured for a call type, the Scorecard tab does not appear for calls of that type.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > Admin > What a debrief does:
A debrief is a structured analysis of a call, shaped by what your organization wants to understand.

While the generic Summary provides an overview of the entire conversation, a debrief template defines specific trackers, such as Customer Pain Points, Next Steps Confirmed, or Competitive Mentions. Call AI analyzes every call using these trackers and extracts relevant insights for each.

Two organizations can use completely different debriefs for the same type of call, and this is intentional. A debrief template reflects your organization's sales methodology, ensuring reps and managers see the information that matters most to your sales process.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > Admin > Best practices:
1. Build each template for one prospect and one purpose

Think of a template as a lens. The most effective templates are designed for a specific audience and a specific use case.

For example:

- A discovery coaching template for managers conducting one-to-one coaching sessions.
- A deal review template for pipeline reviews.
- A handoff template for Account Executive (AE) to Customer Success Manager (CSM) transitions.
- A competitive intelligence template for product marketing.

You can configure up to five active templates for each call type, so use each one to provide a distinct perspective.

2. Give every tracker four parts of guidance

Effective guidance tells Call AI exactly what to extract and how to present it. Each tracker should include the following:

- What qualifies : Clearly define the information that should be extracted.
- What to exclude : Specify similar information that should be ignored.
- What good output looks like : Provide an example of the expected output.
- What to return if nothing is found : Include an explicit fallback statement.

Example:

| Bad guidance | Track when the rep handled objections. |
| --- | --- |
| Good guidance | Identify moments where the rep acknowledged and responded to a customer objection. Ignore general questions or feature clarifications. Summarize each objection and the response (for example, Customer questioned implementation timeline; rep committed to a phased plan). If no objection was raised, state: "No objection was discussed. |

The exclusion rule helps Call AI ignore information that is only loosely related to the tracker, ensuring the insights stay focused and relevant.

This helps verify that the fallback statement is used instead of Call AI generating unnecessary content. Review the output, refine the guidance, and test again before enabling the template. - Discovery Coaching (Managers)
- Deal Review
- Customer Handoff

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Call AI > Admin > Best practices:
- Calls shorter than approximately one minute do not generate debriefs.
- Calls longer than two hours are skipped.
- Debrief quality is best for English language calls. Switching languages during a call can reduce extraction quality.
- Debriefs are generated only for calls recorded after the feature is enabled on your site.

Example debrief template for discovery calls

Call type: Prospecting/Discovery

Intended audience: Managers preparing one-to-one coaching sessions.

| Tracker | Guidance |
| --- | --- |
| Pain points identified | Extract the problems the customer describes and the business impact they mention. Exclude feature requests, wish lists, and casual complaints.Example: Onboarding takes more than six months, resulting in delayed customer adoption. or lost a deal to a competitor with a faster implementation timeline.If none: No pain points surfaced. |
| Qualification coverage | Extract information discussed about the customer's budget, decision-making authority, and timeline. Also, identify any of these areas that were not covered during the conversation. Exclude assumptions or speculation made by the sales representative.If none: No qualification discussed. |
| Competitive mentions | Extract competitors that the customer mentions and include the context in which they were discussed. Exclude competitors mentioned only by the sales representative.If none: No competitors mentioned. |
| Next steps confirmed | Extract the agreed next steps that include both a clear owner and a target date. Exclude vague commitments or intentions, such as We'll reconnect soon.If none: No next steps confirmed. |
| Risks and blockers | Extract the risks or obstacles that the customer identifies as preventing progress, and indicate who is responsible for resolving them. Exclude hypothetical scenarios or potential issues that were not explicitly discussed.If none: No blockers raised. |

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Checklist:
A checklist module contains tasks that you can review or complete as part of your training. Depending on how your admin configures the checklist, you can complete the tasks or view them without marking them as complete.

This article explains how to open and complete a checklist module and how view-only checklists work.

This article explains how to open and complete a checklist module and how view-only checklists work.
chunks.headingPath: Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Checklist
chunks.title: Complete a checklist [learner]

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Checklist > Open a checklist:
To open a checklist module:

1. Sign in to the learning site.
2. On the homepage, in the What’s new in assigned widget, select the checklist module. For example, Acme Sales Onboarding. You can also open an assigned checklist from the Modules tab or directly from the series. The checklist opens. The Overview panel lists the checklist tasks. From the checklist, you can:

- Search for a task in the search bar.
- View the due date, the number of completed tasks, and the total number of tasks.
- View your score and maximum score if scoring is configured for the checklist.

chunks.headingPath: Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Checklist > Open a checklist
chunks.title: Complete a checklist [learner]

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Checklist > Complete checklist tasks:
To complete checklist tasks:

1. Click Start to begin the checklist.
2. Select a task.
3. Review or perform the task.
4. Click Mark complete . Note: If your admin configures the checklist as view-only, you can open and review the tasks, but you cannot mark them as complete.
5. Click Next task to move to the next task.
6. Repeat these steps until you complete all the checklist tasks. After you mark a task complete, the system updates the task status and your checklist progress. If scoring is configured, it also updates your score. Completed tasks display a green check mark.
7. After you complete the final task, click Exit checklist . The system confirms that the module is complete and displays your final score. Select Go to series to return to the series, or select Go to checklist overview to return to the checklist.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Asset Hub:
When you create a customized asset, Mindtickle records which asset each page in your copy came from. That original asset is called the source asset. If a source asset is later changed or becomes unavailable, Mindtickle flags your customized asset, so you never share content that is out of date.

This article explains the labels you will see, what each one means, and how to bring a customized asset up to date.

Note: This feature is in beta.

- Customized assets created using Mix and match are tracked.
- Customized assets created using Edit in PowerPoint for the web or Edit in Google Slides are tracked from the July 2026 release onward. Copies created using those options before this release are not tracked.

Mindtickle UI uses slides for PowerPoint assets and pages for PDF assets. This article uses "page" throughout.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Asset Hub > Labels on individual pages:
Open a customized asset, or open it in the mix and match editor, and each affected page carries a label naming what happened to its source asset.

| Label | What happened to the source asset |
| --- | --- |
| Updated | Its content has changed. |
| Deleted | It has been deleted. This label also appears when a newer version of the source asset no longer contains the page your copy was using. |
| Archived | It has been archived. |
| Expired | It has passed its expiry date. |
| Non-customizable | Your admin has stopped allowing customized assets to be created from it. |
| No access | Your access to it has been restricted. |

Pages labelled Updated are still usable — the content in your copy simply is not the latest. Pages with any of the other labels are no longer usable, because Mindtickle can no longer reach the source they came from.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Asset Hub > Labels on the customized asset:
On the My assets page, the asset itself carries a single label summarizing the state of all its pages.

| Label | When it appears | Can you share it? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No label | No page in the asset is flagged. | Yes. |
| Old version | One or more pages are labelled Updated, and every page in the asset is still usable. | Yes. Sharing is not affected. |
| Unshareable | At least one page in the asset is no longer usable. | No. The Share button is unavailable until you resolve those pages. Anything you shared earlier stays accessible to those recipients. |

Note: Old version and Updated describe the same situation. Old version appears next to the asset name on the My assets page; Updated appears on the individual pages. Unshareable only ever appears next to the asset name — on the pages themselves you will see the specific reason instead.
