chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Asset Hub > Bring a customized asset up to date > Accept all changes at once:
Click Accept changes and Mindtickle does the following in one step:

- Replaces each Updated page with the latest version from its source asset.
- Removes every page that is no longer usable.
- Saves the asset.

The asset then has no pending changes. If it was Unshareable, it becomes shareable again.

Accept changes is available in two places and behaves the same way in both: on the customized asset page, and in the mix and match editor (Edit icon → Mix and match). It is available whenever at least one page in the asset is still usable — including on assets labelled Unshareable.

Note: Accept changes applies every pending change at once. You cannot select individual pages. To keep some pages as they are, use the mix and match editor instead.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Asset Hub > Bring a customized asset up to date > Update pages yourself:
To decide page by page:

1. On the customized asset, click the Edit icon and select Mix and match .
2. Turn on View changed pages only to filter the grid down to the affected pages.
3. Click the open-in-new icon on a page to open its source asset and compare the content.
4. Delete the pages you no longer want, and use Add slides to bring in updated ones.
5. Click Save changes .

Note: You must delete every page labelled Deleted, Archived, Expired, Non-customizable, or No access before you can save. Pages labelled Updated do not block saving.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Asset Hub > Things to be aware of > Your page count and file type can change:
Accepting changes removes unusable pages, so your asset may end up with fewer pages than before.

It may also change file type. A PowerPoint customized asset stays a PowerPoint file only if every remaining page comes from a PowerPoint source; if any remaining page comes from a different file type, the asset is saved as a PDF. A customized asset that is already a PDF always stays a PDF. This is the same rule that applies when you first create a customized asset using mix and match.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Mindtickle Guide for Learners > Asset Hub > Things to be aware of > What is not flagged:
Mindtickle compares the text on each page. The following changes to a source asset produce no label:

- Pages added to the source asset. Your copy is unchanged and nothing is flagged, so open the source asset directly if you want the new content.
- Pages reordered in the source asset, where the content itself has not changed.
- Changes to images, branding, layout, or design where the text has not changed.
- Changes to speaker notes or hidden pages.
- Renaming the source asset, or changing its properties or tags.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > FAQs:
Mindtickle supports the following content and file types:

- Document files, including PPT/PPTX, PDF, DOC/DOCX, XLS/XLSX, SWF, and ZIP
- Images, including JPG, JPEG, PNG, GIF, TIF, and TIFF
- Adobe Illustrator (.ai) files with static thumbnail and preview support
- Videos, including embedded videos from YouTube, Wistia, and Prezi
- Audio files, such as WAV
- Embedded slideshows from Slideshare
- Web-published objects from authoring tools such as Articulate, Captivate, and Camtasia

Note:

- Mindtickle does not support .key (Keynote) files.
- Microsoft Excel macro-enabled Workbook (.xlsm) and Power BI Desktop (.pbix) files are not supported.
- Animated GIF and SWF files are not supported on the mobile app.
- Non-SCORM ZIP files are supported for upload and download in Content Center and Asset Hub, but are not supported in training modules.
- TIF/TIFF and AI file previews are static and do not support editing, annotations, or layer interactions.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > FAQs:
Content (PDF, PPT, XLS, DOC, videos or images) can be uploaded from:

- Computer
- Dropbox
- Box
- Google Drive
- OneDrive
- Salesforce

- YouTube: Paste the YouTube video link or embed code.Note: Ensure that the YouTube video is public.
- SlideShare: Paste the SlideShare link of the presentation. The embed code of the presentation from SlideShare is not supported yet.
- Any content which supports Oembed can be embedded. For example, Prezi, Vimeo, X (formerly Twitter) feed, Flickr.

For more information, see Upload or embed content in a course or quick update.

For information about how to allow media files, see Unblock Email, video, and media (allowlist).

The score and completion of the embedded content can be tracked in Mindtickle analytics for a given learner. As soon as the learner accesses an embedded content, it is marked complete and the learner gets a full score for that content.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > FAQs:
Mindtickle supports the following video formats:

- MP4
- M4V
- FLV
- MOV
- AVI
- MPEG
- MPG
- WMV Note: In DSR, the above formats can be uploaded only via My Assets in Asset Hub. For direct file uploads, DSR supports only .MP4 files.

Video codecs, color spaces, and bit rates

A codec is the format used to encode videos. For optimal results, we recommend using H.264, a widely used codec that offers a good balance of high visual quality and efficient file size. When encoding, select the "High Profile" H.264 setting instead of the "Main Profile" for better performance.

Color spaces define how color information is stored and rendered in a video. We currently support the following color spaces:

- BT.601 or Rec. 601 (standard definition video)
- BT.709 or Rec. 709 (high definition video)

The bit rate (data rate) influences both the visual quality of the video and its file size. Higher bit rates generally result in better quality but larger files.

| Video quality | Bit rate |
| --- | --- |
| 1080p | 4 Mbps - Above |
| 720p | 2.5 Mbps - 3 Mbps |
| 480p | 1.5 Mbps - 2 Mbps |
| 360p | 750 Kbps - 1 Mbps |
| 240p | 500 Kbps - 750 Kbps |
| 144p | 250 Kbps - 500 Kbps |

chunks.title: Supported file types and size limits for uploading and syncing content to Mindtickle [admin]

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Video Tutorials > Admin > Content Development > FAQs > Supported file types and size limits:
The following table outlines the supported file types, their corresponding formats, and the maximum file sizes allowed for each type of file (content). For example, image files cannot exceed 10 MB, while video files are limited to 7 GB. Use this information to ensure your content meets the Mindtickle platform's upload requirements.

| File type | Supported formats | Max file size |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Document | PDF, DOC/DOCX, PPT/PPTX, XLS/XLSX, SWF, ZIP | 500 MB |
| Image | JPG, JPEG, PNG, GIF, TIF/TIFF | 10 MB (250 MB for TIFF) |
| Design/Vector | AI (Adobe Illustrator) | 250 MB |
| Video | MP4, MOV, AVI, WMV, MKV, WEBM, MPEG, MPG, FLV, M4V, VOB | 7 GB |
| Audio | MP3, AAC, WAV, M4A, OGG, OGA, F4A | 200 MB |
| SCORM | ZIP | 5 GB |

Note:

- Reach out to your CSM if you need to increase the file size limits for image, audio, video, or SCORM files.
- Mindtickle supports SCORM 1.1, SCORM 1.2, and SCORM 2004 (all editions), as well as AICC and xAPI packages.
- We recommend SCORM 1.2 or SCORM 2004 (4th edition). We also recommend keeping your SCORM package size under 500 MB. For details on supported SCORM versions, upload steps, and troubleshooting, see SCORM content in Mindtickle .
- Mindtickle also supports non-SCORM .zip files for upload and download in Content Center and Asset Hub. Non-SCORM .zip files are not supported in training modules.
- .tif / .tiff and .ai files support thumbnail generation and static in-platform preview. Original files are preserved for download. Preview support varies by file variant — see Supported .TIFF and .AI file variations below.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Video Tutorials > Admin > Content Development > FAQs > File types not supported:
The following types of files are not supported in content upload or sync:

- File shortcuts, like Google Drive shortcuts
- Corrupt or invalid SCORM files
- Dot files, like .DS_Store
- Microsoft Excel macro-enabled Workbook (.xlsm) and Power BI Desktop (.pbix) files
- Non-SCORM .zip files are not supported in training modules
- Files without extensions
  - Files without extensions are not supported for uploads, but they are supported for syncing.
  - Ensure the file name includes the appropriate extension (e.g., .ppt for PowerPoint files). For example, save a PowerPoint file as XYZ.ppt .

- .tif / .tiff and .ai files display static previews and thumbnails within the platform.
- Original .tif / .tiff and .ai files are preserved for download.
- Non-SCORM .zip files are stored as downloadable assets and do not support preview or inline rendering.
- File type filters are available for Adobe Illustrator ( .ai ) and Image ( .tif / .tiff ) files.

chunks.text:
Help & Support > Help Center Home > Video Tutorials > Admin > Content Development > FAQs > Supported .TIFF and .AI file variations:
TIFF/TIF and Adobe Illustrator formats encompass a wide range of internal variants that differ in compression, color mode, layer structure, and encoding. Preview and thumbnail generation support varies depending on the specific variant of the file. The tables below outline known behavior for both file types.

Note:

- Files that cannot be previewed are still uploaded and stored successfully. A generic thumbnail is displayed in place of a generated preview, and the original file remains available for download.
- File variants not listed in above tables may behave differently.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Video Tutorials > Admin > Content Development > FAQs > Supported .TIFF and .AI file variations > Processing limits:
The following hard limits apply to preview generation for both .tif/.tiff and .ai files. Files that exceed either limit will not generate a preview, regardless of file type or variant.

| Limit | Maximum value |
| --- | --- |
| Image resolution | 100,000,000 pixels (e.g., 10,000 × 10,000 px or 5,000 × 20,000 px) |
| File size for preview conversion | 250 MB |

Note: The upload size limit for .tif/.tiff and .ai files is 250 MB. However, files may still fail preview generation if they exceed the pixel resolution limit, even when the file size is within range.

Help & Support > Help Center Home > Admin > Content Development > FAQs:
Mindtickle supports the following image formats:

- JPG
- JPEG
- PNG
- GIF

The following are the image size and resolution recommendations based on the image location on the Mindtickle platform:

| Image location | Recommended size | Recommended resolution |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Content item | Less than 5 MB | 1280 x 720 pixels |
| Factopedia | Less than 10 MB | 1280 x 720 pixels |
| Question image | Less than 5 MB | 500 x 320 pixels |
| Multiple choice image (options) | Less than 5 MB | 200 x 200 pixels |
| Match image with label (options) | Less than 5 MB | 200 x 200 pixels |
| Find location on map | Less than 5 MB | 550 x 320 pixels |
| Series/module/hub/asset thumbnails * | Less than 10 MB | Any 3:2 aspect ratio(example: 1500 × 1000 pixels) |
| Course map | Less than 5 MB | 1038 x 465 pixels |
| Cover image of learning site | Less than 10 MB | 1024 x 330 pixels |
| Logo for learning site | Less than 10 MB | 960 x 360 pixels |

* Keep series/module/hub/asset thumbnail image sizes under 1 MB to ensure optimal performance for learners when accessing these pages over slow or mobile internet connections.
